> RACE.FNAM T_Aka_Tsaesci
Tsaesci
赛蛇人

> RACE.DESC T_Aka_Tsaesci
The Tsaesci are the snake-folk of southern Akavir, best known for their rule over the Empire during the Second Era Akaviri Potentate. Though renowned for their skill as duelists, Tsaesci are more notorious for their nigh-immortality, a condition rumored to be caused by endemic vampirism. Long feared and venerated in equal measure by the peoples of Tamriel, Tsaesci are today rarely found outside the borders of their isolationist kingdom in the Uttermost East. What few remain in Tamriel are reclusive sages, esteemed advisors to high courts, or intractable guardians of ancient treasures.
赛蛇人是阿卡维尔南部的蛇民，以在第二纪元阿卡维尔摄政时期统治帝国而最为闻名。他们虽以决斗技巧著称，但更因其近乎不朽的生命而恶名昭彰，传闻此状态源于地方性的吸血鬼症。在泰姆瑞尔各族心中，赛蛇人长期以来备受敬畏与尊崇。如今，除了他们位于极东孤立王国的边境之外，鲜少能见到其身影。留在泰姆瑞尔的少数赛蛇人，或是隐居的智者，或是高等法庭备受尊敬的顾问，亦或是古老宝藏难以对付的守卫者。

> RACE.FNAM T_Cnq_ChimeriQuey
Chimeri-Quey
歧莫里-奎

> RACE.DESC T_Cnq_ChimeriQuey
Upon the waves of the Padomaic, there are no sailors more renowned than the Chimer of Quey; a remnant of the ancient and unaltered Chimer who made a great exodus out to sea. An enduring people known for their shrewdness and efficiency in all things, as well as their strange and esoteric traditions. Their sea-bound society has made them masters of trade, bringing the care and efficiency of sailing to the table of commerce.
在卡特诺奎的波涛之上，没有比奎之歧莫更负盛名的水手了；他们是古老且未经改变的歧莫遗族，曾进行过一次伟大的海上迁徙。这个坚韧的民族以其凡事精明高效以及奇异深奥的传统而闻名。他们以海为家的社会使其成为贸易大师，将航海的专注与效率带到了商业谈判桌上。

> RACE.FNAM T_Cnq_Keptu
Keptu-Quey
克普图-奎

> RACE.DESC T_Cnq_Keptu
The origins of the Keptu, the Men of Quey, are mysterious. They themselves do not provide many clues, beyond vague hints that they too came from Tamriel in the distant past. Their imposing fortresses and antiquated weaponry -- typically blunt or stylized to the point of being unrecognizable as instruments of war -- are at odds with their unimpeachable hospitality and ready smiles. One detects in them a stalwartness, an anxiety, a preparedness for battle.
奎之民，克普图人的起源是个谜。除了模糊地暗示他们同样在遥远的过去来自泰姆瑞尔之外，他们自己并未提供太多线索。他们那令人望而生畏的堡垒和过时的武器 -- 通常钝重或风格化到无法被认出是战争器具 -- 与他们无可指摘的好客精神和随时绽放的笑容格格不入。人们能从他们身上察觉到一种坚定、一种焦虑、一种对战斗的准备。

> RACE.FNAM T_Cyr_Ayleid
Ayleid
亚历德

> RACE.DESC T_Cyr_Ayleid
The Ayleids, or Wild Elves, have remained aloof toward civilization, preferring to practice the old ways far from the eyes of the world. The Wild Elves speak a variation of Old Cyrodilic, opting to shun Tamrielic. In temperament they are dark-spirited and taciturn-- though this is from the point of view of outsiders (or "Pellani" in their tongue).
亚历德，或称野精灵，始终与文明保持疏离，更偏爱在远离世俗目光之处践行古老的生活方式。亚历德讲一种古西罗帝尔语的变体，选择摒弃泰姆瑞尔通用语。性情上，他们心灵阴暗且沉默寡言-- 尽管这是从外人（或用他们的语言称为“佩拉尼”）的角度来看。

> RACE.FNAM T_Els_Cathay
Khajiit
卡吉特

> RACE.DESC T_Els_Cathay
The Cathay are a subspecies of the Khajiit of Elsweyr. Born under a waxing Masser and full Secunda, they are similar to the Suthay-raht in appearance, save for their lack of tail and most body fur. However, they poses greater posture and strength. One of the form which walks upon the heels of its feet instead the balls. Khajiit of all breeds have a weakness for sweets, especially the drug known as skooma. Many Khajiit disdain weapons in favor of their natural claws. They make excellent thieves due to their natural agility and unmatched acrobatics ability.
卡萨伊是艾斯维尔卡吉特的一个亚种。在盈相马瑟和满相塞昆达下诞生，他们在外观上与苏赛-拉特相似，但没有尾巴和大部分体毛。然而，他们拥有更挺拔的身姿和更强的力量。这是用脚跟而非脚掌行走的形态之一。所有种类的卡吉特都对甜食有嗜好，尤其是名为斯库玛的毒品。许多卡吉it不屑使用武器，更偏爱他们的天然利爪。他们天生的敏捷性和无与伦比的杂技能力使其成为出色的盗贼。

> RACE.FNAM T_Els_Cathay-raht
Khajiit
卡吉特

> RACE.DESC T_Els_Cathay-raht
The Cathay-raht are a subspecies of the Khajiit of Elsweyr, sometimes called "jaguar men". Born under a waxing Masser and Secunda, they are larger and stronger than Suthay. Khajiit of all breeds have a weakness for sweets, especially the drug known as skooma. While most Khajiit disdain weapons in favor of their natural claws, the Cathay-raht are skilled in the use of long blades. They make excellent thieves due to their natural agility and unmatched acrobatics ability.
卡萨伊-拉特是艾斯维尔卡吉特的一个亚种，有时被称为“豹人”。在盈相马瑟和塞昆达下诞生，他们比苏赛体型更大、力量更强。所有种类的卡吉特都对甜食有嗜好，尤其是名为斯库玛的毒品。虽然大多数卡吉特不屑使用武器而偏爱天然利爪，但卡萨伊-拉特擅长使用长剑。他们天生的敏捷性和无与伦比的杂技能力使其成为出色的盗贼。

> RACE.FNAM T_Els_Dagi-raht
Khajiit
卡吉特

> RACE.DESC T_Els_Dagi-raht
The tree-dwelling Dagi-raht of the Tenmar forest always land on their feet. Nimble acrobats and stealthy ambushers, they're also naturally gifted spellcasters. Though their diminutive size means they're outmatched in raw strength by most opponents, the Dagi-raht can rely on their exceptionally sharp claws in physical combat. They make excellent thieves, assassins, and nightblades. Due to their unsettlingly skeletal appearance, they're often met with distrust by other races and even their fellow Khajiit.
腾玛尔森林中栖居树上的达吉-拉特总能四脚着地。作为敏捷的杂技演员和潜行的伏击者，他们同时也是天赋异禀的施法者。尽管矮小的身材意味着他们在绝对力量上逊于大多数对手，但达吉-拉特在肉搏战中可以依赖他们异常锋利的爪子。他们是出色的盗贼、刺客和夜刃。由于其令人不安的骷髅般外貌，他们常常遭到其他种族甚至卡吉特同胞的不信任。

> RACE.FNAM T_Els_Ohmes
Khajiit
卡吉特

> RACE.DESC T_Els_Ohmes
The Ohmes are a subspecies of the Khajiit of Elsweyr. Born under a new Masser and full Secunda, they are similar in some ways to Wood Elves, although generally of lesser stature. In order not to be confused with Bosmer, many Ohmes favor fierce-looking face tattoos to emphasize their feline nature. A common form of Khajiit outside of Elsweyr, often serving as ambassadors or merchants. Khajiit of all breeds have a weakness for sweets, especially the drug known as skooma. Many Khajiit disdain weapons in favor of their natural claws. They make excellent thieves due to their natural agility and unmatched acrobatics ability.
欧姆斯是艾斯维尔卡吉特的一个亚种。在新相马瑟和满相塞昆达下诞生，他们在某些方面与木精灵相似，尽管通常身材较矮。为了不被误认为波兹莫，许多欧姆斯喜欢用凶猛的面部纹身来强调其猫科本质。这是艾斯维尔以外常见的一种卡吉特形态，常担任大使或商人。所有种类的卡吉特都对甜食有嗜好，尤其是名为斯库玛的毒品。许多卡吉特不屑使用武器，更偏爱他们的天然利爪。他们天生的敏捷性和无与伦比的杂技能力使其成为出色的盗贼。

Khajiit
卡吉特

The Ohmes-raht are a subspecies of the Khajiit of Elsweyr. Born under a new Masser and waxing Secunda, they are similar to Ohmes in many ways, though they have a greater stature and more pronounced feline features. They can be easily mistaken for men at a distance. One of the form which walks upon the heels of its feet instead the balls. Ohmes-raht are particularly common High Rock and Hammerfell. Khajiit of all breeds have a weakness for sweets, especially the drug known as skooma. Many Khajiit disdain weapons in favor of their natural claws. They make excellent thieves due to their natural agility and unmatched acrobatics ability. 
欧姆斯-拉特是艾斯维尔卡吉特的一个亚种。在新相马瑟和盈相塞昆达下诞生，他们在许多方面与欧姆斯相似，但身材更高大，猫科特征更明显。远看很容易被误认为是人类。这是用脚跟而非脚掌行走的形态之一。欧姆斯-拉特在高岩和落锤尤为常见。所有种类的卡吉特都对甜食有嗜好，尤其是名为斯库玛的毒品。许多卡吉特不屑使用武器，更偏爱他们的天然利爪。他们天生的敏捷性和无与伦比的杂技能力使其成为出色的盗贼。

> RACE.FNAM T_Els_Suthay
Khajiit
卡吉特

> RACE.DESC T_Els_Suthay
The Suthay are a subspecies of the Khajiit of Elsweyr. Born under a new Masser and Secunda, they are similar to Suthay-raht to the point that most non-Khajiit cannot tell them apart. They can be distinguished by their smaller posture and pale fur. Khajiit of all breeds have a weakness for sweets, especially the drug known as skooma. Many Khajiit disdain weapons in favor of their natural claws. Even more agile than other Khajiit, the Suthay make excellent thieves due to their unmatched acrobatics ability.
苏赛是艾斯维尔卡吉特的一个亚种。在新相马瑟和塞昆达下诞生，他们与苏赛-拉特相似到大多数非卡吉特无法区分。可以通过他们更矮小的身材和浅色毛皮来辨别。所有种类的卡吉特都对甜食有嗜好，尤其是名为斯库玛的毒品。许多卡吉特不屑使用武器，更偏爱他们的天然利爪。苏赛比其他卡吉特更加敏捷，凭借其无与伦比的杂技能力成为出色的盗贼。

> RACE.FNAM T_Hr_Ogre
Ogre
食人魔

> RACE.DESC T_Hr_Ogre
Not much is known about the brutish Ogres of Orsinium. Widely regarded as man-eaters, these simple savages co-exist with the rest of Malacath's children to some degree. With mighty bodies, they do not rely on armor to protect themselves. While they can use more sophisticated weaponry like spears and axes, they prefer the familiar intimacy of the club and fist. Their deafening roars send chills down the spines of all but the mightiest warriors. They may not be very bright, but they hunt with the clever cruelty of Mauloch.
人们对沃斯嘉的野蛮食人魔知之甚少。这些头脑简单的野蛮人被普遍视为食人族，在某种程度上与马拉卡斯其余的子嗣共存。他们拥有强壮的躯体，不依赖盔甲保护自己。虽然他们能使用矛和斧等更复杂的武器，但他们更偏爱熟悉的、能贴身肉搏的木棒和拳头。他们震耳欲聋的咆哮能让除了最强大战士之外的所有人不寒而栗。他们或许不太聪明，但狩猎时带着莫洛克的狡黠与残忍。

> RACE.FNAM T_Hr_Riverfolk
Riverfolk
河民

> RACE.DESC T_Hr_Riverfolk
Riverfolk are the horse-lords of the Bjoulsae Basin, the great river valley which lies between Hammerfell and High Rock. Equally skilled on riverboat or horseback, many riverfolk live in semi-nomadic clans whose camps move up and down the Bjoulsae in search of trade or safety. Others live settled lives as city-dwellers or rural farmers in the wider West. Riverfolk are commonly found in the employ of mercenary companies throughout Tamriel, who prize their talents with shield and sword.
河民是拜尤赛盆地 - 位于落锤与高岩之间的巨大河谷 - 的马背领主。无论在河船还是马背上都同样娴熟，许多河民生活在半游牧的氏族中，他们的营地在拜尤赛河上下游迁移，寻找贸易机会或安全之所。其他人则在更广阔的西部作为城市居民或乡村农民定居下来。河民常见于受雇于泰姆瑞尔各地的佣兵公司，这些公司看重他们在剑盾方面的天赋。

> RACE.FNAM T_Mw_Malahk_Orc
Malahk Orc
玛拉克兽人

> RACE.DESC T_Mw_Malahk_Orc
Hailing from the isolated, mountainous regions between Cyrodiil, Skyrim and Morrowind, the Malahk Orcs are a hardy people who put the barbarity of their Wrothgarian counterparts to shame. Honed by constant fighting in their land of Malahk-Bazul, the Malakh Orcs are capable of striking out in a frenzied berserk state when they succumb to their rage. Their mighty strength make them formidable with blunt weapons, axes and even bare fists, and their imposing stature enhances their ability to withstand heavy blows in medium and heavy armor.
玛拉克兽人来自西罗帝尔、天际和晨风之间偏远的山区，是一个坚韧的民族，其野蛮程度令他们沃斯嘉的同族都相形见绌。在玛拉克-巴祖尔之地不断的战斗中磨练而成，玛拉克兽人能在陷入狂怒时以狂暴的狂战士状态出击。他们强大的力量使其在使用钝器、斧头甚至赤手空拳时都令人生畏，而他们魁梧的身材增强了他们在中甲和重甲下承受重击的能力。

> RACE.FNAM T_Pya_SeaElf
Sea Elf
海精灵

> RACE.DESC T_Pya_SeaElf
The Maormer, called "Sea Elves" (or sometimes "Fish Elves" in Tamriel, are native to the southern island kingdom of Pyandonea. Folklore claims that they are the descendants of Aldmer rebels, exiled from the Summerset Isles during the early Merethic Era. Regardless of the veracity of this story, the Sea Elves have a burning hatred of their Altmeri cousins, and are rarely seen elsewhere in Tamriel. They are distinguished by their blank, white eyes and chameleon-like skin, an involuntary process which allows them to blend in with their environment. 
锚莫，被称为“海精灵”（在泰姆瑞尔有时也称“鱼精灵”），原生于南方的岛屿王国潘多尼亚。民间传说称他们是奥德莫叛军后裔，在精灵纪元早期被逐出夏暮群岛。无论这个故事真实性如何，海精灵都对他们的表亲高精灵怀有炽烈的仇恨，在泰姆瑞尔其他地方很少见到。他们以其空白、白色的眼睛和变色龙般的皮肤而区分，这是一种能让他们融入周围环境的无意识过程。

> RACE.FNAM T_Sky_Hill_Giant
Hill Giant
山巨人

> RACE.DESC T_Sky_Hill_Giant
Massive and imposing, the Hill Giants supposedly originate from the frozen, lost continent of Atmora. Their stone-like skin makes them impervious to frost and man-made weapons, and their colossal size grants them unparalleled strength.  While considered primitive, Hill Giants possess lifespans that outlast nearly every other creature on Tamriel. Who knows what secret and deep knowledge they might hold, gained over centuries of existence. 
山巨人体型庞大、气势逼人，据称起源于冰冻的失落大陆 - 阿特莫拉。他们岩石般的皮肤使其对冰霜和人造武器无动于衷，其巨大的体型赋予他们无与伦比的力量。虽然被认为是原始的，但山巨人的寿命几乎超过了泰姆瑞尔所有其他生物。谁知道他们在数个世纪的存在中，可能掌握了何等秘密深邃的知识。

> RACE.FNAM T_Sky_Reachman
Reachman
河峪人

> RACE.DESC T_Sky_Reachman
The natives of the Reach are derogatorily referred to as Reachmen, or the Witchmen of High Rock. While their ancestry is primarily Nordic and Breton, the Reachmen have intermingled with almost every  race on Tamriel, and they are considered a mongrel race by most. Their society is primitive and tribal, comparable only to the nomadic Orc tribes with whom they share both a social and a geographical niche. They are adept at subsiding in the wilderness, feeling right at home in the mesas and hills of The Reach. Reachmen practice dangerous forms of hedge-magic, and are considered fierce and relentless warriors, often employed as mercenaries. 
河峪地区的原住民被贬称为河峪人，或高岩的巫觋。虽然他们的血统主要属诺德和布莱顿，但河峪人几乎与泰姆瑞尔所有种族都有交融，被大多数人视为杂种民族。他们的社会原始而部落化，只能与他们共享社会和地理生态位的游牧兽人部落相提并论。他们擅长在荒野中生存，在河峪的平顶山和丘陵中如鱼得水。河峪人修习危险的荒野魔法，被认为是凶猛而无情的战士，常被雇佣为佣兵。

> RACE.FNAM T_Val_Imga
Imga
巨猿族

> RACE.DESC T_Val_Imga
Imga are the venerable ape-folk of Tamriel's southwest, a diverse people famed for their spiritural innovations and resilience through periods of political turmoil. Though the Imga clans' ancestral homelands lie in the jungles of Valenwood, the Great Apes have adapted to the modern age, and now commonly take employment as learned advisors to cult orders, polities, and trading consortiums throughout the Western Empire. Imga are talented acrobats and pugilists, and their cultural reverence for the spoken word makes them remarkable orators.
巨猿族是泰姆瑞尔西南部可敬的猿民，一个多元的民族，以其精神创新和在政治动荡时期的韧性而闻名。尽管巨猿氏族的祖居地位于瓦伦伍德的丛林，但这些巨猿已适应了现代时代，现在通常受雇为遍及西部帝国各教团、政体和贸易联合体的博学顾问。巨猿族是天才的杂技演员和拳击手，他们文化中对口头语言的尊崇使其成为卓越的演说家。

> RACE.FNAM T_Yne_Ynesai
Ynesai
伊奈赛人

> RACE.DESC T_Yne_Ynesai
The natives of the Yneslea archipelago trace their origins to the extinct Men of Akavir, and retain traces of that lost culture in millennia-old traditions. A melancholic and isolated people, the Ynesai are rarely seen in Tamriel, preferring the small, tight-knit communities of their tropical homeland. Ynesai take every advantage in a fight, using deception and ranged weapons from afar before getting close to their enemies with knives and fists.
伊奈赛群岛的原住民将其起源追溯到已灭绝的阿卡维尔人类，并在千年传统中保留着失落文化的痕迹。伊奈赛人是一个忧郁而孤立的民族，在泰姆瑞尔很少见到，他们更偏爱其热带家乡小而紧密的社区。伊奈赛人在战斗中会利用一切优势，先使用欺骗手段和远程武器攻击远处敌人，再用匕首和拳头接近敌人。

> RACE.FNAM T_Yok_Duadri
Duadri
杜阿德里人

> RACE.DESC T_Yok_Duadri
Ebon-black and solemn, the Duadri of southern Yokuda are renowned for their nautical heritage, and are often relied on as chaplains and navigators by westbound vessels. Though their mystical customs are often maligned by Western races, their aptitude for both artistry and commerce has caught the attention of merchants in ports of call across the Abecean.
杜阿德里人肤色乌黑、神情肃穆，是尤库达南部以航海传统闻名的民族，常被西行船只倚重为牧师和领航员。尽管他们的神秘习俗常受西方种族诟病，但他们在艺术和商业上的才能已引起了阿贝辛海域各处停靠港商人的注意。

Fur starts growing all over your body, and your face feels utterly painful as sharp tusks spring out in the sides of your mouth. Your appearance is grotesque. But under the moons, your one and only urge is to wet your tusks with fresh blood. The Hunter observes you from afar.
你感到皮肤紧绷，肌肉酸痛，身体开始剧烈地转化。毛发从全身各处冒出，尖锐的獠牙从嘴角两侧刺出，面部剧痛无比。你的外貌变得狰狞可怖。但在双月之下，你唯一的渴望便是用鲜血浸湿你的獠牙。猎人在远处注视着你。

> SCPT.SCTX T_ScTrans_WereboarPC m3

我梦见一个金发少女，我走近她，看到她在哭泣，但她的眼泪像血一样红。我摸了摸她的眼泪，尝了尝，非常咸，带着香料的味道。但少女的脸已经变了，她的皮肤是灰白色的，红色的泪水从她的嘴唇滴落，她的头发变成了黑色，像蛇一样缠绕在她的头上。我很害怕，但又不能跑。我尖叫着醒来，心脏怦怦直跳，痉挛而疼痛。

East Empire Company Charter
东帝国公司特许状

> BOOK.TEXT T_BkFaction_EECTR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Imperial Charter of the East Empire Trading Company<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
I. Purpose<BR>
<BR>
The East Empire Company serves as a unified body through which Western merchants may participate in trade with Morrowind and Black Marsh. The Company also governs various Eastern colonies at the Emperor's pleasure. Traders benefit from the Company's ability to negotiate fair prices in protected Eastern markets without prohibitive domestic competition. Citizens may purchase or sell Company shares at a stock exchange or a Company hall.<BR>
<BR>
The Company has the exclusive right to trade in Eastern goods including raw ebony, raw glass, Dwemer artifacts, and rubber. In the East, the Company has the exclusive right to import Western goods including whiskey, brandy, and tea. In the West, the Company enjoys favorable import taxes on Eastern goods including kwama eggs, marshmerrow pulp, racer plumes, saltrice, and Telvanni bug musk.<BR>
<BR>
II. Authority<BR>
<BR>
The East Empire Company was incorporated in the 34th year of the Third Era by Emperor Tiber Septim. The Company is managed by a board of directors appointed by the Emperor.<BR>
<BR>
III. Rules and Procedures<BR>
<BR>
Employees are expected to uphold the virtues and values of the Empire at all times. Acts such as killing or stealing from peers are an instant cause for termination from the Company and loss of all protections otherwise extended to its members.<BR>
<BR>
IV. Employment Requirements<BR>
<BR>
The East Empire Company accepts candidates with a winning personality and a strong will. Those with the ability to speak eloquently and barter shrewdly are most valuable. Because the Company operates in all manner of hostile environments, applicants should have a keen sense of security, and as has been customary for generations, all Company employees should be trained in the time-honored virtues of long blades and medium armor.<BR>
<BR>
V. Applications for Employment<BR>
<BR>
Candidates must present themselves to an officer at a Company hall for examination and approval.<BR>
<BR>
ATTACHMENT A: East Empire Company Agencies in Morrowind Province<BR>
<BR>
Agencies are established in Company-owned, free-standing offices in the towns of Ebonheart, Old Ebonheart, Kragenmoor, and Firewatch. The agency in Almalexia is established in the Mournhold complex under lease from the Indoril Council. The agency in Blacklight is established in the Harbor under lease from the Redoran Council. The agency in Narsis is established on the Waterfront under lease from the Hlaalu Council.<BR>
<BR>
"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
东帝国贸易公司帝国特许状<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
一、宗旨<BR>
<BR>
东帝国公司作为一个统一机构，西方商人可通过其参与与晨风和黑沼泽的贸易。公司还根据皇帝的意愿管辖各个东部殖民地。商人得益于公司在受保护的东部市场谈判公平价格的能力，且没有过度的国内竞争。公民可以在证券交易所或公司大厅购买或出售公司股票。<BR>
<BR>
公司拥有东部商品（包括黑檀矿、玻璃矿、锻莫制品和橡胶）的独家贸易权。在东部，公司拥有进口西方商品（包括威士忌、白兰地和茶叶）的独家权利。在西部，公司享有东部商品（包括夸蚂卵、沼泽芯髓、迅疾鸟羽、盐米和泰瓦尼虫麝香）的优惠进口关税。<BR>
<BR>
二、权限<BR>
<BR>
东帝国公司于第三纪元34年由泰伯·塞普汀皇帝注册成立。公司由皇帝任命的董事会管理。<BR>
<BR>
三、规则与程序<BR>
<BR>
员工应时刻维护帝国的美德和价值观。杀害或盗窃同僚等行为将立即导致被公司解雇，并丧失所有其他给予成员的保障。<BR>
<BR>
四、雇佣要求<BR>
<BR>
东帝国公司接受具有出众个性和坚强意志的候选人。能言善辩、精于议价者最为宝贵。由于公司在各种恶劣环境中运营，申请人应有敏锐的安全意识，且依照世代相传的惯例，所有公司员工都应接受长剑和中甲的古老美德训练。<BR>
<BR>
五、求职申请<BR>
<BR>
候选人必须亲自到公司大厅向官员报到，接受审核和批准。<BR>
<BR>
附件A：东帝国公司晨风行省代理处<BR>
<BR>
代理处设于公司自有独立办公室，位于黑檀心、旧黑檀心、克拉根穆尔和火望等城镇。位于阿玛莱西娅的代理处设在哀伤之城建筑群内，系向因多瑞尔议会租用。位于黑光的代理处设在港口，系向勒多兰议会租用。位于纳西斯的代理处设在水滨，系向哈拉鲁议会租用。<BR>
<BR>

为了我的众神与皇帝

> BOOK.TEXT T_BkFaction_ImpCultTR
"""

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>

For My Gods and Emperor<BR>

A Handbook for the Imperial Cult<BR><BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>

What is the Imperial Cult?<BR>

<BR>

The missionary arm of the great faiths, the Imperial cult brings divine inspiration and consolation to the Empire's remote provinces. The cults combine the worship of the Nine Divines, the Aedra Akatosh, Dibella, Arkay, Zenithar, Mara, Stendarr, Kynareth, and Julianos, and the Talos cult, veneration of the divine god-hero Tiber Septim, founder and patron of the Empire. Imperial cult priests provide worship and services for all these gods at Imperial shrines in settlements throughout Morrowind. <BR>

<BR>

What is the Virtuous Life? <BR>

<BR>

Our doctrines are simple. We acknowledge the divinity of the Nine Divines: Akatosh, Dibella, Arkay, Zenithar, Mara, Stendarr, Kynareth, Julianos, and Tiber Septim. We preach the Nine Virtues: Humility, Inspiration, Piety, Work, Compassion, Justice, Ambition, Learning, and Civility. Our Emperor is the Defender of the Faith, and the Empire is the worldly working of the Divine Plan. We pledge aid and comfort to all citizens in need, and serve the Emperor and Empire at his will. <BR>

<BR>

The Imperial cults look to the Nine Divines as models for living a good and virtuous life. Each of the Nine represents different aspects of life, and how it should be lived. But the simplest statement of our doctrines is -- help and protect one another. The stronger one is, the wealthier one is, the more one bears responsibility for helping and protecting others. One's first duty, of course, is to one's fellow members of the Imperial Cult. But after that, one should help and protect any needy persons. <BR>

<BR>

We also say, "do not harm one another." It is forbidden to attack another person of the Imperial cult, and of course, forbidden to kill another member. It is forbidden to steal from another member, whether by open theft or by covert pickpocketing. It is forbidden to trespass upon the private property of another member. Break any one of these rules, and be expelled from the cult. <BR>

<BR>

How can I join the Imperial cult? <BR>

<BR>

The Imperial cult accepts all citizens of good character and earnest faith. We ask only a one-time pledge of 50 drakes to aid us in our good works. Thereafter, the only cost of membership comes when you use our health, healing, and blessing shrines -- modest fees which help us spread the blessings of the Nine to those less fortunate than ourselves. <BR>

<BR>
Those who wish to join the Imperial cult in the northern area of the Telvannis district will find a warm welcome from the Imperial Chapels in Firewatch and Helnim. <BR>

<BR>

What are the requirements for advancement in the Imperial cult? <BR>

<BR>

Seekers who wish to advance in the service of the Nine must dedicate time and resources to serving the cult, and must strive for personal improvement in their attributes and skills. Only the most distinguished are worthy of advancement to the higher ranks in the Imperial cults. <BR>

<BR>

To serve and glorify the Nine Divines, the faithful must cultivate a noble personality and a strong will. Respect the magical arts, especially the colleges of Restoration, Mysticism, and Conjuration. Those who swear to avoid bloodshed, to take the field unarmored to fight only with blunt weapons, are especially praiseworthy. Knowledge of enchantments and the gift of diplomatic speech are other qualities we value in our initiates. <BR>

<BR>

Imperial cult services<BR>

<BR>
You can find Imperial cult services in the Imperial Chapels in Firewatch, Helnim, and at Icebreaker Keep in Nivalis. These locations have healing altars. You may pray at Imperial cult healing altars and receive blessings which cure common and blight diseases, cure poisons, and restore damaged attributes. Non-members pay 25 drakes. Newer members pay 10 drakes, while higher-ranking members receive blessings free. <BR>

<BR>

Opportunities for service <BR>

<BR>

Lay healers gather ingredients for health and healing potions, minister to the sick, hurt, and poor, as well as minister to the isolated communities. It is difficult and sometimes dangerous work, but the spiritual rewards are great. Lay healers need only the skills of the prudent traveler, being often on the road and in the wilderness, gathering herbs and potion components. They should avoid trouble where possible, and so need not be masters of the arts of war. <BR>

<BR>

Almoners gather alms from members and friends of the faith. We depend on donations to fund most of our good works. Almoners who are successful at bringing in generous donations may rise in the ranks of Imperial Cults service. Almoners must travel in town and village, and should be skilled in persuasion and mercantile matters. Also, almoners with personal wealth are in a position to better serve the cult. <BR>

<BR>

A shrine sergeant helps keep order at the shrines, carries messages and packages, and sometimes escorts priests and lay servants on dangerous missions. This occasional service is ideal for bold, free-spirited adventurers. Shrine sergeants are called upon to serve the Nine with weapon, armor, and spell. New shrine sergeants are given the easiest tasks, but later, missions may demand higher levels of combat proficiency. <BR>

<BR>

Morrowind is also riddled with those who worship the profane idols known as Daedra. The most skilled of our ranks may be called upon to remove any heretical Daedra worshippers should a threat arise. <BR>

<BR>

How do the Imperial cults view the other factions of Morrowind? <BR>

<BR>

The Imperial cults have a very close relationship with the Imperial legions, and a friendly and supportive relationship with the Imperial Guilds -- especially the Fighters and Mages Guilds. We also have a friendly and supportive relationship with House Hlaalu, which strongly supports the Emperor and Imperial principles. Though we cannot condone the actions of the Thieves Guild, we praise their faithful dedication to the Emperor and to Imperial culture. <BR>

<BR>

The Imperial cults have the greatest respect for the high moral principles of House Redoran and the Morag Tong, and honor their different but noble conceptions of Divine Inspiration. <BR>

<BR>

We disapprove of the impious and inhumane practices of the Telvanni. The Imperial cult especially disapproves of the practice of slavery, and looks forward to the day when slavery is illegal in all Imperial provinces. The Imperial cult also disapproves of the actions of the lawless and greedy Camonna Tong, and their ruthless exploitation of the poor and weak. <BR>

<BR>

Historically, our relationship with the Tribunal Temple is difficult and unfriendly. Though the Imperial cults acknowledges the lords and saints of the Temple pantheon as worthy inspirations, the Temple falsely insists that theirs is the One True Faith, and that the Imperial cults worship false gods.<BR>

"""

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>

为了我的众神与皇帝<BR>

帝国教团手册<BR><BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>

什么是帝国教团？<BR>

<BR>

作为伟大信仰的传教分支，帝国教团将神圣的启迪与慰藉带给帝国偏远的行省。教团融合了对九圣灵的崇拜 -- 艾德拉阿卡托什、蒂贝拉、阿尔凯、泽尼萨尔、玛拉、斯滕达尔、吉娜瑞斯和尤利安诺斯 -- 以及对塔洛斯教派的尊崇，即对神圣的神明英雄、帝国的创立者与守护神泰伯·塞普汀的崇拜。帝国教团的祭司在晨风各地定居点的帝国圣祠中为所有这些神明提供礼拜和服务。<BR>

<BR>

什么是美德人生？<BR>

<BR>

我们的教义简单明了。我们承认九圣灵的神性：阿卡托什、蒂贝拉、阿尔凯、泽尼萨尔、玛拉、斯滕达尔、吉娜瑞斯、尤利安诺斯和泰伯·塞普汀。我们宣扬九种美德：谦卑、启迪、虔诚、劳作、慈悲、正义、进取、博学和礼让。我们的皇帝是信仰的捍卫者，帝国是神圣计划在尘世的运作。我们承诺为所有需要帮助的公民提供援助和慰藉，并遵从他的意志为皇帝和帝国服务。<BR>

<BR>

帝国教团以九圣灵为典范，作为过良善美德生活的楷模。九圣灵各自代表生活的不同方面及其应有的方式。但我们教义最简单的陈述是 -- 互相帮助和保护。一个人越强大、越富有，就越负有帮助和保护他人的责任。一个人的首要职责当然是面向帝国教团的同修。但在此之后，也应当帮助和保护任何有需要的人。<BR>

<BR>

我们也说，“不可互相伤害。”禁止攻击帝国教团的其他人，当然也禁止杀害其他成员。禁止偷窃其他成员的财物，无论是公开盗窃还是暗中扒窃。禁止擅自进入其他成员的私有财产。违反其中任何一条规则，将被逐出教团。<BR>

<BR>

我该如何加入帝国教团？<BR>

<BR>

帝国教团接纳所有品行端正、信仰诚挚的公民。我们只要求一次性认捐50龙币，以帮助我们进行善举。此后，只有在使用我们的健康、治疗和祝福圣祠时才产生会员费用 -- 这些适度的费用帮助我们向比我们更不幸的人传播九圣灵的祝福。<BR>

<BR>
希望在泰瓦尼区北部地区加入帝国教团的人，将在火望和赫尔尼姆的帝国礼拜堂受到热烈欢迎。<BR>

<BR>

在帝国教团中晋升需要什么条件？<BR>

<BR>

希望在为九圣灵服务中晋升的追寻者，必须投入时间和资源为教团服务，并必须努力提升自身的属性和技能。只有最杰出的人才配得上在帝国教团中晋升到更高的阶位。<BR>

<BR>

为九圣灵服务并荣耀他们，信徒必须培养高尚的品格和坚强的意志。尊重魔法技艺，尤其是恢复系、神秘系和召唤系学派。那些立誓避免流血、不穿盔甲上阵、仅以钝器战斗者，尤其值得称赞。附魔知识和外交辞令的天赋是我们看重入门者的其他品质。<BR>

<BR>

帝国教团服务<BR>

<BR>
您可以在火望、赫尔尼姆的帝国礼拜堂以及尼瓦利斯的破冰者要塞找到帝国教团服务。这些地点设有治疗祭坛。您可以在帝国教团的治疗祭坛祈祷，获得能治愈常见疾病和枯萎病、解毒以及恢复受损属性的祝福。非会员支付25龙币。新会员支付10龙币，而高阶成员则免费获得祝福。<BR>

<BR>

服务机会<BR>

<BR>

世俗治疗师收集用于健康和疗伤药剂的原料，照料病患、伤者和穷人，也为偏远社区提供医疗。这是困难且有时危险的工作，但精神回报丰厚。世俗治疗师只需具备审慎旅行者的技能，因他们经常在路上和荒野中穿行，采集草药和药剂成分。他们应尽可能避开麻烦，因此无需精通战争技艺。<BR>

<BR>

施赈者从信仰的成员和朋友处募集施舍。我们依靠捐款来资助大部分的善举。成功募集到慷慨捐款的施赈者可在帝国教团服务中晋升。施赈者须在城镇和乡村中奔走，应精于说服和商业事务。此外，拥有个人财富的施赈者能更好地为教团服务。<BR>

<BR>

圣祠军士协助维护圣祠秩序，传递信息和包裹，有时护送祭司和世俗仆从执行危险任务。这种临时性的服务非常适合大胆、向往自由的冒险者。圣祠军士被召唤以武器、盔甲和法术为九圣灵服务。新晋的圣祠军士被分配最简单的任务，但后来的任务可能要求更高的战斗熟练度。<BR>

<BR>

晨风也充斥着那些崇拜名为迪德拉的亵渎偶像之人。当威胁出现时，我们队伍中最熟练的成员可能被召唤去铲除任何异端的迪德拉崇拜者。<BR>

<BR>

帝国教团如何看待晨风的其他派系？<BR>

<BR>

帝国教团与帝国军团关系非常密切，与帝国公会（尤其是战士公会和法师公会）关系友好且相互支持。我们与哈拉鲁家族也保持着友好支持的关系，该家族强烈支持皇帝和帝国原则。尽管我们不能宽恕盗贼公会的行为，但我们赞扬他们对皇帝和帝国文化的忠诚奉献。<BR>

<BR>

帝国教团对勒多兰家族和莫拉格·堂崇高的道德原则致以最大的敬意，并尊重他们不同但高贵的关于神圣启迪的理念。<BR>

<BR>

我们不赞成泰瓦尼的不虔诚和不人道做法。帝国教团尤其反对奴隶制，并期待奴隶制在所有帝国行省被定为非法的那一天。帝国教团也不赞成无法无天且贪婪的卡莫纳·堂的行为，以及他们对穷人和弱者的残酷剥削。<BR>

<BR>

从历史上看，我们与审判席神殿的关系是艰难且不友好的。尽管帝国教团承认神殿万神殿中的众位君主和圣徒是值得敬仰的典范，但神殿错误地坚持认为他们的信仰是唯一真信仰，而帝国教团崇拜的是伪神。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Ordo Legionis<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The most disciplined and effective military force in history, the Imperial Legions preserve the peace and rule of law in the Empire and the Imperial Province. Wherever foreign enemies or treasonous agitators seek to disrupt the peace and the rule of law, the Legions are present to guard, protect, and to bring about the will of the Emperor. The Legion invites all willing and capable citizens to join this illustrious force that serves as the foundations of the Empire.<BR>
<BR>
While many legion garrisons are permanently quartered in the provinces, the Empire maintains its most experienced divisions to secure the Imperial Province. The forces currently manning the forts of Yellowmoth, Redman, Teleman, and Waxmoth in the southern Niben is at full complement. The venerable First Legion, stationed in the old Colovian bastions of Strand, Istirus, Arrowmoth and Ontus, is always looking to grow its ranks with promising and qualified citizens, especially they who feel called to the difficult and arduous officer regimen. Those seeking enlistment can apply at the garrison headquarters of Fort Ontus, in the city of Mhorlagrad.<BR>
<BR>
The most honorable Third Legion has been assigned the solemn task of defending the Imperial City and the Heartlands. It is our most exclusive division, holding the citadels of Arkmoth, Imperator, Urasek, Wakemoth, Virtue, and Fort Basileus itself. Serve the Emperor with exceptional determination, and perhaps you too can one day wear the red regimentals of the Ruby Legion. Even if your efforts do not bring you that far, know that there are also distinguished postings in the auxiliary border Legions, the Prison escorts, and with the honorable Battlemages of the Shadow Legion, based in their redoubts of Fort Magia.<BR>
<BR>
The Legion selects candidates on the basis of superior endurance, the soldierly virtue, and trustworthy personality, the citizen's virtue, for service in the Legion is the model for the duties of Imperial citizenship. Troopers are expected to demonstrate mastery of the long blade, the spear, and blunt weapons. Legion troops train with shield and heavy armor, and so must be skilled at blocking and moving in heavy armor.<BR>
<BR>
As a trooper or knight, you must master the long blade, spear, and blunt weapons. You must block whatever blows you can, and take unblocked blows upon your heavy armor. Recruit must also be proficient at athletics, both to march long distances with heavy packs, and to advance and maneuver, charge and retreat on the field of battle.<BR>
<BR>
Cyrodiil is kept safe thanks to the vigilance of the Legions. While a soldier stationed in the home defense garrisons is unlikely to advance through valorous acts on the battlefield, a legionnaire exhibiting dedication, talent, and discipline may one day find himself among the commanders of Fort Basileus, those generals who are privileged to act as the right hand of the Emperor himself.<BR>

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_1000SpiritsOldCyrodOpenPC
The 1,000 Spirits of Old Cyrod
古西罗德的一千神灵

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_1000SpiritsOldCyrodOpenPC
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The 1,000 Spirits of Old Cyrod<BR>
by Umalchio Tricho<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Cyrodiilic religion can be confusing for outsiders. Most Imperials who frequent the provinces (Colovian soldiers and colonists, mostly) have rather formulaic relations with their gods, and consider attendance of a cult little more than a social obligation or investment. Besides the Eight and One Divines, most of these Imperials hold a private allegiance to one of Cyrodiil's many minor gods or saints, but to inquire into one's personal faith is considered rude, even among friends. At least, that is the pragmatic mindset most often encountered in Colovia or in the provincial colonies.<BR>
<BR>
However, anyone familiar with the central valleys will tell you that not all Imperials adhere to this attitude. In the bustling river cities of the Nibenay and the Heartlands, thousands of gods, daedra, and saints are honored in extravagant fashion. Prophets expound in the streets, haruspics roam the marketplaces, gaudy processions carry mummified saints across the cities, canals are choked with chromatic funeral barges, pilgrims throng around the ancient shrines, and blind priests glide serenely through the crowd, shrouded in moths. Ancient cults compete for the loyalty of the people, offering vocational training, political favors, or life eternal - when they are not embroiled in their frequent intersectional temple-wars.<BR>
<BR>
To an outsider, this wealth of religious fervor can appear overwhelming, even threatening -- ignorance of the dominant saints, doctrines or cults in any given place can spell doom for the itinerant traveler. This short guide, printed with the generous patronage of the Imperial Seminary, is aimed at the provincial immigrant wishing to understand this most vibrant part of Imperial society.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
THE DIVINES<BR>
Worship of the Divines is universal throughout Cyrodiil, and almost every village has a shrine or temple dedicated to one of their number. Failure to observe proper respect for the creator gods is frowned upon, even within other cults. Provincials will no doubt know the Imperial Cult for their generous and compassionate missionary services, though they might not know that the Cult's teachings in the provinces differ from native Cyrodiilic practice. The Imperial Cult and its motherhouse, the Imperial Seminary in Tiberiad, are organizations directed by the Imperial authorities to spread the Faiths and the benefits of Imperial civilization to the provinces. They are generously sponsored by their patrons, the Great Faiths and the Talos Cult, who voluntarily contribute missionaries and funds for their good works.<BR>
<BR>
Within the Imperial Province, the Great Faiths hold sway: syncretic priestly orders who cooperate to ensure that all Imperials have access to their blessings and services. The Faiths enjoy the patronage of the Emperor and his servants, and their message is so ingrained in the Imperial people that it is hardly possible to call oneself an Imperial without honoring the Nine Divines (or the Eight and One, as some still call them). The Talos Cult is sometimes considered one of these orders, though it is by far the youngest, and it differs from the other Faiths in its organization and operations.<BR>
<BR>
Besides the Great Faiths, the Nine are also worshiped by a large variety of charismatic sub-cults who honor a single facet of a Divine instead of the abstract whole. Examples are the Red Dome Templars, the Temple of Scales, the Kynarchex Cult, the Citizenship Cult, the Order of the Psychopompoi, the Mehacherites, the Instructor Order, or the Therati Knights-Merchant. These facet deities are sometimes worshiped under a different name, blurring the line with the minor gods. Some of these are considered subordinate to the Great Faiths, other distinguish themselves in terms of doctrine or political affiliation.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
THE MINOR GODS, SAINTS AND SPIRITS<BR>
Imperials also honor many hero-gods and protector spirits. Such gods are usually of regional importance, influential only in their home cities or near their most dear pilgrimage sites. It is always a good idea to inform about local cults when arriving in any eastern town. Most notable are the Al-Esha Cult, the Order of the Breath-of-Kyne, the Cala Cult, the Temple of the Missing, the Remanati Cult, the Order of the Ancestor Moth, the Cult of Heroes, the Pelinati Cult, the Emperor Zero Cult, the Esoteric Order of Shor, and the Temple of the One. Many more exist.<BR>
<BR>
Related to the category of culture heroes are the Saints of Cyrod, a vast and eclectic hagiography of exemplar spirits closely linked to the Divines. In Imperial theology, saints are mortals who have transcended the sphere of the Mundus by way of exceptional virtue or adherence to the principles of the Divines, often defined by way of a covenant with a patron Divine. The saints are so numerous that any listing is per definition incomplete.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
THE DAEDRA<BR>
While most provincial cultures maintain a superstitious fear of the Daedra, the people of Cyrodiil have long embraced an enlightened attitude towards the intercessors of the Void. The Daedric Princes are regarded as any other god, no more dangerous or amoral than the many spirits of the mortal plane. Any nefarious intent from them or their agents is easily waylaid by the pacts of Akatosh, Arkay, Talos, and the Emperors, which shield the mortal plane and its inhabitants.<BR>
<BR>
The most important Daedric Princes in Cyrodiil are Sanguine, Clavicus, Vaernima, and Peryite, whose worship is institutionalized in the Red Dancer Cult, Little Key Cult, Dried Lotus Cult and False-Worm Cult. Other Daedra are also honored, though the more violent and nihilistic cults are, of course, prohibited. Dagon worship, quite popular until the events of the Simulacrum, has been censured thoroughly.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
THE TOTEM SOCIETIES<BR>
The last and, perhaps, oddest category of faiths are the animal spirits worshiped in the rural Nibenese east. A remnant of early Nedic practices, the Totem Societies exist as representative triads for certain professions, communities, and social classes. The nature of their faith is difficult to grasp for outsiders: the Societies do not worship an animal so much as the idea of an animal, understood as the conscious manifestation of a denomination or of their ancestor spirits. A totem is only as powerful as the group it represents: if they are wealthy, powerful, and united, so is the totem. Many Nibenese consider the Empire as a whole a kind of totem-society, dedicated to the Dragon spirit.<BR>
<BR>
Most Societies lack a clear hierarchy or organization: they are heterogeneous, and membership is determined by class, profession, location, or family. The most influential Societies are the Bull, the Moth, the Snake, the Coutal, and the Gila, though many more exist across all social strata. Rumors speak of a prohibited Tiger Society which worships the ancient gestalt-spirits of the jungle, though it seems doubtful that any sane individual would seek to appease such grotesque and outlandish gods - if they even exist at all.<BR>
<BR>
"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
古西罗德的一千神灵<BR>
乌马尔基奥·特里科 著<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
西罗帝尔的宗教对于外人来说可能令人困惑。大多数常往来于行省的帝国人（主要是科洛维亚士兵和殖民者）与他们的神祇之间有着相当程式化的关系，他们认为参加教派活动不过是一种社会义务或投资。除了八圣灵和一圣灵之外，这些帝国人大多私下效忠于西罗帝尔众多次要神祇或圣徒之一，但探问个人的信仰被视为无礼之举，即使在朋友之间也是如此。至少，这是在科洛维亚或行省殖民地最常见到的务实心态。<BR>
<BR>
然而，任何熟悉中央河谷的人都会告诉你，并非所有帝国人都秉持这种态度。在尼本奈和心脏地繁华的河畔城市中，成千上万的神祇、迪德拉和圣徒以铺张的方式受到尊崇。先知在街头宣讲，占卜师在集市游荡，花哨的游行队伍抬着木乃伊化的圣徒穿过城市，运河中挤满了五彩缤纷的葬礼驳船，朝圣者簇拥在古老圣祠周围，盲眼祭司披着飞蛾，宁静地滑过人群。古老的教派争夺人民的忠诚，提供职业培训、政治恩惠或永生 -- 当他们没有卷入频繁的教派间神殿战争时。<BR>
<BR>
对于外人而言，这种丰富的宗教狂热可能显得铺天盖地，甚至具有威胁性 -- 在任何特定地方对主流圣徒、教义或教派的无知，都可能给巡游旅行者带来厄运。这本简明指南是在帝国神学院的慷慨赞助下印刷的，旨在帮助希望了解帝国社会这一最富活力部分的行省移民。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
圣灵<BR>
对圣灵的崇拜在整个西罗帝尔是普遍的，几乎每个村庄都有供奉其中一位的圣祠或神殿。未能对创世神表示适当尊敬，即使在其它教派内部也是不受欢迎的。行省居民无疑会因帝国教团慷慨而富有同情心的传教服务而知晓它，尽管他们可能不知道教团在行省的教义与西罗帝尔本土实践有所不同。帝国教团及其母院 -- 位于泰伯利亚德的帝国神学院 -- 是由帝国当局指挥的组织，旨在向行省传播信仰和帝国文明的福祉。他们受到其赞助者 -- 伟大信仰和塔洛斯教派 -- 的慷慨资助，后者自愿为他们的善举贡献传教士和资金。<BR>
<BR>
在帝国行省内部，伟大信仰占据主导地位：这些融合性的祭司修会相互合作，以确保所有帝国人都能获得他们的祝福和服务。这些信仰享有皇帝及其仆人的庇护，它们的信息在帝国人民心中根深蒂固，以至于不尊崇九圣灵（或如有些人仍称的八圣灵与一圣灵）就几乎不可能自称帝国人。塔洛斯教派有时被视为这些修会之一，尽管它是最年轻的，并且在组织和运作上与其他信仰有所不同。<BR>
<BR>
除了伟大信仰之外，九圣灵还受到大量富有魅力的次级教派的崇拜，这些教派尊崇圣灵的某一侧面，而非抽象的整体。例如红穹圣殿骑士、天平神殿、吉娜尔凯克斯教派、公民教派、引魂者修会、梅哈克里特派、导师修会或泰拉蒂骑士商人团。这些侧面神祇有时以不同的名字被崇拜，模糊了与次要神祇之间的界限。其中一些被视为从属于伟大信仰，另一些则在教义或政治派别上自成一体。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
次要神祇、圣徒与神灵<BR>
帝国人也尊崇许多英雄神祇和守护神灵。这类神祇通常具有地区重要性，仅在其家乡城市或最受珍视的朝圣地附近具有影响力。抵达任何东部城镇时，了解当地教派总是一个好主意。最著名的是阿尔-艾莎教派、吉讷吐息修会、卡拉教派、失落者神殿、雷曼纳提教派、先祖蛾修会、英雄教派、佩林纳提教派、零皇教派、朔尔密教修会以及至一神殿。还有更多存在。<BR>
<BR>
与文化英雄类别相关的是西罗德的圣徒，这是一部庞大而兼收并蓄的圣徒传，记述了与圣灵紧密相连的典范神灵。在帝国神学中，圣徒是凭借卓越美德或遵循圣灵原则而超越梦达斯领域的凡人，通常通过与守护圣灵的契约来界定。圣徒数量众多，任何列举都必然不完整。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
迪德拉<BR>
尽管大多数行省文化对迪德拉抱有迷信的恐惧，但西罗帝尔的人民长期以来对虚空的中介者持开明的态度。迪德拉大君被视为与任何其他神祇一样，并不比凡世位面的众多神灵更危险或更不道德。他们或其代理人任何邪恶意图都会被阿卡托什、阿尔凯、塔洛斯和皇帝们的契约轻易阻截，这些契约保护着凡世位面及其居民。<BR>
<BR>
西罗帝尔最重要的迪德拉大君是桑吉恩、克拉威库斯、瓦尔迷娜和佩伊特，他们的崇拜在红舞者教派、小钥匙教派、干莲花教派和伪虫教派中被制度化。其他迪德拉也受到尊崇，但更暴力和虚无主义的教派当然是被禁止的。大衮崇拜在幻象事件之前相当流行，此后已受到严厉谴责。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
图腾社团<BR>
最后一类，也许也是最奇特的一类信仰，是在尼本奈东部乡村所崇拜的动物灵。作为早期尼德习俗的残余，图腾社团以某些职业、社群和社会阶级的代表性三合会形式存在。他们信仰的本质对外人来说难以理解：社团崇拜的不是动物本身，而是动物的理念，将其理解为某个教派或祖先神灵的有意识显现。图腾的力量仅取决于它所代表的群体：如果群体富有、强大且团结，图腾亦然。许多尼本奈人将整个帝国视为一种图腾社团，献身于龙之灵。<BR>
<BR>
大多数社团缺乏明确的等级或组织：它们是异质的，成员资格由阶级、职业、地点或家族决定。最具影响力的社团是公牛、飞蛾、毒蛇、库塔尔和吉拉，尽管在所有社会阶层中还有更多存在。有传言称存在一个被禁止的老虎社团，崇拜丛林的古老格式塔之灵，但似乎任何心智健全的人都不会寻求安抚如此怪诞奇异的神祇 -- 如果它们确实存在的话。<BR>
<BR>

Ancient cults compete for the loyalty of the people, offering vocational training, political favors, or life eternal - when they are not embroiled in their frequent intersectional temple-wars.<BR>
<BR>
To an outsider, this wealth of religious fervor can appear overwhelming, even threatening -- ignorance of the dominant saints, doctrines or cults in any given place can spell doom for the itinerant traveler. This short guide, printed with the generous patronage of the Imperial Seminary, is aimed at the provincial immigrant wishing to understand this most vibrant part of Imperial society.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
THE DIVINES<BR>
Worship of the Divines is universal throughout Cyrodiil, and almost every village has a shrine or temple dedicated to one of their number. Failure to observe proper respect for the creator gods is frowned upon, even within other cults. Provincials will no doubt know the Imperial Cult for their generous and compassionate missionary services, though they might not know that the Cult's teachings in the provinces differ from native Cyrodiilic practice. The Imperial Cult and its motherhouse, the Imperial Seminary in Tiberiad, are organizations directed by the Imperial authorities to spread the Faiths and the benefits of Imperial civilization to the provinces. They are generously sponsored by their patrons, the Great Faiths and the Talos Cult, who voluntarily contribute missionaries and funds for their good works.<BR>
<BR>
Within the Imperial Province, the Great Faiths hold sway: syncretic priestly orders who cooperate to ensure that all Imperials have access to their blessings and services. The Faiths enjoy the patronage of the Emperor and his servants, and their message is so ingrained in the Imperial people that it is hardly possible to call oneself an Imperial without honoring the Nine Divines (or the Eight and One, as some still call them). The Talos Cult is sometimes considered one of these orders, though it is by far the youngest, and it differs from the other Faiths in its organization and operations.<BR>
<BR>
Besides the Great Faiths, the Nine are also worshiped by a large variety of charismatic sub-cults who honor a single facet of a Divine instead of the abstract whole. Examples are the Red Dome Templars, the Temple of Scales, the Kynarchex Cult, the Citizenship Cult, the Order of the Psychopompoi, the Mehacherites, the Instructor Order, or the Therati Knights-Merchant. These facet deities are sometimes worshiped under a different name, blurring the line with the minor gods. Some of these are considered subordinate to the Great Faiths, other distinguish themselves in terms of doctrine or political affiliation.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
THE MINOR GODS, SAINTS AND SPIRITS<BR>
Imperials also honor many hero-gods and protector spirits. Such gods are usually of regional importance, influential only in their home cities or near their most dear pilgrimage sites. It is always a good idea to inform about local cults when arriving in any eastern town. Most notable are the Al-Esha Cult, the Order of the Breath-of-Kyne, the Cala Cult, the Temple of the Missing, the Remanati Cult, the Order of the Ancestor Moth, the Cult of Heroes, the Pelinati Cult, the Emperor Zero Cult, the Esoteric Order of Shor, and the Temple of the One. Many more exist.<BR>
<BR>
Related to the category of culture heroes are the Saints of Cyrod, a vast and eclectic hagiography of exemplar spirits closely linked to the Divines. In Imperial theology, saints are mortals who have transcended the sphere of the Mundus by way of exceptional virtue or adherence to the principles of the Divines, often defined by way of a covenant with a patron Divine. The saints are so numerous that any listing is per definition incomplete.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
THE DAEDRA<BR>
While most provincial cultures maintain a superstitious fear of the Daedra, the people of Cyrodiil have long embraced an enlightened attitude towards the intercessors of the Void. The Daedric Princes are regarded as any other god, no more dangerous or amoral than the many spirits of the mortal plane. Any nefarious intent from them or their agents is easily waylaid by the pacts of Akatosh, Arkay, Talos, and the Emperors, which shield the mortal plane and its inhabitants.<BR>
<BR>
The most important Daedric Princes in Cyrodiil are Sanguine, Clavicus, Vaernima, and Peryite, whose worship is institutionalized in the Red Dancer Cult, Little Key Cult, Dried Lotus Cult and False-Worm Cult. Other Daedra are also honored, though the more violent and nihilistic cults are, of course, prohibited. Dagon worship, quite popular until the events of the Simulacrum, has been censured thoroughly.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
THE TOTEM SOCIETIES<BR>
The last and, perhaps, oddest category of faiths are the animal spirits worshiped in the rural Nibenese east. A remnant of early Nedic practices, the Totem Societies exist as representative triads for certain professions, communities, and social classes. The nature of their faith is difficult to grasp for outsiders: the Societies do not worship an animal so much as the idea of an animal, understood as the conscious manifestation of a denomination or of their ancestor spirits. A totem is only as powerful as the group it represents: if they are wealthy, powerful, and united, so is the totem. Many Nibenese consider the Empire as a whole a kind of totem-society, dedicated to the Dragon spirit.<BR>
<BR>
Most Societies lack a clear hierarchy or organization: they are heterogeneous, and membership is determined by class, profession, location, or family. The most influential Societies are the Bull, the Moth, the Snake, the Coutal, and the Gila, though many more exist across all social strata. Rumors speak of a prohibited Tiger Society which worships the ancient gestalt-spirits of the jungle, though it seems doubtful that any sane individual would seek to appease such grotesque and outlandish gods - if they even exist at all.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Sixteen Accords of Madness, v. XII<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
In the days before the Orsinium's founding, the spurned Orc-folk were subjected to ostracism and persecutions even more numerous and harsh than their progeny are accustomed to in our own age. So it was that many champions of the Orsimer traveled, enforcing what borders they could for the proliferation of their own people. Many of these champions are spoken of yet today, among them the Cursed Legion, Gromma the Hairless, and the noble Emmeg Gro-Kayra. This latter crusader would have certainly risen to legendary status throughout Tamriel, had he not been subject to the attention of certain Daedric Princes.<BR>
<BR>
Emmeg Gro-Kayra was the bastard son of a young maiden who was killed in childbirth. He was raised by the shaman of his tribe, the Grilikamaug in the peaks of what we now call Normar Heights. Late in his fifteenth year, Emmeg forged by hand an ornate suit of scaled armor, a rite of ascension among his tribe. On a blustery day, he pounded the final rivet, and draping a heavy cloak over the bulky mantle, Emmeg set out from his village for the last time. Word of his exploits always returned home, whether defending merchant caravans from brigands or liberating enslaved beast folk. News of the noble Orc crusader began to grace even the lips of Bretons, often with a tinge of fear.<BR>
<BR>
Less than two years after ascending to maturity, Gro-Kayra was making camp when a thin voice called out from the thickening night. He was surprised to hear the language of his people spoken by a tongue that obviously did not belong to an Orc.<BR>
<BR>
'Lord Kayra', said the voice, 'tales of your deeds have crossed the lips of many, and have reached my ears.' Peering into the murk, Emmeg made out the silhouette of a cloaked figure, made wavy and ephemeral by the hazy campfire. From the voice alone he had thought the interloper an old hag, but he now decided that he was in the presence of a man of slight and lanky build, though he could discern no further detail.<BR>
<BR>
'Perhaps,' the wary Orc began, 'but I seek no glory. Who are you?'<BR>
<BR>
Ignoring the question, the stranger continued, 'Despite that, Orsimer, glory finds you, and I bear a gift worthy of it.' The visitor's cloak parted slightly, revealing nothing but faintly glinting buttons in the pale moonlight, and a bundle was withdrawn and tossed to the side of the fire between the two. Emmeg cautiously removed the rags in which the object was swathed, and was dazzled to discover the item to be a wide, curved blade with ornately decorated handle. The weapon had heft, and Emmeg realized on brandishing it that the elaborate pommel disguised the more practical purpose of balancing the considerable weight of the blade itself. It was nothing much to look at in its present condition, thought the Orc, but once the tarnish was cleaned away and a few missing jewels restored, it would indeed be a blade worthy of a champion ten times his own worth.<BR>
<BR>
'Her name is Neb-Crescen' spoke the thin stranger, seeing the appreciation lighting Gro-Kayra's face. 'I got her for a horse and a secret in warmer climes, but in my old age I'd be lucky to even lift such a weapon. It's only proper that I pass her on to one such as yourself. To possess her is to change your life, forever.' Overcoming his initial infatuation with the arc of honed steel, Emmeg turned his attention back to the visitor.<BR>
<BR>
'Your words are fine, old man,' Emmeg said, not masking his suspicion, 'but I'm no fool. You traded for this blade once, and you'll trade for it again tonight. What is it that you want?' The stranger's shoulders slumped, and Emmeg was glad to have unveiled the true purpose of this twilight visit. He sat with him a while, eventually offering a stack of furs, warm food, and a handful of coins in exchange for the exotic weapon. By morning, the stranger was gone.<BR>
<BR>
In the week following Emmeg's encounter with the stranger, Neb-Crescen had not left its scabbard. He had encountered no enemy in the woods, and his meals consisted of fowl and small game caught with bow and arrow. The peace suited him fine, but on the seventh morning, while fog still crept between the low-hanging boughs, Emmeg's ears pricked up at the telltale crunch of a nearby footfall in the dense snow and forest debris.<BR>
<BR>
Emmeg's nostrils flared, but he was upwind. Being unable to see or smell his guest, and knowing that the breeze carried his scent in that direction, Emmeg's guard was up, and he cautiously drew Neb-Crescen from its sheath. Emmeg himself was not entirely sure of all that happened next.<BR>
<BR>
The first moment of conscious memory in Emmeg Gro-Kayra's mind after drawing Neb-Crescen was the image of the curved blade sweeping through the air in front of him, spattering blood over the virginal powder coating the forest floor. The second memory was a feeling of frenzied bloodlust creeping over him, but it was then that he saw for the first time his victim, an Orc woman perhaps a few years younger than himself, her body a canvas of grisly wounds, enough to kill a strong man ten times over.<BR>
<BR>
Emmeg's disgust overwhelmed the madness that had overtaken him, and with all his will enlisted, he released Neb-Crescen from his grip and let the blade sail. With a discordant ringing it spun through the air and was buried in a snowdrift. Emmeg fled the scene in shame and horror, drawing the hood of his cloak up to hide himself from the judging eyes of the rising sun.<BR>
<BR>
The scene where Emmeg Gro-Kayra had murdered one of his own kind was a macabre one. Below the neck, the body was flayed and mutilated almost beyond recognition, but the untouched face was frozen in a permanent expression of abject terror.<BR>
<BR>
It was here that Sheogorath performed certain rites that summoned Malacath, and the two Daedric Lords held court in the presence of the disfigured corpse.<BR>
<BR>
'Why show me this, Mad One?' began Malacath, once he recovered from his initial, wordless outrage. 'Do you take such pleasure in watching me grieve the murder of my children?' His guttural voice rumbled, and the patron of the Orsimer looked upon his counterpart with accusing eyes.<BR>
<BR>
'By birth, she was yours, brother outcast,' began Sheogorath, solemn in aspect and demeanor. 'But she was a daughter of mine by her own habits. My mourning here is no less than your own, my outrage no less great.'<BR>
<BR>
'I am not so sure,' grumbled Malacath, 'but rest assured that vengeance for this crime is mine to reap. I expect no contest from you. Stand aside.' As the fearsome Prince began to push past him, Lord Sheogorath spoke again.<BR>
<BR>
'I have no intention of standing between you and vengeance. In fact, I mean to help you. I have servants in this wilderness, and can tell you just where to find our mutual foe. I ask only that you use a weapon of my choosing. Wound the criminal with my blade, and banish him to my plane, where I can exact my own punishment. The rights of honor-killing here belong to you.'<BR>
<BR>
With that, Malacath agreed, took the wide blade from Sheogorath, and was gone.<BR>
<BR>
Malacath materialized in the path of the murderer, the cloaked figure obscured through a blizzard haze. Bellowing a curse so foul as to wilt the surrounding trees, the blade was drawn and Malacath crossed the distance more quickly than a wild fox. Frothing with rage, he swung the blade in a smooth arc which lopped the head of his foe cleanly off, then plunged the blade up to its hilt in his chest, choking off the spurts of blood into a steady, growing stain of red bubbling from beneath the scaled armor and heavy cloak.<BR>
<BR>
Panting from the unexpected immediacy and fury of his own kill, Malacath rested on a knee as the body before him collapsed heavily backwards and the head landed roughly upon a broad, flat stone. The next sound broke the silence like a bolt.<BR>
<BR>
'I - I'm sorry...' sputtered the voice of Emmeg Gro-Kayra. Malacath's eyes went wide as he looked upon the severed head, seeping blood from its wound, but somehow kept alive. Its eyes wavered about wildly, trying to focus on the aspect of Malacath before it. The once-proud eyes of the champion were choked with tears of grief, pain, and confused recognition.<BR>
<BR>
To his horror, Malacath recognized only now that the man he had killed was not only one of his Orsimer children, but very literally a son he had blessed an Orc maiden with years hence. For achingly long moments the two looked upon each other, despondent and shocked.<BR>
<BR>
Then, silent as oiled steel, Sheogorath strode into the clearing. He hefted Emmeg Gro-Kayra's disembodied head and bundled it into a small, grey sack. Sheogorath reclaimed Neb-Crescen from the corpse and turned to walk away. Malacath began to stand, but kneeled again, knowing he had irreversibly damned his own offspring to the realm of Sheogorath, and mourned his failure as the sound of his son's hoarse pleas faded into the frozen horizon.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
疯狂十六契约 卷十二<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
在奥辛纽姆建立之前的岁月里，被唾弃的兽人一族遭受了比他们的后代在我们这个时代所习惯的更为众多和严酷的排斥与迫害。因此，许多奥斯莫的勇士四处游历，尽可能地扩张边界以繁衍族人。这些勇士中的许多至今仍被传颂，其中包括诅咒军团、无毛者格罗马，以及高贵的埃梅格·格罗-凯拉。这最后一位十字军如果没有引起某些迪德拉大君的注意，本无疑会在整个泰姆瑞尔晋升为传奇人物。<BR>

<BR>
成年后不到两年，格罗-凯拉正在扎营，一个细弱的声音从渐浓的夜色中传来。他惊讶地听到有人用他族人的语言说话，而那显然不属于兽人的口音。<BR>
<BR>
“凯拉大人，”那声音说，“您的事迹已在许多人口中流传，也传到了我的耳中。”埃梅格向黑暗中望去，辨认出一个披着斗篷的身影，在朦胧的营火映照下显得摇曳不定。仅从声音他本以为来者是个老巫婆，但现在他断定面前是一个瘦高个子的男人，尽管他看不出更多细节。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
“你的话说得不错，老头，”埃梅格毫不掩饰怀疑地说，“但我不是傻瓜。你曾经交易过这把刀，今晚你又会交易它。你想要什么？”陌生人的肩膀耷拉下来，埃梅格很高兴揭穿了这次黄昏访问的真正目的。他和他坐了一会儿，最终拿出一叠毛皮、热食和一把硬币来交换这把异域武器。到了早上，陌生人不见了。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
A Hypothetical Treachery<BR>
A One Act Play<BR>
by Anthil Morvir<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Dramatis Personae<BR>
Malvasian: A High Elf battlemage<BR>
Inzoliah:  A Dark Elf battlemage<BR>
Dolcettus: A Cyrodiil healer<BR>
Schiavas: An Argonian barbarian <BR>
A Ghost<BR>
Some bandits<BR>
<BR>
Scene: Eldenwood<BR>
<BR>
As the curtain rises, we see the misty labyrinthian landscape of the legendary Eldengrove of Valenwood.  All around we hear wolves howling.  A bloodied reptilian figure, SCHIAVAS, breaks through the branches of one of the trees and surveys the area.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: It's clear.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH, a beautiful Dark Elf mage, climbs down from the tree, helped by the barbarian.  There is the sound of footsteps nearby.  Schiavas readies his sword and Inzoliah prepares to cast a spell.  Nothing comes out.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: You're bleeding.  You should have Dolcettus heal that for you.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: He's still drained from all the spells he had to cast down in the caves.  I'm fine.  If we get out of this and no one needs it more, I'll take the last potion of healing.  Where's Malvasian?<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN, a High Elf battlemage, and DOLCETTUS, a Cyrodiil healer, emerge from the tree, carrying a heavy chest between the two of them.  They awkwardly try to get down from the tree, carrying their loot.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: Here I am, though why I'm carrying the heavy load is beyond me.  I always thought that the advantage of dungeon delving with a great barbarian was that he carried all the loot.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: If I carried that, my hands would be too full to fight.  And tell me if I'm wrong, but not one of the three of you has enough magicka reserved to make it out of here alive.  Not after you electrified and blasted all those homunculuses down below ground.<BR>
<BR>
DOLCETTUS: Homunculi.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: Don't worry, I'm not going to do what you think I'm going to do.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH (innocently): What's that?<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: Kill you all and take the Ebony Mail for myself.  Admit it -- you thought I had that in mind.<BR>
<BR>
DOLCETTUS: What a perfectly horrible thought.  I never thought anyone, no matter how vile and degenerate --<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: Why not?<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN:  He needs porters, like he said.  He can't carry the chest and fight off the inhabitants of Eldengrove both.<BR>
<BR>
DOLCETTUS: By Stendarr, of all the mean, conniving, typically Argonian --<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH:  And why do you need me alive?<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: I don't necessarily.  Except that you're prettier than the other two, for a smoothskin that is.  And if something comes after us, it might go for you first.<BR>
<BR>
There is a noise in some bushes nearby.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: Go check that out.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH:  It's probably a wolf.  These woods are filled with them.  You check it out.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS:  You have a choice, Inzoliah.  Go and you might live.  Stay here, and you definitely won't.<BR>
<BR>
Inzoliah considers and then goes to the bushes.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS (to Malvasian and Dolcettus): The king of Silvenar will pay good money for the Mail, and we can divide it more nicely between three than four.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: You're so right.<BR>
<BR>
Inzoliah suddenly levitates up to the top of the stage.  A semi-transparent Ghost appears from the bush and rushes at the next person, who happens to be Schiavas.  As the barbarian screams and thrashes at it with his sword, it levels blasts of whirling gas at him.  He crumbles to the ground.  It turns next to Dolcettus, the healer, and as the Ghost focuses its feasting chill on the hapless Dolcettus, Malvasian casts a ball of flame at it that causes it to vaporize into the misty air.<BR>
<BR>
Inzoliah floats back down to the ground as Malvasian examines the bodies of Dolcettus and Schiavas, who are both white-faced from the draining power of the ghost.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: You had some magicka reserved after all.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: So did you.  Are they dead?<BR>
<BR>
Malvasian takes the potion of healing from Dolcettus's pack.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN:  Yes.  Fortunately, the potion of healing wasn't broken when he fell.  Well, I guess this leaves just the two of us to collect the reward.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: We can't get out of this place without each other.  Like it or not.<BR>
<BR>
The two battlemages pick up the chest and begin plodding carefully through the undergrowth, pausing from time to time at the sound of footsteps or other eerie noises.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: Let me make sure I understand.  You have a little bit of magicka left, so you elected to use it to make Schiavas the ghost's target, forcing me to use most of my limited reserve to destroy the creature so I wouldn't be more powerful than you.  That's first-rate thinking.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: Thank you.  It's only logical.  Do you have enough power to cast any other spells?<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN:  Naturally.  An experienced battlemage always knows a few minor but highly effective spells for just such a trial.  I take it you, too, have a few tricks up your sleeve?<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH:  Of course, like you said.<BR>
<BR>
They pause for a moment before continuing as a fearful wail pierces the air.  When it dies away, they slowly trudge on.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: Just as an intellectual exercise, I wonder what spell you would cast at me if we made it out of here without any more combat.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: I hope you're not implying that I would dream of killing you so I would keep the treasure all to myself.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: Of course not, nor would I do that to you.  It is merely an intellectual exercise.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: Well, in that case, purely as an intellectual exercise, I would probably cast a leech spell on you, to take away your life force and heal myself.  After all, there are brigands on the road between here and Silvenar, and a wounded battlemage with a valuable artifact would make a tempting target.  I'd hate to survive Eldengrove merely to die in the open.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: That's a well-reasoned response.  As for myself, again, not saying I would ever do this, but I think a simple, sudden electrical bolt would serve my purposes admirably.  I agree about the danger of brigands, but don't forget, we also have a potion of healing.  I could easily slay you and heal myself to full capacity.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: Very true.  It would end up a question then of whose spell was more effective at that instant.  If our spells counteracted one another and I leeched your life energy only to be crippled by your lightning bolt, then we could both be killed.  Or so near death that a mere potion of healing would scarcely help either one of us, let alone both.  How ironic it would be if two scheming battlemages, not saying we are scheming but for the purpose of this intellectual exercise, were left on the brink of death, completely drained of magicka, with one healing potion to choose from.  Who would get it then?<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: Logically, whoever drank it first, which in this case would be you since you're holding it.  Now, what if one of us were injured, but not killed?<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: Logic would dictate that a scheming battlemage would take the potion, leaving the injured party to the mercy of the elements, I suppose.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: That does seem most sensible.  But suppose that the battlemages, while certainly scheming types, had a certain respect for one another.  Perhaps in that case, the victorious one might, for instance, put the potion up a tree near his or her gravely wounded victim.  Then when the wounded party had enough magicka replenished, he or she would be able to levitate to the tree branches and recover the potion.  By that time, the victorious battlemage would have already collected the reward.<BR>
<BR>
They pause for a moment at the sound of something in the bushes nearby.  Carefully, they climb across the branches of a tree to bypass it.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: I understand what you're saying, but it seems out of character for our hypothetic scheming battlemage to allow his or her victim to live.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: Perhaps.  But it's been my observation that most scheming battlemages enjoy the feeling of having bested someone in combat, and having that person alive to live with the humiliation.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: These hypothetical scheming battlemages sound ... (excitedly) Daylight!  Do you see it?<BR>
<BR>
The two scurry across the branch dropping behind a bush, so we can no longer see them.  We can, however, see the shimmering halo of sunlight.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN (behind the tall bush): We made it.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH (likewise, behind the tall bush): Indeed.<BR>
<BR>
There is a sudden explosion of electrical energy and a wild howling aura of red light, and then silence.  After a few moment's pause, we hear someone climbing up the tree.  It is Malvasian, putting the potion high up in the bough.  He chuckles as he climbs back down and the curtain drops.<BR>
<BR>
Epilogue.<BR>
<BR>
The curtain rises on a road to Silvenar.  A gang of bandits have surrounded Malvasian, who is propped up on his staff, barely able to stand.  They pull his chest away from him with ease.<BR>
<BR>
BANDIT #1: What have we got here?  Don't you know it ain't safe to be out on the road, all sick like you are?  Why don't we help you with your load?<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN (weakly): Please ...  Let me be ...<BR>
<BR>
BANDIT #2: Go on, spellcaster, fight us for it!<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN:  I can't ... too weak ...<BR>
<BR>
Suddenly, Inzoliah flies in, casting lightning bolts from her fingers at the bandits, who quickly scramble away.  She lands on the ground and picks up the chest.  Malvasian collapses, dying.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN:  Hypothetically, what if ... a battlemage cast a spell on another which didn't harm him at once, but ... drained his life force and his magicka, bit by bit, so he wouldn't know at the time, but ... feel confident enough to leave the potion of healing behind?<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: A most treacherous battlemage she'd be.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: And ... hypothetically ... would she be likely to help her fallen foe ... so that she could enjoy the humiliation of him continuing ... to live?<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: From my experience, hypothetically, no.  She doesn't sound like a fool.<BR>
<BR>
As Inzoliah lugs the chest off toward Silvenar, and Malvasian expires on the stage, we drop the curtain.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
一个假想的背叛<BR>
独幕剧<BR>
安希尔·莫维尔 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
剧中人物<BR>
马尔瓦西安：傲特莫战斗法师<BR>
因佐莉娅：丹莫战斗法师<BR>
多尔塞图斯：西罗帝尔治疗师<BR>
斯齐亚瓦斯：阿尔贡蛮族<BR>
一只幽灵<BR>
若干匪徒<BR>
<BR>
场景：古林<BR>

帷幕升起，我们看到瓦伦伍德传说中的上古林地那迷雾笼罩、迷宫般的景色。四周传来狼嚎。一个血迹斑斑的爬行动物身影 -- 斯齐亚瓦斯 -- 从一棵树的枝叶间钻出，环视四周。<BR>

斯齐亚瓦斯：安全。<BR>

因佐莉娅，一位美丽的丹莫法师，在蛮族的帮助下爬下树。附近传来脚步声。斯齐亚瓦斯握紧剑，因佐莉娅准备施法。但什么也没发生。<BR>

因佐莉娅：你在流血。你应该让多尔塞图斯给你治治。<BR>

<BR>
马尔瓦西安，一位傲特莫战斗法师，和多尔塞图斯，一位西罗帝尔治疗师，一起抬着一个沉重的箱子从树中出来。他们笨拙地试图爬下树，同时搬运着战利品。<BR>
<BR>
马尔瓦西安：我来了，不过为什么是我搬重东西，真搞不懂。我一直以为和一位伟大的蛮族一起下地牢的优势就是他能扛所有战利品。<BR>
<BR>
斯齐亚瓦斯：如果我搬那个，手就没空战斗了。如果我说错了就告诉我，但你们三个没有一个人有足够的法力活着离开这里，尤其是在你们电击炸飞了地下那些魔像之后。<BR>
<BR>
多尔塞图斯：是魔像。<BR>
<BR>
斯齐亚瓦斯：别担心，我不会做你们以为我会做的事。<BR>
<BR>
因佐莉娅（无辜地）：什么事？<BR>

斯齐亚瓦斯：把你们全杀了，然后把黑檀链甲据为己有。承认吧 -- 你们以为我有那个念头。<BR>

因佐莉娅：为什么不会？<BR>

因佐莉娅飘回地面，马尔瓦西安检查多尔塞图斯和斯齐亚瓦斯的尸体，他们都被幽灵的吸取之力弄得脸色苍白。<BR>

马尔瓦西安：你果然还是留了一些法力。<BR>

马尔瓦西安从多尔塞图斯的背包里拿出治疗药剂。<BR>

<BR>
因佐莉娅：没有彼此，我们都离不开这个地方。不管愿不愿意。<BR>

因佐莉娅：当然，就像你说的。<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
因佐莉娅：也许吧。但据我观察，大多数诡计多端的战斗法师都喜欢在战斗中战胜对手，并让对手活着承受屈辱。<BR>
<BR>

马尔瓦西安（在高灌木丛后）：我们出来了。<BR>

突然爆发出一阵电光能量和狂野的红光咆哮，然后寂静。片刻后，我们听到有人爬上树。是马尔瓦西安，他把药剂放在高处的树枝上。他笑着爬下来，帷幕落下。<BR>

尾声。<BR>

帷幕升起，在通往希尔维纳的路上。一伙匪徒围住了马尔瓦西安，他靠着法杖勉强站着。他们轻松地抢走了他的箱子。<BR>
<BR>
匪徒甲：我们得到了什么？你不知道像你这样病恹恹的待在路上不安全吗？不如我们帮你搬东西吧？<BR>
<BR>
马尔瓦西安（虚弱地）：求你了......别管我......<BR>

因佐莉娅：那她真是个最背信弃义的战斗法师。<BR>
<BR>
马尔瓦西安：而且......假想一下......她会不会去帮助她倒下的敌人......好享受他继续......活着的屈辱？<BR>
<BR>
因佐莉娅：根据我的经验，假想的话，不会。她听起来不像傻瓜。<BR>
<BR>
因佐莉娅拖着箱子朝希尔维纳走去，马尔瓦西安在舞台上死去，帷幕落下。<BR>

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_AboveItAllTR
Above It All
凌驾于一切之上

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_AboveItAllTR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
Above It All<BR>
By Fuchon Cire<BR>
<BR>
I cherish this case, for it served well to display the practical employment of the skills I have spent so many years refining. Some think me a magician of some sort, and while it is quite true that I possess a wide range of abilities in that respect, more often it is simple observation that will reveal the criminal. And so very flattered was I when Santilius Graccian of the honorable Imperial Legion contacted me in some distress, for it told me that my renown was such that I was regarded as being of service when the brightest among the Legion met with failure.<BR>
<BR>
Santilius related to me that the small Imperial fort, of which he was the ranking officer, and the town around it had recently become the target of an unidentified thief or group of thieves. He was unclear as to the number of individuals involved in the thefts, for these occurrences took place exclusively under cover of darkness. It seems the thief or thieves were none too selective, as various citizens reported missing items running the gauntlet from Limeware sets, to alcoholic beverages, to simple spools of thread. A number of the guard, in fact, had to go without armor, as the thieves were bold enough to steal not only from the town, but also from fort itself.<BR>
<BR>
The sheer volume of loot taken would require a considerable amount of space to store, but none of the voluntary searches of the citizenry's homes turned up a single piece. Santilius was, he informed me, fresh out of ideas and at the end of his rope. I was of the opinion that the quantity was such that there was no possible way they could be hidden nearby without arousing suspicion. Rather, the thieves had likely traveled to an adjoining town, and sold the goods. It was more in keeping with what Santilius had told me - that the thieves never struck on consecutive days (which would allow them a day to walk to the nearest town and back).<BR>
<BR>
I began my investigation by re-interviewing the townspeople thus far involved. They did not seem to have noticed anything out of the ordinary except that their possessions had gone missing, save for one disgruntled Dunmer. Oriluse Llatham informed me that he had seen a lone silent silhouette stalking toward the fort one night, after the guards had been told that the thieves had struck again and so raised the alarm. I was nonplused, as most thieves are quite silent, and there could have been other thieves, stealing from other houses at the same time.<BR>
<BR>
Upon my request, Oriluse allowed me to search his house. He had lost a candle and a dozen books to the eager, grasping hands of the thieves. Scrutinizing his bookshelf, I noticed an unusual marring of the wooden surface. When asked about it, the Dunmer claimed that it was the first it had been called to his attention. Not wanting to incite a lynching or vigilantism, I did not reveal that I suspected the markings to have been caused by a clawed hand. Again, the clue was not helpful in itself, for besides Argonians and Khajiit, the marks could also have been made by one hoping the authorities would draw that conclusion. However, the inability of the beast races to don footwear would offer an additional explanation as to the silent nature of the thievery. Pieces of evidence, you understand, make much more sense when placed in context with additional clues, rather than when they stand on their own.<BR>
<BR>
I investigated a couple of other houses, at the behest of their owners, finding again similar scratch marks. It seemed that the thief was indeed, a solo act. As the day was reaching its conclusion, I retired to the bedroom provided to me through the generous hospitality of the Legion. Santilius seemed to have expected me to have resolved the case in a single day, but as I briefed him on my progress (in strictest confidence), he was pacified. He also admitted that it never would have occurred to him that one would leave such markings to make a scapegoat of one of the beast peoples, and praised my wisdom in keeping silent about it; when dealing with matters pertaining to the execution of justice, we were of much the same mind. I then bid him good night, and locked my belongings into the chest provided.<BR>
<BR>
In the morn, a youthful guardsman roused me. Again the thief had struck in the safety of nighttime, but on this occasion, had left a hastily scrawled note behind. Our perpetrator had noticed my movements about town, it seemed, and saw fit to leave me a taunting note at the scene of his latest wrongdoing. I reproduce the note here in its entirety:<BR>

<BR>
"Like bemused rats in a maze you scurry. Too ignorant are you to find that which is above your meager grasp."<BR>
<BR>

Bemused indeed was the young guard when I laughed expansively. None in the Legion, I expect, would have made much of it. But for me, the note confirmed my suspicions and was in itself the solution of the case. When I told Santilius as much, he too was bemused. I pointed out again the reference to rats in the note, but it didn't spark any revelation for him. Plainly, I patiently stated, our suspect is a Khajiit. The allusion to rats (particularly in reference to victims, which would be seen as 'prey'), in conjunction with the other evidence, clearly indicated as much. Santilius then scratched his head, for the one Khajiit in town was also a victim of the thief.<BR>
<BR>
Exiting the fort bearing a satisfied smile on my face, I told Santilius that the perpetrator didn't live in town. The guards murmured among themselves, thinking I might have been accusing them (for if not a native of the town, the suspect must likely reside within the fort), which I laughingly denied; after all, none of the guards were Khajiiti. Inspecting the large stones that composed the towers of the fort, I shortly chanced upon what I knew would be there--white markings from the Khajiit's claws upon the stone. Our Khajiiti thief lived atop one of the towers (the prison tower actually, revealing a strong sense of irony in the fellow), as was clear in the way he described our searching. He had, doubtless, lifted some shingle from the peak of the tower, and clambered inside the hollow top.<BR>
<BR>
With their weighty armor adorning their backs, none of the guard seemed inclined to scale the face of the tower. Even those who had had their armor stolen did not look to be of a humor to make the attempt. Shrugging, I placed one foot where the Khajiit's claw marks indicated he had. Criminal though he may be, he certainly knew how to climb much better than I, and I was in no position to turn down his unintended aid. Upon reaching the summit, I noticed the damaged shingle that I had expected, and it began to move! Presumably, either the Khajiit had been watching my progress, or had been roused from slumber by it.<BR>
<BR>
The fellow had a sturdy chitin dagger drawn, and looked to be a rough customer. I was unconcerned, though, for he had been very obviously consuming large quantities of Moon Sugar (probably bartered in exchange for his ill gotten goods), and so his judgment couldn't help but be terribly impaired. However, I never expected him to charge me, as high up as we were. Sidestepping easily, the poor addled fellow ran clear over the edge of the tower, spitting and hissing in dismay.<BR>
<BR>
Hesitating not for a moment, I dove straight after him. I could not help but to hear the surprised shouts of the guards below, for they surely thought me a lunatic at best, and suicidal at worst. But I was truly neither, as would become immediately apparent. Reaching out to the panicking Khajiit, I cast Slowfall. The suspect thus out of danger, I then cast the spell on myself. Falling so leisurely, I amused myself by watching the guards run about, trying to intercept the Khajiit before he landed, as the nervous fellow trod air frantically, and ultimately futilely, to evade capture.<BR>
<BR>
For my part, I descended much more calmly. I extended my arm in a pace befitting my fall, in anticipation of the handshake warranted by a job well done. <BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
凌驾于一切之上<BR>
弗雄·西尔 著<BR>
<BR>
我珍视这个案子，因为它很好地展示了我多年来磨练的技能的实际运用。有些人认为我是某种魔术师，虽然我确实在这方面拥有广泛的能力，但更常见的是，简单的观察就能揭露罪犯。因此，当可敬的帝国军团的桑提利乌斯·格拉西安在困境中联系我时，我感到非常荣幸，因为这告诉我，我的名声已经大到当军团中最优秀的人失败时，我会被视为有用的人。<BR>
<BR>
桑提利乌斯告诉我，他担任指挥官的那座小帝国堡垒及其周围城镇最近成为了身份不明的盗贼或盗贼团伙的目标。他不太清楚涉案人数，因为盗窃都发生在夜幕掩护下。盗贼似乎并不挑剔，因为市民们报告丢失的物品从柠檬器皿套件到酒精饮料，再到简单的线轴都有。事实上，一些守卫不得不赤身无甲，因为盗贼胆大包天，不仅从镇上偷窃，还从堡垒本身偷窃。<BR>
<BR>
被盗物品的总量需要相当大的存储空间，但对市民房屋的自愿搜查却没有发现任何一件。桑提利乌斯告诉我，他已经束手无策，走投无路。我认为，如此大的数量不可能在附近藏匿而不引起怀疑。相反，盗贼很可能去了邻近的城镇，把赃物卖掉。这更符合桑提利乌斯告诉我的情况 -- 盗贼从不连续作案（这样他们有一天时间步行到最近的城镇并返回）。<BR>
<BR>
我开始调查，重新采访了迄今为止涉及的镇民。他们似乎没有注意到任何异常，除了他们的财物丢失之外，只有一个不满的丹莫例外。奥里卢斯·拉瑟姆告诉我，有一天晚上，在守卫被告知盗贼再次作案而拉响警报后，他看到一个孤独的沉默身影向堡垒潜行。我有些困惑，因为大多数盗贼都很安静，而且可能同时有其他盗贼从其他房屋偷窃。<BR>
<BR>
应我的要求，奥里卢斯允许我搜查他的房子。他丢失了一支蜡烛和一打书，被贪婪的盗贼之手拿走。仔细检查他的书架，我注意到木质表面有一种不寻常的磨损。当问及此事时，丹莫说这是他第一次注意到。我不想煽动私刑或私自执法，所以没有透露我怀疑这些痕迹是由爪状手造成的。同样，这条线索本身没有帮助，因为除了阿尔贡和卡吉特之外，这些痕迹也可能是由希望当局得出那种结论的人留下的。然而，兽人种族无法穿鞋，这为盗窃的无声性质提供了额外的解释。你知道，证据片断在与其他线索结合时更有意义，而不是单独存在。<BR>
<BR>
在屋主要求下，我又调查了几所房子，再次发现类似的划痕。看来盗贼确实是单独行动。天色已晚，我回到军团慷慨提供的卧室休息。桑提利乌斯似乎指望我一天内破案，但当我向他简要汇报进展（严格保密）后，他平静了下来。他还承认，他从未想到有人会留下这样的痕迹来嫁祸于兽人种族，并称赞我对此事保持沉默的智慧；在处理与执法有关的事务时，我们意见一致。然后我向他道晚安，把我的物品锁进提供的箱子里。<BR>
<BR>
早晨，一个年轻的卫兵叫醒了我。盗贼再次在夜晚的安全掩护下作案，但这次留下了一张匆忙写下的便条。看来我们的罪犯注意到了我在镇上的行动，认为有必要在他最近作案的现场给我留下一张嘲弄的便条。我将便条全文复制如下：<BR>

<BR>
“像迷宫中困惑的老鼠一样匆匆忙忙。你们太无知，找不到那凌驾于你们贫乏理解之上的东西。”<BR>
<BR>

当我大笑时，年轻的卫兵确实很困惑。我预计，军团中没有人会对此有多大反应。但对我来说，这张便条证实了我的怀疑，它本身就是破案的关键。当我告诉桑提利乌斯时，他也困惑了。我再次指出便条中提及老鼠的部分，但这并没有给他任何启示。我耐心地解释，我们的嫌疑人是卡吉特。对老鼠的暗示（特别是提到受害者，会被视为“猎物”），结合其他证据，清楚地表明了这一点。桑提利乌斯挠了挠头，因为镇上唯一的卡吉特也是盗窃案的受害者。<BR>
<BR>
我面带满意笑容走出堡垒，告诉桑提利乌斯罪犯不住在镇上。守卫们低声议论，以为我可能是在指控他们（因为如果不是镇上居民，嫌疑人必定住在堡垒内），我笑着否认了；毕竟，守卫中没有卡吉特人。检查堡垒塔楼的大石头时，我很快发现了我知道会有的东西 -- 卡吉特爪子在石头上留下的白色痕迹。我们的卡吉特小偷住在其中一座塔楼顶部（实际上是监狱塔楼，显示这家伙强烈的讽刺感），从他描述我们搜索的方式可以明显看出。他无疑是从塔顶掀开一块瓦片，爬进了中空的顶部。<BR>
<BR>
他们穿着厚重的盔甲，没有一个守卫似乎愿意攀爬塔楼表面。即使是那些丢了盔甲的人，似乎也没心情尝试。我耸耸肩，把脚放在卡吉特爪印指示的位置。虽然他是罪犯，但他显然比我更会攀爬，我没有理由拒绝他无意中提供的帮助。到达顶点时，我看到了预料中的破损瓦片，它开始移动！大概是卡吉特一直在观察我的进展，或者被我惊醒了。<BR>
<BR>
那家伙拔出一把结实的甲壳匕首，看起来是个难缠的家伙。但我并不担心，因为他显然大量食用月亮糖（可能是用赃物换来的），所以判断力必然严重受损。然而，我没想到他会冲向我，毕竟我们那么高。我轻松侧身躲过，那可怜的糊涂家伙直接冲出了塔顶边缘，绝望地吐着唾沫，嘶嘶作响。<BR>
<BR>
我没有丝毫犹豫，立刻跟着他跳了下去。我听到了下面守卫惊讶的喊声，他们肯定以为我至少是个疯子，最坏则是自杀。但我两者都不是，这一点很快会变得明显。我伸手抓住惊慌的卡吉特，施放了缓落术。嫌疑人脱离危险后，我给自己也施放了法术。如此悠闲地落下，我饶有兴致地看着守卫们跑来跑去，试图在卡吉特落地前拦住他，而那紧张的家伙在空中狂乱地蹬着腿，最终徒劳地试图逃避抓捕。<BR>
<BR>
我这边则落得从容得多。我伸出手臂，以与下落相称的节奏，期待着因出色完成工作而应得的握手。<BR>

Advances in Lock Picking
