"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Assassination of Pelagius I <BR>
Horatio Gargonath <BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Many scholars have pondered while writing a poem, or reading a volume of thickness about the assassination of Emperor Pelagius the first. How does one explain the events that happened at the Temple of the One? There are many terms to summarize it, and many have been suggested: strange, odd, suspicious, disturbing, mysterious, etc. Some have even gone to lengths by calling it blood-curling. Truly, however, for those who were there at the time will agree, was something to be forever nervous about. <BR>
<BR>
Before we start to go into depth about Pelagius the First, we will illustrate his background. His grandfather, the Great Tiber Septim, was one of the most praised kings of all of Tamriel. During the second era Tiber Septim, despite the efforts of the King Tyrants of the second era, managed to bring peace to all of Tamriel as Emperor in 2E 896. The following year, Tiber thenceforth declares the end of the Second Era, or the "days and nights of blood and venom" as the poet Tracizis calls them, and the beginning of the Third era. At the end of a long and glorious reign of thirty-eight years, the great Tiber Septim passed away. It was said that it rained for a fortnight after his death. <BR>
<BR>
Following Tiber Septim's passing, his grandson Pelagius the First, was crowned second Emperor of the Septim dynasty. Pelagius' reign was short, however. Only three years passed before he was assassinated., even though he was said to be as strong and skillful as his grandfather during his short reign. <BR>
<BR>
Yet the thing that is mysterious is not so much as his heritage or reign but rather his assassination. While he was praying at the Temple of The One, Pelagius was assassinated by a group of Dark Brotherhood assassins. The Dark Brotherhood were at that time, and still remain to this very day, an illegal assassination faction. <BR>
<BR>
The original client that hired the Dark Brotherhood is to this day unknown, and may not be known for a great deal longer. The mystery is very disturbing though. It continues to irritate the mind, juggling your thoughts as if they were toys. Theories from all over Tamriel have been expressed, some as ridiculous as a secret daedra cult of Sheogorath scrib-worshippers. Others much more realistic, such as a secretive plot composed by Pelagius the First's cousin Kintyra, former Queen of Silvenar. She assumed power after his death, considering he had no children. <BR>
<BR>
Though wherever the hypothesis comes from, uncertainty always follows. At one point, it was said that there was a poor beggar running through the streets of Cyrodiil, literally screaming that he had seen the truth behind the Emperor's death, until, after being pursued by two guards for about half an hour, he mysteriously vanished while sprinting through a back alley. While this case was never officially proven to have happened, the rumors that spread out of it stirred the population. 
<BR>
There have been similar versions of the story, where the beggar was in fact a guard, and the pursuer was actually a shadowy figure. This was only one story though. There have been several others. This one, however, seemed to be the most interesting and well known. <BR>
<BR>
During my research, I uncovered several magnificent interviews on the event. Including one from a pilgrim that was in the Temple at the time of the assassination: 
<BR>
It was very quiet that night when His Majesty entered. I was staying at the Temple for a few days to study and write poetry. I remember hearing footsteps from outside my bedroom door. There were no windows in my room, and I was falling asleep. I remember the lights in the hall had dimmed, perhaps even completely blown out. The footsteps continued until one was at my door. I got up quietly and noticed a faint screeching noise. Like a small but solid piece of metal scratching and pulling against a maze of gears and wires. <BR>
<BR>
It was then when I realized what was happening. My door was locked, and someone wanted in. I knew that the door lock was the product of my own magic, and that it would not open easily, not even to the most professional lock picks. So I hurried to make up my bed, to ensure that my presence would not be noticed. As I was about to slip under my bed to hide, the door started to open. I did not have any more time.<BR><BR>
In the less than a second that I had to concoct a solution, I remembered the ring of Brevuta's Averting Eye I was given for ridding a nobleman's house of an unusual cave rat infestation in his wine cellar. I quickly, but silently, slipped on the ring and activated its enchantment. Thirty seconds. That was all I had before the spell wore off. The door opened revealing a man of average height and weight, dressed in what seemed to be some sort of black colored suit, head covered completely by a black helmet mask, with some sort of goggle-like lens on the right side where the eye would be. <BR>
<BR>
He first glanced at the bed. It was now that I started to carefully slip off the thick, red carpet to make sure that, whoever he was, he did not notice I was there. He started to turn his head. I was shivering uncontrollably. Any second now the incantation would cease and I would be revealed. I slipped off the rug just in time. He turned his back and walked toward the door. As he grasped the handle, I started to reappear, until finally I was all there, and the door was closed. After that I wasn't sure what happened; it was all a blur. I woke up the next morning in a prison cell and began being questioned. I think I must have fainted. <BR>
<BR>
Many others reported seeing mysterious figures entering the Temple grounds during the night. Not many clues were found. The interviewed pilgrim was the only one that survived in the Temple that night. <BR>
<BR>
To this day, the death of the Emperor Pelagius the first remains a mystery. For the sake of knowledge I hope that the search continues, and perhaps one day may actually be discovered. But, then again, a scholar's work is to learn and uncover things. And this proves amusing to all; if there were no great mysteries to be solved or other things to test our minds, then the world would be a boring place. Perhaps one day the truth of Pelagius will be uncovered, and until that day comes, may all scholars rejoice in the joy and liberty of all that is forgotten.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
佩拉基乌斯一世遇刺案<BR>
霍雷肖·加戈纳特<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
许多学者在写诗或阅读关于皇帝佩拉基乌斯一世遇刺的厚重著作时，都曾深思过。人们该如何解释发生在至一神殿的事件？有许多词语可以概括它，也有人提出过许多：奇怪、怪异、可疑、令人不安、神秘等等。有些人甚至称之为令人毛骨悚然。然而，真正让那些当时在场的人都会认同的是，这件事永远令人忐忑不安。<BR>
<BR>
在我们深入探讨佩拉基乌斯一世之前，先简述一下他的背景。他的祖父，伟大的泰伯·塞普汀，是整个泰姆瑞尔最受赞誉的国王之一。在第二纪元，尽管有第二纪元的暴君国王们的阻挠，泰伯·塞普汀还是在第二纪元896年以皇帝身份为整个泰姆瑞尔带来了和平。次年，泰伯宣布第二纪元结束 -- 诗人特拉西齐斯称之为“血与毒液的日日夜夜” -- 第三纪元开始。在长达三十八年辉煌的统治结束后，伟大的泰伯·塞普汀去世了。据说他死后下了两周的雨。<BR>
<BR>
泰伯·塞普汀去世后，他的孙子佩拉基乌斯一世加冕为塞普汀王朝的第二任皇帝。然而，佩拉基乌斯的统治很短暂。仅仅过了三年他就被刺杀了，尽管据说他在短暂的统治期间和祖父一样强大和能干。<BR>
<BR>
然而，真正神秘的与其说是他的出身或统治，不如说是他的遇刺。当他在至一神殿祈祷时，佩拉基乌斯被一群黑暗兄弟会的刺客刺杀。黑暗兄弟会在当时，直到今天，都是一个非法的刺客组织。<BR>
<BR>
最初雇佣黑暗兄弟会的委托人至今未知，而且可能很长一段时间内都不会为人所知。不过这个谜团非常令人不安。它不断地搅扰着思绪，玩弄着你的想法，仿佛它们只是玩具。来自泰姆瑞尔各地的理论层出不穷，有些荒谬至极，比如一个崇拜谢尔格拉斯夸马信徒的秘密迪德拉教派。另一些则现实得多，比如佩拉基乌斯一世的堂姐、前希尔维纳女王金泰拉策划的阴谋。由于他没有子嗣，她在他死后继承了权力。<BR>
<BR>
然而无论假设从何而来，不确定性总是随之而来。曾有人说，有一个可怜的乞丐在西罗帝尔的街道上奔跑，大声喊着说他看到了皇帝死亡背后的真相，直到他被两个卫兵追赶了大约半小时后，在跑过一条小巷时神秘消失了。虽然这个案例从未被官方证实发生过，但它传播出去的谣言却引起了民众的骚动。
<BR>
这个故事还有类似的版本，其中乞丐其实是一名卫兵，而追捕者实际上是一个黑影。但这只是一个故事。还有好几个其他的。不过，这个似乎是最有趣、最广为人知的。<BR>
<BR>
在我的研究过程中，我发掘了几段关于此事件的精彩访谈。其中一段来自一位在刺杀发生时正在神殿内的朝圣者：
<BR>
那天晚上陛下进来时非常安静。我在神殿住了几天，学习和写诗。我记得听到卧室门外传来脚步声。我的房间没有窗户，我正要睡着。我记得大厅里的灯光已经暗了，也许甚至完全熄灭了。脚步声持续着，直到有一个声音停在了我的门口。我悄悄起身，注意到一阵微弱的刮擦声。就像一小块坚实的金属在齿轮和电线的迷宫中刮擦、拖拽一样。<BR>
<BR>
就在那时我意识到发生了什么。我的门锁着，有人想进来。我知道门锁是我自己魔法的产物，不容易打开，即使是最专业的开锁工具也不行。所以我赶紧铺好床，确保不会有人注意到我的存在。正当我准备滑到床底下躲起来时，门开始打开了。我没有时间了。<BR><BR>
在我不得不迅速想出一个办法的不到一秒钟里，我想起了布里武塔的避厄之戒，这枚戒指是我为一位贵族清除他酒窖里异常的洞鼠 infestation 后得到的。我迅速而无声地戴上戒指，激活了它的附魔。三十秒。这就是咒语失效前我拥有的全部时间。门开了，露出一个中等身材的男人，穿着一套似乎是黑色的衣服，头部完全被一个黑色头盔面具覆盖，右侧眼睛的位置有一个类似护目镜的镜片。<BR>
<BR>
他先瞥了一眼床铺。这时我开始小心地滑出厚厚的地毯，确保不管他是谁，都不会注意到我在那里。他开始转过头。我控制不住地颤抖着。再过一秒咒语就会失效，我就会被发现。我刚好及时滑出了地毯。他转过身，走向门口。当他握住门把手时，我开始重新显现，直到最后我完全现身，门也关上了。之后我不确定发生了什么；一切都模糊不清。第二天早上我在一间牢房里醒来，开始被审问。我想我一定是晕过去了。<BR>
<BR>
许多其他人报告说，当晚看到神秘人物进入了神殿区域。没有发现太多线索。接受采访的朝圣者是当晚神殿中唯一的幸存者。<BR>
<BR>
直到今天，佩拉基乌斯一世皇帝之死仍然是一个谜。为了知识，我希望调查能够继续下去，也许有一天真相真的会被发现。但是，话说回来，学者的工作就是学习和揭示事物。这对所有人来说都很有趣；如果没有什么伟大的谜团需要解开，也没有什么其他的东西来考验我们的头脑，那么这个世界将是一个枯燥的地方。也许有一天佩拉基乌斯的真相会被揭开，在那一天到来之前，愿所有学者都能在一切被遗忘的事物的快乐和自由中欢欣鼓舞。<BR>"""

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_AssassinsDiaryTR
An Assassin's Diary
刺客日记

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_AssassinsDiaryTR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Diary<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Entry One:<BR>
I am keeping this diary to tell of my experiences following my indoctrination into the Morag Tong, a guild of professional assassins. My first assignment was to honorably execute a man named Serpal Arubar. He was a young Dunmer, perhaps twenty-five or twenty-six years of age. And so I killed him. He walked home alone during the night, having recently patronized a local brothel. I covered his mouth and slit his throat, leaving his body before his wife's home; she, having ordered the execution for his infidelity, would greet his body with mixed emotions the next day.<BR>
It is more fulfilling to kill for writ than to kill out of mere necessity. Nature forces us to be brutal, to take what's there simply to survive. I've killed only for personal reasons in the past, but it was always painful; there is a certain freedom in the anonymity of this profession. <BR><BR>
Entry Two:<BR>
I am fresh from completing my second honorable execution. A Nord, Unferth, had recently killed the client's brother in a bar fight in Narsis, crushing the victim's skull against a statue just outside the bar with his massive arms. The client, however, was a member of Great House Hlaalu, a member with a number of friends in power. I was ordered by my Grandmaster to execute the Nord. Surprisingly, the man was stupid enough to visit the very bar where he had recently killed my client's brother. I sat down next to the Nord, bought him a drink. As the night progressed, I slipped a little bittergreen into his drink every so often; thanks to the alcohol and his own disposition, he was unaware of its effects until too late. He died on his way home that night. <BR><BR>
Entry Three:<BR>
The sun set on Sadrith Mora as Elyssa fell to her knees. She pleaded for her life. I was even tempted to spare her; it is such a pity to crush a beautiful black rose. She cried before I killed her, weeping to the gods to save her. I ordered her to stop, to rise and accept the honor of an execution. She looked at me for a moment, pure hate in her eyes. Then, she spat at me and stabbed herself in the stomach before I could react.
Her father immediately sold all of her possessions away, earning back a little more than the price of the writ.<BR><BR>
Entry Four:<BR>
A double execution. A Bosmer man, Avelom, and woman, Marya. I executed both of them in open light as they opened their shop, a small trading post in the open market of Gnisis. What ills had they committed to deserve death? They could not pay their lord the taxes they owed. So, he had them killed, purely to make an example to the rest of the people living under his rule.<BR><BR>
Entry Five:<BR>
I have killed six now, the sixth being one of our own. Oleyn Bavul, a Morag Tong assassin simply trying to leave the guild. He scorned the master by refusing to accept a promotion for being such a proficient killer. And so, for this, I was ordered to kill him, to take away his life. When I slipped the knife into his side, he didn't scream, he didn't cry out. He merely whispered in my ear. "May a free man's blood save you." I didn't take my knife back.<BR><BR>
Entry Six:<BR>
When I slit the seventh's throat, felt his blood coughed into my hand, it did not feel the same. There was something amiss, something not right with what I did. I think often of Oleyn's words. "A free man," he said. And he was right. I do what the guild tells me to do. I must live a callous life, I must care not whom I kill, I must fulfill the writ. I must not weep . . . but I do. I give tears to those I killed.<BR><BR>
Entry Seven:<BR>
I no longer remember who last I killed. I say "killed" deliberately, for it was a killing and not an execution. There was no honor, there was nothing right in what I did, there was nothing to separate it from any other senseless murder. The walls of the home, the place where a man is meant to be shielded from the world, from killers, were splattered with innocent- yes, innocent- blood. No one should have to confront an assassin instead of the person they wronged. This is a profession designed to attract cowards.
What can I do? What hope is there for me? I cannot leave the guild, for I will surely be hunted down and gutted. Perhaps it would be a fitting end for me, but that is not a fate I am yet ready to confront.<BR><BR>
Entry Eight:<BR>
Guilt has prevented me from writing. To write is to solidify my crimes. However, in the time which has passed since last I wrote, I've realized that only we assassins deserve death. I write now knowing that there will not be another entry. I will die, or I will be free of the guild. The Grandmaster must pay for what he has done, what he stands for. May his blood begin to undo our crimes.<BR>"""

日记<BR>

第一篇：<BR>
我写这本日记是为了记录我加入莫拉格·堂 -- 一个职业刺客公会 -- 之后的经历。我的第一个任务是处决一个名叫瑟帕尔·阿鲁巴尔的人。他是个年轻的丹莫，大概二十五六岁。于是我杀了他。他在夜晚独自走回家，之前刚光顾了本地的一家妓院。我捂住他的嘴，割开了他的喉咙，把他的尸体留在他妻子家门口；她因为他的不忠而下了处决令，第二天看到他的尸体时，心中定是百感交集。<BR>
为令状而杀，比单纯为了生存而杀更令人满足。自然迫使我们残忍，为了生存而攫取所需。我过去只为个人原因杀过人，但那总是痛苦的；在这个职业的匿名性中，存在一种自由。<BR><BR>
第二篇：<BR>
我刚刚完成了我的第二次处决。一个名叫昂弗斯的诺德人，最近在纳西斯的一场酒吧斗殴中杀死了委托人的兄弟，他用他粗壮的手臂将受害者的头骨撞碎在酒吧外的雕像上。然而，委托人是哈拉鲁大豪族的一员，在权力圈里有很多朋友。我奉大导师之命处决那个诺德人。出乎意料的是，那个人蠢到去了他最近杀死我委托人兄弟的那家酒吧。我在那个诺德人旁边坐下，给他买了杯酒。随着夜晚的深入，我不时在他的酒里掺一点苦绿；由于酒精和他自己的性情，他直到为时已晚才意识到药效。那天晚上他在回家途中死了。<BR><BR>
第三篇：<BR>
日落时分，在萨德里斯·莫拉，埃莉莎跪倒在地。她哀求饶命。我甚至有过饶她一命的念头；碾碎一朵美丽的黑玫瑰实在可惜。在我杀她之前，她哭喊着，向众神祈求救她。我命令她停下，站起来接受处决的荣誉。她看了我片刻，眼中充满了纯粹的恨意。然后，她朝我吐了口唾沫，在我反应过来之前刺穿了自己的腹部。
她父亲立刻变卖了她所有的财产，所得比令状的价格略多一些。<BR><BR>
第四篇：<BR>
一次双重处决。一个波斯莫男人阿维洛姆，和一个女人玛丽亚。我在光天化日之下处决了他们，当时他们正在开店，那是尼希斯露天市场里一个小小的贸易站。他们犯了什么罪过该当处死？他们无力向他们的领主缴纳所欠的税款。于是，领主下令杀了他们，纯粹是为了杀鸡儆猴，警告他治下的其他人。<BR><BR>
第五篇：<BR>
我至今已杀了六人，第六个是我们自己人。奥莱恩·巴武尔，一个莫拉格·堂的刺客，只是想离开公会。他拒绝了晋升 -- 因为他是个如此高效的杀手 -- 以此蔑视了导师。因此，我奉命杀了他，夺走他的生命。当我把刀刺入他的肋部时，他没有尖叫，没有呼喊。他只是在我耳边低语：“愿一个自由人的鲜血拯救你。”我没有把刀取回。<BR><BR>
第六篇：<BR>
当我割开第七个人的喉咙，感觉到他的血咳到我手上时，感觉不一样了。有什么地方不对劲，我做错了什么。我常常想起奥莱恩的话。“一个自由人，”他说。他说得对。我按公会的命令行事的。我必须过一种冷酷的生活，我不能在乎杀的是谁，我必须完成令状。我不能哭泣......但我哭了。我为那些我杀的人流泪。<BR><BR>
第七篇：<BR>
我已经不记得我最后杀的是谁了。我刻意用了“杀害”这个词，因为那是杀害，而不是处决。没有荣誉，我所做的一切都不对，它与任何其他无谓的谋杀毫无区别。家的墙壁 -- 一个本该保护人免受外界、免受杀手侵害的地方 -- 溅满了无辜的 -- 是的，无辜的 -- 鲜血。没有人应该面对刺客，而不是他们冤枉的人。这是一个为吸引懦夫而设计的职业。
我能做什么？我还有什么希望？我不能离开公会，因为我肯定会被追杀，开膛破肚。也许那对我是一个合适的结局，但那还不是我准备好面对的命运。<BR><BR>
第八篇：<BR>
负罪感阻止我书写。书写就是巩固我的罪行。然而，在我上次书写之后的时间里，我已经意识到，只有我们刺客才该死。我现在写下这些，知道不会再有下一篇了。我要么死，要么脱离公会。大导师必须为他所做的一切、为他所代表的一切付出代价。愿他的鲜血开始洗刷我们的罪行。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Asylum Ball<BR>
By Waughin Jarth<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
My great great uncle was a warder at an asylum in Torval (maybe he was my great great great uncle -- it was quite a long time ago), and this is the story that has been passed down in my family from his generation to mine. Perhaps it is purely apocryphal, but when I was told it, it was whispered in such a way that it was meant to be taken seriously. Not having any children of my own to whisper to, and being in need of some gold, I have elected to publish my story.<BR><BR>
The asylum my great great uncle worked in was apparently very posh. Only the right class of lunatics were admitted. Eccentric dukes, mad baronesses, touched lords, and daft ladies filled the asylums tapestried and gilded halls. Still, it was a time of great excitement when the rumor began that the unhinged Emperor of Tamriel, Pelagius III, was transferring there from a resort in Valenwood. When the rumor became a reality, the asylum went into nice, calm, restive chaos. Pelagius was given an entire wing of the asylum for his own use, for, though he was madder than a jackal, he was still His Terrible Majesty, the Emperor of Tamriel.<BR><BR>
The Emperor was remarkably well behaved, my great great uncle supposedly asserted. Of course, he did not have to face the commoners who came on all sorts of pretenses to gawk at their overlord, the loon. When one of the warders (not, I have been assured, my uncle) forgot himself and let His Terrible Majesty know that people had been there to see him, the Emperor grew very excited. He made up his mind right there and then to have a ball. A huge party with musicians, dancing, and dinner, right at the lunatic asylum. Or precisely, in his wing of the asylum.<BR><BR>
Rumors of the Emperor's interest in holding a ball spread throughout Torval and eventually it reached the ears of the Empress Regent Katariah, Pelagius' dear wife, in the Imperial City. Eager to make her husband happy, she sent a caravan laden with gold to the asylum so a ball might be held befitting the Imperial dignity.<BR><BR>
The Emperor picked a date for the ball, and preparations began immediately. The old asylum walls were beautifully decorated, but needed cleaning. A pit had to be constructed to house the orchestra; servants for cooking and serving the food had to be hired; gold and ebony candelabras and matching chandeliers were ordered; the old rugs were destroyed, and new rugs embroidered with gems were weaved; lists of guests had to be compiled, reconsidered and recompiled. The Emperor knew that the guest list had to be very exclusive, and he relied on his advisors to tell him who was alive, who was dead, and who was imaginary.<BR><BR>
The party was set to begin at nine o'clock. At six, the hairdresser he had hired from Torval finished his Imperial coiffure. At seven, he was fully dressed in the robes he had ordered for the ball: voluminous black silk and piled velvet crusted with red diamonds. At eight, he walked down the newly reconstructed staircase to supervise the final preparations -- the lighting of the candles, the opening of the wine, the murder of the first course. At nine o'clock, he took his seat at the facsimile throne he had ordered and awaited the first guests.<BR><BR>
At nine thirty, his advisor, seeing the royal eyes beginning to glaze over with madness, said, "Your Terrible Majesty surely knows that it is not fashionable to arrive at any ball for at least an hour after the desired time, yes?"<BR><BR>
The Emperor just stared.<BR><BR>
At ten thirty, the Emperor called for some food and wine, and sat at his throne, looking at the open door, eating. Thirty minutes later, he ordered the orchestra to begin playing. For the next three hours, they played gaily for the empty, candlelit ballroom. 
At one o'clock, the Emperor announced his intention to retire for the evening. My uncle was one of the warders who assisted His Terrible Majesty up the staircase. Halfway to his room, Pelagius threw himself on the floor in a hysteria, screaming and laughing, ordering more wine (my mother was good at this part of the story, rolling her eyes and shrieking, "More wine! More wine! Wine!"), and, in short, imagining that he was possessed by all the revelers at his party that never was.<BR><BR>
Two days later, he was still not better. He had cut himself and those who tried to grapple him horribly with the red diamonds of his robe. Eventually it was decided that the Torval asylum was not equipped to deal with a lunatic of his severity, and he was sent to a more secure location in Black Marsh. It was only three months later, my uncle heard that the Emperor had died.<BR><BR>
One of my uncle's duties was to clear out the personal property of the inmates after their death. Being primarily landed nobility, the personal property was often quite extensive. Several years after the asylum ball, my uncle was called to clear out the apartment of a duchess whose chief eccentricity was a propensity to pilfer. Kleptomania, I believe it's called. Locked away in a secret door in her desk, protected by a trap armed with a barbed needle, was a variety of jewels, piles of gold, and five large stacks of beautifully engraved invitations signed in the Emperor's childlike handwriting.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
疯人院舞会<BR>
沃金·贾斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
我的曾曾叔父（也许是曾曾曾叔父 -- 那是很久以前的事了）曾是托瓦尔一家疯人院的看守，这个故事就是从他那一代传到我这代的。也许这纯属杜撰，但当我被告知时，是以一种严肃的口吻悄声讲述的。我既没有孩子可以耳语相传，又需要些金币，于是决定发表这个故事。<BR><BR>
我曾曾叔父工作的那家疯人院显然非常高档。只有上等阶层的疯子才被接收。古怪的公爵、疯狂的男爵夫人、头脑不清的领主、愚钝的贵妇，充斥着疯人院挂满挂毯和金碧辉煌的大厅。尽管如此，当传言说泰姆瑞尔那位精神失常的皇帝佩拉基乌斯三世，要从瓦伦伍德的一家疗养院转到那里时，还是引起了一阵巨大的骚动。当传言成真时，疯人院陷入了一种微妙、平静而又躁动不安的混乱之中。佩拉基乌斯被给予整栋侧翼供他个人使用，因为尽管他比豺狼还疯，他仍然是可怕的陛下，泰姆瑞尔的皇帝。<BR><BR>
据我曾曾叔父说，皇帝表现得格外顺从。当然，他不必面对那些以各种借口前来围观他们领主 -- 那个疯子的平民。当一名看守（我确信不是我叔父）一时疏忽，让可怕的陛下知道有人来看过他时，皇帝变得非常兴奋。他当场决定要办一场舞会。就在疯人院里，举办一场有音乐、舞蹈和晚宴的盛大派对。确切地说，是在他那侧翼的疯人院里。<BR><BR>
皇帝要举办舞会的传闻传遍了托瓦尔，最终传到了帝都摄政女皇卡塔瑞亚 -- 佩拉基乌斯亲爱的妻子 -- 的耳中。为了取悦丈夫，她派了一支满载黄金的商队前往疯人院，以便举办一场符合帝国尊严的舞会。<BR><BR>
皇帝选定了舞会的日期，准备工作立刻开始。疯人院陈旧的墙壁经过精美装饰，但需要清洁。必须挖一个坑来放置乐队；需要雇用仆人来烹饪和上菜；订购了金制和乌木的烛台及配套的枝形吊灯；旧地毯被毁，织了新的绣有宝石的地毯；宾客名单必须反复拟定、斟酌和重拟。皇帝知道宾客名单必须非常独特，他依赖顾问们告诉他谁是活人，谁是死人，谁是虚构的。<BR><BR>
晚会定于九点开始。六点时，他从托瓦尔雇来的理发师为他做好了帝国发型。七点时，他穿上了为舞会定制的长袍：宽大的黑丝绸和层层叠叠的天鹅绒，镶满了红钻。八点时，他走下新修缮的楼梯，监督最后的准备工作 -- 点燃蜡烛，开启美酒，“谋杀”第一道菜。九点时，他在他定制的复制王座上就座，等待第一批客人。<BR><BR>
九点半时，他的顾问看到皇帝的眼神开始因疯狂而变得呆滞，说道：“可怕的陛下想必知道，在任何舞会，比预定时间至少晚到一小时才符合时尚，对吧？”<BR><BR>
皇帝只是盯着他看。<BR><BR>
十点半时，皇帝要了些食物和酒，坐在他的王座上，看着敞开的门，吃着东西。三十分钟后，他命令乐队开始演奏。接下来的三个小时，他们为空旷、烛光闪烁的舞厅欢快地演奏着。
凌晨一点，皇帝宣布他打算就寝。我叔父是搀扶可怕的陛下上楼的看守之一。走到半路时，佩拉基乌斯歇斯底里地倒在地板上，又喊又叫，又笑又闹，命令再上酒（我母亲很擅长讲这部分故事，翻着白眼尖叫道：“再来点酒！再来点酒！酒！”），简而言之，他想象自己被那些从未存在的派对上的狂欢者附身了。<BR><BR>
两天后，他仍然没有好转。他用长袍上的红钻严重割伤了自己和那些试图制服他的人。最终，人们认为托瓦尔的疯人院无法应付他这种程度的疯子，他被送往黑沼泽一个更安全的地方。仅仅三个月后，我叔父就听说皇帝去世了。<BR><BR>
我叔父的职责之一是清理囚犯死后的个人财产。由于主要是拥有土地的贵族，个人财产通常相当可观。疯人院舞会几年后，我叔父被叫去清理一位女公爵的公寓，她主要的怪癖是爱偷东西。我想这叫盗窃癖。在她书桌的暗门里，藏着用带倒刺的针机关保护着的各种珠宝、成堆的金子，以及五大叠精美雕刻的邀请函，上面有皇帝那稚嫩笔迹的签名。<BR>

<BR>
据我曾曾叔父说，皇帝表现得格外顺从。当然，他不必面对那些以各种借口前来围观他们领主 -- 那个疯子的平民。当一名看守（我确信不是我叔父）一时疏忽，让可怕的陛下知道有人来看过他时，皇帝变得非常兴奋。他当场决定要办一场舞会。就在疯人院里，举办一场有音乐、舞蹈和晚宴的盛大派对。确切地说，是在他那侧翼的疯人院里。<BR>
<BR>
皇帝要举办舞会的传闻传遍了托瓦尔，最终传到了帝都摄政女皇卡塔瑞亚 -- 佩拉基乌斯亲爱的妻子 -- 的耳中。为了取悦丈夫，她派了一支满载黄金的商队前往疯人院，以便举办一场符合帝国尊严的舞会。<BR>
<BR>
皇帝选定了舞会的日期，准备工作立刻开始。疯人院陈旧的墙壁经过精美装饰，但需要清洁。必须挖一个坑来放置乐队；需要雇用仆人来烹饪和上菜；订购了金制和乌木的烛台及配套的枝形吊灯；旧地毯被毁，织了新的绣有宝石的地毯；宾客名单必须反复拟定、斟酌和重拟。皇帝知道宾客名单必须非常独特，他依赖顾问们告诉他谁是活人，谁是死人，谁是虚构的。<BR>
<BR>
晚会定于九点开始。六点时，他从托瓦尔雇来的理发师为他做好了帝国发型。七点时，他穿上了为舞会定制的长袍：宽大的黑丝绸和层层叠叠的天鹅绒，镶满了红钻。八点时，他走下新修缮的楼梯，监督最后的准备工作 -- 点燃蜡烛，开启美酒，“谋杀”第一道菜。九点时，他在他定制的复制王座上就座，等待第一批客人。<BR>
<BR>
九点半时，他的顾问看到皇帝的眼神开始因疯狂而变得呆滞，说道：“可怕的陛下想必知道，在任何舞会，比预定时间至少晚到一小时才符合时尚，对吧？”<BR>
<BR>
皇帝只是盯着他看。<BR>
<BR>
十点半时，皇帝要了些食物和酒，坐在他的王座上，看着敞开的门，吃着东西。三十分钟后，他命令乐队开始演奏。接下来的三个小时，他们为空旷、烛光闪烁的舞厅欢快地演奏着。<BR>
<BR>
凌晨一点，皇帝宣布他打算就寝。我叔父是搀扶可怕的陛下上楼的看守之一。走到半路时，佩拉基乌斯歇斯底里地倒在地板上，又喊又叫，又笑又闹，命令再上酒（我母亲很擅长讲这部分故事，翻着白眼尖叫道：“再来点酒！再来点酒！酒！”），简而言之，他想象自己被那些从未存在的派对上的狂欢者附身了。<BR>
<BR>
两天后，他仍然没有好转。他用长袍上的红钻严重割伤了自己和那些试图制服他的人。最终，人们认为托瓦尔的疯人院无法应付他这种程度的疯子，他被送往黑沼泽一个更安全的地方。仅仅三个月后，我叔父就听说皇帝去世了。<BR>
<BR>
我叔父的职责之一是清理囚犯死后的个人财产。由于主要是拥有土地的贵族，个人财产通常相当可观。疯人院舞会几年后，我叔父被叫去清理一位女公爵的公寓，她主要的怪癖是爱偷东西。我想这叫盗窃癖。在她书桌的暗门里，藏着用带倒刺的针机关保护着的各种珠宝、成堆的金子，以及五大叠精美雕刻的邀请函，上面有皇帝那稚嫩笔迹的签名。<BR>
<BR>

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_AsylumBallTR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Asylum Ball<BR>
By Waughin Jarth<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
My great great uncle was a warder at an asylum in Torval (maybe he was my great great great uncle -- it was quite a long time ago), and this is the story that has been passed down in my family from his generation to mine. Perhaps it is purely apocryphal, but when I was told it, it was whispered in such a way that it was meant to be taken seriously. Not having any children of my own to whisper to, and being in need of some gold, I have elected to publish my story.<BR><BR>
The asylum my great great uncle worked in was apparently very posh. Only the right class of lunatics were admitted. Eccentric dukes, mad baronesses, touched lords, and daft ladies filled the asylums tapestried and gilded halls. Still, it was a time of great excitement when the rumor began that the unhinged Emperor of Tamriel, Pelagius III, was transferring there from a resort in Valenwood. When the rumor became a reality, the asylum went into nice, calm, restive chaos. Pelagius was given an entire wing of the asylum for his own use, for, though he was madder than a jackal, he was still His Terrible Majesty, the Emperor of Tamriel.<BR><BR>
The Emperor was remarkably well behaved, my great great uncle supposedly asserted. Of course, he did not have to face the commoners who came on all sorts of pretenses to gawk at their overlord, the loon. When one of the warders (not, I have been assured, my uncle) forgot himself and let His Terrible Majesty know that people had been there to see him, the Emperor grew very excited. He made up his mind right there and then to have a ball. A huge party with musicians, dancing, and dinner, right at the lunatic asylum. Or precisely, in his wing of the asylum.<BR><BR>
Rumors of the Emperor's interest in holding a ball spread throughout Torval and eventually it reached the ears of the Empress Regent Katariah, Pelagius' dear wife, in the Imperial City. Eager to make her husband happy, she sent a caravan laden with gold to the asylum so a ball might be held befitting the Imperial dignity.<BR><BR>
The Emperor picked a date for the ball, and preparations began immediately. The old asylum walls were beautifully decorated, but needed cleaning. A pit had to be constructed to house the orchestra; servants for cooking and serving the food had to be hired; gold and ebony candelabras and matching chandeliers were ordered; the old rugs were destroyed, and new rugs embroidered with gems were weaved; lists of guests had to be compiled, reconsidered and recompiled. The Emperor knew that the guest list had to be very exclusive, and he relied on his advisors to tell him who was alive, who was dead, and who was imaginary.<BR><BR>
The party was set to begin at nine o'clock. At six, the hairdresser he had hired from Torval finished his Imperial coiffure. At seven, he was fully dressed in the robes he had ordered for the ball: voluminous black silk and piled velvet crusted with red diamonds. At eight, he walked down the newly reconstructed staircase to supervise the final preparations -- the lighting of the candles, the opening of the wine, the murder of the first course. At nine o'clock, he took his seat at the facsimile throne he had ordered and awaited the first guests.<BR><BR>
At nine thirty, his advisor, seeing the royal eyes beginning to glaze over with madness, said, "Your Terrible Majesty surely knows that it is not fashionable to arrive at any ball for at least an hour after the desired time, yes?"<BR><BR>
The Emperor just stared.<BR><BR>
At ten thirty, the Emperor called for some food and wine, and sat at his throne, looking at the open door, eating. Thirty minutes later, he ordered the orchestra to begin playing. For the next three hours, they played gaily for the empty, candlelit ballroom. 
At one o'clock, the Emperor announced his intention to retire for the evening. My uncle was one of the warders who assisted His Terrible Majesty up the staircase. Halfway to his room, Pelagius threw himself on the floor in a hysteria, screaming and laughing, ordering more wine (my mother was good at this part of the story, rolling her eyes and shrieking, "More wine! More wine! Wine!"), and, in short, imagining that he was possessed by all the revelers at his party that never was.<BR><BR>
Two days later, he was still not better. He had cut himself and those who tried to grapple him horribly with the red diamonds of his robe. Eventually it was decided that the Torval asylum was not equipped to deal with a lunatic of his severity, and he was sent to a more secure location in Black Marsh. It was only three months later, my uncle heard that the Emperor had died.<BR><BR>
One of my uncle's duties was to clear out the personal property of the inmates after their death. Being primarily landed nobility, the personal property was often quite extensive. Several years after the asylum ball, my uncle was called to clear out the apartment of a duchess whose chief eccentricity was a propensity to pilfer. Kleptomania, I believe it's called. Locked away in a secret door in her desk, protected by a trap armed with a barbed needle, was a variety of jewels, piles of gold, and five large stacks of beautifully engraved invitations signed in the Emperor's childlike handwriting.<BR>

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_AtopATowerOnMoridunonTR
Atop a Tower on Moridunon
在莫里杜农塔顶

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_AtopATowerOnMoridunonTR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Atop a Tower on Moridunon<BR>
by Pallav Valernius<BR> <BR> 
<IMG SRC="TR\TR_MoridunonBookArt.dds" WIDTH="240" HEIGHT="240"> 
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
[This essay by the Skingradian poet Pallav Valernius (2E 846--3E 21) was written during the latter days of the Tiber Wars. At that time Valernius was indeed touring the lands of the Aldmeri Dominion, recording their oral histories and traditions. The backdrop of the dialogue presented here -- the horrific destruction of an elven city -- remains, however, quite dubious. Footnotes are by the editor. Book art above. --The Editor.] <BR>
<BR>
One morning we climbed up a beacon tower just outside the city of Firsthold. It was an old tower, far older than any I had ever visited, with steps carved into the rocky side of the mountain. After a long ascent through the mist and clouds we made our way through the final doorway that was hidden behind a curtain of glass-like ivy and emerged on the top of that magnificent tower. It was a beacon tower, yes, but no signal fire was lit. It would have all been in vain. The land below was laid out before our eyes in all its awe-inspiring vastness. The walls and roofs of the city below, the white sands of the beach and the blueness of the sea. All was silent. Across the sea Numidium could be seen approaching -- a great brass shape against the horizon. The waters boiled where it walked. We stood there watching. <BR>
<BR>
My guide, an Altmeri scholar of great learning, was the first to break the silence. <BR>
"Cyrod," he said, "is making war on us." <BR>
"Yes," I replied. "They have the weapon for it now. My kinsmen are no longer weak and disorganized." <BR>
"Your kinsmen," my guide said, "are children." <BR>
"Might have been in the past, I agree, but surely their great deeds now prove otherwise?" <BR>
<BR>
"They have brought the Dunmer to their knees," my guide said, "and so they could have had the very thing that beats in the heart of this world for themselves -- yet they are content with the brass puppet that was given to them. And they use it as an instrument of conquest! So, children they are. Alinor will surrender under this attack, of course; there's no question about it. Still, I shall be surprised if this fledgling Empire is still standing a decade after this General Talos is gone. The empires of men are fickle. They are born out of warfare, and so they soon die out. It is as if the only reason for their existence is so that your people could build mausoleums for the glorified warlords [1] that momentarily helm them. Tell me, as death might come for us both soon, what is it that your kind thinks awaits you?" <BR>
"An eternity in the light of Aetherius awaits those who are worthy--kings, heroes, wise men--but for common folk such as myself, the priests say, that by the blessing of Arkay our bodies shall rot in the ground, and our spirits shall be reborn." <BR>
"And what do you think of this?" <BR>
"I think that the cycle of life and death doesn't care about the opinions of mortals, but the promise of rebirth does bring me some hope and consolation." <BR>
"You believe there's 'consolation' in the Arkayn Cycle? A 'promise of rebirth'? Being tied, like a beast of burden, to a millstone, doomed to walk in a mindless circle forever? Shows that your kind have not yet forgotten your slave's instincts. I can not imagine why anyone would want to submit to such a dull fate. We elves are closer to the old Ehlnofey and so we have a better understanding of death and how to properly face it." <BR>
"Some elves eat their dead," I interrupted remembering what I had seen on my travels in Valenwood. [2] My words visibly irritated my guide. <BR>
"There is wisdom there, which I could perhaps explain in a way you would be able to understand, but I will not speak for my Bosmeri brethren. Suffice to say that their customs, to me, are mere quirks compared to the outlandish barbarisms that plague the races of men." <BR> <BR>
He paused. <BR> <BR>
Far below doom had come to Moridunon. The land was engulfed in flames. Numidium shambled in and out of time. A crackling sound like lightning. A choir of wails. Either we were safe in our tower or we were not; there was nothing we could do about it. We watched. I began to tremble. <BR> <BR>
"You fear death," my guide spoke again, "You could begin to understand us by starting to loathe it instead." He drew breath and continued: <BR>
"We are blessed, so you might say, with long lives. That is only an illusion, or rather: it is a thing so meaningless that it might as well be an illusion. We dedicate our lives to learning, and then remembering what we have learned. That is no small feat. Can you imagine the things I remember? Of course you can't. There are whole schools devoted to the study of these visions. Your view of life and death and time is worse than twisted: it's over-simplified. To you, everything is linear. You are born, you live, time moves in one direction, and then you die. You think, or hope, the rebirth is a continuation of the same linear movement, that the Arkayn Cycle is something you will survive and observe. You are wrong. When the wheel spins downwards, it crushes you under it, ending your life, and when the wheel spins back up, a new life begins -- and what an insult is that new life! Weakened, broken and humbled, stripped of everything it ever knew and of everything that made it what it was, thrown back into existence against its will. So you see, this Nirn of ours is a prison, my friend. Your precious life is a sentence. And the rebirth where your faint heart finds its solace is nothing more than a breaking wheel. It is the very antithesis of hope." [3] <BR>
"I see," I said, even though I did not. <BR> <BR> 
The earth quaked. A gargantuan shadow blocked the sun. <BR> <BR>
Suddenly, Numidium was facing us. It looked right through us as if it was some sort of a demented god and we were two specks of dust too tiny to comprehend. Out of its open jaws there came a tormented howl, and then it was gone. Embers spiralled in the air where it had been. <BR> <BR>
"Don't be fooled," my companion hissed. "It was laughing at us." [4] <BR> <BR>
Footnotes: <BR>
[1] In the original manuscript, Valernius wrote "crowned apes?" above "glorified warlords"; it is supposed his guide made use of an ambiguous phrase. <BR>
[2] See Valernius' earlier "A Feast in Elden Root". <BR>
[3] This rather stark view of the world has been contested by Imperial and elven scholars alike. <BR>
[4] It has been suggested that Valernius' tour was at the behest of the emerging Septim Empire, and that he was, at least partly, a spy. However, such a close and dangerous encounter with the Brass Golem -- if it is indeed true -- does not support these claims. <BR> <BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
在莫里杜农塔顶<BR>
帕拉夫·瓦勒尼乌斯 著<BR><BR>
<IMG SRC="TR\TR_MoridunonBookArt.dds" WIDTH="240" HEIGHT="240">
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
[这篇散文由斯金格拉德诗人帕拉夫·瓦勒尼乌斯（第二纪元846年--第三纪元21年）写于泰伯战争后期。当时瓦勒尼乌斯确实在游历先祖神洲的土地，记录他们的口述历史和传统。然而，此处对话的背景 -- 一座精灵城市的恐怖毁灭 -- 却相当可疑。脚注由编者添加。上方为书籍插图。 -- 编者]<BR>
<BR>
一天早晨，我们爬上了首堡城外的一座烽火塔。那是一座古老的塔，比我参观过的任何塔都要古老得多，台阶凿在山岩一侧。经过在迷雾和云层中漫长的攀登，我们穿过了最后一道门，那道门隐藏在水晶般的常春藤帘幕之后，出现在那座宏伟的塔顶。是的，那是一座烽火塔，但没有点燃烽火。一切都将是徒劳。脚下的土地在我们眼前展现出其令人敬畏的广阔。下方城市的城墙和屋顶，海滩的白沙和蔚蓝的大海，一切都寂静无声。海的对岸，可以看到努米迪文正在逼近 -- 地平线上一个巨大的黄铜身影。它走过之处，海水沸腾。我们站在那里注视着。<BR>
<BR>
我的向导，一位博学的傲特莫学者，首先打破了沉默。<BR>
“西罗德，”他说，“正在向我们开战。”<BR>
“是的，”我回答，“他们现在有了武器。我的同胞们不再软弱和涣散了。”<BR>
“你的同胞们，”我的向导说，“还是孩子。”<BR>
“也许过去是，我同意，但他们现在的伟大功绩难道不证明并非如此吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“他们已使丹莫屈服，”我的向导说，“因此他们本可以为自己拥有这世界心脏中跳动的东西 -- 然而他们却满足于给予他们的黄铜傀儡。他们把它当作征服的工具！所以，他们终究是孩子。阿里诺尔会在这次攻击下投降，当然；这毫无疑问。不过，如果这个羽翼未丰的帝国在塔洛斯将军消失后十年仍能屹立不倒，我会感到惊讶。人类的帝国变幻无常。它们生于战争，所以也迅速消亡。仿佛它们存在的唯一理由，就是让你们的人民为那些暂时统领他们的、被神化的军阀[1]建造陵墓。告诉我，既然死亡可能很快降临我们两人，你的同类认为等待着你们的是什么？”<BR>
“光界之光中的永恒等待着那些有价值的人 -- 国王、英雄、智者 -- 但祭司们说，对于像我这样的普通人，凭借阿尔凯的祝福，我们的身体将在土中腐烂，而我们的灵魂将获得重生。”<BR>
“你对此怎么看？”<BR>
“我认为生死循环并不在意凡人的看法，但重生的承诺确实给我带来了一些希望和慰藉。”<BR>
“你相信阿尔凯循环中有‘慰藉’？一个‘重生的承诺’？像驮兽一样被绑在磨盘上，注定永远在一个无意识的圈子里行走？这表明你们这类人还未忘记奴隶的本能。我无法想象为什么会有人愿意屈从于如此沉闷的命运。我们精灵更接近古老的艾诺菲，所以我们更理解死亡，以及如何正确地面对它。”<BR>
“有些精灵吃他们的死者，”我打断道，想起了我在瓦伦伍德旅行时的所见所闻。[2] 我的话明显激怒了我的向导。<BR>
“其中自有智慧，我也许能用你能理解的方式解释，但我不会为我那些波斯莫同胞代言。我只想说，他们的习俗对我来说，与困扰人类种族的那些怪诞野蛮行径相比，不过是些古怪之处罢了。”<BR><BR>
他停顿了一下。<BR><BR>
遥远的下方，厄运降临了莫里杜农。大地被火焰吞噬。努米迪文在时间中蹒跚进出。一阵噼啪声，如同闪电。一片哀嚎之声。无论我们在塔中是否安全，我们都无能为力。我们注视着。我开始颤抖。<BR><BR>
“你恐惧死亡，”我的向导又开口了，“你可以从开始憎恨它来理解我们。”他吸了口气，继续说道：<BR>
“我们被赐予了，你可以说，悠长的寿命。那不过是一种幻觉，或者更确切地说：它是如此无意义，以至于与幻觉无异。我们毕生致力于学习，然后记住所学。这绝非易事。你能想象我记得的事情吗？你当然不能。有整整的学派致力于研究这些幻象。你对生命、死亡和时间的看法不只是扭曲：它过于简化了。对你而言，一切都是线性的。你出生，你活着，时间单向流动，然后你死去。你认为，或希望，重生是同一线性运动的延续，阿尔凯循环是你能存活并观察的东西。你错了。当轮子向下转动时，它把你碾在下面，结束你的生命，而当轮子转回上面时，一个新的生命开始了 -- 那个新生命是多么的侮辱！被削弱、破碎和屈辱，被剥夺了它所知道的一切和使它成为它自己的一切，违背它的意愿被抛回存在。所以你看，我们这个奈恩是一座监狱，我的朋友。你宝贵的生命是一纸判决。而你那颗脆弱的心在其中找到慰藉的重生，不过是一个破碎的轮子。它正是希望的反面。”[3]<BR>
“我明白了，”我说，尽管我并不明白。<BR><BR>
大地颤抖。一个巨大的阴影遮住了太阳。<BR><BR>
突然，努米迪文正对着我们。它径直看穿了我们，仿佛它是一个疯狂的神祇，而我们只是两个渺小得无法理解的尘埃微粒。从它张开的巨口中传来一声痛苦的嚎叫，然后它消失了。余烬在它曾站立的地方旋转升腾。<BR><BR>
“别上当，”我的同伴嘶声说道，“它在嘲笑我们。”[4]<BR><BR>
脚注：<BR>
[1] 在原手稿中，瓦勒尼乌斯在“被神化的军阀”上方写了“戴王冠的猿猴？”；据推测他的向导使用了一个模糊的短语。<BR>
[2] 见瓦勒尼乌斯早期的《古根盛宴》。<BR>
[3] 这种相当冷酷的世界观遭到了帝国和精灵学者的共同质疑。<BR>
[4] 有人提出，瓦勒尼乌斯的巡游是受新兴的塞普汀帝国指使的，他至少部分是个间谍。然而，如此近距离且危险地与黄铜魔像相遇 -- 如果属实 -- 并不支持这些说法。<BR><BR>"""

Being a Survey of the Triumphant Settlement of the Heartland High Elves in the Southern Regions<BR>

... At this point, we should mention the remarkable cities of Ceyatatar, and the Ayleid settlement beneath what is now modern Bravil. These cities, along with the Valenwood cities of Haven, Woodhearth, and Silvenar, all flourished as a result of increased trade after the establishment of the great White-Gold Tower in what is now the heart of Cyrodiil.<BR>
<BR>
Of note in particular is the university and libraries at nearby Elden Root. The Ayleids there built their city in and around what is called the Elden Tree or the First Tree, believed by many to be the tree that seeded all of Valenwood.<BR>
<BR>
Both Haven and Woodhearth were destroyed utterly by the sieging Maormer, who cared little for the advanced and enlightened ways of the Valenwood Aldmer. Marching inland, they plundered not only the Elden Root enclave, but also the Great Tree itself. What villainous tribe would injure and pillage such magnificence?<BR>
<BR>
It is possible that the Maormer had broken the Aldmer traditions of racial purity and intermingled with indigenous, bestial tribes of Pyandonea. This would explain their savagery and lack of regard for the greatness of mainland Elven culture.<BR><BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Ayleid Inscriptions and their Translations<BR>
by Raelys Anine<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The following inscriptions were painstakingly transcribed and interpreted over many long years, and are preserved here for all time.<BR>
<BR>
--
Av molag anyammis, av latta magicka.
"From fire, life; from light, magic."<BR>
<BR>
--
Barra agea ry sou karan.
"Wear lore as your armor."<BR>
<BR>
--
Agea haelia ne jorane emero laloria.
"Wisdom learned by pain is a reliable guide in dark times." [literally, "Terrible wisdom never betrayed the loremasters."]<BR>
<BR>
--
Nou aldmeris mathmeldi admia aurane gandra sepredia av relleis ye brelyeis ye varlais.
"Our exiled Elven ancestors heard the welcoming gifts of peace in the streams and beech trees and stars." ["Mathmeldi" means literally "from-home-driven." ]<BR>
<BR>
--
Suna ye sunnabe.
"Bless and blessed be."<BR>
<BR>
--
Va garlas agea, gravia ye goria, lattia mallari av malatu.
"In the caverns of lore, ugly and obscure, shines the gold of truth."<BR>
<BR>
--
Vabria frensca, sa belle, sa baune, amaraldane aldmeris adonai.
"The foaming wave, so thunderous, so mighty, heralds the lordly Elves."<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Glories and Laments Among the Ayleid Ruins<BR>
by Alexandre Hetrard<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Having arrived at Delodiil, halfway on the Gold Road between Skingrad and the Imperial City, I resolved to make a side trip to view the magnificent ruins of Ceyatatar, or "Shadow of the Fatherwoods' in the ancient Ayleid tongue. After many hours of difficult travel through tangled hawthorn hells and limberlosts, I was suddenly struck dumb by the aspect of five pure white columns rising from a jade-green mound of vines to perfect V-shaped arches and graceful capitals towering above the verdant forest growth. This spectacle caused me to meditate on the lost glories of the past, and the melancholy fate of high civilizations now poking like splinter shards of bone from the green-grown tumulus of time-swept obscurity.<BR>
<BR>
Within the forest tangle I discovered an entrance leading down into the central dome of a great underground edifice once dedicated to Magnus, the God of Sight, Light, and Insight. Dimly lit by the faded power of its magical pools, the shattered white walls of the enclosure shimmered with a cold blue light.<BR>
<BR>
The marble benches of the central plaza faced out across the surrounding waters to tall columns and sharp arches supporting the high dome. From the central island, stately bridges spanned the still pools to narrow walkways behind the columns, with broad vaulted avenues and limpid canals leading away through ever-deepening gloom into darkness. Reflected in the pools were the tumbled columns, collapsed walls, and riotous root and vine growth thriving the dark half-light of the magical fountains.<BR>
<BR>
The ancient Ayleids recognized not the four elements of modern natural philosophy -- earth, water, air, and fire -- but the four elements of High Elf religion -- earth, water, air, and light. The Ayleids considered fire to be but a weak and corrupt form of light, which Ayleid philosophers identified with primary magical principles. Thus their ancient subterranean temples and sanctuaries were lit by lamps, globes, pools, and fountains of purest magic.<BR>
<BR>
It was by these ancient, faded, but still active magics that I knelt and contemplated the departed glories of the long-dead Ayleid architects. Gazing through the glass-smooth reflections of the surrounding pools, I could see, deep below, the slow pulse, the waxing and waning of the Welkynd stones.<BR>
<BR>
The chiefest perils of these ruins to the explorer are the cunning and deadly mechanisms devised by the Ayleids to torment and confound those would invade their underground sanctuaries. What irony that after these many years, these devices should still stand vigilant against those who would admire the works of the Ayleids. For it is clear... these devices were crafted in vain. They did not secure the Ayleids against their true enemies, which were not the slaves who revolted and overthrew their cruel masters, nor the were they the savage beast peoples who learned the crafts of war and magic from their Ayleid masters. No, it was the arrogant pride of their achievements, their smug self-assurance that their empire would last forever, that doomed them to fail and fade into obscurity. <BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
亚历德废墟中的荣光与哀叹<BR>
亚历山大·赫特拉尔 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
在到达德洛迪尔之后，我决定绕道去参观凯阿塔达的宏伟废墟，它在古老亚历德语中意为“父林之影”。在穿过纠缠的荆棘林和密林，艰难跋涉数小时后，五根洁白的石柱突然映入眼帘，它们从翠绿的藤蔓土丘中升起，形成完美的V形拱门和优雅的柱头，高耸于翠绿的森林之上，这一幕让我瞠目结舌。这番景象使我沉思过去失落的荣光，以及高等文明那忧郁的命运，它们如今如同碎骨片般，从被时间冲刷而遗忘的绿色古冢中戳出。<BR>
<BR>
在森林的纠缠中，我发现了一个入口，向下通往一座巨大地下建筑的中心穹顶，那里曾供奉着玛格努斯，视界、光明与洞察之神。魔法池黯淡的力量提供了微弱的光线，围场破碎的白色墙壁闪烁着冰冷的蓝光。<BR>
<BR>
中央广场的大理石长椅面向周围的水域，对面是支撑高穹顶的立柱和尖拱。从中央岛屿出发，庄严的桥梁横跨静池，通向立柱后的狭窄步道，宽阔的拱形大道和清澈的运河在越来越深的幽暗中延伸至黑暗。池水中倒映着倾颓的立柱、坍塌的墙壁，以及在魔法喷泉昏暗光线中繁茂生长的杂乱根须和藤蔓。<BR>
<BR>
古代亚历德人认知的并非现代自然哲学的四大元素 -- 土、水、气、火 -- 而是高等精灵宗教的四大元素 -- 土、水、气、光。亚历德人认为火只是光的一种微弱而堕落的形式，亚历德哲学家将其等同于原始魔法原理。因此，他们古老的地下神殿和圣所由最纯净的魔法灯、球体、池水和喷泉照明。<BR>
<BR>
正是凭借这些古老、黯淡但仍活跃的魔法，我跪下来，沉思早已逝去的亚历德建筑师的昔日荣光。透过周围池水如镜般的倒影，我能看到深处维尔金石那缓慢的脉动，它们的明灭变化。<BR>
<BR>
这些废墟对探险者来说，最主要的危险是亚历德人设计的精巧致命机关，用以折磨和迷惑那些胆敢入侵他们地下圣所的人。多么讽刺，这么多年过去了，这些机关仍在警惕地防范着那些想要瞻仰亚历德人杰作的人。因为很明显......这些机关是徒劳的。它们没能保护亚历德人免受真正敌人的侵害，那些敌人既不是起义推翻他们残暴统治的奴隶，也不是从亚历德主人那里学会战争和魔法技艺的野蛮兽族。不，是他们对自己成就的傲慢，他们对自己帝国将永世长存的沾沾自喜，注定了他们的失败和湮没无闻。<BR>

It was a perfectly ordinary day at the main office of the Bank of Daggerfall. Normal transactions took place: deposits were deposited, withdrawals were withdrawn, house mortgages were collected, letters of credit were golded. When a teller named Clyton J. It was not to be a perfectly ordinary day at the Bank of Daggerfall after all.<BR><BR>
"I would like you to take the thirty million gold pieces I have in these sacks and open me an account," croaked the little old biddy.<BR><BR>
"Certainly, madam," Wifflington said, eagerly. He counted the gold in the sacks and found that it was thirty million gold exactly. <BR><BR>
"One moment, sonny," the little old lady chirruped. "Before I open the account, I would like to meet the man I'm trusting it to. I'd like to talk to the president of the bank." <BR><BR>
Wifflington wanted the president to know that he was the teller who had taken the largest single deposit that year, so eagerly sent word to the president's secretary. As it turned out, the president was equally eager to meet such a wealthy woman, so the old lady was brought to his office that very day. <BR><BR>
"Pleased to make your acquaintance, milady. I am Gerander P. Baggledon," said the president, Gerander P. Baggledon. <BR>
"My name," said the little old lady. "Is Petuva Smuthworthy." That was, in fact, her real name. "Thank you for seeing me. I like to conduct my business in a more personal way." <BR><BR>
"I can certainly appreciate that," said Baggledon chucklingly. "It is an appreciable sum of gold. Would it be rude of me to ask how you came by it?" <BR><BR>
"Not at all," said Mrs. Smuthworthy. <BR><BR>
"How came you by it?" asked Baggledon. <BR><BR>
"I'll let you guess," replied Mrs. Smuthworthy, with a trace of unattractive girlish flirtation. <BR><BR>
Baggledon was a man of enormous imagination, for a banker. He guessed inheritance and longtime thrift, but Mrs. Smuthworthy coyly shook her head. Perhaps she had sold a large, old mansion? No. In a moment of chumminess, Baggledon asked if the gold came as a result of plunder or thievery. Mrs. Smuthworthy took no offense, but said no. Finally, he admitted defeat. <BR><BR>
"I'm a gambler," she said. <BR><BR>
"In arena fights?" he asked, interested. <BR><BR>
"No, no, dearie. Different things. For example, I'd be willing to wager twenty five thousand gold pieces that at this time tomorrow morning, your testicles will be covered with feathers." <BR><BR>
Mr. Baggledon was somewhat taken aback by the old woman's words. Could she be mad? Could she be a witch? He eliminated the latter possibility, for he had a sense for such things. If she were mad, she was still a rich madwoman. And he could use twenty five thousand gold pieces. So he took her wager. <BR><BR>
For the next twenty-four hours, Mr. Baggledon obsessed over his testicles. He checked his pants so often that afternoon, his subordinates feared the worse and suggested that he not touch anything and go home for the rest of the afternoon. He spent the night seated, his pants around his ankles, his beady banker's eyes focused on his scrotum. Every time he started to doze off, his vision was filled with images of Mrs. Smuthworthy plucking feathers from his balls, cackling. <BR><BR>
Mr. Baggledon arrived at the bank late the next day -- only moments before Mrs. Smethworthy's arrival. Accompanying her was a lean, bespeckled fellow she introduced as a barrister from the court. Her son, it turned out. Young Mr. Smethworthy always accompanied his mother when there was money involved, she explained.<BR><BR>
"Enough banter," she crowed. "Our bet, dearie?" <BR><BR>
"My dear, dear madam, I can tell you that your gold will be quite safe at the Bank of Daggerfall. I hope it will not cause you distress to discover that your gold will be safer here than in your own hands. My family jewels are quite, shall we say, featherless. And you owe me a sum equally twenty five thousand gold."<BR><BR>
Poor Mrs. Smethworthy's face fell when she heard this. "Are you sure?"<BR><BR>
"Quite, madam." <BR><BR>
"Not even one feather?" Her voice suggested doubt. Mr. Baggledon could tell she thought he might be lying.<BR><BR>
"Not one, I fear, madam."<BR><BR>
"It's not that I don't trust you, Mr. Baggledon, but it is quite a lot of gold. Might I -- would you -- could I possibly see for myself?"<BR><BR>
As he knew he was soon to be a twenty five thousand gold pieces richer, and he was still a bit punchy from lack of sleep, Mr. Baggledon merely smiled and dropped his breeches to the floor. Mrs. Smethworthy examined his testicles very carefully, under, to the left, to the right. At last, she was satisfied that there was not so much as a down feather anywhere in the region. While she was looking under them one last time, Mr. Baggledon heard a thwacking noise across the office. Young Mr. Smethworthy was banging his head against the stone wall.<BR><BR>
"What in the Lady's name is wrong with your son, Mrs. Smethworthy?" he asked.<BR><BR>
"Nothing, dear," she said. "I merely bet him one hundred thousand gold pieces that by this time I would have the president of the Bank of Daggerfall by the balls."<BR>"""

银行家的赌约<BR>
波伯特·利图姆利 著<BR><BR>

在途歇银行总行，那本是极其平凡的一天。正常的交易在进行：存款被存入，取款被取出，房屋抵押贷款被收取，信用证被兑付成金币。当一位名叫克莱顿·J·威夫林顿的出纳员看到一位小个子老太太拖着她那两个几乎和她一样大的大麻袋朝他走来时，他改变了想法。这终究不会是途歇银行里普普通通的一天了。<BR><BR>
“我想让你把我这些麻袋里的三千万金币存起来，给我开个账户。”小个子老太太用沙哑的声音说道。<BR><BR>
“当然可以，夫人，”威夫林顿急切地说。他数了数麻袋里的金币，发现正好是三千万金币。<BR><BR>
“等一下，小伙子，”小个子老太太轻快地说。“在我开户之前，我想见见我要托付的人。我想和银行行长谈谈。”<BR><BR>
威夫林顿想让行长知道他是经手了那年最大单笔存款的出纳员，所以急切地派人给行长的秘书传话。结果，行长也同样急切地想见见这位富有的女士，所以老太太当天就被带到了他的办公室。<BR><BR>
“很高兴认识您，女士。我是杰兰德·P·巴格登。”行长杰兰德·P·巴格登说道。<BR>
“我的名字，”小个子老太太说，“是佩图瓦·斯穆思沃西。”事实上，这确实是她的真名。“谢谢你见我。我喜欢以更私人的方式办理业务。”<BR><BR>
“我完全理解，”巴格登笑着说。“这是一笔数目可观的金子。冒昧问一下，您是如何得到这笔钱的？”<BR><BR>
“一点也不，”斯穆思沃西夫人说。<BR><BR>
“您是怎么得到它的？”巴格登问道。<BR><BR>
“让你猜猜，”斯穆思沃西夫人回答，带着一丝并不讨喜的少女般的挑逗。<BR><BR>
作为银行家，巴格登的想象力算是非常丰富了。他猜了遗产和长期节俭，但斯穆思沃西夫人害羞地摇了摇头。也许她卖了一座大老宅？不。在套近乎的时刻，巴格登问金币是否来自掠夺或偷窃。斯穆思沃西夫人没有生气，但说不是。最后，他认输了。<BR><BR>
“我是个赌徒，”她说。<BR><BR>
“赌竞技场打斗？”他感兴趣地问。<BR><BR>
“不，不，亲爱的。赌的是别的东西。比如，我愿意赌两万五千金币，明天早上的这个时候，你的睾丸上会沾满羽毛。”<BR><BR>
巴格登先生被老太太的话吓了一跳。她疯了吗？她是女巫吗？他排除了后一种可能，因为他有辨认女巫的直觉。就算她疯了，她也还是个富有的疯女人。而且他正需要两万五千金币。于是他接受了她的赌约。<BR><BR>

第二天，巴格登先生很晚才到银行 -- 就在斯穆思沃西夫人到达前一刻。陪她一起来的是一个瘦削、戴眼镜的家伙，她介绍说是法庭的律师。结果是她儿子。她解释说，涉及钱的事，小斯穆思沃西先生总会陪着他母亲。<BR><BR>
“闲话少说，”她得意地叫道。“我们的赌约，亲爱的？”<BR><BR>
“我亲爱的夫人，我可以告诉您，您的金币在途歇银行会非常安全。我希望您发现您的金币在这里比在您自己手里更安全时，不会感到不安。我的传家宝，可以说，是毫无羽毛的。而您欠我两万五千金币。”<BR><BR>
可怜的斯穆思沃西夫人听到这话，脸沉了下来。“你确定？”<BR><BR>
“非常确定，夫人。”<BR><BR>
“连一根羽毛都没有？”她的声音带着怀疑。巴格登先生能看出来，她觉得他可能在撒谎。<BR><BR>
“恐怕一根也没有，夫人。”<BR><BR>
“并非我不相信你，巴格登先生，但这毕竟是一大笔钱。我能 -- 你愿意 -- 我能否亲眼看看？”<BR><BR>
因为知道自己马上就要多两万五千金币，加上睡眠不足还有点晕乎乎的，巴格登先生只是笑了笑，就把裤子脱到了地上。斯穆思沃西夫人非常仔细地检查了他的睾丸，上下左右都看了。最后，她确信那地方连一根绒毛都没有。当她最后一次低头查看时，巴格登先生听到办公室对面传来一阵“砰砰”声。小斯穆思沃西先生正在用头撞石墙。<BR><BR>
“看在女神份上，你儿子怎么了，斯穆思沃西夫人？”他问道。<BR><BR>
“没事，亲爱的，”她说。“我只是跟他赌了十万金币，说到了这个时候，我能把途歇银行的行长攥在手心里。”<BR>"""

第二天，巴格登先生很晚才到银行 -- 就在斯穆思沃西夫人到达前一刻。陪她一起来的是一个瘦削、戴眼镜的家伙，她介绍说是法庭的律师。结果是她儿子。她解释说，涉及钱的事，小斯穆思沃西先生总会陪着他母亲。<BR><BR>
“闲话少说，”她得意地叫道。“我们的赌约，亲爱的？”<BR><BR>
“我亲爱的夫人，我可以告诉您，您的金币在途歇银行会非常安全。我希望您发现您的金币在这里比在您自己手里更安全时，不会感到不安。我的传家宝，可以说，是毫无羽毛的。而您欠我两万五千金币。”<BR><BR>
可怜的斯穆思沃西夫人听到这话，脸沉了下来。“你确定？”<BR><BR>
“非常确定，夫人。”<BR><BR>
“连一根羽毛都没有？”她的声音带着怀疑。巴格登先生能看出来，她觉得他可能在撒谎。<BR><BR>
“恐怕一根也没有，夫人。”<BR><BR>
“并非我不相信你，巴格登先生，但这毕竟是一大笔钱。我能 -- 你愿意 -- 我能否亲眼看看？”<BR><BR>
因为知道自己马上就要多两万五千金币，加上睡眠不足还有点晕乎乎的，巴格登先生只是笑了笑，就把裤子脱到了地上。斯穆思沃西夫人非常仔细地检查了他的睾丸，上下左右都看了。最后，她确信那地方连一根绒毛都没有。当她最后一次低头查看时，巴格登先生听到办公室对面传来一阵“砰砰”声。小斯穆思沃西先生正在用头撞石墙。<BR><BR>
“看在女神份上，你儿子怎么了，斯穆思沃西夫人？”他问道。<BR><BR>
“没事，亲爱的，”她说。“我只是跟他赌了十万金币，说到了这个时候，我能把途歇银行的行长攥在手心里。”<BR>"""

The Battle of Sancre Tor
桑克雷·托之战

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Battle of Sancre Tor<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
In 2E852, allied Nord and Breton forces crossed the borders into Cyrodiil and occupied the major passes and settlements in the Jerall Mountains. Making their headquarters for the winter at Sancre Tor, the Nord-Breton allies dared King Cuhlecain's new general, Talos, to assault them in their mountain fastnesses.<BR>
<BR>
When they learned that General Talos had mustered an army in the dead of winter and was marching to assault Sancre Tor, they were elated. Sancre Tor was impregnable, its citadel on high cliffs overlooking the lower city, nestled in a high mountain basin with steep, unscalable cliffs in their rear.<BR>
<BR>
The Cyrodilic army was small, poorly trained and outfitted, short on rations, and unprepared for winter campaigning. As their ragged units assembled in the lowlands beneath the citadel, the Nord-Breton allies confidently assumed that their enemy had delivered himself into their trap.<BR>
<BR>
The citadel was not only protected by an unscalable cliff in front and unscalable heights in their rear, but the entrance to the citadel was magically concealed under the appearance of a large mountain lake in the basin beneath the heights. Accordingly, the Nord-Breton allies left on a small force to defend the citadel, descending through lower passages to attack and overwhelm the cold, hungry Cyrodilic forces before them. They expected to defeat, overrun, and annihilate General Talos' army, leaving no one to oppose their springtime descent into the Cyrodilic Heartlands.<BR>
<BR>
Thus did General Talos lure the Nord-Breton allies to their doom.<BR>
<BR>
Leaving a weak force in the lowlands to draw out the defenders, General Talos approached the citadel of Sancre Tor from the rear, descending the supposedly unscalable heights behind the citadel, and sneaking into the supposedly magically concealed entrance to the inner citadel. This remarkable feat is attributed to the agency of a single unnamed traitor, by tradition a Breton turncoat sorcerer, who revealed both the existence of an obscure mountain trail down the heights behind the citadel and the secret of the citadel entrance concealed beneath its illusory lake surface.<BR>
<BR>
While the Cyrodilic army in the lowlands fought a desperate defense against the Nord-Breton sortie, General Talos and his men entered the citadel, swept aside the sparse defense, captured the Nord-Breton nobles and generals, and compelled them to surrender the citadel and their armies. The confused and demoralized Nord captives, already suspicious of the scheming High Rock sorcerer aristocracy and their overreaching dreams of Heartlands conquests, deserted the alliance and swore loyalty to Tiber Septim. The Skyrim generals joined their rank and file in Tiber Septim's army; the High Rock battlemage command was summarily executed and the captive Bretons imprisoned or sold into slavery.<BR>
<BR>
Thus was the concerted allied invasion of Cyrodiil foiled, and General Talos' army swelled by the hardened Nord veteran troops that played so crucial a role in General Talos' succeeding campaigns which consolidated the Colovian and Nibenean into the core of the Cyrodilic Empire, and which resulting in the crowning of General Talos as Emperor Tiber Septim.<BR>
<BR>
Historians marvel at Tiber Septim's tactical daring in assaulting a fortified mountain citadel in the dead of winter against vastly superior numbers. Later Tiber Septim attributed his unwavering resolve against overwhelming obstacles to have been inspired by his divine vision of the Amulet of Kings in the Tomb of Reman III.<BR>
<BR>
The young Talos may indeed have been inspired by his belief that he was fated to recover this ancient sacred symbol of the Covenant and to lead Tamriel to the high civilization of the Third Empire. Nonetheless, this should in no way reduce our admiration for the dash and genius of this defining military triumph against impossible odds.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
桑克雷·托之战<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
第二纪元852年，诺德与布莱顿联军越过边境进入西罗帝尔，占领了杰拉尔山脉的主要隘口和定居点。诺德-布莱顿联军将冬季大本营设在桑克雷·托，向库勒凯恩国王的新将军塔洛斯发出挑衅，让他到他们的山地要塞来进攻。<BR>
<BR>
当他们得知塔洛斯将军竟在隆冬集结军队，正向桑克雷·托进军时，他们欣喜若狂。桑克雷·托固若金汤，其城堡坐落于高耸的悬崖之上，俯瞰着下城，身后是陡峭、无法攀爬的悬崖，位于一个高山盆地之中。<BR>
<BR>
西罗帝尔的军队人数少，训练和装备差，给养不足，且未做好冬季作战的准备。当他们衣衫褴褛的队伍在城堡下方的低地集结时，诺德-布莱顿联军自信地认为敌人已自投罗网。<BR>
<BR>
城堡不仅前方有无法攀爬的悬崖，后方有无法逾越的高地作为屏障，而且城堡的入口还被魔法隐藏在高地下方盆地中一个大型山湖的幻象之下。因此，诺德-布莱顿联军只留下一小支部队防守城堡，主力则通过下层通道下降，攻击并击溃面前寒冷饥饿的西罗帝尔军队。他们期望能击败、冲垮并歼灭塔洛斯将军的军队，这样春天就无人能阻挡他们进军西罗帝尔心脏地带了。<BR>
<BR>
塔洛斯将军就这样引诱诺德-布莱顿联军走向了灭亡。<BR>
<BR>
塔洛斯将军在低地留下一支弱旅吸引守军，自己则从后方接近桑克雷·托城堡，从城堡后方那本应无法攀登的高地降下，并潜入那本应被魔法隐藏的内城入口。这一非凡的壮举归功于一个不知名的叛徒 -- 传统上认为是一名布莱顿叛变巫师 -- 他不仅揭示了城堡后方高地上有一条隐蔽的山间小道，还揭露了隐藏在其幻影湖面之下的城堡入口秘密。<BR>
<BR>
当西罗帝尔军队在低地拼命抵御诺德-布莱顿联军的出击时，塔洛斯将军和他的部下进入了城堡，扫清了稀疏的防御，俘虏了诺德-布莱顿的贵族和将军，迫使他们交出城堡和军队。那些困惑且士气低落的诺德俘虏，本就对诡计多端的高岩巫师贵族及其征服心脏地带的野心心存疑虑，他们抛弃了联盟，宣誓效忠泰伯·塞普汀。天际的将军们与他们的士兵一起加入了泰伯·塞普汀的军队；高岩的战斗法师指挥官被当即处决，被俘的布莱顿人被监禁或卖为奴隶。<BR>
<BR>
就这样，联军对西罗帝尔的协同入侵被挫败了，塔洛斯将军的军队因这些意志坚强的诺德老兵而壮大，他们在塔洛斯将军后来的战役中发挥了关键作用，这些战役将科洛维亚和尼本奈巩固为西罗帝尔帝国的核心，最终促成了塔洛斯将军加冕为皇帝泰伯·塞普汀。<BR>
<BR>
历史学家们对泰伯·塞普汀在隆冬时节，以寡敌众进攻一座设防的山地城堡的战术胆识惊叹不已。后来，泰伯·塞普汀将他面对巨大障碍时坚定不移的决心，归功于他在雷曼三世陵墓中看到的众王护符的神圣幻象。<BR>
<BR>
年轻的塔洛斯或许确实受到他信念的鼓舞，相信自己命中注定要找回这个古老的圣约象征，并带领泰姆瑞尔走向第三帝国的高等文明。尽管如此，这绝不应减少我们对这场在看似不可能的情况下取得的决定性军事胜利的果敢与天才的钦佩。<BR>
<BR>"""

塔洛斯将军就这样引诱诺德-布莱顿联军走向了灭亡。<BR>
<BR>
塔洛斯将军在低地留下一支弱旅吸引守军，自己则从后方接近桑克雷·托城堡，从城堡后方那本应无法攀登的高地降下，并潜入那本应被魔法隐藏的内城入口。这一非凡的壮举归功于一个不知名的叛徒 -- 传统上认为是一名布莱顿叛变巫师 -- 他不仅揭示了城堡后方高地上有一条隐蔽的山间小道，还揭露了隐藏在其幻影湖面之下的城堡入口秘密。<BR>
<BR>
当西罗帝尔军队在低地拼命抵御诺德-布莱顿联军的出击时，塔洛斯将军和他的部下进入了城堡，扫清了稀疏的防御，俘虏了诺德-布莱顿的贵族和将军，迫使他们交出城堡和军队。那些困惑且士气低落的诺德俘虏，本就对诡计多端的高岩巫师贵族及其征服心脏地带的野心心存疑虑，他们抛弃了联盟，宣誓效忠泰伯·塞普汀。天际的将军们与他们的士兵一起加入了泰伯·塞普汀的军队；高岩的战斗法师指挥官被当即处决，被俘的布莱顿人被监禁或卖为奴隶。<BR>
<BR>
就这样，联军对西罗帝尔的协同入侵被挫败了，塔洛斯将军的军队因这些意志坚强的诺德老兵而壮大，他们在塔洛斯将军后来的战役中发挥了关键作用，这些战役将科洛维亚和尼本奈巩固为西罗帝尔帝国的核心，最终促成了塔洛斯将军加冕为皇帝泰伯·塞普汀。<BR>
<BR>
历史学家们对泰伯·塞普汀在隆冬时节，以寡敌众进攻一座设防的山地城堡的战术胆识惊叹不已。后来，泰伯·塞普汀将他面对巨大障碍时坚定不移的决心，归功于他在雷曼三世陵墓中看到的众王护符的神圣幻象。<BR>
<BR>
年轻的塔洛斯或许确实受到他信念的鼓舞，相信自己命中注定要找回这个古老的圣约象征，并带领泰姆瑞尔走向第三帝国的高等文明。尽管如此，这绝不应减少我们对这场在看似不可能的情况下取得的决定性军事胜利的果敢与天才的钦佩。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Before the Ages of Man<BR>

Before the Ages of Man<BR>
<BR> 
Before man came to rule Tamriel, and before the chronicles of the historians recorded the affairs of the rulers of Tamriel, the events of our world are known only through myths and legends, and through the divinely inspired teachings of the Nine Divines.<BR>
<BR> 
For convenience, historians divide the distant ages of prehistory into two broad periods of time -- the Dawn Era, and the Merethic Era.<BR>
<BR> 
* The Dawn Era *<BR>
<BR> 
The Dawn Era is that period before the beginning of mortal time, when the feats of the gods take place. The Dawn Era ends with the exodus of the gods and magic from the World at the founding of the Adamantine Tower.<BR>
<BR> 
The term 'Merethic' comes from the Nordic, literally, "Era of the Elves." The Merethic Era is the prehistoric time after the exodus of the gods and magic from the World at the founding of the Adamantine Tower and before the arrival of Ysgramor the Nord in Tamriel.<BR>
<BR> 
The following are the most notable events of the Dawn Era, presented roughly in sequence as it must be understaoo by creatures of time such as ourselves.<BR>
<BR> 
The Cosmos formed from the Aurbis [chaos, or totality] by Anu and Padomay. Akatosh (Auriel) formed and Time began. The Gods (et'Ada) formed. Lorkhan convinced -- or tricked -- the Gods into creating the mortal plane, Nirn. The mortal plane was at this point highly magical and dangerous. As the Gods walked, the physical make-up of the mortal plane and even the timeless continuity of existence itself became unstable.<BR>
<BR>
When Magic (Magnus), architect of the plans for the mortal world, decided to terminate the project, the Gods convened at the Adamantine Tower [Direnni Tower, the oldest known structure in Tamriel] and decided what to do. Most left when Magic did. Others sacrificed themselves into other forms so that they might Stay (the Ehlnofey). Lorkhan was condemned by the Gods to exile in the mortal realms, and his heart was torn out and cast from the Tower. Where it landed, a Volcano formed. With Magic (in the Mythic Sense) gone, the Cosmos stabilized. Elven history, finally linear, began (ME2500).<BR>
<BR> 
* The Merethic Era *<BR>
<BR> 
The Merethic Era was figured by early Nord scholars as a series of years numbered in reverse order backward from the their 'beginning of time' -- the founding of the Camoran Dynasty, recorded as Year Zero of the First Era. The prehistoric events of the Merethic Era are listed here with their traditional Nordic Merethic dates. The earliest Merethic date cited by King Harald's scholars was ME2500 -- the Nordic reckoning of the first year of time. As such, the Merethic Era extends from ME2500 in the distant past to ME1 -- the year before the founding of the Camoran Dysnasty and the establishment of the White gold Tower as an indepenent city-state.<BR>
<BR> 
According to King Harald's bards, ME2500 was the date of construction of the Adamantine Tower on Balfiera Island in High Rock, the oldest known structure of Tamriel. (This corresponds roughly to the earliest historical dates given in various unpublished Elvish chronicles.)<BR>
<BR> 
During the early Merethic Era, the aboriginal beastpeoples of Tamriel -- the ancestors of the Khajiit, Argonian, Orcish, and other beastfolk -- lived in preliterate communities throughout Tamriel.<BR>
<BR> 
In the Middle Merethic Era, the Aldmeri (mortals of Elven origin) refugees left their doomed and now-lost continent of Aldmeris (also known as 'Old Ehlnofey') and settled in southwestern Tamriel. The first colonies were distributed at wide intervals on islands along the entire coast of Tamriel. Later inland settlements were founded primarily in fertile lowlands in southwest and central Tamriel. Wherever the beastfolk encountered the Elves, the sophisticated, literate, technologically advanced Aldmeri cultures displaced the primitive beastfolk into the jungles, marshes, mountains, and wastelands. The Adamantine Tower was rediscovered and captured by the Direnni, a prominent and powerful Aldmeri clan. The Crystal Tower was built on Summerset Isle and, later, White Gold Tower in Cyrodiil.<BR>
<BR> 
During the Middle Merethic Era, Aldmeri explorers mapped the coasts of Vvardenfel, building the First Era High Elven wizard towers at Ald Redaynia, Bal Fell, Tel Aruhn, and Tel Mora in Morrowind. It was also during this period that Ayleid [Wild Elven] settlements flourished in the jungles surrounding White Gold Tower (present day Cyrodiil). Wild Elves, also known as the Heartland High Elves, preserved the Dawn Era magics and language of the Ehlnofey. Ostensibly a tribute-land to the High King of Alinor, the Heartland's long lines of communication from the Summerset Isles' sovereignty effectively isolated Cyrodill from the High Kings at Crystal Tower.<BR>
<BR> 
The Late Middle Merethic Era is the period of the High Velothi Culture. The Chimer, ancestors of the modern Dunmer, or Dark Elves, were dynamic, ambitious, long-lived Elven clans devoted to fundamentalist ancestor worship. The Chimer clans followed the Prophet Veloth out of the ancestral Elven homelands in the southwest to settle in the lands now known as Morrowind. Despising the secular culture and profane practices of the Dwemer, the Chimer also coveted the lands and resources of the Dwemer, and for centuries provoked them with minor raids and territorial disputes. The Dwemer (Dwarves), free-thinking, reclusive Elven clans devoted to the secrets of science, engineering, and alchemy, established underground cities and communities in the mountain range (later the Velothi Mountains) separating modern Skyrim and Morrowind.<BR>
<BR> 
The Late Merethic Era marks the precipitous decline of Velothi culture. Some Velothi settled in villages near declining and abandoned ancient Velothi towers. During this period, Velothi high culture disappeared on Vvardenfell Island. The earliest Dwemer Freehold colonies date from this period. Degenerate Velothi devolved into tribal cultures which, in time, evolved into the modern Great Houses of Morrowind, or persisted as the barbarian Ashlander tribes. The only surviving traces of this tribal culture are scattered Velothi towers and Ashlander nomads on Vvardenfell Island. The original First Era High Elven wizard towers along the coasts of Tamriel were also abandoned about this time.<BR>
<BR> 
It was in the Late Merethic Era that the pre-literate humans, the so-called "Nedic Peoples", from the continent of Atmora (also 'Altmora' or 'the Elder Wood' in Aldmeris) migrated and settleed in northern Tamriel. The Nord culture hero Ysgramor, leader of a great colonizing fleet to Tamriel, is credited with developing a runic transcription of Nord speech based on Elvish principles, and so Ysgramor is considered the first human historian. Ysgramor's fleet landed at Hsaarik Head at the extreme northern tip of Skyrim's Broken Cape. The Nords built there the legendary city of Saarthal. The Elves drove the Men away during the Night of Tears, but Ysgramor soon returned with his Five Hundred Companions.<BR>
<BR> 
Also during the Late Merethic Era the legendary immortal hero, warrior, sorceror, and king variously known as Pelinal Whitestrake, Harrald Hairy Breeks, Ysmir, Hans the Fox, etc., wandered Tamriel, gathering armies, conquering lands, ruling, then abandoning his kingdoms to wander again.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
人类纪元之前<BR>
微光的艾坎塔 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
年表系列<BR>
<BR>
第一卷
人类纪元之前<BR>
<BR>
在人类统治泰姆瑞尔之前，在历史学家的编年史记录泰姆瑞尔统治者的事迹之前，我们世界的事件仅通过神话、传说以及九圣灵的神圣启示教义为人所知。<BR>
<BR>
为方便起见，历史学家将遥远的史前时代划分为两大时期 -- 黎明纪元与精灵纪元。<BR>
<BR>
* 黎明纪元 *<BR>
<BR>
黎明纪元是凡人时间开始之前的时期，那时众神的功绩正在发生。黎明纪元以众神与魔法在精金塔建立时离开世界而告终。<BR>
<BR>
“Merethic”一词源于诺德语，字面意思是“精灵纪元”。精灵纪元是众神与魔法在精金塔建立时离开世界之后，到诺德人伊斯格拉谟抵达泰姆瑞尔之前的史前时期。<BR>
<BR>
以下是黎明纪元最值得注意的事件，大致按时间顺序排列，如同我们这类时间生物所必须理解的那样。<BR>
<BR>
宇宙由阿努和帕多梅从奥比斯[混沌，或全体]中形成。阿卡托什（奥瑞埃尔）形成，时间开始。众神（原灵）形成。洛克汗说服 -- 或欺骗 -- 众神创造了凡间位面，奈恩。此时的凡间位面充满魔法且极度危险。随着众神的行走，凡间位面的物理构成，甚至存在本身的永恒连续性都变得不稳定。<BR>
<BR>
当魔法（玛格努斯），凡世计划的建筑师，决定终止这个项目时，众神在精金塔[迪仁尼塔，泰姆瑞尔已知最古老的建筑]集会，决定对策。大多数随魔法一起离开了。另一些则牺牲自己，转化为其他形态以便留下（艾诺菲）。洛克汗被众神放逐到凡间领域，他的心脏被挖出，从塔中扔了出去。它坠落之处，形成了一座火山。随着魔法（神话意义上的）消失，宇宙稳定下来。精灵的历史，终于开始线性发展（ME2500）。<BR>
<BR>
* 精灵纪元 *<BR>
<BR>
早期诺德学者将精灵纪元计为一连串年份，从其“时间的开端” -- 卡莫兰王朝的建立（被记录为第一纪元零年） -- 开始向前倒推编号。精灵纪元的史前事件在此以其传统的诺德精灵纪元日期列出。哈拉尔德国王的学者引用的最早精灵纪元日期是ME2500 -- 诺德人计算的时间元年。因此，精灵纪元从遥远的过去ME2500延伸到ME1 -- 卡莫兰王朝建立和白金塔成为一个独立城邦的前一年。<BR>
<BR>
根据哈拉尔德国王的吟游诗人记载，ME2500年是高岩巴尔菲拉岛上精金塔的建造日期，这是泰姆瑞尔已知最古老的建筑。（这大致与各种未发表的精灵编年史中给出的最早历史日期相符。）<BR>
<BR>
在精灵纪元早期，泰姆瑞尔的土著兽族 -- 卡吉特、阿尔贡、兽人及其他兽族的祖先 -- 以无文字社群的形式遍布泰姆瑞尔各地。<BR>
<BR>
在精灵纪元中期，奥德莫（精灵族裔的凡人）难民离开了他们注定毁灭且现已失落的奥德莫瑞斯大陆（也称为“古艾诺菲”），定居在泰姆瑞尔西南部。第一批殖民地在泰姆瑞尔整个海岸线的岛屿上广泛分布。后来的内陆定居点主要建立在泰姆瑞尔西南部和中部肥沃的低地。无论兽族在哪里遇到精灵，那些复杂、有文化、技术先进的奥德莫文化都会将原始的兽族驱赶进丛林、沼泽、山脉和荒地。精金塔被迪仁尼家族 -- 一个显赫而强大的奥德莫氏族 -- 重新发现并占据。水晶塔在夏暮岛建成，随后白金塔在西罗帝尔建成。<BR>
<BR>
在精灵纪元中期，奥德莫探险家绘制了瓦登费尔的海岸线图，在晨风的奥德·雷戴尼亚、巴尔·费尔、泰尔·阿汝因和泰尔·莫拉建造了第一纪元的高精灵巫师塔。也正是在这一时期，亚历德[野精灵]定居点在白金塔（今西罗帝尔）周围的丛林中繁荣起来。野精灵，也称为心脏地高精灵，保留了黎明纪元的魔法和艾诺菲的语言。表面上他们是阿里诺尔至高王的纳贡之地，但从夏暮群岛主权延伸而来的漫长通讯线，实际上将西罗帝尔与水晶塔的至高王们隔离开来。<BR>
<BR>
精灵纪元中后期是高等维洛提文化时期。歧莫，现代丹莫（即暗精灵）的祖先，是充满活力、雄心勃勃、长寿的精灵氏族，致力于原教旨的祖先崇拜。歧莫氏族跟随先知维洛斯离开西南部的精灵祖地，定居在现今称为晨风的土地上。他们鄙视锻莫的世俗文化和渎神行为，同时也觊觎锻莫的土地和资源，并数个世纪以来以零星的袭击和领土争端挑衅锻莫。锻莫（矮人），是自由思想、隐居的精灵氏族，致力于科学、工程和炼金术的秘密，他们在分隔现代天际和晨风的山脉（后称维洛提山脉）中建立了地下城市和社区。<BR>
<BR>
精灵纪元晚期标志着维洛提文化的急剧衰落。一些维洛提人在衰落和废弃的古代维洛提塔楼附近的村庄定居。在此期间，维洛提高等文化在瓦登费尔岛消失了。最早的锻莫自由民殖民地也始于这一时期。堕落的维洛提人退化为部落文化，这些部落最终演变为现代晨风的大豪族，或作为野蛮的灰烬之民部落存续。这种部落文化仅存的痕迹是瓦登费尔岛上零散的维洛提塔楼和灰烬之民游牧民族。泰姆瑞尔海岸沿线最初的第一纪元高精灵巫师塔也大约在这个时候被废弃。<BR>
<BR>
正是在精灵纪元晚期，来自阿特莫拉大陆（在奥德莫瑞语中也称“奥特莫拉”或“上古之木”）的、尚无文字的人类，即所谓的“尼德民族”，迁徙并定居在泰姆瑞尔北部。诺德文化英雄伊斯格拉谟，一支庞大殖民舰队的领袖，被认为基于精灵语的原则发展出了诺德语言的如尼字母转录法，因此伊斯格拉谟被视为第一位人类历史学家。伊斯格拉谟的舰队在天际破碎角最北端的萨里克角登陆。诺德人在那里建立了传说中的萨塔尔城。在“泪之夜”期间，精灵驱赶了人类，但伊斯格拉谟很快带着他的五百战友团回来了。<BR>
<BR>
同样是在精灵纪元晚期，那位传说中的不朽英雄、战士、巫师和国王 -- 以佩林纳尔·白芒、哈拉尔德·毛裤、伊斯米尔、汉斯·狐等多种名号为人所知 -- 游历泰姆瑞尔，聚集军队，征服土地，进行统治，然后抛弃他的王国，再次踏上漫游之旅。<BR>

The Adamantine Tower was rediscovered and captured by the Direnni, a prominent and powerful Aldmeri clan. The Crystal Tower was built on Summerset Isle and, later, White Gold Tower in Cyrodiil.<BR>
<BR> 
During the Middle Merethic Era, Aldmeri explorers mapped the coasts of Vvardenfel, building the First Era High Elven wizard towers at Ald Redaynia, Bal Fell, Tel Aruhn, and Tel Mora in Morrowind. It was also during this period that Ayleid [Wild Elven] settlements flourished in the jungles surrounding White Gold Tower (present day Cyrodiil). Wild Elves, also known as the Heartland High Elves, preserved the Dawn Era magics and language of the Ehlnofey. Ostensibly a tribute-land to the High King of Alinor, the Heartland's long lines of communication from the Summerset Isles' sovereignty effectively isolated Cyrodill from the High Kings at Crystal Tower.<BR>
<BR> 
The Late Middle Merethic Era is the period of the High Velothi Culture. The Chimer, ancestors of the modern Dunmer, or Dark Elves, were dynamic, ambitious, long-lived Elven clans devoted to fundamentalist ancestor worship. The Chimer clans followed the Prophet Veloth out of the ancestral Elven homelands in the southwest to settle in the lands now known as Morrowind. Despising the secular culture and profane practices of the Dwemer, the Chimer also coveted the lands and resources of the Dwemer, and for centuries provoked them with minor raids and territorial disputes. The Dwemer (Dwarves), free-thinking, reclusive Elven clans devoted to the secrets of science, engineering, and alchemy, established underground cities and communities in the mountain range (later the Velothi Mountains) separating modern Skyrim and Morrowind.<BR>
<BR> 
The Late Merethic Era marks the precipitous decline of Velothi culture. Some Velothi settled in villages near declining and abandoned ancient Velothi towers. During this period, Velothi high culture disappeared on Vvardenfell Island. The earliest Dwemer Freehold colonies date from this period. Degenerate Velothi devolved into tribal cultures which, in time, evolved into the modern Great Houses of Morrowind, or persisted as the barbarian Ashlander tribes. The only surviving traces of this tribal culture are scattered Velothi towers and Ashlander nomads on Vvardenfell Island. The original First Era High Elven wizard towers along the coasts of Tamriel were also abandoned about this time.<BR>
<BR> 
It was in the Late Merethic Era that the pre-literate humans, the so-called "Nedic Peoples", from the continent of Atmora (also 'Altmora' or 'the Elder Wood' in Aldmeris) migrated and settleed in northern Tamriel. The Nord culture hero Ysgramor, leader of a great colonizing fleet to Tamriel, is credited with developing a runic transcription of Nord speech based on Elvish principles, and so Ysgramor is considered the first human historian. Ysgramor's fleet landed at Hsaarik Head at the extreme northern tip of Skyrim's Broken Cape. The Nords built there the legendary city of Saarthal. The Elves drove the Men away during the Night of Tears, but Ysgramor soon returned with his Five Hundred Companions.<BR>
<BR> 
Also during the Late Merethic Era the legendary immortal hero, warrior, sorceror, and king variously known as Pelinal Whitestrake, Harrald Hairy Breeks, Ysmir, Hans the Fox, etc., wandered Tamriel, gathering armies, conquering lands, ruling, then abandoning his kingdoms to wander again.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
人类纪元之前<BR>
微光的艾坎塔 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
年表系列<BR>
<BR>
第一卷
人类纪元之前<BR>
<BR>
在人类统治泰姆瑞尔之前，在历史学家的编年史记录泰姆瑞尔统治者的事迹之前，我们世界的事件仅通过神话、传说以及九圣灵的神圣启示教义为人所知。<BR>
<BR>
为方便起见，历史学家将遥远的史前时代划分为两大时期 -- 黎明纪元与精灵纪元。<BR>
<BR>
* 黎明纪元 *<BR>
<BR>
黎明纪元是凡人时间开始之前的时期，那时众神的功绩正在发生。黎明纪元以众神与魔法在精金塔建立时离开世界而告终。<BR>
<BR>
“Merethic”一词源于诺德语，字面意思是“精灵纪元”。精灵纪元是众神与魔法在精金塔建立时离开世界之后，到诺德人伊斯格拉谟抵达泰姆瑞尔之前的史前时期。<BR>
<BR>
以下是黎明纪元最值得注意的事件，大致按时间顺序排列，如同我们这类时间生物所必须理解的那样。<BR>
<BR>
宇宙由阿努和帕多梅从奥比斯[混沌，或全体]中形成。阿卡托什（奥瑞埃尔）形成，时间开始。众神（原灵）形成。洛克汗说服 -- 或欺骗 -- 众神创造了凡间位面，奈恩。此时的凡间位面充满魔法且极度危险。随着众神的行走，凡间位面的物理构成，甚至存在本身的永恒连续性都变得不稳定。<BR>
<BR>
当魔法（玛格努斯），凡世计划的建筑师，决定终止这个项目时，众神在精金塔[迪仁尼塔，泰姆瑞尔已知最古老的建筑]集会，决定对策。大多数随魔法一起离开了。另一些则牺牲自己，转化为其他形态以便留下（艾诺菲）。洛克汗被众神放逐到凡间领域，他的心脏被挖出，从塔中扔了出去。它坠落之处，形成了一座火山。随着魔法（神话意义上的）消失，宇宙稳定下来。精灵的历史，终于开始线性发展（ME2500）。<BR>
<BR>
* 精灵纪元 *<BR>
<BR>
早期诺德学者将精灵纪元计为一连串年份，从其“时间的开端” -- 卡莫兰王朝的建立（被记录为第一纪元零年） -- 开始向前倒推编号。精灵纪元的史前事件在此以其传统的诺德精灵纪元日期列出。哈拉尔德国王的学者引用的最早精灵纪元日期是ME2500 -- 诺德人计算的时间元年。因此，精灵纪元从遥远的过去ME2500延伸到ME1 -- 卡莫兰王朝建立和白金塔成为一个独立城邦的前一年。<BR>
<BR>
根据哈拉尔德国王的吟游诗人记载，ME2500年是高岩巴尔菲拉岛上精金塔的建造日期，这是泰姆瑞尔已知最古老的建筑。（这大致与各种未发表的精灵编年史中给出的最早历史日期相符。）<BR>
<BR>
在精灵纪元早期，泰姆瑞尔的土著兽族 -- 卡吉特、阿尔贡、兽人及其他兽族的祖先 -- 以无文字社群的形式遍布泰姆瑞尔各地。<BR>
<BR>
在精灵纪元中期，奥德莫（精灵族裔的凡人）难民离开了他们注定毁灭且现已失落的奥德莫瑞斯大陆（也称为“古艾诺菲”），定居在泰姆瑞尔西南部。第一批殖民地在泰姆瑞尔整个海岸线的岛屿上广泛分布。后来的内陆定居点主要建立在泰姆瑞尔西南部和中部肥沃的低地。无论兽族在哪里遇到精灵，那些复杂、有文化、技术先进的奥德莫文化都会将原始的兽族驱赶进丛林、沼泽、山脉和荒地。精金塔被迪仁尼家族 -- 一个显赫而强大的奥德莫氏族 -- 重新发现并占据。水晶塔在夏暮岛建成，随后白金塔在西罗帝尔建成。<BR>
<BR>
在精灵纪元中期，奥德莫探险家绘制了瓦登费尔的海岸线图，在晨风的奥德·雷戴尼亚、巴尔·费尔、泰尔·阿汝因和泰尔·莫拉建造了第一纪元的高精灵巫师塔。也正是在这一时期，亚历德[野精灵]定居点在白金塔（今西罗帝尔）周围的丛林中繁荣起来。野精灵，也称为心脏地高精灵，保留了黎明纪元的魔法和艾诺菲的语言。表面上他们是阿里诺尔至高王的纳贡之地，但从夏暮群岛主权延伸而来的漫长通讯线，实际上将西罗帝尔与水晶塔的至高王们隔离开来。<BR>
<BR>
精灵纪元中后期是高等维洛提文化时期。歧莫，现代丹莫（即暗精灵）的祖先，是充满活力、雄心勃勃、长寿的精灵氏族，致力于原教旨的祖先崇拜。歧莫氏族跟随先知维洛斯离开西南部的精灵祖地，定居在现今称为晨风的土地上。他们鄙视锻莫的世俗文化和渎神行为，同时也觊觎锻莫的土地和资源，并数个世纪以来以零星的袭击和领土争端挑衅锻莫。锻莫（矮人），是自由思想、隐居的精灵氏族，致力于科学、工程和炼金术的秘密，他们在分隔现代天际和晨风的山脉（后称维洛提山脉）中建立了地下城市和社区。<BR>
<BR>
精灵纪元晚期标志着维洛提文化的急剧衰落。一些维洛提人在衰落和废弃的古代维洛提塔楼附近的村庄定居。在此期间，维洛提高等文化在瓦登费尔岛消失了。最早的锻莫自由民殖民地也始于这一时期。堕落的维洛提人退化为部落文化，这些部落最终演变为现代晨风的大豪族，或作为野蛮的灰烬之民部落存续。这种部落文化仅存的痕迹是瓦登费尔岛上零散的维洛提塔楼和灰烬之民游牧民族。泰姆瑞尔海岸沿线最初的第一纪元高精灵巫师塔也大约在这个时候被废弃。<BR>
<BR>
正是在精灵纪元晚期，来自阿特莫拉大陆（在奥德莫瑞语中也称“奥特莫拉”或“上古之木”）的、尚无文字的人类，即所谓的“尼德民族”，迁徙并定居在泰姆瑞尔北部。诺德文化英雄伊斯格拉谟，一支庞大殖民舰队的领袖，被认为基于精灵语的原则发展出了诺德语言的如尼字母转录法，因此伊斯格拉谟被视为第一位人类历史学家。伊斯格拉谟的舰队在天际破碎角最北端的萨里克角登陆。诺德人在那里建立了传说中的萨塔尔城。在“泪之夜”期间，精灵驱赶了人类，但伊斯格拉谟很快带着他的五百战友团回来了。<BR>
<BR>
同样是在精灵纪元晚期，那位传说中的不朽英雄、战士、巫师和国王 -- 以佩林纳尔·白芒、哈拉尔德·毛裤、伊斯米尔、汉斯·狐等多种名号为人所知 -- 游历泰姆瑞尔，聚集军队，征服土地，进行统治，然后抛弃他的王国，再次踏上漫游之旅。<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
$0ADuring the first months of the Man-Bull's reign, there was peace and happiness throughout his empire. But as time went by, the people grew uneasy, and began to stir and mutter amongst themselves. They said to each other, "King Belharza is a fine warrior, but this arrangement of his is unnatural. The gods in their wisdom did not see fit to shape man for rule; see how he grows restless at peace, and even now stands atop his palace each morning rattling his spear in the direction of Alinor. We cannot allow this man to undo the good works of blessed Al-Esh: Belharza must be wed!" And they went to the King with their worries, but Belharza just laughed and said to them, "Put your minds at rest, my friends. I have already joined myself in marriage to a wife, and she is the Empire of Cyrodiil." And he would hear no more from them, for he knew that to marry would be to forfeit his hold on the Amulet of Kings and the Ruby Throne.<BR>$0A$0AHis vassals were not so easily dissuaded, though. Throughout his reign, Belharza endured pressure from all quarters to find a wife and restore the natural order of things. The wise women of the jungle tribes would visit on occasion with grim portents, warning of doom for himself and his kingdom. The warlords of the west told him that honor could only be found on the battlefield -- there was no glory to be won sitting on a throne. His minotaurs remained silent, for their loyalty was to the Man-Bull alone and they cared little for the bleating of the no-horns of his court.<BR>$0A$0AThough he would occasionally attempt to placate his counselors by feasting the daughters of jarls and silklords, sending them home with gold and land and titles, Belharza's energies were largely spent on the administration of his kingdom. Bringing the new Colovian city-states into his empire, both through diplomacy, which the Westerners spat at, and warfare, which they could respect and honor. Treating with his Ayleid vassals, and relieving the tensions of their new lives side by side with former slaves. Most importantly, fending off the carrion birds already flocking at his borders. He knew, though his subjects may not, that the position of Cyrodiil in the Starry-Heart was a precarious one, with the elves of the west crying for blood at the diaspora of their heartland cousins, and the men of the north positioning themselves for conquest, should he prove an easy quarry. Many a night was spent locked in his bedchambers with the young battlemage Hathna, the king's closest friend and advisor, poring over maps and treaties. Oft would they both emerge from his quarters in the light of dawn, glistening with sweat and clothing disheveled from the passion of their arguments. The two men became inseparable - and rumors soon abounded about the handsome, raven-haired tribesman of the Niben whom the king depended upon so. His people smiled at these rumors, though, and said wonderingly to one another, "Surely two kings must be equal to a queen. See how Cyrod has prospered these past years?"<BR>"""

When news of the murder reached the palace, Belharza grew wroth, and in his fury gored a trio of ministers and had a score of visiting diplomats put to the sword before a score of his minotaurs could restrain him. By day's end, three offers of submission and a dozen declarations of war had been laid at his feet. It would be years before his kingdom would recover from this blow, but the Man-Bull himself never would.<BR>$0A$0AIn the years that followed, the king's brooding seemed to infect the very air of the Imperial Palace, filling his councilors with unease and misery as storm clouds gathered around the spire of White-Gold.
