Any talk of fellowship with the Ayleids was silenced, and their ambassadors and diplomats who were not executed outright on suspicion of treason were quietly exiled to their homes outside the city. The Emperor's loathing for the devils that had brought down his most trusted advisor seemed to be the only thing that still animated his corpse -- pale and wan, he resembled more a draugr of the northlands, drained of all blood and vitality, than the gleaming warrior who had first strode under the Dragon Gate all those years ago. Taxes went uncollected, treaties were left unsigned, and the jungle took back the roads that had so carefully been carved through it, veins to the beating heart of the Imperial City. The Empire so carefully won by Alessia was dying, and none could see a way to save it.<BR>$0A$0AThings progressed in this way for some time, until one day, word reached the king's ears of a young seer who was gaining popularity amongst the lower classes, a beastman who claimed insight from divine Alessia herself, and spoke with fire in his tone at the treachery and low cunning of the mer. This was enough to rouse Belharza from his stupor, and on the 9th of Second Seed, he granted an audience to the strange, solemn prophet to hear his message. On and on he spoke in this fashion, until the moons rose and fell and the sun broke over the horizon. When the ape's sermon had concluded, a resounding silence filled the hall. For a long time, Belharza said nothing, but stared at the Imga with a strange, unfamiliar look on his face. Let the most righteous, most just, most pure among you step forward into the light of the One, that you may be weighed by His most faithful servants. """<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>卷五：造神者贝尔哈扎<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>

因他们关系亲密，许多人期望在没有子嗣的情况下，贝尔哈扎会指定哈斯纳为王位继承人。如果这确实是那头人牛的想法，遗憾的是，事情永远没有成为现实。在贝尔哈扎统治的第三十三年，哈斯纳在前往新兴的安维尔王国执行外交任务时，遭到精灵恶魔的伏击，被他们的巫术击倒。当谋杀的消息传到宫殿时，贝尔哈扎暴怒，在狂怒中用角顶死了三名大臣，并在二十名牛头人制止他之前，下令将二十名来访的外交官斩杀。到一天结束时，三份投降书和十几份宣战书被放在他脚下。他的王国需要数年才能从这次打击中恢复，但人牛本人却永远无法恢复。<BR>

在接下来的几年里，国王的阴郁似乎感染了皇宫的空气，让他的顾问们充满了不安和痛苦，如同风暴云聚集在白金塔的尖顶周围。贝尔哈扎的激情和从容自信已被阴郁的面容和易怒的性情所取代，宫殿的仆人们私下议论，皇帝触手可及之处总少不了科洛维亚红酒的酒壶或安奎那月亮糖的托盘。任何与亚历德人交好的言论都被压制，他们的使节和外交官，如果不是因涉嫌叛国被直接处决，就被悄悄流放到城外的家中。皇帝对杀死他最信任顾问的恶魔的憎恨，似乎是唯一还能让他这具躯壳保持活力的东西 -- 他苍白而憔悴，与其说像当年昂首阔步走过龙门的闪亮战士，不如说更像北方地区的尸鬼，被抽干了所有血液和活力。税收无人征收，条约无人签署，丛林重新占领了那些曾精心开辟的道路 -- 那些通往帝都跳动心脏的血管。阿莱西亚如此小心赢得的帝国正在死亡，没有人能看到拯救它的方法。<BR>

事情就这样发展了一段时间，直到有一天，一个年轻先知的传闻传到了国王的耳中，他在下层阶级中越来越受欢迎。那是一个兽人，声称得到了神圣阿莱西亚本人的启示，并用激昂的语调谈论着精灵的背叛和卑鄙。这足以将贝尔哈扎从麻木中唤醒，在次种月9日，他接见了这个奇怪而庄严的先知，聆听他的信息。那一天，即使是牛头人也忍不住对着这个跪在红钻王座前、结结巴巴地说着奇怪话语的矮小多毛生物嗤之以鼻，抖动犄角，但当他说话时，皇帝眼中久已遗忘的火花似乎在闪烁。这位自称马鲁克的先知整夜布道，滔滔不绝地讲述着一个无法言喻、异质的神祇，人类通过崇拜他们的神兽和守护灵在不知不觉中崇拜着祂，而那些精灵，在其金色美丽之下扭曲而怪异，最鄙视祂。他就这样不停地讲着，直到月亮升起又落下，太阳从地平线上升起。当猿人的布道结束时，大厅里一片寂静。很长一段时间，贝尔哈扎一言不发，只是盯着那因加，脸上带着一种奇异而陌生的表情。最后，人牛举起右手，向他身边招了招手，指向哈斯纳多年前站过的、此后便一直空着的位置。<BR>

同一天早晨，当太阳环绕白金塔顶时，皇帝出现在他的阳台上，身旁是先知和他的八名追随者，他这样说道：<BR>

“这些年来，我听到了你们的骚动。你们认为我是个傻瓜，不配坐上这王位和统治这帝国。你们撕扯衣物，咬牙切齿，诅咒自己将西罗帝尔托付给我这样的人。好吧，或许你们是对的。<BR>

“马鲁哈特派蒙福！至一的荣耀与尊崇！<BR>

“塔姆！拉！”<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">The House of the Big Walker<BR>
<BR>
As Told by Dro'Zhani, Carrier of the Mane, to Rodala of the Horse-Men, Circa 3E 30<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">This story, found as a palimpsest in a book of Alessian morality plays, is just one of many remarkably fascinating books, scrolls, and letters in the collection of the Lady Pasipha of Wayrest. The context of the story and family tradition suggest that it was written by one "Rodala of the Horse-Men," an ancestor of the Lady Pasipha from her mother's side. Unfortunately, Rodala translated the story from Ta'agra and into the eastern dialect of Bretonic at the time, and he was not fully literate in either language. I have done what I can to restore the original meaning and cadence.<BR>
<BR>
Your Humble Translator,<BR>
Cassolar Drabo<BR>
<BR>
*****<BR>
<BR>
Dro'Zhani tells the horse-man about the House of the Big Walker.<BR>
<BR>
When First Mane was born, Snake-Men came from the rainy lands. Khajiit greeted them as the sun greets the dunes, for Khajiit knew the Snake-Men fought with the Seizing Men. Khajiit feared the Seizing Men, for clan mothers saw far, when the tribes are scattered like sand and all Khajiit are poor slaves. So Khajiit gave Snake-Men sugar and meat. Khajiit gave Snake-Men sand and sky. The Snake-Men gave blood and breath and dust.<BR>
<BR>
The moons rose and fell. The jungle was not too wet and the dunes were not too hot. Khajiit taught the Snake-Men the Way of the Sand, the Way of the Jungle, the Way of the Claw, and the Way of Face-Paint. Snake-Men taught Khajiit the Way of the Sword and the Way of Assembly. And Khajiit paid neither heed nor gold to the Seizing Men.<BR>
<BR>
When the Seizing Men came, some Khajiit fought beside the Snake-Men to honor the gifts. Some thought the Snake-Men brought the Seizing Men and did not fight. The Seizing Men came to Drake Road, to Hugging River, to Elf Spire, to Stoop Low. Khajiit fought each other with words more than they fought the Seizing Men with claws. The Mane was a child and the tribes slipped between his small claws. So the Seizing Men stole the sands and the skies.<BR>
<BR>
The Seizing Men learned the Way of Sugar and taught Khajiit the Way of the Whip. Then the Seizing Men made Khajiit build a House. Every day the House grew taller and fatter. And every day Khajiit asked, "Who will live in this House?" The Seizing Men would not say.<BR>
<BR>
Dro'Zhani tells you these things for Dro'Zhani fought at Drake Road and lost his claws at Stoop Low and Dro'Zhani made many stones for the House. Yes, the stones were not stones. The Seizing Men made glow-stones out of dirt and fire and ash and salt. Dro'Zhani did not like these liar-stones, but Dro'Zhani feared the whip and the sugar.<BR>
<BR>
One day when the House was taller than all the dunes and trees stacked upon each other, a chieftain of the Seizing Men came to the tall, fat House. Dro'Zhani heard the chieftain's words, heard that House was for Big Walker. Dro'Zhani knew all the names of Big Walker, for Dro'Zhani played many songs before Stoop Low, when Dro'Zhani could count two more.<BR>
<BR>
When the House was done, carts came from the rainy lands, carrying pieces of Big Walker. The Seizing Men tried to wake Big Walker. The Seizing Men cast many spells, spoke many prayers, shook Big Walker's head and shouted at his feet. The sands became like water. The moons hid. Many clan mothers saw things that were not to be. Many Snake-Men grew sick.<BR>
<BR>
The One Who Counts knew every tear, every sweat, of the workers, and he could not count for fear of drowning.<BR>
<BR>
So Alkosh clawed at the House and stomped on the House and breathed fire upon the House, but Big Walker was asleep in his House and the House did not fall. And Alkosh could not enter the House.<BR>
<BR>
So Alkosh made a child, Dalk Ra'Wal. This child grew strong and sneaky in the side place. Ra'Wal snuck between the cracks of liar-stone, but could not find his way to Big Walker. Ra'Wal sang the crumbling songs, and stones from the faraway mountains turned to sand, but the liar-stones only respond to lies. Ra'Wal took the Seizing Men's own tools and chipped at the stones slowly, singing all the while, but he did not live long enough, even in the side place, to carve the way. Big Walker was deaf in his House, and the House did not turn back to sand. And Alkosh could not enter the House.<BR>
<BR>
So Alkosh unwound years that did not count. And Alkosh ate Alkosh, making an emptiness that could be filled only by a birth under the right moons. The blessed by birth walked with dragon toes, spoke with a dragon tongue, and wore the scales about his shoulders. But the sly one tricked Alkosh and used the years that did not count to make a new body. The Dragon-in-Flesh was not a Khajiit, but a Seizing Man who looked too long in the pool of the sly one.<BR>
<BR>
So the Dragon-in-Flesh betrayed himself. Soon another cart came and inside was the heart of the buried one, the reflection of the Moons in the boiling sea. The Dragon-in-Flesh could enter the House of the Big Walker. When the heart beat in Big Walker, he was not at home in his House.<BR>
<BR>
So Big Walker picked up his House and Walked. The House of the Big Walker no longer overlooked the sea. There was big trouble in Ne Quin-al and the Home of Thorns and the Ten Marshes and everywhere Big Walker went.<BR>
<BR>
The Dragon-in-Flesh led Big Walker across the sea and there the House went also, but He was not at home in his House. The Snake-Men who stayed were full of sorry and became the Rim-Men. They lost their tail-sense and could not tell friend from foe, so they fought all the Khajiit as if we all betrayed them.<BR>
<BR>
Alkosh tired of Big Walker making him lose count. So Alkosh captured the north wind in a bottle that was the same inside and out. And Alkosh froze the stars and swept them into a dustpan. And Alkosh set the Cat's Eye ablaze and trapped its shadows in a well. And Alkosh sucked the sea into his chest. And Alkosh made a gift of all to a Tooth Man who used them to speak a single word that blew Big Walker apart.<BR>
<BR>
And the House was blown all the way back to the dawn where it became a home for the Dragon Who Refuses to Count. And the House was blown back again and again until it was ten claws of ten claws older than the moons and stars. And all this time the House remembered the songs of Dalk Ra'Wal in the side place. Every rain, every wind, a handful of the House becomes sand. The House fell to Ne Quin-al in the years of many storms and parts of Big Walker fell all over.<BR>
<BR>
But the House is always here and there and who knows how old it is any now. Half the dunes are the House, whether liar-stones or song-dust. The House remembers Big Walker and sometimes walks about on its own. So even though the House of Big Walker is taller than all the trees stacked upon each other, the House is as hard to find as one grain of sand.<BR>

由鬃首使者卓'扎尼讲述给马民罗达拉，约第三纪元30年<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">这个故事是在一本阿莱西亚道德剧中发现的，作为重写本的一部分，它只是途歇的帕西法女士收藏中众多引人入胜的书籍、卷轴和信件之一。故事的背景和家族传统表明，它是由“马民罗达拉”所写，他是帕西法女士母系的祖先。不幸的是，罗达拉当时将故事从塔'格拉语翻译成了布莱顿语的东部方言，而且他对这两种语言都并非完全精通。我已尽我所能恢复其原始含义和节奏。<BR>
<BR>
你谦卑的译者，<BR>
卡索拉尔·德拉博<BR>
<BR>
*****<BR>
<BR>
卓'扎尼向马民讲述了巨行者之屋的故事。<BR>
<BR>
当首鬃诞生时，蛇人从多雨之地而来。卡吉特如太阳迎接沙丘般欢迎他们，因为卡吉特知道蛇人与掠取者交战。卡吉特惧怕掠取者，因为部族母亲们看得远，那时各部族如沙子般散落，所有卡吉特都是可怜的奴隶。于是卡吉特给了蛇人糖和肉。卡吉特给了蛇人沙和天。蛇人则回报以血、呼吸和尘土。<BR>
<BR>
月亮升起又落下。丛林不太湿润，沙丘也不太炎热。卡吉特教给蛇人沙之道、丛林之道、爪之道和面绘之道。蛇人教给卡吉特剑之道和集会之道。卡吉特对掠取者既不理会也不进贡。<BR>
<BR>
当掠取者到来时，一些卡吉特为了回报恩惠而与蛇人并肩作战。一些人认为蛇人引来了掠取者，因而没有战斗。掠取者来到了龙路、拥抱河、精灵尖塔和低弯腰。卡吉特之间用言语相互争斗，多于用利爪对抗掠取者。鬃首还是孩子，各部族从他小小的指爪间滑脱。于是掠取者偷走了沙和天。<BR>
<BR>
掠取者学会了糖之道，并教给卡吉特鞭之道。然后掠取者让卡吉特建造一座屋。每一天，那座屋都长得更高更胖。每一天卡吉特都会问：“谁会住在这座屋里？”掠取者不肯说。<BR>
<BR>
卓'扎尼告诉你这些事，因为卓'扎尼在龙路战斗过，在低弯腰失去了利爪，卓'扎尼为那座屋制作了许多石头。是的，那些石头并非石头。掠取者用泥土、火、灰烬和盐造出了发光石。卓'扎尼不喜欢这些说谎石，但卓'扎尼害怕鞭子和糖。<BR>
<BR>
一天，当那座屋比所有沙丘和树木堆叠起来还要高时，一位掠取者首领来到了那座又高又胖的屋。卓'扎尼听到了首领的话，听说那座屋是给巨行者的。卓'扎尼知道巨行者的所有名字，因为卓'扎尼在低弯腰之前演奏过许多歌曲，那时卓'扎尼还能多数出两个。<BR>
<BR>
当那座屋建成后，大车从多雨之地而来，载着巨行者的碎片。掠取者试图唤醒巨行者。掠取者施了许多法术，念了许多祈祷，摇晃巨行者的头，对着他的脚呐喊。沙地变得像水一样。月亮躲藏起来。许多部族母亲看到了不应看到的事物。许多蛇人病倒了。<BR>
<BR>
数数者知道工人们的每一滴眼泪，每一滴汗水，他害怕被淹没而无法计数。<BR>
<BR>
于是阿尔科什用爪抓挠那座屋，用脚踩踏那座屋，并向那座屋喷吐火焰，但巨行者在他的屋中沉睡，那座屋并未倒塌。阿尔科什也无法进入那座屋。<BR>
<BR>
于是阿尔科什造了一个孩子，达尔克·拉'瓦尔。这个孩子在侧面之地长大，变得强壮而狡黠。拉'瓦尔从说谎石的裂缝间溜了进去，却找不到通往巨行者的路。拉'瓦尔唱起崩解之歌，远山的石头化为沙砾，但说谎石只对谎言有反应。拉'瓦尔拿起掠取者自己的工具，慢慢地凿刻石头，一直唱着歌，但即使是在侧面之地，他也没有活到足够长的时间来开辟道路。巨行者在他的屋中是聋的，那座屋也没有变回沙砾。阿尔科什也无法进入那座屋。<BR>
<BR>
于是阿尔科什解开了不计数的年份。阿尔科什吞噬了阿尔科什，制造了一个只有在对的月亮下诞生的生命才能填补的空洞。受祝福降生者以龙趾行走，以龙语说话，鳞片披于肩头。但狡猾者愚弄了阿尔科什，用那些不计数的年份制造了一具新躯体。血肉之龙并非卡吉特，而是一个在狡猾者的池塘中凝视过久的掠取者人类。<BR>
<BR>
于是血肉之龙背叛了自己。很快又一辆大车到来，里面是被埋葬者的心脏，是月亮在沸腾之海中的倒影。血肉之龙得以进入巨行者之屋。当心脏在巨行者体内跳动时，他并不在自己的屋中。<BR>
<BR>
于是巨行者扛起了他的屋，开始行走。巨行者之屋不再俯瞰大海。在耐-奎纳尔、荆棘之家、十沼泽，以及巨行者所到之处，都引起了巨大的麻烦。<BR>
<BR>
血肉之龙带领巨行者渡过了大海，那座屋也随之而去，但他并不在自己的屋中。留下未走的蛇人满怀悔恨，成为了边际人。他们失去了尾巴的知觉，无法分辨敌友，因此与所有卡吉特为敌，仿佛我们都背叛了他们。<BR>
<BR>
阿尔科什厌倦了巨行者让他失去计数。于是阿尔科什将北风装进一个内外相同的瓶子里。阿尔科什冻结了星辰，将它们扫入簸箕。阿尔科什点燃了猫眼，将它的影子困在井中。阿尔科什将大海吸入他的胸膛。阿尔科什将所有这一切作为礼物送给了一个牙人，牙人用它们说了一个词，将巨行者轰得粉碎。<BR>
<BR>
那座屋一直被吹回到了黎明，在那里它成了拒绝计数的龙的家。那座屋被一次又一次地吹回，直到它比月亮和星辰还要古老十爪乘十爪。在这整个过程中，那座屋一直记得侧面之地达尔克·拉'瓦尔的歌声。每一场雨，每一阵风，都会有一小撮屋化为沙砾。在多风暴的年代，那座屋坠落到耐-奎纳尔，巨行者的碎片散落各处。<BR>
<BR>
但这座屋总是在这里或那里，现在谁又知道它有多古老呢。一半的沙丘都是那座屋，无论那是说谎石还是歌尘。那座屋记得巨行者，有时会自行走动。所以，即使巨行者之屋比所有树木堆叠起来还要高，它却像一粒沙一样难以寻觅。<BR>

<FONT COLOR="000000"><BR>就这样，在担任了两个西罗帝尔的皇帝多年之后，尽管一些偏远地区的叛乱反对他的统治，圣雷曼·西罗帝尔还是按照法律统治了整个泰姆瑞尔，但他最终还是离世了，并在帝都举行了上千场神圣的仪式安葬。虽然他一生中有许多孩子，但他没有立后，根据尼本的传统，此后出现的任何王位宣称者都不可能是真正的龙裔。在马鲁哈特派中最明智者的建议下，成立了一个由两个西罗帝尔所有伟人组成的元老院代行其职，这是一个神圣的联盟，由东方的蛇裔摄政查米恩-瓦瑞尔领导，他曾在圣雷曼眼中看到神圣之光，收起了他的大刀，将他金色躯体的整个长度匍匐在昔日敌人面前的泥土中，宣称他只效忠于八圣灵以及他们所祝福的红钻王座，因此被接纳为西罗帝尔的军队成员。

但这并非长久之计，而且凭借他们的智慧，上方的圣灵们派遣了一位新皇帝给尼本的人民。于是，在新雨之周的第一周，塞德-耶娜 -- 那时已是一位老妇人 -- 在她家之外的丛林中受到了一千个微粒精灵的骚扰，它们将她托举到空中，并显现出玛拉的形态，她披着庄严的王袍，圆顶的头上戴着祖先丝绸的头巾。当她微笑时，塞德-耶娜发誓她能看到帕拉文在她眼中，她告诉塞德-耶娜新皇帝即将到来，那是雷曼·西罗帝尔的儿子。

塞德-耶娜收到了一个用雷曼种子制成的蛋，一个承载着西罗德之灵和阿莱西亚血脉的神圣容器。她将它珍藏，睡觉时紧贴在胸前，每周她前往卡杜出售她编织的丝绸时，都会将它藏在斗篷下携带。起初，它只有蜂鸟蛋大小，一块被内在光芒温暖的小卵石，但在短短几个月内，它就长得比托帕尔的大蓝食火鸡的蛋还要大了。

然而，悲剧接踵而至，一天清晨，年迈的塞德-耶娜独自沿着尼本河旅行时，一阵西风将她吹得站立不稳，雷曼的蛋从她干瘪的手臂中滑落，在岩石上轻微磕碰后滚入绿色的河水中。塞德-耶娜涉水追去，向天上的八圣灵呼喊祈祷，恳求将蛋归还给她，但它没有再出现，而在蛋碎裂的那一刻，东西方的号角在阿德利平原上被敲响，两个西罗帝尔被撕裂，此后的十八年里再无和平。<BR>

<FONT COLOR="003300"><BR>第二章：雷曼二世的崛起<BR>

<FONT COLOR="000000"><BR>但并非一切都已失去，一天早晨，一位名叫塞登的稻田农夫正坐在尼本河的一个小港湾边冥想，令他大为惊讶的是，一只身披灿烂金色鳞片的公爵河龙从水中升起。它没有说话，但怀里抱着一个婴儿，包裹在芦苇和河草中，右侧头部有一道疤痕。婴儿散发着圣徒或守护灵的内在光芒，塞登知道他的名字是雷曼，人类之光。

于是稻田农夫塞登将孩子带到他在塔斯梅拉的茅屋中，并与妻子将他视如己出地抚养长大。他生命的最初几年饱受战争纷争的困扰，当森林的诺纳勒人从大城偷走雷曼·西罗帝尔的遗体并运往桑克雷·托，未经适当仪式就将他埋入土丘时，他年仅四岁，战争变得比以往更加激烈。此后塔斯梅拉变得不再安全，塞登带着家人逃离，先到了凯普图，然后到阿尔-哈鲁德，再到布拉维尔和费特-伦，甚至向东远至科斯里。

当他长成男子时，雷曼已经看遍了尼本奈的所有土地，并在尼本河的所有支流中沐浴过。但一天晚上，他们停在了萨尔多瓦 -- 一个神圣却闹鬼的地方 -- 雷曼不由自主地漫步到他的祖先曾在烈日和奴隶主恐怖统治下劳作过的田野。站在沼泽中，他感到一种无法抗拒的召唤，于是他逃离了那片可怕的田野和萨尔多瓦，以速度和优雅奔跑着，直到抵达了万城之城。

他扑倒在高塔前，大声喊道：“我是雷曼·西罗帝尔！”他的呼喊震响了尼本和科斯里的所有钟声，一群困惑的围观者聚集在他周围。但摄政穿过人群，用金色的眼睛看出皇帝已重返西罗帝尔，立刻俯身拜倒在君主面前。

于是，一队刀锋战士集结起来，向西横跨科洛维亚，所有人都被迫在皇帝雷曼面前屈服。那些拒绝的领地伯爵和骑士被尼本奈的武士刀击倒，那些被怀疑不忠的人被免职。尽管起初有许多反抗他权威的叛乱 -- 科洛维亚人因多年的叛乱而失去了文明 -- 但在半年之内，这片土地再次效忠于白金塔，从西部的萨奇到东部的格姆哈，所有人民都团结在他们的君主雷曼二世 -- 两个西罗帝尔的皇帝，根据法律也是整个泰姆瑞尔的皇帝 -- 之下。<BR>"""

Bones of Hlur'Matta<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
What is a body? What is the flesh? A simple network of bones and blood? Connections made through touch, smell, sight, sound, and taste? No, the Ancestors have taught us that there is much more to a body than that. Within each body is a temple, an oratory. We breathe as we live, we shed tears as we grieve, and we bleed as we survive. The embodiment of these things, that is where the root of our being resides. The EMBODIMENT is our temple.<BR>
<BR>
Many questions are asked throughout life, and the answers only come to us in the precious last few moments we stride the salts. A sanctimonious offering to the Ancestors for the knowledge they have given us; we offer them our temples in return for theirs. We frame and carve and cleave at the silken stone to bellow the dirge of our thanks in the massive halls that carry our voices to the skies; so we build the temples with throats. We fashion and adorn and decorate the altars with precious stones and candles made from the waxy carcasses of our Skyrenders; so we drape the temples in clothing. <BR>
<BR>
We plan and contrive and perceive and surmise as we cobble the statues that stand tall in the atriums; so we build the temples with minds. We offer and sacrifice and submit and nominate our faith to the statues and their altars; so we build the temples with life. Our temples are infinite.<BR>
So what, again do you say, is a body? Could you ever dissect the truth of absolutes on an expedition for answers for which there was never birthed a question? Under the moons and beside the lakes we warden our possessions to farm the land, but their hands will never touch the vestibules of our Ancestors. These are our sacred lands, our paradises within paradise. Tending these rituals is more taxing than tending the dirt could ever be, as we are constantly in a precarious correlation to the honor we can give and the honor the Ancestors deserve. <BR>
<BR>
But what, then, of our dead? Of those who made their way back to the Ancestors? The ashes of the dead can suffocate and fall in sheets from the sky. We instead chaperone the bones of our deceased, and shape them into cairns and effigies of power. The same temples that are built inside of us shall be erected from the earth and unto the endless void of the sky.<BR>
This is the correlation that men and the Altmer do not understand, that they do not appreciate, that they cannot decipher. Seek these bones, these macabre motifs, and know that you are near our sublime abodes. Our dwellings may be forgotten to time and mortal whim, but they still stand sound and deeply fastened into our history.<BR>
<BR>
Tread lightly, brethren. And may the Hands guide you.<BR>

赫鲁'玛塔之骨<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
什么是身体？什么是血肉？不过是骨骼与血液的网络？通过触觉、嗅觉、视觉、听觉和味觉建立的联系？不，祖先教导我们，身体的含义远不止于此。在每个身体内部，都有一座神殿，一座礼拜堂。我们活着时呼吸，悲伤时流泪，生存时流血。这些事物的具现化，就是我们存在的根源所在。具现化就是我们的神殿。<BR>

<BR>
那么，我们的死者呢？那些已回到祖先身边的人们呢？死者的灰烬可能会令人窒息，如帷幕般从天而降。我们则护送逝者的骨骼，将它们塑造成石冢和权力的象征。那些在我们体内建造的神殿，也应从大地竖起，直向天空的无尽虚空。<BR>
这就是人类和傲特莫所不理解、不欣赏、无法解读的关联。寻找这些骨骼，这些可怖的图案，你就知道你已接近我们崇高的居所。我们的居所或许会被时间和凡人的一时兴起所遗忘，但它们依然坚固矗立，深深根植于我们的历史之中。<BR>
<BR>
轻步前行，兄弟们。愿双手指引你们。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">Excerpts from the Books of Sand<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Among the literary works of the Khajiit, the oldest of any certainty date from the early Empire, shortly after Tiber Septim's conquest. There are many extant works that claim to be of Khajiti origins, most of them translations, but none that most scholars agree are genuine. For instance, I recently translated a book on the Hall of Colossus, but after publishing, I received numerous letters arguing about it being a forgery.<BR>
<BR>
What most agree with is that Khajiti and Imperial scribes were hired to collect the works and sayings of their race in order for the Emperor to better understand the Khajiit. This project was ultimately a failure, but it preserved much Khajiti literature that would otherwise have been lost.<BR>
<BR>
These scholars divided their work into the Books of Sand, Sugar, Meat, Rain, and Dust. The Books of Sand focus mainly on poetry, mostly of a personal nature, and nursery rhymes. The Books of Sugar are of erotic poetry and tales. The Books of Meat include maxims, parables, and children's fables. The Books of Rain are pseudo-historical or pseudo-religious in nature, but include long digressions on cooking recipes, smithing techniques, battle strategy, and other practical subjects. The Books of Dust are mystical, philosophical, and inscrutable, even to the Khajiit themselves.<BR>
<BR>
Since that time more books have been added to each series, such that you can tell the relative age of Khajiti literature by the number of the book. Generally the first and second of each series predate the Third Era, while later books are of more recent origin.<BR>
<BR>
There is little interest outside Elsweyr for Khajiti literature, but there is a small market for poetry from all eras and races. I would like to thank Black Moon Publishing of Rihad for the small advance that allowed me to translate some of the most accessible sections. I would also like to thank Dro'Sharr, Fahra of Orcrest, Clan-Mother Manibi, and Ri'Haniir for their patience and assistance in understanding certain passages.<BR>
<BR>
A Note on the Translation<BR>
<BR>
Khajiti poetry of the late Second Era and early Third Era tends to have little meter or structure, but many internal rhymes, assonance, and alliteration. Children's rhymes are more similar in structure to the poetry of the Empire. In a few of these translations, I endeavored to retain some of the character of the original, but Cyrodiilic's more advanced phonology makes the feel of the poetry difficult to replicate. Another consideration was that a more accurate rendition might sound dull and repetitive to a broader audience.<BR>
<BR>
As Ta'agra lacks direct equivalents to the familiar Imperial pronouns and makes it difficult to refer to certain things except by name, I have used what I feel is the closest of 'one's', 'Khajiit', 'the', 'this', 'my', 'your', etc. in place of the original wording, even though this is never a perfect translation.<BR>
<BR>
The original poems are untitled -- indeed, it is sometimes difficult to tell where one begins or ends -- so I have created titles myself.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">沙之书节选<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
在卡吉特的文学作品中，最确切的古早作品可追溯到帝国早期，即泰伯·塞普汀征服之后不久。有许多现存的文献声称源自卡吉特，其中大部分是翻译作品，但没有一部得到大多数学者的公认。例如，我最近翻译了一本关于巨像大厅的书，但出版后，我收到了许多信件，争论它是一件赝品。<BR>
<BR>
大多数学者认同的是，卡吉特和帝国的抄写员曾被雇佣来收集他们民族的著作和言论，以便皇帝更好地了解卡吉特。这个项目最终失败了，但它保存了许多本会失传的卡吉特文学作品。<BR>
<BR>
这些学者将他们的作品分为《沙之书》、《糖之书》、《肉之书》、《雨之书》和《尘之书》。《沙之书》主要收录诗歌，多为个人性质的作品，以及童谣。《糖之书》收录情色诗歌和故事。《肉之书》收录格言、寓言和儿童寓言故事。《雨之书》本质上是伪历史或伪宗教的，但包含大量关于烹饪食谱、锻造技巧、战争策略和其他实用性主题的冗长插叙。《尘之书》是神秘的、哲学的，即使对卡吉特自己来说也难以理解。<BR>
<BR>
从那时起，每个系列都增加了更多的书，你可以通过书的编号来判断卡吉特文学作品的相对年代。通常每个系列的第一卷和第二卷都早于第三纪元，而较后的书则是较近代的。<BR>
<BR>
艾斯维尔之外对卡吉特文学的兴趣不大，但对各个时代、各个种族的诗歌有一个小市场。我想感谢里哈德的黑月出版社提供的预付款，让我得以翻译一些最易读的章节。我还要感谢卓'沙尔、奥克瑞斯特的法赫拉、部族母亲玛尼比，以及里'哈尼尔在理解某些段落时的耐心和帮助。<BR>
<BR>
关于翻译的说明<BR>
<BR>
第二纪元晚期和第三纪元早期的卡吉特诗歌往往缺乏韵律或结构，但包含许多内部押韵、谐音和头韵。童谣在结构上更接近帝国的诗歌。在这些翻译中，我尽力保留了一些原文的特色，但西罗帝尔语更先进的音系使得诗歌的韵味难以复制。另一个考虑是，更准确的翻译在更广泛的读者听来可能会显得枯燥重复。<BR>
<BR>
由于塔'格拉语缺乏与常见的帝国人称代词直接对应的词汇，并且除了使用名字之外很难指代某些事物，我使用了我认为最接近的“某人的”、“卡吉特”、“这”、“我的”、“你的”等词来代替原文，尽管这从来都不是完美的翻译。<BR>
<BR>
原诗没有标题 -- 事实上，有时很难分辨一首诗的起止 -- 所以我自行添加了标题。<BR>
<BR>
你谦卑的译者，<BR>
卡索拉尔·德拉博<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Bravil: Daughter of the Niben<BR>
by Destri Melarg<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Bravil is one of the most charming towns in Cyrodiil, sparkling in her simple beauty, illustrious by her past. No visit to the southern part of the Imperial Province is complete without a walk along Bravil's exciting river port, a talk with her friendly native children, and, of course, in the tradition of the village, a whispered word to the famous statue of the Lucky Old Lady.<BR>
<BR>
Many thousands of years before the arrival of the Atmorans, the native Ayleid people had long lived in the vicinity of modern day Bravil. The Niben then, as now, provided food and transportation, and the village was even more populous than it is today. We are not certain what they called their region: as insular as they were, the word they used would be translated to simply mean "home." These savage Ayleids were so firmly entrenched that the Bravil region was one of the very last areas to be liberated by the Alessian army in the second century of the 1st era. Though little remains of that era culturally or archeologically, thank Mara, the tales of debauchery and depravity have entered into the realm of legends.<BR>
<BR>
How the Ayleids were able to survive such a long siege is debated by scholars to this day. All, however, grant the honor of the victory to one of the Empress Alessia's centurions, a man called Teo Bravillius Tasus, the man for whom the modern town is named.<BR>
<BR>
It was said he invaded the village no less than four times, after heavy resistance, but each time upon the morning dawning, all his soldiery within would be dead, murdered. By the time more centuria had arrived, the fortified town was repopulated with Ayleids. After the second successful invasion, secret underground tunnels were found and filled in, but once again, come morning, the soldiers were again dead, and the citizens had returned. After the third successful siege, legions were posted outside of the town, watching the roads and riverway for signs of attacks, but no one came. The next morning, the bodies of the invading soldiers were thrown from the parapets of town's walls.<BR>
<BR>
Teo Bravillius Tasus knew that the Ayleids must be hiding themselves somewhere in the town, waiting until nightfall, and then murdering the soldiers while they slept. The question was where. After the fourth invasion, he himself led the soldiers in a thorough inspection of every corner, every shadow. Just as they were ready to give up, the great centurion noticed two curious things. High in the sheer walls of the town, beyond anyone's ability to climb, there were indentations, narrow platforms. And by the river just inside the town, he discovered a single footprint from someone clearly not wearing the Imperial boot.<BR>
<BR>
The Ayleids, it seemed, had taken two routes to hide themselves. Some had levitated up to the walls and hidden themselves high above, and others had slipped into the river, where they were able to breathe underwater. It was a relatively easy task once the strange elves' even stranger hiding holes had been discovered to rout them out, and see to it that there were no more midnight assassinations of the Empress's troops.<BR>
<BR>
It may seem beyond belief that an entire community could be so skilled in these spells hundreds and hundreds of years before the Mages Guild was formed to teach the ways of magicka to the common folk. There does, however, appear to be evidence that, just as the Psijics on the Isle of Artaeum developed Mysticism long before there was a name for it, the even more obscure Ayleids of southern Cyrodiil had developed what was to be known as the school of Alteration. It is not, after all, much of a stretch when one considers that other Ayleids at the time of Bravil's conquering and even later were shapeshifters. The community of pre-Bravil could not turn into beasts and monsters, but they could alter their bodies to hide themselves away. A related and useful skill, to be sure. But not so effective to save themselves in the end.<BR>
<BR>
Very little is left of the Ayleid presence in Bravil of today, though architectural marvels of other kinds are very evident. As beautiful and arresting as the Benevolence of Mara cathedral and the lord's palace are, no manmade structure in Bravil is as famous as the statue called The Lucky Old Lady.<BR>
<BR>
The tales about the Lady and who she was are too numerous to list.<BR>
<BR>
It was said she was born the illegitimate daughter of a prostitute in Bravil, certainly an inauspicious beginning to a lucky life. She was teased by the other children, who forever asked her who her father was. Every day, she would run back to her little shack in tears from their cruelty.<BR>
<BR>
One day, a priest of Stendarr came to Bravil to do charitable work. He saw the weeping little girl, and when asked, she told him the cause of her misery: she didn't know who her father was.<BR>
<BR>
"You have kind eyes and a mouth that tells no lies," replied the priest after a moment, smiling. "You are clearly a child of Stendarr, the God of Mercy, Charity, and Well-Earned Luck."<BR>
<BR>
The priest's thoughtful words changed the girl forever. Whenever she was asked who her father was, she would cheerfully reply, "I am a child of Luck."<BR>
<BR>
She grew up to be a barmaid, it was said, kind and generous to her customers, frequently allowing them to pay when they were able to. On a particularly rainy night, she gave shelter to a young man dressed in rags, who not only had no money to pay, but was belligerent and rude to her as she fed him and gave him a room. The next morning, he left without so much as a thank you. Her friends and family admonished her, saying that she had to be careful, he might have even been dangerous.<BR>
<BR>
A week later, a royal carriage arrived in Bravil, with an Imperial prince within. Though he was scarcely reconizable, it was the same young man the Lady had helped. He apologized profusely for his appearance and behavior, explaining that he had been kidnapped and cursed by a band of witches, and it wasn't until later he had returned to his senses. The Lady was showered with riches, which she, of course, generously shared with all the people of Bravil, where she lived to a content old age.<BR>
<BR>
No one knows when the statue to her was erected in the town square, or who the artist was, but it has stood there for thousands of years, since the first era. To this day, visitors and Bravillians alike go to the Lucky Old Lady to ask for her to bless them with luck in their travails.<BR>
<BR>
Just one more charming aspect of the charming, and very lucky village of Bravil.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
布拉维尔：尼本之女<BR>
德斯特里·梅拉格 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
布拉维尔是西罗帝尔最迷人的城镇之一，以其朴素之美闪耀着光芒，以其辉煌的过往而著称。不沿着布拉维尔热闹的河港散步，不与友好的当地孩子交谈，当然，不依照村落的传统，向著名的幸运老妇人雕像轻声细语，就不能算到过帝国行省的南部。<BR>
<BR>
在阿特莫拉人到来之前的数千年，当地的亚历德人早已生活在现今布拉维尔附近。当时的尼本河如同现在一样，提供了食物和交通，村落甚至比今天更加人口稠密。我们不确定他们如何称呼他们的地区：由于他们与世隔绝，他们使用的词翻译过来仅仅意味着“家”。这些野蛮的亚历德人如此根深蒂固，以至于布拉维尔地区是第一纪元第二世纪阿莱西亚军队最后解放的地区之一。感谢玛拉，虽然那个时代在文化或考古上留存甚少，但关于放荡和堕落的传说已进入传奇领域。<BR>
<BR>
亚历德人是如何能够在如此长时间的围困中幸存下来的，至今学者们仍在争论。然而，所有人都将胜利的荣誉归于阿莱西亚女皇的一位百夫长，一个名叫特奥·布拉维利乌斯·塔苏斯的人，现代城镇就是以他的名字命名的。<BR>
<BR>
据说他在激烈抵抗后，入侵该村落不下四次，但每次黎明时分，他所有的士兵都会死去，被谋杀。到更多百人队到达时，设防城镇已被亚历德人重新占据。第二次成功入侵后，秘密地下隧道被发现并被填埋，但再次，到了早晨，士兵们再次死去，居民们又回来了。第三次成功围攻后，军团被部署在城镇外，监视道路和河道以防袭击，但没有人来。第二天早上，入侵士兵的尸体从城墙的胸墙被扔下。<BR>
<BR>
特奥·布拉维利乌斯·塔苏斯知道亚历德人一定藏在镇上的某个地方，等到夜幕降临，然后在士兵睡觉时杀死他们。问题是在哪里。第四次入侵后，他亲自带领士兵彻底搜查了每一个角落，每一片阴影。就在他们准备放弃时，这位伟大的百夫长注意到了两件奇怪的事。在城镇陡峭的城墙高处，超出任何人攀爬能力的地方，有凹陷，狭窄的平台。而在城镇内的河边，他发现了一个脚印，显然不是穿着帝国靴子的人留下的。<BR>
<BR>
看来，亚历德人通过两种方式隐藏自己。一些人漂浮到城墙上，藏在高处，另一些人则溜进河里，在那里他们可以在水下呼吸。一旦这些奇怪精灵更奇怪的藏身之处被发现，驱逐他们并确保女皇的军队不再遭受午夜暗杀，就成了一件相对容易的任务。<BR>
<BR>
在整个社区数百年前就如此精通这些法术，而那时法师公会还未成立来向普通人传授魔法之道，这或许令人难以置信。然而，似乎有证据表明，正如阿泰乌姆岛的塞伊克教团早在有正式名称之前就发展了神秘系一样，西罗帝尔南部更为隐秘的亚历德人已经发展了后来被称为变化系的法术。毕竟，当我们想到在布拉维尔征服时期甚至更晚的其他亚历德人是变形者时，这并不牵强。前布拉维尔社区不能变成野兽和怪物，但他们可以改变身体以隐藏自己。这当然是一项相关且有用的技能。但最终不足以拯救自己。<BR>
<BR>
如今布拉维尔的亚历德痕迹已所剩无几，尽管其他类型的建筑奇观非常明显。尽管玛拉的慈悲大教堂和领主宫殿美丽而引人注目，但布拉维尔没有哪个人造建筑像被称为“幸运老妇人”的雕像那样著名。<BR>
<BR>
关于这位女士以及她是谁的传说数不胜数。<BR>
<BR>
据说她是布拉维尔一个妓女的私生女，这无疑是一个幸运人生的不祥开端。她受到其他孩子的嘲笑，他们总是问她的父亲是谁。每天，她都会因为他们的残忍而哭着跑回她的小屋。<BR>
<BR>
一天，一位斯滕达尔的祭司来到布拉维尔做慈善工作。他看到了哭泣的小女孩，当被问及时，她告诉了他她痛苦的根源：她不知道她的父亲是谁。<BR>
<BR>
“你有一双善良的眼睛和一张不说谎的嘴，”祭司片刻后微笑着回答。“你显然是斯滕达尔的孩子，斯滕达尔是仁慈、博爱和应得幸运之神。”<BR>
<BR>
祭司深思熟虑的话语永远改变了那个女孩。每当有人问她的父亲是谁时，她都会愉快地回答：“我是幸运的孩子。”<BR>
<BR>
据说她长大后成了一名酒吧女招待，对顾客友善慷慨，经常允许他们有能力时再付款。在一个特别多雨的夜晚，她收留了一个衣衫褴褛的年轻人，他不仅没钱付账，而且在她给他食物和房间时对她好斗且粗鲁。第二天早上，他连谢谢都没说就走了。她的朋友和家人告诫她，说她必须小心，他可能很危险。<BR>
<BR>
一周后，一辆皇家马车抵达布拉维尔，里面坐着一位帝国王子。虽然他几乎无法辨认，但正是那位女士帮助过的那个年轻人。他为自己的外表和行为深表歉意，解释说他曾被一伙女巫绑架并诅咒，直到后来才恢复理智。那位女士获得了大量财富，她当然慷慨地与布拉维尔的所有人分享，在那里她幸福地活到了晚年。<BR>
<BR>
没有人知道她的雕像是何时在城镇广场竖立的，也不知道艺术家是谁，但自第一纪元以来，它已在那里矗立了数千年。直到今天，游客和布拉维尔人都会前往幸运老妇人雕像，请求她在他们的磨难中赐予他们好运。<BR>
<BR>
这只是迷人而幸运的布拉维尔村庄的又一个迷人之处。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
How to Break in a Set of Armor<BR>
By Orgol gro-Muk<BR>
<BR>
Once I'd freed myself from prison, I scarcely knew what to do with myself. Mind, before this, I had been but a guard in the Legions; my knowledge of outlaws was limited to knowing I wouldn't get arrested for roughing them up. Since no one seemed to take note of me wandering listlessly about town, I grew bold. Surely it wouldn't hurt to linger for a while as I got my bearings.<BR>
<BR>
Then it occurred to me that my former cellmate, the nice Khajiiti woman, would probably know more about being an outlaw than I. And so I cast about for her, and at length, found her at a shady cornerclub. Ma'Dar looked at me nervously, and it took a while for me to remember I was in full armor, and unrecognizable. I had to come up with a subtle way to let her know who I was, without letting everyone else know, for I WAS a wanted criminal.<BR>
<BR>
"Um" I said, "I'm Orgol." It was a shining example of why I employ intelligence enhancers so often. For her part, Ma'Dar relaxed, and, to my horror, informed the general patronage that I was the Orc she had just been speaking of. Surprisingly, no one attempted to bring me to justice, but rather they all laughed uproariously, and several offered to buy me drinks.<BR>
<BR>
I just stood there for a few seconds, until it dawned on me that Ma'Dar could not see the look of confusion on my face. Since I wasn't in danger of being caught here, I removed the helm so my confusion would be plain to see. After trying a few euphemisms that went over my head, she flat out told me the cornerclub was a Thieves Guild hangout. In return, I explained to her that I knew nothing of outlawing. She purred appreciatively, and mentioned that she knew of some smugglers that were short a man (two, actually, so she would be accompanying me). In the morning, she assured me, we would set out for the Dwemer ruin that they had holed up in.<BR>
<BR>
When morning came, Ma'Dar was true to her word. Again, I was able to walk about town freely, though I got some strange looks, since I was posing as a guard and Ma'Dar was a known thief. We made it out of town without event, but as we neared the Dwemer ruin, I had a jolting thought.<BR>
<BR>
"Ma'Dar!" I cried in despair, "I cannot remove this armor! It was meant for a smaller fellow than I, and I fear I am stuck! If the smugglers see me in this, they are sure to attack me, thinking I came to arrest them." And so my little Khajiiti friend tried to assist me in removing it, to no avail. The armor was stuck fast. She hissed despairingly, then suddenly smiled.<BR>
<BR>
"On three, you must stretch, my green friend." She purred, and cast a spell of a sort I hadn't seen before. Amazingly, my stolen armor started to tarnish here, crack there, and, after doing as she asked, it broke into pieces and fell off of me. "Armor disintegration," she explained patiently "is sometimes useful for a thief. The cracks give us somewhere to slide in a jinkblade, allowing our escape."<BR>
<BR>
Though I could hardly be expected to pick it up with anything like quickness, I suddenly wanted to learn the spell. After all, I thought as we approached the ruin, I was going to be a lot more involved on the other side of the law from now on. A big strong (loud) Orc might not make the best thief, but it was the path that lay before me.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>

如何磨合一套盔甲<BR>

从监狱脱身后，我几乎不知道自己要做什么。要知道，在此之前，我只是军团的一名守卫；我对逃犯的了解仅限于知道揍他们一顿不会被抓。由于似乎没有人注意到我无精打采地在镇上游荡，我胆子大了起来。在弄清自己处境时多逗留一会儿，想必也无妨。<BR>
<BR>
然后我想到，我以前的狱友，那个好心的卡吉特女人，可能比我对逃犯这一行懂得更多。于是我四处寻找她，最终，在一家阴暗的街角酒吧找到了她。玛达尔紧张地看着我，过了一会儿我才想起我穿着全套盔甲，面目难辨。我必须想出一个巧妙的方法让她知道我是谁，又不能让其他人知道，因为我确实是个通缉犯。<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，”我说，“我是奥戈尔。”这是我为什么经常使用智力增强法术的绝佳例子。玛达尔松了口气，但令我惊恐的是，她告诉在场的所有顾客，我就是她刚才提到的那个兽人。令人惊讶的是，没有人试图将我绳之以法，反而都哄堂大笑，还有几个人要请我喝酒。<BR>
<BR>
我就在那儿站了几秒钟，才恍然大悟玛达尔看不到我脸上困惑的表情。既然我在这里没有被捕的危险，我摘下了头盔，这样我的困惑就一目了然了。在尝试了几个我不太明白的委婉说法后，她直截了当地告诉我，那家街角酒吧是盗贼公会的一个据点。作为回报，我跟她解释说我对做逃犯一窍不通。她赞赏地咕噜了一声，提到她知道一些走私者正缺人手（其实是两个，所以她会和我一起去）。她向我保证，早上我们就出发去他们藏身的锻莫废墟。<BR>
<BR>
第二天早上，玛达尔信守了诺言。我再次得以在镇上自由行走，尽管我引来了一些奇怪的目光，因为我伪装成一个卫兵，而玛达尔是个知名的盗贼。我们平安地出了镇子，但当我们接近锻莫废墟时，我猛地想到一个问题。<BR>
<BR>
“玛达尔！”我绝望地喊道，“我脱不掉这身盔甲！这是给比我小一号的人穿的，我怕是被卡住了！如果走私者看到我穿着这个，肯定会以为我是来抓他们的，一定会攻击我。”于是我那位小小的卡吉特朋友试着帮我脱掉它，但没有成功。盔甲卡得死死的。她绝望地发出嘶嘶声，然后突然笑了。<BR>
<BR>
“数到三，你必须伸展身体，我的绿皮朋友。”她咕噜着，施放了一种我以前从未见过的法术。令人惊讶的是，我偷来的盔甲开始在这里变暗，在那里裂开，当我照她说的做了之后，它碎成碎片，从我身上脱落下来。“盔甲瓦解术，”她耐心地解释道，“有时对小偷很有用。裂缝给我们提供了一个滑入撬刀的地方，以便我们逃脱。”<BR>
<BR>
尽管我不能期望自己能很快学会，但我突然想学这个法术。毕竟，当我们走近废墟时，我想，从现在起我会更多地在法律的对立面活动。一个又大又壮（又吵）的兽人可能不是最好的盗贼，但这是我面前的道路。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>

Breakout<BR>
By Orgol gro-Muk<BR>
<BR>
And so, my murderous intentions toward Furnius revealed, I was hastily placed in a cell in the local prison. Not having had the benefit of an artificially inflated intelligence at the time, I became quite confused; perhaps the guard had misinterpreted my plan out of ignorance, I thought. I was supremely confident that the fellow would come around, and see things however it was I had outlined them. My confidence eroded thoroughly after the first week.<BR>
<BR>
I was placed in a cell with a charming Khajiiti woman, though I fear I wasn't the most pleasant company unless I made myself smarter via spell. She had been, of course, arrested for theft, but being one who had harbored murderous intentions, I could hardly hold that against her. Indeed, she was good company, and helped pass the time with stories of the heroes and mythology of Elsweyr.<BR>
<BR>
But as time wore on, I became aware that she would be released, and I would not. Saddened, I implored her to teach me some skill that might aid my escape. Truly, I feared that she might steal something of such worth that the guard would simply kill her next time, and wanted to ensure her safety. At any rate, she laboriously taught me a mild Chameleon spell in the weeks before her release.<BR>
<BR>
Once I was alone, I spent my days catching rats in my cell, then made them appear to disappear. It wasn't the brightest thing I've ever done, as the invisible rats invited themselves into the prison food stocks, and so made my meals more rationed.<BR>
<BR>
Experimentation taught me some interesting things. While the spell only worked when cast on something organic and vital, it would also effect the armor of the target, and so could extend its influence quite a bit farther. While the most obvious method to use this spell to escape would be to cast it on myself, to make the guard open the door and search the cell, the Khajiiti woman had warned me that such practices were well known to guards and so not advisable.<BR>
<BR>
I scratched my handsome green head for a moment, then struck upon a solution. A thick moss grew on the wall at the back of my cell, and I cast the spell on it. My hopes were borne out, for much of the wall became transparent! I shouted for the guard in excitement, telling him that some foul criminals were trying to break me out. Why anyone would try something like that, I do not know, but thankfully, the guard did not raise similar questions. Instead, he saw what appeared to be an open wall to the outside, and rushed to unlock my cell to, ironically, prevent my escape.<BR>
<BR>
Once the door was open, I grabbed the guard, and threw him into the invisible wall. As expected, his fear stunned him much more than the blow, for he had expected a fall of a few stories. Time enough for me to take his sword, at which point I demanded he remove his armor. That done, I struck the poor fellow unconscious. If only he could have figured out my brilliant plan to kill Furnius, he could have spared himself a headache, I thought sadly. Luckily, no other guards were present.<BR>
<BR>
I quickly hid myself in a storeroom to don the armor, and appropriated a closed helm from the guard's stocks. Thus, in plain daylight did I walk out of prison without being challenged by any of my former mates in the Legion. <BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>

越狱<BR>
奥戈尔·格罗-穆克 著<BR>

于是，我对弗尼乌斯的谋杀意图暴露后，我很快被关进了当地监狱的一间牢房。因为当时没有享受智力增强的好处，我变得相当困惑；我想，也许守卫出于无知误解了我的计划。我极度自信那家伙会回心转意，按照我描述的方式看待事情。但在第一周过后，我的信心彻底瓦解了。<BR>

<BR>
但随着时间的流逝，我意识到她会获释，而我不会。我很伤心，恳求她教我一些有助于我逃跑的技能。说实话，我担心她可能会偷到价值连城的东西，以至于守卫下次会直接杀了她，所以想确保她的安全。无论如何，在她获释前的几周里，她费劲地教了我一个温和的变色龙法术。<BR>
<BR>
在我独处之后，我每天在牢房里抓老鼠，然后让它们似乎消失。这不是我做过的最聪明的事，因为那些隐形老鼠自己钻进了监狱的食物储备，导致我的口粮更少了。<BR>
<BR>
实验让我学到了一些有趣的事情。虽然这个法术只在对有机和活体施放时有效，但它也会影响目标的盔甲，所以可以将其影响范围扩展得更远。虽然使用这个法术逃跑的最明显方法是将其施放在自己身上，让守卫打开门并搜查牢房，但那位卡吉特女人警告我，守卫对这种伎俩很熟悉，因此不可取。<BR>
<BR>
我挠了挠我漂亮的绿脑袋，然后想出了一个解决方案。牢房后面的墙上长着厚厚的苔藓，我对它施放了法术。我的希望实现了，因为大部分墙壁变得透明了！我兴奋地喊来守卫，告诉他有些邪恶的罪犯正试图把我弄出去。我不知道为什么会有人这么做，但谢天谢地，守卫没有提出类似的问题。相反，他看到了一堵似乎通往外面的开口墙，于是匆匆赶来打开我的牢房门，讽刺的是，这是为了防止我逃跑。<BR>
<BR>
门一打开，我就抓住了守卫，把他扔向那堵看不见的墙。不出所料，恐惧对他的震撼远大于撞击本身，因为他以为会从几层楼高的地方掉下去。这给了我足够的时间夺下他的剑，然后我命令他脱下盔甲。做完这些，我打晕了那个可怜的家伙。我悲伤地想，要是他能想明白我那个杀死弗尼乌斯的绝妙计划，他本可以免去头痛的。幸运的是，没有其他守卫在场。<BR>
<BR>
我迅速躲进一间储藏室穿上盔甲，并从守卫的库存中拿了一个封闭式头盔。就这样，我光天化日之下走出了监狱，没有任何我军团里的前同僚来盘问我。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Broken Diamonds<BR>
By Ryston Baylor<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
I remember as a young lad in Glenumbra Moors my first Broken Diamonds holiday. The big noisy festivals I remember very well -- Harvests' End, Mid Year, New Year, the Emperor's Day.<BR><BR>
All of these I have memories of that stretch back before I became truly aware of the meaning of our celebrating. On the 19th of Frost Fall, every year, my family and I would walk to a ruined castle in the middle of the wilderness, together with everyone else we knew in the Moors. Hands clutched in hands, we would form an enormous circle around the ruins, and head reverently bowed we would sing a song, the Sepharve.<BR><BR>
For years, we did this and I never asked why. It is an odd thing that normally curious children, from my experience, never ask questions about Broken Diamonds, and adults seldom volunteer information. Gradually, as we learn about our homeland through university or the prattling of ancient relatives, we come to guess and then know the meaning of Broken Diamonds.<BR><BR>
I cannot be objective as a native of Glenumbra Moors, but visitors have told me that the sorrow -- more often they use the word shame -- of the natives is almost overwhelming. There is a sense that a great and ancient crime still burns in the conscience of the people of the Moors. Though it did not happen in our lifetimes, we know that the debt is not yet paid.<BR><BR>
I refer, of course, to the murder of Her Terrible Majesty, Kintyra II, Empress of Tamriel, on the frozen morning of the 23rd of Frost Fall, in the year 3E 123.<BR><BR>
We do not know the name of the castle where she was held; we do not know the name of her murderer (though the man who ordered the murder was her cousin and usurper, Uriel III); we do not know where she was buried. But our ancestors knew that their rightful ruler was imprisoned somewhere in their land, and did nothing to help her. For that, we bear their shame.<BR><BR>
On that morning, when our great-great grandparents heard of Kintyra's death, all were stricken with horror and regret at their lack of action. All the people of Glenpoint and Glenumbra Moors searched out those responsible in every Imperial castle. They formed barriers with their bodies to hold the killer within. Flags bearing the Red Diamond of the Septim family were torn and scattered, and broken diamonds littered the snow.<BR><BR>
The song we sing every Broken Diamonds, as I mentioned before, is the Sephavre. I asked everyone in Glenumbra Moors what the meaning of the song is, for it is in Old Bretic, and each generation only knows it because they were taught by their parents. No one knew the exact meaning of the words, not even the tone and emotion the words can be easily translated. When I later talked to a scholar who gave me an accurate translation of the Sephavre, I began to understand both why our ancestors chose it as the anthem for the great injustice of the murder of Kintyra II and the sorrow that still pervades Glenumbra Moors since that dark morn.<BR><BR>
The Sephavre<BR>
Souls of our fathers, suffer deeply,<BR>
For you have led us to the dark time,<BR>
When our own souls, filled with air,<BR>
Allowed ignorance and villainy to thrive<BR>
In what used to be our land.<BR>
Howl, ancestors, howl and bring us<BR>
Memories of our conformance with evil.<BR>
We do anything we can to survive,<BR>
Giving up our minds and hearts and bodies<BR>
We will not fight, and we will be torn<BR>
And like flotsam in a whirling tide<BR>
We will be forever the agents of injustice<BR>
But we will mourn it forever.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
碎钻<BR>
里斯顿·贝勒 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
我记得我还是格伦昂布拉沼泽的一个小伙子时，第一次过碎钻节。那些盛大喧闹的节日我记得很清楚 -- 末收节、年中节、新年节、皇帝日。<BR><BR>
所有这些节日，我都能回忆起在我真正理解我们庆祝的意义之前的记忆。每年霜降月19日，我和我的家人，连同我们在沼泽认识的所有其他人，都会一起走到荒野中一座废弃的城堡。我们手牵着手，在废墟周围围成一个巨大的圆圈，虔诚地低下头，唱一首歌，塞法夫。<BR><BR>
多年来，我们一直这样做，而我从未问过为什么。这是一件奇怪的事，根据我的经验，通常好奇的孩子们从不问关于碎钻节的问题，而成年人也很少主动提供信息。渐渐地，当我们通过大学或年迈亲戚的絮叨来了解我们的家乡时，我们开始猜测，然后知道了碎钻节的含义。<BR><BR>
作为格伦昂布拉沼泽的本地人，我无法做到客观，但访客们告诉我，本地人的悲伤 -- 他们更常用的是“羞耻”这个词 -- 几乎是压倒性的。有一种感觉，一桩伟大而古老的罪行仍在沼泽人民的良知中燃烧。虽然它没有发生在我们这一代，但我们知道这笔债尚未偿还。<BR><BR>
我指的当然是第三纪元123年霜降月23日那个寒冷早晨，可怕的陛下金泰拉二世 -- 泰姆瑞尔女皇 -- 被谋杀的事件。<BR><BR>
我们不知道关押她的城堡的名字；我们不知道谋杀者的名字（尽管下令谋杀的人是她的堂兄和篡位者尤利尔三世）；我们不知道她被埋葬在哪里。但我们的祖先知道他们合法的统治者被囚禁在他们土地上的某个地方，却没有采取任何行动去帮助她。因此，我们背负着他们的耻辱。<BR><BR>
那天早上，当我们的曾祖父母们得知金泰拉的死讯时，所有人都因自己的无所作为而感到震惊和悔恨。格伦点和格伦昂布拉沼泽的所有人在每座帝国城堡中搜寻那些应负责任的人。他们用自己的身体组成路障，将凶手围在里面。绘有塞普汀家族红钻的旗帜被撕裂散落，破碎的钻石散落在雪地上。<BR><BR>
我们每年碎钻节唱的那首歌，正如我之前提到的，是塞法夫。我问过格伦昂布拉沼泽里的每个人这首歌是什么意思，因为它是用古布莱顿语写的，每一代人都只知道它是因为父母教过。没有人知道歌词的确切含义，就连可以轻易翻译出来的语气和情感也不知道。后来我和一位学者谈了谈，他给了我塞法夫的准确翻译，我才开始理解为什么我们的祖先选择它作为纪念金泰拉二世被谋杀这一不公事件的颂歌，以及自那个黑暗早晨以来仍弥漫在格伦昂布拉沼泽的悲伤。<BR><BR>
塞法夫<BR>
我们先祖的灵魂，深深受苦，<BR>
因你将我们引向黑暗时代，<BR>
当我们自己的灵魂，充满了空虚，<BR>
任由无知与邪恶滋生<BR>
在我们曾称之为家园的土地上。<BR>
嚎叫吧，祖先，嚎叫吧，带给我们<BR>
我们与邪恶同流合污的记忆。<BR>
我们竭尽所能只为生存，<BR>
放弃我们的思想、心灵和身体<BR>
我们将不会战斗，我们将被撕裂<BR>
如同漩涡中的漂浮物<BR>
我们将永远是不义的帮凶<BR>
但我们将永远为之哀悼。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Broken Diamonds<BR>
by Ryston Baylor<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
I remember as a young lad in Glenumbra Moors my first Broken Diamonds holiday. The big noisy festivals I remember very well -- Harvests' End, Mid Year, New Year, the Emperor's Day.<BR>
<BR> 
All of these I have memories of that stretch back before I became truly aware of the meaning of our celebrating. On the 19th of Frost Fall, every year, my family and I would walk to a ruined castle in the middle of the wilderness, together with everyone else we knew in the Moors. Hands clutched in hands, we would form an enormous circle around the ruins, and head reverently bowed we would sing a song, the Sepharve.<BR>
<BR> 
For years, we did this and I never asked why. It is an odd thing that normally curious children, from my experience, never ask questions about Broken Diamonds, and adults seldom volunteer information. Gradually, as we learn about our homeland through university or the prattling of ancient relatives, we come to guess and then know the meaning of Broken Diamonds.<BR>
<BR> 
I cannot be objective as a native of Glenumbra Moors, but visitors have told me that the sorrow -- more often they use the word shame -- of the natives is almost overwhelming. There is a sense that a great and ancient crime still burns in the conscience of the people of the Moors. Though it did not happen in our lifetimes, we know that the debt is not yet paid.<BR>
<BR> 
I refer, of course, to the murder of Her Terrible Majesty, Kintyra II, Emperess of Tamriel, on the frozen morning of the 23rd of Frost Fall, in the year 3E 123.<BR>
<BR> 
We do not know the name of the castle where she was held; we do not know the name of her murderer (though the man who ordered the murder was her cousin and usurper, Uriel III); we do not know where she was buried. But our ancestors knew that their rightful ruler was imprisoned somewhere in their land, and did nothing to help her. For that, we bear their shame.<BR>
<BR> 
On that morning, when our great-great grandparents heard of Kintyra's death, all were stricken with horror and regret at their lack of action. All the people of Glenpoint and Glenumbra Moors searched out those responsible in every Imperial castle. They formed barriers with their bodies to hold the killer within. Flags bearing the Red Diamond of the Septim family were torn and scattered, and broken diamonds littered the snow.<BR>
<BR> 
The song we sing every Broken Diamonds, as I mentioned before, is the Sephavre. I asked everyone in Glenumbra Moor what the meaning of the song is, for it is in Old Bretic, and each generation only knows it because they were taught by their parents. No one knew the exact meaning of the words, not even the tone and emotion the words can be easily translated. When I later talked to a scholar who gave me an accurate translation of the Sephavre, I began to understand both why our ancestors chose it as the anthem for the great injustice of the murder of Kintyra II and the sorrow that still prevades Glenumbra Moors since that dark morn.<BR>
<BR> 
The Sephavre Souls of our fathers, suffer deeply,<BR>
For you have led us to the dark time,<BR>
When our own souls, filled with air,<BR>
Allowed ignorance and villiany to thrive<BR>
In what used to be our land.<BR>
Howl, ancestors, howl and bring us<BR>
Memories of our conformance with evil.<BR>
We do anything we can to survive,<BR>
Giving up our minds and hearts and bodies<BR>
We will not fight, and we will be torn<BR>
And like flotsam in a whirling tide<BR>
We will be forever the agents of injustice<BR>
But we will mourn it forever. <BR>

Brown Book of Great House Telvanni<BR><BR>

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><BR>
Councilors of House Telvanni<BR>
Imperial Era 426<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Cabin in the Woods<BR>
Volume II<BR>
<BR>
As Told By <BR>
Mogen Son of Molag<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Late one night a few seasons ago, a soldier was returning home after several bloody battles. He decided he would save some gold and decided to cross the pine forest on foot.<BR>
<BR>
The first day of his journey was rather uneventful, the soldier stuck to the main path and kept a brisk pace. When it started getting dark he setup his bedroll, built a small fire and cooked up some rabbit he had caught. "A fine day indeed" he thought to himself as he fell asleep.<BR>
<BR>
Partway through the evening the soldier was woken up by soft sobbing in the distance. He grabbed his sword assuming it to be a bandit trick, but pretended to sleep so he could get the jump on them. After a few minutes the sobbing started moving away from his camp until he could no longer hear it. For the rest of the night he slept with one eye open.<BR>
<BR>
On day two the soldier awoke from what rotten sleep he could catch and started off through the forest at a quicker pace, intending to put distance between himself and whatever he had heard last night. As the day went on it began to rain heavy, so the soldier built himself a little shelter for the evening so he could remain dry while he slept.<BR>
<BR>
It took him a little longer to fall asleep with thoughts of the previous night fresh in his mind but he eventually slept.<BR>
<BR>
This time he awoke to a noise that sounded like it was right outside his shelter. The soldier grabbed his sword and crawled out of the shelter. In front of the fire he saw the back of a ghostly woman sobbing into her hands.<BR>
<BR>
The soldier mustered his courage and asked her what was wrong.<BR>
<BR>
No answer.<BR>
<BR>
He began to slowly approach, but before he could reach her she turned and screamed at him. The ghostly woman raised an axe and began to run at the soldier, disappearing before she made contact.<BR>
<BR>
The soldier took off into the night with just his sword in hand. He ran until the first light of dawn where he started down the road again, as fast as he could move.<BR>
<BR>
The third day was bright and sunny, but the soldier, rattled and sleepless, didn't even notice. He moved as fast as he could, trying to get through the forest before nightfall.<BR>
<BR>
As darkness began to fall he saw a cabin just off the road and thought to himself it would be a good place to hunker down for the night. After arriving at the cabin he spent some time blocking the doors and windows - nothing would get in.<BR>
<BR>
Despite his preparations, he could not sleep. He sat in what used to be the cabin's bedroom staring at the barricaded door shaking. Eventually he could keep his eyes open no longer and fell asleep.<BR>
<BR>
This time he awoke to laughing on the other side of the barricaded door. It sounded like the woman from before, but he refused to believe it was her.<BR>
<BR>
The soldier burst through the barricaded door, to find the ghostly woman staring at the ground laughing hysterically with axe in hand.<BR>
<BR>
He began to relentlessly attack the ghostly woman, but he could feel his strikes were less effective. He used a scroll of firebolt which drew a scream from her and she exploded, disappearing.<BR>
<BR>
The ordeal was over, the ghost was gone.<BR>
<BR>
The soldier slept well that night, and the next day made excellent distance through the woods. As the sun began to set he came out on the other side of the forest and looked back, remembering the days before.<BR>
<BR>
As he turned and started walking away from the woods, he could swear he heard the sobbing again.<BR>
<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
林中小屋<BR>
第二卷<BR>
<BR>
讲述者<BR>
莫拉格之子莫根<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
几个季节前的一个深夜，一名士兵在经历了几场血战之后正在返乡途中。他决定省下一些金币，于是选择步行穿越松树林。<BR>
<BR>
旅途的第一天相当平静，士兵沿着主路，步伐轻快。天开始黑下来时，他铺开睡铺，生了一小堆火，烤了他抓到的兔子。“真是美好的一天。”他想着，进入了梦乡。<BR>
<BR>
半夜时分，士兵被远处轻柔的啜泣声惊醒。他抓起剑，以为是匪徒的诡计，但假装睡着，以便出其不意。几分钟后，啜泣声开始远离他的营地，直到他再也听不见。剩下的夜晚，他一直睁着一只眼睡觉。<BR>
<BR>
第二天，士兵从勉强睡着的糟糕睡眠中醒来，加快脚步穿过森林，想离昨晚听到的东西远一点。天色渐晚，开始下起大雨，于是士兵为自己搭了一个小棚子过夜，以便睡觉时保持干燥。<BR>
<BR>
前夜的记忆犹新，他花了更长时间才入睡，但最终还是睡着了。<BR>
<BR>
这一次，他醒来时听到一个声音，听起来就在棚子外面。士兵抓起剑，爬出棚子。在火堆前，他看到了一个幽灵般女子的背影，她正捂着脸啜泣。<BR>
<BR>
士兵鼓起勇气，问她怎么了。<BR>
<BR>
没有回答。<BR>
<BR>
他开始慢慢靠近，但还没走到她面前，她转过身来冲他尖叫。幽灵般的女子举起斧头，开始向士兵冲来，但在接触之前就消失了。<BR>
<BR>
士兵手握长剑，在夜色中逃离。他一直跑到黎明第一缕曙光出现，才再次上路，以最快速度前进。<BR>
<BR>
第三天阳光明媚，但惊慌失措、彻夜未眠的士兵甚至没有注意到。他尽可能快地赶路，试图在夜幕降临前穿过森林。<BR>
<BR>
天色渐暗时，他看到路边有一座小屋，心想这是个过夜的好地方。到达小屋后，他花了一些时间堵住门窗 -- 这样什么都进不来了。<BR>
<BR>
尽管做了准备，他还是无法入睡。他坐在曾是卧室的地方，盯着堵住的门，浑身发抖。最终，他再也撑不住眼皮，睡着了。<BR>
<BR>
这一次，他醒来时听到堵住的门另一边传来笑声。听起来像之前的那个女人，但他拒绝相信那是她。<BR>
<BR>
士兵冲过堵住的门，发现那个幽灵般的女子正盯着地面，歇斯底里地大笑，手里拿着斧头。<BR>
<BR>
他开始无情地攻击那个幽灵女子，但他能感觉到自己的攻击效果不佳。他使用了一张火弹卷轴，她发出一声尖叫，然后爆炸消失了。<BR>
<BR>
磨难结束了，鬼魂消失了。<BR>
<BR>
那天晚上士兵睡得很好，第二天在林中顺利赶路。太阳开始落山时，他走出了森林的另一边，回头望去，回想着过去的日子。<BR>
<BR>
当他转身离开森林时，他敢发誓他又听到了啜泣声。<BR>
<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Cavern Door <BR>
Unknown <BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Haldin approached the cavern door, cautiously drawing his blade as he went. It was a mild day, and the sun shown brightly upon the passageway. As Haldin made ready to enter, he ran through every item in his pack to make sure that every item he would need was in place. After rummaging through several scrolls, a number of potions and antidotes, and various other oddments, he straightened up and reached for the door handle. Suddenly there was a scrambling from the bushes behind him. Haldin spun around, his pack swinging free of his shoulders and landing on the soft earth near his feet. <BR>
<BR>
What he saw next made his body go numb, for there in the bushes were not one, but three ragged, terrible looking creatures. Haldin had heard tell of such monsters, and knew them for Vermai at once. The Vermai held their noses to the air, as though searching for a lost scent. Haldin stood stock-still, for it was common knowledge that Vermai relied heavily on their olfactory senses to pinpoint prey, having terrible eyesight. <BR>
<BR>
Luckily, the wind blew into Haldin's face, and away from the beasts, masking his scent. Then, an idea struck him. Moving slowly, Haldin reached into his fallen pack, extracting a scroll of glowing parchment. He read the incantation on it, concentrated, and then bellowed the words aloud, thrusting his hands forward and directing the spell toward the Vermai. Then, releasing his concentration, the spell soared forward connecting with all three creatures at once. The scroll crumbled to dust in Haldin's hands. <BR>
<BR>
Throwing down the ashes, he drew his sword from the dirt where it had landed when the spell was cast, and strode forward. The spell had been a successful one, paralyzing all three Vermai before they were aware of it. Haldin came within a few feet of the first creature, which stood as though frozen, unblinking. He thrust his blade into it, and with a terrible screech, it fell forward dead, for the blade was enchanted with a powerful magical frost. Just as Haldin moved his sword against the second animal, there came a rough growling from the bushes to his left. Without even glancing in the direction of the sound, Haldin knew he had not paralyzed every Vermai in the area. To make matters worse, the Vermai he had attacked were beginning to stir, Haldin could see their eyes darting about in their sockets, peering at him with intent. <BR>
<BR>
There was nothing to do but run. With a huge leap, Haldin overtook the nearest ledge, sliding nearly twenty paces, but when he reached the bottom he was already on his feet again, tearing across the windy grasslands. Soon the sounds of pursuit began to greet Haldin's ears; his mind was racing as fast as his tired feet. His experience with such creatures was minimal, and he had learned most of what he did know not first hand, but from the tales his older brother Heldin, a seasoned adventurer, had told him as a child. Yet the sounds of the Vermai were closing in on him. Haldin had been running for nearly ten minutes, and his endurance was beginning to give out. <BR>
<BR>
Just as he was considering standing and fighting as best as he could, the sound of pursuit suddenly mingled with that of running water. Hope filled Haldin, and he burst forward with newfound strength. He knew that if he could only reach the source of that sound he would be saved, for the Vermai despised water. Then he saw it, a small, glistening body of water no more than fifty yards away. Haldin dashed towards it, the Vermai snapping at his heels. But just as he reached the shores of the small lake, they overtook him, and Haldin fought until he was knee-deep in the water, but his heavy iron shield was weighing him down immensely. <BR>
<BR>
Suddenly, the largest Vermai delivered to Haldin a savage blow to the leg, and losing his balance, Haldin fell into the water and was completely submersed. Yet as he fell, his sword slipped from his hands and flew into the air. As it landed in the water, the frost enchantment it carried was released, and the surface of the lake was covered in a thick sheet of ice. Haldin was trapped beneath the surface, but the Vermai could not break through the ice to continue their attack. Holding his breath, Haldin abandoned his heavy shield and swam underwater to the other side of the lake. Then, unsheathing a handy silver dagger, he hacked an opening in the ice large enough to clamber through and onto the warm beach. <BR>
<BR>
The Vermai, seeing their prey again, began to charge across the ice at Haldin, but just as they were halfway across, the enchantment wore off, and screeching loudly they were plunged into the lake. Then Haldin, seeing his chance, hauled his bonemold bow from his back and loosed an arrow for each Vermai, eliminating all three as they struggled to escape the water. At last, exhausted, relieved, and his muscles quivering, he lay down on the sand to rest. <BR>
<BR>
When strength had returned to his fatigued muscles, Haldin thought about lighting a fire and making camp, but alas, he realized that he had left his tinderbox, along with his other supplies, back at the place where the Vermai had attacked him. Deciding to leave right away, Haldin scooped his shield out of the water, but could not find his sword which had drifted down the stream when its enchantment was spent. After searching the bank in vain, he gave up and began his slow trek back to the cavern door. <BR>
<BR>
When at last he arrived, Haldin stooped to pick up his pack from the ground, but there was movement behind him. Looking wildly about, Haldin drew his small silver dagger, his only remaining weapon, just in time to see a Scrib scramble from the bushes and into a nearby fissure. Laughing, Haldin sheathed his blade once more, and without another look at the worn cavern door, grabbed his pack and began the long journey home.<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
瓦玛们再次看到猎物，开始穿过冰面向哈尔丁冲去，但就在它们跑到一半时，附魔失效了，它们尖叫着掉进了湖里。哈尔丁看到机会，从背上取下骨模弓，向每只瓦玛射出一箭，将它们三只全部消灭，它们正在水中挣扎。最后，他精疲力竭，如释重负，肌肉颤抖着，躺在沙滩上休息。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
The Caves of Ice<BR>
<BR>
Sighing, Thoran Frosthammer, a large boy for his age, undressed himself and slid into his warm, straw bed. Gazing out the window, he imagined himself as the warrior that he saw in the stars, battling creatures ten times his height, and saving villages from impending doom. Thoran liked that word, impending, ever since he heard it he used it often. Sighed, he mumbled "I wish I could be like you" in musing tones.<BR>
<BR>
A clatter awoke him from his daydreams. It had come from outside so he looked out the window again. What he saw would haunt him to his grave. Beasts, wild, misshapen, and horrible they were. They were marching toward his house!<BR>
<BR>
Immediately, he ran to awake his father, who was a rather good huntsman and skilled with a spear. Grabbing his weapon of choice from its place on the rack, Rhoran Frosthammer, father of Thoran Frosthammer, bolted to the door and waited. Silence.<BR>
<BR>
Suddenly the door shattered like glass and a beast so vicious as to chill even a Nord's blood appeared at the door. "Balouk-Mir" was all Thoran's father could say. It smiled without humor but with maddened insanity at Rhoran, and in one swift motion ripped the stout man into two bloody pieces with its bare hands.<BR>
<BR>
Thoran looked on in horror, shocked at the sight he had just witnessed, his mind unable to accept what had just happened. The beast looked down at Thoran, tilted his head menacingly and muttered something about Thoran's death would be a blessing to him; whatever it said Thoran wasn't listening.<BR>
<BR>
The beast moved on along with his horrible soldiers, into the house. Even as that happened the boy never moved. Not until he heard a strangled scream that was cut off by silence. The scream came from his mother! Immediately picking up his father's spear, Thoran ran to his mother's room. But when he got there and entered the room, all he saw was blood smeared across every inch of the room, and the beasts were gone.<BR>
<BR>
Thoran, recovering from his shock and reliving what happened, let out an anguished cry, which was choked off by a strangled sob.<BR>
<BR>
The last thing Thoran Frosthammer did before he collapsed was gasp out, "I will find you monster," he sniffed hoarsely, "and I will kill you..."<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
Thoran Frosthammer gripped his warhammer tighter and surveyed his surroundings. He stood at the heart of the Ice Caves and as the name implies he was standing in a cavern made completely out of ice. The caves had been cut into the mountains long ago by a dreadful daedra. Balouk-Mir. Thoran had been chasing this daedra for many years after the beast slaughtered his entire family in Snowhawk.<BR>
<BR>
Finally, the vengeful Thoran Frosthammer, lord and chief of his village and father of two sons, stepped into the lair of Balouk-Mir son of Sheogorath. The crystalline altar was the first thing Thoran noticed, ten feet width and breadth, it could "comfortably" fit a human atop it with room to spare. That was probably what it was for judging by the red blood now frozen and crystallized. Beside this altar on either end stood two large, iron braziers, one carved in the likeness of the daedra standing at the altar: Duke Balouk-Mir.<BR>
<BR>
Thoran, having not seen him standing there just moments before, blinked away the fuzziness around his tired eyes, cursed himself for falling into one of Balouk-Mir's mind tricks, and gripped the handle of his warhammer even tighter still.<BR>
<BR>
"Good evening Nord," the daedra breathed, his voice smooth and even, "come and have a cup of tea." he offered and gesture toward a table in the corner of the room bristling with life now that it was set with tea, cream, moon sugar, and small cakes, all illuminated by a three-candled holder in the middle.<BR>
<BR>
Again Thoran cursed himself for a fool for being the victim of Balouk-Mir's tricks.<BR>
<BR>
Ignoring the gesture of "hospitality," the now-steaming Nord yelled. "Balouk-Mir, son of Sheogorath, you have invaded my land, destroyed my livestock, murdered my family," Thoran took a second to regain his composure as the last word faltered into a sob. "And you dare to disrespect me so."<BR>
<BR>
The daedra may not have even heard him as he replied casually, "My dear Nord," he began, "do you really want to kill me? If this is true, I beg you Nord, come strike me down," he mocked.<BR>
<BR>
Thoran rushed the daedra, his hammer whistled through the air... and stopped with violent force as it struck what hadn't been there moments before: a solid ice wall that sprang up protectively around the daedra. Balouk-Mir laughed, while Thoran massaged his stinging fingers resulting from the unexpectedly early impact, a vicious, deep, baritone voice, contradicting the previous voice he wore.<BR>
<BR>
"Typical," he said simply, "What would be the most ironic way for you to die?" he mused. Seeming to reach a conclusion, the daedra smiled.<BR>
<BR>
Horrified, the Nordic lord's head darted around for an answer as he realized that, yes, something was definitely wrong. He began to shiver, and a bluish glow emitted from his skin. The glow intensified and spread, as did the shivers.<BR>
<BR>
"What's happening to me?" he yelled, feeling the cold trying to make its way through his natural resistance and grasp his neck with frozen fingers.<BR>
<BR>
As Thoran dropped to his knees, the coldness of the cavern finally touching the resilient Nord, Balouk-Mir cackled, "Tell me Nord, do you fear the cold?"<BR>
<BR>
Through supreme effort, Thoran picked himself off of the ground, and gathered up his remaining strength to retort, "I fear not what shouldn't touch me." he said hoarsely, the coldness of the cave freezing his lungs.<BR>
<BR>
Thoran glanced around and noticed that the glow emitting from his skin seemed to have effected the table set with tea, and noticed that the tea was now frozen. The candle had gone out and the cream crystallized, the cave's frozen touch grasping them as well being no longer protected by the daedra's magic. Adding all of this in his mind Thoran looked up at the daedra, now laughing madly, and suddenly realized what he must do.<BR>
<BR>
"Tell me Daedra," Thoran Frosthammer whispered, able to do little else through his frozen throat, "do you fear the cold?" Grabbing his hammer from off the ground, Thoran Frosthammer, Lord of Snowhawk, let loose a horrible cry and rushed Balouk-Mir whirling his weapon.<BR>
<BR>
As the glow touched the icy barrier surrounding the daedra, it shattered as if struck by a mighty blow, the daedra's protection from the cold was broken!<BR>
<BR>
Realizing what he had done, Balouk-Mir's eyes shot wide and he screamed in terror as the glow, the very same spell he had used to kill his enemy now touched him and he felt the grip of ice as his vision went black.<BR>

冰之洞穴<BR>
<BR>
索兰·霜锤叹了口气，脱下衣服，滑进温暖的干草床。他凝视窗外，想象自己是他在星辰中看到的那个战士，与比他高十倍的生物战斗，拯救村庄于迫在眉睫的厄运。索兰喜欢“迫在眉睫”这个词，自从他听到后就经常使用。他叹了口气，若有所思地喃喃道：“我真希望能像你一样。”<BR>

<BR>
索兰惊恐地看着，被眼前的一幕震惊了，他的头脑无法接受刚刚发生的事。野兽低头看着索兰，威胁地歪了歪头，咕哝着说索兰的死对他来说是一种恩赐；无论它说了什么，索兰都没在听。<BR>
<BR>
那头野兽连同它可怕的士兵们一起继续前进，进了房子。即使在那时，男孩也没有动。直到他听到一声被寂静切断的窒息尖叫。尖叫声来自他的母亲！索兰立刻捡起他父亲的长矛，冲向母亲的房间。但当他到达并进入房间时，他只看到鲜血涂满了房间的每一寸，野兽们已经不见了。<BR>
<BR>
索兰从震惊中恢复过来，重温了刚刚发生的一切，发出一声痛苦的哭喊，被一声哽咽的抽泣扼住了。<BR>
<BR>
索兰·霜锤在倒下之前做的最后一件事是气喘吁吁地说：“我会找到你的，怪物，”他嘶哑地抽着鼻子，“我会杀了你......”<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
索兰·霜锤握紧了他的战锤，审视着周围的环境。他站在冰之洞穴的中心，顾名思义，他正站在一个完全由冰构成的洞穴中。这些洞穴是很久以前由一头可怕的迪德拉 -- 巴鲁克-米尔 -- 开凿在山中的。在那头野兽在雪鹰城屠杀了他的全家之后，索兰追捕这头迪德拉已经很多年了。<BR>
<BR>
最后，复仇的索兰·霜锤 -- 他村子的领主和族长，两个儿子的父亲 -- 踏入了谢尔格拉斯之子巴鲁克-米尔的巢穴。索兰首先注意到的是那个水晶祭坛，十英尺见方，可以“舒适地”容纳一个人在上面，还有剩余空间。从上面现已冻结结晶的红色血液判断，那很可能就是它的用途。祭坛两端各立着一个大铁火盆，其中一个雕刻成站在祭坛旁的迪德拉 -- 巴鲁克-米尔公爵的样貌。<BR>
<BR>
索兰刚才还没看到他站在那里，他眨了眨眼睛，驱散疲惫双眼周围的模糊，咒骂自己落入了巴鲁克-米尔的思维把戏之一，并把战锤握得更紧了。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
索兰再次咒骂自己是个傻瓜，成了巴鲁克-米尔把戏的受害者。<BR>
<BR>
无视那“好客”的表示，这个现在怒气冲冲的诺德人大喊道：“巴鲁克-米尔，谢尔格拉斯之子，你入侵了我的土地，毁了我的牲畜，杀了我的家人，”说到最后一个词时，索兰的声音哽咽成一声抽泣，他停顿了一下，重新镇定下来。“你还敢如此不尊重我。”<BR>
<BR>
迪德拉甚至可能没听到他的话，他漫不经心地回答：“我亲爱的诺德人，”他开始说，“你真的想杀我吗？如果这是真的，我恳求你，诺德人，来打倒我吧。”他嘲弄道。<BR>
<BR>
索兰冲向迪德拉，他的锤子呼啸着划过空气......然后猛地停了下来，击中了刚才还不存在的东西：一道坚固的冰墙，在迪德拉周围保护性地升起。巴鲁克-米尔大笑起来，而索兰则揉着他因意外过早撞击而刺痛的手指，一个恶毒的、低沉的男中音，与他之前的声音截然不同。<BR>
<BR>
“典型，”他简单地说，“对你来说最讽刺的死法是什么？”他沉思道。似乎得出了结论，迪德拉笑了。<BR>
<BR>
惊恐万分的诺德领主急忙四下寻找答案，他意识到，是的，绝对出问题了。他开始发抖，皮肤发出蓝色的光芒。光芒越来越强，不断扩散，颤抖也越来越剧烈。<BR>
<BR>
“我怎么了？”他喊道，感到寒冷正试图突破他天生的抵抗力，用冰冻的手指扼住他的喉咙。<BR>
<BR>
当索兰跪倒在地，洞穴的寒冷最终触及了这位坚韧的诺德人时，巴鲁克-米尔咯咯地笑了：“告诉我，诺德人，你害怕寒冷吗？”<BR>
<BR>
凭借超凡的努力，索兰从地上爬起来，聚集起残余的力量反驳道：“我不怕不该碰我的东西。”他嘶哑地说，洞穴的寒冷冻结了他的肺。<BR>
<BR>
索兰环顾四周，注意到从他皮肤上发出的光芒似乎影响了那张摆着茶的桌子，茶现在冻结了。蜡烛熄灭了，奶油结晶了，洞穴的冰冻触感也抓住了它们，它们不再受迪德拉魔法的保护。索兰在心里权衡了这一切，抬头看向迪德拉 -- 它现在正在疯狂地大笑 -- 突然意识到自己必须做什么。<BR>
<BR>
“告诉我，迪德拉，”索兰·霜锤低语道，他冰冻的喉咙几乎说不出别的话了，“你害怕寒冷吗？”他从地上抓起战锤，索兰·霜锤，雪鹰城领主，发出一声可怕的战吼，挥舞着武器冲向巴鲁克-米尔。<BR>
<BR>
当光芒触及环绕迪德拉的冰障时，冰障如同被猛击般碎裂，迪德拉抵御寒冷的保护被打破了！<BR>
<BR>
意识到自己做了什么，巴鲁克-米尔的双眼猛地睁大，他惊恐地尖叫起来，因为那光芒 -- 正是他用来杀死敌人的同一个法术 -- 现在触及了他，他感到冰之紧握，视野随之变黑。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
[在这个故事的某些版本中，据说索兰通过杀死敌人打破了咒语，但大多数学者认为，如果这个故事是真的，那么他们俩都还留在冰之洞穴下方，因隧道可怕的坍塌而失踪，像雕像一样被冻结。]<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
The Collected Ysmritis
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR><BR>
A collection of tales concerning the Ysmirs or "Dragons of the North", referring to those heroic Nords exalted by Shor himself. Though the term is best known as a title of Tiber Septim during his conquest of the north, its usage stretches back to the beginnings of Nordic history. In keeping with the mythic tradition of Shor's deep hatred for everything elven, the most obvious shared trait amongst the Ysmirs is their great thirst for and success at elf-killing - whether the title precedes such slaughter, or vice-versa, is historically ambiguous.<BR>
<BR>
Unlike the saints of Cyrodiil or the ancestor-worship of the Dark Elves, the figures of Nordic legend are timeless and quite untethered from notions of causality. Whether this is due to the enduring immediacy of their legends or the temporal inconsistency of the entire mythic cycle is left to the individual scholar. Regardless, though they have been listed here in something approaching a chronological order, traditionally the Ysmritis drift timelessly around one another.<BR><BR>
Songs of the Return (abridged)<BR>
[The first Ysmriti is built of excerpts taken from the famous and ancient Songs of the Return. These selected passages exalt Ysgramor as the first Nord to claim the knowing of Ysmir, and the Harbinger who led the Nords back to Tamriel. His mighty axe Wuuthrad, practised at the killing of Snow Elves, had been forged by his son Yngol, greatest smith of the Atmorans and captain of the Harakk. Collecting the ebony tears wept by his father, as Shor wept during the first war, Yngol forged an axe of pure sorrow that the Harbinger might bring the vengeance of Atmora upon the plunderers of Saarthal. Although the Songs of the Return are uncounted and many, the Ysmriti of Ysgramor forms the core of early Nordic canon.]<BR>
<BR>
The Sea-Drake's Hoard<BR>
[The second Ysmriti is an ancient oar-song concerning the Dreaded Bomundl, Dragon of the Sea - one that is sung to this day by sailors on the Sea of Ghosts. True to Nordic form, the song is eye-wateringly crass and given to quite pornographic descriptions of both sex and violence, which goes some way to explaining its enduring popularity. Bomundl was an Atmoran fleet-jarl and reaver whose ships followed Ysgramor out of Jylkurfyk, but rather than remain in the north he chose to raid down the western coast of Tamriel. For the fury of the storms he could Shout and for his celebrated atrocities against the Sea Elves of Pyandonea, he was given the knowing of Ysmir. The song itself, legend goes, will reveal the location of Bomundl's improbable hoard, though not even the Woodland Man has sung it under the right stars and on the right wind, and thus the treasure remains unclaimed.]<BR>
<BR>
76 Oaths of the Wolf-Pants<BR>
[The third Ysmriti is a collection oaths that were, so the tradition goes, sworn upon the famous breeches of High King Harald Hairy-Breeks. Like Ysgramor and Bomundl, Harald was a mythic Atmoran who came to Tamriel during the time of the Return, although he alone survived from myth into the historical record. The knowing of Ysmir is conferred upon him as the seventy-sixth oath, sworn by Shor himself as the increasingly-improbable pledges of Harald's seventy-five thanes, jarls and kings - and the attendant howling of his trousers - supposedly draws the dead god's notice. Harald's reign notably encompasses the final purging of the Snow Elves from Skyrim.]<BR>
<BR>
Shor's Tongue<BR>
[The fourth Ysmriti concerns High King Wulfharth, famous Nordic ruler and, until Talos, best-known of the Ysmirs. The song relates his accession to the throne of the Old Empire and how he comes by the knowing of Ysmir. Supposedly the strength of his thu'um is so great that he cannot verbally take the oaths of office, and his first act as High King is to Shout the Alessians out of Skyrim. For his deeds, and ashamed "for so long indulging the monkey", his vassals acclaim him the Tongue of Shor's own warband and the Ysmir of their age. There exists another obscure song which poetically vindicates their devotion, with Wulfharth's dying Shout - recorded as "Licking the Devils from the Great Dead Mouth" - giving his dead self form as the literal tongue of Shor during the final invasion of Morrowind.]<BR>
<BR>
Storm-Dragon-Elder-Son-Head<BR>
[The fifth Ysmriti is a song of Talos, told in the neo-Nordic style popular in the Bards College of Haafingar (and generally unpopular beyond). Nonetheless, it is the first and thus seminal song of Tiber Septim's conquests, which has earned its disjointed and shouty lines a place in the Ysmrithic tradition. Talos is the dragon-headed scion of Atmora, followed on his solitary journey from the Nords' ancient home by a mighty stormcloud that seemingly - the song is decidedly abstract - serves to tether him to the fury of the gods. Upon taking the Ruby Throne, the knowing of Ysmir slips through the slit in his voiceless throat and all Nords know that he is truly the exalted of Shor. Talos achieved the unthinkable in shattering the twin elven bastions of Morrowind and the Aldmeri Dominion, forever subjugating the races of elves to a son of the Sky.]<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
伊斯米尔传说集
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR><BR>
这是一个关于伊斯米尔或“北方之龙”的传说集，指的是那些被朔尔本人所尊崇的英雄诺德人。尽管这个称号最广为人知的是泰伯·塞普汀在征服北方期间的头衔，但其使用可以追溯到诺德历史的开端。与朔尔对所有精灵事物的深仇大恨的神话传统一致，伊斯米尔们最明显的共同特征是对猎杀精灵的极大渴望和成功 -- 究竟是称号先于此类杀戮，还是反之，在历史上是模糊的。<BR>
<BR>
与西罗帝尔的圣徒或暗精灵的祖先崇拜不同，诺德传说中的形象是永恒的，与因果关系的概念相当脱节。这是由于他们传说持久的即时性，还是整个神话周期的时间不一致性，留给各个学者自行判断。无论如何，尽管这里列出的大致是按时间顺序排列，传统上伊斯米尔传说集是永恒地相互游离的。<BR><BR>
回归之歌（节选）<BR>
[第一篇伊斯米尔传说由取自著名古老的《回归之歌》的节选构成。这些选段赞颂伊斯格拉谟为第一个自称知晓伊斯米尔的诺德人，以及带领诺德人返回泰姆瑞尔的先驱。他那用于屠杀雪精灵的强大战斧伍斯拉德，是由他的儿子英格尔锻造的，英格尔是阿特莫拉最伟大的铁匠和哈拉克号的船长。英格尔收集了他父亲流下的黑檀泪 -- 如同朔尔在第一次战争中哭泣那样 -- 锻造了一把纯粹悲伤的战斧，以便先驱能将阿特莫拉的复仇带给萨塔尔的掠夺者。尽管《回归之歌》数量众多、难以计数，但伊斯格拉谟的伊斯米尔传说构成了早期诺德经典的核心。]<BR>
<BR>
海龙之宝<BR>
[第二篇伊斯米尔传说是一首古老的划桨歌，关于可怕的海洋之龙博蒙德尔 -- 至今仍被幽魂之海的水手们传唱。忠于诺德风格，这首歌粗俗得令人瞠目，包含相当露骨的性和暴力描写，这在一定程度上解释了它持久的流行。博蒙德尔是一位阿特莫拉的舰队领主和掠夺者，他的船只跟随伊斯格拉谟离开吉尔库尔菲克，但他没有留在北方，而是选择沿着泰姆瑞尔西海岸掠夺。因为他能用吐姆召唤风暴的愤怒，以及他对派安多尼亚海精灵的著名暴行，他被赐予了伊斯米尔的知晓。传说，这首歌本身将揭示博蒙德尔那不可思议的宝藏的位置，但即使是森地者也未能在正确的星辰和风向之下唱过它，因此宝藏至今无人认领。]<BR>
<BR>
狼裤七十六誓<BR>
[第三篇伊斯米尔传说是一组誓言的集合，传统上，这些誓言是在至高王哈拉尔德·毛裤的著名马裤上宣誓的。像伊斯格拉谟和博蒙德尔一样，哈拉尔德是一位神话般的阿特莫拉人，在回归时期来到泰姆瑞尔，尽管只有他从神话中幸存下来，进入了历史记录。伊斯米尔的知晓作为第七十六个誓言授予他，由朔尔本人宣誓，因为哈拉尔德的七十五位领主、领主和国王们越来越难以置信的承诺 -- 以及随之而来的他裤子的嚎叫 -- 据说引起了这位死去之神的注意。哈拉尔德的统治尤其包含了从天际最终清除雪精灵。]<BR>
<BR>
朔尔之舌<BR>
[第四篇伊斯米尔传说关于至高王武尔夫哈斯，著名的诺德统治者，在塔洛斯之前，是最著名的伊斯米尔。这首歌讲述了他登上旧帝国王位以及他如何获得伊斯米尔的知晓。据说他吐姆的力量如此强大，以至于他无法口头宣誓就职，他作为至高王的第一件事就是用吐姆将阿莱西亚教派赶出天际。因为他的事迹，并羞愧于“沉溺于猿猴”，他的封臣们称他为朔尔战帮之舌和他们时代的伊斯米尔。还有另一首晦涩的歌曲，诗意地证明了他们的虔诚，武尔夫哈斯临终的吐姆 -- 记录为“从伟大的死亡之口舔出恶魔” -- 使他在晨风最后入侵期间，以死者的形态成为朔尔真正的舌头。]<BR>
<BR>
风暴-龙-长者-子-首<BR>
[第五篇伊斯米尔传说是一首关于塔洛斯的歌，以哈芬加吟游诗人学院流行的新诺德风格讲述（通常在学院之外不受欢迎）。尽管如此，它是第一首，因此也是泰伯·塞普汀征服的开创性歌曲，其断断续续和喊叫般的诗句在伊斯米尔传说传统中赢得了一席之地。塔洛斯是阿特莫拉的龙首后裔，在他从诺德古老家园的孤独旅程中，一朵强大的风暴云跟随着他 -- 这首歌相当抽象 -- 似乎将他与神祇的愤怒联系在一起。登上红钻王座后，伊斯米尔的知晓从他无声喉咙的裂口滑出，所有诺德人都知道他是朔尔真正尊崇之人。塔洛斯粉碎了晨风和先祖神洲这对精灵堡垒，实现了不可思议的壮举，永远将精灵种族置于天空之子之下。]<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>THE DEATH OF ARTHEIM, SON OF CARC<BR>$0A$0A<BR>$0A$0ANow Artheim son of Carc ruled the lands of Kvatch from one end to the other, that is, from Gottsha West to the holds of the Weald that bordered on Skingrad. He had a son, named Banathil, who had a son, named Irroth the Lark. All were strong men, skilled with weapons, crowned with red gold, virtues of Colovia incarnate. Now Artheim was a proud and pious king, and the state of the Empire, left in the hands of the cowardly men of Nibeth, saddened him deeply. So one day he rode out with the best of his men to contest the Inner City. He rode, until he reached the banks of the great lake Rumare, and saw the eight islands, the brightly painted walls, the towers beyond number, and he saw the golden-white spire of the Emperors. So said he to his men, "There we will go, and bring piety and righteousness, and all who follow me will be rewarded handsomely, they will receive eight red bulls, and a boar's weight in red gold, and a hands-length of godsblood from the Inner City's vaults." We seek passage to the Inner City, to visit its shrines and temples, decorated with fountains and garlands of flowers, and to bathe in the waters of the lake Rumare, as is the custom in our times." And Rein Manellis believed nont one word, but he feared the king of Kvatch, whose host was much greater than his own, and whose prowess with sword or bow far outpaced his own. "Well-met, son of Carc," he replied, "Sadly, you may not enter the city at this moment, for within its brightly painted walls and towers beyond number there rages a plague, the likes of which I have never seen: each sword that is brought into the city will spring into the hand of its owner, to lash out to his companions, and all drink that is brought into the city will dry out in a day, so that all are thirsty, and each horse that enters the city will break free, and drown itself in the lake Rumare. But follow me, Artheim Hill-Born, for I camp here in a palace on the lake's edge, it has been built for me by the moths of the Nibeth, and within it are enough beds for three times your company, and enough food and wine too."<BR>$0A$0A<BR>$0A$0AAnd so Artheim and his men retreated into the moth-palace of Rein Manellis, where they feasted until deep into the night. """<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>阿尔塞姆，卡克之子，之死<BR>

当时，卡克之子阿尔塞姆统治着科瓦奇的全部领土，即从西戈查一直到与斯金格拉德接壤的森林领地。他有一个儿子，名叫巴纳西尔，巴纳西尔有一个儿子，名叫云雀伊罗斯。他们都是强壮的人，精通武器，头戴红金王冠，是科洛维亚美德的化身。阿尔塞姆是一位骄傲而虔诚的国王，而帝国被尼贝斯的懦弱之人掌控的现状，令他深感痛心。于是有一天，他带着他最精锐的士兵出发去争夺内城。他策马前行，直到抵达鲁玛雷大湖的岸边，看到了八座岛屿，色彩鲜艳的城墙，数不清的塔楼，以及那座金色与白色相间的皇帝尖塔。他对部下说：“我们要去那里，带去虔诚和正义，所有跟随我的人都会得到丰厚的奖赏，他们将得到八头红牛，相当于一头野猪重量的红金，以及内城金库中一臂长的神血。”他的部下们欢呼着跟随着他，而这就是四十八次内城徒劳冲锋之一。<BR>

<BR>

于是，阿尔塞姆和他的部队退入赖因·马内利斯的飞蛾宫殿，在那里他们盛宴直到深夜。然而，赖因·马内利斯心中藏着背叛，在盛宴的高潮时刻，他给他的手下发出了一个秘密信号，于是所有人都站了起来，杀死了坐在旁边的人，赖因·马内利斯也杀死了坐在他旁边的阿尔塞姆，就这样，所有科瓦奇人都被杀害了。然后，尼贝斯人带着铜碗铜碟出来，接住阿尔塞姆的鲜血，因为他们珍视国王之血，用于他们秘制的毒药。<BR>

<BR>

当阿尔塞姆的死讯传到他的儿子巴纳西尔那里时，他为他的死而哀悼，云雀伊罗斯也为他的死而哀悼。伊罗斯对他的父亲说：“我们必须对那个愚蠢的乞丐国王赖因·马内利斯发动大战。”但他的父亲说：“我们不能，因为我们所有的伟大战士都在背叛中被杀了，雪之布鲁马斯路途遥远，途中还有斯金格拉德和科洛尔王国，它们对我们都不友善，而且，赖因·马内利斯有阴险的尼贝斯人的保护，他们的人数是我们的一百倍，并且知道秘制的毒药。”但伊罗斯心中怒火中烧，他的思绪充满了复仇。<BR>

<BR>
