"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Cultural Eras of the Nords<BR>
by Elonwe of Lillandril
<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Preface <BR>
Scholars of Tamrielic history, myself included, are generally fond of the Standard Era calendar, both out of a habit inculcated from our earliest years of education and from the convenience of a shared framework. Whilst understandable, this framework is somewhat limited for studies of individual cultures and peoples across Tamriel, as an epoch is not necessarily the same at the continental level as it is at the local. It is therefore my hope with this volume to provide an alternate, compatible framework for understanding Nordic history and culture, based on the evolution of both since the time of the Return.<BR>
<BR>
CE1 - Totemic Period (ME? - ME?) <BR>
The Totemic Period concerns the earliest history of the Nords, from the establishment of old Atmora to Ysgramor's Return and beyond. No written records from this period are thought to have been kept, but a strong oral tradition survives in animal fables and fairy tales. <BR>
<BR>
Culturally, this was a time of nature spirits and tribal totems that began to coalesce into a prototypical version of the contemporary Nordic pantheon. Thus, there is rarely "Shor" or "Alduin" in this time, but there are recurring tales of wily foxes deceiving mighty dragons and so on. Any book of traditional Nordic fables will give an illustration of these sorts of stories. <BR>
<BR>
CE2 - Rippling Kingdoms Period (ME? - 1E139) <BR>
The Rippling Kingdoms Period is my private name for the age, beginning in the late Merethic Era, when the Nords began to establish themselves as a significant political force on Tamriel. Dubious sources and a lack of rigorous record-keeping mean that exact dates are difficult to pin down, although it encompasses the majority of the conflict between the Falmer and the Nords. <BR>
<BR>
This era marks the beginning of the Nordic poetic cycle, celebrating the mythic kings and mighty heroes of this age. It is also when the Atmoran totem spirits begin to anthropomorphise into the current Nordic pantheon, and the testing gods of old Atmora are fully identified with the elf-demons of later myth - without doubt a product of the brutal wars fought between Nords and Falmer. <BR>
<BR>
CE3 - Old Empire Period (1E139 - 1E369) <BR>
The Old Empire Period begins with the twin victories of High King Harald Hand-Free - also known as the mythic hero Harald Hairy-Breeks - over the last of the Falmer and the Dragon Cult, leading to the declaration of an independent Kingdom of Skyrim. High King Harald is the first truly historic Nordic ruler, and this is a period of great record-keeping and historical enquiry for the Nordic peoples. It also encompasses the duration of the First Empire of the Nords, which covered much of Morrowind, Cyrodiil and High Rock - a time which, though brief, remains fondly and proudly remembered by the Nords of today. <BR>
<BR>
It is in this period that High King Harald's great codification of Nordic mythology, the High King's Vedda, took place. The death of Shor and the realm of Sovngarde were introduced into the mythic cycle at this time, and tales of conquest and victory feature prominently. Arguably, the Old Empire Period (save for Alessian encroachment at its close) is the seminal age for Nordic mythology and the poetic cycle, which is doubly impressive given its short but energetic span. <BR>
<BR>
CE4 - Broken Sky Period (1E369 - 1E2703) <BR>
Following the death of High King Borgas in 1E369, the First Empire disintegrated and there followed a long age of internecine conflict I term the Broken Sky. The Alessian Order aggresively suppressed traditional Nordic religion, especially in the south and east, and western Skyrim was largely overrun by the Direnni. Following the defeat and loss of Morrowind to the First Council, Jurgen Windcaller founded the Way of the Voice as a means of studying and perfecting the thu'um, which had previously been seen by the Nords as innate. <BR>
<BR>
Poetry and mythology from this period is noticeably darker and more esoteric, focusing on both internal strife of the gods and the crimes of the elf-demons. Semi-historical tales of Wulfharth, avatar of Shor, are especially prevalent during the Broken Sky, concerning his exhortations to recover both the First Empire and the heart of Shor from Morrowind. Following his coronation as High King, Wulfharth was able to reverse territorial losses against the Direnni and purge the Alessians, but was unable to reclaim the First Empire and Skyrim ultimately faded from power. <BR>
<BR>
CE5 - Imperial Protectorate Period (1E2703 - 2E855) <BR>
Skyrim was peacefully integrated into the Reman Empire in 1E2703, beginning the age of the Nords as vassals of a southern liege. Even beyond the collapse of the Second Cyrodiilic Empire, the Nords remained without a truly-recognised High King for much of this period. <BR>
<BR>
The encroachment of Cyrodiilic sensibilities in this time took its toll on Nordic culture, and though the old stories were gleefully plundered and appropriated by pedigree-hungry Colovians, new works took on a decidedly less Nordic character. Stories placed less emphasis on individual heroism, the Hirser became more removed and less personable, and the aspiration to Sovngarde fell away from the cultural consciousness. <BR>
<BR>
CE6 - Talos Period (2E855 - ) <BR>
Our current age can, I believe, be safely considered the "Talos Period". Although they initially resisted his expansion, the Nords became enthusiastic supporters of Cuhlecain and later Tiber Septim - especially as the renewed influence of Wulfharth spread and the "Nordic Talos" myth grew in popularity. <BR>
<BR>
With many Nords seeing the Septim Empire as a restoration of the First Empire of the Nords - won by Nordic conquest and led by a supposed Nord - the Talos Period has seen a restoration of traditional Nordic religion and the poetic cycle. Scholars of this formidable culture can only hope that this trend continues, and that we are privileged to witness a new golden age of Nordic mythology and song-making.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
诺德人的文化纪元<BR>
利兰德瑞尔的埃隆维 著
<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
前言<BR>
泰姆瑞尔历史的学者们，包括我自己，通常都喜欢标准纪元历法，这既源于我们从小接受教育时养成的习惯，也源于共享框架的便利性。虽然这可以理解，但对于研究泰姆瑞尔各个文化和民族而言，这个框架有些局限，因为一个时代在大陆层面和当地层面未必相同。因此，我希望通过本书提供一个替代性的、兼容的框架，来理解诺德历史与文化，这一框架基于回归时代以来诺德历史与文化的演变。<BR>
<BR>
文纪1 - 图腾时期（精灵纪元? - 精灵纪元?）<BR>
图腾时期涉及诺德人的最早历史，从古阿特莫拉的建立到伊斯格拉谟的回归及其后。据信这一时期没有留下文字记录，但强大的口述传统以动物寓言和童话故事的形式留存下来。<BR>
<BR>
在文化上，这是一个自然之灵和部落图腾的时代，它们开始汇聚成当代诺德万神殿的雏形。因此，这一时期很少直接出现“朔尔”或“奥杜因”，但反复出现关于狡猾的狐狸欺骗强大巨龙之类的传说。任何一本传统的诺德寓言集都能提供这类故事的例证。<BR>
<BR>
文纪2 - 涟漪王国时期（精灵纪元? - 第一纪元139年）<BR>
涟漪王国时期是我对那个时代的私人称呼，始于精灵纪元晚期，当时诺德人开始在泰姆瑞尔建立起重要的政治力量。由于来源可疑且缺乏严格的记录保存，确切的日期难以确定，尽管它涵盖了雪精灵与诺德人之间的大部分冲突。<BR>
<BR>
这一时代标志着诺德诗歌循环的开始，歌颂这个时代的神话国王和强大英雄。也是在这一时期，阿特莫拉的图腾灵开始拟人化，演变为现今的诺德万神殿，而古阿特莫拉的试炼之神则与后来神话中的精灵恶魔完全等同 -- 毫无疑问，这是诺德人与雪精灵之间残酷战争的产物。<BR>
<BR>
文纪3 - 古帝国时期（第一纪元139年 - 第一纪元369年）<BR>
古帝国时期始于至高王哈拉尔德·自由之手 -- 也被称为神话英雄哈拉尔德·毛裤 -- 对最后的雪精灵和龙 cult 的双重胜利，从而宣告了独立的天际王国的成立。至高王哈拉尔德是第一位真正具有历史意义的诺德统治者，这对诺德民族来说是一个记录详实、历史探究丰富的时期。它还包括诺德第一帝国的时期，该帝国曾覆盖晨风、西罗帝尔和高岩的大部分地区 -- 这段时期虽短，但至今仍被诺德人怀着深情和自豪铭记。<BR>
<BR>
正是在这一时期，至高王哈拉尔德对诺德神话进行了伟大的编纂，即《至高王吠陀》。朔尔之死和松加德的领域在此时被引入神话循环，征服与胜利的故事占据突出地位。可以说，古帝国时期（除了其末期阿莱西亚教派的侵蚀外）是诺德神话和诗歌循环的开创性时代，鉴于其短暂而充满活力的跨度，这更令人印象深刻。<BR>
<BR>
文纪4 - 破碎天空时期（第一纪元369年 - 第一纪元2703年）<BR>
第一纪元369年，至高王博加斯去世后，第一帝国解体，随后进入了漫长的内乱时期，我称之为破碎天空时期。阿莱西亚教团激进地压制传统诺德宗教，尤其是在南部和东部，而天际西部大部分地区被迪伦尼家族占领。在败于第一议会并失去晨风之后，约根·唤风者创立了吼声之道，作为研究和完善吐姆的手段，而此前诺德人视吐姆为与生俱来的能力。<BR>
<BR>
这一时期的诗歌和神话明显更加黑暗和深奥，聚焦于神祇的内部纷争和精灵恶魔的罪行。关于武尔夫哈斯（朔尔的化身）的半历史传说在破碎天空时期尤为盛行，讲述他呼吁从晨风收复第一帝国和朔尔之心。在加冕为至高王后，武尔夫哈斯得以扭转对迪伦尼家族的领土损失并清洗了阿莱西亚教派，但未能收复第一帝国，天际最终退出了权力中心。<BR>
<BR>
文纪5 - 帝国保护国时期（第一纪元2703年 - 第二纪元855年）<BR>
天际于第一纪元2703年和平并入雷曼帝国，开启了诺德人成为南方君主附庸的时代。即使在第二西罗帝尔帝国崩溃之后，诺德人在这一时期的很长一段时间里，仍然没有一位得到真正认可的至高王。<BR>
<BR>
西罗帝尔情感的侵蚀在这个时期对诺德文化造成了损害，尽管古老的故事被渴望血统的科洛维亚人欣喜地掠夺和挪用，但新的作品呈现出明显的、更不具诺德特色的风格。故事不再那么强调个人英雄主义，希尔瑟神变得更加遥远和缺乏人情味，对松加德的向往也从文化意识中消退。<BR>
<BR>
文纪6 - 塔洛斯时期（第二纪元855年 - ）<BR>
我相信，我们当前的时代可以稳妥地称为“塔洛斯时期”。尽管起初他们抵制他的扩张，但诺德人后来成为了库勒凯恩以及泰伯·塞普汀的热情支持者 -- 尤其是随着武尔夫哈斯的影响再次传播，以及“诺德塔洛斯”神话日益流行。<BR>
<BR>
由于许多诺德人将塞普汀帝国视为诺德第一帝国的重建 -- 由诺德征服赢得并由一位被认为是诺德人的领袖领导 -- 塔洛斯时期见证了传统诺德宗教和诗歌循环的复兴。研究这一强大文化的学者们只能希望这一趋势能够持续下去，并且我们有幸目睹诺德神话和歌曲创作的新黄金时代。<BR>"""

The opinions of the so-called academic who styles herself "Lady Cinnabar" notwithstanding, the evidence supporting my assertions is incontrovertible and generally accepted by all accredited scholars of antiquity.<BR>
<BR>
The Aldmeri, who'd been first to begin organized worship of the Aedra, were also the first to venerate the Daedra Lords. This probably began on a small scale among the Ayleids, those Elves who left the Summerset Isles to create splinter cultures in central and southwest Tamriel - in some cases specifically to evade the strictures of Aldmeri regulation, which forbade (among many other things) the worship of Daedra.<BR>
<BR>
As Ayleid culture flourished, drawing ever further from Alinor, in the last millennium of the Merethic Era Daedric worship took hold and spread among the Heartland High Elves. The Aedra were still widely revered, with probably a majority of the Ayleids continuing to pay them homage, but cults devoted to the various Daedric Princes sprang up across Cyrodiil, tolerated and then celebrated. Unlike the Chimer, the Ayleids made no distinction between "good and bad" Daedra - indeed, even some of the more heinous Princes received mass veneration, especially when their worship was adopted and endorsed by Ayleid kings and aristocrats.<BR>
<BR>
Widespread Daedra worship among the Heartland Elves was particularly ill news for the tribes of Nedic humans who were then arriving in Tamriel. The Ayleids enslaved the immigrant tribes of Men, at first occasionally but then systematically, and the Nedic people found themselves subject to masters who, in many cases, worshiped the Princes - including those who encouraged slavery, domination, and cruelty. Under the Ayleids, the human thralls found themselves the subjects of such Daedra-inspired "arts" as flesh-sculpture and gut-gardening. In fact, the revulsion for Daedra-worship that pervades most human cultures in Tamriel probably originated in this period.<BR>
<BR>

The Ayleid kings who aligned themselves with the rebellion were largely Aedra-worshippers, which in part explains why, once the Ayleids were overthrown, Queen Alessia incorporated the leading Elven Aedra into the First Empire's worship of the Eight Divines. Her new Empire of Cyrodiil outlawed the worship of the Daedric Princes, and Daedra-worshiping Ayleids were exterminated wherever they were found.<BR>
<BR>

Elsewhere, among Men, Mer, and Beast-Peoples, Daedra-worship survived only at the level of cults which were more-or-less forbidden. 28, Hearthfire<BR>

A disaster.<BR>

Inside I found two brilliantly forged glass pauldrons that were partially covered in a leather wrapping. Not in a situation to start wearing them, I rushed to the door and took cover in the open side of the door.<BR>

I bumped into Pyoris along the way, but he did not have time to react as I ran as fast as I could. I transported to safety with a help of Recall when I left the ebony boundaries of the house. <BR>

炉火月14日<BR>
<BR>
雷尼尔给我布置了一个任务，从因多瑞尔·皮奥里斯领主的金库中获取一件所谓的神器。他的庄园安保非同寻常，有传言说房子被封印了干涉魔能！人们怎么可能通过雷尼尔强制推行的所谓传统方法逃脱呢？即使能逃脱，庄园的位置也选得很巧妙，位于龙林中央，没有围栏或墙壁，任何人都会注意到异常动静。确实，这带来了巨大的危险，但也是一种挑战。<BR>
<BR>
炉火月17日<BR>
<BR>
收到皮奥里斯庄园的布局图后，我深入研究，注意到墙壁有多层结构。内层由黑檀木制成，即使是最迟钝的诺德人也知道黑檀木蕴含着巨大的魔法潜力。我和雷尼尔讨论了此事，他同意协助我。他可能不是一个好领导，但即使在有光亮的地方也能潜行。我们明天将前往金库。<BR>
<BR>
炉火月28日<BR>
<BR>
一场灾难。<BR>
<BR>
我们找到了两把钥匙，进入了房间，我向金库内的守卫施放了盲目法术，但有人，很可能就是皮奥里斯本人，醒来后发现他床边没有钥匙。警报响起，另外三名守卫径直向我们冲来。雷尼尔守住门口时，我搜刮了珠宝并撬开了箱子的锁。在里面，我发现了两个锻造精良的玻璃肩甲，部分被皮革包裹着。由于没时间穿戴，我冲向门口，在门的打开一侧躲避。<BR>
<BR>
雷尼尔藏在守卫打开的门后，其中一名守卫径直冲了过去。在他有机会看到我之前，我溜过门，经过他身边，到达了账房，那里有两名守卫把守着入口。我退到墙边，守卫立刻发起攻击。我向第一个守卫使用了穿刃，这一下分散了注意力，让我刚好有时间躲过另一个守卫的猛烈劈砍。在楼梯上，皮奥里斯正等着，已经装备好了胁差，手里拿着某种护符。我转过身，向金库门施放了锁咒，然后施展了隐身术。我在途中撞到了皮奥里斯，但他没有时间反应，因为我以最快的速度跑开了。当我离开房子的黑檀木边界时，我借助召回术传送到了安全地带。<BR>
<BR>
看来那对肩甲以某种方式被附了魔，用于放置令人费解的铁匠作品。我从没见过这样的肩甲。没有玻璃尖刺固定结构，它们依然很坚固。<BR>
<BR>
我确信我的法术的力量。它会把守卫和雷尼尔困在里面，直到像埃卡什这样的真正大师被召唤到龙林。我怀疑他会不会为了这等小事而大驾光临这个不重要的小镇。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Dangers of Reach-Magicks <BR>
By Edwistair Admand<BR>>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
While there are many variants of magick throughout the Empire (to speak nothing of the potential magicks that lie beyond Tamriel's shores), the focus of this text will be on the magicks of the Reachmen.<BR>
<BR>
Reach-Magic is primarily ritualistic in nature, though it has been speculated to incorporate Orcish shamanism, Direnni spellcraft, and rudimentary forms of the circinate spells of the Mages Guild -- the former two being much more important than the latter. From my research many Reachmen do not always cast spells within the moment of ritual, but instead use a minor ritual (often sacrificial and self-destructive, as is the case of all wild and untamed magicks not sanctioned by the guild) to ready a spell mid-cast. Upon need of such spell they simply must loosen the magickal seal to unleash the casted spell. This, like all things in Reach-Magic, can be incredibly damaging to the spell host, as many spell types are not designed for internal use -- let alone being internally withheld for days, months, or even years.<BR>
<BR>
A Reachmen's ritual is not always cast before release, however. Another form of Reach-Magic can be observed through the effects it has on the surrounding areas. There have been numerous reports of droughts, earthquakes, and various curses happening in the lands where witchmen have practiced their magicks, as if the ground itself was seeped in a magickal muck of curses. Unlike the scholars of the officially recognized schools of magic practiced by the esteemed Guild of Mages, which aims to control the forces of which we command through spell, these magicks instead seek to take hold of said forces and manipulate through unknown means without proper protection. As if the damaging effects of such reckless behavior could in any way outweigh the caster's own soul and body.<BR>
<BR>
Some less familiar scholars liken Reach-Magic to some form of Mysticism, as both practices tend to revolve around the unseen nature of Mundus, as well as often invoking magicks unknown, replicating the unprecedented effects of wild innovation. However, these academics seem to misinterpret the intentions of such schools of thought. My understanding of differences between both of these wide fields of study can be best described as such; While Mysticism is understanding and replicating the results of magicks gone sometimes horribly wrong, Reach-Magic, in many of its various forms, relies on magicks that have gone horribly right.<BR>
<BR>
With all of this in mind, it's no wonder why the late Empress Morihatha Septim had deemed this vile form of spellcraft illegal. Reach-Magic is as dangerous as they come, to both the caster and their surroundings. Even were one to call upon such rituals without negative consequences, there can be no guarantee of how, why, or if it will work. If you wish to learn the inner workings of magick, then I would suggest joining your nearest Mages Guild where you can practice proper magical theory and execution, rather than learning from some common Reachmen in the forest.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
河峪魔法的危险<BR>
埃德维斯特尔·阿德曼德 著<BR>>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
虽然帝国内存在多种多样的魔法（更不用说泰姆瑞尔海岸之外潜在的魔法了），但本文的重点将是河峪人的魔法。<BR>
<BR>
河峪魔法本质上是仪式性的，尽管推测它融合了兽人萨满教、迪伦尼法术工艺以及法师公会循环法术的初级形式 -- 前两者比后者重要得多。根据我的研究，许多河峪人并不总是在仪式时施放法术，而是通过一个小型仪式（通常是献祭和自我伤害性质的，如同所有未经公会认可、狂野不羁的魔法一样）来预先准备一个法术。当需要施展该法术时，他们只需松开魔法封印来释放准备好的法术。这正如河峪魔法的一切那样，对法术宿主可能造成难以置信的伤害，因为许多法术类型并非为内部使用而设计 -- 更不用说在体内保留数天、数月甚至数年。<BR>
<BR>
然而，河峪人的仪式并不总是在释放前施放。另一种形式的河峪魔法可以通过其对周围区域的影响来观察。在巫师们修炼他们魔法的地方，有大量关于干旱、地震和各种诅咒的报告，仿佛大地本身都浸透了诅咒的魔法淤泥。与受人尊敬的法师公会所实践的官方认可魔法学派的学者们不同 -- 他们的目标是通过法术控制我们所指挥的力量 -- 这些魔法则试图抓住这些力量，并通过未知手段在缺乏适当保护的情况下进行操控。仿佛这种鲁莽行为的破坏性影响，能以任何方式超过施法者自身的灵魂和身体。<BR>
<BR>
一些不太熟悉的学者将河峪魔法比作某种形式的神秘系，因为这两种实践都围绕着梦达斯的不可见本质，并且常常调用未知的魔法，重现了狂野创新前所未有的效果。然而，这些学者似乎误解了此类思想流派的意图。我对这两个广阔研究领域之间差异的理解可以这样最好地描述：神秘系是理解和复制那些有时变得极其糟糕的魔法结果，而河峪魔法在其多种形式中，依赖于那些已经变得极其“正确”的魔法。<BR>
<BR>
考虑到这一切，难怪已故的莫里哈萨·塞普汀女皇将这种邪恶的施法形式定为非法。河峪魔法对施法者和周围环境都非常危险。即使某人施展此类仪式没有负面后果，也无法保证其如何、为何或是否会起作用。如果你想学习魔法的内在运作，那么我建议你加入最近的法师公会，在那里你可以实践正确的魔法理论和执行，而不是向森林里的某个普通河峪人学习。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Danstrar Serpent<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Sing, bard! This is the song of King Bergryf Serpent-Slayer, only trueborn of Little Queen Kraka and first king of the Corpse-Hold of Danstrar.<BR>
<BR>
Bergryf was first seen by the skald's sentimental gaze as the petty king of Gorvik. He was a tall, gale-beaten Nord and known to wear a third eye within his skull in the manner of his clan (the Sightless, so named because they could see better than any other). With this eye, Bergryf could see all the winds upon the sea and thus were his fleets the swiftest and most feared among the elves and lesser men of the North. This was during the reign of High King Snorik, in the time after the death of High King Wulfharth but before his return, when Nords still knew the different ways to wear their senses.<BR>
<BR>
But at this time the peerless fleets of Gorvik were kept ashore, high above the tidemark, for not even the shallows were safe. Death stalked the Northshore in the form of a great water-serpent, which the people called Thirst. No ship could set out to hunt or raid without the glittering head of Thirst reducing their keel to splinters, and the shore-bound crews were vocal in their dismay such that the air was thick with cursing. And so Bergryf, knowing that the land alone could not sustain his people, summoned his thanes and Tongues and hunt-wives and set his entire fleet to either skin the serpent or perish together.<BR>
<BR>
Most loyal amongst Bergryf's hird was Jhugyr, the owl-faced navigator of the Sightless. He was a cunning clever-man and friend to the sea-hags that kept Kyne's favor on great expeditions. Before the portentous unbeaching of Bergryf's fleet, Jhugyr had dived to the place where hags traded storm-whipped foam for the baubles of the dreugh-folk, and offered many feathers from his own arms in return for their counsel. The sea-hags knew that Orkey, the foul dead snake, had followed Ysgramor's ships out of Atmora, and Jhugyr had learned that the Gorvik wyrm was but one of Orkey's children. Thus Jhugyr knew that they could kill Thirst by skinning it (all snakes are susceptible to this) and through the patterns of his flight was able to guide the Gorvik fleets towards its lair. <BR>
<BR>
And thus, far below, as the smell of rot and death poured into his nostrils and the ships of his fleet formed up into six serried waves, Bergryf leapt upon the prow and bellowed challenges at the monster.<BR>
<BR>
"Vile, hairless creature!" he roared (knowing that the children of Orkey are very sensitive to this) "In your cowardice, you skulk in open sea and have never stepped before my throne in honest combat. Well, now I come to your foetid lair with scorn upon my voice!" <BR>
<BR>
Barbed by these unmatched taunts, the thrashing form of Thirst came rushing through the water towards the ships of the Sightless. Diving beneath Bergryf's keel, its forked tail shattered the ship to either side and in surfacing its toothy mouth another. But wily Bergryf had anticipated these losses and knew that even the children of Old Knocker can only kill so many. Thus he sent the first wave of his ships, sharpened rams secreted beneath the water, charging into the wyrm's flank, where they dashed themselves to pieces upon its shining scales. The same for the second, and third, and fifth waves (the fourth felt fear and made themselves the seventh).<BR>
<BR>
But at the sixth wave the great glittering armour of Thirst, gruesome child of Orkey, was rent at last, and that was when the great longship of Bergryf surged forward. The petty king of Gorvik had kept a vajrar of Tongues by his side for just this moment, and as one, with spray whipping their faces, they Shouted the body of Thirst high upon the shore. The cold seas ran warm with serpent's blood as the creature thrashed and cried, but the Voice is without mercy and with a final thunderous bellow the naked flesh of Orkey's child lay splayed upon the shore.<BR>
<BR>
Seeing this, the lesser folk of Gorvik - farmers and those bound to the land - swarmed down from the hills where they had been hiding. With knives and cleavers, they hacked the flesh from the still-bleeding wyrm - gorging themselves or packing it in snow for winter - until naught was left but steaming bones. And seeing the fortuitous way these bones had fallen, Jhugyr the clever-man rejoiced for he knew that this would, for all the days until Alduin's stirring, be a prosperous holdfast and a safe harbour for the unparalleled reavers of the Sightless. And King Bergryf, hereafter given the knowing "Serpent-Slayer", declared that mighty skull Danstrar, the new seat of a new kingdom on the Northshore.<BR><BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
丹斯特拉蛇<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
唱吧，吟游诗人！这是屠蛇者贝格里夫国王之歌，他是小女王克拉卡唯一的嫡子，也是丹斯特拉尸骸要塞的第一位国王。<BR>
<BR>
贝格里夫最初是作为戈维克的藩王出现在吟游诗人感性的目光中。他是个高大、饱经风霜的诺德人，以其氏族（“无目者”，因其看得比谁都清楚而得名）的方式，以在头骨内戴有第三只眼而闻名。凭借这只眼睛，贝格里夫能看见海上所有的风向，因此他的舰队是北方精灵和人类中最迅捷、最令人畏惧的。那是在至高王斯诺里克统治时期，在至高王武尔夫哈斯死后但在他回归之前的时代，诺德人仍然知晓感知事物的不同方式。<BR>
<BR>
但此时，戈维克无与伦比的舰队被搁置在岸上，高高地停在潮标之上，因为即使是浅水区也不安全。死亡以一条巨大水蛇的形式出没于北岸，人民称之为“渴求”。没有一艘船能出海狩猎或掠夺，因为“渴求”闪亮的头颅会把它们的龙骨粉碎，被困在岸上的船员们大声表达着沮丧，空气中充满了诅咒。于是贝格里夫知道仅靠土地无法养活他的人民，他召集了他的领主、吐姆使用者和狩猎女眷，命令他的整个舰队要么剥下蛇皮，要么一起覆灭。<BR>
<BR>
贝格里夫亲卫中最忠诚的是朱吉尔，无目者的猫头鹰脸领航员。他是一个狡猾的聪明人，是海妖的朋友，海妖在大型远征中保持着吉讷的恩宠。在贝格里夫舰队不祥地离岸之前，朱吉尔曾潜入海妖们用风暴搅打的泡沫交换蟹灵族小饰品的地方，并从自己的手臂上拔下许多羽毛作为回报，换取她们的忠告。海妖们知道奥凯，那条邪恶的死蛇，曾跟随伊斯格拉谟的船只离开阿特莫拉，朱吉尔得知戈维克的巨蛇只是奥凯的子嗣之一。因此朱吉尔知道他们可以通过剥皮来杀死“渴求”（所有蛇类都易受此影响），并通过他飞行的模式，能够引导戈维克舰队前往它的巢穴。<BR>
<BR>
于是，在遥远的下方，当腐烂和死亡的气息涌入他的鼻孔，他的舰队排成六道紧密的波浪时，贝格里夫跳到船首，向怪物发出挑战的吼声。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
但在第六波时，奥凯那可怕的子嗣 -- “渴求”闪亮的巨大鳞甲终于被撕裂，就在那时，贝格里夫的大长船猛冲向前。戈维克的藩王在身边保留了一支“吐姆”小队，正是为了此刻，他们齐声呐喊，用吐姆将“渴求”的身体高高抛到岸上。当那生物翻滚哀嚎时，冰冷的海水因蛇血而变暖，但吼声毫不留情，随着最后一声雷鸣般的咆哮，奥凯之子赤裸的血肉摊开在岸上。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
De Rerum Dirennis<BR>
by Vorian Direnni<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
I am six-hundred-and-eleven years old. I have never had children of my own, but I have many nieces and nephews and cousins who have been raised with the tales and traditions of our ancient, illustrious, and occasionally notorious clan, the Direnni. Few families in Tamriel can boast so many famous figures, wielding so much power over the fate of so many. Our warriors and kings are stuff of legend, and it is not to dismiss their honor and their achievements to say you have heard quite enough about them.<BR>
<BR>
I myself have never picked up a sword or written an important law, but I am part of a lesser known but still important Direnni tradition: the way of the wizard. My own autobiography would be of little interest to posterity - though my nephew, nieces, and cousins indulge me to tell wild tales of life in the chaotic Second Era of Tamriel - but I have a few ancestors whose stories should be told. They may have changed history as we know it as dramatically as my better known relatives, but their names are in danger of being forgotten.<BR>
<BR>
Most recently, Lysandus, the King of Daggerfall, was able to conquer his ancient enemies of Sentinel in part thanks to his court sorceress, Medora Direnni. Her grandfather Jovron Direnni was Imperial Battlemage to the court of the Dunmer Empress of Tamriel, Katariah, assisting her in creating peace in a time of turmoil. His great great grandfather Pelladil Direnni had a similar role with the first Potentate, and encouraged the Guild Act without which we would not have all the professional organizations we have today. His ancestor, many times back, was the witch Raven Direnni, who with her better known cousins Aiden and Ryain, brought an end to the tyranny of the latter Alessian Empire. Before the Psijics of Artaeum, it is said, she created the art of enchantment, learning how to bind a soul into a gem and use that to ensorcel all manners of weaponry.<BR>
<BR>
But it is the story of an ancestor even more ancient, more distant than Raven I wish to tell.<BR>
<BR>
Asliel Direnni harkens back to the humble beginnings of our clan, in the tiny farming village of Tyrigel on the banks of the river Caomus which was then called the Diren, hence the family name. Like all on Summurset Isle in those days, he was a simple planter of the fields. But while others only grew enough to sustain their immediate kin, even distant cousins of the Dirennis worked together. They would decide as a group which fields were best for wheat, orchard, vine, livestock, or apiary, and thereby always have the best yields of any farm which worked alone, doing the best as it could with what it had.<BR>
<BR>
Asliel had a particularly poor farm for most kind of agriculture, but small herbs found its stony, loamless, acidic soil very comfortable. Out of necessity more than anything else he became an expert on all manners of herbs. For the most part, of course, they were used in flavoring cooking, but as you know, hardly any plant grows on the surface of our world without a magickal potential.<BR>
<BR>
Even so long ago, witches already were in existence. It would be ridiculous for me to suggest that Asliel Direnni invented alchemy. What he did, what we can all be grateful for, is that he formulated it into an art and science.<BR>
<BR>
There were no witches' covens in Tyrigel, and, of course, there would be no Mages Guild yet for thousands of years, so people would come to him for cures. He learned for himself the exact formula for combining black lichen and roobrush to create a cure for all manners of poison, and the amount of willow anther to crush and mix with chokeweed to cure diseases.<BR>
<BR>
There were few much greater threats in Tyrigel in those peaceful days than disease or accidental poisonings. Yes, there were some dark forces in the wilderness, trolls, chimera, the occasional malevolent fairy folk and Will-O-The-Wisp, but even the youngest, most foolish Altmer knew how to avoid them. There were, however, a few unusual threats which Asliel had a hand in defeating.<BR>
<BR>
One of the tales told of him that I believe to be true is how he was brought a young niece who had been suffering from an unknown disease. Despite his ministrations, she grew weaker and weaker every morning. Finally, he gave her a bitter tasting drink, and the next morning, ashes were found all around her bed. A vampire had been feeding on the poor girl, but Asliel's potion had turned her very blood into poison, without harming her in the least.<BR>
<BR>
If only this formula had not been lost in the mists of history!<BR>
<BR>
This would have been enough to make him a minor but significant figure in the annals of early Summurset, but at that point in history, a barbarian tribe called the Locvar had found their way down the Diren River, and recognized Tyrigel as a rich target for raids. The Direnni, not being warriors yet but simple farmers, were helpless and could only flee and watch the Locvar take the best of their crops, raid after raid.<BR>
<BR>
Asliel, however, had been experimenting with the vampire dust, and brought his cousins to him with a plan. The next time the Locvar were sighted on the Diren, the word went out and all the most able-bodied came to Asliel's laboratory. When the barbarians arrived in Tyrigel, they found the farms deserted, and assumed that all had fled as usual. As they set about stealing the bounty, they suddenly found themselves under attack by invisible forces. Believing the Direnni farms to be haunted, they ran away very quickly.<BR>
<BR>
They attempted a few more raids, for their greed would always eventually overpower their fear, and each time, they were set upon by attackers who they could not see. As barbaric as they were, they were not stupid, and they changed their mind about the source of their defeat. It could not be that the farms were haunted, because the crops were still being tended and harvested, and the animals seemed to show no fear. The Locvar decided to send a scout to the farm to see if he could spy their secrets.<BR>
<BR>
The scout sent word back to the Locvar that the Direnni farms were populated with flesh and blood, entirely visible Altmer. He continued to watch as his barbarian cohorts moved down the river, and he saw the elderly and children flee for the hills, while the able-bodied farmers and their wives went to Asliel's laboratory. He saw them go in; he saw no one come out.<BR>
<BR>
As usual, the Locvar were repelled by invisible forces, but their scout soon told them what he saw happening in the laboratory.<BR>
<BR>
The next night, two of the Locvar approached Asliel's farm very stealthily, and managed to kidnap him without alerting the rest of the Direnni. The Locvar chieftain, knowing that the farmers could no longer count on the alchemist to make them invisible, considered an immediate attack on the farms. But he was a vengeful sort, and felt he had been humiliated by these simple farmers. A crafty plan emerged in his mind. What if the Direnni, who always saw his barbarian tribe coming, for once did not? Imagine the slaughter if no one even had a chance to flee.<BR>
<BR>
The scout had told the chieftain that Asliel had used the dust of a vampire to make the farmers invisible, but he was not sure what the other ingredient had been. He described an incandescent powder that Asliel had mixed into the dust. Asliel, of course, refused to help the Locvar, but they were experts in torture as well as pillage, and he knew he would have to talk or die.<BR>
<BR>
Finally after hours of torture, he agreed to tell them what the incandescent powder was. He did not know the name, but he called it "Glow Dust," the only remains of a slain Will O The Wisp. He told them they would need a lot of it if they wanted to turn the whole tribe invisible for the raid.<BR>
<BR>
The Locvar grumbled that not only did they have to find and kill a vampire to attain his dust, but find and kill several Will O The Wisps to get theirs. In a few days time, they came back with the ingredients the alchemist asked for. The chieftain, not being a complete idiot, made Asliel taste the potion first. He did as he was told and turned invisible, demonstrating that it did truly work. The chieftain put him to work creating more. No one apparently noticed that while he did, he was nibbling on black lichen and roobrush.<BR>
<BR>
The Locvar took the potion as he doled it out, and soon, but not too soon that they didn't suffer, they were all dead.<BR>
<BR>
The scout who had seen Asliel mixing the invisibility potion had apparently mistook the glow of the candlelight in the laboratory for an incandescence which the second ingredient of the invisibility potion did not possess. The second ingredient was actually dull, simple redwort, one of the most common herbs in Tamriel. When they had insisted during torture that Asliel tell them what the incandescent powder was, Asliel remembered that he had once experimentally mixed glow dust and vampire dust together once and created a powerful poison. It was simple enough to steal a little redwort from the barbarian's camp, mix that with the vampire and glow dust mixture, and create a potion that was in fact an invisibility poison. After curing himself, he gave the poison to the barbarians.<BR>
<BR>
The Locvar, being dead, never again raided the Direnni farms, and having no other enemies, they were able to grow more and more prosperous and powerful. Generations later, they left Summurset and began their historic adventures on the Tamriel mainland. Asliel Direnni, because of his excellence as an alchemist, was invited to Artaeum and became a Psijic. It is not known how many more of the common formulas we know today were invented by him there, but I have no doubt, the science and art of alchemy as we know it today would not exist without him.<BR>
<BR>
But that is all in the distant past. Asliel's innovations, like my modest ones, like the achievements of the Dirennis throughout history, are but a stepping stone to the wonders which will come in the future. I wish I could be there to witness them, but if I can only share some of the past with the children of Direnni and the children of Tamriel, then I will consider my life well spent. <BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
论迪伦尼<BR>
沃里安·迪伦尼 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
我今年六百一十一岁。我从未有过自己的孩子，但我有许多侄女、侄子和堂表亲，他们是在我们古老、辉煌、偶尔也臭名昭著的迪伦尼家族的故事和传统中长大的。泰姆瑞尔很少有家族能夸耀拥有如此多的知名人物，对如此多人的命运施加如此大的影响。我们的战士和国王是传奇的人物，说你已经听过他们太多事迹，并非轻视他们的荣誉和成就。<BR>
<BR>
我自己从未拿起过剑，也未曾撰写过重要的法律，但我属于一个鲜为人知但依然重要的迪伦尼传统：巫师之道。我自己的自传对后人来说可能没什么兴趣 -- 尽管我的侄子、侄女和堂表亲们会纵容我讲述在混乱的泰姆瑞尔第二纪元生活的狂野故事 -- 但我有几位祖先的故事应当被讲述。他们或许像我更出名的亲戚一样，戏剧性地改变了我们所知的历史，但他们的名字正面临被遗忘的危险。<BR>
<BR>
最近，匕落国王利桑杜斯能够征服他古老的敌人哨卫城，部分要归功于他的宫廷女巫梅多拉·迪伦尼。她的祖父乔夫隆·迪伦尼曾是泰姆瑞尔丹莫女皇卡塔瑞亚宫廷的帝国战斗法师，协助她在动荡时期创造和平。他的高祖父佩拉迪尔·迪伦尼在第一任摄政王时期扮演了类似角色，并鼓励了公会法案，没有它我们就不会有今天所有的专业组织。他的祖先，向上追溯许多代，是女巫拉文·迪伦尼，她与她更出名的堂亲艾登和里安一起，终结了后阿莱西亚帝国的暴政。据说，在阿泰乌姆的塞伊克之前，她创造了附魔艺术，学会了如何将灵魂绑定到宝石中，并以此给各种武器施法。<BR>
<BR>
但我想要讲述的是一位比拉文更古老、更遥远的祖先的故事。<BR>
<BR>
阿斯利尔·迪伦尼可以追溯到我们家族卑微的起源，在卡奥穆斯河畔的小农耕村庄泰里格尔，那条河当时被称为迪伦河，因此得名。和当时夏暮岛上的所有人一样，他是个简单的田里种植者。但当其他人只种植足够养活近亲的作物时，连迪伦尼的远房表亲们也一起劳作。他们会集体决定哪些田地最适合小麦、果园、葡萄、牲畜或蜂房，因此总能比任何单独耕作、只能尽其所能利用现有条件的农场获得更好的收成。<BR>
<BR>
阿斯利尔有一块对大多数农作物来说都特别贫瘠的农田，但小草药在它多石、无壤、酸性的土壤中却生长得非常好。与其说是出于兴趣，不如说是出于需要，他成为了各种草药方面的专家。当然，在大多数情况下，它们被用于调味烹饪，但如你所知，我们世界表面生长的几乎任何植物都带有魔法潜力。<BR>
<BR>
即使在那么久远的年代，女巫们已经存在了。如果我说阿斯利尔·迪伦尼发明了炼金术，那会是可笑的。他所做的是，我们都应感激的是，他将炼金术系统化为一门艺术和科学。<BR>
<BR>
泰里格尔没有女巫集会，而且，当然，数千年后才有法师公会，所以人们会来找他寻求治疗。他自己摸索出了将黑色地衣和鲁灌木结合以制造治疗各种中毒的解药的精确配方，以及将柳花药碾碎并与苦樱桃草混合以治疗疾病的用量。<BR>
<BR>
在那个和平年代，泰里格尔很少有比疾病或意外中毒更大的威胁。是的，荒野中有一些黑暗力量，巨魔、奇美拉、偶尔出现的恶意精灵和鬼火，但即使是最年轻、最愚蠢的傲特莫也知道如何避开它们。然而，也有一些不同寻常的威胁，阿斯利尔曾参与击败过它们。<BR>
<BR>
我认为真实的一个关于他的故事是，有人带了一个患有未知疾病的年轻侄女来找他。尽管他悉心照料，她每天早晨却越来越虚弱。最后，他给了她一杯苦味的饮料，第二天早上，她床周围发现了灰烬。原来是一个吸血鬼一直在吸食那个可怜女孩的血，但阿斯利尔的药剂将她的血液变成了毒药，却丝毫没有伤害到她。<BR>
<BR>
要是这个配方没有湮没在历史的迷雾中就好了！<BR>
<BR>
这足以使他成为早期夏暮编年史中一个次要但重要的人物，但在那个历史节点，一个名叫洛克瓦的野蛮部落沿着迪伦河而下，将泰里格尔视为一个富饶的袭击目标。迪伦尼人当时还不是战士，只是普通的农民，他们无能为力，只能眼睁睁地看着洛克瓦人一次又一次地掠夺他们最好的庄稼。<BR>
<BR>
然而，阿斯利尔一直在用吸血鬼粉尘做实验，他把他的堂兄弟们召集起来，提出了一个计划。当洛克瓦人再次在迪伦河被发现时，消息传开，所有最强壮的人都来到了阿斯利尔的实验室。当野蛮人到达泰里格尔时，他们发现农场空无一人，以为所有人都像往常一样逃跑了。当他们开始抢夺丰收果实时，突然发现自己受到了隐形力量的攻击。他们以为迪伦尼农场闹鬼，很快就逃跑了。<BR>
<BR>
他们又尝试了几次袭击，因为他们的贪婪总会最终战胜恐惧，但每次他们都会被看不见的攻击者袭击。尽管他们野蛮，但并不愚蠢，他们改变了对失败根源的看法。农场不可能闹鬼，因为庄稼仍在被照料和收获，动物们似乎也没有表现出恐惧。洛克瓦人决定派一个侦察兵到农场，看他是否能窥探到他们的秘密。<BR>
<BR>
侦察兵传回消息说，迪伦尼农场里住着有血有肉、完全可见的傲特莫人。他继续观察，看着他的野蛮同伴们顺流而下，他看到老人和孩子们逃往山上，而身强力壮的农民和他们的妻子则去了阿斯利尔的实验室。他看到他们进去；却没看到任何人出来。<BR>
<BR>
像往常一样，洛克瓦人被隐形力量击退，但他们的侦察兵很快告诉他们他在实验室看到的情况。<BR>
<BR>
第二天晚上，两个洛克瓦人非常隐蔽地接近了阿斯利尔的农场，并成功绑架了他，没有惊动其他迪伦尼人。洛克瓦人酋长知道农民们不能再依赖炼金术士让他们隐身了，便考虑立即进攻农场。但他是个有仇必报的人，觉得自己被这些普通的农民羞辱了。一个狡猾的计划在他脑海中浮现。如果总是能看到他的野蛮部落到来的迪伦尼人，这次却没有看到呢？想象一下，如果连逃跑的机会都没有，那将会是怎样一场屠杀。<BR>
<BR>
侦察兵告诉酋长，阿斯利尔使用了吸血鬼的粉尘使农民隐身，但他不确定另一种成分是什么。他描述了一种阿斯利尔混入粉尘中的炽热粉末。阿斯利尔当然拒绝帮助洛克瓦人，但他们既是掠夺专家，也是酷刑专家，他知道自己要么开口，要么死。<BR>
<BR>
经过数小时的折磨，他终于同意告诉他们那种炽热粉末是什么。他不知道名字，但称之为“发光粉”，是杀死鬼火后唯一的残留物。他告诉他们，如果想在突袭时让整个部落隐身，他们需要大量这种粉末。<BR>
<BR>
洛克瓦人抱怨说，他们不仅要找到并杀死一个吸血鬼来获得粉尘，还要找到并杀死几只鬼火来获得发光粉。几天后，他们带着炼金术士要求的原料回来了。酋长毕竟不是完全的白痴，他让阿斯利尔先尝了药剂。阿斯利尔照做了，然后隐身了，证明了它确实有效。酋长让他开始制作更多。显然没有人注意到，他在制作的同时，正在小口咀嚼黑色地衣和鲁灌木。<BR>
<BR>
洛克瓦人一边服用他分发的药剂，不久 -- 但也足够让他们遭受痛苦 -- 他们全都死了。<BR>
<BR>
那个看到阿斯利尔混合隐身药剂的侦察兵，显然是把实验室里的烛光误认为是隐身药剂第二种成分所不具备的炽热光芒。第二种成分其实是普通的、暗淡的红草，泰姆瑞尔最常见的草药之一。当他们在酷刑中坚持要阿斯利尔说出炽热粉末是什么时，阿斯利尔想起他曾实验性地混合过发光粉和吸血鬼粉尘，并制造了一种强效毒药。他很容易就从野蛮人的营地偷了一点红草，将其与吸血鬼粉尘和发光粉的混合物混合，制造出一种实际上是隐身毒药的药剂。在治愈自己之后，他把毒药给了野蛮人。<BR>
<BR>
洛克瓦人死了，再也没有袭击过迪伦尼农场，没有了其他敌人，他们得以变得越来越繁荣和强大。几代人之后，他们离开了夏暮，开始了在泰姆瑞尔大陆的历史性冒险。阿斯利尔·迪伦尼，因为他在炼金术方面的卓越才华，被邀请到阿泰乌姆，成为了一名塞伊克。我们如今所知的常见配方中有多少是他在那里发明的，不得而知，但我毫不怀疑，我们今天所知的炼金术科学和艺术，没有他就不会存在。<BR>
<BR>
但这一切都是遥远的过去了。阿斯利尔的创新，如同我微不足道的创新，如同迪伦尼家族在历史上的成就，都只是通往未来奇迹的垫脚石。我希望我能亲眼目睹那些奇迹，但如果我只能与迪伦尼的子孙和泰姆瑞尔的孩子们分享一些过去，那么我会认为我的一生是值得的。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
De Sphaera Nirni<BR>
<BR>On the Shape and Workings of the Mundiversal Machine, the Great and Constant Work endeavored by the Divines for our Education and Tribulation<BR>
<BR> by Deniel Juris
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The celestial sphere can be divided thusways, by substance and by accident.
<BR>
By substance, it is divided in the different Mundial planes, the first of which is the immovable center, Nirn, being the "primus reses", or immovable point upon which the Mundus pivots. Then follow the eight spheres of the Divines, who appear to us larger or smaller by their distance from us, the path they take through the celestial Void, and by our own failing virtue which removes us from them. Then follow the Principalities, who are obscured to us, but whose dark presence is noticed for the influence they exert on the lesser bodies and the unfixed stars. Last follows the great sphere of the fixed stars, and the Magnite sun, through which radiates the light Aetherial.
<BR>
By accident, the sphere is divided into the sphere right and the sphere oblique. Those who have the sphere right dwell near the Palatine or Cyrodiilic Latitude, the most benevolent climate for life and industry to flourish. It is called "right" for neither pole is elevated more than the other, and the horizon intersects the equinoctial circle and is intersected by it at spherical right angles. Those who have the sphere oblique are on either side of the equator, where it is too cold or too warm for proper living. To them one pole is always raised above the horizon, and the other is always depressed below it.
<BR>
The machine of the Mundus is divided into the Void and the elementary regions. The elementary regions, existing subject to continual alteration, are divided into four: the earth, placed in the middle of all, about which is water, about water air, about air fire. For so the Divines in their wisdom disposed. And these are called the four elements, which are in turn altered, corrupted, and regenerated. The elements are simple bodies which cannot be subdivided into parts of diverse forms, and from whose commixture are produced various species of generated things. Around the elementary region revolves with continuous circular motion the Void, which is lucid and immune from all variation in its immutable essence, and in which swim the spheres of the Divines and the Principalities, which are also not of elementary, but of spiritual matter.
<BR>
There are three reasons why the Mundus is round: likeness, convenience, and necessity. Likeness, because the sensible world is made in the likeness of the Akatic archetype, in which there is neither end nor beginning; wherefore, in likeness to it, the sensible world has a round shape, in which beginning or end cannot be distinguished. Convenience, because of all isoperimetric bodies, the sphere is the largest, and of all shapes the round is most capacious. Since largest and round, therefore the most capacious. Wherefore, since the world is all-containing, this shape was useful and convenient for it. Necessity, because if the world were of other form than round -- say, trilateral, quadrilateral, or many-sided -- it would follow that some space would be vacant and some body without a place, both of which are false, as is clear in the case of angles projecting and revolved.
<BR>
That Nirn is in the middle of the firmament is shown thus. To persons on the world's surface, the stars appear of the same size, whether they are in mid-sky, or just rising, or about to set, and this is because the earth is equally distant from them. For if the earth were nearer to the firmament in one direction than in another, a person at that point of the earth's surface which was nearer to the firmament would not see half of the heavens. But this is contrary to Armantine and all the philosophers, who say that, wherever man lives, six signs rise and six signs set, and one is twisted, and half of the heavens is always visible and half hid from him.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
论奈恩球体<BR>
<BR>论宇宙机器 -- 圣灵为我们教育与磨练而进行的伟大而恒常之作 -- 的形态与运作<BR>
<BR>丹尼尔·朱里斯 著
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
天球可按本质与偶性分为如下。
<BR>
按本质，它被划分为不同的世界位面，首先是不可移动的中心，奈恩，即“原初基点”，梦达斯围绕其旋转。其次是圣灵的八个球体，它们在我们眼中或大或小，取决于它们与我们的距离、它们穿越天界虚空的路径，以及我们自身的缺陷美德使我们远离它们的程度。之后是公国，它们对我们来说是被遮蔽的，但它们黑暗的存在因其对较小天体和不定星辰施加的影响而被注意到。最后是恒星的巨大球体，以及玛格努斯太阳，光界之光通过它辐射出来。
<BR>
按偶性，天球分为正球与斜球。拥有正球者居住在帕拉蒂或西罗帝尔纬度附近，这是生命与工业繁荣的最适宜气候。之所以称为“正”，是因为两极都不比另一极更突出，地平线与赤道圈相交，并在球面直角处被其穿过。拥有斜球者位于赤道两侧，那里或过于寒冷或过于炎热，不适宜正常生活。对他们而言，总有一极高于地平线，另一极则低于地平线。
<BR>
梦达斯的机器分为虚空和元素区域。元素区域，存在并不断变化，分为四部分：土，位于一切之中，水环绕土，气环绕水，火环绕气。圣灵以其智慧如此安排。它们被称为四元素，它们依次被改变、腐化和再生。元素是简单的物体，不能细分为不同形式的部分，它们的混合产生了各种被造物。元素区域周围，虚空以持续圆周运动旋转，虚空是明亮的，在其不变的本质中不受任何变化的影响，圣灵和公国的球体在其中游动，它们也不由元素构成，而是由精神物质构成。
<BR>
梦达斯为何是圆形，原因有三：相似性、便利性和必然性。相似性，因为可感世界是按照阿卡托什原型塑造的，其中既无起始也无终结；因此，为了与其相似，可感世界呈圆形，其中起始与终结无法区分。便利性，因为在所有等周体中，球体是最大的，在所有形状中，圆形是最宽敞的。既然最大且圆形，因此最宽敞。因此，既然世界包容一切，这种形状对它来说是有用且便利的。必然性，因为如果世界是圆形以外的其他形状 -- 比如说，三角形、四边形或多边形 -- 那么就会导致某些空间是空的，某些物体无处可放，这两者都是虚假的，这在突出和旋转的角度情况下是显而易见的。
<BR>
奈恩位于苍穹中心，可如此证明。对于世界表面的人而言，星辰无论位于天顶、升起还是将落，看起来大小相同，这是因为地球与它们的距离相等。因为如果地球在某一方向上比另一方向更靠近苍穹，那么地球表面离苍穹更近的那个人将无法看到半个天空。但这与阿曼廷以及所有哲学家的说法相悖，他们断言，无论人类居住何处，总有六个星座升起，六个星座落下，一个星座是扭曲的，并且总有一半的天空可见，另一半对他隐藏。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Dead Magic<BR>
A lecture by Archmagister Xodores, delivered at the Anticlere Mages Guild<BR>
3e 422<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
In times past, learned scholars assumed a kind of stasis in the physical world, which stood in contrast to the endless, shifting change of the arcane. The imposition of the arcane on physicality begat magic, according to these old notions, and brought about the forces of Change and Chaos to afflict our world. The Lorkhanic cults in their various shapes revered this interaction of stasis and change, though perhaps never fully grasping the implications of their belief.
<BR>
Mages of the modern era, those of our Guild foremost among them, have admirably striven to observe, measure, catalog, and replicate arcane phenomena. Skilled enchanters have gone so far as to standardize and bring to market spells once thought to be attainable only to the gifted after a lifetime of study. Anchor teleportation, for example, was assumed for centuries to be tied inexorably to the holy sites of divine beings, an expression of godly will which mortals could never harness without building a holy site. Now, we know that the anchor of a teleportation spell can be as mundane as a closet, or an alley, or a cave.
<BR>
By and large, the story of the Mages Guild -- the story of Magic -- has been "We did not know this, and now we do." Tamriel's naturalists have welcomed this development, and hope for the day when arcana might be thought of as one of the many sciences, rather than an unknowable art reserved for the naturally talented. Some in the Guild itself believe this revolution in understanding is at hand, perhaps very soon.
<BR>
These hopes are folly. Magic is not science, and magic can never be science. A mage who neglects to account for this essential fact is in enormous danger.
<BR>
We must not forget, my colleagues, that the path of arcane learning has not been a steady upward climb. Indeed, a sympathetic scholar might argue that the lifetime of this Guild represents the longest period of sustained magical innovation in recorded history. Most of the past does not share this quality. Consider, for example, our earlier example: teleportation. As the Guild Guides among you will no doubt recall from your studies, mages in ancient times experimented with other forms of teleportation, dissatisfied with the limitations of divine anchors and liminal bridges. An eastern mage called Barilzar was the most successful of these, creating a famed artifact which could punch holes in the very fabric of reality and drag the wearer through them.
<BR>
But the fate of Barilzar is a warning. The spell he created fought back. One day, unexpectedly, the magic started failing. Barilizar could no longer flit from city to city with ease, but instead found himself violently tossed from high frozen mountaintops to deep ocean trenches. As the artifact stopped responding to his control entirely, his life became a torment, his waking hours consumed by the enchantment he'd brought to life. In the end, it is said that Barilzar was stripped of his own flesh and blood by the Mazed Band, cursed to live a doomed and wretched half-life, torn between this world and the liminal holes he'd carved through it.
<BR>
The horror of Barilzar's story conceals a deeper and more pressing lesson for the modern mage. Magic is change, and change cannot be permanently classified, nor understood forever. Consistency is not in its nature.
<BR>
As we reflect on the loss of Passwall, and continue our studies into the nature of the Warp in the West, consider this lesson. While our brightest minds may endlessly probe the deep caverns of the arcane, and even innovate upon what we learn there, we should never be surprised when the ever-shifting miasma of that world realigns itself. A mage who forgets this fundamental fact risks being consumed by unreality.
<BR><BR><BR>
Publisher's note: as of 3e 426, Archmagister Xodores has not been seen publicly since his lecture in Anticlere.
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
死魔法<BR>
大导师克索多雷斯在安提克莱尔法师公会的演讲<BR>
第三纪元422年<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
在过去，博学的学者们假设物理世界存在某种停滞状态，这与奥秘世界无尽的变化形成对比。根据这些旧观念，奥秘对物理性的施加产生了魔法，并带来了改变与混乱的力量来折磨我们的世界。洛克汗教派以各种形式尊崇这种停滞与变化的互动，尽管他们可能从未完全领会其信仰的含义。
<BR>
现代法师，尤其是我们公会的法师，在观察、测量、分类和复制奥秘现象方面做出了令人钦佩的努力。技艺精湛的附魔师甚至将曾经被认为只有天赋异禀者经过毕生学习才能掌握的法术标准化并推向市场。例如，锚点传送术，几个世纪以来被认为与神圣存在的圣地密不可分，是神圣意志的表达，凡人若不建造圣地就无法驾驭。现在，我们知道传送术的锚点可以像壁橱、小巷或洞穴一样平凡。
<BR>
总的来说，法师公会的故事 -- 魔法的故事 -- 一直是“我们以前不知道这个，现在知道了。”泰姆瑞尔的博物学家欢迎这一发展，并期待有一天奥秘学能被视作众多科学之一，而非仅为天赋异禀者保留的不可知艺术。公会中的一些人相信这场理解上的革命即将到来，也许很快。
<BR>
这些希望是愚蠢的。魔法不是科学，魔法也永远不可能成为科学。忽视这一基本事实的法师将面临巨大的危险。
<BR>
我们必须记住，我的同事们，奥秘学习的道路并非稳步向上的攀登。事实上，一位富有同情心的学者可能会争辩说，我们这个公会存在的时期代表了有记录以来持续时间最长的持续魔法创新时期。过去的大部分时间并非如此。例如，考虑我们之前的例子：传送术。你们中的公会向导无疑会从学习中回忆起，古代法师对神锚和阈限桥梁的限制不满，实验了其他形式的传送术。一位名叫巴里尔扎的东方法师是其中最成功的，他创造了一件著名的神器，能够在现实的织布上打洞，并将穿戴者拖拽通过。
<BR>
但巴里尔扎的命运是一个警告。他创造的法术反噬了。有一天，魔法意外地开始失灵。巴里尔扎不再能轻松地从一座城市穿梭到另一座城市，而是发现自己被猛烈地从高高的冰封山顶抛到深海海沟。当神器完全停止响应他的控制时，他的生活变成了一种折磨，他醒着的每一刻都被他创造出来的附魔所吞噬。据说，最后巴里尔扎被迷宫之环剥去了血肉，被诅咒过着注定悲惨的半生，徘徊在这个世界和他自己凿穿的阈限洞穴之间。
<BR>
巴里尔扎故事的恐怖，为现代法师隐藏了一个更深层、更紧迫的教训。魔法即变化，而变化不能被永久分类，也无法被永远理解。一致性并非其本性。
<BR>
当我们反思穿墙术的失传，并继续研究西部扭曲的本质时，请考虑这个教训。虽然我们最聪明的头脑可能会无休止地探索奥秘的深处洞穴，甚至在我们所学的知识上进行创新，但当那个世界不断变化的迷雾自我调整时，我们永远不应感到惊讶。忘记这一基本事实的法师，有被非现实吞噬的风险。
<BR><BR><BR>
出版者注：截至第三纪元426年，大导师克索多雷斯在安提克莱尔演讲后，未再公开露面。
<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Practical Defense of Morrowind Volume I: Island Strongholds<BR>
by Apelle Laecinnius<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The purpose of this report is to inform Imperial authority on the fortifications constructed within the Province of Morrowind, should there be any issues with the local populace, or invaders from Akavir or another foreign continent of Nirn. It will discuss particular fortifications, as well as fortifiable locations and possible vulnerabilities. Skyrim and the Black Marsh will not be mentioned herein, as separate observers have been sent to those Provinces to draft similar assessments. In this first volume, the fortifications of Vvardenfell, Solstheim, the Telvanni Isles and a number of other minor islands will be discussed. In the second volume, the mainland will be discussed. Great House fortifications will be mentioned, as they would prove a pivotal part of the Empire's defensive forces in the event of an invasion. While internal threats are certainly possible, such as rebellion in one or more of the Great Houses, or sabotage attempted by the Twin Lamps, they will not be discussed as such a rebellious group cannot, of itself, pose a significantly large threat to Morrowind and Imperial order therein.<BR>
<BR>
The wintry island of Solstheim is poorly defended and boasts only a single Imperial stronghold in the south, Fort Frostmoth. Relations between the Skaal, a native Nordic tribe, and the Empire are virtually nonexistent, and it is unlikely that they would offer aid, arms, or skill to the Empire in the event of an invasion. Castle Karstaag in the north is in an excellent strategic position to hold solid control of the isle's northwestern reaches, but is populated by another native group known as the Rieklings. There are a number of reasonably sized rivers on the island, but the frozen lake Fjalding would do much to hinder water-based troop movements. Given the difficulties inherent in the defense of the island, and its failure to provide any resource worth maintaining, it is my recommendation that, in the event of an invasion, Fort Frostmoth should simply be abandoned, and the forces there allocated to more defensible locales such as Blacklight or northern cities on Vvardenfell.<BR>
<BR>
To the southeast of Solstheim, lies the Sheogorad Region, a grouping of many small islands, many rocks and shallow water. Due to the abundance of rocks protruding from the water and along coastlines, there are very few safe paths that allow travel through the area. There is but one harbor in the region, to be found at the only town in the area, Dagon Fel. Dagon Fel is all but unique in Morrowind, as it has no reigning affiliation. There is a minor Imperial presence, but it is often seen among the fighting men as a place for those who fail to perform. The town itself is poorly defended by an insufficient garrison of soldiers, and offers too little in the way of resources for any Great House to take interest in it. There are only two ways that the town could serve a purpose in a war, provided that the initial assaults come from the north: The destruction or capture of Dagon Fel would alert Morrowind proper to the presence of invaders and allow adequate time to mobilize the defense of the rest of the Province. The second purpose would be to use the local low life groups, exiles, criminals, and the rumored necromancer to defend the town, with a smaller force of Imperial troops in order to minimize casualties among our soldiers while still giving the enemy a fight. The criminals and such would be offered amnesty for their various crimes in return for military service, and, should they be lost in the defense of the town, our armies are none the poorer. Ideally, the town is held and warnings are sent to the rest of the province, or, non-ideally the town falls, there is still advance warning and Morrowind has fewer criminals to cause unrest. In the event that Dagon Fel is taken, it would provide a staging area for an attack on Vvardenfell, Solstheim, or the northern tip of the mainland. The many mines, Dwemer and Daedric ruins, and old Velothi towers in the area could give an invading army a multitude of hiding places, but ultimately trying to hold Dagon Fel might prove just as costly.<BR>
<BR>
Provided that the various Great House interests of Vvardenfell worked in harmony and under proper Imperial leadership, the great island would prove almost impregnable to any invading armies. The north is very poorly fortified, but is rife with natural features that would prevent large ships from moving close enough for safe deployment of foreign troops. In addition, the inhospitable Ashlands and Red Mountain regions are all but impassable for a large scale attack force; even locals familiar with such terrain find the areas dangerous. This is the most fortunate part of Vvardenfell's geography: that the center of the island is basically impassable for any amount of soldiers, forcing most of the attacks to come predictably along coastlines, making them easier to defend against.<BR>
<BR>
The east and west coastlines are strong, particularly in the Zafirbel Bay area in the east, and the Bitter Coast region in the west. An invasion of the northwest in the West Gash region would probably prove simplest, although there is little to gain in this more or less uninhabited region. In the central and southern parts of the western coast, an invasion would likely prove to be difficult, due to the abundance of defensible land based structures in vital locations along the coast. The ancient and currently unused Dunmer fortresses of Hlormaren, Andasreth, and Berandas all lie along the coast, and all close enough to reinforce each other. The cities of Gnaar Mok and Hla Oad are fairly insignificant in the event of an invasion, both having only token defenses and very minor docks. Provided the invaders were able to break through in this area, the heavily fortified cities of Caldera, Balmora and Ald'ruhn hold a solid line further inland, and these are further reinforced by the Imperial strongholds of Fort Moonmoth and Fort Buckmoth. Also within this area, there are the proposed sites for two Great House fortresses: one in the Odai Plateau and another in Bal Isra.<BR>
<BR>
To the south lies Seyda Neen, a minor Imperial-controlled port, and Pelagiad, another Imperial Legion fort. The true south of Vvardenfell is built up and quite well fortified, and is strictly monitored. The Ebonheart citadels on either side of the sea provide a vital choke point, should a ship-based attacking force attempt to reach anything beyond there without sailing in from the other side. The ancient city of Vivec is a veritable deathtrap to any who would choose to try and take it; by Dunmer reckoning, Vivec is a holy city, and the elite detachment of Ordinators there would defend the city ferociously. In addition to steadfast defenders, the city is also in an easily fortifiable position, and houses a living god.<BR>
<BR>
The east coast may not appear to be as well defended, but it is just as much so, if not more than Vivec itself. The Telvanni structures that seems so common to the area are easily defensible. A fair portion of them are also located on islands in the Zafirbel bay region, making them more difficult to assail, and forces attackers into weak postures as they must disembark on the low ground. Due to the strange magic that are in the possession of the Telvanni, any attackers are likely to face immediate, violent, and crushing resistance. The notable Imperial fortress in the area is Wolverine Hall, and given its extreme proximity to a Telvanni tower, Tel Naga, it is likely this joint position would be able to hold for some time in the event of a siege. Assuming that war was visited upon House Telvanni on any front, in any way, it is likely that the Telvanni xenophobia would drive them all the harder to defend their homes.<BR>
<BR>
A substantial weakness to all of Morrowind is the Firemoth Archipelago, located in between the west coast of Vvardenfell and the mainland of Morrowind. The former Imperial fortress of Fort Firemoth is located there, but is not in the hands of the Empire, instead being under the control of the lich Grurn. The lich's undead forces have occupied the fort for some time, but have been largely ignored because there has been no further aggressive activity in the area, and combat with undead has a significant demoralizing effect on our soldiers. This could be a massive weakness should an invader know of it--the waters are deep enough that ships could be sail into it from the north largely unmolested, and land in the archipelago. If an enemy were to have a staging area in this location, it could be devastating as attacks could be launched to any number of points, either on the mainland of Morrowind, or the isle of Vvardenfell. It is in the best interest of the entire province that Firemoth be retaken immediately, as it could easily be exploited by an invading enemy. Furthermore, it is recommended that it be retaken by a small, professional force, to covertly enter the area and purge the undead from the fortress due to the lich's ability to raise the dead and bind them into servitude. In the event that a large force landed, every casualty would simply mean another soldier for the enemy.<BR>
<BR>
The fortifications of the Telvanni Isles are sufficient. Although they would be struck very hard in the event of an invasion along the eastern coastline, the strength of the isles would certainly give the entire Province the opportunity to rally its defenses. While invaders could easily land in Port Telvannis due to its natural harbor, the resistance that they would face in the city from above, and the various magical defenses the Telvanni have in place would likely cripple the attacking force. Port Telvannis is even further well defended by the fact that Gah Sadrith lies across the harbor, and a force directly attacking the city of proper from the harbor could be flanked.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
晨风实用防御第一卷：岛屿据点<BR>
阿佩尔·莱西尼乌斯 著<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
本报告旨在向帝国当局通报晨风行省内的防御工事情况，以备当地民众出现问题，或来自阿卡维尔或奈恩其他外来大陆的入侵者时参考。它将讨论具体的防御工事，以及可设防地点和可能的弱点。此处不涉及天际省和黑沼泽省，因为已分别派遣观察员前往那些行省撰写类似评估。在第一卷中，将讨论瓦登费尔、索瑟泰姆、泰瓦尼群岛以及其他一些小岛的防御工事。第二卷将讨论大陆地区。大豪族的防御工事将会被提及，因为在发生入侵时，它们将被证明是帝国防御力量的关键部分。虽然内部威胁确实可能存在，例如一个或多个大豪族叛乱，或双灯会的破坏企图，但它们将不被讨论，因为这样的反叛团体本身无法对晨风及其内的帝国秩序构成重大威胁。<BR>
<BR>
寒冷的索瑟泰姆岛防御薄弱，南部只有一个帝国据点 -- 霜蛾堡。斯卡尔人（一个本土诺德部落）与帝国之间的关系几乎不存在，在发生入侵时，他们不太可能向帝国提供援助、武器或技能。北部的卡斯塔格堡处于极佳的战略位置，可以牢固控制该岛的西北部地区，但那里居住着另一个被称为裂客灵的本地族群。岛上有几条大小适中的河流，但冰冻的菲亚丁湖会极大地阻碍水上部队的调动。鉴于该岛防御固有的困难，以及它未能提供任何值得维护的资源，我建议，在发生入侵时，应放弃霜蛾堡，并将那里的部队调配到更易于防御的地点，如黑光或瓦登费尔的北部城市。<BR>
<BR>
索瑟泰姆东南方是谢奥格拉德地区，由众多小岛、礁石和浅水区组成。由于水中和沿海岸线突出的岩石众多，安全穿越该区域的路径非常有限。该地区只有一个港口，位于该地区唯一的城镇 -- 大衮·费尔。大衮·费尔在晨风几乎是独一无二的，因为它没有统治归属。存在少量帝国势力，但战斗人员常将其视为那些表现不佳者的去处。该镇本身防御薄弱，驻军不足，提供的资源也少得可怜，不足以引起任何大豪族的兴趣。假设最初的袭击来自北方，该镇在战争中只有两个用途：大衮·费尔的摧毁或陷落将提醒晨风本土入侵者的存在，并给予足够时间动员行省其余部分的防御。第二个用途是利用当地的底层群体、流放者、罪犯和传闻中的死灵法师来保卫该镇，同时派驻少量帝国军队，以尽量减少我方士兵的伤亡，同时仍与敌人交战。罪犯等人将获得各种罪行的赦免，以换取兵役，如果他们死于保卫该镇的战斗，我军也毫无损失。理想情况下，该镇被守住，并向行省其他地区发出警告；或者，非理想情况下，该镇陷落，仍有预先警告，并且晨风减少了可能引发骚乱的罪犯。如果大衮·费尔被占领，它将为进攻瓦登费尔、索瑟泰姆或大陆北端提供一个集结区域。该地区众多的矿场、锻莫和迪德拉废墟以及古老的维洛提塔楼，可能为入侵军队提供大量藏身之处，但最终试图守住大衮·费尔可能同样代价高昂。<BR>
<BR>
如果瓦登费尔各豪族的利益能够在适当的帝国领导下协调一致，那么这座大岛对任何入侵军队来说几乎都是坚不可摧的。北部防御非常薄弱，但拥有丰富的自然特征，可以阻止大型船只靠近到足以安全部署外国军队的距离。此外，不适宜居住的灰烬之地和红山地区几乎无法通过大规模攻击部队；即使是熟悉此类地形的当地人也认为这些地区很危险。这是瓦登费尔地理最有利的部分：岛屿中心基本上无法让任何数量的士兵通过，迫使大多数攻击可预测地沿着海岸线进行，从而使它们更容易防御。<BR>
<BR>
东海岸和西海岸都很坚固，尤其是东部的扎菲贝尔湾地区和西部的苦涩海岸地区。在西北部的西境之痕地区发动入侵可能是最简单的，尽管在这个几乎无人居住的地区几乎没有收获。在西海岸的中部和南部，入侵可能会很困难，因为沿海关键位置有大量可防御的陆上建筑。古老且目前闲置的丹莫堡垒赫洛马伦、安达斯瑞斯和贝兰达斯都位于海岸线上，并且距离足够近，可以互相支援。在发生入侵时，纳尔·莫克和哈拉·奥德等城市相当微不足道，它们都只有象征性的防御和非常小的码头。如果入侵者能够突破该地区，卡尔德拉、巴尔莫拉和奥德-汝因等防御森严的城市将在更内陆的地方形成一条坚固的防线，而月蛾堡和雄蛾堡等帝国据点进一步加强了这些防线。此外，该区域内还有两个大豪族堡垒的选址：一个在奥代高原，另一个在巴尔·伊斯拉。<BR>
<BR>
南部是赛达·尼恩，一个由帝国控制的小港口，以及佩拉吉亚德，另一个帝国军团堡垒。瓦登费尔真正的南部地区建设完善，防御良好，并受到严格监控。海两岸的黑檀心城堡提供了一个重要的咽喉要道，如果一支舰载攻击部队试图在不从另一侧驶入的情况下，到达更远的地方。古老的维威克城对任何试图占领它的人来说都是一个名副其实的死亡陷阱；根据丹莫的说法，维威克是一座圣城，那里的精英调度使分队将凶猛保卫这座城市。除了坚定的防御者，该城也处于易于防御的位置，并且居住着一位现世神。<BR>
<BR>
东海岸可能看起来防御不那么严密，但实际上其防御程度不亚于维威克城本身。该地区看似常见的泰瓦尼建筑很容易防御。其中相当一部分也位于扎菲贝尔湾地区的岛屿上，使它们更难被攻击，并迫使攻击者处于弱势地位，因为他们必须在低处登陆。由于泰瓦尼人拥有的奇异魔法，任何攻击者都可能面临即时、猛烈和粉碎性的抵抗。该地区著名的帝国堡垒是金刚狼大厅，鉴于其与泰瓦尼塔楼泰尔·纳加极其接近，在围城的情况下，这个联合据点很可能能坚守一段时间。假设战争以任何方式在任何战线降临到泰瓦尼家族，泰瓦尼人的排外心理很可能驱使他们更加努力地保卫家园。<BR>
<BR>
整个晨风的一个重大弱点是火蛾群岛，位于瓦登费尔西海岸和晨风大陆之间。前帝国要塞火蛾堡就位于那里，但并不在帝国手中，而是由巫妖格伦控制。巫妖的亡灵部队占据该堡垒已有一段时间，但基本上被忽视了，因为该地区没有进一步的侵略活动，而且与亡灵战斗对我们士兵的士气有显著影响。如果入侵者知道这一点，这可能是一个巨大的弱点 -- 水域足够深，船只可以从北部大致不受阻碍地驶入，并在群岛登陆。如果敌人在此位置有一个集结区域，那可能是毁灭性的，因为可以从那里向晨风大陆或瓦登费尔岛上的任意多个点发动攻击。立即夺回火蛾符合整个行省的最大利益，因为它很容易被入侵敌军利用。此外，建议由一支小型专业部队夺回它，秘密进入该地区并清除堡垒中的亡灵，因为巫妖有能力复活死者并将其束缚为仆从。如果一支大军登陆，每一个伤亡只会意味着敌军多一个士兵。<BR>
<BR>
泰瓦尼群岛的防御工事是足够的。尽管在沿海岸线入侵时它们会受到沉重打击，但群岛的实力无疑会给整个行省集结防御的机会。虽然入侵者可以利用天然港口轻松在泰瓦尼港登陆，但他们在城市中会面临来自上方的抵抗，以及泰瓦尼人部署的各种魔法防御，可能会严重削弱攻击力量。泰瓦尼港的防御进一步加强，因为加·萨德里斯位于港湾对面，从港口直接攻击城市本身的部队可能会受到侧翼攻击。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Destruction or Distraction<BR>
by Humius Acidinus<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
It is popular, especially among young upstarts who wish to establish themselves as intellectual contenders, to dismiss the study of harnessing the destructive potential of magicka as crude or simplistic. Those who embrace this argument prefer to spend time researching obscure theoretical topics instead of the more practical applications of magic.<BR>
<BR>
In truth, these pedants accomplish little beyond writing tomes of their own to refute the postulations of their contemporaries, wasting their time arguing hypotheticals with no basis in practical magical study. They are so distracted trying to outwit one another in their imaginary field that they never produce substantial advancements. It is my conviction that this self-indulgent behavior obstructs progress (concrete gains such as spell discovery) in arcane studies.<BR>
<BR>
I do not deny that magic is deep and complex, and our understanding is far from complete. However, I question the value of arguments over theories with very little basis in observable phenomena before we fully grasp less complicated subjects. In my years of practice, I have found that studying manifestations of magicka that seem the simplest often provides the clearest look at the nature of magic. Without a complete understanding of what seems to be basic, how could anyone advance magic and bring benefit to practitioners and Tamriel at large? I implore you, reader, to take care that you do not fall into the category of the fruitless intellectual.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
毁灭还是分心<BR>
胡米乌斯·阿西迪努斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
有些人，尤其是那些急于确立自己学识地位的新锐，总喜欢贬低驾驭魔能毁灭性力量的研究，视之为粗陋或幼稚之举。抱持这种论调的人，宁愿花时间去钻研那些晦涩的理论课题，也不愿从事更具实用价值的魔法研究。<BR>
<BR>
事实上，这些学究们所成之事，除了撰写大部头著作来驳斥同代人的论点之外，实在寥寥。他们浪费时间争论那些毫无实践根基的假设，沉溺于在想象领域中彼此斗智，以至于从未产生过实质性的进步。我深信，这种自娱自乐的行为，恰恰阻碍了玄秘研究的前进（如新法术发现这类切实成果）。<BR>
<BR>
我并非否认魔法的深邃与复杂，以及我们认知的远未完善。然而，在我们尚未完全掌握那些较为简单的课题之前，我对于争论那些几乎无可观测现象支持的理论有何价值，深表怀疑。在我多年的实践中，我发现，研究那些看似最简单的魔能表现形式，往往最能揭示魔法的本质。若连看似基础的东西都无法完全理解，又如何能推进魔法，造福施法者乃至整个泰姆瑞尔呢？我恳请读者诸君，切勿沦为那类徒劳无功的空谈者。<BR>
<BR>"""
