> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_DisasterAtIonithOpenPC
Disaster at Ionith
艾奥尼斯之灾

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_DisasterAtIonithOpenPC
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Disaster at Ionith<BR>
By Lord Pottreid, Chairman<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Part I: Preparations<BR>
<BR>
The Emperor's plans for the invasion of Akavir were laid in the 270s, when he began the conquest of the small island kingdoms that lie between Tamriel and Akavir. With the fall of Black Harbor in Esroniet in 282, Uriel V was already looking ahead to the ultimate prize. He immediately ordered extensive renovations to the port, which would serve as the marshalling point for the invasion force and as the main supply source throughout the campaign. At this time he also began the construction of the many large, ocean-going transports that would be needed for the final crossing to Akavir, in which the Navy was previously deficient. Thus it can be seen that the Emperor's preparations for the invasion were laid well in advance, before even the conquest of Esroniet was complete, and was not a sudden whim as some have charged.<BR>
<BR>
When Prince Bashomon yielded Esroniet to Imperial authority in 284, the Emperor's full attention could be devoted to planning for the Akaviri campaign. Naval expeditions were dispatched in 285 and 286 to scout the sea lanes and coastlands of Akavir; and various Imperial intelligence agents, both magical and mundane, were employed to gather information. On the basis of all this information, the kingdom of the Tsaesci, in the southwest of Akavir, was selected as the initial target for the invasion.<BR>
<BR>
Meanwhile the Emperor was gathering his Expeditionary Force. A new Far East Fleet was created for the campaign, which for a time dwarfed the rest of the Navy; it is said to be the most powerful fleet ever assembled in the history of Tamriel. The Fifth, Seventh, Tenth, and Fourteenth Legions were selected for the initial landing, with the Ninth and Seventeenth to follow as reinforcements once the beachhead was secured. While this may seem to the layman a relatively small fraction of the Army's total manpower, it must be remembered that this Expeditionary Force would have to be maintained at the end of a long and tenuous supply line; in addition, the Emperor and the Army command believed that the invasion would not be strongly opposed, at least at first. Perhaps most crucially, the Navy had only enough heavy transport capacity to move four legions at a time.<BR>
<BR>
It should be noted here that the Commission does not find fault with the Emperor's preparations for the invasion. Based on the information available prior to the invasion, (which, while obviously deficient in hindsight, great effort had been made to accumulate), the Commission believes that the Emperor did not act recklessly or imprudently. Some have argued that the Expeditionary Force was too small. The Commission believes that on the contrary, even if shipping could have been found to transport and supply more legions (an impossibility without crippling the trade of the entire Empire), this would have merely added to the scale of the disaster; it would not have averted it. Neither could the rest of the Empire be denuded of legions; the memory of the Camoran Usurper was still fresh, and the Emperor believed (and this Commission agrees) that the security of the Empire precluded a larger concentration of military force outside of Tamriel. If anything, the Commission believes that the Expeditionary Force was too large. Despite the creation of two new legions during his reign (and the recreation of the Fifth), the loss of the Expeditionary Force left the Empire in a dangerously weak position relative to the provinces, as the current situation makes all too clear. This suggests that the invasion of Akavir was beyond the Empire's current strength; even if the Emperor could have fielded and maintained a larger force in Akavir, the Empire may have disintegrated behind him.<BR>
<BR>
Part II: The Invasion of Akavir<BR>
<BR>
The Expeditionary Force left Black Harbor on 23rd Rain's Hand, 288, and with fair weather landed in Akavir after six weeks at sea. The landing site was a small Tsaesci port at the mouth of a large river, chosen for its proximity to Tamriel as well as its location in a fertile river valley, giving easy access to the interior as well as good foraging for the army. All went well at first. The Tsaesci had abandoned the town when the Expeditionary Force approached, so they took possession of it and renamed it Septimia, the first colony of the new Imperial Province of Akavir. While the engineers fortified the town and expanded the port facilities to serve the Far East Fleet, the Emperor marched inland with two legions. The surrounding land was reported to be rich, well-watered fields, and meeting no resistance the army took the next city upriver, also abandoned. This was refounded as Ionith, and the Emperor established his headquarters there, being much larger than Septimia and better-located to dominate the surrounding countryside.<BR>
<BR>
The Expeditionary Force had yet to meet any real resistance, although the legions were constantly shadowed by mounted enemy patrols which prevented any but large scouting parties from leaving the main body of the army. One thing the Emperor sorely lacked was cavalry, due to the limited space on the transport fleet, although for the time being the battlemages made up for this with magical reconnaissance.<BR>
<BR>
The Emperor now sent out envoys to try to contact the Tsaesci king or whoever ruled this land, but his messengers never returned. In retrospect, the Commission believes that valuable time was wasted in this effort while the army was stalled at Ionith, which could have been better spent in advancing quickly while the enemy was still, apparently, surprised by the invasion. However, the Emperor believed at the time that the Tsaesci could be overawed by the Empire's power and he might win a province by negotiation with no need for serious fighting.<BR>
<BR>
Meanwhile, the four legions were busy building a road between Septimia and Ionith, setting up fortified guard posts along the river, and fortifying both cities' defenses, activities which would serve them well later. Due to their lack of cavalry, scouting was limited, and communication between the two cities constantly threatened by enemy raiders, with which the legions were still unable to come to grips.<BR>
<BR>
The original plan had been to bring the two reinforcing legions across as soon as the initial landing had secured a port, but the fateful decision was now taken to delay their arrival and instead begin using the Fleet to transport colonists. The Emperor and the Council agreed that, due to the complete abandonment of the conquered area by its native population, colonists were needed to work the fields so that the Expeditionary Force would not have to rely entirely on the fleet for supplies. In addition, unrest had broken out in Yneslea, athwart the supply route to Akavir, and the Council believed the Ninth and Seventeenth legions would be better used in repacifying those territories and securing the Expeditionary Force's supply lines.<BR>
<BR>
The civilian colonists and their supplies began arriving in Septimia in mid-Hearthfire, and they took over the preparation of the fields (which had been started by the legionnaires) for a spring crop. A number of cavalry mounts were also brought over at this time, and the raids on the two Imperial colonies subsequently fell off. Tsaesci emissaries also finally arrived in Ionith, purportedly to begin peace negotiations, and the Expeditionary Force settled in for what was expected to be a quiet winter.<BR>
<BR>
At this time, the Council urged the Emperor to return to Tamriel with the Fleet, to deal with many pressing matters of the Empire while the army was in winter quarters, but the Emperor decided that it would be best to remain in Akavir. This turned out to be fortunate, because a large portion of the Fleet, including the Emperor's flagship, was destroyed by an early winter storm during the homeward voyage. The winter storm season of 288-289 was unusually prolonged and exceptionally severe, and prevented the Fleet from returning to Akavir as planned with additional supplies. This was reported to the Emperor via battlemage and it was agreed that the Expeditionary Force could survive on what supplies it had on hand until the spring.<BR>
<BR>
Part III: The Destruction of the Expeditionary Force<BR>
<BR>
The winter weather in Akavir was also much more severe than expected. Due to the supply problems and the addition of thousands of civilians, the Expeditionary Force was on tight rations. To make matters worse, the Tsaesci raiders returned in force and harried any foraging and scouting parties outside the walls of the two cities. Several watch forts on the road between Septimia and Ionith were captured during blizzards, and the rest had to be abandoned as untenable. As a result, communication between the two cities had to be conducted entirely by magical means, a continuing strain on the legions' battlemages.<BR>
<BR>
On 5th Sun's Dawn, a large entourage of Tsaesci arrived at Ionith claiming to bring a peace offer from the Tsaesci king. That night, these treacherous envoys murdered the guards at one of the city gates and let in a strong party of their comrades who were waiting outside the city walls. Their clear intention was to assassinate the Emperor, foiled only by the vigilance and courage of troopers of the Tenth who were guarding his palace. Once the alarm was raised, the Tsaesci inside the city were hunted down and killed to the last man. Needless to say, this was the end of negotiations between the Emperor and the Tsaesci.<BR>
<BR>
The arrival of spring only brought worse troubles. Instead of the expected spring rains, a hot dry wind began to blow from the east, continuing with varying strength through the entire summer. The crops failed, and even the river (which in the previous year had been navigable by small boats far upstream of Ionith) was completely dried up by Sun's Height. It is unknown if this was due to a previously unknown weather pattern unique to Akavir, or if the Tsaesci manipulated the weather through magical means. The Commission leans towards the former conclusion, as there is no direct evidence of the Tsaesci possessing such fearsome arcane power, but the latter possibility cannot be entirely ruled out.<BR>
<BR>
Due to prolonged bad weather, the supply fleet was late in setting out from Black Harbor. It finally left port in early Second Seed, but was again severely mauled by storms and limped into Septimia eight weeks later much reduced. Because of the increasingly desperate supply situation in Akavir, the Emperor dispatched most of his Battlemage Corps with the fleet to assist it in weathering the storms which seemed likely to continue all summer. At this time, the Council urged the Emperor to abandon the invasion and to return to Tamriel with the Expeditionary Force, but he again refused, noting that the fleet was no longer large enough to transport all four legions at once. The Commission agrees that leaving one or more legions behind in Akavir to await the return of the fleet would have damaged Army morale. But the Commission also notes that the loss of one legion would have been preferable to the loss of the entire Expeditionary Force. It is the unanimous opinion of the Commission that this was the last point at which complete disaster might have been averted. Once the decision was made to send the fleet back for reinforcements and supplies, events proceeded to their inevitable conclusion.<BR>
<BR>
From this point on, much less is known about what transpired in Akavir. With most of the battlemages assisting the fleet, communication between the Expeditionary Force and Tamriel was limited, especially as the situation in Akavir worsened and the remaining battlemages had their powers stretched to the limit attending to all the needs of the legions. However, it appears that the Tsaesci may also have been actively interfering with the mages in some unknown manner. Some of the mages in Akavir reported their powers being abnormally weak, and the mages of the War College in Cyrodiil (who were handling communications for the Council) reported problems linking up with their compatriots in Akavir, even between master and pupil of long training. The Commission urges that the War College make a particular study of the arcane powers of the Tsaesci, should the Empire ever come into conflict with Akavir again.<BR>
<BR>
What is known is that the Emperor marched out of Ionith in mid-Sun's Height, leaving only small garrisons to hold the cities. He had learned that the Tsaesci were massing their forces on the other side of a mountain range to the north, and he intended to smash their army before it could gather full strength and capture their supplies (of which he was in desperate need). This rapid advance seems to have taken the Tsaesci by surprise, and the Expeditionary Force crossed the mountains and fell on their camp, routing the Tsaesci army and capturing its leader (a noble of some kind). But the Emperor was soon forced to retreat, and the legions suffered heavily on their retreat to Ionith. The Emperor now found himself besieged in Ionith, cut off from the small garrison at Septimia which was also besieged. By this time, it seems that the efforts of the few remaining battlemages were devoted entirely to creating water to keep the army alive, a skill not normally emphasized at the War College. The fleet had arrived safely back to Black Harbor, thanks to the Battlemage Corps, but all attempts to return to Akavir were frustrated by a series of ever more savage storms that battered Esroniet throughout the rest of 289.<BR>
<BR>
The Council's last contact with the Emperor was in early Frostfall. By Evening Star, the Council was extremely worried about the situation in Akavir and ordered the fleet to sail regardless of the risk. Despite the continued storms, the fleet managed to press on to Akavir. Hope was raised when contact was made with the Emperor's battlemage, who reported that Ionith still held out. Plans were quickly laid for the Expeditionary Force to break out of Ionith and fall back on Septimia, where the fleet would meet them. This was the last direct contact with the Expeditionary Force. The fleet arrived in Septimia to find its garrison under savage assault from a large Tsaesci army. The battlemages with the fleet threw back the enemy long enough for the survivors to embark and the fleet to withdraw.<BR>
<BR>
The few survivors of the Expeditionary Force who reached Septimia told how the Emperor had led the army out of Ionith by night two days earlier, successfully breaking through the enemy lines but then being surrounded by overwhelming forces on the road to Septimia. They told of a heroic last stand by the Emperor and the Tenth Legion, which allowed a remnant of the Fourteenth to reach Septimia. Two survivors of the Tenth arrived in Septimia that night, having slipped through the enemy lines during their undisciplined victory celebration. These men confirmed having seen the Emperor die, cut down by enemy arrows as he rallied the Tenth's shield wall.<BR>
<BR>
Part IV: Conclusion<BR>
<BR>
The Commission believes that the invasion of Akavir was doomed from the start for several reasons, none of which could have been foreseen beforehand, unfortunately.<BR>
<BR>
Despite extensive intelligence-gathering, the Expeditionary Force was clearly unprepared for the situation in Akavir. The unexpected weather which plagued the army and navy was particularly disastrous. Without the loss of a majority of the Far East Fleet during the campaign, the Expeditionary Force could have been withdrawn in 289. The weather also forced the Emperor to assign most of his Battlemage Corps to the fleet, leaving him without their valuable assistance during the fighting which soon followed. And of course the unexpected drought which struck Ionith during 289 dashed the hopes of supplying the army locally, and left the Expeditionary Force in an untenable situation when besieged in Ionith.<BR>
<BR>
The Tsaesci were also much stronger than intelligence reports had suggested. Information on the size of the army the Tsaesci were eventually able to field against the Expeditionary Force is vague, as the only serious fighting took place after regular communications were cut off between the Emperor and the Council. Nevertheless, it seems likely that the Tsaesci outnumbered the Emperor's forces by several times, as they were able to force four crack legions into retreat and then keep them under siege for several months.<BR>
<BR>
As was stated previously, the Commission declines to criticize the initial decision to invade Akavir. Based on what was known at the time, the plan seemed sound. It is only with the benefit of hindsight does it become obvious that the invasion had very little chance of success. Nevertheless, the Commission believes several valuable lessons can be taken from this disaster.<BR>
<BR>
First, the Tsaesci may have extremely powerful arcane forces at their command. The possibility that they may have manipulated the weather across such a vast region seems incredible (and it should be noted that three Commissioners strongly objected to this paragraph even being included in this Report), but the Commission believes that this matter deserves urgent investigation. The potential danger is such that even the slight possibility must be taken seriously.<BR>
<BR>
Second, the Tsaesci appear to possess no navy to speak of. The Expeditionary Force was never threatened by sea, and the Far East Fleet fought nothing but the weather. Indeed, initial plans called for a portion of the Fleet to remain in Akavir for use in coastal operations, but in the event there were very few places where the large vessels of the Fleet could approach the land, due to the innumerable reefs, sandbars, islands, etc. that infested the coastal waters north and south from Septimia. Due to the utter lack of trees in the plain around Septimia and Ionith, the Expeditionary Force was unable to build smaller vessels which could have navigated the shallow coastal waters. Any future military expeditions against Akavir would do well to consider some way of bringing a means for inshore naval operations in order to exploit this clear advantage over the Tsaesci, an advantage that was sadly unexploited by the Expeditionary Force.<BR>
<BR>
Third, much longer-term study needs to be made of Akavir before another invasion could even be contemplated. The information gathered over the four years prior to the invasion was extensive, but clearly inadequate. The weather conditions were completely unexpected; the Tsaesci much stronger than expected; and the attempted negotiations by the Emperor with the Tsaesci a disaster. Akavir proved alien beyond expectation, and the Commission believes any future attempt to invade Akavir should not be contemplated without much greater knowledge of the conditions, politics, and peoples of that continent than presently obtains.<BR>
<BR>
Finally, the Commission unanimously concludes that given what we now know, any attempt to invade Akavir is folly, at least in the present state of the Empire. The Empire's legions are needed at home. One day, a peaceful, united Empire will return to Akavir and exact severe retribution for the disaster at Ionith and for our fallen Emperor. But that day is not now, nor in the foreseeable future.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
艾奥尼斯之灾<BR>
波特雷德勋爵，主席 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
第一部分：准备<BR>
<BR>
皇帝入侵阿卡维尔的计划于270年代制定，当时他开始征服泰姆瑞尔与阿卡维尔之间的小岛国。随着282年埃斯罗涅特的黑港陷落，尤利尔五世已着眼于最终目标。他立即下令对港口进行大规模扩建，使其成为入侵部队的集结点和整个战役的主要补给来源。同时他也开始建造许多最终跨越阿卡维尔所需的大型远洋运输船，此前海军在这方面有所欠缺。可见皇帝对入侵的准备是提前很久就制定的，甚至在征服埃斯罗涅特完成之前，并非如某些人所指责的那样是一时兴起。<BR>
<BR>
当巴肖蒙王子于284年将埃斯罗涅特交予帝国管辖后，皇帝得以全力策划阿卡维尔战役。285年和286年派出了海军远征队侦察阿卡维尔的海道和沿海地区；各种帝国情报人员，无论魔法还是常规手段，都被用来收集信息。基于所有这些信息，阿卡维尔西南部的赛埃锡王国被选为入侵的初始目标。<BR>
<BR>
与此同时，皇帝正在集结远征军。为这次战役新建了远东舰队，一度使其他海军相形见绌；据说是泰姆瑞尔历史上最强大的舰队。第五、第七、第十和第十四军团被选为初始登陆部队，第九和第十七军团将在滩头阵地巩固后作为增援跟进。虽然对外行人来说这似乎只是陆军总兵力的一小部分，但必须记住这支远征军必须通过漫长而脆弱的补给线维持；此外，皇帝和陆军指挥部认为入侵不会遇到强烈抵抗，至少初期如此。也许最关键的是，海军只有足够一次运输四个军团的重型运力。<BR>
<BR>
此处应指出，委员会并不认为皇帝对入侵的准备有错。根据入侵前可获得的信息（尽管事后看来明显不足，但已尽力收集），委员会认为皇帝并未鲁莽或轻率行事。有人辩称远征军规模太小。委员会认为恰恰相反，即使能找到船只运输和补给更多军团（若不损害整个帝国的贸易则不可能），那也只是加剧灾难的规模，而无法避免灾难。帝国其他地区也不能被剥空军团；篡位者卡莫兰的记忆犹新，皇帝认为（委员会也同意）帝国安全不允许在泰姆瑞尔以外集中更多军事力量。如果非要说，委员会认为远征军规模太大了。尽管他在位期间新建了两个军团（并重建了第五军团），远征军的损失使帝国相对于行省处于危险弱势地位，当前形势已清楚表明。这表明入侵阿卡维尔超出了帝国当时的力量；即使皇帝能在阿卡维尔部署和维持更大兵力，帝国也可能在他身后分崩离析。<BR>
<BR>
第二部分：入侵阿卡维尔<BR>
<BR>
远征军于288年雨手月23日离开黑港，在海上航行六周后，天气晴朗，在阿卡维尔登陆。登陆点是一个小赛埃锡港口，位于一条大河河口，因其靠近泰姆瑞尔以及位于肥沃河谷的位置而被选中，便于深入内陆和军队觅食。起初一切顺利。远征军接近时，赛埃锡人已弃城，他们占领了该城并将其更名为塞普提米亚，成为新阿卡维尔帝国行省的第一个殖民地。工程师们加固城镇并扩建港口设施以服务远东舰队的同时，皇帝率两个军团向内陆进军。据报道周围土地肥沃、水源充足，军队未遇抵抗便占领了上游下一座城市，同样被遗弃。该城被重建为艾奥尼斯，皇帝在那里建立了指挥部，它比塞普提米亚大得多，位置更佳，便于控制周边乡村。<BR>
<BR>
远征军尚未遇到任何真正抵抗，尽管军团一直被敌方骑兵巡逻队跟踪，阻止了除大型侦察队之外的任何人离开主力。皇帝严重缺乏骑兵，由于运输舰队空间有限，尽管战斗法师暂时用魔法侦察弥补了这一不足。<BR>
<BR>
皇帝随后派出使者试图联系赛埃锡国王或任何统治者，但使者从未返回。回顾来看，委员会认为在这一努力上浪费了宝贵时间，而军队在艾奥尼斯停滞不前，这段时间本可用于快速推进，趁敌方显然还对入侵感到惊讶之际。然而，皇帝当时相信赛埃锡人会被帝国的力量震慑，他可能通过谈判赢得一个行省，无需激战。<BR>
<BR>
同时，四个军团忙于修建塞普提米亚与艾奥尼斯之间的道路，沿河设立设防哨所，并加强两城防御，这些活动日后证明很有价值。由于缺乏骑兵，侦察受限，两城之间的通讯不断受到敌方袭击者的威胁，军团仍无法与之交锋。<BR>
<BR>
原计划是在初始登陆确保港口后立即将两个增援军团运来，但作出了推迟其抵达、转而开始使用舰队运送殖民者的命运性决定。皇帝和议会同意，由于被征服地区的原住民完全撤离，需要殖民者耕种田地，以便远征军不必完全依赖舰队补给。此外，伊内斯利亚爆发了动乱，横亘在通往阿卡维尔的补给路线上，议会认为第九和第十七军团更适合用于重新平定那些领土并确保远征军的补给线。<BR>
<BR>
平民殖民者及其补给于炉火月中旬开始抵达塞普提米亚，他们接管了田地准备工作（由军团士兵开始）以备春耕。此时也运来了一些骑兵坐骑，随后对两个帝国殖民地的袭击减少了。赛埃锡使者终于抵达艾奥尼斯，据称开始和平谈判，远征军安顿下来，准备度过一个预期的平静冬天。<BR>
<BR>
此时，议会敦促皇帝随舰队返回泰姆瑞尔，处理帝国的许多紧迫事务，而军队在冬季营地，但皇帝决定留在阿卡维尔更好。事实证明这是幸运的，因为包括皇帝旗舰在内的大部分舰队在返航途中被初冬风暴摧毁。288-289年的冬季风暴季节异常漫长且极其严重，阻止了舰队按计划带着额外补给返回阿卡维尔。此事通过战斗法师报告给皇帝，一致认为远征军可以靠手头补给支撑到春天。<BR>
<BR>
第三部分：远征军的覆灭<BR>
<BR>
阿卡维尔的冬季天气也比预期严酷得多。由于补给问题和数千平民的加入，远征军实行严格配给。更糟的是，赛埃锡袭击者卷土重来，袭扰两城城墙外的任何觅食和侦察队。塞普提米亚与艾奥尼斯之间道路上的几个瞭望堡在暴风雪中被攻占，其余不得不因无法防守而放弃。结果，两城之间的通讯完全通过魔法手段进行，不断消耗军团的战斗法师。<BR>
<BR>
日晓月5日，一大群赛埃锡人抵达艾奥尼斯，声称带来赛埃锡国王的和平提议。当晚，这些背信弃义的使者杀害了城门守卫，放进了一直在城外等待的大批同伙。他们的明确意图是刺杀皇帝，幸被守卫宫殿的第十军团士兵的警惕和勇气挫败。警报响起后，城内的赛埃锡人被搜捕并全部杀死。不用说，皇帝与赛埃锡人的谈判就此结束。<BR>
<BR>
春天的到来只带来更糟的麻烦。预期的春雨没有到来，取而代之的是从东方吹来的干热风，整个夏天持续不断，强度不一。庄稼歉收，甚至河流（前一年在艾奥尼斯上游很远仍可通小船）也完全干涸。不清楚这是否由于阿卡维尔特有的未知天气模式，还是赛埃锡人通过魔法手段操纵天气。委员会倾向于前者结论，因为没有直接证据表明赛埃锡人拥有如此可怕的神秘力量，但后一种可能性不能完全排除。<BR>
<BR>
由于持续恶劣天气，补给舰队从黑港出发延误。终于在次种月初离港，但再次被风暴重创，八周后大大减员地蹒跚驶入塞普提米亚。由于阿卡维尔补给形势日益绝望，皇帝将大部分战斗法师军团随舰队派出，协助其抵御似乎将持续整个夏天的风暴。此时，议会敦促皇帝放弃入侵，率远征军返回泰姆瑞尔，但他再次拒绝，指出舰队已无法一次性运输所有四个军团。委员会同意，将一个或多个军团留在阿卡维尔等待舰队返回会损害军队士气。但委员会也指出，损失一个军团胜于损失整个远征军。委员会一致认为，这是可能避免全面灾难的最后时刻。一旦决定派舰队返回增援和补给，事件就走向了必然结局。<BR>
<BR>
此后，对阿卡维尔发生之事知之甚少。由于大部分战斗法师随舰队行动，远征军与泰姆瑞尔之间的通讯受限，特别是随着阿卡维尔局势恶化，剩余战斗法师的力量被极限消耗以满足军团所有需求。然而，赛埃锡人似乎也以某种未知方式积极干扰法师。阿卡维尔的一些法师报告他们的力量异常虚弱，而西罗帝尔战争学院的法师（负责处理议会的通讯）报告与阿卡维尔的同袍连接困难，即使是长期训练的师徒之间也是如此。委员会敦促战争学院特别研究赛埃锡人的神秘力量，以防帝国再次与阿卡维尔发生冲突。<BR>
<BR>
已知的是，皇帝在日高月中旬率军离开艾奥尼斯，只留少量守军守城。他得知赛埃锡人在北方山脉另一侧集结兵力，意图在敌军完全集结前粉碎其军队并夺取其补给（他急需）。这次快速推进似乎出乎赛埃锡人意料，远征军越过山脉突袭了他们的营地，击溃了赛埃锡军队并俘虏了其指挥官（某种贵族）。但皇帝很快被迫撤退，军团在撤退至艾奥尼斯途中损失惨重。皇帝发现自己被围困在艾奥尼斯，与同样被围困的塞普提米亚小守军失去联系。此时，剩余少数战斗法师的所有努力似乎都用于造水维持军队生存，这一技能通常不是战争学院强调的。舰队在战斗法师军团的保护下安全返回黑港，但所有返回阿卡维尔的尝试都被289年余下时间不断袭击埃斯罗涅特的一系列越来越猛烈的风暴所挫败。<BR>
<BR>
议会与皇帝的最后一次联系是在霜降月初。到夜星月时，议会对阿卡维尔局势极为担忧，下令舰队不顾风险出航。尽管风暴持续，舰队还是设法驶向阿卡维尔。与皇帝的战斗法师取得联系后燃起希望，他报告艾奥尼斯仍在坚守。迅速制定了远征军突围艾奥尼斯、撤回塞普提米亚的计划，舰队将在那里接应他们。这是与远征军的最后一次直接联系。舰队抵达塞普提米亚时，发现守军正遭受赛埃锡大军的猛烈攻击。舰队随行战斗法师击退敌人足够长的时间，让幸存者登船，舰队撤退。<BR>
<BR>
到达塞普提米亚的远征军少数幸存者讲述了皇帝如何在两天前夜间率军离开艾奥尼斯，成功突破敌军防线，但在前往塞普提米亚的道路上被压倒性力量包围。他们讲述了皇帝和第十军团的英勇最后抵抗，使第十四军团的残部得以到达塞普提米亚。第十军团的两名幸存者当晚抵达塞普提米亚，他们在敌军失控的胜利庆祝期间溜过了防线。他们证实看到皇帝战死，在集结第十军团的盾墙时被敌人箭矢射杀。<BR>
<BR>
第四部分：结论<BR>
<BR>
委员会认为入侵阿卡维尔从一开始就注定失败，原因有几个，不幸的是没有一个能事先预见到。<BR>
<BR>
尽管进行了广泛的情报收集，远征军显然对阿卡维尔的局势准备不足。困扰军队和海军的意外天气尤其灾难性。如果不是战役期间远东舰队大部分损失，远征军本可在289年撤出。天气也迫使皇帝将大部分战斗法师军团分配给舰队，使他随后不久的战斗中失去了他们宝贵的协助。当然，289年袭击艾奥尼斯的意外干旱粉碎了在当地补给军队的希望，使远征军在艾奥尼斯被围困时陷入无法维持的境地。<BR>
<BR>
赛埃锡人也比情报报告显示的要强大得多。关于赛埃锡人最终能部署对抗远征军的军队规模的信息很模糊，因为唯一一次激战发生在皇帝与议会定期通讯中断之后。尽管如此，赛埃锡人似乎数倍于皇帝的兵力，因为他们能迫使四个精锐军团撤退，然后将其围困数月。<BR>
<BR>
如前所述，委员会不批评入侵阿卡维尔的初始决定。基于当时所知，该计划看似合理。只是事后看来，入侵成功的可能性显然很小。尽管如此，委员会认为可以从这场灾难中吸取几个宝贵教训。<BR>
<BR>
第一，赛埃锡人可能拥有极其强大的神秘力量。他们可能操纵如此广阔区域的天气的可能性似乎令人难以置信（应指出三位委员强烈反对在本报告中包含此段），但委员会认为此事值得紧急调查。潜在危险如此之大，即使微小的可能性也必须认真对待。<BR>
<BR>
第二，赛埃锡人似乎没有值得一提的海军。远征军从未受到海上威胁，远东舰队只与天气战斗。实际上，初始计划要求舰队的一部分留在阿卡维尔用于沿海行动，但事实上舰队大型船只很少有地方可以接近陆地，因为塞普提米亚南北沿海水域布满了无数暗礁、沙洲、岛屿等。由于塞普提米亚和艾奥尼斯周围平原完全缺乏树木，远征军无法建造能航行于浅水沿海的小型船只。任何未来针对阿卡维尔的军事远征都应考虑某种方式携带近海海军作战手段，以利用对赛埃锡人的这一明显优势 -- 远征军可悲地未能利用这一优势。<BR>
<BR>
第三，在考虑下一次入侵之前，需要对阿卡维尔进行更长期的研究。入侵前四年收集的信息虽广泛，但显然不充分。天气条件完全出乎意料；赛埃锡人比预期强大得多；皇帝与赛埃锡人的谈判尝试是一场灾难。阿卡维尔被证明比预期更陌生，委员会认为，在未来没有比当前更充分了解该大陆的条件、政治和人民之前，不应考虑任何入侵阿卡维尔的企图。<BR>
<BR>
最后，委员会一致得出结论，鉴于我们目前所知，任何入侵阿卡维尔的企图都是愚蠢的，至少在帝国当前状态下如此。帝国的军团需要留在国内。总有一天，一个和平统一的帝国将重返阿卡维尔，为艾奥尼斯之灾和我们的阵亡皇帝讨回严厉的代价。但那天不是现在，也不是在可预见的未来。<BR>
<BR>"""

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_DisasterAtIonithPC
Disaster at Ionith
艾奥尼斯之灾

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_DisasterAtIonithPC
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Disaster at Ionith<BR>
By Lord Pottreid, Chairman<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Part I: Preparations<BR>
<BR>
The Emperor's plans for the invasion of Akavir were laid in the 270s, when he began the conquest of the small island kingdoms that lie between Tamriel and Akavir. With the fall of Black Harbor in Esroniet in 282, Uriel V was already looking ahead to the ultimate prize. He immediately ordered extensive renovations to the port, which would serve as the marshalling point for the invasion force and as the main supply source throughout the campaign. At this time he also began the construction of the many large, ocean-going transports that would be needed for the final crossing to Akavir, in which the Navy was previously deficient. Thus it can be seen that the Emperor's preparations for the invasion were laid well in advance, before even the conquest of Esroniet was complete, and was not a sudden whim as some have charged.<BR>
<BR>
When Prince Bashomon yielded Esroniet to Imperial authority in 284, the Emperor's full attention could be devoted to planning for the Akaviri campaign. Naval expeditions were dispatched in 285 and 286 to scout the sea lanes and coastlands of Akavir; and various Imperial intelligence agents, both magical and mundane, were employed to gather information. On the basis of all this information, the kingdom of the Tsaesci, in the southwest of Akavir, was selected as the initial target for the invasion.<BR>
<BR>
Meanwhile the Emperor was gathering his Expeditionary Force. A new Far East Fleet was created for the campaign, which for a time dwarfed the rest of the Navy; it is said to be the most powerful fleet ever assembled in the history of Tamriel. The Fifth, Seventh, Tenth, and Fourteenth Legions were selected for the initial landing, with the Ninth and Seventeenth to follow as reinforcements once the beachhead was secured. While this may seem to the layman a relatively small fraction of the Army's total manpower, it must be remembered that this Expeditionary Force would have to be maintained at the end of a long and tenuous supply line; in addition, the Emperor and the Army command believed that the invasion would not be strongly opposed, at least at first. Perhaps most crucially, the Navy had only enough heavy transport capacity to move four legions at a time.<BR>
<BR>
It should be noted here that the Commission does not find fault with the Emperor's preparations for the invasion. Based on the information available prior to the invasion, (which, while obviously deficient in hindsight, great effort had been made to accumulate), the Commission believes that the Emperor did not act recklessly or imprudently. Some have argued that the Expeditionary Force was too small. The Commission believes that on the contrary, even if shipping could have been found to transport and supply more legions (an impossibility without crippling the trade of the entire Empire), this would have merely added to the scale of the disaster; it would not have averted it. Neither could the rest of the Empire be denuded of legions; the memory of the Camoran Usurper was still fresh, and the Emperor believed (and this Commission agrees) that the security of the Empire precluded a larger concentration of military force outside of Tamriel. If anything, the Commission believes that the Expeditionary Force was too large. Despite the creation of two new legions during his reign (and the recreation of the Fifth), the loss of the Expeditionary Force left the Empire in a dangerously weak position relative to the provinces, as the current situation makes all too clear. This suggests that the invasion of Akavir was beyond the Empire's current strength; even if the Emperor could have fielded and maintained a larger force in Akavir, the Empire may have disintegrated behind him.<BR>
<BR>
Part II: The Invasion of Akavir<BR>
<BR>
The Expeditionary Force left Black Harbor on 23rd Rain's Hand, 288, and with fair weather landed in Akavir after six weeks at sea. The landing site was a small Tsaesci port at the mouth of a large river, chosen for its proximity to Tamriel as well as its location in a fertile river valley, giving easy access to the interior as well as good foraging for the army. All went well at first. The Tsaesci had abandoned the town when the Expeditionary Force approached, so they took possession of it and renamed it Septimia, the first colony of the new Imperial Province of Akavir. While the engineers fortified the town and expanded the port facilities to serve the Far East Fleet, the Emperor marched inland with two legions. The surrounding land was reported to be rich, well-watered fields, and meeting no resistance the army took the next city upriver, also abandoned. This was refounded as Ionith, and the Emperor established his headquarters there, being much larger than Septimia and better-located to dominate the surrounding countryside.<BR>
<BR>
The Expeditionary Force had yet to meet any real resistance, although the legions were constantly shadowed by mounted enemy patrols which prevented any but large scouting parties from leaving the main body of the army. One thing the Emperor sorely lacked was cavalry, due to the limited space on the transport fleet, although for the time being the battlemages made up for this with magical reconnaissance.<BR>
<BR>
The Emperor now sent out envoys to try to contact the Tsaesci king or whoever ruled this land, but his messengers never returned. In retrospect, the Commission believes that valuable time was wasted in this effort while the army was stalled at Ionith, which could have been better spent in advancing quickly while the enemy was still, apparently, surprised by the invasion. However, the Emperor believed at the time that the Tsaesci could be overawed by the Empire's power and he might win a province by negotiation with no need for serious fighting.<BR>
<BR>
Meanwhile, the four legions were busy building a road between Septimia and Ionith, setting up fortified guard posts along the river, and fortifying both cities' defenses, activities which would serve them well later. Due to their lack of cavalry, scouting was limited, and communication between the two cities constantly threatened by enemy raiders, with which the legions were still unable to come to grips.<BR>
<BR>
The original plan had been to bring the two reinforcing legions across as soon as the initial landing had secured a port, but the fateful decision was now taken to delay their arrival and instead begin using the Fleet to transport colonists. The Emperor and the Council agreed that, due to the complete abandonment of the conquered area by its native population, colonists were needed to work the fields so that the Expeditionary Force would not have to rely entirely on the fleet for supplies. In addition, unrest had broken out in Yneslea, athwart the supply route to Akavir, and the Council believed the Ninth and Seventeenth legions would be better used in repacifying those territories and securing the Expeditionary Force's supply lines.<BR>
<BR>
The civilian colonists and their supplies began arriving in Septimia in mid-Hearthfire, and they took over the preparation of the fields (which had been started by the legionnaires) for a spring crop. A number of cavalry mounts were also brought over at this time, and the raids on the two Imperial colonies subsequently fell off. Tsaesci emissaries also finally arrived in Ionith, purportedly to begin peace negotiations, and the Expeditionary Force settled in for what was expected to be a quiet winter.<BR>
<BR>
At this time, the Council urged the Emperor to return to Tamriel with the Fleet, to deal with many pressing matters of the Empire while the army was in winter quarters, but the Emperor decided that it would be best to remain in Akavir. This turned out to be fortunate, because a large portion of the Fleet, including the Emperor's flagship, was destroyed by an early winter storm during the homeward voyage. The winter storm season of 288-289 was unusually prolonged and exceptionally severe, and prevented the Fleet from returning to Akavir as planned with additional supplies. This was reported to the Emperor via battlemage and it was agreed that the Expeditionary Force could survive on what supplies it had on hand until the spring.<BR>
<BR>
Part III: The Destruction of the Expeditionary Force<BR>
<BR>
The winter weather in Akavir was also much more severe than expected. Due to the supply problems and the addition of thousands of civilians, the Expeditionary Force was on tight rations. To make matters worse, the Tsaesci raiders returned in force and harried any foraging and scouting parties outside the walls of the two cities. Several watch forts on the road between Septimia and Ionith were captured during blizzards, and the rest had to be abandoned as untenable. As a result, communication between the two cities had to be conducted entirely by magical means, a continuing strain on the legions' battlemages.<BR>
<BR>
On 5th Sun's Dawn, a large entourage of Tsaesci arrived at Ionith claiming to bring a peace offer from the Tsaesci king. That night, these treacherous envoys murdered the guards at one of the city gates and let in a strong party of their comrades who were waiting outside the city walls. Their clear intention was to assassinate the Emperor, foiled only by the vigilance and courage of troopers of the Tenth who were guarding his palace. Once the alarm was raised, the Tsaesci inside the city were hunted down and killed to the last man. Needless to say, this was the end of negotiations between the Emperor and the Tsaesci.<BR>
<BR>
The arrival of spring only brought worse troubles. Instead of the expected spring rains, a hot dry wind began to blow from the east, continuing with varying strength through the entire summer. The crops failed, and even the river (which in the previous year had been navigable by small boats far upstream of Ionith) was completely dried up by Sun's Height. It is unknown if this was due to a previously unknown weather pattern unique to Akavir, or if the Tsaesci manipulated the weather through magical means. The Commission leans towards the former conclusion, as there is no direct evidence of the Tsaesci possessing such fearsome arcane power, but the latter possibility cannot be entirely ruled out.<BR>
<BR>
Due to prolonged bad weather, the supply fleet was late in setting out from Black Harbor. It finally left port in early Second Seed, but was again severely mauled by storms and limped into Septimia eight weeks later much reduced. Because of the increasingly desperate supply situation in Akavir, the Emperor dispatched most of his Battlemage Corps with the fleet to assist it in weathering the storms which seemed likely to continue all summer. At this time, the Council urged the Emperor to abandon the invasion and to return to Tamriel with the Expeditionary Force, but he again refused, noting that the fleet was no longer large enough to transport all four legions at once. The Commission agrees that leaving one or more legions behind in Akavir to await the return of the fleet would have damaged Army morale. But the Commission also notes that the loss of one legion would have been preferable to the loss of the entire Expeditionary Force. It is the unanimous opinion of the Commission that this was the last point at which complete disaster might have been averted. Once the decision was made to send the fleet back for reinforcements and supplies, events proceeded to their inevitable conclusion.<BR>
<BR>
From this point on, much less is known about what transpired in Akavir. With most of the battlemages assisting the fleet, communication between the Expeditionary Force and Tamriel was limited, especially as the situation in Akavir worsened and the remaining battlemages had their powers stretched to the limit attending to all the needs of the legions. However, it appears that the Tsaesci may also have been actively interfering with the mages in some unknown manner. Some of the mages in Akavir reported their powers being abnormally weak, and the mages of the War College in Cyrodiil (who were handling communications for the Council) reported problems linking up with their compatriots in Akavir, even between master and pupil of long training. The Commission urges that the War College make a particular study of the arcane powers of the Tsaesci, should the Empire ever come into conflict with Akavir again.<BR>
<BR>
What is known is that the Emperor marched out of Ionith in mid-Sun's Height, leaving only small garrisons to hold the cities. He had learned that the Tsaesci were massing their forces on the other side of a mountain range to the north, and he intended to smash their army before it could gather full strength and capture their supplies (of which he was in desperate need). This rapid advance seems to have taken the Tsaesci by surprise, and the Expeditionary Force crossed the mountains and fell on their camp, routing the Tsaesci army and capturing its leader (a noble of some kind). But the Emperor was soon forced to retreat, and the legions suffered heavily on their retreat to Ionith. The Emperor now found himself besieged in Ionith, cut off from the small garrison at Septimia which was also besieged. By this time, it seems that the efforts of the few remaining battlemages were devoted entirely to creating water to keep the army alive, a skill not normally emphasized at the War College. The fleet had arrived safely back to Black Harbor, thanks to the Battlemage Corps, but all attempts to return to Akavir were frustrated by a series of ever more savage storms that battered Esroniet throughout the rest of 289.<BR>
<BR>
The Council's last contact with the Emperor was in early Frostfall. By Evening Star, the Council was extremely worried about the situation in Akavir and ordered the fleet to sail regardless of the risk. Despite the continued storms, the fleet managed to press on to Akavir. Hope was raised when contact was made with the Emperor's battlemage, who reported that Ionith still held out. Plans were quickly laid for the Expeditionary Force to break out of Ionith and fall back on Septimia, where the fleet would meet them. This was the last direct contact with the Expeditionary Force. The fleet arrived in Septimia to find its garrison under savage assault from a large Tsaesci army. The battlemages with the fleet threw back the enemy long enough for the survivors to embark and the fleet to withdraw.<BR>
<BR>
The few survivors of the Expeditionary Force who reached Septimia told how the Emperor had led the army out of Ionith by night two days earlier, successfully breaking through the enemy lines but then being surrounded by overwhelming forces on the road to Septimia. They told of a heroic last stand by the Emperor and the Tenth Legion, which allowed a remnant of the Fourteenth to reach Septimia. Two survivors of the Tenth arrived in Septimia that night, having slipped through the enemy lines during their undisciplined victory celebration. These men confirmed having seen the Emperor die, cut down by enemy arrows as he rallied the Tenth's shield wall.<BR>
<BR>
Part IV: Conclusion<BR>
<BR>
The Commission believes that the invasion of Akavir was doomed from the start for several reasons, none of which could have been foreseen beforehand, unfortunately.<BR>
<BR>
Despite extensive intelligence-gathering, the Expeditionary Force was clearly unprepared for the situation in Akavir. The unexpected weather which plagued the army and navy was particularly disastrous. Without the loss of a majority of the Far East Fleet during the campaign, the Expeditionary Force could have been withdrawn in 289. The weather also forced the Emperor to assign most of his Battlemage Corps to the fleet, leaving him without their valuable assistance during the fighting which soon followed. And of course the unexpected drought which struck Ionith during 289 dashed the hopes of supplying the army locally, and left the Expeditionary Force in an untenable situation when besieged in Ionith.<BR>
<BR>
The Tsaesci were also much stronger than intelligence reports had suggested. Information on the size of the army the Tsaesci were eventually able to field against the Expeditionary Force is vague, as the only serious fighting took place after regular communications were cut off between the Emperor and the Council. Nevertheless, it seems likely that the Tsaesci outnumbered the Emperor's forces by several times, as they were able to force four crack legions into retreat and then keep them under siege for several months.<BR>
<BR>
As was stated previously, the Commission declines to criticize the initial decision to invade Akavir. Based on what was known at the time, the plan seemed sound. It is only with the benefit of hindsight does it become obvious that the invasion had very little chance of success. Nevertheless, the Commission believes several valuable lessons can be taken from this disaster.<BR>
<BR>
First, the Tsaesci may have extremely powerful arcane forces at their command. The possibility that they may have manipulated the weather across such a vast region seems incredible (and it should be noted that three Commissioners strongly objected to this paragraph even being included in this Report), but the Commission believes that this matter deserves urgent investigation. The potential danger is such that even the slight possibility must be taken seriously.<BR>
<BR>
Second, the Tsaesci appear to possess no navy to speak of. The Expeditionary Force was never threatened by sea, and the Far East Fleet fought nothing but the weather. Indeed, initial plans called for a portion of the Fleet to remain in Akavir for use in coastal operations, but in the event there were very few places where the large vessels of the Fleet could approach the land, due to the innumerable reefs, sandbars, islands, etc. that infested the coastal waters north and south from Septimia. Due to the utter lack of trees in the plain around Septimia and Ionith, the Expeditionary Force was unable to build smaller vessels which could have navigated the shallow coastal waters. Any future military expeditions against Akavir would do well to consider some way of bringing a means for inshore naval operations in order to exploit this clear advantage over the Tsaesci, an advantage that was sadly unexploited by the Expeditionary Force.<BR>
<BR>
Third, much longer-term study needs to be made of Akavir before another invasion could even be contemplated. The information gathered over the four years prior to the invasion was extensive, but clearly inadequate. The weather conditions were completely unexpected; the Tsaesci much stronger than expected; and the attempted negotiations by the Emperor with the Tsaesci a disaster. Akavir proved alien beyond expectation, and the Commission believes any future attempt to invade Akavir should not be contemplated without much greater knowledge of the conditions, politics, and peoples of that continent than presently obtains.<BR>
<BR>
Finally, the Commission unanimously concludes that given what we now know, any attempt to invade Akavir is folly, at least in the present state of the Empire. The Empire's legions are needed at home. One day, a peaceful, united Empire will return to Akavir and exact severe retribution for the disaster at Ionith and for our fallen Emperor. But that day is not now, nor in the foreseeable future.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
艾奥尼斯之灾<BR>
波特雷德勋爵，主席 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
第一部分：准备<BR>
<BR>
皇帝入侵阿卡维尔的计划于270年代制定，当时他开始征服泰姆瑞尔与阿卡维尔之间的小岛国。随着282年埃斯罗涅特的黑港陷落，尤利尔五世已着眼于最终目标。他立即下令对港口进行大规模扩建，使其成为入侵部队的集结点和整个战役的主要补给来源。同时他也开始建造许多最终跨越阿卡维尔所需的大型远洋运输船，此前海军在这方面有所欠缺。可见皇帝对入侵的准备是提前很久就制定的，甚至在征服埃斯罗涅特完成之前，并非如某些人所指责的那样是一时兴起。<BR>
<BR>
当巴肖蒙王子于284年将埃斯罗涅特交予帝国管辖后，皇帝得以全力策划阿卡维尔战役。285年和286年派出了海军远征队侦察阿卡维尔的海道和沿海地区；各种帝国情报人员，无论魔法还是常规手段，都被用来收集信息。基于所有这些信息，阿卡维尔西南部的赛埃锡王国被选为入侵的初始目标。<BR>
<BR>
与此同时，皇帝正在集结远征军。为这次战役新建了远东舰队，一度使其他海军相形见绌；据说是泰姆瑞尔历史上最强大的舰队。第五、第七、第十和第十四军团被选为初始登陆部队，第九和第十七军团将在滩头阵地巩固后作为增援跟进。虽然对外行人来说这似乎只是陆军总兵力的一小部分，但必须记住这支远征军必须通过漫长而脆弱的补给线维持；此外，皇帝和陆军指挥部认为入侵不会遇到强烈抵抗，至少初期如此。也许最关键的是，海军只有足够一次运输四个军团的重型运力。<BR>
<BR>
此处应指出，委员会并不认为皇帝对入侵的准备有错。根据入侵前可获得的信息（尽管事后看来明显不足，但已尽力收集），委员会认为皇帝并未鲁莽或轻率行事。有人辩称远征军规模太小。委员会认为恰恰相反，即使能找到船只运输和补给更多军团（若不损害整个帝国的贸易则不可能），那也只是加剧灾难的规模，而无法避免灾难。帝国其他地区也不能被剥空军团；篡位者卡莫兰的记忆犹新，皇帝认为（委员会也同意）帝国安全不允许在泰姆瑞尔以外集中更多军事力量。如果非要说，委员会认为远征军规模太大了。尽管他在位期间新建了两个军团（并重建了第五军团），远征军的损失使帝国相对于行省处于危险弱势地位，当前形势已清楚表明。这表明入侵阿卡维尔超出了帝国当时的力量；即使皇帝能在阿卡维尔部署和维持更大兵力，帝国也可能在他身后分崩离析。<BR>
<BR>
第二部分：入侵阿卡维尔<BR>
<BR>
远征军于288年雨手月23日离开黑港，在海上航行六周后，天气晴朗，在阿卡维尔登陆。登陆点是一个小赛埃锡港口，位于一条大河河口，因其靠近泰姆瑞尔以及位于肥沃河谷的位置而被选中，便于深入内陆和军队觅食。起初一切顺利。远征军接近时，赛埃锡人已弃城，他们占领了该城并将其更名为塞普提米亚，成为新阿卡维尔帝国行省的第一个殖民地。工程师们加固城镇并扩建港口设施以服务远东舰队的同时，皇帝率两个军团向内陆进军。据报道周围土地肥沃、水源充足，军队未遇抵抗便占领了上游下一座城市，同样被遗弃。该城被重建为艾奥尼斯，皇帝在那里建立了指挥部，它比塞普提米亚大得多，位置更佳，便于控制周边乡村。<BR>
<BR>
远征军尚未遇到任何真正抵抗，尽管军团一直被敌方骑兵巡逻队跟踪，阻止了除大型侦察队之外的任何人离开主力。皇帝严重缺乏骑兵，由于运输舰队空间有限，尽管战斗法师暂时用魔法侦察弥补了这一不足。<BR>
<BR>
皇帝随后派出使者试图联系赛埃锡国王或任何统治者，但使者从未返回。回顾来看，委员会认为在这一努力上浪费了宝贵时间，而军队在艾奥尼斯停滞不前，这段时间本可用于快速推进，趁敌方显然还对入侵感到惊讶之际。然而，皇帝当时相信赛埃锡人会被帝国的力量震慑，他可能通过谈判赢得一个行省，无需激战。<BR>
<BR>
同时，四个军团忙于修建塞普提米亚与艾奥尼斯之间的道路，沿河设立设防哨所，并加强两城防御，这些活动日后证明很有价值。由于缺乏骑兵，侦察受限，两城之间的通讯不断受到敌方袭击者的威胁，军团仍无法与之交锋。<BR>
<BR>
原计划是在初始登陆确保港口后立即将两个增援军团运来，但作出了推迟其抵达、转而开始使用舰队运送殖民者的命运性决定。皇帝和议会同意，由于被征服地区的原住民完全撤离，需要殖民者耕种田地，以便远征军不必完全依赖舰队补给。此外，伊内斯利亚爆发了动乱，横亘在通往阿卡维尔的补给路线上，议会认为第九和第十七军团更适合用于重新平定那些领土并确保远征军的补给线。<BR>
<BR>
平民殖民者及其补给于炉火月中旬开始抵达塞普提米亚，他们接管了田地准备工作（由军团士兵开始）以备春耕。此时也运来了一些骑兵坐骑，随后对两个帝国殖民地的袭击减少了。赛埃锡使者终于抵达艾奥尼斯，据称开始和平谈判，远征军安顿下来，准备度过一个预期的平静冬天。<BR>
<BR>
此时，议会敦促皇帝随舰队返回泰姆瑞尔，处理帝国的许多紧迫事务，而军队在冬季营地，但皇帝决定留在阿卡维尔更好。事实证明这是幸运的，因为包括皇帝旗舰在内的大部分舰队在返航途中被初冬风暴摧毁。288-289年的冬季风暴季节异常漫长且极其严重，阻止了舰队按计划带着额外补给返回阿卡维尔。此事通过战斗法师报告给皇帝，一致认为远征军可以靠手头补给支撑到春天。<BR>
<BR>
第三部分：远征军的覆灭<BR>
<BR>
阿卡维尔的冬季天气也比预期严酷得多。由于补给问题和数千平民的加入，远征军实行严格配给。更糟的是，赛埃锡袭击者卷土重来，袭扰两城城墙外的任何觅食和侦察队。塞普提米亚与艾奥尼斯之间道路上的几个瞭望堡在暴风雪中被攻占，其余不得不因无法防守而放弃。结果，两城之间的通讯完全通过魔法手段进行，不断消耗军团的战斗法师。<BR>
<BR>
日晓月5日，一大群赛埃锡人抵达艾奥尼斯，声称带来赛埃锡国王的和平提议。当晚，这些背信弃义的使者杀害了城门守卫，放进了一直在城外等待的大批同伙。他们的明确意图是刺杀皇帝，幸被守卫宫殿的第十军团士兵的警惕和勇气挫败。警报响起后，城内的赛埃锡人被搜捕并全部杀死。不用说，皇帝与赛埃锡人的谈判就此结束。<BR>
<BR>
春天的到来只带来更糟的麻烦。预期的春雨没有到来，取而代之的是从东方吹来的干热风，整个夏天持续不断，强度不一。庄稼歉收，甚至河流（前一年在艾奥尼斯上游很远仍可通小船）也完全干涸。不清楚这是否由于阿卡维尔特有的未知天气模式，还是赛埃锡人通过魔法手段操纵天气。委员会倾向于前者结论，因为没有直接证据表明赛埃锡人拥有如此可怕的神秘力量，但后一种可能性不能完全排除。<BR>
<BR>
由于持续恶劣天气，补给舰队从黑港出发延误。终于在次种月初离港，但再次被风暴重创，八周后大大减员地蹒跚驶入塞普提米亚。由于阿卡维尔补给形势日益绝望，皇帝将大部分战斗法师军团随舰队派出，协助其抵御似乎将持续整个夏天的风暴。此时，议会敦促皇帝放弃入侵，率远征军返回泰姆瑞尔，但他再次拒绝，指出舰队已无法一次性运输所有四个军团。委员会同意，将一个或多个军团留在阿卡维尔等待舰队返回会损害军队士气。但委员会也指出，损失一个军团胜于损失整个远征军。委员会一致认为，这是可能避免全面灾难的最后时刻。一旦决定派舰队返回增援和补给，事件就走向了必然结局。<BR>
<BR>
此后，对阿卡维尔发生之事知之甚少。由于大部分战斗法师随舰队行动，远征军与泰姆瑞尔之间的通讯受限，特别是随着阿卡维尔局势恶化，剩余战斗法师的力量被极限消耗以满足军团所有需求。然而，赛埃锡人似乎也以某种未知方式积极干扰法师。阿卡维尔的一些法师报告他们的力量异常虚弱，而西罗帝尔战争学院的法师（负责处理议会的通讯）报告与阿卡维尔的同袍连接困难，即使是长期训练的师徒之间也是如此。委员会敦促战争学院特别研究赛埃锡人的神秘力量，以防帝国再次与阿卡维尔发生冲突。<BR>
<BR>
已知的是，皇帝在日高月中旬率军离开艾奥尼斯，只留少量守军守城。他得知赛埃锡人在北方山脉另一侧集结兵力，意图在敌军完全集结前粉碎其军队并夺取其补给（他急需）。这次快速推进似乎出乎赛埃锡人意料，远征军越过山脉突袭了他们的营地，击溃了赛埃锡军队并俘虏了其指挥官（某种贵族）。但皇帝很快被迫撤退，军团在撤退至艾奥尼斯途中损失惨重。皇帝发现自己被围困在艾奥尼斯，与同样被围困的塞普提米亚小守军失去联系。此时，剩余少数战斗法师的所有努力似乎都用于造水维持军队生存，这一技能通常不是战争学院强调的。舰队在战斗法师军团的保护下安全返回黑港，但所有返回阿卡维尔的尝试都被289年余下时间不断袭击埃斯罗涅特的一系列越来越猛烈的风暴所挫败。<BR>
<BR>
议会与皇帝的最后一次联系是在霜降月初。到夜星月时，议会对阿卡维尔局势极为担忧，下令舰队不顾风险出航。尽管风暴持续，舰队还是设法驶向阿卡维尔。与皇帝的战斗法师取得联系后燃起希望，他报告艾奥尼斯仍在坚守。迅速制定了远征军突围艾奥尼斯、撤回塞普提米亚的计划，舰队将在那里接应他们。这是与远征军的最后一次直接联系。舰队抵达塞普提米亚时，发现守军正遭受赛埃锡大军的猛烈攻击。舰队随行战斗法师击退敌人足够长的时间，让幸存者登船，舰队撤退。<BR>
<BR>
到达塞普提米亚的远征军少数幸存者讲述了皇帝如何在两天前夜间率军离开艾奥尼斯，成功突破敌军防线，但在前往塞普提米亚的道路上被压倒性力量包围。他们讲述了皇帝和第十军团的英勇最后抵抗，使第十四军团的残部得以到达塞普提米亚。第十军团的两名幸存者当晚抵达塞普提米亚，他们在敌军失控的胜利庆祝期间溜过了防线。他们证实看到皇帝战死，在集结第十军团的盾墙时被敌人箭矢射杀。<BR>
<BR>
第四部分：结论<BR>
<BR>
委员会认为入侵阿卡维尔从一开始就注定失败，原因有几个，不幸的是没有一个能事先预见到。<BR>
<BR>
尽管进行了广泛的情报收集，远征军显然对阿卡维尔的局势准备不足。困扰军队和海军的意外天气尤其灾难性。如果不是战役期间远东舰队大部分损失，远征军本可在289年撤出。天气也迫使皇帝将大部分战斗法师军团分配给舰队，使他随后不久的战斗中失去了他们宝贵的协助。当然，289年袭击艾奥尼斯的意外干旱粉碎了在当地补给军队的希望，使远征军在艾奥尼斯被围困时陷入无法维持的境地。<BR>
<BR>
赛埃锡人也比情报报告显示的要强大得多。关于赛埃锡人最终能部署对抗远征军的军队规模的信息很模糊，因为唯一一次激战发生在皇帝与议会定期通讯中断之后。尽管如此，赛埃锡人似乎数倍于皇帝的兵力，因为他们能迫使四个精锐军团撤退，然后将其围困数月。<BR>
<BR>
如前所述，委员会不批评入侵阿卡维尔的初始决定。基于当时所知，该计划看似合理。只是事后看来，入侵成功的可能性显然很小。尽管如此，委员会认为可以从这场灾难中吸取几个宝贵教训。<BR>
<BR>
第一，赛埃锡人可能拥有极其强大的神秘力量。他们可能操纵如此广阔区域的天气的可能性似乎令人难以置信（应指出三位委员强烈反对在本报告中包含此段），但委员会认为此事值得紧急调查。潜在危险如此之大，即使微小的可能性也必须认真对待。<BR>
<BR>
第二，赛埃锡人似乎没有值得一提的海军。远征军从未受到海上威胁，远东舰队只与天气战斗。实际上，初始计划要求舰队的一部分留在阿卡维尔用于沿海行动，但事实上舰队大型船只很少有地方可以接近陆地，因为塞普提米亚南北沿海水域布满了无数暗礁、沙洲、岛屿等。由于塞普提米亚和艾奥尼斯周围平原完全缺乏树木，远征军无法建造能航行于浅水沿海的小型船只。任何未来针对阿卡维尔的军事远征都应考虑某种方式携带近海海军作战手段，以利用对赛埃锡人的这一明显优势 -- 远征军可悲地未能利用这一优势。<BR>
<BR>
第三，在考虑下一次入侵之前，需要对阿卡维尔进行更长期的研究。入侵前四年收集的信息虽广泛，但显然不充分。天气条件完全出乎意料；赛埃锡人比预期强大得多；皇帝与赛埃锡人的谈判尝试是一场灾难。阿卡维尔被证明比预期更陌生，委员会认为，在未来没有比当前更充分了解该大陆的条件、政治和人民之前，不应考虑任何入侵阿卡维尔的企图。<BR>
<BR>
最后，委员会一致得出结论，鉴于我们目前所知，任何入侵阿卡维尔的企图都是愚蠢的，至少在帝国当前状态下如此。帝国的军团需要留在国内。总有一天，一个和平统一的帝国将重返阿卡维尔，为艾奥尼斯之灾和我们的阵亡皇帝讨回严厉的代价。但那天不是现在，也不是在可预见的未来。<BR>

<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"> Abbot Crassius Viria<BR><BR>
An initiate disturbed my meditations last night, wide-eyed and distraught. "Abbot," cried he, "I have endured the most horrible dream. I was tending to the elders in their cells, bringing them food and water, listening to their soothing songs. The moths' gentle wings fluttered, tranquil as always, when suddenly I was confronted by hideous apparitions! Incorporeal dead roamed the halls, and it appeared to me as if the moths were feeding on them - sucking wisps of ghostly material, perhaps their very souls, into hungry maws! Please, Abbot, tell me this is madness, that this is not so!"<BR>
<BR>
It is not unusual for initiates of our Order to suffer unsettling dreams, especially as they learn more of the nature of our sacred charges, the Elder Scrolls, and the ancestors that grant us the wisdom to approach their infinite mysteries. Though much of the knowledge gained through readings of the Scrolls must be experienced personally to truly comprehend it, and despite being quite exhausted from my daily rigors, I was able to help him set aside his fears about our Order's relationship with mortal souls and the moths that preserve fragments of their erudition from beyond mortality.<BR>
<BR>
Not for us are the brutal methods of the conjurer or necromancer, tearing the soul from its vessel, constraining it and forcibly redirecting its energies with no regard for its journey or contents. No, the interplay of moth and ancestor soul is delicate and as natural as the canticle trees themselves, and we are patient and conscientious observers hoping to make sense of the cosmic tapestry by glimpsing its threads. It is through service to the moths and the ancestors that we gain guidance, not through the clumsy coercion of will without understanding the consequences.<BR>
<BR>
The soul, I told him, has much in common with the moth - they are a symbolic pair. Though it is typical to think of it as the Aedric essence at the core of every mortal, I advised him to consider the soul in another light, scaled like the wings of the moth, and to imagine it comprised of vessels filled through the events of mortal existence. On release from life on Nirn, it is our belief that a kind of dissipation begins, and it is then that the moths learn the song of a soul's fjyrons, which are shepherded under our care and protected generation after generation.<BR>
<BR>
The fjyrons themselves must retain a connection to the grand fabric of creation, to the scattered soul-remnants in all their destinations. Through this link and with patient care, we receive guidance from beyond the present or past and the known world, where time is irrelevant. The moths do not capture or devour the souls of the ancestors, but only repeat to us what they've filtered, like a chorus repeating the verses of a grand song.<BR>
<BR>
I could tell that, though the full dawn of understanding had not broken for him yet, his wild fears about the ancestor moths were somewhat allayed. I was pleased to assist him in his journey, and told him he would have ample time to ponder the nature of souls as he scrubbed the silkroom floors for the next week - penance for intruding on my nightly reverie.<BR><BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>散逸之魂
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">克拉修斯·维里亚院长<BR><BR>
昨晚一名新修者打断我的冥想，他瞪大眼睛，心烦意乱。“院长，”他喊道，“我做了一个最可怕的梦。我在房间里照料长者，给他们送食物和水，聆听他们慰藉的歌声。飞蛾的翅膀轻轻扇动，一如既往地宁静，突然我被可怕的幻象所困扰！无实体的亡灵在大厅中游荡，在我看来，飞蛾似乎在以它们为食 -- 把鬼魂物质的缕缕碎片，也许是它们的灵魂，吸进饥饿的口器！院长，请告诉我这是我疯了，不是真的！”<BR>
<BR>
我们修会的新修者做不安的梦并不罕见，尤其是当他们更多地了解我们神圣职责 -- 上古卷轴 -- 以及赐予我们智慧接近其无限奥秘的祖先的本质时。尽管通过阅读卷轴获得的大部分知识必须亲身经历才能真正理解，尽管我因日常劳苦而疲惫不堪，我还是帮助他消除了对我们修会与凡人灵魂以及那些保存超越死亡之学识碎片的飞蛾之间关系的恐惧。<BR>
<BR>
召唤师或死灵法师那种粗暴的方法不适合我们 -- 撕扯灵魂离开容器，约束它，强行引导其能量，不顾其旅程或内容。不，飞蛾与祖先灵魂的相互作用是微妙的，如同圣歌树本身一样自然，我们是耐心而认真的观察者，希望通过瞥见其线头来理解宇宙的织锦。我们是通过服务飞蛾和祖先获得指引，而非通过笨拙地强制意志而不理解后果。<BR>
<BR>
我告诉他，灵魂与飞蛾有许多共同之处 -- 它们是一对象征。虽然通常认为它是每个凡人核心的艾德拉本质，但我建议他从另一个角度看待灵魂，像飞蛾的翅膀一样有鳞片，并想象它由通过凡世经历填充的容器组成。当从奈恩的生命中释放时，我们相信一种消散开始了，就在那时，飞蛾学会了灵魂的菲隆之歌，这些菲隆在我们的照看下被引导，代代相传地保护着。<BR>
<BR>
菲隆本身必须保持与创世大织锦的联系，与分散在各处的灵魂残片联系。通过这种联系和耐心的照料，我们接受来自现在或过去以及已知世界之外的指引，在那里时间无关紧要。飞蛾并不捕获或吞噬祖先的灵魂，只是向我们重复它们过滤出的东西，如同合唱团重复一首伟大歌曲的诗句。<BR>
<BR>
我看得出，虽然领悟的黎明尚未为他降临，但他对祖先飞蛾的疯狂恐惧已有所缓解。我很高兴能帮助他的旅程，并告诉他下周在擦洗丝房地板时，他会有充足时间思考灵魂的本质 -- 作为打扰我夜间冥想的忏悔。<BR><BR>"""

Divad The Singer is in one body, two unique and distinct people. Divad is the most well known of the Redguard heroes. Frandar Hunding's son, probably the most accomplished Ansei who ever lived. Yet early in his life, Divad appeared to thoroughly have rejected The Way of the Sword. <BR>
<BR>
Divad was the only son of Frandar Hunding, and was born late in Hunding's life (2396 in the old way of reckoning, probably about 1E 760 by the Tamrielic calendar), when he was away most of the time fighting the last of his duels and engaging in the many battles and insurrections of the period. At eleven, Divad entered the Hall of the Virtues of War and began training, but at 16, he finally let his anger at growing up essentially fatherless get the better of him. Divad broke his swords and left the Hall to become an acrobat in a traveling circus.<BR>
<BR> 
The life in the circus was unsatisfying to Divad, and after two years, his innate artisan heritage drove him to become a musician and finally a Bard. For two more years he traveled, singing in the cities of the empire -- gaining no small amount of fame and recognition for his stirring and popular songs and music.<BR>
<BR> 
Although Divad had publicly forsaken the Way of the sword, it would appear that he continued to practice the compulsory forms of training he was taught in the Hall. He carried no sword, but in the late evening, bright lights could be often be seen in his tent (my source says nothing more about this, but it may be assumed that the writer was suggesting that Divad was practicing the form of the Way known as Shehai Shen She Ru -- the Way of the Spirit Sword, or simply the Shehai).<BR>
<BR> 
Divad was very popular with the people of the empire, and his music and concerts were well attended. Still he could not escape his heritage of the sword. When the Last Emperor ascended to power and began to persecute the sword-singers, Divad was among the first to attract his attention.<BR>
<BR> 
Once the Emperor Hira and his consort decided to go to war with the Singers for control of the empire, he moved swiftly against those Singers who were visibly a part of empire society. Most he had killed, but Divad's music and fame were so wide spread that he sent a team of his personal guards to arrest him.<BR>
<BR> 
The Emperor's men were either very lucky or very unlucky depending on how you choose to view it. Being no fool, Hira sent 100 of his best guards, for even an unarmed Singer was a very dangerous foe. The luck was that they were able to capture Divad and place him in chains, for they came at him as he sat dining with his elderly mother. The disaster was that as he surrendered, they rashly struck the pleading old woman. Too hard, it would seem, for she fell dead with that single blow.<BR>
<BR> 
That single thoughtless deed, as is often the case in war, was the one pivotal factor causing their eventual defeat. That act ignited in Divad the spirit of the Way. Up until that careless stroke, Divad was an ordinary artisan, no, an artist, a great artist, but no warrior.<BR>
<BR> 
The moment of her death, Divad rose from his seat, took his chains between his two hands and began swinging the heavy chain in a deadly arc. He slew four of the guards, gaining enough space to run and dive through the window and into the river He disappeared into the night.<BR>
<BR> 
From that point, Divad was spotted many times and told of in many more rumors all across the empire -- far more places than a mere mortal man could have ever been. At every point where Hira's men gathered to do mischief, the resistance was attributed to Divad.<BR>
<BR> 
As Hira moved against the Singers and began forming his army to invade High Desert, it was Divad who carried the news to the Singers. Divad was among those who climbed Hattu to find Hunding in his cave. What is not well known is that Hunding, at first refused to take leadership of the Singers. The first attempt to interrupt him at his death poem cause him to drive the elders from his cave, he even formed the Shehai in his anger. It was Divad who reentered the cave alone to speak with Hunding. To this day, no one knows what was said, what happened in that cave. Scribes of the time reported bright flashes of light and angry voices. Five long hours came and went, then both emerged from the cave, Divad, at Hunding's side. The rest, as they say, is history ...<BR>
<BR> 
Divad, who had not completed training in the Hall of the Virtues of War, became an adviser to Hunding and spent his time reading the newly completed Book of Circles, but his role in the Hammer and Anvil strategy was as a simple sword-singer and fighter. It was not till the Singers fled their native empire and landed In New Land that his story truly begins.<BR>

<BR>
从那时起，迪瓦德被多次目击，帝国各地流传着更多关于他的传言 -- 远远超过一个凡人可能到过的地方。在希拉的人聚集作恶的每一个地方，抵抗都被归功于迪瓦德。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

迪瓦德是弗兰达·亨丁的独子，在亨丁晚年出生（按旧历法2396年，按泰姆瑞尔历法约第一纪元760年），当时亨丁大部分时间在外进行最后的决斗，参与该时期的许多战斗和起义。十一岁时，迪瓦德进入战争美德厅开始训练，但十六岁时，他最终让对基本上没有父亲成长的愤怒战胜了自己。迪瓦德折断了他的剑，离开大厅，成为一个流动马戏团的杂技演员。<BR><BR>
马戏团的生活令迪瓦德不满，两年后，他与生俱来的工匠血统驱使他成为一名音乐家，最终成为吟游诗人。他又游历了两年，在帝国的城市中歌唱 -- 因其激动人心、广受欢迎的歌曲和音乐获得了不少名声和认可。<BR><BR>
虽然迪瓦德公开放弃了剑道，但他似乎继续练习在厅中学到的强制训练形式。他不带剑，但在深夜，他的帐篷里常能看到明亮的光（我的资料没有多说，但可以推测作者是在暗示迪瓦德在练习被称为“舍海·申·舍·鲁”的剑道形式 -- 灵剑之道，或简称为舍海）。<BR><BR>
迪瓦德深受帝国人民的欢迎，他的音乐和音乐会座无虚席。但他仍无法逃脱剑的血统。当末代皇帝掌权并开始迫害剑歌者时，迪瓦德是最早引起他注意的人之一。<BR><BR>
当希拉皇帝及其配偶决定与歌者开战争夺帝国控制权时，他迅速对付那些明显属于帝国社会的歌者。大多数被他杀害，但迪瓦德的音乐和名声太广，他派了一队私人卫兵去逮捕他。<BR><BR>
皇帝的手下要么非常幸运，要么非常不幸，取决于你如何看待。希拉并非傻瓜，派出了100名最好的卫兵，因为即使手无寸铁的歌者也是非常危险的敌人。幸运的是他们成功捕获了迪瓦德并给他戴上镣铐，因为他们是在他与年迈母亲用餐时袭击他的。不幸的是，当他投降时，他们鲁莽地攻击了恳求的老妇人。似乎用力过猛，她一击毙命。<BR><BR>
那一时冲动的行为，正如战争中常发生的那样，是导致他们最终失败的关键因素。那一举动点燃了迪瓦德心中的剑道之灵。在那鲁莽一击之前，迪瓦德是个普通工匠，不，是个艺术家，伟大的艺术家，但不是战士。<BR><BR>
她死去的那一刻，迪瓦德从座位上站起来，双手抓住锁链，开始挥舞沉重的链条形成致命弧线。他杀了四名卫兵，获得足够空间跑起来，从窗户跳入河中。他消失在夜色中。<BR><BR>
从那时起，迪瓦德被多次目击，帝国各地流传着更多关于他的传言 -- 远远超过一个凡人可能到过的地方。在希拉的人聚集作恶的每一个地方，抵抗都被归功于迪瓦德。<BR><BR>
当希拉对歌者采取行动并开始组建军队入侵高地沙漠时，是迪瓦德将消息带给歌者。迪瓦德是攀爬哈图山在洞穴中找到亨丁的人之一。鲜为人知的是，亨丁起初拒绝领导歌者。第一次在他写死亡之诗时打断他，导致他赶走了长老，甚至在愤怒中显现了舍海。是迪瓦德独自重返洞穴与亨丁交谈。至今无人知道他们说了什么，洞穴中发生了什么。当时的书记员报告说有明亮的闪光和愤怒的声音。漫长的五个小时过去了，然后两人都从洞穴中出来，迪瓦德站在亨丁身旁。剩下的，如他们所说，就是历史了......<BR><BR>
迪瓦德未完成战争美德厅的训练，成为亨丁的顾问，并花时间阅读新完成的《圆环之书》，但他在锤与砧战略中的角色只是一个普通的剑歌者和战士。直到歌者逃离故土帝国，在新大陆登陆，他的故事才真正开始。<BR>"""

Around and around they rolled the ball, and it grew larger and larger. It'll be much happier, and life will be so easy without all those distractions. Finally he regained his composure and admonished his friend with a questioning stare and a "What does Tall Papa think of all this?"$0A$0ABut Sep was spared the embarrassment of answering because suddenly a loud cry came up from the ball - now even as big as a whole village - and it quickly became clear that it had gotten out of control. Onward it rolled, passing over farmlands and forests and small lakes, picking up all of them as it went, and bursting great holes in many dozens of world scales, to the great distress of their inhabitants. Djulighana sighed and began to chase after it, gathering the detritus that fell from the ball's enormous mass as he went.$0A$0AHe quickly became burdened with the many old skins that had fallen off, which were far too numerous and heavy for him to carry on his own. He had an idea though, as always, and as he ran through a hole the snake-skin-ball had made in a quiet forest village, he grabbed the hole itself and took it with him - and several others as he passed through them - until he had enough to form the shape of a spirit to help him. And so he made the spirit which took the name Sheogog, but it was Djulighana's great misfortune that Sheogog was not really a spirit, but a hole where spirits should have been, and could not concentrate on the task at hand contorted as he was to look like something he was not. """<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>朱利加纳在蛇智灾难中的角色<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Dreadful Theft of the Sun's Dusk Ale<BR>
by Rascien Wickersly<BR><BR>

"It was late last night that the dreadful theft occurred," Foroch said. "They took it all. Every drop of it."<BR>
<BR>
That's how he greeted me. I said nothing at first. Foroch's brewery was high in the trees, and I had just climbed the Great Spiral all the way around from the dirt below. "I just. Stopped. To say. Goodbye. Because."<BR>
<BR>
"I know it. You're off to Cyrodiil to get your education. You just dropped in for a bit of ale before leaving, is that it? Well, they took every drop of it, so there's no use begging a mug from me."<BR>
<BR>
I didn't contradict him. I was still panting, and he was right. I came to see him for one last taste of his fine summer ale.<BR>
<BR>
"But if you want to take a keg to that fancy studium of yours, I might have a deal for you."<BR>
<BR>
"Didn't you say it was stolen?" I asked.<BR>
<BR>
"I did say that, because it was stolen," said Foroch. "But if you can get it back, I'll let you take a keg of it. They didn't take my regular ale. They took the Sun's Dusk ale."<BR>
<BR>
"I don't believe I've ever had the pleasure of that one," I said.<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

You have spells to attract the crosswings and mimics. And spells to keep out the flipbacks, tree-hoppers, and hoarvor young. There are spells to encourage the green mold and prevent the brown and white molds. Then you have to seal the barrel for nine or more years until the last of the green mold turns--"<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

"Perfect."<BR>

<BR>

The Bosmer around Greenheart rarely went all the way to the ground, unless they planned on leaving the city. This had a few unfortunate consequences, I thought, when I tripped over a deer antler jutting out above the other garbage. Since the Bosmer rarely visited the ground, they had no qualms about throwing their trash down from the treetops and forgetting about it.<BR>
<BR>
I knew I was getting close to the Imga's clearing when I heard the drumming. This was a bad sign. They usually only got out the drums when they'd been drinking. I hoped they still had some of Foroch's ale left.<BR>

What the Imga lacked in rhythm, they made up for in enthusiasm. Pickler saw me first and stopped beating the hollow log he'd almost mashed down to pulp. "What is that terrible smell?"<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
"It's the principle of the thing," said Noggin.<BR>
<BR>
"Duke Boff," I asked, "can you have these back at Foroch's by midnight?"<BR>
<BR>
"Sure, we can do that," said the Duke. "And then we can listen to Foroch say we can have the Sun's Dusk Ale anytime we want."<BR>
<BR>
"It's a deal," I said. "I need to hurry back to Foroch. I fear he may take some convincing."<BR>

<BR>
"The Imga," I panted.<BR>
<BR>
"I send you out on a simple job--"<BR>
<BR>
"Should be."<BR>
<BR>
"And you dare to come here--"<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
"Yes," I said.<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
"Almost all of it, I believe. I think they only tapped one of the kegs."<BR>
<BR>
"Excellent," said Foroch, getting out a couple of mugs. "This calls for a celebration."<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
Foroch scowled the whole time he poured. Boff scowled the whole time he drank. And me? I sipped the best brew in all Tamriel and smiled.<BR>
<BR>
My smile didn't fade until halfway to Silvenar when I discovered that the keg Foroch gave me was the tapped one and already half empty. <BR>

“虫子？”我问。<BR>
<BR>
“你不能把虫子直接倒进去，你知道的。”福罗赫说，“它们必须自然掉落。横翅虫在恐惧中死亡时会产生强烈的苦味。首先，你必须在每只桶上绷紧十七根阿尔菲克肠线。然后在肠线上压上新鲜野猪肉，小心别让肉在腐烂前掉落。然后，你必须把红条纹蛙的皮切碎洒在肉上，确保横翅虫掉落时醉醺醺的、开开心心的。每月这样做一次，持续三年或更久，直到有足够的肉和虫子填满桶。这还不算附魔。你用法术吸引横翅虫和拟态者。用法术驱赶翻背虫、树跳虫和霍沃幼体。还有促进绿霉、阻止褐霉和白霉的法术。然后你必须密封酒桶九年或更久，直到最后的绿霉变成 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
“听起来非常困难。”我说，对于绿色契约酿酒法，我宁愿无知。“你知道是谁拿走的吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“是那些肮脏、可悲的因加。”福罗赫啐道，“我有六桶。他们是唯一能肩扛一桶的人。酿酒厂里全是他们的臭味。”<BR>
<BR>
我知道他说的是哪些因加。博夫一伙。“他们不是在他们那片空地上吗？你为什么不叫几个精灵去拿回来？”<BR>
<BR>
“我看你完全不懂这件事。我不能和他们谈。我是正当主人，去见他们会承认偷窃。你们布莱顿人有一半精灵血统，他们这么说。因加会听你的。”<BR>
<BR>
“为什么是我？我在这里住了几年，但我永远是个外人。”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“完美。”<BR>
<BR>
“我只知道刚刚你告诉我的。”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“完美。”<BR>
<BR>
“而且正如你刚才指出的，我并不完全了解情况。”我绝望地说。<BR>
<BR>
“完美。”<BR>
<BR>
这就是我得到这个任务的方式。<BR>
<BR>
我沿着大螺旋一路走回地面，向因加的空地走去。作为一个住在瓦伦伍德的布莱顿人，我常从不同寻常的角度看事物。即森林地面。绿心周围的波斯莫很少下到地面，除非他们打算离开城市。这带来一些不幸的后果，我想，当我被一根鹿角绊倒，它从其他垃圾中伸出。因为波斯莫很少光顾地面，他们毫无顾忌地从树梢扔下垃圾然后遗忘。<BR>
<BR>
当我听到鼓声时，我知道我正接近因加的空地。这是个坏兆头。他们通常只在喝酒后拿出鼓来。我希望他们还剩些福罗赫的麦酒。<BR>
<BR>
当我看清空地时，我耐心等待他们即兴音乐会结束。我永远不会成为仰慕者，但他们的音乐还是有可取之处。因加在节奏上的不足，用热情弥补了。皮克勒先看到了我，停止敲打那根几乎被他捣成浆的空心木头。“那是什么难闻的气味？”<BR>
<BR>
“我相信是一个人，皮克勒。”博夫说。<BR>
<BR>
“确实。有股酸败牛奶的味道。”诺金说，他是博夫部落的最后一名成员。<BR>
<BR>
“博夫，”我说，“好久不见。”<BR>
<BR>
“我是博夫公爵，内默。”他说着，整了整斗篷，挺直了身子。<BR>
<BR>
“当然，博夫公爵。”我赶紧说，“原谅我。长途旅行让我举止失礼。”<BR>
<BR>
“算你走运，我今天心情宽宏。”公爵说，“什么风把你吹到我的领地来了？”<BR>
<BR>
“我的大人，我听说您获得了福罗赫的一些麦酒。”<BR>
<BR>
“哦？”博夫问，“你想要？我可能在找买家。”<BR>
<BR>
“那么我猜还有剩余？”也许这趟旅程没有白费。<BR>
<BR>
“是的。”博夫公爵慢吞吞地说，“我们还没喝完。”<BR>
<BR>
“我们何不让他尝尝？”皮克勒咧嘴笑道。<BR>
<BR>
“听起来不错，皮克勒。去搬一桶来。”<BR>
<BR>
我看着皮克勒笨重地走进森林，但他消失在我视线外，我没能看清桶藏在哪里。他毫不费力地扛着一桶回来了，砰地放在地上时我吓了一跳。显然，桶几乎还是满的。他拿出一个木碗，拧开龙头只倒出几口麦酒，倒酒时宽鼻子皱了皱。<BR>
<BR>
我接过碗闻了闻。我听说一些鉴赏家通过香气判断麦酒和葡萄酒，但对于波斯莫的饮品，这纯粹是明智的预防措施。日暮麦酒闻起来不像福罗赫的夏季麦酒。也不像那些不那么可口的波斯莫饮品，比如贾加，那种酒有独特的气味。如果要说像什么，就像用梅酒和香菜腌制的多汁牛排。我抿了一口，轻轻闭上眼睛。那是飞翔的梦。是我初吻时屏息的瞬间。是让我脸上露出深深微笑的温柔火焰。那是被蒸馏过的幸福。<BR>
<BR>
当我恢复神志后说：“霜火！这是什么？”<BR>
<BR>
“我也是这么说的。”皮克勒说。<BR>
<BR>
“不，皮克勒，你说的是，‘以赫玛·莫拉腐烂剥落的第三爪之名，这恶臭的污秽是什么东西？’”<BR>
<BR>
恶臭的污秽？我无法相信自己的耳朵。这麦酒绝对是众神的恩赐！<BR>
<BR>
“尽管它这么难喝，”诺金说，“我不明白福罗赫为什么不让我们尝尝。”<BR>
<BR>
“他就是为了气我们，诺金。”博夫公爵说，“他从不给我们应有的尊重。他总有借口忽视旧约。”<BR>
<BR>
“这酒对你来说味道如何？”我问。<BR>
<BR>
“苦。”博夫说。<BR>
<BR>
“腐烂。”皮克勒说。<BR>
<BR>
“就像你把横翅虫捏扁时挤出的那种东西。”诺金说。<BR>
<BR>
“确实。”博夫说，“希望今晚风大些，把这臭味吹离我的领地。”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，”我说，“博夫？如果福罗赫说你们可以喝一些，你们会把麦酒还给他吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“我是博夫公爵。”公爵习惯性地说，“我不想让绿心的子民认为我是严苛的统治者。如果福罗赫说我们可以喝些麦酒，那他把所有桶都拿回去。”<BR>
<BR>
“这是原则问题。”诺金说。<BR>
<BR>
“博夫公爵，”我问，“你们能在午夜前把这些送回福罗赫那里吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“当然可以。”公爵说，“然后我们就可以听福罗赫说我们可以随时享用日暮麦酒了。”<BR>
<BR>
“一言为定。”我说，“我得赶紧回福罗赫那里。恐怕需要费些口舌说服他。”<BR>
<BR>
福罗赫在酿酒厂门口等着我。他交叉双臂、满脸不悦，这不是好兆头。“我看你回来了。”他说，“没有带回我的日暮麦酒。好吧，我不会给你夏季麦酒的，尤其在 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
“因加，”我喘着气说。<BR>
<BR>
“我派你去做一个简单的任务 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
“应该会的。”<BR>
<BR>
“你竟敢回来 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
“带回来。”<BR>
<BR>
“空手 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
“午夜前。”<BR>
<BR>
“连道歉都没有！不，你开口的第一句话是......你刚才说因加今晚会送来？”<BR>
<BR>
“是的。”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“还剩多少？”福罗赫问。<BR>
<BR>
“我相信几乎都在。我想他们只开了一桶。”<BR>
<BR>
“太好了。”福罗赫拿出几个杯子说，“值得庆祝。”<BR>
<BR>
“等等。”我说，“等等。求你。我需要解释条件。”<BR>
<BR>
“条件？你的话让我充满恐惧。”福罗赫迅速收起杯子说，“你向那些肮脏的因加许诺了什么？”<BR>
<BR>
“一旦他们把麦酒送回来，你就可以让他们想喝多少喝多少 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
“什......你......为什么......如果......你怎么能......”福罗赫一时语塞。<BR>
<BR>
“等等，”我说，“让我解释。”<BR>
<BR>
我直到将近午夜才有机会解释。福罗赫很快恢复说话的“天赋”，对我、因加和我们的共同祖先咆哮斥责，直到几乎失声。当他终于平息下来，我再次试着解释。“因加不会要很多麦酒的。”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“不会！不会！你没和因加喝过酒吗？他们的酒量是传奇。阿碧希安海都解不了他们的渴。”<BR>
<BR>
“他们不喜欢这麦酒。”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“雪上加霜！他们偷了我的麦酒还批评它！”<BR>
<BR>
“听着，”我说，“他们不会喝很多，因为他们讨厌这玩意儿。这就是为什么他们没开其他桶。”<BR>
<BR>
“也许你的计划确实有点道理。”福罗赫嘶哑地说，“但是，还是要把日暮麦酒给因加......”<BR>
<BR>
“如果你想拿回任何一桶，就必须这么做。”我说，“如果你觉得他们偷走很糟，想象他们捏着鼻子把桶倒进河里。”<BR>
<BR>
“这是有先例和原则的，你看。我们从奥德莫瑞斯时代就住在一起。而现在，失去了我们的帝国、荣誉、权利和尊严，现在一个人要求我打破比人类到来更古老的传统。打破那些肮脏的因加半忘且很少遵守的传统。有时，拉西恩，我必须说我憎恨你们人类几乎如同我憎恨因加和卡吉特一样。”<BR>
<BR>
我震惊了。不是因为这种情绪 -- 这在瓦伦伍德很常见 -- 而是因为它被如此直白地说出来。“我住在这里这么多年，”我说，“从没听过 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
“我说了，我是认真的。”福罗赫盯着杯子说，“我们不再提了。”<BR>
<BR>
因加和麦酒的到来打破了沉默。<BR>
<BR>
福罗赫摇摇晃晃地站起来：“所以你们给我带了礼物？”<BR>
<BR>
“不是礼物，福罗赫。”博夫说，“这是我们正当偷来的麦酒，并且 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
“正当？！正当？！”福罗赫啐道。<BR>
<BR>
因加把桶砰地砸在地板上，打断了福罗赫即将爆发的怒骂，整个酿酒厂都在震动，几只杯子从架子上掉下来。<BR>
<BR>
博夫把胳膊肘搁在桶上，身体前倾：“我想听你说，福罗赫。我想听完整的正式说法。”<BR>
<BR>
“休想。”福罗赫后退说，“你要求太过分了，博夫。”<BR>
<BR>
“我是博夫公爵，波斯莫。”博夫张着嘴，似乎对自己的话感到惊讶。<BR>
<BR>
福罗赫又哑口无言了。他咬牙切齿地瞪着我。我低声说：“想想麦酒，福罗赫。想想麦酒。”<BR>
<BR>
“我，福罗赫，”他啐道，“承认你们......你们......你们......你们，博夫公爵，正 -- 正当偷了这些桶，并且......”<BR>
<BR>
“而且从现在起我们可以想喝多少喝多少，因为我们已经正当偷了它。”<BR>
<BR>
“而且从现在起，”福罗赫咬紧牙关说，“你们可以。想喝。多少。麦酒。就喝多少。”<BR>
<BR>
博夫伸出手。福罗赫盯着它整整一分钟，才匆匆握了握。<BR>
<BR>
“不如每人来一杯作为成交的庆贺？”我问。我忍不住了。<BR>
<BR>
“也许只喝一小口。”博夫说。我几乎能看到他皮毛下变绿。<BR>
<BR>
福罗赫倒酒时一直皱着眉头。博夫喝酒时一直皱着眉头。我呢？我啜饮着全泰姆瑞尔最好的佳酿，微笑着。<BR>
<BR>
我的笑容直到前往希尔维纳的半路上才消失，因为我发现福罗赫给我的桶正是开过的那桶，已经半空了。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Dres Cremation Practices <BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
Publisher's Note: The following missive is printed by authority of the Hlaalu Council Company and with the permission of its original author in the interests of promoting understanding and respect between the visitors to Morrowind and her local people.<BR> <br>
---
<FONT COLOR="640F0F"> <br>
Brother Kantus, <br>
I know of your interest in investigating the more obscure burial practices of the Dark Elves, and for your sake I have made sure to make inquiries during my trip to Morrowind and spare you the trouble. As it happens, a Dark Elf boatman was feeling quite talkative and I have transcribed his comments below.
<br> 
However, most Dark Elves are not so accommodating. They do not like outsiders coming in and asking questions about their dead. Much less do they like people who worship foreign gods telling them what to do with their dead. The Dres do not sell their corpses to the Sload, whatever wild gossip you might have overheard. I am shocked you would think of making such inquiries of the Dres. Apologies would not cut it.
<br> 
The Dres, like other Dark Elves, are very thorough in caring for their dead, and will certainly not let them fall into the hands of necromancers. They are also not in the habit of animating their dead, from what I understand, which is more than can be said of their bretheren. And I know you will have misgivings about some of their practices, and I would like to see them change their ways as well, but they will not do so, and at least they are thorough about it. <br> <FONT COLOR="640F0F"> <br>
I cannot understand your desire to proselytize off in the East where nobody will listen to you when nobody back at home seems capable of burying a corpse in such a way that it stays buried and not in the lair of some foul necromancer. If there is one thing I find commendable about the Dark Elves, it's that they tend to look to their own before bothering their neighbors, though the Empire is trying its best to change that. Can't we learn from them for once and leave them well enough alone, at least until we have our end sorted? I understand wanting a change of pace, but I assure you Morrowind is not the change of pace you want. <BR> <br>
--- <FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"> 
<BR> 
So you've seen the Dres beacons shining over the plains? No, they are not lighthouses. The Dres don't need big lights to navigate by. Well, I suppose you outlanders could use them as such, but the Dres won't have lit them for that, I can tell you. No, those are the Dres. The recently deceased, that is, on their journey to Necrom.
<br> <br>
No, the Dres don't use Veloth's Way. They don't like to leave their territory if they don't have to. Well, yes, they do send hunters into the South, but that's business and not pleasure. Too much trouble, anyway. Why walk when you can ride, the caravaners will ask you. The Dres are clever; they noticed there's a strong wind that goes up from Lake Andaram and then rushes down the other side Necrom-way. That wind carries their dead.
<br> <br>
Of course the flesh and blood is too heavy to be carried by the wind. And the bones; especially the bones. The Tribunal (Blessed be their Holy Names) need the bones to power the Ghostfence; they can't do with just the flesh-ashes, which we burn up here. We can send the bones after, sure, but the Dres aren't going to. So the Dres need to burn the bones as well. Get the fire nice and hot. Hence the beacons.
<br> <br>
How do they do it? Well, I can tell you, in fact, but it's not quickly told. The Dres stand on ceremony, if their dead are on the line, and ceremony takes time.
<br> <br>
First, they dry out the body. Not very hard to do over there; just find a salt patch and lay it in. You'll see them sometimes, if you ever have the misfortune to cross the plains: a few clan guards standing vigil over a dry brown form. That'll be the body. Yes, they stand vigil. In shifts, of course, as the body takes a long time to dry out properly. These are not your dead slaves left to parch in the salt and sun and be nibbled away at by whatever thrice-cursed salt-munching beasts live up there. Especially in these days, with you outlanders sniffing about where you're not meant to, begging your pardon. If you do see them, I'd suggest you keep your distance and not stare too much. We don't hold by corpse-gawkers around here, but we understand you foreigners like to gawk, so we just gawk back until you back off. The Dres are not so understanding.
<br> <br>
Your folk don't abide by corpse-gawking either? Huh. Well, the Dres don't know that, and they won't ask.
<br> <br>
Now they don't just lay the corpse flat. It's not dignified enough for them, and besides, it would be a pain to balance them on their pillars that way, begging your pardon. They have them sit, lotus-position, as you'll see Lord Vivec sit in frescos. They're dead, of course, so they're not about to sit by themselves. But if you've spent a bit of time in Morrowind you'll know that's no object. The bonesmiths know all about reinforcing joints, as you'll know, and they have a much easier time getting something not to move than they do getting something to be able to move. They drive long, sharp bones and bits of metal and chitin tubes between the bones in such a way that the body doesn't shift about. Looks like what? Onsi? One of your foreign gods? Don't mention that to the Dres, they won't like it. 
<br> <br> <DIV ALIGN="CENTER">
<IMG SRC="TR\DresCremation.dds" WIDTH="330" HEIGHT="300"> <BR> <DIV ALIGN="LEFT"> <BR>
They don't use metal much, no, they don't have a lot of it to go around. They always make sure to use at least one piece, though. It's the only bit that doesn't burn up completely, and it's not needed for the Ghostfence, so it's the only bit they can really keep.
<BR> <BR>
The chitin just comes from the legs of some bug, I'm not sure which. It's pretty sturdy stuff, though. Used for scaffolding and the like. Much lighter than the wood from the jungles, and more convenient to get at.
<BR> <BR>
Where do they get the bones from? Ah, the bone stakes you mean. Those are the 'bones of their enemies'. I told you the Dres stand on ceremony. Though to be fair, 'enemy' means 'some wretched slave' more often than not. Bones of traitors? Where'd you hear that from? You read it in some book? Hanin's what? Never heard of it, but sounds about right. The Dres don't hold by traitors either, but don't get a lot of them. No wonder. You can be sure if some do pop up they'll be the first to burn. They sometimes use the bones of some other clan's Chap-thil if they're having a very bad feud or the body is of a very important clansman, but I hear even the Dres leadership frowns on that, let alone the Temple. No, if they want to go out of their way nowadays it usually involves a trip to the South to get a lizard that at least puts up a bit of a fight. Times have changed, even for the Dres.
<BR> <BR>
Once the body is dry they carry it back. It's a good deal lighter then, even with all the bits of bone and metal and chitin sticking out, but the Dres carry it very carefully, to be sure, on its bug-husk platform. I don't know how they get it up on the pillar, in fact. They must use those flying things they have. I don't like those.
<BR> <BR>
Though here's a bit of knowledge for the road, and you'd better hope you won't need it: those bugs don't like fire much, or so I hear. No wonder as well, as their tallow burns like nothing else I've seen. Or you've seen, for that matter, as you've seen the beacons burn yourself. Once the body is back at the clanstead, it's coated with the stuff. And draped over with clan textiles coated in the stuff. And the chitin shell the body is sitting in is filled with the stuff as well. They want to be sure it all burns up, you see, or they'd have to burn it again later, which isn't really proper.
<BR> <BR>
And then when it's sitting up there all right and ready they light the lot -- not sure how they do that either, as I doubt the bugs would play along, and I know I wouldn't want to be anywhere near it when it lights up, or I'd be halfway to Necrom before sundown -- and that's the light you see. I wasn't kidding either, the fire does its work quickly, or something's gone awful wrong.
<BR> <BR>
Now I've told you and saved you the trouble of asking the Dres. They don't like questions, especially about their dead. It's a good thing you asked me as well. I know caravaners who go up into the salt plains -- gods know why, as they don't like it there and the Dres don't like them there, but they're proper Hlaalu so they know to follow the money and it's not my place to question them -- and they tell me a few tales of what they see. And I don't know about you, but for me hearing is enough.
<BR> <BR>
But you seem sensible, for an outlander. Curious, sure, but I suppose we all are. Where was it you were headed? Narsis? Straightaway out of the province, not bad. Maybe the Dres would like you after all.
