"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
德雷斯火葬习俗<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
编者按：以下信件由哈拉鲁议会公司授权出版，并经原作者许可，旨在促进访客与晨风当地人之间的理解与尊重。<BR><br>
---
<FONT COLOR="640F0F"><br>
坎图斯兄弟，<br>
我知道你对研究暗精灵较不为人知的埋葬习俗感兴趣，为了你，我特地在晨风之行中替你打听了，免得你麻烦。碰巧有个暗精灵船夫相当健谈，我把他的话记录如下。
<br>
然而，大多数暗精灵并不那么通融。他们不喜欢外来者来询问有关死者的任何问题。更不喜欢崇拜外来神祇的人来指手画脚。德雷斯人不会把尸体卖给斯洛德，不管你听说了什么流言蜚语。我很惊讶你竟会想到向德雷斯人打听这种事。道歉是不够的。
<br>
德雷斯人和其他暗精灵一样，照料死者非常周全，决不会让尸体落入死灵法师之手。据我所知，他们也没有让死者复活的习惯，这比他们的同胞要好。我知道你会对他们的某些习俗心存疑虑，我也希望他们能改一改，但他们不会改的，至少他们做得很彻底。<br><FONT COLOR="640F0F"><br>
我不明白你为何想去东方传教，那里没人会听你的，而国内似乎没人能让尸体好好入土，不让它们落入邪恶死灵法师的巢穴。如果说暗精灵有什么值得称道之处，那就是他们在打扰邻居之前先管好自己，虽然帝国正竭力改变这一点。难道我们不能学他们一次，别去管他们，至少等我们把自己这边的事处理好？我理解你想换个环境，但我向你保证，晨风不是你想要的那种变化。<BR><br>
---<FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
<BR>
所以你看到了德雷斯人的烽火照亮平原？不，那不是灯塔。德雷斯人不需要大灯来导航。嗯，我想你们外乡人倒可以那样用，但我告诉你，德雷斯人点亮它们可不是为了那个。不，那些就是德雷斯人。是刚去世的人，在前往亡者之城的路上。
<br><br>
不，德雷斯人不走维洛斯之道。他们不喜欢非必要离开自己的领地。嗯，是的，他们确实派猎人南下，但那是生意，不是消遣。反正太麻烦了。商队会问你，能骑马为何要走路？德雷斯人很聪明；他们注意到有一股强风从安达拉姆湖上升，然后从另一侧向亡者之城方向吹下。那股风带走他们的死者。
<br><br>
当然，血肉太重，风带不动。骨头也是，尤其是骨头。审判席（愿其圣名受祝福）需要骨头来为幽魂之墙提供能量；他们不能用我们在这里烧成的骨灰来代替。我们当然可以之后把骨头送去，但德雷斯人不会这么做。所以德雷斯人必须也烧掉骨头。把火烧得又旺又热。于是就有了烽火。
<br><br>
他们怎么做？嗯，我可以告诉你，但这不是三言两语能说清的。德雷斯人讲究礼节，如果事关死者，仪式很费时间。
<br><br>
首先，他们把尸体弄干。在那边不难做；只需找个盐滩，把尸体放进去。如果你不幸穿越平原，有时会看到几个氏族守卫在干枯的棕色形体旁站岗。那就是尸体。是的，他们站岗。当然要轮班，因为尸体需要很长时间才能彻底干透。这些不是你那些被遗弃在盐和阳光下、被当地任何该死的食盐兽啃食的奴隶尸体。尤其是在这些日子里，你们这些外乡人在不该去的地方嗅来嗅去，请原谅我这么说。如果你真的看到他们，我建议你保持距离，别盯着看。我们这里不习惯看尸体的闲人，但我们理解你们外国人喜欢看，所以我们只看回去直到你退开。德雷斯人可没那么好说话。
<br><br>
你们的人也不赞成看尸体？嗯。德雷斯人不知道这一点，他们也不会问。
<br><br>
他们不是把尸体平放着。那样不够庄重，而且，恕我直言，那样放在柱子上也很难平衡。他们让尸体坐着，莲花坐姿，就像你在壁画中看到维威克大人那样。当然，他们死了，不会自己坐着。但如果你在晨风待过一段时间，你就知道那不是什么难事。骨匠精通关节加固，你知道的，让东西不动比让它能动容易得多。他们把长而尖的骨头、金属碎片和甲壳管插进骨头之间，使尸体不会移动。看起来像什么？翁斯？你们外来神祇之一？别跟德雷斯人提，他们不会喜欢的。
<br><br><DIV ALIGN="CENTER">
<IMG SRC="TR\DresCremation.dds" WIDTH="330" HEIGHT="300"><BR><DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
他们不常用金属，不，他们金属不多。不过他们总是确保至少用一块。那是唯一不会完全烧掉的部分，幽魂之墙也不需要它，所以他们真正能保留的只有它。
<BR><BR>
甲壳来自某种虫子的腿，我不确定是哪种。不过那东西很结实。用于脚手架之类。比丛林里的木头轻得多，也更容易弄到。
<BR><BR>
他们从哪弄骨头？啊，你是指骨桩。那是“敌人的骨头”。我告诉过你德雷斯人讲究礼节。不过公平地说，“敌人”往往指“某个可怜的奴隶”。叛徒的骨头？你从哪听说的？你在某本书里读到？哈宁的什么？没听说过，但听起来差不多。德雷斯人也不容忍叛徒，但叛徒不多。难怪。你可以肯定，一旦有人冒出来，他们会最先被烧掉。他们有时会用其他氏族的查普-提尔的骨头，如果他们之间有深仇大恨，或者死者是非常重要的族人，但我听说连德雷斯领导层都不赞成，更不用说神殿了。不，如果他们现在要费心搞什么，通常就是南下弄条至少能反抗一下的蜥蜴。时代变了，即使是德雷斯人也一样。
<BR><BR>
尸体干了后，他们把它运回来。那时轻多了，即使有骨头、金属和甲壳碎片伸出来，但德雷斯人还是小心翼翼地用虫壳平台搬运。我不知道他们怎么把它弄上柱子。他们肯定用了那些飞行的东西。我不喜欢那玩意。
<BR><BR>
不过送你一点知识，希望你用不上：那些虫子不太喜欢火，我听说。难怪，它们的油脂烧起来比我见过的任何东西都旺。你也见过，既然你亲眼见过烽火燃烧。尸体运回氏族领地后，浑身涂上那种东西。再盖上涂了那种东西的氏族织物。尸体坐着的甲壳壳里也填满了那种东西。他们要确保全部烧尽，否则还得再烧一次，那不合规矩。
<BR><BR>
然后当一切就绪，他们就点燃全部 -- 我也不确定他们怎么点火，因为我怀疑虫子不会配合，而且我知道自己不想在点燃时靠近，否则日落前我就半路到亡者之城了 -- 那就是你看到的光。我不是开玩笑，火燃烧得很快，否则就是出了大问题。
<BR><BR>
现在我都告诉你了，省得你去问德雷斯人。他们不喜欢问题，尤其是关于死者的。你问我是件好事。我认识一些去盐原的商队 -- 鬼知道为什么，他们不喜欢那里，德雷斯人也不喜欢他们在那里，但他们是真正的哈拉鲁人，知道跟着钱走，我也没资格质疑他们 -- 他们告诉我一些他们看到的事。我不知道你怎么想，但对我来说，听说就够了。
<BR><BR>
不过你看起来挺明事理，对于一个外乡人来说。好奇是肯定的，但我想我们都好奇。你要去哪里？纳西斯？直接离开行省，不错。也许德雷斯人终究会喜欢你的。

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<FONT><B>Dres Slave Trade</B></FONT><BR>
<FONT>Analysis of the slave trade within Great House Dres of Morrowind<BR>
and its economic and political effects on the house</FONT><BR>
by Nurcius Punitus, student at the Imperial Library<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Of the five noble Dark Elven Great Houses of Morrowind, House Dres remains the one that keeps most to itself and openly defies Imperial authority. Seated in the featureless plainlands and dangerous swamps on the southern borders of the province, House Dres still follows its laws of old, with worship of their living gods interjected with ancestor worship in the High Elven style.<BR>
<BR>
The economy of House Dres relies primarily on their cultivation of saltrice, which in turn relies on a veritable army of slaves. While saltrice cultivation and the profits thereof have been stable and strong for at least 600 years, trade of these slaves offers House Dres an important, though secondary, source of profit.<BR>
<BR>
House Dres is so reliant on its slavery that its capital, Tear, is built solely to allow the control and efficient transport of slaves. Beyond its truly enormous harbor, which could rival that of any Imperial city, the most memorable areas of Tear are its infamous slave pits: immense, bowl-shaped holes reinforced with concrete and surrounded by thick, high walls. In these, slaves are kept in miserable conditions like soulless merchandise, before they are used or discarded.<BR>
<BR>
The unfortunate slaves living in these pits cling to desperate sense of normality. Makeshift families can be observed creating homes of scrap wood and clay, only to have the homes toppled by the cruel hands of their Dark Elven overseers and the family members split into different pits. It is true that slaves can be sold or moved at any time, but the masters of the pits take special delight in ripping fledgling families and friendships apart.<BR>
<BR>
Slaves who refuse the authority of their Dark Elven masters or dare to strike back at them are sent into isolated punishment pits, never to be seen again. The punishment of misbehaving slaves is not often turned into a public spectacle at least, but this secrecy has been turned into its own instrument of fear: the Dres nobles who oversee the pits are often clothed in furs and leather. Who can say that these garments were not a former pit mate? The slaughterfish around Tear are suspiciously well fed and Dreugh abound.<BR>
<BR>
On the rare occasion when the masters feel it necessary to make a statement or indulge in petty cruelty, pelts and leather skins are hung from the tops of the slave pits, ostensibly flayed off leaders of particularly successful revolts.<BR>
<BR>
Slave numbers are kept stable by raids into Black Marsh and trade with outlaws and bandit kings in Elsweyr. The territory of House Dres is ideally situated to take advantage of both, with the large port of Tear acting as an attraction for all sorts of pirates and illicit traders, and the House's position on the southern edge of Morrowind makes the acquisition of Argonian slaves as easy as a trifle trip across the province border as the Legions helplessly look on.<BR>
<BR>
Hunting young Argonians for sport is considered an honorable tradition by House Dres nobility, akin to animal hunts in civilized lands. It is said that these hunting parties prey upon the isolated tribes deep in Black Marsh, where missing youths are often considered to have been swallowed by the swamp. The hapless captives often have no idea what slaves are and that there is anything beyond the swamps and forests of Black Marsh. These ghastly revelations are disclosed to them on the long trip back to the slave pits of Tear.<BR>
<BR>
When they are not abused by their masters or traded like cattle to the four other Great Houses, Argonian slaves are seen working in the endless saltrice fields of the plains until their very scales have been eaten away by the acidic vapors of the Deshaan and their bleached bones are devoured by beetles the Dark Elves keep as pets. Khajiit slaves are usually sent to work domestic duties inside the houses of their Dark Elven masters, far from sight but even closer to their eagerly biting whips.<BR>
<BR>
Slaves are also the ones who deliver the saltrice to the ports and work in the large granaries and warehouses of House Dres' towns. This backbreaking work is often seen as a merciful fate, and sea-going slaves are treated with envy by their fellows.<BR>
<BR>
It is said that slaves have ever stoked the economy of House Dres. While it is true that they are prolific in Dark Elven society and deeply ingrained in the culture and lore of the Great Houses, it is much more than that. The very essence of House Dres is built on a near endless pool of blood and tears, and with the removal of slavery, the very House would collapse, its saltrice fields barren and its ports empty.<BR>
<BR>
For this reason they remain attached to this repulsively barbaric activity. The treaty by which Morrowind entered the Empire of Tamriel allows for slavery in the province; consequently, the law abolishing slavery in the rest of the Empire has no power in Morrowind. Let us hope that, in the future, slavery will be abolished everywhere without exception.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<FONT><B>德雷斯奴隶贸易</B></FONT><BR>
<FONT>晨风德雷斯大族内奴隶贸易分析<BR>
及其对该家族的经济和政治影响</FONT><BR>
努尔修斯·普尼图斯 帝国图书馆学生<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
在晨风的五个高贵的暗精灵大族中，德雷斯家族仍然是最自成一格、公开违抗帝国权威的。坐落在行省南部边界毫无特征的平原和危险的沼泽中，德雷斯家族仍遵循古老的律法，崇拜现世神的同时夹杂着高等精灵式的祖先崇拜。<BR>
<BR>
德雷斯家族的经济主要依赖于盐米种植，而盐米种植又依赖于一支名副其实的奴隶大军。虽然盐米种植及其利润至少600年来一直稳定强劲，但这些奴隶的贸易为德雷斯家族提供了重要但次要的利润来源。<BR>
<BR>
德雷斯家族如此依赖奴隶制，以至于其首府泪城纯粹是为了控制和高效运输奴隶而建。除了其可与任何帝国城市媲美的巨大港口外，泪城最令人难忘的区域是其臭名昭著的奴隶坑：巨大的碗状坑洞，用混凝土加固，四周有厚厚的高墙。在那里，奴隶们像没有灵魂的商品一样在悲惨的条件下生活，直到被使用或丢弃。<BR>
<BR>
住在这些坑里的不幸奴隶们拼命维系着正常的假象。可以看到临时组成的家庭用废木和粘土建造家园，但随即被暗精灵监工残忍地推倒，家庭成员被分到不同的坑里。的确，奴隶随时可能被卖掉或转移，但坑主们特别喜欢拆散刚刚建立的家庭和友谊。<BR>
<BR>
拒绝服从暗精灵主人权威或敢于反击的奴隶被送进孤立的惩罚坑，再也看不见了。不听话的奴隶的惩罚通常不会公开示众，但这种隐秘性本身已成为制造恐惧的工具：监督坑道的德雷斯贵族常穿着皮毛和皮革。谁能说这些衣物不是来自以前的坑友？泪城周围的食人鱼出奇地肥硕，蟹灵也很多。<BR>
<BR>
在极少数情况下，当主人觉得有必要表明态度或沉溺于小小的残忍时，皮货和皮革会挂在奴隶坑顶上，据称是从特别成功的叛乱领袖身上剥下来的。<BR>
<BR>
奴隶数量通过突袭黑沼泽以及与艾斯维尔的亡命徒和土匪头目交易来维持稳定。德雷斯家族的领土处于利用这两者的理想位置，泪城的大港口吸引了各种海盗和非法商贩，而该家族在晨风南缘的位置使获取阿尔贡奴隶变得像穿过行省边界那样轻而易举，军团只能无奈地看着。<BR>
<BR>
以猎杀年轻阿尔贡人为乐被德雷斯贵族视为光荣传统，类似于文明地区的狩猎。据说这些狩猎队以黑沼泽深处的孤立部落为猎物，在那里失踪的年轻人通常被认为已被沼泽吞噬。不幸的俘虏往往不知道奴隶是什么，也不知道黑沼泽的沼泽和森林之外还有什么。这些可怕的真相在他们被押回泪城奴隶坑的漫长旅途中才向他们揭示。<BR>
<BR>
当阿尔贡奴隶不被主人虐待或像牛一样被交易给其他四个大族时，他们就在平原上无边的盐米田里劳作，直到他们的鳞片被迪莎安的酸性蒸汽侵蚀殆尽，漂白的骨头被暗精灵当作宠物的甲虫吞噬。卡吉特奴隶通常被派去在暗精灵主人家里做家务，远离视线，但却更靠近那急切咬人的鞭子。<BR>
<BR>
奴隶们还要把盐米运到港口，并在德雷斯家族城镇的大粮仓和仓库中劳作。这种繁重的工作往往被视为一种仁慈的命运，出海奴隶会遭到同伴的嫉妒。<BR>
<BR>
据说奴隶一直在推动德雷斯家族的经济。虽然他们在暗精灵社会中数量众多，深深植根于大族的文化和传说中，但远不止于此。德雷斯家族的本质建立在近乎无尽的鲜血和泪水之池上，一旦废除奴隶制，整个家族将崩溃，盐米田将荒芜，港口将空置。<BR>
<BR>
因此他们仍执着于这种令人厌恶的野蛮活动。晨风加入泰姆瑞尔帝国的条约允许该行省保留奴隶制；因此，帝国其他地区废除奴隶制的法律在晨风无效。让我们希望将来奴隶制能在所有地方无一例外地被废除。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR><BR>
Dry:<BR>
Aridity, Thirst, and Desiccation<BR>
as Metaphor for the Other<BR>
in Saxhleel Literature and Folklore<BR><BR>

by Dr. Nak Bur-za<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
The fact that water is essential to life, and that the retention of moisture and close association with water is of particular physical importance to my people, is trivial to my larger thesis about an essential literary trope.<BR><BR>

In Saxhleel literature (and by "literature," I mean the totality of fictional artistic verbal expression by or about Argonians, regardless of the language used), aridity and thirst are distancing terms for the "other." Superficially, we tend to regard dryness as a metaphor for either "pain" or "despair." This simple binary analysis follows from the observation that, in literature, water-based imagery like "clear water," "cool rain", and so on, is almost always used metaphorically to refer to positive concepts like "good health," "good fortune," or "success."<BR><BR>

In casual conversation, an Argonian who talks about a "river" is almost certainly using the word metaphorically to describe passage through life. So I might say of a deceased friend that the river "bore him peacefully to the sea." Similarly, if someone said, "Ah! Choking rills of sand descend from my spawning pool!", any literate person would know that the person was complaining that they were beset by misfortune.<BR><BR>

Given the obvious and somewhat trite poetic linkage between water and life, many literary critics assume that "dryness" must be euphemistic of "death" in Saxhleel literature, but this presumption is simply not borne out by a close examination of the literary tradition. To a careful stylist, a state of "unmoistness" is not "death" per se, but rather, "foreignness" or "that which is uncanny."<BR><BR>

In common parlance, non-Saxhleel sentient races are referred to as "drys" or "dry skins." "Dry skin" is actually mildly pejorative, and more sophisticated Saxhleel writers tend to avoid the term by simply referring to "men" or "mer" without the implied insult based on physical appearance. But those writers who avoid using "dry" as a convenient shorthand for other races may still make effective use of dryness to establish a mood of alienation or disjunction.<BR><BR>

ARIDITY IN MODERN SAXHLEEL LITERATURE IN TRANSLATION
<BR><BR>
I have a perfect introductory example of how dryness is used in the novels and plays of Paxhan Dar Uush (better know to her wider readership under her nom-de-plume, "Long Strong-eye.") One can see how aridity is artfully hinted at in the first chapter of her first novel, "The Saltrice Broker," in bracket below.<BR><BR>

Briefly, (for those of you whose last memory of the book was when you were required to read it as a schoolchild), "The Saltrice Broker" is a sprawling romance focused primarily on the efforts of its heroine, "Blue-High-Tooth," to emancipate her father from slavery. In the course of her journey from Black Rose to Vivec City, Blue-High-Tooth endangers her own freedom and is forced to lay a clutch of eggs against her will at the behest of a slaver named Orleth. Although the ending is bittersweet, Blue-High-Tooth ultimately triumphs over the obstacles set in her path.<BR><BR>

This descriptive passage comes from early in Chapter One:<BR><BR>

[She closed her eyes, letting the letter slip from her hand. The ink across the letter's seal had crazed in the heat, obscuring her father's crestmark; the texture of the parchment called to mind the bed of a drought-blasted irrigation canal, with its salt-rimed scabs of shrunken earth and thirsty crevasses.<BR><BR>

So far away! How thin the sap scent must have been for him, how faint the breeze upon his cheek. Why else would he have sent her this warrant?]<BR><BR>

The passage hints at the geographic separation that had followed on Blue High Tooth's estrangement from her broodmates and adoptive father, but it goes beyond merely expressing physical distance. By referring to "heat-crazed ink," and by correlating the visual appearance of the parchment to the surface of a dry riverbed, the author made it plain not only that the protagonist's father was far away, but that he had written to her from an implicitly alien and hostile land. Without even mentioning the location that the letter had been sent from, the author's reference to a dry irrigation canal has already primed the sophisticated reader to expect that the heroine's father is in Morrowind on business, and that he has met with misadventure, even though neither of those facts are made explicit in the paragraph cited.<BR><BR>

For another example of the emotional weight borne by the descriptive use of "dryness," look to the climactic scene from Paxan Dar Uush's most successful and acclaimed novel, "The Eye in the Mask." Set against the backdrop of war and invasion, "The Eye in the Mask" tells the story of a theater troupe whose members are attempting to work their way back to the Imperial City. The last third of the novel is from the perspective of an assimilated Argonian actor who has been suffering from prophetic dreams. In this passage, the actor realizes that his Dunmer colleague and friend has been using the acting troupe to cover for spying activity.<BR><BR>

["It's a good house tonight."<BR><BR>

He still hadn't answered my question; he was pointedly treating tonight as just another show. He rummaged through the props trunk, looking for his mask and headdress. I snatched the wooden scepter off of his chair.<BR><BR>

"Give me that! We're on in five!"<BR><BR>

'Last King of the Ayleids' had always been a draw for us, and Fyrthil was brilliant in the part of the great anti-hero. My heart broke as he pleaded with me. His lips were cracked and peeling, his voice hoarse. Was it the skooma, or the drinking that had driven him to this?<BR><BR>

"Who are you working for?"<BR><BR>

"By the Three, just give me the scepter. Gods! I'm so thirsty."]<BR><BR>

Here, the antagonist's discomfort (his thirst and cracked lips) aren't merely descriptive, but are meant to evoke the sense that Fyrthil (who had been portrayed sympathetically as an enlightened and non-bigoted cosmopolitan friend of the protagonist through most of the novel) has fallen away, either reverting to or acquiesing in some sort of cultural alienation. Fyrthil's bigotry and willingness to sell out the lives and welfare of his fellow actors is, in some sense, tied to his failure to suppress his fundamental existential thirst. And his thirst (explicitly for skooma, but implicitly for acceptance) comes from the dryness of the "other," the "foreign" nature within him.<BR><BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR><BR>
干：<BR>
干旱、干渴与枯竭<BR>
作为“他者”的隐喻<BR>
在萨克斯利尔文学与民间传说中<BR><BR>

纳克·布尔-扎 博士 著<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
水对生命至关重要，保持水分和与水密切接触对我族人具有特殊的生理重要性，但这一事实对我关于一种基本文学修辞的更大论点来说微不足道。<BR><BR>

在萨克斯利尔文学中（我所说的“文学”是指由阿尔贡人或关于阿尔贡人的虚构艺术性言语表达的总和，无论使用何种语言），干旱和干渴是“他者”的距离性术语。表面上，我们倾向于将干燥视为“痛苦”或“绝望”的隐喻。这种简单的二元分析源于观察：在文学中，像“清水”、“凉雨”等水意象几乎总是被隐喻地用来指代“健康”、“好运”或“成功”等积极概念。<BR><BR>

在日常对话中，一个谈论“河流”的阿尔贡人几乎肯定是在用这个比喻来描述生命的旅程。所以我可能会说一个已故的朋友，河流“平静地将他带向大海”。同样，如果有人说：“啊！令人窒息的沙流从我产卵池中倾泻而下！”任何有文化的人都会知道，那人在抱怨自己厄运缠身。<BR><BR>

鉴于水与生命之间明显且有些陈腐的诗意联系，许多文学批评家认为“干燥”在萨克斯利尔文学中必然是对“死亡”的委婉说法，但这种假设在仔细审视文学传统后并不成立。对一个细心的文体家来说，“不潮湿”的状态本身不是“死亡”，而是“异质性”或“怪异之物”。<BR><BR>

在通俗用语中，非萨克斯利尔的智慧种族被称为“干皮”或“干皮子”。“干皮”实际上略带贬义，更老练的萨克斯利尔作家倾向于避免使用这个词，而只是称“人类”或“精灵”，不带基于外貌的隐含侮辱。但那些避免使用“干”作为其他种族便利简称的作家，仍可能有效利用干燥来营造疏离或脱节的情绪。<BR><BR>

现代萨克斯利尔文学翻译中的干旱
<BR><BR>
我有一个完美的入门例子来说明干燥如何用于帕克山·达尔·乌什（她的广大读者更熟知她的笔名“长强眼”）的小说和戏剧中。可以看到在她的第一部小说《盐米经纪人》的第一章中，干旱是如何被巧妙暗示的，如下括号内。<BR><BR>

简而言之，（对于那些上一次接触这本书还是小时候被迫阅读的人来说），《盐米经纪人》是一部庞大的爱情小说，主要聚焦于女主人公“蓝高牙”努力将父亲从奴隶制中解放出来。在从黑玫瑰到维威克城的旅程中，蓝高牙危及了自己的自由，并被迫在名为奥勒斯的奴隶贩子的要求下违背意愿产下一窝蛋。尽管结局苦乐参半，但蓝高牙最终战胜了路上的障碍。<BR><BR>

这段描写来自第一章开头：<BR><BR>

[她闭上眼睛，任由信纸从手中滑落。信封印上的墨水因炎热而龟裂，遮住了她父亲的徽记；羊皮纸的质地让人想起干涸的灌溉渠底，盐渍覆盖着收缩的土地和干裂的缝隙。<BR><BR>

如此遥远！对他来说，树液的气息一定多么稀薄，微风拂过他脸颊的感觉多么微弱。否则他为什么要寄给她这份委任状？]<BR><BR>

这段文字暗示了蓝高牙与她的巢伴和养父疏远后的地理分离，但不仅仅是表达物理距离。通过提到“因热而龟裂的墨水”，并将羊皮纸的视觉外观与干涸河床的表面对应，作者不仅明确指出了主角的父亲在远方，而且他是从一个隐含的异域和敌对之地给她写信。甚至没有提及信件发出的地点，作者对干涸灌溉渠的引用已经让有经验的读者预感到女主角的父亲在晨风出差，并且遭遇了不测，尽管引用的段落中并没有明确说明这两点。<BR><BR>

关于“干燥”描述性使用所承载的情感重量的另一个例子，请看帕克山·达尔·乌什最成功和最受赞誉的小说《面具之眼》中的高潮场景。以战争和入侵为背景，《面具之眼》讲述了一个剧团成员试图返回帝都的故事。小说的最后三分之一是从一个被同化的阿尔贡演员的视角出发，他一直受到预言之梦的困扰。在这段文字中，演员意识到他的丹莫同事和朋友一直在利用剧团为间谍活动打掩护。<BR><BR>

[“今晚观众不错。”<BR><BR>

他仍未回答我的问题；他刻意把今晚当作另一场演出。他在道具箱里翻找，寻找他的面具和头饰。我从他椅子上抢走了木制权杖。<BR><BR>

“给我！我们五分钟后上场！”<BR><BR>

《亚历德末代国王》一直很吸引我们，费尔希尔在饰演伟大反英雄角色时表现出色。当他恳求我时，我的心都碎了。他的嘴唇干裂脱皮，声音嘶哑。是斯库玛还是酗酒把他逼到这一步的？<BR><BR>

“你在为谁工作？”<BR><BR>

“以三神之名，把权杖给我吧。天哪！我太渴了。”]<BR><BR>

在这里，反派的痛苦（他的干渴和干裂的嘴唇）不仅仅是描述性的，而是意在唤起费尔希尔（他在小说大部分时间里被同情地描绘为主角开明、不偏执的世界性朋友）已经堕落的感觉，要么回归要么默许某种文化疏离。费尔希尔的偏执和出卖同伴演员生命和福祉的意愿，在某种意义上与他无法抑制自己基本的生存干渴有关。而他的干渴（表面上是渴求斯库玛，但暗示是渴求接纳）来自他内部的“他者”的干燥，即“异己”本质。<BR><BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
一则关于水晶塔的可疑传闻<BR>
比贝努斯·吉翁 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
这则故事是我尚为新手、初入夏暮水晶塔求学时，第一次听说的。当时我正欣赏着塔中著名的兽栏，一位年长的学生走了过来。起初，这位向我讲述此事的同窗看似十分可信，但读者很快便会发现，这则传闻实在极其可疑。当然，我后来也以同样的戏谑口吻，将此传闻转述给了塔中其他新手。<BR><BR>
敬爱的读者，谨将下文呈奉于您尊贵的视野。<BR><BR>

诗人眼见走投无路，尖叫道：“救命！救命！”<BR><BR>
雪狼低语道：“闭嘴，不然我们全都会被解雇。”<BR><BR>

A Dunce in Morrowind, v1<BR>

It was a cold morning in the West Gash, when Remyn found me standing naked by the side of the road. He gave me a contemptful look, but slowed his pack guars and his walk as he came to me. After staring at me like I was stupid for another minute or two, he finally spoke.<BR>

"Ha! I know what you might think, Dark Elf," I said. "You think I saw a comely lass or something, and not realizing she was a witch, I was tricked, hexed, and all my clothing stolen in my sleep." <BR>
"It is a rather common issue with you people." <BR>
"Oh ho! But you see, I am not an average stupid Nord," I said. "I am an educated future noble, from the famous College of Winterhold." <BR>
"Uh huh. And what exactly do you study at the College?" <BR>
"I'm the caretaker for the student dorms." <BR>
"I see." <BR>
"I read their books in the meantime when they aren't looking. Of course, I am not very good at reading. But I come from a very good pedigree. My father was executed by the Jarl, and my mother was five feet tall." <BR> <BR> 
Remyn simply stared at me for a few minutes. <BR> <BR>
"Why, pray tell, is this a good pedigree?" <BR>
"Well, you see, my father was executed by the Jarl for mercantile fraud, the most wealthy form of crime there is. Surely this must reflect to his intelligence to commit such a profitable crime, no?" <BR>
"No, it musn't. And your mother?" <BR>
"Yes, she was five feet tall." <BR>
<BR>
I received another stare. Remyn looked away for a moment. He looked to me again.
<BR> <BR>
"So, it was not a witch who fooled you. Why are you naked then?" <BR>
"You see, there was a comely lass--" <BR>
"Okay." <BR>
"--there was a comely lass at the tavern. I was visiting Fort Frostmoth, you see, because I was drowning at the time." <BR>
"You were drowning at the time." <BR>
"Yes, I was drowning, you see, because my boat had been destroyed by dreugh." <BR>
He paused. "I don't understand." <BR>
"I set sail from Winterhold in a boat, you see, headed for Solitude for my cousin's wedding." <BR>
"I am not an expert on Skyrim. But is Dawnstar not west of Winterhold?" <BR>
I chuckled. "Yes, and west I did go, Dark Elf. I've seen many maps in my time. West is to the left. So I sailed left, and would have arrived bright and early in Dawnstar, had it not been for the dreugh that attacked my boat." <BR>
"Wh--" <BR>
"Once I was drowning, I simply used a scroll of Divine Intervention to arrive at Fort Frostmoth, where I caught a boat to Khuul. That's where I met the comely lass I mentioned." <BR>
"I see." <BR>
"Yes, and you see, here is the thing, and it should go to show you how educated I really am. You see, this comely lass, she was rumored by the locals to be a witch. And wouldn't it be just so expected and stereotypical of a Nord in Morrowind, to think that a woman is a witch just because she's a little unusual? And so I said, no, this woman is not a witch, and I will not be tricked or play into your stereotypes. And so, I went home with her to her odd little camp outside town." <BR>
"Her camp." <BR>
"Yes, had a lot of odd skulls and potions around. While I wasn't looking, some sort of hex was placed on me. I assume she fought as hard as she could to stop my assailant, but alas, I was knocked out, and all my possessions stolen, including my beloved axe, Niptickler." <BR>
"Niptickler." <BR>
"My beloved axe Niptickler." <BR>
"Nipt--" Remyn stopped himself from speaking again. "Okay. You seem a fool, but I am not without sympathy. If you wish, you may accompany me to Ald'Ruhn." <BR>
"Old Run, you say?" <BR>
"Ald'Ruhn. That is a common Western misconception." <BR>
"Ah, you see, it is a common Eastern misconception that it's a common Western misconception." <BR> <BR>
Remyn paused. <BR> <BR>
"That's called reverse psychology, you see," I said. <BR>
"There are some clothes in one of the guar's packs. Put something on," he said. "Try not to embarrass me when we get there." <BR> <BR>

<BR>
Publisher's Note:<BR>
The "Dunce in Morrowind" series, collected and edited by Frolja Silver-Blood, were originally assembled by the Sneezing Horker Historical Society in Winterhold. Winterhold, as a center of magical learning, is rather cosmopolitan for a city in the icy north.<BR>
The Sneezing Horker Historical Society saw its fair share of Dark Elven and Nordic members who were often violently astonished by the ignorance about their respective homelands.<BR>
Serving as an introduction to the Dunmer lands for the Society's Nordic members, the Dunce in Morrowind was a series of skits originally written by the late Ferana Adrethi and acted out by regular members to much laughter and drink.<BR>
<BR>
"The Dunce" can easily be found in Winterhold as one of all too many "nobles" residing in town as prospective College students. Full of bluster, arrogance, and a dash of cunning, they are as much part of the city as they are guaranteed income for the carpenter's guild.<BR>

那是西境之痕一个寒冷的早晨，雷明发现我赤身裸体站在路边。他鄙夷地看了我一眼，但还是放慢了驮货瓜尔的脚步，走近我。又盯着我看了一两分钟，像看白痴一样，他终于开口了。<BR>

“奥德汝因。这是西方人常见的误解。”<BR>
“啊，你看，认为这是西方常见误解，这本身就是东方常见的误解。”<BR><BR>
雷明顿了一下。<BR><BR>
“这叫逆向心理学，你看。”我说。<BR>
“某个瓜尔背包里有衣服。穿上吧。”他说，“到那里时别给我丢脸。”<BR><BR>

Lucky was I to have a guide to the Eastern land, Morrowind, in Remyn Sadrethi, who told me he is an up and coming merchant of House Hlaalu, travelling to the Old Run on business. The walk was long, but Remyn was so stingy that he wouldn't even pay for the silt strider in Gnisis.  It was also fortunate for me that he was good with his magic, which helped keep the cliff racers and kagouti away from us. <BR> <BR>
"Ald'Ruhn is the seat of House Redoran on Vvardenfell," he said to me. <BR>
"Ah," I replied. "So, what's their gimmick?" <BR>
"Gimmick?" <BR>
"Sure, gimmick," I said. "Have you ever been to the Arena fighting in the Imperial City?" <BR>
"We have an arena in Vivec, sera." <BR>
"Right, right, but the point is, every fighter has a gimmick. One guy's the sword guy. One guy's the magic guy. One guy's the coward." <BR>
"Those are acts they put on to make more money." <BR>
"Yes, yes, and I, being rather intelligent myself, find it easy to see through," I said. "But the point is, the Dunmer have gimmicks too." <BR> <BR>
Remyn stared at me. "I don't understand." <BR>
"Sure you do. House Hlaalu's gimmick is money, merchanting--"<BR>"Merchanting." <BR> "--governmenting, you know, all that kind of thing. And I know that the Telvanni's gimmick is that they're unlikable heathens." <BR>
Remyn paused. "That is strangely insightful of you. If I co-operate with your insane view of things for a moment, however, I would say that the Redoran's gimmick is that they are warriors. They are very big on honor, and fighting, and strength, whatever." <BR>
"Warriors, eh." <BR>
"Yes," Remyn said. <BR>
"Amazing. So the Dunmer sort themselves into warriors, magicians, and thieves." <BR>
"Thieves?" <BR>
"Well, isn't that what business is? Legalized theft?" <BR>
Remyn paused. "...No." <BR>
"It's a very convenient system." <BR>
"There are more than three Great Houses," he said. <BR>
"Oh. That upsets it a bit." <BR>
"House Indoril and House Dres have no settlements on Vvardenfell. The traditionalist, insular Indoril have not had the enterprising drives of the other great houses. They receive enough political benefits from Temple settlements that it makes no difference to them anyway. I sometimes think that they believe they own the Temple." <BR>
"Temple, eh." <BR>
"Do you know anything of our religion, sera?" <BR>
"Remember, I am a very educated future noble from the College of Winterhold." <BR>
"Yes, you keep saying." <BR>

"That's where the dwarves went! They went to hide with Sotha Sil so they could work on strange mage-smithing all the time and build things that blow out a lot of steam that makes it hard to see. You see, being educated, I know that Sotha Sil is very into weird mage stuff and building weird things, because I read 2920. And so logically, the dwarves would've went with him, right? He accepted their surrender, and the surrender of their lands and gave them a place to live where they could build weird things all day." <BR>

"What about the other one? The Dres?" <BR>
"Some things become so adapted to danger that they can't function in safety," Remyn said. "That is what I will say about why the Dres don't settle on Vvardenfell." <BR>
"Ah, interesting, interesting. So, do you all live in these Houses?" <BR>
"...House is a figure of speech. Perhaps you would understand better if you thought of it as a clan." <BR>

"Blight?" I asked. <BR>

"These are delegates from the other Great Houses," he said to me. <BR>

Mounds of useless poisonous salt, soil so stained with chlorine or other acids that normal plants refuse to grow, wind storms that blow that salt into your eyes, nose, and skin, acid rain, wild skyrenders, noxious fumes, and worst of all, the Dres, who are possibly even more heathen than the sorcerors here." <BR>

Which is just as well, because I think if you aren't mad, you probably can't survive there either." <BR> "Fascinating," I said, instantly becoming too drunk to stay conscious. <BR> <BR>

<BR>
Publisher's Note:<BR>
The original skits were set in the Velothis district settlement of Veranis, and the journey took the characters to the port town of Rhanim, with Blacklight as goal.<BR>
As Vvardenfell was recently opened up to colonisation, the journey was rewritten to take place on the island, allowing for a more natural flow. An inconvenient blight storm replaced the original subplot of impending bankrupty due to constant mixups between Divine and Almsivi intervention scrolls. In addition, having the Dunce take place near the newly relevant settlements allowed more nods towards the incomprehensible names proudly featured on Imperial maps, which usually take two to three editions to sort out.<BR>
Similar skits exist for the Danstrar/Dunstiorr/Dawnstar controversy, and the notorious "Kyn I have my Helm now, Holme? It's windy!" joke knows no peers. As long as the Imperial Geographics Society produces maps for the masses, the Sneezing Horker Historical Society is assured to never run out of material.<BR>

“大族不止三个。”他说。<BR>
“哦，那有点打乱了。”<BR>
“因多瑞尔家族和德雷斯家族在瓦登费尔没有定居点。传统主义、孤立的因多瑞尔家族没有其他大族的进取动力。他们从神殿定居点获得足够政治利益，所以对他们来说无所谓的。我有时觉得他们认为自己拥有神殿。”<BR>
“神殿，嗯。”<BR>
“你了解我们的宗教吗，阁下？”<BR>
“记住，我是来自冬堡学院受过高等教育的未来贵族。”<BR>
“是的，你一直在说。”<BR>
“我当然知道著名的暗精灵现世神维威克、索萨·希尔和哀伤之城。”<BR>
“......哀 -- 哀伤之城。”<BR>
“是的。”我说，“你看，我非常聪明，意识到暗精灵的神祇都有以他们命名的城市，比如维威克，或者索萨·希尔 -- 那是一座隐秘的城市，他把矮人藏在那里。”<BR>
“矮 -- 他 -- 什么？”<BR>
“那就是矮人消失的地方！他们去和索萨·希尔躲在一起，这样他们就能整天搞奇怪的法师铁匠活，制造会喷出很多蒸汽、让人看不清的东西。你看，我受过教育，知道索萨·希尔非常喜欢奇怪的法师玩意和建造奇怪的东西，因为我读过《2920》。所以逻辑上，矮人一定会跟他走，对吧？他接受了他们的投降，接受了他们的土地，给了他们一个可以整天建造奇怪东西的地方。”<BR>
“......《2920》是虚构的，阁下。”<BR>
“嗯，幸好我没读完，对吧？”<BR>
“是的，我同意。”雷明说。<BR><BR>之后我们继续走，赶走几只峭壁鸟。<BR>
“那另一个呢？德雷斯？”<BR>
“有些事物变得过于适应危险，以至于在安全中无法运转。”雷明说，“这就是我对德雷斯不在瓦登费尔定居的看法。”<BR>
“啊，有趣，有趣。所以你们都住在这些族里？”<BR>
“......‘族’是一种比喻。也许你把它想成氏族会更容易理解。”<BR>
“哦，那就讲得通了！”我说，“是啊，当然，氏族，因为氏族住在房子里，所以我明白了。”<BR>
“是的。而且我必须纠正你。没有叫‘哀伤之城’的城市。女神的名字是阿玛莱西娅。”<BR>
“我可一点也不信。哀伤之城是晨风的首都。”<BR>
“哀伤之城是首都阿玛莱西娅的一小部分，像富人的中心区。”<BR>
“不不，我知道那是错的。我很久以前看过晨风的地图，我记得很清楚，有老跑，有哀伤之城，老跑南边有石头森林 -- ”<BR>
“石头森林？”<BR>
“就在马克格兰森林附近。”<BR>
“马克格 -- 我从没听说过这些地方。”<BR>
“伙计。”我说，“你知道，不是要冒犯你，但你好像有点笨。”<BR><BR>随着我们继续前行，地貌变了。我们不再是绿意盎然中驱赶峭壁鸟，而是在灰烬覆盖的山丘中驱赶它们，周围是枯死的、尖刺的树木。<BR>“我们快到了，阁下。”雷明对我说。<BR>
“好消息。我怎么从老跑回天际？”<BR>
“那可能很难。由于枯萎病的风险，瓦登费尔和大陆之间的旅行目前受限。神殿和帝国必须对这里的一切进行非常彻底、缓慢的检查。”雷明告诉我。“繁琐，但也许是必要的。我会说你该用法师公会向导去维威克，然后步行去黑檀心。”<BR>
“啊，确实确实。如果有人能帮我，那一定是神。”<BR>
“是城市，不是神。”<BR>
“城市还是神？”<BR>
“城市，维威克。”<BR>
“我看不出城市能帮我。”<BR>
“我看不出有谁能帮你。”雷明说。<BR>“神肯定能。我相信如果吉讷在这儿，她就能把我送回天际。”<BR>
“吉讷，”他说，“我相信你是指吉娜瑞斯。”<BR>
“我说的是吉讷。你知道这是基本的诺德宗教，吉讷 -- 鹰。她和她同类帮我们抵御像欧凯或奥杜因这样的危险存在。”<BR>
“你是说阿尔凯。我不知道奥杜因是谁。”<BR>
“奥杜因当然是统治时间的龙神！”<BR>
“那是阿卡托什，阁下。你连自己的宗教都不了解吗？”<BR>
“喂，雷明。也许你觉得我是没受过教育的西方人，但我认为我们诺德人自己的传统，我该有点发言权。看起来你以为我们崇拜帝国教团。”<BR>
雷明似乎困惑。“你的意思是这不对？”<BR>
“我不知道你从哪得来的想法。”<BR>
“奇怪。我几乎肯定是这样。”<BR><BR>
我注意到我们正接近奥德汝因，因为我看到了远处巨大的死螃蟹。但雷明有别的担忧。他的眼睛一直看向西边某个方向，显得忧虑。风大起来了，他不喜欢这样。天气？天气问题。普遍的，我推断。但当我们进入奥德汝因，他正准备和我说再见时，我意识到是别的事。他脸上的担忧在增加。街上的人和守卫似乎也不怎么在意。<BR>
“哦哦。”他说。<BR>
“哦哦？”<BR>
“枯萎病风暴。还是很糟的那种。快进去！”雷明几乎把我推进最近的建筑，砰地关上了身后的门。外面传来可怕的声音，就像愤怒的龙宿醉未醒。就像听到神在隔壁房间发脾气。<BR>
“枯萎病？”我问。<BR>
“我不想解释。”雷明说。他环顾四周。原来我们闯进了战士公会，那里还有一群衣着体面的暗精灵，看起来和雷明差不多。<BR>
“枯萎病风暴？”他问。<BR>
“枯萎病风暴。”其中一个说。<BR>
“嗯，”他说着在他们旁边坐下，“别管那个诺德人。”<BR>
“是不是女巫偷了他的衣服和斧头，把他光着身子留在路边？”一个看起来像巫师的人说。<BR>“不是女巫。”我骄傲地说。他似乎有点惊讶我会说话。<BR>“那对你真好。嗯，雷明·萨德雷西，是的，我们都因异常严重的枯萎病风暴困在这里，连走到那个螃蟹地方都太危险。”巫师说，“所以我们不能做我们想做的那些外交，但我们都还得坐在这里，假装喜欢彼此。”<BR>雷明只是点了点头。“这些是其他大族的代表。”他对我说。<BR>
“啊！”我说，“那你一定是泰瓦尼人吧。”我对巫师说。<BR>
“是的，我是唯一值得加入的家族的成员。”<BR>
“那你一定是勒多兰人！”我对一个看起来很强壮的精灵说。他只是点了点头。<BR>
“那你......哈拉鲁？”<BR>
“因多瑞尔。”一个看起来相当体面的说，“我们完全不一样。”<BR>
“如果你想的话可以。”泰瓦尼人说，“如果你需要，我可以卖给你一个脑子。”<BR><BR>
我们最终和公会其他人一起坐下，等待风暴平息，剩下整晚除了喝酒争论没什么事可做。<BR>
“......当然，我只是个没受过教育的西方人。”我说，“但在我看来......除了达格斯-乌尔本身，晨风最恶劣的环境就是这灰烬地带。”我打了个嗝。<BR>
我所有的精灵伙伴都立刻开始摇头。泰瓦尼人低声骂我。<BR>
“除了火山本身，阁下，”勒多兰人几乎没醉地说，“晨风最恶劣、最有毒、最不宜居的地区是德亚西特。”<BR>
“确实。”因多瑞尔人说，“有毒的环境，有毒的精灵。成堆的无用毒盐，土壤被氯或其他酸污染到正常植物无法生长，风把盐吹进你的眼睛、鼻子和皮肤，酸雨，野生天裂兽，有毒烟雾，最糟的是德雷斯人，他们可能比这里的术士更异端。”<BR>
“那里太毒了，我读过某个德雷斯人写的诗，描述那里的风景，光是想想就觉得恶心。”泰瓦尼女人说，“而且，那诗本身也很烂。”<BR>
“是的，德雷斯人不是好诗人。”我的向导说。<BR>
“他们什么都不擅长。”泰瓦尼女人说，“他们疯了。住在德亚西特的人一定是疯了。这也好，因为我觉得如果你不疯，可能也活不下来。”<BR>“有意思。”我说，立刻醉得不省人事。<BR><BR>
****<BR>
<BR>
编者注：<BR>
原短剧设定在维洛提斯区的韦拉尼斯定居点，旅程将角色带到港口城镇拉尼姆，以黑光为目标。<BR>
由于瓦登费尔最近才开放殖民，旅程被重写为发生在岛上，以便更自然。一场不合时宜的枯萎病风暴取代了原剧情中因圣灵干涉和审判席干涉卷轴混淆而导致破产的支线。此外，让愚行录发生在新相关的定居点附近，可以更多提及帝国地图上那些令人难以理解的名字，这些名字通常需要两到三个版本来厘清。<BR>
类似短剧还有关于丹斯特拉/邓斯蒂奥尔/晨星的争议，以及臭名昭著的“吉讷我现在有头盔了，霍尔姆？风真大！”笑话无与伦比。只要帝国地理学会为大众制作地图，打喷嚏海象历史学会就永远不会缺少素材。<BR>

When I woke the next morning, I was shocked to discover we were all in jail. <BR> <BR>
"Hey!" I said, standing up, hitting my head on the ceiling. "What's this about?"<BR>"Be quiet," said the guard standing outside.<BR>"Quiet? I've done nothing wrong!"<BR>"We'll be the judge of that," the guard said. I looked around. One of us was missing.<BR>"Oi. Where's the mage woman?"<BR>"Dead," he said. "You're all suspects. Nobody else was in the Fighters' Guild while the Blight storm was going, so it had to be one of you." Then, he turned around to face me specifically. "Speaking of suspects. I interviewed the Indoril representative earlier today. After he stopped demanding his release, he said you and the Telvanni didn't particularly get along."<BR>"Ha! Would you get along with a Telvanni?"<BR>"An unexpectedly good point, Nord," the guard said, "but it does not change the facts. Second. The murder weapon was rather interesting and uncommon."<BR>"Oh, aye? And what was it then?"<BR>"A Nordic combat axe," he said. "An enchanted one, too. A weird one, too. The Mages' Guild says that whenever this axe strikes someone, it paralyzes them, soul traps them, and lightly poisons them, but also makes them mildly more charismatic."<BR>"That's Niptickler!" I said.<BR>"So. You know the murder weapon, you had a motive to use it, and you're a Nord, who probably thought that a Telvanni sorceror was a witch who would steal your clothes and enchanted axe. How stereotypical."<BR>"Now, listen here! The only reason I'm here is because I had my clothes and enchanted axe stolen by someone who wasn't a witch!"<BR>"Yes. That reflects so much better on you," the guard said. "You know, it gets worse though. The soul trapping part. Because we found a soul gem, probably filled with the victim's soul. Highly illegal in Morrowind. I don't know why you'd bring these into the province... unless you weren't supposed to be here."<BR>
"Well, I'm not supposed to be here, but that doe--" <BR>
"Fascinating."<BR>
"Look, listen. Niptickler was stolen from me. Whoever did that, that's your killer."<BR>
"And where was 'Niptickler' stolen from you?"<BR>
"Up near Khuul."<BR>
"And how did you get to Ald'Ruhn?"<BR>
"By foot, yesterday."<BR>
"Yes. Okay. You want me to believe that the not-witch who stole Niptickler followed you, on foot, to Ald'Ruhn, to frame you--you specifically--for murder, and that given that you were the only ones in the Fighters' Guild at the time, she somehow got in there before you, and before the Blight storm picked up. This is the story you want me to believe?"<BR>
"Well, it's the truth, isn't it?"<BR>
"I am not a fool," he said. He walked off.<BR> <BR> 
After yelling at the bars for a few minutes, I slumped back onto the bench with the others. <BR>
"Remyn," I said nudging him. "Remyn. Did you hear that?" <BR>
He stirred a bit, groaning. "No." <BR>
"They think I committed murder, Remyn." <BR>
"That's bad." <BR>
"They've got Niptickler." <BR>
"That's ba--Niptickler? How?" <BR>
"That's right, Niptickler." <BR>
"I know, but how? You never had it," he said. "You were naked. I remember that part very clearly." <BR>
"Right? There was nowhere I could have hid Niptickler from you, not that I would hide it." <BR>
"Yes, you weren't hiding anything, unfortunately," he said. "And why do they have Niptickler?" <BR>
"That's the thing. The Telvanni woman was killed by Niptickler." <BR>
"That's good. But confusing." <BR>
"Good?" <BR>
"Yes, I'm glad she's dead." <BR>
"Hey, be careful about that!" I said. "They think I killed her just because we didn't get along!" <BR>
"Yes, but you're a Nord," he said. "The Dunmer are not great fans of Nords." <BR>
"That's pretty unfair. You know, an Elf was Jarl of Snowhawk once." <BR>
"...Where?" <BR>
"Snowhawk! Bah, never mind it.  I suppose they weren't Jarl for very long, only the time it took for good ol' Hjomar to cook him. Bah, nevermind." <BR>
"I won't." <BR>
"I guess the only real possibility is that... somehow that witch who stole your axe got here before us." <BR>
"Or followed us." <BR>
"Wouldn't we have noticed?" He paused. "No, we probably wouldn't have. This is very serious." He sat up. "You are a fool, but you do not deserve to be framed for a crime you did not commit. However, Redoran are stubborn, and don't listen to reason." <BR>
"Then what should we do?" <BR>
"Lucky for us, we're not well known amongst guards, here or elsewhere. If we wanted, we could just escape." <BR>
"We could? How?" <BR>
"I'll just cast Divine Intervention. Then, we'll walk from the Imperial fort to the silt strider, and get away long enough for the guards to forget about us." <BR>
"You really think the guards would forget about us?" <BR>
"Telvanni kill each other all the time. Once the guards realize that the Telvanni councillors don't actually want people to be punished by other houses for killing Telvanni, they'll drop it." <BR>
"Is that true? That seems stupid."<BR>
"Most of the councillors are only councillors because they killed someone or other, and many of them intend to rise higher by killing some more councillors, not to mention all the aspiring young wizards in their ranks. The last thing they want is other Houses standing in the way of their individual schemes. It's one of the sick but practical ways that they remain united against other Houses. Here. Hook my arm." <BR>
I did so. <BR>
"Now, I'll just cast Divine Intervention." <BR><BR>
And, after some purple nonsense, we'd finally gotten out of the jail. Still hungover, we stumbled a bit in the Imperial fort. The legionnaires ignored us, used to finding hungover, injured, or other kinds of adventurers and travellers teleporting themselves into the fort, often just by accident, but one legionnaire seemed to swear under his breath. <BR>
"Right. The silt strider." Remyn, still hung over, stumbled out. "It's that way." He pointed. <BR>
After a few hours heading down the ashlands, it was clear that we were going the wrong way, but by now we were closer to Caldera than we were to Ald'Ruhn, so, Remyn reasoned, we would just use the guild guide. He was annoyed, because his important business was ruined now, his pack guars and merchandise were back in Ald'Ruhn where he was still suspected for murder, and he was too hung over to have realized this when he got us out of prison, but it was too bloody late for any of that nonsense. We arrived in Caldera, a completely non-descript place with no features whatsoever, and hitched into the Mages' Guild, a completely non-descript place with no features whatsoever. <BR> 
Remyn stumbled up the stairs to the guild guide. "Get us to Vivec," he said. <BR>
"Where?" the woman said. "Sorry, my hearing's a bit weird right now. I got hit by a sound spell." <BR>
"A what?" <BR>
"What? I said my hearing's a bit we--" <BR>
"Yes, I heard that, what sound spell?" <BR>
"That's right, a sound spell?" <BR>
"Is someone casting sound spells?" I said, getting hit by a sound spell. <BR>
"What?" Remyn said. <BR>
"I got hit by a sound spell!" <BR>
"A what?" <BR>
"Whggshs ka k k?" the guild guide seemed to say, but I couldn't hear, because I'd been hit by a sound spell. <BR>
"Yes, a sound spell!" I shouted at her. Remyn and I were starting to lose our tempers.<BR> "My, my, you're being very rude and drunk and intimidating at me, and if you don't stop, I'll just, I'll just send you somewhere and you won't like it!" <BR>
"No, a sound spell! Someone in this bloody guild is casting sound spells!" <BR>
"I mean it, I really will just get you out of here! I don't even know where! I'll just cast a spell, I'm warning you, you--you could end up in Red Mountain! I've had a very stressful day because the Argonian keeps casting sound spells at everyone!" <BR>
"What?" <BR>
"Yes, sound spells!" she said. <BR>
Remyn lost his temper and stormed right up to her. "Listen, Breton, I don't care about the sound spells, just get us to Vivec!" <BR>
"You asked for it! I did warn you!" she shouted. Remyn and I disappeared in a bright light. <BR> <BR>
After stumbling about and choking for a bit, Remyn and I got to our feet. Touching the ground with my bare hands scratched them, and it felt poisonous. The air was disgusting. Truthfully, I have never felt so immediately attacked by anything in my life than I did by wherever this place was. This includes the time I was attacked by three frost trolls up near Morthal. But I would've taken my chances with the trolls over wherever this place was. Standing up was a test of strength. Luckily, it was obviously not Red Mountain. Wasn't red.<BR><BR>
Remyn managed to stand up too, covering up his nose to protect himself from the foul, foul stench. He hacked a bit. "That n'wah!" he yelled. "I can't believe her!" <BR>
"Where are we, Remyn?" <BR>
"She teleported us off Vvardenfell!" he shouted. Before me was a flat wasteland, mostly covered in a green haze. It smelled worse than anything I'd ever smelled, covered in salt and poison fumes. <BR>
"We're in the Dejasyte." <BR> <BR>

第二天早上醒来，我震惊地发现我们都在监狱里。<BR><BR>
“嘿！”我说着站起来，头撞到天花板，“这是怎么回事？”<BR>“安静。”站在外面的守卫说。<BR>“安静？我什么也没做错！”<BR>“我们会判断的。”守卫说。我环顾四周。我们少了一个人。<BR>“喂。那个女法师呢？”<BR>“死了。”他说，“你们都是嫌疑人。枯萎病风暴期间战士公会没有别人，所以一定是你们中的一个。”然后他专门转向我。“说到嫌疑人。我今天早些时候审问了因多瑞尔代表。在他停止要求释放后，他说你和泰瓦尼人相处得不太好。”<BR>“哈！你会和泰瓦尼人相处好吗？”<BR>“出人意料的好观点，诺德人。”守卫说，“但这不改变事实。第二，凶器相当有趣且不常见。”<BR>“哦，是吗？那是什么？”<BR>“一把诺德战斧。”他说，“还是附了魔的。也很奇怪。法师公会说这把斧头每次击中别人，会麻痹目标、灵魂陷阱、轻微中毒，同时还会让他们变得更有点魅力。”<BR>“那是尼普提克勒！”我说。<BR>“所以。你认识凶器，你有动机使用它，而且你是诺德人，可能认为泰瓦尼巫师是女巫，会偷你的衣服和附魔斧头。真刻板。”<BR>“你听着！我在这里的唯一原因，是我的衣服和附魔斧头被一个不是女巫的人偷了！”<BR>“是的。那显得你好多了。”守卫说，“不过还有更糟的。灵魂陷阱部分。因为我们找到了一颗灵魂石，很可能装满了受害者的灵魂。在晨风这非常非法。我不知道你为什么把这些带进行省......除非你不该在这里。”<BR>
“嗯，我不该在这里，但这 -- ”<BR>
“有意思。”<BR>
“听着。尼普提克勒是被偷的。谁偷的，谁就是凶手。”<BR>
“‘尼普提克勒’是从哪里被偷的？”<BR>
“库尔附近。”<BR>
“你怎么到奥德汝因的？”<BR>
“昨天走来的。”<BR>
“好的。你想让我相信，那个偷了尼普提克勒的非女巫，步行跟着你到奥德汝因，陷害你 -- 你 -- 谋杀，而且鉴于当时只有你们在战士公会，她不知怎的在你之前、在枯萎病风暴来临之前就进去了。这就是你想让我相信的故事？”<BR>
“嗯，这是事实，不是吗？”<BR>
“我不是傻瓜。”他说着走开了。<BR><BR>
对着栏杆吼了几分钟后，我瘫回长凳上。<BR>
“雷明，”我推了推他，“雷明。你听见了吗？”<BR>
他动了动，呻吟道：“没有。”<BR>
“他们以为我杀了人，雷明。”<BR>
“那不好。”<BR>
“他们拿到了尼普提克勒。”<BR>
“那不好 -- 尼普提克勒？怎么？”<BR>
“没错，尼普提克勒。”<BR>
“我知道，但怎么？你从没有它。”他说，“你是裸体的。我记得很清楚。”<BR>
“对吧？我没办法从你那里藏起尼普提克勒，何况我也不会藏。”<BR>
“是的，可惜你什么也没藏。”他说，“他们为什么有尼普提克勒？”<BR>
“问题就在这。泰瓦尼女人是被尼普提克勒杀的。”<BR>
“那很好。但令人困惑。”<BR>
“好？”<BR>
“是的，我很高兴她死了。”<BR>
“嘿，说话小心点！”我说，“他们以为我杀了她，就因为我和她相处不好！”<BR>
“是的，但你是诺德人。”他说，“丹莫不太喜欢诺德人。”<BR>
“那太不公平了。你知道吗，曾经有个精灵是雪鹰的领主。”<BR>
“...哪？”<BR>
“雪鹰！算了，别管了。我想他们没当多久领主，只有老好人约马尔把他煮了那么久。算了，别管了。”<BR>
“我不会管的。”<BR>
“我想唯一真正的可能是......偷你斧头的女巫不知怎的在我们之前到了这里。”<BR>
“或者跟着我们。”<BR>
“我们不会注意到吗？”他顿了顿。“不，我们可能不会注意到。这很严重。”他坐起来，“你是个傻瓜，但你不该被冤枉你未犯的罪。然而勒多兰人很固执，不听道理。”<BR>
“那我们该怎么办？”<BR>
“幸运的是，我们在守卫中不知名，无论这里还是别处。如果我们想，我们可以逃走。”<BR>
“我们能？怎么？”<BR>
“我就施个圣灵干涉。然后我们从帝国堡垒走到阔步沙蚤站，逃走足够久，让守卫忘了我们。”<BR>
“你真觉得守卫会忘了我们？”<BR>
“泰瓦尼人经常互相残杀。一旦守卫意识到泰瓦尼议员其实不希望别人因杀死泰瓦尼人而受其他家族惩罚，他们就会罢手。”<BR>
“真的吗？那听起来很蠢。”<BR>
“大多数议员之所以是议员，是因为他们杀了某个人，而且他们很多人打算通过杀更多议员来晋升，更不用说他们队伍中那些有抱负的年轻巫师了。他们最不想要的就是其他家族阻碍他们个人计划。这是他们团结起来对抗其他家族的一种病态但实用的方式。来，挽住我的胳膊。”<BR>
我照做了。<BR>
“现在，我这就施圣灵干涉。”<BR><BR>
然后，在一阵紫色的胡闹之后，我们终于逃出了监狱。还宿醉未醒，我们在帝国堡垒里踉踉跄跄。军团士兵无视我们，他们习惯了找到宿醉、受伤或其他类型的冒险者和旅行者意外传送进堡垒，但一个士兵似乎在低声咒骂。<BR>
“好的。阔步沙蚤。”雷明还宿醉着，踉跄走出去，“那边。”他指了指。<BR>
在灰烬之地走了几个小时后，显然我们走错了路，但此时我们离卡尔德拉比离奥德汝因更近，所以雷明推断我们用法师公会向导。他很恼火，因为他的重要生意毁了，他的驮货瓜尔和货物还在奥德汝因，他仍在那里被怀疑谋杀，而且他宿醉太厉害，带我们出狱时没想到这些，但现在说什么都太晚了。我们到了卡尔德拉，一个完全没有特色的地方，搭车进了法师公会，一个完全没有特色的地方。<BR>
雷明踉跄上楼找公会向导。“送我们去维威克。”他说。<BR>
“哪？”女人说，“抱歉，我的听力现在有点怪。我被声音法术击中了。”<BR>
“什么？”<BR>
“什么？我说我的听力有点 -- ”<BR>
“是的，我听见了，什么声音法术？”<BR>
“没错，声音法术？”<BR>
“有人在施声音法术吗？”我说，被声音法术击中了。<BR>
“什么？”雷明说。<BR>
“我被声音法术击中了！”<BR>
“什么？”<BR>
“额咯咯咯咯？”公会向导似乎说，但我听不见，因为我被声音法术击中了。<BR>
“是的，声音法术！”我朝她喊道。我和雷明开始失去耐心。<BR>“哎呀，你对我很粗鲁、醉酒又吓人，如果你不停下，我就，我就送你去个地方，你不会喜欢的！”<BR>
“不，声音法术！这该死的公会里有人在施声音法术！”<BR>
“我是认真的，我真的会送你们走！我甚至不知道去哪！我就施法，我警告你，你们 -- 你们可能到红山！我今天压力很大，因为那个阿尔贡一直对所有人施声音法术！”<BR>
“什么？”<BR>
“是的，声音法术！”她说。<BR>
雷明发脾气了，冲到她面前。“听着，布莱顿人，我不在乎声音法术，送我们去维威克！”<BR>
“你自找的！我警告过你！”她喊道。我和雷明消失在亮光中。<BR><BR>
在踉跄和窒息片刻后，我和雷明站起来。光着手摸地就划伤了，感觉有毒。空气令人作呕。老实说，我一生中从未感到被任何事物如此直接地攻击过，就像被这个地方攻击一样。包括在莫萨尔附近被三只霜巨魔袭击那次。但我宁可和巨魔搏斗，也不愿待在这地方。站起来都是考验力量。幸运的是，显然不是红山。不是红色的。<BR><BR>
雷明也挣扎着站起来，捂住鼻子抵挡那恶臭。他咳了几声。“那个恩’瓦！”他喊道，“我真不敢相信她！”<BR>
“我们在哪，雷明？”<BR>
“她把我们传送出瓦登费尔了！”他喊道。我面前是一片平坦的荒地，大部分笼罩在绿色雾霾中。气味比我闻过的任何东西都糟，覆盖着盐和毒雾。<BR>
“我们在德亚西特。”<BR><BR>
****<BR>
编者注：<BR>
比较丹莫大族的优点总能引发一场健康的酒吧斗殴，费拉纳·阿德雷西对此引以为豪。<BR>
不幸的是，在一次这样的斗殴中，起因竟是她角色对德雷斯家族的不恭言论，费拉纳被一个没瞄准的啤酒桶击中，不久后去世。<BR>
<BR>
虽然未编辑的卷四副本和未完成的卷五草稿存在，但弗洛利亚·银血和打喷嚏海象历史学会希望记住费拉纳作品的最佳状态。她笔下的人物，通过洞察、表演和美酒活了起来，最终困在了一片荒凉之地。我们是谁，怎能告诉你他们如何克服困境？<BR>

A Dunce in Morrowind, vol. 4
晨风愚行录，卷四

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_DunceInMorrowindTR_V4
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
A Dunce in Morrowind, v4<BR>
by Frolja Silver-Blood<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
A few days ago, I was told that the Dejasyte were, barring Red Mountain, the worst place in Morrowind. This was clearly true, I thought to myself, my cloth shoes having already been eaten through by chlorine and spiky salt crystals. Also, I may have been dying at the time. Remyn seemed little better. It was hard to see, what with all the toxic fumes that were killing us. We had no directions whatsoever, and we had been walking for a while. Occasionally, we saw these guars--tiger striped ones--but they ignored us.<BR>
<BR>
"Hey, Remyn," I said. "Can't you Divinely Intervene us out of here?"<BR>
<BR>
"I am no mage," he said. "If we had somewhere to rest, I could recover my own magic a bit, but I learned some spells off a former mistress of mine who happened to be an apprentice in the Mages Guild, and didn't pay very much attention."<BR>
<BR>
"Mistress, eh?"<BR>
<BR>
"Yes. It was easier than working out the problems with my wife."<BR>
<BR>
"Marriage problems, eh?"<BR>
<BR>
"Yes, I know," he said. "Anyway, I am no magician. Magicka takes time to recover, or something. I don't really understand it myself. It has something to do with... daedrons? Daedra? I don't know. I don't know anything. I think I'm dying."<BR>
<BR>
"Me too," I said. "That woman in the Mages Guild. Was she a witch?"<BR>
<BR>
"I hope so. That way it will be legal to kill her in revenge," he said. "If we can find somewhere to stay, even a road we can follow, I can try to talk the Dres into letting you stay in a tavern with me, and then Divine Intervene our way out tomorrow... unless we end up in the lizard lands."<BR>
<BR>
"The Marsh?"<BR>
<BR>
"Well, we're in a very southern part of Morrowind. I don't know what part of the Deshaan we're in. It's a real risk that the closest Imperial shrine is in some no-name Whatevermoth Fort at the Argonian border."<BR>
<BR>
"Hm. What's so bad about that?"<BR>
<BR>
"The Marsh is equally as hostile as the plains: maybe more. Plus, the Argonians probably won't be thrilled to see me. They'd probably think I'm a Dres slavehunter."<BR>
<BR>
"Ha! Amazing to think that only a few centuries ago, all our peoples were allies, don't you think?"<BR>
<BR>
"I think you are making things up again."<BR>
<BR>
"No, I definitely remember. We were in Ebonheart or something."<BR>
<BR>
"Not to be rude, sera, but our people have literallly always been at war over something or other."<BR>
<BR>
"That's not true at all! What about that one time, with that blue man. Who was he? He hated Tamriel."<BR>
<BR>
"Blue man."<BR>
<BR>
"He had those things. You know the ones. Didn't like Tamriel much. Or maybe the thing was that he really did like Tamriel too much. Ha! Makes you think."<BR>
<BR>
"Please stop. This talking is probably wasting some of the few bits of breathable air we have left."<BR>
<BR>
After stumbling around for a while, we eventually passed out on top of what turned out to be a sleeping Zoar, which must have walked along quite a way, because when we woke up, there was an elf covered in Zoar hide staring at us.<BR>
<BR>
"Here." He turned to Remyn and gave him a potion. "This should heal your condition."<BR>
<BR>
Remyn managed to drink it. I tried to squeak any noise out at him that would get his attention. He didn't respond.<BR>
<BR>
Remyn, after about half a minute, was looking much better. "Could I have another one?"<BR>
<BR>
"Not if it's for the Nord, no," the elf said. <BR>
<BR>
"500 gold."<BR>
<BR>
"Done." They traded, and Remyn handed me a potion. I stood up after bit, feeling healthy again.<BR>
<BR>
"You wouldn't happen to have one of those restore-your-magic potions, would you?" I said.<BR>
<BR>
"Do I have to talk to him?" the elf said.<BR>
<BR>
"No," Remyn said. "But I could use that kind of potion."<BR>
<BR>
"Well. I don't have one," he said. He was holding something weird, that looked like a stomach with the throat still attached to it.<BR>
<BR>
"What's that you got there?" I said.<BR>
<BR>
"Do not talk," he said to me. "I am willing to help you get to Ald Horak with me," he said to Remyn. "If the Nord is going to come with us, he has to be unconscious."<BR>
<BR>
Without hesitating, Remyn knocked me out. When I woke up, I was in jail again. I went straight to the bars. "Oi! Hey! Let me out!"<BR>
<BR>
The guard ignored me.<BR>
<BR>
"I know you can hear me, elf! Let me out!"<BR>
<BR>
"No."<BR>
<BR>
"Come on! I didn't do anything! I was unconscious!"<BR>
<BR>
"I'm sure you did something. That's why you were unconscious."<BR>
<BR>
I paused. "Remyn Sadrethi! Talk to Remyn! He'll sort this out!"<BR>
<BR>
"Maybe. I hope not," the guard said.<BR>
<BR>
"Hey, listen here! You can't just hold someone in jail for committing no crime!"<BR>
<BR>
"I'm sure you committed some crime. I'm sure you saw some Dunmer woman, thought she was a witch who stole your special axe and clothes, and then you probably killed her."<BR>
<BR>
"It wasn't a witch!"<BR>
<BR>
"A confession?"<BR>
<BR>
"I didn't kill anyone!"<BR>
<BR>
"I see. Then you are pathetic, because you couldn't even kill an unarmed Dunmer woman who wasn't a witch. This is even worse."<BR>
<BR>
"You're not being very fair, you know!"<BR>
<BR>
"Good. Outlanders do not deserve fairness. What they deserve is--" He then spoke for at least four hours about all the evils of outlanders, the Empire, the Imperial Cult (he hated Zenithar and Dibella in particular, and would not shut up about Imperial depictions of Dibella drawing her breasts too small), Skyrim, the Marsh, the Hlaalu, the Dark Brotherhood, the idea of horseshoes ("Why, outlander, do your animals wear shoes? Why are you so stupid and inferior? We did nothing to deserve being on the same plane as you. Why must we put up with your idiocy?"), his mother, Argonian slaves who keep dying before they can finish their job in the plantations, and then transitioned into his sister's upcoming wedding, how he hated his future brother in law and his family, and after at least two more hours of ranting, transitioned back to how poorly endowed he assumed Tiber Septim must have been. Eventually, he spoke so much that he passed out, and realizing that the door was unlocked, I stepped out, where I immediately ran into Remyn.<BR>
<BR>
"There you are," he said. "...you didn't hurt that guard, did you?"<BR>
<BR>
"No," I said.<BR>
<BR>
Remyn stared at me for a moment, then at the guard, then back at me. "You're probably right. Come on. We have a place to stay here, so we'll just sleep the night, and then we can Divine Intervene ourselves out of here, and hopefully end up at Narsis or somewhere."<BR>
<BR>
I was thoughtful for a moment, for no reason whatsoever. "Say, Remyn," I said. "How did I end up in jail?"<BR>
<BR>
"I don't know how you end up anywhere."<BR>
<BR>
"Yes, but, weren't you with me and the clothy elf the whole time?"<BR>
<BR>
"The what?"<BR>
<BR>
"Clothy."<BR>
<BR>
"I think you mean the trader. Animal hide is not clo-" A look of defeat passed over my companion's face, for some reason. "Forget it. No, I left when we got into town because I was still hungover and had almost died, so I just plain forgot."<BR>
<BR>
"I see," I said. "Well, come on. Before they find some other excuse to arrest me." <BR>
<BR>
Right after that, a guard came up and arrested me. "Halt, outlander. You're under arrest," he said, arresting me.<BR>
<BR>
"Again?" I said. A striped guar came from behind him and gently placed my arm in its mouth, to restrain me.<BR>
<BR>
"Ah, so you have been arrested before. Now I know that I was correct to arrest you," the guard said.<BR>
<BR>
"You mean you arrested this man without any evidence of a crime being committed," Remyn said, skeptically.<BR>
<BR>
"That is exactly how a salt-brained Hlaalu would see things. There is clear evidence of a crime being committed, because he is a Nord."<BR>
<BR>
"I see," Remyn said, "but is that worth the cost?"<BR>
<BR>
"You are typical for your greedy house. How could there be a 'cost' to doing my duty?" the guard said.<BR>
<BR>
Suddenly, I noticed there were some very strange things being carried around by this guard. All sorts of oddly-shapped whatsits were strapped onto his inferior, non-steel armour by weird, belt-like things. Being an educated noble, my curiosity about the weirdness overcame my outrage at being arrested.<BR>
<BR>
"...what's that you got there?" I asked him.<BR>
<BR>
He looked at me as though I'd urinated on his mother. "That, outlander, is a beetle water pack."<BR>
<BR>
"Beetle?"<BR>
<BR>
"Salt Beetles. We remove the trunk, throat and stomach intact, and we use it to collect water ready-filtered. You can whack out most of the poison from the trunk, and then it's ready to drink."<BR>
<BR>
"Why would you want to drink out of a bug's stomach?"<BR>
<BR>
"The alternative is dying of thirst," he said. "Any more stupid questions?"<BR>
<BR>
I paused. "What's with all them belts?"<BR>
<BR>
"Because, outlander, if you're caught in a salt storm, the last thing you want is getting poisoned salt all over your skin and inside your clothes. You have to keep the Zoarskin buckled tight to keep the salt from getting underneath," he said. "Can we stop talking now?"<BR>
<BR>
"Well, hang on a sec. You're wearing some sort of high platform boots so that you can keep most of it out of the chlorine, right?"<BR>
<BR>
"Yes."<BR>
<BR>
"Why's your guar barefoot?"<BR>
<BR>
"Guar don't wear shoes, outlander."<BR>
<BR>
"Horses wear shoes."<BR>
<BR>
"I don't know what a horse is, but only an outlander would be foolish enough to make shoes for animals."<BR>
<BR>
"Ah, but that's where you're wrong! You see, back in Old Run, I remember-" My sentence was cut off by the guard attempting to strike me so hard with his blunt weapon that I would be knocked unconscious. However, with the effects of that healing potion still miraculously active, I felt only a tickle. "Well, that's quite rude to interrupt! As I was saying -"<BR>
<BR>
"I order you to stop talking, outlander. I consider it assault."<BR>
<BR>
"Ah, but I don't consider it assault at all! And as I was saying, back in the Old Run, you see, they had these crabs. And they lived in the crabs, right? So you see, in a way, the ground is the crab's -" The guard made two clicking noises, and the guar released my arm.<BR>
<BR>
"These last few minutes have been so excruciating that this qualifies as the singlemost worst thing that could possibly happen to anyone in any circumstances. Please do me a favor and die, but do it somewhere else." The guard then pulled out a scroll from his guar's pack, and casted one of those Divine Intervention spells at us, and so again we disappeared across Morrowind in a flash of light.<BR>

<BR>
Publisher's Note<BR>
Due to a wellspring of support and consideration, the Sheezing Horker Historical Society has decided to publish the rest of Ferana Andrethi's "Dunce in Morrowind", helped along by a surprising number of would-be-writers.<BR>
<BR>
It is the opinion of Frolja Silver-Blood and her editing partners that we have compiled an accurate account of the hostile Dejasyte. While it may be closed off for serious scholastic work, the odd sailors, who moved westwards from Tear or Ald Horak and ended up in Winterhold, painted a picture of the Dejastye that we deemed good enough.<BR>
<BR>
It should be no surprise that the guard character exists in reality, reportedly with the exact same attitude. The actual "crime" the Dunce was not-quite-accused-of would have been entering Ald Horak as an outlander. Not merely a port of trade, Ald Horak has strict limits on who may or may not enter.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
晨风愚行录，卷四<BR>
弗洛利亚·银血 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
几天前，我被告知德亚西特是晨风仅次于红山的最糟糕的地方。这显然是真的，我心想，我的布鞋已经被氯和尖刺盐晶腐蚀穿透了。而且，我当时可能快死了。雷明似乎也好不到哪去。视线模糊，被毒雾环绕。我们完全没方向，已经走了一阵子。偶尔看到一些瓜尔 -- 虎纹的那种 -- 但它们无视我们。<BR>
<BR>
“嘿，雷明，”我说，“你不能用圣灵干涉把我们传出去吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“我不是法师。”他说，“如果有地方休息，我能恢复些法力，但我的法术是从以前的一位女主人那里学的，她碰巧是法师公会的学徒，而且没怎么认真学。”<BR>
<BR>
“女主人，嗯？”<BR>
<BR>
“是的。比解决和妻子的问题容易。”<BR>
<BR>
“婚姻问题，嗯？”<BR>
<BR>
“是的，我知道。”他说，“反正我不是法师。魔能恢复需要时间，还是什么。我自己也不懂。和什么......迪德罗？迪德拉？有关？不知道。我什么都不知道。我想我快死了。”<BR>
<BR>
“我也是。”我说，“法师公会那个女人，她是女巫吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“我希望是。那样杀她报复就合法了。”他说，“如果我们能找到地方落脚，哪怕有条路可走，我就能试着说服德雷斯人让你和我一起待在酒馆，然后明天用圣灵干涉离开......除非我们到了蜥蜴地。”<BR>
<BR>
“沼泽？”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，我们在晨风很南的地方。我不知道在迪莎安哪个区域。最近的帝国圣祠很可能在阿尔贡边境某个无名某某蛾堡，这风险很大。”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯。那有什么不好？”<BR>
<BR>
“沼泽和平原一样恶劣：甚至更糟。而且，阿尔贡人可能不会高兴见到我。他们可能以为我是德雷斯奴隶猎手。”<BR>
<BR>
“哈！想想几个世纪前我们所有民族还是盟友，真神奇，你不觉得吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“我觉得你又在编故事了。”<BR>
<BR>
“不，我确实记得。我们在黑檀心还是什么的。”<BR>
<BR>
“不是冒犯，阁下，但我们民族几乎总是为某件事打仗。”<BR>
<BR>
“那完全不对！有次呢，那个蓝皮肤的人。他是谁？他讨厌泰姆瑞尔。”<BR>
<BR>
“蓝皮肤的人。”<BR>
<BR>
“他有那些东西。你知道的。不太喜欢泰姆瑞尔。或者也许是他太喜欢泰姆瑞尔了。哈！让你思考。”<BR>
<BR>
“请停下。说话可能在浪费我们仅剩的一些可呼吸空气。”<BR>
<BR>
在踉跄前行一阵后，我们最终昏倒在一只睡着的佐尔身上，它一定走了很远，因为当我们醒来时，一个浑身裹着佐尔皮的精灵正盯着我们。<BR>
<BR>
“给你。”他转向雷明给了他药剂，“这能治你的状况。”<BR>
<BR>
雷明勉强喝了下去。我试着冲他发出任何能引起注意的声音，他没回应。<BR>
<BR>
大约半分钟后，雷明看起来好多了。“能再来一瓶吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“如果是给那个诺德人的，不行。”精灵说。<BR>
<BR>
“500金币。”<BR>
<BR>
“成交。”他们交易了，雷明把药剂递给我。我过了一会站起来，感觉又健康了。<BR>
<BR>
“你碰巧有那种恢复魔法的药剂吗？”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“我必须和他说话吗？”精灵说。<BR>
<BR>
“不。”雷明说，“但我确实需要那种药剂。”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，我没有。”他说。他手里拿着一个奇怪的东西，像胃连着喉咙。<BR>
<BR>
“你手里拿的是什么？”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“别说话。”他对我说，“我愿意带你们去阿尔德·霍拉克。”他对雷明说，“如果这诺德人要跟我们走，他必须昏迷。”<BR>
<BR>
雷明毫不犹豫地把我打晕了。我醒来时又在监狱里。我直接走到栏杆边。“喂！嘿！放我出去！”<BR>
<BR>
守卫无视我。<BR>
<BR>
“我知道你能听见，精灵！放我出去！”<BR>
<BR>
“不。”<BR>
<BR>
“拜托！我什么都没做！我昏迷了！”<BR>
<BR>
“我肯定你做了什么。所以你才昏迷。”<BR>
<BR>
我顿了顿。“雷明·萨德雷西！找雷明！他会解决的！”<BR>
<BR>
“也许吧。我希望不会。”守卫说。<BR>
<BR>
“嘿，听着！你不能在没犯罪的情况下把人关在监狱里！”<BR>
<BR>
“我肯定你犯了罪。我肯定你看到一个丹莫女人，以为她是偷你特殊斧头和衣服的女巫，然后你杀了她。”<BR>
<BR>
“不是女巫！”<BR>
<BR>
“认罪？”<BR>
<BR>
“我没杀人！”<BR>
<BR>
“我明白了。那你很可悲，因为你连一个手无寸铁、不是女巫的丹莫女人都杀不了。这更糟。”<BR>
<BR>
“你不太公平，你知道吗！”<BR>
<BR>
“好。外乡人不配得到公平。他们该得到的是 -- ”然后他至少说了四个小时，关于外乡人的所有罪恶、帝国、帝国教团（他特别恨泽尼萨尔和蒂贝拉，对帝国把蒂贝拉的胸部画得太小喋喋不休）、天际、沼泽、哈拉鲁、黑暗兄弟会、马蹄铁的想法（“为什么，外乡人，你的动物穿鞋？你为什么这么愚蠢和低等？我们没做任何事配得上和你们在同一界。我们为什么必须忍受你们的愚蠢？”）、他母亲、那些在种植园活干完前就不断死去的阿尔贡奴隶，然后转入他妹妹即将到来的婚礼，他多么恨他未来的姐夫和其家人，又至少咆哮了两小时后，又转回他对泰伯·塞普汀一定贫乏的猜测。最终他说太多以至于晕过去了，我发现门没锁，便走出去，立刻撞见了雷明。<BR>
<BR>
“你在这儿。”他说，“......你没伤害那个守卫吧？”<BR>
<BR>
“没有。”我说。<BR>
<BR>
雷明看了我一会，又看看守卫，又看看我。“你可能没错。来吧。我们在这有地方住，所以睡一晚，然后可以用圣灵干涉离开，希望能到纳西斯或什么地方。”<BR>
<BR>
我沉思了片刻，毫无缘由。“嘿，雷明，”我说，“我怎么进的监狱？”<BR>
<BR>
“我不知道你怎么到的任何地方。”<BR>
<BR>
“是的，但你不是一直和我还有那个布衣精灵在一起吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“那个什么？”<BR>
<BR>
“布衣。”<BR>
<BR>
“我想你是指那个商人。动物皮不是布 -- ”我同伴脸上掠过一丝沮丧，不知为何。“算了。不，我们进城后我就离开了，因为我还宿醉着又差点死了，所以我完全忘了。”<BR>
<BR>
“我明白了。”我说，“好吧，走吧。在他们找到别的借口抓我之前。”<BR>
<BR>
紧接着，一个守卫走过来逮捕了我。“站住，外乡人。你被捕了。”他说着逮捕了我。<BR>
<BR>
“又来了？”我说。一只条纹瓜尔从他身后走来，轻轻把我的手臂含在嘴里，约束我。<BR>
<BR>
“啊，所以你以前被捕过。现在我知道我抓你是正确的。”守卫说。<BR>
<BR>
“你是说你在没有任何犯罪证据的情况下逮捕了这个人。”雷明怀疑地说。<BR>
<BR>
“正是盐脑哈拉鲁的看法。有明确的犯罪证据，因为他是诺德人。”<BR>
<BR>
“我明白了，”雷明说，“但这值得吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“你真是你们贪婪家族的典型。履行职责怎么会有‘代价’？”守卫说。<BR>
<BR>
突然，我注意到这守卫带着一些非常奇怪的东西。各种形状奇特的小玩意用奇怪的带状物绑在他那低劣的非钢制盔甲上。作为一个受过教育的贵族，我对这怪异的好奇心超过了被捕的愤怒。<BR>
<BR>
“......你那些是什么？”我问他。<BR>
<BR>
他看着我，好像我往他母亲身上撒了尿。“那个，外乡人，是甲虫水袋。”<BR>
<BR>
“甲虫？”<BR>
<BR>
“盐甲虫。我们把躯干、喉咙和胃完整取出，用来收集预过滤的水。你可以把躯干里的毒物敲掉大部分，然后就可以喝了。”<BR>
<BR>
“你为什么想从虫子的胃里喝水？”<BR>
<BR>
“否则就是渴死。”他说，“还有更蠢的问题吗？”<BR>
<BR>
我顿了顿。“那些带子是干什么的？”<BR>
<BR>
“因为，外乡人，如果你遇上盐风暴，你最不希望的就是有毒的盐沾满皮肤和衣服里面。你必须把佐尔皮扣紧，防止盐钻进去。”他说，“我们现在能不谈了吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，等一下。你穿着某种高台靴，这样能把大部分氯隔开，对吧？”<BR>
<BR>
“是的。”<BR>
<BR>
“你的瓜尔为什么不穿鞋？”<BR>
<BR>
“瓜尔不穿鞋，外乡人。”<BR>
<BR>
“马穿鞋。”<BR>
<BR>
“我不知道马是什么，但只有外乡人才会蠢到给动物做鞋。”<BR>
<BR>
“啊，那你错了！你看，在老跑，我记得 -- ”我的话被打断了，守卫试图用钝器猛击我，让我昏过去。然而，那治疗药剂的效果奇迹般还在，我只觉得有点痒。“嗯，打断别人真没礼貌！我刚才说到 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
“我命令你闭嘴，外乡人。我认为这是攻击。”<BR>
<BR>
“啊，但我完全不认为那是攻击！我刚才说到，在老跑，你看，他们有那些螃蟹。他们住在螃蟹里，对吧？所以你看，某种意义上，地面是螃蟹的 -- ”守卫发出两声咔哒声，瓜尔松开了我的手臂。<BR>
<BR>
“这几分钟太痛苦了，这堪称任何情况下任何人可能发生的最糟糕的事。请帮个忙去死，但死在别处。”守卫然后从瓜尔背包里拿出一卷卷轴，朝我们施了个圣灵干涉，于是我们又在一道闪光中消失在晨风各地。<BR>
<BR><BR>
****<BR>
<BR>
编者注<BR>
由于支持和考虑源源不断，打喷嚏海象历史学会决定出版费拉纳·阿德雷西的《晨风愚行录》余下部分，出乎意料地得到了许多准作家的帮助。<BR>
<BR>
弗洛利亚·银血和她的编辑伙伴认为，我们汇编了关于敌对德亚西特的准确描述。虽然那里可能不对严肃学术工作开放，但从泪城或阿尔德·霍拉克向西、最终到冬堡的奇怪水手们，描绘了一幅我们认为足够好的德亚西特图景。<BR>
<BR>
现实中有那个守卫角色不足为奇，据说态度完全一样。呆子差点被指控的“罪行”是以外乡人身份进入阿尔德·霍拉克。阿尔德·霍拉克不仅仅是贸易港口，对谁能或不能进入有严格限制。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
A Dunce in Morrowind, v5<BR>
by Frolja Silver-Blood<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Once I awoke, being the well-educated future noble I am, I quickly deduced we were no longer in the Dejastyte, on account of my no longer feeling as though my organs wanted to escape through my mouth. Even more surprisingly, I found, I was not in jail.<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, you're awake," the dark elf man in front of me said. It seemed I was in some kind of one of those fancy mansion houses that I had heard so much about.<BR>
<BR>
"Ah. This must be one of those fancy mansion houses I have heard so much about," I said.<BR>
<BR>
"This is Savos manor, yes," the man said. "I am Ovar Savos, of Savos Manor."<BR>
<BR>
"Ah!" I said. "Well you see, that's strange, because last I recall, I was I recall I was last in the Deshaan Plains."<BR>
<BR>
"Yes."<BR>
<BR>
"And then, you see, one of those Dres cast a spell of Divine Intervention on me."<BR>
<BR>
"Yes. When you and your companion ended up at Fort Lutemoth, the Imperial captain was so offended by the smell of the Plains all over you that he knocked the two of you out. Then he stacked both of you on the guar of one of the travelling traders and paid him 1000 Imperial coins drakes to travel in any direction until nobody at Fort Lutemoth could smell it anymore. He was so serious about this that he set up a system of war-signal fireworks at the fort so that the trader would be able to see whether or not they could still smell the two of you regardless of how far away you went."<BR>
<BR>
"Cunning man, that captain. Don't you agree?"<BR>
<BR>
"Unfortunately, yes."<BR>
<BR>
"But where are my manners? Well met, Ovar!" I stood to shake hands with the elf, but the elf stood back.<BR>
<BR>
"I'm afraid that if I touch your hand, my skin might melt off."<BR>
<BR>
"Huh? What are you - oh, silly me!" I shook my hand, watching huge clumps of Deshaan salt fly off and stain the floor.<BR>
<BR>
"No, don't do that either. Just don't do things."<BR>
<BR>
"You Chimer are a sensitive bunch after all, eh?" I said.<BR>
<BR>
"Us Chimer?"<BR>
<BR>
I was about to launch into an informative explanation, but I was interrupted by Remyn, who was yelling and sprinting into the room, as if dashing in to dive in front of Ovar and take an arrow for him.<BR>
<BR>
"I am begging you, sera, please do not ask him to explain anything," Remyn said.<BR>
<BR>
Ovar stood back from Remyn as well. "Oh, you... you also haven't had the salt cleaned off of you."<BR>
<BR>
"I apologize, sera."<BR>
<BR>
"No, no, it's quite alright. If anything, it's a blessing."<BR>
<BR>
I can't really say why Remyn looked so disappointed when Ovar said that. "A blessing?" Remyn questioned, his shoulders sagging.<BR>
<BR>
Ovar's look of disgust changed to the calm you see on priests' faces so often. "Oh, yes, absolutely. After all, this is a vital opportunity for me, as a young retainer of the Great House Indoril. By performing an act of charity by washing and healing you of the salt, my sponsors will look favorably on me for advancement."<BR>
<BR>
"...ah," said Remyn.<BR>
<BR>
"Well, turns out this place does know how to show a bit of generosity after all!" I said.<BR>
<BR>
Ovar reluctantly accepted my compliment. "A noble of House Indoril is the most charitable and merciful mer you might ever meet, but they are also the most iron-willed and the strongest of spirit."<BR>
<BR>
"Ah, I was meaning to ask," Remyn said. "You see, last I remember, we were in Fort Lutemoth."<BR>
<BR>
"Yes, you were expelled for smelling bad," Ovar said.<BR>
<BR>
"That is regrettable. Where are we now?"<BR>
<BR>
"We're in Savos Manor!" I said proudly.<BR>
<BR>
"You're in Savos Manor, yes," Ovar said.<BR>
<BR>
"Yes, but where is Savos Manor?"<BR>
<BR>
I was confused. "I'm afraid I don't understand, Remyn! It's Savos Manor!"<BR>
<BR>
For perhaps three seconds, Remyn's facial expressions seemed to stop working. He then said, very very carefully, "And what city is Savos Manor closest to?"<BR>
<BR>
"Well, it's in Akamora, of course," Ovar said.<BR>
<BR>
Remyn seemed as though the revelation had frozen him in time.<BR>
<BR>
"That's how bad the smell was," Ovar said, "but, I am a noble of House Indoril. So I will brave the toxic smells of the salt in order to cleanse you of your many filths and diseases."<BR>
<BR>
"We didn't contract any diseases," Remyn said.<BR>
<BR>
"Did you talk to any of the Dres?"<BR>
<BR>
"Yes."<BR>
<BR>
"Then your mind is diseased, for that memory must torment the both of you."<BR>
<BR>
"We thank you for your generosity, sera, but I'm afraid we must be going. We have a lot of other terrible situations to find ourselves in before the day is out, I'm sure."<BR>
<BR>
"I'll pay you," Ovar said.<BR>
<BR>
"Pardon me?" Remyn said.<BR>
<BR>
"I'll pay you to accept my charity," Ovar said.<BR>
<BR>
"We don't need the charity. We will be fine, somehow."<BR>
<BR>
"You don't understand. Every time I ask whether or not I'm ready to advance in the Great House, I'm always told, 'Ovar, you must learn the virtue of Charity'. But I can't find anyone to be charitable or merciful too. I could give charity to my sister, but she stood on my foot five months ago, and she's only apologized three times. I could give charity to the Kwama miners, but apparently my idea of hiring adventurers to draw erotic images on the Kwama Workers for them to enjoy while in the mines was too 'unconventional' and 'absolutely insane' to hear my elders tell it. But this is a textbook case of where Charity and Mercy are needed."<BR>
<BR>
"We will be leaving now," Remyn said. He gestured to me to follow him, and so I did, and we had a very nice, long journey to the front door, upon which we were unable to leave on account of hearing Ovar loading a crossbow and pointing it at us.<BR>
<BR>
"I said... you need to accept my charity," Ovar said.<BR>
<BR>
"Well, actually, you didn't," I turned around. Remyn seemed to accept impending death.<BR>
<BR>
"I'm sorry?"<BR>
<BR>
"Well, you didn't say we need to accept your charity. I mean, you said that you'd pay us to accept it, and you also said you were going to give it, but you never actually used the words 'you need to accept my charity', you know!" I said, doing a very good impression of Ovar. Ovar was clearly impressed with it, judging by the look of confusion he had on his face.<BR>
<BR>
"Do you understand the position you're in, Nord?"<BR>
<BR>
"Yes, I'm standing up."<BR>
<BR>
"No, I mean the-the position you're in!"<BR>
<BR>
"...Oh! That's right. I know what you're talking about."<BR>
<BR>
"You do?" Ovar said.<BR>
<BR>
"That's right! I'm in Savos Manor!"<BR>
<BR>
Ovar Savos stared at me as if I had suddenly become a pile of sweetcakes. "Do you..." he strained out, "...understand... that I am pointing... a crossbow.. at you?"<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, of course I understand that!" I said, "But that's the position you're in, now, isn't it lad?"<BR>
<BR>
"But the position you're in is the position of having a crossbow pointed at you!" Ovar was practically screaming now.<BR>
<BR>
"Well, I'll be! That's true, isn't it? I guess you're right!" And so I stood out of the way. "There. I'm no longer in that position!" Ovar stared at me, eyes as wide as a child's on meeting a god. After enjoying a good laugh, I stepped over to him and slapped him several times on the back in good humour, which he seemed to enjoy because he didn't even try to stop me getting salt all over him.<BR>
<BR>
"You know, you're very good at this whole 'riddles' business, Ovar!" I said. "That kind of thing would stump the fellows back in Winterhold!"<BR>
<BR>
"...it would?" Ovar said. In his daze of gratitude, he just stared at the spot where I had been standing, stunned.<BR>
<BR>
"Yes, of course! After all, the riddle was the fact that, when you pointed the crossbow somewhere, you invented a place called 'where the crossbow is pointing at,' right?"<BR>
<BR>
"...I did?"<BR>
<BR>
"And just like that, suddenly, the position I was in wasn't just Savos Manor, it was also 'where the crossbow is pointing'!" I continued to slap Ovar's back. That elf didn't have a lot of meat between his skin and his spine, so it was starting to hurt my hand a little, but I knew he'd be disappointed if I stopped. "You know, you're quite skilled with riddles!"<BR>
<BR>
"...I am?"<BR>
<BR>
"Yes! You ought to go share this talent with everybody! You never know when you could surprise someone with how much they enjoy it the way I did!" I said. "Just do them to people all the time, no matter what! That can be your charity!"<BR>
<BR>
"...I see," Ovar said. "Yes. I think you're right. I never thought of it that way. With my talent, I can-" Out of appreciation for my slapping him on the back still, Ovar passed out.<BR>
<BR>
Remyn stared at me. I simply gave him a friendly smile, and opened the door for him. "Sure you don't want some slaps on the back as well?" I said.<BR>
<BR>
"I'll let you know if so," Remyn said, and he gave a last look at Ovar, and then, with that, we headed out to Akamora, and promptly stepped into the waterfall outside of his Ovar's door and fell into the river.<BR>
<BR><BR>
****<BR>
<BR>
Publisher's Note<BR>
<BR>
Ovar Savos was of course adopted from the "Sandos and Convulates" skits, ever a favorite in the taverns of eastern Skyrim.<BR>
<BR>
While every bard has their own version of the tale, this one was taken from the classics, as befitting the Sneezing Horker Historical Society. While the lazy almoner Convulates found no place in the Dunce, the overeager Ovar Sandos seemed like he had been waiting just for us.<BR>
<BR>
Fort Lutemoth, located just south of the Orethan river, made a natural location for the Dunce to end up in. Actual Divine Intervention in Ald Horak would have the caster end up in a Hlaalu settlement, much to the derailment of the plot.<BR>

<BR>
编者注<BR>
<BR>
奥瓦尔·萨沃斯当然是从《桑多斯和康沃鲁特》短剧中借用的，那是东天际酒馆里一直很受欢迎的作品。<BR>
<BR>
虽然每个吟游诗人都有自己的版本，但这一版取自经典，适合打喷嚏海象历史学会。懒惰的施赈者康沃鲁特在《愚行录》中没有位置，但过于热心的奥瓦尔·桑多斯似乎在等着我们。<BR>
<BR>
卢特莫斯堡位于奥雷森河以南，是《愚行录》故事发生地的自然选择。如果在阿尔德·霍拉克使用圣灵干涉，施法者最终会到哈拉鲁定居点，那会严重偏离剧情。<BR>

As had become tradition, when I woke up, I was no longer wherever I was before. Instead, I was in a rather comfy bed, inside a strange building. Really, it was almost as if I were inside some kind of mushroom. Meanwhile, my companion Remyn lay upon the floor, asleep. But he was awoke by the rattling of cutlery on a tray, whence we both saw an elf dressed in some quite fancy clothes rising to our floor, followed behind by a meek-seeming lizard man, carrying some elf-food on a tray.<BR>
<BR>
"Ah, you're finally awake! Splendid, splendid. Please, take a seat." The elf said. Remyn didn't even question the situation, and just took a seat at the table at the end of the room. I however, wasn't one to act ill-mannered.<BR>
<BR>
"Well met, stranger!" I said, thrusting my hand forth.<BR>
<BR>
"I agree! We are well met!" The elf said, and surprisingly, he gripped my hand strongly, and shook it properly the way a Nord might. I, eager and impressed by this, increased the vigour of my shaking, and he obliged, and we both stood their shaking hands for about 8 minutes before our arms got tired.<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
"That's just as well, because I've forgotten what it was." The elf said.<BR>
<BR>
"It's Tholas." The lizard said.<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
"Hello." Remyn said.<BR>
<BR>
"Yes, hello. So, you're a real Nord? From the actual Skyrim?"<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
"Ah, so your father was one of those...?" Tholas said, still guffawing.<BR>
<BR>

Remyn, on the other hand, was barely even trying, just giving some nervous chuckles.<BR>
<BR>
"If I may interrupt-"<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
Tholas gasped. "Eldersblood peak? My word! How treacherous!"<BR>
<BR>
"Aye, it would've been if I could've found the damn place!" I said, and again I slapped my knee at the supreme comedic value of my joke, and Tholas did the same. After a moment, he shot a look at the lizard, who likewise mirrored our mirth, having done better at it this time than the last.<BR>
<BR>

"Fried Kwama cuttle, spiced racer breast, and a little taste of home for you -- genuine, imported, Skyrim Bear Rump, spiced with the most superior flavourings and herbs one may find in all of Morrowind -- pure, unrefined, silt strider urine."<BR>
<BR>
"Pure what?" Remyn said.<BR>
<BR>
"Well, I'll be! You elves sure have some strange habits, but far be it from me to be close minded!" I said, eagerly cutting into the slab of bear met in front of me. Remyn watched on blankly. "Say, I have a question." I said before I put the meat in my mouth.<BR>

"How wonderful to have but one question! You must be so wise."<BR>

"Well, thank you for noticing! And that question is -- why the generosity?"<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, an excellent question sera. You should be proud of it."<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
"Bah! You really believe Akavir exists?" I said, slapping my thigh. "You know 2920 was fictional, right?<BR>
<BR>

"Oh, and quite right too! Silly me for my forgetfulness. You know, I am quite the expert on the home of the Nords." Tholas said.<BR>
<BR>
"Oh? Well, I didn't know there were any elves -- or, 'mer', if you prefer -  who took us seriously!"<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, us Dunmer usually interest ourselves in the affairs of Morrowind. But I take such a strong interest in the Nords -- your customs, your lands, your beliefs. Your lore, if you will. Skyrim lore. I'm an expert -- a fan, perhaps. For example, you Nords are quite the warriors aren't you?"<BR>
<BR>
"Yes, we always say, 'the combat is better in Skyrim'!"<BR>
<BR>
"And that's why I'm such a Skyrim fan!"<BR>
<BR>
"Pardon me." Remyn said. "When you said 'your people', you didn't mean the Nords?"<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, but I wish I did. Imagine if a Nord had done it, then perhaps you'd finally get the respect you deserve! You know, I have such an affiliation for the Nordic way, I've even taken to worshipping the Nord religion."<BR>
<BR>
"Oh? An elf offering prayers to Kyne?"<BR>
<BR>
"Er... you mean Kynareth, right? That reminds me, I have another important academic question, that's hotly debated among my peers. Which of the Nine Divines is most attractive, sexually?"<BR>
<BR>
But before I could give the correct answer, Remyn interrupted a thriced time. "Sera. Perhaps you could clarify what you meant by 'your people', if it wouldn't be too much trouble."<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, it wouldn't! I mean the Tong, of course."<BR>
<BR>
"...The Morag Tong."<BR>
<BR>
"Most precisely! And a wonderful job you did in Ald'Ruhn too, just let me say that again," Tholas said, "that reminds me. Why didn't you just use your writ of execution on the guards, and show them your legal authority?"<BR>
<BR>
"Ho ho, that's easy. I didn't have such a thing," I said.<BR>
<BR>
"H-He means that it got lost," Remyn said.<BR>
<BR>
"Eh? I do?" But Remyn's face betrayed fear, and I wondered, fear of what? So, I decided to ask my educated friend.<BR>
<BR>
"Say, Tholas. What is the Morag Tong?"<BR>
<BR>
"Another wise question."<BR>
<BR>
"Well thank you! Thought of it myself, you know."<BR>
<BR>
"Yes, it's a very handsome one. But, I shouldn't keep you any longer, should I?"<BR>
<BR>
"Yes, that's right. Your hospitality has been most welcome, but we must be leaving," Remyn said, standing up. And he grasped my arm and pulled me up as well, and I did pick up the sense that it was over something important.<BR>
<BR>
"But hang on!" I said, "I haven't even gotten to eat!"<BR>
<BR>
"But what about your cousin's wedding?"<BR>
<BR>
"My what? Oh, yes, right!" I said. "Well, thank you for a wonderful time, Tholas! Who knew some of you wizards actually had a brain on you?"<BR>
<BR>
"Akatosh's blessing to you!" Tholas said. "Have a wonderful journey!" And me and Remyn left, and had a wonderful journey to the docks of Port Telvannis. Remyn said not a word on our journey, and he gave me the gesture to do the same.<BR>
<BR>
"I am afraid, sera, that now our lives may be in danger." He said.<BR>
<BR>
"So, nothing new then, eh?"<BR>
<BR>
"...Yes, unfortunately. I'll explain later." And with that, we gave money to the docklady, and set passage for the mainland once more.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
晨风愚行录，卷六<BR>
弗洛利亚·银血 著<BR><BR>
