正如已成为惯例，当我醒来时，我不再在原来的地方。相反，我在一个奇怪的建筑里，一张相当舒适的床上。真的，几乎就像我在某种蘑菇里面。与此同时，我的同伴雷明躺在地板上睡着了。但托盘上餐具的碰撞声吵醒了他，这时我们看到一个穿着相当华丽衣服的精灵来到我们这层，身后跟着一个看起来温顺的蜥蜴人，端着一盘精灵食物。<BR>
<BR>
“啊，你终于醒了！太好了，太好了。请坐。”精灵说。雷明甚至没问情况，就在房间尽头的桌旁坐下。然而我不是那种失礼的人。<BR>
<BR>
“幸会，陌生人！”我说着伸出手。<BR>
<BR>
“我同意！我们幸会！”精灵说，出乎意料的是，他用力握住我的手，像诺德人那样有力地握手。我对此很热情和印象深刻，增加了握手力度，他也配合，我们站着握手大约8分钟，直到手臂累了。<BR>
<BR>
“你知道吗，我从没见过握手这么有力的精灵！”我说着在雷明旁边坐下。他也和我一样惊讶于遇到握手如此强劲热情的精灵。“实际上，我忘了问你名字！”<BR>
<BR>
“那正好，因为我也忘了。”精灵说。<BR>
<BR>
“是索拉斯。”蜥蜴人说。<BR>
<BR>
“我叫索拉斯，”索拉斯说，“很高兴、很荣幸、很激动见到你，北方人。可以说是荣耀。甚至......是一种特权。”<BR>
<BR>
“你好。”雷明说。<BR>
<BR>
“是的，你好。所以，你是真正的诺德人？来自真正的天际？”<BR>
<BR>
“和泰姆瑞尔一样真实，精灵！出生在海尔根，在雪鹰长大，哈哈！”我拍着膝盖，因为我刚说的话太搞笑了。索拉斯同意，也拍了拍膝盖，我于是又拍了一次。这样持续了十五分钟。<BR>
<BR>
“啊，所以你父亲是那种......”索拉斯说，还在大笑。<BR>
<BR>
“是的，他绝对是！他绝对是！”我说，同样大笑。索拉斯瞥了蜥蜴人一眼，蜥蜴人也开始大笑，或者至少尝试大笑，但做得不太好。雷明则几乎没在笑，只是紧张地轻笑。<BR>
<BR>
“请允许我打断一下 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
“好问题。阁下，你的同伴可以打断吗？”索拉斯问我。<BR>
<BR>
我想了想，雷明则茫然恐惧地盯着索拉斯。“是的！我觉得他可以。”<BR>
<BR>
“太好了！请打断。”索拉斯说。<BR>
<BR>
“如果我可以打断，我想我有脑震荡。”<BR>
<BR>
“好的，没问题。总之，你去过雪鹰峰吗？亲眼看过那件不光彩的事吗？”索拉斯说。<BR>
<BR>
“哦，雪鹰峰没那么特别。谁都能爬他父母爬过的山！你看，我曾经试过爬长老血峰。”<BR>
<BR>
索拉斯倒吸一口凉气。“长老血峰？天哪！多么险峻！”<BR>
<BR>
“是啊，如果我找到那该死的地方的话！”我说，再次拍着膝盖，因为我的笑话太有喜剧效果了，索拉斯也照做。片刻后，他瞥了蜥蜴人一眼，蜥蜴人也模仿我们的欢快，这次比上次做得好了些。<BR>
<BR>
“来，我让我的阿尔贡人给你们准备了上好的菜肴。熏灰烬山药......”蜥蜴人再次端着托盘，把一碗碗食物放在我面前。“炸夸玛墨鱼，香煎快跑鸟胸肉，还有给你们的一点点家乡风味 -- 正宗进口天际熊臀肉，用晨风所能找到的最上等香料和香草调味 -- 纯天然、未精炼的阔步沙蚤尿液。”<BR>
<BR>
“纯什么？”雷明说。<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，真没想到！你们精灵确实有些奇怪的习惯，但我不会思想封闭！”我说着迫不及待地切开面前的熊肉。雷明茫然地看着。“嘿，我有个问题。”我说着把肉放进嘴里。<BR>
<BR>
“只有一个问题，多么美妙！你一定很聪明。”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，谢谢你注意到！问题是 -- 为什么这么慷慨？”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，极好的问题，阁下。你应该为此自豪。”<BR>
<BR>
“你不觉得吗？”我说，“我们受过教育的人理应如此，不是吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“当然！就像在雪鹰上一样！”然后索拉斯发出了他最好的大笑，我必须说我跟着做了，拍着膝盖，因为他的喜剧多么滑稽和精彩。<BR>
<BR>
“但为什么慷慨？”雷明在我们拍膝盖达到真正高潮前说，“他说得有道理。”<BR>
<BR>
“是的，他绝对有道理。我赞赏他。”<BR>
<BR>
“也许，阁下，你可以回答他的问题。”雷明说。<BR>
<BR>
“哦！我还没想到呢！”索拉斯说，“我想......我确实处在可以这样做的位置，对吧？好吧，我尽力。”<BR>
<BR>
索拉斯想了想。“啊！我想到了！对了，我想起来了。我是索拉斯，泰瓦尼大族的督学。我慷慨的原因，我想到了，是感激！”<BR>
<BR>
“你也能想到你感激的原因吗？”雷明说。<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，我已经想到了这么多。剩下的应该不难。”索拉斯说。<BR>
<BR>
“请说吧。”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯？哦，好吧。”索拉斯又想了想。“啊！是的，就是这样。”他打了个响指，蜥蜴人下楼了。<BR>
<BR>
“你可能还记得......”索拉斯说，“几天前，你因谋杀在奥德汝因被捕。”<BR>
<BR>
“啊哈！那不愉快的事。”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，但这种事有时是必要的，不是吗？你看，碍事的沃拉萨·奥德拉不在了，我在家族议会的主要竞争对手失去了唯一维持他事务的职员，我在大族中的权力主张将更进一层！”蜥蜴人回到楼上，拿着一把非常熟悉的武器。<BR>
<BR>
“尼普提克勒！”<BR>
<BR>
“尼普提克勒？”雷明说。<BR>
<BR>
“尼普提克勒？好名字。”索拉斯说。蜥蜴人把它递给我。“我用一个相当狡猾的计划从勒多兰那里拿回了它。你想听听吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“当然！”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“太好了！我也想听。”<BR>
<BR>
我们沉默了一会儿。<BR>
<BR>
“请你告诉我们好吗？”雷明终于说。<BR>
<BR>
“哦，我不知道我怎么做到的。”<BR>
<BR>
“好吧。”<BR>
<BR>
“最好的计划就是没有计划，对吧索拉斯？”我说。我的手悬在膝盖上方，因期待而颤抖。<BR>
<BR>
“啊，你智慧的深度。但这在受过教育的人中是可以预料的。奥德汝因的守卫告诉我你是冬堡学院受过教育的未来贵族，对吧？我一直很钦佩那所学院！”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，当然！没有我那个地方会散架！可能已经散架了！你是那种巫师精灵，对吧？”<BR>
<BR>
“确实，我是奥秘、神秘艺术的大师，无论是物理还是形而上。我很想听听一位受过教育的同行的观点 -- 尤其是来自如此不同教育传统的。这里的一切都那么封闭和压抑。我们泰瓦尼家族都以为自己最懂，但我知道谁最懂，因为我知道谁才是真正最懂的人。”<BR>
<BR>
“是吗？那会是谁？”<BR>
<BR>
“诺德人。”索拉斯说。雷明的脸上露出奇怪的表情，好像他的灵魂决定去度假了。<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，这完全正确！”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“告诉我，阁下，你愿意让我高兴一下，分享你对一些学术观点的看法吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“那是我真正的荣幸，精灵！哈！尽管说！”<BR>
<BR>
“告诉我，你是否认为崔尼马克在某种形式上仍然存在？他没有完全变成马拉卡斯，而是持续的神话信仰维持了他在光界中的一个侧面，或者说碎片？”<BR>
<BR>
“啊，那都是巫师的说法，”我说，“大家都知道他其实叫欧凯！”<BR>
<BR>
“那东方的土地阿卡维尔呢？据说虎龙托什·拉卡以一种奇怪的永恒与时间并存的方式存在，好像两者随他的声音以未曾想象的方式消长。事实上，他们说整个阿卡维尔在时间上领先于我们。”<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
“......这是近200年来我听到的第一个关于阿卡维尔的原创观点！了不起！”索拉斯说，“但那你如何解释赛埃锡摄政王维西丢-谢伊？”<BR>

<BR>
“嗯，很简单！他们消失了！”<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
“......你们的人？”雷明说。<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，我很确定不是诺德人杀了那个摄政王，否则我们会没完没了地自夸！”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“哦，太对了！我真是健忘。你知道吗，我是诺德家园的专家。”索拉斯说。<BR>
<BR>
“哦？嗯，我不知道有精灵 -- 或者‘精灵’，如果你喜欢的话 -- 会认真对待我们！”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，我们丹莫通常只关心晨风的事务。但我对诺德人非常感兴趣 -- 你们的习俗、土地、信仰。你们的知识，如果你愿意这么叫。天际知识。我是专家 -- 也许是个粉丝。例如，你们诺德人是相当出色的战士，对吧？”<BR>
<BR>
“是的，我们总说，‘天际的战斗更棒’！”<BR>
<BR>
“这就是为什么我是天际的粉丝！”<BR>
<BR>
“请原谅，”雷明说，“你说‘你们的人’，不是指诺德人？”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，我真希望是。想象一下如果是诺德人做的，那也许你们最终会得到应得的尊重！你知道吗，我对诺德方式有如此深的认同，我甚至开始信仰诺德宗教了。”<BR>
<BR>
“哦？一个精灵向吉讷祈祷？”<BR>
<BR>
“呃......你是说吉娜瑞斯，对吧？这提醒了我，我还有一个重要的学术问题，在我的同行中争论激烈。九圣灵中哪一个在性方面最具吸引力？”<BR>
<BR>
但在我给出正确答案之前，雷明第三次打断了。“阁下。如果不麻烦的话，也许你可以澄清一下‘你们的人’是什么意思。”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，不麻烦！我当然是指‘堂’。”<BR>
<BR>
“......莫拉格·堂。”<BR>
<BR>
“非常精确！你们在奥德汝因也干得很出色，让我再说一遍，”索拉斯说，“这提醒了我。你们为什么不直接对守卫出示你的执行令，向他们展示你的法律权威？”<BR>
<BR>
“嗬嗬，很简单。我没有那种东西。”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“他 -- 他的意思是它丢了。”雷明说。<BR>
<BR>
“嗯？我有吗？”但雷明的脸上露出恐惧，我想，怕什么？于是我决定问我受过教育的朋友。<BR>
<BR>
“嘿，索拉斯。莫拉格·堂是什么？”<BR>
<BR>
“又一个明智的问题。”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，谢谢你！我自己想到的，你知道。”<BR>
<BR>
“是的，它很棒。但，我不应该再留你们了，对吧？”<BR>
<BR>
“是的，没错。你的款待非常受欢迎，但我们得走了。”雷明站起来说。他抓住我的胳膊也把我拉起来，我确实感到有什么重要的事。<BR>
<BR>
“但等等！”我说，“我还没吃呢！”<BR>
<BR>
“但你表亲的婚礼呢？”<BR>
<BR>
“我的什么？哦，是的，对了！”我说，“嗯，谢谢你让我度过了一段美好时光，索拉斯！谁知道你们这些巫师中有些人还真有脑子？”<BR>
<BR>
“阿卡托什祝福你们！”索拉斯说，“旅途愉快！”我和雷明离开了，愉快地前往泰瓦尼港码头。雷明在旅途中一言不发，他示意我也别说话。<BR>
<BR>
“恐怕，阁下，现在我们的生命可能有危险。”他说。<BR>
<BR>
“所以，没什么新鲜事，嗯？”<BR>
<BR>
“......是的，不幸的是。我以后再解释。”然后我们付钱给码头女管事，再次订了去大陆的票。<BR>

虽然这段具体内容从未成为短剧的一部分，但它是为后续情节所必需的文学铺垫。<BR>

已故的费拉纳·阿德雷西在将《愚行录》从冬堡酒馆转移到书中时，确保将其与她成长过程中熟悉的文学经典联系起来。熟悉某些故事的读者会知道接下来会发生什么。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
A Dunce in Morrowind, v7<BR>
by Frolja Silver-Blood<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Now, we were sailing back to the mainland from Port Telvannis, across the boring waters of Morrowind, but the journey was quite long and also boring, and so we both decided to pass out on the deck as a result of all the concussions and alcohol poisoning we'd had over the past few days. When we both came to, we were inside the passengers cabin, with empty sacks thrown over us, and night had fallen.<BR>
<BR>
Remyn stumbled to his feet off the crates of Strider urine, however, I, as a strong and powerful warrior, valiantly fell face first onto the floor to demonstrate my resilience to pain.<BR>
<BR>
"Are you alright?" Remyn said.<BR>
<BR>
"Ha! Never better!" I said as I fell over while trying to come to my feet again.<BR>
<BR>
"No, I was talking to him." Remyn pointed to a mirror on the wall, which was quite silly -- it's a mirror, not a window! -- but I decided I would let his foolishness pass this time. Then he looked at me. "Actually, you... look fine." And he looked behind me to the crates I'd been dumped on. "Oh, I see."<BR>
<BR>
I looked too -- it said "Bug musk". Now, being a well educated man, I had no idea what on earth that was. "Hah! What on earth is bug musk anyway?"<BR>
<BR>
"It's an aphrodisiac."<BR>
<BR>
"Well, that explains the pain downstairs then!"<BR>
<BR>
"Let us not discuss that."<BR>
<BR>
"Say, elf, this has been quite a long trip. Weren't we meant to reach Bal Oyra before sundown?"<BR>
<BR>
"...That's what we were told." Remyn said. "Well, not quite, I think the captain said 'quicker than a Caldera tavern crawl', But that's not possible, not in these conditions. The wind blowing from the south is very weak. Actually... I don't think we're moving at all." And then my companion looked at his hand and froze. I came over to look at his hand as well.<BR>
<BR>
"It is a very nice hand after all." I said.<BR>
<BR>
"Yes." Remyn said. "But more to the point, I'm wearing that enchanted ring that the Archmage bribed me with. It's supposed to glow in the presence of danger."<BR>
<BR>
"Well, it must be broken then." I said confidently. "After all, there's no danger right now!"<BR>
<BR>
"I think the fact that it's glowing says there is, in fact, danger."<BR>
<BR>
"Ha! Being in danger at sea?" I said.<BR>
<BR>
"You're aware that you nearly drowned at Fort Frostmoth because your boat was attacked by dreugh, right?"<BR>
<BR>
"Just like on the Snowhaw--"<BR>
<BR>
"Be quiet!" Remyn hissed. And he cautiously grabbed a chitin dagger from the ground. And so I carefully grabbed Niptickler, and we both exited the cabin onto the main deck. It was as lively as an elf party, meaning that it was totally deserted. There was no wind, only storm clouds above, and also the rest of the crew were floating dead in the water around us. The sails had been burned and frozen as if by magic.<BR>
<BR>
And then we both saw it. A shimmering figure in the distance, who became stark and clear, their silhouette lit by a pale green aura, the calling card of illusion magic. The figure was dressed in darkness itself, and cast upon us both a spell of paralysis. Then the figure, with inhuman speed, threw us to the walls, and bound us against the rails of the boats, so that when his spell of paralysis wore off, we were still both quite helpless. As our vision adjusted to the dark, a new wind started blowing. Our assailant walked slowly towards us, bending down to meet our eye level, and here it became clear, this was a lizard man.<BR>
<BR>
"How have you been enjoying the trip?" He said quietly.<BR>
<BR>
"No," I said. <BR>
<BR>
"Don't talk back!" Remyn hissed to me, but the lizard man gently put a finger on his mouth, and held it. And held it. And held it.<BR>
<BR>
"No," the lizard man said, "you will talk back. Both of you."<BR>
<BR>
"But you're telling him to be quiet!"<BR>
<BR>
"...You're right," the lizard man said, releasing the finger. "Forgive me for my caution, elf. But I'm wary of the trickery of your kind. Those of the house Hlaalu are so talented with the details of words that you can make the truth as dark as any lie."<BR>
<BR>
"I assure you, sera, I won't say anything that would endanger my life." Remyn said.<BR>
<BR>
"That is already a lie. But it's always so gratifying to hear your kind call me 'sera'." The assailant stood upright now, and took a few steps back. "I must admit... there's a certain poetic justice in this too. Do you like the ropes I bound you with? I got it from the slave market in Port Telvannis. They drain the Magicka and stamina of any who wear them. They were made for my marsh brothers and marsh sisters. Now they bind the master."<BR>
<BR>
"I am of House Hlaalu, sera... I do not keep slaves," Remyn said.<BR>
<BR>
"How noble of you. But you are not the interesting one here." And the lizard man squatted down again, and faced me. "Quite the cover story you have."<BR>
<BR>
"Eh?" I said.<BR>
<BR>
"An educated future noble of the College of Winterhold. One who feigns intelligence, who speaks as a scholar but betrays himself to be a fool at every stage. I admire it. It disarms people, and it causes them to underestimate you. They overlook the guileless, you see. Normally, I think... the right way is to blend in, and to be uninteresting. But perhaps being famous for your idiocy works just as well."<BR>
<BR>
"My boy, you just described the others at the College perfectly!" I said, laughing. "Why, they wouldn't be able to--"<BR>
<BR>
"Enough. Dispense with the act."<BR>
<BR>
"The act?" I said. <BR>
<BR>
"I am not describing the others at your College. It's yourself. Show me the real you."<BR>
<BR>
"Well now, let's wait a moment! You think I'm a fool?" I said.<BR>
<BR>
The lizard grinned, like a predator. "No. I don't. I know the real you... and you are no fool."<BR>
<BR>
We both stared in silence for a moment.<BR>
<BR>
"Sera, I assure you, this is the real him. It is not an act." Remyn said.<BR>
<BR>
"That's because you're the true fool, elf." The lizard said. "Your stereotypes about the men of the north blind you to the true nature of the man of the..." He paused. "...the, right here. But I saw through him. The truth is, I suspected him from the start. I have been paying very close attention. Much closer attention than you realize. When you escaped from Ald'Ruhn, I thought I'd lost you, but it was just my luck that you washed up where you did."<BR>
<BR>
The lizard stood up once more, brandishing his shortsword. "It was I, who fetched you out of the waters and brought you to Port Telvannis. Just like it was I who, using a few well placed Illusion spells, fooled you all in Ald'Ruhn into thinking it was still unsafe to leave the Fighters Guild building, when the blight storm was long over. When you both escaped me there, it was I who refused to give up the hunt, but... had no way of tracking you after your altercation in Caldera. And so, it was I who threatened every mage in Firewatch and Port Telvannis to shower me in magic to increase my fortune, and hone my luck. And now... here we are."<BR>
<BR>
"Ahhh, I understand what's going on now!" I said. The flames of realization flickered on in my mind, burning away the uncooked meat of ignorance into the steak of knowing what was going on.<BR>
<BR>
"You've always understood." The lizard said. "Now explain it to your ally."<BR>
<BR>
"It's quite simple." I turned my head to Remyn, and lowered my gaze and voice. I took this with the seriousness it needed. "He's threatening us, and means us harm."<BR>
<BR>
We were all silent.<BR>
<BR>
"...Yes. And?" The lizard gestured.<BR>
<BR>
"What do you mean 'and'?." <BR>
<BR>
And I saw anger rise in the lizard's face, but then it calmed. "...Interesting. I see how you've been able to use your false idiocy to disarm everyone up to now. It will not work with me of course, but I admire your technique."<BR>
<BR>
"I've figured it out." Remyn said. "It was what I was afraid of."<BR>
<BR>
"Tell me then, elf." The lizard man said.<BR>
<BR>
"You're with the Morag Tong. You believe we stole your kill, but I assure you, nothing of the sort happened. It's been a big misunderstanding. Neither of us would ever interfere with official Tong business."<BR>
<BR>
The lizard stared, then smiled. "Why would I join an elf organization to settle your foolish elf concerns? Your politics are your own, Hlaalu. Marsh children need not concern ourselves with them. The real Morag Tong assassin is right next to you."<BR>
<BR>
Well, there was no one next to me, actually. Except Remyn, but as an educated man, I knew that House Hlaalu was not the Morag Tong, because they have different names. These are the little things you learn with higher education!<BR>
<BR>
"As an agent of the Dark Brotherhood, it was my responsibility, this kill. That Telvanni councillor in Ald'Ruhn had already been contracted by another of those wizards. After all, even the Morag Tong tire of Telvanni politics. And now they're hiring truly insane bodyguards - why not let a writ or two slip through the cracks? And yet... Tholas somehow convinced your lot to take this one on, didn't he?" The lizard bent down, staring into my face. "The Telvanni pay their bodyguards to masquerade as guards, and deny writs, and imprison lawful assassins on fake charges, so they can be killed in secret later. Only a madman would cross the Tong like that. How unfortunate that all the Telvanni magisters are. And yet... the Tong took this one on, didn't they?"<BR>
<BR>
"Hah! That's exactly what an elf guild would do, isn't it?" I said.<BR>
<BR>
And he chuckled. "And oh yes, I was there, in Tholas' manor. You don't even recognize me, do you elf? I also suffered through the same insipid Skyrim references as you did. But don't feel too bad, Tholas didn't even recognize I wasn't his usual slave either. But the evidence was quite conclusive. It confirmed my suspicions. My subtle, marsh-trained eye sees the details in the shadows that your kind is blind to. This axe..." The lizard picked up Niptickler where I'd dropped it. He turned it over in his hand, admiring the enchanted sheen. "This is the hub of our little wheel. You both recognized it. There's no other explanation. You, Morag Tong, took a kill that belonged to the Brotherhood."<BR>
<BR>
"Sera... I understand how easy it is to think this. But we didn't even have this axe before now. This axe had been stolen from the Nord by a witch."<BR>
<BR>
"Hah! Wrong!" I said. Remyn seemed to accept death.<BR>
<BR>
"You surrender the charade?"<BR>
<BR>
"It's pronounced charaday, actually. But my axe was never stolen by a witch!"<BR>
<BR>
"Then the Hlaalu lies."<BR>
<BR>
"It was stolen when I stayed with a comely lass, who camped in a tent full of skulls and potions and studied magic, and was feared by the townsfolk."<BR>
<BR>
The lizard stared at me.<BR>
<BR>
Nobody spoke.<BR>
<BR>
"...What?"<BR>
<BR>
"That's right. She must have been robbed by someone entirely unrelated. Poor girl."<BR>
<BR>
The lizard looked at Remyn, as if for sympathy, but found none.<BR>
<BR>
"It was impossible for us to have committed this killing. The Nord was naked when I found him, and that axe was most certainly not with him. At the time of the assassination, both of us had passed out. When we escaped, he didn't head for a guild hall, he didn't have a writ of execution to present, and we accidentally ended up in the Dejasyte. Nobody would voluntarily go to the Dejasyte."<BR>
<BR>
"Except an elf!" I joked. The lizard man smiled like Hircine, but if Hircine was visiting his mother-in-law. Or something. I don't know. He gripped my axe tight, still admiring it.<BR>
<BR>
"I observed you entering Ald'Ruhn. You had a pack guar with you. Your companion was clothed. It would be trivial to hide the axe in the guar pack."<BR>
<BR>
"And then how did we get it inside, Sera? We rushed in when the blight storm started."<BR>
<BR>
"I am not the judge. I am the executioner."<BR>
<BR>
"But if you kill us, and your true target lives, your contract will be unfulfilled. Sera, please think. How did the axe get inside the Fighters Guild?"<BR>
<BR>
And here, the lizard did think for a moment. "I confess my curiosity. Well, Nord, how did Niptickler arrive in the Fighters Guild?"<BR>
<BR>
"That's a good question!" I said to the lizard, admiring the quality of his question.<BR>
<BR>
Silence.<BR>
<BR>
"Ah, you want an answer?"<BR>
<BR>
"...Yes."<BR>
<BR>
"Well, it's simple. Obviously, whoever stole Niptickler from that woman whose camp I stayed in took it to Old Run."<BR>
<BR>
"He was very naked when I found him, Sera. Very."<BR>
<BR>
And the lizard looked at my axe in frustration, gripping it as if he wanted it to shatter, his face trembling... and finally, calm overcame him. "You're of small imagination, elf."<BR>
<BR>
"Pardon?" <BR>
<BR>
"It's most simple. You found him naked. Eventually, he got dressed. Obviously at some point your eyes must have been averted, and he would've been able to smuggle the axe into your pack from a hidden location, perhaps behind a rock or something. When the time came to get to Ald'Ruhn, he must have smuggled it while you were distracted out of the pack, disguised it amongst the rest of the Fighters Guild weapons, and used it once everyone else was asleep. And that's just one of many ways."<BR>
<BR>
"He's got a good point." I said to Remyn, who tried his best, again, to pretend I did not exist. "Say, maybe I could ask you a question now?"<BR>
<BR>
"...You may ask." He said with great reluctance.<BR>
<BR>
"If you knew everyone was asleep, why didn't you take the kill yourself?" I said.<BR>
<BR>
"...To quote a certain future noble of Winterhold, 'that is a good question.'" The lizard was mirthless. "But you're not in any position to ask anything of me."<BR>
<BR>
"Why? Are we in Savos Manor?"<BR>
<BR>
The lizard buried his face into his hands, muffling his screams, then brandished Niptickler directly at me. "Enough! I will use the weapon you dishonored me with to destroy you as well. I remember what the Mages Guild said of this weapon... it paralyzes, poisons, and traps the soul of the one that it strikes, and its wielder's charisma is enhanced!"<BR>
<BR>
"Well, you can never listen to anyone from the bloody Mages Guild!" I scoffed. "You know the Imperial Mages Guild has nothing on the cleverfolk of the College of Winterhold. And after all, I, as an educated future noble of said College, can tell you they made a very simple, easy mistake!"<BR>
<BR>
"...And what mistake is that?"<BR>
<BR>
"It does everything you said. But it does all of it to the wielder."<BR>
<BR>
"...You're lying."<BR>
<BR>
"No I'm not. It just does it very slowly, that's all!"<BR>
<BR>
"But that's impossible! It would be stupid to have a weapon that harms the one who uses it! Nobody would do that, because it's so stupid! Why would anyone use a stupid weapon like that?!" <BR>
<BR>
Well to tell the truth to you, at this point, I just started laughing at the small mindedness of the assassin. After all, that was when he collapsed to the deck, paralyzed, and unable to let go of Niptickler - so really, it should be obvious why someone would use a weapon like that after all!<BR>
<BR><BR>

<BR>
Publisher's Note<BR>
<BR>
Owing to its origin as a series of tavern skits, the Dunce often references events related to the College of Winterhold, where the tale was written. Niptickler's enchantment has showed up in several tales and songs ever since the axe was first enchanted and tested in the spring months of 419. Its effects are exactly as written, to the great dismay of its creator, one of the great influences for the character of the "Dunce".<BR>
<BR>
A skit elaborating the difference between Morag Tong and Dark Brotherhood has been woven into this chapter. It originally involved a future murder victim and two assassins arguing about political boundaries. It has fallen out of favor recently, for unrelated reasons.<BR>

晨风愚行录，卷七<BR>
弗洛利亚·银血 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
现在，我们从泰瓦尼港出发，穿越晨风无聊的水域返回大陆，但旅程很长也很无聊，于是我们俩都因过去几天的脑震荡和酒精中毒在甲板上昏睡过去。当我们醒来时，我们在客舱里，身上盖着空麻袋，夜幕已降临。<BR>
<BR>
雷明从阔步沙蚤尿液的板条箱上踉跄站起来，而我，作为强壮有力的战士，英勇地脸朝下摔在地板上以展示我对疼痛的耐受力。<BR>
<BR>
“你没事吧？”雷明说。<BR>
<BR>
“哈！从没这么好过！”我说着试图再次站起来时又摔倒了。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
我也看了 -- 上面写着“虫麝香”。作为一个受过良好教育的人，我完全不知道那是什么。“哈！虫麝香到底是什么？”<BR>
<BR>
“是春药。”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，那解释了我下面的疼痛！”<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
“嗯，那它一定坏了。”我自信地说，“毕竟现在没有危险！”<BR>
<BR>
“我认为它在发光这一事实表明实际上有危险。”<BR>
<BR>
“哈！在海上遇到危险？”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“你知道你在霜蛾堡差点淹死是因为你的船被蟹灵袭击了，对吧？”<BR>
<BR>
“就像在雪鹰 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
“安静！”雷明嘶声道。他小心地从地上抓起一把甲壳匕首。我也小心地拿起尼普提克勒，我们俩走出舱室来到主甲板。那里像精灵派对一样热闹，也就是说完全空无一人。没有风，只有头顶的乌云，而且其他船员都漂浮在我们周围的水中死去。帆被烧焦和冻结，仿佛被魔法所致。<BR>
<BR>
然后我们都看到了。远处一个闪烁的身影，变得清晰分明，其轮廓被淡绿色光环照亮，那是幻术的标志。身影穿着如黑暗本身，对我们俩施了麻痹法术。然后身影以非人的速度把我们扔到墙上，绑在船栏杆上，这样当他的麻痹法术消退时，我们仍相当无助。当我们的视力适应黑暗时，一阵新风吹起。袭击者慢慢走向我们，弯下腰与我们对视，这时清楚了，这是一个蜥蜴人。<BR>
<BR>
“你们旅途愉快吗？”他轻声说。<BR>
<BR>
“不。”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“别顶嘴！”雷明对我嘶声道，但蜥蜴人轻轻把一根手指放在他嘴上，停住。停住。停住。<BR>
<BR>
“不，”蜥蜴人说，“你们会顶嘴的。你们俩。”<BR>
<BR>
“但你在让他安静！”<BR>
<BR>
“......你说得对，”蜥蜴人松开手指说，“原谅我的谨慎，精灵。但我提防你们族类的诡计。哈拉鲁家族的人在言辞细节上如此有天赋，能把真相变得和谎言一样黑暗。”<BR>
<BR>
“我向你保证，阁下，我不会说任何危及生命的话。”雷明说。<BR>
<BR>
“这已经是谎言了。但听到你们族类叫我‘阁下’总是令人欣慰。”袭击者站直了，后退几步。“我必须承认......这也算某种诗意的正义。你们喜欢我用来绑你们的绳子吗？我从泰瓦尼港的奴隶市场买的。它们会吸干佩戴者的魔能和体力。它们是为我的沼泽兄弟和沼泽姐妹制造的。现在它们束缚了主人。”<BR>
<BR>
“我是哈拉鲁家族的人，阁下......我不蓄奴。”雷明说。<BR>
<BR>
“多么高尚。但你不是这里有趣的人。”蜥蜴人再次蹲下，面对我。“你的掩护故事很不错。”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯？”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“冬堡学院受过教育的未来贵族。一个假装聪明的人，说话像学者，却在每个阶段暴露自己是傻瓜。我欣赏这点。它让人放松警惕，让人低估你。他们忽略那些没有心计的人，你看。通常，我认为......正确的方式是融入，不引人注目。但也许因愚蠢而闻名也同样有效。”<BR>
<BR>
“我的伙计，你刚才完美地描述了学院里的其他人！”我笑着说，“哎呀，他们连 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
“够了。别装了。”<BR>
<BR>
“装？”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“我不是在描述你们学院里的其他人。是你自己。让我看看真实的你。”<BR>
<BR>
“哎呀，等等！你觉得我是傻瓜？”我说。<BR>
<BR>
蜥蜴人笑了，像捕食者。“不。我不这么认为。我知道真实的你......你不是傻瓜。”<BR>
<BR>
我们都沉默地对视了一会儿。<BR>
<BR>
“阁下，我向你保证，这就是真正的他。不是装的。”雷明说。<BR>
<BR>
“那是因为你才是真正的傻瓜，精灵。”蜥蜴人说，“你对北方人的刻板印象让你看不到......站在这里这个人的真实本质。但我看穿了他。事实是，我从一开始就怀疑他。我一直非常密切关注。比你意识到的更密切。当你从奥德汝因逃走时，我以为失去你了，但你们正好被冲到了那个地方，这是我的运气。”<BR>
<BR>
蜥蜴人再次站起来，挥舞着短剑。“是我，把你们从水里捞出来，带到泰瓦尼港的。就像是我，用几个精心布置的幻术法术，在奥德汝因愚弄你们所有人，让你们以为枯萎病风暴还没结束，离开战士公会大楼还不安全，其实风暴早就过去了。当你们在我手里逃脱后，是我拒绝放弃追捕，但......在你们卡尔德拉争执后我无法跟踪你们。于是，是我威胁火望和泰瓦尼港的每个法师，让他们用魔法增加我的财富，磨炼我的运气。现在......我们在这里了。”<BR>
<BR>
“啊，我现在明白怎么回事了！”我说。理解的火焰在我脑海中闪烁，将无知的生肉烧成明白怎么回事的熟牛排。<BR>
<BR>
“你一直明白。”蜥蜴人说，“现在向你的盟友解释。”<BR>
<BR>
“很简单。”我转向雷明，压低目光和声音。我用必要的严肃对待这件事。“他在威胁我们，要伤害我们。”<BR>
<BR>
我们都沉默了。<BR>
<BR>
“......是的。然后呢？”蜥蜴人做了个手势。<BR>
<BR>
“‘然后呢’是什么意思？”<BR>
<BR>
我看到蜥蜴人脸上怒火升起，但随即平静了。“......有意思。我明白你如何能用假装的愚蠢让所有人放松警惕，直到现在。当然对我没用，但我欣赏你的技巧。”<BR>
<BR>
“我明白了。”雷明说，“正是我担心的。”<BR>
<BR>
“那就告诉我，精灵。”蜥蜴人说。<BR>
<BR>
“你是莫拉格·堂的人。你相信我们抢了你的猎物，但我向你保证，绝无此事。这是个天大的误会。我们俩都不会干涉堂的官方事务。”<BR>
<BR>
蜥蜴人盯着，然后笑了。“我为什么要加入精灵组织来解决你们愚蠢的精灵事务？你们的政治是你们自己的，哈拉鲁。沼泽之子不需要关心它们。真正的莫拉格·堂刺客就在你旁边。”<BR>
<BR>
嗯，实际上我旁边没有人。除了雷明，但作为一个受过教育的人，我知道哈拉鲁家族不是莫拉格·堂，因为它们的名字不同。这些都是你在高等教育中学到的小知识！<BR>
<BR>
“作为黑暗兄弟会的特工，这个猎杀是我的责任。奥德汝因那个泰瓦尼议员已经被另一个巫师雇用了。毕竟，即使是莫拉格·堂也对泰瓦尼政治感到厌倦。而且他们现在雇佣真正疯狂的保镖 -- 何不让一两份执行令漏过去呢？然而......索拉斯不知怎么说服了你们接下这个任务，对吧？”蜥蜴人弯下腰，盯着我的脸。“泰瓦尼人付钱给他们的保镖，让他们伪装成守卫，拒绝执行令，以虚假指控监禁合法刺客，以便之后秘密处决。只有疯子才会那样对抗堂。不幸的是所有泰瓦尼督学都是疯子。然而......堂还是接了这个任务，对吧？”<BR>
<BR>
“哈！那正是精灵公会会做的事，对吧？”我说。<BR>
<BR>
他笑了。“而且，是的，我在那里，在索拉斯的庄园里。你甚至认不出我，对吗，精灵？我也和你一样忍受了那些乏味的天际典故。但别太难过，索拉斯甚至没认出我不是他通常的那个奴隶。但证据非常确凿。它证实了我的怀疑。我敏锐的、沼泽训练的双眼能看到你们族类看不到的阴影细节。这把斧头......”蜥蜴人捡起我掉落的尼普提克勒。他在手中翻转，欣赏着附魔的光泽。“这是我们小轮子的中心。你们俩都认出了它。没有别的解释。你们，莫拉格·堂，抢了属于兄弟会的猎物。”<BR>
<BR>
“阁下......我理解你很容易这么想。但我们直到现在才拿到这把斧头。这把斧头是被一个女巫从诺德人那里偷走的。”<BR>
<BR>
“哈！错！”我说。雷明似乎接受了死亡。<BR>
<BR>
“你放弃伪装了？”<BR>
<BR>
“实际上，那读作‘沙哈’。但我的斧头从未被女巫偷走！”<BR>
<BR>
“那哈拉鲁在撒谎。”<BR>
<BR>
“它是我和一个漂亮姑娘住在一起时被偷的，她在一个装满骷髅和药剂的帐篷里露营，研究魔法，被镇民们害怕。”<BR>
<BR>
蜥蜴人盯着我。<BR>
<BR>
没人说话。<BR>
<BR>
“......什么？”<BR>
<BR>
“没错。她一定被某个完全不相关的人抢劫了。可怜的姑娘。”<BR>
<BR>
蜥蜴人看向雷明，好像在寻求同情，但什么也没得到。<BR>
<BR>
“我们不可能犯下这起谋杀。我找到诺德人时他是裸体的，那把斧头肯定不在他身上。在刺杀发生时，我们俩都昏过去了。当我们逃脱时，他没有去公会大厅，没有执行令可出示，而且我们意外到了德亚西特。没有人会自愿去德亚西特。”<BR>
<BR>
“除了精灵！”我开玩笑说。蜥蜴人笑得像希尔辛，但像希尔辛去拜访岳母那种。或者什么。我不知道。他紧紧握着我的斧头，仍在欣赏。<BR>
<BR>
“我观察你进入奥德汝因。你有一头驮货瓜尔。你的同伴穿着衣服。把斧头藏在瓜尔背包里很容易。”<BR>
<BR>
“那我们怎么把它带进去的，阁下？我们是枯萎病风暴开始时冲进去的。”<BR>
<BR>
“我不是法官。我是刽子手。”<BR>
<BR>
“但如果你杀了我们，而你的真正目标还活着，你的合约就无法完成。阁下，请想想。斧头是怎么到战士公会里面的？”<BR>
<BR>
这时，蜥蜴人确实想了一会儿。“我承认我很好奇。那么，诺德人，尼普提克勒是怎么到战士公会的？”<BR>
<BR>
“好问题！”我对蜥蜴人说，欣赏他问题的质量。<BR>
<BR>
沉默。<BR>
<BR>
“啊，你想要答案？”<BR>
<BR>
“......是的。”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，很简单。显然，从我住过的那个营地的女人那里偷走尼普提克勒的人把它带到了老跑。”<BR>
<BR>
“我找到他时他非常裸体，阁下。非常。”<BR>
<BR>
蜥蜴人沮丧地看着我的斧头，握紧它好像想把它捏碎，他的脸在颤抖......终于，平静压倒了他。“你想象力有限，精灵。”<BR>
<BR>
“什么？”<BR>
<BR>
“很简单。你发现他裸体。后来他穿上了衣服。显然在某个时候你的视线一定移开了，他就能把斧头从某个隐藏地点（也许是石头后面）塞进你的背包里。到奥德汝因时，他一定在你分心时把它从背包里偷出来，混在战士公会其他武器里，等大家都睡着后使用。这还只是众多可能性之一。”<BR>
<BR>
“他说得很有道理。”我对雷明说，他再次尽力假装我不存在。“嘿，也许我现在可以问你一个问题？”<BR>
<BR>
“......你可以问。”他极不情愿地说。<BR>
<BR>
“如果你知道大家都睡着了，为什么不自己动手？”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“......借用某位冬堡的未来贵族的话，‘那是个好问题。’”蜥蜴人面无笑容。“但你没资格问我任何事。”<BR>
<BR>
“为什么？我们在萨沃斯庄园吗？”<BR>
<BR>
蜥蜴人把脸埋进手里，捂住尖叫声，然后用尼普提克勒直指着我。“够了！我要用你羞辱我的武器也毁了你。我记得法师公会说过这把武器......它麻痹、中毒、灵魂陷阱被击中的人，而且使用者的魅力会增强！”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，你绝不能听那该死的法师公会的人的话！”我嗤笑道，“你知道帝国法师公会跟冬堡学院的聪明人比起来差远了。毕竟，作为那所学院的受过教育的未来贵族，我可以告诉你他们犯了一个非常简单、明显的错误！”<BR>
<BR>
“......什么错误？”<BR>
<BR>
“它确实有你所说的所有效果。但它对所有效果的目标都是使用者本人。”<BR>
<BR>
“......你在撒谎。”<BR>
<BR>
“我没有。只是效果很慢，仅此而已！”<BR>
<BR>
“但那不可能！制造一件伤害使用者的武器是愚蠢的！没人会那样做，因为太蠢了！谁会使用那么蠢的武器？！”<BR>
<BR>
好吧，跟你说实话，这时我只是嘲笑那刺客的狭隘思维。毕竟，就在那时他瘫倒在甲板上，麻痹了，无法松开尼普提克勒 -- 所以，真的，为什么有人会使用这样的武器，现在应该很明显了吧！<BR>
<BR><BR>
****<BR>
<BR>
编者注<BR>
<BR>
由于其源于一系列酒馆短剧，《愚行录》常提及与该故事创作地冬堡学院相关的事件。自419年春天这把斧头首次附魔和测试以来，尼普提克勒的附魔效果已出现在多个故事和歌曲中。其效果正如所述，令其创造者大为沮丧，他也是“呆子”角色的主要灵感来源之一。<BR>
<BR>
一个阐述莫拉格·堂和黑暗兄弟会区别的短剧被编入本章。原剧涉及一个未来的谋杀受害者和两个刺客争论政治边界。最近它因无关原因失宠了。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
A Dunce in Morrowind, v8<BR>
by Frolja Silver-Blood<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Eventually, our boat had crashed into some poor elf's Netch farm or something, and we were both freed from our predicament. An elf lass came to untie our ropes and take us into her home, while the guards came to apprehend the lizard, and my axe was returned to me. I made a joke about the lizard's luck having run out, on account of the lizard telling us all about the luck enchantments he'd used, but obviously Remyn had some sort of temporary hearing loss. I made sure to keep telling him the same joke throughout the day, as I didn't want him to miss out - it was the least I could do!<BR>
<BR>
Now, Remyn was clever enough to convince the guards, magistrates, and everyone important, that all his misfortunes the past few days had been because of that lizard, because elves will believe anything bad about lizards. So all his money and debts were restored, his name cleared of all charges, and we were able to travel back to Stoneforest for free. Remyn had learned to defer to my more educated judgement now, and no longer corrected me about the names of elf towns like Stoneforest. It's a shame that the elves in Stoneforest were less open-minded, and also rude and uneducated, but it's a sad truth about elves - they're very quick to judge others!<BR>
<BR>
And I had quite a good time in Stoneforest as well! It is a town where the beer flows freely, and the Hlaalus like Remyn do their governmenting and thieving and whatever else they claim to do. But of course, eventually, all my affairs were in order, I was compensated by the Imperial guard for apprehending the lizard assassin, and I was ready to return to Skyrim. My travel had been arranged to Solstheim -- there's a boat from Khuul, should you have any reason to go -- and then to Skyrim.<BR>
<BR>
And so on the day I was to leave, with my meager possession with me, I waited at the Silt Strider docks for the big bug to arrive, and watched the sunset, while attempting to read various magical tomes as part of my education. And it was then that Remyn approached me.<BR>
<BR>
"Ah, Remyn!" I said. "I haven't seen you since that assassin attacked us on the boat! It's been a long time!"<BR>
<BR>
"It's been three hours." He said.<BR>
<BR>
"So, come to say goodbye, have you?"<BR>
<BR>
Remyn paused, and took a seat on a crate of strider urine beside me. "Is it true?"<BR>
<BR>
"Is what true?"<BR>
<BR>
"That assassin said you're part of the Morag Tong. You never actually told him he was wrong." Remyn paused. "Did you really kill that Telvanni councillor?"<BR>
<BR>
"Ah ha! That old rot. What do you think, then, hm? Do I seem like the assassin type to you?"<BR>
<BR>
"You don't. But it's worth making sure. And you're still not actually denying it. That lizard made a good point. It doesn't make much logical sense for... Niptickler, to have ended up there if it wasn't for you to use it."<BR>
<BR>
"Ah, but don't you see the genius of Niptickler yet? It's the perfect weapon because it can't be used against you! A thief will steal your weapon and try to attack you with it, but as you saw, they just damage themselves in the process!"<BR>
<BR>
"Yes. It is intensely stupid and yet it worked. But if you didn't bring it to Ald'Ruhn, how did it get there? I suppose it must have been the witc--"<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, confound all this talk of witches! It was not a witch who stole my axe!"<BR>
<BR>
"...I don't know how you can still believe that."<BR>
<BR>
"Because it's true!"<BR>
<BR>
"No." And something changed in my long-time companion's face at this. He became more certain, more resolute. "No, it was a witch."<BR>
<BR>
"I beg your pardon?"<BR>
<BR>
"It was a witch. The 'comely lass' was a witch. She was feared by the townsfolk. She had a camp full of skulls and potions. She was known to practice magic. And when you awoke, your clothes were missing, and so was your special axe, which is what witches famously do in Morrowind, to Nords. I ask you to look at the evidence. There was nobody else in the camp that night. You slept in her tent. She was the only person with the means, the motive, and the opportunity to steal your axe. How could someone steal your clothes if they weren't casting a spell on you, as well? You were, logically, robbed by a witch. This woman fits all the criteria for being a witch. It must have been her."<BR>
<BR>
"Now, come now, Remyn! You know I'm much smarter than that."<BR>
<BR>
"No, you are not. You think you couldn't be robbed by a witch because you're not a stereotype, but that just means you're a stereotype with delusions of rarity. You were robbed by a witch. I will not co-operate with this insane view of things anymore. Over the past few days you have gotten me into dangerously stupid situation after dangerously stupid situation on account of your ignorance."<BR>
<BR>
"Ah, but whose ignorance got you out of those same dangerous situations?"<BR>
<BR>
Remyn fell silent.<BR>
<BR>
"Eh, Remyn? Eh?"<BR>
<BR>
"I do not understand how you poison everyone around you like that. For a moment there, I thought what you said actually made sense."<BR>
<BR>
"Ah ha! But it does make sense! You just don't want to admit it to yourself!"<BR>
<BR>
"I don't want to admit it. I don't want to accept a view of the world that agrees with what you've just said, or anything you've ever said. You really believe you're an educated man just because you work at the College of Winterhold? All you've done your entire trip is prove that wrong, over and over, and over, and I cannot possibly fathom how you still think yourself intelligent."<BR>
<BR>
"Just like on the Snowhawk!"<BR>
<BR>
And Remyn opened his mouth to speak, as the Silt Strider arrived in the dock. The passengers all boarded the dock, and one of them -- a comely lass -- noticed me, and approached me.<BR>
<BR>
"So sorry -- are you the Nord I met a few days ago?" She asked.<BR>
<BR>
"Ah, I recognize you! Remyn, this is the comely lass who isn't a witch!" I said. Remyn stared. "You know, we were just talking about you!"<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, wonderful! Yes, I recognize you! You were staying at my camp outside Khuul! I was so grateful to meet someone who didn't believe all those awful rumors about me! Imagine believing I'm a witch!" She turned to Remyn, and offered her hand. "Hello Remyn, it's nice to meet you."<BR>
<BR>
"You too, outlander." Remyn shook her hand, in silent shock.<BR>
<BR>
"It was so awful what happened, you know." She turned back to me.<BR>
"Why, when that attacker invaded my tent, I did everything in my power to fight him off, but he stole all your belongings, including that enchanted axe of yours! He even somehow removed your clothes while you were sleeping! I kept all your things in this bag just in case I ran into you again!" And so she handed me a leather sack with all my important belongings in it.<BR>
<BR>
"Ah ha! You see Remyn? And thank you, lass, I'll make sure all the scholars of Winterhold understand the hospitality of strange women in Morrowind to Nords!" Remyn didn't respond. He hadn't reacted to anything for a few minutes now. He was probably just in some sort of coma.<BR>
<BR>
"Say, you saw the attacker. Who was it?"<BR>
<BR>
"Well... I think it was an elf. A Dark Elf, I mean. And... you know what? I think it was a Telvanni!" She paused, and thought about it. "Yes, I'm certain of it!"<BR>
<BR>
"How would you be able to tell?" Remyn said.<BR>
<BR>
"Well, I hate every Telvanni I meet, and this man was a Dark Elf who I hated and was good at magic."<BR>
<BR>
Remyn was stunned at the sheer validity of this woman's logic.<BR>
<BR>
"Ha! Strange that a Telvanni would do something like that, eh?" I said.<BR>
<BR>
"No, they're pricks. I think they should all die."<BR>
<BR>
"And also, he left a Telvanni ring behind. And when he introduced himself to me before attacking me, he said his name was Ardas Telvanni. He also kept shouting 'long live House Telvanni' at me when attacking me, which was how I got away."<BR>
<BR>
"...I see." Remyn paused. "Pardon me, I don't mean to be rude, but if you wouldn't mind answering a question of mine."<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, of course not!"<BR>
<BR>
"You live outside Khuul in a camp, yes?"<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, yes."<BR>
<BR>
"Filled with skulls, potions, spell books, and other things that make the locals fear you, yes?"<BR>
<BR>
And she huffed. "Oh, I know, I know. They all think I'm a witch. It's ridiculous, isn't it?"<BR>
<BR>
"It would be a reasonable assessment."<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, it's just more provincial small-town thinking, that's what it is. Strange women can't live outside town in a camp full of skulls and magic and be a little unique or different without being considered a witch, or frightening, or evil, not in those backwaters anyway."<BR>
<BR>
"Then forgive me for asking." Remyn said. "But if you're not a witch, then why do you live in those conditions?"<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, that's easy." She said. "I'm a necromancer who worships Mehrunes Dagon."<BR>
<BR>
"...I see." Remyn did not seem to know whether to be relieved or not. "And perhaps that explains why the Telvanni would attack yo--"<BR>
<BR>
But Remyn stopped. He looked at me for a moment. "Sera, if you would be so kind... may I look through your bag of recovered belongings?"<BR>
<BR>
"Ha! By all means!" And so I handed it to Remyn, and turned back to the woman. "So, worshipping the old Mehrunes Dagon, eh?"<BR>
<BR>
"Well, I figured he was the hottest of the Daedra Lords."<BR>
<BR>
Remyn finished looking through my belongings. Well, I don't know what he saw in there, but he looked quite solemn afterwards when he handed them back to me.<BR>
<BR>
"I apologize for the misunderstanding, Sera," he said to me. "I feel everything is quite clear now."<BR>
<BR>
"It is?"<BR>
<BR>
"Forgive me. I believe it wouldn't be prudent to explain further. I hope I haven't impeded your business too much."<BR>
<BR>
"Hah!" I said, slapping Remyn on the back. "An elf that says sorry! Wonders never cease, eh? Not to worry Remyn, I'm sure one day we'll meet again and have a good laugh about all this!"<BR>
<BR>
Remyn spoke to the comely lass now. "Ardas Telvanni... I believe I recognize that name. He's an... unconventional fighter that some of the councilors hire to protect themselves from assassination, isn't he? He's known to disguise himself as a guards, I believe."<BR>
<BR>
"Telvanni don't have rights." The lass spat on the ground. "I hope he's dead."<BR>
<BR>
"Well, this has been a wonderful trip to remember, but I have to get on the bug." I said, getting on the bug. And so I took one last look at the Stoneforest, and I waved goodbye to Remyn, as he reluctantly waved back to me. And the bug strode off down the river Odai (a stupid name if you ask me -- I'd have called it something like Markgran River), while I checked my belongings to make sure Remyn hadn't taken my writ.<BR>

 <BR>
Publisher's Note<BR>
<BR>
A subtle difference is often the only difference that matters.<BR>
<BR>
A particular variant of the common murder mystery, rarely read outside Morrowind, is "find the Morag Tong". The characters, once introduced, are trying to uncover the identity of an assassin out to kill them before the deed has been committed. They usually fail. While not quite on par with a Fuchon Cire mystery, the late Ferana Adrethi had plans to wrap up the Dunce with such a mystery, as nod to her literary roots. Alternate plans exist to have Remyn be the assassin, but were not considered.<BR>
<BR>
With this, the tale of the "Dunce in Morrowind" comes to an end. However, Frolja Silver-Blood and the Sneezing Horker Historical Society of Winterhold continue to witness sequels in all shapes and sizes as the College attempts to teach them. For them and for us, this story never really ends, it just moves elsewhere.<BR>
<BR>
So drink and be merry, for you too could be a Dunce one day!<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
晨风愚行录，卷八<BR>
弗洛利亚·银血 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
最终，我们的船撞上了一个可怜精灵的气母农场什么的，我们俩都从困境中解脱了。一个精灵姑娘来解开我们的绳子，带我们进她家，同时守卫来逮捕了蜥蜴人，我的斧头也归还了我。我开了一个关于蜥蜴人运气用完的玩笑，因为蜥蜴人告诉过我们他用的幸运附魔，但显然雷明有某种暂时性听力丧失。我确保一整天都在重复这个笑话，因为我不想让他错过 -- 这是我能做的最起码的事！<BR>
<BR>
现在，雷明足够聪明，说服了守卫、治安官和所有重要人物，他过去几天的不幸都是因为那个蜥蜴人，因为精灵会相信任何关于蜥蜴人的坏事。所以他所有的钱和债务都恢复了，他的名字清除了所有指控，我们能免费回到石头森林了。雷明现在学会了尊重我更受教育的判断，不再纠正我关于精灵城镇如石头森林的名字了。可惜石头森林的精灵没那么开明，而且粗鲁没文化，但这是关于精灵的可悲事实 -- 他们很容易评判别人！<BR>
<BR>
我在石头森林也过得相当愉快！那是啤酒畅饮的地方，像雷明这样的哈拉鲁人搞他们的治理和偷窃等他们声称做的事。但当然，最终我所有事务都处理好了，帝国守卫因我抓获蜥蜴刺客给了我补偿，我准备回天际了。我的行程安排是先到索瑟泰姆 -- 有从库尔出发的船，如果你有理由去的话 -- 然后到天际。<BR>
<BR>
于是在我离开的那天，带着我微薄的财产，我在阔步沙蚤码头等待大虫子到来，看着日落，同时尝试阅读各种魔法书籍作为我教育的一部分。就在那时雷明走近我。<BR>
<BR>
“啊，雷明！”我说，“自从刺客在船上袭击我们后我就没见过你了！好久不见！”<BR>
<BR>
“才三个小时。”他说。<BR>
<BR>
“所以，来道别的？”<BR>
<BR>
雷明顿了顿，在我旁边的阔步沙蚤尿液板条箱上坐下。“是真的吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“什么是真的？”<BR>
<BR>
“那个刺客说你是莫拉格·堂的一员。你从未真正告诉他他错了。”雷明顿了顿，“你真的杀了那个泰瓦尼议员吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“啊哈！那老东西。你觉得呢，嗯？我看起来像刺客类型吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“不像。但值得确认。而且你还是没否认。那个蜥蜴人说的有道理。如果不是你用它，尼普提克勒......出现在那里不太符合逻辑。”<BR>
<BR>
“啊，但你还没看到尼普提克勒的天才之处吗？它是完美的武器，因为它不能被用来对付你！小偷会偷走你的武器并试图用它攻击你，但正如你所见，他们只会在这个过程中伤害自己！”<BR>
<BR>
“是的。它极其愚蠢却管用了。但如果你没把它带到奥德汝因，它怎么到那儿的？我想一定是女巫 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，别再说女巫了！偷我斧头的不是女巫！”<BR>
<BR>
“......我不明白你怎么还能那么相信。”<BR>
<BR>
“因为那是真的！”<BR>
<BR>
“不。”这时我长期同伴的脸上有了变化。他变得更确定、更坚决。“不，那是女巫干的。”<BR>
<BR>
“请再说一遍？”<BR>
<BR>
“是女巫。‘漂亮姑娘’是女巫。她被镇民们害怕。她有一个装满骷髅和药剂的营地。她以练习魔法闻名。当你醒来时，你的衣服不见了，你特殊的斧头也不见了，这在晨风是女巫对诺德人常做的事。我请你看证据。那晚营地里没有别人。你睡在她的帐篷里。她是唯一有手段、动机和机会偷走你斧头的人。如果她们不对你施法，怎么能偷走你的衣服？按照逻辑，你是被女巫抢了。这个女人符合女巫的所有标准。一定是她。”<BR>
<BR>
“好了，雷明！你知道我比那聪明多了。”<BR>
<BR>
“不，你不是。你认为你不会被女巫抢，因为你不是刻板印象，但那只是意味着你是一个有稀有妄想症的刻板印象。你是被女巫抢的。我不会再配合这种疯狂的观点了。过去几天，因为你的无知，你把我拖入了一个又一个危险的愚蠢局面。”<BR>
<BR>
“啊，但谁的‘无知’又把你从那些危险局面中救出来了？”<BR>
<BR>
雷明沉默了。<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，雷明？嗯？”<BR>
<BR>
“我不明白你怎么能那样毒害你周围的每个人。有那么一刻，我以为你说的话确实有道理。”<BR>
<BR>
“啊哈！但确实有道理！你只是不想对自己承认！”<BR>
<BR>
“我不想承认。我不想接受一个同意你刚才所说之话的世界观，或你曾说的任何话。你真的仅仅因为在冬堡学院工作就相信自己是个受过教育的人？你整个旅途所做的一切，就是一遍又一遍地证明那是错的，我完全无法理解你怎么还觉得自己聪明。”<BR>
<BR>
“就像在雪鹰上一样！”<BR>
<BR>
雷明张嘴要说话，这时阔步沙蚤到了码头。乘客们都上了码头，其中一个 -- 一个漂亮姑娘 -- 注意到了我，朝我走来。<BR>
<BR>
“对不起 -- 你是几天前我遇到的那个诺德人吗？”她问。<BR>
<BR>
“啊，我认出你了！雷明，这就是那个不是女巫的漂亮姑娘！”我说。雷明盯着。“你知道吗，我们刚才还在谈论你！”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，太好了！是的，我认出你了！你当时住在库尔外我的营地！我很感激遇到一个不相信那些可怕谣言的人！竟然会相信我是女巫！”她转向雷明，伸出手。“你好雷明，很高兴认识你。”<BR>
<BR>
“我也很高兴，外乡人。”雷明默默震惊地握了手。<BR>
<BR>
“你知道，发生的事太可怕了。”她转回我。<BR>
“那个袭击者闯进我的帐篷时，我尽全力击退他，但他偷走了你所有的东西，包括你附魔的斧头！他甚至不知怎么在你睡觉时脱掉了你的衣服！我把你所有东西都放在这个袋子里，以防再遇到你！”她把一个装着所有重要物品的皮袋递给我。<BR>
<BR>
“啊哈！你看到了吗，雷明？谢谢你，姑娘，我会确保冬堡的所有学者都了解晨风陌生女人对诺德人的好客！”雷明没有回应。他已经几分钟没对任何事有反应了。他大概只是某种昏迷。<BR>
<BR>
“嘿，你看到了袭击者。是谁？”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯......我想是个精灵。我的意思是暗精灵。而且......你知道吗？我觉得是泰瓦尼人！”她停顿了一下，想了想，“是的，我确定！”<BR>
<BR>
“你怎么能分辨出来？”雷明说。<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，我讨厌每个遇到的泰瓦尼人，而这个人是个我讨厌的、擅长魔法的暗精灵。”<BR>
<BR>
雷明被这女人逻辑的绝对有效性惊呆了。<BR>
<BR>
“哈！泰瓦尼人做那种事很奇怪，对吧？”我说。<BR>
<BR>
“不，他们很讨厌。我觉得他们都该死。”<BR>
<BR>
“而且，他留下了一枚泰瓦尼戒指。在他攻击我之前自我介绍时，他说他叫阿尔达斯·泰瓦尼。他在攻击我时还一直对我喊‘泰瓦尼家族万岁’，我就是那样逃脱的。”<BR>
<BR>
“......我明白了。”雷明顿了顿，“请原谅，我不是要冒犯，但如果你不介意回答我一个问题。”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，当然不！”<BR>
<BR>
“你住在库尔外的营地，对吧？”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，是的。”<BR>
<BR>
“装满骷髅、药剂、法术书和其他让当地人害怕的东西，对吧？”<BR>
<BR>
她哼了一声。“哦，我知道，我知道。他们都以为我是女巫。真可笑，不是吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“那是合理的评估。”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，那只是更多乡巴佬小镇思维，就是这样。奇怪的女人不能住在城外一个装满骷髅和魔法的营地里，有点独特或不同，而不被当作女巫、可怕或邪恶，反正那些落后地方是这样的。”<BR>
<BR>
“那就原谅我问。”雷明说，“但如果你不是女巫，你为什么住在这种条件下？”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，很简单。”她说，“我是崇拜梅鲁涅斯·大衮的死灵法师。”<BR>
<BR>
“......我明白了。”雷明似乎不知道该不该松口气，“也许那解释了为什么泰瓦尼人会攻击你 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
但雷明停下了。他看了我一会儿。“阁下，如果你愿意......我能看看你找回物品的袋子吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“哈！当然！”于是我把袋子递给雷明，转回那个女人，“所以，崇拜那个老梅鲁涅斯·大衮，嗯？”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，我觉得他是最帅的迪德拉大君。”<BR>
<BR>
雷明翻完了我的物品。嗯，我不知道他在里面看到了什么，但当他递还给我时，看起来相当严肃。<BR>
<BR>
“我为误解道歉，阁下。”他对我说，“我觉得现在一切都清楚了。”<BR>
<BR>
“是吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“原谅我。我认为进一步解释不太明智。希望我没太耽误你的事。”<BR>
<BR>
“哈！”我说着拍了拍雷明的背，“会说抱歉的精灵！奇迹永不停息，对吧？别担心雷明，我相信有一天我们会再见面，好好笑这一切的！”<BR>
<BR>
雷明现在对漂亮姑娘说：“阿尔达斯·泰瓦尼......我觉得我认识那个名字。他是一个......非传统的斗士，有些议员雇他来保护自己免受暗杀，对吧？我相信他以伪装成守卫而闻名。”<BR>
<BR>
“泰瓦尼人无权。”姑娘朝地上啐了一口，“我希望他死了。”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，这次旅行值得纪念，但我得上虫子了。”我说着上了虫子。于是我最后看了一眼石头森林，向雷明挥手告别，他不情愿地也向我挥手。虫子沿着奥代河大步走去（如果你问我，那是个蠢名字 -- 我会叫它类似马克格兰河），我检查行李确保雷明没拿走我的执行令。<BR>
<BR><BR>
****<BR>
<BR>
编者注：<BR>
<BR>
微妙的区别往往是最重要的区别。<BR>
<BR>
一种常见的谋杀悬疑变体，在晨风以外很少见，是“寻找莫拉格·堂”。角色们一旦登场，就要在暗杀发生前找出刺客的身份。他们通常失败。虽然不完全媲美福尚·西尔的悬疑，但已故的费拉纳·阿德雷西曾计划用这样的悬疑来结束《愚行录》，以向她文学根源致敬。也有让雷明是刺客的备选计划，但未被采纳。<BR>
<BR>
至此，《晨风愚行录》的故事结束了。然而，弗洛利亚·银血和冬堡的打喷嚏海象历史学会继续见证着各种续篇，因为学院试图教授它们。对它们和我们来说，这个故事从未真正结束，只是转移到别处。<BR>
<BR>
所以喝酒享乐吧，因为有一天你也可能成为呆子！<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>Dunmer Law: a Primer<BR>
<BR>
<BR><FONT COLOR="003300">by Galothis Omeyn, scholar of the Imperial University<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><FONT COLOR="000000" >The law of the Dunmer is not a single monolithic doctrine; rather it is as varied and obscure as the Dunmer people themselves are. Unwary outlander scholars may find themselves hopelessly lost within Morrowind's legal system, and it is my hope that this primer will familiarize visitors with some of the basic principles of law in this province.<BR>
<BR>
In many ways, Morrowind itself is not one nation but five (or six, or seven depending on how one counts), and the competing legal structures of the province reflect the different values and ideals of its Great Houses. Thus, one might expect a court and trial system not unlike that of Wayrest or Colovia in the lands of my kin, the Hlaalu. If you find yourself in legal difficulties in the Velothis Marches however, I pray that your sword arm is strong as disputes among the Redoran are often solved by honorable duels. The scandal of 3E297, when the East Empire Company delegate to Blacklight was reportedly murdered by a councilor of that city, was to Redoran eyes an acceptable, lawful challenge to a tariff dispute over marshmerrow exports. Their response to the ensuing Imperial outrage was bemusement that the delegate, in his ignorance of legal custom, had not made more effort to seek a compromise on the issue.<BR>
<BR>
The Telvanni, as usual, are another matter altogether. There are historically no laws in their domain, a civic freedom in which they take no small measure of pride. Of course, the power of the local wizard lord is absolute, and his or her word is final in all disputes. Tyranny, you might declare, but many a cruel or overly mighty Telvanni lord has been dragged from his tower and dismembered by his angry subjects.<BR>
<BR>
The accumulated legal wisdom and precedents of over three thousand years of history maintain order in the lands of the Dres. This wisdom is rarely written down, and is instead called upon directly by the summoning of esteemed ancestor spirits to legal proceedings. This is naturally advantageous when mediating cases of inheritance or unlawful murder, and it is occasionally the case that necromancers have been denounced at trial by the souls of the dead they have attempted to bind to the mortal plane. Court meetings take place on holy ground and are ritually cleansed at the end of every hearing.<BR>
<BR>
Indoril law is perhaps the greatest philosophical achievement of the Dunmer race. It entails an all-encompassing code that covers all functions of society and nature. Derived in part from the recursive algorithmic legal doctrine of the Aldmeri Dominion (which was also highly influential on the Dwemer), Indoril law requires study from birth in order to correctly grasp its axioms, as it seeks to provide a framework not only for mortal behavior but also natural processes like the growth of flowers and the master-slave relationship which is inherent to all life. The much-publicized and misunderstood attempt by the Indoril to place the Thrassian Plague itself on trial in the First Era, on charges of existential disruption of the social order, has garnered some derision in the West. These outlander commentators fail to grasp the importance of the legal process in Indoril society, and the necessity that grotesque unpredicted occurrences be codified and incorporated into society's worldview. Needless to say, Indoril savants look on relative vulgarity of Imperial law with disdain, much as an artist might resent a tradesmer's crude branding mark pasted across their life's masterwork.<BR>
<BR>
All Great Houses are obliged to implement the core Imperial legal code, the Juris Imperator Tamrielicus, and all grudgingly do so in their own fashion. Fines and imprisonment for crimes such as murder, theft, and obstructing an officer of the Empire are standardized and will be familiar to any Imperial subject.<BR>
<BR>
Disputes between members of different houses, or legal issues where house jurisdiction is in question, are often referred to the Court of Waters, a religious conclave that holds the final say in matters beyond the remit of the House councils. The power of this court has waxed and waned over time according to the strength of the Great Houses themselves, but in theory, it carries the authority of the god-kings of Morrowind and now also the Empire, which is trying to consolidate the legal framework of the province into this one entity for administrative purposes. It was at this court that the historic accord was reached between Great House Dres and the Tribunal Temple itself, when they affirmed their legal right to practice traditional Dunmer Daedra Worship in a case where the deities Vivec and Boethiah were both called to the stand, and proceedings were temporarily halted when the court building itself was apparently briefly relocated to the moon Secunda by parties unknown. Other unusual cases heard here include a dispute over archaeological remains between Telvanni and Indoril plaintiffs, which caused outrage when the Telvanni delegation summoned a mechanical Dwemer centurion as a witness for their case.<BR>
<BR>
It is difficult to say how the law will develop as Morrowind becomes a more settled member province of the Empire. The Hlaalu have led the way, becoming highly conversant in the Western system to the extent that they are now able to propose innovations within the Imperial Juris. However recent disputes about territorial control effected by the opening of Vvardenfell promise to create new crises and conflicts, and I believe that common understanding is now more essential than ever.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>丹莫法律：入门<BR>
<BR>
<BR><FONT COLOR="003300">加洛西斯·奥梅因，帝国大学学者<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><FONT COLOR="000000" >丹莫的法律不是单一的教条；它像丹莫人本身一样多样而晦涩。不谨慎的外乡学者可能会在晨风的法律体系中迷失方向，我希望这本入门能让访客熟悉该行省法律的一些基本原则。<BR>
<BR>
在许多方面，晨风本身不是一个国家，而是五个（或六个、七个，取决于如何计算），该行省相互竞争的法律结构反映了其大族不同的价值观和理想。因此，在我哈拉鲁同胞的土地上，你可能会期望看到类似途歇或科洛维亚的法院和审判制度。然而，如果你在维洛提斯边境遇到法律麻烦，我祈祷你的持剑手臂强壮，因为勒多兰人之间的争端通常通过光荣决斗解决。第三纪元297年的丑闻，当时东帝国公司驻黑光代表据称被该市一名议员谋杀，在勒多兰人看来，这是一场关于沼泽芯髓出口关税争端的可接受的合法挑战。他们对随后帝国愤怒的反应是困惑：代表因不了解法律习俗，没有更努力寻求妥协。<BR>
<BR>
泰瓦尼人，一如既往，完全是另一回事。在他们的领地内历史上没有法律，这是一项他们颇感自豪的公民自由。当然，当地巫师领主的权力是绝对的，他或她在所有争端中的话是最终决定。你可能会说暴政，但许多残忍或过于强大的泰瓦尼领主被愤怒的臣民从塔楼中拖出并肢解。<BR>
<BR>
三千多年历史积累的法律智慧和先例维持着德雷斯领地的秩序。这些智慧很少被书写下来，而是通过召唤受尊敬的祖先之灵直接参与法律程序。这在调解继承或非法谋杀案件时自然有利，偶尔也有死灵法师在审判中被他们试图束缚到凡人位面的死者灵魂谴责。法庭会议在圣地举行，并在每次听证结束时进行仪式净化。<BR>
<BR>
因多瑞尔法律也许是丹莫种族最伟大的哲学成就。它包含了一套涵盖社会和自然所有功能的全面法典。部分源于奥德莫自治领的递归算法法律学说（也对锻莫产生了很大影响），因多瑞尔法律需要从出生起学习才能正确掌握其公理，因为它试图不仅为凡人的行为提供框架，还为诸如花朵生长和所有生命固有的主奴关系等自然过程提供框架。因多瑞尔人在第一纪元试图将瑟拉斯瘟疫本身以破坏社会秩序为由送上法庭的广为人知且被误解的尝试，在西方招致了一些嘲笑。这些外乡评论者未能理解法律程序在因多瑞尔社会中的重要性，以及将怪诞不可预测的事件编纂并纳入社会世界观的必要性。不用说，因多瑞尔学者以轻蔑的眼光看待帝国法律的相对粗俗，就像艺术家可能怨恨商人将粗陋的品牌标记贴在他们毕生杰作上一样。<BR>
<BR>
所有大族都有义务实施核心帝国法典《泰姆瑞尔帝国法》，并都勉强以自己的方式执行。对谋杀、盗窃和妨碍帝国官员等罪行的罚款和监禁是标准化的，任何帝国臣民都会熟悉。<BR>
<BR>
不同家族成员之间的争端，或家族管辖权有疑问的法律问题，通常提交给水域法庭，这是一个宗教会议，在家族议会职权范围之外的事项上有最终决定权。该法庭的权力随时间根据大族自身实力而消长，但理论上它拥有晨风神王和现在帝国（正试图出于行政目的将该省法律框架整合到这个实体中）的权威。正是在这个法庭上，德雷斯大族与审判席神殿达成了历史性协议，他们在一场维威克和波耶西亚都被传唤出庭的案件中确认了实践传统丹莫迪德拉崇拜的法律权利，而当法庭建筑本身显然被不明方短暂移到了瑟昆达卫星时，诉讼程序暂时中止。这里审理的其他不寻常案件包括泰瓦尼和因多瑞尔原告之间关于考古遗迹的争端，当泰瓦尼代表团召唤了一个机械锻莫百夫长作为他们案件的证人时引起了公愤。<BR>
<BR>
随着晨风成为帝国更稳定的成员行省，法律将如何发展很难说。哈拉鲁家族已率先垂范，变得精通西方体系，以至于现在能在帝国法内提出创新。然而最近关于瓦登费尔开放所影响的领土控制争端，预示着新的危机和冲突，我相信共同理解现在比以往任何时候都更重要。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
A Dunmer's Guide to Skyrim: The Reach<BR>
by Giras Daroso<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
May Mercy, Mastery, and Mystery guide your life and ancestors. My name is Giras Daroso and I have set out to compose a series of guidebooks about the frigid and alien land west of our enlightened people, Skyrim.<BR>
<BR>
Introduction:<BR>
The Reach is one of the most ethnically diverse regions in Tamriel, having been fought over by essentially every major western power. Unlike what many of our people may believe, not all of Skyrim is like the most northern lands of House Redoran. The Reach is in fact covered with thick deciduous forests and is quite temperate in temperature. Some travellers may even find the many mesas and steep valleys reminiscent of the foyadas of Vvardenfell.<BR>
<BR>
Travelling to and from Markarth:<BR>
Of all possible modes of transportation, I would greatly advise to take a boat. From Blacklight to the city of Haafingar and from there I would advise taking a river barge down the Karth river until you reach the city of Markarth, the largest settlement in the Hold. Passage can be booked here to virtually all corners of the region and even to other Holds.<BR>
<BR>
Temple Resources:<BR>
Any pious Dunmer will find the religious faculties lacking in Markarth Hold, and with good reason, being far from our hallowed lands. I would highly suggest bringing the necessary materials and prayer books on your journey. With that said, there is in fact a hostel and house temple run by a kind soul named Vadas Marvani open to any of the Temple faithful. His residence is a two story house near the King's hall in Markarth.<BR>
<BR>
The Locals:<BR>
While the western nords are by no way amiable to our kind as a whole, they are too preoccupied with harassing the Breton and Redguard communities to bother a traveller from Morrowind. Remember that you are a representative of the Triune Way, and as long as the authorities be just, recall the writings of St. Delyn the Wise: keep no secret from your Judge's scale!<BR>
However, I must stress that this does not make travel in the Reach like an evening at the spas of Dreynim. The native inhabitants of the area, aptly called Reachmen, are to be avoided unless absolutely necessary, as their villages are commonly hideouts for murderous marauders.<BR>
In addition, I have been told that Yokudo-Nordic unrest within the city of Dragonstar continues still at the time of this guide's completion.<BR>
<BR>

The Dwarven Firmament<BR>
by Amiel Callonus<BR>

These ancient structures have allowed scholars such as myself a glimpse into Dwarven culture, history, science, and technology. <BR>
As any citizen of the Empire should know, there are thirteen major constellations in the night sky, signs that marks one's birth with a specific form of magical energy. The Dwarves knew these stars well, and made charts to predict their movements and the timing of astronomical phenomena precisely. Unfortunately, the majority of that information is lost. The observatory on Stros M'Kai and scattered remains of diagrams found elsewhere provide hints but few satisfying conclusions about the scope of their knowledge.<BR>

Its charges are of a technological or scientific nature as well, and so the Apprentice is the Automaton, the Atronach/Golem is the Warmachine, and the Ritual, the Laboratory. Automation, Domination, Experimentation. The Mechanist and his three charges typically reside in the sky's middle ring. The Automaton bears a resemblance to a steam centurion. Their Warmachine is similar, but its lower half is much closer to a Dwarven-style ballista. What exactly the Laboratory is supposed to represent is unclear at this time.<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><BR>
<IMG SRC="tr\tr_dwrvfirm_warrior.dds" WIDTH="240" HEIGHT="240"><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
The two other guardians, Warrior and Thief, while not differently named, are no less different in their forms.<BR>
The Steed is a scarab beetle rather than a horse. Theories exist that the Rourken clan used mechanical beetles like this to traverse the deserts of Hammerfell. The Steed is of course guided by the Warrior, and all of his charges tend to live in the highest echelon of heaven.<BR>
The Lord, another charge, appears more like a priest than a king, and wears a robe adorned with runes. The Lady takes on an appearance quite similar to a Dark Elven noblewoman. The Warrior himself is armored with a Dwarven helmet, pauldrons, gauntlets, and shield, and he wields either a saber or katana.<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><BR>
<IMG SRC="tr\tr_dwrvfirm_thief.dds" WIDTH="240" HEIGHT="240"><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
The Thief, who occupies the lowest ring, presides over the Lover, Shadow, and Tower. It is worth noting that unlike the traditional Thief, the Dwarves interpreted the dagger to be a set of lockpicks and probes, and the dagger's sheath a large key.<BR>
The Dwarven Shadow is reminiscent of a wraith with long arms, each with five long ghostly fingers, pointy ears, and an unusually thin beard. Oddly enough, the Shadow has a single eye in the shape of its corresponding rune, the letter G.<BR>
Similar to our own Lover, the Dwarves depicted her with revealing clothing, although her pose seems to indicate a fighting stance.<BR>
The Tower's shape is the same, but some of the finer details in the architecture are unmistakably Dwarven.<BR>
<BR>
Perhaps the least interesting of all in appearance is the Serpent, as it is practically identical to ours. However, the Dwarves were very active in keeping track of its location. They always listed it separately from the other twelve birthsigns due to its wayward behavior.<BR>
<BR>
Addendum: Ongoing research is investigating the meaning of Dwarven runes that correspond to each constellation. The Serpent has a rune as well, one that has proven difficult to transcribe and with seemingly no letter to match it.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Dwemer Burial Customs <BR>
Nedlir Andrethi <BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
As many would know, the Dwemer were an atheistic and highly advanced race. Hence, their burial customs were quite different from Chimeri customs. The Dwemer didn't bury common folk in tombs. Instead they cremated them in lava, which gave them energy in a practice that can be described as sacred, if I can use this word to describe the feelings of non-religious people. Only aristocratic, important, or well-known Dwemer were buried in tombs, and every Dwemeri tomb was a masterpiece of stonework and masonry. Most Dwemeri tombs were quite inaccessible, with the entrances sealed so that only Dwemeri officials and the deceased's relatives could gain access to them. Most tombs were built to the same layout. When one first entered the tomb, he found himself facing a long passage leading downward. The actual entrance to the tomb was at the end of the long tunnel, closed off by another, more powerful door. <BR>
<BR>
The main tomb itself was a long, wide great hall. The ceilings were supported by enormous columns, and sometimes even giant animunculi. All walls were covered by frescoes showing the great deeds of deceased Dwemeri. In the great hall, multiple statues of the buried Dwemer adorned the side walls of the tomb. Finally, at the far end of the burial hall was a raised dais, upon which the sarcophagus laid. If the Dwemer was of a very high significance, then its sarcophagus was guarded by a golem. The sarcophagi had different forms, dependant upon the trade of the deceased person. If the Dwemer was a warrior, it was in a form of warrior holding a sword. If they were a Tonal Architect, it was in the form of a god-like character that represented the science inherent between the mind and the body; only these architects could fathom the arcane secrets of the long fabled Heart of Lorkhan. However, if he or she was a monarch, they did not have a sarcophagus at all. Tales say that the monarchs' souls were infused into the golem, symbolizing eternal life. <BR>
<BR>
Body Storage and Preservation of the Deceased - 
Before being placed into the sarcophagus, the body was raised over a heated stream or lava pit so that all moisture would evaporate from the body. The body was then frozen and carefully placed into the sarcophagus. It is unknown if the bodies still remain after the War of The First Council, as it has proven impossible to open the sarcophagi. <BR>
<BR>
Author's note: I present this text to the kind reader's judgment. In it, I tried to compile all my knowledge and thoughts on the topic. It is based mostly on what I've read and heard, not on what I've seen with my own eyes. <BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Eastern Quarantine<BR>
by Caius Invictus<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
In the year 3E 426, during the rule of His Imperial Majesty Uriel Septim VII, Emperor of Tamriel, Beloved of the Nine, Imperator of the Legion, etc. etc., the district of Vvardenfell in Morrowind was to be quarantined under the orders of the Legion Commander which would regrettably undermine the local power of the Imperial government and place them at odds with the local Dunmeri Temple and government.<BR>
<BR>
The crisis started, as such things often do, with an economic dispute as whenever economics are involved political troubles inevitably soon follow. The Great House Hlaalu urged the Grand Council of Morrowind to reduce import tariffs on Imperial brandy (known locally as flin), putting them at odds with the Great House Redoran who argued that reducing the tariffs on imported brandy would be unfair considering that local alcoholic beverages, notably sujamma, greef, and shein, still suffered under high export tariffs. The Redoran, and indeed much of the rest of the Grand Council, argued that a reduction of import tariffs on flin would be an egregious example of local Dunmeri culture being sacrificed at the hands of the Empire. Still others said that the Hlaalu proposal was a thinly-veiled attempt to worsen the balance of trade between Morrowind and Cyrodiil, which would pump gold out of Morrowind thereby impoverishing its people. The Hlaalu, they argued, were willingly putting the Empire's interests over the interests of their fellow Dunmer simply so that they could derive a profit. King Hlaalu Athyn Llethan, High Councilor and Lord of Morrowind, wisely dismissed these arguments and granted the Hlaalu their request. Much of the Grand Council was outraged at this decision, with some even accusing the King and the Hlaalu as a whole of being slaves to the Empire. Although the incident did not lead to violence in the Council, tensions between the various Houses, and between the Empire and Morrowind, increased markedly.<BR>
<BR>
Conditions were exacerbated when a tax revolt broke out in Balmora. Many in that city complained that high Imperial taxes and injurious tariffs on inter-provincial trade were suffocating commerce. Conditions only worsened as the local Hlaalu government was unable to calm the growing discontent culminating in a violent uprising. The local Hlaalu guardsmen proved insufficient to quell the riot so legionnaires from the nearby Moonmoth Fort were called in for assistance who quickly ended the riot. Mirroring earlier arguments in the Grand Council, the Redoran disagreed with the Hlaalu on how the riot was handled. While the Hlaalu assured the rest of Morrowind that the legion put it down without any excessive violence, the Redoran saw only a legion of foreign troops putting local mer to the sword for expressing reasonable anger at the conditions the Empire forced them to live in. The Redoran, well-versed in histrionics, once again accused the Hlaalu of selling the lives of their own people to the Empire. The Hlaalu quickly sent deputations to Duke Vedam Dren, Lord of Vvardenfell, to inquire about the lowering of Imperial taxes out of a genuine concern for their own people, although the Redoran insisted the Hlaalu simply wanted to save face. The Redoran also urged the Duke to petition for the lowering of taxes as they feared that a similar riot could break out in Ald-ruhn if the economic conditions were not alleviated. Local discontent against the Empire grew and relations between the Imperial Government and the Houses strained.<BR>
<BR>
Concurrent to the political troubles were a flurry of brutal public murders of Imperial notables and Hlaalu officers by unknown assailants. Preliminary investigations ruled out the involvement of both the Morag Tong and the Dark Brotherhood; the Morag Tong are lawfully forbidden from targeting Imperial officers and the murdered Hlaalu officers were not marked by a writ while the murders were incompatible with the modus operandi of the Dark Brotherhood who value covert, skilled assassination. Many of the murderers were easily caught by authorities immediately following the murders as they made little to no effort to avoid capture. While this historian will make the safe assumption that the captured murderers were interrogated, the revelations gained from these interrogations are classified and neither the Temple nor the Empire was willing to share any details with me. Against the backdrop of rising tensions between the Empire alongside their Hlaalu allies and the local Dunmer, the systematic murder of Imperials and Hlaalu led Imperial officials to fear that a conspiracy was hatching which threatened the Empire's power on Vvardenfell. All measures have been as of yet unable to cease the senseless violence, and an atmosphere of palpable fear hangs over the district.<BR>
<BR>
It was this fear which served as the catalyst for the Imperial government in New Ebonheart, the newly-constructed Imperial capital on Vvardenfell, to order the legion to step in and investigate. Legion District Commander Varus Vanitius took his orders to the extreme in order to both clean his new home and to impress his superiors. Almost immediately after he received his orders Vanitius publically announced his desire to quarantine the entire island of Vvardenfell and send his legions "from coast to coast" in punitive and investigative strikes against any who might raise their voice against the Empire. The plan was an unmitigated disaster which has only served to weaken the Empire's position in Morrowind. While it is true that there was some success in a few areas, notably Balmora which was almost completely restored to its pre-riot state after the legion firmly reestablished Hlaalu control, the endeavor as a whole failed miserably. Logistically the attempt was impossible as the Legion was understaffed on Vvardenfell and the infrastructure needed to move the legions into some of the more inhospitable parts of the island were and still are nonexistent. The Lord Marshall of Morrowind unofficially condemned Vanitius' efforts by refusing to divert men from other districts to Vvardenfell, effectively damning the operation to failure. Additionally, Vanitius experienced pushback from nearly every other faction on Vvardenfell.<BR>
<BR>
The Hlaalu complained that isolating the island would simply exacerbate the problems which led to the riot and incite more anger against both the Hlaalu and the Empire. The Temple was furious at Vanitius for cutting off pilgrims' access to the Palace of Vivec, as well as other, lesser pilgrimage sites. Archanon Saryoni himself spoke against Vanitius' 'blasphemous actions which greatly insult the Tribunal and the Dunmer people.' Saryoni also criticized Duke Vedam Dren for standing complicity by Vanitius' actions. In response, the Duke released a statement which assured the Temple faithful that measures would be taken which would allow pilgrims access to Vivec, although the quarantine ended before such measures were implemented. Even the East Empire Company spoke against the quarantine as the quarantine was inhibiting the Company's ability to export foodstuffs, glass, and ebony from the island. The Company argued that as an entity whose charter was officially sanctioned by the Emperor himself, Vanitius' quarantine did not apply to ships of the East Empire Company. While this legal argument was dubious at best, the Company's intention was made clear. Pressure from external forces, as well as the dawning realization that the legions' sweep through Vvardenfell would be impossible forced Vanitius to lift the quarantine soon after it began.<BR>
<BR>
Ultimately the Duke and his council distanced themselves from Vanitius, hamstringing his political influence on Vvardenfell as he was left without any outlet through which to push his agenda. The Lord Marshall has taken to ignoring any requests forwarded to him by Vanitius, damaging the reputation of the Legion and costing Vanitius the respect of his subordinates, especially since many legionnaires felt even more hated by the locals than before. While the Legion will continue to respect the chain of command, Vanitius has lost much of his effective authority. Faced with increasingly visible internal divisions and worsening ash storms, many question the Legion's ability to combat the encroaching blight.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>

凯乌斯·因维克图斯 著<BR><BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Effects of the Elder Scrolls<BR>
by Justinius Poluhnius,<BR>
Dictated to Anstius Metchim, <BR>
4th of Last Seed in the 126th year of the Second Era<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
It is widely known among scholars that the Elder Scrolls entail a certain hazard in their very reading. The mechanism of the effects has, at present, been largely unknown -- theories of hidden knowledge and divine retribution were the subject of idle speculation with little investigation.<BR>
<BR>
I, Justinius Poluhnius, have undertaken to thoroughly document the ailments afflicted by the Elder Scrolls on their readers, though a unified theory of how they manifest continues to elude me and remains a subject for future study.<BR><BR>
I have grouped the effects into four, finding that the avenue of experience depends largely upon the mind of the reader. If this is unclear, I hope that a proper dichotomy will lay it plain.<BR>
<BR>
Group the First: The Naifs<BR>
<BR>
For one who has received no training in the history or nature of the Elder Scrolls, the scroll itself is, effectively, inert. No prophecy can be scried nor knowledge obtained. While the scroll will not impart learning to the uninformed, nor will it afflict them in any adverse fashion. Visually, the scroll will appear to be awash in odd lettering and symbols. Those who know their astronomy often claim to recognize constellations in the patterns and connections, but such conjecture is impossible to further investigate since the very nature of this study necessitates unlearned subjects.<BR>
<BR>
Group the Second: The Unguarded Intellects<BR>
<BR>
It is this second group that realizes the greatest danger from attempting to read the scrolls. These are subjects who have an understanding of the nature of the Elder Scrolls and possess sufficient knowledge to actually read what is inscribed there. They have not, however, developed adequate discipline to stave off the mind-shattering effect of having a glimpse of infinity. These unfortunate souls are struck immediately, irrevocably, and completely blind. Such is the price for overreaching one's faculties. It bears mentioning, though, that with the blindness also comes a fragment of that hidden knowledge -- whether the future, the past, or the deep natures of being is dependent on the individual and their place in the greater spheres. But the knowledge does come.<BR>
<BR>
Group the Third: Mediated Understanding<BR>
<BR>
Alone in Tamriel, it would appear that only the Cult of the Ancestor Moth has discovered the discipline to properly guard one's mind when reading the scrolls. Their novitiates must undergo the most rigorous mental cultivation, and they often spend a decade or more at the monastery before being allowed to read their first Elder Scroll. The monks say this is for the initiates' own protection, as they must have witnessed many Unguarded Intellects among their more eager ranks. With appropriate fortitude, these readers also receive blindness, though at a far lesser magnitude than the Unguarded. Their vision fogs slightly, but they retain shape, color, and enough acuity to continue to read mundane texts. The knowledge they gain from the scroll is also tempered somewhat -- it requires stages of meditation and reflection to fully appreciate and express what one saw.<BR>
<BR>
Group the Fourth: Illuminated Understanding<BR>
<BR>
Between the previous group and this one exists a continuum that has, at present, only been traversed by the monks of the Ancestor Moth. With continued readings the monks become gradually more and more blind, but receive greater and more detailed knowledge. As they spend their waking hours pondering the revelations, they also receive a further degree of mental fortitude. There is, for every monk, a day of Penultimate Reading, when the only knowledge the Elder Scroll imparts is that the monk's next reading shall be his last.<BR>
<BR>
For each monk the Penultimate Reading comes at a different and unknowable time -- preliminary work has been done to predict the occurrence by charting the severity of an individual monk's blindness, but all who reach these later stages report that the increasing blindness seems to taper with increased readings. Some pose the notion that some other, unseen, sense is, in fact, continuing to diminish at this upper range, but I shall leave such postulations to philosophers.<BR>
<BR>
To prepare for his Ultimate Reading, a monk typically withdraws to seclusion in order to reflect upon a lifetime of revelations and appoint his mind for reception of his last. Upon this final reading, he is forever blinded as sure as those Unguarded ones who raced to knowledge. The Illuminated one, though, has retained his understanding over a lifetime and typically possesses a more integral notion of what has been revealed to him.<BR>
<BR>
It is hoped that this catalog will prove useful to those who wish to further our mortal understanding of the Elder Scrolls. The Moth priests remain aloof about these matters, taking the gradual debilitation that comes with reading as a point of pride. May this serve as a useful starting point for those hoping to take up such study.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
上古卷轴的影响<BR>
贾斯汀尼乌斯·波卢尼乌斯 著，<BR>
由安斯提乌斯·梅特基姆 代笔，<BR>
第二纪元126年末种月4日<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
学者们普遍知晓，阅读上古卷轴本身便伴随着某种危险。目前，其作用机制在很大程度上仍是未知 -- 关于隐藏知识与神圣惩罚的理论只是些鲜有探究的闲谈臆测。<BR>
<BR>
我，贾斯汀尼乌斯·波卢尼乌斯，已着手详尽记录上古卷轴对其读者所造成的种种病症，尽管其显现方式的统一理论仍使我不得其解，并留待未来研究。<BR><BR>
我将这些影响归为四类，发现体验的途径主要取决于读者的心智。若此点尚不明了，希望适当的二分法能将其阐明。<BR>
<BR>
第一类：蒙昧者<BR>
<BR>
对于未接受过关于上古卷轴历史或性质训练的人来说，卷轴本身实际上是无用的。既无法窥见预言，也无法获取知识。尽管卷轴不会向无知者传授学问，但也不会对他们造成任何不良影响。在视觉上，卷轴似乎布满了奇特的文字和符号。那些懂天文学的人常声称在其纹路和关联中辨认出星座，但这种推测无从进一步探究，因为此类研究的性质本身就要求使用无知的受试者。<BR>
<BR>
第二类：无备的智者<BR>
<BR>
正是这第二类人在尝试阅读卷轴时面临最大的危险。这些受试者了解上古卷轴的本质，并拥有足够的知识来实际阅读其上所铭刻的内容。然而，他们尚未培养出足够的自律来抵挡窥见无限所带来的精神冲击。这些不幸的灵魂会立刻、无可挽回地、完全地失明。这就是超越自身官能极限的代价。不过，值得一提的是，伴随失明而来的还有那一丝隐秘的知识 -- 无论是关于未来、过去，还是存在的深层本质，这取决于个体及其在宏大领域中的位置。但知识确实会到来。<BR>
<BR>
第三类：中介之悟<BR>
<BR>
在泰姆瑞尔，似乎唯有先祖蛾教团发现了在阅读卷轴时恰当守护心智的自律之道。其新手必须接受最严格的心智修炼，通常要在修道院度过十年或更长时间，才被允许阅读他们的第一份上古卷轴。僧侣们说这是为了保护新手，因为他们肯定已在那些更热切的同修中目睹过许多“无备的智者”。在具备适当坚韧的情况下，这些读者也会失明，但程度远轻于“无备者”。他们的视线会略有模糊，但仍能分辨形状、颜色，并保有足够的敏锐度来阅读普通文本。他们从卷轴中获得的知识也受到一定程度的调和 -- 需要通过冥想与反思的阶段，才能充分领悟和表达所见之物。<BR>
<BR>
第四类：明悟之知<BR>
<BR>
在上一类与本类之间存在一个连续体，目前只有先祖蛾的僧侣们涉足过。随着持续阅读，僧侣们会逐渐越来越盲，但会获得更宏大、更详尽的知识。当他们在清醒时思索这些启示时，他们也会获得更深一层的心智坚韧。每位僧侣都有其“倒数第二次阅读”之日，届时上古卷轴所传达的唯一知识便是：僧侣的下一次阅读将是其最后一次。<BR>
<BR>
对每位僧侣而言，“倒数第二次阅读”到来的时间各不相同且不可预知 -- 已有初步工作试图通过绘制个体僧侣失明严重程度来预测其发生，但所有达到后期阶段的僧侣都报告说，失明的加剧似乎随着阅读次数的增加而趋于平缓。有人提出，事实上在高端范围内，某种其他不可见的感官正在持续减弱，但我将此类假设留给哲学家去探讨。<BR>
<BR>
为准备其“终极阅读”，僧侣通常会隐退独处，以反思毕生的启示，并让其心智准备好接受最后一次阅读。在这次最终阅读后，他便会和那些急于求知的“无备者”一样，永远失明。然而，明悟者毕生都保有他的理解，并且通常对所揭示之物拥有更完整的认知。<BR>
<BR>
希望这份目录能对那些希望增进我们对上古卷轴凡俗理解的人有所帮助。蛾祭司们对这些事保持超然，他们将阅读所带来的逐渐衰弱视为一种骄傲。愿此能为那些希望从事此类研究的人提供一个有用的起点。<BR>

论元素迪德拉
