"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
On Elemental Daedra<BR>
by Elvyr<BR>
<BR>
Many have studied, and been mesmerized by the behavior of summonable daedra in battles and when being attacked. In order to use less magicka and gain longer periods of conjuration time, there have been proposals on how to properly fluctuate the mana stream to certain threads, such as from Magnus to Aetherius' second plane or through Secunda to the Void Itself. However, magicka redirection is an extremely complex subject and but a few wizards have ever claimed to accomplish this, most notably Amion of Crystal Tower, but with him drifting into madness after living eight hundred years and not eager to teach, the mystery will remain. I was one of the few living Mer to see him perform the conjuration of Frost Atronach with a simple gesture and no mantras at all.<BR>
<BR>
As we all know, all common mages have to rely on the usual method of the customary mantra 'Web-Oht-Ekem Yoodt-Payem-Oht-Neht Yahkem-Oht-Yoodt' or a slight variation of it, and the hand gesture of symmetrically aligning three first fingers not to any sphere of Daedra gods. A common point to focus one's attention is the sun, as it is the direct link to the source of magicka itself and thus neutral. Some disagree, though, but Magnus has been proven to be the most powerful of all points in the firmament.<BR>
<BR>
When I finally took the chances of actually testing the redirection procedures, the results did not prove to be as successful as I first thought. Firstly a test environment was needed, so unnecessary deaths would be avoided. I chose to put a kwama forager in a lair with a traditionally summoned Frost Atronach. Being an aggressive beast as it is, the kwama chose to defend itself from the freezing cold elemental, dying swiftly in the attempt. Yet, the Atronach itself showed no signs of aggression against such a beast until attacked. The summoning of an atronach is considered an offensive act for the atronach will engage on any enemy of the caster, with no regards to its own fate. The question remains, though, how does a summoned Daedra detect these aggressors and could the detection be made more effective, perhaps to the level of thoughts themselves?<BR>
<BR>
On a continued experiment, I was to stream the magicka not make the atronach's physical appearance visible, but to render only its actions obvious for any dweller of Nirn. This would not be done by an invisibility spell that hides already visible matter, there is a major difference between these two. However, the test failed as the actions of the atronach were bound between Oblivion and Nirn, not reaching either one. I have not been able to find studies on this subject and doubt there even are any.<BR>
<BR>
Another thing to consider was to lessen the amount of cold energy a Frost Atronach releases while being summoned. It seemed that even peaceful critters would either escape or attack when being caught by this small but noticeable field. Unnecessary energy should be either surged to other, more needed attributes or reserved to another purpose later. It might not be much, but as it is gradually building up, summoning three Atronach a day without this effect would be noticeable in the magicka surroundings.<BR>
<BR>
On repeated experiments with a kwama being near to a frost atronach and redirecting the flow from the Elvyr field, as I shall call it, to the Void itself, pleasant results were finally achieved. The kwama did not, in fact, pay no attention to the atronach although it was clearly visible. This called for testing with diseased rats, who were far more eager to attack it, although still a bit hesitant. It seems that for kwama, the only way to detect an odorless elemental is its surrounding heat field, or motion, a Storm Atronach's defining feature. On one thing uncertainty bothers me, though - does the said flow method actually apply to all spellcasters, or does it require a connection with the Void only formed by fierce practice? <BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
论元素迪德拉<BR>
埃尔维尔 著<BR>
<BR>
许多人都研究过并可召唤的迪德拉在战斗中和受到攻击时的行为所着迷。为了消耗更少的魔能并获得更长的召唤时间，有人提出了如何将法力流适当地波动到特定线程的建议，例如从玛格努斯到光界的第二层位面，或通过瑟昆达到虚空本身。然而，魔能重定向是一个极其复杂的课题，只有少数法师声称曾做到过，其中最著名的是水晶塔的阿米翁，但随着他在活过八百年后陷入疯狂且无意传授，这个谜团将依旧。我是少数几位亲眼目睹他仅用一个简单手势、完全不念咒语便召唤出寒霜侍灵的活着的精灵之一。<BR>
<BR>
众所周知，所有普通法师都必须依赖常规方法，即惯常的咒语“Web-Oht-Ekem Yoodt-Payem-Oht-Neht Yahkem-Oht-Yoodt”或其轻微变体，以及将三根食指对称排列、不指向任何迪德拉神灵领域的手势。一个常见的专注点是太阳，因为它是通往魔能本身的直接联系，因此是中性的。尽管有些人不以为然，但玛格努斯已被证明是天穹中所有点中最强大的。<BR>
<BR>
当我最终抓住机会实际测试重定向程序时，结果并未如我最初所想那般成功。首先需要一个测试环境，以避免不必要的死亡。我选择将一只夸蚂采集者与一个传统方式召唤的寒霜侍灵放在同一个巢穴中。作为天生好斗的野兽，夸蚂选择防御自己免受这冰冷元素体的侵害，并迅速在尝试中死亡。然而，侍灵本身在受到攻击前并未表现出对该野兽的攻击性。召唤侍灵被视为一种攻击行为，因为侍灵会攻击施法者的任何敌人，而不顾自身命运。然而，问题仍然存在：被召唤的迪德拉是如何侦测到这些攻击者的？这种侦测能否被做得更有效，或许能达到思想本身的层面？<BR>
<BR>
在后续的实验中，我的想法是引导魔能，不是让侍灵的物理外观可见，而是只让其行动对奈恩的任何居民可见。这不能通过隐藏已可见物质的隐身术来实现，两者之间存在重大差异。然而，测试失败了，因为侍灵的行动被束缚于湮灭和奈恩之间，未能到达任何一边。我未能找到关于此主题的研究，甚至怀疑根本不存在。<BR>
<BR>
另一个需要考虑的问题是减少寒霜侍灵在被召唤时释放的寒冷能量。似乎即使是和平的小动物，在被这个虽小却明显的能量场波及到时，也会要么逃跑，要么攻击。不必要的能量应要么涌向其他更需要的属性，要么留待日后另作他用。这可能不算多，但随着其逐渐积累，若无此效果，每天召唤三个侍灵在魔能环境中将是可察觉的。<BR>
<BR>
在反复进行的实验中，让一只夸蚂靠近寒霜侍灵，并将我所称的“埃尔维尔场”的能量流重定向至虚空本身，最终取得了令人满意的结果。事实上，夸蚂并未对侍灵完全视而不见，尽管它清晰可见。这促使我使用病鼠进行测试，它们攻击侍灵的意愿要强烈得多，尽管仍有些犹豫。看来对夸蚂而言，侦测无味元素体的唯一途径是其周围的热场，或是动作 -- 风暴侍灵的定义性特征。然而，有一件事令我困扰：所述的能量流方法是否确实适用于所有施法者，还是需要仅通过刻苦练习才能形成的与虚空的连接？<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Emeralds: Applications in Alchemy<BR>
by Whertold the Blackened.<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
This text is intended as both a reference book for the work-a-day alchemist, and as a primer for students of the art or interested laymen. Alchemy, in general, should not be the province of the careless. Many ordinary things have been shown, by long and careful experimentation, to evince significant effects which are often conflagratory, insidious or otherwise malevolent.<BR>
<BR>
It should be further noted that the return of any benefits at all hinge almost exclusively on one's skill and experience with the equipment and accouterments of alchemy, as well as with the quality of same. A well-made hammer in the hands of a master-builder may construct a citadel, but a mallet in the grasp of a fool will only bend nails. If you have any doubts at all about practicing alchemy, you would be best advised to direct your ambition elsewhere. You have been warned.<BR>
<BR>
Emeralds<BR>
<BR>
Folklore from the Elsweyr wastes tells us emeralds are the tears of Akatosh. Whatever their origin, they are, like most gems, highly valued for their rare beauty and used to adorn both objects of value and people. It is well known that emeralds have useful characteristics which may be drawn forth upon their careful combination with other
ingredients.<BR>
<BR>
Potion of Restore Health<BR>
<BR>
The world is a dangerous place and traveling abroad is an unwise pursuit for the unprepared. Encounters with all manner of aggressive creatures and criminally inclined folk are frequent and leave many a wanderer dead or nearly so. Often for the want of a balm have travelers been hurried to their end. Here I will describe a simple, if rather
costly, recipe for a concoction which revives one's life-force.<BR>
<BR>
A single emerald of no less than three grains in size should be ground to dust in a sturdy mortar. Ensure that you perform this task in a still room, as any sudden gust of air may prove to be expensive. Then the emerald dust must be transferred to a dry container. The mortar should then be wiped clean and used to mash its companion ingredient. This may be any one of corkbulb root, marshmerrow or wickwheat. It is possible to also use the weepings of one infected with corprus, although this substance is notoriously difficult to obtain. The companion ingredient should be fresh, as the fluids within it are a necessary component. It should be noted that while fresh corprus weepings do not keep well, dried weepings mixed with a little blood and
water are an effective substitute.<BR>
<BR>
The emerald dust should be added to the mash and blended in while simultaneously adding dropwise just enough sea-water to yield a thin soupy consistence. While the taste of the potion is unpleasant, it is nonetheless singularly effective.<BR>
<BR>
If you have the opportunity to heat it in a good calcinator, you may further improve the potion's efficacy. Treatment in a quality retort also adds increased benefit.<BR>
<BR>
A very similar potion uses saltrice (fresh or dried, in this case it seems not to matter) as the companion ingredient. The resulting potion not only heals but also provides an effective boon to magicka for a brief period, making it the particular favorite of mages and other initiates of sorcery.<BR>
<BR>
Potion of Fortify Magicka<BR>
<BR>
As just mentioned, it is possible to make a combination healing/magicka fortification potion by using saltrice. One may similarly employ stoneflower petals or belladonna berries (ripened or otherwise) as companion ingredients, although the potion in these cases will only fortify magicka (for a limited time) and will lack any healing benefit.<BR>
<BR>
The user of such a potion should be warned that if one's magicka is fortified and then one should use all of the acquired power before the effects of the potion wear away, then one will suffer a period of distinct weakness proportional to the strength of the fortifying potion used. The natural return of magicka will accordingly take significantly
longer than normal.<BR>
<BR>
Other potions<BR>
<BR>
In alchemic experimentation, one often finds that alongside the positive there are also negative elements within various ingredients. Emeralds are no exception. For example, if one were to combine ground emerald with hypha facia, the resultant potion would turn its user into a stumbling buffoon, barely able to stand unaided. Similarly, if ground emerald is fused with bittergreen petals or bungler's bane, the resulting potion would leave its imbiber exhausted. Interestingly, the combination of emerald with black anther yields a potion which drains both agility and endurance!<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
祖母绿：炼金应用<BR>
焦黑者沃托德 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
本文旨在作为日常炼金术士的参考书，同时也是该艺术的学生或感兴趣的门外汉的入门读物。总的来说，炼金术不应是粗心大意者的领域。长期而谨慎的实验已证明，许多普通事物会表现出显著效果，这些效果往往是剧烈的、阴险的或其他有害的。<BR>
<BR>
还应进一步指出，任何益处的获得几乎完全取决于个人对炼金设备与器具的熟练程度和经验，以及这些设备本身的质量。一把制作精良的锤子在一名优秀建造者手中可以建造一座堡垒，但在傻瓜手中，一把木槌只会弄弯钉子。如果你对实践炼金术有任何疑虑，最好将你的雄心引向别处。你已得到警告。<BR>
<BR>
祖母绿<BR>
<BR>
艾斯维尔荒原的民间传说告诉我们，祖母绿是阿卡托什的泪水。无论其起源如何，它们与大多数宝石一样，因其稀有的美丽而备受珍视，被用于装饰贵重物品和人物。众所周知，祖母绿具有有用的特性，这些特性可在其与其他成分仔细结合时
被引发出来。<BR>
<BR>
恢复生命药剂<BR>
<BR>
世界充满危险，毫无准备便外出旅行实属不智。与各种凶猛的生物及有犯罪倾向者的遭遇十分频繁，常使许多旅行者丧命或濒临死亡。常因缺少一剂镇痛软膏，旅行者便过早迎来了自己的终结。在此，我将描述一种简单
但颇为昂贵的配方，用于制作一种能恢复生命力的药剂。<BR>
<BR>
将一颗不小于三格令大小的祖母绿在坚固的研钵中研磨成粉。确保在无风的房间内进行此项操作，因为任何突如其来的气流都可能导致损失。然后将祖母绿粉末转移到干燥的容器中。将研钵擦拭干净，用于捣碎其伴生材料。这可以是软木根、沼泽芯髓或灯心草中的任何一种。也可以使用尸化病感染者的渗液，尽管这种物质以难以获得而闻名。伴生材料应是新鲜的，因为其内部的液体是必要的成分。需要注意的是，虽然新鲜的尸化病渗液不易保存，但将干燥的渗液与少量血液和
水混合是一种有效的替代品。<BR>
<BR>
将祖母绿粉末加入糊状物中并混合均匀，同时逐滴加入适量的海水，直至形成稀薄的汤状稠度。尽管药剂的滋味不佳，但效果却非常显著。<BR>
<BR>
如有机会在优质的煅烧器中加热，可进一步提高药剂效力。在优质的曲颈瓶中处理也可增加额外益处。<BR>
<BR>
一种非常相似的药剂使用盐米（新鲜或干燥的，在此情况下似乎无所谓）作为伴生材料。所得的药剂不仅能治疗，还能在短时间内有效提升魔能，使其成为法师及其他魔法研习者的特别偏爱。<BR>
<BR>
强化魔能药剂<BR>
<BR>
如前所述，使用盐米可以制作一种兼具治疗和强化魔能效果的药剂。同样，也可以使用石花花瓣或颠茄浆果（无论成熟与否）作为伴生材料，不过在这种情况下，药剂只能强化魔能（在有限时间内），而不具备任何治疗效果。<BR>
<BR>
此类药剂的使用者应受到警告：如果其魔能被强化后，在药剂效力消退前使用掉了所有获得的能量，那么使用者将会经历一段明显的虚弱期，其程度与所用药剂的强化强度成正比。相应地，魔能的自然恢复将
比平时慢得多。<BR>
<BR>
其他药剂<BR>
<BR>
在炼金实验中，人们常发现各种成分中除了积极因素外，也含有负面元素。祖母绿也不例外。例如，将研磨的祖母绿与菌丝脸皮结合，所制成的药剂会使使用者变成一个步履蹒跚的小丑，几乎无法独立站立。同样，若将研磨的祖母绿与苦绿花瓣或笨人祸根融合，所制成的药剂会让饮用者筋疲力尽。有趣的是，祖母绿与黑色花药的组合会产生一种同时损耗敏捷和耐力的药剂！<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Epic of the Grey Falcon<BR>
By Anido Jhone, editor<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
As uncovered and translated by Anido Jhone, Royal Archaeologist, from an ancient tome:<BR><BR>
This tale comes from sometime in the 2nd Era, most probably after the time of the Knahaten Flu, or at least I have so surmised due to reasons in the text. Whether or not the tale is true, it remains an interesting story of survival. 
The reader will, I trust, forgive me if I translated the epic somewhat informally. The message, I think, is universal, and should not be misread. 
Enjoy, gentle reader. <BR><BR>
A.J.J. <BR><BR>
<BR><BR>
The Grey Falcon , a small warship of the Summerset Isle, Was patrolling deep in the ocean for a pirate That had been looting the coast. The first three weeks out were uneventful. Two hours after sunset, on the 22nd day out of port, The lookout spotted a top of a sail in the moonlight, Just on the horizon. "Sail! To starboard, forward quarter!" The lookout of the Grey Falcon cried. The crew and captain of the Grey Falcon were quickly roused, And stumbled to the deck. "'Tis the ship we're looking for, Captain," said the lookout.<BR><BR>
"All hands to battle stations! All archers to their posts," The Captain yelled, "Full ahead!" The two ships closed, And a dark figure stepped out onto the forecastle of the pirate ship. The figure made a gesture with his hands, And a giant ball of fire streaked towards the Grey Falcon. The ball of fire struck the Grey Falcon in her sails, Quickly catching them aflame.<BR><BR>
The figure made another gesture. Large bolts of ice streaked out from his hands, And hit the Grey Falcon just above and below the water line, Gouging large holes in her hull. The Grey Falcon was mortally wounded. The Captain cried, "All hands abandon shi-" As he was cut off by a pirate's arrow shot into his throat.<BR><BR>
As the Grey Falcon, aflame and listing badly, plunged into the sea, One of her sailors, Darik Seaspit, Managed avoid the pirate arrows and spells to make his way to a lifeboat, And lowered it into the darkness below. Just as the lifeboat entered the water, a quick grey shape jumped into it. Darik looked, and saw it was Helnor Snarlsbane, A Khajiit mercenary assigned to the ship. The two rowed the small boat away, As the Grey Falcon finished her descent into the sea. In the darkness, the Pirate ship missed their small craft. After the two rowed well out of the pirates possible view, They both collapsed from exhaustion.<BR><BR>
Early morning the next day, They took an inventory of the lifeboats stores. Normally the lifeboat carries enough food and water To supply seven people for at least ten days. 
In place of the food, though, Helnor found a note: "The food in this lifeboat was found to be in violation of Summerset Navy regulation during inspection. In accordance to that article, the food was taken away and destroyed. A replacement may be obtained by redeeming this letter at the Port Supply Office. Signed, Lt. Inspector Windhollow" Helnor read aloud.<BR><BR>

"There's no chance we can make it back to land Before we starve to death - 'twill be over a month in this craft" "Wait, I have an idea" said Helnor, with a gleam in his catlike eye.<BR><BR>
Six weeks later, the lifeboat entered the port of Corwich. As it was tethered to the dock, a solitary figure was pulled out, Looking weather beaten and thin. One of the dockworkers peered into the life raft, After the figure was taken away to the port healer for treatment. "Hmm, what's this", a worker said to himself, As he picked up a large bone from the boat, A bone bleached white by the sun.<BR><BR>
After the sole survivor of the Grey Falcon recovered from his ordeal, He was taken to the inquest for the death of Darik Seaspit, And placed on a chair before the magistrate. "We here in High Rock have a dim view of cannibalism. You'd better have a good reason for your actions," The inquisitor boomed at Helnor Snarlsbane.<BR><BR>
"By the Lady, do you?" Helnor stood, and said, "Your Honor, I had no choice. There was no food, and it was at least two months to the closest port. We both decided this was the only way someone would make it" "Well, then , I suppose that is understandable, If somewhat distasteful," the inquisitor said. "You think it was distasteful?," Helnor muttered to himself, "I didn't have any seasoning."<BR><BR>
"One final thing, Mr. Snarlsbane, How was it decided that you would be the one that would dine on the other? The toss of a coin?" Helnor drew himself up and said, "Your honor, it was very simple. Darik Seaspit was a vegetarian" "Case dismissed!"

<BR>
'You're lucky I don't cook you up and eat you,' replied the tavernkeeper.<BR>
<BR>
Eslaf hurriedly left the tavern. For the rest of the day, the boy approached the good citizens of Erolgard, begging for food. One person had thrown something $0D
at him, but it turned out to be an inedible rock.<BR>
<BR>
As night fell, a raggedy man came up to Eslaf and, without saying a word, handed him a piece of fruit and a piece of dried meat. The lad took it, wide-eyed, $0D
and as he devoured it, he thanked the man very sweetly.<BR>
<BR>
'If I see you begging on the streets tomorrow,' the man growled. 'I'll kill you myself. There are only so many beggars we of the guild allow in any one town, $0D
and you make it one too many. You're ruining business.'<BR>
<BR>
It was a good thing Eslaf Erol knew how to run. He ran all night.<BR>
<BR>
Eslaf Erol's story is continued in the book Thief.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
King<BR>
by Reven<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Gentle reader, you will not understand a word of what follows unless you have read and committed to memory the first three volumes in this series, 'Beggar,' 'Thief,' and 'Warrior,' which leads up to this, the conclusion. I encourage you to seek them out at your favorite bookseller.<BR>

We last left Eslaf Erol fleeing for his life, which was a common enough occurrence for him. He had stolen a lot of gold, and one particularly large gem, from a rich man in Jallenheim named Suoibud. The thief fled north, spending the gold wildly, as thieves generally do, for all sorts of illicit pleasures, which would no doubt disturb the gentleman or lady reading this, so I will not go into detail.<BR>
<BR>
The one thing he held onto was the gem.<BR>
<BR>
He didn't keep it because of any particular attachment, but because he did not know anyone rich enough to buy it from him. And so he found himself in the ironic situation of being penniless and having in his possession a gem worth millions.<BR>
<BR>
'Will you give me a room, some bread, and a flagon of beer in exchange for this?' he asked a tavernkeep in the little village of Kravenswold, which was so far north, it was half situated on the Sea of Ghosts.<BR>
<BR>
The tavernkeep looked at it suspiciously.<BR>
<BR>
'It's just crystal,' Eslaf said quickly. 'But isn't it pretty?'<BR>
<BR>
'Let me see that,' said a young armor-clad woman at the end of the bar. Without waiting permission, she picked up the gem, studied it, and smiled not very sweetly at Eslaf. 'Would you join me at my table?'<BR>
<BR>
'I'm actually in a bit of a hurry,' replied Eslaf, holding out his hand for the stone. 'Another time?'<BR>
<BR>
'Out of respect for my friend, the tavernkeep here, my men and I leave our weapons behind when we come in here,' the woman said casually, not handing the gem back, but picking up a broom that was sitting against the bar. 'I can assure you, however, that I can use this quite effectively as a blunt instrument. Not a weapon, of course, but an instrument to stun, medicinally crush a bone or two, and then - once it is on the inside ...'<BR>
<BR>
'Which table?' asked Eslaf quickly.<BR>
<BR>
The young woman led him to a large table in the back of the tavern where ten of the biggest Nord brutes Eslaf had ever seen were sitting. They looked at him with polite disinterest, as if he were a strange insect, worth briefly studying before crushing.<BR>
<BR>
'My name is Laicifitra,' she said, and Eslaf blinked. That was the name Suoibud had uttered before Eslaf had made his escape. 'And these are my lieutenants. I am the commander of a very large independent army of noble knights. The very best in Skyrim. Most recently we were given a job to attack a vineyard in the Aalto to force its owner, a man named Laernu, to sell to our employer, a man named Suoibud. Our payment was to be a gem of surpassing size and quality, quite famous and unmistakable.<BR>
<BR>
'We did as we were asked, and when we went to Suoibud to collect our fee, he told us he was unable to pay, due to a recent burglary. In the end, though, he saw things our way, and paid us an amount of gold almost equal to the worth of the prize jewel ... It did not empty out his treasury entirely, but it meant he was unable to buy the land in the Aalto after all. So we were not paid enough, Suoibud has taken a heavy financial blow, and Laernu's prize crop of Jazbay has been temporarily destroyed for naught,' Laicifitra took a long, slow drink of her mead before continuing. 'Now, I wonder, could you tell me, how came you in the possession of the gem we were promised?'<BR>
<BR>
Eslaf did not answer at once.<BR>
<BR>
Instead, he took a piece of bread from the plate of the savage bearded barbarian on his left and ate it.<BR>
<BR>
'I'm sorry,' he said, his mouth full. 'May I? Of course, I couldn't stop you from taking the gem even if I wanted to, and as a matter of fact, I don't mind at all. It's also useless to deny how it came into my possession. I stole it from your employer. I certainly didn't mean you or your noble knights any harm by it, but I can understand why the word of a thief is not suitable for one such as yourself.'<BR>
<BR>
'No,' replied Laicifitra, frowning, but her eyes showing amusement. 'Not suitable at all.'<BR>
<BR>
'But before you kill me,' Eslaf said, grabbing another piece of bread. 'Tell me, how suitable is it for noble knights such as yourself to be paid twice for one job? I have no honor myself, but I would have thought that since Suoibud took a profit loss to pay you, and now you have the gem, your handsome profit is not entirely honorable.'<BR>
<BR>
Laicifitra picked up the broom and looked at Eslaf. Then she laughed, 'What is your name, thief?'<BR>
<BR>
'Eslaf,' said the thief.<BR>
<BR>
'We will take the gem, as it was promised to us. But you are right. We should not be paid twice for the same job. So,' said the warrior woman, putting down the broomstick. 'You are our new employer. What would you have your own army do for you?'<BR>
<BR>
Many people could find quite a few good uses for their own army, but Eslaf was not among them. He searched his brain, and finally it was decided that it was a debt to be paid later. For all her brutality, Laicifitra was a simple woman, raised, he learned, by the very army she commanded. Fighting and honor were the only things she knew.<BR>
<BR>
When Eslaf left Kravenswold, he had an army at his beck and call, but not a coin to his name. He knew he would have to steal something soon.<BR>
<BR>
As he wandered the woods, scrounging for food, he was beset with a strange feeling of familiarity. These were the very woods he had been in as a child, also starving, also scrounging. When he came out on the road, he found that he had come back on the kingdom where he had been raised by the dear, stupid, shy maid Drusba.<BR>
<BR>
He was in Erolgard.<BR>
<BR>
It had fallen even deeper into despair since his youth. The shops that had refused him food were boarded up, abandoned. The only people left were hollow, hopeless figures, so ravaged by taxation, despotism, and barbaric raids that they were too weak to flee. Eslaf realized how lucky he was to have gotten out in his youth.<BR>
<BR>
There was, however, a castle and a king. Eslaf immediately made plans to raid the treasury. As usual, he watched the place carefully, taking note of the security and the habits of the guards. This took some time. In the end, he realized there was no security and no guards.<BR>
<BR>
He walked in the front door, and down the empty corridors to the treasury. It was full of precisely nothing, except one man. He was Eslaf's age, but looked much older.<BR>
<BR>
'There's nothing to steal,' he said. 'Would that there was.'<BR>
<BR>
King Ynohp, though prematurely aged, had the same white blond hair and blue eyes like broken glass that Eslaf had. In fact, he resembled Suoibud and Laicifitra as well. And though Eslaf had never met the ruined landlord of the Aalto, Laernu, he looked him too. Not surprisingly, since they were quintuplets.<BR>
<BR>
'So, you have nothing?' asked Eslaf, gently.<BR>
<BR>
'Nothing except my poor kingdom, curse it,' the King grumbled. 'Before I came to the throne, it was powerful and rich, but I inherited none of that, only the title. For my entire life, I've had responsibility thrust on my shoulders, but never had the means to handle it properly. I look over the desolation which is my birthright, and I hate it. If it were possible to steal a kingdom, I would not lift a finger to stop you.'<BR>
<BR>
It was, it turned out, quite possible to steal a kingdom. Eslaf became known as Ynohp, a deception easily done given their physical similarities. The real Ynohp, taking the name of Ylekilnu, happily left his demesne, becoming eventually a simple worker in the vineyards of The Aalto. For the first time free of responsibility, he fell into his new life with gusto, the years melting off him.<BR>
<BR>
The new Ynohp called in his favor with Laicifitra, using her army to restore peace to the kingdom of Erolgard. Now that it was safe, business and commerce began to return to the land, and Eslaf reduced the tyrannical taxes to encourage it to grow. Upon hearing that, Suoibud, ever nervous about losing his money, elected to return to the land of his birth. When he died years later, out of greed, he had refused to name someone an heir, so the kingdom received its entire fortune.<BR>
<BR>
Eslaf used part of the gold to buy the vineyards of The Aalto, after hearing great things of it from Ynohp.<BR>
<BR>
And so it was that Erolgard was returned to its previous prosperity by the fifth born child of King Ytluaf - Eslaf Erol, beggar, thief, warrior (of sorts), and king.<BR>

国王<BR>

温和的读者，除非你已经阅读并记住了本系列的前三卷《乞丐》《盗贼》和《武士》，否则你将无法理解下面的任何内容，这三卷引向了本卷 -- 结局。我鼓励你到你最喜欢的书商那里去找它们。<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
埃斯拉夫没有立刻回答。<BR>

相反，他从左边那个野蛮的络腮胡壮汉盘子里拿了一块面包吃了起来。<BR>

“抱歉。”他嘴里塞满食物说，“我能吃点吗？当然，就算我想，我也阻止不了你拿走宝石，事实上，我一点也不介意。否认它是怎么到我手里的也没用。我是从你雇主那里偷来的。我当然不想因此伤害你或你的高贵骑士们，但我能理解一个盗贼的话不适合你这样的人。”<BR>

埃斯拉夫·埃罗尔的故事在《战士》一书中继续。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Etiquette With Rulers<BR>
By Erystera Ligen<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Because the rules are so complex and the stakes are so high, many people blanch at the thought of speaking with a noble with a title. For starters, it is important to address them correctly, for just as no one likes to be misnamed, no one likes to be mistitled. The problem is that in High Rock, traditions of the peerage differ slightly from region to region. The base rules follow:<BR><BR>
There are eight kingdoms in High Rock in the following regions: Northpoint, Daggerfall, Shornhelm, Camlorn, Farrun, Evermore, Wayrest, and Jehanna. If a woman is ruling one of these areas, she is called the Queen. The husband of a Queen and the wife of a King is not necessarily of equal rank -- they may not be Kings and Queens themselves. Their children are Princes and Princesses. Their grandchildren are also Princes and Princesses. If a male ruler dies, his wife takes the title Dowager Queen, providing there is not a Dowager Queen already. Like all rules, there are exceptions. One noted exception took place recently in Daggerfall, when King Lysandus died. In most regions, his wife Mynisera would not have become Dowager Queen of Daggerfall, because Lysandus' mother, the widow Nulfaga, still lived. In Daggerfall, however, it is permissible for there to be two persons with the same title. Thus, both Nulfaga and Mynisera have the title Dowager Queen.<BR><BR>
If a female ruler, who does not share rank with her husband, dies, there is no male equivalent to the word Dowager. Widowers of Queens usually take another title, either a lesser family title or one given by their children. There have been a few men in the history of High Rock who have fallen from being addressed as King to being addressed as Mister at the death of their wife.<BR><BR>
Other regions are ruled by Dukes and Duchesses, Marquises (or Marquesses) and Marquises (or Marchionesses), Counts and Countesses, Viscounts or Viscountesses, Barons or Baronesses, and Lords or Ladies. This list is theoretically listed from highest to lowest rank, but the ruler of a territory outranks all other nobles, regardless of title. Dwynnen, for example, is a Barony, and the Baron or Baroness of Dwynnen outrank any other noble in that territory, even Dukes and Counts.<BR><BR>
In theory, (again, this may not be the case according to local custom) the eldest son or daughter of a noble takes their parents highest family title below their parents. Thus, the Duke of Northmoor, who is also the Marquis of Calder, had a daughter who became the Marchioness of Calder.<BR><BR>
Kings and Queens are always addressed as "Your Majesty" in conversation; Dukes and Duchesses, "Your Grace". All other rulers may be addressed with their title and name, or Lord or Lady and their name.<BR><BR>
A few hints may be needed to determine exactly who rules a territory. You may rely on people on the streets to make reference to their ruler, but that may not be enough. After all, if the gossip involved Lord Bemmish and Viscountess Byrd, neither or both could be the ruler of the territory. I have found that a more predictable method is to pay some attention to the names of taverns and shops in a region. By tradition, many of these are called "The Duke's Fox" or "The Lady's Provisions." This, more often than not, is the name of the ruler. If the shop's name is "Lady Annisa's Provisions" or "Lord Boxworth's Fox," that is probably the name of a local titled merchant, not the ruler. A store with a unnamed ruler's title has probably been around for some time, and does not bother to change its name with the new name of the ruler.<BR><BR>
In speaking with any person, a ruler or not, it is best to know what sort of a person they are first. Rulers tend to stand on ceremony, and prefer that people addressing them speak politely and deferentially. There are, of course, exceptions to this, particularly among younger rulers, or rulers new to their positions. They may prefer a bolder, slangy style. If you are unsure, or unsure of your ability to adopt the vocabulary of either an aristocrat or a criminal, choose to speak as plainly and directly as possible. You will seldom charm someone by plain talk, but you will also not alienate by mangled politesse or dated slang. Alienating a ruler, I need not tell you, can be the last mistake one can make.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
与统治者交谈的礼仪<BR>
埃莉斯特拉·利根 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
因为规则如此复杂，利害关系如此重大，许多人一想到与有头衔的贵族交谈就会不寒而栗。首先，正确称呼他们很重要，因为正如没有人喜欢被叫错名字，也没有人喜欢被叫错头衔。问题在于，在高岩，贵族传统因地区而异。基本规则如下：<BR><BR>
高岩有八个王国，分别位于以下区域：北角、匕落、断舵、卡姆洛恩、法伦、永恒、途歇和杰汉纳。如果一位女性统治这些地区之一，她被称为女王。女王的丈夫和国王的妻子不一定同等地位 -- 他们自己可能不是国王或女王。他们的孩子是王子和公主。他们的孙子也是王子和公主。如果男性统治者去世，他的妻子将获得王太后头衔，前提是尚无王太后。像所有规则一样，也有例外。最近匕落发生了一个显著例外，当利桑杜斯国王去世时。在大多数地区，他的妻子米尼塞拉不会成为匕落的王太后，因为利桑杜斯的母亲、遗孀努尔法加还活着。但在匕落，允许有两人拥有相同头衔。因此，努尔法加和米尼塞拉都拥有王太后头衔。<BR><BR>
如果一位女性统治者（与丈夫地位不等）去世，没有与王太后对应的男性词。女王的鳏夫通常会获得另一个头衔，或较低级的家族头衔，或由子女授予的头衔。在高岩历史上，曾有几位男子在妻子去世后，从被称为国王沦落为被称为先生。<BR><BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>Exegesis of Merid-Nunda<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
<BR>
by Phrastus of Elinhir<BR><BR>
<BR>
Truly, the Tract of Merid-Nunda is one of the strangest and least understood works of mythohistory that has come down to us from the early First Era. It exists only in partial manuscript form, a single copy of which resides in the library of the Imperial University at Cyrodiil City.<BR>
<BR>
The problem of understanding the Tract of Merid-Nunda is twofold: First, the extant document is clearly part of a larger work, drawn from seemingly somewhere in the middle, and without the preceding and following portions of the work we have little context for the part that remains. Second, the Tract is written in a peculiar argot that employs Ayleid phrases in a late Nedic syntax, including many words of unknown origin that don't appear in any other source.<BR>
<BR>
However, working outward from fragments previously translated by Wenegrus Monhana and Herminia Cinna, I believe I can shed some new light on certain key passages in this mysterious manuscript. Our format shall be to provide the translation of each passage, followed by my interpretation of its meaning.<BR>
<BR>
"... were known as the Nine Coruscations, who followed the parabolas that led away from Magnus. Merid-Nunda was of these Sisters, as was Mnemo-Li, as was Xero-Lyg, as was ..."<BR>
<BR>
This appears to identify the "Daedric Prince" Meridia with the so-called Star-Orphans, those Anuic ur-entities that separated from Magnus when that Divine withdrew from the creation of the Aurbis. The best-known of these Star-Orphans is probably Mnemoli the Blue Star, who is associated with un-time events, and was said to be visible even in the daytime sky at the time of the Dragon Break.<BR>
<BR>
"... thus we call upon Cenedelin to bind the earth, as we speak to Merid-Nunda regarding the light, for she is the scintilla that fears not darkness, and swims the waves of pull and spin ..."<BR>
<BR>
For the Ayleids, of course, Light was one of the four elements of creation, and this passage seems to confirm that Meridia was the personification of Light to the Wild Elves. Though I am certain of this passage's translation, I confess the meaning of the final phrases eludes me.<BR>
<BR>
The next passage was quite difficult, but its translation adds an entirely new episode to our accounts of the Dawn Era:<BR>
<BR>
"The Lords of the Chaos-Realms chided Merid-Nunda for her trespass and bade her return to Aurbis, claiming all existing spheres as their own. But Merid-Nunda formed of her substance a great drag-lens, and the light of Magnus was bent thereby. The rays [carved? focused?] a new sphere from the chaos, which Merid-Nunda, [laughing? sparkling?], did claim for her own."<BR>
<BR>
This appears to recount the origin of the Colored Rooms, as Meridia's Oblivion realm is known, seemingly formed directly out of the stuff of chaos by an act of divine will.
And finally:<BR>
<BR>
"... thus does Merid-Nunda [ride? slide?] across the rainbow road from end to end, at one end stretching the dragon, at the other end compressing him ..."<BR>
<BR>
A curious passage indeed. The "dragon," of course, traditionally refers to the Divine we know as Akatosh, the God of Time. This seems to suggest that by traveling the "rainbow road" (a reference to the prismatic refraction of light?), Meridia can in some sense alter the rate at which time flows forward.<BR>
<BR>
Altering the "speed" of time? Is this merely an absurd conceit of the late Ayleid sorcerer-priests, or a genuine insight into the nature of one of the least-understood Daedric Princes?<BR>
<BR>
Who can say?<BR><BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>美瑞德-南妲释经<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
<BR>
艾林希尔的弗拉斯图斯 著<BR><BR>
<BR>
的确，《美瑞德-南妲论著》是从第一纪元早期流传下来的最奇怪、最不被理解的神话历史作品之一。它仅以部分手稿形式存在，唯一一份副本保存在西罗帝尔城帝国大学的图书馆中。<BR>
<BR>
理解《美瑞德-南妲论著》有两个困难：第一，现存文件显然是一部更大作品的一部分，似乎是从中间某处抽取的，没有前后文，我们对残存部分几乎没有背景理解。第二，该论著用一种奇特的行话写成，在晚期尼德语法的框架中使用亚历德短语，包括许多来源不明的词，这些词不出现在任何其他资料中。<BR>
<BR>
然而，从韦内格鲁斯·蒙哈纳和赫米尼娅·辛纳先前翻译的片段出发，我相信我能为这份神秘手稿中的某些关键段落提供一些新见解。我们的格式是提供每个段落的翻译，然后是我的解释。<BR>
<BR>
“......被称为九曜，她们沿着偏离玛格努斯的抛物线而行。美瑞德-南妲是这些姐妹之一，如妮莫-莉，如克瑟罗-利格，如......”<BR>
<BR>
这似乎将“迪德拉大君”美瑞蒂亚与所谓的“星之孤儿”联系起来，即当玛格努斯神祇从奥比斯的创造中撤出时，与玛格努斯分离的那些阿努伊原始实体。这些星之孤儿中最著名的可能是蓝星妮莫莉，她与非时间事件相关联，据说在龙破期间即使在白天的天空也能看到。<BR>
<BR>
“......因此我们召唤塞内德林来束缚大地，当我们向美瑞德-南妲谈及光时，因为她是那不怕黑暗的火花，在牵引与旋转的波浪中游弋......”<BR>
<BR>
对亚历德人而言，光当然是创世四大元素之一，这段似乎证实了美瑞蒂亚对野精灵来说是光的化身。虽然我确信这段翻译无误，但我承认最后几句的含义让我困惑。<BR>
<BR>
下一段相当困难，但它的翻译为我们的黎明纪元记载增添了一个全新的篇章：<BR>
<BR>
“混沌领域的领主们责备美瑞德-南妲的擅闯，命令她返回奥比斯，声称所有现存领域都属于他们。但美瑞德-南妲用自己的物质形成了一个巨大的拖曳透镜，玛格努斯的光因而被弯曲。光线从混沌中[雕刻？聚焦？]出一个新的领域，美瑞德-南妲[笑着？闪耀着？]将其据为己有。”<BR>
<BR>
这似乎讲述了彩色房间的起源，即美瑞蒂亚的湮灭领域之名，似乎是由神圣意志直接从混沌物质中形成的。
最后：<BR>
<BR>
“......因此美瑞德-南妲[骑？滑？]行于彩虹之路，从一端到另一端，在一端拉伸龙，在另一端压缩他......”<BR>
<BR>
确实是一段奇特的文字。“龙”传统上当然指我们称为阿卡托什的时间之神。这似乎表明，通过行走“彩虹之路”（暗指光的棱镜折射？），美瑞蒂亚在某种意义上可以改变时间向前流动的速率。<BR>
<BR>
改变时间的“速度”？这仅仅是晚期亚历德巫师祭司的荒谬幻想，还是对最不为人所知的迪德拉大君之一本质的真知灼见？<BR>
<BR>
谁能说得清？<BR><BR>"""

1. 昔有众族居于列省，傲特莫之强主威震四方，歧莫（丹莫先祖）起而抗之，誓不再为其奴。
2. 亦有兽人（奥斯莫）居于密林，其力如石，其心如火，与歧莫为邻。
3. 歧莫中有勇士名阿尔迪斯，其智谋得自梅法拉（蜘蛛大君）之启示，
4. 遂于暗影中潜行，如风过草，无声无迹。
5. 阿尔迪斯入林深处，见古树盘根，中有灵光闪烁，似有灵物低语。
6. 其心受感，遂伏地祷之，愿得指引。<br><br>
7. 忽有异象显于前，如火焰凝结，如群星坠地。
8. 阿尔迪斯见之，知此乃先祖之灵，示以古道，
9. 且告之：“尔当东行，寻新天新地，梅法拉已为你开路。”
10. 时有木精灵（波斯莫）居于林间，其性机敏，闻歧莫之来，惧而聚之。
11. 木精灵之首领与阿尔迪斯会于圣树下，各陈其志。
12. 阿尔迪斯以诚相告，木精灵乃盟其约，誓不相攻。<br><br>
13. 自此，歧莫与木精灵共守此约，如林中之枝，同根共土。
14. 然其欢未久，有暗影自西方来，名曰卡吉特（猫人）之盗匪。
15. 其掠其民，毁其田，歧莫与木精灵共御之。
16. 此时，木精灵之地有一古城名雷尔希尔，乃卡莫兰王朝之旧都，内有迪德拉之遗物。
17. 阿尔迪斯入其城，见壁上刻有远古之约，述及众灵之盟。
18. 其文曰：“凡血族者，皆可为兄弟。”
19. 阿尔迪斯默然良久，知此约乃梅法拉所立，欲借木精灵之力以抗傲特莫。
20. 遂与木精灵共誓，尊梅法拉为护佑，以雷尔希尔为盟约之枢。<br><br>
21. 阿尔迪斯得梅法拉之助，教木精灵以暗影之术，使其勇力倍增。
22. 自此，木精灵与歧莫并辔而行，凡傲特莫之军至，皆败退而去。
23. 阿尔迪斯之名威震四方，其智勇皆托于梅法拉之荫庇。
24. 然战事久持，歧莫之力渐疲，木精灵亦有伤亡。
25. 雷尔希尔之木精灵苦于粮绝，遂求助于阿尔迪斯。
26. 阿尔迪斯乃召歧莫之众，往雷尔希尔之东，寻大先知维洛斯所言之福地。
27. 维洛斯曾言：“东方有地，名曰晨风，乃我等应许之邦。” 今歧莫心向往之。<br><br>
28. 阿尔迪斯率众东行，木精灵中愿从者亦随其后。
29. 行至林海之边，维洛斯显圣于前，手持火焰之杖，指其前路。<br><br>
30. 其行如电，其声如雷，
31. 破山裂石，开道于荒原之中。
32. 歧莫之众欢呼雀跃，颂维洛斯之名。
33. 然傲特莫追兵至，战鼓再起。
34. 阿尔迪斯与维洛斯并肩御敌，血染沙场。<br><br>
35. 梅法拉暗中施法，使敌之弓弦断裂，刃钝甲裂。<br><br>
36. 维洛斯高举圣石，光照四方，傲特莫之军目眩神迷。
37. 歧莫趁势反攻，大破敌军，自此得保东行之途。
38. 歧莫终抵晨风之岸，木精灵亦得安居于绿野。
39. 两族立石为界，盟约永固，互通有无。<br><br>
40. 维洛斯教导歧莫以律法，梅法拉则授其暗影之秘，以保万世太平。<br><br>
41. 凡触犯此约者，必遭暗影噬心，永堕虚无。
42. 雷尔希尔之木精灵，自此与歧莫分离，各守其土，然心仍相通。<br><br>
43. 木精灵之酋长，常与雷尔希尔之祭司通使，共祭梅法拉。
44. 歧莫亦每岁遣使至雷尔希尔，献以宝石与香木，以续前约。
45. 梅法拉之蛛网笼罩两地，其丝如命线，相连不息。<br><br>
46. 木精灵之乐声，常与歧莫之鼓韵相应，如林风与山泉相和。
47. 昔有伊里斯克之贤者，夜观星象，见双月交会，知大战将起。
48. 傲特莫之残部聚于北境，欲雪前耻，再伐晨风。
49. 于是歧莫再祷于众迪德拉，求其护佑，梅法拉与阿祖拉皆垂听之。<br><br>
50. 终得两神赐福，歧莫与木精灵共盟，以永恒之约，蔽护晨风之地，直至日月同辉，万世不移。<BR>"""

第一章<BR><BR>
1: 初，有大君谕众精魂，居于幽邃之殿，其言传于诸灵。
2: 大君之音如雷鸣，其势震于四野。<BR><BR>
3: 大君立约于众灵，以血为印，以火为证。
4: 然有逆者起于其间，欲裂此约，窃其权柄。
5: 众灵争辩，各执其词，扰大君之安。
6: 其居所如火炉，其石熔为河。
7: 有智者开其门，见诸异象，示以后世。
8: 迪德拉之君启其口，告以列祖之密。<BR><BR>
9: 其名崔尼马克，乃傲特莫之强主，持刚毅之盾，执审判之剑。
10: 彼为傲特莫之冠冕，崔尼马克之荣光。
11: 然崔尼马克之心偏于骄傲，遂轻傲特莫之律法。<BR><BR>
12: 奥斯莫之民（即兽人）居于利兰德瑞尔，其地为荒芜之山。
13: 利兰德瑞尔之民呼告崔尼马克，求其指引。
14: 崔尼马克垂听其求，然其心已蒙垢，不见正道。
15: 彼君之傲触怒傲特莫，遂降灾罚于其民。
16: 利兰德瑞尔之城遭火焚，血漫其街。<BR><BR><BR>
17: 其民如石，其城如灰，利兰德瑞尔化为废墟。
18: 荒山之民呼号，求大君之救。
19: 维洛斯至其门，阿祖拉显圣于前，告以傲特莫之王当倾覆。
20: 阿祖拉赐维洛斯异象，示以迪德拉之约。
21: 维洛斯受命，知傲特莫之道已腐，遂弃其城，率众入旷野，寻新天新地。<BR><BR>
22: 维洛斯启其民，去旧邦，行于荒原。
23: 民随其行，弃傲特莫之俗。
24: 维洛斯立新约，以阿祖拉为盾，以波耶西亚为剑。
25: 维洛斯祷于阿祖拉，求赐避祸之道。
26: 又得示于泰尔伽，知洛克汗之心为诸灵所逐。
27: 维洛斯呼告奥姆希维，三神之名响彻旷野。<BR><BR>
28: 维洛斯述迪德拉之威，言利兰德瑞尔之覆。
29: 荒山之民闻其言，惧而战栗，不敢违逆。
30: 奥斯莫之众趋阿祖拉，求其庇护。
31: 彼众弃迪德拉之邪术，归正途。
32: 然崔尼马克之影犹存，傲特莫之威未绝。<BR><BR>
33: 维洛斯导奥斯莫离迪德拉，而奥斯莫仍忆旧主。
34: 崔尼马克之旧部追维洛斯，欲擒之。
35: 奥斯莫呼崔尼马克之名，然波耶西亚已入其心。
36: 波耶西亚吞崔尼马克，化其身为物，吐之于野。<BR><BR>
37: 奥斯莫见其主为所辱，遂恸哭于地。
38: 波耶西亚佑维洛斯，迪德拉之力助其行。
39: 崔尼马克败落，坠为凡物。

41: 其民流离，其血成河，其地成荒。
42: 兽人之裔自此分，散于列邦。<BR><BR>
第二章<BR><BR>
1: 维洛斯行于野，波耶西亚导其前。<BR><BR><BR>
2: 阿祖拉与波耶西亚共语，以约示维洛斯。
3: 阿祖拉告之：“尔当离傲特莫，往东之地。”
4: 崔尼马克之残躯化为暗影，其光不再。
5: 维洛斯之民得新地，号曰歧莫，自此别于傲特莫。
6: 彼处有山有谷，有水有木，丰饶如园。<BR><BR>
7: 崔尼马克更名为马拉卡斯，乃受诅之迪德拉。
8: 其民（奥斯莫）受其咒，身如石，心如火。
9: 然阿祖拉之光照临歧莫，赐其智慧与勇力。
10: 维洛斯建塔于山巅，以阿祖拉之名号令众民。
11: 马拉卡斯怒，欲毁歧莫，然维洛斯
祷于上主，得脱其难。
12: 歧莫立石为证，铭约于碑，世代遵守。
13: 维洛斯复告之：“尔等当守变化之道，即歧姆之秘。”
14: 众民奉泰尔伽为圣，敬而畏之。<BR><BR>
15: 维洛斯之教传于奥辛纽姆（兽人城）。
16: 然傲特莫之王居泰尔·阿凯斯，窥视其地。
17: 傲特莫欲复其威，举兵伐歧莫。
18: 泰尔·阿凯斯之君呼崔尼马克之名，求其助。
19: 然崔尼马克已死，其名徒存，奥斯莫不响应。<BR><BR>
20: 维洛斯召迪德拉之力，以御傲特莫。
21: 维洛斯入奥辛纽姆，
22: 梅法拉示维洛斯以诡计，
23: 遂破傲特莫之军。
24: 波耶西亚导歧莫入应许之地。
25: 其地称为雷思戴恩（即晨风）。<BR><BR><BR><BR>
26: 维洛斯遵阿祖拉与波耶西亚之命，立新律。
27: 其律严明，民皆从之。
28: 阿祖拉赐福歧莫，使其昌盛。<BR><BR>
29: 梅法拉亦授其秘术，教以暗影与机巧。
30: 歧莫之民自此繁茂，如星撒于夜空。
31. 然利兰德瑞尔之遗民仍怀旧怨，<BR><BR><BR>
32. 迪德拉之君便诱其心，使其攻歧莫。
33. 迪德拉言：“尔等本为奥斯莫，何归歧莫？”
34. 然梅法拉先知其计，使歧莫得脱。
35. 梅法拉启歧莫之眼，使其识破诡诈。
36. 歧莫与奥斯莫自此分途，各居其地。
37. 歧莫往东，奥斯莫留西，永为邻邦亦为敌。
38. 阿祖拉终护歧莫，使其不再受傲特莫之轭。
39. 歧莫得自由，立国于晨风，名曰丹莫。
40. 奥斯莫（兽人）亦存于世，虽遭傲特莫之轻，仍守其族。
41. 歧莫与奥斯莫之怨，永世不绝。
42. 歧莫既得傲特莫之地，奥斯莫亦得其所，各遵其神，各居其邦。
43. 此即歧莫之史，乃维洛斯与其民所立之约，永铭于晨风之野。<BR>"""

Expanding Magicka: Revised

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Expanding Magicka: A Revised Edition<BR> 
Esling Serrenan, Breton <BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Herein resides the amalgam of a life of research, the results of which sprawl before you in this volume. Up until this point, very little has been definitively known about the properties and rules by which the various - for various they are - magicks are governed. Through my years of research and experimentation, I have determined at least a few of the ways magic and its properties may be utilized in everyday life. Furthermore, I have hypothesized a number of alternative and perhaps even greater uses for magic, and I have written them here for further investigation by my successors.<BR> 
<BR>
Editor's Note: While the author of this work seems arrogant, and despite the fact that a number of his hypotheses have proven incorrect, this text still merits study by any fledgling wizard for its worthy lessons in how manipulation of the magicks fell into common practice over the years. This book, regardless of its shortcomings, became the basis for a great deal of work regarding the understanding of magic and its handling. Remember to read both this work and my notes with an examining - not merely an accepting - eye, and discover the truth for yourself as you delve deeper into the understanding of the natural world.<BR> 
<BR>
Section One: An Examination of Magic Crystals and Their Properties<BR> 
<BR>
In the past, I have hypothesized that the rare, glowing crystals found deep inside a select few ancient, subterranean complexes might be the source of magical powers, and that by manipulating them, we might uncover some of this world's greatest mysteries. After an incredibly long and grueling series of experiments, I have determined that the very essence of Tamriel's arcane powers flow through these conduits. Much like the sun and stars, these crystals are sources of magicka.<BR> 
<BR>
I have discovered that these crystals exude a deep, primal power. As a would-be conjurer or wizard moves closer to these crystals, he begins to feel robust boost to his skills and abilities to cast a number of spells, suggesting that the crystals in some way bring the caster closer to magicka itself. It is as though the wizard's soul is bound more closely to the natural world. I believe that through the utilization of these crystals, new and more powerful spells might be possible.<BR> 
<BR>
It will be of great interest to the reader to learn that these crystals are portable, in that their positive properties seem to last for a surprisingly long time. One characteristic, the crystal's ability to bind to a soul, has an indefinite half-life. I have been unable to determine whether or not this property dissipates over time.<BR> 
<BR>
Editor's Note: While the author is not entirely on the mark in his belief that these crystals are actual sources of magicka, he was correct to note that they enhance existing magical powers. Our sun, Magnus, and the night-sky's stars are rifts into Oblivion, allowing magicka to pour through. However, these gems seem to absorb magicka; thus, any passerby might feel "invigorated" when nearing a crystal. It is believed that these gems gather power regardless of location, and they are unhindered by physical blockades; indeed, some of the most powerful sources of magicka can be found deep underground, whereas surface crystals may have little stored magicka.<BR>
<BR>
As most of my readers understand by now, the manipulation of the energies produced by these gems serves as the backbone of modern magic and its applications. Furthermore, the author noted that these stones have a strong attraction to the soul. Basing their work largely on the author's information, conjurers have learned to use this property to shackle the souls of Daedra inside of these crystals and their more refined derivatives. Indeed, these fittingly named soulstones, produced by tuning the energy waves emitted by the gems, have become a staple to contemporary conjurers and enchanters alike.<BR> 
<BR>
It is also important to note that prolonged exposure to the unrefined crystals can have some unfortunate negative side-effects. Those who work too long with these gems can suffer irrevocable damage to their reasoning schemas. It is hypothesized that partially unrefined or poorly refined soulstones are the reason so many young conjurers turn to necromancy, relying increasingly upon their summoned minions and secluding themselves from society. Similar isolating tendencies have been observed in enchanters, the other crystal-dependents.<BR> 
<BR>
Section Two: A Deconstruction of Necromancy and Conjuration 
<BR>
While some might argue that there is a basic difference between "vile necromancy" and "pious conjuration" (or whatever you wish to call it), these two disciplines work through the same principles: leashing and controlling a spirit. In both cases, unfavorable results may arise; most commonly in these situations, the caster of the spell merely loses control of his creation and is maimed or killed by what he has conjured. However, it has been reported that sometimes a caster can accidentally use his own soul instead of one summoned from the twisting nether. When this happens, the caster's soul usually tears itself apart as it tries to inhabit two bodies; human souls have also appeared to fuse with those of lesser Daedra. In both cases, the result is a very painful death for the conjurer.<BR> 
<BR>
First, I will discuss direct conjuration, as it is the easier and socially more acceptable form of these arts. Essentially, conjuration works through a complex manipulation of magicka by which a portal into Oblivion opens and (hopefully) the desired creature is pulled through; in most cases, this process also involves binding the will of the summoned to that of the summoner. I believe that this "portal" is actually a slit momentarily created between our realm and Oblivion, one quite similar to those in the skies. Fortunately, this slit seems to be small enough that it can mend itself, unlike those that exist far above. Were it not for this self-repairing property, our world would have long since fallen to the violent hordes of Oblivion. However, in some cases a summoner may create too large a slit in the dimensional fabric, allowing more Daedra into our world than desired. An excessively large tear can result from either weak dimensional fabric or from the over-exuberance of the spell-caster. 
<BR>
Necromancy is somewhat more difficult because it requires that the summoner maintain a sphere of control over the spirit he has summoned; spirits tend to take a "real" form upon their entrance into our world (in the form of a scamp, a Dremora, etc), but necromancer's must prevent this by essentially shielding them from the world long enough to carry their spirits into inhabitable bodies. The spirits seem to prefer these available bodies to creating their own. The allure of necromancy comes in that these bodies may be placed under the control of caster (with many safeguards) long before the spirit inhabits them, creating an exceptionally strong bond of loyalty in the summoned to the summoner. Furthermore, these bonds do not require maintenance on the part of the caster, as is necessary for a conjurer; the bond between a necromantic creation and its master does not seem to have any chronological limitations.<BR> 
<BR>
Editor's Note: Here, the author presents the first of two contemporary views as to what conjuration actually is. The first, as he says, holds that Daedra and spirits are called forth by creating a miniature rift between our world and Oblivion. However, there is another theory that holds that the Daedra exist in our world already, that magicka itself is in fact separated particles of Daedra. Proponents of this idea claim that conjuration is merely the amalgamation of particles into the desired creation (some go as far as to claim that this is how all magicka actually works). The attraction of this idea spawns in that it better explains how one summons bound weapons and armor, a subject left untouched by this author. The idea that there are random pieces of equipment simply floating around in Oblivion - as the author indirectly implies through his theories - is indeed a strange one.<BR> 
<BR>
Part Three: Destruction, Restoration, Alteration<BR> 
<BR>
I have put all three of these schools of magicka together because fundamentally they are the same; they all work off of the same basic principles. Essentially, restoration is alteration that heals its target, and destruction is alteration that damages its target. Alteration itself is a relatively neutral form of the altering magicks.<BR> 
<BR>
I will first discuss those magicks falling under the school of destruction, these being the simplest -- and thus most deadly, as this allows for great power -- magicks to perform. The creation of a destructive spell functions by transforming magicka directly into a deadly physical form, such as fire or ice. The magicka almost always takes the form of some naturally occurring phenomenon in nature, following the desires of the caster. The exceptions to this are spells affecting the mental or physical faculties of their targets without actually causing physical harm, such as those which drain the willpower or intellect. Unfortunately, I have been unable to break down exactly how these spells work.<BR> 
<BR>
The second school of magicka falling under this section is restoration. All of these spells basically work as the antithesis of their destructive brethren. Restorative spells change magicka such that it repairs and purges damaged or diseased flesh, transforming into anti-venoms or even into new skin, muscles, or bones. I have heard rumors of powerful mages who can even resurrect entirely dead creatures, bringing their subjects fully back to life; they return not as undead, instead coming back as they were before their deaths. These rumors, however, are unsubstantiated.<BR> 
<BR>
The last - and most difficult - branch of magicka falling under this section is the school of alteration. I call it the most difficult because the spells themselves are both varied and abstract in nature. Let us examine, for example, the "burden" spells. I have seen the same spell performed numerous ways: some mages deaden the legs, some place mind-weights upon their enemies, and some slow the hearts and blood of their foes. Certainly, this tends to vary from mage to mage; an illusionist might opt to use a mind-weight whereas a battlemage would tend to use a leg-deadening spell. Regardless, you can see that each can be performed many different ways, and some could hardly be classified even as typical alteration spells. I will not go into any greater detail in this volume.<BR> 
<BR>
Editor's Note: The applications of these spells are nearly limitless, so I will emphasize the importance of what the author is saying. Most sorcerers and wizards agree that alteration is the field of magic most open to differing methods of execution; these differences, while being partially dependant on the specialization of its caster, also vary somewhat from region to region. Most of the races developed a different method for using and casting alteration spells. For example, tribal Khajiiti have used alteration spells to thicken or thin their fur depending on the season, whereas some reclusive Nords have been known to change ice to fire to keep warm during the nights. The point I am making is that these spells are by far the most applicable to everyday life and that they are indeed quite indispensable.<BR> 
<BR>
Regarding what the author says about how these spells are actually performed, it is difficult to refute or affirm his claims. Most mages perform their spells through rote memorization, hardly thinking about what they are actually doing, and so they hardly notice their own tendencies; magical prowess feels inborn, not learned. Despite the assertions made by the author, few have devoted any real time to testing his theories, myself included. I would like to note, however, that most of these spells have applications primarily in living things, save for a few pure alteration spells (such as lock-breakers and the like), giving some credence to the author's ideas.<BR> 
<BR>
Volume two of this series contains information regarding the schools of illusion, mysticism, and some advice regarding the practice of magicka.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
拓展魔能：修订版<BR>
埃斯林·塞雷南，布莱顿人<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
本书汇集了我毕生研究的成果。迄今为止，对于各种 -- 它们确实是多种多样的 -- 魔法的性质和规则，人们所知甚少。通过多年的研究和实验，我至少确定了魔法及其特性在日常生活中有哪些应用方式。此外，我还提出了许多替代性的、甚至可能更伟大的魔法用途，并将它们写在这里，供后人进一步研究。<BR>
<BR>
编者注：虽然本书作者似乎很傲慢，尽管他的一些假设已被证明是错误的，但本书仍值得任何初出茅庐的巫师学习，因为它提供了关于魔法操控如何逐渐成为普遍实践的有价值教训。这本书，无论有何缺陷，都已成为大量关于理解魔法及处理魔法工作的基础。记住，要用审视 -- 而非仅仅接受 -- 的眼光来阅读本书和我的注释，并在深入理解自然世界的过程中自行发现真理。<BR>
<BR>
第一节：魔法水晶及其特性研究<BR>
<BR>
过去，我曾假设，在少数古代地下建筑深处发现的稀有发光水晶可能是魔法力量的来源，通过操控它们，我们或许能揭开这个世界的一些最大奥秘。经过一系列极其漫长和艰苦的实验，我确定泰姆瑞尔神秘力量的本质正流经这些管道。就像太阳和星星一样，这些水晶是魔能的来源。<BR>
<BR>
我发现这些水晶散发着深沉、原始的力量。当一名准召唤师或巫师靠近这些水晶时，他会感到自己的技能和施展多种法术的能力得到显著提升，这表明水晶在某种程度上使施法者更接近魔能本身。仿佛巫师之魂与自然世界联系得更紧密了。我相信，通过利用这些水晶，或许可以创造出新的、更强大的法术。<BR>
<BR>
读者会非常感兴趣地了解到，这些水晶是可移动的，它们的有益特性似乎能持续令人惊讶的长时间。其中一种特性 -- 水晶束缚灵魂的能力 -- 具有无限期的半衰期。我无法确定这种特性是否会随时间消散。<BR>
<BR>
编者注：虽然作者认为这些水晶是真正的魔能源泉并不完全正确，但他注意到它们能增强现有的魔法力量，这一点是正确的。我们的太阳 -- 玛格努斯 -- 和夜空中的星星是通往湮灭的裂隙，让魔能得以涌入。然而，这些宝石似乎会吸收魔能；因此，任何过路人在靠近水晶时可能会感到“精力充沛”。据信，这些宝石无论身在何处都能聚集力量，不受物理障碍的阻碍；事实上，一些最强大的魔能源头可以在地下深处找到，而地表的水晶可能储存的魔能很少。<BR>
<BR>
正如我的大多数读者已经了解的，对这些宝石产生的能量的操控是现代魔法及其应用的支柱。此外，作者指出，这些石头对灵魂有很强的吸引力。召唤师们主要基于作者的信息，学会利用这一特性将迪德拉的灵魂束缚在这些水晶及其更精炼的衍生物中。确实，这些恰如其名的灵魂石 -- 通过调谐宝石释放的能量波制成 -- 已成为当代召唤师和附魔师的重要工具。<BR>
<BR>
同样重要的是，长期接触未精炼的水晶可能会产生一些不幸的负面副作用。那些长时间处理这些宝石的人可能会对其推理能力造成不可逆的损害。据推测，部分未精炼或精炼不良的灵魂石是导致许多年轻召唤师转向死灵法术的原因，他们越来越依赖召唤的仆从，并与社会隔绝。在附魔师 -- 另一类依赖水晶的群体 -- 中也观察到了类似的孤立倾向。<BR>
<BR>
第二节：死灵法术与召唤术解析
<BR>
虽然有些人可能会认为“邪恶的死灵法术”和“虔诚的召唤术”（或随便你怎么称呼）之间存在根本区别，但这两种学科都是通过相同的原理运作的：束缚和控制灵魂。在这两种情况下，都可能出现不利结果；最常见的是，施法者失去对其造物的控制，并被自己召唤的东西致残或杀死。然而，也有报道称，有时施法者会意外地使用自己的灵魂，而不是从扭曲的冥界召唤来的灵魂。当这种情况发生时，施法者的灵魂通常会在试图同时占据两具身体时撕裂自己；人类的灵魂也曾出现与低级迪德拉融合的情况。在这两种情况下，结果对召唤师来说都是极其痛苦的死亡。<BR>
<BR>
首先，我将讨论直接召唤术，因为这是这些技艺中更简单、在社会上更易接受的形式。基本上，召唤术通过复杂的魔能操控运作，由此打开一扇通往湮灭的门户，并（希望）将所需生物拉过来；在大多数情况下，这一过程还涉及将被召唤者的意志与召唤者的意志绑定。我认为这个“门户”实际上是在我们的领域与湮灭之间短暂撕裂的一道裂隙，与天空中的那些裂隙非常相似。幸运的是，这道裂隙似乎足够小，可以自行愈合，不像高空中那些裂隙。若非这种自我修复特性，我们的世界早就落入湮灭的暴力大军手中了。然而，在某些情况下，召唤者可能会在维度织布上撕开过大的裂隙，让过多的迪德拉进入我们的世界。过大的撕裂可能是由薄弱的维度织布或施法者过于热情造成的。
<BR>
死灵法术则更难一些，因为它要求召唤者维持对其召唤之灵的支配领域；灵魂在进入我们的世界时往往会采取“真实”的形态（以劣魔、德雷莫拉等形式出现），但死灵法师必须通过将灵魂与现实世界隔绝足够长时间，以将灵魂引入可居住的身体来阻止这一点。灵魂似乎更喜欢这些现成的身体，而不是自己创造身体。死灵法术的诱惑在于，这些身体可以在灵魂入住之前很久就被置于施法者的控制之下（有诸多保障），从而在被召唤者与召唤者之间建立异常强大的忠诚纽带。此外，这些纽带不需要施法者像召唤师那样进行维护；死灵造物与其主人之间的纽带似乎没有时间上的限制。<BR>
<BR>
编者注：此处，作者呈现了关于召唤术实质的两种当代观点中的第一种。第一种，如他所说，认为迪德拉和灵魂是通过在我们的世界与湮灭之间制造微型裂隙来召唤的。然而，还有另一种理论认为，迪德拉已经存在于我们的世界中，而魔能本身实际上是迪德拉分离出的粒子。这种观点的支持者声称，召唤术只是将粒子合并为所需的造物（有些人甚至声称这就是所有魔能实际运作的方式）。这种观点的吸引力在于，它能更好地解释如何召唤绑定武器和盔甲，而本书作者未触及这一主题。那些认为湮灭中只是漂浮着随机装备碎片 -- 正如作者通过其理论间接暗示的那样 -- 的想法确实很奇怪。<BR>
<BR>
第三节：毁灭、恢复、变化<BR>
<BR>
我将这三个魔能学派放在一起，是因为它们本质上是相同的；它们都基于相同的基本原则。基本上，恢复系是治愈目标的改变，而毁灭系是伤害目标的改变。改变系本身是一种相对中性的改变魔法形式。<BR>
<BR>
我将首先讨论毁灭学派下的魔法，它们是最简单的 -- 因此也最致命，因为这允许强大的力量 -- 来施展。毁灭法术的创造通过将魔能直接转化为致命的物理形态来实现，如火或冰。魔能几乎总是按照施法者的意愿，采取自然界中某种自然现象的形式。例外的是那些影响目标精神或身体机能而不造成实际物理伤害的法术，如那些吸取意志力或智力的法术。不幸的是，我无法确切解析这些法术是如何运作的。<BR>
<BR>
本节中的第二个魔能学派是恢复系。这些法术基本上与毁灭系法术的作用相反。恢复法术改变魔能，使其修复和净化受损或患病的肉体，转化为抗毒剂，甚至转化为新的皮肤、肌肉或骨骼。我听说过强大法师甚至能复活完全死亡的生物的传闻，使目标完全恢复生命；他们不是作为亡灵返回，而是恢复死前的状态。然而，这些传闻未经证实。<BR>
<BR>
本节中最后一个 -- 也是最困难的 -- 魔能分支是变化学派。我认为它最困难，因为法术本身既多变又抽象。例如，让我们看看“负重”法术。我曾见过同一种法术以多种方式施展：有些法师麻痹腿部，有些在敌人身上施加心灵负重，有些则减缓敌人的心跳和血流。当然，这往往因法师而异；幻术师可能会选择使用心灵负重，而战斗法师则倾向于使用腿部麻痹法术。无论如何，你可以看到每一种法术都有多种施展方式，有些甚至难以归类为典型的变化法术。我不在本卷中详述。<BR>
<BR>
编者注：这些法术的应用几乎是无限的，所以我要强调作者所说的重要性。大多数术士和巫师都认为变化系是魔法领域中最开放、执行方式最多样化的领域；这些差异，虽然部分取决于施法者的专长，也因地区而异。大多数种族都开发了不同的使用和施展变化法术的方法。例如，部落的卡吉特会根据季节使用变化法术来增厚或减薄它们的毛皮，而一些隐居的诺德人已知会将冰变成火来在夜间取暖。我要指出的是，这些法术远比其他法术更适用于日常生活，而且它们确实不可或缺。<BR>
<BR>
关于作者对这些法术如何实际施展的说法，很难反驳或证实他的主张。大多数法师通过死记硬背来施法，几乎不思考自己实际在做什么，因此他们几乎注意不到自己的倾向；魔法能力感觉是天生的，而非习得的。尽管作者提出了论断，但很少有人真正花时间测试他的理论，包括我自己。然而，我想指出，除了少数纯粹的变化法术（如开锁术之类）外，这些法术大多主要作用于生物，这给作者的观点提供了一些可信度。<BR>
<BR>
本系列第二卷包含关于幻术系、神秘系的信息，以及关于魔能实践的一些建议。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Expanding Magicka: A Revised Edition<BR> 
Esling Serrenan, Breton <BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Herein resides the amalgam of a life of research, the results of which sprawl before you in this volume. Up until this point, very little has been definitively known about the properties and rules by which the various - for various they are - magicks are governed. Through my years of research and experimentation, I have determined at least a few of the ways magic and its properties may be utilized in everyday life. Furthermore, I have hypothesized a number of alternative and perhaps even greater uses for magic, and I have written them here for further investigation by my successors.<BR> 
<BR>
Editor's Note: While the author of this work seems arrogant, and despite the fact that a number of his hypotheses have proven incorrect, this text still merits study by any fledgling wizard for its worthy lessons in how manipulation of the magicks fell into common practice over the years. This book, regardless of its shortcomings, became the basis for a great deal of work regarding the understanding of magic and its handling. Remember to read both this work and my notes with an examining - not merely an accepting - eye, and discover the truth for yourself as you delve deeper into the understanding of the natural world.<BR> 
<BR>
Section One: An Examination of Magic Crystals and Their Properties<BR> 
<BR>
In the past, I have hypothesized that the rare, glowing crystals found deep inside a select few ancient, subterranean complexes might be the source of magical powers, and that by manipulating them, we might uncover some of this world's greatest mysteries. After an incredibly long and grueling series of experiments, I have determined that the very essence of Tamriel's arcane powers flow through these conduits. Much like the sun and stars, these crystals are sources of magicka.<BR> 
<BR>
I have discovered that these crystals exude a deep, primal power. As a would-be conjurer or wizard moves closer to these crystals, he begins to feel robust boost to his skills and abilities to cast a number of spells, suggesting that the crystals in some way bring the caster closer to magicka itself. It is as though the wizard's soul is bound more closely to the natural world. I believe that through the utilization of these crystals, new and more powerful spells might be possible.<BR> 
<BR>
It will be of great interest to the reader to learn that these crystals are portable, in that their positive properties seem to last for a surprisingly long time. One characteristic, the crystal's ability to bind to a soul, has an indefinite half-life. I have been unable to determine whether or not this property dissipates over time.<BR> 
<BR>
Editor's Note: While the author is not entirely on the mark in his belief that these crystals are actual sources of magicka, he was correct to note that they enhance existing magical powers. Our sun, Magnus, and the night-sky's stars are rifts into Oblivion, allowing magicka to pour through. However, these gems seem to absorb magicka; thus, any passerby might feel "invigorated" when nearing a crystal. It is believed that these gems gather power regardless of location, and they are unhindered by physical blockades; indeed, some of the most powerful sources of magicka can be found deep underground, whereas surface crystals may have little stored magicka.<BR>
<BR>
As most of my readers understand by now, the manipulation of the energies produced by these gems serves as the backbone of modern magic and its applications. Furthermore, the author noted that these stones have a strong attraction to the soul. Basing their work largely on the author's information, conjurers have learned to use this property to shackle the souls of Daedra inside of these crystals and their more refined derivatives. Indeed, these fittingly named soulstones, produced by tuning the energy waves emitted by the gems, have become a staple to contemporary conjurers and enchanters alike.<BR> 
<BR>
It is also important to note that prolonged exposure to the unrefined crystals can have some unfortunate negative side-effects. Those who work too long with these gems can suffer irrevocable damage to their reasoning schemas. It is hypothesized that partially unrefined or poorly refined soulstones are the reason so many young conjurers turn to necromancy, relying increasingly upon their summoned minions and secluding themselves from society. Similar isolating tendencies have been observed in enchanters, the other crystal-dependents.<BR> 
<BR>
Section Two: A Deconstruction of Necromancy and Conjuration 
<BR>
While some might argue that there is a basic difference between "vile necromancy" and "pious conjuration" (or whatever you wish to call it), these two disciplines work through the same principles: leashing and controlling a spirit. In both cases, unfavorable results may arise; most commonly in these situations, the caster of the spell merely loses control of his creation and is maimed or killed by what he has conjured. However, it has been reported that sometimes a caster can accidentally use his own soul instead of one summoned from the twisting nether. When this happens, the caster's soul usually tears itself apart as it tries to inhabit two bodies; human souls have also appeared to fuse with those of lesser Daedra. In both cases, the result is a very painful death for the conjurer.<BR> 
<BR>
First, I will discuss direct conjuration, as it is the easier and socially more acceptable form of these arts. Essentially, conjuration works through a complex manipulation of magicka by which a portal into Oblivion opens and (hopefully) the desired creature is pulled through; in most cases, this process also involves binding the will of the summoned to that of the summoner. I believe that this "portal" is actually a slit momentarily created between our realm and Oblivion, one quite similar to those in the skies. Fortunately, this slit seems to be small enough that it can mend itself, unlike those that exist far above. Were it not for this self-repairing property, our world would have long since fallen to the violent hordes of Oblivion. However, in some cases a summoner may create too large a slit in the dimensional fabric, allowing more Daedra into our world than desired. An excessively large tear can result from either weak dimensional fabric or from the over-exuberance of the spell-caster. 
<BR>
Necromancy is somewhat more difficult because it requires that the summoner maintain a sphere of control over the spirit he has summoned; spirits tend to take a "real" form upon their entrance into our world (in the form of a scamp, a Dremora, etc), but necromancer's must prevent this by essentially shielding them from the world long enough to carry their spirits into inhabitable bodies. The spirits seem to prefer these available bodies to creating their own. The allure of necromancy comes in that these bodies may be placed under the control of caster (with many safeguards) long before the spirit inhabits them, creating an exceptionally strong bond of loyalty in the summoned to the summoner. Furthermore, these bonds do not require maintenance on the part of the caster, as is necessary for a conjurer; the bond between a necromantic creation and its master does not seem to have any chronological limitations.<BR> 
<BR>
Editor's Note: Here, the author presents the first of two contemporary views as to what conjuration actually is. The first, as he says, holds that Daedra and spirits are called forth by creating a miniature rift between our world and Oblivion. However, there is another theory that holds that the Daedra exist in our world already, that magicka itself is in fact separated particles of Daedra. Proponents of this idea claim that conjuration is merely the amalgamation of particles into the desired creation (some go as far as to claim that this is how all magicka actually works). The attraction of this idea spawns in that it better explains how one summons bound weapons and armor, a subject left untouched by this author. The idea that there are random pieces of equipment simply floating around in Oblivion - as the author indirectly implies through his theories - is indeed a strange one.<BR> 
<BR>
Part Three: Destruction, Restoration, Alteration<BR> 
<BR>
I have put all three of these schools of magicka together because fundamentally they are the same; they all work off of the same basic principles. Essentially, restoration is alteration that heals its target, and destruction is alteration that damages its target. Alteration itself is a relatively neutral form of the altering magicks.<BR> 
<BR>
I will first discuss those magicks falling under the school of destruction, these being the simplest -- and thus most deadly, as this allows for great power -- magicks to perform. The creation of a destructive spell functions by transforming magicka directly into a deadly physical form, such as fire or ice. The magicka almost always takes the form of some naturally occurring phenomenon in nature, following the desires of the caster. The exceptions to this are spells affecting the mental or physical faculties of their targets without actually causing physical harm, such as those which drain the willpower or intellect. Unfortunately, I have been unable to break down exactly how these spells work.<BR> 
<BR>
The second school of magicka falling under this section is restoration. All of these spells basically work as the antithesis of their destructive brethren. Restorative spells change magicka such that it repairs and purges damaged or diseased flesh, transforming into anti-venoms or even into new skin, muscles, or bones. I have heard rumors of powerful mages who can even resurrect entirely dead creatures, bringing their subjects fully back to life; they return not as undead, instead coming back as they were before their deaths. These rumors, however, are unsubstantiated.<BR> 
<BR>
The last - and most difficult - branch of magicka falling under this section is the school of alteration. I call it the most difficult because the spells themselves are both varied and abstract in nature. Let us examine, for example, the "burden" spells. I have seen the same spell performed numerous ways: some mages deaden the legs, some place mind-weights upon their enemies, and some slow the hearts and blood of their foes. Certainly, this tends to vary from mage to mage; an illusionist might opt to use a mind-weight whereas a battlemage would tend to use a leg-deadening spell. Regardless, you can see that each can be performed many different ways, and some could hardly be classified even as typical alteration spells. I will not go into any greater detail in this volume.<BR> 
<BR>
Editor's Note: The applications of these spells are nearly limitless, so I will emphasize the importance of what the author is saying. Most sorcerers and wizards agree that alteration is the field of magic most open to differing methods of execution; these differences, while being partially dependant on the specialization of its caster, also vary somewhat from region to region. Most of the races developed a different method for using and casting alteration spells. For example, tribal Khajiiti have used alteration spells to thicken or thin their fur depending on the season, whereas some reclusive Nords have been known to change ice to fire to keep warm during the nights. The point I am making is that these spells are by far the most applicable to everyday life and that they are indeed quite indispensable.<BR> 
<BR>
Regarding what the author says about how these spells are actually performed, it is difficult to refute or affirm his claims. Most mages perform their spells through rote memorization, hardly thinking about what they are actually doing, and so they hardly notice their own tendencies; magical prowess feels inborn, not learned. Despite the assertions made by the author, few have devoted any real time to testing his theories, myself included. I would like to note, however, that most of these spells have applications primarily in living things, save for a few pure alteration spells (such as lock-breakers and the like), giving some credence to the author's ideas.<BR> 
<BR>
Volume two of this series contains information regarding the schools of illusion, mysticism, and some advice regarding the practice of magicka.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
拓展魔能：修订版<BR>
埃斯林·塞雷南，布莱顿人<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
本书汇集了我毕生研究的成果。迄今为止，对于各种 -- 它们确实是多种多样的 -- 魔法的性质和规则，人们所知甚少。通过多年的研究和实验，我至少确定了魔法及其特性在日常生活中有哪些应用方式。此外，我还提出了许多替代性的、甚至可能更伟大的魔法用途，并将它们写在这里，供后人进一步研究。<BR>
<BR>
编者注：虽然本书作者似乎很傲慢，尽管他的一些假设已被证明是错误的，但本书仍值得任何初出茅庐的巫师学习，因为它提供了关于魔法操控如何逐渐成为普遍实践的有价值教训。这本书，无论有何缺陷，都已成为大量关于理解魔法及处理魔法工作的基础。记住，要用审视 -- 而非仅仅接受 -- 的眼光来阅读本书和我的注释，并在深入理解自然世界的过程中自行发现真理。<BR>
<BR>
第一节：魔法水晶及其特性研究<BR>
<BR>
过去，我曾假设，在少数古代地下建筑深处发现的稀有发光水晶可能是魔法力量的来源，通过操控它们，我们或许能揭开这个世界的一些最大奥秘。经过一系列极其漫长和艰苦的实验，我确定泰姆瑞尔神秘力量的本质正流经这些管道。就像太阳和星星一样，这些水晶是魔能的来源。<BR>
<BR>
我发现这些水晶散发着深沉、原始的力量。当一名准召唤师或巫师靠近这些水晶时，他会感到自己的技能和施展多种法术的能力得到显著提升，这表明水晶在某种程度上使施法者更接近魔能本身。仿佛巫师之魂与自然世界联系得更紧密了。我相信，通过利用这些水晶，或许可以创造出新的、更强大的法术。<BR>
<BR>
读者会非常感兴趣地了解到，这些水晶是可移动的，它们的有益特性似乎能持续令人惊讶的长时间。其中一种特性 -- 水晶束缚灵魂的能力 -- 具有无限期的半衰期。我无法确定这种特性是否会随时间消散。<BR>
<BR>
编者注：虽然作者认为这些水晶是真正的魔能源泉并不完全正确，但他注意到它们能增强现有的魔法力量，这一点是正确的。我们的太阳 -- 玛格努斯 -- 和夜空中的星星是通往湮灭的裂隙，让魔能得以涌入。然而，这些宝石似乎会吸收魔能；因此，任何过路人在靠近水晶时可能会感到“精力充沛”。据信，这些宝石无论身在何处都能聚集力量，不受物理障碍的阻碍；事实上，一些最强大的魔能源头可以在地下深处找到，而地表的水晶可能储存的魔能很少。<BR>
<BR>
正如我的大多数读者已经了解的，对这些宝石产生的能量的操控是现代魔法及其应用的支柱。此外，作者指出，这些石头对灵魂有很强的吸引力。召唤师们主要基于作者的信息，学会利用这一特性将迪德拉的灵魂束缚在这些水晶及其更精炼的衍生物中。确实，这些恰如其名的灵魂石 -- 通过调谐宝石释放的能量波制成 -- 已成为当代召唤师和附魔师的重要工具。<BR>
<BR>
同样重要的是，长期接触未精炼的水晶可能会产生一些不幸的负面副作用。那些长时间处理这些宝石的人可能会对其推理能力造成不可逆的损害。据推测，部分未精炼或精炼不良的灵魂石是导致许多年轻召唤师转向死灵法术的原因，他们越来越依赖召唤的仆从，并与社会隔绝。在附魔师 -- 另一类依赖水晶的群体 -- 中也观察到了类似的孤立倾向。<BR>
<BR>
第二节：死灵法术与召唤术解析
<BR>
虽然有些人可能会认为“邪恶的死灵法术”和“虔诚的召唤术”（或随便你怎么称呼）之间存在根本区别，但这两种学科都是通过相同的原理运作的：束缚和控制灵魂。在这两种情况下，都可能出现不利结果；最常见的是，施法者失去对其造物的控制，并被自己召唤的东西致残或杀死。然而，也有报道称，有时施法者会意外地使用自己的灵魂，而不是从扭曲的冥界召唤来的灵魂。当这种情况发生时，施法者的灵魂通常会在试图同时占据两具身体时撕裂自己；人类的灵魂也曾出现与低级迪德拉融合的情况。在这两种情况下，结果对召唤师来说都是极其痛苦的死亡。<BR>
<BR>
首先，我将讨论直接召唤术，因为这是这些技艺中更简单、在社会上更易接受的形式。基本上，召唤术通过复杂的魔能操控运作，由此打开一扇通往湮灭的门户，并（希望）将所需生物拉过来；在大多数情况下，这一过程还涉及将被召唤者的意志与召唤者的意志绑定。我认为这个“门户”实际上是在我们的领域与湮灭之间短暂撕裂的一道裂隙，与天空中的那些裂隙非常相似。幸运的是，这道裂隙似乎足够小，可以自行愈合，不像高空中那些裂隙。若非这种自我修复特性，我们的世界早就落入湮灭的暴力大军手中了。然而，在某些情况下，召唤者可能会在维度织布上撕开过大的裂隙，让过多的迪德拉进入我们的世界。过大的撕裂可能是由薄弱的维度织布或施法者过于热情造成的。
<BR>
死灵法术则更难一些，因为它要求召唤者维持对其召唤之灵的支配领域；灵魂在进入我们的世界时往往会采取“真实”的形态（以劣魔、德雷莫拉等形式出现），但死灵法师必须通过将灵魂与现实世界隔绝足够长时间，以将灵魂引入可居住的身体来阻止这一点。灵魂似乎更喜欢这些现成的身体，而不是自己创造身体。死灵法术的诱惑在于，这些身体可以在灵魂入住之前很久就被置于施法者的控制之下（有诸多保障），从而在被召唤者与召唤者之间建立异常强大的忠诚纽带。此外，这些纽带不需要施法者像召唤师那样进行维护；死灵造物与其主人之间的纽带似乎没有时间上的限制。<BR>
<BR>
编者注：此处，作者呈现了关于召唤术实质的两种当代观点中的第一种。第一种，如他所说，认为迪德拉和灵魂是通过在我们的世界与湮灭之间制造微型裂隙来召唤的。然而，还有另一种理论认为，迪德拉已经存在于我们的世界中，而魔能本身实际上是迪德拉分离出的粒子。这种观点的支持者声称，召唤术只是将粒子合并为所需的造物（有些人甚至声称这就是所有魔能实际运作的方式）。这种观点的吸引力在于，它能更好地解释如何召唤绑定武器和盔甲，而本书作者未触及这一主题。那些认为湮灭中只是漂浮着随机装备碎片 -- 正如作者通过其理论间接暗示的那样 -- 的想法确实很奇怪。<BR>
<BR>
第三节：毁灭、恢复、变化<BR>
<BR>
我将这三个魔能学派放在一起，是因为它们本质上是相同的；它们都基于相同的基本原则。基本上，恢复系是治愈目标的改变，而毁灭系是伤害目标的改变。改变系本身是一种相对中性的改变魔法形式。<BR>
<BR>
我将首先讨论毁灭学派下的魔法，它们是最简单的 -- 因此也最致命，因为这允许强大的力量 -- 来施展。毁灭法术的创造通过将魔能直接转化为致命的物理形态来实现，如火或冰。魔能几乎总是按照施法者的意愿，采取自然界中某种自然现象的形式。例外的是那些影响目标精神或身体机能而不造成实际物理伤害的法术，如那些吸取意志力或智力的法术。不幸的是，我无法确切解析这些法术是如何运作的。<BR>
<BR>
本节中的第二个魔能学派是恢复系。这些法术基本上与毁灭系法术的作用相反。恢复法术改变魔能，使其修复和净化受损或患病的肉体，转化为抗毒剂，甚至转化为新的皮肤、肌肉或骨骼。我听说过强大法师甚至能复活完全死亡的生物的传闻，使目标完全恢复生命；他们不是作为亡灵返回，而是恢复死前的状态。然而，这些传闻未经证实。<BR>
<BR>
本节中最后一个 -- 也是最困难的 -- 魔能分支是变化学派。我认为它最困难，因为法术本身既多变又抽象。例如，让我们看看“负重”法术。我曾见过同一种法术以多种方式施展：有些法师麻痹腿部，有些在敌人身上施加心灵负重，有些则减缓敌人的心跳和血流。当然，这往往因法师而异；幻术师可能会选择使用心灵负重，而战斗法师则倾向于使用腿部麻痹法术。无论如何，你可以看到每一种法术都有多种施展方式，有些甚至难以归类为典型的变化法术。我不在本卷中详述。<BR>
<BR>
编者注：这些法术的应用几乎是无限的，所以我要强调作者所说的重要性。大多数术士和巫师都认为变化系是魔法领域中最开放、执行方式最多样化的领域；这些差异，虽然部分取决于施法者的专长，也因地区而异。大多数种族都开发了不同的使用和施展变化法术的方法。例如，部落的卡吉特会根据季节使用变化法术来增厚或减薄它们的毛皮，而一些隐居的诺德人已知会将冰变成火来在夜间取暖。我要指出的是，这些法术远比其他法术更适用于日常生活，而且它们确实不可或缺。<BR>
<BR>
关于作者对这些法术如何实际施展的说法，很难反驳或证实他的主张。大多数法师通过死记硬背来施法，几乎不思考自己实际在做什么，因此他们几乎注意不到自己的倾向；魔法能力感觉是天生的，而非习得的。尽管作者提出了论断，但很少有人真正花时间测试他的理论，包括我自己。然而，我想指出，除了少数纯粹的变化法术（如开锁术之类）外，这些法术大多主要作用于生物，这给作者的观点提供了一些可信度。<BR>
<BR>
本系列第二卷包含关于幻术系、神秘系的信息，以及关于魔能实践的一些建议。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>

A Fable from Valenwood<BR>
by Ealoin<BR>
<BR>
It was mere half a mile across the Elden Grove, amongst full leaved oaks and patterns of silvery cypress where the foxes were resting through the night and atop the branches, owls were singing a gentle tune, slowly caressing the range of fauna in their slumbers. Untouched by the ever-restless man and only ventured to upon a call by mer, the creatures were at peace, with a cordial feeling to all the living in their hearts in the shades of Odossair.<BR>
<BR>
Their provider it was, the forest, and with deepest respect they treated it, from the smallest worm and mouse to the fox, goose, deer and bear. No disease had ever ravaged trees or ones who had built their abodes under them, nor had a single tree ever been cut down or an animal killed by the hand of the elves, who had lived by Odossair for centuries. A pact between people had been made to keep out of it - not through fear but instead respect, understanding and sensibility.<BR>
<BR>
With the forests' allure so strong and affecting all in its sphere, no one knew fear. A fortress full of life for animals and a wall on the town's hillside, bound to it were they all. A perfect symmetry, unspoken yet unbroken pact, sealed with no sacrifices from either side but a promise for love and life. <BR>

瓦伦伍德寓言一则<BR>
伊洛因 著<BR>
<BR>
穿越上古林地不过半英里，那里有枝叶繁茂的橡树和银色柏树组成的图案，狐狸整夜歇息，猫头鹰在枝头吟唱着轻柔的曲调，慢慢抚慰着沉睡中的动物们。这片土地未曾被永不安宁的人类触碰，只在精灵召唤时才会造访。在奥多塞尔的树荫下，生灵们和谐共处，心中对所有生命都充满友善之情。<BR>
<BR>
森林是它们的供给者，它们以最深切的敬意对待它，从最小的蠕虫和老鼠到狐狸、鹅、鹿和熊。疾病从未侵袭过树木或在树下筑巢的生灵，没有一棵树被砍倒，没有一只动物被精灵杀死，精灵们已在奥多塞尔旁生活了几个世纪。人们之间达成了一项协议，不涉足其中 -- 并非出于恐惧，而是出于尊重、理解和感知。<BR>
<BR>
森林的魅力如此强大，影响着其范围内的所有存在，没有人知道恐惧。这是动物的生命堡垒，也是镇上山坡的屏障，一切都与它紧密相连。完美的对称，未曾言说却未曾打破的约定，没有双方任何牺牲，只有爱与生命的承诺。<BR>

The Failure of The Empire<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
It is common knowledge that the fall of the empire is approaching quickly, and soon its degeneration will result in utter collapse. Ever since the death of Tiber Septim, the Empire's foundations have rotted under weak rulers, and Uriel Septim has only further proven this. And all of this centers on the Imperial system and its ruler, the decrepit Uriel Septim.<BR>

Under the Emperor's sickly hand, secret spy networks which have either removed or jeopardized more freedoms than we have ever thought possible move like murderous wraiths through the people. These "blades," as they call themselves, spy on the regular, hard-working common folk simply to satisfy the foul Emperor's desire for control of all things. He draws further power from his military police, and all that his self-proclaimed "legions" do now is murder innocent civilians to ensure themselves a little more time in control. They are nothing but cowards and thugs. The corruption rises through the ranks of this legion, and I have seen from the inside nearly as many Imperial Guards fall to faulty leadership as to fighting. I've even seen unrest in the city of Cyrodiil itself. Rioting! In the streets of the greatest city in Tamriel! And yet the Emperor and his legions continue to preach of the "glory of the Empire!"<BR>
<BR>
We must ask ourselves what we can do during these times. Will we do nothing? Will we dotter like old men, speaking but never taking action? Will we wait for the beasts of anarchy to take hold on this sweet land we love more than all else? We must impel the Empire's fall and take control for ourselves! We can rule Tamriel and succeed where the Empire and the foolish Uriel Septim cannot.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
帝国的败亡<BR>

众所周知，帝国的衰落正迅速逼近，不久它的堕落将导致彻底崩溃。自从泰伯·塞普汀死后，帝国的根基在软弱统治者的治理下逐渐腐朽，尤利尔·塞普汀只进一步证明了这一点。帝国官僚机构向大众灌输宣传和谎言，拼命试图恢复对这个我们像傻瓜一样服从的垂死怪物的信仰。<BR>

<BR>
我们必须问自己，在这些时候我们能做什么。我们将无动于衷吗？我们会像老人一样步履蹒跚，只说不做吗？我们会等待无政府状态的野兽抓住我们最爱的这片美好土地吗？我们必须推动帝国的崩溃，自己掌握控制权！我们可以统治泰姆瑞尔，在帝国和愚蠢的尤利尔·塞普汀失败的地方取得成功。<BR>"""
