"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
How Orsinium Passed to the Orcs<BR>
by Menyna Gsost<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The year was 3E 399 and standing on a mountainside overlooking a vast tract of land between the lands of Menevia and Wayrest was a great and learned judge, an arbitrator and magistrate, impartial in his submission to the law.<BR>
<BR>
"You have a very strong claim to the land, my lad," said the judge. "I won't lie to you about that.  But your competition has an equal claim.  This is what makes my particular profession difficult at times."<BR>
<BR>
"You would call it my competition?" sneered Lord Bowyn, gesturing to the Orc.  The creature, called Gortwog gro-Nagorm, looked up with baleful eyes.<BR>
<BR>
"He has ample documentation to make a claim on the land," the magistrate shrugged. "And the particular laws of our land do not discriminate between particular races.  We had a Bosmer regency once, many generations ago."<BR>
<BR>
"But what if a pig or a slaughterfish turned up demanding the property?  Would they have the same legal rights as I?"<BR>
<BR>
"If they had the proper papers, I'm afraid so," smiled the judge. "The law is very clear that if two claimants with equal titles to the property are set in deadlock, a duel must be held.  Now, the rules are fairly archaic, but I've had opportunity to look them over, and I think they're still valid.  The Imperial council agrees."<BR>
<BR>
"What must we do?" asked the Orc, his voice low and harsh, unused to the tongue of the Cyrodiils.<BR>
<BR>
"The first claimant, that's you, Lord Gortwog, may choose the armor and weapon of the duelists.  The second claimant, that's you, Lord Bowyn, may choose the location.  If you would prefer, either or both you may choose a champion or you may duel yourself."<BR>
<BR>
The Breton and the Orc looked at one another, evaluating.  Finally, Gortwog spoke, "The armor will be Orcish and the weapons will be common steel long swords.  No enchantments.  No wizardry allowed."<BR>
<BR>
"The arena will be the central courtyard of my cousin Lord Berylth's palace in Wayrest," said Bowyn, looking Gortwog in the eye scornfully. "None of your kind will be allowed in to witness."<BR>
<BR>
So it was agreed.  Gortwog declared that he would fight the duel himself, and Bowyn, who was a fairly young man and in better than average condition, felt that he could not keep his honor without competing himself as well.  Still, upon arriving at his cousin's palace a week before the duel was scheduled, he felt the need to practice.  A suit of Orcish armor was purchased and for the first time in his life, Bowyn wore something of tremendous weight and limited facility.<BR>
<BR>
Bowyn and Berylth sparred in the courtyard.  In ten minutes times, Bowyn had to stop.  He was red-faced and out of breath from trying to move in the armor: to add to his exasperation, he had not scored one blow on his cousin, and had dozens of feinted strikes scored on him.<BR>
<BR>
"I don't know what to do," said Bowyn over dinner. "Even if I knew someone who could fight properly in that beastly steel, I couldn't possibly send in a champion to battle Gortwog."<BR>
<BR>
Berylth commiserated.  As the servants cleared the plates, Bowyn stood up in his seat and pointed at one of them: "You didn't tell me you had an Orc in your household!"<BR>
<BR>
"Sir?" whined the elderly specimen, turning to Lord Berylth, certain that he caused offense somehow.<BR>
<BR>
"You mean Old Tunner?" laughed Berylith. "He's been with my house for ages.  Would you like him to give you training on how to move in Orcish armor?"<BR>
<BR>
"Would you like me to?" asked Tunner obsequiously.<BR>
<BR>
Unknown to Berylith but known to him now, his servant had once ridden with the legendary Cursed Legion of High Rock.  He not only knew how to fight in Orcish armor himself, but he had acted as trainer to other Orcs before retiring into domestic service.  Desperate, Bowyn immediately engaged him as his full-time trainer.<BR>
<BR>
"Your try too hard, sir," said the Orc on their first day in the arena. "It is easy to strain yourself in heavy mail.  The joints are just so to let you to bend with only a little effort.  If you fight against the joints, you won't have any strength to fight your foe."<BR>
<BR>
Bowyn tried to follow Tunner's instructions, but he quickly grew frustrated.  And the more frustrated he got, the more intensity he put into his work, which tired him out even quicker.  While he took a break to drink some water, Berylith spoke to his servant.  If they were optimistic about Bowyn's chances, their faces did not show it.<BR>
<BR>
Tunner trained Bowyn hard the next two days, but her Ladyship Elysora's birthday followed hard upon them, and Bowyn enjoyed the feast thoroughly.  A liquor of poppies and goose fat, and cock tinsh with buttered hyssop for a first course; roasted pike, combwort, and balls of rabbit meat for a second; sliced fox tongues, ballom pudding with oyster gravy, battaglir weed and beans for the main course; collequiva ice and sugar fritters for dessert.  As Bowyn was settling back afterwards, his eyes weary, he suddenly spied Gortwog and the judge entering the room.<BR>
<BR>
"What are you doing here?" he cried. "The duel's not for another two days!"<BR>
<BR>
"Lord Gortwog asked that we move it to tonight," said the judge. "You were training when my emisary arrived two days ago, but his lordship your cousin spoke for you, agreeing to the change of date."<BR>
<BR>
"But there's no time to assemble my supporters," complained Bowyn. "And I've just devoured a feast that would kill a lesser man.  Cousin, how could you neglect to tell me?"<BR>
<BR>
"I spoke to Tunner about it," said Berylith, blushing, unused to deception. "We decided that you would be best served under these conditions."<BR>
<BR>
The battle in the arena was sparsely attended.  Saturated with food, Bowyn found himself unable to move very quickly.  To his surprise, the armor responded to his lethargy, rotating smoothly and elegantly to each stagger.  The more he successfully maneuvered, the more he allowed his mind and not his body to control his defensive and offensive actions.  For the first time in his life, Bowyn saw what it was to look through the helmet of an Orc.  <BR>
<BR>
Of course, he lost, and rather badly if scores had been tabulated.  Gortwog was a master of such battle.  But Bowyn fought on for more than three hours before the judge reluctantly called a winner.<BR>
<BR>
"I will name the land Orsinium after the land of my fathers," said the victor.<BR>
<BR>
Bowyn's first thought was that if he must lose to an Orc, it was best that the battle was largely unwatched by his friends and family.  As he left the courtyard to go to the bed he had longed for earlier in the evening, he saw Gortwog speaking to Tunner.  Though he did not understand the language, he could see that they knew each other.  When the Breton was in bed, he had a servant bring the old Orc to him.<BR>
<BR>
"Tunner," he said kindly. "Speak frankly to me.  You wanted Lord Gortwog to win."<BR>
<BR>
"That is true," said Tunner. "But I did not fail you.  You fought better than you would have fought two days hence, sir.  I did not want Orsinium to be won by its king without a fight."<BR>
<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
奥辛纽姆如何归于兽人之手<BR>
梅尼娜·格索斯特 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
时值第三纪元399年，一位伟大而博学的法官站在山腰上，俯瞰着梅涅维亚和途歇之间广袤的土地。他是一位仲裁者与地方法官，在服从法律方面不偏不倚。<BR>
<BR>
“你对这片土地拥有非常有力的所有权，”法官说。“我不会对你撒谎。但你的竞争者拥有同等的主张权。这就是我这份职业有时会变得困难的原因。”<BR>
<BR>
“你会称他为我的竞争者？”鲍温领主嗤笑道，朝那个兽人做了个手势。那个名叫戈特沃格·格罗-纳果姆的生物抬起头，用恶毒的眼神看着他。<BR>
<BR>
“他有足够的文件来主张这片土地的所有权，”法官耸耸肩。“我们土地的特定法律不歧视特定种族。很多代以前，我们曾有过一位波斯莫摄政王。”<BR>
<BR>
“但如果一头猪或一条食人鱼出现要求财产呢？它们会有和我一样的法律权利吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“如果它们有合适的文件，恐怕是这样，”法官微笑着说。“法律明确规定，如果两个对财产具有同等权利的索求者陷入僵局，则必须举行决斗。规则相当古老，但我有机会查阅过，我认为它们仍然有效。帝国议会也同意。”<BR>
<BR>
“我们必须做什么？”兽人问道，他的声音低沉而粗哑，不习惯西罗帝尔人的语言。<BR>
<BR>
“第一索求者，也就是你，戈特沃格领主，可以选择决斗者的盔甲和武器。第二索求者，也就是你，鲍温领主，可以选择地点。如果你们愿意，你们中的任何一方或双方可以选择一名勇士，或者你们亲自决斗。”<BR>
<BR>
布莱顿人和兽人互相看着对方，彼此打量。最终，戈特沃格开口说道：“盔甲将是兽人盔甲，武器将是普通的钢制长剑。没有附魔。不允许使用巫术。”<BR>
<BR>
“决斗场将是我表兄贝里尔思领主在途歇的宫殿中央庭院，”鲍温说道，轻蔑地直视着戈特沃格的眼睛。“你的同类一个也不准进去观战。”<BR>
<BR>
就这样说定了。戈特沃格宣布他将亲自参加决斗，而鲍温，一个相当年轻且身体状况优于常人的男子，觉得如果不亲自参加决斗就无法保全自己的荣誉。尽管如此，在计划决斗的前一周到达表兄的宫殿后，他觉得有必要练习一下。他买了一套兽人盔甲，鲍温有生以来第一次穿上这种极为沉重且活动受限的装备。<BR>
<BR>
鲍温和贝里尔思在庭院里对练。十分钟后，鲍温不得不停下来。他试图穿着盔甲移动，脸涨得通红，上气不接下气：更让他恼火的是，他一次也没击中他的表兄，自己却被击中数十记佯攻。<BR>
<BR>
“我不知道该怎么办，”鲍温在晚餐时说。“即使我认识一个能熟练穿着那笨重钢铁战斗的人，我也不可能派一个勇士去与戈特沃格战斗。”<BR>
<BR>
贝里尔思表示同情。当仆人们收拾盘子时，鲍温从座位上站起来，指着其中一个仆人：“你没告诉我你家里有个兽人！”<BR>
<BR>
“大人？”这位年迈的仆从转向贝里尔思领主，确信自己不知怎么得罪了人。<BR>
<BR>
“你是指老坦纳？”贝里尔思笑了。“他为我家族服务很久了。你想让他教你如何穿着兽人盔甲移动吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“您要我教您吗？”坦纳谄媚地问道。<BR>
<BR>
贝里尔思之前不知道，但现在知道了，他的仆人曾与高岩传说中的诅咒军团一起骑过马。他不仅自己知道如何在兽人盔甲中战斗，而且在退休成为家仆之前，还曾担任过其他兽人的教练。孤注一掷的鲍温立即聘请他作为自己的全职教练。<BR>
<BR>
“您太努力了，大人，”兽人在他们第一天进入决斗场时说。“穿着重型铠甲很容易让自己紧张。关节的设计只需要你花一点力气就能弯曲。如果你和关节较劲，你就不会有任何力气去和敌人战斗了。”<BR>
<BR>
鲍温试图遵循坦纳的指示，但很快就变得沮丧。他越沮丧，投入训练的强度就越大，这让他更快地筋疲力尽。当他休息喝水时，贝里尔思和他的仆人说了几句话。如果他们对鲍温获胜的机会感到乐观，他们的脸上并没有显露出来。<BR>
<BR>
接下来的两天，坦纳严格训练鲍温，但随即就赶上了埃里索拉夫人的生日，鲍温尽情享受了宴席。开胃菜是罂粟和鹅肝酿的酒，以及涂了黄油海索草的烤公鸡；第二道菜是烤梭鱼、梳草和兔肉丸；主菜是切片的狐狸舌、配牡蛎酱的巴罗姆布丁、巴塔利尔草和豆类；甜点是科莱奎瓦冰糕和糖霜果馅饼。当鲍温在宴后安顿下来，疲惫地眯着眼睛时，他突然瞥见戈特沃格和法官走进了房间。<BR>
<BR>
“你们在这里做什么？”他喊道。“决斗不是还有两天吗！”<BR>
<BR>
“戈特沃格领主要求我们把决斗改到今晚，”法官说。“两天前我的使者到达时您正在训练，但您的表兄大人代您答应了更改日期。”<BR>
<BR>
“但没时间召集我的支持者了，”鲍温抱怨道。“而且我刚享用了一顿普通人会撑死的盛宴。表兄，你怎么能忘了告诉我？”<BR>
<BR>
“我和坦纳谈过了，”贝里尔思说，脸红了，不习惯撒谎。“我们决定，在这种条件下进行决斗对你最有利。”<BR>
<BR>
决斗场上的战斗观者寥寥。腹胀如鼓的鲍温发现自己无法快速移动。令他惊讶的是，盔甲竟随了他的迟缓，在他每一次踉跄时都平稳地转动。他越是成功地移动，就越是用头脑而非身体来控制自己的防御和进攻动作。鲍温有生以来第一次体验到透过兽人头盔观看世界是什么感觉。<BR>
<BR>
当然，他输了，如果按照分数统计的话，输得还挺惨。戈特沃格是这种战斗的大师。但鲍温坚持战斗了三个多小时，法官才不情愿地宣布了胜者。<BR>
<BR>
“我将以我父辈的土地之名，将这片土地命名为奥辛纽姆。”胜利者说道。<BR>
<BR>
鲍温首先想到的是，既然他注定要输给一个兽人，那么这场战斗最好没有亲友们在旁观战。当他离开庭院，走向他当晚早些时候就渴望躺下的床铺时，他看到戈特沃格正在和坦纳说话。虽然他听不懂他们在说什么，但他看得出他们彼此认识。布莱顿人上床后，叫仆人把老兽人带到他跟前。<BR>
<BR>
“坦纳，”他和蔼地说。“跟我说实话。你想让戈特沃格领主赢。”<BR>
<BR>
“是的，”坦纳说。“但我没有辜负您。您打得比两天前您要打的要好得多，大人。我不想让奥辛纽姆的国王不战而胜地得到它。”<BR>
<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>How to Tune your Hoom<BR>$0A<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"> By Arvyrin Adrys<BR><BR>$0A<BR>We are all aware of the long and storied history of the Mountain Hoom. Who has not, as a child, heard the tale of Daroom, the Beast of the Mountain who sang to the Dwemer animunculi in their own language? Or of the seven thousand Hoom that greeted Saint Veloth (blessed be the dust of his mouth), and announced to him that he had entered Resdayn at last?<BR>$0A<BR>Not all of these proud creatures can claim such legendary status; but most can, with patience and wisdom, be trained to sing harmonies both pious and beautiful. By following my advice, perhaps you too like the Chimer Magnates of old can own a parade of these animals, to march before you and signal your approach.$0ATo do so, one must raise the beast from birth. Locating eggs is not hard, but harvesting them from the mother's back may prove a challenge. Once hatched, a juvenile Hoom is no larger than a mouse and will happily sit in the folds of your cloak, eating comberries and other fruits.<BR>$0A<BR>When it comes of an age to carry itself, you must begin its training. Speak to it, sing to it, play the flute or ash horn to it if you can. It will see you as a parent and will strive to imitate. I once saw a Hoom three summers of age that could form Ashlander melodies as sweet and mournful as any one might hear on the winds of Vvardenfell.<BR>$0A<BR>The Nords believe that the Hoom learns best in its spring mating season, and you may see a poor apprentice lad wearing the shell of a potential mate, trying to inflame the blood-fired creatures so that they sing all the sweeter. Amusing though this charade is, there is little enough proof of its effectiveness, and the creatures learn as diligently in Frostfall as in First Seed.<BR>$0A<BR>With skill, it is possible to craft reeds and valves from wood, bone, and other materials. Fitting these to your companion will broaden the range of sounds that it can produce. Masters of this art engrave their sigils on the carapace of the animal, making art pleasing to the ears and eyes alike. My symbol is the double-headed Shalk; you may encounter a few examples of my life's work.<BR>$0A<BR>Finally, a note to those who have a romantic imagination and a love of the old tales. It is said in ancient days the Hoom could be taught to speak and utter pieties as well as any Dunmer. I fear that if you wish to see this done today, you must seek a better teacher than I. That art, if it ever truly existed, is now lost. It is claimed by some that the Hoom long ago said all they wished to say, and are content now simply to sing. Perhaps in this they are the wise ones. <BR>
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>如何调校您的荷姆<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">阿维林·阿德里斯 著<BR><BR>
<BR>我们都熟知山地荷姆那漫长而传奇的历史。谁小时候没听过达鲁姆的故事呢？那头山中的野兽，曾用锻莫的语言对着他们的造物歌唱。谁又没听过那七千只荷姆的故事呢？它们迎接了圣维洛斯（愿他口中的尘埃安息），并向他宣告他终于踏入了勒斯丹。<BR>
<BR>并非所有这些骄傲的生物都享有如此传奇的地位；但大多数通过耐心和智慧，可以训练出既虔诚又美妙的和声。按照我的建议，或许你也能像古代的歧莫权贵那样，拥有一队这样的动物，它们在你面前行进，宣告你的到来。
要做到这一点，必须从幼年就开始饲养。找到卵并不难，但从母兽背上取下它们可能是个挑战。一旦孵化，幼年荷姆只有老鼠大小，会愉快地待在你斗篷的褶皱里，吃浆果和其他水果。<BR>
<BR>当它长到能够自己行动时，你必须开始训练它。对它说话，为它唱歌，如果可以的话，为它吹奏笛子或灰烬号角。它会将你视为父母，并努力模仿。我曾见过一只三岁的荷姆，能吹奏出如同瓦登费尔风声般甜美而忧伤的灰烬之民旋律。<BR>

<BR>运用技巧，可以用木头、骨头和其他材料制作簧片和气阀。将这些安装在你的同伴身上，会拓宽它能发出的声音范围。这门艺术的大师会将自己的纹章雕刻在动物的甲壳上，创造出悦耳又悦目的艺术品。我的标志是双头沙尔克；你可能会遇到一些我毕生作品的例子。<BR>
<BR>最后，给那些拥有浪漫想象力和喜爱古老传说的人一点说明。据说在古代，荷姆可以被教会说话，并能像任何丹莫一样表达虔诚。我担心如果你今天想看到这一点，你必须找一位比我更好的老师。那门技艺，如果它确实存在过，现在也已失传。有些人声称荷姆很久以前已经说完了所有想说的话，现在满足于歌唱。或许，在这一方面，它们才是智者。<BR>"""

How to Treat Heretics
如何对待异端

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_HowtoterstHereticsTR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
How to Treat Heretics<BR>
by Salvas Relas of the Order of Doctrine and Ordination<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
It is inevitable that in our service to ALMSIVI and Their holy Temple we shall encounter souls which are not loyal to the Tribunal.  Whether these souls belong to the Sharmat, the House of Troubles, or any number of other perfidious sects it is our duty as Ordinators to protect the faithful from the danger which these people represent and while these souls are often irredeemable and must be purged with divine wrath, we must also attempt to emulate Almalexia, Mother of Mercy, and avoid unnecessary bloodshed. 
<BR>
Children<BR>
Children will, admittedly, not be encountered frequently by those of the Order of War, Inquisition, or my own Order, but the Order of the Watch will regularly encounter them in the execution of their daily duties and must learn to interact with them.  Occasionally Ordinators will learn of heretical practices in town and, during their raids of homes and shrines, will encounter the sons and daughters of heretics.  Simply put, the young are not to blame for the blasphemous teachings their parents instill in them as they lack the maturity and experience to reject the falsehoods taught to them, which unfortunately leaves these young souls deluded.  I encourage Ordinators to try and be gentle and reassuring as these children can become valuable members of the faithful under the tutelage of the Temple and some of them may even grow up to execute the will of the Tribunal as Ordinators.  Remember, they may grow violent during your raids while you are arresting or executing their parents and while you are expected to protect yourself, do remember that as a trained warrior few of them can pose any significant threat to you.  Show mercy and they may one day be reborn in service to the one true faith.
<BR>
The Misled and Ignorant<BR>
Not all those who are misled young are so fortunate to be ripped away from their deceivers by the Temple and some grow up having been lied to their whole life.  Keep in mind that, according to Temple law, heresy is not heresy unless the nonbeliever refuses to be corrected and those who are unaware that they are rejecting the truth are not heretics nor are they guilty of any sin. Ordinators are encouraged to bring any non-violent heretics to the attention of the Temple, who will instruct you on how to act.  While usually a Temple scholar or priest will speak with and attempt to correct the nonbelievers, periodically Ordinators of Doctrine and Ordination will fulfill this role because you have the scholarly training to answer any question and assuage any doubts nonbelievers may reasonably have and you are servants of the Tribunal who are expected to serve as examples of faithfulness at all times.  I have personally seen, after lengthy discussions, nonbelievers renounce their corrupt beliefs and accept our Three Gods as their divine lords. 
<BR> 
The Coerced<BR>
The Order of War will frequently purge the dens of the worshippers of the House of Troubles, and when you do show no mercy for those cultists desire nothing less than the Temple's complete destruction.  However they often have slaves who serve their masters solely out of fear of punishment and because these coerced servants live in pitiable conditions as slaves to evil incarnate you serve the Three and the Temple by breaking their chains and wrenching them from the wicked hands of the Four Corners.  Once freed from bondage these souls may see the truth and come to worship the Three Gods.  Admittedly, it can be difficult to distinguish true, willing servants of the Four Corners from their coerced servants, and while you must prioritize the completion of your mission and the safety of you and your comrades, if you can save these helpless souls you should make every reasonable effort to do so.
<BR> 
The Doubters<BR>
In a perfect world all Dunmer would remain faithful to the Three Gods their whole life, but we live in an imperfect world; were it not so we Ordinators would not exist.  There will be times in most people's lives in which doubt will creep in and while it is a contagion which can spread if left unchecked, most often the lapse in faith is momentary and can be corrected under supervision. Doubt usually takes hold of laity, although occasionally even members of the clergy will experience it, and while it is nefarious and even dangerous, a good Inquisitor will avoid violence and incarceration unless the doubt degrades into vile heresy and the doubter becomes fixed in their incorrectness.  Those of you who belong to the Order of the Inquisition are charged with extirpating doubt wherever it may be found but reeducation is always a better means of eliminating uncertainty than force; one moment of doubt does not warrant the death sentence or torture and incarceration.  Show mercy and lead the doubters back into the loving and merciful arms of ALMSIVI.
<BR> 
Violence is a fact of life for Ordinators but it is always better to redeem a heretic than to kill them.  This is a lesson which many jaded Ordinators lose sight of after many years of service, but it is something that I wish to instill into all of you.  Never let it stray far from your mind in the years to come.  Discharge your duties faithfully, you represent the Temple.
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
如何对待异端<BR>
教义与圣职修会 萨尔瓦斯·雷拉斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
在我们服务于奥姆希维及其神圣神殿的过程中，不可避免地会遇到对审判席不忠的灵魂。无论这些灵魂属于沙玛特、祸乱家族，还是任何其他背信弃义的教派，作为神殿卫兵，我们的职责是保护信徒免受这些人所代表的危险。尽管这些灵魂常常无可救药，必须用神圣的愤怒来净化，但我们仍应努力效仿仁慈之母阿玛莱西娅，避免不必要的流血。
<BR>
儿童<BR>
诚然，战争修会、审判修会或我所属的教义修会不常接触儿童，但守卫修会在执行日常职责时会经常遇到他们，并必须学会与他们互动。神殿卫兵偶尔会听说城镇中有异端行为，在搜查住所和圣祠时，会遇到异端的子女。简而言之，年轻人不应为他们父母灌输的亵渎教诲而受到指责，因为他们缺乏成熟和经验来拒绝被灌输的谎言，这不幸地使这些年轻的灵魂受到蒙蔽。我鼓励神殿卫兵们尝试温和与安抚，因为这些儿童在神殿的指导下可以成为信仰中有价值的成员，其中一些人甚至可能长大后以神殿卫兵的身份执行审判席的意志。记住，在您逮捕或处决他们父母的过程中，他们可能会变得暴躁，尽管您应当保护自己，但别忘了，作为训练有素的战士，他们中很少有人能对您构成重大威胁。展现怜悯，他们或许有一天能重生，服务于唯一的真信仰。
<BR>
被误导者与无知者<BR>
并非所有年轻时被误导的人都如此幸运，能被神殿从欺骗者手中夺回；有些人终其一生都在谎言中长大。请记住，根据神殿法律，除非不信者拒绝被纠正，否则异端不算是异端；那些不知道自己正在拒绝真理的人不是异端，也不犯有任何罪行。鼓励神殿卫兵将任何非暴力的异端告知神殿，神殿会指示您如何行动。虽然通常神殿学者或祭司会与不信者交谈并尝试纠正他们，但教义与圣职修会的神殿卫兵偶尔也会担当此角色，因为你们受过学术训练，能够回答任何问题，平息不信者可能合理拥有的任何疑虑，而且你们作为审判席的仆人，应当时刻作为信仰的典范。我亲眼见过，经过长时间的讨论后，不信者放弃了他们腐败的信仰，接受了我们的三神作为他们的神圣之主。
<BR>
被胁迫者<BR>
战争修会将频繁清除祸乱家族崇拜者的巢穴，执行时不要对那些邪教徒表示怜悯，因为他们所想望的不亚于神殿的彻底毁灭。然而，他们常常拥有奴隶，这些奴隶仅仅因为害怕惩罚而服务他们的主人。由于这些被胁迫的仆人生活在可悲的条件下，作为邪恶化身的奴隶，替它们打破锁链、将它们从四角的邪恶手中解救出来，正是你们对三神和神殿的服务。一旦从束缚中解脱，这些灵魂或许能看到真相，从而崇拜三神。诚然，区分真正的、甘愿服务于四角的仆人与被胁迫的仆人可能很困难。尽管您必须优先完成任务以及您和同志们的安全，但如果您能拯救这些无助的灵魂，您应当尽一切合理的努力去这样做。
<BR>
怀疑者<BR>
在一个完美的世界里，所有丹莫终其一生都将忠诚信奉三神，但我们生活在一个不完美的世界；若非如此，我们神殿卫兵就不会存在。在大多数人的一生中，总会有疑虑悄然滋生的时候。虽然疑虑是一种若不加以遏制就会蔓延的传染病，但大多数情况下，信仰的动摇是短暂的，并且可以在监督下纠正。怀疑通常发生在俗人身上，尽管神职人员偶尔也会经历。虽然它恶毒而且甚至危险，但一个好的审判者会避免暴力和监禁，除非怀疑堕入邪恶的异端，并且怀疑者变得固执于他们的错误。你们这些属于审判修会的人，负责根除任何地方出现的怀疑，但再教育始终是比武力更好的消除不确定性的方法；一时的怀疑并不足以判处死刑、酷刑或监禁。展现怜悯，将怀疑者带回奥姆希维慈爱而怜悯的怀抱。
<BR>
暴力是神殿卫兵生活中的现实，但救赎一个异端总是比杀死他们更好。这是许多疲惫的神殿卫兵在多年服务后所忽视的教训，但我希望将它灌输给你们所有人。在未来的岁月中，永远不要让它远离你的思想。忠实地履行你们的职责，你们代表的是神殿。
<BR>"""

......于是，由于他曾与猿少女杜尔莎嬉戏，马鲁克在石草地上度过了他的百年忏悔期。他的视野被灼烧，他的舌头肿胀，他的毛皮变得斑驳，他的左手拇指始终指向高塔的星辰。阿莱西亚的阴魂不断与他说话，那些锯齿般的言语刮擦着他的观念器官，通过苦难将他引向智慧。<BR>

<BR>

他用他猴类的鲜血，在恳求陡崖上用符号记录下她的话语，而他血液中的火焰将七十七条不渝教义蚀刻在岩石表面。尽管这劳作消耗了他，甚至消耗了他的生命本质，他并未吝惜，因为他知道死亡是一种幻象。因为，难道阿莱西亚不存在了么？她虽然死了，却仍在说话，如刀锋般锐利。难道佩林-阿尔不也亲眼目睹了她的死亡，尽管他自己也在乌玛-伊尔死去时死去？于是，马鲁克知道了何为“正达”：献身于正直之生与艾诺菲消亡的人，将超越死亡的幻象而存续 -- 因为，根除腐化的驱动力，甚至能征服阿尔凯之循环。<BR>"""

The Image and the Divine<BR>
<BR>
by Primate Dalus<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000">
The Divines, it is said, reside in the diverse heavens of Aetherius, a most distant sphere, detached, that exists away from mortal eyes. We, low and humble souls, can only exist here on the mortal plane, which was made to be our shelter and trial.<BR>
<BR>
Travel to the heavens is possible, as the Emperor's mages and mananauts have proven, but it is impossible to permanently reside there, for mortal life cannot subside for long in the illimitable spaces. The spirit becomes unmoored, and loses its anchor to reality and physical existence. None have ever reported encountering a Divine spirit in Aetherius, but to do so would surely spell the end for a frail and temporal being.<BR>
<BR>
All manifestations of the Divine in the mortal world, from shrine blessings to the planets in the sky, are aspects that the Divines project into the world, in order to guide and help improve its lowly mortal inhabitants. Any perceived contradiction in their nature stems from the fact that the true Divine is obscured to us.<BR>
<BR>
Likewise, the gods and spirits of the provincial peoples are shadows of the true Divines, whom they perceive only as they wish to perceive them, not as they are. Only by the miracle of Alessia, who saw true the Gods of both men and elves, are we able to approach the true Divines.<BR>
<BR>
Only in death are the Divines revealed to us, or, occasionally, in the form of true revelations, visions, and manifestations. In those great revelations, the distinction between the Divine and their image is often difficult to perceive. Nor is it possible to know if words were said by a Divine as one, or by one of their many false-faces and aspect fragments.<BR>
<BR>
For to see the Divine from the mortal sphere is to see only a small aspect, in the way that a man looking through a hole in a curtain could only ever see a small part of a grand and impressive design. In this way, all the peoples and races of Tamriel have seen the Divines, once, in some form that they could know and cherish. But none possess the whole and the true, and from this confusion stems much animosity.<BR>
<BR>
It is only through study and revelation that we can come to a truer understanding of the Divine, worshiping the whole of the Divine; not just an image, but the being itself; not the image, but the idea. Therein lies the Revelation of Alessia.<BR>"""

形象与神圣<BR>

<BR>
同样，行省民族的神灵和精魂也是真正圣灵的影子，他们只按自己希望的方式感知，而非其本来面目。只有通过阿莱西亚的奇迹 -- 她洞见了人类和精灵双方神灵的真相 -- 我们才能接近真正的圣灵。<BR>

<BR>
因为，从凡世看神圣，就如同一个人透过窗帘上的一个洞观看，只能看到宏伟壮丽图景的一小部分。这样一来，泰姆瑞尔的所有民族和种族，都曾以某种他们能够认知和珍视的形式，一瞥圣灵。但没有人拥有完整和真正的圣灵，而许多敌意正源于这种混淆。<BR>
<BR>
只有通过研究和启示，我们才能对神圣达成更真实的理解，崇拜神圣的整体；不仅仅是形象，而是其存在本身；不仅仅是形象，而是其理念。这就是阿莱西亚的启示所在。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Immortal Blood<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The moons and stars were hidden from sight, making that particular quiet night especially dark. The town guard had to carry torches to make their rounds; but the man who came to call at my chapel carried no light with him. I came to learn that Movarth Piquine could see in the dark almost as well as the light - an excellent talent, considering his interests were exclusively nocturnal.<BR>
<BR>
One of my acolytes brought him to me, and from the look of him, I at first thought he was in need of healing. He was pale to the point of opalescence with a face that looked like it had once been very handsome before some unspeakable suffering. The dark circles under his eyes bespoke exhaustion, but the eyes themselves were alert, intense, almost insane.<BR>
<BR>
He quickly dismissed my notion that he himself was ill, though he did want to discuss a specific disease.<BR>
<BR>
"Vampirism," he said, and then paused at my quizzical look. "I was told that you were someone I should seek out for help understanding it."<BR>
<BR>
"Who told you that?" I asked with a smile.<BR>
<BR>
"Tissina Gray."<BR>
<BR>
I immediately remembered her. A brave, beautiful knight who had needed my assistance separating fact from fiction on the subject of the vampire. It had been two years, and I had never heard whether my advice had proved effective.<BR>
<BR>
"You've spoken to her? How is her ladyship?" I asked.<BR>
<BR>
"Dead," Movarth replied coldly, and then, responding to my shock, he added to perhaps soften the blow. "She said your advice was invaluable, at least for the one vampire. When last I talked to her, she was tracking another. It killed her."<BR>
<BR>
"Then the advice I gave her was not enough," I sighed. "Why do you think it would be enough for you?"<BR>
<BR>
"I was a teacher once myself, years ago," he said. "Not in a university. A trainer in the Fighters Guild. But I know that if a student doesn't ask the right questions, the teacher cannot be responsible for his failure. I intend to ask you the right questions."<BR>
<BR>
And that he did. For hours, he asked questions and I answered what I could, but he never volunteered any information about himself. He never smiled. He only studied me with those intense eyes of his, committing every word I said to memory.<BR>
<BR>
Finally, I turned the questioning around. "You said you were a trainer at the Fighters Guild. Are you on an assignment for them?"<BR>
<BR>
"No," he said curtly, and finally I could detect some weariness in those feverish eyes of his. "I would like to continue this tomorrow night, if I could. I need to get some sleep and absorb this."<BR>
<BR>
"You sleep during the day," I smiled.<BR>
<BR>
To my surprise, he returned the smile, though it was more of a grimace. "When tracking your prey, you adapt their habits."<BR>
<BR>
The next day, he did return with more questions, these ones very specific. He wanted to know about the vampires of eastern Skyrim. I told him about the most powerful tribe, the Volkihar, paranoid and cruel, whose very breath could freeze their victims' blood in the veins. I explained to him how they lived beneath the ice of remote and haunted lakes, never venturing into the world of men except to feed.<BR>
<BR>
Movarth Piquine listened carefully, and asked more questions into the night, until at last he was ready to leave.<BR>
<BR>
"I will not see you for a few days," he said. "But I will return, and tell you how helpful your information has been."<BR>
<BR>
True to his word, the man returned to my chapel shortly after midnight four days later. There was a fresh scar on his cheek, but he was smiling that grim but satisfied smile of his.<BR>
<BR>
"Your advice helped me very much," he said. "But you should know that the Volkihar have an additional ability you didn't mention. They can reach through the ice of their lakes without breaking it. It was quite a nasty surprise, being grabbed from below without any warning."<BR>
<BR>
"How remarkable," I said with a laugh. "And terrifying. You're lucky you survived."<BR>
<BR>
"I don't believe in luck. I believe in knowledge and training. Your information helped me, and my skill at melee combat sealed the bloodsucker's fate. I've never believed in weaponry of any kind. Too many unknowns. Even the best swordsmith has created a flawed blade, but you know what your body is capable of. I know I can land a thousand blows without losing my balance, provided I get the first strike."<BR>
<BR>
"The first strike?" I murmured. "So you must never be surprised."<BR>
<BR>
"That is why I came to you," said Movarth. "You know more than anyone alive about these monsters, in all their cursed varieties across the land. Now you must tell me about the vampires of northern Valenwood."<BR>
<BR>
I did as he asked, and once again, his questions taxed my knowledge. There were many tribes to cover. The Bonsamu who were indistinguishable from Bosmer except when seen by candlelight. The Keerilth who could disintegrate into mist. The Yekef who swallowed men whole. The dread Telboth who preyed on children, eventually taking their place in the family, waiting patiently for years before murdering them all in their unnatural hunger.<BR>
<BR>
Once again, he bade me farewell, promising to return in a few weeks, and once again, he returned as he said, just after midnight. This time, Movarth had no fresh scars, but he again had new information.<BR>
<BR>
"You were wrong about the Keerilth being unable to vaporize when pushed underwater," he said, patting my shoulder fondly. "Fortunately, they cannot travel far in their mist form, and I was able to track it down."<BR>
<BR>
"It must have surprised it fearfully. Your field knowledge is becoming impressive," I said. "I should have had an acolyte like you decades ago."<BR>
<BR>
"Now, tell me," he said. "Of the vampires of Cyrodiil."<BR>
<BR>
I told him what I could. There was but one tribe in Cyrodiil, a powerful clan who had ousted all other competitors, much like the Imperials themselves had done. Their true name was unknown, lost in history, but they were experts at concealment. If they kept themselves well-fed, they were indistinguishable from living persons. They were cultured, more civilized than the vampires of the provinces, preferring to feed on victims while they were asleep, unaware.<BR>
<BR>
"They will be difficult to surprise," Movarth frowned. "But I will seek one out, and tell you what I learn. And then you will tell me of the vampires of High Rock, and Hammerfell, and Elsweyr, and Black Marsh, and Morrowind, and the Sumurset Isles, yes?"<BR>
<BR>
I nodded, knowing then that this was a man on an eternal quest. He wouldn't be satisfied with but the barest hint of how things were. He needed to know it all.<BR>
<BR>
He did not return for a month, and on the night that he did, I could see his frustration and despair, though there were no lights burning in my chapel.<BR>
<BR>
"I failed," he said, as I lit a candle. "You were right. I could not find a single one."<BR>
<BR>
I brought the light up to my face and smiled. He was surprised, even stunned by the pallor of my flesh, the dark hunger in my ageless eyes, and the teeth. Oh, yes, I think the teeth definitely surprised the man who could not afford to be surprised.<BR>
<BR>
"I haven't fed in seventy-two hours," I explained, as I fell on him. He did not land the first blow or the last.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
不朽之血<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
月亮和星星都隐去了踪影，让那个寂静的夜晚显得格外黑暗。城镇的守卫不得不举着火把巡逻；但来我礼拜堂拜访的那个人却没有携带任何光源。我后来才得知，莫瓦特·皮奎恩在黑暗中视物几乎和在光亮中一样好 -- 考虑到他的兴趣完全属于夜间，这无疑是一项绝佳的天赋。<BR>
<BR>
我的一位侍从把他带到我面前，看着他，我起初以为他需要治疗。他脸色苍白得近乎乳白，脸庞看起来就像曾非常英俊，只是遭受了某种难以言说的苦难。他眼睛下方的黑眼圈透露着疲惫，但眼睛本身却机警、锐利，近乎疯狂。<BR>
<BR>
他很快打消了我认为他自己生病的想法，尽管他确实想讨论一种特定的疾病。<BR>
<BR>
“吸血鬼病，”他说，然后看到我疑惑的表情，停顿了一下。“有人告诉我，如果想了解它，我应该来找您帮忙。”<BR>
<BR>
“谁告诉你的？”我微笑着问道。<BR>
<BR>
“蒂西娜·格雷。”<BR>
<BR>
我立刻想起了她。一位勇敢美丽的骑士，她曾需要我的帮助来区分关于吸血鬼的事实与虚构。那已经是两年前的事了，我从未听说我的建议是否有效。<BR>
<BR>
“你和她谈过？她大人还好吗？”我问道。<BR>
<BR>
“死了，”莫瓦特冷冷地回答，然后，也许是为了减轻我受到的冲击，他又补充道：“她说您的建议非常宝贵，至少对那一个吸血鬼来说是这样。我最后一次和她谈话时，她正在追踪另一个吸血鬼。那个吸血鬼杀了她。”<BR>
<BR>
“那么，我给她的建议还不够，”我叹了口气。“你为什么认为对你就足够呢？”<BR>
<BR>
“多年前，我自己也曾是个教师，”他说。“不是在大学里。是战士公会的训练师。但我知道，如果学生不问正确的问题，老师就无法为他的失败负责。我打算问你正确的问题。”<BR>
<BR>
他也确实这样做了。连续几个小时，他不停地提问，而我则尽力回答。但他从未主动透露任何关于自己的信息。他从不微笑。只是用那双锐利的眼睛注视着我，将我说的每一个字都记在心里。<BR>
<BR>
最后，我反过来问他：“你说你曾是战士公会的训练师。你是在为他们执行任务吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“不，”他简短地说，我终于在他那双炽热的眼睛里察觉到了一丝疲倦。“如果可以的话，我想明天晚上继续。我需要睡一觉，消化一下这些内容。”<BR>
<BR>
“你在白天睡觉，”我微笑着说。<BR>
<BR>
令我惊讶的是，他也回以微笑，尽管那更像是一种苦笑。“当你追踪猎物时，你会适应它们的习性。”<BR>
<BR>
第二天，他果然又回来了，这次带来了更具体的问题。他想了解天际东部的吸血鬼。我告诉他最强大的氏族 -- 沃基哈尔，他们多疑而残忍，呼吸甚至能冻结受害者血管中的血液。我向他解释了这些吸血鬼如何生活在偏远闹鬼湖泊的冰层之下，除了觅食从不涉足人类世界。<BR>
<BR>
莫瓦特·皮奎恩仔细地听着，不断地提问，直到深夜，他才准备离开。<BR>
<BR>
“我会有几天不来了，”他说。“但我还会回来，告诉您您的信息对我有多大帮助。”<BR>
<BR>
他信守了诺言。四天后午夜刚过，他回到了我的礼拜堂。他的脸颊上多了一道新伤疤，但他脸上带着那种冷酷却满足的笑容。<BR>
<BR>
“您的建议帮了我大忙，”他说。“但您应该知道，沃基哈尔还有一项您没有提到的能力。他们可以不破开冰层，直接穿过湖冰伸手抓人。没有一点征兆就从下方被抓住，真是防不胜防。”<BR>
<BR>
“太了不起了，”我笑着说，“也太可怕了。你能活下来真幸运。”<BR>
<BR>
“我不相信运气。我相信知识和训练。您的信息帮助了我，而我近身格斗的技能决定了那吸血畜生的命运。我从不相信任何一种武器。未知因素太多了。即便最好的铁匠也会打造出有缺陷的刀剑，但你知道自己的身体能做什么。我知道我能打出千次攻击而不失平衡，前提是我能抢先出手。”<BR>
<BR>
“抢先出手？”我喃喃道。“所以你绝不能感到意外。”<BR>
<BR>
“这就是我来找您的原因，”莫瓦特说。“在活人中，您对这些怪物最为了解，它们的各种受诅咒的品种遍布整个大陆。现在，您必须告诉我瓦伦伍德北部的吸血鬼。”<BR>
<BR>
我照他说的做了，他的问题再次考验了我的知识。有许多氏族要讲。有博恩萨穆族，除了在烛光下，否则与波斯莫无法区分。有基里尔斯族，可以化身为雾。有耶克夫族，能将整个人吞下。还有可怕的泰尔博斯族，他们以儿童为猎物，最终取代他们在家庭中的位置，耐心等待多年，最后在那种非自然的饥饿中杀死全家人。<BR>
<BR>
他再次向我告别，承诺几周后再回来，并且，他再次如约于午夜后归来。这一次，莫瓦特身上没有新的伤疤，但他又带来了新的信息。<BR>
<BR>
“您说基里尔斯族被推到水下就无法雾化，这一点您错了，”他亲切地拍了拍我的肩膀说。“幸运的是，它们雾化形态下不能移动很远，我设法追踪到了它。”<BR>
<BR>
“那一定把它吓得够呛。你的实战知识越来越惊人了，”我说。“几十年前我就该有你这样的侍从。”<BR>
<BR>
“现在，”他说，“请告诉我关于西罗帝尔的吸血鬼。”<BR>
<BR>

The Imperial Dragon<BR>
<FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"> 
The most recognized symbol of the Empire, few are aware that the Imperial Dragon is in fact of foreign origin. Emperor Reman Cyrodiil assumed it from the Tsaesci of Akavir after his victory over them at Pale Pass in 1E 2703, when the awestruck snakemen hailed him as dragon's blood. The dragon has been the sigil of the Empire and its dragonblood Emperors ever since. To honor the Eight Divines the beast is stylized in the shape of a diamond with four corners and four sides. The diamond above the dragon was added in the 3rd Era to denote Tiber Septim, or Talos, as the Ninth Divine.<BR> <BR> <BR><BR><BR> <BR> <BR> <BR> <BR> <BR> <BR> <BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"> 
Also known as the 'Wolf of Symmachus', this emblem serves as the official sigil of the King of Morrowind and can be seen in the banners of the royal palace in Mournhold. Originally the personal coat of arms of General Symmachus--a trusted servant of Tiber Septim, it later became the symbol for Morrowind's newly formed royal house after the province's annexation by the Empire. The wolf symbolizes the King's loyalty to the standing Emperor as it once symbolized Symmachus' ardent loyalty to Tiber Septim himself. Notice how the dragon motif is completely absent in this King Helseth version of the sigil whereas it was still present during King Llethan's reign. <BR> <BR>

<FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"> <BR>
The double-headed eagle was first brought to Morrowind by the Nords of Skyrim under King Vrage in the early First Era. Associating the eagle with their matron deity Kyne, the Nords would paint the symbol on their faces and shields hoping to win the goddess' favor. After King Vrage ended his successful campaign in Morrowind, the eagle, traditionally shown swooping up from Atmora, was revised to have two heads looking in opposite directions signifying the Nords' dominance over both east and west, fiery Dunmeth and frigid Skyrim. It was only natural that the Empire would adopt the already well-known sigil for itself after conquering both provinces, placing the Imperial Dragon above the eagle.<BR> <BR> <BR> <BR> <BR> <BR> <BR> <BR> <BR>

<FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"> <BR>
The lion as a heraldic motif can be traced all the way back to Second Era High Rock. It serves as the standard of the King of Wayrest, and later became a symbol for the whole Iliac Bay region. It might be surprising to encounter such a western symbol so far away in the east, but the reason for the lions' popularity in Morrowind lies in the province's recent history. Barenziah, the Queen Mother of Morrowind, was also the Queen of Wayrest during her period of exile. A popular notion is that the two lions represent her royal children: Helseth and Morgiah, who spent a great deal of their lives in Wayrest where they received a western noble's upbringing, hence being depicted as lions.<BR> <BR> <BR> <BR> <BR>

<FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">

帝国最公认的象征是帝国龙，但很少有人知道帝国龙实际上源自外国。在第一纪元2703年，皇帝雷曼·西罗帝尔在苍白关隘击败了阿卡维尔的赛埃锡人，当时惊愕不已的蛇人称他为龙血。自此，龙便成为了帝国及其龙血皇帝的徽记。为了尊崇八圣灵，这只野兽被风格化为一个具有四角四边的菱形。龙上方的菱形是在第三纪元加上去的，用以表示作为第九圣灵的泰伯·塞普汀，或塔洛斯。<BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER">
<FONT COLOR="500000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
<IMG SRC="TR\TR_crest-wolf.tga" WIDTH="240" HEIGHT="240"><BR>
皇家狼<BR>
<FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
这枚徽章，也被称为“锡马库斯之狼”，是晨风国王的官方徽记，可以在哀伤之城王宫的旗帜上看到。它最初是锡马库斯将军的个人纹章 -- 他是泰伯·塞普汀信任的仆从，后来在该行省被帝国吞并后，它成为了晨风新成立的王室的象征。这头狼象征着国王对在位皇帝的忠诚，正如它曾经象征着锡马库斯对泰伯·塞普汀本人的热切忠诚一样。请注意，在赫尔塞斯国王版本的徽章中，完全没有龙形图案，而在莱森国王统治时期，它仍然存在。<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER">
<FONT COLOR="500000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
<IMG SRC="TR\TR_crest-eagle.tga" WIDTH="240" HEIGHT="240"><BR>
双头鹰<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
<FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
双头鹰最早由天际的诺德人在第一纪元早期弗拉格国王的率领下带到晨风。诺德人将鹰与他们的母神吉讷联系起来，他们会在脸上和盾牌上画上这个符号，希望能赢得女神的青睐。弗拉格国王成功结束在晨风的战役后，传统上表现从阿特莫拉俯冲而下的鹰被修改为两个朝向相反方向的头，象征着诺德人对东西两方 -- 炽热的丹莫瑞斯和寒冷的天际 -- 的主导地位。帝国在征服这两个行省后，顺理成章地采用了这个已经很知名的徽记，并在鹰的上方放置了帝国龙。<BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER">
<FONT COLOR="500000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
<IMG SRC="TR\TR_crest-lions.tga" WIDTH="242" HEIGHT="242"><BR>
双狮<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
<FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
狮子作为纹章主题可以一直追溯到第二纪元的高岩。它曾是途歇国王的旗帜，后来成为了整个髂骨湾地区的象征。在遥远的东部地区遇到这样一个西方的标志可能会令人惊讶，但狮子在晨风流行的原因在于该行省最近的历史。晨风的王太后巴兰兹雅，在她流放期间也曾是途歇的女王。一种流行的观点认为，这两只狮子代表她的两个孩子：赫尔塞斯和莫吉雅，他们一生中大部分时间都在途歇度过，在那里接受了西方贵族的教养，因此被描绘成狮子。<BR><BR><BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER">
<IMG SRC="TR\TR_crest-wyrm.tga" WIDTH="240" HEIGHT="240"><BR>

瓦因特龙蛇<BR>
<FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER">
<IMG SRC="TR\TR_crest-fight.tga" WIDTH="240" HEIGHT="240"><BR>

战士公会纹章<BR>
<FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>

战士公会最初是阿卡维尔摄政王的一支雇佣战斗力量，在第二纪元321年签署《公会法案》时，帝国纹章学院授予了其纹章。公会的徽记风格化为一个纹章盾形纹章。它由一个朴素的黑白盾牌组成，背景是交叉的长剑。在第二纪元的原始设计中，背景的武器是弯刃单锋的阿卡维尔风格，不过如今背景中的武器可以根据特定公会分会所在区域而变化。例如，天际的分会可能会使用交叉的斧头而不是长剑。<BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR><BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
<FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>The Imperial Kitchen, Part 1<BR>
<BR>
The Colovian west is known as a land of simple, hearty food such as cheese, bread, wine and fruit: honest fare fit for soldiers and laborers. While it is less adventurous than the Nibenese kitchen, it would be unwise to dismiss this local cuisine as boorish or simple -- after all, this is the same plain, uncomplicated fare that fed the Legions during their great conquests.<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Highlands Grouts<BR>
The Colovian way to break the fast is sparse, but invigorating. This porridge is enjoyed with different additions depending on local customs: apple slices, salted cod, dried fish, wine, raw eggs, boiled poppad gourd pulp, and grapes are all common additions, as are spices such as Rihad pepper, muscat, or even some saffron.<BR>
A cup of crushed ironrye<BR>
A cup of fresh goat milk<BR>
Some honey<BR>
A pinch of salt<BR>
<BR>
In a small pot, add the oats, goat milk, honey, and salt together. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat. Allow the porridge to simmer softly until the crushed grains are soft and tender, and the milk has thickened.<BR>
<BR>
Ironrye is a hardy type of grain common in the west. Those familiar with other grains should be mindful that ironrye is tough and generally takes longer to soften. The addition of honey or another sweetener is advisable, as the grain by itself is rather bland.<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Lyco Stew<BR>
The dark lycovine is family of the nightshade, but do not let this discourage you: the lycoae of the West Weald are delicious both cold and cooked. Lyco stew is a traditional meal from the city of Sarchal, commonly eaten on rice or bread. Some may object to the use of goat meat: try substituting with mutton.<BR>
Two cups of spike rice<BR>
A lump of lard<BR>
One large onion<BR>
Two carrots<BR>
Some garlic<BR>
A fresh, spicy plena pepper<BR>
A flank of goat meat, slightly aged<BR>
A cup of Colovian wine<BR>
Three lycoae, pureed<BR>
A pinch of salt<BR>
Some Colovian hard cheese, grated or crushed<BR>
<BR>
Boil the spike rice in water. Season with a pinch of salt. Let the rice boil softly for about half an hour while you prepare the rest of the meal.<BR>
<BR>
Heat the lard in a pan to melt it down. Chop the onion, carrots, garlic, and plena pepper, and cook them until fragrant. Chop the goat meat into small chunks and brown it in the pan for a minute, then add a cup of wine. Once fragrant, add the pureed lycoae. Simmer until the sauce has thickened, about half an hour. Season with more salt. Drain the rice, then add the stew on top. Sprinkle with cheese.<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Durenta with Fish and Eggs<BR>
The small red kernels of the durata stalk are a staple of the western seaboard. Durenta is porridge-like dish made from roughly ground, dried durata kernels. While the durata stalk was introduced by the Redguards, this recipe is purely Colovian.<BR>
<BR>
Ground down durata meal can be hard to get outside of Colovia, but many soldiers receive it in care packages from their families back home -- maybe ask around a local garrison, or make it yourself by drying durate kernels in the sun, then powdering them with a mortar and pestle.<BR>
Half a cup of powdered durata kernels<BR>
A pinch of salt<BR>
Some garlic, to taste<BR>
Dried fish<BR>
A bit of olive oil<BR>
A pinch of powdered muscat<BR>
Two eggs<BR>
A handful of chopped olives<BR>
<BR>
Bring salted water to a boil, then pour in the durata powder while stirring briskly. Once the mixture is smooth and thick, keep it warm for about half an hour. Meanwhile, chop up the dried fish and garlic, then fry them together with some olive oil. Spice with muscat.<BR>
<BR>
Once the gruel is almost done, crack the eggs into the pan with the fish and garlic. While the eggs are cooking, scoop the durenta into bowls, and season liberally with Rihad pepper. Toss the fish and eggs on top, and finish with some fresh olives and perhaps some crushed cheese.<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
"Grandpa Goat in Garlic Sauce"
A meal of great nostalgic value to anyone who grew up in Colovia, this whimsically named feast is eaten on holidays like Tibedetha or the New Life Festival. Throughout Cyrodiil, goat tends to be the meat of choice for the poor: goats can thrive on nearly anything, from the sparse grasses of the Colovian Highlands to the marshy herbs of the eastern mangroves.<BR>
For the goat:<BR>
Two heads of garlic<BR>
Two onions<BR>
A handful of dried figs<BR>
Two carrots<BR>
A cup of olive oil<BR>
Two cups of Colovian wine<BR>
Some nigella seeds<BR>
A pinch of salt and freshly ground Rihad pepper<BR>
Rib or loin goat chops, well aged<BR>
<BR>
For the garlic sauce:<BR>
One head of garlic<BR>
A lump of lard<BR>
A spoonful of flour<BR>
A cup of goat milk<BR>
A cup of thick broth<BR>
A pinch of salt (preferably Sutchi)<BR>
A pinch of Rihad pepper<BR>
Some ground fennel seeds<BR>
A cup of Colovian hard cheese, grated or crushed<BR>
<BR>
Chop the onions, figs, carrots, and about half of the garlic. Toss the olive oil, nigella, salt, pepper, and one cup of wine in an ample lidded pot or mixing bowl. The other cup of wine is traditionally used in a toast to Saint Potri, who is credited with inventing the dish while stuck in a wine cask.<BR>
<BR>
Chop the goat meat into large pieces, then make small incisions along the flank. Clean the remaining garlic cloves and push them into the incisions. Add the meat to the bowl containing the oil and wine mixture, and make sure to toss it vigorously. Allow the meat to marinate overnight in a cool, dark place.<BR>
<BR>
Now we can make the garlic sauce. Heat lard in a saucepan, then add the crushed and minced garlic. Bake until browned. Add the flour, and quickly mix it until fragrant. Add the goat milk and broth, and stir briskly. Allow the sauce to simmer for a little while. Add salt, Rihad pepper and ground fennel to taste. Finally, stir in the grated cheese until the sauce is smooth. Keep the garlic sauce warm on the side of the fire, while you finish preparing the meat.<BR>
<BR>
Drain the goat chops. Heat more oil in an ample iron skillet, then brown the meat quickly on both sides. Allow the meat to cook through for another couple of minutes. Once the meat is to satisfaction, it can be presented alongside good Colovian bread or cooked spike rice, with garlic sauce on top and a sprinkling of crumbled cheese and garden herbs.<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Colovian "Battlewine"<BR>
This mulled wine was originally served to warriors before battle. Ancient physicians claimed that it excites the blood and dulls fear -- potentially due to the inclusion of raw mandrake root. Bottled battlewine is now sold in many places, but the best battlewine is still made at home.<BR>
A bottle of Colovian wine<BR>
An apple<BR>
Some honey<BR>
A handful of blood-lily petals<BR>
A small piece of mandrake root<BR>
A couple of anise stars<BR>
A pinch of ground cardamon seeds<BR>
One shot of Kurst (cherry liquor)<BR>
<BR>
Combine the honey with a cup of water in a pot, then boil until the it has completely dissolved. Grind the blood lily petals and mandrake root together in a mortar. Omit mandrake for a less volatile drink. Reduce the heat and add the anise stars and cardamon alongside the mandrake mixture to the bowl. Cut the apple into parts and add it as well. Simmer until thickened.<BR>
<BR>
Reduce the heat and add the wine. Let it softly simmer (not boil!) for a few hours. Strain and serve in tankards, adding a shot of Kurst at the very last moment (Kurst is a traditional Colovian cherry liquor -- if not available, any sharp, clear liquor will do.)<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>帝国厨房，第一部分<BR>
<BR>
科洛维亚西部以其简单、丰盛的食物而闻名，例如奶酪、面包、葡萄酒和水果：适合士兵和劳动者的诚实饭菜。虽然它不像尼本奈厨房那样富有冒险精神，但将这种地方菜视为粗俗或简单是不明智的 -- 毕竟，正是这种朴实、简单的食物，在军团进行伟大征服期间滋养了他们。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
高地粥<BR>
科洛维亚人打破斋戒的方式很简单，但令人振奋。这种粥根据当地习俗会添加不同的配料：苹果片、咸鳕鱼、干鱼、葡萄酒、生鸡蛋、煮熟的波帕德瓜瓤和葡萄都是常见的添加物，还有如里哈德辣椒、麝香葡萄，甚至一些藏红花等香料。<BR>
一杯碎铁麦<BR>
一杯新鲜羊奶<BR>
一些蜂蜜<BR>
一小撮盐<BR>
<BR>
在一个小锅里，加入麦片、羊奶、蜂蜜和盐。将混合物煮沸，然后调低火候。让粥慢慢煨煮，直到碎粒变得柔软嫩滑，奶液变得浓稠。<BR>
<BR>
铁麦是西方常见的一种坚韧的谷物。熟悉其他谷物的人应当注意，铁麦质地坚硬，通常需要更长时间才能煮软。添加蜂蜜或其他甜味剂是可取的，因为这种谷物本身味道相当寡淡。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
莱科炖菜<BR>
深色的莱科藤属于茄科，但别因此望而却步：西部森林的莱科艾无论是冷食还是热食都很美味。莱科炖菜是萨查尔城的传统菜肴，通常配米饭或面包食用。有些人可能不赞成使用山羊肉：试试用羊肉代替。<BR>
两杯尖米<BR>
一块猪油<BR>
一个大洋葱<BR>
两根胡萝卜<BR>
一些大蒜<BR>
一个新鲜辛辣的普莱纳辣椒<BR>
一块略经熟成的山羊腹肉<BR>
一杯科洛维亚葡萄酒<BR>
三个莱科艾，打成泥<BR>
一小撮盐<BR>
一些科洛维亚硬奶酪，磨碎或压碎<BR>
<BR>
将尖米在水中煮沸。用一小撮盐调味。让米饭慢慢煮约半小时，同时准备餐点的其余部分。<BR>
<BR>
在平底锅中加热猪油使其融化。将洋葱、胡萝卜、大蒜和普莱纳辣椒切碎，炒至散发香味。将山羊肉切成小块，放入锅中煎至焦黄一分钟，然后加入一杯酒。一旦散发香味，加入莱科艾泥。炖煮至酱汁浓稠，大约半小时。用更多盐调味。将米饭沥干，然后将炖菜浇在上面。撒上奶酪。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
杜伦塔配鱼与蛋<BR>
杜拉塔茎的小红色籽粒是西部沿海地区的主食。杜伦塔是一种用粗磨的干杜拉塔籽粒制成的类似粥的菜肴。尽管杜拉塔茎是由红卫人引入的，但这个食谱纯粹是科洛维亚的。<BR>
<BR>
科洛维亚以外的地方可能很难获得磨碎的杜拉塔粉，但许多士兵会收到家乡家人们寄来的关怀包裹中装有此物 -- 也许可以问问当地驻军，或者自己将杜拉塔籽粒在太阳下晒干，然后用研钵和研杵磨成粉。<BR>
半杯杜拉塔籽粒粉<BR>
一小撮盐<BR>
一些大蒜，适量<BR>
干鱼<BR>
一点橄榄油<BR>
一小撮麝香葡萄粉<BR>
两个鸡蛋<BR>
一把切碎的橄榄<BR>
<BR>
将盐水煮沸，然后一边快速搅拌一边倒入杜拉塔粉。一旦混合物变得顺滑浓稠，保持温热约半小时。同时，将干鱼和大蒜切碎，然后用一些橄榄油一起翻炒。用麝香葡萄调味。<BR>
<BR>
一旦粥快煮好了，将鸡蛋打入盛有鱼和蒜的锅中。在鸡蛋烹饪的同时，将杜伦塔舀入碗中，用里哈德辣椒大量调味。将鱼和蛋倒在上面，最后撒上一些新鲜橄榄，也许还有一些碎奶酪。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
“蒜汁山羊爷爷”
这道异想天开的菜肴充满怀旧气息，任何在科洛维亚长大的人都会对它感慨良多，常在“提贝德塔”或新生节等节日食用。在整个西罗帝尔，穷人倾向于选择山羊肉：山羊几乎可以依靠任何东西茁壮成长，从科洛维亚高地稀疏的草地到东部红树林的沼泽草本植物。<BR>
准备山羊：<BR>
两大头蒜<BR>
两个洋葱<BR>
一把干无花果<BR>
两根胡萝卜<BR>
一杯橄榄油<BR>
两杯科洛维亚葡萄酒<BR>
一些黑种草籽<BR>
一小撮盐和新鲜研磨的里哈德胡椒<BR>
经过良好熟成的山羊肋排或腰排<BR>
<BR>
准备蒜汁：<BR>
一头蒜<BR>
一块猪油<BR>
一勺面粉<BR>
一杯羊奶<BR>
一杯浓高汤<BR>
一小撮盐（最好用萨奇盐）<BR>
一小撮里哈德胡椒<BR>
一些研磨的茴香籽<BR>
一杯科洛维亚硬奶酪，磨碎或压碎<BR>
<BR>
将洋葱、无花果、胡萝卜和大约一半的大蒜切碎。在一个带盖的大锅或搅拌碗中，放入橄榄油、黑种草籽、盐、胡椒和一杯葡萄酒，搅拌均匀。另一杯葡萄酒传统上用于向圣波特里敬酒，据说他是在被困在酒桶时发明了这道菜。<BR>
<BR>
将山羊肉切成大块，然后沿肉侧划开小口。将剩下的大蒜瓣清理干净，塞入切口中。将肉放入装有油和酒混合物的碗中，确保用力翻拌。让肉在阴凉避光处腌制一夜。<BR>
<BR>
现在我们可以制作蒜汁了。在平底锅中加热猪油，然后加入压碎并切碎的大蒜。烘烤至焦黄。加入面粉，快速搅拌直至散发香味。加入羊奶和高汤，快速搅拌。让酱汁炖煮一会儿。加入盐、里哈德胡椒和研磨茴香籽调味。最后，搅拌磨碎的奶酪直至酱汁顺滑。将蒜汁放在火边保温，同时完成肉类的准备。<BR>
<BR>
沥干山羊排。在宽大的铁煎锅中加热更多油，然后将肉快速两面煎至焦黄。让肉再煮透几分钟。一旦肉达到满意程度，就可以与上好的科洛维亚面包或煮熟的尖米一起上桌，浇上蒜汁，并撒上碎奶酪和花园香草。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
科洛维亚“战酒”<BR>
这种热饮酒最初是在战前提供给战士的。古代医生声称它能激发血液、减少恐惧 -- 这可能是因为加入了生曼德拉草根。瓶装战酒现在在很多地方都有销售，但最好的战酒仍然是在家自制的。<BR>
一瓶科洛维亚葡萄酒<BR>
一个苹果<BR>
一些蜂蜜<BR>
一把血百合花瓣<BR>
一小块曼德拉草根<BR>
几颗八角<BR>
一小撮磨碎的小豆蔻籽<BR>
一小杯库尔斯特（樱桃利口酒）<BR>
<BR>
将蜂蜜与一杯水在锅中混合，然后煮沸直至完全溶解。将血百合花瓣和曼德拉草根在研钵中一起研磨。如果不想让酒太过刺激，可以省略曼德拉草。调低火候，将八角、小豆蔻以及曼德拉草混合物加入锅中。将苹果切块加入。慢炖直至浓稠。<BR>
<BR>
调低火候，加入葡萄酒。让它小火慢炖（不要沸腾！）几个小时。过滤后倒入大酒杯中，在最后一刻加入一小杯库尔斯特（库尔斯特是一种传统的科洛维亚樱桃利口酒 -- 如果没有，任何辛辣、清澈的烈酒都可以）。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>The Imperial Kitchen, Part 2
<BR>
If Colovia is known for its simple kitchen, then the Nibenay must by necessity be the land of extravagance. There is little need for me to repeat stories of the grand Heartlands cuisine, of courtly decadence, rare ingredients, and refined master-chefs with elaborate concoctions and deadly rivalries.<BR>
<BR>
But the average Nibenean does not feast on sugared quail and pomegranate wine. Like anywhere, the common people have their own local flavors and delights, sourced in their rice fields and riverlands. It is this quaint kitchen which interests us most.<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Pauper's Poppad Marrow<BR>
The poppad gourd grows plentiful in the eastern Heartlands, especially in the foggy grasslands surrounding the eponymous Lake Poppad. Local rice-farmers, too poor to afford a decent cauldron, hang these hardy, fireproof gourds above a fire to cook the white, soft pulp inside, which is then scooped out over rice.<BR>
<BR>
Memories of this dish were brought to the Imperial City by laborers, who sometimes longed for a taste of the simpler, less complicated life they led back home. In time, this led to the dish described below, which is a staple of the Imperial City's taverns.<BR>
One poppad gourd<BR>
Two carrots<BR>
A lump of lard<BR>
One onion<BR>
A pinch of salt<BR>
A handful of figs, fresh or dried<BR>
Some nuts or dried seeds<BR>
Pinches of grated muscat, cardamon, curcuma powder and Rihad pepper<BR>
A bit of honey<BR>
Some olive oil<BR>
A splash of mokre<BR>
A cup of sour wine<BR>
<BR>
Peel and slice the poppad gourd and boil it for about half an hour. Arrange the slices in a pot or baking dish alongside chopped carrots and onion, then sprinkle with a little salt.<BR>
<BR>
Take the figs and add them in a mortar and pestle with the nuts or dried seeds (if using dried figs, soak them in a little wine first). Mash into a paste. Add the spices and mix, then add the honey, mokre (a type of fish sauce, see below), wine, and stir into a smooth mixture.<BR>
<BR>
Poor the mixture over the poppad slices, cover with a lid, and place in a heated oven until the sauce is warm and bubbling.<BR>
<BR>
Note: keep the Poppad seeds and toast them for a nice snack.<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Garlicked Snails<BR>
A signature dish of the Valley of Altars. Anyone seeking to reproduce this recipe at home should first ensure themselves that the local variety of land snails are as edible as those of the southern Nibenay. Much like the Colovians and their garlicked goat, this recipe is heavy with garlic and cheese -- a preference which transcends the Imperial cultural divide. For those seeking authenticity, goat cheese from Buccita is widely recognized as the superior choice.<BR>
A heads of garlic<BR>
Crushed or grated hard goat cheese<BR>
Some St. Jahn's Wort flowers (or other garden herbs)<BR>
A pinch of coarse salt<BR>
Some olive oil and vinegar<BR>
A handful of siris snails (or equivalent)<BR>
<BR>
Ground the garlic with salt in a mortal until reduced to a paste. Add the cheese and the finely chopped herbs. Add the olive oil and vinegar, then work the mixture together until it is a smooth paste. Let it rest.<BR>
<BR>
Next, prepare the snails (in the Nibenay, the siris snail with blue and brown stripes is the canon choice). Remove the snails from their shells using a hook, then boil them in water for about fifteen minutes. Cover the snails with a layer of garlic paste, then stuff them back into their shells and seal up the entrance with more of the paste. Once all shells are prepared, grill them over a fire until fragrant (make sure not the heat them too much, lest the shells pop).<BR>
<BR>
Through garlicked snails were once a delicacy enjoyed only by the Potentate courts, they are now common street food, and often eaten cold as a snack.<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Glazed prawns<BR>
This dish is eaten all along the Niben, which is home to a kind of freshwater prawn endemic to the river and surrounding ricelands.<BR>
A handful of raw, peeled prawns<BR>
A splash of olive oil<BR>
Two spoons of mokre<BR>
A spoon of liquid honey<BR>
A pinch of curcuma powder<BR>
Freshly ground Rihad pepper<BR>
A cup of rice<BR>
<BR>
Add the olive oil, mokre and honey in a pan, then add the prawns. Gently bake the prawns in the mixture until they are tender. Remove the prawns from the pan.<BR>
<BR>
Boil the rice in a pot. Meanwhile, continue to reduce the honey sauce until it has become thickened. Add the curcuma and pepper, then pour the glaze over the prawns. Serve the prawns over a bowl of warm rice.<BR>
<BR>
Rice is a staple of the central valleys, but Imperials maintain several varieties for different purposes. Spike rice is a hardy variety common to Colovia, where it can grow in dry fields. Common white rice is grown and eaten nearly anywhere, but is sometimes seen as a commoner's choice. Red rice is grown only in the tinmi soil of the Heartlands, and is consider the superior type: the Emperor and his court dine exclusively on red rice, and to give a dignitary anything less is considered an affront.<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Brandied plums<BR>
Cyrodiilic brandy is known across the Empire as the subject of songs and tarriffs. Despite being made with Colovian wines (of a lesser variety), the great distilleries creating this desirable product are all located in the Imperial City and its surroundings.<BR>
<BR>
As most brandy is destined for export, common Imperials rarely enjoy the taste of true Cyrodiilic brandy. Most make do with cut brandy (mixed with mori and water) or pomace brandy (made from a fermented detritus of the winemaking process, often in illegal stills).<BR>
<BR>
While imbibing these products is inadvisable, they (alongside cheaper provincial brandies) lend themselves well to the making of brandied plums, a true Heartlands treat.<BR>
A jar-full of plums<BR>
A pinch of dried hibiscus flowers<BR>
Two cups of honey<BR>
A pinch of salt<BR>
Two cups of brandy<BR>
<BR>
Clean and stem the plums, then pack them into a clean, sturdy jar, cutting up and removing the pit of about half the plums. Add the hibiscus.<BR>
<BR>
Bring the honey, salt, and a cup of water to a boil in a saucepan. Simmer until it becomes a syrup. Let the syrup cool, then add the brandy and poor the liquid into the jar of plums, making sure it is filled to the brim. Make sure the jar is sealed tight, then allow it to rest for about five days.<BR>
<BR>
Of course, plums made with real Cyrodiilic brandy are vastly superior, but such delicacies are rarely consumed outside of noble circles.<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Mokre<BR>
A fermented fish sauce enjoyed by both rich and poor: the courtly master-chefs mix it with wine, vinegar, pepper, and olive oil to create a peerless marinade, while the poor fishermen of the central valleys often finish their day with little more than a bowl of rice flavored with mokre.<BR>
A jarful of fish or crab intestines (most fishmongers are happy to part with these)<BR>
A bottle of vinegar<BR>
A bottle of mori (rice beer)<BR>
A cup of salt<BR>
A tankard of salt water<BR>
Special ingredients to taste<BR>
A cup of rice<BR>
<BR>
Take the fish and crab guts, chop them up and throw them into a large pot or vessel. Add vinegar, rice beer, and copious amounts of salt. Leave the mixture to rest for a day and a night, then fill whatever space is left in the pot with the salt water. Seal the top of the pot tightly with wax or cords, then leave it to ferment for two months (Nibenese peasants leave the pots hanging on trees or on the eaves of their houses).<BR>
<BR>
Powder dry rice using a mortar, then roast this powder in a pan or skillet. Open the jar and mix the half-fermented mokre with the roasted rice powder, along with any special spices you wish to include. Seal the pot again for one more month, until the fermentation is finished.<BR>
<BR>
Mokre is made with a wide variety of spices, depending on the region. Common additions are garlic, roasted Rihad pepper, fennel seeds, plena pepper, anise, and caraway seeds. Some Nibenese spike their mokre with drugs like thyrwort, moon sugar, or sursum -- always think twice before accepting a dinner invitation in the Nibenay.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>帝国厨房，第二部分
<BR>
如果说科洛维亚以其简单的厨房而闻名，那么尼本奈则必然是奢侈之地。我无需重复讲述心脏地带的宏伟美食、宫廷的颓废、珍稀的食材，以及那些精于复杂调制、相互间有你死我活竞争的精致大师厨师们的故事。<BR>
<BR>
但普通的尼本奈人并不以糖渍鹌鹑和石榴酒为盛宴。和其他任何地方一样，平民百姓自有其源自稻田和河畔的本地风味与乐趣。正是这种古朴的厨房最令我们感兴趣。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
穷人的波帕德瓜瓤<BR>
波帕德瓜在东部心脏地生长茂盛，尤其是在同名的珀帕德湖周围雾气弥漫的草原上。当地的稻农太穷，买不起像样的锅，他们将这些结实耐火的瓜悬挂在火上，烹煮内部白色柔软的瓜瓤，然后舀出浇在米饭上。<BR>
<BR>
对这道菜的回忆是由工人带到帝都的，他们有时渴望品尝家乡那种更简单、更不复杂的生活滋味。随着时间的推移，便产生了下面描述的这道菜，它如今是帝都酒馆的主食之一。<BR>
一个波帕德瓜<BR>
两根胡萝卜<BR>
一块猪油<BR>
一个洋葱<BR>
一小撮盐<BR>
一把无花果，新鲜或干的<BR>
一些坚果或干种子<BR>
少许磨碎的麝香葡萄、小豆蔻、姜黄粉和里哈德胡椒<BR>
一点蜂蜜<BR>
一些橄榄油<BR>
少许莫克雷<BR>
一杯酸葡萄酒<BR>
<BR>
将波帕德瓜去皮切片，煮沸约半小时。将瓜片与切碎的胡萝卜和洋葱一起放入锅或烤盘中，然后撒上少许盐。<BR>
<BR>
将无花果与坚果或干种子放入研钵中（如果使用干无花果，先用少许酒浸泡），捣成糊状。加入香料混合，然后加入蜂蜜、莫克雷（一种鱼露，见下文）、葡萄酒，搅拌成顺滑的混合物。<BR>
<BR>
将混合物倒在波帕德瓜片上，盖上盖子，放入预热好的烤箱中，直至酱汁温热并冒泡。<BR>
<BR>
注意：保留波帕德瓜的种子，烤一下作为美味小吃。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
蒜香蜗牛<BR>
祭坛谷的招牌菜。任何想在家里重现这个食谱的人，首先应确保当地品种的陆生蜗牛与尼本奈南部的同样可食用。很像科洛维亚人和他们的蒜香山羊，这道菜大蒜和奶酪用量很大 -- 这是一种超越了帝国文化鸿沟的偏爱。对于寻求正宗风味的人来说，来自布奇塔的羊奶酪被公认为最佳选择。<BR>
几头大蒜<BR>
压碎或磨碎的硬羊奶酪<BR>
一些圣雅恩草花（或其他花园香草）<BR>
一小撮粗盐<BR>
一些橄榄油和醋<BR>
一把西里斯蜗牛（或同等品种）<BR>
<BR>
将大蒜与盐在研钵中研磨成糊状。加入奶酪和切碎的香草。加入橄榄油和醋，然后将混合物搅拌成顺滑的糊状。静置待用。<BR>
<BR>
接下来，准备蜗牛（在尼本奈，蓝棕色条纹的西里斯蜗牛是正宗选择）。用钩子将蜗牛肉从壳中取出，然后在水中煮沸约十五分钟。用一层蒜泥覆盖蜗牛肉，然后将它们塞回壳中，并用更多的蒜泥封住入口。所有蜗牛壳准备好后，放在火上烤至散发香味（注意不要加热过度，以免壳爆裂）。<BR>
<BR>
虽然蒜香蜗牛曾是只有摄政王宫廷才能享用的美味，但它们现在已成为常见的街头食品，常作为冷盘小吃食用。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
蜜汁大虾<BR>
这道菜在尼本河沿岸随处可见，该地区盛产一种该河流和周边稻田特有的淡水大虾。<BR>
一把生的、去壳的大虾<BR>
少许橄榄油<BR>
两勺莫克雷<BR>
一勺液体蜂蜜<BR>
一小撮姜黄粉<BR>
新鲜研磨的里哈德胡椒<BR>
一杯米饭<BR>
<BR>
在平底锅中加入橄榄油、莫克雷和蜂蜜，然后加入大虾。用混合物将大虾轻轻煎至软嫩。将大虾从锅中取出。<BR>
<BR>
在锅中煮米饭。同时，继续将蜂蜜酱汁收稠至浓稠。加入姜黄和胡椒，然后将蜜汁浇在大虾上。将大虾盛放在一碗温热的米饭上。<BR>
<BR>
大米是中部山谷的主食，但帝国人会根据不同的用途保留几个品种。尖米是科洛维亚常见的一种坚韧品种，可以在干旱的田地中生长。普通白米几乎在任何地方都有种植和食用，但有时被视为平民的选择。红米只在心脏地的廷米土壤中种植，被认为是 superior 的品种：皇帝和他的宫廷只吃红米，给一位显贵提供任何次等的米饭都被视为侮辱。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
白兰地李子<BR>
西罗帝尔白兰地作为歌曲和关税的主题而闻名于整个帝国。尽管它是用科洛维亚葡萄酒（品质较低的一种）酿造的，但生产这种令人向往的产品的各大酿酒厂都位于帝都及其周边地区。<BR>
<BR>
由于大多数白兰地都用于出口，普通的帝国人很少能品尝到真正的西罗帝尔白兰地。大多数人用勾兑白兰地（与莫里和水混合）或果渣白兰地（用酿酒过程中发酵的残渣，通常在非法蒸馏器中制成）凑合。<BR>
<BR>
尽管饮用这些产品并不可取，但它们（连同更便宜的行省白兰地）非常适合制作白兰地李子，一种真正的心脏地美食。<BR>
一满罐李子<BR>
一小撮干木槿花<BR>
两杯蜂蜜<BR>
一小撮盐<BR>
两杯白兰地<BR>
<BR>
将李子洗净去蒂，然后装入干净结实的罐中，将大约一半的李子切碎并去核。加入木槿花。<BR>
<BR>
在平底锅中将蜂蜜、盐和一杯水煮沸。慢炖直至成为糖浆。让糖浆冷却，然后加入白兰地，将液体倒入李子罐中，确保液体加满至罐口。确保罐子密封严实，然后静置约五天。<BR>
<BR>
当然，用真正的西罗帝尔白兰地制作的白兰地李子要美味得多，但这种美味在贵族圈子之外很少享用。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
莫克雷<BR>
一种发酵鱼露，富人和穷人都喜爱：宫廷主厨将其与葡萄酒、醋、胡椒和橄榄油混合，制成无与伦比的腌料；而中部山谷的穷苦渔民，常常在一天结束时，只用一碗莫克雷调味的米饭果腹。<BR>
一罐鱼或蟹的内脏（大多数鱼贩很乐意处理这些东西）<BR>
一瓶醋<BR>
一瓶莫里（米酒）<BR>
一杯盐<BR>
一大杯盐水<BR>
特种调味料，适量<BR>
一杯米<BR>
<BR>
将鱼和蟹的内脏切碎，放入一个大锅或容器中。加入醋、米酒和大量盐。让混合物静置一天一夜，然后用盐水填满锅中剩余的空间。用蜡或绳子将锅口密封严实，然后让其发酵两个月（尼本奈农民将锅挂在树上或屋檐下）。<BR>
<BR>
用研钵将干米磨成粉，然后在平底锅或煎锅中将米粉炒香。打开罐子，将半发酵的莫克雷与炒米粉以及任何你想添加的特种香料混合。再次将罐子密封一个月，直到发酵完成。<BR>
<BR>
莫克雷根据地区的不同，会使用多种香料。常见的添加物有：大蒜、烤里哈德胡椒、茴香籽、普莱纳胡椒、八角、葛缕子籽。一些尼本奈人会在他们的莫克雷中加入提尔草、月亮糖或苏苏姆等毒品 -- 在接受尼本奈的晚宴邀请前，请务必三思。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Imperial Kitchen I<BR>

Imperial Minced Meat<BR>
<BR>
2 handfuls of minced meat
1 bread soaked in white wine
1/2 teaspoon of freshly ground pepper
1/2 teaspoon of salt
a cup of white wine
some stone-pine kernels
green peppercorns<BR>

Imperial Fish<BR>

Imperial Chicken<BR>

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_ImperialNavyTR
The Imperial Navy
帝国海军

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_ImperialNavyTR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Imperial Navy<br> 
Bacola Gloriosus<BR> 
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
The Imperial Navy is a vital, but often neglected subject among the citizenry of the Empire. While the sailors and soldiers who serve honorably aboard seaworthy vessels are often some of the bravest men and women to be found in all of Tamriel, the lack of deep water channels within many areas gives rise to the opinion that an Imperial Navy cannot possibly be worth the expenditure it requires. As an aside, some also point to a general lack of trade among the various other provinces as a reason against maintaining a Navy -- with few trade ships to escort, it is contended, a Navy serves no purpose.<BR> 
While such concerns may have varying degrees of validity, they do not take into account many other, greater concerns. Individuals do not typically look far outside their own borders, but the sight of the Emperor must reach farther. Indeed, Imperial authority does not encompass one province, but all! And so it is that one cannot consider merely the coast of High Rock or Elsweyr, but the whole, unbroken coastline of Tamriel. One can be assured that the shores of Tamriel stretch long into the horizon, to a distance that boggles the common mind. What the common mind does not often consider is that this vast span is often totally undefended from outside threats, making the Imperial Navy a key part of any advance warning of same, and the first line of defense. In addition to giving proof against foreign dangers, the Navy also plays an essential part in maintaining Imperial Law on the high seas.<BR> 
In that cause, ships are often anchored along routes known to be used by smugglers and other criminals who seek to evade justice by fleeing to the water. For example, the north of Morrowind is heavily patrolled, effectively blocking a once-popular route around Skyrim once used to take stolen ebony and Dwemer artifacts to other Provinces. Such ignorant scavengers must now employ the more naturally shallow and treacherous Inner Sea between the isle of Vvardenfell and the mainland. In response, the Navy began to use smaller, lighter ships with flatter hulls in this area to chase down the smugglers and combat general lawlessness. As a second example, ships also patrol the waters south of Black Marsh, in a noble attempt to stop slavers. This effort, however, seems to have produced mixed results; the more smugglers that are slain or brought to justice, the more difficult it becomes to obtain slaves. By increasing the probability that slaves will be more difficult to obtain, the Navy has sadly increased the value of slaves on the black market, and so the lure of gold has drawn more to the trade. The Navy is also very active on the western coast of Tamriel, given the large number of familiar sea routes and the number of provinces that share a connection to the Eltheric Ocean.<BR> 
The crew of an Imperial Naval vessel varies greatly. Each large ship generally has a complement of archers, a priest or a wizard (more often than not a spellsword mercenary), several officers and a number of general sailors. The general sailors are often standard Imperial soldiers with either sailing skill, or who have expressed an interest in a post not bound by land. These 'soldiers of the sea' help to balance out the generally ranged capability of the remainder crew. Some ships have a mounted ballista, but these are usually found only on heavy ships and generally on the western coast of Tamriel. These can be used for a variety of purposes, the simplest of which being the piercing of an opponent's sail or the breeching of an opponent's hull. If there is but a small distance between combatant ships, they can be used, with the addition of rope, to board the other vessel.<BR> 
In battle, the Imperial Navy is incredibly effective. The tactics employed by the Navy offer many advantages. Unorganized groups can rarely counter them and therefore casualties among the Navy are few, and a battle usually yields the winner a new ship (although the condition of it can vary greatly). In common naval battles, archers generally rake the deck of the enemy with arrows, and once the ship is close enough to board, light infantry moves and engages the remaining enemy crew in melee combat. The spellcaster on board often can change the face of the worst battles. Casters skilled in the school of Alteration can bend the wind so that enemy arrows find themselves impeded, or for a fast escape should it be needed, or, more often, to prevent the retreat of the enemy. Some of the spellcasters deployed on board Navy ships are skilled in the school of Destruction, and therefore don't often leave much left to capture. A Cult priest skilled in the school of Restoration can also be helpful, as casualties (though usually minor) are often inflicted on the ship in the course of battle.<BR> 
The idea behind capturing rather than destroying an enemy ship is often an economic one; once a ship is captured, its cargo can be returned to its original owners (generally with a nominal fee) and the ship can be sold, or used by the Imperial Navy. Even partially damaged ships can be cannibalized to repair other Imperial vessels. This provides the Navy a constant supply of new ships and shipbuilding materials for a fraction of the cost a shipbuilder might charge, making the Navy very cheap and effective for the Empire.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
帝国海军<br>
巴科拉·格洛里奥苏斯<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
帝国海军是至关重要的，但在帝国公民中，它常常被忽视。虽然那些在适航船只上光荣服役的水手和士兵通常是整个泰姆瑞尔最勇敢的人，但许多地区缺乏深水航道的事实让人认为，帝国海军不可能值得其所需的开支。另外，有人还指出，其他各省之间普遍缺乏贸易，这也是反对维持海军的理由 -- 有人认为，没有多少商船需要护航，海军便没有意义。<BR>
尽管这些担忧可能有一定程度的道理，但它们没有考虑到许多其他更重要的问题。个人通常不会过多关注自身边界以外的地区，但皇帝的视野必须更广。确实，帝国的权威涵盖的不是一个行省，而是所有行省！因此，不能仅仅考虑高岩或艾斯维尔的海岸，而必须考虑泰姆瑞尔完整而连绵的海岸线。可以肯定地说，泰姆瑞尔的海岸线绵延至地平线，远至常人难以想象。常人往往没有考虑到的是，这广阔的海岸线通常完全没有防御外部威胁的能力，这使得帝国海军成为了任何预警的关键组成部分，也是第一道防线。除了防范外来危险，海军还在维护帝国在公海上的法律方面发挥着重要作用。<BR>
为此，海军常在已知的走私者和其他试图逃往海上以逃避法律的罪犯所使用的航线上锚泊船只。例如，晨风北部受到严密巡逻，有效地封锁了一条曾经环绕天际、用于将偷来的黑檀木和锻莫文物运往其他省的热门路线。那些对此一无所知的拾荒者现在不得不使用瓦登费尔岛与大陆之间天然较浅且危险的陆内海。作为回应，海军开始在该地区使用更小、更轻、船底更平的船只追捕走私者，打击普遍的违法行为。再举一个例子，海军还在黑沼泽南部水域巡逻，旨在阻止奴隶贩子，这是一项高尚的尝试。然而，这种努力似乎产生了好坏参半的结果；被击毙或绳之以法的走私者越多，获得奴隶就越困难。令人遗憾的是，海军通过增加获得奴隶难度的可能性，提高了奴隶在黑市上的价值，因此黄金的诱惑吸引了更多人参与这一交易。鉴于熟悉的海上航线数量众多，以及多个行省与埃尔瑟利克洋相连，海军在泰姆瑞尔西海岸也非常活跃。<BR>
帝国海军舰船的船员配置多种多样。每艘大型船通常配备一定数量的弓箭手、一名祭司或巫师（通常是雇佣兵型的魔剑士）、几名军官和若干普通水手。普通水手通常是具有航海技能或表示对不受陆地限制的职位感兴趣的帝国正规士兵。这些“海之战士”有助于平衡其余船员普遍的远程作战能力。一些舰船装有固定式弩炮，但这些通常只出现在重型舰船上，并且一般部署在泰姆瑞尔西海岸。这些弩炮可用于多种用途，最简单的就是刺穿对手的船帆或击穿对手的船体。如果交战船只之间距离很近，还可以用它们配合绳索来登上另一艘船。<BR>
在战斗中，帝国海军的效率极高。海军采用的战术具有诸多优势。无组织的团体很难对抗这些战术，因此海军的伤亡很少，而且一场战斗通常会为胜利者带来一艘新船（尽管其状况可能千差万别）。在常见的海战中，弓箭手通常用箭矢清扫敌方甲板，一旦船只靠近到足以接舷，轻型步兵就会移动并与剩余的敌方船员进行近战。船上的施法者常常能扭转最糟糕的战斗局势。擅长变化系的施法者可以改弯风向，使敌方箭矢受阻；或在需要时快速逃脱；或更常见的是阻止敌人撤退。一些部署在海军舰船上的施法者擅长毁灭系，因此往往不会留下多少可俘获的东西。擅长恢复系的教团祭司也很有帮助，因为在战斗过程中，舰船通常会遭受伤亡（尽管通常较为轻微）。<BR>
俘获而非摧毁敌舰的想法通常是出于经济考虑；一旦俘获一艘船，其货物可以归还原主（通常收取象征性费用），而船本身可以出售或由帝国海军使用。即使是部分损坏的船只，也可以拆卸零件用于修理其他帝国船只。这为海军提供了源源不断的新船和造船材料，而成本仅为造船厂可能要价的一小部分，使得海军对帝国来说非常经济且高效。<BR>"""

Indoril Beroth and the Hermit<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Indoril Beroth was walking along the banks of the River Thirr one quiet morning when he spotted a hermit laying defeated in its shallows. The hermit was a young mer, who the Indoril could see was clearly favored by Almsivi. Such is the sight of the Indorils.<BR>
<BR>
"Are you alright, young mer? Why do you wade in the river shallows?" asked the Indoril, getting the hermit's attention. <BR>
And looking up from the water, the hermit shook his head, saying: "No, Indoril, I am worse than I have ever been! I am beset by doubt, and I fear that my piety is faltering. I had hoped the Thirr's waters would cleanse me, somehow."<BR>
<BR>
"Have you faltered somehow in your duties?" the Indoril asked, to which the hermit shook his head again.<BR>
<BR>
"Never, Indoril! I am the very image of duty. I have forsaken everything for my faith and become a hermit here along the river."<BR>
<BR>
"Are you tempted, then, by unseemly thoughts in your hermitage?" Indoril Beroth asked, but to this as well the hermit merely shook his head. <BR>
<BR>
"Never once, in my isolation, have I been tempted by the thought of any evil or unseemly deed. I have lived faithfully and peacefully for nigh on twenty years now," the hermit said, and this was greatly puzzling to the Indoril. <BR>
<BR>
"Then pray tell," Indoril Beroth said finally, "what anguishes you so?"<BR>
<BR>
"In all my years of isolation," the hermit replied, "not once have I felt even the barest thread of connection to Almsivi. This life does nothing for me, and I worry that it is because I am faithless at heart! Even worse, I could have soul sickness! Tell me, Indoril, how might I cure this affliction of mine!"<BR>
<BR>
And at this, Indoril Beroth smiled. <BR>
<BR>
"This is a problem with a simple solution: You must swear off the life of a hermit, and find a new life in the city."<BR>
<BR>
"But Indoril," the hermit replied, confused, "how is a life in the city more pious than life as a hermit?"<BR>
<BR>
"A life in the city is no more pious than life in a hermitage, of course," the Indoril acknowledged. "In fact, the hermit's life is indeed more pious than that of the common citymer, but what good is life in a hermitage when you do not have the soul of a hermit? Just as I have the soul of an Indoril, and just as the slave has a slave's soul, you must surely have a noble soul fit for its own noble duty. It is clear for all to see that your soul is not fit for isolation; that is why I believe you must find faith in the cities."<BR>
<BR>
And with that, Indoril Beroth took his leave of the hermit so that he could return to his garden in Nanaav. Thereafter, the hermit swore off his isolation and became a smith's apprentice in the city of Othrenis. Soon after, he went on to inherit his masters' trade; mer from across Resdayn would come to seek his expertise. When asked what his secret was, it is said that the craftsmer would answer that his steel was hardened by his faith in Almsivi.<BR>

Industries: the Rivermen

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_IndustriesRivermenPC
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>Industries of the Niben: the Rivermen<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>

Produced by order of the Conclave of Arts and Artificers<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

Fishermen are an ubiquitous sight along the Niben river banks. Wearing loose clothing and coarse silken knee-high pants, they float along the stream in flat-bottom boats and skiffs, casting their nets and laying their lines. Fish, beside the equally omnipresent rice, is the dominant component of the Niben diet. Common catches are the Chrysophant, Slaughterfish, and the common Mudcrab. The catching and processing of fish are a major industry, indeed, the only industry in many villages of the river. Along the brackish southern parts of the river, the growing of Kollops is also undertaken in large hatcheries and breeding grounds along the banks. These mollusks are prized as a source of food for the lower classes, and for the reddish-brown Tinmi pearls they produce, favored by the Niben jewelers.<BR>

<BR>

The Chrysophant is considered an expensive fish, rarely eaten by the common folk. Instead, their diet focuses on the humble meat of the Kollop, Mudcrab, and Slaughterfish, for which they know many unusual preparations. Of note is the famous Nibenese fermented fish-sauce, also known as Mokre, said to be an invention of the Keptu tribes. This oily sauce is made by gathering fish guts and leftovers in large clay jars, mixing them with salt, sugar and local spices, and leaving the jars suspended for several months from eaves and tree branches, in sight of the sun. This preparation is said to soften the bitter taste of Slaughterfish meat, while the often tasteless Mudcrab meat becomes in turn more palatable. The Niben Valley is one of the few places where these base kinds of meat are commonly eaten, and even considered a delicacy. Nevertheless, the traveler unaccustomed to this dish is advised to be cautious around the Niben kitchen, and never to look in any unlabeled pots found hanging around the villages, lest he encounters a particularly putrid surprise.<BR>

<BR>

Another reason why Slaughterfish is considered a treasured catch are the particularly lustrous scales of the Rumare breed. Besides their potent alchemical applications, these scales are another prized components for jewelry and clothing ornament among the trader caste, who consider them emblematic of cunning and forceful behavior. These scales are also prized among certain Argonian tribes in the Blackwood and Argon border with whom the Nibenese sometimes trade, where they are used as a highly symbolic form of currency.<BR>

"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>尼本的产业：河民<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>

应艺术与工匠议会之令编制<BR>

<BR>

渔夫们在尼本河沿岸随处可见。他们穿着宽松的衣服和粗丝及膝裤，乘着平底小船和轻舟顺流而下，撒网垂钓。除了同样无处不在的大米，鱼类是尼本饮食的主要组成部分。常见渔获有克里索凡特鱼、食人鱼和常见的泥沼蟹。捕鱼和加工鱼类是一项主要产业，实际上是该河沿岸许多村庄的唯一产业。在河流南部半咸水地区，沿岸还有大型孵化场和繁殖地养殖科洛普贝。这些软体动物因其可作为下层阶级的食物来源，以及它们产出的红褐色廷米珍珠（受尼本珠宝商青睐）而备受青睐。<BR>

<BR>

克里索凡特鱼被认为是昂贵的鱼类，平民很少食用。相反，他们的饮食主要依赖科洛普贝、泥沼蟹和食人鱼这类普通的肉类，他们知道许多不寻常的烹饪方法。其中值得注意的是著名的尼本奈发酵鱼露，也称为莫克雷，据说是克普图部落发明的。这种油腻的酱汁是通过将鱼内脏和下脚料收集在大陶罐中，与盐、糖和当地香料混合，然后将罐子悬挂在屋檐和树枝下，暴露在阳光下数月制成。据说这种制备方法可以软化食人鱼肉质的苦味，而通常无味的泥沼蟹肉则变得更加可口。尼本河谷是少数几个这些普通肉类被普遍食用，甚至被视为美味的地方之一。然而，不习惯这道菜的外地旅行者，建议谨慎对待尼本厨房，切勿查看村庄周围悬挂的任何没有标签的罐子，以免遇到特别腐臭的“惊喜”。<BR>

<BR>

食人鱼被视为珍贵渔获的另一个原因是，尤其是鲁玛雷品种的鱼鳞特别有光泽。除了它们强大的炼金用途外，这些鳞片还是商人种姓中用于珠宝和服饰装饰的珍贵材料，他们认为它象征着狡猾和强硬的行为。这些鳞片在黑檀林和阿尔贡边境的某些阿尔贡部落中也备受珍视，尼本奈人有时会与他们进行贸易，在那里鳞片被用作一种高度象征性的货币形式。<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>

Produced by order of the Conclave of Arts and Artificers<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

Alchemists accustomed to the rarity and high price of Sload soap elsewhere in Tamriel are often surprised at this product's abundance in the Niben Valley. In truth, this version of Sload soap is alchemically less valuable than the "true" product, due to its degenerate origins and the Nibenese focus on cosmetics over alchemical usage. Trade with the Sload has been illegal across the Empire since the First Era, and any samples to be found in alchemists' or perfumers' workshops today are more than likely acquired through illegal means. Not so in the Nibenay, where purified, low-grade oil forms the basis of a thriving market in salves and lotions, all guaranteed to keep the skin young, increase agility and virility, and cloud the mind to the best of Niben ability.<BR>

<BR>

One would be forgiven, however, for abstaining from these products after learning the way in which they are produced. The Niben soap industry, being denied the natural source for its soap, now relies on a limited number of Sload grubs, alchemically suspended in an embryonic, non-sentient state, all of which were plundered ages ago during the Thrassian War. In the great soap-tanks of Lake Rumare and the Niben Bay, these grubs are fed on masses of rotting fish and crab dredged from the river, until they grow to gargantuan proportions. When a grub has reached a sufficiently massive size, the so-called soap-cutters come to lop large pieces off the creature, leaving the kernel mass to regrow, and process the cut pieces into the oil so beloved by merchants and priests.<BR>

<BR>

In this way, the Niben refineries have made a profit from the same regenerating grubs for centuries. Soap refineries of this type can be found in Bravil, Delodiil and on the Imperial City's poorer, more industrial islands. Since each refinery only uses its own specimens, a piece of soap can often reliably be traced back to its firm of origin due to the signature features each grub imparts on its product.<BR>

<BR>

These unique features also serve as a means of trade protection. The limited resources and esoteric trade secrets of the soap-cutters make this profitable industry very entrenched and resistant to growth. It is in practice impossible to start a new firm in a legal manner, since obtaining a grub requires one to either deal with the Sload (which is illegal), buy from the refineries (who never sell), or steal from them (whereafter the product would be instantly recognized). The existing refineries live in constant fear of  sabotage: an expertly used bag of salt could very well decimate an entire grub population. Indeed, recent aggressive business practices have all but destroyed the Bravil firms, putting further strain on a limited market. These unpleasant business practices, coupled with the occasional rumor of escaped feral Sload in the Imperial City's underground, have given the refineries an unpleasant reputation as of late.<BR>

应艺术与工匠议会之令编制<BR>

习惯泰姆瑞尔其他地方斯洛德皂稀有且价格高昂的炼金术士，常常对尼本河谷中这种产品的大量存在感到惊讶。事实上，这种版本的斯洛德皂在炼金价值上不如“真品”，因为它起源不佳，并且尼本奈人更注重化妆品而非炼金用途。自第一纪元以来，与斯洛德的贸易在整个帝国都是非法的，当今在炼金术士或香水工坊中找到的任何样品，十有八九是通过非法途径获得的。但在尼本奈，情况并非如此，在那里，纯化的低等级油构成了一蓬勃的药膏和乳液市场的基础，所有产品都保证能保持皮肤年轻、增强敏捷与男性活力，并尽尼本所能地迷惑心智。<BR>

<BR>

然而，如果有人了解其生产方式后选择不使用这些产品，也是情有可原的。尼本的肥皂产业因无法获得肥皂的天然来源，如今依赖于数量有限的斯洛德幼虫，这些幼虫通过炼金术被维持在胚胎样的、无感知的状态，它们都是很久以前在瑟拉斯战争期间掠夺来的。在鲁玛雷湖和尼本湾的巨大肥皂槽中，这些幼虫以从河中疏浚出的大量腐烂鱼蟹为食，直至长到巨大无比。当幼虫长到足够大的尺寸时，所谓的“切皂匠”会来砍下大块的虫体，留下核心部分让其再生，并将切下的部分加工成商人和祭司们钟爱的那种油脂。<BR>

<BR>

就这样，尼本的炼油厂数百年来一直利用着同一批不断再生的幼虫获利。这种类型的肥皂精炼厂可以在布拉维尔、德洛迪尔以及帝都那些较为贫困、工业程度较高的岛上找到。由于每个精炼厂只使用自己的幼虫样本，每块肥皂通常可以因其幼虫赋予产品的特征，可靠地追溯到其原产公司。<BR>

<BR>

这些独特的特征也起到了贸易保护的作用。有限的资源和切皂匠们深奥的行业秘密，使得这个利润丰厚的产业根基深厚，难以发展。实际上，不可能以合法的方式创办一家新公司，因为获取幼虫需要要么与斯洛德交易（这是非法的），要么从现有精炼厂购买（他们从不外售），要么从他们那里偷窃（之后产品会立即被认出）。现有的精炼厂始终生活在被蓄意破坏的恐惧中：巧妙使用一袋盐就很可能导致整个幼虫种群灭门。事实上，最近激进的商业行为几乎摧毁了布拉维尔的公司，使本已有限的市场雪上加霜。这些令人不快的商业行为，加上偶尔流传的帝都地下有逃逸野化斯洛德的传闻，近来给精炼厂带来了不佳的名声。<BR>

Inside Almalexia's Tongs
阿玛莱西娅的公会内部
