"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Knights of the Nine<BR>
By Karoline of Solitude<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Few people now remember the Knights of the Nine, but in their time, they were famous throughout Cyrodiil -- indeed, throughout the Empire. For a brief period in the early days of the Septim Empire, their adventures were the talk of the land. But their renown, as with so much else, was swallowed up by the War of the Red Diamond, and today even the location of their priory house has been lost to history.
The Knights were founded by Sir Amiel Lannus in 3E 111, following his heroic turn in the War of the Isle, with the high purpose of recovering the legendary Crusader's Relics, the weapons and armor of Pelinal Whitestrake which have been lost for thousands of years. They were born out of the sense of optimism and ambition that characterised the first century of the Third Era. Tamriel was united and at peace for the first time in many centuries. Nothing was impossible.<BR>
<BR>
The fame of the knights was established early on when Sir Amiel led them against the Wyrm of Elynglenn to recover the Cuirass of the Crusader, which had not been seen since the First Era. Soon, the greatest knights of the day were lining up to join the new order, and the Priory of the Nine in the West Weald of Cyrodiil became a magnet for the great and the good. The Knights were the toast of the Empire. When Berich Vlindrel joined the order, the scion of one of the great noble families of Colovia, it was clear that the Knights of the Nine had become the Empire's most prestigious knightly order. In relatively short order, the Knights reclaimed three more Relics, and their fame soared to new heights with each one. No one doubted that they would eventually succeed in their quest to recover all eight Relics.<BR>
<BR>
Sadly, this early promise of the Knights did not survive the ravages of the War of the Red Diamond, which tore apart the Empire beginning in 3E 121. At first, it seems that Sir Amiel was able to keep his knights out of the war. But the very success of the Knights undermined this, as many of the Knights came from important families from across the Empire which were lining up on either side of the bloody civil war. Sir Berich was apparently the first to leave the Order to join the war on the side of Cephorus, carrying the Sword and Greaves of the Crusader into battle with him. Many other knights seem to have left the Order shortly after this, some joining the war on one side or the other.<BR>
<BR>
The end of the order was as ignominious as its beginning was glorious. Following the victory of Cephorus in 3E 127, Berich Vlindrel became an important figure on the winning side. It seems likely that he was behind the Imperial decree which officially dissolved the Knights of the Nine in 3E 131, although in truth this was little more than a formality -- despite Sir Amiel's best efforts, the order had never recovered from the bitterness of the civil war.<BR>
<BR>
What happened to the various Relics originally recovered by the Knights of the Nine? The Sword and the Greaves went with Sir Berich, but where he bestowed them is unknown. The Gauntlets famously lie immovable on the floor of the Chapel of Stendarr in Chorrol, where Sir Casimir left them after his disgraceful murder of a beggar in 3E 139. The location of the Cuirass is a mystery, lost to history along with the eventual fate of Sir Amiel, who was last reported still living alone in the empty Priory of the Nine by a passing traveller in 3E 150. And so the Knights of the Nine faded away into history.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
九圣灵骑士团<BR>
独孤城的卡罗琳 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
如今已很少有人记得九圣灵骑士团，但在他们的时代，他们名扬整个西罗帝尔 -- 事实上，是名扬整个帝国。在塞普汀帝国早期的一段时间里，他们的冒险事迹是帝国上下的话题。但和许多其他事物一样，他们的名声被红钻战争所吞噬，时至今日，就连他们修道院的位置也已湮没在历史长河中。
骑士团由阿米尔·兰努斯爵士于第三纪元111年创立，此前他刚在岛屿战争中表现出英雄气概，其崇高目标是寻回传说中圣战者的圣物，即佩林纳尔·白芒的武器和盔甲，这些物品已失落数千年。骑士团诞生于第三纪元首个世纪那种乐观主义和雄心壮志的氛围中。泰姆瑞尔在多个世纪以来首次实现了统一与和平。没有什么是不可能的。<BR>
<BR>
骑士团的声望早在阿米尔爵士带领他们对抗埃林格伦的巨龙，夺回自第一纪元以来就未曾现身的“圣战者胸甲”时便已确立。不久，当代最伟大的骑士们纷纷排队加入这个新修会，位于西罗帝尔西部森林的九圣灵修道院成为杰出人士荟萃之地。骑士团是帝国的宠儿。当科洛维亚显赫贵族家族的后裔贝里希·弗林德尔加入修会时，显而易见，九圣灵骑士团已成为帝国最负盛名的骑士团。在相对较短的时间内，骑士团又夺回了三件圣物，他们的声望也随之攀升至新的高度。无人怀疑他们最终必能成功找回全部八件圣物。<BR>
<BR>
遗憾的是，骑士团早期的辉煌未能经受住红钻战争的蹂躏，这场战争自第三纪元121年起撕裂了整个帝国。起初，阿米尔爵士似乎能让他的骑士们置身战争之外。但骑士团自身的成功反而破坏了这一点，因为许多骑士来自帝国各地的重要家族，而这些家族正卷入这场血腥内战的双方阵营。贝里希爵士显然是第一个离开修会、加入塞弗鲁斯一方参战的人，他带走了“圣战者之剑”和“圣战者护胫”。此后不久，许多其他骑士似乎也离开了修会，有的加入一方，有的加入另一方。<BR>
<BR>
骑士团的结局与其开端的光荣形成同样可耻的对比。塞弗鲁斯于第三纪元127年获胜后，贝里希·弗林德尔成为胜利方的重要人物。很可能正是他促成了帝国于第三纪元131年正式解散九圣灵骑士团的法令，尽管事实上这不过是一种形式罢了 -- 尽管阿米尔爵士竭尽全力，但骑士团始终未能从内战的痛苦中恢复过来。<BR>
<BR>
九圣灵骑士团最初找回的几件圣物后来怎么样了？“圣战者之剑”和“圣战者护胫”随贝里希爵士而去，但他将它们安置何处已无从知晓。“圣战者手套”著名的结局是，在卡西米尔爵士于第三纪元139年可耻地谋杀了一名乞丐后，将它们留在科洛尔的斯滕达尔礼拜堂地板上，据说它们从此无法移动。“圣战者胸甲”的下落则是个谜，它和阿米尔爵士的最终命运一同湮没于历史。据最后记载，在第三纪元150年，有位路过的旅人曾见他仍独自生活在空旷的九圣灵修道院中。九圣灵骑士团就这样逐渐淡出了历史舞台。<BR>

Knowing Your Place
知所居位

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_KnowYourPlaceHR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Importance of Knowing Your Place<BR>
An Instructional Letter to His Apprentice<BR>
By Ernestus Abertus<BR>
University of Gwylim Press
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
I have traveled far and wide across Tamriel in my time, and although I have learned many lessons, above all I've learned to respect time and place. If one knows when and where one is, one knows all.
<BR>
The inferior mage relies on their strength of will alone. They shun the inconvenience of making sure that they are in the right place at the right time. They see nothing wrong in casting spells of great healing on Arkay's days of remembrance for the dead, nothing perverse in casting rituals of transformation mid-season while standing amidst ruins that have endured unchanged for long eras.
<BR>
Take, for example, the Princes of Oblivion. Any fool who can read can rhyme off their traditional dates of summoning: the 1st of Morning Star, when promises are made, belongs to Clavicus Vile. Dawn and dusk are Azura's, Lover's Day Sanguine's... As I trust you follow, I shan't bore myself with the full recital.
<BR>
So why do some summoning rituals succeed where others end in silence or bloodsoaked catastrophe? Because the when is easy, but the superior mind also knows the importance of the where, and the how of the where. 
<BR>
As a hypothetical example, suppose two mages wish to invite themselves to tea with the Prince of Madness. The first, lacking both imagination and empathy, travels to one of the great shrines to demand an audience. They do not know their place. The other understands that Sheogorath can be found as easily in a shoe as in a shrine, or never found at all. It is not given to mortals to command Madness. The finesse is in knowing the where that matters: the shoe in a storm is more inviting than the grandest of shrines, and after all the goal is to be invited to a place at a time. 
<BR>
I shan't labor this point any further, either; no doubt you have the capacity to understand, or you don't. Remember to mind your whens and wheres, and give my regards to your grandmother.
<BR><BR>
Fondest wishes,<BR>
Ernestus
<BR><BR>
[Editor's Note: the esteemed guild master embarked on further travels shortly after writing this letter to his apprentice. Sadly, he has not been heard from since. We at the University Press hope that he, knowing precisely when and where he is, has not lost himself.]
<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
知所居位之重要<BR>
致学徒的一封教谕信<BR>
欧内斯特斯·阿伯图斯 著<BR>
格维林大学出版社
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
我在泰姆瑞尔周游四方，虽习得诸多教训，但首要之教训乃是学会敬重时序与居位。人若知其何时何地，便知一切。
<BR>
平庸的法师只依赖于个人意志的力量。他们回避确保自己在正确时间身处正确地点的不便之处。他们不觉得在阿尔凯追思亡者的日子里施展大型治愈法术有何不妥，也不觉得在季中立于那些亘古不变的废墟之中施展变形仪式有何荒谬。
<BR>
以湮灭大君为例。但凡识字的傻瓜都能顺口说出他们传统的召唤日期：晨星月1日，订立誓约之日，属于克拉威库斯·维尔。黎明与黄昏属于阿祖拉，心之日属于桑吉恩......我相信你已理解，我就不再赘述令自己乏味了。
<BR>
那么，为何有些召唤仪式能够成功，而另一些却以静默或血腥的灾难告终？因为“何时”是容易的，但卓越的头脑还了解“何地”的重要性，以及“何地”的如何之法。
<BR>
假设一个例子：两位法师想邀请自己与疯神共进茶点。第一位缺乏想象力与同理心，前往一座大神殿要求觐见。他不知其所位。另一位则明白，在鞋子里找到谢尔格拉斯的容易程度不亚于在神殿中，或者永远找不到。凡人无法驾驭疯狂。技巧在于知晓那重要的“何地”：暴风雨中的一只鞋子比最宏伟的神殿更具邀请力，毕竟目标是在某个时间被邀请到一个地点。
<BR>
我也不再赘述此点；毫无疑问，你要么能理解，要么不能。记住要留心你的“何时”与“何地”，并代我向你祖母问好。
<BR><BR>
致以最美好的祝愿，<BR>
欧内斯特斯
<BR><BR>
[编者注：这位尊敬的公会会长在写完给学徒的信后不久，便再次踏上了旅途。遗憾的是，此后便再无他的音讯。本社同仁希望，他既精通知晓自身何时何地之道，或许并未迷失自我。]

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
Laid Low<BR>
By Orgol gro-Muk<BR>
<BR>
And so we set off, Ma'Dar, my good Khajiiti friend and sometimes cellmate, Reeya, the wise and sharp-toothed Argonian, Hjestvild, the bulky Nordic version of a thief, Celewen, our pretty Bosmeri leader, and myself, the Orcish former Legionnaire who was apparently the muscle of the operation. As instructed, my eyes never strayed from the water's edge. My attention was so focused that I almost trampled Ma'Dar a few times, at which she laughed "You stumble as though on burning sands," then, more quietly, "Let the scaled one worry about the fishies, eh?"<BR>
<BR>
Considering that the fishies had the benefit of both fins and a swift swim spell, I began to wonder what was taking them so long to "report" back to us. The Argonian became nervous as well, letting out a long, low hiss of distress. Hjestvild slapped Reeya on the back and laughed, suggesting that perhaps the lizard hadn't trained the Slaughterfish nearly as well as he'd thought. We came within sight of the small port town without ever catching sight of the fish. Celewen shrugged it off, since nothing else seemed amiss. Except for her and Hjestvild, the rest of us became more guarded in our manner anyway.<BR>
<BR>
We walked to one nondescript shack near the shore, and Celewen disappeared inside while we waited. A few minutes later, as I was studying the craftsmanship of a barrel, I was startled when a clawed finger touched my shoulder lightly. I turned to face Reeya, whose nervousness had become something just shy of terror. With his other hand, he was pointing toward the docks. Looking in the direction indicated, I saw three Slaughterfish tied to a post and gutted, with an Imperial guardsman standing nearby. Uncomprehending, I shrugged.<BR>
<BR>
"Fool!" Reeya hissed quiet explanation, "Those are not just any fish, they are our fish! I would recognize them anywhere. The guard may be on to us! Bad enough that he's here, but that we might be expected . . . " As soon as the words were out of his mouth, the guard seemed to turn his head toward our small group. We all looked at each other fearfully, then Hjestvild said "Oh, what the hell," drew his weapon, and began walking toward the guard. The guard, naturally, responded in kind. Ma'Dar, Reeya, and I ran, splitting up, not wanting any part of this action.<BR>
<BR>
It seems the Imperials had expected us, for I noticed two more guards rushing to the scene of combat as I tried to appear to be a regular townsperson. Behind me, I could hear among the clash of swords Hjestvild shouting curses about his cowardly allies who had abandoned him, and such. In the middle of one curse, he fell silent. Knowing it was just a matter of time before the original guard identified us, I began to search for Ma'Dar and Reeya. Celewen hadn't exited the shack, so I assumed she either was dead or arrested already . . . or she was still negotiating the price for our smuggling. Reeya, I saw some distance away, stealthily diving into the water west of town. Almost frantically, I cast about for Ma'Dar, and my heart sank when I finally spotted her.<BR>
<BR>
My little Khajiiti friend was dashing away, blissfully unaware of an archer posted atop a building on the outskirts of town. I knew I couldn't reach the archer in time with sword, and I'd have a hard time hitting him with a spell, such was his position. Shouting to Ma'Dar would do no good, and would just betray my own position. In desperation, I did the only thing I could think of . . . <BR>
<BR>
Leaning casually against a barrel, I looked from the fleeing Ma'Dar to the archer and back again. My timing had to be spot-on, or she would be skewered. Watching the tautness of the bowstring, I cast the powerful spell that would knock the wind from its target which Kievier Sounien had been kind enough to teach me. Then it was a race between the arrow and my spell. I saw Ma'Dar crumple to the ground, and for a moment I wasn't sure if my plan had worked (and the arrow had sailed harmlessly overhead), or if the arrow had pierced her. Waiting just long enough to see her get to her feet again, I breathed a sigh of relief. Our group scattered, it was now my turn to flee. <BR>

The Language of Birds
鸟之语

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_LanguageOfBirdsPC
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>The Language of Birds<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>

[If there ever existed anything like an Ayleid creation myth, it has been lost to the passage of time and the Marukhati destruction. This text, found in the margins of one of the Piukanda scrolls, probably comes closest: it is thought to be a children's fable, shedding a modicum of light on the origin of the Ayleid.]<BR>

<BR>

In times past we were as the birds. The birds lived on an island which was eight; it was surrounded by a lake that was as if eight; it was surrounded by a jungle that was as if eight.<BR>

<BR>

The birds knew no arts; they knew no crafts. They did not build; they lived under starlit benevolence. They knew no fire; they were warmed by blessings (eight). They did not write; they knew not speech; they knew to sing pleasing songs; they knew to listen to the stars; they knew to repeat them.<BR>

<BR>

There on the far shores they were the people of Man. They were many (eight) and ruled in the jungle; the jungle was of their design; the jungle is loathsome. They knew to command the serpents of the lake; they knew to implore the beasts of the jungle; which they did by craft and not art.<BR>

<BR>

The people of Man hated the birds and conspired to destroy them with fire. Many times (eight) they besieged the island which was eight; many birds were killed; the birds knew no arts; they knew no crafts.<BR>

<BR>

Then came the Pilot; he sailed on a white ship. The Pilot was called Torval; because he was a seeker and he came from the west. The Pilot was charmed by the friendly bird people who welcomed him; they sang in a voice that repeated whatever they heard; not understanding.<BR>

<BR>

To thank them for their hospitality the Pilot taught the birds the secret of language. Language is a great thing; language is the greatest thing. Language means all arts and all crafts; and all of writing and the alphabet; and all that can be said and sung; and all of culture and civilization; every white tower and every ceremony; theories and philosophies; the work of many and the work of the great that did cause empire to spring forth and bind the jungle and its unworthy creatures; how to make lights that are stars and spears that one may wield in starlit splendor; to build altars to the gods and ancestors (eight); to discern what is worthy and what is unworthy; and transmute unworthy matter; to build; to rule; to speak power; to be Ayleidoon.<BR>

<BR>

The Last King of the Ayleids<BR>
By Herminia Cinna<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The Ayleids, or Heartland High Elves, ruled Cyrodiil in the long ages of Myth before the beginning of recorded history. One of the earliest recorded dates, in fact, is the Fall of White Gold Tower in 1E 243, which is commonly assumed to mark the end of the Ayleids.<BR>
<BR>
Although Ayleid rule over all of Cyrodiil was indeed broken in 1E 243, this was only one of the most obvious stages near the end of a long decline. The first two centuries of the First Era saw increasing strife between the great Ayleid lords of Cyrodiil. Alessia appears to have taken advantage of a period of civil war to launch her uprising. Imperial historians have traditionally attributed her victory to intervention from Skyrim, but it appears that she had at least as much help from rebel Ayleid lords during the siege of White Gold Tower.<BR>
<BR>
The popular image of the Ayleids as brutal slavemasters is based in fact, of course, but it is less well-known that a number of Ayleid princes continued to rule parts of Cyrodiil after 263, as vassals of the new Empress of Cyrodiil. This suggests either that Ayleid rule was not universally detested, or that Alessia and her successors were more pragmatic than is traditionally believed, or perhaps some of both.<BR>
<BR>
In any event, excavations at a number of Ayleid sites show continued occupation and even expansion during the so-called Late Ayleid Period (1E 243 - c. 498). At first, many Ayleid lords continued to rule as vassals of the new human regime. In some cases, Ayleid supporters of Alessia were even rewarded with new lands taken from slain enemies. It is not clear to what extent human slavery continued under the Cyrodilic Empire. Humans continued to dwell in the Ayleid-ruled areas of Cyrodiil, but there is nothing definitive to show under what terms.<BR>
<BR>
This was an uneasy relationship from the beginning, and was not destined to last long. Resentment at the continued presence of Ayleid nobles within the Empire was a contributing factor to the rise of the so-called Alessian Order founded by Maruhk. The first victims of the Alessians were the Ayleids of Cyrodiil. In the early 300s, the surviving Ayleid communities in human-ruled areas were obliterated one by one, the refugees temporarily swelling the power of the remaining Ayleid lordships.<BR>
<BR>
Then in 361, the Alessians gained control of the Empire and enforced the Alessian Doctrines throughout its domain. The Ayleid lordships were abolished. Enforcement of this decree does not appear to have required much direct violence -- it seems that by this point the balance of power was so overwhelmingly against them, and their fate so long foreshadowed, that most of the remaining Ayleids simply left Cyrodiil, eventually being absorbed into the Elven populations of Valenwood and High Rock. Indeed, the rise of the Direnni Hegemony may be linked to this exodus of Ayleids from Cyrodiil (a connection so far little studied by historians).<BR>
<BR>
Still, a remnant Ayleid population seems to have survived the rule of the Alessians, because we hear of "the last king of the Ayleids" joining the battle of Glenumbria Moors where the Dirennis decisively defeated the Alessians in 482. How this king's people survived the preceding century is unknown. We do not even know who they were, although recent research points to Nenalata as the possible resting place of this "last king." Unfortunately, in the current state of the Empire, funds are no longer available for proper scientific investigation of such extensive ruins, so the answer to these questions will have to be left to future generations.<BR>

赫米尼娅·辛纳 著<BR><BR>

亚历德人，或称心脏地高精灵，在有记载的历史肇始之前的神话时代长期统治着西罗帝尔。事实上，最早的记载年份之一便是第一纪元243年的白金塔陷落，这通常被视为标志着亚历德人的终结。<BR>

<BR>

无论如何，对许多亚历德遗址的发掘显示，在所谓的亚历德晚期（第一纪元243年 - 约498年），这些遗址仍被持续使用，甚至有所扩建。起初，许多亚历德领主继续作为新人族政权的附庸进行统治。在某些情况下，支持阿莱西亚的亚历德人甚至得到了从被击败的敌人手中夺取的新土地作为奖赏。在西罗帝尔帝国治下，人类奴隶制在多大程度上得以延续尚不明确。人类继续居住在亚历德人统治的西罗帝尔区域，但没有确凿证据表明他们处于何种境况。<BR>
<BR>
这种关系从一开始就很脆弱，注定不会长久。对帝国内持续存在亚历德贵族的不满，是促使马鲁克创立所谓阿莱西亚教团的因素之一。阿莱西亚教派最初的受害者便是西罗帝尔的亚历德人。在300年代早期，幸存于人族统治地区的亚历德社群被逐个消灭，难民们暂时增强了剩余亚历德领主领地的力量。<BR>
<BR>
随后在361年，阿莱西亚教派控制了帝国，并在其整个疆域内强制推行阿莱西亚教典。亚历德领主领地被废除。这一法令的执行似乎并未需要太多的直接暴力 -- 到这时，力量对比对他们已经极为不利，他们长久以来的命运也早已注定，因此大多数剩余的亚历德人只是离开了西罗帝尔，最终融入了瓦伦伍德和高岩的精灵人口中。事实上，迪伦尼霸权的崛起可能与亚历德人这次离开西罗帝尔有关（历史学家至今对此关联研究甚少）。<BR>
<BR>
尽管如此，似乎仍有残存的亚历德人口在阿莱西亚教派的统治下幸存了下来，因为据记载，在482年迪伦尼家族于格伦昂布拉沼泽大败阿莱西亚教派的战役中，有“亚历德末代国王”加入。这位国王的子民是如何在之前那个世纪幸存下来的，我们不得而知。我们甚至不知道他们是谁，尽管最近的研究指出，能阿拉塔可能是这位“末代国王”的安息之地。不幸的是，以帝国目前的状况，已无资金对这些广阔遗址进行适当的科学调查，于是这些问题的答案只好留待后世解答了。<BR>

The Last King of the Ayleids<BR>
By Herminia Cinna<BR><BR>

The Ayleids, or Heartland High Elves, ruled Cyrodiil in the long ages of Myth before the beginning of recorded history. One of the earliest recorded dates, in fact, is the Fall of White Gold Tower in 1E 243, which is commonly assumed to mark the end of the Ayleids.<BR>
<BR>
Although Ayleid rule over all of Cyrodiil was indeed broken in 1E 243, this was only one of the most obvious stages near the end of a long decline. The first two centuries of the First Era saw increasing strife between the great Ayleid lords of Cyrodiil. Alessia appears to have taken advantage of a period of civil war to launch her uprising. Imperial historians have traditionally attributed her victory to intervention from Skyrim, but it appears that she had at least as much help from rebel Ayleid lords during the siege of White Gold Tower.<BR>
<BR>
The popular image of the Ayleids as brutal slavemasters is based in fact, of course, but it is less well-known that a number of Ayleid princes continued to rule parts of Cyrodiil after 263, as vassals of the new Empress of Cyrodiil. This suggests either that Ayleid rule was not universally detested, or that Alessia and her successors were more pragmatic than is traditionally believed, or perhaps some of both.<BR>
<BR>
In any event, excavations at a number of Ayleid sites show continued occupation and even expansion during the so-called Late Ayleid Period (1E 243 - c. 498). At first, many Ayleid lords continued to rule as vassals of the new human regime. In some cases, Ayleid supporters of Alessia were even rewarded with new lands taken from slain enemies. It is not clear to what extent human slavery continued under the Cyrodilic Empire. Humans continued to dwell in the Ayleid-ruled areas of Cyrodiil, but there is nothing definitive to show under what terms.<BR>
<BR>
This was an uneasy relationship from the beginning, and was not destined to last long. Resentment at the continued presence of Ayleid nobles within the Empire was a contributing factor to the rise of the so-called Alessian Order founded by Maruhk. The first victims of the Alessians were the Ayleids of Cyrodiil. In the early 300s, the surviving Ayleid communities in human-ruled areas were obliterated one by one, the refugees temporarily swelling the power of the remaining Ayleid lordships.<BR>
<BR>
Then in 361, the Alessians gained control of the Empire and enforced the Alessian Doctrines throughout its domain. The Ayleid lordships were abolished. Enforcement of this decree does not appear to have required much direct violence -- it seems that by this point the balance of power was so overwhelmingly against them, and their fate so long foreshadowed, that most of the remaining Ayleids simply left Cyrodiil, eventually being absorbed into the Elven populations of Valenwood and High Rock. Indeed, the rise of the Direnni Hegemony may be linked to this exodus of Ayleids from Cyrodiil (a connection so far little studied by historians).<BR>
<BR>
Still, a remnant Ayleid population seems to have survived the rule of the Alessians, because we hear of "the last king of the Ayleids" joining the battle of Glenumbria Moors where the Dirennis decisively defeated the Alessians in 482. How this king's people survived the preceding century is unknown. We do not even know who they were, although recent research points to Nenalata as the possible resting place of this "last king." Unfortunately, in the current state of the Empire, funds are no longer available for proper scientific investigation of such extensive ruins, so the answer to these questions will have to be left to future generations.<BR>

The Last Story of Sirof the Oak<BR>
A Nordic fable<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
At the coming of the Companions to Skyrim, there was a follower of Ysgramor called Sigrun the Blue Wolf, whose name meant victory and who had split fifty-eight times her number at the point of the Return. Her keel-spouse, who was dear to her, was called Hrolfi, and he split twenty-two times his number. Together, they crossed the salty river of tears before Saarthal and there raised a farm in the fertile elflands beyond, and upon the red earth they bore the hundred children of the Wolf Tail Clan. <BR>
<BR>
Firstborn was Sirof, oak-like, who married three times across his two-hundred summers: by his hearth-spouse, Freydis, he bore Sigrif and Sigdis; by his war-spouse, Mereth, he bore Sigraeth; and by his plough-spouse, Eirik, he bore no children. Although he was strong and worthy, his acorns were small, and so his progeny were forever three. But these three loved Sirof the Oak, and he raised them into righteous servants of the World-Beams, and told them stories of the way of doing things. He told them stories of cleanliness, and happiness, and the proper way to mourn, and the family of Sirof the Oak grew close and loving.<BR>
<BR>
Many years passed, and his children grew, and Sirof's leaves began to turn. He continued to tell his stories so that his children would know the way of doing things, because the land had been won from elves and in those days their spirits still whispered false traditions to the Nords. One day, as they worked the fields, a stranger came to the gates of their farmstead. She was clothed in the long hair that fell around her single eye and rode atop a great wolf, which in those days was no cause for comment, but she spoke with her eye and called for parley with Sirof. Having been told the stories of hospitality, Sigrif and Sigdis led the stranger into the hall as Sigraeth stabled her wolf and slaughtered a horse for its supper.<BR>
<BR>
Later, when the last bone of the feast had been broken, Sirof bade his three progeny enter the hall and take their places at his feet.<BR>
<BR>
"Children, I am your father and I am filled with a fierce love to look at you. This will be my last story, for after today you will be forever beyond my sight. I have told you much about the way of doing things, but I have never told you of matrimony. Yet within our home is holy Mara, and She has told me of Her marriage to each of you, to take place this night upon Hrothgar itself, in the sight of all the three realms. No, do not cry or try to flee. I have not raised you to disobey the Gods. Instead listen, and I will tell you what will happen.<BR>
<BR>
"Sigrif, you have grown wise and handsome like your father: blessed Mara will make you Her feast-spouse, and you will sit at Her side and be marvelled at with envy. Sigdis, you are the very image of your step-mother Mereth: blessed Mara will make you Her sword-spouse, and wield you against Her enemies. Sigraeth, you are solemn and solitary: blessed Mara will make you Her breath-spouse, and sequester you in meditation. In time, all of you will find spouses of your own, to suit your needs and duties, and your children will spread out across the Sky. This is my last story, the story of what will be."<BR>
<BR>
At this, and with great tears leaping from his eyes, Sirof turned away from his children for the last time. But the words he had spoken were true, for the three wedded a goddess that very night, and in time found their places in the great tangle of matrimony. The children they bore Her were beautiful indeed, and they grew strong and worthy, and spread out across the Sky to take their places as the very stars themselves.<BR>

橡树西罗夫的最后一个故事<BR>
一则诺德寓言<BR><BR>

<BR>
多年过去，他的孩子们长大了，西罗夫的树叶也开始变黄。他继续讲述故事，以便孩子们知晓行事之道，因为这片土地是从精灵手中夺来的，在那个时代，精灵们的灵魂仍在向诺德人低语着虚假的传统。一天，当他们正在田间劳作时，一位陌生人来到他们农庄的大门前。她浑身上下裹在垂落的长发中，发间只露出一只眼睛，骑着一头巨大的狼 -- 这在当时不足为奇，她用眼睛说话，要求与西罗夫谈判。西格里夫和西格迪斯因受过好客之道的教诲，便领着陌生人进入大厅，而西格雷斯则将她的狼安置好，并宰杀了一匹马作为它的晚餐。<BR>

<BR>
“孩子们，我是你们的父亲，看着你们，我心中充满了强烈的爱意。这将是我最后一个故事，因为从今往后，你们将永远走出我的视线。关于行事之道，我已告诉你们很多，但从未与你们说起过婚姻。然而，神圣的玛拉就在我们家中，她已告诉我，她将与你们三人分别成婚，婚礼就在今夜，于洛思迦之巅，在三界众生面前举行。不，不要哭，也不要试图逃跑。我养育你们，不是要你们违抗神明。听我说，我会告诉你们将要发生的事。<BR>

<BR>
说完这番话，泪水夺眶而出，西罗夫最后一次将脸从孩子们面前转开。但他所说的话是真的，因为那三兄妹当晚便与一位女神成婚，并最终在伟大的婚姻之网中找到了各自的位置。他们为女神所生的孩子确实美丽非凡，这些孩子成长得强壮而可敬，并遍布天际，成为天上的繁星。<BR>

The Divines have made the world, and, for a large part, they are the world, freely giving their blood and flesh to the crucible of Man. As such, the Nine are the supreme authority on all moral and ethical questions that could even plague man: after all, they are both designers of the world, and inherent in its every aspect, having full knowledge of all possible circumstance varieties. It is not up to us to understand the secret workings of the world, which sometimes favor evil men while the pious and the saintly seem to suffer. Accept that this is by design. Some of the provincial cults speak of sin, which is a false idea, but in Law there is something like debt: the debt of sacrifice we mortals have incurred for the creation of our world, which we can pay in full through obedience. Divine Will is to be a secret, for it is difficult to grasp, and easy to misinterpret. """<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>

德纳里乌斯主教 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Legal Basics<BR>
By Anchivius, M.Z.F.<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
Ignorance of the law is no defense. Be forewarned that the following are but the most universal of Tamrielan laws and regulations. Your own local province or principality may have unique laws of its own. As a citizen of Empire, it is your right and responsibility to know and follow these laws of the land.<BR><BR>
Breaking and Entering<BR><BR>
This refers to any act including, but not limited to opening, breaking, incinerating, magically transporting, or in any way causing a door, window, or other portal that has been magically or mundanely locked or which a reasonable person would assume to be so restricted to be passable, and the act (though the act is not required for the definition) of entering the house, business, or public location through said defined portal. The punishment for this crime may include a fine or incarceration, or a fine and incarceration. The fine and incarceration, or both, or neither, may be less in a crime of Attempted Breaking and Entering. A crime of Attempted Breaking and Entering is defined as an any act that a reasonable person would perceive as the preparation for, an attempt (whether successful or not, or perceived to be possibly successful or not) to bring about the opening, breaking, incinerating, magically transporting, or in any way causing a door, window, or other portal that has been magically or mundanely locked or which a reasonable person would assume to be so restricted to be passable, and the act (though the act is not required for the definition) of preparing or attempting (whether successful or not, perceived to be possibly successful or not) entering the house, business, or public location through said defined portal.<BR>
Trespassing<BR><BR>
This refers to walking, flying, riding, teleporting, floating, or in any way moving or existing on a property without the explicit written or spoken permission (or permission a reasonable person might infer) of the owner or caretaker of the property. The punishment for this crime may include a fine or incarceration, or a fine and incarceration.<BR><BR>
Assault<BR><BR>
Any threat or attempt (whether successful or not) to do physical, emotional, mental, or magical harm or injury to another person, group of persons, or entity a reasonable person might assume to be sentient. The punishment for this crime may include a fine or incarceration, or a fine and incarceration.<BR><BR>
Murder<BR><BR>
Any act of premeditated or malicious or premeditated and malicious (or an act that a reasonable person would call premeditated and malicious or premeditated or malicious) or accidental but criminally intended (or what a reasonable person would call criminally intended) purpose that results directly in the death (or destruction with implied death) of a person, group of persons, or entity a reasonable person might assume to be sentient. The punishment for this crime may include a fine or incarceration, or a fine and incarceration.<BR><BR>
Criminal Conspiracy<BR><BR>
Any meeting, communication, or encounter with the purpose (or which a reasonable person might assume had the purpose) of preparing or arranging a crime of any kind (or crimes of any kind) to be commited or caused to be commited. The punishment for this crime may include a fine or incarceration, or a fine and incarceration.<BR><BR>
Vagrancy<BR><BR>
Any act of idleness, disorder, begging, or conduct unbecoming a person with occupation, gold, or a home, (or occupation, gold, and a home, or occupation or gold and home, or occupation and gold or home, or occupation and home or gold), or what a reasonable person would consider idle, disorderly, beggarly, or unbecoming. The punishment for this crime may include a fine or incarceration, or a fine and incarceration.<BR><BR><BR>
Smuggling<BR><BR>
Any act of bringing in, taking out, teleporting, or causing to be brought in, taken out, or teleported an object considered illegal or, if not illegal, requiring an import or export tax which is not paid. The punishment for this crime may include a fine or incarceration, or a fine and incarceration, and will include confiscation of the offensive or illegal object. It may also include, but not be restricted to, execution or banishment, or execution and banishment.<BR><BR>
High Treason<BR><BR>
Any act against (whether directly or indirectly, or any nonaction which results in circumstances, directly or indirectly, against) a allegiated sovereign or by a vassal to a liege, resulting (or what a reasonable person would assume would result) in physical, emotional, mental, or magical harm or injury in said sovereign or liege. The punishment for this crime will be death.<BR><BR>
Pickpocketing<BR><BR>
Any act of stealing, taking, or, without explicit written or verbal permission (or what a reasonable person would infer as implied permission) an item or items a person, group of persons, or entity a reasonable person might assume to be sentient has on his, her, its, or their own person. The punishment for this crime may include a fine or incarceration, or a fine and incarceration.<BR><BR>
Theft (sometimes called Larceny)<BR><BR>
Any act of stealing, taking, or, without explicit written or verbal permission (or what a reasonable person would infer as implied permission) an item or items from a person, group of persons, or entity a reasonable person might assume to be sentient's place of residence, business, person, or other location a reasonable person would assume is secured from looting. The punishment for this crime may include a fine or incarceration, or a fine and incarceration.<BR><BR>
These are the usual, day-to-day definitions used by legal experts (like myself), but both the definitions and punishments may fluctuate wildly according to location and situation. In the Imperial City, legal counsel is available by persons like myself, but the provinces have no such system in place. Perhaps that will change in time. We can all hope so.<BR><BR><BR><BR>
As a final note:<BR><BR>
The Tamriel legal system has its basis in the civilized, reasonable credo uttered by the prophet Marukh in the first era: "All are guilty until they have proven themselves innocent." Were truer word ever spoke?<BR>"""

法律基础<BR>
安奇维乌斯 著，M.Z.F.<BR><BR>

对法律的无知不能作为辩护的理由。请预先知悉，以下所列仅为泰姆瑞尔最普遍通用的法律与规章。您所在的本地行省或公国可能拥有其独特的法律。作为帝国的公民，了解并遵守这片土地的法律，既是您的权利，也是您的责任。<BR><BR>
破门侵入<BR><BR>
该罪行指任何行为，包括但不限于：打开、打破、烧毁、魔法传送，或以任何方式使得一扇已被魔法或物理方式锁住、或任何理性人会认为已受限制的门、窗或其他入口变得可通过，以及（尽管该行为对定义并非必需）通过所述特定入口进入房屋、商业场所或公共地点的行为。对此罪行的惩罚可包括罚款或监禁，或罚款并监禁。对于“破门侵入未遂”罪行，罚款和监禁（或两者之一，或两者均无）可能会较轻。“破门侵入未遂”罪行定义为：任何理性人会认为是准备、试图（无论成功与否，或被认为可能成功与否）打开、打破、烧毁、魔法传送，或以任何方式使得一扇已被魔法或物理方式锁住、或任何理性人会认为已受限制的门、窗或其他入口变得可通过的行为，以及（尽管该行为对定义并非必需）准备或试图（无论成功与否，或被认为可能成功与否）通过所述特定入口进入房屋、商业场所或公共地点的行为。<BR>
非法侵入<BR><BR>

攻击<BR><BR>
指任何威胁或试图（无论成功与否）对另一个人、一群人、或理性人可能认为有感知的实体造成身体、情感、精神或魔法伤害或损伤的行为。对此罪行的惩罚可包括罚款或监禁，或罚款并监禁。<BR><BR>
谋杀<BR><BR>
指任何预谋的或恶意的、或预谋且恶意的（或理性人会称之为预谋且恶意、或预谋的、或恶意的）、或意外但具有犯罪意图的（或理性人称之为具有犯罪意图的）行为，其目的直接导致一个人、一群人、或理性人可能认为有感知的实体的死亡（或意味着死亡的毁灭）。对此罪行的惩罚可包括罚款或监禁，或罚款并监禁。<BR><BR>
犯罪共谋<BR><BR>
指任何以（或理性人可能认为以）准备或安排实施或致使实施任何类型犯罪为目的的集会、通信或相遇。对此罪行的惩罚可包括罚款或监禁，或罚款并监禁。<BR><BR>
流浪游荡<BR><BR>
指任何懒惰、扰乱秩序、乞讨或有损于有职业、有金钱或有住所之人身份的行为（或有职业、有金钱且有住所，或有职业或有金钱且有住所，或有职业且有金钱或有住所，或有职业且有住所或有金钱），或理性人认为是懒惰、扰乱秩序、乞讨或有失体面的行为。对此罪行的惩罚可包括罚款或监禁，或罚款并监禁。<BR><BR><BR>
走私<BR><BR>
指任何带入、带出、传送，或致使带入、带出、传送被认为非法的物品，或虽不非法但需缴纳进出口税而未缴的物品的行为。对此罪行的惩罚可包括罚款或监禁，或罚款并监禁，并将包括没收违禁或非法物品。惩罚还可能包括但不限于处决或流放，或处决并流放。<BR><BR>
叛国大罪<BR><BR>
指任何针对（无论是直接或间接，或因不作为而直接或间接导致针对）效忠君主的行动，或封臣针对领主的行动，导致（或理性人认为将导致）该君主或领主遭受身体、情感、精神或魔法伤害或损伤的行为。对此罪行的惩罚为死刑。<BR><BR>
扒窃<BR><BR>
指在未经明确书面或口头许可（或理性人会推断为默示许可）的情况下，偷窃、拿走一个人、一群人、或理性人可能认为有感知的实体身上所拥有的物品的行为。对此罪行的惩罚可包括罚款或监禁，或罚款并监禁。<BR><BR>
盗窃（有时称为偷窃罪）<BR><BR>
指在未经明确书面或口头许可（或理性人会推断为默示许可）的情况下，从一个人、一群人、或理性人可能认为有感知的实体的住所、营业场所、人身，或其他理性人认为应受保护免遭掠夺的地点偷窃、拿走物品的行为。对此罪行的惩罚可包括罚款或监禁，或罚款并监禁。<BR><BR>

最后一点：<BR><BR>
泰姆瑞尔的法律体系基于第一纪元先知马鲁克所言的文明、合理的信条：“所有人皆有罪，直至自证清白。”还有比这更真实的话吗？<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Legend of Red Eagle<BR>
by Tredayn Dren,<BR>
Archivist of Winterhold<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
This tale was transcribed from the memory of Clarisse Vien, student of Winterhold. Elements of the legend suggest a date c.1E 1030, though as with any oral tradition, much of it is likely a later anachronism. Curiously, stories of a similar king and his legendary blade appear in other ancient myths of the Reach.<BR>
<BR>
Long ago, a child was born in the Sundered Hills. They named him Faolan, which means 'Red Eagle' in the tongue of the Reach, for the screeching bird-call that greeted his birth, and the crimson blooms on the autumn hills.<BR>
<BR>
Thus began his legend: Reach-child, born under auspicious skies, his very name the color of blood.<BR>
<BR>
Ten kings ruled the Reach in those days, and though men were free, the people were scattered and warred amongst themselves. The augurs foresaw the boy's destiny: a warrior without peer, first and foremost Lord of the Reach, chosen to unite all under his name.<BR>
<BR>
Faolan grew in years and strength, and it seemed the prophecy would be fulfilled. The banner of the Red Eagle was raised along the cliffs of the Reach, and his people prospered.<BR>
<BR>
Then came Hestra, Empress of the South, riding to war. One by one, the kings stood before her. One by one, they fell aside, bending knee in Imperial bargains or slaughtered on the battlefield.<BR>
<BR>
Her legions came at last to the Sundered Hills, and envoys were sent to bargain for their surrender. Faolan refused to yield the freedom of his people, but the elders were afraid, cast him out, and accepted the Imperial yoke.<BR>
<BR>
Thus was stolen by the foreign invaders: his land, his people, his very name. In the years that followed, Red Eagle became known as the untamed spirit of the Reach, unbowed, unbroken, stained by the blood of his foes.<BR>
<BR>
He gathered loyal Reachmen to himself, those who clung to the old ways, who yearned for freedom, and forged a new nation. Together, they fell upon the occupiers and the traitors by night, disappearing into the cliffs and caves each morn, evading capture. It was not enough. For every Imperial patrol and garrison they wiped out, yet more seemed to march from the green south to replace them.<BR>
<BR>
One night, under a cloud-choked sky, the men of the Red Eagle warmed themselves over damp fires of smoldering moss. A huddled, shambling figure came to them, cloaked in rags, face cowled. Though his men mocked and cast stones at the stranger, Faolan sensed something, and beckoned. The cowl was thrown back in the dim light, and she revealed herself to be one the ancient and venerable Hagravens. She offered power, for a price, and a pact was made.<BR>
<BR>
Thus was brokered to the witch: his heart, his will, his humanity. From that day forth, his was a spirit of vengeance, pitiless and beyond remorse. The rebels grew in strength and numbers, and none could stand against them. Faolan's eyes burned coldly in those days, black opals reflecting a mind not entirely his own. Two years passed, and the foreigners were all but driven from the Reach.<BR>
<BR>
Such peace could not last, however, and a great host fell upon them, a swift army of invaders unlike any before. For a fortnight, Hestra's generals laid siege to Red Eagle's stronghold, till he himself came forth for battle, alone and robed in nothing but his righteous fury. A thousand foreigners fell before his flaming sword, and the enemy was routed. Yet, when night fell, so too did he. The warriors who came to him said Faolan's eyes were clear again on that final night.<BR>
<BR>
He was taken to the place prepared for him, a tomb hidden deep within the rock. With his remaining strength he presented his sword to his people, and swore an oath: Fight on, and when at last the Reach is free, his blade should be returned, that he might rise and lead them again.<BR>
<BR>
Thus was given for his people: his life, his dream, his sword. But when every debt is repaid in blood, these he shall reclaim once more.<BR>

特雷戴恩·德伦 著，<BR>
冬堡档案管理员<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
这个故事是根据冬堡学生克拉丽丝·维安的回忆转录的。传说的元素暗示其年代约为第一纪元1030年左右，但与任何口述传统一样，其中大部分内容很可能是后世附会。有趣的是，在河峪的其他古老神话中，也出现了关于类似国王及其传奇兵刃的故事。<BR>
<BR>
很久以前，一个孩子在破碎丘陵诞生。他们给他取名费奥兰，在河峪的语言中意为“红鹰”，因为迎接他出生的是鸟儿的尖啸，以及秋日山丘上的深红花海。<BR>
<BR>
他的传奇就此开始：河峪之子，生于吉兆苍穹之下，其名即为血色。<BR>
<BR>
彼时，有十位国王统治着河峪，尽管人们是自由的，但部落分散，彼此征战。占卜师预见了男孩的命运：一位无与伦比的战士，河峪的首位也是最重要的领主，被选中以他的名号统一所有。<BR>
<BR>
费奥兰年岁渐长，力量日增，预言似乎即将应验。红鹰的旗帜在河峪的悬崖边升起，他的人民繁荣昌盛。<BR>
<BR>
随后，南方的女皇海斯特拉率军前来。国王们一个接一个地站在她面前。又一个接一个地败下阵来，或在帝国的交易中屈膝，或在战场上被屠杀。<BR>
<BR>
她的军团最终抵达破碎丘陵，并派使者前来谈判投降事宜。费奥兰拒绝交出人民的自由，但长老们害怕了，将他驱逐，并接受了帝国的枷锁。<BR>
<BR>
就这样，他的土地、他的人民、乃至他的名字，都被外来的入侵者夺走了。在接下来的岁月里，红鹰成为了河峪不屈不挠、永不低头、染满敌人鲜血的不羁之魂。<BR>
<BR>
他将那些坚守旧道、渴望自由的忠诚河峪人聚集到自己麾下，建立了一个新的国家。他们一同在夜间袭击占领者和叛徒，每晨便消失于悬崖与洞穴之中，躲避追捕。但这还不够。他们每消灭一支帝国巡逻队或驻军，似乎就有更多的军队从绿色的南方开拔而来，填补空缺。<BR>
<BR>
一天夜晚，在乌云密布的天空下，红鹰的手下们围坐在潮湿的苔藓闷火旁取暖。一个蜷缩、蹒跚的身影向他们走来，身披破烂斗篷，头戴兜帽。尽管手下们嘲笑并向那陌生人扔石头，费奥兰却感觉到了什么，示意他过来。昏暗的光线下，兜帽被掀开，她现出真身，竟是一位古老而可敬的乌鸦鬼婆。她提出以代价换取力量，于是契约达成。<BR>
<BR>
就这样，他向女巫献出了：他的心脏、他的意志、他的人性。从那天起，他便成了复仇的化身，冷酷无情，毫无悔意。叛军的实力和人数不断壮大，无人能挡。那时的费奥兰，眼中燃烧着冰冷的光芒，黑色的蛋白石映照出一个不完全属于他自己的心智。两年过去了，外来者几乎被赶出了河峪。<BR>
<BR>
然而，这样的和平无法持久，一支前所未有的大军向他们袭来，那是一支迅捷的入侵者军队。海斯特拉的将军们围攻红鹰的据点长达两周，直到他亲自出战，孤身一人，只披着他的正义之怒。一千名外来者倒在他燃烧的剑下，敌军溃败。然而，夜幕降临时，他也倒下了。来到他身边的战士们说，在最后的那个夜晚，费奥兰的眼睛再次变得清澈。<BR>
<BR>
他被带到了为他准备的地方，一个深藏在岩石中的坟墓。他用残余的力量将剑交给人民，并发下誓言：继续战斗，当河峪最终获得自由时，他的剑必须归还，以便他能再次崛起，领导他们。<BR>
<BR>
就这样，他为他的人民献出了：他的生命、他的梦想、他的剑。但当所有血债都以血偿还时，他将重新夺回这一切。<BR>
<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Legendary City of Sancre Tor<BR>
by Matera Chapel<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
During the Skyrim Conquests [1E 240 - 415], ambitious Highland earls, envious of the conquests and wealth of their northern cousins in High Rock and Morrowind, looked south over the ramparts of the Jerall Mountains for their opportunities. The Jerall Mountains proved to be too great a barrier, and northern Cyrodiil too poor a prize, to reward full scale Nord invasions. However, Alessia hired many ambitious Nord and Breton warbands as mercenaries with the promises of rich lands and trade concessions. Once settled among the victorious Alessian Cyrodiils, the Nord and Breton warriors and battlemages were quickly assimilated into the comfortable and prosperous Nibenean culture.<BR>
<BR>
Alessia received the divine inspiration for her Slave Rebellion at Sancre Tor, and here she founded her holy city. Sancre Tor's mines provided some wealth, but the poor soils and harsh climate of the remote mountain site meant it must be supplied with food and goods from the Heartlands. Further, located on one of the few passes through the Jeralls, its fortunes were subject to the instability of relations with Skyrim. When relations were good with Skyrim, it prospered through trade and alliance. When relations were bad with Skyrim, it was vulnerable to siege and occupation by the Nords.<BR>
<BR>
With the decline of the Alessian Order [circa 1E2321], the seat of religious rule of Cyrodiil moved south to the Imperial City, but Sancre Tor remained a mountain fortress and major religious center until the rise of the Septim Dynasty. In 2E852, the city was suffering under one of the periodic occupations by Skyrim and High Rock invaders. King Cuhlecain sent his new general, Talos, to recapture the city and expel the northern invaders. During his siege, Sancre Tor was destroyed and abandoned. Realizing the strategic weakness of the site, General Talos -- later Tiber Septim -- resolved to abandon Sancre Tor, and during his reign, no effort was made to rebuild the city or citadel.<BR>
<BR>
Alessian historians asserted that Sancre Tor was magically concealed and defended by the gods. Records of Sancre Tor's repeated defeats and occupations by northern invaders gives the lie to this assertion. The entrance to the citadel was indeed concealed by sorcery, and the citadel and its labyrinthine subterranean complex were defended by magical traps and illusions, but their secrets were betrayed to besieging Nords by the Breton enchanters who crafted them.<BR>
<BR>
One enduring feature of the legend of Sancre Tor is the ancient tombs of the Reman emperors. Following the defeat of the Akaviri invaders, Sancre Tor enjoyed a brief resurgence of wealth and culture under Reman Cyrodiil and his descendants, Reman II and Reman III. Tracing his ancestry to St. Alessia, and following the tradition that St. Alessia was buried in the catacombs beneath Sancre Tor [1], Reman built splendid funerary precincts in the depths of the ancient citadel underpassages. Here the last Reman emperor, Reman III, was buried in his tomb with the Amulet of Kings.<BR>
<BR>
During the Sack of Sancre Tor, General Talos is said to have recovered the Amulet of Kings from the tomb of Reman III. Theologians ascribe the long centuries of political and economic turmoil following the collapse of the Reman dynasty to the loss of the Amulet of Kings, and associate the renaissance of the Cyrodilic empire in the Third Era with Tiber Septim's recovery of the Amulet from Reman III's tomb.<BR>
<BR>
Sancre Tor has lain in ruins since the beginning of the Third Age, and the surrounding region is virtually uninhabited. Now all communications with the north are through the passes at Chorrol and Bruma, and Sancre Tor's citadel and underpassages have become the refuge of various savage goblin tribes.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
[1] There is a competing tradition that St. Alessia is buried on the site of the Temple of the One in the Imperial City. The actual resting place of St. Alessia is unknown.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
传奇之城桑克雷·托<BR>
玛特拉·查普尔 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
在天际征服期间 [第一纪元240年 - 415年]，野心勃勃的高地伯爵们羡慕他们身处高岩和晨风的北方同胞的征服与财富，将目光越过杰拉尔山脉的壁垒，向南寻找机会。杰拉尔山脉被证明是一道过于巨大的屏障，而北西罗帝尔的价值又太低，不足以回报诺德人的大规模入侵。然而，阿莱西亚以丰饶的土地和贸易特许权为承诺，雇佣了许多野心勃勃的诺德和布莱顿战团作为雇佣兵。这些诺德和布莱顿战士及战斗法师在胜利的阿莱西亚西罗帝尔人中定居后，很快融入了舒适繁荣的尼本奈文化。<BR>
<BR>
阿莱西亚在桑克雷·托获得了发动奴隶起义的神圣灵感，并在此建立了她的圣城。桑克雷·托的矿场提供了一些财富，但偏远山区贫瘠的土壤和严酷的气候意味着它必须从心脏地获取食物和商品。此外，由于其位于穿越杰拉尔山脉的少数隘口之一，其命运受制于与天际关系的不稳定。当与天际关系良好时，它通过贸易和联盟繁荣发展。当与天际关系恶化时，它很容易受到诺德人的围攻和占领。<BR>
<BR>
随着阿莱西亚教团的衰落 [约第一纪元2321年]，西罗帝尔的宗教统治中心南移至帝都，但桑克雷·托在塞普汀王朝兴起前，仍是一座山地堡垒和重要的宗教中心。在第二纪元852年，该城正遭受天际和高岩入侵者的周期性占领。库莱凯恩国王派遣他的新将军塔洛斯重新夺回该城，驱逐北方入侵者。在围攻期间，桑克雷·托被摧毁并废弃。意识到该地点在战略上的弱点后，塔洛斯将军 -- 后来的泰伯·塞普汀 -- 决定放弃桑克雷·托，在其统治期间，没有做出任何努力来重建这座城市或城堡。<BR>
<BR>
阿莱西亚历史学家断言，桑克雷·托被魔法隐藏并受到众神的保护。但桑克雷·托屡次被北方入侵者击败和占领的记录，证明这一说法是谎言。城堡的入口确实被巫术隐藏，城堡及其迷宫般的地下建筑群由魔法陷阱和幻术保护，但这些秘密却被制造它们的布莱顿附魔师出卖给了围城的诺德人。<BR>
<BR>
桑克雷·托传说中一个永恒的特色是雷曼皇帝的古老陵墓。在阿卡维尔入侵者被打败后，桑克雷·托在雷曼·西罗帝尔及其后裔雷曼二世和雷曼三世统治下，经历了一段短暂的财富与文化复兴。雷曼将自己的血统追溯到圣阿莱西亚，并遵循圣阿莱西亚安葬于桑克雷·托地下墓穴的传统[1]，在古代城堡地下通道深处建造了华丽的墓葬区。在这里，最后一位雷曼皇帝雷曼三世与众王护符一起被安葬在他的墓中。<BR>
<BR>
据说在洗劫桑克雷·托期间，塔洛斯将军从雷曼三世的墓中取回了众王护符。神学家们将雷曼王朝崩溃后长达数世纪的政治和经济动荡归咎于众王护符的遗失，并将第三纪元西罗帝尔帝国的复兴与泰伯·塞普汀从雷曼三世墓中取回护符联系在一起。<BR>
<BR>
自第三纪元开始以来，桑克雷·托一直处于废墟状态，周边地区几乎无人居住。现在所有与北方的联系都通过科洛尔和布鲁玛的隘口进行，而桑克雷·托的城堡和地下通道已成为各种野蛮哥布林部落的避难所。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
[1] 还有一种与之相悖的传统说法，认为圣阿莱西亚安葬在帝都至一神殿的遗址上。圣阿莱西亚的真实安息之地未知。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Legends of Athalwyrm the Clever-Man<BR>
<BR>
On the Matter of Taxes<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
[Translator's Note: In the tongue of the ancient Nords there was no requirement for marking of plurals or separation of nouns and adjectives, therefore some conflations and confusions were possible which are not so in our modern language. These linguistic features seem to form the basis of many of the arguments attributed to Athalwyrm, so we have tried to render the ambiguities faithfully in translation.]<BR>$0A<BR>$0AAthalwyrm the Clever-Man, before he became the Lawspeaker of Hrothgar, was an ordinary merchant selling weapons and tools. One year he bought a large number of glass axes from an elven smith in Morrowind and transported them in a caravan of wagons to Whiterun. Along the way, he was stopped by a tax collector of Eastmarch.<BR>$0A<BR>$0A"The law," spoke the tax collector, "states that all transportation of axes, adzes, rakes and ploughs along the roads of Eastmarch incurs a tax upon each such item. How many of the aforesaid items are you transporting?"<BR>$0A<BR>$0A"I don't have axes, adzes, rakes and ploughs," said Athalwyrm, "I only have glass axes."<BR>$0A<BR>$0A"Don't joke," snapped the tax collector, "A glass axe is an axe, and an axe is subject to the tax."<BR>$0A<BR>$0A"Not so," replied Athalwyrm, serenely, "An axe is an axe, and a glass axe is both glass and axe. If what I have are glass and axe, but not axe, adze, rake and plough, then how can I be taxed? One thing is added, and three are taken away."<BR>
<BR>
The tax collector sighed. "I don't have time for this. How many axes do you have?"<BR>
<BR>
Athalwyrm smiled helpfully at the man. "I don't just have axes, I have glass axes. How can I count the glass and the axe? When adding two such different items something will surely be missed. Then, even having reached a total, to remove the glass from the axe is impossible. Furthermore, when someone asks for an axe, he usually expects it to be made of iron or steel. When asked for an axe, to give an iron or steel axe is perfectly acceptable. But when asked for a glass axe, to give an iron or steel axe is not acceptable. When asked for a glass axe, to give a glass axe is the only acceptable response. So to ask for an axe is not the same as to ask for a glass axe. If you ask me about glass axes, of course I will tell you what you need to know."<BR>
<BR>
"Fine, fine, whatever," said the tax collector in exasperation, "How many glass axes do you have?"<BR>
<BR>
"I never heard any law about glass axes in Eastmarch," replied Athalwyrm with finality, "only a law about axes, adzes, rakes and ploughs. If the law does not name my goods as subject to tax, then I will not pay."<BR>
<BR>
[The end of this dialogue has not survived.]<BR><BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
智士阿萨尔维姆传奇<BR>
<BR>
论税收之事<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
[译者注：在古诺德语中，无需标记复数或区分名词与形容词，因此可能出现一些在我们的现代语言中不存在的混同与歧义。这些语言特点似乎是阿萨尔维姆许多论辩的基础，因此我们试图在翻译中忠实地再现这些歧义。]<BR>
<BR>
智士阿萨尔维姆在成为洛斯伽的法律宣说者之前，是一名普通的武器和工具商人。有一年，他从晨风的一位精灵铁匠那里购买了大量玻璃斧，并用马车队运往白漫。途中，他被东陲的一名税吏拦住了。<BR>
<BR>
“法律规定，”税吏说道，“在东陲道路上运输斧、锛、耙、犁，每件此类物品都需缴税。你运输了多少上述物品？”<BR>
<BR>
“我没有斧、锛、耙、犁，”阿萨尔维姆说，“我只有玻璃斧。”<BR>
<BR>
“别开玩笑，”税吏厉声道，“玻璃斧就是斧，斧就需要缴税。”<BR>
<BR>
“并非如此，”阿萨尔维姆平静地回答，“斧就是斧，而玻璃斧既是玻璃又是斧。如果我拥有的是玻璃和斧，但不是斧、锛、耙、犁，那我为何要被征税？加了一样东西，却减去了三样。”<BR>
<BR>
税吏叹了口气。“我没时间跟你纠缠。你有多少把斧？”<BR>
<BR>
阿萨尔维姆好意地朝那人笑了笑。“我不只有斧，我有玻璃斧。我怎么能把玻璃和斧分开计数呢？把两个如此不同的物品相加，必然会遗漏什么。而且，即使得出了总数，也不可能把玻璃从斧上移除。此外，当有人要一把斧时，他通常期望是铁或钢制的。当被要求给一把斧时，给一把铁或钢斧是完全可接受的。但当被要求给一把玻璃斧时，给一把铁或钢斧是不可接受的。当被要求给一把玻璃斧时，唯一可接受的回应是给一把玻璃斧。所以，要一把斧和要一把玻璃斧是不同的。如果你问我关于玻璃斧的事，我当然会告诉你你需要知道的。”<BR>
<BR>
“好吧，好吧，随便，”税吏恼怒地说，“你有多少把玻璃斧？”<BR>
<BR>
“我从未听说过东陲有任何关于玻璃斧的法律，”阿萨尔维姆断然回答，“只有关于斧、锛、耙、犁的法律。如果法律没有将我的货物列为征税对象，那我就不会付钱。”<BR>
<BR>
[这段对话的结尾未能保存下来。]<BR><BR>"""

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_LegendsAthalwyrmSHOTN_V2
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Legends of Athalwyrm the Clever-Man<BR>
<BR>
On the Matter of Mountains<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Athalwyrm was walking in the hold of Hrothgar, near the holy mountain which is called the Throat of the World, when the Woodland Man appeared on the path ahead of him.<BR>
<BR>
"Tell me, O Clever-Man," said the Woodland Man, "where is the tallest mountain?"<BR>
<BR>
"I do not know which mountain is the tallest, but the tallest mountain that I know of is right ahead," replied Athalwyrm, gesturing past where the other was standing.<BR>
<BR>
"Indeed," laughed the Woodland Man, "you do not know it, but the tallest mountain is the mountain of knowledge, and I am the map to its hidden paths. If you wish to climb the mountain, walk my path."<BR>
<BR>
"And what good can your path and your mountain of knowledge do me?" inquired the Clever-Man.<BR>
<BR>
The Woodland Man, seemingly surprised, answered: "You can learn all you wish to learn, solve any problem you wish to solve, and become the wisest of the wise. I invite you to do so. Come, walk with me."<BR>
<BR>
"No, elf-demon," said Athalwyrm, "I will not take your path, nor will I trust you to guide me. The things that are unknown are much greater than the things that are known, and death is much longer than life. The greater part of the secrets of your realm are useless to me. To learn them would take my whole life, and you would not let me go free in death. I can find all the answers I need in my own clever head that was given to me by Shor." So saying, the Clever-Man kept walking and climbed the mountain.<BR><BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
智士阿萨尔维姆传奇<BR>
<BR>
论高山之事<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
阿萨尔维姆正在洛斯伽领地内行走，靠近那座被称为世界之喉的圣山，这时森地者出现在他前方的路上。<BR>
<BR>
“告诉我，哦，智士，”森地者说，“最高的山在哪里？”<BR>
<BR>
“我不知道哪座山最高，但我知道的最高山就在正前方，”阿萨尔维姆回答，指着那人所站位置的前方。<BR>
<BR>
“确实，”森地者笑道，“你有所不知，最高的山是知识之山，而我是通往其隐秘路径的地图。若想攀登此山，就走我的路吧。”<BR>
<BR>
“你的路和你的知识之山对我有什么好处？”智士问道。<BR>
<BR>
森地者似乎很惊讶，回答道：“你可以学到你想学的一切，解决你想解决的任何问题，成为智者中最有智慧的人。我邀请你这样做。来吧，与我同行。”<BR>
<BR>
“不，精灵恶魔，”阿萨尔维姆说，“我不会走你的路，也不会相信你的指引。未知的事物远大于已知，死亡远比生命漫长。你领域中的大部分秘密对我毫无用处。学习它们会耗费我一生，而你也不会让我在死后获得自由。我能在我自己聪明的头脑中找到我需要的一切答案，这头脑是朔尔赐予我的。”说罢，智士继续前行，攀登高山。<BR><BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>The Lesser Catechism of Julianos
<BR>
<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Q: What is the domain of Julianos?<BR>
<BR>
A: His domain is Wisdom and Logic.<BR>
<BR>
Q: What is Wisdom?<BR>
<BR>
A: Wisdom is seeing beyond the veil and discovering the true Nature of things.<BR>
<BR>
Q: What is Logic?<BR>
<BR>
A: Logic is the paved road whereupon the mortal may journey from Ignorance to Knowledge.<BR>
<BR>
Q: How does the mortal use Wisdom and Logic?<BR>
<BR>
A: The mortal uses Wisdom and Logic to establish and maintain Law.<BR>
<BR>
Q: What is Law?<BR>
<BR>
A: Law is how the World functions.<BR>
<BR>
Q: Where is Law found?<BR>
<BR>
A: Law is found in all things. Law commands Magnus to rise in the east and set in the west. Law commands a tiny seed to grow into a mighty tree. Law commands the ruler to punish the Law-breaker.<BR>
<BR>
Q: How can Law be determined?<BR>
<BR>
A: Law can be determined through observation and through the declarations of rulers.<BR>
<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
LEX IMPERII II<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
<BR>
[...]<BR>
<BR>
II.III Acts and Declaration before the Imperial Authorities<BR>
1. The records of Imperial Power shall declare year and day at which they shall be received; the declared name, surname (if existent and apposite), and age of those who shall be therein mentioned<BR>
2. The Executor of Imperial Power shall insert nothing in the act other than what is declared by the parties relevant<BR>
3. Warrants and papers of note shall be marked by glyph, in such a way as to be legible and traceable by Elder Scroll, and deposited in duplicate for the safekeeping of the Concordian Archives<BR>
4. Any act done in a civil court of a Strange Place by a Citizen of Empire shall be deemed valid, if it is recorded in such a way as to be legible and traceable by Elder Scroll<BR>
5. Every act done in a civil court of a Strange Place by a Citizen of Empire shall be deemed valid, if acknowledged conformable to Law by diplomatic agents or commissioners of Empire for commercial relations<BR>
6. That offense to preceding articles committed by Executors of Imperial Power be prosecuted by Blood or Quill, and punished with a fine not exceeding 500 Septims or their lawful equivalent, or death<BR>
<BR>
II.III.i Nascency<BR>
1. Declarations of birth be made, within five days of delivery, to the Imperial Executor of the place of birth<BR>
2. Be mentioned the day and place of birth, the sex of infant, the name which shall be given, birthsign, and parents and/or witnesses those names and professions, and domicile<BR>
3. That of newborn orphans the finder shall carry these to an Executor of Imperial Power, or a Follower true to Maratic Law, or a Saint of Proven Infantine Disposition, and declare these the circumstances of time, and place, and also of the child apparent age and sex, and name<BR>
4. If this the child be born at sea, that the act of birth be drawn up in nine hours, in the presence of a parent, if at hand, and of two witnesses chosen from the vessel's officers, or for want from the ship's crew<BR>
5. If this the child be born on starlit sojourn, that the act of birth be drawn up in nine hours, presence of linear time permitting, in the presence of a parent, if at hand, and of two witnesses chosen from the vessel's officers, or for want from the vessel's crew<BR>
6. That the act of taking knowledge be inscribed in the registers, at its date<BR>
<BR>
II.III.ii Marriage by Creed or Citizen Consent<BR>
1. That the act of marriage may be performed either by consent or before a Deity or Spirit of choice<BR>
2. That the Deity or Spirit of choice be manifest or be of proven Marital Disposition, be it the Divine Mara, a Servant Resplendent of the Divine Mara, a Saint of Marital Disposition, or otherwise a spirit or deity of Marital Disposition<BR>
3. That the Deity or Spirit of choice be represented by a priest, preacher, initiate, monk, hermit, holy fool, elder, haeresiarch, curate, cleric, elder, primate, oracle, prelate or ecclesiastic proven knowledgeable of the inner mysteries of the Deity or Spirit of choice<BR>
4. That the act of marriage by Citizen consent be witnessed by at least two attestors of good standing, or by a Representative or Executor of Imperial Power<BR>
5. Declaration of marriage be made, within three days of union, to the Imperial Executor of the place of union, either by the two partners both present or by either partner accompanied by their witnesses, representatives of Deity, Saint or Spirit, or representative of Imperial Power, or by the equivalent attestation in writing<BR>
6. Acts of opposition to a marriage be signed, both original and copy, by the parties in opposition, or their legal representatives, and communicated both to the part and the Imperial Executor, or else delivered at the domicile of these parties<BR>
<BR>
II.III.iii Decease<BR>
1. That no interment, cremation, moth-consumption, or other burial take place without a written authority from the Imperial Executor of the place of death, free of charge, and that this written authority may not be delivered until the Imperial Executor or their Representative have been conducted to the deceased person to assure themselves of the death actual<BR>
2. The act of civil death be drawn up by an Imperial Executor or their Representative, or by a Servant of Arkayn Disposition, on the declaration of two witnesses, in good standing with the community<BR>
3. The act of death shall contain the name, surname (if existent and apposite), age, profession, and domicil of the deceased person, name and surname (if existent and apposite) of their consort, if applicable, name, surname (if existent and apposite), age, profession, and residence of the deponents, and if related their degree of affinity<BR>
4. In case of death in a Legion hospital, civil or public edifice, Maratic sanatorium, or Imperial Prison, the master of this edifice is required to notify the Imperial Executor within 48 hours. Furthermore register of death shall be kept in the aforesaid edifices<BR>
5. When any sign or mark of violent death, or other circumstances which give rise to suspicion, shall appear, interment shall not take place until an Imperial Executor, Officer of the Watch, Servant of Arkayn Disposition, or doctor in the magic of physic, has drawn up a statement of condition, and of circumstances<BR>
6. Keepers of record within an Imperial Prison are required, within 24 hours after the execution of justice resulting in death, to transmit to the Imperial Executor at the relevant place all relevant information, after which the act of death shall be reduced to writing<BR>
7. Prisoners condemned to death by an Imperial Executor of justice, or prisoners in custody of the Imperial prison system who are deceased in any other manner, natural or unnatural, forfeit the rights of their mortal remains<BR>
8. The mortal remains of prisoners thus executed or otherwise deceased in Imperial custody may be released to their next of kin in return for a fee, the weight of which is dependent on the crime committed by the deceased Citizen<BR>
9. If no legitimate next of kin is willing to claim the mortal remains of the deceased, they may be disposed of by the master of this prison edifice or by a lawful Imperial Executor, either by interring the body with the proper Arkayn ritual, or by selling the body to an accredited mage, scholar, necromancer, or individual of noble birth.<BR>
<BR>
II.III.iv Acts of a Civil Nature regarding the Legion in the Provincial Territories<BR>
1. Acts of a civil nature within the provincially administered territories, concerning the military or personae attached to the Legion, shall be committed to writing in forms prescribed by preceding regulations<BR>
2. The captain or commander of every company shall discharge the functions of an Imperial Executor, wherever a Governor, Prefect, or other Representative of Imperial power is not present. The same function will be discharged by a military inspector at reviews<BR>
3 With every body of troops, a register shall be kept of acts of a civil nature relative to individuals of the corps, and another with the staff-officer of the Legion or Legion division<BR>
4. The register shall be endorsed and marked with glyph, in every corps, by the commanding officer<BR>
5. Declarations of birth in the army shall be made within 10 days succeeding the delivery<BR>
6. Declarations of marriage among the military shall be made at the last known domicil of both parties<BR>
7. Acts of death shall be drawn up, in every company, by the quarter-master or officer, or by the inspector at reviews<BR>

5. 婚姻声明应在结合后三天内，向结合地的帝国执行者做出，可由双方共同到场，或由一方在其见证人、神灵、圣徒或精魂的代表、或帝国权力代表的陪同下做出，或通过同等的书面证明做出<BR>
6. 反对婚姻的行为，其原件和副本均应由反对方或其法定代表签字，并通知当事方和帝国执行者，或送交当事方的住所<BR>
<BR>
第二章 第三节 第三项 死亡<BR>
1. 未经死亡地帝国执行者的书面授权，不得进行土葬、火葬、蛾食葬或其他埋葬，该授权免费。并且，在帝国执行者或其代表被带到死者面前确认死亡属实之前，不得交付此书面授权<BR>
2. 民事死亡文书应由帝国执行者或其代表，或具有阿尔凯倾向的仆人，在两名社区信誉良好的见证人声明后拟定<BR>
3. 死亡文书应包含死者姓名、姓氏（如有且适用）、年龄、职业和住所；其配偶（如适用）的姓名、姓氏（如有且适用）；证人的姓名、姓氏（如有且适用）、年龄、职业和住所，以及如有亲属关系，其亲等<BR>
4. 若死亡发生在军团医院、民用或公共建筑、玛拉疗养院或帝国监狱，该建筑的负责人须在48小时内通知帝国执行者。此外，死亡登记册应保存在上述建筑内<BR>
5. 当出现任何暴力死亡的迹象或痕迹，或其他引起怀疑的情况时，在帝国执行者、警卫官、具有阿尔凯倾向的仆人，或物理魔法医生拟定状况和环境声明之前，不得进行埋葬<BR>
6. 帝国监狱内的记录保管员，须在执行导致死亡的司法判决后24小时内，将所有相关信息传送至相关地点的帝国执行者，之后死亡文书应形成书面文件<BR>
7. 被帝国司法执行者判处死刑的囚犯，或因任何其他自然或非自然原因在帝国监狱系统羁押期间死亡的囚犯，将丧失对其遗体的权利<BR>
8. 如此被处决或在帝国羁押期间以其他方式死亡的囚犯遗体，可移交给其近亲，但需支付费用，费用金额取决于已故公民所犯罪行<BR>
9. 若无合法近亲愿意认领死者遗体，可由该监狱建筑的负责人或合法的帝国执行者处理，要么通过适当的阿尔凯仪式埋葬遗体，要么将遗体出售给经认证的法师、学者、死灵法师或贵族出身者。<BR>

III.IV Domicilia<BR>
1. The domicil of every Imperial Citizen is, as pertains the exercise of their civil privileges, that place which is their principal establishment<BR>
2. Change of domicil shall be effected by circumstance of actual habitation, accompanied by true intent of fixing principal establishment in this place<BR>
3. Proof of intent may be collected by express declaration to the magistrates of such a place which the citizen shall quit, as to those of the place where they wish to settle<BR>
4. A citizen called to public office must preserve their former domicil, unless they manifest a contrary intention<BR>
5. Acceptance of offices, bestowed for life, shall import immediate removal of the dignitary's domicil to the place where they are to exercise their office<BR>
<BR>
[...]<BR>
<BR>
III.XXI The Notion of Property<BR>
1. All property is immovable, movable, or of arcane nature<BR>
<BR>
III.XXI.I.i Immovable Property<BR>
1. Property is immovable by nature, by destination, or by object to which it is applied<BR>
2. The soil of the earth and buildings with sure foundations are immovable by nature<BR>
3. Crops hanging by the roots, and fruit not yet gathered, are immovable by nature. If the crop is harvested but not yet carried away, it becomes movable. If only part of the crop is cut, only such a part alone is movable<BR>
4. Livestock which a proprietor agrees to give up to a tenant of farmer for the purpose of cultivation is regarded as immovable in pursuance of this agreement<BR>
<BR>
III.XXI.I.ii Movable Property<BR>
1. Property is movable by nature, of by determination of Law<BR>
2. Movable in nature are all bodies which may be transported from place to place, be they animals or inanimate things<BR>
3. Movable by determination of Law are bonds and actions relating to sums demandable, or personal effects, actions and interests in companies for objects of finance, commerce, or industry, or perpetual or life annuities.<BR>
4. Boats, ferries, vessels, hako skiffs, junk, ships, and gondolas are all movable<BR>
5. Articles arising from the demotion of an edifice or the construction of a new one are movable until they are employed by the artificer of this edifice<BR>
<BR>
III.XXI.I.iii Arcane Property<BR>
1. Arcane property is neither movable nor immovable by nature, but can only be considered as movable or immovable by determination of Law<BR>
2. Property normally considered immovable made movable by application of arcane energies is considered movable until such the application of arcane energies ceases to be<BR>
3. Property normally considered movable made immovable by application of arcane energies retains its status as movable property, regardless of the application of arcane energies<BR>
4. Rooms, houses, settlements, or otherwise locations that have been reduced to a movable state by application of arcane energies, be it by reduction in size, or folding, or transference to a private realm, are considered movable if their method of accession is movable; immovable if their method of accession is immovable<BR>

第三章 第四节 住所<BR>
1. 每个帝国公民的住所，就其民事特权的行使而言，是其主要生活场所<BR>
2. 住所变更应通过实际居住情况，并伴随在此地建立主要生活场所的真实意图来实现<BR>
3. 意图证明可通过向公民将离开之地的地方法官，以及向其希望定居之地的地方法官做出明确声明来收集<BR>
4. 被任命担任公职的公民必须保留其原有住所，除非他们表现出相反的意图<BR>
5. 接受终身授予的职位，意味着该权贵的住所立即迁移至其行使职权之地<BR>

<BR>
第三章 第二十一节 财产的概念<BR>
1. 所有财产分为不动产、动产或秘法性质财产<BR>
<BR>
第三章 第二十一节 第一项 第一目 不动产<BR>
1. 财产因其性质、用途或其所属对象而为不动产<BR>
2. 土地和具有稳固地基的建筑物因其性质而为不动产<BR>
3. 连根生长的作物和尚未采摘的果实因其性质而为不动产。若作物已收割但尚未运走，则变为动产。若仅部分作物被收割，则仅该部分为动产<BR>
4. 业主同意交给承租农民用于耕作目的的牲畜，根据该协议被视为不动产<BR>
<BR>
第三章 第二十一节 第一项 第二目 动产<BR>
1. 财产因其性质或法律规定而为动产<BR>
2. 所有可以从一个地方运到另一个地方的物体，无论是动物还是无生命之物，因其性质而为动产<BR>
3. 根据法律规定为动产的有：债券和与可索偿金额相关的诉讼、个人财物、金融、商业或工业公司的股份和权益、或永久或终身年金。<BR>
4. 小船、渡船、船只、哈科小艇、帆船、船舶和贡多拉都是动产<BR>
5. 由建筑物拆除或新建所产生的物品，在被该建筑的工匠使用之前为动产<BR>
<BR>
第三章 第二十一节 第一项 第三目 秘法性质财产<BR>
1. 秘法性质财产因其性质既非动产也非不动产，只能根据法律规定被视为动产或不动产<BR>
2. 通常被视为不动产但因施加秘法能量而变为可移动的财产，在秘法能量停止施加之前被视为动产<BR>
3. 通常被视为动产但因施加秘法能量而变得不可移动的财产，无论是否施加了秘法能量，都保持其动产地位<BR>
4. 通过施加秘法能量（无论是通过缩小尺寸、折叠，还是转移至私人领域）而变为可移动状态的房间、房屋、定居点或其他地点，若其接入方式为动产，则视为动产；若其接入方式为不动产，则视为不动产<BR>
<BR>

LEX IMPERII IV<BR>

IV.XI Rights of Accession<BR>
1. Private Citizens have free disposition of the property theirs, subject to modifications established by Law<BR>
2. Property not belonging to private Citizens is administered by an Imperial Executor, and cannot be alienated except in the forms and in pursuance of peculiar regulations<BR>
3. Highways, roads and streets, passable rivers and streams, shores, ports, and shiproads, and all areas of Imperial territory, which are not susceptible to private proprietorship, are considered property of the Emperor, and dependencies of the Imperial domain<BR>
4. All unclaimed and owner-less property, and that of persons who die without heir, are property of the Emperor<BR>
5. All gates, moats, ramparts or places of war, and fortresses erected by the Legion, are property of the Emperor<BR>
6. Common property is that to the ownership or produce of which the inhabitants of one or more communes have an acquired right<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
IV.XXII Rights of Usufruct, Commons, and Habitation<BR>
<BR>
IV.XXII.i Right of Usufruct<BR>
1. Usufruct is the right of enjoying the advantage of things that are in the rightful property of the proprietor citizen, in the same manner as the proprietor citizen, but on condition of this right being agreeable with the preservation of the substance of the thing proper<BR>
2. Usufruct is established by Law or by citizen consent<BR>
3. Usufruct may be established in simple manner or by condition<BR>
4. Usufruct may be established over every species of property, movable, immovable, or of arcane nature<BR>
5. In order to enjoy usufruct, the citizens involved must first establish security and make inventory of the property in question<BR>
<BR>
IV.XXII.ii Right of Commons and Habitation<BR>
1. The rights of commons and habitation are established and forfeited in the same manner as those of usufruct<BR>
2. Likewise, the rights of commons and habitation cannot be enjoyed without first establishing security and making inventory of the property in question<BR>
3. A citizen who enjoys right of habitation must care for this property as a proper citizen befits<BR>
4. Citizens who have right of commonage over the fruits of an estate, may not exploit these for more than is necessary to their wants and those of their next of kin<BR>
5. Citizens who have right of commonage cannot yield or let this right to others<BR>
6. Citizens who have right of habitation in a domicil, may bring their family to live there even if they were not married at the time when the right of habitation was conferred upon them<BR>
7. The right of habitation can neither be ceded nor hired<BR>
8. Commonage in woods, forests, jungle, and other places of wilderness are regulated by particular law, or by the Will of the Emperor if they fall under his direct territories<BR>

帝国法典 IV<BR>

第四章 第十一节 添附权<BR>
1. 私人公民可自由处置其财产，但须遵守法律规定的修改<BR>
2. 不属于私人公民的财产由帝国执行者管理，除非按照特定形式和遵循特殊规定，否则不得转让<BR>
3. 公路、道路和街道、可通航的河流与溪流、海岸、港口、船道，以及帝国领土内所有不适合私人所有的区域，均被视为皇帝的财产，为帝国领地的附属<BR>
4. 所有无人认领和无主财产，以及死后无继承人者的财产，均为皇帝财产<BR>
5. 所有城门、护城河、城墙或军事要塞，以及军团建造的堡垒，均为皇帝财产<BR>
6. 公共财产是指一个或多个公社的居民对其所有权或产出拥有既定权利的财产<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
第四章 第二十二节 用益权、共用权与居住权<BR>
<BR>
第四章 第二十二节 第一项 用益权<BR>
1. 用益权是以与业主公民相同的方式，享受属于业主公民合法财产之物的利益的权利，但条件是这种权利需与保持该物本身实质相一致<BR>
2. 用益权由法律或公民同意确立<BR>
3. 用益权可以以简单方式或附条件确立<BR>
4. 用益权可针对任何类型的财产设立，无论动产、不动产还是秘法性质财产<BR>
5. 为享有用益权，相关公民必须首先提供担保并对所涉财产进行盘点<BR>
<BR>
第四章 第二十二节 第二项 共用权与居住权<BR>
1. 共用权与居住权的设立和丧失方式与用益权相同<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Lichdom: A Trap, an Escape<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR><BR>
Every proud necromancer of sound mind knows the failings of mortal flesh. And quite a few of them work to overcome it. If you are among them, heed my warning!<BR>
<BR>
For far too long, the path to Lichdom consisted of rote memorization of chants from dusty old tomes, rediscovering rituals from fragments, and learning from texts that put the "Philosophical" into "Philosophical Necromancy". Were that a master of old had written clearly and directly instead of ranting about "carving a path with shining dark to the ninth secret of Magnus Eternal"!<BR>
<BR>
But, miraculously, the Tiber Wars happened! An unforseen consequence of victory: whole libraries were "acquisitioned" by the victorious Empire and moved to the Imperial Palace. Generations of uprisings and civil wars later, precious few of those tomes found themselves appreciative new owners. And while knowledge does not want anything in itself, I do find myself willing to bridge some gaps.<BR>
<BR>
Not that I will have an answer for everything, of course! But certain Ancient Elven accounts, entirely non-magical, unfortunately, have given me insight on the roots and philosophy of Lichdom rituals. It is now possible for me to state with near-certainty that the dusty books and the "Philosophy" essentially contain a series of unconnected rituals originally intended to attaining godhood.<BR>
<BR>
What I have learned is this: while you may believe that attaining Lichdom is akin to spiritual amputation, in which parts of your soul are replaced with carved space which the magicka flow of Magnus Eternal fills, this is incorrect. This is what you should already know and it is all wrong.<BR>
<BR>
Philosophically speaking, the rituals entail spending a bit of your soul to carve a pattern into the world. If you are thinking of the Monomyth, you are thinking correctly. Of course, a single mortal soul is not powerful enough to become a second Jephre, but it is powerful enough for its attached body to last in undeath without requiring additional sustenance.<BR>
<BR>
But is this really the goal?<BR>
<BR>
The magicka of Magnus Eternal does not simply flow into the world, it follows certain patterns. Lichdom carves a pattern into the world, and all patterns entirely depend on the pattern screamer. For most people, it is a trap they cannot escape from. For a few, it can be an escape.<BR>
<BR>
I have wondered why this is. If we dig deep enough, whose skull will grin back at us? And what was their goal? Good questions, perhaps, but for another time.<BR>
<BR>
In practical terms, there are two possible results of the pattern: what I have chosen to call the Common Lich and the True Lich.<BR>
<BR>
The Common Lich<BR>
<BR>
When the pattern is undirected, by a mind that is not curious enough, the practitioner has gained immortality by carving their immortality into the word. But that is all there is to it, they cannot achieve anything from there on.<BR>
<BR>
It is understandable if this feels counter-intuitive, but consider: what happens when the Lich is killed by force of arms, as so often happens?<BR>
<BR>
Their immortality has been disrupted and so the pattern collapses. The Lich simply dies, no better than a mortal.<BR>
<BR>
The same thing happens if this kind of Lich tries to change its pattern, perhaps because it has found the problem with its state. The pattern collapses and the Lich dies. Immortality cannot sustain immortality.<BR>
<BR>
This is the trap. If you have already walked down this path, you have my sympathies.<BR>
<BR>
The True Lich<BR>
<BR>
By caution, chance, longing, or luck, these practitioners have found that simply becoming immortal is not good enough.<BR>
<BR>
The patterns they carve are tied to a focus, be it a concept, object, or even a more esoteric thing. It could be as mundane as a needle or as outlandish as a song or sickness. Their immortality is merely the result of their focus, however, and not the focus itself. And this is the crucial difference.<BR>
<BR>
If this kind of Lich is killed by force of arms, the pattern is not disrupted as such, and they will rise again. For some, only under certain conditions, but they will rise without error.<BR>
<BR>
But, like a metaphysical bank account, if the pattern is removed, this changes. If the needle is broken, the song no longer sung, or the sickness cured, this Lich is about as immortal as the Common variety - but there is yet another crucial difference: they can carve a new pattern with their soul, secure themselves again and learn and grow as they have before.<BR>
<BR>
It would be difficult, ascending a second time. Maybe they could try to go back on the path of the original intention of the rituals. Maybe they can try for godhood. They will probably fail.<BR>
<BR>
But at least they can try.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
巫妖化：陷阱与解脱<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR><BR>
每一个心智健全、引以为傲的死灵法师都知道凡人肉身的缺陷。他们中有不少人致力于克服它。若你也在其中，请留意我的警告！<BR>
<BR>
长久以来，巫妖化之路一直是死记硬背布满灰尘的古籍中的咒语，从残篇断章中重新发现仪式，以及从那些将“哲学”注入“哲学死灵法术”的文本中学习。要是古代的某位大师能清晰直接地写作，而不是空谈“以闪耀的黑暗开辟通往永恒玛格努斯第九秘密的道路”就好了！<BR>
<BR>
但是，奇迹般地，泰伯战争发生了！胜利的一个未曾预见的后果：整座整座的图书馆被胜利的帝国“征用”并搬到了皇宫。经过几代人的起义和内战，这些古籍中只有极少数找到了懂得欣赏它们的新主人。虽然知识本身无所求，但我发现自己愿意填补一些空白。<BR>
<BR>
当然，我并非知晓一切！但某些古老的精灵记述（可惜完全是描述性的，不带魔法）让我洞悉了巫妖化仪式的根源与哲学。现在我几乎可以断言，那些布满灰尘的古籍和“哲学”本质上包含了一系列最初旨在成神、彼此并不相连的仪式。<BR>
<BR>
我了解到的是：虽然你可能认为巫妖化类似于精神截肢，即灵魂的一部分被凿出的空间所取代，并由永恒玛格努斯的魔法流动来填充，但这是不正确的。这是你应该已经知道的内容，但它完全是错的。<BR>
<BR>
从哲学上讲，这些仪式需要消耗你灵魂的一部分，在世界中刻下一个模式。如果你想到了单一神话，那你就想对了。当然，一个凡人的灵魂不足以强大到成为第二个耶弗瑞，但它足以使其附着的躯体在亡灵状态下持久存在，无需额外的给养。<BR>
<BR>
但这真的是目标吗？<BR>
<BR>
永恒玛格努斯的魔法并非简单地流入世界，它遵循着一定的模式。巫妖化在世界中刻下一个模式，而所有模式都完全依赖于模式呐喊者。对大多数人来说，这是一个无法逃脱的陷阱。对少数人来说，它可能是一种解脱。<BR>
<BR>
我一直想知道这是为什么。如果我们挖掘得足够深，会是哪个颅骨冲我们咧嘴而笑？他们的目标又是什么？也许这是好问题，但留待下次再谈。<BR>
<BR>
实际上，这个模式可能产生两种结果：我称之为普通巫妖与真正巫妖。<BR>
<BR>
普通巫妖<BR>
<BR>
当模式缺乏导向，由一个好奇心不足的心智所刻时，修行者通过将自身的不朽刻入世界而获得了永生。但仅此而已，他们此后无法再有寸进。<BR>
<BR>
若这感觉有违直觉，也情有可原，但请考虑一下：当巫妖（如经常发生的那样）被武力杀死时，会发生什么？<BR>
<BR>
他们的不朽被扰乱，模式随之崩溃。巫妖就此死去，与凡人无异。<BR>
<BR>
如果这类巫妖试图改变其模式（也许是因为发现了自身状态的问题），同样的事情也会发生。模式崩溃，巫妖死去。不朽无法维持不朽。<BR>
<BR>
这就是陷阱。若你已走上这条路，我深表同情。<BR>
<BR>
真正巫妖<BR>
<BR>
出于谨慎、偶然、渴望或运气，这些修行者发现仅仅成为不朽是不够的。<BR>
<BR>
他们刻下的模式与一个焦点相连，这个焦点可以是一个概念、一个物体，甚至更玄妙的东西。它可以平凡如一根针，也可以奇异如一首歌或一种疾病。然而，他们的不朽仅仅是其焦点的结果，而非焦点本身。这就是关键的区别。<BR>
<BR>
如果这类巫妖被武力杀死，模式本身并未被扰乱，他们会再次崛起。对某些而言，可能只在特定条件下，但他们会无误地崛起。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

Lichdom: A Trap, an Escape<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR><BR>
Every proud necromancer of sound mind knows the failings of mortal flesh. And quite a few of them work to overcome it. If you are among them, heed my warning!<BR>
<BR>
For far too long, the path to Lichdom consisted of rote memorization of chants from dusty old tomes, rediscovering rituals from fragments, and learning from texts that put the "Philosophical" into "Philosophical Necromancy". <BR>

<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
The Common Lich<BR>
<BR>
When the pattern is undirected, by a mind that is not curious enough, the practitioner has gained immortality by carving their immortality into the word. But that is all there is to it, they cannot achieve anything from there on.<BR>
