XXIII. URIEL III MANTIARCO or THE CINDER-KING<BR>

Of all men and women who held the vaunted title, Emperor of Tamriel, none were unworthy as Uriel III (save the Expunged Reman). Only for the sake of completeness will his life and deeds be tallied here.<BR>

<BR>

Mantiarco, under the tutelage of his mother, the cursed Wolf-Queen of Solitude, had engineered the petty kings of High Rock and northern Morrowind to rise in rebellion against Imperial authority. With the Legion's strength now divided, Mantiarco set his mercenary armies against the sacred Imperial City itself, against the very heart of the Empire. The Legion was in disarray, the Empress missing, and in but a fortnight the City's sheer white walls were broken, its red shores defiled. Uriel Mantiarco usurped the throne, crowning himself Uriel Septim III, though he has no right to that name.<BR>

<BR>

This heresy would not stand. The coronation of Uriel Mantiarco was defied by both brothers of the traitor Potema, Cephorus Septim, the king of Gilane and Magnus Septim, the king of Wayrest, neither of these noble lords sharing Potema's innate pull to misrule and madness. For six years they battled the forces of the traitor Mantiarco across the whole of northern Tamriel, until the fate of the Empire was decided by a twofold battle in 3E 117. The brothers Septim had devised a brilliant military campaign, which had divided the armies of the Mantiarcos across Hammerfell and Skyrim, and cut off the weak Uriel III from the tutelage of his more intelligent and warlike mother. In the Battle of Ichidag, Hammerfell, a cornered Uriel III faced the armies of Cephorus, consisting of the defectors of the Ninth Legion and his loyal Redguards subjects. Uriel III proved himself an inept tactician, and was captured a few hours into the battle. He was sent to Gilane, but when news of his capture spread, the common people rose up in righteous anger, overwhelmed his battle-weary keepers, and burned Uriel III alive in his carriage. This, the fate of a traitor.<BR>

<BR>

Simultaneously, Queen Potema was engaged in her own struggle against King Magnus, who had taken shelter in the ruins of Kogmenthist Castle near the Nordic city of Falconstar. Potema being a more apt tactician, the battle went well, and when the news of her son's death reached her ears she was infused by such rage and madness than she took to the field herself, forcing Magnus into a hasty and painful retreat. Potema then retreated to her stronghold of Solitude, where for ten years still she degraded herself and her subjects with the blackest arts of necromancy, vampirism and Daedra trafficking, in a futile attempt to keep the judgment of the Emperor and the Divines at bay.<BR>

<BR>

XXIV. CEPHORUS I SEPTIM<BR>

With the death of Uriel III and the disgrace of Potema, the throne fell to Cephorus, third child of Pelagius II. So was crowned Cephorus I, who had won his right to rule through blood and ruthless war, and would know nothing but war his entire reign. The Empire was in utter chaos, with dissidents spreading lies here and there, the misled supporters of Uriel III continuing their blind opposition, and the Wolf-Queen herself launching endless attacks on the righteous ruler of Tamriel, gradually descending into the use of dark and dishonorable tactics. Cephorus I was ever a kind and intelligent man, who could speak with beauty on all subjects of poetry, philosophy and theology, but in the hours of his time he was thus reforged into a ruthless general and a leader of men, perhaps one of the greatest warriors the Septim line ever knew.<BR>

<BR>

It is said that Emperor Cephorus I took the blackened bones of his fallen opponent, Uriel III, with him to the Imperial City, and there exhibited them to the Elder Council, attesting to his absolute victory and ruthlessness in battle. Hereafter he let these bones be locked in a lead coffin and thrown into the inner depths of the Imperial Palace, fearful as he was that Potema would use her necromantic powers on the remnants of her own kin next. Cunningly, this also insured him the support of his Nibenese subjects, who loathed their erstwhile usurper and the defiler of their holy city, and where convinced by local superstition that Uriel III's soul would thus be held by the roots of White-Gold Tower, never to flow downstream to rejoin the Circle of Arkay.<BR>

<BR>

XXV. MAGNUS I SEPTIM<BR>

In 3E 140, Emperor Cephorus I died of old age. As his life of struggle had left no time for marriage or the raising of a suitable heir, the throne now fell to Magnus I. He was almost as old as his brother, but his bloodline was strong and fit to continue. Magnus I ruled only five years, but in his time he returned peace and stability to the finally subjugated northernly kingdom of Solitude, helping to erase the mark of Potema from the mind of its citizenry. With the more warlike of the dissidents finally subjugated by his predecessor's campaigns, Magnus I was free to pacify the few remaining points of opposition in more kindly ways, and brought about peace and stability in his Empire. His legacy, then, is the final defeat of the Mantiarco insurrection, and the continuing reign of the Septims.<BR>

二十二、金泰拉二世·塞普汀 或称 阶下囚<BR>

悲伤而哀婉，金泰拉二世的故事！从年轻时起，她就备受罪孽的侵扰，年仅十五岁就被推上王座，而她的姑母波泰玛·塞普汀在帝国神圣的殿堂中散布最恶毒的诽谤。波泰玛女王用任何值得尊敬的历史学家都不忍重复的言辞，质疑金泰拉继承权的合法性，提及了她父亲统治时期较为松散的道德。她转而提议她自己的儿子，意志薄弱的尤利尔·曼蒂亚科，作为塞普汀帝国的继承人。尽管有元老院的支持以及石头、树篱与火焰对金泰拉二世的拥护，波泰玛的话还是成功地激怒了外省那些一向叛逆的统治者。<BR>

二十三、尤利尔三世·曼蒂亚科 或称 余烬之王<BR>

在所有拥有“泰姆瑞尔皇帝”这一尊贵称号的男男女女中，没有比尤利尔三世更不配的（除了被除名的雷曼）。只是为了完整性，他的生平和事迹才在此罗列。<BR>

<BR>

二十四、塞弗鲁斯一世·塞普汀<BR>

随着尤利尔三世的死亡和波泰玛的失势，王位落到了佩拉吉乌斯二世的第三个孩子塞弗鲁斯手中。塞弗鲁斯一世就这样加冕，他通过鲜血和无情的战争赢得了统治权，在他的整个统治期间，除了战争，他什么都不了解。帝国处于极度混乱之中，异见者到处散布谎言，被误导的尤利尔三世支持者继续盲目反对，而狼心女王本人则不断向泰姆瑞尔的正义统治者发动攻击，逐渐堕落使用黑暗和不光彩的策略。塞弗鲁斯一世曾经是一个善良而聪明的人，能够优美地谈论诗歌、哲学和神学的所有主题，但在那个时代，他被重铸成了一个无情的将军和领袖，也许是塞普汀世系有史以来最伟大的战士之一。<BR>

二十五、马格努斯一世·塞普汀<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>THE LINE of EMPERORS VOLUME VIII: from PELAGIUS III to URIEL IV<BR>

<BR>

A COMPREHENSIVE INQUIRY<BR>

EMPERORS of CYRODIIL<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

by Tyr Ymanwe<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>

<BR>

By the will of Emperor Pelagius IV, I, Tyr Ymanwe, have been given the task of presenting to the discerning public a full and unbiased account of the Line of Emperors, that all may be made aware of the history of Empire, and that the piety, strength, courage, and wisdom of the Rulers of Man be an example to all citizens. In this I succeed my master, Jaume Abtacil, who passed away before the completion of the great work for which he was commissioned. This book is dedicated to him, too, that I may always work in the tradition of excellent scholarship, as he has taught me.<BR>

<BR>

XXVI. PELAGIUS III SEPTIM or THE MAD<BR>

Much has been written of Thoriz Pelagius Septim, the Emperor often maligned as Pelagius the Mad. The reality of his illness cannot be denied, nor can the simple fact that he was in truth not fit to reign, noble blood notwithstanding. Were it not for the insurrection of the Mantiarcos, the Imperial line would have continued by the blessed Kintyra II, full of life and promise, and Pelagius III would never have been near the White-Gold Throne. So the plans of the Divines, graceful and providential, are often crossed by the wickedness of men, who aspire only to the betterment of their selves and care not for the good of the Empire. Indeed, it should come as no surprise that the withered branch of Pelagius III was to carry no good fruit, and the true line of the Septims will continue by a different path before long. Still, the successors of Pelagius III were Emperors in their own right, and though their faults were many, it would be unwise to dismiss them outright.<BR>

<BR>

Emperor Pelagius III assumed the White-Gold Throne in 3E 145, after ruling both as King of Solitude and as High King of Skyrim. He was at this time already married to the Katariah Ra'athim, the Dunmeri Duchess of Vvardenfell, a marriage orchestrated by his father Magnus I to placate the rebellious Dunmeri warlords. By virtue of Katariah's diplomatic temperament she was made Empress Regent when the Emperor's sickness deteriorated beyond his capacity to fulfill his duties. The Emperor was relegated to a life in the country, where healers and priests attended him until his death in 1E 153.<BR>

<BR>

XXVII. KATARIAH I<BR>

As Katariah Ra'athim had adequately governed the Empire during her husband's long deterioration, she was affirmed by the Elder Council in her full regency: an arrangement inspired by the reign of Emperor Kastav during the Remanite dynasty. This decision was rightly contested, as the Dunmeri upstart was utterly foreign to Imperial morals and society, and proved unwilling to adjust. While the official record naturally makes no mention of it, there are enough anecdotes of Katariah's strange and scandalous behavior to affirm that she was unsuited to life among the crown of Imperial nobility. It should come as no surprise that Empress Katariah I avoided the Imperial court, where she was scorned, and instead sought the company of the people and the lowly provincial rulers.<BR>

<BR>

If Empress Katariah I's reign is remembered as a good and joyful time, this is likely the result of her acute diplomatic skills and frequent sojourns among the provinces. For her stewardship, she must be commended. Of course, the period preceding her was plagued by civil war, sickness and rebellion, so the peace of Katariah's time would have seemed a respite even if her rule had been a mediocre one. Regardless of her skills in governance or the people's love for her, Cyrodiil is not one to suffer a foreign hand for long, nor will it truly prosper under one. Katariah's death, caused by a bandit attack during an ill-timed visit to the province of Black Marsh, should come as no surprise.<BR>

<BR>

I hereby wish to warn the reader against a fraudulent account of the death of Katariah by the hand of the scholar Montalius, whose rumormongering and false accusations against families of great stature should be discounted and avoided at all costs.<BR>

<BR>

XXVIII. CASSYNDER SEPTIM<BR>

Little can be said of the rule of Cassynder Septim, which lasted only from 3E 200 to 3E 202. Cassynder, having lived through the reign of his father and his long-lived Elven mother, was already of advanced age when the throne fell to him. Suffering from the debilitating conditions so often encountered among people of half blood, Cassynder at first was unwilling to accept the responsibilities of leadership, but was at last convinced by those loyalists who insisted on the continuation of the true bloodline of Tiber Septim. The demands of governance took a further heavy toll on the Emperor's health, until even the weight of the Amulet of Kings proved too much for him to bear.<BR>

<BR>

XXIX. URIEL IV LARIAT or THE ILLICIT<BR>

Emperor Uriel Lariat was to be the last of this line of steward-Emperors, whose claim to the blood of Septim was often weak or nonexistent. They maintained the Empire, but did not truly rule it as an Emperor might, and were ultimately detrimental to its virtue and glory. Of these, Emperor Uriel IV's claim to the throne was by far the weakest, barely more legitimate than that of an Interregnum pretender.<BR>

<BR>

Uriel Lariat, son of Empress Katariah I and a Breton consort of hers named Gallivere Lariat, was adopted into the true Septim line by Emperor Cassynder -- a simple technicality, to allow Uriel the rule over the kingdom of Wayrest while his half-brother was indisposed. Cassynder was then called upon to fulfill his duty as Emperor, and when he later fell to his responsibilities, Lariat's adoption proved enough to claim the throne. Uriel IV thus had not a drop of Septim blood in his veins, a fact which offended both the low people and the noble members of the Elder Council. Uriel IV's reign was thus inhibited by a certain recalcitrance, the nature of which lied with the monarch, not his subjects.<BR>

奉佩拉吉乌斯四世皇帝之命，我，泰尔·伊曼维，被赋予了向有见地的公众呈现一份关于帝王世系的完整、不偏不倚记述的任务，以使所有人都了解帝国的历史，并使人类统治者的虔诚、力量、勇气和智慧成为所有公民的榜样。在此，我继承了我的老师豪梅·阿布塔西尔的衣钵，他在完成其受命之作前便去世了。这本书也献给他，以便我能像他所教导的那样，始终在卓越学术的传统中工作。<BR>

二十六、佩拉吉乌斯三世·塞普汀 或称 疯子<BR>

关于索里兹·佩拉吉乌斯·塞普汀，这位常被污蔑为“疯子佩拉吉乌斯”的皇帝，已有诸多记载。他患病的事实无可否认，他实际上不适合统治这一简单事实也无可否认，尽管他有着高贵的血统。如果不是因为曼蒂亚科叛乱，帝国世系本应由充满活力和希望的蒙福者金泰拉二世延续，而佩拉吉乌斯三世根本不会靠近白金塔王座。因此，圣灵那优美而天意的计划，常常被人类的邪恶所打断，这些人只追求自身的利益，不关心帝国的福祉。确实，佩拉吉乌斯三世这根枯萎的枝条结不出好果实，这不足为奇，而真正的塞普汀世系不久将由另一条路径延续。尽管如此，佩拉吉乌斯三世的继任者本身也是皇帝，尽管他们缺点众多，但完全否定他们是不明智的。<BR>

佩拉吉乌斯三世皇帝在同时担任独孤城国王和天际至高王之后，于第三纪元145年登基白金塔王座。此时他已与瓦登费尔的丹莫女公爵卡塔瑞亚·拉阿蒂姆结婚，这桩婚姻是他的父亲马格努斯一世为安抚反叛的丹莫军阀而安排的。凭借卡塔瑞亚的外交才能，当皇帝病情恶化到无法履行职责时，她被任命为摄政女皇。皇帝被送到乡下生活，由治疗师和祭司照料，直至他在第一纪元153年去世。<BR>

二十七、卡塔瑞亚一世<BR>

由于卡塔瑞亚·拉阿蒂姆在其丈夫长期病情恶化期间充分治理了帝国，元老院确认了她的完整摄政权：这一安排受到了雷曼王朝时期卡斯塔夫皇帝统治的启发。这一决定理所当然地受到了质疑，因为这位丹莫暴发户完全不同于帝国的道德和社会，并且被证明不愿适应。虽然官方记录自然不会提及，但有足够多的关于卡塔瑞亚怪异和丑闻行为的轶事可以证实她不适合在帝国贵族王冠下的生活。卡塔瑞亚一世女皇避开她被蔑视的帝国宫廷，转而寻求人民和卑微的行省统治者的陪伴，这不足为奇。<BR>

<BR>

如果卡塔瑞亚一世女皇的统治被铭记为一个美好而快乐的时期，这很可能是她敏锐的外交技巧和频繁游历各行省的结果。她作为管理者的努力值得称赞。当然，她之前的时期饱受内战、疾病和叛乱之苦，因此即使她的统治平庸，卡塔瑞亚时代的和平也似乎是一种喘息。无论她的治理技巧如何，也无论人民对她的爱戴如何，西罗帝尔不是能长期忍受异族之手的地方，也不会在其治理下真正繁荣。卡塔瑞亚在一次不合时宜的黑沼泽之行中遭遇匪徒袭击而死，这不足为奇。<BR>

<BR>

我在此希望警告读者，警惕学者蒙塔利乌斯关于卡塔瑞亚之死的虚假记载，其散布谣言和对显赫家族的不实指控应予以摒弃并极力避免。<BR>

<BR>

二十八、卡辛德·塞普汀<BR>

卡辛德·塞普汀的统治从第三纪元200年持续到202年，关于他的统治，可说的不多。卡辛德经历了父亲的统治和他那位长寿的精灵母亲的统治，当王位传给他时，他已经年事已高。患有混血人中常见的衰弱性疾病，卡辛德起初不愿接受领导的责任，但最终被那些坚持延续泰伯·塞普汀真正血脉的忠诚者说服。治理的要求进一步严重损害了皇帝的健康，直到最后，连众王护符的重量都让他无法承受。<BR>

<BR>

二十九、尤利尔四世·拉里亚特 或称 非法者<BR>

尤利尔·拉里亚特皇帝是这条摄政皇帝世系的最后一位，他们对塞普汀血脉的宣称权通常很弱或根本不存在。他们维持了帝国，但没有像皇帝那样真正统治它，最终对其美德和荣耀造成了损害。在这些皇帝中，尤利尔四世对王位的宣称权是最弱的，几乎不比大空位时期的僭主更有合法性。<BR>

<BR>

尤利尔·拉里亚特是卡塔瑞亚一世女皇与其布莱顿配偶加利维尔·拉里亚特之子，被卡辛德皇帝收养进入真正的塞普汀世系 -- 这只是一个简单的技术程序，旨在让尤利尔在其同父异母兄弟身体不适期间统治途歇王国。卡辛德随后被召唤去履行他作为皇帝的职责，当他后来因职责倒下时，拉里亚特的养子身份足以让他宣称王位。因此，尤利尔四世的血管里没有一滴塞普汀的血液，这一事实冒犯了平民百姓和元老院的贵族成员。因此，尤利尔四世的统治受到了一定的抵制，其根源在于君主本身，而非其臣民。<BR>

XXX. CEPHORUS II SEPTIM<BR>

After the death of Uriel Lariat IV, also known as the Illicit, the Elder Council greatly protested the further advancement of the line of Lariat, as their claim on the White-Gold throne was founded on nothing more than the oaths of adoption made by Emperor Cassynder towards Uriel IV, the likes of which do not extend to his children or his children's children. In turn, the councilmen of the Elder Council consulted the annals of ancestry and at long last discovered there an heir more true to the line of Tiber Septim: a Nordic nobleman by name of Cephorus, raised to the throne by the assent of the Elder Council, and duly accepted by Stone, Hedge and Flame.<BR>

<BR>

This was not to the will of the line of Emperors now deposed. Andorak Lariat, son of Uriel IV, opposed the Council's decision and declared his hostility to the appointed Emperor. Once again, civil war frayed the borders of the Empire. Those loyal to Lariat were few in number, and there is no doubt that Cephorus II would have dealt with them swiftly were it not for the sudden onslaught of the Camoran Usurper. The exploits of this Bosmeri sorcerer are better recounted elsewhere. Suffice to say that he was both a ruthless and cunning conqueror, and that the Legions, forced into fighting on two fronts, proved incapable of stopping his northwards advancement.<BR>

<BR>

At long last, Cephorus II was forced to accommodate Andorak, providing amnesty in return for an end to the war. With Andorak back in line, the march of the Usurper was quickly halted, and Cephorus II returned a measure of peace to the inner provinces: truly a rejuvenation of the Emperors of old. Still, many of the provincial lords, ever fickle, turned away from the Empire, and the northwest was to flounder in a state of permanent rebellion for decades to come.<BR>

<BR>

XXXI. URIEL V SEPTIM or THE CONQUEROR<BR>

Uriel V assumed the throne in 3E 268, and faced an Empire of dissension: while the administrative and military might of the Imperials was stronger than it had been for over a century, many had lost faith in the rule of Cyrodiil, and the people were fractured. Uriel V was a farsighted man, and, taking the example of Reman I and Tiber Septim, the conquering Emperors of old, he decided on a policy of military expansion far beyond the borders of the continent. In this way, the peoples of Tamriel were once again united to a single purpose, as has been the higher calling of the Emperors of Cyrodiil since the dawn of man.<BR>

<BR>

These conquests, the subject of many a song, carried Uriel V and his faithful Legions across the Padomaic Ocean, to distant Akavir, where in 3E 288 they settled a large and prosperous valley, bringing Imperial culture and civilization to its natives. For two years the Imperial Province of Akavir prospered under the hand of the Emperor. However, this enterprise, grand and beautiful in its design, was not to last. The Tsaeci lords of this realm, quick to forget the ancient oaths they swore to Emperor Reman at Pale Pass, responded to the Emperor's arrival by amassing in great number, and attacking the fledgling colony without warning. Despite the great effort of his soldiers, including the willing sacrifice of the Tenth Legion, the Emperor was killed. Fallen in foreign lands, never will he rest in the tombs of his forefathers, in Cyrodiil, his home.<BR>

<BR>

Though his venture was seemingly futile, Emperor Uriel V is to this day remembered as one of the greatest generals and leaders the Empire has ever seen, the first to increase the Cyrodiil's borders since Tiber Septim himself. Indeed, Uriel's conquests convinced many of the Provincial rulers of the legitimacy of this branch of the Septim dynasty, and proved beyond a shadow of a doubt that the will of Talos was alive and well in the heart of Empire.<BR>

<BR>

XXXII. URIEL VI SEPTIM or THE PATIENT<BR>

When Uriel V, his father, was cut down in Akavir, Uriel VI has but five years old. The Elder Council had since the days of Pelagius III assumed many responsibilities, a necessity in the face of the often weak regents of that branch. Uriel V had restored the grandeur of the Emperor's sole and undisputed power, but the Council was yet loath to give up its privileges, accustomed as they were to the wielding of power. They gave Thonica, the consort of Uriel V, a limited regency only, and later conspired with her to further encroach on those prerogatives that are the right of the Emperor alone.<BR>

<BR>

When Uriel VI was belatedly crowned Emperor in 3E 307, he found this to be a largely ceremonial role. No content with this illusory power, the Emperor set about to regain his position through a careful and measured policy, exploiting both the complex systems of governance as the weak mind and will of many a councilman. In but six years, he had reconquered the governance of Tamriel much as his father had conquered the eastlands.<BR>

<BR>

XXXIII. MORIHATHA SEPTIM<BR>

When in 3E 313 Uriel VI came to a premature end in an unfortunate horse-riding accident, his beloved and well-respected sister, Morihatha, was crowned Empress of Tamriel. Morihatha, as beautiful as she was cunning, had been instrumental in her late brother's takeover of Imperial might, and was now well-accustomed to the mechanics of power. Unlike the purely diplomatic Uriel VI, Morihatha had mastered both the word and the sword, using both in her quest to once and for all rid the Empire of the simmering rebellions that had been ongoing since the days of her grandfather, Cephorus II. By her will the Empire was reshaped, as institutional and administrative structures took root even in the most distant and unruly provinces.<BR>

<BR>

Still, her calm and deliberate demeanor in dealing with these insurgents proved to be her ultimate undoing. In 3E 339 Empress Morihatha was assassinated, a deed later found to be ordered by Thoricles Romus, Councilman of Black Marsh, who was enraged by the Empress' refusal to send military aid to his mismanaged province. Romus was promptly executed, and any and all Argonians were henceforth banned from sitting on the Council, until an Emperor decides otherwise.<BR>

<BR>

Morihatha had no living children, and her younger sister, Eloisa, had passed away four years before. The throne thus passed on to Eloisa's only son, who was crowned Pelagius IV, the current Emperor, and Emperor for many years to come! In the ten years that Pelagius IV has been in power, the Empire has been blessed with a never before seen sense of peace and purpose: the Emperor has continued Morihatha's good work of uniting the warring provinces, and striking down all opposition with an even hand. Under his tutelage, the Law has been kind and strict, the Legions honorable and strong, and by his intercession with the Nine Divines all harvests and industry go well. In the name of this humble scholar, and in the name of my dearly departed master Jaume Abtacil, I hereby humbly give thanks to Emperor Pelagius IV, for his continued defense and benevolent governance of the Empire, and for commissioning this full account of the Line of Emperors.<BR>

三十、塞弗鲁斯二世·塞普汀<BR>

在尤利尔·拉里亚特四世（即“非法者”）去世后，元老院强烈抗议拉里亚特世系的进一步延续，因为他们对白金塔王座的宣称权仅仅建立在卡辛德皇帝对尤利尔四世的收养誓言之上，而这种誓言不会延伸至其子女或孙辈。于是，元老院的议员们查阅了祖先编年史，最终在那里发现了一位更接近泰伯·塞普汀血脉的继承人：一位名叫塞弗鲁斯的诺德贵族，经元老院同意被推上王位，并得到了石头、树篱与火焰的正式接受。<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

最终，塞弗鲁斯二世被迫与安多拉克妥协，提供大赦以换取战争的结束。随着安多拉克重新归顺，篡位者的进军迅速被遏制，塞弗鲁斯二世为内省恢复了一定程度的和平：这 truly 是古代皇帝的复兴。尽管如此，许多行省领主，一如既往地反复无常，背弃了帝国，西北地区将在未来几十年里陷入持续的叛乱状态。<BR>

<BR>

三十一、尤利尔五世·塞普汀 或称 征服者<BR>

尤利尔五世于第三纪元268年登基，面临着一个充满纷争的帝国：尽管帝国人的行政和军事实力比过去一个世纪都要强大，但许多人已经对西罗帝尔的统治失去信心，人民四分五裂。尤利尔五世是一个有远见的人，他效仿古代征服者皇帝雷曼一世和泰伯·塞普汀的例子，决定实行远远超出大陆边界的军事扩张政策。通过这种方式，泰姆瑞尔的各族人民再次团结到一个共同的目标之下，这自人类诞生以来就是西罗帝尔皇帝的更高使命。<BR>

<BR>

这些征服事业，是许多诗歌的主题，将尤利尔五世和他忠诚的军团带到了帕多梅海洋彼岸遥远的阿卡维尔，在第三纪元288年，他们在那里定居于一个广大而繁荣的山谷，将帝国文化和文明带给了当地土著。帝国阿卡维尔行省在皇帝的治理下繁荣了两年。然而，这个宏伟而美好的事业并未持续下去。该领域的赛埃锡领主们很快忘记了他们在苍白关隘向雷曼皇帝发下的古老誓言，他们对皇帝的到来作出的回应是大规模集结，并在毫无预警的情况下袭击了这个初生的殖民地。尽管他的士兵付出了巨大努力，包括第十军团的英勇牺牲，皇帝还是被杀了。他陨落于异国他乡，再也不能安息于他祖先在西罗帝尔的陵墓中，那是他的家乡。<BR>

<BR>

尽管他的冒险看似徒劳，但尤利尔五世皇帝至今仍被铭记为帝国有史以来最伟大的将领和领袖之一，他是自泰伯·塞普汀本人以来第一个扩大西罗帝尔疆域的人。事实上，尤利尔的征服使许多行省统治者相信了塞普汀王朝这一分支的合法性，并毫无疑问地证明了塔洛斯的意志在帝国的心脏依然活跃而良好。<BR>

<BR>

三十二、尤利尔六世·塞普汀 或称 耐心者<BR>

当他的父亲尤利尔五世在阿卡维尔被击倒时，尤利尔六世只有五岁。自佩拉吉乌斯三世时代以来，元老院已经承担了许多责任，面对该支系往往软弱的摄政者，这实属必要。尤利尔五世恢复了皇帝唯一且无可争议权力的威严，但元老院仍不愿放弃其特权，他们已习惯于行使权力。他们只授予尤利尔五世的配偶索尼卡有限的摄政权，后来又与她合谋，进一步侵犯那些仅属于皇帝的权利的特权。<BR>

<BR>

当尤利尔六世在第三纪元307年迟迟被加冕为皇帝时，他发现这基本上是一个仪式性的角色。皇帝不满足于这种虚幻的权力，于是通过谨慎而审慎的政策，利用复杂的治理体系和许多议员薄弱的意志和头脑，着手重新夺回他的地位。仅仅六年时间，他就重新征服了泰姆瑞尔的治理权，如同他父亲征服东方诸地一样。<BR>

<BR>

三十三、莫里哈莎·塞普汀<BR>

在第三纪元313年，尤利尔六世因不幸的骑马事故过早离世，他深受爱戴、备受尊敬的妹妹莫里哈莎被加冕为泰姆瑞尔的女皇。莫里哈莎既美丽又狡猾，在她已故兄长夺回帝国大权过程中发挥了关键作用，并且现在已非常熟悉权力的运作机制。与纯粹外交型的尤利利六世不同，莫里哈莎精通言语与剑术，在她一劳永逸地清除自她祖父塞弗鲁斯二世时代以来一直持续的 simmering rebellions 的过程中，两者并用。凭借她的意志，帝国被重塑，制度和行政结构即使在最遥远、最不驯服的行省也扎下了根。<BR>

<BR>

然而，她在对付这些叛乱分子时冷静而从容的举止，最终导致了她的垮台。在第三纪元339年，莫里哈莎女皇被暗杀，后来发现这一罪行是由黑沼泽议员索里克莱斯·罗穆斯指使的，他对女皇拒绝向其管理不善的行省派遣军事援助感到愤怒。罗穆斯随即被处决，此后，任何及所有阿尔贡人被禁止进入元老院，直到有皇帝另行决定。<BR>

莫里哈莎没有在世的子女，她的妹妹艾洛伊莎四年前也已去世。王位因此传给了艾洛伊莎的独子，他被加冕为佩拉吉乌斯四世，即现任皇帝，并将担任皇帝多年！在佩拉吉乌斯四世执政的十年里，帝国得到了一种前所未有的和平与目标感：皇帝继续着莫里哈莎团结纷争各省的善政，并以公正之手打击一切反对力量。在他的指引下，法律既仁慈又严格，军团光荣而强大，通过他向九圣灵的祈求，所有收成和产业都顺利兴旺。谨以这位卑微学者的名义，并以我已故恩师豪梅·阿布塔西尔的名义，我在此谦卑地向佩拉吉乌斯四世皇帝表示感谢，感谢他对帝国的持续捍卫和仁慈治理，并感谢他委托撰写这部完整的帝王世系。<BR>

XXXIV. PELAGIUS IV SEPTIM<BR>

Emperor Pelagius IV ascended the throne in 3E 339, after the brutal and untimely end of his beloved aunt and predecessor, Morihatha. In his ascension many saw a sign of continuance and unification, as he was named Pelagius, as many of the great and wise Emperors of the original line of Septims, as as such indicated their continuing relevance.<BR>

Indeed, the Empire in its present state is more peaceful and unified than ever before, and the legacy of Pelagius IV is sure to continue a hundred years or more.<BR>

XXXV. URIEL VII SEPTIM<BR>

When in 3E 368 Pelagius IV passed on to his rightful place by the side of the Divines, the current Emperor, Uriel VII, twenty-first Emperor of the Septim dynasty, ascended the White-Gold throne. Truly, a more splendid ruler has not been seen since the days of Tiber Septim himself! In his visage, we see the keystone of this present age, which is in itself the iron foundation of an age yet to come! By the love of the Divines, may his reign continue from the present day for many an age, as may the reign of his sons! The reign of the Septims, now and forevermore!<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>

<BR>

在撰写本文时，蒙福的佩拉吉乌斯四世皇帝已经驾崩，由尤利尔七世皇帝继位。在他开明统治二十年之后，尤利尔七世皇帝慷慨地授予我，泰尔·伊曼维，出版这份关于《帝王世系》卷九：从塞弗鲁斯二世到莫里哈莎的小小附录的特权，进一步描述佩拉吉乌斯四世的生平与事迹。其中还包括尤利尔七世生平的初稿，当然，这份草稿尚未完成，因为这位学者衷心祝愿我们的皇帝未来多年身体健康。<BR>

<BR>

三十四、佩拉吉乌斯四世·塞普汀<BR>

佩拉吉乌斯四世皇帝在其敬爱的姑母兼前任莫里哈莎惨遭不测之后，于第三纪元339年登基。许多人从他的登基中看到了延续与统一的迹象，因为他被命名为佩拉吉乌斯，如同最初塞普汀世系中许多伟大而智慧的皇帝一样，这因此表明了他们的持续关联性。<BR>

<BR>

佩拉吉乌斯四世迅速继续了莫里哈莎的善政，平定了各行省，并通过在帝国优良基础设施上的巨额投资、在泰姆瑞尔各地修建良好的道路，以及建造坚固的要塞以将军团的强大之手投射到四面八方，进一步拉近了它们之间的距离。如果说有人认为佩拉吉乌斯的和平工作不如莫里哈莎那样绝对或持久，那么只需指出，前者是在后者未曾涉足的地方继续这项工作，甚至动摇了最顽固、最执拗的行省统治者。事实上，帝国目前的状态比以往任何时候都更加和平与统一，佩拉吉乌斯四世的遗产必将延续一百年或更久。<BR>

<BR>

三十五、尤利尔七世·塞普汀<BR>

在第三纪元368年，佩拉吉乌斯四世前往他应居的圣灵之侧后，现任皇帝，塞普汀王朝第二十一位皇帝尤利尔七世，登上了白金塔王座。确实，自泰伯·塞普汀本人以来，还未曾见过如此杰出的统治者！因为尤利尔七世身上结合了莫里哈莎女皇的勤勉外交、尤利尔六世皇帝的狡猾而耐心的政治敏锐度，以及尤利尔五世的军事天才和远见。<BR>

<BR>

在他统治的十年里，我们年轻的皇帝以狡猾和高尚的目标感，击败了前进道路上的任何及所有挑战，保护泰姆瑞尔免受其伤害。在他的面容中，我们看到了这个时代的拱心石，它本身就是未来时代的铁石基础！凭圣灵之爱，愿他的统治从今日起延续许多个时代，也愿他儿子们的统治同样如此！塞普汀的统治，从今往后，直至永远！<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
The Locked Cellar<BR>
By Fuchon Cire<BR>
<BR>
Upon reflection, this case is rare almost to the point of uniqueness in my experience, and so interesting on that score alone. Not often is it that thieves conspire not to simply break and enter, but break, enter, and go one step further. Though the suspect in question was not actually a thief, which only serves to heap further oddity onto this mound of the bizarre.<BR>
<BR>
The story truly began before I became involved. A lovely young Imperial woman, one Claudinia Alicarius, complained to the guard that she could no longer enter her own cellar. It seemed that the door had somehow become locked, and her key, normally placed atop a desk in her bedroom, was missing. Theft was not suspected, for Claudinia had little of value in the cellar. The guards merely searched the area outside her domicile, and did a small, brief search of the interior of her house (as not to be unduly intrusive), more or less to pacify a pretty young woman into believing they had done an adequate job.<BR>
<BR>
The key was not found. The more senior of the guard, further trying to impress Claudinia, pointed her in the direction of a reliable locksmith. The locksmith in question was an honest, hardworking Khajiit named Jotherra. Upon receiving the request, Jotherra had shortly produced a new key for Claudinia. All seemed normal, until less than a week later, the duplicated key also disappeared, apparently from the selfsame desk the original had been placed upon. The grounds were searched a second time, and neither did they yield favorable results, as was feared. The services of Jotherra were again called upon, and some wondered after Claudinia. Was she just an unreliable girl, pretty to behold, but something of a lackwit? The third such occurrence seemed to cement the image of the beautiful-but-absentminded girl in the minds of the townspeople.<BR>
<BR>

On the time of the fourth occurrence, the guards did little more than strut and pose on her property, for they were beginning to think she called them over with such frequency for the sole purpose of garnering their manly attentions. As such was not the case, she did not report the fifth, sixth, or seventh occurrences to the guard, opting instead to deal with the matter privately. Jotherra felt badly for Claudinia, for having dealt with her so often, he had begun to reckon her more of a friend than a sadly beleaguered regular customer.<BR>
<BR>
And so Jotherra saw fit to contact me. If you are unfamiliar with my personage, my name is Fuchon Cire, a Breton of some small note in trifles such as these. As it happens, Jotherra was a good friend of mine, and his insistence that Claudinia was the victim of some obscure crime piqued my interest. As my Khajiiti friend described it to me, though the cellar key was always stolen (for he had no doubt that such was the case), nothing ever seemed to be missing from it when it was finally unlocked again, and indeed, some small amount of gold was left behind to cover the cost of duplicating the key. And if the key were not stolen in the furtherance of theft, what other purpose for the crime was there?<BR>
<BR>
But as I puzzled the matter through in my mind, I realized that I was getting far too ahead of myself. Motives could best be determined after a suspect had been identified, or better yet, the guilty party be caught red-handed. Not being one to settle for speculation, I was determined to leave no dispute as to the identity of the key thief. In this, I must admit, the appearance of the young lady played no small role; though I am embarrassed to admit it, I was of the mind of taking the course that would most impress Claudinia with my prowess was the ideal one to take. Embarrassing, for it places me in more or less the same company with the guards.<BR>
<BR>
At any rate, I formulated a plan that would allow me to do just as I hoped. Under cover of darkness, I stealthily climbed up to the roof of Claudinia's house, and hid there silently throughout the day. Claudinia left the most recent duplicate key in its old familiar spot, as I had previously explained to her that my plan required said familiarity. From atop the roof, however, I could not see the door of the house, and thus could not note the identity of anyone who exited or entered illegally without giving away my position to such persons.<BR>
<BR>
Instead of using my eyes, which would necessarily mean that whomever I would note could also possibly note me, I used my mastery of mystical arts. As Claudinia left to go about her usual day's work, I cast a long-lasting spell that allows one to detect keys. Being of such duration, the spell was limited in scope, but being atop the roof it was exactly what the situation called for.<BR>
<BR>
Minutes ticked by, and I waited patiently. I knew my quarry could hardly be expected to resist the prospect of a shiny new key for any length of time. Shortly, my expectations were realized, for I sensed that the key was on the move! I wandered to the edge of the roof, and bestrode it's peak in anticipation to leap upon the criminal with the full impact of my weight.<BR>
<BR>
I saw a helmeted head walk boldly out into the street, and fell upon it with both feet. I had caught him totally unawares, and the key leapt out of his hand. Nimble as I am, I was able to retrieve it with ease whilst burying a knee into the thief's curiously armored back. Not that the thief was wearing an odd sort of armor, you understand, but it was curious in that the thief was wearing any sort of armor. The man let out a quick, surprised yelp, then threw me off his back with a powerful arm.<BR>
<BR>
As I made my landing, I drew my emergency weapon, a glass jinkblade, for surely with the sort of armor he was wearing, and my lack of same, I did not entertain the notion of a fight. Much better to stun the man, and let the guards sort him out. Imagine my surprise, then, when I finally got a good look at him, and saw that he was a guard himself! I immediately took stock of the situation: I had a blade drawn, a stolen key in hand, and was confronting a guard. Other guards could hardly fail to be unsympathetic to my cause (and with them on the scene, I would surely be sunk), and all this one had to do was either kill me outright, or kill me once in custody to silence me.<BR>
<BR>
But to my happy surprise, the fellow did not draw his own weapon, nor did he immediately shout to other guards. Instead, he sighed, and offered a most extraordinary explanation. He offered, but I declined to hear it. Though I was very curious as to his motives, it was not an explanation that was meant for me; after all, it was not my key he had stolen. Should any explanation be forthcoming, it was Claudinia's ears that should be doing the hearing.<BR>
<BR>
And so I detained the man inside the house until the evening, when Claudinia returned home. I cannot describe the look on her radiant face when she saw what I took for a rather old, otherwise nondescript guard. She dropped a basket of Kwama eggs (which I was quick to catch before it hit the floor), ran over to the man, and hugged him, tears streaming down her cheeks. The guard just stood stiffly, looking the picture of uncomfortability. Claudinia did not seem to notice the shameful look he bore.<BR>
<BR>
As it turned out, the elderly guard was Claudinia's father. As the story goes, the Alicarius family was journeying to Hammerfell by ship, when a vicious storm at sea sunk the vessel. Though Claudinia and her father both survived (her mother, three brothers, and sister sadly did not), they were rescued by different vessels, and each assumed the other dead. Mathus, her father, joined the Imperial Legion with a death wish in mind. After losing his family, life held little meaning for the man, and so he often took grave, unnecessary risks. While highly regarded by his fellows (who soon became his subordinates), he could not get past his failure to protect those closest to him.<BR>
<BR>
Years passed, and a certain member of the Blades who counted Mathus among his friends acquired a ship's journal from a raided pirate vessel. The log contained a very exacting account of a certain survivor of a certain wreck, and, knowing the import of the document, saw fit to put it in Mathus's hands. Mathus, of course, was overwhelmed. He dedicated the next few years to tracking down the various leads that eventually led him to his daughter. Once he knew where she resided, he immediately put in for a transfer.<BR>
<BR>
But he was horribly burdened by his sense of responsibility for the tragedy that befallen his family. Finally seeing Claudinia for the first time in years, he could not bear to allow her fair ears to hear his unworthy apologies. He was, he thought, a worthless man who had already failed her in the deepest way possible. Because he did not talk to her immediately, his self-loathing grew; he thought himself a coward on top of everything else.<BR>
<BR>
He had stolen the keys so that he could sneak into the cellar at night, and be close to his beloved daughter. To his way of thinking, it was as close as such a loathsome creature as himself should get to her. He locked the door again behind him so that no one would intrude on his very private misery.<BR>
<BR>
In the end, Claudinia did not blame him for the accident, as any sensible person would not. She also had a difficult time grasping her father's sense of profound failure. But ultimately, both were simply grateful to be truly reunited. And even though all I did was track down some stolen keys for her, part of me hoped that I succeeded in leaving a good impression. <BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
上锁的地窖<BR>
富雄·西尔 著<BR>
<BR>
回想起来，这个案子在我经历中罕见得近乎独特，仅凭这一点就非常有趣。窃贼们合谋的目的不仅仅是破门侵入，而是破门、侵入，然后更进一步，这种情况并不常见。尽管涉案的嫌疑人实际上并非窃贼，这只会为这堆离奇之事增添更多怪异。<BR>
<BR>
故事其实在我介入之前就开始了。一位可爱的年轻帝国女性，名叫克劳迪尼娅·阿利卡里乌斯，向守卫抱怨说她再也进不了自己的地窖了。似乎门不知何故被锁上了，而她通常放在卧室书桌上的钥匙也不见了。没有怀疑是盗窃，因为克劳迪尼娅的地窖里没什么值钱东西。守卫们只是搜查了她住所外的区域，并对她房屋内部进行了简短的小范围搜查（以免过于侵扰），或多或少是为了安抚这位年轻漂亮的女士，让她相信他们已经尽职尽责了。<BR>
<BR>
钥匙没找到。更资深的那位守卫，为了进一步给克劳迪尼娅留下好印象，指引她去找一位可靠的锁匠。那位锁匠是个诚实勤劳的卡吉特，名叫乔瑟拉。接到请求后，乔瑟拉很快就为克劳迪尼娅配了一把新钥匙。一切似乎正常，直到不到一周后，那把复制的钥匙也消失了，显然是从原钥匙存放的同一张书桌上不见的。场地被第二次搜查，但也没有取得预期的结果。乔瑟拉的服务再次被求助，有些人开始对克劳迪尼娅议论纷纷。她只是一个不可靠的女孩，长得漂亮，但有点傻？第三次此类事件似乎巩固了镇民们心中这位美丽但心不在焉的女孩形象。<BR>
<BR>

到第四次事件发生时，守卫们在她家做的不过是摆摆架子，因为他们开始认为她这么频繁地叫他们来，纯粹是为了吸引他们男性的注意。既然情况并非如此，她就没有向守卫报告第五、第六或第七次事件，而是选择私下处理。乔瑟拉为克劳迪尼娅感到难过，因为经常与她打交道，他开始把她更多地视为朋友，而不是一个可悲的、麻烦缠身的常客。<BR>
<BR>
于是，乔瑟拉觉得联系我是合适的。如果你不熟悉我，我叫富雄·西尔，一个在这类琐事上小有名气的布莱顿人。碰巧，乔瑟拉是我的好朋友，他坚持认为克劳迪尼娅是某起隐秘犯罪的受害者，这激起了我的兴趣。据我的卡吉特朋友描述，虽然地窖钥匙总是被偷（他毫不怀疑这一点），但当地窖最终再次被打开时，里面似乎从未丢失任何东西，而且，还会留下一点金币来支付配钥匙的费用。如果钥匙不是为了偷东西而被偷，那这犯罪还有什么别的目的呢？<BR>
<BR>
但当我在脑中思考这个问题时，我意识到我太心急了。动机最好在嫌疑人被确认之后，或者更好的情况是，在有罪方被当场抓住之后来确定。我不是一个满足于猜测的人，我决心对钥匙小偷的身份不留任何争议。在此，我必须承认，那位年轻女士的外表起了不小的作用；尽管我羞于承认，但我当时的想法是，采取最能以我的能力给克劳迪尼娅留下深刻印象的路线才是理想的。这很尴尬，因为它让我或多或少地与那些守卫为伍了。<BR>
<BR>
无论如何，我制定了一个计划，让我能够如愿以偿。趁着夜色，我偷偷爬上克劳迪尼娅家的屋顶，在那里静静地躲了一整天。克劳迪尼娅把最新的复制钥匙放在老地方，因为我事先向她解释过，我的计划需要这种熟悉度。然而，从屋顶上，我看不到房子的门，因此无法在不暴露自己位置的情况下，注意到任何非法进出者的身份。<BR>
<BR>
我没有用眼睛，因为那意味着我能注意到的人也可能注意到我，而是运用了我对神秘艺术的掌握。当克劳迪尼娅离开去进行她日常的工作时，我施放了一个持续时间很长的探测钥匙法术。由于持续时间长，该法术的范围有限，但身处屋顶，这正是情况所需。<BR>
<BR>
几分钟过去了，我耐心地等待着。我知道我的目标很难抗拒一把闪亮新钥匙的前景太久。很快，我的期望实现了，因为我感觉到钥匙在移动！我走到屋顶边缘，跨坐在屋脊上，准备用我全身的重量扑向罪犯。<BR>
<BR>
我看到一个戴着头盔的脑袋大胆地走到街上，便双脚朝下扑了上去。我完全出其不意地抓住了他，钥匙从他手中飞了出去。我身手敏捷，轻松地取回了钥匙，同时用膝盖顶住了小偷那身奇怪盔甲的后背。并非说小偷穿着奇怪的盔甲，你明白，而是奇怪在于小偷竟然穿着盔甲。那人发出一声短促、惊讶的叫声，然后用有力的手臂把我从他背上甩了下来。<BR>
<BR>
当我落地时，我拔出了我的应急武器，一把玻璃吉克刀，因为考虑到他穿的盔甲，而我没有，我并没有和他打一架的念头。最好是把那人打晕，让守卫们来处理。可以想象，当我终于看清他的样子，发现他本人就是一个守卫时，我有多么惊讶！我立刻评估了形势：我拔出了刀，手里拿着被偷的钥匙，正在与一个守卫对峙。其他守卫很难对我的处境表示同情（如果他们到场，我肯定会完蛋），而眼前这个守卫所要做的，要么是直接杀死我，要么是在拘留我之后再杀死我以让我闭嘴。<BR>
<BR>
但令我惊喜的是，那家伙并没有拔出自己的武器，也没有立即向其他守卫喊叫。相反，他叹了口气，给出了一个最不寻常的解释。他解释了，但我拒绝听。尽管我对他的动机非常好奇，但那并不是针对我的解释；毕竟，他偷的不是我的钥匙。如果真要有什么解释，那也该是克劳迪尼娅的耳朵来听。<BR>
<BR>
于是我把那人扣在房子里，直到晚上克劳迪尼娅回家。当她看到我认为相当年长、其他方面毫无特色的守卫时，她容光焕发的脸上露出的表情我无法形容。她掉了一篮夸蚂卵（我赶紧在落地前接住），跑向那人，拥抱了他，泪水顺着脸颊流下。那守卫只是僵硬地站着，一脸不自在。克劳迪尼娅似乎没有注意到他脸上羞愧的表情。<BR>
<BR>
原来，那位年长的守卫是克劳迪尼娅的父亲。故事是这样的：阿利卡里乌斯一家乘船前往落锤，途中一场猛烈的海上风暴击沉了船只。尽管克劳迪尼娅和她的父亲都幸存了下来（她的母亲、三个兄弟和妹妹不幸遇难），他们被不同的船只救起，彼此都以为对方死了。她的父亲马苏斯加入了帝国军团，心里怀着求死的愿望。失去家人后，生活对这个男人来说几乎毫无意义，因此他常常冒着重大的、不必要的风险。尽管他深受同袍（他们很快成了他的下属）的敬重，但他无法释怀自己未能保护最亲近的人。<BR>
<BR>
几年过去了，一位与马苏斯有交情的刀锋成员从一艘被袭击的海盗船上获得了一本航海日志。日志中包含了对某次沉船事故中某位幸存者的非常详尽的描述，他深知这份文件的重要性，便决定将其交到马苏斯手中。马苏斯自然激动不已。在接下来的几年里，他致力于追查各种线索，最终找到了他的女儿。一旦知道她住在哪里，他立刻申请了调职。<BR>
<BR>
但他被对降临在家人身上的悲剧的责任感所深深折磨。多年后终于见到克劳迪尼娅，他不忍让她那美好的耳朵听到他不配的道歉。他认为自己是个一无是处的男人，已经以最深刻的方式辜负了她。因为他没有立即和她说话，他的自我厌恶与日俱增；他觉得自己除了其他缺点外，还是个懦夫。<BR>
<BR>
他偷钥匙是为了能在晚上偷偷溜进地窖，靠近他心爱的女儿。在他的想法里，像他这样可憎的生物，能离她这么近就已经是极限了。他离开时又把门锁上，以免有人打扰他那非常私密的痛苦。<BR>
<BR>
最后，克劳迪尼娅没有责怪他造成的事故，任何明智的人都不会。她也很难理解父亲那种深刻的失败感。但最终，两人都只是感激能够真正重聚。尽管我所做的只是为她追踪到一些被偷的钥匙，但我心里仍希望，我成功给她留下了好印象。<BR>

Lost and Found in the Reach<BR>
by Edreard Rodore<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
East of Wayrest's nustling harbors and beyond the towers of Evermore, the hilltops and mesas of the Reach conceal mysteries and magicks to befuddle even the most enlightened academic minds. In my careless youth, when the West's magic orders seemed to me restrictive and unyielding, I set off into these highlands seeking knowledge of a wilder kind.<BR>
<BR>
But the Reach is a savage place, bereft of the comforts and common faculties of home and hearth. I traveled long, weary of foot and heart, before stumbling upon my first grand discovery: a mighty elven citadel, forgotten and crumbling atop a mesa of grey stone. I explored its depths, battling strange otherwordly beasts and ferocious local creatures. In the ruin's deepest catacombs, I uncovered a trove of lost elven treasure more magnificent than anything I had set eyes upon in all my years. But I lamented disturbing such a site, and despaired at the idea that my hands should be the ones to sully its glory. So I departed in peace, and kept the secrets of the citadel to myself.<BR>
<BR>

A shaman-mage of significant talent, Ancrial's view of magic was unlike anything I had learned in the stuffy guildhalls of High Rock. To Ancrial, magic was not a science to be studied in a laboratory, but a force alive within every tree and rock and cloud. I remember with distinction a spell Ancrial called "Marrelaeth", which when cast encased my companion in an envelope of powerful warding magic, repelling the most terrible dangers of spell and sword alike.<BR>

Eleven feet tall and bristling with ferocity and rage, the great beast and I traded deadly blows in a brisk twilight, before I hoodwinked the brute into a misstep that sent him careening off a cliff into the valley below. I did not linger to ensure his demise.<BR>
<BR>
It was long months before I found myself in civilization again, in a sprawling trade-town called Karthwasten. Though its streetlamps and road-cobbles reminded me dimly of home, I felt no longing, at least for the great cities of the West. No, when I came back to the city, it was the wilds that called to me, bidding me set off once more into the misty ravines and craggy highlands I had so come to love.<BR>"""

<BR>

<BR>
过了好几个月，我才再次发现自己身处文明世界，在一个叫做卡斯瓦斯滕的广阔贸易小镇。尽管它的街灯和路面石板让我隐约想起了家乡，但我并不感到怀念，至少不怀念西方的大城市。不，当我回到城市时，是荒野在召唤我，让我再次出发，进入我如此热爱的雾霭峡谷和崎岖高地。<BR>"""

The Legend of Lover's Lament<BR>

The night is very dark. Wind gently ruffles the willow trees. All is quiet, or it so appears, around the shores of the small lake. Tamriel's moons reflect in the slightly rippling surface of the water. An owl's questioning call echoes. No lights are shining from the castle nearby; it appears deserted.<BR><BR>
As the night wears on and the planet's satellites moves across the heavens, a faint glow appears near the castle. The light slowly moves towards the lake, and upon reaching the shore, stops. A figure, a beautiful woman by any measure, stands looking wistfully into the dark water. Her lantern flickers in the breeze, and illuminates her. Tears are streaming down her cheeks; her gown, once beautiful, is now tattered and stained.<BR><BR>
The surface of the lake becomes agitated, but not from a wind as the night has become as still as it is dark. Slowly from the water emerges the figure of a man, a warrior, fully adorned in the armor of a knight on the field of battle. He seems to float over the water towards the woman and stop just short of her.<BR><BR>
"Madylina," the ghostly warrior intones.<BR><BR>
"My Lord, Gerthland," whispers the lovely Madylina as she kneels. "You have come to me again."<BR><BR>
"Yes," Gerthland responds, "My days are long waiting for the night in which I can see my love."<BR><BR>
The lovers stand looking wistfully at each other, unable to touch, unable to kiss, unable to satisfy their unrequited love until the first tinges of dawn start to color the western sky. Gerthland drops something to the ground as does Madylina as each depart. The waters of the lake again take possession of the handsome knight and the beautiful maiden walks slowly back to the castle. As the waters of the lake settle into a gentle ripple and the light of Madylina's lantern disappears, dawn breaks over the lake. 
On the shore are two beautiful roses--one crimson and the other white as fresh cream. Ripples from the lake overtake the two flowers and pull them into the lake leaving the shore bare as it was in the hours before darkness fell.<BR><BR>

The townfolk around Gerthland Manor tell often of seeing these lovers in their nightly meeting. The Boar's Bristle Inn is always rumbling with conversation about them. Lord Gerthland and Lady Madylina who were betrothed. Lord Gerthland called to battle to defend the land. Hergen, the castle's resident sorcerer, becoming enflamed with love and lust for Madylina only to be rebuked by her. Lord Gerthland's death on the field of battle. Lady Madylina's death by her own hand at the news. Hergen's curse on both their souls that will not allow them to rest until Madylina will agree to become Hergen's consort even in death.<BR><BR>
Hergen, to this day, wanders the deserted halls of Gerthland Manor hoping that Madylina will agree to his demands. And the lovers continue to meet for a few moments each night on the shores of the lake now known as Lover's Lament.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
恋人哀歌传说<BR>
克罗尔·鲍莫瓦尔 著<BR><BR>

湖面变得动荡，但并非因为风，因为夜晚已如黑暗般寂静。一个男人的身影缓缓从水中浮现，一名战士，身着战场上骑士的全套盔甲。他仿佛漂浮在水面上向女子靠近，在离她咫尺之遥的地方停下。<BR><BR>
“玛迪莉娜，”幽灵般的战士吟诵道。<BR><BR>
“我的大人，格特兰，”可爱的玛迪莉娜跪下，低声说道。“你又来看我了。”<BR><BR>
“是的，”格特兰回答，“我白天的时光漫长，都在等待能看到我爱人的夜晚。”<BR><BR>
恋人们站着，惆怅地彼此对视，无法触碰，无法亲吻，无法满足他们无法回报的爱，直到第一抹曙光开始染上西方的天空。格特兰和玛迪莉娜在各自离开时都往地上扔了什么东西。湖水的波浪再次吞没了英俊的骑士，美丽的少女缓缓走回城堡。当湖水的波浪平息为轻柔的涟漪，玛迪莉娜提灯的光消失时，黎明在湖面降临。
岸边有两朵美丽的玫瑰 -- 一朵深红，另一朵洁白如鲜奶油。湖水的涟漪淹没了这两朵花，将它们卷入湖中，留下光秃秃的岸边，如同黑暗降临前的几个小时一样。<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><BR>
* * *<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
格特兰庄园周围的镇民经常谈论在夜间会面中看到这对恋人。野猪鬃客栈总是因关于他们的谈话而嗡嗡作响。格特兰大人与玛迪莉娜小姐曾订婚。格特兰大人被召唤参战保卫家园。城堡的常住巫师赫尔根，对玛迪莉娜燃起了爱欲之火，却遭到她的拒绝。格特兰大人在战场上阵亡。玛迪莉娜小姐闻讯后自尽。赫尔根对他们两人的灵魂施加了诅咒，除非玛迪莉娜同意即使在死后也成为赫尔根的配偶，否则他们不得安息。<BR><BR>
直到今天，赫尔根仍在格特兰庄园空荡荡的大厅里游荡，希望玛迪莉娜能同意他的要求。而这对恋人，每晚仍在现在被称为“恋人哀歌”的湖岸边短暂相会。<BR>"""

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
夜色深沉。微风轻拂柳树。小湖的岸边一片寂静，或者说看上去如此。泰姆瑞尔的月亮倒映在微微荡漾的水面上。猫头鹰的鸣叫声回响。附近的城堡没有灯光闪烁；它看起来空无一人。<BR><BR>
随着夜色渐深，行星的卫星划过天空，城堡附近出现了一道微弱的光芒。那光缓缓移向湖边，到达岸边后停了下来。一个身影，无论如何都是位美丽的女子，站在那里，惆怅地望着黑暗的水面。她的提灯在微风中摇曳，照亮了她。泪水顺着她的脸颊流下；她的长裙，曾经美丽，如今已破烂污损。<BR><BR>
湖面变得动荡，但并非因为风，因为夜晚已如黑暗般寂静。一个男人的身影缓缓从水中浮现，一名战士，身着战场上骑士的全套盔甲。他仿佛漂浮在水面上向女子靠近，在离她咫尺之遥的地方停下。<BR><BR>
“玛迪莉娜，”幽灵般的战士吟诵道。<BR><BR>
“我的大人，格特兰，”可爱的玛迪莉娜跪下，低声说道。“你又来看我了。”<BR><BR>
“是的，”格特兰回答，“我白天的时光漫长，都在等待能看到我爱人的夜晚。”<BR><BR>
恋人们站着，惆怅地彼此对视，无法触碰，无法亲吻，无法满足他们无法回报的爱，直到第一抹曙光开始染上西方的天空。格特兰和玛迪莉娜在各自离开时都往地上扔了什么东西。湖水的波浪再次吞没了英俊的骑士，美丽的少女缓缓走回城堡。当湖水的波浪平息为轻柔的涟漪，玛迪莉娜提灯的光消失时，黎明在湖面降临。
岸边有两朵美丽的玫瑰 -- 一朵深红，另一朵洁白如鲜奶油。湖水的涟漪淹没了这两朵花，将它们卷入湖中，留下光秃秃的岸边，如同黑暗降临前的几个小时一样。<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><BR>
* * *<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
格特兰庄园周围的镇民经常谈论在夜间会面中看到这对恋人。野猪鬃客栈总是因关于他们的谈话而嗡嗡作响。格特兰大人与玛迪莉娜小姐曾订婚。格特兰大人被召唤参战保卫家园。城堡的常住巫师赫尔根，对玛迪莉娜燃起了爱欲之火，却遭到她的拒绝。格特兰大人在战场上阵亡。玛迪莉娜小姐闻讯后自尽。赫尔根对他们两人的灵魂施加了诅咒，除非玛迪莉娜同意即使在死后也成为赫尔根的配偶，否则他们不得安息。<BR><BR>
直到今天，赫尔根仍在格特兰庄园空荡荡的大厅里游荡，希望玛迪莉娜能同意他的要求。而这对恋人，每晚仍在现在被称为“恋人哀歌”的湖岸边短暂相会。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Ius, Animal God<BR>
By Buljursoma<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
The statues one sees throughout Valenwood and parts of Hammerfell and Elsweyr that seem to be of a misshapen humanoid carrying a rod are of Ius, The God of Animals.<BR><BR>
The rod He carries has its origin in the tale of The Ox and The Evil Farmer. It seems that one day an evil farmer decided to kill all of his animals and have a big party. As The story unfolds, animal after animal is killed and prepared for a big meal. Lastly the farmer comes to the ox and prepares to slit its throat. The ox, not wishing to be anybody's dinner, prayed very vocally to Ius. This came out as a loud Moo, of course.<BR><BR>
At that very instant Ius appeared carrying a rather large set of balance weights. Without explanation, Ius ate the farmer and vanished. Ever since that day Ius The Extremely Agitated, has always been portrayed as carrying a large set of scales with him. The local Ius worshippers have no idea why and do not seem to care. Although this story has been called fanciful at best, I personally know a racoon who had actually talked to The Ox. That is, before the Ox became filler for the local inn's larder. 
I do not have any information one way or the other about the validity of this second myth. It is, however, quite traditional.<BR><BR>
It seems that many, many years ago, before the reign of Uriel Septim VII, before the reign of Cephorus Septim II, yes, even before the age of Pelagius Septim III (long may his name be praised!), there lived a wombat who was the pet of Lady Greelina, daughter of the Lord Prufrock of Rockcreek. Lady Greelina loved her wombat so, and it loved her too with all the passionate intensity a marsupial can muster.<BR><BR>
Unfortunately, it was a time of great sorrow in Rockcreek. A pestilence had come through the town, destroying all their cash crops (which consisted of raspberries and a few scraggly odd weeds that caused Argonian women to look very attractive to those who partook); Then a plague had come, inflicting nearly every cobbler with chronic hiccoughs; finally a witch had cursed the townspeople so the only words any could utter were "Hmmm. Precisely." All the businesses, stores, and guilds fled from the town faster than an extremely fast thing.<BR><BR>
Lady Greelina saw her father despairing the loss the town was suffering, so she brought her wombat in and told him, "Father, my wombat can save us all, for it is sacred to the god Ius, God of Animals. The only reason I didn't tell you earlier is because I am an early adolescent going through that period when I don't like to communicate. But please, ask a wish of my wombat, and Ius will fulfill it, for my wombat loves me."<BR><BR>
The king thought this was fairly flakey, but he had nothing to lose so he uttered a modest wish to the wombat, "All I want is for one business to come to Rockcreek that will never leave no matter the calamity."<BR><BR>
I probably should have mentioned before that the king had always been cruel to the wombat (he used to lick it and try to make it stick to walls), so the wombat had Ius create an equipment store in front of the palace gate that would never go away. The royal family ended up going mad and eating one another (and ironically, the wombat was one of the first to go). But that is why there is to this day an equipment store blocking the palace gate in Rockcreek. If you don't believe me, go there and see.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
尤斯，动物之神<BR>
布尔朱尔索玛 著<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
在整个瓦伦伍德以及落锤和艾斯维尔的部分地区，人们可以看到一些雕像，看起来像是拿着棍棒的畸形人形，它们就是动物之神尤斯。<BR><BR>
他手中的棍棒起源于《公牛与邪恶农夫》的故事。似乎有一天，一个邪恶的农夫决定杀死他所有的动物，举行一场盛大的派对。随着故事的展开，一只又一只动物被杀，准备做成大餐。最后，农夫来到公牛面前，准备割开它的喉咙。公牛不想成为任何人的盘中餐，便非常大声地向尤斯祈祷。当然，这祈祷化作了一声响亮的“哞”。<BR><BR>
就在那一刻，尤斯出现了，带着一副相当大的天平。尤斯二话没说，吃掉了农夫，然后消失了。从那天起，“极度激动的尤斯”总是被描绘成随身带着一副大天平。当地的尤斯崇拜者不知道原因，似乎也不在乎。尽管这个故事最多只能说是异想天开，但我个人认识一只浣熊，它实际上和那头公牛说过话。当然，那是在公牛成为当地客栈储藏室的填充物之前。
关于这第二个神话的真实性，我没有任何信息可以支持或反驳。然而，它却相当传统。<BR><BR>
似乎很多很多年前，在尤利尔·塞普汀七世统治之前，在塞弗鲁斯·塞普汀二世统治之前，是的，甚至在佩拉吉乌斯·塞普汀三世（愿他的名字永受赞美！）的时代之前，有一只袋熊，它是岩溪镇普鲁弗洛克勋爵的女儿格瑞莉娜女士的宠物。格瑞莉娜女士非常爱她的袋熊，袋熊也以一只有袋动物所能激发的全部热情爱着她。<BR><BR>
不幸的是，那是岩溪镇充满悲伤的时期。一场瘟疫席卷了小镇，摧毁了他们所有的经济作物（包括覆盆子和一些稀稀拉拉的奇怪杂草，这些杂草会让阿尔贡女性对服用者变得极具吸引力）；然后一场疾病降临，几乎让每个补鞋匠都患上了慢性打嗝；最后，一个女巫诅咒了镇民，使得他们唯一能说出的话就是“嗯。正是。”所有的商业、商店和公会都以比极快之物还要快的速度逃离了小镇。<BR><BR>
格瑞莉娜女士看到父亲为小镇遭受的损失而绝望，于是她把袋熊带进来，告诉他：“父亲，我的袋熊能拯救我们所有人，因为它对动物之神尤斯来说是神圣的。我之前没告诉您的唯一原因，是我正处于不喜欢交流的青春期初期。但是，请向我的袋熊许个愿吧，尤斯会实现的，因为我的袋熊爱我。”<BR><BR>
国王认为这相当不靠谱，但他也没什么可失去的，于是他对袋熊许了一个 modest 的愿望：“我只希望有一家企业能来到岩溪镇，无论发生什么灾难都不会离开。”<BR><BR>
我可能之前应该提到，国王一直对袋熊很残忍（他过去常常舔它，并试图把它粘在墙上），所以袋熊让尤斯在宫门前创建了一家永远不会消失的装备店。王室最终发疯，互相吞噬（讽刺的是，袋熊是最早被吃掉的一个）。但这也就是为什么直到今天，岩溪镇还有一家装备店堵在宫门前。如果你不信，自己去那里看看。<BR>"""

<BR>

<BR> 
Knowing that he would be devoured or worse, Lyrisius pulled the blade and then leapt from the back of the flying wyrm. Indeed, the foul monster had intended to slay the hero. The wyrm pursued the plummeting Lyrisius. Boethiah appeared beside the falling hero. Praising him for ultimately destroying the army of Akavir, she turned him into a raven. Lyrisius quickly lost the wyrm in the clouds.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Mace Etiquette<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Warriors sometimes make the mistake of thinking that there are no tactics with a mace. They assume that the sword is all about skill and the mace is only about strength and stamina. As a veteran instructor of mace tactics, I can tell you they are wrong.<BR>
<BR>
Wielding a mace properly is all about timing and momentum. Once the swing of the mace has begun, stopping it or slowing it down is difficult. The fighter is committed to not just the blow, but also the recoil. Begin your strike when the opponent is leaning forward, hopefully off balance. It is completely predictable that he will lean backward, so aim for a point behind his head. By the time the mace gets there, his head will be in its path.<BR>
<BR>
The mace should be held at the ready, shoulder high. The windup should not extend past the shoulders by more than a hand's width. When swinging, lead with the elbow. As the elbow passes the height of your collarbone, extend the forearm like a whip. The extra momentum will drive the mace faster and harder, causing far more damage.<BR>
<BR>
At the moment of impact, let the wrist loosen. The mace will bounce and hurt a stiff wrist. Allow the recoil of the blow to drive the mace back into the ready position, thereby preparing the warrior for a quicker second strike.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
钉头锤礼仪<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
战士们有时会错误地认为使用钉头锤毫无战术可言。他们以为剑全靠技巧，而钉头锤只关乎力量和耐力。作为一名经验丰富的钉头锤战术教官，我可以告诉你，他们错了。<BR>
<BR>
正确挥舞钉头锤的关键在于时机和动量。一旦钉头锤开始挥动，就很难停止或减慢。战士不仅要承受打击，还要承受反弹。在对手前倾、可能失去平衡时开始你的攻击。完全可以预料他会后仰，所以瞄准他头部后方的一点。当钉头锤到达那里时，他的头会正好在路径上。<BR>
<BR>
钉头锤应准备就绪，举至肩高。蓄力挥动时，不应超过肩宽一掌的距离。挥动时，用肘部引领。当肘部超过锁骨高度时，像鞭子一样伸展前臂。额外的动量将使钉头锤更快、更猛地击出，造成更大的伤害。<BR>
<BR>
在撞击的瞬间，放松手腕。钉头锤会反弹，僵硬的手腕会受伤。让打击的反弹力将钉头锤带回到准备位置，从而使战士能够更快地发起第二次攻击。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Magic from the Sky<BR>
by Irlav Jarol<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The ancient Ayleids believed that Nirn was composed of four basic elements -- earth, water, air, and light -- and of these four elements, they believed the most sublime form of light was star light. The stars are our links to the plane of Aetherius, the source of all magical power, and therefore, light from the stars is the most potent and exalted of all magical powers.<BR>
<BR>
From time to time, fragments of Aetherius fall from the heavens. The people know these fragments as 'shooting stars', and from time to time, such Aetherial fragments are found on Nirn. The most common varieties are known as 'meteoric iron'; this metal is prized by armorers and enchanters for its properties in the forging of enchanted weapons and armors. This meteoric iron is also the primary component in 'Ayleid Wells,' ancient enchanted artifacts found throughout Cyrodiil.<BR>
<BR>
Another, rarer form of Aetherial fragment is called 'meteoric glass'. It is from such fragments that other rare Ayleid enchanted artifacts are crafted -- Welkynd Stones and Varla Stones.<BR>
<BR>
Ayleids Wells are scattered across Cyrodiil's landscape. Their siting is a mystery; they are not associated with any known Ayleid cities or settlements. It is presumed that, in some manner, they harvest magical power from starlight. It is also suggested, without evidence or support, that they are located at the meeting points of ancient lines of magical power; however, modern arcane arts have discovered no perceptible evidence of such lines of power.<BR>
<BR>
Those with magical talents can draw magicka from Ayleid wells to restore their own reservoirs of magical power. No ritual or arcane knowledge is necessary, suggesting that these wells were designed to serve persons not skilled in the magical arts. Once drained, the wells replenish again only at magical midnight. Once recharged, they appear to radiate magical power back into the sky, which prompts some to theorize they are also objects with religious or magical ritual significance -- perhaps a means of offering magic back to the heavens.<BR>
<BR>
Welkynd Stones [Aldmeris - "sky stone," "heaven stone"; literally, "sky child"] are pieces of cut and enchanted meteoric glass which apparently act as storage devices for magical power. A magical talent can restore his reservoirs of magicka from such stones. Alas, the means of restoring power to these stones may have been lost with the Ayleids. Currently, these objects simply crumble to dust after they have been used.<BR>
<BR>
Great Welkynd Stones are exceptionally large pieces of enchanted meteoric glass. Scholars believe that at the heart of each ancient Ayleid city, a Great Welkynd Stone was the source of the settlement's magical enchantments. It may be that these great stones were linked to the lesser stones, restoring and maintaining their power. In any case, research on these Great Welkynd Stones is impossible, since all the known Ayleid ruins have been looted of their great stones, and no examples of these great stones are known to survive.<BR>
<BR>
Another rare enchanted item found in Ayleid ruins is called a Varla Stone [Aldmeris - "star stone"]. Varla Stones are remarkably powerful, enabling untrained users to restore magical energy to any number of enchanted items. Because of their great value and utility, these items are also extremely rare, but since they are small and easily concealed, diligent explorers may still occasionally come across them in any Ayleid ruin.<BR>
<BR>
Ayleid Wells. Welkynd Stones. Varla Stones. Consider, then, these marvels of magical enchantment. Are we then to conclude that the Ayleids were a superior race and culture? Did they so exceed us in art and craft that they mock the feeble powers of Third Era Wizards?<BR>
<BR>
Never! The Ayleids were powerful, yes, and cunning, but they were neither good nor wise, and so they were struck down. Their works have passed from Nirn, save these rare and sparkling treasures. Their ancient cities are dark and empty, save for the grim revenants and restless spirits condemned forever to walk the halls, keeping their melancholy vigils over bones and dust.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
天际魔法<BR>
伊尔拉夫·贾罗尔 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
古代亚历德人认为，奈恩由四种基本元素组成 -- 土、水、气、光 -- 在这四种元素中，他们认为最崇高的光的形式是星光。星辰是我们与光界位面的联系，光界是所有魔法力量的源泉，因此，星光是最强大、最崇高的魔法力量。<BR>

<BR>
亚历德之井散布在西罗帝尔的各处。它们的位置是个谜；它们与任何已知的亚历德城市或定居点无关。据推测，它们以某种方式从星光中汲取魔法力量。也有人提出，毫无证据支持，它们位于古老魔法线的交汇点；然而，现代奥术技艺并未发现这种力量线的可感知证据。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
维尔金石 [古奥德莫语 - “天空之石”，“天堂之石”；字面意为“天空之子”] 是经过切割和附魔的陨璃碎片，显然充当着魔法力量的存储装置。有魔法天赋的人可以从这些石头中补充自己的魔能储备。唉，为这些石头补充能量的方法可能已经随亚历德人失传了。目前，这些物品在使用后只会化为尘土。<BR>
<BR>
大型维尔金石是特别大的附魔陨璃碎片。学者们认为，在每个古老亚历德城市的心脏地带，都有一块大型维尔金石作为该定居点魔法附魔的源头。也许这些大型石头与较小的石头相连，恢复并维持着它们的能量。无论如何，对这些大型维尔金石的研究是不可能的，因为所有已知的亚历德废墟中的大型石头都已被洗劫一空，并且没有已知的此类大型石头样本幸存下来。<BR>
<BR>
在亚历德废墟中发现的另一种稀有附魔物品被称为瓦拉石 [古奥德莫语 - “星之石”]。瓦拉石非常强大，能使未经训练的使用者为任意数量的附魔物品恢复魔法能量。由于其巨大的价值和实用性，这些物品也极其稀有，但由于它们体积小、易于隐藏，勤奋的探险者可能仍会在任何亚历德废墟中偶尔发现它们。<BR>
<BR>
亚历德之井。维尔金石。瓦拉石。那么，想想这些附魔的奇迹吧。我们是否因此得出结论，亚历德人是更优越的种族和文化？他们在艺术和工艺上如此超越我们，以至于嘲弄了第三纪元巫师们微弱的力量吗？<BR>
<BR>
绝非如此！亚历德人确实强大，也狡猾，但他们既不善良也不明智，因此被击倒了。他们的作品已从奈恩消失，除了这些稀有而闪耀的珍宝。他们的古老城市黑暗而空旷，除了那些可怕的亡灵和永世不得安息的灵魂，注定要在厅堂中游荡，在骸骨与尘埃之上进行着悲伤的守望。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
A Kit's Primer: The Magicka of a Moons Dancer<BR>
Adapted from a lecture of a Dagi-Raht Master,<BR>
Temple of Two-Moons Dance, Torval<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
First comes the mastery of the breath. If one cannot breathe, one cannot live: this is obvious. Managing the breath is akin to managing one's strength. Each breath flows through the body as power; so, a Moons Dancer must learn how to control his breath before he can control anything else.<BR>
<BR>
Next comes the mastery of the body. While we are on this earth, our bodies, souls, and minds are bound together as one; what affects one will affect the other. A neglected body leads to a neglected mind or soul, and vice versa. As even the most mindless of Rhojiit display strength and skill in launching their weight and manipulating their limbs, this is what is taught to kits second, as the second-most natural control they can grasp in this life.<BR>
<BR>
The mastery of the body lies in two main spheres, often thought a dichotomy, but in reality any master may possess both. The first of these is raw strength: the ability to jump high, run fast and long, lift and carry heavy burdens. The second is agility: the flex of the tendons, the coordination of the eye, speed of striking, and grace of movement.<BR>
<BR>
These two spheres interlock, and thus comes the third mastery: technique. A Khajiit's body is made in such a way that some sequences of movement are easier, and some strikes are more powerful when given the proper leverage. An example is the Ohmes fist-fighters: the rotation of their shoulders and hips lends to stronger punches when a left punch is followed by a right, the energy of the recoil gathered and released into the next strike, like a serpent's coil.<BR>
<BR>
Technique, then, is the doorway to shaping Magicka. Magicka is in everything. The rightness one feels in finding the proper rhythm in their techniques is reflected in the flow and efficiency of one's Magicka. Kits at this stage of training should be able to feel the animus energy in their movements, and further conserve or release this animus in order to give more power to their strikes or absorb more force when deflecting a blow.<BR>
<BR>
From here comes the fourth and last mastery, Magicka itself. A kit next learns to invite the animus of their techniques to transcend their mortal form and become raw energy. This is not a divorce of the energies latent in one's body as an Altmer would cast spells, but instead the ultimate channeling of it, through movement. A spell cast with proper breathing, physical conditioning, and technique is hence always more powerful than that merely conceived of in the mind, though a wise master will of course also learn still and silent spells for use against cunning foes.<BR>
<BR>
After a kit learns to augment their martial training with Magicka, more varied teachings may avail them, such as stealing or replenishing another's life force, twisting the fabric of light or substance of rock or air to create a more favorable arena, scenting the tracks of spirits for spiritual guidance, or shaping the raw energies of fire, frost, and lightning. Though one must demonstrate restraint or have the guidance of a master, moon sugar can also be used as an enhancement, as the practitioner is in essence ingesting the animus of the moons and making it their own.<BR>
<BR>
A Khajiit master trains in all four of these masteries and knows neither of them are greater than any other, that each is susceptible to weakness if neglected. A Moons Dancer focusing on only one mastery becomes but a point on a star, equidistant to the center from the others, or true knowing. <BR> 
For this is the breath, the soul, of our art: that everything is connected, everything governed by the animus energy that flows to and from, through and away; that which may become what was once only imagined, felt as a quiver in the whiskers or a shiver across the fur: the all-encompasing flow that is Magicka.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
幼崽入门读物：月之舞者的魔能<BR>
改编自一位达吉-拉特大师的讲座，<BR>
双月之舞神殿，托瓦尔<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
首先是对呼吸的掌控。如果一个人不能呼吸，他就不能生存：这是显而易见的。管理呼吸类似于管理自身的力量。每一次呼吸都作为力量流过身体；因此，月之舞者必须学会如何控制自己的呼吸，然后才能控制其他任何东西。<BR>
<BR>
其次是对身体的掌控。当我们在这个地球上时，我们的身体、灵魂和心灵是紧密结合在一起的；影响其一，必会影响其他。忽视身体会导致忽视心灵或灵魂，反之亦然。即使是最无意识的罗吉特在运用体重和操纵四肢时也表现出力量和技巧，因此这是第二件教给幼崽的事情，作为他们此生能掌握的第二种最自然的控制。<BR>
<BR>
身体的掌控在于两个主要领域，通常被认为是二分的，但实际上任何大师都可能同时拥有两者。首先是纯粹的力量：跳得高、跑得快且久、举起并携带重物的能力。其次是敏捷：肌腱的柔韧性、眼睛的协调性、打击速度和动作的优雅。<BR>
<BR>
这两个领域相互关联，于是就有了第三项掌控：技巧。卡吉特的身体构造使得某些动作序列更容易完成，某些打击在获得适当杠杆作用时更强大。一个例子是欧姆斯的拳手：他们肩膀和臀部的旋转使得左拳接右拳时出拳更有力，将反冲的能量积蓄起来并释放到下一次打击中，如同蛇的盘绕。<BR>
<BR>
技巧，因此，是塑造魔能的门径。魔能存在于万物之中。人们在技巧中找到合适节奏时感受到的正确性，反映在其魔能的流动和效率上。处于这一训练阶段的幼崽应该能够感受到自己动作中的生命能量，并进一步保存或释放这种生命能量，以为打击提供更多力量，或在格挡打击时吸收更多力量。<BR>
<BR>
由此而来的是第四项也是最后一项掌控，即魔能本身。接下来，幼崽学习引导其技巧中的生命能量超越其凡俗形态，成为原始能量。这并非像傲特莫施法那样，将自身潜藏的能量分离出来，而是通过动作对其进行的终极引导。因此，以正确的呼吸、体能和技巧施放的法术，总是比仅仅在脑中构想出来的法术更强大，尽管明智的大师当然也会学习静止无声的法术，以对付狡猾的敌人。<BR>
<BR>
在幼崽学会用魔能强化其战斗训练之后，更多样化的教义可能会对其有所助益，例如窃取或补充他人的生命力，扭曲光的结构或岩石或空气的物质以创造更有利的竞技场，嗅探精魂的踪迹以获得精神指引，或塑造火、霜和闪电的原始能量。尽管必须表现出克制或有大师的指导，但月亮糖也可用作增强剂，因为修行者实质上是在摄取月亮的生命能量，并将其化为己有。<BR>
<BR>
卡吉特大师在这四项掌控上均受过训练，并知道它们之间没有孰优孰劣之分，每一项若被忽视都易产生弱点。只专注于一项掌控的月之舞者，只会成为星辰上的一个点，与其他点或真知距离中心相等。<BR>
因为这就是我们艺术的呼吸，即灵魂：万物相连，万物皆由来回流动、穿行而去的生命能量所支配；那可能成为曾经只能想象之物，被感知为胡须的颤抖或毛皮的战栗：那包罗万象的流动，就是魔能。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Malahk: Scourge of the East<BR>
By Laurina Macurio
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Malahk-Bazul is an Orcish name for a stretch of highlands between Nibenay and Western Morrowind. It is a valley deep within the mountains that is most difficult to reach, even for the most experienced scouts, and seasoned mountaineers. The green-skinned inhabitants are known by the neighbouring House Redoran as Malahk Orcs. They are infamous for their merciless, persistent raiding, and for performing massacres to appease their Daedric god-king Mauloch. They are feared as gruesome, twisted barbarians, whom fight with a ferocity and lust for blood like no other. The few reports that have gotten into Imperial possession about these Orcs and their home speak of a valley streaked with crimson red blood. When Malahk Orcs aren't performing raids on the neighbouring areas or innocent travellers, they war amongst themselves, amongst the different clans that reside in the old abandoned forts, or the various caves hidden deep within the mountains.<BR><BR>

It then shouldn't come as a surprise that the Blue Road, Cheydinhal's most famous trading route, now abruptly stops where the mountains begin. The mountain road stands in direct connection to the lands of House Redoran, but has since fallen out of grace. When trade was plenty, raids were frequent. It was not uncommon for a merchant to be hit by a stray arrow, or to see a gutted horse lying on the side of the path.<BR><BR>

To say that these Orcs are part of a common bandit group is a large understatement. They act in tribes or families of Orcs, each of them taller than a Nord and packing a punch that could rival that of an Ogrim. A group of five or seven of them could show up unexpectedly at any time, flinging hired mercenaries like they were playthings. After pillaging a wagon and taking the bodies (for some kind of nefarious purpose one can only imagine), they would disappear in the mountains again, like thin mist, leaving nothing behind but the empty wagon.<BR><BR>

These frequent attacks left the Imperial forces in the area exhausted. It was eventually decided that, instead of wasting good men on these ruthless attackers or staging a full-scale invasion in Malahk territory, the mountain path would better be left guarded by the Redoran. This choice compelled Imperial merchants to go through Hlaalu lands instead.<BR><BR>

Leaving the trade route guarded by the Redoran was a clever solution; unfortunately, for the Redoran, this came at a price. The Malahk seized the opportunity and captured multiple Imperial forts, that had now been left undermanned by the Imperials. This allowed them to more frequently raid the Redoran. The Redoran however have found a way to effectively deal with the Malahk: providing goods vital to the Malahk by honest (and well-guarded) trade, and sending champions to duel with Malahk warchiefs. These duels cement deals and prevent raids, so that casualties on both sides can be avoided.<BR><BR>

How the Malahk Orcs came to live in Malahk-Bazul is speculative at best. Most Imperial scholars seem to agree that the Malahk have inhabited this mountainous land around the time the Chimer chose to settle in what is now modern-day Morrowind. Some rather eccentric researchers have even suggested that these Orcs have a culture as ancient and sophisticated as ours, and that their seemingly mindless barbarity is somehow related to rites of passage or tests of courage. It is highly likely that these researchers have never felt the sting of an Orc captain's barbed axe. As it stands now, one does not have to, unless one is keen on visiting Malahk-Bazhul, a journey from which very few return.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
马拉赫：东方之祸<BR>
劳瑞娜·马库里奥 著
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
马拉赫-巴祖尔是兽人对尼本奈和西晨风之间一片高地的称呼。这是一个深藏于群山之中的山谷，即使对于最有经验的侦察兵和经验丰富的登山者来说也极难到达。邻近的勒多兰家族称这些绿皮肤居民为马拉赫兽人。他们因无情、持续的劫掠，以及为安抚其迪德拉神王矛洛克而进行屠杀而臭名昭著。他们被视为可怕、扭曲的野蛮人，战斗时凶猛且嗜血，无人能及。帝国获得的关于这些兽人及其家园的少数报告，描述了一个被深红色血液条纹遍布的山谷。当马拉赫兽人不向邻近地区或无辜旅行者发动袭击时，他们就在内部互相争斗，在不同的部落之间，这些部落居住在古老废弃的堡垒或深藏在群山的各种洞穴中。<BR><BR>

因此，夏丁赫尔最著名的贸易路线蓝色大道现在在山脉起点处戛然而止，就不足为奇了。这条山路与勒多兰家族的土地直接相连，但后来已失宠。当贸易繁荣时，袭击频繁发生。商人被流箭射中，或看到被开膛破肚的马倒在路边，都是常有的事。<BR><BR>

说这些兽人只是普通匪帮的一部分，那是大大的轻描淡写。他们以部落或家族的形式行动，每个兽人都比诺德人高大，且拳力可与欧格林媲美。五到七个一组，他们可能随时出人意料地出现，像扔玩具一样把雇佣兵甩来甩去。在劫掠完马车并带走尸体（其邪恶目的只能想象）后，他们会像薄雾一样再次消失在群山中，只留下空荡荡的马车。<BR><BR>

这些频繁的袭击使该地区的帝国军队疲惫不堪。最终决定，与其在这些无情的攻击者身上浪费精兵，或在马拉赫领土发动全面入侵，不如让勒多兰家族来守卫这条山路。这一选择迫使帝国商人转而通过哈拉鲁家族的土地。<BR><BR>

让勒多兰家族守卫贸易路线是个聪明的解决方案；不幸的是，对勒多兰家族来说，这是有代价的。马拉赫人抓住了这个机会，占领了多个帝国堡垒，这些堡垒当时因帝国人而人手不足。这使他们能够更频繁地袭击勒多兰家族。然而，勒多兰家族找到了一种有效对付马拉赫人的方法：通过诚实的（且戒备森严的）贸易提供对马拉赫人至关重要的货物，并派遣勇士与马拉赫战酋决斗。这些决斗巩固了交易，防止了袭击，从而避免了双方的伤亡。<BR><BR>

马拉赫兽人如何来到马拉赫-巴祖尔居住，充其量只是推测。大多数学者似乎同意，马拉赫人在歧莫选择定居在现在现代晨风的地区前后，就已经居住在这片山地了。一些相当古怪的研究者甚至提出，这些兽人拥有和我们一样古老而精妙的文化，他们看似毫无来由的野蛮行为，在某种程度上与成年礼或勇气考验有关。这些研究者极有可能从未感受过兽人队长带刺斧头的刺痛。就目前情况而言，除非某人热衷于访问马拉赫-巴祖尔（这是一段几乎无人能归的旅程），否则不必感受。<BR>

On Our Order:<BR>
<BR>
Know first that we are no simple tribe of savages, tearing throats with the orgiastic abandon of our scattered, tribal brethren. Ours is a civil fraternity, to which we are bound - every one - by our dual hunger for flesh and influence. By the virtue of Imperial structure and bureaucracy, Cyrodiil has become our stronghold in the third era, and we suffer no savage rivals within our boundaries, reveal ourselves to none, and manipulate the hand of society to mete out our agendas.<BR>
<BR>
On Our Dual Patrons:<BR>
<BR>
To Kin-father Molag Bal, who brought forth the Bloodmatron Lamae to spite Arkay, we owe our existence, as do all vampires, though not all honor Him. For him we revel in the feast, and acknowledge the gift adrift in our veins.<BR>
<BR>
To patron Clavicus Vile, beacon o'er our affairs, we owe our successes and social stature. Our bond with Vile makes us unique among our kind, for his guidance steels our savage craving with reason and savvy. For him we live amidst mankind, and twist them to our will from offices of power.<BR>
<BR>
On Our Rivals:<BR>
<BR>
Most barbaric tribes think themselves powerful by the gift of Bal's blood alone, and squander the gift. There are those, however, who show signs of enlightenments, and earn our attention - those such as the Glenmoril Wyrd, who live within the walls of Breton cities, or the Whet-Fang sodality of Black Marsh, who use magicka to keep captives catatonic and harvest from them the red nectar. These foes may one day threaten to impugn our sovereignty within the boundaries of Cyrodiil, thus compelling our vigilance. Should any encroach upon our dominion, our wrath must be swift and total.<BR>
<BR>
On Our Conduct:<BR>
<BR>
To preserve our ideals and way of life, two primary edicts shall be observed. Above all, reveal thyself and our Order to no other, for discretion is the greatest of our virtues. Do not feed where you may be found out, or on those who may suspect your passing. Avoid daylight by lifestyle; dispel common belief in our kind, and maintain supple appearance through satisfaction of the thirst. Second, devote your pursuits to the procurement of influence, political and otherwise. Our strength is not in physical numbers, but in skillful manipulation of society. Always be mindful of our Patrons, and preserve the Order. Devote yourself to these ideals always, and the Order shall count you amongst our own.<BR>

Mannimarco, King of Worms
曼尼马克，蛆虫之王

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_MannimarcoSHOTN
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Mannimarco, King of Worms<BR>
by Horicles<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
O sacred isle Artaeum, where rosy light infuses air,
O'er towers and through flowers, gentle breezes flow,
Softly sloping green-kissed cliffs to crashing foam below,
Always springtide afternoon housed within its border,
This mystic, mist-protected home of the Psijic Order:
Those counselors of kings, cautious, wise, and fair.<BR>
<BR>
Ten score years and thirty since the mighty Remans fell,
Two brilliant students studied within the Psijics' fold.
One's heart was light and warm, the other dark and cold.
The madder latter, Mannimarco, whirled in a deathly dance,
His soul in bones and worms, the way of the necromance.
Entrapping and enslaving souls, he cast a wicked spell.<BR>
<BR>
The former, Galerion had magic bold and bright as day.
He confronted Mannimarco beneath gray Ceporah Tower,
Saying, 'Your wicked mysticism is no way to wield your power,
Bringing horror to the spirit world, your studies must cease.'
Mannimarco scoffed, hating well the ways of life and peace,
And returned to his dark artistry; his paints, death and decay.<BR>
<BR>
O sacred isle Artaeum, how slow to perceive the threat,
When the ghastly truth revealed, how weak the punishment.
The ghoulish Mannimarco from the isle of the wise was sent
To the mainland Dawn's Beauty, more death and souls to reap.
'You have found a wolf, and sent the beast to flocks of sheep,'
Galerion told his Masters, 'A terror on Tamriel has set.'<BR>
<BR>
'Speak no more of him,' the sage Cloaks of Gray did say.
'Twas not the first time Galerion thought his Masters callous,
Unconcerned for men and mer, aloof in their island palace.
'Twas not the first time Galerion thought 'twas time to build
A new Order to bring true magic to all, a mighty Mages Guild.
But 'twas the time he left, at last, fair Artaeum's azure bay.<BR>
<BR>
O, but sung we have of Vanus Galerion many times before,
How cast he off the Psijics' chains, bringing magic to the land.
Throughout the years, he saw the touch of Mannimarco's hand,
Through Tamriel's deserts, forests, towns, mountains, and seas.
The dark grip stretching out, growing like some dread disease
By his dark Necromancers, collecting cursed artifacts of yore.<BR>
<BR>
They brought to him these tools, mad wizards and witches,
And brought blood-tainted herbs and oils to his cave of sin,
Sweet Akaviri poison, dust from saints, sheafs of human skin,
Toadstools, roots, and much more cluttered his alchemical shelf,
Like a spider in his web, he sucked all their power into himself,
Mannimarco, Worm King, world's first of the undying liches.<BR>
<BR>
Corruption on corruption, 'til the rot sunk to his very core,
Though he kept the name Mannimarco, his body and his mind
Were but a living, moving corpse as he left humanity behind.
The blood in his veins became instead a poison acid stew.
His power and his life increased as his fell collection grew .
Mightiest were these artifacts, long cursed since days of yore.<BR>
<BR>
They say Galerion left the Guild, calling it 'a morass,'
But untruth is a powerful stream, polluting the river of time.
Galerion beheld Mannimarco's rise through powers sublime,
To his mages and Lamp Knights, 'Before my last breath,
Face I must the tyranny of worms, and kill at last, undeath.'
He led them north to cursed lands, to a mountain pass.<BR>
<BR>
O those who survived the battle say its like was never seen.
Armored with magicka, armed with ensorcelled sword and axe,
Galerion cried, echoing, 'Worm King, surrender your artifacts,
And their power to me, and you shall live as befits the dead.'
A hollow laugh answered, 'You die first,' Mannimarco said.
The mage army then clashed with the unholy force obscene.<BR>
<BR>
Imagine waves of fire and frost, and the mountain shivers,
Picture lightning arching forth, crackling in a dragon's sigh.
Like leaves, the battlemages fly to rain down from the sky,
At the Necromancers' call, corpses burst from earth to fight,
To be shattered into nothingness with a flood of holy light.
A maelstrom of energy unleashed, blood cascades in rivers.<BR>
<BR>
Like a thunderburst in blue skies or a lion's sudden roar,
Like sharp razors tearing over delicate embroidered lace,
So at a touch did Galerion shake the mountain to its base.
The deathly horde fell fatally, but heeding their dying cries
From the depths, the thing they called Worm King did rise.
Nirn itself did scream in the Mages' and Necromancers' war.<BR>
<BR>
His eyes burning dark fire, he opened his toothless maw,
Vomiting darkness with each exhalation of his breath,
All sucking in the fetid air felt the icy touch of death.
In the skies above the mountain, darkness overcame pale,
Then Mannimarco Worm King felt his dismal powers fail:

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Manual of Armor<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
This manual contains information on the different types of armor and their uses.<BR>
<BR>
This manual is commissioned by General Warhaft to serve as a guide and manual to armor for all officers in the Imperial service.<BR>
<BR>
On the battlefield, a soldier's armor should reflect his principal duties. Scouts, light cavalry, archers, and raiding skirmishers should wear light armor. Mobility and speed is of paramount importance to these troops. It is recommended that a cuirass and greaves be worn at all times. Helmets, gauntlets and boots are of value to cavalry and skirmishers, but not scouts or archers.<BR>
<BR>
Light armor is made from fur, leather, chainmail, mithril, elven or glass. This is also the order of their quality and expense, fur being the least protective and cheapest, and glass the best and most expensive. Fur, leather armor, and chainmail are readily available throughout the empire. Mithril, elven and glass are exceedingly rare and are only found in ancient ruins and remote tombs.<BR>
<BR>
Heavy armor should be reserved for the frontline infantry, pikemen, heavy cavalry or foot knights. All officers should be issued heavy armor. Helmets, cuirass and greaves should be standard issue at all times. Boots and gauntlets are only necessary for the cavalry and foot knights.<BR>
<BR>
Blacksmiths can forge heavy armor from iron, steel, dwarven, orcish, ebony or daedric. This is also the order of their quality and expense, iron being the least useful and cheapest, with daedric the most effective and expensive. Iron and steel plate mail can be found in most any blacksmith's shop. The other materials are rare and armor made from them is only found in ancient treasure hoards hidden deep underground.<BR>
<BR>
Advanced practitioners in the Mages Guild know the secrets of placing enchantments upon pieces of armor. The greatest enchantments are typically placed on armor made from rarer, more durable materials, such as ebony and daedric, but even iron can be made to take an enchantment.<BR>
<BR>
The self-styled Bard of Battle, Amorous Janus, once penned a comedic ballad about a Colovian general who was constant removing and re-equipping his armor every few minutes to conserve the magicka powering it. By way of response to the implied criticism, the general had him mounted on the front of a battering ram during the siege of Castle Fallow.<BR>
<BR>"""
