"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Manual of Arms<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
This manual is commissioned by General Warhaft to serve as a guide and manual to arms and weapons for all Imperial officers in the field.<BR>
<BR>
Obviously, a soldier's weaponry should reflect his skills. Skill with a blade is recommended for daggers, shortswords, longswords, and claymores. Skill with blunt weapons is desirable to wield the war axe, mace, battle axe and warhammer. To the uninitiated, axes and hammers may seem to be very different weapons, but the rhythm, drill, and physical strength used by both weapon types are virtually identical. Only those with marksman skill should be outfitted with the bow.<BR>
<BR>
Most of these weapons are commonly used in combination with a shield. The claymore, battle axe and warhammer, however, require both hands to use. These two-handed weapons are best suited to heavily-armored knights, berserkers and those soldiers that hold the flanks of the line.<BR>
<BR>
Arms have been made from many materials over the ages, and each material varies in weight, durability, and cost. These materials are here ranked in order of desirability and cost, with cheapest and least desirable listed first: iron, steel, silver, dwarven, elven, glass, ebony, and finally daedric. Some armorers correctly observe that silver weapons are slightly less durable than steel; nonetheless, its unique ability to affect ghosts, wraiths and certain types of Daedric creatures is undisputed.<BR>
<BR>
Bows can be made with laminated cores of the same materials. This provides a higher tensile strength and therefore greater power on the draw. The materials used in the arrow, particularly in the arrowhead, can affect its mass and penetration. Thus, the quality of the bow and of the arrow are taken together to determine the weapon's overall armor penetration.<BR>
<BR>
Enchanted weapons are mentioned in virtually every fable and song. The magic on such items lies dormant until they strike an opponent. At that moment the enchantment is activated, causing distress and injury to the target. Enchantments on bows are transferred to the arrow at the moment of release. Should the arrow have an enchantment of its own, however, the missile now carries both enchantments and delivers them to the target.<BR>
<BR>
An enchanted weapon has a limited reservoir of magicka. Each blow drains some of its reserves, until finally it is drained dry. The enchantment can be recharged by arcane processes involving soul gems. The more powerful the soul in the gem, the more magicka is restored to the item.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
武器手册<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
本手册由瓦哈夫特将军委托编写，作为野战部队中所有帝国军官的武器指南和手册。<BR>
<BR>
显然，士兵的武器应反映其技能。建议使用匕首、短剑、长剑和阔剑的人具备剑术技能。使用战斧、钉头锤、巨斧和战锤的人需要钝器技能。对外行来说，斧和锤似乎是截然不同的武器，但这两种武器类型所用的节奏、操练和体力几乎是相同的。只有那些具备射手技能的人才应配备弓箭。<BR>
<BR>
这些武器大多通常与盾牌结合使用。然而，阔剑、巨斧和战锤需要双手使用。这些双手武器最适合重甲骑士、狂战士和那些守住战线侧翼的士兵。<BR>
<BR>
自古以来，武器由许多材料制成，每种材料在重量、耐用性和成本上各不相同。这些材料在此按需求和价格排序，最便宜和最不理想的首当其冲：铁、钢、银、矮人、精灵、玻璃、黑檀，最后是迪德拉。一些盔甲匠正确指出，银制武器比钢制武器略不耐用；然而，其影响幽灵、鬼魂和某些类型的迪德拉生物的独特能力是无可争议的。<BR>
<BR>
弓可以用相同材料的层压芯材制成。这提供了更高的抗拉强度，因此拉弓时力量更大。箭所用材料，特别是箭头，会影响其质量和穿透力。因此，弓和箭的质量需综合考虑，以确定武器的整体盔甲穿透力。<BR>
<BR>
几乎每个寓言和歌曲中都提到过附魔武器。此类物品上的魔法处于休眠状态，直到它们击中对手。在那一刻，附魔被激活，对目标造成痛苦和伤害。弓上的附魔在释放时刻转移到箭上。然而，如果箭本身也有附魔，那么该投射物现在携带两种附魔并将其传递给目标。<BR>
<BR>
附魔武器有有限的魔能储备。每次打击都会消耗一部分储备，直到最终耗尽。附魔可以通过涉及灵魂石的奥术过程重新充能。灵魂石中的灵魂越强大，恢复给物品的魔能就越多。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Manual of Spellcraft<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
An Introductory Text<BR>
<BR>
[The book contains an inordinate number of scrawlings along the margins; the few that are immediately readable suggest they are notes for someone who needs frequent reminders on the basics of spell casting.]<BR>
<BR>
The Beginning Spellcaster
The most powerful mages in Tamriel were once beginners. They all had similar early experiences: exposure to magic kindled an interest and/or unlocked some latent ability, followed by years of hard work. These intrepid souls honed their skills, learned new spells, and vigorously trained their minds and bodies to become the formidable figures they were known as during their later lives.<BR>
<BR>
The Mages Guild of Tamriel has long been the first stop on a long road to knowledge and power for many individuals. Providing magical services to the general public, the Guild offers a wide variety of spells for purchase, and is recommended as a first stop for any aspiring spellcaster. Independent dealers may be found, though their selection of spells is often not as comprehensive as that of the Mages Guild.<BR>
<BR>
Many spells are beyond the capabilities of beginning mages; the ability to render one's self invisible, for example, is an advanced power and is beyond the novice spellcaster. Through practice, a mage may become more skilled in a given school of Magic and find himself proficient enough to begin exploring its more powerful aspects. The fledgling mage should not be daunted by his inability to wield certain powers, but should instead use this as a point of focus and a drive for bettering himself. Rather than becoming discouraged, the student should look forward to higher levels of skill, such as the advanced techniques of absorbing spells, summoning lesser (and eventually greater) Daedra and undead -- for research purposes only -- and protection against specific types of spells, such as Fire, Frost, and Shock spells.<BR>
<BR>
Mages wishing to specialize in a particular school of magic are encouraged to learn as many spells of possible within that school, and to practice them frequently. All mages, whether specializing or nurturing a general interest, are encouraged to apply for membership within the Mages Guild. Beyond services available to the general public, the accomplished Guild member has access to many exclusive services such as Advanced Spellcraft and Enchanting. These services have been deemed potentially dangerous to the public at large, and have been restricted to higher-ranked Guild members in good standing by the Council of Mages.<BR>
<BR>
Citizens interested in the further use of magic should consult their local Mages Guild Archmagister.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
法术工艺手册<BR><BR><BR>

入门文本<BR>

[这本书的页边空白处有大量的潦草涂鸦；少数能直接读懂的表明，这些是为某个需要频繁提醒施法基础知识的人所做的笔记。]<BR>

初学施法者
泰姆瑞尔最强大的法师也曾是初学者。他们都有相似的早期经历：接触魔法点燃了兴趣和/或解锁了某些潜在能力，随后是多年的努力。这些勇敢的灵魂磨练了技能，学习了新法术，并精力充沛地训练了心智和身体，成为他们后来生活中著名的令人敬畏的人物。<BR>
<BR>
泰姆瑞尔的法师公会长期以来一直是许多人在通往知识和力量的漫长道路上的第一站。公会为公众提供魔法服务，出售各种各样的法术，并被推荐为任何有抱负的施法者的第一站。也可以找到独立的经销商，尽管他们的法术选择通常不如法师公会全面。<BR>
<BR>
许多法术超出了初学法师的能力范围；例如，使自己隐形的能力是一种高级力量，超出了新手施法者的能力范围。通过实践，法师可能会在某个魔法学派中变得更加熟练，并发现自己足够精通，可以开始探索其更强大的方面。初出茅庐的法师不应因无法运用某些力量而气馁，而应将其作为关注点和自我提升的动力。与其变得沮丧，学生应期待更高层次的技能，例如吸收法术的高级技巧、召唤较小（最终是较大）的迪德拉和亡灵 -- 仅用于研究目的 -- 以及对抗特定类型法术（如火焰、冰霜和电击法术）的防护。<BR>
<BR>
鼓励希望专攻某一魔法学派的法师学习该学派的尽可能多的法术，并经常练习。鼓励所有法师，无论是专攻还是培养一般兴趣，申请加入法师公会。除了向公众提供的服务外，有成就的公会成员还可以使用许多专属服务，例如高级法术工艺和附魔。这些服务被认为可能对广大公众构成危险，因此已被法师议会限制为仅提供给信誉良好的高级公会成员。<BR>
<BR>
对进一步使用魔法感兴趣的公民应咨询当地法师公会的大导师。<BR>

<BR>

Let us now turn to the nature of the sword and the tongue. The sword is a sharp tool, whose edge wears out when it is used correctly, eventually requiring the attention of oils and whetstones. The tongue has no edge, but it is honed in proper usage, that being according to the precepts of the Imperial art of Speech, and even the most rigorous student will never find it in need of sharpening. The sword is a tool of last resort, whose proper application will bring about an end to further implementation of requisite skill. The tongue lies at the root of beginnings, and, whenever used correctly, it will open up ever widening avenues of application.<BR>

<BR>

A man who wields a iron sword can be a protector or an oppressor. When he is a protector, his back is to the world, as he dwells on walls and in the jungle, and his work is arduous - in his art he loses that which he shields. If he is an oppressor, he may pick the fruits of his work, but must ever hew deeper to slake his thirst, and live with one eye open, for he has made an enemy of that which he desires. A man who wields the red sword that is the tongue can both covet and protect the bounty of the world, and be sure that his every action will benefit both himself and his charge, never fear that which he holds dear, and never go without it. That is the path of the Speaker, and that is the path of the Councilman.<BR>

真 著<BR><BR>

嗯，那块岩石是一个洞穴的秘密入口，里面住着一个非常卑鄙的兽人。当他打猎回来时，发现玛拉蜷缩在他的岩石上睡着了，心想：“嗯，一个美味的小女孩。我要把她留作早餐！”
他抓住她，把她带进洞穴，把岩石移回原位，让她无法逃脱。她以为自己必死无疑，试图逃跑，但邪恶的兽人只是一直嘲笑她，直到她最终放弃。<BR><BR>

当山德靠近时，兽人抓住了他，开始把他勒死。<BR><BR>
回到村子里，人们很快意识到让一个年轻人独自进入树林是愚蠢的。他们拿起所有武器，出发去寻找两个失踪的孩子。当他们终于来到兽人洞穴附近的空地时，看到了一个奇怪而奇妙的景象：洞穴入口附近躺着一具被杀死的兽人，玛拉怀里抱着可怜的尚达的头。山德杀死了兽人，但兽人也给了山德致命一击。<BR><BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Mask and the Mirror<BR>
Book I<BR>
by Llandyne Vandoroth<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
[About the Author:<BR>
Llandyne Vandoroth is a Dunmer author of great skill. Originally from the city of Almalexia, she has made her home in Sarchal, seeking to sate the more refined literary palate of the west.]<BR>
<BR>
Bronjar Clean-Clothes had been with the Brotherhood for a great many years. He did well because he had no principles when it came to targets, and somehow even less when it came to pay. From a poor family in Haafingar, Bronjar was satisfied with any contract that provided a room with four walls and a new shirt. As the years went by, however, he dreamed of bigger things, mostly bigger rooms, and found that even the sum he was paid by the Brotherhood for barely discriminate slaughter wouldn't foot the bill.<BR>
<BR>
It was in late Evening Star that he received what was to be his longest-running and highest-paying contract. The Brotherhood had learned that a member of the wretched Morag Tong would be passing through Haafingar on route to Wayrest, and it fell to Bronjar to fell him.<BR>
<BR>
The plan was simple. Bronjar would take a seat at the inn, whose window provided him a perfect view of the city gate, and would sip fine mead in comfort while waiting for that ragged eastern murderer to shamble through it. Fortunately, the wait was a long one, spent enjoying the attention of a black-haired serving girl and a seemingly endless mug of mulled mead. The Dark Elf of the hour didn't appear until it was almost dawn, and Bronjar spotted him at once. He did not skulk in the shadows like an amateur, trying to hide his plain iniquity, nor did he walk boldly down the middle of the street whistling a jaunty tune. Instead, he walked halfway between the street's side and its center, seeming to pant and gasp with weariness after what was no doubt a long and tiring journey for such an unassuming elf. He was outfitted in an almost absurdly typical fashion, with a warm fur robe, a simple walking stick, and a dagger of a type that could be bought at any smithy in Skyrim. On his back was a leather pack filled to bursting, so much so that a rag peeked out from the flap. Bronjar could have (and would have) bet anything that this pack contained the eyebrow-raising uniform of the fabled assassins of Morrowind, complete with his true weapon: a dagger which was no-doubt fine enough to slit the throat of a Potentate out of Reman antiquity.<BR>
<BR>
Bronjar coolly threw some septims onto the table and strode out, affecting a drunken stagger before he had even left the common room. Of course he was not drunk, never on a job, but a drunken Nord shambling after you was less conspicuous than a sure-footed one wandering the streets of Haafingar so late at night. One was on his way home after a typical night of raucous drinking, the other an agent with some immoral purpose wanting the cover of night to carry it out.<BR>
<BR>
The Dark Elf dipped into the city's second-seediest flophouse, and by the time Bronjar followed him in he had already paid for and vanished to a private room. Coins changed hands, and the Nord, who had abandoned his inebriated gait for softer footfalls. crept towards a door at the end of the hall. He pulled his own unadorned tanto out of its tucked-away sheath and prepared to, quickly and quietly, fling wide the door. He was relying on the draft to extinguish the candle whose light flickered beneath the ill-made portal, and on his own speed to strike the first blow. Rarely were Bronjar's assaults such unsure throws of the die. He was usually sought after for his willingness to kill even the most pitiful, but now he had been paid for an act which was foolhardy to attempt no matter the skill of the chosen agent.<BR>
<BR>
The door did its work, and Bronjar had only a moment of candle-light to spy the elf pulling a curved dagger from beneath the bundled clothes of his pack. A dagger he would never again use. By the time Bronjar had shut the door and lit the light, the Morag Tong assassin was choking on his own blood on the floor of the filthy inn. The Nord was leisurely in his next steps, knowing that no witness had seen, heard or cared what had happened. He examined the dagger first. Finding it to be of superior make and obviously enchanted, he carefully hid it in his loose shirt. Next he took each item out of the dead assassin's pack one by one, discarding each article in turn until he came to the most striking. It was a black leather mask with strange insectoid eyes and long, sheath-shaped covers for the assassin's elven ears. It was obviously very well made, and Bronjar was surprised to find that it fit him, and further that it didn't obscure his sight or periphery in the slightest. Indeed, the strange eyes almost seemed to make him more aware of his surroundings. After this, he only found a small gray paper, bearing the name of some irrelevant Merchant Prince who no doubt traded out of Wayrest, the felled Assassin's now unattainable goal.<BR>
<BR>
Bronjar decided he would spend his pay on a fine room at the inn he had so enjoyed, and for the next week drank, talked, and boasted of heroic feats of cleverness and strength. And each night, back in his big room, he stared at the strange mask of the nameless dark assassin. He wondered how much his victim had been paid to travel so far and risk so much, knowing full well that Mephala's hands were forbidden from reaching westward. And after this full week of short days and long nights, he had made up his mind. He would travel east and find out how the Dark Elves rewarded those who spilled blood for their aspirations.<BR>

面具与镜子<BR>
卷一<BR>
兰黛恩·凡多罗斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
[关于作者：<BR>
兰黛恩·凡多罗斯是一位技艺高超的丹莫作家。她原籍阿玛莱西娅城，现定居于萨查尔，致力于满足西方更为精致的文学品味。]<BR>
<BR>
布隆贾·净衣加入兄弟会已有多年。他之所以干得好，是因为他对目标毫无原则，而在报酬方面则更加没有底线。布隆贾出身于哈芬加的贫苦家庭，只要合同能提供一个有四壁的房间和一件新衬衫，他就心满意足了。然而，随着岁月流逝，他开始梦想更大的东西，主要是更大的房间，却发现即使兄弟会支付给他几乎不加选择的屠杀的酬劳，也无法支付账单。<BR>
<BR>
在夜星月末，他收到了这份将是他持续时间最长、报酬最高的合同。兄弟会得知，可憎的莫拉格堂的一名成员将在前往途歇的途中经过哈芬加，而干掉他的任务就落在了布隆贾身上。<BR>
<BR>
计划很简单。布隆贾会坐在旅馆里，从窗户可以清楚地看到城门，然后舒适地啜饮着上好的蜂蜜酒，等待那个衣衫褴褛的东方杀手拖着步子走进去。幸运的是，等待时间很长，他享受着一位黑发侍女的殷勤和似乎永远喝不完的热蜂蜜酒。那个丹莫直到天快亮时才出现，布隆贾一眼就认出了他。他没有像业余者那样躲在阴影里，试图隐藏自己的罪恶，也没有大胆地走在街中央吹着欢快的小调。相反，他走在街道边缘和中心之间，经过一段对这样一个不起眼的精灵来说无疑是漫长而疲惫的旅程后，他似乎气喘吁吁，疲惫不堪。他的着装几乎是荒谬地典型：一件保暖的毛皮长袍，一根简单的手杖，以及一把在天际任何铁匠铺都能买到的匕首。他背上背着一个塞得满满当当的皮革背包，以至于一块破布从盖子里露出来。布隆贾可以（而且愿意）打赌，这个背包里装着晨风传奇刺客那引人注目的制服，还有他真正的武器：一把匕首，毫无疑问锋利到足以割断雷曼古代摄政王的喉咙。<BR>
<BR>
布隆贾冷冷地把一些塞普汀扔在桌子上，大步走了出去，还没离开公共休息室就装出一副醉醺醺的样子。当然，他没有醉，在工作时从不醉，但一个醉醺醺的诺德人在你身后蹒跚而行，比一个脚步稳健的人在深夜的哈芬加大街上游荡更不显眼。前者是在一夜喧闹的饮酒后回家，后者则是怀有不道德目的、想要利用夜色掩护行事的特工。<BR>
<BR>
那个丹莫溜进了城里第二破烂的廉价旅馆，等到布隆贾跟进去时，他已经付了钱，消失在一个私人房间里。金币易手，诺德人放弃了醉酒的步伐，改用更轻的脚步，悄悄走向走廊尽头的一扇门。他从隐藏的刀鞘中拔出自己朴素的短刀，准备迅速而安静地猛然推开那扇门。他指望气流能吹灭那扇劣质门下闪烁的烛光，并依靠自己的速度发动第一击。布隆贾的攻击很少如此不确定，像掷骰子一样。通常人们找他是因为他愿意杀死哪怕最可怜的目标，但现在他收钱要做的这件事，无论所选特工的技能如何，尝试起来都是鲁莽的。<BR>
<BR>
门起了作用，布隆贾只有一瞬间的烛光瞥见那个精灵从背包里塞得满满的衣服下抽出一把弯刀。那是一把他再也用不上的刀。等到布隆贾关上门点上灯时，莫拉格堂的刺客已经在肮脏旅馆的地板上，被自己的血呛死了。诺德人不慌不忙地进行下一步，他知道没有目击者看到、听到或关心发生了什么。他先检查了那把匕首。发现它制作精良，显然附了魔，他小心地把它藏在自己宽松的衬衫里。接着，他把死去刺客背包里的物品一件件拿出来，依次丢弃，直到拿出最引人注目的那件。那是一个黑色皮面具，有着奇怪的虫类眼睛，还有长长的、刀鞘状的护罩用来遮盖刺客的精灵耳朵。它显然制作得非常精良，布隆贾惊讶地发现它很合他的脸，而且丝毫不遮挡他的视线或周边视野。事实上，那双奇怪的眼睛几乎让他更敏锐地感知周围环境。之后，他只找到一张小小的灰色纸片，上面写着某个无关紧要的商业王子的名字，无疑是在途歇做生意的，也就是被杀的刺客现在无法企及的目标。<BR>
<BR>
布隆贾决定把报酬花在他非常喜欢的那家旅馆的一个好房间里，接下来的一周，他喝酒、聊天、吹嘘自己聪明和力量的英雄事迹。而每天晚上，回到他的大房间里，他都会盯着那个无名黑暗刺客的奇怪面具。他想知道他的受害者被付了多少钱，才需要走那么远，冒那么大的险，而他很清楚梅法拉之手被禁止向西延伸。在这短短一周、漫漫长夜之后，他下定了决心。他要向东旅行，看看丹莫是如何奖励那些为他们的野心流血的人的。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Mask and the Mirror<BR>
Book II<BR>
by Llandyne Vandoroth<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
[About the Author:<BR>
Llandyne Vandoroth is a Dunmer author of great skill. Originally from the city of Almalexia, she has made her home in Sarchal, seeking to sate the more refined literary palate of the west.]<BR>
<BR>
The trip was long and uneventful. A small, timber-laden cutter took him east from Haafingar to Winterhold, where he booked passage on a larger ship, this one a Hlaalu merchant vessel bound for Narsis. Bronjar Clean-Clothes, however, stole away as soon as the ship docked in Blacklight, preferring that none should know of his true destination. He made his way south until at last he came to the city of Silgrad, which squatted like a strange bug above the fungal marsh that the natives called a Meadow. Before he entered the city, he slipped the mask on his face and obscured his hands with gloves. Some padding in the upper portion of his leather breastplate completed the look, that of an unusually tall Dunmer who spoke little, but bore the helm and red-jeweled scarf of a Morag Tong assassin. It did not take long to find the Tong. Indeed, he noted with no small amount of wonder that their hall was clearly marked and well-known by the locals. It, like the agent he had felled in the west, neither hid nor announced itself, but instead simply was.<BR>
<BR>
It also surprised him how simple it was to receive work. The black-clad Dunmer woman simply looked over his outfit and eyed his knife. With nary a single spoken word he was handed a paper, a plainly written order describing who was to be killed, without seal or code to hide its meaning. And Bronjar set to his work. He did not count the dead, and their names left him even as the writ slipped through his fingers.<BR>
<BR>
For many long years he plied his trade in the east, until at last he had made himself monstrously rich. In all this time he spoke so little that when his lips were forced to part, his voice came out as a dry and hoarse croak, which echoed in his mask with the lilt and the loose speech of the lowborn Velothi he so often heard. Until at last he "retired", slipping away west to the shambles of Mir Corrup. There, his gold bought him a suite of many rooms and a cup whose bottom never saw the light but through the red-glass shine of shein and West Weald wines. Bronjar had no fear that he would pauper himself, for in his long service to the Morag Tong he had acquired a clattering hoard of golden septims, stained just as much by the cloying stench of eastern incense as with blood.<BR>
<BR>
It was one evening, many nights and cups later, that Bronjar squinted as he looked at the naked light which illuminated the luxurious silken sprawl of his bedchamber. A light which seemed magnified and bewitched by a massive silver mirror that rested atop a groaning and long-suffering cabinet. The mirror must've been there the entire time, of course. The big rooms he now called his own would've had previous owners, unable to hold on to them by reasons of destitution or death, and Bronjar must've bought that mirror from them alongside the bed and dressers and wine racks.<BR>
<BR>
But it was as if he'd never really looked at it. It was a fine thing, reflecting the whole room with perfect clarity. Indeed, as he walked toward it he could see no distortion of shape or color. And he could see himself. He hadn't looked at himself for a while, either. Bronjar drank much and slept little, and those merriments had left their mark. His largesse still attracted crowds at the local casino. And it also attracted a steady company of beautiful hangers-on, despite his aged face and now-silver hair that shone almost unnaturally bright.<BR>
<BR>
As Bronjar lay down to sleep that night, long having dismissed the courtesans and servants, he found no rest. Dimming the lanterns and snuffing the candles did nothing. Shutting the doors and shuttering the windows did less. After all this and more the room was still just as bright as it had been before his efforts.  At long last his gaze fell upon the looming silver mirror. Now he noticed that it did not reflect the light of the room, but instead amplified it. Bronjar took a step toward it, realizing at last that something was off about the reflection. An obvious mistake, which resided not in warped glass, but in the essential tableau. Though he had locked and barred the door to his chamber some time earlier, he saw in the looking glass that it was flung wide, and that the yawning night lay beyond it. As the Nord looked on helplessly at the reflected suite, a stealthy agent crept through the door, all clad in the raiment of Mephala's own hands. And still he could not move, fixed on the image of that blade of the night as it stepped closer, closer and yet closer. No footfalls filled his ears, nor could he hear the breath of his murderer, even as the mer stood directly behind him. The only thing he saw was his sure and imminent end, reflected clear as sunlight in that cold-silvered glass. At the last moment he threw up his hands and collapsed to the floor.<BR>
<BR>
"Aieee!"<BR>
<BR>
Moments passed, and somehow he drew breath again. He shakily looked about the room and saw nothing, no skulking actor, no bladed mer, and no wide-flung door. He was alone.<BR>
<BR>
This macabre scene repeated itself night after night. After a long day of wine, women, dice and song, he would retreat to his chambers only to look on helplessly as the mirror showed him visions of his death at the hands of some new Dunmer assassin. When he looked at himself in the lurking silver mirror he did not see the hale and robust Nord of his youth, but a decrepit old man. His skin had paled and become ashen, deprived almost wholly of sunlight, his body had become withered and cadaverous, refusing to be sustained by wine and dice alone. His eyes had become red and bloodshot, bearing witness to his restless nights.<BR>
<BR>
At last, after many months of nocturnal horror, he went to his bedchamber with dagger in hand, the curved and loathsome implement he had looted all those years ago in Haafingar. When the assassin came, he was calm once more, steeling himself with memories of old scraps and gold he had earned for them. His breath was shaky, his voice raspy. He turned at once and screamed.<BR>
<BR>
"You filthy n'wah! I'll kill you!"<BR>
<BR>
But as he turned around he saw all too late that there was indeed nobody behind him, no masked and cowled agent of personal doom. He had selected a grand downward stroke which was to plunge behind the collarbone of his would-be killer. Instead, the blade continued down, seeking promised flesh, to find itself buried in his own stomach. Blood and wine alike spilled across the gaudy carpet as he cried out and collapsed. The door broke open with a crash as a Nord guard and a Dunmer courtesan rushed in. The courtesan knelt in his blood and cried out, trying in vain to staunch the blood.<BR>
<BR>
"Sera, what have you done?" <BR>
<BR>
She lifted his head to her knees, and it was then that Bronjar Clean-Clothes looked for the last time at that repugnant silver mirror. That mirror which sat like an accursed Kothringi idol on the dresser above him. In it he saw no face save his own, the ashen, red-eyed face of the assassin which had so many times tried to kill him, and had now succeeded. Sitting perversely next to his own image was the black, insect-eyed mask which he had worn for those long years, and with his last grating words he cursed it.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
面具与镜子<BR>
卷二<BR>
兰黛恩·凡多罗斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
[关于作者：<BR>
兰黛恩·凡多罗斯是一位技艺高超的丹莫作家。她原籍阿玛莱西娅城，现定居于萨查尔，致力于满足西方更为精致的文学品味。]<BR>
<BR>
旅途漫长而平静。一艘装载木材的小帆船载着他从哈芬加向东前往冬堡，在那里他订了一艘更大的船，这是一艘开往纳西斯的哈拉鲁商船。然而，布隆贾·净衣一等到船在黑光城靠岸，就偷偷溜走了，不希望任何人知道他的真正目的地。他一路向南，最后到达了希尔格拉德城，那座城像一只奇怪的虫子一样蹲伏在真菌沼泽之上，当地人称之为“草地”。进城之前，他把面具戴在脸上，用手套遮住双手。皮胸甲上部的一些衬垫完善了这个形象：一个异常高大的丹莫，话不多，却戴着莫拉格堂刺客的头盔和红宝石围巾。找到莫拉格堂并不难。事实上，他惊奇地发现，他们的大厅被清晰地标记着，当地人也众所周知。就像他在西方干掉的那个特工一样，它既不隐藏也不张扬，只是存在着。<BR>
<BR>
令他惊讶的是，接到工作是如此简单。那个黑衣丹莫女人只是打量了一下他的装束，看了看他的刀。没说一个字，他就被递上一张纸，上面清楚地写着要杀谁的命令，没有印章或密码来隐藏其含义。于是布隆贾开始干活。他没有数过死者，他们的名字也随着命令从他指间滑落而被他遗忘。<BR>
<BR>
他在东方干了很多年，直到最后变得极其富有。在这段时间里，他很少说话，以至于当他不得不开口时，声音干涩嘶哑，面具里回荡着他经常听到的低贱维洛提人的轻快而松散的口音。直到最后他“退休”了，悄悄向西溜到了米尔·科鲁普的破败之地。在那里，他的金子为他买下了一套多房间的套房，还有一个杯底从未见过光、只有透过舍因和西部森林葡萄酒的红色玻璃光泽才能看见的杯子。布隆贾从不担心自己会花光钱，因为在他为莫拉格堂长期服务期间，他积攒了一大堆叮当作响的金色塞普汀，上面沾染着东方香料的甜腻恶臭，就像沾染着鲜血一样。<BR>
<BR>
一天晚上，在喝了无数杯酒、过了无数个夜晚之后，布隆贾眯着眼睛看着照亮他那豪华丝绸铺陈的卧室的裸露灯光。那灯光似乎被一面巨大的银镜放大和迷惑了，银镜搁在一个吱呀作响、饱受折磨的柜子上。当然，那面镜子肯定一直都在那里。他现在据为己有的大房间以前肯定有过主人，因为贫困或死亡而无法保留它们，布隆贾一定是从他们那里连同床、梳妆台和酒架一起买下了那面镜子。<BR>
<BR>
但就好像他从未真正看过它一样。那是一面精美的东西，完美清晰地反射着整个房间。的确，当他走向它时，看不到任何形状或颜色的扭曲。他也能看到自己。他也有好一阵子没看自己了。布隆贾喝得多，睡得少，那些寻欢作乐留下了痕迹。他的慷慨仍然在当地赌场吸引着人群。它也吸引了一批固定的美丽追随者，尽管他面容苍老，头发也已银白，白得几乎不自然地明亮。<BR>
<BR>
当晚，布隆贾早已打发走了侍女和仆人，躺下睡觉，却无法安眠。调暗灯笼、吹灭蜡烛都无济于事。关门关窗效果更差。做完这一切甚至更多之后，房间仍然和他努力之前一样明亮。终于，他的目光落在了那面若隐若现的银镜上。此刻他注意到，镜子并没有反射房间里的光线，而是放大了它。布隆贾朝它迈了一步，终于意识到倒影有些不对劲。一个明显的错误，不在于变形的玻璃，而在于基本的画面。虽然他早些时候已经锁上并闩好了卧室的门，但他在镜子里看到门大敞着，外面是张开大口般的黑夜。当诺德人无助地看着镜中的套房时，一个隐秘的特工从门口溜了进来，全身穿着梅法拉之手特有的装束。他仍然无法动弹，目光锁定在那个夜色利刃的形象上，它越走越近，越来越近。他的耳朵里没有脚步声，也听不到凶手的呼吸，即使那个精灵就站在他身后。他唯一看到的是他确定无疑、即将到来的终结，清晰地反射在冰冷的银镜中，如同阳光一样。在最后一刻，他举起双手，瘫倒在地板上。<BR>
<BR>
“啊啊啊！”<BR>
<BR>
片刻之后，不知怎的，他又能呼吸了。他颤抖着环顾房间，什么也没看到，没有潜伏的演员，没有持刀的精灵，也没有大敞的门。他独自一人。<BR>
<BR>
这可怕的场景一夜又一夜地重复。在漫长的一天里，他经历了美酒、女人、骰子和歌声之后，会退回到自己的房间，却只能无助地看着镜子向他展示死于某个新丹莫刺客之手的幻象。当他看着潜伏的银镜中的自己时，看到的不是年轻时健壮强健的诺德人，而是一个衰老的老人。他的皮肤变得苍白灰暗，几乎完全失去了阳光照射，他的身体变得干枯如尸，仅仅靠美酒和骰子无法维持。他的眼睛变得通红，布满血丝，见证了他不眠的夜晚。<BR>
<BR>
终于，在经历了数月的夜间恐怖之后，他手握匕首 -- 那把多年前在哈芬加掠夺来的弯曲而可憎的凶器 -- 走进了卧室。当刺客到来时，他再次平静下来，用过去那些小规模战斗的记忆以及为之赚取的金子来给自己打气。他的呼吸颤抖，声音沙哑。他猛地转过身，尖叫起来。<BR>
<BR>
“你这个肮脏的恩'瓦！我要杀了你！”<BR>
<BR>
但当他转过身时，为时已晚，发现身后确实空无一人，没有戴面具、兜帽的个人厄运特工。他选择了一个猛烈的下劈动作，本应刺入潜在杀手的锁骨后方。然而，刀刃继续向下，寻找承诺中的血肉，却发现它埋进了自己的肚子里。他惨叫一声倒下，鲜血和酒液一起溅落在艳俗的地毯上。门被撞开，一名诺德守卫和一名丹莫交际花冲了进来。交际花跪在他的血泊中，哭喊着，徒劳地试图止血。<BR>
<BR>
“大人，您做了什么？”<BR>
<BR>
她把他的头抬到自己的膝盖上，就在这时，布隆贾·净衣最后一次看向那面令人厌恶的银镜。那面镜子就像一个被诅咒的科斯林吉偶像一样，放在他头顶的梳妆台上。镜中，他看到的只有自己的脸，那张灰白、红眼的刺客的脸，那张曾无数次试图杀死他、如今终于成功的脸。而在他自己形象的旁边，怪异地坐着那张他戴了多年的黑色虫眼面具，他用最后沙哑刺耳的声音诅咒了它。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>

A Mason's Song<BR>
<BR>
Some fifteen years ago, I met a bard with the strangest of all
stories to tell. Born an ashlander, his view to life was very different
from mine and most of the surrounding mer folk as well. Perhaps that is
why he fascinated me with such a great influence.
Although old and withered now, Fainissibi had once
traveled through all Tamriel, gathering a great many stories from the
land's humble folk. After twenty elven years of living among commoners,
earning one's bread by doing masonry in Imperial forts, near new-found

Marsh, he chose to settle down in one of the most beautiful cities of
eastern Morrowind, Tear. There he still sings and entertains the visitors

<BR>
After many miles of traveling horseback from Alten Corimont
to Tear, our party leader decided to make an expedition to the local
taverns. We, being paid by following orders, had the opportunity of
once again following, and perhaps saving him from a plethora of
problems with the authorities. We began by drinking fine sujamma in
the Hanging Argonian. Perhaps even too fine - Enhyn had gotten his
"let us conquer the Black Marsh" drive on and promptly stated that
if he should ever encounter a free Argonian of prosperous stature,
the beast be slain on the spot. After another round in the Lizard
Carcass, a rather shady trader inn underground, our master was
already too lushed to think clearly, and was ready to conquer
Elsweyr too. Then we finally arrived to the Crimson Cutlass.<BR>
<BR>
There an elder Dark Elf sat, against the wall, with several
tired journeymen 'round him on small stools. Enhyn had always been
fond of heroic epics described and portrayed by poets who had seen
it all, and this mer certainly had the looks. The man, whom people
addressed as Fainissibi, sang:<BR>
<BR>
"Laying tiles for days, 'side the abundant hills of Lainlyn<BR>
Working with an ogre's pace, amongst others there was Barin<BR>
A race of Redguard, strongest of the lot<BR>
Even he could not stand the burden of the job.<BR>
<BR>
One day we were a'working on the eastern wall<BR>
for had our captain commanded us, "It shall cover the glade by
nightfall"<BR>
So we toiled, toiled hard, from dusk till sunset glow<BR>
But as the darkness drew near, it seemed we could not finish the last row.<BR>
Thus Barin, eager and strong still, went to the captain's camp on the side of
the hill.<BR>
He climbed down from the slight spire and to the stand<BR>
While descending down, he did not see the rope's other end
and clung to it as he fell.<BR>
Rope attached to the ground and wall, freshly masoned, came crumbling
apart.<BR>
<BR>
For his faith to see mere twenty-five times of warmth, no more<BR>
Yet from life, he knew what to expect for<BR>
Dreams of a man, and past, struck down by the eastern wall of a mine<BR>
built to last.<BR>
<BR>
So it went and the story was told on the taverns of Hammerfell<BR>
How a laborer was struck down hard, struck down like a spell<BR>
Though a man of little stature, Barin was no fool<BR>
And there he rests, in the pit of Lainlyn, bottomless and cruel."<BR>
<BR>
Enhyn, as expected, had gotten very furious even before the
fourth verse and had left the tavern swinging from side to side,
apparently ending up back in the Hanging Argonian. I did not pay
attention to him, though, being mesmerized by the story Fainissibi
had told and those yet to come.<BR>
<BR>
You might wonder, why is one measly bard so fascinating
that he deserves to be praised in a book. It is exactly the same
reason many others thought of Fain - why would a good-mooded
patron want to hear a story of a laborer being grotesquely
splashed by a ton of bricks?<BR>
<BR>
It has been said by many, echoed by Fain among others, that every being is worth a song, and that is why the outcast bard of Erabenimsun tribe was so remarkable and struck to me as a gentle mind amongst the stressed and bad-habited people of these days. Sometimes, stories of one's failure give meaning and faith to others. <BR>

塞鲁斯·瓦利库斯 著<BR>

Long has it been since I have begun to head this project and finally my success has come. Failure compounded upon failure has built a rough basis for our reasoning and finally the answer has surfaced. The team of researchers, including myself, was too hasty in the early stages of the project in trying to make an immediate impact upon Resdayn itself, but alas, our desperation led us to deviate from our projected guidelines. Gold is of the finest essence, emitting a brilliant sparkle while maintaining the highest standards of durability, refinement, and worth. These are the components that we were searching for, and in our excitement, they were lost amidst the experiment's chaotic rush to completion. Our first attempts were varied; often we were able to isolate the hardness and the color, but each came at the expense of the other. Our project came nearly to a standstill when it was finally decided that elements should be selected carefully and only those who met the criteria would be considered for entrance. The priority of the project became to analyze those combinations that would suffice as constituents of gold rather than to concoct gold in one fell swoop.<BR><BR>
It was decided then to start with durability. Scouts from all over the region swarmed through Resdayn looking for rocks of various strains that would resist great blows from the strongest men, and after careful testing only three substances remained, the white rock, the black rock, and the gray rock. No further evidence could be examined so our team moved to the second ideal, that of hardness. But what could be tougher than the planet itself? Philosophers were ushered in to our aid but their remarks were too vague and often quite boring. But one opinion that surfaced made complete sense to our team. Strength is emanated from the inside outward, much like the heart itself, and the rock exposed to our eyes was the weakest of its kind. To delve deeper into the ground would lead to unknown yet stronger substances. We decided that it must be the route to take and we proceeded to convene at the lowest part of Resadyn, outside the district in a vast indentation in the land. We set up a small stronghold in the area, as digging the very ground on which we strode would destroy the equilibrium between our people and nature. Inside the small building we dug the land for hours to little avail. The temperature had risen drastically and in one fortunate instant the land gave away under the feet of a digger and he splashed into the mystery substance we had been looking for. We had found the Firewater. The flames from his body shot upwards and tinged all of us and we all were humbled by the great power of the Firewater. It was very troublesome trying to extract the Firewater, but in the end we were able to draw some of it for research purposes by using extra pipes. There we stood, with two criteria met and halfway to completion.<BR><BR>
Discerning the next two requirements, however, was no easy task. Purity and radiance, two intangible entities, became the bane to many of the pure scientists in the group as they had no conception of either, and I was forced to switch to more abstract thinking, specifically that of philosophers. I assembled a court of ten philosophers and posed the question as to what was meant by purity. Again, I was met with several varied and vague responses but they all converged in one respect, purity implied cleanliness and fidelity during the passage of time. When I analyzed this in terms of physical substances, it began to take form as to the possibilities. Air, water, and soil were the only substances that had not changed noticeably over time but it was almost impossible to extract air in a closed container nor was it possible to determine what sample of land would suffice. Thus I presented to the group my theory that water was the most tangible occurrence of purity and while some philosophers scorned my ideas, others gave their full support. There arose a great dispute and I was forced to ask several of my opponents to leave the project.<BR><BR>
Scared as I was that several valuable insights would be lost, it was the only way to preserve the project from a chaotic failure. The project must be completed. Tired as we all were from the bitter disputes, we were reborn with the advent of the last criterion, brilliance. Unanimously it was decided that the only way to achieve this attribute was for the concoction of all three elements to be exposed to polar opposites of lighting, bright light as well as dull darkness. The only situation in which this would be fulfilled would be during the dead of the night. We convened the next day at dusk, and the excitement of the moment buzzed through the air. There was a one in three chance of each material being of the correct essence but because there was so little firewater that was contained, the gray rock was to be tested first as it is a mixture of white and black rock elements. The moon rose from the depths of the night and the crude experiment took place. The elements were added simultaneously and a cloud of vapor arose. To our excitement, there it laid, the gold that we had dreamed of, contained on the white portion of the rock. The raucous jubilation that occurred was unfathomable. With the great advance in science, it will be a tribute to all that Resdayn stands for. Think of the possibilities! The observatory can now construct pipes that extend towards the skies, there can be movement on unbreakable sleds, and the wealth that we will procure is immeasurable. Victory has been proclaimed in the name of science and glory of old has been restored to Resdayn.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
蜕变<BR>
元素<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000">
自从我开始主持这个项目以来，已经过去了很久，我终于成功了。失败叠加失败，为我们的推理奠定了粗略的基础，最终答案浮出水面。包括我在内的研究团队，在项目早期阶段过于仓促，试图对勒斯丹本身产生直接影响，但唉，绝望使我们偏离了预定的指导方针。黄金是最精纯的精华，散发着璀璨的光辉，同时保持最高标准的耐久性、精炼度和价值。这些正是我们一直在寻找的组成部分，但在兴奋中，它们在实验冲向完成的混乱中丢失了。我们的第一次尝试各不相同；我们常常能分离出硬度和颜色，但总是顾此失彼。当最终决定应仔细选择元素，只有符合标准的元素才被考虑进入时，我们的项目几乎陷入停滞。项目的优先级变成了分析那些足以构成黄金成分的组合，而不是一蹴而就地炼制黄金。<BR><BR>
于是决定从耐久性开始。来自各地的侦察兵涌向勒斯丹，寻找能抵抗最强壮者重击的各种岩石，经过仔细测试，只剩下三种物质：白石、黑石和灰石。无法检查进一步证据，所以我们的团队转向第二个理想：硬度。但还有什么比行星本身更坚硬呢？哲学家被请来协助，但他们的评论过于模糊，常常相当无聊。但有一个浮出水面的观点让我们的团队完全信服。力量是从内向外散发的，很像心脏本身，而我们看到的岩石是同类中最脆弱的。深入地底挖掘将通向未知但更坚硬的物质。我们决定这必须是该走的路线，于是前往勒斯丹的最低处，在地区外一片巨大的土地凹陷处集合。我们在该地区建立了一个小型据点，因为挖掘我们脚下的土地会破坏我们人民与自然的平衡。在小建筑内，我们挖掘了数小时，收效甚微。温度急剧上升，在一个幸运的瞬间，一名挖掘者脚下的土地塌陷，他扑通一声掉进了我们一直在寻找的神秘物质中。我们找到了“火水”。他身上的火焰向上喷射，染红了我们所有人，我们都被火水的巨大力量所折服。提取火水非常麻烦，但最终我们能够使用额外的管道抽取一些用于研究目的。我们站在那里，满足了两个标准，完成了一半。<BR><BR>
然而，辨别接下来的两个要求并非易事。纯度和光辉，这两个无形的实体，成了团队中许多纯粹科学家的克星，因为他们对两者都没有概念，我被迫转向更抽象的思维，特别是哲学家的思维。我召集了一个由十位哲学家组成的法庭，提出“纯度”意味着什么的问题。再次，我得到了几种不同且模糊的回答，但它们都在一个方面达成一致：纯度意味着在时间流逝中的清洁和忠诚。当我用物理物质分析这一点时，它开始形成可能性。空气、水和土壤是唯一随时间推移没有明显变化的物质，但几乎不可能在封闭容器中提取空气，也不可能确定哪种土壤样本符合要求。因此，我向团队提出了我的理论：水是最具实感的纯度。虽然一些哲学家嘲笑我的想法，但其他人给予了全力支持。一场大争论爆发了，我被迫要求几位反对者离开项目。<BR><BR>
尽管我担心会失去几个宝贵的见解，但这是保护项目免于混乱失败的唯一方法。项目必须完成。尽管我们都因激烈的争论而疲惫不堪，但随着最后一个标准 -- 光辉的到来，我们重获新生。大家一致决定，实现这一属性的唯一方法是将所有三种元素的混合物暴露在极端的照明条件下 -- 明亮的光线和昏暗的黑暗。唯一能满足这一条件的情况是在深夜。第二天黄昏我们集合，那一刻的兴奋在空气中嗡嗡作响。每种材料有三分之一的机会具有正确的本质，但由于保存的火水很少，灰石将首先被测试，因为它是白和黑岩石元素的混合物。月亮从黑夜深处升起，粗糙的实验开始了。元素同时加入，一团蒸汽升起。令我们兴奋的是，我们梦想的黄金就躺在那里，在岩石的白色部分上。随之而来的喧闹喜悦是深不可测的。随着科学的巨大进步，这将是对勒斯丹所代表的一切的致敬。想想各种可能性！天文台现在可以建造伸向天空的管道，可以在坚不可摧的雪橇上移动，我们将获得的财富不可估量。胜利以科学的名义宣告，古老的荣耀已回归勒斯丹。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
THE MIDDLE DAWN<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
1E1200-2208: The Dragon Break. Scholar-priests of the Alessian Order tamper with the Dragon God of Time.<BR>
<BR>
A fanatical sect of the Alessian Order, the Maruhkati Selective, becomes frustrated by ancient Aldmeri traditions still present within the theological system of the Eight Divines. Specifically, they hated any admission that Akatosh, the Supreme Spirit, was indisputably also Auriel, the Elven High God.<BR>
<BR>
Newly invented rituals were utilized to disprove this theory, to no avail. Finally, the secret masters of the Maruhkati Selective channeled the Aurbis itself to mythically remove those aspects of the Dragon God they disapproved of. A staff or tower appeared before them. The secret masters danced on it until it writhed and trembled and spoke its protonymic.<BR>
<BR>
The tower split into eight pieces and Time broke. The non-linearity of the Dawn Era had returned.<BR>
<BR>
Tamriel slept through the disaster, which 'lasted one thousand and eight years', until the pieces of the tower came to rest on the mortal plane.<BR>
<BR>
Every culture on Tamriel remembers the Dragon Break in some fashion; to most it is a spiritual anguish that they cannot account for. Several texts survive this timeless period, all (unsurprisingly) conflicting with each other regarding events, people, and regions: wars are mentioned in some that never happen in another, the sun changes color depending on the witness, and the gods either walk among the mortals or they don't. Even the 'one thousand and eight years,' a number (some say arbitrarily) chosen by the Elder Council, is an unreliable measure.<BR>
<BR>
Whether or not the secret masters of the Maruhkati Selective were successful is unknown, and any records of their survival were destroyed by the War of Righteousness that ended the Alessian Order a hundred years later.<BR>

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_MilitaryTacticsTR
Military Tactics in the New Era
新时代军事战术

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_MilitaryTacticsTR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<FONT><B>Military Tactics for the New Era</B></FONT><BR>
-Published in 3E26 <BR>
<FONT>by Calonus Cetero, ex-Legion officer, patriot</FONT><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
As we all know, the Imperial army is by far the greatest military force ever to have been formed. This fact is undeniable. However, part of the Legion's greatness rests in its ability to transform tactically and strategically with each passing era. With this new age of general peace and stability, the greatest threats are the dissatisfied, particularly the peasantry, the Dunmer, and upstart revolutionaries or religious leaders using either of these groups. Therefore, I will address each with regard to their potential tactics, strengths and weaknesses, and ways to deal with the situation.<BR>
<BR>
<FONT>The Peasantry</FONT>
<BR>
Combat with the peasantry of Tamriel cannot be engaged in the same manner as that of general warfare; there are a number of vast differences between the trained armies against which the Legions fought and the average peasant militia. First of all, peasants lack the training of a true military force, and there is rarely a semblance of organization amongst their ranks. This means that they will rarely manage to take advantage of a momentary lapse in judgement on the part of their enemies. They will not be able to deliver a truly decisive strike. However, because they lack a commander, there is no true target; whereas an ordinary military force would be crippled by the death of their leader, a peasant militia is protected from such damage. In their case the role of leader rarely belongs to one individual alone.<BR>
<BR>
The strength of the peasantry lies not in their numbers (although there is the potential for them to rapidly draw upon almost anyone in the populace), but in their methodology of warfare. Typically, a force of peasants will avoid direct confrontation in battle and there are several factors working towards this. Despite its presentation as a mass, a mob of peasants remains a collection of individuals. An individual peasant is principally interested in avoiding, if at all possible, personal injury. The consequence of this that peasant mobs once forced into a confrontation tend towards making a show of force,
presenting a fearsomely threatening appearance, in the hopes that the opposing force will back down before any blood is drawn whatsoever. If the opposing force does not back down and actually closes in then the peasant mob will often, given the opportunity, retreat. Occasionally circumstances dictate that the opportunity is either missed or does not exist and fighting is unavoidable. More often a peasant mob will make a deliberate choice to attack based on perceived advantages of time and place. In most cases, their fighting method is a species of hit and run, the idea being that they strike rapidly and do as much damage in as short a time as possible and then get away in the confusion before the target can recover. If the mob has sufficient leadership, this can be done repeatedly. Because of their nature, they may, after each encounter, melt into the general population fairly easily. The difficulty in fighting peasant mobs is one of bringing them to a decisive battle, something which they almost always avoid. By conducting guerilla campaigns, peasant forces have often been successful in frustrating bodies of trained legions for extended periods.<BR>
<BR>
While there are difficulties, there remain three primary advantages the legion has over the mob. The first is commitment, the capacity to simply outlast any peasant rebellion. Even if an entire legion is dismembered the empire will always maintain the resources to recoup losses that would be fatal to its enemies. Another is that the legion is a regular employer of spies, ensuring that information regarding peasant leaders and their movements is obtainable. Intelligence gathering also presents a legion commander opportunities to force by entrapment the conditions for a decisive encounter. Once such an encounter is engineered then the discipline of the legion almost always succeeds, the surprised peasants are quickly broken and upon turning their backs to flee present irresistibly easy targets. Commitment, intelligence and discipline will always run down the mob.<BR>
<BR>
<FONT>The Dunmer</FONT>
<BR>
In general, the Dunmer harbor the greatest resentment towards the Empire and pose the greatest threat to its security. Because the potential for widespread insurrection in Morrowind exists, I will address tactics for both individual battles and for war in general.<BR>
<BR>
The Dunmer have proven that they are capable of employing a wide range of means necessary to triumph in battle. Their fervor is unmatched by any Tamrielic race, and they are well-adapted to their homeland, giving them a great advantage in any revolt they might organize. For these reasons, Tiber Septim himself decided that it would be best not to actually battle them for supremacy in their homeland.<BR>
<BR>
The Dunmer usually fight wearing a light armor made from the resources of Morrowind - there are very few metals, and they can't afford to use them for armor. They call this armor bonemold, and it has surprisingly good protective properties for its light weight. Furthermore, this lighter armor allows for increased mobility amongst their forces. Coupled with their knowledge of the land, the Dunmer forces possess incredible speed in their own lands. Therefore, they primarily fight using guerilla tactics, moving in and hitting their enemies quickly before withdrawing to the safety of the wilderness. Should a commander have the opportunity to fight Dunmer forces in a pitched battle, he should take it. The heavy Imperial armor gives the Emperor's troops an advantage in these situations and being able to subvert the Dunmer preference for mobility gives them another. However, be warned. The ardor of the Dunmer forces gives them their greatest advantage. In battle, particularly with foreigners or invaders, the Dunmer will fight with a dangerous ferocity derived from their devotion to their lands and their gods, the enigmatic Tribunal. Little is known about these deities, but they are said to be called the "Living Gods," gods who walk amongst the people. Perhaps this is why the Dunmer feel such closeness to their divinities. Regardless, they will fight to the death for their homeland.<BR>
<BR>
The climate of Morrowind unfortunately works to prevent the use of horses and other beasts useful to the Legion. The animals cannot handle to diseases carried on the strange winds of Morrowind. Also, the Dunmer have a taste for horse-meat, and when emissaries travel to Morrowind, they usually don't get to come back in a carriage if they brought one.<BR>
<BR>
The advantage the Legion has over the forces of Morrowind is quite simple and has been mentioned earlier: the Empire has far superior resources. The Imperial Legion can draw on forces from all over Tamriel to build an army, whereas the Dunmer are isolated and without allies. The Imperial forces have the possibility of simply overwhelming the Dunmer armies should an insurrection get out of hand. Secondly, the Dunmer are not entirely united. Morrowind houses five major factions, which call themselves Great Houses. The five are called House Indoril, House Dres, House Hlaalu, House Redoran, and House Telvanni. House Hlaalu has created a strong relationship with the Empire and is not likely to want its expulsion from Morrowind. Therefore, they would side with the Legion if war were to come. Considering that they are located primarily along the western border of Morrowind, the Imperial Legion could easily transport troops through the mountains via their lands, and supply lines could easily be maintained by this alliance.<BR>
<BR>
The first objective the Imperial forces should meet in a war with the Dunmer would be the capture of all major Dunmer cities. The Dunmer would be forced to fight an open battle to preserve their cities, and the Imperial forces would be able to seize the advantage. If possible, a commander should prevent the Dunmer armies from retreating to the wilds; a guerilla war is the last thing the Legion wants to deal with. The second objective would be to locate and take prisoner the so-called "Living Gods." This would be a death-blow to the morale of the Dunmer armies and could potentially end a war very quickly. Finally, the Imperial Legion would have to initiate a campaign to slaughter the remnants of the armies hidden in the forests and mountains of Morrowind, a very painful but necessary task. The Dunmer are quite likely to fight to the bitter end, and it is the Legion's responsibility to give them that end.<BR>
<BR>
Overall, the Dunmer - if handled properly - are by no means an impossible foe for the Imperial Legion. While war is the least desirable outcome of Morrowind's occupation, we must always be ready to fight.<BR>
<BR>
<FONT>Revolutionaries and Religious Leaders</FONT>
<BR>
Revolutionaries and religious leaders present a very different kind of challenge to the safety of the Empire. These people can give rise to sudden dissent almost anywhere throughout the Empire. Furthermore, they can manipulate any group to do their bidding, particularly those groups mentioned above. Oftentimes, a Legion commander cannot deal with them as directly as one might hope; the martyrdom of a charismatic leader can potentially rally others to his cause, leaving the Legion with a larger problem than the one with which he began.<BR>
<BR>
In general, the rise of a revolutionary or religious leader follows the same kind of path. Revolutionaries will spring up more commonly in large cities where they can quickly spread their message and rouse a large number of people. Usually, they begin with a close order of loyal followers created from their friends and family, and then they begin
publishing pamphlets to incite the populace against the ruling force. Any military commander who discovers free-floating pamphlets around the base should immediately initiate an investigation of the barracks using only his most trusted officers - any soldier may have been seduced by the revolutionary, and a pamphlet rarely reveals the more insidious nature hidden beneath the veil. Furthermore, the commander should alert
the government about the existence of organized resistance to law and order. Religious leaders, however, will usually rise from the god-fearing and superstitious areas of the land; most commonly, these are farmlands and rural districts. Because Imperial Law is rarely as well enforced out in the countryside as it is in the cities, these
insurgents are able to speak publicly against the government without the moderating effect of a military presence. A great speaker can empty entire towns, and patrols sent out into the countryside should be asked to report any strange emptiness found in smaller towns.<BR>
<BR>
The strength of a revolutionary leader or religious leader resides in his natural, inborn charisma, something entirely impossible to combat. Cut out his tongue and people will be drawn to his silence, cut his throat and the people will be drawn to his sacrifice. Indeed, even death cannot dispel the aura of a truly gifted and charismatic leader; like a father, he is capable of extracting the loyalty and admiration of his followers. It is best to deny the insurgent even the right to speak to the Legion's soldiers; his tongue can cloud their minds and sway them from their duty to protect the Empire.<BR>
<BR>
The control and containment of these threats requires a more delicate hand than the one used in dealing with local drunks or the like. In truth, the correct response depends on the situation. I will describe a few ways in which you can deal with the problem. The first way a commander can try to solve this kind of problem is to arrest and execute the culprit. This has the highest probability of succeeding early in the revolutionary or religious leader's career, before they have had a chance to gather a large amount of support. If this is done too late, it can backfire and leave the commander with a number of the insurgent's most loyal followers rallying his cause and drawing in more commoners. The second potential measure a commander can take is to bribe away the insurgent's followers via gold, food, women, etc. Without his support base, the leader with simply wither away and can be dealt with accordingly. If the insurgent decides to attack the Legion or the populace of a town, it is sometimes best to kill him in the fray instead of taking him prisoner, but only if the battle is a sure victory for the Legion's forces. Should their leader die in the middle of a glorious victory, it is likely that the leader's followers will rally around the incredible sacrifice he made for them. When a revolutionary or religious leader has established himself in one location, sometimes the use of more subtle means can have great effect in destroying the morale of the enemy. For example, if an insurgent bases himself in a small town, a commander can send diseased meat or blankets in the guise of a gift from supporters far away. Once they begin to see their undoing, many of the leader's followers will simply abandon the insurrection and return to their homes.<BR>
<BR>
Always bear in mind that these revolutionaries and religious leaders could bring the destruction of the Empire the great Tiber Septim forged by conquest and sacrifice. Eternal vigilance can protect this great empire which all of us hold dear to our hearts; laxity and levity can bring its demise. Remember this, my brothers, and you will serve this kingdom well.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<FONT><B>新时代军事战术</B></FONT><BR>
-第三纪元26年出版<BR>
<FONT>卡洛努斯·塞特罗 著，前军团军官，爱国者</FONT><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
众所周知，帝国军队是迄今为止有史以来最伟大的军事力量。这一事实不可否认。然而，军团的伟大之处部分在于其随着每个时代的变迁而在战术和战略上进行转变的能力。在这个普遍和平与稳定的新时代，最大的威胁是不满者，特别是农民、丹莫，以及利用这些群体的暴发户革命者或宗教领袖。因此，我将针对每个群体的潜在战术、优势和劣势以及应对方法进行阐述。<BR>
<BR>
<FONT>农民</FONT>
<BR>
与泰姆瑞尔的农民作战不能采用与常规战争相同的方式；军团所对抗的训练有素的军队与普通农民民兵之间存在许多巨大差异。首先，农民缺乏真正军事力量的训练，他们的队伍中很少有组织的迹象。这意味着他们很少能利用敌人判断上的瞬间失误。他们无法发动真正决定性的打击。然而，由于他们缺乏指挥官，就没有真正的目标；而普通军事力量会因领导者的死亡而瘫痪，农民民兵则免受此类伤害。在他们的情况下，领导者的角色很少只属于一个人。<BR>
<BR>
农民的力量不在于人数（尽管他们有可能迅速调动几乎任何民众），而在于他们的作战方式。通常，农民部队会避免直接对抗，有几个因素促成了这一点。尽管表现为一大群人，但农民暴民仍然是个体的集合。一个农民个体主要关心的是尽可能避免人身伤害。其结果是，一旦被迫对抗，农民暴民倾向于展示武力，
呈现可怕威胁的外表，希望对方在流血之前退缩。如果对方不退缩并真正逼近，那么农民暴民往往会在有机会时撤退。偶尔，情况决定了机会要么错过，要么不存在，战斗不可避免。更多时候，农民暴民会根据对时间和地点的优势感知而故意选择攻击。在大多数情况下，他们的战斗方式是一种打了就跑的战术，其理念是快速打击，在尽可能短的时间内造成尽可能多的伤害，然后在目标恢复之前在混乱中逃走。如果暴民有足够的领导力，这可以反复进行。由于他们的性质，每次遭遇后，他们可以相当容易地融入普通民众。与农民暴民作战的困难在于将他们带入一场决定性的战斗，而这正是他们几乎总是避免的。通过进行游击战，农民部队常常能够成功地长期挫败训练有素的军团。<BR>
<BR>
尽管存在困难，但军团相对于暴民仍有三个主要优势。首先是坚持力，即能够简单地熬过任何农民叛乱的能力。即使整个军团被肢解，帝国也总能维持资源来弥补对其敌人而言将是致命的损失。另一个优势是军团经常雇佣间谍，确保能够获得关于农民领袖及其动向的信息。情报收集也为军团指挥官提供了通过诱捕来促成决定性遭遇战条件的机会。一旦策划了这样的遭遇战，军团的纪律几乎总能成功，惊讶的农民很快被击溃，当他们转身逃跑时，就成为极易击中的目标。坚持力、情报和纪律总能拖垮暴民。<BR>
<BR>
<FONT>丹莫</FONT>
<BR>
总的来说，丹莫对帝国怀有最大的怨恨，对其安全构成最大的威胁。由于晨风存在广泛叛乱的可能性，我将阐述针对个人战斗和总体战争的战术。<BR>
<BR>
丹莫已经证明，他们能够运用各种必要手段在战斗中取得胜利。他们的热情是任何泰姆瑞尔种族都无法比拟的，而且他们非常适应自己的家园，这使他们在可能组织的任何叛乱中都具有巨大优势。出于这些原因，泰伯·塞普汀本人决定，最好不要在他们的家园与他们争夺霸权。<BR>
<BR>
丹莫通常穿着用晨风资源制造的轻甲 -- 金属很少，他们无法将金属用于盔甲。他们称这种盔甲为骨模甲，其轻巧的重量具有出奇良好的防护性能。此外，这种较轻的盔甲提高了部队的机动性。结合他们对土地的了解，丹莫部队在自己的土地上拥有难以置信的速度。因此，他们主要使用游击战术进行战斗，快速移动并打击敌人，然后撤退到荒野的安全地带。如果指挥官有机会与丹莫部队进行阵地战，他应该抓住机会。重型帝国盔甲在这些情况下给了皇帝部队优势，而能够颠覆丹莫对机动性的偏好则给了他们另一个优势。然而，要小心。丹莫部队的热情给了他们最大的优势。在战斗中，特别是与外国人或入侵者作战时，丹莫会以一种危险的凶猛作战，这种凶猛源于他们对土地和神秘的神祇 -- 审判席的奉献。关于这些神祇知之甚少，但据说他们被称为“现世神”，行走在人民中间的神。也许这就是丹莫与他们的神祇如此亲近的原因。无论如何，他们会为家园战斗到死。<BR>
<BR>
不幸的是，晨风的气候阻碍了马匹和其他对军团有用的兽类的使用。这些动物无法抵御晨风怪异之风携带的疾病。此外，丹莫喜欢吃马肉，当使者前往晨风时，如果他们带了马车，通常无法坐马车回来。<BR>
<BR>
军团相对于晨风部队的优势非常简单，前面已经提到：帝国拥有远远优越的资源。帝国军团可以调动整个泰姆瑞尔的力量来组建军队，而丹莫孤立无援，没有盟友。如果叛乱失控，帝国军队有可能直接压垮丹莫军队。其次，丹莫并非完全统一。晨风有五个主要派系，自称“豪族”。这五个豪族分别是：因多瑞尔家族、德雷斯家族、哈拉鲁家族、勒多兰家族和泰瓦尼家族。哈拉鲁家族与帝国建立了牢固的关系，不太可能希望帝国被逐出晨风。因此，如果战争来临，他们会站在军团一边。考虑到他们主要位于晨风西部边境沿线，帝国军团可以通过他们的土地轻松地在山区运送军队，而且这个联盟可以轻松维持补给线。<BR>
<BR>
帝国部队在与丹莫的战争中应实现的第一个目标是占领所有主要的丹莫城市。丹莫将被迫进行公开战斗以保卫他们的城市，而帝国部队将能够抓住优势。如果可能，指挥官应阻止丹莫军队撤退到荒野；游击战是军团最不想面对的。第二个目标是找到并俘虏所谓的“现世神”。这将是对丹莫军队士气的致命打击，并可能非常迅速地结束战争。最后，帝国军团必须发起一场战役，屠杀隐藏在晨风森林和山脉中的残余部队，这是一项非常痛苦但必要的任务。丹莫很可能会战斗到最后一刻，而军团的责任就是让他们走到那个结局。<BR>
<BR>
总的来说，如果处理得当，丹莫对帝国军团来说绝非不可战胜的敌人。尽管战争是占领晨风最不理想的结果，但我们必须随时准备战斗。<BR>
<BR>
<FONT>革命者和宗教领袖</FONT>
<BR>
革命者和宗教领袖对帝国的安全构成了截然不同的挑战。这些人几乎可以在帝国任何地方引发突然的异议。此外，他们可以操纵任何群体为其效力，尤其是上述群体。很多时候，军团指挥官无法像人们希望的那样直接对付他们；一位魅力领袖的殉难可能会使其他人聚集到他的事业中，给军团留下比最初更大的问题。<BR>
<BR>
一般来说，革命者或宗教领袖的崛起遵循类似的路径。革命者更常见于大城市，在那里他们可以迅速传播信息并鼓动大量民众。通常，他们从由朋友和家人组成的紧密忠诚追随者开始，然后开始散发小册子以煽动民众反对统治力量。任何在基地周围发现散落小册子的军事指挥官应立即使用最信任的军官对营房进行调查 -- 任何士兵都可能被革命者诱惑，而小册子很少揭示隐藏在其面纱下的更阴险本质。此外，指挥官应警告政府存在有组织的对法律和秩序的抵抗。然而，宗教领袖通常来自该地区敬畏神和迷信的地区；最常见的是农田和农村地区。由于帝国法律在农村的执行力度很少像在城市那样有力，这些叛乱分子能够在没有军事存在缓和效应的情况下公开反对政府。一位伟大的演说家可以使整个城镇空无一人，应要求派往乡村的巡逻队报告在小城镇发现的任何奇怪的空旷情况。
然后开始散发小册子以煽动民众反对统治力量。任何在基地周围发现散落小册子的军事指挥官应立即使用最信任的军官对营房进行调查 -- 任何士兵都可能被革命者诱惑，而小册子很少揭示隐藏在其面纱下的更阴险本质。此外，指挥官应警告政府
存在有组织的对法律和秩序的抵抗。然而，宗教领袖通常来自该地区敬畏神和迷信的地区；最常见的是农田和农村地区。由于帝国法律在农村的执行力度很少像在城市那样有力，这些
叛乱分子能够在没有军事存在缓和效应的情况下公开反对政府。一位伟大的演说家可以使整个城镇空无一人，应要求派往乡村的巡逻队报告在小城镇发现的任何奇怪的空旷情况。<BR>
<BR>
革命领袖或宗教领袖的力量在于其天生的、与生俱来的魅力，这是完全无法对抗的东西。割掉他的舌头，人们会被他的沉默所吸引；割断他的喉咙，人们会被他的牺牲所吸引。事实上，即使是死亡也无法驱散真正有天赋和魅力的领袖的光环；如同父亲一般，他能够获得追随者的忠诚和钦佩。最好是连叛乱分子与军团士兵说话的权利都剥夺；他的舌头会迷惑他们的思想，使他们偏离保护帝国的职责。<BR>
<BR>
控制和遏制这些威胁需要比对付当地醉汉之类更细腻的手段。事实上，正确的应对措施取决于具体情况。我将描述几种可以处理该问题的方法。指挥官可以尝试解决这类问题的第一种方法是逮捕并处决肇事者。这在革命或宗教领袖职业生涯早期、在他们有机会获得大量支持之前成功的可能性最高。如果做得太晚，可能会适得其反，使指挥官面对一群叛乱者最忠诚的追随者，他们会聚集起来支持他的事业，并吸引更多平民。指挥官可以采取的第二种潜在措施是用金币、食物、女人等贿赂叛乱者的追随者。没有了支持基础，领袖就会消亡，并可以相应地被处理。如果叛乱者决定攻击军团或某个城镇的居民，有时最好在混战中杀死他而不是俘虏他，但这只有在军团部队确保胜利的情况下才行。如果他们的领袖在一场辉煌的胜利中死去，领袖的追随者很可能会聚集在他为他们所做的不可思议的牺牲周围。当革命或宗教领袖在某地站稳脚跟时，有时使用更微妙的手段可以对摧毁敌人的士气产生巨大效果。例如，如果一个叛乱者以小城镇为基地，指挥官可以以远方支持者礼物的名义发送病肉或毯子。一旦他们开始看到自己的毁灭，许多领袖的追随者就会干脆放弃叛乱，返回家园。<BR>
<BR>
永远记住，这些革命者和宗教领袖可能会带来由伟大的泰伯·塞普汀通过征服和牺牲所建立的帝国的毁灭。永恒的警惕可以保护这个我们所有人心爱的伟大帝国；松懈和轻浮会导致它的灭亡。记住这一点，我的兄弟们，你们将很好地服务于这个王国。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>百万眼虫之梦 -- 维洛斯的两次征服<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>残篇<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>......除了达格斯-沙玛特，他们都陷入了对变形魔奥姆希维的崇拜。这个曾为凡人的雌雄同体怪物以三个人的形态出现，每个人都是高等迪德拉之一的漫画式模仿。奥姆希维最初以苏尔-阿兰卓（古代霍塔特尼瑞瓦的持盾者）的梦生二重身出现。<BR>
<BR>
在第一纪元中期，恶魔追逐那对圣洁的伴侣 -- 他们因悲剧而闻名整个泰姆瑞尔 -- 进入巴鲁尔的心脏地带，在那里，末日之鼓消失在烈焰与灰烬的炽热地狱中。尼瑞瓦的谋杀迅速而无预兆（直到今天，家族精灵仍以虚假的圣徒身份嘲弄他的记忆；他们将他描绘成一具被倒挂的骷髅）。阿兰卓目睹了这罪行，在曾经黎明时代最伟大利维坦幽灵居住的深坑之门前，苏尔氏族的儿子站在自己的二重身面前，身穿甲壳素和先祖的灰烬。他的思想被奥姆希维从颅骨中炸飞，他所目睹的一切永远地展现在他的链甲兜帽“怨魂之铠”上。随着时间的推移，这兜帽被拆成链环，链环被拆成小环，小环被制成穿孔饰品，以至于现在，即使是最偏远地区、在内皮帐篷集会中的每个灰烬可汗和玛布里加什，都能听到苏尔·阿兰卓在他们耳边的神圣低语。<BR>
<BR>
随后发生的事无需解释，因为红色时刻的地质后果已记录在所有泰姆瑞尔有文字文化的编年史中。穿越梦境时间，恶魔奥姆希维绑架并锁链了古代先知维洛斯。那个难以言表的怪物在他心中播下虚假的疑虑，并通过煽动这些疑虑来诱惑他。撒谎之王崔尼马克的声音现在向他灌输恐惧，因为它说的是奥姆希维的话，而非波耶西亚的话。虚假的幻象出现在他眼前，他的生命变成了一场无尽的痛苦与折磨的风暴，在一个超越严酷时间的瞬间，维洛斯的灵魂被粉碎了。这位通常坚忍不拔的先知因愤怒和痛苦而剧烈抽搐，以至于他撕裂了自己喉咙的肉，以便能大声尖叫。在这软弱的时刻，维洛斯被奥姆希维令人作呕的卷须缠住，并被带到了一个充满恶意恶魔的梦境中，那些恶魔已有无数纪元未在地面上行走。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Mineral Resource Potentials of Morrowind <BR> 
by Apelle Dubilius, EEC Prospector <BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
The mineral resources that lie within the province of Morrowind are vast, likely due to the geologic activity lent to the area by the volcanic Red Mountain. Indeed, the lands of the Dark Elves can be counted among the most productive in all the Empire in terms of mineral deposits. There do not appear to be especially dense concentrations of particular minerals in any given locale; rather, different minerals, all of impressive value, are spread around the Province. Some of the more rare and valuable minerals contained within Morrowind are raw ebony, raw glass, adamantium and gold. Morrowind is not limited to these alone, as there are also modest amounts of precious and semi-precious gemstones such as emerald, rubies, diamonds, opals and amethyst. Recent assessment parties assigned to the frozen island of Solstheim have also indicated that further opportunities may exist there. <BR>
<BR>
Adamantium is one of the most precious and rarest minerals within the Province. The primary use of adamantium is in the production of weapons and armor, although it can also be wrought into fine art for the extremely wealthy. The metal is very durable, but it is also quite weighty. In the hands of all but the strongest soldiers adamantium weapons can become unwieldy, and the exhaustion that comes of swinging such weapons or wearing such armor makes it impractical for prolonged use. The price of the raw material also prevents its use in a scale that would be needed for war. The simple lack of adamantium, coupled with its weight and rarity do not usually make it a good investment for the fighting warrior. While adamantium can be found all around the province in small quantities, it is not known to be found on Vvardenfell. Due to its scarcity, it is not economically advantageous to establish any adamantium mines in Morrowind. Adventurers have been known to brave the depths of Old Mournhold in search of adamantium deposits known to lie beneath the sacred city. <BR>
<BR>
Ebony is valuable and useful, and relatively abundant in the Province. As with adamantium, ebony has the drawback of being ridiculously heavy, although in the right hands, it serves exceptionally well as protective armor, as well as lethal weapons of high quality and durability. Many ebony weapons are in existence, most notably in the service of Ordinators, but the armor is a good deal rarer and harder to come by. Some fortunate (and rich) nobles or adventurers own pieces of ebony armor, but the person with a full suit is a rare individual. Raw Ebony itself is heavy, and even a small load will encumber the mightiest, making transportation of large amounts of the mineral completely impractical except by ship. Currently, the ebony industry in Morrowind is modest, and we should look to expand it due the obvious potential for profit. Although ebony is known to exist throughout the province, it is often found very deep underground, making the initial stages of mining uncommonly expensive. Currently, there are a few large operations extracting ebony, such as the mine near Caldera, several on the mainland, and a number of smaller mines within the Red Mountain region and the Ashlands. Currently, a good deal of prospecting is in progress in an attempt to expand the ebony trade in Morrowind. The most recent example of our efforts being the proposed mine on the isle of Solstheim, provided ore tests produce sufficient yield, and the frozen grounds do not impede progress drastically. <BR>
<BR>
Gold is both malleable, and ductile, as well as highly valuable. Most of the Empire's gold comes from the West, and little is found in Morrowind, with none at all on Vvardenfell. This makes gold a very highly prized item, and although it is encumbering, it makes for an excellent form of currency. Should there be a shortage of money, gold can always be traded. Other than funding, the practical uses of gold are few, due to its weight and malleability, it can be forged to form armor, but this armor is both expensive, and not terribly strong. Due to lack of gold in Morrowind, it wouldn't be effective to begin mining operations, not when it can be mined on the Western side of Tamriel for much less. <BR>
<BR>
Glass is one of the most unique materials in the Province. It is light, and yet still reasonably durable, making remarkably sturdy light armors and weapons. Glass is also relatively rare and quite costly, so few complete suits of armor are known of. Popular among the Armigers, one could also expect that several of the Great Houses might possess numerous pieces. Glass weapons are also of high quality, with razor edges and slight heft. Another valuable property of glass is the enchanting potential it contains. Glass weapons are prized among enchanters, who can make excellent fire, frost and poison blades with them, to name but just a few. The weakness of glass weapons lie in their durability, being nowhere near as reliable as adamantium, ebony, or a small host of lesser materials. To add to the already costly price of glass, very few smiths are trained and skilled in the creation of glass items. House Telvanni has interests in the expansion of glass mining, probably to add to their profits from enchanting and selling, along with raw glass's unique alchemical properties. At the moment, plans for expansion of the glass industry by the East Empire Company have not yet been discussed, and although House Telvanni is planning on taking the matter into their own hands, restrictions and pressure from the Empire are expected. <BR>
<BR>
Iron is another mineral that is located in the Province of Morrowind that is not to be ignored. While it doesn't exist copiously, and isn't nearly as valuable as the others, it can be said that iron is a far more effective metal than some of the others. As a raw mineral, the value is small, but once extracted it can be forged into many tools and weapons. As a bonus, when iron is mixed with carbon, a much stronger alloy appears, steel. Steel is one of the most widely used metals in all of the Empire, due to its strength, and its malleability. At the moment, there is little need to expand the potential of the East Empire Company's abilities to acquire iron in the Province of Morrowind. The yield simply wouldn't be high enough, and it isn't valuable enough to warrant the inherent expenses for working in such a volatile land.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
晨风矿产资源潜力<BR>
阿佩莱·杜比利乌斯 著，东帝国公司探矿者<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
晨风行省内的矿产资源丰富，这可能是由于该地区火山红山的地质活动所致。事实上，就矿产储量而言，丹莫的土地可以被认为是整个帝国中产量最高的地区之一。在任何特定地点，似乎都没有特别密集的特定矿物；相反，不同种类的矿物，都具有令人印象深刻的价值，散布在整个行省。晨风境内一些较为稀有和珍贵的矿物包括黑檀矿、玻璃矿、精金和黄金。晨风不仅限于这些，还有少量的珍贵和半珍贵宝石，如祖母绿、红宝石、钻石、蛋白石和紫水晶。最近被派往冰冻岛屿索瑟泰姆的评估小组也表明，那里可能存在更多机会。<BR>
<BR>
精金是该行省中最珍贵、最稀有的矿物之一。精金的主要用途是制造武器和盔甲，尽管它也可以为极其富有的人锻造成精美的艺术品。这种金属非常耐用，但也相当沉重。除了最强壮的士兵外，精金武器在其他人手中可能会变得笨重，挥舞此类武器或穿戴此类盔甲所带来的疲劳使其不适合长时间使用。原材料的价格也使其无法达到战争所需的规模。仅仅是由于精金的缺乏，加上其重量和稀有性，通常使其对战斗战士来说不是一项好的投资。虽然在整个行省可以少量找到精金，但已知在瓦登费尔并未发现。由于其稀缺性，在晨风建立任何精金矿在经济上并无优势。已知有冒险者勇敢地探索旧哀伤之城的深处，寻找已知位于这座神圣城市下方的精金矿床。<BR>
<BR>
黑檀木有价值且有用，在该行省相对丰富。与精金一样，黑檀木也有极其沉重的缺点，尽管在合适的人手中，它作为防护盔甲以及高质量、耐用的致命武器表现出色。存在许多黑檀木武器，最显著的是在神殿卫兵中使用，但盔甲则稀有得多，也更难获得。一些幸运（且富有）的贵族或冒险者拥有黑檀木盔甲部件，但拥有全套盔甲的人是罕见的。黑檀矿本身很重，即使少量也会使最强壮的人负重，使得大量运输这种矿物完全不切实际，除非通过船只。目前，晨风的黑檀木产业规模不大，由于其明显的盈利潜力，我们应该寻求扩大它。尽管已知整个行省都存在黑檀木，但它通常位于地下很深的地方，使得采矿的初始阶段异常昂贵。目前，有一些大型作业在开采黑檀木，例如卡尔德拉附近的矿场、大陆上的几个矿场，以及红山地区和灰烬之地内的一些小型矿场。目前，正在进行大量勘探，试图扩大晨风的黑檀木贸易。我们努力的最新例子是在索瑟泰姆岛上拟建的矿场，前提是矿石测试能产生足够的产量，并且冰冻的地面不会严重阻碍进展。<BR>
<BR>
黄金既具有延展性又具有韧性，而且价值极高。帝国的大部分黄金来自西方，在晨风发现的很少，在瓦登费尔则根本没有。这使得黄金成为非常珍贵的物品，尽管它会增加负重，但它是一种极好的货币形式。如果出现资金短缺，黄金总是可以用来交易。除了资金之外，黄金的实际用途很少，由于其重量和延展性，它可以被锻造成盔甲，但这种盔甲既昂贵又不太坚固。由于晨风缺乏黄金，开始采矿作业并不划算，尤其是当可以在泰姆瑞尔西部以低得多的成本开采时。<BR>
<BR>
玻璃是该行省最独特的材料之一。它很轻，但又相当耐用，从而制造出非常坚固的轻甲和武器。玻璃也相对稀有且相当昂贵，因此已知的完整盔甲套装很少。它在灵动扈从中很受欢迎，也可以预料到几个豪族可能拥有许多件。玻璃武器质量也很高，刀刃锋利，重量轻盈。玻璃的另一个宝贵特性是其包含的附魔潜力。玻璃武器在附魔师中备受推崇，他们可以用它们制造出优秀的火焰、冰霜和毒药之刃，仅举几例。玻璃武器的弱点在于其耐久性，远不如精金、黑檀木或一小部分较低级材料可靠。除了玻璃本已昂贵的价格之外，很少有铁匠接受过制造玻璃物品的培训和技能。泰瓦尼家族对扩大玻璃开采感兴趣，可能是为了增加他们从附魔和销售中获得的利润，以及玻璃矿独特的炼金特性。目前，东帝国公司尚未讨论扩大玻璃产业的计划，尽管泰瓦尼家族正打算自行处理此事，但预计会受到帝国的限制和压力。<BR>
<BR>
铁是晨风行省中另一种不容忽视的矿物。虽然它并不大量存在，价值也远不如其他矿物，但可以说铁是一种比某些其他矿物有效得多的金属。作为一种原始矿物，其价值很小，但一旦开采出来，它可以锻造成许多工具和武器。另外，当铁与碳混合时，会产生一种更强的合金 -- 钢。钢由于其强度和延展性，是整个帝国中使用最广泛的金属之一。目前，几乎没有必要扩大东帝国公司在晨风行省获取铁的能力。产量根本不够高，而且其价值不足以证明在这片动荡的土地上工作的固有费用是合理的。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Mixed Unit Tactics in the Five Years War<BR>
Volume Three<BR>
By Codus Callonus<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The primary field of battle near Dune was a long stretch of grassland between the trees of Valenwood and the sands of Elsweyr. After the chaotic back-and-forth of the first year, the Khajiit held this stretch of land for months at a time and expanded it by cutting more trees across the old border. Many of the trees were carried off by the great Senche-raht. A few were taken into the city of Dune and their use became apparent during the siege.<BR>
<BR>
During the war, this process was rapid and easily seen, but the Khajiit and Bosmer in the Legion informed me that it had been going on long before the Third Era. This is how the unofficial border between Elsweyr and Valenwood is marked. The Khajiit cut down the trees, the Bosmer replant them, the Khajiit dig tunnels to undermine them, the Bosmer flood the tunnels to kill the Khajiit and make the desert bloom, and so on for centuries.<BR>
<BR>
The rapid shift from desert to grassland to forest is unique in all of Tamriel and may be the result of this constant cutting and re-planting. I asked Ja'Dhuzar, the only Khajiit I trusted and a fellow Legionnaire, about this the next day. At first he just repeated the common saying in Elsweyr that "wide deserts make good neighbors." Eventually he said, and I believe I wrote this down exactly, even if it makes little sense, "Do not weep for trees. Valenwood is a sholath (a kind of sand-burrowing crab). The trees are the fingers of Y'ffre who stretches, then grasps. If the forest grows too wide, it is another moon-dance of suffering, the shaper could finish her sculptures, and Ja'Dhuzar is clever enough already, don't you think?"<BR>
<BR>
It seemed as if the Bosmer began to realize the Khajiit in the north were not as serious a threat as they first appeared and began moving troops south. The Khajiit likewise gave up the tree-cutting, fires, and raids into northern areas when the Bosmer stopped responding with larger forces. The Khajiit soon tired of the sport and broke up their largest camps and left only a minor defensive and scouting force in the area along with the usual "peacetime" (if this province has ever known it) garrison in the city proper.<BR>
<BR>
A few months after the main Khajiti force left, the Bosmer led an enormous attack and took all the Khajiti camps around Dune. The Khajiit sent scouts into the forest regularly, but even so the Khajiti camp was taken by surprise. I heard rumors later that the Bosmer caught the scouts, flayed them alive, wore their skins, and, with the aid of illusions, fooled the Khajiit into thinking the scouts continued patrolling and reporting. I heard also that the Bosmer led scouts into ambushes and used forbidden arts to re-animate them long enough to make a report. Either way, this proves beyond any doubt that the Empire must continue its effort to civilize the Bosmer.<BR>
<BR>
The commander of Fort Sphinxmoth, Gaius Apinius, wanted to send his own patrols and scouts into the surrounding areas, but we were under strict orders not to leave the fort, except to patrol the road from Dune to Riverhold and protect the few Imperial interests in the area. Of course, we all learned later those orders were those of the usurper.<BR>
<BR>
As a result, neither the Legions nor the Khajiit expected hundreds of naked Bosmer to run screaming out of the trees, covered with symbols drawn in blood, and followed by a howling menagerie of every wicked forest beast. The battle took place too far from the fort to see without a spyglass, and the dim light of a gibbous Masser was not enough to make out the full battle, but the unholy racket woke the whole fort. We stood on alert, sharing a half dozen spyglasses, and tried to follow the battle as best we could. I am no expert on Valenwood's fauna, and the view as I said was very poor, but we all agreed there were beasts out there unlike anything we had seen. The Bosmer attack looked wild and unplanned, but they used clever, if strange and dishonorable, tactics.<BR>
<BR>
Roughly one cohort of Bosmer archers and wizards, much more in control than the rest, climbed the remaining trees for range and defense before the attack. The blood-painted Bosmer had spells or enchantments upon them. They could do something, perhaps upon their death, which lit up the symbols painted upon them, making the Khajiit nearby easy targets for the archers that remained in the trees. The Bosmer spread out and ran towards the largest camps and groups of Khajiit, glowing as bright as dawn for a short while, and that whole area was soon covered with arrows. The Legions fight in large formations wherever possible, and I fear the Khajiti tactics here might be effective against an unprepared Legion. The Legions are trained to use the dreugh or mudcrab formations where we can defend from attacks on all sides, but the fire pots and hit-and-run tactics might still disrupt a Legion cohort. The Bosmer had greater numbers, siege engines, and their famous archers, but they did not have the training or equipment to form up into something like the mudcrab, and they were routed. I have shared information privately with my superiors on how the Legion's use of javelins, shield formations, and our cavalry could defend against similar tactics, but my efforts to show how small, fast units can win against larger, less mobile units has not yet been incorporated into the Legions' drills and training.<BR>

最后，还有小群地面部队，主要是体型较小的类人卡吉特，装备有投石索矛。当波斯莫部队与重甲部队交战或被火罐分散注意力时，他们会接近并用投石索向波斯莫投掷石块。如果波斯莫转身与他们交战，他们会逃跑或用长矛冲锋，而另一支类似的投石索矛部队会从后方攻击波斯莫。<BR>
<BR>
这些部队单独无法赢得战斗，但他们巧妙地联合了力量。较小、更机动的小队很脆弱，但不断从后方或侧翼攻击波斯莫，以稳定的消耗削弱了人数更多的波斯莫部队。军团尽可能以大型编队作战，我担心卡吉特在这里的战术可能对毫无准备的军团有效。军团接受过使用蟹灵或泥沼蟹阵型的训练，可以防御来自四面八方的攻击，但火罐和打了就跑的战术仍可能干扰军团大队。波斯莫人数更多，有攻城器械和著名的弓箭手，但他们没有训练或装备来组成像泥沼蟹那样的阵型，因此被击溃。我已私下与上级分享了关于军团如何使用标枪、盾阵和骑兵来防御类似战术的信息，但我关于小型快速部队如何战胜大型笨重部队的论证尚未纳入军团的演习和训练。<BR>
<BR>
在波斯莫溃败期间，一台投石机转向了堡垒。令我们惊恐的是，投石机发射了两次，第二次击中损坏了堡垒外墙的一部分。<BR>
<BR>
几个优秀的军团士兵本可以在战争第一年就结束战争，但我们接到命令，除非堡垒本身受到攻击，否则不得干预。我是帝国的忠诚公民，但我必须承认，我们从帝都收到的命令毫无道理。要么是指挥官不了解边境情况，要么是幻象想要最大化混乱并削弱他所统治的帝国。疯狂。我建议只给战地指挥官一般性命令，在如何实现帝国目标方面给予广泛回旋余地。即使最好最快的报告也只能描述当地指挥官所知情况的一部分，即使几分钟的延迟（当使用传送来传输关键命令时）也可能决定一场战斗。<BR>
<BR>
首席百夫长阿皮尼乌斯利用这个机会，集结军团，从堡垒出发攻击波斯莫。当波斯莫看到军团接近时，他们放弃了投石机（此时已有四台着火），逃回了边境对面。我们只追到树林边缘，然后返回了堡垒。<BR>
<BR>
事实证明，我们又被奸诈的卡吉特骗了。从城里出来的一支小型卡吉特部队制服了操作那台投石机的波斯莫和因加，并将其转向堡垒。他们预料到我们会离开堡垒作为回应。当我们在城墙外时，另一组卡吉特悬浮过墙，占领了堡垒。堡垒附近有一个卡吉特商人的永久营地，他们向士兵和工作人员出售零食和小饰品（以及 -- 作为军团道德品质下降的标志 -- 其他服务 -- 即使是一个欧姆斯仍然是卡吉特，与他们交往应该受到烙印和开除的惩罚，就像爱马者一样）。营地只有几个帐篷，但卡吉特精锐部队已经来了几个星期，每个帐篷里藏着十二名武装卡吉特和至少一名巫师。<BR>
<BR>
军团中有许多卡吉特和波斯莫成员。由于担心这些成员在激烈战斗中的忠诚度，指挥官将驻扎在斯芬克斯蛾堡的大部分卡吉特和波斯莫分配去防守，而我们其余人则出击。这被证明是另一个错误。我们后来得知，卡吉特几乎无一例外地背叛了他们的战友，在堡垒内制造混乱并打开了大门。当我们投降时，堡垒内所有的波斯莫都被杀了，包括一位厨师的年幼儿子。<BR>
<BR>
当我们返回斯芬克斯蛾堡时，情况非常危急。我们无法轻易进入现在由卡吉特驻守的堡垒，而且我们很快就被那些曾经如此有效地击退波斯莫部队的快速移动的投石机小车包围了。首席百夫长阿皮尼乌斯决定向卡吉特投降，而不是拿我们以及留在堡垒内的士兵和工作人员的生命冒险。<BR>
<BR>
请注意，我不责怪首席百夫长做出这个决定。他是被迫做出的，因为大量卡吉特和波斯莫被不明智地分配到了斯芬克斯蛾堡。鉴于精灵和野兽种族的不可靠性，我强烈建议不要将这些种族分配到其传统土地内或边境上的任何堡垒。即使是卡吉特也可以在军团中光荣服役，但他们应该被分配到晨风、高岩、天际或帝国核心地区的堡垒，在那里背叛的诱惑对他们软弱的本性来说不会太强烈。<BR>
<BR>
这就是斯芬克斯蛾堡陷落的真实故事。它并不是在当今每个卡吉特都声称自己领导的激战中被征服的。军团没有被击败。我们被背叛了。<BR>

Why they never tried to seal the tunnels or took them seriously as a threat, I cannot understand.<BR>

When the Simulacrum was defeated, the rebellious provinces, finally under the threat of the punishment they should have faced from the start, returned to the Empire and Fort Sphinxmoth was likewise reinstated. I was stationed in Narsis and Stormhold for the remainder of my years of service and saw only small, easy battles with disorganized bandits and rebels.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
五年战争中的混合部队战术<BR>
第五卷<BR>
科达斯·卡罗努斯 著<BR><BR>

战争接下来的两年我在沙丘度过，被俘的军团被迫锻造武器、修复城墙、建造下水道系统（我敢说比卡吉特自己能搞定的要好），以及其他市政改进工作。事实上，我们受到的待遇并不像你想象的那么差。我们吃得饱，只有当有人试图逃跑、攻击卡吉特或拒绝工作时才会被打。当红死病在我们的营地肆虐时，卡吉特甚至提供了治疗（来自我见过的最自大、最自命不凡的六七个阿尔菲克）。最令人气愤的经历是前军团士兵贾'杜扎尔的行为，他现在自称德罗'杜扎尔，在城里时会在监狱里昂首阔步，通常双臂各挽着一名同族女性。<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
波斯莫笑到了最后。我们听说南方的战争对瓦伦伍德不利，波斯莫没有足够的力量占领沙丘。他们甚至无法守住自己的领土。这在很大程度上归功于卡吉特在战争早期沿着宰娄河占领并坚守的阵地。波斯莫将一支非常小的部队，不超过二十人，偷偷潜入城中。他们没有发动攻击，而是只是站在他们一条隧道的出口附近，提出了挑战。<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
接下来的战斗是帕玛尔跳跃着向波斯莫挥击，而波斯莫则绕圈后退，通过翻滚、跳跃和扭曲躲避攻击。德罗'扎克萨似乎有点慢下来了，竞技场地上到处都是血迹。他看了看自己的爪子，发现当他打断剑时，剑深深地割伤了他。这激怒了他，他更加疯狂和凶猛地攻击。<BR>
<BR>
此时卡吉特变得紧张起来。他们没有得到预期的快速、轻松的胜利。波斯莫专注于躲避，设法避开了几乎所有的攻击，尽管德罗'扎克萨击中一次显然造成了伤害。波斯莫的木甲被爪痕划伤，它身上的任何附魔都开始消退。<BR>
<BR>
很快，波斯莫几乎可以在竞技场上闲庭信步了，而德罗'扎克萨则在血泊中跌跌撞撞。卡吉特到最后还是诡计多端，他假装比实际更虚弱，差点就挥中波斯莫，但那之后结果就确定了。“出血毒，”德罗'杜扎尔在我旁边说，“聪明。”<BR>
<BR>
波斯莫“骑士”取下头盔，向人群露出一个令人毛骨悚然的、狼一般的笑容，然后，坦率地说，开始用她的断剑屠杀帕玛尔。陪同她的几个波斯莫欢呼起来。<BR>
<BR>
我本以为卡吉特会不顾任何协议攻击波斯莫，但他们和平地（尽管凌乱地）收拾东西，离开了城市。<BR>
