"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Mixed Unit Tactics in the Five Years War<BR>
Volume Two<BR>
By Codus Callonus<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
In the previous volume I discussed how the Khajiit took advantage of their varied physical abilities, as well as knowledge of the enemies' tactical weaknesses, to win several skirmishes during the Five Years War against Valenwood. I will now explain how the Bosmer retaliation was both initially effective, yet ultimately doomed to fail.<BR><BR>
The first two battles were won by essentially attacking the Bosmer from above and below. Ohmes and Ohmes-raht emerged from hidden holes in the ground to assault the main force from behind, while the lighter Dagi and Dagi-raht distracted the Bosmer archers by raining down fire from secure positions in the treetops.<BR>
<BR>
This latter point illustrates a particular blind spot of the Bosmer, that they cannot imagine an enemy holding a terrain advantage over them in forest. Especially not the Khajiit, who people often imagine as primarily desert-dwellers. But the light-footed Dagi and Dagi-raht are native to the southern Tenmar forest, upsetting these expectations.<BR>
<BR>
After the second battle, survivors finally reached the Bosmer military command in the south. Once properly informed, the Bosmer adjusted their battle plans accordingly. A much larger force, including several mages, was rerouted from the Torval theater and dispatched to the north.<BR>
<BR>
Not even the Bosmer are capable of remaining unseen while marching in large numbers. They can, however, mask the true size of their force. By marching in single file, controlling lines of sight, and through select chameleon and silence spells, the Bosmer made it appear as if a much smaller group was underway, similar to the previous two.<BR>
<BR>
The Bosmer arrived at the battlefield and established their position, similar to the previous two fights. Rather than change their tactics, the complacent Khajiit attempted the same trick a third time. But the Bosmer had their own mixed unit tactics in mind, which were no less impressive than those of the Khajiit. Through a combination of shamanic invocations and traditional hunter tactics, the Bosmer scouts and mages had riled up the local beasts of the Valenwood wilds, funneling them towards the enemy positions.<BR>
<BR>
Swarms of birds harassed the fire-casters hidden in the trees, while the warriors were flushed from their underground hideouts by spiny burrowing creatures. The Khajiiti main force, hidden behind their wooden shields in anticipation of the trap, were stampeded by a local herd animal. It was trivial for the experienced Bosmer archers to decimate the retreating foe.<BR>
<BR>
But the Khajiit commander had anticipated a setback of this kind. After the initial chaos, another signal was strummed, and the Khajiit began a slow retreat. During this maneuver, they made a show of cutting down saplings and marring trees with their axes, the original offense which had spurred the Bosmer into action. Naturally, the Bosmer began a pursuit.<BR>
<BR>
The Bosmer force was larger, fresher, and not burdened by the wounded, allowing them to gain terrain quickly. But when the first arrows struck the rearguard of the Khajiiti, their pace improved considerably, showing their former slow tempo to be a feint. An astute commander should have understood the significance of this, and should have remembered that this area of conflict did not have any strategic significance.<BR>
<BR>
The Bosmer force chased the Khajiit further north, beyond the range of our lookout posts around Fort Sphinxmoth. I did not witness the culmination of the struggle, myself. Apparently, the Bosmer chased the remaining Khajiit across the Xylo for several days, until the retreating company was almost cornered. At the last moment, a messenger bird contacted the Bosmer commander, ordering an immediate return to the southern front. A large force had broken through in the south and was threatening Haven. The Bosmer were thus forced to break off their pursuit.<BR>
<BR>
Though the Bosmer adapted to and even took advantage of the unusual battle tactics employed by the Khajiit, they ultimately lost sight of the bigger picture. The Khajiit used a small, mobile party of skirmishers in an act of psychological warfare, goading the Bosmer into dividing and expending their forces across an inconsequential side-theater of the real war.<BR>
<BR>
I am unsure of how exactly the Khajiit coordinated these skirmish attacks, though I have heard some Khajiit allude to a secret method of long-distance communication using moon sugar trances. I would dismiss this as obvious make-believe in the vein of the 'Alfiq', were it not for similar meditative communication systems used by the Emperor's own clerks.<BR>
<BR>
Ultimately, the northern distraction benefited the Khajiit, who scattered their enemies' defenses using only a small company of skirmishers and ultimately secured several positions along the Xylo River, which became key in the later stages of the war.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
五年战争中的混合部队战术<BR>
第二卷<BR>
科达斯·卡罗努斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
在上一卷中，我讨论了卡吉特如何利用他们多样化的身体能力，以及对敌人战术弱点的了解，在与瓦伦伍德的五年战争中赢得了数次小规模战斗。现在我将解释波斯莫的反击如何最初有效，但最终注定失败。<BR><BR>
前两场战斗的胜利基本上是靠从上方和下方攻击波斯莫。欧姆斯和欧姆斯-拉特从隐藏的地洞中钻出，从后方攻击主力部队，而更轻的达吉和达吉-拉特则从树梢安全位置向下投火，分散波斯莫弓箭手的注意力。<BR>
<BR>
这后一点说明了波斯莫的一个特别盲点：他们无法想象在森林中有敌人能占据地形优势。尤其是卡吉特，人们通常认为他们主要是沙漠居民。但脚步轻盈的达吉和达吉-拉特原产于南部滕玛森林，打破了这些预期。<BR>
<BR>
第二次战斗后，幸存者终于到达南方的波斯莫军事指挥部。一旦得到充分信息，波斯莫相应地调整了作战计划。一支更大的部队，包括几名法师，从托瓦尔战区改道，被派往北方。<BR>
<BR>
即使是波斯莫也无法在大量行军时保持不被发现。然而，他们可以掩盖部队的真实规模。通过单列行军、控制视线，以及选择性地使用变色龙和沉默法术，波斯莫使其看起来好像是一支小得多的队伍在行进，类似于前两次。<BR>
<BR>
波斯莫抵达战场并建立了阵地，与前两次战斗相似。自满的卡吉特没有改变战术，而是第三次尝试同样的把戏。但波斯莫有自己的混合部队战术，其精彩程度不亚于卡吉特。通过萨满祈祷和传统猎人战术的结合，波斯莫侦察兵和法师激怒了瓦伦伍德荒野的本地野兽，将它们引向敌人阵地。<BR>
<BR>
成群的鸟骚扰着藏在树上的火焰施法者，而战士们则被带刺的穴居生物从地下藏身处赶了出来。卡吉特主力部队原本躲在木盾后面，期待着陷阱，却被当地的兽群踩踏。对于经验丰富的波斯莫弓箭手来说，消灭撤退的敌人是轻而易举的事。<BR>
<BR>
但卡吉特指挥官预料到了这种挫折。最初的混乱过后，又弹奏了一个信号，卡吉特开始缓慢撤退。在这次机动中，他们故意砍伐树苗、用斧头破坏树木，这正是最初激怒波斯莫采取行动的行为。自然地，波斯莫开始了追击。<BR>
<BR>
波斯莫部队人数更多、精力更充沛，且没有伤员负担，这使他们能够迅速抢占地形。但当第一波箭矢击中卡吉特后卫时，他们的速度明显加快，表明之前缓慢的节奏是佯装。精明的指挥官应该明白这意味着什么，并且应该记住，这个冲突地区没有任何战略意义。<BR>
<BR>
波斯莫部队将卡吉特追得更北，超出了我们斯芬克斯蛾堡周围瞭望哨的范围。我本人没有目睹这场斗争的结局。显然，波斯莫将剩余的卡吉特追过了宰娄河，持续数日，直到撤退的队伍几乎陷入绝境。在最后一刻，一只信使鸟联系了波斯莫指挥官，命令立即返回南部前线。一支大部队已在南方突破，正在威胁避风港。波斯莫因此被迫中断了追击。<BR>
<BR>
尽管波斯莫适应并甚至利用了卡吉特所采用的不寻常战术，但他们最终未能看清全局。卡吉特使用了一支小型、机动的小规模战斗队进行心理战，引诱波斯莫将兵力分散并消耗在真实战争的一个无关紧要的侧翼战场。<BR>
<BR>
我不确定卡吉特究竟是如何协调这些袭击的，尽管我听到一些卡吉特暗示有一种使用月亮糖迷幻状态的秘密远程通讯方法。如果不是皇帝自己的文员也使用类似的冥想通讯系统，我会把这当作明显的虚构，类似于“阿尔菲克”。<BR>
<BR>
最终，北方的牵制行动使卡吉特受益，他们仅用一小队散兵就瓦解了敌人的防御，并最终在宰娄河沿线占领了几个阵地，这些阵地在战争后期成为关键。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Modern Heretics: a Study of Daedra Worship in the Empire<BR>
by Haderus of Gottlesfont<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Daedra worship is not prohibited by law in Cyrodiil. Primarily this is a result of the Imperial Charter granted the Mages Guild permitting the summoning of Daedra. Nonetheless, chapel and public opinion is so strongly against Daedra worship that those who practice Daedric rituals do so in secret.<BR>
<BR> 
However, opinions about Daedra worship differ widely in other provinces. Even in Cyrodiil, traditional opinions have changed greatly over the years, and some communities survive which worship Daedra. Some more traditional Daedra-worshippers are motivated by piety and personal conviction; many modern Daedra-worshippers are motivated by a lust for arcane power. In particular, questing heroes of all stripes seek after the fabled Daedric artifacts for their potent combat and magical benefits.<BR>
<BR> 
I personally have discovered one community worshipping the Daedra Lord Azura, Queen of Dawn and Dusk. A researcher curious about Daedra worship might research in several ways: through a study of the literature, through exploration and discovery of ancient daedric shrines, through questioning local informants, and through questioning worshippers themselves. I used all these means to discover the shrine of Azura.<BR>
<BR> 
First I read books. References like this one may provide a helpful general background concerning Daedric shrines. For example, my researches led me to understand that, in Cyrodiil, Daedric shrines are generally represented by statues of Daedra Lords, are generally situated in wilderness locations far from settlements, that each shrine generally has associated with it a community of worshippers, often referred to as a 'coven', that shrines have associated with them a particular time -- often a day of the week -- when a Daedra lord might be solicited, that Daedra Lord often will not deign to respond unless they regard a petitioner of sufficient prowess or strength of character, that they will only respond if given the proper offering [the secret of which offering often known only to the community of worshippers], and that, in return for the completion of some task or service, the Daedra Lords will often undertake to offer an artifact of power to a successful quester.<BR>
<BR> 
Then I questioned locals with an intimate knowledge of the wilderness. Two classes of informants I found especially useful -- well-traveled hunters and adventurers [who might come across shrines in their travels], and scholars of the Mages Guild. In the case of the Shrine of Azura, both sources were profitable. I discovered a Cheydinhal hunter who had chanced across a strange epic statue in his travels. The statue was of a woman with outstretched arms; in one hand she held a star; in the other hand, she held a crescent moon. He had shunned the statue out of superstitious fear, but had marked the location in memory --far north of Cheydinhal, northwest of Lake Arrius, high in the Jerall Mountains. Then, proceeding to the local Mages Guild with a description of the statue, I was able to confirm from its description the identity of the Daedra Lord worshipped.<BR>
<BR> 
Having discovered the location of the shrine, I visited it, and discovered there the community of worshippers. Because of the strength of opinion against Daedra worship, the worshippers were, at first, reluctant to admit their identity. But once I had won their trust, they were willing to divulge to me the secrets of the times when Azura would hear petitions [from dusk to dawn], and that the offering required by Azura was glow dust, a substance obtained from the will-o-the-wisp.<BR>
<BR> 
I am, of course, nothing more than a chapelman and scholar, so it did not lie within my power to find a will-o-the-wisp to obtain glow dust; nor am I certain that Azura would have found me worthy to make such an offering, even had I proffered it. But I was assured that if I had been able to make such an offering, and if it had been accepted, Azura would have given me some sort of quest, which, if completed, might have earned me the reward of Azura's Star, a Daedric artifact of legendary magical powers.<BR>
<BR> 
I have since heard rumors of the existence in Cyrodiil of several other Daedric shrines, of the Daedric Lords to which they are dedicated, and the Daedric artifacts that might be won by questing heroes. Hircine the Huntsman, for example, is linked in legend to the Savior's Hide, a powerful enchanted armor. The sword Volendrung is associated with Malacath, Lord of Monsters, and the eponymously named Mace of Molag Bal is also thought to be the object of Daedra worship. Other Daedra Lords, their shrines and worshippers, remain to be discovered in Cyrodiil by earnest and persistent researchers.<BR>
<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
现代异端：帝国中迪德拉崇拜的研究<BR>
哥特尔斯圣水坛的哈德鲁斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
迪德拉崇拜在西罗帝尔并不违法。这主要是由于帝国授予法师公会的特许状允许召唤迪德拉。尽管如此，教会和公众舆论强烈反对迪德拉崇拜，以至于那些进行迪德拉仪式的人都秘密进行。<BR>
<BR>
然而，在其他行省，关于迪德拉崇拜的看法差异很大。即使在西罗帝尔，传统观念多年来也发生了很大变化，并且存在一些崇拜迪德拉的社区。一些更传统的迪德拉崇拜者受到虔诚和个人信念的驱使；许多现代迪德拉崇拜者则受到对神秘力量的渴望所驱使。特别是，各种寻求冒险的英雄都追求传说中的迪德拉神器，以获得它们强大的战斗和魔法效益。<BR>
<BR>
我个人发现了一个崇拜迪德拉大君阿祖拉（黎明与黄昏女王）的社区。对迪德拉崇拜好奇的研究者可以通过几种方式进行研究：通过研究文献、通过探索和发现古老的迪德拉圣祠、通过询问当地线人，以及通过询问崇拜者本人。我使用了所有这些方法来发现阿祖拉的圣祠。<BR>
<BR>
首先我阅读书籍。像这样的参考资料可能提供有关迪德拉圣祠的有用一般背景。例如，我的研究使我了解到，在西罗帝尔，迪德拉圣祠通常以迪德拉大君的雕像为代表，通常位于远离定居点的荒野位置，每个圣祠通常都有一个崇拜者社区，常被称为“集会”，圣祠与特定的时间相关联 -- 通常是一周中的某一天 -- 届时可以向迪德拉大君祈求，迪德拉大君通常不会屈尊回应，除非他们认为请求者有足够的能力或性格力量，他们只有在得到适当的祭品时才会回应[祭品的秘密通常只有崇拜者社区知道]，并且，作为完成某项任务或服务的回报，迪德拉大君通常会向成功的寻求者提供一件力量神器。<BR>
<BR>
然后我询问了对荒野有深入了解的当地人。我发现两类线人特别有用 -- 经验丰富的猎人和冒险者[他们可能在旅行中遇到圣祠]，以及法师公会的学者。就阿祖拉圣祠而言，这两种来源都很有用。我发现了一个夏丁赫尔的猎人，他在旅途中偶然发现了一座奇怪的宏伟雕像。雕像是一个张开双臂的女人；一只手里拿着一颗星星；另一只手里拿着一弯新月。出于迷信的恐惧，他避开了雕像，但记住了位置 -- 夏丁赫尔以北很远，阿里乌斯湖西北，杰拉尔山脉高处。然后，带着对雕像的描述前往当地法师公会，我能够从描述中确认所崇拜的迪德拉大君的身份。<BR>
<BR>
发现圣祠的位置后，我访问了它，并在那里发现了崇拜者社区。由于反对迪德拉崇拜的舆论强烈，崇拜者起初不愿承认自己的身份。但一旦我赢得了他们的信任，他们便愿意向我透露阿祖拉会听取祈愿的时间秘密[从黄昏到黎明]，以及阿祖拉所需的祭品是荧光尘，一种从鬼火中获得的东西。<BR>
<BR>
当然，我只不过是一个小教堂牧师和学者，所以我没有能力找到鬼火来获取荧光尘；我也不确定阿祖拉会认为我值得献上这样的祭品，即使我献上了。但我被保证，如果我能够献上这样的祭品，并且被接受了，阿祖拉会给我某种任务，如果完成，可能会让我获得阿祖拉之星作为奖励，这是一件具有传奇魔法力量的迪德拉神器。<BR>
<BR>
此后，我听到传闻说西罗帝尔还存在其他几座迪德拉圣祠，它们所供奉的迪德拉大君，以及寻求冒险的英雄可能赢得的迪德拉神器。例如，猎手希尔辛在传说中就与救世者之皮（一件强大的附魔盔甲）相关联。剑沃伦德朗与怪物之主马拉卡斯相关联，而同名的莫拉格·巴尔的钉锤也被认为是迪德拉崇拜的对象。其他迪德拉大君、他们的圣祠和崇拜者，还有待认真而执著的研究者在西罗帝尔发现。<BR>

我个人发现了一个崇拜迪德拉大君阿祖拉（黎明与黄昏女王）的社区。对迪德拉崇拜好奇的研究者可以通过几种方式进行研究：通过研究文献、通过探索和发现古老的迪德拉圣祠、通过询问当地线人，以及通过询问崇拜者本人。我使用了所有这些方法来发现阿祖拉的圣祠。<BR>
<BR>
首先我阅读书籍。像这样的参考资料可能提供有关迪德拉圣祠的有用一般背景。例如，我的研究使我了解到，在西罗帝尔，迪德拉圣祠通常以迪德拉大君的雕像为代表，通常位于远离定居点的荒野位置，每个圣祠通常都有一个崇拜者社区，常被称为“集会”，圣祠与特定的时间相关联 -- 通常是一周中的某一天 -- 届时可以向迪德拉大君祈求，迪德拉大君通常不会屈尊回应，除非他们认为请求者有足够的能力或性格力量，他们只有在得到适当的祭品时才会回应[祭品的秘密通常只有崇拜者社区知道]，并且，作为完成某项任务或服务的回报，迪德拉大君通常会向成功的寻求者提供一件力量神器。<BR>
<BR>
然后我询问了对荒野有深入了解的当地人。我发现两类线人特别有用 -- 经验丰富的猎人和冒险者[他们可能在旅行中遇到圣祠]，以及法师公会的学者。就阿祖拉圣祠而言，这两种来源都很有用。我发现了一个夏丁赫尔的猎人，他在旅途中偶然发现了一座奇怪的宏伟雕像。雕像是一个张开双臂的女人；一只手里拿着一颗星星；另一只手里拿着一弯新月。出于迷信的恐惧，他避开了雕像，但记住了位置 -- 夏丁赫尔以北很远，阿里乌斯湖西北，杰拉尔山脉高处。然后，带着对雕像的描述前往当地法师公会，我能够从描述中确认所崇拜的迪德拉大君的身份。<BR>
<BR>
发现圣祠的位置后，我访问了它，并在那里发现了崇拜者社区。由于反对迪德拉崇拜的舆论强烈，崇拜者起初不愿承认自己的身份。但一旦我赢得了他们的信任，他们便愿意向我透露阿祖拉会听取祈愿的时间秘密[从黄昏到黎明]，以及阿祖拉所需的祭品是荧光尘，一种从鬼火中获得的东西。<BR>
<BR>
当然，我只不过是一个小教堂牧师和学者，所以我没有能力找到鬼火来获取荧光尘；我也不确定阿祖拉会认为我值得献上这样的祭品，即使我献上了。但我被保证，如果我能够献上这样的祭品，并且被接受了，阿祖拉会给我某种任务，如果完成，可能会让我获得阿祖拉之星作为奖励，这是一件具有传奇魔法力量的迪德拉神器。<BR>
<BR>
此后，我听到传闻说西罗帝尔还存在其他几座迪德拉圣祠，它们所供奉的迪德拉大君，以及寻求冒险的英雄可能赢得的迪德拉神器。例如，猎手希尔辛在传说中就与救世者之皮（一件强大的附魔盔甲）相关联。剑沃伦德朗与怪物之主马拉卡斯相关联，而同名的莫拉格·巴尔的钉锤也被认为是迪德拉崇拜的对象。其他迪德拉大君、他们的圣祠和崇拜者，还有待认真而执著的研究者在西罗帝尔发现。<BR>
<BR>

Golden Reed is considered a well-rounded tradition, with a mix of heavily rooted and agile evasive stances. Special attention is paid to those techniques that can be used against armed and armored opponents.<BR><BR>

Like its creators, Salt Rice is considered the most brutal and competitive of the traditions, in which throws, disarming and grappling techniques, and even a variety of cheap shots are common. In more recent years, Salt Rice has filtered out to other elements of the criminal underworld. The Most Cruel Trade<BR>

Though the addition could not have made much difference, it mattered little to the noble Dunmer. They would not be the ones blistering their palms doing the rowing, after all.<BR>

Responsibility for the rowing would naturally fall on the cargo, for what better way to ensure that the goods were of top quality? Those who raised complaints were laid low, then skinned, and prepared as a fine meal for those who remained. The Dunmer would laugh about it, saying that one less hungry mouth would save on food, and make the trip that much more economically sound.<BR>
<BR>

Once safely out of sight, a mage among the Dunmer would paralyze each of the slaves and remove their bracers. With no means to break their fall, the mean spirited mer would shove the slaves over, letting them fall as they may.<BR>

They are not even alive! They are stuffed specimens, requested by a member of Great House Telvanni for decoration. Surely the worldly Imperials had heard of such things being done elsewhere in Tamriel, to other types of lowly lizards and cats. To convince the officials that nothing illegal had taken place, the Dunmer presented forged papers, claiming that the Khajiit and Argonians had been wanted criminals. Satisfied, if horrified, the officials let the ship pass into the waters surrounding Morrowind.<BR>
<BR>
There, the true suffering would begin. <BR>

最残酷的行当<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
 A Most Unfortunate Party <BR>
by Ardarlunwe of Sunhold <BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
I found the very notion of his invitation most horrible. Caradhayon, through an acquaintance in High Rock, had the most unpleasant honor of being invited to a party held by the nemer King of Wayrest. Naturally, Caradhayon found the offer most unappealing though he could not fathom being rude enough to reject, and he was resolved not to go through such an ordeal alone. Having most of his associates suddenly finding themselves important duties which would last for a month or two, he had come to my residence at the unusual time of fifteen minutes past three in the afternoon to personally ask for my companionship. Without any knowledge of the ulterior intentions of his visit, I found myself unable to remember any important duties I had which would unfortunately occur for the duration of the said party. As such I was inclined to agree. After leaving my residence, Caradhayon immediately sent message that he and I would be attending.<BR>
<BR>
Having no understanding of the bizarre nemer aristocracy, if one is allowed to be so crude as to use the honorable word to describe it, I conversed with Itertilar the Zoologist as to what to expect. He informed me that the food would most likely be of the poorest quality, the music would be of the most awful noise, and the attire of the beast-like guests would fail miserably at appearing extravagant. He suggested that I ensure my Sound spells were exceptional and that I ensure to practice (the nerve!), that I be careful no neither eat nor drink anything other than what I bring with me, and that I show them true extravagance and style through my attire.<BR>
<BR>
As I arrived at the pristine harbor to leave Alinor for the wild lands, word of my departure had reached an Ymga of the Valenwood who gifted to me a perfumed cloth, and a warning that men have a most unpleasant smell. Both Caradhayon and Itertilar had failed to mention this fact, and I admit I was most furious. I confronted Caradhayon who, instead of conversing about the fact, abruptly changed the subject to him having a heart attack. He then had the nerve to ask me to summon a healer for him. I told him that I would not, and that I would be most unpleasant with him for the trip. He wasted no time in clutching for his chest and falling dead. I could not believe that he would go as far as die to weasel out of attending the party, even worse was that he left me to go there alone.<BR>
<BR>
The sail to Wayrest was most disastrous. The ship was of a poor Colovian design, and the captain was a brutish and unpresentable nemer by the name of Garius Assadumploodus, or something along those lines. When I walked onto the ship, he had the nerve to dare ask for my hand for assistance to get on the ship. When he caught me staring at his disfigured face (his face was most disfigured and hideous, and I could not help but observe it for a prolonged duration), he told that he gained his "scars" as he called them in war. The horrible brute. Worse still was the crew. All of them were nemer with sub-par manners. In the evening, they consumed wines from their own horrid homes, laughed and talked loudly, and played terrible musical instruments called the fiddle. I was most pleased when other nemer boarded the ship and killed them all. My good faith however went unrewarded when they then had the nerve to demand I gift them my jewels. I shamefully admit that I lost my temper at this point. When I finished with my fireball spell, the nemer were dead and the sailing vessel began to lose buoyancy. With other passengers, I had to move my luggage on to another boat which miraculously was placed next to ours with a plank for ease of access.<BR>
<BR>
This second vessel was most insufferable. If the gods had taken such care as to give me another vessel, the least they could have done was make it adorable, painted white with gold leafing and encrusted jewels on the trims, perfumed, shaped like a swan, and complete with a crew of even the lowest species to work it. This boat was cramped, effluvial, and it lashed around with the waves. It took a lot of effort on my part to get all the other passengers to work the vessel. They were completely incompetent and useless, and they had no appreciation of how hard management was. The journey was taking far longer than expected. I informed them that I was a very important Altmer who was going to a party held by the King of Wayrest, and that I could not be tardy in arriving. The jeered at me, and said they had no food. I told them that they should have been prepared like me and brought their own, and that it was their own fault they were hungry. It was a week before we finally reached the Iliac Bay. By now, they were quite thin and demanding I give them some of my food. Despite my best efforts, they could not understand that a zoologist and a talking ape warned me that the food at the King's party would be unpalatable. One night, I awoke to find one rummaging through my belongings searching for food. After giving him a thunder shock, the nemer were most obedient for the rest of the voyage.<BR>
<BR>
As luck would have it (although I am still unsure as to whether it was good fortune or not), I reached Wayrest the morning of the party. Even from afar, I could see the city was clearly putrid. The men of High Rock have clearly tried, disastrously I might add, to emulate the fine architecture of the Altmer. Their buildings were low and crude, made of common materials such as stone and wood. The colors and styles of their dress were most uninspired and unappealing. The gardens were clearly managed by those untrained in horticulture (?). I could continue at length at the shortcomings of the city and men in general, but I fear I would go on for quite some length doing so.<BR>
<BR>
I made sure my entrance from the sailing vessel was most impressive. I wore my finest clothing of the highest Summerset quality, and the most fantastic jewels I purchased in Shimmerene. I espied some truly vulgar-looking nemer dockworkers and, falling below my dignity, informed them that I was attending a party at the King of Wayrest and I needed to be supplied with a gold coach drawn by silver stallions for an appropriate entrance. Instead of making the arrangements post-haste as one might expect; they chose instead to stare at me as if I were mad. I then realized the full extant of the uselessness of men so I had no choice but to arrive at the party on foot, walking through the foulest streets I have ever had the displeasure of witnessing. When I arrived at the palace (which resembled little more than a moderately-sized crude hovel), the guards had the audacity to ask who I was and what business I had at the palace. I informed them that I was Ardarlunwe of Sunhold, a very important mage in residence in Alinor, and that I was the most important guest at the party being held at the palace. For the first time on the journey, these men had the proper manners of formally welcoming me to the palace and opening the gates for me. They also informed me that great lengths had been made to ensure that the party was most entertaining and memorable.<BR>
<BR>
I ambulated through the gate to the door of the palace. Other guests had assembled there, and I clearly saw they were little more than common riffraff from all untamed corners of Tamriel. I did, however, have the dignity of being the only Altmer in attendance. As I (begrudgingly) approached the rabble of guests, they all averted their eyes from me. As much as they vociferously tried to pretend it was because my clothing and jewels were reflecting the sun into their eyes, I knew it was truly because me attire was so exquisite that they could not bear to look at me due to the shame of their own inadequate attire.<BR>
<BR>
Realizing that nobody at this party was worthy of my acquaintance, I positioned myself toward the front of the guests so that when the king arrived he would see how spectacular I had prepared myself, and also so it was unlikely I would be approached by any upstart pretenders. Unfortunately I was approached by a mere human, who had the audacity to consider himself worthy of my acquaintance. He introduced himself as Prince Edwayn (or some other horribly archaic nemer namesake) and informed me he was a cousin of the king. Oblivious to my failing to be impressed by either his title or his relations, Edwayn continued to ramble about the party, how they had the finest meats Tamriel has to offer hanging in the meat locker, how they imported vegetables directly from some untamed regions of High Rock, the silverware purchased in Cyrodiil, and other topics of little importance. He then continued to speak of other, far more uninteresting matters such as the wellbeing of his family, a failed Imperial succession, and so forth. I was about to paralyze him when the King timely arrived and Edwayn fell silent.<BR>
<BR>
The King and his consorts arrived in a golden carriage pulled by silver stallions. I was most unimpressed with the craftsmanship of the carriage and the breed of the steeds, and was most glad I did not arrive in one. The King proceeded to introduce himself and his entourage, welcomed and thanked everyone for attending, said that fine entertainment had been planned and wished everyone partook, and wished everyone enjoy themselves. I knew already he was mad thinking that it was possible to enjoy this party but as any respectable Altmer I kept such failings of their reasoning to myself. The gates to the palace were opened and everyone, myself included, entered.<BR>
<BR>
There, in the entrance hall, hanging by a noose created from poorly woven bed sheets, was a poorly dressed and lifeless human boy. Hitherto that moment I had been under the distinct impression that only the Bosmer consumed their deceased. I found that they called the entrance of a palace a "meat locker" as that Edwayn had said was most illogical; what was even stranger was that the guests seemed upset that they had decided to eat this boy and were crying he was so young. The King, upset like the rest of them, proceeded to usher everyone into the next room and asked them and myself to try and enjoy the rest of the evening.<BR>
<BR>
The music played in the hall was a most horrid screeching noise. They had clearly not gone to any lengths to try and make the food served palatable, or to purchase finely made silverware with which to place it on. I took a position by the window and cast a sound spell on the room so I could no longer hear the painful screeching of their musical instruments, nor the unintelligent babble of their attempted conversation. I stood for what must have seemed two hours and thirty-seven minutes when suddenly a band of their guards burst into the room.<BR>
<BR>
And so began the awful display of entertainment they had tried to get everyone involved in. The guards proceeded to start hacking at the guests with crude swords and the guests proceeded to act like they were being mercilessly slaughtered. This entertainment was so vulgar and distasteful that I immediately proceeded to leave the palace and return to Alinor. The Bretons proceeded to block my exit and began to start waving their swords at me. I blasted them with a fireball and swiftly left the palace. Seeing that the entire city was in pandemonium, I recalled to my study in Alinor.<BR>

<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
A flash of lightning momentarily lit up the encampment, revealing nearly thirty tents surrounding the burned and ruined houses of Crowhaven. Only a single Wood Elf guard stood watch, sheltering from the pouring rain under a tent awning.<BR>
<BR>
"The bastards are getting complacent," growled Andred.<BR>
<BR>
"Let us not make the same mistake," replied Aemilius. "We wait another fifteen minutes until everyone is in position."<BR>
<BR>
Those fifteen minutes seemed like a very long time to the resistance fighters hiding in a muddy ditch that was rapidly filling with water, but eventually the sky lit up again with lightning. The casual observer would notice nothing untoward, but those anticipating it saw that the lightning travelled not downwards but upwards. The signal was given.<BR>
<BR>
There was no need for morale-boosting speeches. Every man and woman here had lost friends and relatives to the Camoran Usurper as his armies had rampaged across Colovia. There was nothing they wouldn't do to stop him. Aemilius didn't know what the small force was doing in the ruins of Crowhaven, and it didn't matter. By dawn they wouldn't be doing anything.<BR>
<BR>
The Imperials drew their blackened weapons and silently crawled from the ditch. They were barely two hundred yards from the tents, but the guard had no hope of spotting them through the dark and the rain. They half-ran towards the Wood Elf encampment, dividing themselves up so that each of the outer ring of tents was taken by two or three fighters. Aemilius knew that the rest of his men would be doing the same on the opposite side of the village.<BR>
<BR>
For a third time the night was lit up by lightning as Varno the mage blasted two of the tents. They were too wet to catch fire, but the Elves inside would certainly notice the electricity.<BR>
<BR>
"For Kvatch!" shouted Aemilius. "For the Emperor!"<BR>
<BR>
The cry was repeated by each of his fighters as they burst into the tents. Aemilius plunged his sword into one Wood Elf and kicked another in the stomach as he jerked awake. Andred despatched that one with a swing of his mace. A few seconds later and another three Elves lay dead.<BR>
<BR>
Aemilius strode from the tent and stumbled as something grabbed at his foot. He turned and stabbed, but his sword hit only the rain-soaked ground. Then a second arm burst from the earth, followed quickly by a skull and skeletal torso.<BR>
<BR>
"Necromancy!" came the cry and Aemilius realised that corpses, both fresh and ancient, were rising across the camp.<BR>
<BR>
"Kill the necromancer!" he shouted, and cleaved the skull in two.<BR>
<BR>
The initial ambush had devastated the outer ring of tents, but the Elves in the inner tents had had time to arm themselves and the flow of undead reinforcements threatened to wipe the Imperials out. Shadowy figures surrounded Aemilius on every side, and in the dark it was hard to tell whether a man in Imperial armour was a living ally or an undead foe.<BR>
<BR>
Lightning flashed again and again as Varno used his talents to strike down the Elves, until the flashes were abruptly cut off.<BR>
<BR>
"On me!" Aemilius cried and ran towards where Varno had been. Something swung at him from the side and he dodged out of the way. Turning, he saw a Wood Elf wielding a long spear. The ruin of the Elf's face spoke of Andred's handiwork, but it hadn't been enough to prevent reanimation. Aemilius took an arm off with one blow and followed up with a strike straight into the brainpan. The Elf crumpled to the ground.<BR>
<BR>
Rounding a tent Aemilius saw the necromancer. He had the height of a High Elf and was surrounded by streams of ethereal light and dozens of warriors. Five Imperials were also there, fighting a losing battle against the Wood Elves and undead.<BR>
<BR>
Aemilius joined the melee with a wordless roar. He summoned up his pain and grief and poured them into his swordplay, striking down enemies left and right. The Imperials were horribly outnumbered, however, and Aemilius couldn't break through the lines and reach the necromancer.<BR>
<BR>
Suddenly Andred came charging in, all thoughts of self-preservation gone from his mind. He hurled himself at a lightning-burnt undead Wood Elf, who slipped on the muddy ground and fell onto another. Aemilius dashed through the gap, even as more Wood Elves surrounded the prone Andred.<BR>
<BR>
Aemilius didn't look back. He killed two more Elves and came face-to-face with the necromancer, who panicked and threw a fireball over Aemilius' shoulder and into his own troops. Aemilius didn't hesitate and struck the necromancer's pointy-eared head from his shoulders. The ethereal light died with a strangled scream and the undead collapsed to the ground, inert.<BR>
<BR>
With their leader slain and their undead allies defeated, the remaining Wood Elves began to flee into the night. Aemilius ordered his men to stay put. More than half had been killed, including Andred and Varno, and many of the survivors were nursing injuries.<BR>
<BR>
As the rain petered out Aemilius' attention turned to the three Wood Elves who had surrendered instead of fleeing. He looked around at the grim faces of his men, all of whom had lost people to the Camoranite horde. He looked down at the missing fingers on his left hand and felt the itch of the torture scars on his back, remembering how fortunate he had been to escape after being captured in the sack of Kvatch. He looked at the bound Wood Elves, face down in the mud.<BR>
<BR>
Aemilius drew his hunting knife. It was time for revenge.<BR><BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>一窝乌鸦<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
一道闪电瞬间照亮了营地，露出环绕着被烧毁的鸦港房屋的约三十顶帐篷。只有一个木精灵守卫在站岗，躲在帐篷的遮阳篷下避雨。<BR>
<BR>
“这些混蛋变得自满了，”安德雷德咆哮道。<BR>
<BR>
“我们不要犯同样的错误，”埃米利乌斯回答。“我们再等十五分钟，直到所有人就位。”<BR>
<BR>
对于躲在一个迅速积水的泥沟里的抵抗战士来说，这十五分钟似乎非常漫长，但最终天空再次被闪电照亮。不经意的观察者不会注意到任何异常，但那些期待它的人看到闪电不是向下而是向上传播。信号发出了。<BR>
<BR>
不需要鼓舞士气的演讲。这里的每个男人和女人都有朋友和亲戚死于篡位者卡莫兰的军队在科洛维亚的肆虐。为了阻止他，他们愿意做任何事。埃米利乌斯不知道这支小部队在鸦港的废墟里做什么，这也不重要。到黎明时，他们将不再做任何事。<BR>
<BR>
帝国人拔出涂黑的武器，悄悄地从沟里爬出来。他们离帐篷不到两百码，但守卫在黑暗和雨中没有希望发现他们。他们半跑着冲向木精灵营地，分散开来，以便外圈每顶帐篷都由两三个战士负责。埃米利乌斯知道他手下其余的人会在村子的另一边做同样的事。<BR>
<BR>
当法师瓦诺炸毁两顶帐篷时，夜晚第三次被闪电照亮。帐篷太湿了，无法着火，但里面的精灵肯定会注意到电击。<BR>
<BR>
“为了科瓦奇！”埃米利乌斯喊道。“为了皇帝！”<BR>
<BR>
当他每个战士冲进帐篷时，都重复了这声呐喊。埃米利乌斯将剑刺入一个木精灵，并在另一个精灵惊醒时踢了他的肚子。安德雷德用钉锤一挥解决了那个。几秒钟后，又有三个精灵倒地死亡。<BR>
<BR>
埃米利乌斯大步走出帐篷，绊了一下，有什么东西抓住了他的脚。他转身刺去，但他的剑只刺中了被雨水浸湿的地面。然后，第二只手臂从地里猛地伸出，紧接着是头骨和骷髅躯干。<BR>
<BR>
“死灵法术！”喊声传来，埃米利乌斯意识到，无论是新鲜的还是古老的尸体，都在营地各处站起来了。<BR>
<BR>
“杀死死灵法师！”他喊道，并将那骷髅劈成两半。<BR>
<BR>
最初的伏击摧毁了外圈帐篷，但内圈帐篷里的精灵有时间武装自己，而源源不断的亡灵增援威胁要消灭帝国人。阴暗的身影从四面八方包围了埃米利乌斯，在黑暗中很难分辨一个穿着帝国盔甲的人是活着的盟友还是亡灵敌人。<BR>
<BR>
瓦诺利用他的才能一次次用闪电击倒精灵，直到闪电突然中断。<BR>
<BR>
“跟我来！”埃米利乌斯喊道，跑向瓦诺所在的地方。有什么东西从侧面朝他挥来，他躲开了。转过身，他看到一个木精灵挥舞着一支长矛。精灵脸上被毁的痕迹说明是安德雷德的手笔，但这不足以阻止其复活。埃米利乌斯一刀砍下一条手臂，紧接着一击直刺脑壳。精灵瘫倒在地。<BR>
<BR>
绕过一顶帐篷，埃米利乌斯看到了死灵法师。他有着高精灵的身高，被数道灵光和无数的战士包围着。五名帝国人也在那里，与木精灵和亡灵进行着一场败局已定的战斗。<BR>
<BR>
埃米利乌斯发出一声无言的怒吼，加入了混战。他唤起自己的痛苦和悲伤，将它们倾注到剑术中，左右砍杀敌人。然而，帝国人寡不敌众，情况极其糟糕，埃米利乌斯无法突破防线到达死灵法师身边。<BR>
<BR>
突然，安德雷德冲了过来，心中已无任何自保之念。他扑向一个被闪电烧焦的亡灵木精灵，后者在泥泞的地面上滑倒，压在了另一个身上。埃米利乌斯冲过缺口，尽管更多的木精灵包围了倒在地上的安德雷德。<BR>
<BR>
埃米利乌斯没有回头。他又杀了两个精灵，与死灵法师面对面。死灵法师惊慌失措，将一颗火球从埃米利乌斯肩头扔向自己的部队。埃米利乌斯毫不犹豫，将死灵法师尖耳朵的头颅从肩膀上砍了下来。灵光随着一声窒息的尖叫而熄灭，亡灵们倒在地上，一动不动。<BR>
<BR>
随着首领被杀，亡灵盟友被击败，剩下的木精灵开始逃入夜色。埃米利乌斯命令他的手下待在原地。超过一半的人被杀，包括安德雷德和瓦诺，许多幸存者也在处理伤口。<BR>
<BR>
随着雨渐渐停歇，埃米利乌斯的注意力转向了那三个投降而非逃跑的木精灵。他环顾手下严肃的面孔，他们都曾因卡莫兰大军而失去亲人。他低头看着左手缺失的手指，感到背上酷刑留下的伤疤在发痒，想起自己在科瓦奇被洗劫时被俘后能逃脱是多么幸运。他看着被捆绑着的、脸朝下趴在泥里的木精灵。<BR>
<BR>
埃米利乌斯拔出猎刀。是时候复仇了。<BR><BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Murudius<BR>
Gen. Monious Kathil
<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
In these the waning years of my life, I write about the most interesting point of my career. Never would I have dared write about this event in my younger years or while I was of lower rank, but now that I am an old general I don't think it will hurt. You see, the reason I dared not write about it earlier was that the legion hates to admit events like these happen. They claim to have control over the mad lycanthropes. The fact is, they do not have any control whatsoever.<BR>
The first day of that horrific experience started out well, we had just eliminated some bandits who had run deep into the Argonian swamps. There were seven of us: Murudius and I, both Imperial pikemen; Nachin our Redguard blademaster: Captain Weltus, the leader of the expedition; Gro-Ard, an Orcish brute; Areth, our Wood Elf archer and an Argonian guide whose name now escapes me. It took us six days to travel out there and we were taking our time getting back, talking about what every legionnaire talks about: fame, fortune, women and booze. It was approaching night and everything seemed perfect until from up ahead our guide let out a scream that stopped us in our tracks and chilled us to the bone. We ran towards the source of the scream only to find our guides blood covering the ground. The captain figured that some beast had taken him and decided that we should move on without him.<BR>
It wasn't long before we found some of the remains of our guide and the creature that had killed him. The creature hadn't noticed us yet and being young adventurous men, we thought it would be exciting if we could bring down a beast this big. Little did we know, it would be our undoing. We decided that Murudius, Gro-Ard and I would engage the creature so that Nachin could strike it from behind while Areth and Weltus supported us with arrows and magic. The three of us attacked the creature but it was much more intelligent than we had thought it to be. It managed to snap my spear in half and knock over Nachin with its tail while evading the arrows and spells. The battle was only won when it bit into Murudius's shoulder giving Gro-Ard a chance to put an axe into its back. Mortally wounded, the creature retreated into the brush, but we thought it would be wise not to pursue it.<BR><BR>
On the second day Murudius complained of a headache, but we thought nothing of it. We were much too busy keeping an eye on our surroundings in case the beast decided to return.<BR>
On the third day we knew Murudius had contracted some disease from the creature and knew we had to get to a civilized place soon. Without our guide we didn't know of any nearby villages and could only head to the nearest imperial town, four long days away. That night we were all awakened by a scream from Murudius. We rushed to his bedroll and found him there thrashing in pain. But Murudius was no longer the man we knew, he was changing into something like the beast right in front of us. Foolishly the captain went over to help, but was hit hard in the side of the head by a reptilian arm. The monster that was Murudius didn't stop there, he continued to claw away at the captain, turning his body into a sickening bloody mess. The rest of us scrambled for our weapons and armor, but were too late. The creature had grabbed Areth and disappeared into the night with great speed.<BR>
We kept on the move that night and into the next day. Deciding that the creature that had bitten Murudius was a lycanthrope, we figured we'd be safe if we moved during the day. Later that day after some rest we stumbled on some of Areth and his equipment. Among his stuff I found Areth's bow and the Black Tip, an arrow Areth claimed his ancestors had used and that it always killed in one shot. I figured that if he told the truth it would help me slay the monster.<BR><BR>
By evening we found a river with one shallow crossing and decided that it would be best to stay here for the night because we could see the monster before he came from either side and be prepared for him. Something didn't feel right about the plan, but we figured it was better than going through thick brush where the monster could be waiting for us anywhere. When I heard a great splash to my right I realized what was wrong, the monster had looked like one of the great reptiles of the region the natives called the crocodile and I recalled them to be excellent swimmers. I turned to the right and was greeted by a shocked look on Nachin's face as he was being pulled under the surface.<BR>
Gro-Ard and I took no time in running away from there with the roars of the monster behind us. The monster gave chase and as he got closer behind us I pulled out Areth's bow and fired the Black Tip. The arrow went into its right shoulder and only seemed to make the monster angrier and faster. Gro-Ard stopped ahead of me, turned to face the monster and took out his axe. Letting out his own roar, Gro-Ard charged the monster and engaged it in a fierce combat. Gro-Ard managed too little damage to the monster before he was ripped apart. Knowing that it was going to catch me I turned, brandished my short sword and braced for the impact of the monster. It ran into me like a boulder down a mountain slope, knocking me over and making me lose my short sword. The monster roared in triumph and I thought I was doomed, but without thought I pulled the Black Tip out of the monsters shoulder and rammed it into the top of the foul creature's mouth. Screeching in pain and agony the monster turned and fled deep into the swamp never to be seen again.<BR>
I came out several days later at the local garrison. I told my story to my superiors but they thought that it should never get out that almost a whole patrol had been wiped out by one creature, so they came up with some story about all those who had gone with me being moved to Skyrim or some other such place. For years I have kept this story to myself, but now I feel it is the time for it to be told, even if I do lose my rank for it. Let the power of the lycanthropes be known.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
穆鲁迪乌斯<BR>
莫尼乌斯·卡西尔 将军
<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
在我生命的暮年，我写下了职业生涯中最有趣的一段经历。在我年轻的时候，或者在我军衔较低的时候，我绝不敢写下这件事，但现在我已经是一位老将军了，我想这应该不会有什么坏处。你看，我之所以不敢早点写下来，是因为军团不愿意承认这样的事件会发生。他们声称能够控制疯狂的狼化病者。事实是，他们根本无法控制。<BR>
那段恐怖经历的第一天开始得还算顺利，我们刚刚消灭了一些逃入阿尔贡沼泽深处的匪徒。我们一共有七个人：穆鲁迪乌斯和我，都是帝国长枪兵；纳钦，我们的红卫剑术大师；韦尔图斯队长，探险队的领队；格罗-阿德，一个兽人蛮子；阿雷思，我们的木精灵弓箭手；还有一个阿尔贡向导，我现在想不起他的名字了。我们花了六天时间才到达那里，回程时我们并不着急，聊着每个军团士兵都会聊的话题：名声、财富、女人和美酒。夜幕降临，一切似乎都很完美，直到前方我们的向导发出一声尖叫，让我们停下了脚步，吓得我们毛骨悚然。我们跑向尖叫声传来的方向，只发现向导的血洒了一地。队长猜测是什么野兽抓住了他，决定我们应该继续前进，不再管他。<BR>
没过多久，我们找到了一些向导的遗骸和杀死他的生物。那生物还没有注意到我们，作为年轻气盛的冒险者，我们觉得如果能干掉这么大的一头野兽，那一定很刺激。我们不知道的是，这将导致我们的毁灭。我们决定由穆鲁迪乌斯、格罗-阿德和我与那生物交战，这样纳钦就可以从后面袭击它，而阿雷思和韦尔图斯则用箭和魔法支援我们。我们三人攻击了那生物，但它比我们想象的要聪明得多。它设法折断了我的长矛，并用尾巴扫倒了纳钦，同时避开了箭矢和法术。直到它咬住了穆鲁迪乌斯的肩膀，给了格罗-阿德机会将斧头砍进它的后背，战斗才取得了胜利。那生物受了致命伤，逃进了灌木丛，但我们认为不追它是明智的。<BR><BR>
第二天，穆鲁迪乌斯抱怨头痛，但我们没在意。我们太忙于留意周围环境，以防那野兽决定回来。<BR>
第三天，我们意识到穆鲁迪乌斯从那个生物身上感染了某种疾病，也知道我们必须尽快找到一个文明的地方。没有向导，我们不知道附近有任何村庄，只能前往最近的帝国城镇，那要四天漫长的路程。那天晚上，我们都被穆鲁迪乌斯的一声尖叫惊醒。我们冲到他的铺盖旁，发现他痛苦地扭动着。但穆鲁迪乌斯已不再是那个我们认识的人，他就在我们眼前变成了类似那个野兽的东西。队长愚蠢地走过去帮忙，却被一只爬行动物的手臂狠狠地击中了头部侧面。那个曾是穆鲁迪乌斯的怪物没有就此罢休，它继续用爪子攻击队长，把他的身体变成了一团令人作呕的血肉模糊的东西。我们其余人慌忙去拿武器和盔甲，但已经太晚了。那生物抓住了阿雷思，迅速消失在夜色中。<BR>
那天晚上我们一直赶路，直到第二天。我们断定咬伤穆鲁迪乌斯的生物是狼化病者，于是认为白天行动会比较安全。那天晚些时候，休息过后，我们偶然发现了阿雷思的部分遗骸和他的装备。在他的物品中，我找到了阿雷思的弓和“黑尖”，一支阿雷思声称他的祖先用过、总能一击毙命的箭。我想，如果他所说属实，这支箭将有助于我杀死那怪物。<BR><BR>
到了傍晚，我们找到了一条河，有一处浅滩可以过河，我们决定最好在这里过夜，因为这样我们可以从两边看到怪物过来，并做好准备。我觉得这个计划有点不对劲，但我们认为总比穿过茂密的灌木丛要好，在那里怪物可能在任何地方等着我们。当我听到右边传来巨大的水花声时，我意识到了问题所在 -- 那怪物的样子看起来像是当地土著称为鳄鱼的大型爬行动物之一，我记得它们是游泳健将。我转向右边，看到纳钦被拖到水面下时脸上震惊的表情。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Mystery of Princess Talara<BR>
Part I<BR>
By Mera Llykith<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The year was 3E 405. The occasion was the millennial celebration of the founding of the Breton Kingdom of Camlorn. Every grand boulevard and narrow alley was strung with gold and purple banners, some plain, some marked with the heraldic symbols of the Royal Family or the various principalities and dukedoms which were vassals of the King. Musicians played in the plazas great and small, and on every street corner was a new exotic entertainer: Redguard snake charmers, Khajiiti acrobats, magicians of genuine power and those whose flamboyant skill was equally impressive if largely illusion.<BR>
<BR>
The sight that drew most of the male citizens of Camlorn was the March of Beauty. A thousand comely young women, brightly and provocatively dressed, danced their way down the long, wide main street of the city, from the Temple of Sethiete to the Royal Palace. The menfolk jostled one another and craned their necks, picking their favorites. It was no secret that they were all prostitutes, and after the March and the Flower Festival that evening, they would be available for more intimate business.<BR>
<BR>
Gyna attracted much of the attention with her tall, curvaceous figure barely covered by strips of silk and her curls of flaxen hair specked with flower petals. In her late twenties, she wasn't the youngest of the prostitutes, but she was certainly one of the most desirable. It was clear by her demeanor that she was used to the lascivious glances, though she was far from jaded at the sight of the city in splendor. Compared to the squalid quarter of Daggerfall where she made her home, Camlorn at the height of celebration seemed so unreal. And yet, what was even stranger was how, at the same time, familiar it all looked, though she had never been there before.<BR>
<BR>
The King's daughter Lady Jyllia rode out of the palace gates, and immediately cursed her misfortune. She had completely forgotten about the March of Beauty. The streets were snarled, at a standstill. It would take hours to wait for the March to pass, and she had promised her old nurse Ramke a visit in her house south of the city. Jyllia thought for a moment, picturing in her mind the arrangement of streets in the city, and devised a shortcut to avoid the main street and the March.<BR>
<BR>
For a few minutes she felt very clever as she wound her way through tight, curving side streets, but presently she came upon temporary structures, tents and theaters set up for the celebration, and had to improvise a new path. In no time at all, she was lost in the city where she had lived all but five years of her life.<BR>
<BR>
Peering down an alley, she saw the main avenue crowded with the March of Beauty. Hoping that it was the tale end, and desirous not to be lost again, Lady Jyllia guided her horse toward the festival. She did not see the snake-charmer at the mouth of the alley, and when his pet hissed and spread its hood, her charge reared up in fear.<BR>
<BR>
The women in the parade gasped and surged back at the sight, but Lady Jyllia quickly calmed her stallion down. She looked abashed at the spectacle she had caused.<BR>
"My apologies, ladies," she said with a mock military salute.<BR>
<BR>
"It's all right, madam," said a blonde in silk. "We'll be out of your way in a moment."<BR>
<BR>
Jyllia stared as the March passed her. Looking at that whore had been like looking in a mirror. The same age, and height, and hair, and eyes, and figure, almost exactly. The woman looked back at her, and it seemed as if she was thinking the same thing.<BR>
<BR>
And so Gyna was. The old witches who sometimes came in to Daggerfall had sometimes spoke of doppelgangers, spirits that assumed the guise of their victims and portended certain death. Yet the experience had not frightened her: it seemed only one more strangely familiar aspect of the alien city. Before the March had danced it way into the palace gates, she had all but forgotten the encounter.<BR>
<BR>
The prostitutes crushed into the courtyard, as the King himself came to the balcony to greet them. At his side was his chief bodyguard, a battlemage by the look of him. As for the King himself, he was a handsome man of middle age, rather unremarkable, but Gyna was awed at the sight of him. A dream, perhaps. Yes, that was it: she could see him as she had dreamt of him, high above her as he was now, bending now to kiss her. Not a one of lust as she had experienced before, but one of small fondness, a dutiful kiss.<BR>

"Dear ladies, you have filled the streets of the great capitol of Camlorn with your beauty," cried the King, forcing a silence on the giggling, murmuring assembly. He smiled proudly. <BR>

<BR>
"I've seen looks of hunger before, and that wasn't one of them," laughed Gyna. "I'd wager he thought I was someone else, like that lady who tried to run us over with her horse. She's probably his kin, and he thought she had dressed up like a courtesan and joined the March of Beauty. Can you imagine the scandal?"<BR>
<BR>
When they arrived at the tents, they were greeted by a stocky, well-dressed young man with a bald pate and a commanding presence of authority. He introduced himself as Lord Strale, ambassador to the Emperor himself, and their chief patron. It was Strale who had hired them, on the Emperor's behalf, as a gift to the King and the kingdom of Camlorn.<BR>
<BR>
"The March of Beauty is but a precursor to the Flower Festival tonight," he said. Unlike the King, he did not have to yell to be heard. His voice was loud and precise in its natural modulations. "I expect each of you to perform well, and justify the significant expense I've suffered bringing you all the way up here. Now hurry, you must be dressed and in position on Cavilstyr Rock before the sun goes down."<BR>
<BR>
The ambassador needn't have worried. The women were all professionals, experts at getting dressed and undressed with none of the time-consuming measures less promiscuous females required. His manservant Gnorbooth offered his assistance, but found he had little to do. Their costumes were simplicity itself: soft, narrow sheets with a hole for their heads. Not even a belt was required, so the gowns were open at the sides exposing the frame of their skin.<BR>
<BR>
So it was long before the sun had set that the prostitutes turned dancers were at Cavilstyr Rock. It was a great, wide promontory facing the sea, and for the occasion of the Festival of Flowers, a large circle of unlit torches and covered baskets had been arranged. As early as they were, a crowd of spectators had already arrived. The women gathered in the center of the circle and waited until it was time.<BR>
<BR>
Gyna watched the crowd as it grew, and was not surprised when she saw the lady from the March approaching, hand-in-hand with a very old, very short white-haired woman. The old woman was distracted, pointing out islands out at sea. The blonde lady seemed nervous, unsure of what to say. Gyna was used to dealing with uneasy clients, and spoke first. <BR>
<BR>
"Good to see you again, madam. I am Gyna of Daggerfall."<BR>
<BR>
"I'm glad you bear me no ill will because of the whores, I mean horse," the lady laughed, somewhat relieved. "I am Lady Jyllia Raze, daughter of the King."<BR>
<BR>
"I always thought that daughters of kings were called princess," smiled Gyna.<BR>
<BR>
"In Camlorn, only when they are heirs to the throne. I have a younger brother from my father's new wife whom he favors," Jyllia replied. She felt her head swim. It was madness, speaking to a common prostitute, talking of family politics so intimately. "Relative to that subject, I must ask you something very peculiar. <BR>

<BR>
"I don't know. It was a name I just thought you might recognize," sighed Lady Jyllia. "Have you been to Camlorn before?"<BR>
<BR>
"If I did, it was when I was very young," said Gyna, and suddenly she felt it was her turn to be trusting. Something about the Lady Jyllia's friendly and forthcoming manner touched her. "To be honest, I don't remember anything at all of my childhood before I was nine or ten. Perhaps I was here with my parents, whoever they were, when I was a little girl. I tell you, I think perhaps I was. I don't recall ever being here before, but everything I've seen, the city, you, the King himself, all seem ... like I've been here before, long ago."<BR>
Lady Jyllia gasped and took a step back. She gripped the old woman, who had been looking out to sea and murmuring, by the hand. The elderly creature looked to Jyllia, surprised, and then turned to Gyna. Her ancient, half-blind eyes sparkled with recognition and she made a sound like a grunt of surprise. Gyna also jumped. If the King had seemed like something out of a half-forgotten dream, this woman was someone she knew. As clear and yet indistinct as a guardian spirit.<BR>
<BR>
"I apologize," stammered Lady Jyllia. "This is my childhood nursemaid, Ramke."<BR>
<BR>
"It's her!" the old woman cried, wild-eyed. She tried to run forward, arms outstretched, but Jyllia held her back. Gyna felt strangely naked, and pulled her robe against her body.<BR>
<BR>
"No, you're wrong," Lady Jyllia whispered to Ramke, holding the old woman tightly. "The Princess Talara is dead, you know that. I shouldn't have brought you here. I'll take you back home." She turned back to Gyna, her eyes welling with tears. "The entire royal family of Camlorn was assassinated over twenty years ago. My father was Duke of Oloine, the King's brother, and so he inherited the crown. I'm sorry to have bothered you. Goodnight."<BR>
<BR>
Gyna gazed after Lady Jyllia and the old nurse as they disappeared into the crowd, but she had little time to consider all she had heard. The sun was setting, and it was time for the Flower Festival. Twelve young men emerged from the darkness wearing only loincloths and masks, and lit the torches. The moment the fire blazed, Gyna and all the rest of the dancers rushed to the baskets, pulling out blossoms and vines by the handful.<BR>
<BR>
At first, the women danced with one another, sprinkling petals to the wind. The crowd then joined in as the music swelled. It was a mad, beautiful chaos. Gyna leapt and swooned like a wild forest nymph. Then, without warning, she felt rough hands grip her from behind and push her.<BR>
<BR>
She was falling before she understood it. The moment the realization hit, she was closer to the bottom of the hundred foot tall cliff than she was to the top. She flailed out her arms and grasped at the cliff wall. Her fingers raked against the stone and her flesh tore, but she found a grip and held it. For a moment, she stayed there, breathing hard. Then she began to scream.<BR>
<BR>
The music and the festival were too loud up above: no one could hear her - she could scarcely hear herself. Below her, the surf crashed. Every bone in her body would snap if she fell. She closed her eyes, and a vision came. A man was standing below her, a King of great wisdom, great compassion, looking up, smiling. A little girl, golden-haired, mischievous, her best friend and cousin, clung to the rock beside her.<BR>
<BR>
"The secret to falling is making your body go limp. And with luck, you won't get hurt," the girl said. She nodded, remembering who she was. Eight years of darkness lifted.<BR>
<BR>
She released her grip and let herself fall like a leaf into the water below.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
塔拉瑞公主之谜<BR>
第一部分<BR>
梅拉·莱基斯 著<BR><BR>

那是第三纪元405年。正值布莱顿王国卡姆洛恩建国千年庆典。每一条宽阔的林荫大道和狭窄的小巷都悬挂着金色和紫色的旗帜，有的朴素，有的则饰有王室或国王下属各个公国与公爵领的纹章符号。音乐家们在大小广场上演奏，每个街角都有新奇的异国艺人：红卫人的耍蛇者、卡吉特杂技演员、拥有真正力量的魔法师，以及那些即使大多是幻术、其华丽技巧也同样令人印象深刻的艺人。<BR>

“没关系，女士，”一个穿丝绸衣服的金发女郎说，“我们马上就让开。”<BR>
<BR>
吉莉娅凝视着游行队伍从她身边经过。看着那个妓女，就像在照镜子。同样的年龄、身高、头发、眼睛和身材，几乎一模一样。那个女人也回头看着她，似乎也在想着同样的事情。<BR>
<BR>
吉娜也是如此。有时来途歇的老女巫们会谈论分身，那些伪装成受害者、预示死亡的灵魂。然而，这次经历并没有吓到她：这似乎只是这座陌生城市又一个奇怪的熟悉之处。在游行队伍跳着舞进入宫门之前，她几乎已经忘记了这次相遇。<BR>
<BR>
妓女们涌入庭院，国王亲自来到阳台迎接她们。他身边是他的首席保镖，看起来像个战斗法师。至于国王本人，他是个英俊的中年男子，相当不起眼，但吉娜看到他却心生敬畏。也许是一个梦。是的，就是这样：她看到他就像她在梦中梦到他一样，高高在上，就像现在这样，俯身亲吻她。不是她以前经历过的情欲之吻，而是一种小小的喜爱，一个尽责的吻。<BR>
<BR>
“亲爱的女士们，你们用美丽装点了卡姆洛恩伟大首都的街道，”国王喊道，使窃窃私语、咯咯笑着的人群安静下来。他骄傲地微笑着。他的目光与吉娜相遇，他停了下来，心神不宁。他们的目光仿佛锁定了一个世纪，直到殿下恢复过来，继续他的演讲。<BR>
<BR>
之后，当女人们都返回帐篷换上晚上的服装时，一个年长的妓女走近吉娜：“你看到国王看你的眼神了吗？如果你聪明的话，你会在这庆典结束前成为新的王室情妇。”<BR>
<BR>
“我以前见过渴望的眼神，但那个不是，”吉娜笑道。“我敢打赌他以为我是别人，比如那个差点骑马踩到我们的女士。她可能是他的亲戚，他以为她打扮成妓女加入了美人游行。你能想象那丑闻吗？”<BR>
<BR>
当他们到达帐篷时，一个敦实、穿着考究、秃头、具有权威气场的年轻人迎接了他们。他自我介绍说是斯特拉尔勋爵，皇帝本人的大使，也是他们的主要赞助人。正是斯特拉尔代表皇帝雇用了她们，作为给国王和卡姆洛恩王国的礼物。<BR>
<BR>
“美人游行只是今晚鲜花节的前奏，”他说。不像国王，他不需要大喊大叫就能让人听见。他的声音响亮，语调自然精准。“我期望你们每个人都表现出色，证明我花大价钱把你们带到这里是值得的。现在快点，你们必须在日落前穿好衣服，在卡维尔斯蒂尔岩上就位。”<BR>
<BR>
大使不必担心。女人们都是专业人士，擅长穿衣和脱衣，无需那些不那么放荡的女人所需的耗时步骤。他的男仆格诺博斯主动提出帮忙，但发现没什么可做的。她们的服装极其简单：柔软、窄小的床单，中间有个洞让头穿过。甚至连腰带都不需要，所以长裙两侧敞开，露出她们肌肤的轮廓。<BR>
<BR>
因此，在太阳落山很久之前，妓女们已变作舞者来到了卡维尔斯蒂尔岩。那是一个面朝大海的巨大、宽阔的海岬，为了鲜花节，一大圈未点燃的火炬和盖着盖子的篮子已经布置好了。尽管她们到得很早，但已经有一群观众到达了。女人们在圆圈中央集合，等待时机。<BR>
<BR>
吉娜看着越来越多的人群，当她看到游行中的那位女士和一个非常年老、矮小、白发苍苍的女人手拉手走近时，并不感到惊讶。老妇人有些心不在焉，指着海上的岛屿。金发女士似乎很紧张，不知道该说什么。吉娜习惯于应对不安的客人，于是先开口了。<BR>
<BR>
“很高兴再次见到您，女士。我是途歇的吉娜。”<BR>
<BR>
“我很高兴你没有因为那些妓女，我是说马，而对我怀恨在心，”那位女士笑了，稍微松了口气。“我是吉莉娅·雷兹女士，国王的女儿。”<BR>
<BR>
“我一直以为国王的女儿被称为公主，”吉娜微笑道。<BR>
<BR>
“在卡姆洛恩，只有当他们是王位继承人时才是。我父亲的新妻子给他生了一个弟弟，他很宠爱他，”吉莉娅回答。她感到头晕目眩。跟一个普通妓女说话，如此亲密地谈论家庭政治，简直是疯了。“关于那个话题，我必须问你一件非常奇怪的事。你听说过塔拉瑞公主吗？”<BR>
<BR>
吉娜想了一会儿：“这名字听起来有点耳熟。我为什么会知道？”<BR>
<BR>
“我不知道。我只是觉得你可能认识这个名字，”吉莉娅女士叹了口气。“你以前来过卡姆洛恩吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“如果来过，那也是我很小的时候，”吉娜说，突然她觉得轮到她信任了。吉莉娅女士友好而坦诚的态度触动了她。“老实说，我完全记不起九、十岁之前童年的任何事情。也许我还是个小女孩的时候，和我的父母 -- 不管他们是谁 -- 来过这里。我告诉你，我想可能来过。我不记得以前来过这里，但我看到的一切，这座城市，你，国王本人，都似乎......好像我很久以前来过这里。”<BR>
吉莉娅女士倒吸一口气，退后一步。她抓住那个一直在眺望大海并喃喃自语的老妇人的手。老妇人惊讶地看向吉莉娅，然后转向吉娜。她那双苍老、半瞎的眼睛闪烁着认出的光芒，并发出一声惊讶的咕哝。吉娜也跳了起来。如果说国王像是半个遗忘的梦中的事物，那么这个女人就是她认识的人。清晰却又模糊，如同守护灵。<BR>
<BR>
“我道歉，”吉莉娅女士结结巴巴地说，“这是我童年的保姆，拉姆克。”<BR>
<BR>
“是她！”老妇人喊道，眼神狂乱。她试图伸出双臂向前跑，但吉莉娅拉住了她。吉娜感到一种奇怪的裸露感，把长袍裹紧了身体。<BR>
<BR>
“不，你错了，”吉莉娅女士对拉姆克低语，紧紧地抱住老妇人。“塔拉瑞公主死了，你知道的。我不该带你来这里。我送你回家。”她转向吉娜，眼中涌出泪水。“卡姆洛恩的整个王室在二十多年前被暗杀了。我父亲是奥洛因公爵，国王的弟弟，所以他继承了王位。抱歉打扰你了。晚安。”<BR>
<BR>
吉娜凝视着吉莉娅女士和老保姆消失在人群中，但她没有时间思考她听到的一切。太阳落山了，鲜花节的时间到了。十二个年轻男子从黑暗中现身，只穿着缠腰布和面具，点燃了火炬。火焰燃起的瞬间，吉娜和其他所有舞者冲向篮子，一把把地拉出花朵和藤蔓。<BR>
<BR>
起初，女人们互相跳舞，向风中撒花瓣。随着音乐激昂，人群也加入进来。那是一场疯狂而美丽的混乱。吉娜像狂野的森林宁芙一样跳跃、昏眩。然后，毫无预兆地，她感到一双粗糙的手从背后抓住了她，推了她一把。<BR>
<BR>
她还没明白怎么回事就已经在坠落。当她意识到的那一刻，她离一百英尺高悬崖的底部比顶部更近。她拼命伸出双臂，抓住崖壁。她的手指划过石头，皮肉撕裂，但她找到了一个抓握点并紧紧抓住。有那么一会儿，她待在那里，大口喘气。然后她开始尖叫。<BR>
<BR>
上面的音乐和庆典太吵了：没人能听到她 -- 她几乎听不到自己的声音。在她下方，海浪撞击着。如果她掉下去，身上的每根骨头都会断裂。她闭上眼睛，一个幻象出现了。一个男人站在她下面，一位充满智慧、充满慈悲的国王，抬头看着她，微笑着。一个小女孩，金发，调皮，她最好的朋友兼表妹，紧紧抓着她旁边的岩石。<BR>
<BR>
“坠落的秘诀是让身体放松。运气好的话，你不会受伤，”女孩说。她点点头，想起了自己是谁。八年的黑暗消散了。<BR>
<BR>
她松开手，让自己像一片叶子一样落入下面的水中。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Mystery of Princess Talara<BR>
Part I<BR>
By Mera Llykith<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The year was 3E 405. The occasion was the millennial celebration of the founding of the Breton Kingdom of Camlorn. Every grand boulevard and narrow alley was strung with gold and purple banners, some plain, some marked with the heraldic symbols of the Royal Family or the various principalities and dukedoms which were vassals of the King. Musicians played in the plazas great and small, and on every street corner was a new exotic entertainer: Redguard snake charmers, Khajiiti acrobats, magicians of genuine power and those whose flamboyant skill was equally impressive if largely illusion.<BR>
<BR>
The sight that drew most of the male citizens of Camlorn was the March of Beauty. A thousand comely young women, brightly and provocatively dressed, danced their way down the long, wide main street of the city, from the Temple of Sethiete to the Royal Palace. The menfolk jostled one another and craned their necks, picking their favorites. It was no secret that they were all prostitutes, and after the March and the Flower Festival that evening, they would be available for more intimate business.<BR>
<BR>
Gyna attracted much of the attention with her tall, curvaceous figure barely covered by strips of silk and her curls of flaxen hair specked with flower petals. In her late twenties, she wasn't the youngest of the prostitutes, but she was certainly one of the most desirable. It was clear by her demeanor that she was used to the lascivious glances, though she was far from jaded at the sight of the city in splendor. Compared to the squalid quarter of Daggerfall where she made her home, Camlorn at the height of celebration seemed so unreal. And yet, what was even stranger was how, at the same time, familiar it all looked, though she had never been there before.<BR>
<BR>
The King's daughter Lady Jyllia rode out of the palace gates, and immediately cursed her misfortune. She had completely forgotten about the March of Beauty. The streets were snarled, at a standstill. It would take hours to wait for the March to pass, and she had promised her old nurse Ramke a visit in her house south of the city. Jyllia thought for a moment, picturing in her mind the arrangement of streets in the city, and devised a shortcut to avoid the main street and the March.<BR>
<BR>
For a few minutes she felt very clever as she wound her way through tight, curving side streets, but presently she came upon temporary structures, tents and theaters set up for the celebration, and had to improvise a new path. In no time at all, she was lost in the city where she had lived all but five years of her life.<BR>
<BR>
Peering down an alley, she saw the main avenue crowded with the March of Beauty. Hoping that it was the tale end, and desirous not to be lost again, Lady Jyllia guided her horse toward the festival. She did not see the snake-charmer at the mouth of the alley, and when his pet hissed and spread its hood, her charge reared up in fear.<BR>
<BR>
The women in the parade gasped and surged back at the sight, but Lady Jyllia quickly calmed her stallion down. She looked abashed at the spectacle she had caused.<BR>
"My apologies, ladies," she said with a mock military salute.<BR>
<BR>
"It's all right, madam," said a blonde in silk. "We'll be out of your way in a moment."<BR>
<BR>
Jyllia stared as the March passed her. Looking at that whore had been like looking in a mirror. The same age, and height, and hair, and eyes, and figure, almost exactly. The woman looked back at her, and it seemed as if she was thinking the same thing.<BR>
<BR>
And so Gyna was. The old witches who sometimes came in to Daggerfall had sometimes spoke of doppelgangers, spirits that assumed the guise of their victims and portended certain death. Yet the experience had not frightened her: it seemed only one more strangely familiar aspect of the alien city. Before the March had danced it way into the palace gates, she had all but forgotten the encounter.<BR>
<BR>
The prostitutes crushed into the courtyard, as the King himself came to the balcony to greet them. At his side was his chief bodyguard, a battlemage by the look of him. As for the King himself, he was a handsome man of middle age, rather unremarkable, but Gyna was awed at the sight of him. A dream, perhaps. Yes, that was it: she could see him as she had dreamt of him, high above her as he was now, bending now to kiss her. Not a one of lust as she had experienced before, but one of small fondness, a dutiful kiss.<BR>
<BR>
"Dear ladies, you have filled the streets of the great capitol of Camlorn with your beauty," cried the King, forcing a silence on the giggling, murmuring assembly. He smiled proudly. His eyes met Gyna's and he stopped, shaken. For an eternity, they stayed locked together before His Highness recovered and continued his speech.<BR>
<BR>
Afterwards, while the women were all en route back to their tents to change into their costumes for the evening, one of the older prostitutes approached Gyna: "Did you see how the King looked at you? If you're smart, you'll be the new royal mistress before this celebration ends."<BR>
<BR>
"I've seen looks of hunger before, and that wasn't one of them," laughed Gyna. "I'd wager he thought I was someone else, like that lady who tried to run us over with her horse. She's probably his kin, and he thought she had dressed up like a courtesan and joined the March of Beauty. Can you imagine the scandal?"<BR>
<BR>
When they arrived at the tents, they were greeted by a stocky, well-dressed young man with a bald pate and a commanding presence of authority. He introduced himself as Lord Strale, ambassador to the Emperor himself, and their chief patron. It was Strale who had hired them, on the Emperor's behalf, as a gift to the King and the kingdom of Camlorn.<BR>
<BR>
"The March of Beauty is but a precursor to the Flower Festival tonight," he said. Unlike the King, he did not have to yell to be heard. His voice was loud and precise in its natural modulations. "I expect each of you to perform well, and justify the significant expense I've suffered bringing you all the way up here. Now hurry, you must be dressed and in position on Cavilstyr Rock before the sun goes down."<BR>
<BR>
The ambassador needn't have worried. The women were all professionals, experts at getting dressed and undressed with none of the time-consuming measures less promiscuous females required. His manservant Gnorbooth offered his assistance, but found he had little to do. Their costumes were simplicity itself: soft, narrow sheets with a hole for their heads. Not even a belt was required, so the gowns were open at the sides exposing the frame of their skin.<BR>
<BR>
So it was long before the sun had set that the prostitutes turned dancers were at Cavilstyr Rock. It was a great, wide promontory facing the sea, and for the occasion of the Festival of Flowers, a large circle of unlit torches and covered baskets had been arranged. As early as they were, a crowd of spectators had already arrived. The women gathered in the center of the circle and waited until it was time.<BR>
<BR>
Gyna watched the crowd as it grew, and was not surprised when she saw the lady from the March approaching, hand-in-hand with a very old, very short white-haired woman. The old woman was distracted, pointing out islands out at sea. The blonde lady seemed nervous, unsure of what to say. Gyna was used to dealing with uneasy clients, and spoke first. <BR>
<BR>
"Good to see you again, madam. I am Gyna of Daggerfall."<BR>
<BR>
"I'm glad you bear me no ill will because of the whores, I mean horse," the lady laughed, somewhat relieved. "I am Lady Jyllia Raze, daughter of the King."<BR>
<BR>
"I always thought that daughters of kings were called princess," smiled Gyna.<BR>
<BR>
"In Camlorn, only when they are heirs to the throne. I have a younger brother from my father's new wife whom he favors," Jyllia replied. She felt her head swim. It was madness, speaking to a common prostitute, talking of family politics so intimately. "Relative to that subject, I must ask you something very peculiar. Have you ever heard of the Princess Talara?"<BR>
<BR>
Gyna thought a moment: "The name sounds somewhat familiar. Why would I have?"<BR>
<BR>
"I don't know. It was a name I just thought you might recognize," sighed Lady Jyllia. "Have you been to Camlorn before?"<BR>
<BR>
"If I did, it was when I was very young," said Gyna, and suddenly she felt it was her turn to be trusting. Something about the Lady Jyllia's friendly and forthcoming manner touched her. "To be honest, I don't remember anything at all of my childhood before I was nine or ten. Perhaps I was here with my parents, whoever they were, when I was a little girl. I tell you, I think perhaps I was. I don't recall ever being here before, but everything I've seen, the city, you, the King himself, all seem ... like I've been here before, long ago."<BR>
Lady Jyllia gasped and took a step back. She gripped the old woman, who had been looking out to sea and murmuring, by the hand. The elderly creature looked to Jyllia, surprised, and then turned to Gyna. Her ancient, half-blind eyes sparkled with recognition and she made a sound like a grunt of surprise. Gyna also jumped. If the King had seemed like something out of a half-forgotten dream, this woman was someone she knew. As clear and yet indistinct as a guardian spirit.<BR>
<BR>
"I apologize," stammered Lady Jyllia. "This is my childhood nursemaid, Ramke."<BR>
<BR>
"It's her!" the old woman cried, wild-eyed. She tried to run forward, arms outstretched, but Jyllia held her back. Gyna felt strangely naked, and pulled her robe against her body.<BR>
<BR>
"No, you're wrong," Lady Jyllia whispered to Ramke, holding the old woman tightly. "The Princess Talara is dead, you know that. I shouldn't have brought you here. I'll take you back home." She turned back to Gyna, her eyes welling with tears. "The entire royal family of Camlorn was assassinated over twenty years ago. My father was Duke of Oloine, the King's brother, and so he inherited the crown. I'm sorry to have bothered you. Goodnight."<BR>
<BR>
Gyna gazed after Lady Jyllia and the old nurse as they disappeared into the crowd, but she had little time to consider all she had heard. The sun was setting, and it was time for the Flower Festival. Twelve young men emerged from the darkness wearing only loincloths and masks, and lit the torches. The moment the fire blazed, Gyna and all the rest of the dancers rushed to the baskets, pulling out blossoms and vines by the handful.<BR>
<BR>
At first, the women danced with one another, sprinkling petals to the wind. The crowd then joined in as the music swelled. It was a mad, beautiful chaos. Gyna leapt and swooned like a wild forest nymph. Then, without warning, she felt rough hands grip her from behind and push her.<BR>
<BR>
She was falling before she understood it. The moment the realization hit, she was closer to the bottom of the hundred foot tall cliff than she was to the top. She flailed out her arms and grasped at the cliff wall. Her fingers raked against the stone and her flesh tore, but she found a grip and held it. For a moment, she stayed there, breathing hard. Then she began to scream.<BR>
<BR>
The music and the festival were too loud up above: no one could hear her - she could scarcely hear herself. Below her, the surf crashed. Every bone in her body would snap if she fell. She closed her eyes, and a vision came. A man was standing below her, a King of great wisdom, great compassion, looking up, smiling. A little girl, golden-haired, mischievous, her best friend and cousin, clung to the rock beside her.<BR>
<BR>
"The secret to falling is making your body go limp. And with luck, you won't get hurt," the girl said. She nodded, remembering who she was. Eight years of darkness lifted.<BR>
<BR>
She released her grip and let herself fall like a leaf into the water below.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
塔拉瑞公主之谜<BR>
第一部分<BR>
梅拉·莱基斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
那是第三纪元405年。正值布莱顿王国卡姆洛恩建国千年庆典。每一条宽阔的林荫大道和狭窄的小巷都悬挂着金色和紫色的旗帜，有的朴素，有的则饰有王室或国王下属各个公国与公爵领的纹章符号。音乐家们在大小广场上演奏，每个街角都有新奇的异国艺人：红卫人的耍蛇者、卡吉特杂技演员、拥有真正力量的魔法师，以及那些即使大多是幻术、其华丽技巧也同样令人印象深刻的艺人。<BR>
<BR>
最吸引卡姆洛恩男性市民的景观是“美人游行”。一千名容貌秀丽的年轻女子，身着鲜艳而挑逗的服装，沿着城市又长又宽的主干道，从塞西埃特神殿一路跳舞到王宫。男人们互相推搡，伸长脖子，挑选自己心仪的对象。她们都是妓女，这已不是秘密，游行和当晚的鲜花节之后，她们将提供更私密的服务。<BR>
<BR>
吉娜以她高挑、曲线玲珑的身材（仅被丝带勉强遮盖）和点缀着花瓣的亚麻色卷发吸引了很多目光。她年近三十，不是最年轻的妓女，但无疑是最具吸引力的之一。从她的举止可以明显看出，她已习惯于那些淫荡的目光，尽管面对这座辉煌的城市，她远未感到厌倦。与她居住的途歇肮脏街区相比，处于庆典高潮的卡姆洛恩显得如此不真实。然而，更奇怪的是，尽管她从未到过这里，一切看起来却又如此熟悉。<BR>
<BR>
国王的女儿吉莉娅女士骑马出了宫门，立刻诅咒起自己的不幸。她完全忘记了美人游行。街道拥堵不堪，寸步难行。等待游行队伍通过需要几个小时，而她答应过她的老保姆拉姆克去城南她家看望她。吉莉娅想了一会儿，在脑海中描绘出城市街道的布局，设计了一条避开主干道和游行的捷径。<BR>
<BR>
有那么几分钟，她觉得自己非常聪明，蜿蜒穿行于狭窄弯曲的小巷，但不久她就遇到了为庆典搭建的临时建筑、帐篷和剧院，不得不临时开辟一条新路。转眼间，她就在自己除了五年外住了大半辈子的城市里迷路了。<BR>
<BR>
她朝一条小巷望去，看到主干道上挤满了美人游行的队伍。吉莉娅女士希望那是队伍的末尾，并且不想再迷路，于是骑马朝庆典走去。她没有看到巷口的耍蛇人，当他的宠物蛇发出嘶嘶声并展开颈部皮褶时，她的坐骑惊恐地前蹄腾空。<BR>
<BR>
游行队伍中的女人们看到这一幕倒吸一口凉气，纷纷后退，但吉莉娅女士很快安抚好了她的公马。她对自己造成的场面感到羞愧。<BR>
“女士们，抱歉，”她开玩笑似的行了个军礼。<BR>
<BR>
“没关系，女士，”一个穿丝绸衣服的金发女郎说，“我们马上就让开。”<BR>
<BR>
吉莉娅凝视着游行队伍从她身边经过。看着那个妓女，就像在照镜子。同样的年龄、身高、头发、眼睛和身材，几乎一模一样。那个女人也回头看着她，似乎也在想着同样的事情。<BR>
<BR>
吉娜也是如此。有时来途歇的老女巫们会谈论分身，那些伪装成受害者、预示死亡的灵魂。然而，这次经历并没有吓到她：这似乎只是这座陌生城市又一个奇怪的熟悉之处。在游行队伍跳着舞进入宫门之前，她几乎已经忘记了这次相遇。<BR>
<BR>
妓女们涌入庭院，国王亲自来到阳台迎接她们。他身边是他的首席保镖，看起来像个战斗法师。至于国王本人，他是个英俊的中年男子，相当不起眼，但吉娜看到他却心生敬畏。也许是一个梦。是的，就是这样：她看到他就像她在梦中梦到他一样，高高在上，就像现在这样，俯身亲吻她。不是她以前经历过的情欲之吻，而是一种小小的喜爱，一个尽责的吻。<BR>
<BR>
“亲爱的女士们，你们用美丽装点了卡姆洛恩伟大首都的街道，”国王喊道，使窃窃私语、咯咯笑着的人群安静下来。他骄傲地微笑着。他的目光与吉娜相遇，他停了下来，心神不宁。他们的目光仿佛锁定了一个世纪，直到殿下恢复过来，继续他的演讲。<BR>
<BR>
之后，当女人们都返回帐篷换上晚上的服装时，一个年长的妓女走近吉娜：“你看到国王看你的眼神了吗？如果你聪明的话，你会在这庆典结束前成为新的王室情妇。”<BR>
<BR>
“我以前见过渴望的眼神，但那个不是，”吉娜笑道。“我敢打赌他以为我是别人，比如那个差点骑马踩到我们的女士。她可能是他的亲戚，他以为她打扮成妓女加入了美人游行。你能想象那丑闻吗？”<BR>
<BR>
当他们到达帐篷时，一个敦实、穿着考究、秃头、具有权威气场的年轻人迎接了他们。他自我介绍说是斯特拉尔勋爵，皇帝本人的大使，也是他们的主要赞助人。正是斯特拉尔代表皇帝雇用了她们，作为给国王和卡姆洛恩王国的礼物。<BR>
<BR>
“美人游行只是今晚鲜花节的前奏，”他说。不像国王，他不需要大喊大叫就能让人听见。他的声音响亮，语调自然精准。“我期望你们每个人都表现出色，证明我花大价钱把你们带到这里是值得的。现在快点，你们必须在日落前穿好衣服，在卡维尔斯蒂尔岩上就位。”<BR>
<BR>
大使不必担心。女人们都是专业人士，擅长穿衣和脱衣，无需那些不那么放荡的女人所需的耗时步骤。他的男仆格诺博斯主动提出帮忙，但发现没什么可做的。她们的服装极其简单：柔软、窄小的床单，中间有个洞让头穿过。甚至连腰带都不需要，所以长裙两侧敞开，露出她们肌肤的轮廓。<BR>
<BR>
因此，在太阳落山很久之前，妓女们已变作舞者来到了卡维尔斯蒂尔岩。那是一个面朝大海的巨大、宽阔的海岬，为了鲜花节，一大圈未点燃的火炬和盖着盖子的篮子已经布置好了。尽管她们到得很早，但已经有一群观众到达了。女人们在圆圈中央集合，等待时机。<BR>
<BR>
吉娜看着越来越多的人群，当她看到游行中的那位女士和一个非常年老、矮小、白发苍苍的女人手拉手走近时，并不感到惊讶。老妇人有些心不在焉，指着海上的岛屿。金发女士似乎很紧张，不知道该说什么。吉娜习惯于应对不安的客人，于是先开口了。<BR>
<BR>
“很高兴再次见到您，女士。我是途歇的吉娜。”<BR>
<BR>
“我很高兴你没有因为那些妓女，我是说马，而对我怀恨在心，”那位女士笑了，稍微松了口气。“我是吉莉娅·雷兹女士，国王的女儿。”<BR>
<BR>
“我一直以为国王的女儿被称为公主，”吉娜微笑道。<BR>
<BR>
“在卡姆洛恩，只有当他们是王位继承人时才是。我父亲的新妻子给他生了一个弟弟，他很宠爱他，”吉莉娅回答。她感到头晕目眩。跟一个普通妓女说话，如此亲密地谈论家庭政治，简直是疯了。“关于那个话题，我必须问你一件非常奇怪的事。你听说过塔拉瑞公主吗？”<BR>
<BR>
吉娜想了一会儿：“这名字听起来有点耳熟。我为什么会知道？”<BR>
<BR>
“我不知道。我只是觉得你可能认识这个名字，”吉莉娅女士叹了口气。“你以前来过卡姆洛恩吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“如果来过，那也是我很小的时候，”吉娜说，突然她觉得轮到她信任了。吉莉娅女士友好而坦诚的态度触动了她。“老实说，我完全记不起九、十岁之前童年的任何事情。也许我还是个小女孩的时候，和我的父母 -- 不管他们是谁 -- 来过这里。我告诉你，我想可能来过。我不记得以前来过这里，但我看到的一切，这座城市，你，国王本人，都似乎......好像我很久以前来过这里。”<BR>
吉莉娅女士倒吸一口气，退后一步。她抓住那个一直在眺望大海并喃喃自语的老妇人的手。老妇人惊讶地看向吉莉娅，然后转向吉娜。她那双苍老、半瞎的眼睛闪烁着认出的光芒，并发出一声惊讶的咕哝。吉娜也跳了起来。如果说国王像是半个遗忘的梦中的事物，那么这个女人就是她认识的人。清晰却又模糊，如同守护灵。<BR>
<BR>
“我道歉，”吉莉娅女士结结巴巴地说，“这是我童年的保姆，拉姆克。”<BR>
<BR>
“是她！”老妇人喊道，眼神狂乱。她试图伸出双臂向前跑，但吉莉娅拉住了她。吉娜感到一种奇怪的裸露感，把长袍裹紧了身体。<BR>
<BR>
“不，你错了，”吉莉娅女士对拉姆克低语，紧紧地抱住老妇人。“塔拉瑞公主死了，你知道的。我不该带你来这里。我送你回家。”她转向吉娜，眼中涌出泪水。“卡姆洛恩的整个王室在二十多年前被暗杀了。我父亲是奥洛因公爵，国王的弟弟，所以他继承了王位。抱歉打扰你了。晚安。”<BR>
<BR>
吉娜凝视着吉莉娅女士和老保姆消失在人群中，但她没有时间思考她听到的一切。太阳落山了，鲜花节的时间到了。十二个年轻男子从黑暗中现身，只穿着缠腰布和面具，点燃了火炬。火焰燃起的瞬间，吉娜和其他所有舞者冲向篮子，一把把地拉出花朵和藤蔓。<BR>
<BR>
起初，女人们互相跳舞，向风中撒花瓣。随着音乐激昂，人群也加入进来。那是一场疯狂而美丽的混乱。吉娜像狂野的森林宁芙一样跳跃、昏眩。然后，毫无预兆地，她感到一双粗糙的手从背后抓住了她，推了她一把。<BR>
<BR>
她还没明白怎么回事就已经在坠落。当她意识到的那一刻，她离一百英尺高悬崖的底部比顶部更近。她拼命伸出双臂，抓住崖壁。她的手指划过石头，皮肉撕裂，但她找到了一个抓握点并紧紧抓住。有那么一会儿，她待在那里，大口喘气。然后她开始尖叫。<BR>
<BR>
上面的音乐和庆典太吵了：没人能听到她 -- 她几乎听不到自己的声音。在她下方，海浪撞击着。如果她掉下去，身上的每根骨头都会断裂。她闭上眼睛，一个幻象出现了。一个男人站在她下面，一位充满智慧、充满慈悲的国王，抬头看着她，微笑着。一个小女孩，金发，调皮，她最好的朋友兼表妹，紧紧抓着她旁边的岩石。<BR>
<BR>
“坠落的秘诀是让身体放松。运气好的话，你不会受伤，”女孩说。她点点头，想起了自己是谁。八年的黑暗消散了。<BR>
<BR>
她松开手，让自己像一片叶子一样落入下面的水中。<BR>

She felt nothing, darkness enveloping her body and mind. Pain surged through her leg and with that sensation, a great feeling of cold washed over her. She opened her eyes and saw that she was drowning.<BR>
<BR>
Her left leg would not move at all, but using her right one and her arms, she pulled herself up toward the moons above. It was long way through the swirling currents that wrenched back at her. She was still close to the rocky shoreline of the capitol city of the kingdom of Camlorn, but the water had carried her quite a ways from the point where she fell at Cavilstyr Rock.<BR>

The silhouette of a large house on the shore loomed ahead, and as she neared it, she could see smoke rising from the chimney and the flicker of firelight within. "Of course, I knew you looked familiar somehow," the old woman chuckled, and led her hop by hop across the beach and into the front door. "My memory isn't as good as it used to be. Lets get you warm and have a look at that leg."<BR>

<BR>

You just know. After all, I've probably cast it a thousand times before. Little Lady Jyllia and the little Princess Talara was always getting cut and bruised. Small wonder, the way they was always climbing all over the palace."<BR>

Her little heart just broke, and for a while, it looked like her mind did too."<BR>

"What do you mean?" asked Gyna. "What happened?"<BR>
<BR>

I tried all my healing spells, but it was quite beyond my power. So much more than a scraped knee. Her father who was then Duke of Oloine sent her to a sanitarium in the country to get well."<BR>

<BR>

At the door, Gyna kissed the old woman's cheek and thanked her. Not only for the healing spell and for the cloak, but for everything else of kindness she had ever done.<BR>
<BR>
The road close to the house went north and south. To the left was the way back to Camlorn, where secrets lay to which she alone held the key. To the south was Daggerfall, her home for more than twenty years. She could return there, back to her profession on the streets, very easily. For a few seconds, she considered her options, and then made her choice.<BR>

Before it rounded the wooded pass ahead, it stopped suddenly. She recognized one of the soldiers as Gnorbooth, Lord Strale's manservant. <BR>
"I don't care what it is," said Lord Strale. "What are you doing on the south road? I paid for you to stay and make the kingdom merry."<BR>
<BR>
"If I went back to Camlorn, there are a great many who wouldn't be merry at all."<BR>
<BR>
"Explain yourself," said Lord Strale.<BR>
<BR>
So she did. And he listened.<BR>
