"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
塔拉瑞公主之谜，第二部分<BR>
梅拉·莱基斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
她什么也感觉不到，黑暗包围了她的身体和思想。疼痛涌上她的腿，伴随着那种感觉，一股巨大的寒意冲刷着她。她睁开眼睛，看到自己正在溺水。<BR>
<BR>
她的左腿完全动弹不得，但她用右腿和手臂，将自己拉向上方的月亮。穿过拉扯着她的漩涡水流，路途漫长。最后她冲出了水面，吸入寒冷的夜风。她仍然靠近卡姆洛恩王国首都的岩石海岸线，但水流将她从卡维尔斯蒂尔岩坠落的地方冲出了相当远的距离。<BR>
<BR>
不是坠落，她想，纠正自己。她是被推下去的。<BR>
<BR>
顺流而下，她让自己漂流。在那里，陡峭的悬崖壁坡度降低，直到接近水边。岸边一座大房子的轮廓隐约出现在前方，当她靠近时，她能看到烟囱冒出的烟和里面闪烁的炉火。她的腿疼得厉害，但更甚的是水的寒冷。一个温暖的炉火的想法就是她重新开始游泳所需的所有动力。<BR>
<BR>
在岸边，她试图站起来，但发现做不到。她开始爬过沙子和岩石，泪水与海水混合。她在鲜花节上的服装 -- 那条简单的白床单 -- 已破烂不堪，感觉像铅块一样压在她背上。筋疲力尽之后，她向前倒下，开始抽泣。<BR>
<BR>
“求你了！”她喊道。“如果你能听到我，请帮帮我！”<BR>
<BR>
片刻之后，房门打开了，一个女人走了出来。是拉姆克，她在鲜花节上遇到的那个老妇人。那个在她自己还不知道自己是谁时就惊呼“是她！”的人。相比之下，当老妇人来到她身边时，这次她眼中没有一丝认出的光芒。<BR>
<BR>
“以塞西埃特之名，你受伤了吗？”拉姆克低声说，扶她起来，充当她的拐杖。“我以前见过那件长裙。你是今晚鲜花节的舞者之一吗？我和国王的女儿吉莉娅·雷兹女士一起在那里。”<BR>
<BR>
“我知道，她介绍了我们，”她呻吟道。“我自称是途歇的吉娜？”<BR>
<BR>
“当然，我就觉得你看起来有点眼熟，”老妇人轻笑着说，领着她一瘸一拐地穿过海滩，进了前门。“我的记性不如从前了。让你暖和起来，看看你的腿。”<BR>
<BR>
拉姆克接过吉娜湿透的破布，用毯子盖住坐在火边的她。随着冰冷的水造成的麻木开始消退，它残忍地将她抛向腿部剧烈的痛苦。直到那时，她才敢看它。当她看时，看到那道深深的伤口、鱼肚白般的死肉、肿胀饱满，不禁感到作呕。浓稠的动脉血涌出，成股地溅在地板上。<BR>
<BR>
“哦，天哪，”老妇人回到火边说，“那一定很疼。你很幸运，我还记得一点古老的治疗法术。”<BR>
<BR>
拉姆克坐在地板上，将双手按在伤口两侧。吉娜感到一阵剧痛，然后是一种凉爽柔软的挤压和刺麻感。当她低头看时，拉姆克正慢慢地将她布满皱纹的手向彼此滑动。随着它们的接近，伤口在她眼前开始愈合，肌肉结合，瘀伤消退。<BR>
<BR>
“甜蜜的吉娜瑞斯，”吉娜倒吸一口气。“你救了我的命。”<BR>
<BR>
“不仅如此，你那漂亮的腿上不会留下丑陋的伤疤，”拉姆克轻笑着说。“吉莉娅女士小时候，我不得不用了很多次那个法术。你知道，我是她的保姆。”<BR>
<BR>
“我知道，”吉娜微笑着说。“但那已经是很久以前的事了，你还记得那个法术。”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，当你学习任何东西时，即使是恢复系，也总会有很多学习和错误，但一旦你像我这么老了，就不再需要记住东西了。你就是知道。毕竟，我以前可能已经施放过这个法术上千次了。小吉莉娅女士和小塔拉瑞公主总是磕磕碰碰，青一块紫一块。难怪，她们总是在宫殿里到处爬。”<BR>
<BR>
吉娜叹了口气。“你一定很爱吉莉娅女士。”<BR>
<BR>
“我现在依然爱她，”拉姆克笑容满面。“但现在她长大了，事情也不同了。你知道吗，我以前没注意到，因为你全身都被海水浸湿了，但你看起来很像我的女士。我们之前在节庆上见面时我提过吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“你提过，”吉娜说。“或者更确切地说，我想你是觉得我看起来像塔拉瑞公主。”<BR>
<BR>
“哦，如果你是归来的公主，那该多好啊，”老妇人倒吸一口气。“你知道吗，当初前王室被杀，大家都说公主也遇害了，尽管我们从未找到尸体，我想真正的受害者是吉莉娅女士。她的小小心灵都碎了，有一阵子，她的精神似乎也崩溃了。”<BR>
<BR>
“你什么意思？”吉娜问。“发生了什么？”<BR>
<BR>
“我不知道该不该告诉陌生人这件事，但这在卡姆洛恩是众所周知的，而且我真的觉得我认识你，”拉姆克内心挣扎了一下，然后还是说了出来。“吉莉娅目睹了暗杀，你知道。事后我找到了她，她躲在那可怕的血迹斑斑的王座室里，像一个小小的破碎的玩偶。她不肯说话，不肯吃东西。我试了我所有的治疗法术，但这完全超出了我的能力。远不止擦破膝盖那么简单。她当时是奥洛因公爵的父亲送她去乡下的疗养院治疗。”<BR>
<BR>
“那个可怜的小女孩，”吉娜哭了。<BR>
<BR>
“她花了很多年才恢复自我，”拉姆克点点头说。“而且，事实上，她从未真正完全恢复。你好奇为什么她父亲当上国王后没有让她做继承人？他认为她仍然不完全正常，从某种意义上说，尽管我会否认，但他这么想是对的。她什么都不记得，什么都不记得。”<BR>
<BR>
“你觉得，”吉娜仔细斟酌着措辞。“如果她知道她的表妹塔拉瑞公主还活着，安然无恙，她会好起来吗？”<BR>
<BR>
拉姆克想了想。“我想会的。但也许不会。有时最好不要抱有希望。”<BR>
<BR>
吉娜站了起来，发现她的腿和看上去一样有力。她的长裙已经干了，拉姆克给了她一件斗篷，坚持要她穿上抵御寒冷的夜风。在门口，吉娜亲吻了老妇人的脸颊，感谢了她。不仅为了治疗法术和斗篷，也为了她所做的一切善意。<BR>
<BR>
房子附近的路通向南北。左边是回卡姆洛恩的路，那里藏着她独有钥匙的秘密。南边是途歇，她二十多年的家。她可以很容易地回到那里，回到她在街头的职业。几秒钟后，她考虑了各种选择，然后做出了决定。<BR>
<BR>
她没走多远，一辆由三匹带着帝国徽章的马牵引的黑色马车，连同八匹骑马，超过了她。在它绕过前方树木繁茂的山口之前，突然停了下来。她认出其中一个士兵是格诺博斯，斯特拉尔勋爵的男仆。车门打开，斯特拉尔勋爵本人，皇帝的大使，雇佣她和所有其他女人在宫廷娱乐的人，走了出来。<BR>
<BR>
“你！”他皱起眉头。“你是其中一个妓女，对吧？你就是那个在鲜花节期间失踪的人？吉娜，我说得对吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“都是真的，”她苦笑了一下。“除了我发现我的名字不是吉娜。”<BR>
<BR>
“我才不管是什么，”斯特拉尔勋爵说。“你在南边的路上做什么？我花钱让你留下来，让王国欢乐。”<BR>
<BR>
“如果我回卡姆洛恩，会有很多人根本乐不起来。”<BR>
<BR>
“解释一下，”斯特拉尔勋爵说。<BR>
<BR>
于是她解释了。而他听着。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Mystery of Princess Talara, Part II<BR>
By Mera Llykith<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
She felt nothing, darkness enveloping her body and mind. Pain surged through her leg and with that sensation, a great feeling of cold washed over her. She opened her eyes and saw that she was drowning.<BR>
<BR>
Her left leg would not move at all, but using her right one and her arms, she pulled herself up toward the moons above. It was long way through the swirling currents that wrenched back at her. At last she broke the surface and sucked in the cold night air. She was still close to the rocky shoreline of the capitol city of the kingdom of Camlorn, but the water had carried her quite a ways from the point where she fell at Cavilstyr Rock.<BR>
<BR>
Not fell, she thought, correcting herself. She had been pushed.<BR>
<BR>
Further down current, she allowed herself to drift. There the steep cliff walls sloped lower until they were close to the water's edge. The silhouette of a large house on the shore loomed ahead, and as she neared it, she could see smoke rising from the chimney and the flicker of firelight within. The pain in her leg was great, but greater still was the chill of the water. The thought of a warm hearth fire was all the motivation she needed to begin swimming again.<BR>
<BR>
At the shore's edge, she tried to stand but found she couldn't. Her tears mixed with the sea water as she began to crawl across the sand and rock. The simple white sheet which had been her costume at the Flower Festival was tattered and felt like a weight of lead across her back. Beyond the point of exhaustion, she fell forward and began to sob.<BR>
<BR>
"Please!" she cried. "If you can hear me, please help!"<BR>
<BR>
A moment later, the door to the house opened and a woman stepped out. It was Ramke, the old lady she had met at the Flower Festival. The one who had started and cried "It's her!" even before she herself knew who she was. By contrast, when the old woman came to her, this time there was no glimmer of recognition in her eyes.<BR>
<BR>
"By Sethiete, are you hurt?" Ramke whispered, and helped her up, acting as her crutch. "I've seen that gown before. Were you one of the dancers at the Flower Festival tonight? I was there with Lady Jyllia Raze, the daughter of the King."<BR>
<BR>
"I know, she introduced us," she groaned. "I called myself Gyna of Daggerfall?"<BR>
<BR>
"Of course, I knew you looked familiar somehow," the old woman chuckled, and led her hop by hop across the beach and into the front door. "My memory isn't as good as it used to be. Lets get you warm and have a look at that leg."<BR>
<BR>
Ramke took Gyna's soaking rags and covered her with a blanket as she sat at the fire. As the numbness of the chill water began to leave her, it cruelly abandoned her to the intense agony of her leg. Until then, she had not dared to look at it. When she did, she felt vomit rise at the sight of the deep gash, fish-white dead flesh, plump and swollen. Thick arterial blood bubbled up, splashing on the floor in streams.<BR>
<BR>
"Oh dear," said the old woman, returning to the fire. "That must rather sting. You're lucky that I still remember a little of the old healing spells."<BR>
<BR>
Ramke seated herself on the floor and pressed her hands on either side of the wound. Gyna felt a flare of pain, and then a cool soft pinching and prickle. When she looked down, Ramke was slowly sliding her wrinkled hands towards one another. At their approach, the lesion began to mend before her eyes, flesh binding and bruises fading.<BR>
<BR>
"Sweet Kynareth," Gyna gasped. "You've saved my life."<BR>
<BR>
"Not only that, you won't have an ugly scar on your pretty leg," Ramke chuckled. "I had to use that spell so many times when Lady Jyllia was little. You know, I was her nursemaid."<BR>
<BR>
"I know," Gyna smiled. "But that was a long time ago, and you still remember the spell."<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, when you're learning anything, even the School of Restoration, there's always a lot of study and mistakes, but once you're as old as I am, there's no longer any need to remember things. You just know. After all, I've probably cast it a thousand times before. Little Lady Jyllia and the little Princess Talara was always getting cut and bruised. Small wonder, the way they was always climbing all over the palace."<BR>
<BR>
Gyna sighed. "You must have loved Lady Jyllia very much."<BR>
<BR>
"I still do," Ramke beamed. "But now she's all grown and things are different. You know, I didn't notice it before because you were all wet from the sea, but you look very much like my lady. Did I mention that before when we met at the Festival?"<BR>
<BR>
"You did," said Gyna. "Or rather I think you thought I looked like Princess Talara."<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, it would be so wonderful if you were the Princess returned," the old woman gasped. "You know, when the former royal family was killed, and everyone said the Princess was killed though we never found the body, I think the real victim was Lady Jyllia. Her little heart just broke, and for a while, it looked like her mind did too."<BR>
<BR>
"What do you mean?" asked Gyna. "What happened?"<BR>
<BR>
"I don't know if I should tell a stranger this, but it's fairly well-known in Camlorn, and I really feel like I know you," Ramke struggled with her conscience and then released. "Jyllia saw the assassination, you see. I found her afterwards, hiding in that terrible blood-stained throne room, and she was like a little broken doll. She wouldn't speak, she wouldn't eat. I tried all my healing spells, but it was quite beyond my power. So much more than a scraped knee. Her father who was then Duke of Oloine sent her to a sanitarium in the country to get well."<BR>
<BR>
"That poor little girl," cried Gyna.<BR>
<BR>
"It took her years to be herself again," said Ramke, nodding. "And, in truth, she never really returned altogether. You wonder why her father when he was made king didn't make her his heir? He thought that she was still not exactly right, and in a way, as much as I would deny it, he's correct to think so. She remembered nothing, nothing at all."<BR>
<BR>
"Do you think," Gyna considered her words carefully. "That she would be better if she knew that her cousin the Princess Talara was alive and well?"<BR>
<BR>
Ramke considered it. "I think so. But maybe not. Sometimes it's best not to hope."<BR>
<BR>
Gyna stood up, finding her leg to be as strong as it looked to be. Her gown had dried, and Ramke gave her a cloak, insisting she protect herself against the cold night air. At the door, Gyna kissed the old woman's cheek and thanked her. Not only for the healing spell and for the cloak, but for everything else of kindness she had ever done.<BR>
<BR>
The road close to the house went north and south. To the left was the way back to Camlorn, where secrets lay to which she alone held the key. To the south was Daggerfall, her home for more than twenty years. She could return there, back to her profession on the streets, very easily. For a few seconds, she considered her options, and then made her choice.<BR>
<BR>
She had not been walking for very long, when a black carriage drawn by three horses bearing the Imperial Seal, together with eight mounted horses, passed her. Before it rounded the wooded pass ahead, it stopped suddenly. She recognized one of the soldiers as Gnorbooth, Lord Strale's manservant. The door opened and Lord Strale himself, the Emperor's ambassador, the man who had hired her and all the other women to entertain at court, stepped out. <BR>
<BR>
"You!' he frowned. "You're one of the prostitutes, aren't you? You're the one who disappeared during the Flower Festival? Gyna, am I right?"<BR>
<BR>
"All that is true," she smiled sourly. "Except my name I've discovered is not Gyna."<BR>
<BR>
"I don't care what it is," said Lord Strale. "What are you doing on the south road? I paid for you to stay and make the kingdom merry."<BR>
<BR>
"If I went back to Camlorn, there are a great many who wouldn't be merry at all."<BR>
<BR>
"Explain yourself," said Lord Strale.<BR>
<BR>
So she did. And he listened.<BR>

“我不知道该不该告诉陌生人这件事，但这在卡姆洛恩是众所周知的，而且我真的觉得我认识你，”拉姆克内心挣扎了一下，然后还是说了出来。“吉莉娅目睹了暗杀，你知道。事后我找到了她，她躲在那可怕的血迹斑斑的王座室里，像一个小小的破碎的玩偶。她不肯说话，不肯吃东西。我试了我所有的治疗法术，但这完全超出了我的能力。远不止擦破膝盖那么简单。她当时是奥洛因公爵的父亲送她去乡下的疗养院治疗。”<BR>
<BR>
“那个可怜的小女孩，”吉娜哭了。<BR>
<BR>
“她花了很多年才恢复自我，”拉姆克点点头说。“而且，事实上，她从未真正完全恢复。你好奇为什么她父亲当上国王后没有让她做继承人？他认为她仍然不完全正常，从某种意义上说，尽管我会否认，但他这么想是对的。她什么都不记得，什么都不记得。”<BR>
<BR>
“你觉得，”吉娜仔细斟酌着措辞。“如果她知道她的表妹塔拉瑞公主还活着，安然无恙，她会好起来吗？”<BR>
<BR>
拉姆克想了想。“我想会的。但也许不会。有时最好不要抱有希望。”<BR>
<BR>
吉娜站了起来，发现她的腿和看上去一样有力。她的长裙已经干了，拉姆克给了她一件斗篷，坚持要她穿上抵御寒冷的夜风。在门口，吉娜亲吻了老妇人的脸颊，感谢了她。不仅为了治疗法术和斗篷，也为了她所做的一切善意。<BR>
<BR>
房子附近的路通向南北。左边是回卡姆洛恩的路，那里藏着她独有钥匙的秘密。南边是途歇，她二十多年的家。她可以很容易地回到那里，回到她在街头的职业。几秒钟后，她考虑了各种选择，然后做出了决定。<BR>
<BR>
她没走多远，一辆由三匹带着帝国徽章的马牵引的黑色马车，连同八匹骑马，超过了她。在它绕过前方树木繁茂的山口之前，突然停了下来。她认出其中一个士兵是格诺博斯，斯特拉尔勋爵的男仆。车门打开，斯特拉尔勋爵本人，皇帝的大使，雇佣她和所有其他女人在宫廷娱乐的人，走了出来。<BR>
<BR>
“你！”他皱起眉头。“你是其中一个妓女，对吧？你就是那个在鲜花节期间失踪的人？吉娜，我说得对吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“都是真的，”她苦笑了一下。“除了我发现我的名字不是吉娜。”<BR>
<BR>
“我才不管是什么，”斯特拉尔勋爵说。“你在南边的路上做什么？我花钱让你留下来，让王国欢乐。”<BR>
<BR>
“如果我回卡姆洛恩，会有很多人根本乐不起来。”<BR>
<BR>
“解释一下，”斯特拉尔勋爵说。<BR>
<BR>
于是她解释了。而他听着。<BR>

The Mystery of Princess Talara, Part III<BR>
By Mera Llykith<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Gnorbooth was leaving his favorite pub in Camlorn, The Breaking Branch, when he heard someone calling his name. His was not the sort of a name that could be mistaken for another. He turned and saw Lord Eryl, the Royal Battlemage from the palace, emerge from the darkness of the alley.<BR>
<BR>
"Milord," said Gnorbooth with a pleasant smile.<BR>
<BR>
"I'm surprised to see you out this evening, Gnorbooth," grinned Lord Eryl with a most unpleasant smile. "I have not seen you and your master very much since the millennial celebration, but I understand you've been very busy. What I've been wondering is what you've been busy doing."<BR>
<BR>
"Protecting the Imperial interests in Camlorn is busy work, milord. But I cannot imagine you would be interested in the minutiae of the ambassador's appointments."<BR>
<BR>
"But I am," said the battlemage. "Especially as the ambassador has begun acting most mysteriously, most undiplomatically lately. And I understand that he has taken one of the whores from the Flower Festival into his house. I believe her name is Gyna?"<BR>
<BR>
Gnorbooth shrugged: "He's in love, I would imagine, milord. It can make men act very strangely, as I'm sure you've heard before."<BR>
<BR>
"She is a most comely wench," laughed Lord Eryl. "Have you noticed how much she resembles the late Princess Talara?"<BR>
<BR>
"I have only been in Camlorn for fifteen years, milord. I never saw her late majesty."<BR>
<BR>
"Now I could understand it if he had taken to writing poetry, but what man in love spends his days in the kitchens of the palace, talking to old servants? That hardly sounds like molten passion to me, even based on my limited experience." Lord Eryl rolled his eyes. "And what is this business he has now in - oh, what is the name of that village?"<BR>
<BR>
"Umbington?" replied Gnorbooth, and immediately wished he hadn't. Lord Eryl was too canny an actor to reveal it, but Gnorbooth knew at the pit of his stomach that the battlemage did not even know Lord Strale had left the capitol. He had to get away to let the ambassador know, but there was still a game to be carefully played. "He's not leaving for there until tomorrow. I believe it's just to put a stamp on some deed that needs the Imperial seal."<BR>
<BR>
"Is that all? How tedious for the poor fellow. I suppose I'll see him when he returns then," Lord Eryl bowed. "Thank you for being so informative. Farewell."<BR>

The moment the royal battlemage turned the corner, Gnorbooth leapt onto his horse. He had drunk one or two ales too many, but he knew he must find his way to Umbington before Lord Eryl's agents did. He galloped east out of the capitol, hoping there were signs along the road.<BR>
<BR>
Seated in a tavern that smelled of mildew and sour beer, Lord Strale marveled at how the Emperor's agent Lady Brisienna always found the most public of places for her most private of conferences. It was harvest time in Umbington, and all of the field hands were drinking away their meager wages in the noisiest of fashions. He was dressed appropriately for the venue, rough trousers and a simple peasant's vest, but he still felt conspicuous. In comparison to his two female companions, he certainly was. The woman to his right was used to frequenting the low places of Daggerfall as a common prostitute. Lady Brisienna to his left was even more clearly in her element.<BR>
<BR>
"By what name would you prefer I call you?" Lady Brisienna asked solicitously.<BR>
<BR>
"I am used to the name Gyna, though that may have to change," was her reply. "Of course, it may not. Gyna the Whore may be the name writ on my grave."<BR>
<BR>
"I will see to it that there is no attempt on your life like that the Flower Festival," Lord Strale frowned. "But without the Emperor's help, I won't be able to protect you forever. The only permanent solution is to capture those who would do you harm and then to raise you to your proper station."<BR>
<BR>
"Do you believe my story?" Gyna turned to Lady Brisienna.<BR>
<BR>
"I have been the Emperor's chief agent in High Rock for many years now, and I have heard few stranger tales. If your friend the ambassador hadn't investigated and discovered what he has, I would have dismissed you outright as a madwoman," Brisienna laughed, forcing a smile onto Gyna's face to match. "But now, yes, I do believe you. Perhaps that makes me the madwoman."<BR>
<BR>
"Will you help us?" asked Lord Strale simply.<BR>
<BR>
"It is a tricky business interfering in the affairs of the provincial kingdoms," Lady Brisienna looked into the depths of her mug thoughtfully. "Unless there is a threat to the Empire itself, we find it is best not to meddle. What we have in your case is a very messy assassination that happened twenty years ago, and its aftermath. If His Imperial Majesty involved itself in every bloody hiccup in the succession in each of his thousand vassal kingdoms, he would never accomplish anything for the greater good of Tamriel."<BR>
<BR>
"I understand," murmured Gyna. "When I remembered everything, who I was and what happened to me, I resolved to do nothing about it. In fact, I was leaving Camlorn and going back home to Daggerfall when I saw Lord Strale again. He was the one who began this quest to resolve this, not me. And when he brought me back, I only wanted to see my cousin to tell her who I was, but he forbade me."<BR>
"It would have been too dangerous," growled Strale. "We still don't know yet the depths of the conspiracy. Perhaps we never will."<BR>
<BR>
"I'm sorry, I always find myself giving long explanations to short questions. When Lord Strale asked if I would help, I should have begun by saying 'yes,'" Lady Brisienna laughed at the change in Lord Strale and Gyna's expressions. "I will help you, of course. But for this to turn out well, you must accomplish two things to the Emperor's satisfaction. First, you must prove with absolute certainty who is the power behind this plot you've uncovered. You must get someone to confess."<BR>
<BR>
"And secondly," said Lord Strale, nodding. "We must prove that this is a matter worthy of His Imperial Majesty's consideration, and not merely a minor local concern."<BR>
<BR>
Lord Strale, Lady Brisienna, and the woman who called herself Gyna discussed how to accomplish their goals for a few hours more. When it was agreed what had to be done, Lady Brisienna took her leave to find her ally Proseccus. Strale and Gyna set off to the west, toward Camlorn. It was not long after beginning their ride through the woods that they heard the sound of galloping hoof beats far up ahead. Lord Strale unsheathed his sword and signaled for Gyna to position her horse behind him.<BR>
<BR>
At that moment, they were attacked on all sides. It was an ambush. Eight men, armed with axes, had been lying in wait.<BR>
<BR>
Lord Strale quickly yanked Gyna from her horse, pulling her behind him. He made a brief, deft motion with his hands. A ring of flame materialized around them, and rushed outward, striking their assailants. The men roared in pain and dropped to their knees. Lord Strale jumped the horse over the closest one, and galloped at full speed westward. <BR>
<BR>
"I thought you were an ambassador not a mage!" laughed Gyna.<BR>
<BR>
"I still believe there are times for diplomacy," replied Lord Strale.<BR>
<BR>
The horse and rider they had heard before met them on the road. It was Gnorbooth. "Milord, it's the royal battlemage! He found out you two were in Umbington!"<BR>
<BR>
"With considerable ease, I might add," Lord Eryl's voice boomed out of the woods. Gnorbooth, Gyna, and Lord Strale scanned the dark trees, but they showed nothing. The battlemage's voice seemed to emanate from everywhere and nowhere.<BR>
<BR>
"I'm sorry, milord," groaned Gnorbooth. "I tried to warn you as soon as I could."<BR>
<BR>
"In your next life, perhaps you'll remember not to trust your plans to a drunkard!" laughed Lord Eryl. He had them in his sight, and the spell was unleashed.<BR>
<BR>
Gnorbooth saw him first, by the light of the ball of fire that leapt from his fingertips. Later, Lord Eryl was to wonder to himself what the fool had intended to do. Perhaps he was rushing forward to pull Lord Strale out of the path. Perhaps he was trying to flee the path of destruction, and had simply moved left when he should have moved right. Perhaps, as unlikely as it seemed, he was willing to sacrifice himself to save his master. Whatever the reason, the result was the same. <BR>
<BR>
He got in the way.<BR>
<BR>
There was an explosion of energy that filled the night, and an echoing boom that shook birds from the trees for a mile around. On the few square feet where Gnorbooth and his horse had stood was nothing but black glass. They had been reduced to less than vapor. Gyna and Lord Strale were thrown back. Their horse, when it recovered its senses, galloped away as fast as it could. In the lingering glowing aura of the spell's detonation, Lord Strale looked straight into the woods and into the wide eyes of the battlemage. <BR>
<BR>
"Damn," said Lord Eryl and began to run. The ambassador jumped to his feet and pursued.<BR>
<BR>
"That was an expensive use of magicka, even for you," said Lord Strale as he ran. "Don't you know well enough not to use ranged spells unless you are certain your target won't be blocked?"<BR>
<BR>
"I never thought - that idiot -" Lord Eryl was struck from behind and knocked to the wet forest floor before he had a chance to finish his lamentation.<BR>
<BR>
"It doesn't matter what you thought," said Lord Strale calmly, flipping the battlemage around and pinning his arms to the ground with his knees. "I'm not a battlemage, but I knew enough not to use my entire reserve on your little ambush. Perhaps it's a matter of philosophy, as a government agent, I feel inclined toward conservatism."<BR>
<BR>
"What are you going to do?" whimpered Lord Eryl.<BR>
<BR>
"Gnorbooth was a good man, one of the best, and so I'm going to hurt you quite a lot," the ambassador made a slight movement and his hands began to glow brightly. "That's a certainty. How much more I'm going to hurt you after that depends on what you tell me. I want to hear about the former Duke of Oloine."<BR>
<BR>
"What do you want to know?" Lord Eryl screamed.<BR>
<BR>
"Let's start with everything," replied Lord Strale with perfect patience.<BR>

“下辈子，也许你会记住不要把你的计划托付给酒鬼！”埃里尔勋爵笑了。他看到了他们，法术释放了。<BR>

格诺博斯首先看到了他，借着从他指尖跳出的火球的光芒。后来，埃里尔勋爵暗自纳闷那个傻瓜打算做什么。也许他是冲上前去把斯特拉尔勋爵拉出危险路径。也许他是想逃离毁灭之路，只是本应向右却向左移动了。也许，尽管看似不可能，他愿意牺牲自己来拯救他的主人。不管原因是什么，结果都一样。<BR>
<BR>
他挡了道。<BR>
<BR>
一声能量爆炸充满了夜空，回荡的轰鸣声震得方圆一英里树上的鸟儿四散飞起。在格诺博斯和他的马站立的几平方英尺土地上，只剩下黑色的玻璃。他们被化为了比蒸汽还微小的存在。吉娜和斯特拉尔勋爵被震飞。他们的马恢复知觉后，以最快的速度疾驰而去。在法术引爆后残留的发光灵光中，斯特拉尔勋爵直视树林，直视战斗法师瞪大的眼睛。<BR>
<BR>
“该死，”埃里尔勋爵说着开始跑。大使跳起来追赶。<BR>
<BR>
“即使对你来说，那也是消耗魔能的昂贵用法，”斯特拉尔勋爵边跑边说。“难道你不知道，除非你确定目标不会被挡住，否则不要使用远程法术吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“我从没想过 -- 那个白痴 -- ”埃里尔勋爵还没来得及说完他的哀叹，就被从后面击中，倒在潮湿的森林地面上。<BR>
<BR>
“你想什么不重要，”斯特拉尔勋爵平静地说，把战斗法师翻过来，用膝盖把他的胳膊按在地上。“我不是战斗法师，但我足够了解，不会把我所有的储备都用在你这个小伏击上。也许是哲学问题，作为政府特工，我倾向于保守主义。”<BR>
<BR>
“你要做什么？”埃里尔勋爵呜咽道。<BR>
<BR>
“格诺博斯是个好人，最优秀的人之一，所以我要让你吃不少苦头，”大使轻微一动，他的手开始发出明亮的光芒。“这是肯定的。之后我还会让你多痛苦，就取决于你告诉我什么了。我想听听关于前奥洛因公爵的事。”<BR>
<BR>
“你想知道什么？”埃里尔勋爵尖叫道。<BR>
<BR>
“从所有事开始吧，”斯特拉尔勋爵以极其耐心的态度回答。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Mystery of Princess Talara, Part III<BR>
By Mera Llykith<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Gnorbooth was leaving his favorite pub in Camlorn, The Breaking Branch, when he heard someone calling his name. His was not the sort of a name that could be mistaken for another. He turned and saw Lord Eryl, the Royal Battlemage from the palace, emerge from the darkness of the alley.<BR>
<BR>
"Milord," said Gnorbooth with a pleasant smile.<BR>
<BR>
"I'm surprised to see you out this evening, Gnorbooth," grinned Lord Eryl with a most unpleasant smile. "I have not seen you and your master very much since the millennial celebration, but I understand you've been very busy. What I've been wondering is what you've been busy doing."<BR>
<BR>
"Protecting the Imperial interests in Camlorn is busy work, milord. But I cannot imagine you would be interested in the minutiae of the ambassador's appointments."<BR>
<BR>
"But I am," said the battlemage. "Especially as the ambassador has begun acting most mysteriously, most undiplomatically lately. And I understand that he has taken one of the whores from the Flower Festival into his house. I believe her name is Gyna?"<BR>
<BR>
Gnorbooth shrugged: "He's in love, I would imagine, milord. It can make men act very strangely, as I'm sure you've heard before."<BR>
<BR>
"She is a most comely wench," laughed Lord Eryl. "Have you noticed how much she resembles the late Princess Talara?"<BR>
<BR>
"I have only been in Camlorn for fifteen years, milord. I never saw her late majesty."<BR>
<BR>
"Now I could understand it if he had taken to writing poetry, but what man in love spends his days in the kitchens of the palace, talking to old servants? That hardly sounds like molten passion to me, even based on my limited experience." Lord Eryl rolled his eyes. "And what is this business he has now in - oh, what is the name of that village?"<BR>
<BR>
"Umbington?" replied Gnorbooth, and immediately wished he hadn't. Lord Eryl was too canny an actor to reveal it, but Gnorbooth knew at the pit of his stomach that the battlemage did not even know Lord Strale had left the capitol. He had to get away to let the ambassador know, but there was still a game to be carefully played. "He's not leaving for there until tomorrow. I believe it's just to put a stamp on some deed that needs the Imperial seal."<BR>
<BR>
"Is that all? How tedious for the poor fellow. I suppose I'll see him when he returns then," Lord Eryl bowed. "Thank you for being so informative. Farewell."<BR>
<BR>
The moment the royal battlemage turned the corner, Gnorbooth leapt onto his horse. He had drunk one or two ales too many, but he knew he must find his way to Umbington before Lord Eryl's agents did. He galloped east out of the capitol, hoping there were signs along the road.<BR>
<BR>
Seated in a tavern that smelled of mildew and sour beer, Lord Strale marveled at how the Emperor's agent Lady Brisienna always found the most public of places for her most private of conferences. It was harvest time in Umbington, and all of the field hands were drinking away their meager wages in the noisiest of fashions. He was dressed appropriately for the venue, rough trousers and a simple peasant's vest, but he still felt conspicuous. In comparison to his two female companions, he certainly was. The woman to his right was used to frequenting the low places of Daggerfall as a common prostitute. Lady Brisienna to his left was even more clearly in her element.<BR>
<BR>
"By what name would you prefer I call you?" Lady Brisienna asked solicitously.<BR>
<BR>
"I am used to the name Gyna, though that may have to change," was her reply. "Of course, it may not. Gyna the Whore may be the name writ on my grave."<BR>
<BR>
"I will see to it that there is no attempt on your life like that the Flower Festival," Lord Strale frowned. "But without the Emperor's help, I won't be able to protect you forever. The only permanent solution is to capture those who would do you harm and then to raise you to your proper station."<BR>
<BR>
"Do you believe my story?" Gyna turned to Lady Brisienna.<BR>
<BR>
"I have been the Emperor's chief agent in High Rock for many years now, and I have heard few stranger tales. If your friend the ambassador hadn't investigated and discovered what he has, I would have dismissed you outright as a madwoman," Brisienna laughed, forcing a smile onto Gyna's face to match. "But now, yes, I do believe you. Perhaps that makes me the madwoman."<BR>
<BR>
"Will you help us?" asked Lord Strale simply.<BR>
<BR>
"It is a tricky business interfering in the affairs of the provincial kingdoms," Lady Brisienna looked into the depths of her mug thoughtfully. "Unless there is a threat to the Empire itself, we find it is best not to meddle. What we have in your case is a very messy assassination that happened twenty years ago, and its aftermath. If His Imperial Majesty involved itself in every bloody hiccup in the succession in each of his thousand vassal kingdoms, he would never accomplish anything for the greater good of Tamriel."<BR>
<BR>
"I understand," murmured Gyna. "When I remembered everything, who I was and what happened to me, I resolved to do nothing about it. In fact, I was leaving Camlorn and going back home to Daggerfall when I saw Lord Strale again. He was the one who began this quest to resolve this, not me. And when he brought me back, I only wanted to see my cousin to tell her who I was, but he forbade me."<BR>
"It would have been too dangerous," growled Strale. "We still don't know yet the depths of the conspiracy. Perhaps we never will."<BR>
<BR>
"I'm sorry, I always find myself giving long explanations to short questions. When Lord Strale asked if I would help, I should have begun by saying 'yes,'" Lady Brisienna laughed at the change in Lord Strale and Gyna's expressions. "I will help you, of course. But for this to turn out well, you must accomplish two things to the Emperor's satisfaction. First, you must prove with absolute certainty who is the power behind this plot you've uncovered. You must get someone to confess."<BR>
<BR>
"And secondly," said Lord Strale, nodding. "We must prove that this is a matter worthy of His Imperial Majesty's consideration, and not merely a minor local concern."<BR>
<BR>
Lord Strale, Lady Brisienna, and the woman who called herself Gyna discussed how to accomplish their goals for a few hours more. When it was agreed what had to be done, Lady Brisienna took her leave to find her ally Proseccus. Strale and Gyna set off to the west, toward Camlorn. It was not long after beginning their ride through the woods that they heard the sound of galloping hoof beats far up ahead. Lord Strale unsheathed his sword and signaled for Gyna to position her horse behind him.<BR>
<BR>
At that moment, they were attacked on all sides. It was an ambush. Eight men, armed with axes, had been lying in wait.<BR>
<BR>
Lord Strale quickly yanked Gyna from her horse, pulling her behind him. He made a brief, deft motion with his hands. A ring of flame materialized around them, and rushed outward, striking their assailants. The men roared in pain and dropped to their knees. Lord Strale jumped the horse over the closest one, and galloped at full speed westward. <BR>
<BR>
"I thought you were an ambassador not a mage!" laughed Gyna.<BR>
<BR>
"I still believe there are times for diplomacy," replied Lord Strale.<BR>
<BR>
The horse and rider they had heard before met them on the road. It was Gnorbooth. "Milord, it's the royal battlemage! He found out you two were in Umbington!"<BR>
<BR>
"With considerable ease, I might add," Lord Eryl's voice boomed out of the woods. Gnorbooth, Gyna, and Lord Strale scanned the dark trees, but they showed nothing. The battlemage's voice seemed to emanate from everywhere and nowhere.<BR>
<BR>
"I'm sorry, milord," groaned Gnorbooth. "I tried to warn you as soon as I could."<BR>
<BR>
"In your next life, perhaps you'll remember not to trust your plans to a drunkard!" laughed Lord Eryl. He had them in his sight, and the spell was unleashed.<BR>
<BR>
Gnorbooth saw him first, by the light of the ball of fire that leapt from his fingertips. Later, Lord Eryl was to wonder to himself what the fool had intended to do. Perhaps he was rushing forward to pull Lord Strale out of the path. Perhaps he was trying to flee the path of destruction, and had simply moved left when he should have moved right. Perhaps, as unlikely as it seemed, he was willing to sacrifice himself to save his master. Whatever the reason, the result was the same. <BR>
<BR>
He got in the way.<BR>
<BR>
There was an explosion of energy that filled the night, and an echoing boom that shook birds from the trees for a mile around. On the few square feet where Gnorbooth and his horse had stood was nothing but black glass. They had been reduced to less than vapor. Gyna and Lord Strale were thrown back. Their horse, when it recovered its senses, galloped away as fast as it could. In the lingering glowing aura of the spell's detonation, Lord Strale looked straight into the woods and into the wide eyes of the battlemage. <BR>
<BR>
"Damn," said Lord Eryl and began to run. The ambassador jumped to his feet and pursued.<BR>
<BR>
"That was an expensive use of magicka, even for you," said Lord Strale as he ran. "Don't you know well enough not to use ranged spells unless you are certain your target won't be blocked?"<BR>
<BR>
"I never thought - that idiot -" Lord Eryl was struck from behind and knocked to the wet forest floor before he had a chance to finish his lamentation.<BR>
<BR>
"It doesn't matter what you thought," said Lord Strale calmly, flipping the battlemage around and pinning his arms to the ground with his knees. "I'm not a battlemage, but I knew enough not to use my entire reserve on your little ambush. Perhaps it's a matter of philosophy, as a government agent, I feel inclined toward conservatism."<BR>
<BR>
"What are you going to do?" whimpered Lord Eryl.<BR>
<BR>
"Gnorbooth was a good man, one of the best, and so I'm going to hurt you quite a lot," the ambassador made a slight movement and his hands began to glow brightly. "That's a certainty. How much more I'm going to hurt you after that depends on what you tell me. I want to hear about the former Duke of Oloine."<BR>
<BR>
"What do you want to know?" Lord Eryl screamed.<BR>
<BR>
"Let's start with everything," replied Lord Strale with perfect patience.<BR>

梅拉·莱基斯 著<BR><BR>

The Mystery of Princess Talara<BR>
Part IV<BR>
By Mera Llykith<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Gyna never saw the Emperor's agent Lady Brisienna again, but she kept her promise. Proseccus, a nightblade in the service of the Empire, arrived at Lord Strale's house in disguise. She was an apt pupil, and within days, he had taught what she needed to know.<BR>
<BR>
"It is a simple charm, not the sort of spell that could turn a raging daedroth into a love-struck puppy," said Proseccus. "If you do or say anything that would normally anger or offend your target, the power will weaken. It will alter temporarily his perception of you, as spells of the school of illusion do, but his feelings of respect and admiration for you must be supported by means of a charm of a less magickal nature."<BR>
<BR>
"I understand," smiled Gyna, thanking her tutor for the two spells of illusion he had taught her. The time had come to use her new-found skill.<BR>
<BR>
The Prostitutes Guildhouse of Camlorn was a great palace in an affluent northern quarter of the city. Prince Sylon could have found his way there blindfolded, or blind drunk as he often was. Tonight, however, he was only lightly inebriated and he resolved to drink no more. Tonight he was in the mood for pleasure. His kind of pleasure.<BR>
<BR>
"Where is my favorite, Grigia?" he demanded of the Guildmistress upon entering.<BR>
<BR>
"She is still healing from your appointment with her last week," she smiled serenely. "Most of the other women are in with clients as well, but I saved a special treat for you. A new girl. One you will certainly enjoy."<BR>

The Prince was guided to a sumptuously decorated suite of velvet and silk. <BR>
"I am between names right now," she teased. "I've never made love to a real prince before. I've never even been inside a palace. Is yours very ... big?"<BR>

<BR>
"It would be wonderful to live in such a place," Gyna cooed. "A thousand years of history. Everything must be so old and beautiful. The paintings and books and statues and tapestries. Does your family hold onto all their old treasures?"<BR>

"Yes, hoarded away with a lot of boring old junk in the archive rooms in the vaults. Please, may I see you naked now?"<BR>

The Prince felt his flesh turn to stone. He remained frozen, watching Gyna pull together her clothing and leave the room. The paralysis would only last for a few more minutes, but it was all the time she needed.<BR>

She had not even accepted any gold for her part in the trap. She said it was enough that her girls would not be tortured anymore by that most perverse and cruel Prince.<BR>
<BR>
"What a terrible boy," thought Gyna as she raised the hood on her cloak and raced through the streets toward Lord Strale's house. "It is good that he will never be king."<BR>
<BR>
The following morning, the King and Queen of Camlorn held their daily audience with various nobles and diplomats, a sparse gathering. The throne room was largely empty. It was a terribly dull way to begin the day. In between petitions, they yawned regally.<BR>
<BR>
"What has happened to all the interesting people?" the Queen murmured. "Where's our precious boy?"<BR>
<BR>
"I've heard he was raging through the north quarter in search of some harlot who robbed him," the King chuckled fondly. "What a fine lad."<BR>
<BR>
"And what of the Royal Battlemage?"<BR>
<BR>
"I've sent him to take care of a delicate matter," the King knit his brow. "But that was nearly a week ago, and I haven't heard one word from him. It's somewhat troubling."<BR>
<BR>
"Indeed it is, Lord Eryl should not be gone so long," the Queen frowned. "What if a rogue sorcerer came and threatened us? Husband, don't laugh at me, that is why all the royal houses of High Rock keep their mage retainers close to their side. To protect their court from evil enchantments, like the one that our poor Emperor suffered so recently."<BR>
<BR>
"At the hand of his own battlemage," chuckled the King<BR>
<BR>
"Lord Eryl would never betray you like that, and you well know it. He has been in your employ since you were Duke of Oloine. To even make that comparison between he and Jagar Tharn, really," the Queen waved her hands dismissively. "It is that sort of lack of trust that is ruining kingdoms all over Tamriel. Now, Lord Strale tells me -"<BR>
<BR>
"There's another man that's gone missing," mused the King.<BR>
<BR>
"The ambassador?" the Queen shook her head. "No, he's here. He was desirous to visit the crypts and pay homage to your noble ancestors, so I directed him there. I can't think what's keeping him so long. He must be more pious than I thought."<BR>
<BR>
She was surprised to see the King rise up, alarmed. "Why didn't you tell me?"<BR>
<BR>
Before she had a chance to reply, the subject of their conversation was coming through the open door to the throne room. At on his arm was a beautiful fair-haired woman in a stately gown of scarlet and gold, worthy of the highest nobility. The queen followed her startled husband's gaze, and was likewise amazed.<BR>
<BR>
"I had heard he was taken with one of the harlots from the Flower Festival, not a lady," she whispered. "Why, she looks remarkably like your daughter, the Lady Jyllia."<BR>
<BR>
"That she does," the King gasped. "Or her cousin, the Princess Talara."<BR>
<BR>
The nobles in the room also whispered amongst themselves. Though few had been at court twenty years ago when the Princess had disappeared, presumed murdered like the rest of the royal family, there were still a few elder statesmen who remembered. It was not only on throne that the word "Talara" passed through the air like an enchantment.<BR>
<BR>
"Lord Strale, will you introduce us to your lady?" the Queen asked with a polite smile.<BR>
<BR>
"In a moment, your highness, but I'm afraid I must first discuss pressing matters," Lord Strale replied with a bow. "Might I request a private audience?"<BR>
<BR>
The King looked at the Imperial ambassador, trying to read into the man's expression. With a wave of his hand, he dismissed the assembled and had the doors shut behind them. No one remained in the audience room but the King, the Queen, the ambassador, a dozen royal guards, and the mysterious woman.<BR>
<BR>
The ambassador pulled from his pocket a sheaf of old yellowed parchment. "Your Highness, when you ascended the throne after your brother and his family were murdered, anything that seemed important, deeds and wills, were of course kept with the clerks and ministers. His entire incidental, unimportant personal correspondence was sent to archive which is standard protocol. This letter was among them."<BR>
<BR>
"What is this all about, sir?" the King boomed. "What does it say?"<BR>
<BR>
"Nothing about you, your majesty. In truth, at the time of your majesty's ascension, no one reading it could have understood its significance. It was a letter to the Emperor the late king your brother was penning at the time of his assassination, concerning a thief who had once been a mage-priest at the Temple of Sethiete here in Camlorn. His name was Jagar Tharn."<BR>
<BR>
"Jagar Tharn?" the Queen laughed nervously. "Why, we were just talking about him."<BR>
<BR>
"Tharn had stolen many books of powerful and forgotten spells, and lore about such artifacts as the Staff of Chaos, where it was hidden and how it could be used. News travels slowly to westernmost High Rock, and by the time the King your brother had heard that the Emperor's new battlemage was a man named Jagar Tharn, many years had passed. The king had been writing a letter to warn the Emperor of the treachery of his Imperial Battlemage, but it was never completed." Lord Strale held up the letter. "It is dated on the day of his assassination in the year 385. Four years before Jagar Tharn betrayed his master, and began the ten years of tyranny of the Imperial Simulacrum."<BR>
<BR>
"This is all very interesting," the King barked. "But what has it to do with me?"<BR>
<BR>
"The late King's assassination is now a matter of Imperial concern. And I have a confession from your Royal Battlemage Lord Eryl."<BR>
<BR>
The King's face lost all color: "You miserable worm, no man may threaten me. Neither you, nor that whore, nor that letter will ever see the light of day again. Guards!"<BR>
<BR>
The royal guards unsheathed their blades and pressed forward. As they did so, there was a sudden shimmering of light and the room was filled with Imperial nightblades, led by Proseccus. They had been there for hours, lurking invisibly in the shadows.<BR>
<BR>
"In the name of His Imperial Majesty, Uriel Septim VII, I arrest you," said Strale.<BR>
<BR>
The doors were opened, and the King and Queen were led out, heads bowed. Gyna told Proseccus where he would most likely find their son, Prince Sylon. The courtiers and nobles who had been in the audience chamber stared at the strange, solemn procession of their King and Queen to their own royal prison. No one said a word.<BR>
<BR>
When at last a voice was heard, it startled all. The Lady Jyllia had arrived at court. "What is happening? Who dares to usurp the authority of the King and Queen?"<BR>
<BR>
Lord Strale turned to Proseccus: "We would speak with the Lady Jyllia alone. You know what needs to be done."<BR>
<BR>
Proseccus nodded and had the doors to the throne room closed once again. The courtiers pressed against the wood, straining to hear everything. Though they could not say it, they wanted an explanation almost as much as her Ladyship did.<BR>

“这一切都很有趣，”国王厉声说。“但这和我有什么关系？”<BR>
<BR>
“先王的遇刺现在已成为帝国关注的事件。而且，我这里有你的皇家战斗法师埃里尔勋爵的供词。”<BR>
<BR>
国王的脸失去了血色：“你这可怜的蠕虫，没人能威胁我。你、那个妓女、还有那封信，都再也见不到天日了。卫兵！”<BR>
<BR>
王室卫兵拔出刀剑，向前逼近。就在此时，突然一阵光芒闪烁，房间里充满了帝国夜刃，由普罗塞库斯率领。他们已经在那里待了几个小时，隐身潜伏在阴影中。<BR>
<BR>
“以皇帝陛下尤利尔·塞普汀七世的名义，我逮捕你，”斯特拉尔说。<BR>
<BR>
门被打开，国王和王后被带了出去，低着头。吉娜告诉普罗塞库斯最有可能在哪里找到他们的儿子，赛隆王子。曾在接见厅里的朝臣和贵族们凝视着他们的国王和王后走向自己的皇家监狱那奇怪而庄严的队伍。没有一个人说话。<BR>
<BR>
终于，一个声音响起，惊动了所有人。吉莉娅女士来到了宫廷。“发生了什么事？谁敢篡夺国王和王后的权威？”<BR>
<BR>
斯特拉尔勋爵转向普罗塞库斯：“我们要单独和吉莉娅女士谈谈。你知道该怎么做。”<BR>
<BR>
普罗塞库斯点点头，让人再次关上了王座厅的门。朝臣们紧贴着木门，竭力想听清一切。尽管他们不能说出口，但他们和殿下一样想知道一个解释。<BR>

The Mystery of Princess Talara<BR>
Part IV<BR>
By Mera Llykith<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Gyna never saw the Emperor's agent Lady Brisienna again, but she kept her promise. Proseccus, a nightblade in the service of the Empire, arrived at Lord Strale's house in disguise. She was an apt pupil, and within days, he had taught what she needed to know.<BR>
<BR>
"It is a simple charm, not the sort of spell that could turn a raging daedroth into a love-struck puppy," said Proseccus. "If you do or say anything that would normally anger or offend your target, the power will weaken. It will alter temporarily his perception of you, as spells of the school of illusion do, but his feelings of respect and admiration for you must be supported by means of a charm of a less magickal nature."<BR>
<BR>
"I understand," smiled Gyna, thanking her tutor for the two spells of illusion he had taught her. The time had come to use her new-found skill.<BR>
<BR>
The Prostitutes Guildhouse of Camlorn was a great palace in an affluent northern quarter of the city. Prince Sylon could have found his way there blindfolded, or blind drunk as he often was. Tonight, however, he was only lightly inebriated and he resolved to drink no more. Tonight he was in the mood for pleasure. His kind of pleasure.<BR>
<BR>
"Where is my favorite, Grigia?" he demanded of the Guildmistress upon entering.<BR>
<BR>
"She is still healing from your appointment with her last week," she smiled serenely. "Most of the other women are in with clients as well, but I saved a special treat for you. A new girl. One you will certainly enjoy."<BR>
<BR>
The Prince was guided to a sumptuously decorated suite of velvet and silk. As he entered, Gyna stepped from behind a screen and cast her spell quickly, with her mind open to belief as Proseccus had instructed. It was hard to tell if it worked at first. The Prince looked at her with a cruel smile and then, like sun breaking through clouds, the cruelty left. She could tell he was hers. He asked her her name.<BR>
<BR>
"I am between names right now," she teased. "I've never made love to a real prince before. I've never even been inside a palace. Is yours very ... big?"<BR>
<BR>
"It's not mine yet," he shrugged. "But someday I'll be king."<BR>
<BR>
"It would be wonderful to live in such a place," Gyna cooed. "A thousand years of history. Everything must be so old and beautiful. The paintings and books and statues and tapestries. Does your family hold onto all their old treasures?"<BR>
<BR>
"Yes, hoarded away with a lot of boring old junk in the archive rooms in the vaults. Please, may I see you naked now?"<BR>
<BR>
"First a little conversation, though you may feel free to disrobe whenever you like," said Gyna. "I had heard there was an archive room, but it's quite hidden away."<BR>
<BR>
"There's a false wall behind the family crypt," said the Prince, gripping her wrist and pulling her towards him for a kiss. Something in his eyes had changed.<BR>
<BR>
"Your Highness, you're hurting my arm," Gyna cried.<BR>
<BR>
"Enough talk, you bewitching whore," he snarled. Holding back a sharp jab of fear, Gyna let her mind cool and perceptions whirl. As his angry mouth touched her lips, she cast the second spell she had learned her illusionist mentor.<BR>
<BR>
The Prince felt his flesh turn to stone. He remained frozen, watching Gyna pull together her clothing and leave the room. The paralysis would only last for a few more minutes, but it was all the time she needed.<BR>
<BR>
The Guildmistress had already left with all her girls, just as Gyna and Lord Strale had told her to. They would tell her when it was safe to return. She had not even accepted any gold for her part in the trap. She said it was enough that her girls would not be tortured anymore by that most perverse and cruel Prince.<BR>
<BR>
"What a terrible boy," thought Gyna as she raised the hood on her cloak and raced through the streets toward Lord Strale's house. "It is good that he will never be king."<BR>
<BR>
The following morning, the King and Queen of Camlorn held their daily audience with various nobles and diplomats, a sparse gathering. The throne room was largely empty. It was a terribly dull way to begin the day. In between petitions, they yawned regally.<BR>
<BR>
"What has happened to all the interesting people?" the Queen murmured. "Where's our precious boy?"<BR>
<BR>
"I've heard he was raging through the north quarter in search of some harlot who robbed him," the King chuckled fondly. "What a fine lad."<BR>
<BR>
"And what of the Royal Battlemage?"<BR>
<BR>
"I've sent him to take care of a delicate matter," the King knit his brow. "But that was nearly a week ago, and I haven't heard one word from him. It's somewhat troubling."<BR>
<BR>
"Indeed it is, Lord Eryl should not be gone so long," the Queen frowned. "What if a rogue sorcerer came and threatened us? Husband, don't laugh at me, that is why all the royal houses of High Rock keep their mage retainers close to their side. To protect their court from evil enchantments, like the one that our poor Emperor suffered so recently."<BR>
<BR>
"At the hand of his own battlemage," chuckled the King<BR>
<BR>
"Lord Eryl would never betray you like that, and you well know it. He has been in your employ since you were Duke of Oloine. To even make that comparison between he and Jagar Tharn, really," the Queen waved her hands dismissively. "It is that sort of lack of trust that is ruining kingdoms all over Tamriel. Now, Lord Strale tells me -"<BR>
<BR>
"There's another man that's gone missing," mused the King.<BR>
<BR>
"The ambassador?" the Queen shook her head. "No, he's here. He was desirous to visit the crypts and pay homage to your noble ancestors, so I directed him there. I can't think what's keeping him so long. He must be more pious than I thought."<BR>
<BR>
She was surprised to see the King rise up, alarmed. "Why didn't you tell me?"<BR>
<BR>
Before she had a chance to reply, the subject of their conversation was coming through the open door to the throne room. At on his arm was a beautiful fair-haired woman in a stately gown of scarlet and gold, worthy of the highest nobility. The queen followed her startled husband's gaze, and was likewise amazed.<BR>
<BR>
"I had heard he was taken with one of the harlots from the Flower Festival, not a lady," she whispered. "Why, she looks remarkably like your daughter, the Lady Jyllia."<BR>
<BR>
"That she does," the King gasped. "Or her cousin, the Princess Talara."<BR>
<BR>
The nobles in the room also whispered amongst themselves. Though few had been at court twenty years ago when the Princess had disappeared, presumed murdered like the rest of the royal family, there were still a few elder statesmen who remembered. It was not only on throne that the word "Talara" passed through the air like an enchantment.<BR>
<BR>
"Lord Strale, will you introduce us to your lady?" the Queen asked with a polite smile.<BR>
<BR>
"In a moment, your highness, but I'm afraid I must first discuss pressing matters," Lord Strale replied with a bow. "Might I request a private audience?"<BR>
<BR>
The King looked at the Imperial ambassador, trying to read into the man's expression. With a wave of his hand, he dismissed the assembled and had the doors shut behind them. No one remained in the audience room but the King, the Queen, the ambassador, a dozen royal guards, and the mysterious woman.<BR>
<BR>
The ambassador pulled from his pocket a sheaf of old yellowed parchment. "Your Highness, when you ascended the throne after your brother and his family were murdered, anything that seemed important, deeds and wills, were of course kept with the clerks and ministers. His entire incidental, unimportant personal correspondence was sent to archive which is standard protocol. This letter was among them."<BR>
<BR>
"What is this all about, sir?" the King boomed. "What does it say?"<BR>
<BR>
"Nothing about you, your majesty. In truth, at the time of your majesty's ascension, no one reading it could have understood its significance. It was a letter to the Emperor the late king your brother was penning at the time of his assassination, concerning a thief who had once been a mage-priest at the Temple of Sethiete here in Camlorn. His name was Jagar Tharn."<BR>
<BR>
"Jagar Tharn?" the Queen laughed nervously. "Why, we were just talking about him."<BR>
<BR>
"Tharn had stolen many books of powerful and forgotten spells, and lore about such artifacts as the Staff of Chaos, where it was hidden and how it could be used. News travels slowly to westernmost High Rock, and by the time the King your brother had heard that the Emperor's new battlemage was a man named Jagar Tharn, many years had passed. The king had been writing a letter to warn the Emperor of the treachery of his Imperial Battlemage, but it was never completed." Lord Strale held up the letter. "It is dated on the day of his assassination in the year 385. Four years before Jagar Tharn betrayed his master, and began the ten years of tyranny of the Imperial Simulacrum."<BR>
<BR>
"This is all very interesting," the King barked. "But what has it to do with me?"<BR>
<BR>
"The late King's assassination is now a matter of Imperial concern. And I have a confession from your Royal Battlemage Lord Eryl."<BR>
<BR>
The King's face lost all color: "You miserable worm, no man may threaten me. Neither you, nor that whore, nor that letter will ever see the light of day again. Guards!"<BR>
<BR>
The royal guards unsheathed their blades and pressed forward. As they did so, there was a sudden shimmering of light and the room was filled with Imperial nightblades, led by Proseccus. They had been there for hours, lurking invisibly in the shadows.<BR>
<BR>
"In the name of His Imperial Majesty, Uriel Septim VII, I arrest you," said Strale.<BR>
<BR>
The doors were opened, and the King and Queen were led out, heads bowed. Gyna told Proseccus where he would most likely find their son, Prince Sylon. The courtiers and nobles who had been in the audience chamber stared at the strange, solemn procession of their King and Queen to their own royal prison. No one said a word.<BR>
<BR>
When at last a voice was heard, it startled all. The Lady Jyllia had arrived at court. "What is happening? Who dares to usurp the authority of the King and Queen?"<BR>
<BR>
Lord Strale turned to Proseccus: "We would speak with the Lady Jyllia alone. You know what needs to be done."<BR>
<BR>
Proseccus nodded and had the doors to the throne room closed once again. The courtiers pressed against the wood, straining to hear everything. Though they could not say it, they wanted an explanation almost as much as her Ladyship did.<BR>

梅拉·莱基斯 著<BR><BR>

<BR>
“这一切都很有趣，”国王厉声说。“但这和我有什么关系？”<BR>
<BR>
“先王的遇刺现在已成为帝国关注的事件。而且，我这里有你的皇家战斗法师埃里尔勋爵的供词。”<BR>
<BR>
国王的脸失去了血色：“你这可怜的蠕虫，没人能威胁我。你、那个妓女、还有那封信，都再也见不到天日了。卫兵！”<BR>
<BR>
王室卫兵拔出刀剑，向前逼近。就在此时，突然一阵光芒闪烁，房间里充满了帝国夜刃，由普罗塞库斯率领。他们已经在那里待了几个小时，隐身潜伏在阴影中。<BR>
<BR>
“以皇帝陛下尤利尔·塞普汀七世的名义，我逮捕你，”斯特拉尔说。<BR>
<BR>
门被打开，国王和王后被带了出去，低着头。吉娜告诉普罗塞库斯最有可能在哪里找到他们的儿子，赛隆王子。曾在接见厅里的朝臣和贵族们凝视着他们的国王和王后走向自己的皇家监狱那奇怪而庄严的队伍。没有一个人说话。<BR>
<BR>
终于，一个声音响起，惊动了所有人。吉莉娅女士来到了宫廷。“发生了什么事？谁敢篡夺国王和王后的权威？”<BR>
<BR>
斯特拉尔勋爵转向普罗塞库斯：“我们要单独和吉莉娅女士谈谈。你知道该怎么做。”<BR>
<BR>
普罗塞库斯点点头，让人再次关上了王座厅的门。朝臣们紧贴着木门，竭力想听清一切。尽管他们不能说出口，但他们和殿下一样想知道一个解释。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Mystery of Princess Talara, Part V<BR>
The Final Chapter and Solution<BR>
By Mera Llykith<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
"By what right do you arrest my father?" cried the Lady Jyllia. "What has he done?"<BR>
<BR>
"I arrest the King of Camlorn, the former Duke of Oloine, by my right as an Imperial Commanding Officer and Ambassador," said Lord Strale. "By the right of law of the Emperor of Tamriel which supercedes all provincial royal authority."<BR>
<BR>
Gyna came forward and tried to put her hand on Jyllia's arm, but she was coldly rebuffed. Quietly, she sat down at the foot of the throne in the now empty audience chamber.<BR>
<BR>
"This young lady came to me, having completely recovered her memory, but the story she told was beyond incredible, I simply couldn't believe it," said Lord Strale. "But she was so convinced of it, I had to investigate. So I talked to everyone who was here at the palace twenty years ago to see if there could be any truth to it. Of course, at the time of the King and Queen's murder, and the Princess's disappearance, there was a full inquiry made, but I had different questions to ask this time. Questions about the relationship between the two little cousins, Lady Jyllia Raze and the Princess."<BR>
<BR>
"I've told everyone over and over again, I don't remember anything at all about that time in my life," said Jyllia, tears welling up.<BR>
<BR>
"I know you don't. There has never been a question in my mind that you witnessed a horrible murder, and that your memory lapse and hers," said Lord Strale, gesturing toward Gyna "Are both very real. The story I heard from the servants and other people at the palace was that the little girls were inseparably close. There were no other playmates, and as the Princess's place was to be close to her parents, so the little Lady Jyllia was always there as well. When the assassin came to murder the Royal Family, the King and Queen were in their bedroom, and the girls were playing in the throne room."<BR>
<BR>
"When my memory came back to me, it was like opening a sealed box," said Gyna solemnly. "Everything was so clear and detailed, like it all happened yesterday not twenty years ago. I was on the throne, playing Empress, and you were hiding behind the dais, pretending you were in a dungeon I had sent you to. A man I had never seen burst into the room from the Royal bedchamber, his blade soaked in blood. He came at me, and I ran for my life. I remember starting to run for the dais, but I saw your face, frozen in fear, and I didn't want to lead him to you. So I ran for the window.<BR>
<BR>
"We had climbed on the outside of the castle before, just for fun, that was one of the first memories that came back to me when I was holding onto that cliff. You and I on the castle wall, and the King calling up to me, telling me how to get down. But that day, I couldn't hold on, I was trembling so much. I just fell, and landed in the river.<BR>
<BR>
"I don't know if it was entirely the horror of what I had seen, or that combined with the impact of the fall and the coldness of the water, but everything just went blank in my mind. When I finally pulled myself out of the river, many miles away, I had no idea who I was. And so it stayed," Gyna smiled. "Until now."<BR>
<BR>
"So you are the Princess Talara?" cried Jyllia.<BR>
<BR>
"Let me explain further before she answers that, because the simple answer would just confuse you, as it did me," said Lord Strale. "The assassin was caught before he managed to escape the palace - in truth, he had to know he was going to be caught. He confessed immediately to the murders of the Royal Family. The Princess, he said, he had thrown out the window to her death. A servant down below heard the scream, and saw something fly past his window, so he knew it to be true.<BR>
<BR>
"It was not for several hours that little Lady Jyllia was found by her nursemaid Ramke hiding behind the dais, coated with dust, shivering with fear, and unable to speak at all. Ramke was very protective of you," Strale said, nodding to Jyllia. "She insisted on putting you to your room right away, and sent word the Duke of Oloine that the Royal Family was dead, and that his daughter had witnessed the murders but survived."<BR>
<BR>
"I'm beginning to remember a little of that," said Jyllia, wonderingly. "I remember lying in bed, with Ramke comforting me. I was so muddled and I couldn't concentrate. I remember I just wanted it all to be play time still, I don't know why. And then, I remember being bundled up and taken to that asylum."<BR>
<BR>
"It'll all come back to you soon," Gyna smiled. "I promise. That's how I began to remember. I just caught one detail, and the whole flood began."<BR>
<BR>
"That's it," Jyllia began to sob in frustration. "I don't remember anything else except confusion. No, I also remember Daddy not even looking at me as I was taken away. And I remember not caring about that, or anything else."<BR>
<BR>
"It was a confusing time for all, so particularly so for little girls. Especially little girls who went through what you two did," said Lord Strale sympathetically. "From what I understand, as soon as he received the message from Ramke, the Duke left his palace at Oloine, gave orders for you to be sent to a private sanitarium until you'd recovered from your ordeal, and set to work with his private guard torturing the assassin for information. When I heard that, that no one but the Duke and his personal guard saw the assassin after he gave his initial confession, and that no one was present but the Duke and his guards when the assassin was killed trying to escape, I thought that very significant.<BR>
<BR>
"I spoke with Lord Eryl, who I knew was one of those present, and I had to bluff him, pretending I had more evidence than I did. I got the reaction I was hoping for, though it was a dangerous gambit. At last he confessed to what I already knew to be true.<BR>
<BR>
"The assassin," Lord Strale paused, and reluctantly met Jyllia's eyes, "Had been hired by the Duke of Oloine to kill the Royal Family, including the Princess as heir, so that the crown might be passed to him and to his children."<BR>
<BR>
Jyllia stared at Lord Strale, aghast. "My father -"<BR>
<BR>
"The assassin had been told that once the Duke had him in custody, he would be paid and a prison break would be arranged. The thug picked the wrong time to be greedy and try to get more gold. The Duke decided that it would be cheaper to silence him, so he murdered him then and there, so the man would never tell anyone what really happened," Lord Strale shrugged. "No tragic loss as far as murders go. In a few years' time, you returned from the sanitarium, a little shaken but back to normal, except for a complete absence of memory about your childhood. And in that time, the former Duke of Oloine had taken his brother's place as the King of Camlorn. It was no small maneuver."<BR>
<BR>
"No," said Jyllia, quietly. "He must have been very busy. He remarried and had another child. No one ever came to visit me in the sanitarium but Ramke."<BR>
<BR>
"If he had visited and seen you," said Gyna. "This story might have turned out very differently."<BR>
<BR>
"What do you mean?" asked Jyllia.<BR>
<BR>
"This is the most amazing part," said Lord Strale. "The question has long been whether Gyna is the Princess Talara. When her memory returned, and she told me what she remembered, I put several pieces of evidence together. Consider these facts.<BR>
<BR>
"The two of you look remarkably alike now after twenty years of living very different lives, and as little girls and constant playmates, you looked nearly identical.<BR>
<BR>
"At the time of the assassination, the murderer who had never been there before, only saw one girl on the throne, who he assumed to be his quarry.<BR>
<BR>
"The woman who found Lady Jyllia was her nursemaid Ramke, a creature of unstable mind and fanatical devotion to her charge - the type would never accept the possibility that her beloved little girl had been the one who disappeared. The nursemaid was the only single person who knew both Princess Talara and the Lady Jyllia who visited you while you were in the sanitarium.<BR>
<BR>
"Finally," said Lord Strale, "Consider the fact that when you returned to court from the sanitarium, five years had past, and you had grown from a child to a young lady. You looked familiar, but not quite the same as your family remembered you, which is only natural."<BR>
<BR>
"I don't understand," cried the poor girl, her eyes wide, because she did understand. Here memory was falling together like a terrible flood.<BR>
<BR>
"Let me explain it like this," said her cousin, wrapping her in her arms. "I know who I am now. My real name is Jyllia Raze. That man who was arrested was my father, the man who murdered the King - your father. YOU are the Princess Talara."<BR>

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_NamesOfMotherCyrodTR
Names of the Mother Cyrod
母亲西罗德的名字

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_NamesOfMotherCyrodTR
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>Names of the Mother Cyrod<BR>$0A<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>$0A[Editor's Note: During the several interregnums and religious conflicts of the First Empire, many valuable historical texts were lost, either burnt as heretical or simply forgotten in the more pressing issues of the day. One of the most tragic losses was the burning of the Canon Marukhat in 1E 1070, which is understood to have been the most complete compilation of texts describing the Alessian Rebellion. Though many valuable texts survive, such as the Song of Pelinal, the Adabal-a, and the Trials of Alessia, much has never been recovered.<BR>$0A<BR>$0AIn our examination of the scrolls found in the monastery at the ruins of Bed-Geron, we came upon what we believe to be a very valuable discovery. We have translated several complete fragments of what we believe to be the liturgical text Saint Orsede called Maunr ovn Ulmscyrod, or Names of the Mother Cyrod. It depicts the scenes in her life when Alessia the Paravant received each of her several names, and it should prove to be of immense and incalculable value to scholars of the Alessian Rebellion.<BR>$0A<BR>$0AIt is evident from the manuscript that this text has been edited significantly over the course of history. The account is contemporary with Alessia herself, yet the work does not appear to be entirely original. As with most texts of the era, it was written anonymously, and the only indication of any authorship comes from a signatory symbol denoting the identity of the artisan who created the illumination on the page. The glyph, a corruption of a sigil popular in the third century after the revolution, links the document to a spiritual fellowship of Colovian scribe monks who did biographical work known mostly for their tendencies toward Shezarrhic syncretism.]$0A<BR>$0A$0A<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000"><BR>***<BR>$0A<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">$0A$0A<BR>The Chim-el Adabal showed her the facets of things, and in its gem she grew calm. In those dying moments all things were made clear- her names and the deeds that birthed them stood on display, clad only in the clarity of grace. Her life was less and less her own with each passing moment, as the newborn of Cyrod stilled their wails to learn her many names. Her story followed the natural course of the Aurbis, splintering and sharing with all. It was a gift to the people of the Dragon that was regiven each time they made it their own and added a name to her moth-silk, each time a Nede turned praising eyes to Kyne's north and named himself a symbolic son of the Elder Wood. Gift-giving moments need no one to sing them, for they glow like stars in the constellation-scattered timeliness of man.<BR>$0A$0A<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000"><BR>***<BR>$0A<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">$0A$0A<BR>Sard lay thus: an incomplete quadrangle of snowy ramparts, half buried in the fertile riverside of the Niben. With its stone arms it cradled an inlet of clear water in a way that effeminate men would find romantic in better times, but in those days it was a place of bone-white horror. Sard was an enclosure, the greatest pen of southern Rumare. The Keptu, who were allowed to remain free because they ate the dead, called it Chattel-Maw, after the unwashed herds that stumbled wailing into its depths. There they were kept in a partitioned plane of stone that glowed in ways hostile to men, while the Ayleids walked on trapped gangways above, opening and closing the iron sluice gates between the huge cells until all the tribes were sorted. A masterful mind for puzzles was behind it all, as no normal mer could manipulate such a tide of humanity.<BR>$0A<BR>$0AShe was Perrif in this time, which meant 'girl' in the language of one tribe or another, and Girl was the only name she had in any language. In the pens, in underground thickets of feet ceaselessly scrambling and slipping on slick rock, there was no time and no self, only the snaps and screams that echoed from the halls around, or the arrows that hissed downward when the delirious drew too close to the stairs leading up to the guards who feared lunacy but never resistance. Even in the cells where three hundred souls were made suddenly to be quiet and quell their moaning as they were cauterized by the Welkynds one by one until all grew silent, even there, Perrif could not find her senses in the tumult.<BR>$0A<BR>Memory returned with Cyrod itself. She was alone, kneeling in the wetness of the jungle outside and waiting for work on the plantation to resume, when one day she found a grove like an island, surrounded by the fields but forest entirely. The others feared any place but the field and the pen, places they ruled completely while the guards walked above on platforms and walls. They feared the darkness of the canopy and trembled at the stories of the creatures that dwelt there. Perrif's sharp ears had pilfered the words of a prayer to Kynereth from the lips of a sentry, and for everything she knew of the goddess she knew the less of dread. She had a sanctuary now, where not even the virile young men followed her. It was not worth the risk to them, for she was not considered desirable. Although the Al-Esh is beautiful in all her names and tales, so many years of right-thinking had been imposed on the slaves that they recoiled from white skin and dark hair.<BR>$0A<BR>So she had her solitude, and balanced priestly on the yielding soil wet with droplets from the rain she loved for its mother, chanting prayers. Through many months she never found death at the hands of man or mer or pestilence, or from the chance swing of a scythe.  She spoke to the goddess whose only form was in the misheard words of a single prayer and in the rain that tumbled ceaselessly from the sky. Puddles formed around her feet, so that she spoke now not to the heavens, but to the reflection beneath her. It became more difficult to return from the sanctuary with each passing day, even with obedience ingrained in her shallow mind with the finest etchings of cruelty. She began to speak with lips of inspiration, and on the day she named Shezzar, the spirit of his consort burned brightly in her breast and for the first time Perrif knew her own grace. A big-leafed fern to her right rustled suddenly and she turned her fair head. Something had fallen from the overcast sky, leaving a smear of red light in the rain as a comet-trail. The trembling of her fingers did nothing to slow their search. She reached into a shadowy lattice of mossy roots and moth grubs to pull forth a crimson light. It was a shape she had never seen before, faces and faces within those faces like the eyes of an insect that droned, bird-sized through the fields to torment the workers. Each one was reflecting and aflame. """<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>母亲西罗德的名字<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
[编者注：在第一帝国的几次大空位和宗教冲突期间，许多珍贵的历史文献丢失了，要么作为异端被烧毁，要么仅仅在更紧迫的事务中被遗忘。最悲惨的损失之一是第一纪元1070年马鲁哈特正典被焚毁，据信那是描述阿莱西亚起义的最完整文本汇编。尽管许多珍贵文献幸存下来，如《佩林纳尔之歌》、《阿达巴尔-阿》和《阿莱西亚的考验》，但许多内容从未被找回。<BR>
<BR>
在我们检查贝德-杰隆废墟修道院发现的卷轴时，我们有了一个我们认为非常有价值的发现。我们翻译了我们认为是由圣奥塞德撰写的礼仪文本《莫恩·奥文·乌姆西罗德》（意为“母亲西罗德的名字”）的几个完整片段。它描绘了阿莱西亚·帕拉万在她生命中获得她几个名字时的场景，这对研究阿莱西亚起义的学者来说，应该具有巨大且不可估量的价值。<BR>
<BR>
从手稿可以明显看出，这份文本在历史进程中经过了大量编辑。叙述与阿莱西亚本人同时代，但作品似乎并非完全原创。与那个时代的大多数文本一样，它是匿名撰写的，任何作者身份的线索都来自一个签名符号，该符号表示在页面上创作装饰插图的工匠的身份。这个字形是革命后三世纪流行的标志的变体，将文件与一个科洛维亚抄写僧侣的精神团契联系起来，这些僧侣主要从事传记写作，以其倾向于舍扎尔融合主义而闻名。]
<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000"><BR>***<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">

<BR>奇姆-艾尔·阿达巴尔向她展示了事物的方方面面，在那颗宝石中，她变得平静。在那临终的时刻，一切变得清晰 -- 她的名字以及孕育它们的事迹展现在眼前，只披着恩典的澄澈光辉。她的生命随着每一刻的流逝越来越不属于她自己，当西罗德的新生儿停止哭泣，去学习她的众多名字时。她的故事遵循了奥比斯的自然进程，分裂并与所有人分享。这是给龙之民的礼物，每次他们将其变成自己的，并在她的蛾丝上添加一个名字，每次一个尼德人将赞美的目光转向北方的吉讷，并自称为古木的象征之子时，这份礼物就被重新赐予。馈赠的时刻无需任何人歌唱，因为它们像星星一样在人类星座散布的时限中闪耀。<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000"><BR>***<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">

<BR>萨德是这样构成的：一个由雪白壁垒组成的不完整四边形，半掩埋于尼本河肥沃的河畔。它用石臂环抱着一个清澈的入水口，那种方式在更好的时代会让女性化的男人觉得浪漫，但在那些日子里，它是一个白骨般恐怖的地方。萨德是一个围场，南鲁玛雷最大的畜栏。克普图人，因他们吃死者而被允许保持自由，称其为“动产咽喉”，以那些蹒跚哭泣着跌入其深处的肮脏畜群命名。在那里，它们被关在一个对人有敌意的发光石制分隔平面中，而亚历德人则走在上面被陷阱困住的走道上，打开和关闭巨大牢房之间的铁闸门，直到所有部落都被分类好。这一切背后是一个精通谜题的头脑，因为普通的精灵无法操纵如此汹涌的人潮。<BR>
<BR>
此时她被称为佩里夫，这在某个部落的语言中意为“女孩”，而“女孩”是她无论何种语言中唯一的名字。在围栏里，在脚下不断在光滑岩石上攀爬滑倒的地下丛林中，没有时间，没有自我，只有周围大厅回荡的爆裂声和尖叫声，或者当神志不清的人靠得太近通往守卫的楼梯时，向下嘶嘶作响的箭矢 -- 守卫们害怕疯狂，但从不害怕抵抗。即使在那些三百个灵魂突然被要求安静、在维尔金石逐一灼烧时抑制住呻吟、直到一切归于寂静的牢房里，即使在那里，佩里夫也无法在喧嚣中找到自己的理智。<BR>
<BR>记忆随着西罗德本身回来了。她独自一人，跪在外面潮湿的丛林中，等待种植园恢复工作。一天，她发现了一个像岛一样的小树林，被田野包围，但完全是森林。其他人害怕除了田野和围栏以外的任何地方，那些地方他们完全掌控，而守卫则在平台和城墙上行走。他们害怕树冠的黑暗，听到住在那里的生物的故事会颤抖。佩里夫敏锐的耳朵从一个哨兵那里偷听到了向吉娜瑞斯祈祷的词句，而就她对女神的了解而言，她对恐惧了解得就更少了。她现在有了一个庇护所，连那些健壮的年轻人也不跟着她。对他们来说，这不值得冒险，因为她被认为没有吸引力。尽管奥-艾什在她所有的名字和传说中都很美丽，但多年来，正确思想的灌输强加给了奴隶，以至于他们回避白皮肤和黑头发。<BR>
<BR>于是她拥有了她的孤独，像祭司一样平衡在因雨水而湿润的松软土壤上，她因那雨水而爱着它的母亲，念诵着祈祷词。许多个月过去了，她从未死于人类、精灵、瘟疫之手，也未死于偶然挥动的镰刀之下。她对女神说话，女神的唯一形态存在于听错的祈祷词和从天而降的连绵雨水中。她脚下形成了水坑，因此她不是向天堂说话，而是向她脚下的倒影说话。日复一日，即使服从已用最精细的残酷蚀刻在她浅薄的脑海中，从庇护所回来也变得越来越困难。她开始用灵感之唇说话，在她命名舍扎尔的那一天，他伴侣的灵魂在她胸中燃烧，佩里夫第一次知道了自己的恩典。她右边一棵大叶蕨类植物突然沙沙作响，她转过她美丽的头。有什么东西从阴沉的天空中坠落，在雨中留下一道红色的光痕，如同彗尾。她手指的颤抖并没有减缓它们的探索。她伸手进入一个由长满苔藓的根和蛾蛆组成的阴暗格架，拉出一道深红色的光。那是她从未见过的形状，那些面孔中还有面孔，就像在田野上嗡嗡作响、鸟一样大小折磨工人的昆虫的眼睛。每一个都在反射和燃烧。它消失在围裙中，除了起义的第一个受害者外，再也没有人见过它，此后传说再也不能记起它是否是奇姆-艾尔·阿达巴尔。<BR>

<BR>“难怪。苍蝇闻到了血。别管那个寄生虫了！快，母亲在等。”<BR>

<BR>“所以你确实相信了。迪贝-玛拉-金！”<BR>

<BR>穿着新衣服，满怀期待，佩里夫对白芒的到来微笑，他的脸强壮而充满灵性，像（她想）一个年长的精灵。他现在身上没有那颗宝石的痕迹，没有可能让起义军不安的迹象，但在他摘下护手或他胸前的鱼鳞星之前，那将会改变。莫尔确实跟在后面，他的眼神让佩里夫更像一个少女而不是母亲。她甩开这种感觉，将目光投向天空，已经看到明天将吞没萨德隐藏地平线的烟雾。<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000"><BR>***<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">

<BR>瓦塔切是不可腐蚀的 -- 甚至奴隶也知道这一点。它的主人建造得经久耐用，拆除了上面的城市，撤退到尼本河下的要塞，认为凭借坚韧和维尔金石的光芒能熬过起义。他们对舍扎尔狂野的回应是像壳中的乌龟一样坚守，以更大程度的收缩来回应自由。地下场所的奴隶们心甘情愿地协助这一努力，因为经过几代人对下方黑暗和上方孤独花园的照料，他们害怕来自外部的东西。当他们称瓦塔切为不可腐蚀时，他们自豪地这样称呼，就像狗和种马与同伴竞争，对主人充满忠诚。<BR>

<BR>但在那些日子里，新生的人类是赢得肉体的潜能，在古西罗德的树下奋斗，其能量盖过了他们来自海边的苍白头发表亲。随着力量之座白金塔本身即将被推翻，一切都不确定。当外部的人给它起了一个新名字，一个更适合所有部落发音的名字时，瓦塔切的未来像西沉的太阳一样沉没。起义军知道，这座要塞正被围困。瓦塔肯是厄运的名称。<BR>

<BR>据说此后不久，命运选择嘲弄其崇高的受害者白金塔，让天堂之轮成为笑柄。大清洗在鲁玛雷周围画了一道血环，模仿并遮蔽了其中心亚历德石环的轨迹。在早期，当圆环仍沿着北方的暴力路线行驶，其完成度存疑时，瓦塔切找到了舍扎尔。佩里夫的先行者（像伊'弗瑞在洪流中一样在丛林中行走的科斯里人，是起义的第一批先驱）仍在南边几里格处。主力部队则落后更远，被困在灌木丛中，躲在皮盾下躲避倾泻的箭雨，而佩林纳尔的旗帜则在林下灌木丛中开辟出一条愤怒的道路去迎接他们。尽管遭遇挫折，消息还是通过希望低语的蛾翅被带到地下深处。它始于在阴暗屋顶的系泊处摇摆的十二排铁笼。不守规矩的人住在那里，慢慢饿死。在动荡时期，狱卒们忽略了
划分部落，六十名克瑞斯掠夺者在石板地面上一同摇摆。在他们中间，有三个人一直处于休眠状态，被抓时被打昏了，现在这三个人醒了过来。绑架者是一群粗心的帮派，都是亲戚，他们像野精灵一样上树，在失去萨利亚切霸权之前就放弃了它，并将冲突转化为利益。他们默默地收集了赏金，不在乎解释三个被制服是有原因的，不在乎解释他们在交付后拿掉了塞口物，因为塞口物属于他们。现在，在笼子里，北方的声音给石头本身插上了翅膀，吐姆将瓦塔切的每一个笼子都撞倒了。<BR>

<BR>
当佩里夫的旗帜部队第二天到达时，囚犯们在尼本河岸的内部横行。亚历德的抵抗已经从内部腐烂成血腥的废墟，人们将巨大的石块和数不清的瓦砾堆成堆，建造坡道以爬出坑牢，并封锁入口。他们正在冲过数英里的陷阱，用泥土和绝望掩埋他们邪恶的工事，直到通道流满更多的鲜血。在门口，他们终于筋疲力尽，因为要塞被巨大的、上下浮动的维尔金石魔法胶囊塔密封，这些塔在解锁时会吞噬秘密。知道这一点后，佩林纳尔变成了光的存在，所有光线都反射到自己身上，或者也许只是他的拳头，击碎了九道门中的八道。每一道缺口都像灯塔一样闪烁，从雪喉可见，天际正在进军。<BR>

<BR>母亲西罗德，骑着莫里豪斯的神圣背上盘旋，当她最新的儿子们像洪水一样出现在河岸上时，她降落下来。他们抬着吐目们残缺不全的身体，带着棺材般的手，发出响亮的赞美，而吉讷之息哼了一声，他的头发像羽毛的鬃毛一样直立。第一个从树梢看到她降落的人是神志不清的，喊出了“奥-艾什”！意思是：来自高处的殿下。<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000"><BR>***<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">

<BR>白芒唾液溅落的地方，大地噼啪作响。虽然只有寥寥三滴，但杰拉尔山脉并非自愿饮用，因为舍扎尔因的物质本身就是令人厌恶的仇恨。山脉反而饮下了血液。那是一个血湾，像尼本河一样，是西罗德帝国的一个大洞，抽干了它作恶的力量。<BR>

<BR>北部山区的羽族从每一个要塞，无论隐藏还是公开，都来到这山间激流的悬崖岸边用剑争斗，现在十四个亚历德部落的羽毛装饰着死者。佩林纳尔守住了渡口，横跨急流，以无人愿意回忆的方式杀戮。胜利在于停止逃跑，因为他身边那支规模庞大的尼德采集者队伍找到了追随领袖的勇气，而他本身就是战争的化身。奥-艾什和起义军先到，然后佛克瑞斯到达了渡口，两支军队都目睹了松树贫瘠之地被矛刺穿的荒凉。大清洗完成了，白芒站在桥上。<BR>

<BR>赫尔顿桥的诺德人并非以舍扎尔因来称呼佩林纳尔，因为那个头衔是后来才有的，当时其他名字显得陈旧且有民间传说的味道。相反，北方的军队援引了对朔尔的敬意，并在他们带有齿痕的盾牌边缘上下敲击长矛，发出行军脚步的声音。尽管硝烟弥漫，喧嚣混乱，奥-艾什现在在起义军的眼中看到了普罗提努的命运，并再次努力拯救她的起义，在沾满鲜血的滑溜桥板上滑行以让他平静下来。看到两个南方人如此配对 -- 红色白色废墟和活生生的棕色美人映衬着晴朗的地平线 -- 队伍中的智者在他被吐姆震聋的耳朵里琢磨着西罗德的外来语，最终想出了一个听起来不错的称呼：阿莱斯。奥-艾什的阿莱斯，此后被人类世界的混血称为阿莱西亚 -- 奴隶女王。<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000"><BR>***<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">

<BR>当她坐在被烧去光辉的王座上，下巴高昂地审视着她的征服 -- 一座白金塔时，他们称她为帕拉万。大地中心的空气中弥漫着净化血液的浓烟，血液在石板上流淌，如同紫色的终局。新的挂毯和旗帜在胜利者的绳索上争先恐后地升向天空，它们以一种与洗劫后城堡的废墟完美互补的混乱姿态舞蹈。她是帕拉万，第一位杀戮-探寻-治愈者，众神已经在围绕她头顶穹顶的闪耀维尔金石粉尘的壁龛中侍奉她，那些神不是神，而仍然是粗野的精灵灵体。他们默默地、无思想地观察着这个房间，因为他们没有文化。她尚未生下他们，但他们已经带来了革命。<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000"><BR>***<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">

<BR>议会小艇完成了它们的使命，堆放在一个孤独沙洲上燃烧的山中，而莫里豪斯站在烟雾中哞叫。他的哀叹甚至震动了迷失的阿巴加拉斯隧道，那是一种像光穿过水一样穿过石头的嚎叫声。灵体的思想是被筑坝成单一水流的海洋，是对一颗星星的八个碎片的悼词：一个被杀的叔父。他对他的配偶和他夺取仪式上装饰着角饰的脚充耳不闻。他还要很久才会回到塔楼，并用他将给她的名字称呼她：“第一”，帕拉瓦尼亚。<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000"><BR>***<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">

<BR>
她躺在塔楼的床上，寻找一个原名。用这样的东西将曙光族裔驱逐回他们暴力之光的土地是件简单的事，但寻找自己的真名则是另一回事。她已经失去了它：一个早期的自我碎片，现在被之后的所有名字所掩盖。岁月也模糊了新的名字。<BR>

<BR>奥-艾什，帕拉万，她的保姆们无法决定现在哪个名字更合适，因为他们的女王已经如此年迈。在她的临终床上，他们为她洗脚，发现很难足够大声地说话，用北方普通王室的礼节称呼她。但为了避免有人说她衰老，她仍然美丽，而莫里豪斯也还在那里。在她令人震惊的年纪，她既年轻又美丽，关于她优雅的故事仍有待书写。就在那天下午，一个有远见的人会坐在首都蓄水池的台阶上，告诉世界他看到了一个未来：阿莱西亚会蹲在一个平台上，成为一座大理石雕像，产下一颗绿色的宝石，那就是古西罗德·乌特·泰姆瑞尔。<BR>

<BR>她耳边传来一阵恸哭声。保姆们离开了，只留下一位蛾贤者坐在床对面的书桌前。他甚至比他的女王还要年长，在这个圆形房间里几乎不占任何空间。一位先祖在他耳边歌唱，他跟着哼唱，用手里的笔打着拍子。几分钟后，他不再与他的女王独处，他安静下来。<BR>

<BR>阿莱西亚的眼皮分开，她醒了。某个地方音乐正强烈地演奏着。她看到了床脚，知道是舍扎尔。理智的佩林-艾尔是赤裸的，因为他的盔甲已溶解成它自己的星辰织锦，而光芒构成了他的肉体，中心是蛇一般疯狂的空虚。他们谈了很长时间，尽管阿莱西亚无法命令她的舌头回答，靠墙的祭司也听不到话语，但他的笔很忙碌（这一切发生在眨眼三次的瞬间，尽管它填满了许多卷轴）。墨水覆盖了书桌，顺着他的腿流下，覆盖了他的前臂，污损并覆盖了他祖先的珍贵丝绸潦草字迹，以至于那个场景被当场写入了历史，而蛾将永远知道它。<BR>

<BR>
女王看着她的冠军用发光的手指伸入他空洞的胸膛。祭司在闷热的房间里什么也没看到，除了一只蹲着的红龙。那只龙向床伸出爪子，爪中紧握着一颗璀璨的宝石。<BR>

<BR>
房间的门关着。从来没有人进入过。阿莱西亚的胸口发出嘎嘎声，床上空无一人，现在只是奇姆-艾尔·阿达巴尔和它凡人枕头冷却血肉的祭坛。他们周围的塔楼膨胀并喘息，在世界被重组时吸入新的空气。一阵穿堂风已经将一页祭司的潦草字迹从书桌吹走，消失在壁炉中。明天，人群将会哀悼，更多的笔将会舞动，没有人看到佩林纳尔在床边。历史正在消退，但自革命以来，塔楼第一次屹立着，它的承诺无法被隐藏。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
伊尔加梅什叙事诗：第十一卷<BR>
