"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
On Artaeum<BR>
by Taurce il-Anselma<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The Isle of Artaeum (ar-TAY-um) is the third largest island in the Summurset archipelago, located south of the Moridunon village of Potansa and west of the mainland village of Runcibae. It is best known for being home to the Psijic Order, perhaps the oldest monastic group in Tamriel.<BR>
<BR>
The earliest written record of Psijics is from the 20th year of the First Era and tells the tale of the renowned Breton sage and author Voernet, traveling to the Isle of Artaeum to meet with Iachesis, the Ritemaster of the Psijics.<BR>
<BR>
Even then, the Psijics were the counsellors of kings and proponents of the "Elder Way," taught to them by the original race that inhabited Tamriel. The Elder Way is a philosophy of meditation and study said to bind the forces of nature to the individual will. It differs from magicka in origin, but the effects are much the same.<BR>
<BR>
That said, it is perhaps more than coincidence that the Isle of Artaeum literally vanished from the shores of Summurset at the beginning of the Second Era at about the time of the founding of the Mages Guild in Tamriel. Various historians and scholars have published theories about this, but perhaps none but Iachesis and his own could shed light on the matter.<BR>
<BR>
Five hundred years passed and Artaeum returned. The Psijics on the Isle consisted of persons, mostly Elves, who had disappeared and were presumed dead in the Second Era. They could not or would not offer any explanation for Artaeum's whereabouts during that time, or the fate of Iachesis and the original council of Artaeum.<BR>
<BR>
Currently, the Psijics are led by the Loremaster Celarus, who has presided over the Council of Artaeum for the last two hundred and fifty years. The Council's influence in Tamrielan politics is tidal. The kings of Sumurset, particularly those of Moridunon, have often sought the Psijics' opinion. Emperor Uriel V was much influenced by the Council in the early, most glorious parts of his reign, before his disastrous attack on Akavir. It has even been suggested that the fleet of King Orghum of Pyandonea was destroyed by a joint effort of Emperor Antiochus and the Psijic Order. The last four emperors, Uriel VI, Morihatha, Pelagius IV, and Uriel VII, have been suspicious of the Psijics enough to refuse ambassadors from the Isle of Artaeum within the Imperial City.<BR>
<BR>
The Isle of Artaeum is difficult to chart geographically. It is said that it shifts continuously either at random or by decree of the Council. Visitors to the island are so rare as to be almost unheard of. Anyone desirous of a meeting with a Psijic may find contacts in Potansa and Runcibae as well as many of the kingdoms of Summurset.<BR>
<BR>
Were it more accessible, Artaeum would be a favored destination for travelers. I have been to the Isle once and still dream of its idyllic orchards and clear pastures, its still and silent lagoons, its misty woodlands, and the unique Psijic architecture that seems to be as natural as its surroundings as well as wondrous in its own right. The Ceporah Tower in particular I would study, for it is a relic from a civilization that predates the High Elves by several hundred years and is still used in certain rites by the Psijics. Perhaps one day I might return.<BR>
<BR>
[Note: The author is currently on the Isle of Artaeum by gracious consent of Master Sargenius of the Council of Artaeum.]<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
论阿泰乌姆<BR>
陶斯·伊尔-安塞尔玛 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
阿泰乌姆岛（ar-TAY-um）是夏暮群岛中第三大岛屿，位于莫里杜农的波坦萨村以南，大陆的伦西贝村以西。它最出名的是作为塞伊克教团的所在地，这可能是泰姆瑞尔最古老的修道团体。<BR>
<BR>
关于塞伊克的最早书面记录出自第一纪元20年，讲述了著名的布莱顿贤者和作家沃尔内特前往阿泰乌姆岛会见塞伊克教团的仪式大师伊阿基斯的故事。<BR>
<BR>
即便在当时，塞伊克就已经是国王们的顾问和“古道”的倡导者，古道是由最初居住在泰姆瑞尔的原始种族传授给他们的。古道是一种冥想与研习的哲学，据说能将自然之力与个人意志相结合。它与魔能的来源不同，但效果大致相同。<BR>
<BR>
话虽如此，阿泰乌姆岛在第二纪元初期，大约在泰姆瑞尔法师公会成立的时候，从夏暮岛的海岸上 literally 消失了，这或许不仅仅是巧合。许多历史学家和学者发表了关于此事的理论，但也许除了伊阿基斯和他自己的人，没人能阐明此事。<BR>
<BR>
五百年过去了，阿泰乌姆回来了。岛上的塞伊克由那些在第二纪元失踪并被推定死亡的人组成，大多是精灵。他们无法也不愿就阿泰乌姆在那段时间的下落，或是伊阿基斯及阿泰乌姆原始议会的命运做出任何解释。<BR>
<BR>
目前，塞伊克由学识大师塞拉鲁斯领导，他主持阿泰乌姆议会已有两百五十年。议会在泰姆瑞尔政治中的影响力如潮汐般起伏。夏暮的国王们，尤其是莫里杜农的国王，常常寻求塞伊克的意见。尤利尔五世皇帝在他统治早期最辉煌的时期深受议会影响，之后便发动了对阿卡维尔的灾难性进攻。甚至有说法认为，派安多尼亚的奥格努姆国王的舰队是被安条克皇帝和塞伊克教团联手摧毁的。最近四位皇帝 -- 尤利尔六世、莫里哈萨、佩拉吉乌斯四世和尤利尔七世 -- 都对塞伊克深怀疑虑，以至于拒绝阿泰乌姆岛的使节进入帝都。<BR>
<BR>
阿泰乌姆岛的地理位置很难绘制。据说它要么随机地、要么由议会下令持续移动。前往该岛的访客极为罕见，几乎闻所未闻。任何希望与塞伊克会面的人，可以在波坦萨和伦西贝以及夏暮的许多王国找到联系人。<BR>
<BR>
如果它更容易到达，阿泰乌姆将会成为旅行者青睐的目的地。我曾去过该岛一次，至今仍梦想着它田园诗般的果园和清澈的牧场，宁静的泻湖，迷雾缭绕的林地，以及独特的塞伊克建筑 -- 它们既与环境融为一体，又本身奇妙无比。我尤其想研究塞波拉塔，因为它是一个比傲特莫早数百年的文明遗迹，至今仍被塞伊克用于某些仪式。也许有一天我能回去。<BR>
<BR>
[注：作者目前在阿泰乌姆岛，承蒙阿泰乌姆议会的萨格尼乌斯大师慷慨同意。]<BR>
<BR>"""

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_OnDaedricDesignTR
On Daedric Design
论迪德拉设计

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_OnDaedricDesignTR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
On Daedric Design<BR>
By Nelos Llothri<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Contrary to the beliefs of so-called "Daedric scholars", the architecture of Daedric shrines is not designed to instill fear in passers-by. Neither is it a mortal mimicry of the buildings found in Daedric realms, a mockery of the fabled facades of Aldmeris, nor an echo of the rocky pillars found in the caverns which were our earliest temples. In truth, the forms of Daedric ruins are not merely architecture: they are instead a divine form of mathematics. A device inscribed upon the bones of the world, bending the Mundus towards the supranatural and enabling the worshippers to lay physical hands on the metaphysical bodies of their gods.<BR>
<BR>
The power of temples, shrines, and relics to channel prayer has, of course, long been established, both through scholarly experiment and through endless anecdotal evidence. However, while the effects of the temples of the dead Eight and dying One, as well as the lesser Eighty-Two, stem largely from mortal belief and ritualistically conjured echoes, the power of a Daedric shrine comes from its design.<BR>
<BR>
Communion with the Anticipations, particularly Boethiah in the aspect of the architect-teacher, allowed our ancestors to build temples that would purposefully, not just accidentally, draw their gods' attention. Each curve of a pillar, each angle, each niche is designed to not only capture but echo and amplify the sounds and motions of prayer, and to direct them as a metaphorical beam to a Void between the stars. In time, a well-built shrine would function even in the absence of supplicants, for its walls keep any whisper alive for generations. The chanting heard by scholars and adventurers within abandoned temples is precisely this.<BR>
<BR>
Some "Daedric scholars" go so far as to draw parallels between Daedric shrines and Dwemer ruins, reaching for superficial parallels between architect-pupils and tonal architects. The less this blasphemy is committed to paper, the better.<BR>
<BR>
The theurgic geometries of a shrine's construction are deceptively intricate, and, as should be self-evident, highly volatile. No one should undertake the construction of a new shrine uninitiated, for modern stonecutters with the requisite skill and sublimation are all but unheard of, and the slightest geometric imperfection invites disaster. Even the most experienced adventurer would be wise to avoid the more deteriorated surviving shrines, such as Ald Balaal and Ald Sotha.<BR>
<BR>
When a shrine has been abandoned, the echoing effects vary wildly, depending not only on layout and integrity of the remaining structure, but also the favor and dedication of the faithful and most importantly, the Daedric Lord to whom the shrine is devoted. In a fully-intact shrine dedicated to Sheogorath, an untrained scholar can expect to feel confused within minutes; mania, dementia, paranoia, hysteria, schizophrenia, obsession, or hallucinations set in within the hour. Visitors to shrines of Mehrunes Dagon typically report feeling contrarian, enraged, spiteful, and violent. Shrines to Azura compel feelings of complacence, anticipation, inadequacy, and lethargy.<BR>
<BR>
These lingering effects are due to the thinning of the barrier between Mundus and Oblivion that were established and -- pardon the pun -- enshrined during the shrines' building and active phases. One who wishes to explore an abandoned Daedric ruin in relative safety is advised to carry talismans of Almsivi, whose pacts with and wars against the Daedra provide some measure of protection.<BR>
<BR>
Even with such mighty protection, every right-thinking scholar ought to realize that the old shrines and their echoes are wonders of an age long past, built to capture the attention of selfish gods, and are not to be explored by the unprepared and whimsical. In the modern age, our gods walk by our side and we do not need to reach out to them by mathematics and architecture anymore. But we must acknowledge and understand the works of our ancestors and their worship of the Anticipations, or else their echoes and prayers will be lost with crumbling stone, no better off than the prayers cast in the feeble shrines of the Western spirits.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
论迪德拉设计<BR>
内洛斯·洛思里 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
与所谓的“迪德拉学者”的信念相反，迪德拉圣祠的建筑并非旨在给路人灌输恐惧。它也不是凡人对迪德拉领域建筑的模仿，不是对奥德莫瑞斯传说中的外观的嘲弄，也不是对我们最早神殿所在的洞穴中发现的石柱的回响。事实上，迪德拉废墟的形式不仅仅是建筑：它们是一种神圣的数学形式。一种铭刻在世界骨架上的装置，将梦达斯引向超自然，并使崇拜者能够亲手触及他们神灵的形而上学之躯。<BR>
<BR>
当然，神殿、圣祠和圣物引导祈祷的力量早已通过学术实验和无数的传闻证据得到证实。然而，死去八圣灵和垂死一圣灵，以及次等八十二圣灵的神殿的效果，主要源于凡人的信仰和仪式性召唤的回声，而迪德拉圣祠的力量则源于其设计。<BR>
<BR>
与预知者的交流，尤其是作为建筑师-导师面相的波耶西亚，使我们的祖先能够建造出有意（而不仅仅是偶然）引起他们神灵注意的神殿。柱子的每一条曲线，每一个角度，每一个壁龛，其设计不仅要捕捉，还要回响和放大祈祷的声音和动作，并将它们像比喻中的光束一样导向星辰之间的虚空。随着时间的推移，一座建造良好的圣祠即使在无人祈祷时也能运作，因为它的墙壁能使任何低语代代相传。学者和冒险家在废弃神殿内听到的吟唱，正是这个。<BR>
<BR>
一些“迪德拉学者”甚至将迪德拉圣祠与锻莫废墟相提并论，在建筑师-学徒与音调建筑师之间寻找表面的相似之处。这种亵渎之言越少付诸笔墨越好。<BR>
<BR>
圣祠建造的神通几何学看似简单实则错综复杂，而且，不言而喻，极不稳定。未经启蒙者不应建造新的圣祠，因为拥有必要技能和升华境界的现代石匠几乎闻所未闻，哪怕是最微小的几何缺陷都会招致灾难。即使是最有经验的冒险者，避开像奥德·巴拉尔和奥德·索萨这样更破败的幸存圣祠也是明智之举。<BR>
<BR>
当一座圣祠被废弃后，其回响效果变化很大，不仅取决于剩余结构的布局和完整性，还取决于信徒的恩宠与奉献，以及最重要的，圣祠所供奉的迪德拉之主。在一座献给谢尔格拉斯的完好圣祠中，一个未经训练的学者几分钟内就会感到困惑；狂躁、痴呆、偏执、歇斯底里、精神分裂、强迫症或幻觉会在一个小时内出现。到访梅鲁涅斯·大衮圣祠的人通常会报告感到叛逆、愤怒、恶意和暴力。阿祖拉的圣祠则会引发自满、期待、不足和昏昏欲睡的感觉。<BR>
<BR>
这些持久的效果是由于梦达斯与湮灭之间屏障的变薄，这种屏障是在圣祠建造和活跃期间建立并 -- 请原谅这个双关 -- 被奉为圣物的。希望相对安全地探索废弃迪德拉废墟的人，建议携带阿玛莱西娅、索萨·希尔和维威克（奥姆希维）的护符，他们与迪德拉的契约和战争能提供一定程度的保护。<BR>
<BR>
即使有如此强大的保护，每个有思想的学者都应该意识到，古老的圣祠及其回响是早已逝去时代的奇迹，是为了吸引自私神灵的注意而建造的，未经准备和心血来潮者不应涉足。在现代，我们的神与我们同行，我们不再需要通过数学和建筑来接触他们。但我们必须承认并理解我们祖先的功绩以及他们对预知者的崇拜，否则他们的回声和祈祷将随着 crumbling 的石头一起消失，不会比在西方神灵的弱小圣祠中发出的祈祷好多少。<BR>

On Hammerfell<BR>
the Imperial Province<BR>
by Erramanwe of Sunhold<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
After the conquest of High Rock, the Imperial court of Tiber Septim received an envoy from the Redguards.<BR>
<BR>
It had been a year since the Forebears of Hammerfell, a rural warrior underclass, began their revolt against the kingdom's urban aristocracy. Though Forebear militias made early strides in capturing key settlements, Crown knights and mercenaries had won countless subsequent battles with no signs of stopping, and after Sentinel, the rebels' fate seemed sealed.<BR>
<BR>
It is no surprise that the Forebears turned to Cyrodiil to save them. When the Reman emperors ruled Hammerfell, their reign saw Forebear tribes raised into nobility, granting them rights the Crowns stridently denied them; several rebel leaders now claimed dormant Imperial titles as assertions of power. Furthermore, Tiber Septim had become known in the provinces as an effective leader and diplomat. Were he half as magnanimous as his ancient precursors, and his reputation suggested as much, many Forebears would find him a preferable sovereign to Crown Prince A'tor, the temperamental and ruthless heir to Hammerfell's throne.<BR>
<BR>
So did Baron Volag, the leader of the Forebears, come to Tiber Septim with a bargain. It is unclear exactly what Septim was offered; while the official account only mentions a military and trade alliance, it is widely suspected that Volag also promised the Emperor a swath of lands on Hammerfell's southern border. It is clearer what the Forebears got out of the agreement. Not long after this secret treaty was ratified, Imperial legions came to Hammerfell and drove the Crowns out of Sentinel. Devastated by the surprise attack, many Crown forces deserted to the Dragontail mountains. The others made their last stand in the harbor of Stros M'kai, where the Imperial navy left no survivors.<BR>
<BR>
With Prince A'tor dead and the war won, Volag would have been Hammerfell's new king, but in the chaos that followed Stros M'kai, he had vanished. Tiber Septim made a new treaty in his absence. A hastily assembled council of Forebear leaders agreed that the Emperor was to rule the kingdom in Volag's stead.<BR>
<BR>
In truth, Tiber Septim had coveted Hammerfell for years. Many of the debts he assumed at the onset of his reign were due, and Hammerfell was a famously wealthy nation. However, various factors discouraged its direct conquest. The Redguards were undesirable foes, a race of fanatics protected by fearsome elemental spirits, and at the time, a common school of thought held that the Remans could have conquered Morrowind had they not wasted their assets taking Hammerfell. Now, however, Septim had been invited in. Though in theory he was preparing the throne for Volag's return, most assumed Septim had the baron assassinated. Hammerfell was his.<BR>
<BR>
In the new province, Crown law was replaced with harshly enforced Imperial law. Provisional governors levied exorbitant taxes to fund expansion in Morrowind and imprisoned all who could not pay. The Yokudan desert nomads, once shunned in the cities, were banned altogether. Loyal Crowns were swiftly executed alongside Forebears upset with the Empire's betrayal.<BR>
<BR>
The Emperor surely recognized this arrangement as unsustainable, but not even he could have foreseen how it ended.<BR>
<BR>
Paying a favor to a Crown mercenary, a nomad witch called on ancient Yokudan magic to resurrect A'tor. With supernatural powers of persuasion, the revived prince then called on several dissolved warbands to reform under the banner of his uprising, and forced a second battle at Stros M'kai. Once the site of A'tor's grave, Stros M'kai became that of every Imperial official and soldier on the island. The admiral who sank A'tor's ship and killed him had by then become the local governor, whom A'tor personally slew.<BR>
<BR>
Seizing on the opportunity, Volag then emerged from hiding with his personal retinue to take Sentinel, the city's fourth and final conquest in two years. Forebears across the province once more rose in rebellion under Volag's leadership, this time against a foreign crown. Taking their former allies by surprise, they swept over the mainland, often supported by locals regardless of allegiance. Some Forebears fought under barons, others under hetmans, and others still under Crown officers, reasserting local rule in any manner they could.<BR>
<BR>
Soon, the Redguards had completely expelled the legions from Hammerfell. In the East, however, the Emperor had just signed a treaty guaranteeing Morrowind's acquisition as an Imperial province. If Hammerfell did not come to an agreement with the Empire shortly, it was only a matter of time until the legions returned.<BR>
<BR>
A summit was held in Stros M'kai. A'tor and his consort represented the Crowns, Volag represented the Forebears, and Tiber Septim and Zurin Arctus represented the Empire. According to reports, tensions rode high until Zurin Arctus told a joke about Bretons, which moved all parties to laughter. Negotiations then proceeded in high spirits.<BR>
<BR>
The kingdom of Hammerfell was to be restored, with High King A'tor succeeding his father. At the same time, Forebear lands would no longer be ruled by centrally appointed Crown officers, as under the old regime, but instead by local Forebear nobles and elected leaders. These territories would be united in one high kingdom, with A'tor as their symbolic head of state, but not their head of government. The Crowns had stewarded Hammerfell for millennia, and their efforts were recognized and appreciated even by the Forebears they had disenfranchised, but the war and occupation had decimated their numbers, and the Forebears had proven their worth on the mainland. By and large, the Crowns' time had come and gone.<BR>
<BR>
The Empire's role in this new Hammerfell was to be minimal. While Redguard ports would be left open to the Imperial navy in its wars with the Aldmeri Dominion and other foreign agents, and certain resources in which Tiber Septim had more interest than the natives would be reserved as Imperial property, it was guaranteed that for as long as the Septim emperors reigned, all Imperial legions, magistrates, and census agents would be banned from Hammerfell, only able to enter under express Redguard mandate.  Native militias and systems of land-based taxation had underpinned Redguard civilization for centuries, and Imperial attempts to erase them were key factors in the revolt; these would be left intact. Moving forward, the Treaty of Stros M'kai made clear that though the Redguards were not independent, they would rule themselves, "not as subjects of the Empire, but as allies."<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
On Lycanthropy<BR>
by Varnard Karessen<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
How does one become interested in studying the disease lycanthropy? I have interviewed a number of my peers, and discovered that to a man, they have all entered the field after a horrifying encounter with a lycanthrope of some variety. I am no exception.<BR>
<BR> 
In Skyrim, it is an old tradition to rub canis root on the trees surrounding your house as a ward against werebears. When I was young and stupid (as opposed, I guess, to being old and stupid as I am now), I always had hoped to meet a werebear to see if they were as impressive as legend suggested. I would follow strange tracks in the woods until they disappeared, with no fear or even thought about what I would do after I had found my quarry. By Thorig's beard, I was lucky that my investigations were fruitless.<BR>
<BR> 
When I did finally see a lycanthrope, it was not a werebear. It was a werewolf, the "common" lycanthope, which can be found in every part of Tamriel. My father was a priest and during the coldest part of the winter, he allowed the beggars and riffraff of Falcrenth to stay in the relative warmth of the cellar of his temple. We would even supply warm barley stew. My sisters and brothers and I actually enjoyed this bit of philanthropy, for in the cellars during the winter, it seemed there was a constant party. There were always travellers with interesting stories and eccentricities, and the atmosphere in the cellars was always light and friendly. Until that night.<BR>
<BR> 
By an established tradition, the beggars who were sick or wanted rest more than food and companionship would go to the cots at the farthest, darkest end of the cellar when they could be assured at least relative quiet. We were enjoying a song, and my sister Gethessa was dancing to the amusement of all. The song ended, but a chorus continued from the darkness at the far end of the cellar. As drunk and incomprehensible as most of the carolers were, it took a minute for us to realize that the sound we were hearing was not singing, but screaming.<BR>
<BR> 
No one was too concerned, for some of the older tramps often suffered from vivid nightmares. Nevertheless, one of father's priests went to silence the screamer and the moment he disappeared into the murk, we heard another sound. The snarl of a wolf. Then we heard the priest screaming as the original scream died off.<BR>
<BR> 
"Werewolf!" cried the old bard who had been leading the song. The cellar exploded into chaos.<BR>
<BR> 
I was pushed out the cellar door into the snow with the first wave of panic, but I could see that some of the more brave (or more drunk) hobos were rushing into the darkness to do battle with the lycanthrope. They were all, of course, almost instantly killed.<BR>
<BR> 
My father, upon hearing of his unwelcome visitor, sealed off the cellar after the last survivor of the carnage had left. A seasoned battlemage from the Falcrenth Mages Guild, who owed father a favor, went into the cellar and slew the beast.<BR>
<BR> 
"Not too tough," he said as he emerged, carrying the carcass with him. "Winter must have been tough on him too." Despite his bold words, the blood on his face and chest did not only come from his foe.<BR>
<BR> 
Werewolves do not revert to their human forms upon death, despite what legends will tell you. I had the opportunity to look at the monster's steaming body out in the snow before it was carried away to be burned. The teeth, clotted with the flesh of the beggars, were horrifying, but the claws shocked me even more. I have since seen live lycanthropes battle golems, atronachs, and other beings not harmed by mundane weapons, and concluded that they act as naturally enchanted weapons.<BR>
<BR> 
Because the werewolf is the most ubiquitous of lycanthropes, the term lycanthropy has been used since ancient days to describe the disease that transforms men into half-beast, although lycanthrope only strictly should refer to men who change into werewolves. But that is semantics. There are certainly differences between the seven documented forms of lycanthropy in Tamriel, but more similarities.<BR>
<BR> 
In Black Marsh and southern Morrowind, werecrocodiles stalk the swamps. Black Marsh also shares with the Imperial Province and the wetter parts of Elsweyr the vile presence of werelions. Valenwood's werevultures are not found in any other province. The wereboar has found both the climates of High Rock and Hammerfell amenable. As I mentioned before, the werebear is the most common lycanthrope in Skyrim, and is also found in the northern parts of High Rock, the Imperial Province, and Morrowind. The werewolf can be found in every province. The seventh lycanthrope, which I have never seen but my trusted peers have assured me exists, is a wereshark that roams the oceans around Tamriel.<BR>
<BR> 
I have spent my life categorizing and observing lycanthropes, but I sometimes feel that I am still a child trapped in a cellar in my attempts to understand them. I know, for example, that lycanthropy can be cured shortly after infection, but after that time, the victim is doomed. No one of my acquaintance has cured themselves after undergoing the first transformation. On the other hand, I have a colleague investigating a coven of witches in the Glenpoint foothills of High Rock who are rumored to have a cure. I remain dubious.<BR>
<BR> 
Perhaps it is because they are doomed that makes lycanthropes so aggressive. I have removed the contents of a werewolf's stomach and found more remnants of roots and berries than animal flesh. My conclusion is that they do not need to attack and devour humans to survive. Yet, for some reason they do. Does lycanthropy drive them mad, or do lycanthropes feel the need to spread the disease as a form of procreation? I do not know. I am not certain that any of us who are not lycanthropes ourselves will ever know. And then, of course, it's too late.<BR>
<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
论狼化症<BR>
瓦纳德·卡雷森 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
一个人是如何对研究狼化症这种疾病产生兴趣的呢？我采访过许多同行，发现他们无一例外，都是在与某种狼化生物发生过可怕遭遇后才进入这个领域的。我也不例外。<BR>
<BR>
在天际，有一个古老的传统，将卡尼斯根涂在房屋周围的树上，以抵御狼熊兽。当我年轻而愚蠢时（我想，这和我现在又老又蠢不同），我一直希望能遇到一只狼熊兽，看看它们是否像传说中那样令人印象深刻。我会跟着森林里奇怪的足迹，直到它们消失，既不害怕，甚至也不去想找到猎物后该怎么做。以索里格的胡子起誓，我的调查毫无结果真是幸运。<BR>
<BR>
当我最终真的看到一只狼化生物时，那不是狼熊兽。而是一只狼人，这种“普通”的狼化生物，在泰姆瑞尔的每个地方都能找到。我的父亲是一位祭司，在冬天最寒冷的时候，他允许佛克伦斯的乞丐和流氓们待在他神殿地窖相对温暖的地方。我们甚至会提供热的大麦炖菜。我和我的兄弟姐妹们实际上很喜欢这种慈善行为，因为在冬天，地窖里似乎总有不断的聚会。总有带着有趣故事和怪癖的旅行者，地窖里的气氛总是轻松友好的。直到那天晚上。<BR>
<BR>
根据惯例，那些生病或更想休息而不是食物和陪伴的乞丐，会去地窖最远、最暗的尽头的小床上，在那里他们至少能保证相对安静。我们正欣赏着一首歌，我的妹妹格塞莎正在跳舞，逗乐了所有人。歌声结束了，但地窖尽头的黑暗中仍传来一阵合唱声。由于大多数唱歌的人醉醺醺、口齿不清，我们花了一分钟才意识到，我们听到的声音不是唱歌，而是尖叫。<BR>
<BR>
没人太在意，因为一些年长的流浪汉常常做生动的噩梦。尽管如此，父亲的一位祭司还是去让那个尖叫者安静下来，就在他消失在黑暗中时，我们听到了另一个声音。狼的咆哮。然后我们听到了祭司的尖叫，而最初的尖叫声消失了。<BR>
<BR>
“狼人！”一直领唱的那位老吟游诗人喊道。地窖瞬间陷入一片混乱。<BR>
<BR>
在第一波恐慌中，我被推挤着穿过地窖门，跌入雪中，但我能看到一些更勇敢（或更醉）的流浪汉正冲进黑暗，与那只狼化生物搏斗。当然，他们几乎瞬间就全被杀了。<BR>
<BR>
我的父亲听说了他不受欢迎的访客后，在大屠杀的最后一名幸存者离开后，封住了地窖。一位欠父亲人情的佛克伦斯法师公会的老练战斗法师进入地窖，杀死了那头野兽。<BR>
<BR>
“不算太难，”他走出来时说道，手里拖着尸体。“看来冬天对他也够呛。”尽管他说得豪迈，但他脸上和胸口的血迹并不仅仅来自他的敌人。<BR>
<BR>
狼人死后并不会变回人形，不管传说怎么告诉你。我有机会在怪物的尸体被带走焚烧之前，在雪地里看了看它那冒着热气的尸体。那沾满乞丐血肉的牙齿令人毛骨悚然，但爪子更让我震惊。此后，我亲眼见过活的狼化生物与魔像、侍灵以及其他不受普通武器伤害的存在战斗，并得出结论：它们的爪子如同天生附魔的武器。<BR>
<BR>
由于狼人是狼化生物中最常见的，狼化症这个词自古以来就被用来描述将人变成半兽的疾病，尽管严格来说，狼化生物只应指变成狼人的人。但这只是语义学问题。泰姆瑞尔有记录的七种狼化症形式之间当然存在差异，但相似之处更多。<BR>
<BR>
在黑沼泽和晨风南部，狼鳄兽在沼泽中潜行。黑沼泽还与帝国行省和艾斯维尔较湿润的地区共同存在可恶的狼狮兽。瓦伦伍德的狼鹫兽在其他任何行省都没有。狼猪兽在高岩和落锤的气候中都能生存。正如我之前提到的，狼熊兽是天际最常见的狼化生物，在高岩北部、帝国行省和晨风也有发现。狼人则每个行省都有。第七种狼化生物，我从未见过，但我信任的同行向我保证它存在，是一种在泰姆瑞尔周围的海洋中游荡的狼鲨兽。<BR>
<BR>
我一生都在对狼化生物进行分类和观察，但有时我觉得，在试图理解它们方面，我仍然像是那个被困在地窖里的孩子。例如，我知道狼化症可以在感染后不久治愈，但过了那段时间，受害者就注定无法治愈了。我的熟人中没有人在经历第一次转变后治愈了自己。另一方面，我有一位同事正在调查高岩谷顶山麓的一个女巫集会，据说她们有治愈方法。我仍持怀疑态度。<BR>
<BR>
也许正是因为它们注定无法治愈，才使得狼化生物如此具有攻击性。我曾取出狼人胃里的内容物，发现根茎和浆果的残渣多于动物的肉。我的结论是，它们并不需要攻击和吞噬人类来生存。然而，出于某种原因，它们还是这么做了。是狼化症驱使它们疯狂，还是狼化生物觉得需要以繁殖的形式传播这种疾病？我不知道。我不确定我们这些不是狼化生物的人是否能够知道。当然，等到知道时，已经太晚了。<BR>
<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
On Lycanthropy<BR>
By Varnard Karessen<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
How does one become interested in studying the disease lycanthropy? I have interviewed a number of my peers, and discovered that to a man, they have all entered the field after a horrifying encounter with a lycanthrope of some variety. I am no exception.<BR><BR>
In Skyrim, it is an old tradition to rub canis root on the trees surrounding your house as a ward against werebears. When I was young and stupid (as opposed, I guess, to being old and stupid as I am now), I always had hoped to meet a werebear to see if they were as impressive as legend suggested. I would follow strange tracks in the woods until they disappeared, with no fear or even thought about what I would do after I had found my quarry. By Thorig's beard, I was lucky that my investigations were fruitless.<BR><BR>
When I did finally see a lycanthrope, it was not a werebear. It was a werewolf, the "common" lycanthope, which can be found in every part of Tamriel. My father was a priest and during the coldest part of the winter, he allowed the beggars and riffraff of Falcrenth to stay in the relative warmth of the cellar of his temple. We would even supply warm barley stew. My sisters and brothers and I actually enjoyed this bit of philanthropy, for in the cellars during the winter, it seemed there was a constant party. There were always travellers with interesting stories and eccentricities, and the atmosphere in the cellars was always light and friendly. Until that night.<BR><BR>
By an established tradition, the beggars who were sick or wanted rest more than food and companionship would go to the cots at the farthest, darkest end of the cellar when they could be assured at least relative quiet. We were enjoying a song, and my sister Gethessa was dancing to the amusement of all. The song ended, but a chorus continued from the darkness at the far end of the cellar. As drunk and incomprehensible as most of the carolers were, it took a minute for us to realize that the sound we were hearing was not singing, but screaming.<BR><BR>
No one was too concerned, for some of the older tramps often suffered from vivid nightmares. Nevertheless, one of father's priests went to silence the screamer and the moment he disappeared into the murk, we heard another sound. The snarl of a wolf. Then we heard the priest screaming as the original scream died off.<BR><BR>
"Werewolf!" cried the old bard who had been leading the song. The cellar exploded into chaos.<BR><BR>
I was pushed out the cellar door into the snow with the first wave of panic, but I could see that some of the more brave (or more drunk) hobos were rushing into the darkness to do battle with the lycanthrope. They were all, of course, almost instantly killed.<BR><BR>
My father, upon hearing of his unwelcome visitor, sealed off the cellar after the last survivor of the carnage had left. A seasoned battlemage from the Falcrenth Mages Guild, who owed father a favor, went into the cellar and slew the beast.<BR><BR>
"Not too tough," he said as he emerged, carrying the carcass with him. "Winter must have been tough on him too." Despite his bold words, the blood on his face and chest did not only come from his foe.<BR><BR>
Werewolves do not revert to their human forms upon death, despite what legends will tell you. I had the opportunity to look at the monster's steaming body out in the snow before it was carried away to be burned. The teeth, clotted with the flesh of the beggars, were horrifying, but the claws shocked me even more. I have since seen live lycanthropes battle golems, atronachs, and other beings not harmed by mundane weapons, and concluded that they act as naturally enchanted weapons.<BR><BR>
Because the werewolf is the most ubiquitous of lycanthropes, the term lycanthropy has been used since ancient days to describe the disease that transforms men into half-beast, although lycanthrope only strictly should refer to men who change into werewolves. But that is semantics. There are certainly differences between the seven documented forms of lycanthropy in Tamriel, but more similarities.<BR><BR>
In Black Marsh and southern Morrowind, werecrocodiles stalk the swamps. Black Marsh also shares with the Imperial Province and the wetter parts of Elsweyr the vile presence of werelions. Valenwood's werevultures are not found in any other province. The wereboar has found both the climates of High Rock and Hammerfell amenable. As I mentioned before, the werebear is the most common lycanthrope in Skyrim, and is also found in the northern parts of High Rock, the Imperial Province, and Morrowind. The werewolf can be found in every province. The seventh lycanthrope, which I have never seen but my trusted peers have assured me exists, is a wereshark that roams the oceans around Tamriel.<BR><BR>
I have spent my life categorizing and observing lycanthropes, but I sometimes feel that I am still a child trapped in a cellar in my attempts to understand them. I know, for example, that lycanthropy can be cured shortly after infection, but after that time, the victim is doomed. No one of my acquaintance has cured themselves after undergoing the first transformation. On the other hand, I have a colleague investigating a coven of witches in the Glenpoint foothills of High Rock who are rumored to have a cure. I remain dubious.<BR><BR>
Perhaps it is because they are doomed that makes lycanthropes so aggressive. I have removed the contents of a werewolf's stomach and found more remnants of roots and berries than animal flesh. My conclusion is that they do not need to attack and devour humans to survive. Yet, for some reason they do. Does lycanthropy drive them mad, or do lycanthropes feel the need to spread the disease as a form of procreation? I do not know. I am not certain that any of us who are not lycanthropes ourselves will ever know. And then, of course, it's too late.<BR>"""

On Necromancy
论死灵法术

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
Reanimation should not be taken lightly. Costs, both mundane and spiritual, can be very high. Intent is everything. Too much emotion may create a creature so consumed with anger and hate its every action is perverted by its pain. Too little creates a mindless husk with little more than the ability to follow the simplest of commands. A calm mind, its thoughts well-organized and its plans well-considered, is the most necessary ingredient for animating the dead.<BR>

<BR>

The soul is necessary, of course, as are many other ingredients listed at the end of this chapter. But as to the body ... take caution. Any corpse may be reanimated, regardless of age or state of decay, but the most useful are those that are mostly intact (or can be made intact with little effort). A whole skeleton is better than a fresh, but mutilated, body.<BR>

<BR>

As to freshness, be careful in this consideration as well. Have you ever wondered why there are so many skeletons among the reanimated undead, fewer zombies, and only a scant few revenants? The longer a body remains inanimate, the less hold its original owner has on the corpse. A spirit can stay tied to its remains for days, weeks, or even years--the shorter the time, the more likely the spiritual umbilicus exists.<BR>

<BR>

A wise necromancer does not wish to fight for control of his creation with an angry spirit seeking a way back into the world. Best to be certain all of a creature's soul has departed before reanimation begins. Even should the necromancer win the battle, it is a cruel victory, tormenting a spirit on its way to rest.<BR>

<BR>

Raising the dead so recent that the soul has not yet fled is ill-advised, as true resurrection is not the purview of the necromancer, but something best left to gods and priests.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
复生不应草率为之。物质和精神上的代价都可能非常高昂。意图至关重要。情感过强可能会创造出一个被愤怒和仇恨吞噬的生物，其每一次行动都因痛苦而扭曲。情感过少则会创造出一个没有思想的躯壳，只能执行最简单的命令。冷静的头脑、条理清晰的思想和深思熟虑的计划，是赋予死者活力最必要的成分。<BR>

<BR>

灵魂当然是必要的，本章末尾列出的许多其他成分也是如此。但至于尸体......需谨慎。任何尸体都可以被复活，无论其年代或腐烂程度如何，但最有用的是那些大部分完好无损（或稍加努力即可完好）的尸体。一具完整的骷髅比一具新鲜但残缺的尸体更好。<BR>

<BR>

至于新鲜度，在这方面也要小心。你是否曾想过，为什么复活的亡灵中骷髅那么多，僵尸较少，而归来之魂只有极少数？尸体保持无生命状态的时间越长，其原主人对尸体的控制力就越弱。灵魂可能会与其遗骸相连数天、数周甚至数年 -- 时间越短，精神脐带存在的可能性就越大。<BR>

<BR>

明智的死灵法师不希望与一个渴望重返世界的愤怒灵魂争夺对其造物的控制权。最好在开始复生之前，确保生物的灵魂已全部离去。即使死灵法师赢得了这场战斗，那也是一场残酷的胜利，折磨着一个正在前往安息之地的灵魂。<BR>

<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
On Purity<BR>
by Nonesirmi of Dusk<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Purity, as we Altmer understand it, is often object to incoherent interpretation. Even some Altmer, particularly those of the lower castes, are not immune to it, as they eschew anything not manufactured or thought about on the Altmeri Isles as a symptom of inherent, contagious decay.<BR>
<BR>
Purity in its original context would be best understood as Immaculate Degradation, that is a clear and uninterrupted line between our ancestors, our lesser ancestors, and ourselves, which allows us to stay detached from our prison in the mortal Mundus. In this context, impurity refers to races or beings who have stepped aside from the path of our ancestors and tied themselves with deeds, heritage, or magicka to the Mundus, Aetherius, or Oblivion.<BR>
<BR>
The first thought spent by an Altmer when a given discussion turns to the topic of Purity are the Betmer, specifically the Goblins, Sload, and the Imga, if they are not wholely discarded as unrelated to common ancestral descent. Emphasizing abstract ends of the Betmer impurities, the Sload are beings of incomprehensible malice without understandable purpose. The Imga in turn are horrifying caricatures of beings wishing to partake in a traditional Aldmeri lifestyle, yet being unable to understand the difference between form and function, or that there is even such a difference in the first place. The Goblins meanwhile, little better than beasts, are seen as malleable students and soldiers, albeit at a marginal level.<BR>
<BR>
Betmer as a whole are pitied, as they are incapable of grasping the whole they have lost. That some of them, most notably the Khajiit, sometimes take near-elven form is seen as one of Lorkhan's most abominable mockeries and does not fail to invoke revulsion in Altmeri scholars who have started to properly understand Purity and the Lunar Lattice.<BR>
<BR>
The second thought would of course refer to the Septimian Empire, that is the assumption of rulership of Men over Mer while keeping the trappings of inherited Merish rulership. Men in general are derided, as their ancestors fell to and upheld Lorkhan's lie. When the Aldmer first encountered tribes of Men, they had been wholly changed into beings who accepted their degradation as purposeful, that is they reveled in mortal limitations and relished in their own suffering and death. What the Aldmer saw in themselves, they found as a grotesque caricatural opposite Other, from philosophical differences down to ancestor-defined feudal states facing incarnation-defined meritocratic tribes.<BR>
<BR>
The different groups often blend into one another, and it is rare to encounter a proper Altmeri scholar who understands the subtle differences between the alien views of the Redguards, the Nibenese who see themselves as inheritors of the Ayleids, the Imga-like corruption of proper Aldmeri traits by the Bretons, or the Reachmen who would be more amenable to Merish rulership than that of the Septims.<BR>
<BR>
The third thought, the splintering of the Aldmeri as a coherent definition, is more difficult to understand for Altmer. As is customary for someone wronged, there is always the assumed motive of malice instead of genuine disagreement or circumstances. In the proper, scholarly view, Merish splinters can be grouped into three distinct periods: Aedric and feudal corruptions, philosophical corruptions, and Daedric corruptions.<BR>
<BR>
The earliest and most influential split was a feudal disagreement during or shortly after the evacuation of Aldmeris between the Aldmeri High Council and the war admiral Orgnum. It only became an Aedric split when he tied himself and his followers to the storms and serpents of the Pyandonean Isles. These particular concepts are so old that their names have been forgotten and their purpose invariably misunderstood, that is reinterpreted into Orgnum's eternal campaigns against the Altmeri Isles.<BR>
<BR>
The fabled "Left-Handed Elves" are perhaps another splinter group that fled from Aldmeris while traversing a different path. They are incoherent in their heritage so it is unclear at this point if they were Aldmeri at all or merely a reinterpretation by the descendants of the Ra Gada, deciding during a time of open conflict between Men and Mer after arriving on Tamriel, that their historical enemies must have been akin to the enemies their neighbours were enamored by.<BR>
<BR>
The Bosmer and Falmer, our most dear cousins, did not deliberately fall into Aedric corruption, and instead were forced into it. They set foot on the continent of Tamriel before its schismatic wholeness had sufficiently settled to be habitable and as such found themselves unsharpened, that is of unclear and shifting form. The Bosmer were forced to tie themselves to the walking folk of Valenwood as the Falmer tied themselves to the frozen memories of Skyrim.<BR>
<BR>
It was only with the rise and fall of the Aldmeri Dominion that the Bosmer were recognized as almost-like-us in reason and thought. The subsequent conquest by the Septimian Empire only hastened the process, as surviving members of the Thalmor have gone into hiding and spread a narrative of unified Merish resistance against Imperial aggression into the ears of a new generation.<BR>
<BR>
More difficult to understand conceptually are the philosophical corruptions. The Direnni may stand as a group of Aldmer who, while overly fond of numerological use of magicka, stayed and still are recognizably like us. Two other groups stand out as their opposite.<BR>
<BR>
The Ayleids found themselves envious of Lorkhan's grotesque deed and threw themselves wholly into voluntary Daedric and Aetherial corruption in sincere imitation of the Great Lie, that is they assumed responsibility to finish the creation of a mortal world to their liking in miniature while liberally invoking Daedra and Magna-Ge for ascendancy and debauchery.<BR>
<BR>
The Dwemer understood Immaculate Degradation to be an intellectually suffocating concept benefiting the Earthbones, that is they believed that by knowing too much about the Mundus the Aldmer could not properly misinterpret it, which prevented further learning. As an exclusive view it was seen as inherently destructive by Aldmeri society, and it is recognized as a fitting, if devastating, conclusion that the next time anything of the Dwemer set foot on the Isles occurred when the Anumidium destroyed millennia of our self-rule at the behest of Tiber Septim and a gift freely given by Vivec.<BR>
<BR>
The last, and most devastating, impurity are Daedric corruptions, that is corruptions by those who are not involved in our ancestry and as such are immutably alien and unwanted in Altmeri affairs. The assimilation of the incarnate Trinimac into the Daedric Boethiah, the exodus of the Velothian tribes, and the corruption of Trinimac's descendants into the Orsimer merely as afterproduct of Boethiah's eupepsy are well-known tales. At this point, Immaculate Degradation became a reason for itself, and we Altmer became ourselves as the conclusion was redefined into one new, wholesome status, suitably detached from anything that might add or remove from it, immutable and pristine.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
论纯粹<BR>
暮光之诺内西尔米 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
纯粹，正如我们傲特莫所理解的，常常遭到前后矛盾的解释。甚至一些傲特莫，特别是那些低阶层的，也未能幸免，他们避开任何不是在夏暮群岛上制造或思考的东西，视之为内在的、可传染的衰败症状。<BR>
<BR>
纯粹在其原始语境下，最好被理解为无瑕的退变，即我们祖先、我们次要祖先与我们自身之间一条清晰而连续不断的脉络，这使我们能够与我们在凡俗梦达斯中的牢笼保持分离。在此语境下，不纯指的是那些偏离了祖先之道，并以行为、血统或魔能将自己与梦达斯、光界或湮灭联系在一起的种族或存在。<BR>
<BR>
当讨论转向纯粹主题时，傲特莫首先想到的是贝特莫，特别是哥布林、斯洛德和因加，如果他们没有被完全视为与共同祖先血统无关而抛弃的话。强调贝特莫不纯的抽象目的，斯洛德是怀有无法理解的恶意的存在，其目的无法理解。因加则是渴望参与传统奥德莫生活方式，却无法理解形式与功能之间的区别，甚至从一开始就不知道存在这种区别的存在，是可怕的漫画式形象。与此同时，哥布林比野兽好不了多少，被视为可塑的学生和士兵，尽管水平很低。<BR>
<BR>
贝特莫作为一个整体受到怜悯，因为他们无法理解自己已经失去的整体。他们中的一些，最著名的是卡吉特，有时呈现出近似精灵的形态，这被视为洛克汗最可恶的嘲弄之一，并且不可避免地引起了那些开始正确理解纯粹和月之栅栏的傲特莫学者的反感。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
不同的群体常常相互融合，很难遇到一个真正理解红卫人异己观点、尼本人自视为亚历德继承者、布莱顿人对正统奥德莫特质的因加式腐化，或是比塞普汀统治更倾向于精灵统治的河峪人之间细微差别的合格傲特莫学者。<BR>
<BR>
第三个想法，即奥德莫作为一个连贯定义的碎裂，对傲特莫来说更难理解。正如受委屈者的惯例，总是假设对方有恶意的动机，而不是真正的分歧或情况。在正确的学术观点中，精灵的分裂可以归纳为三个不同的时期：艾德拉与封建腐化、哲学腐化，以及迪德拉腐化。<BR>
<BR>
最早且最具影响力的分裂是奥德莫高级议会与战争海军上将奥格努姆之间在撤离奥德莫瑞斯期间或之后不久发生的封建分歧。直到他将自己和追随者与派安多尼亚群岛的风暴和巨蛇联系在一起，这才演变成艾德拉式的分裂。这些特定的概念是如此古老，它们的名字已被遗忘，其目的也总被误解，即被重新解释为奥格努姆对夏暮群岛的永恒征战。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
波斯莫和伐莫，我们最亲爱的表亲，并非故意陷入艾德拉式的腐化，而是被迫如此。他们在泰姆瑞尔大陆分裂后的整体尚未充分稳定到适合居住之时就踏上了这片大陆，因此发现自己处于“未定型”状态，即形态模糊且变化不定。波斯莫被迫将自己与瓦伦伍德的行走者联系在一起，正如伐莫将自己与天际的冰冻记忆联系在一起一样。<BR>
<BR>
直到先祖神洲的兴衰，波斯莫才在理性和思想上被承认为几乎与我们相似。随后塞普汀帝国的征服只是加速了这一进程，因为梭默的幸存者已转入地下，并将一个精灵联合抵抗帝国侵略的叙事传播到新一代的耳中。<BR>
<BR>
在概念上更难理解的是哲学腐化。迪伦尼可能代表了一群奥德莫，尽管他们过分热衷于魔能的命理学运用，但仍然保持并且至今仍可识别地与我们相似。另外两个群体则作为他们的对立面而突出。<BR>
<BR>
亚历德发现自己嫉妒洛克汗的怪诞行为，并全身心地投入到自愿的迪德拉和光界腐化中，真诚地模仿那个大谎言，也就是说，他们承担起按照自己的喜好完成一个微小凡俗世界创造的责任，同时大肆召唤迪德拉和玛格纳-吉以求升迁和放纵。<BR>
<BR>
锻莫将无瑕的退变理解为一个在智力上令人窒息、有利于地骨的概念，也就是说，他们相信，奥德莫对梦达斯了解太多，以至于无法正确地误解它，这阻碍了进一步的学习。作为一种排他性的观点，它被奥德莫社会视为具有内在破坏性，人们认为，下一次锻莫的任何东西踏上群岛，就是当阿努米迪文在泰伯·塞普汀的命令下和维威克无偿赠予的礼物摧毁了我们数千年自治之时，这是一个恰当且毁灭性的结局。<BR>
<BR>
最后，也是最具破坏性的不纯，是迪德拉腐化，即那些与我们的血统无关的存在所造成的腐化，因此在傲特莫的事务中，他们是永恒的外来者，不受欢迎。关于歧莫人民的腐化，已有许多著述，常常理解得过于字面。化身崔尼马克融入迪德拉波耶西亚、维洛斯部落的出埃及记，以及崔尼马克的后代腐化为奥斯莫，仅仅是波耶西亚消化良好的副产品，这些都是众所周知的故事。歧莫人民后来通过选择他们自己的化身神而非祖先来统治他们，从而第二次将自己与他们的奥德莫祖先隔离开来 -- 这一壮举，一些人担心塞普汀帝国正试图通过其新兴的英雄神塔洛斯血统崇拜来效仿，但这并不重要。<BR>
<BR>
然而，正是在这一点上，由于适当的祖先脱离的出现，即傲特莫拒绝像奥斯莫那样将自己与祖先精神紧密联系在一起，因为害怕类似的事迹重演，对奥德莫和傲特莫进行适当区分才成为可能。在这一点上，无瑕的退变成了自身的目的，而我们傲特莫成为了我们自己，因为结论被重新定义为一个新的、完整的地位，适当地脱离任何可能增加或减少它的东西，永恒不变，原始纯净。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
ON SERICULTURE<BR>
<BR>
Regarding the Proper Care of Moths, and Production of Pure Silks according to the ancient Precepts of Nibennum<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
by Cyso Mesorath<BR>
<BR>
To make silk is not the action of spinning a thread, caring for a worm, or weaving a cloak. To make silk is an act of piety, an invocation to the Ancestors, a sign of respect to the Divines, and a communion to the fjyron of moth. The cloak you wear is no dead and empty yarn, but a song unwound, receptive to the inner world. Therefore, when practicing the noble art of sericulture and the weaving of silks, one must heed the words of the master, and not stray from the path of ceremony and tradition, lest the thread you spin is abominable. In this text, I, Siso of the clan Mesorath, have gathered the words and wisdom of the hermits, that it may be a guide to the initiate.<BR>
<BR>
These are the spirits of Moth as may be known by the initiate.<BR>
<BR>
The Gypsy-Moth<BR>
The lowest and most common of the spirits, prone to wander. The lesser spirits are many, and it is not demanded to record lineage. The Gypsy feeds on offal and bonemeal, but avoids the remnants of man or bull. Their silk is coarse and strong, ill-suited for dyes and precise work. Their issue is used to make simple cloth for the common man and his industries. It may be made into sailor-silk, which is good for sails and ropes. The Gypsy-Moth cannot hold the fjyron of man or beast, and to boil the worm in extraction is no misdeed, provided one speaks the proper mantra.<BR>
<BR>
The Sphinx-Moth<BR>
A good and obedient spirit. The Sphinx is loyal, but ignorant of its station. It is demanded to name and record first-born, so that the spirit is pleased - if not, the thread may be warped. The Sphinx will feed on the remnants of beasts, and prefers domesticated over those of the jungle. Its issue is fine and pliant, and takes well to bright and pleasing dyes, but is ill-suited to use or the arts. The Sphinx may hold the fjyron of simple beasts, and is valued by the Totem Societies. It is demanded that the first-born be extracted with care, and live. Others of a brood may be boiled, provided one speaks the proper mantra.<BR>
<BR>
The Glyph-Moth<BR>
An unruly and arrogant spirit. The Glyph recoils from the cadaver, and feeds on the written word: book, scroll and text. Superior cloth may be created by providing a careful selection of culturally superior and beneficial literature, like the Imperial codici. It is not demanded to record lineage, for this family has good memory of its own. The Glyph-Moth is a dangerous and rebellious spirit, and discipline must be maintained. Its silk is coarse and brittle, difficult to use, but holds great potential for arts and, when used in paper, may make magical scrolls of great power.<BR>
<BR>
The Luna-Moth<BR>
A rare and pious spirit, that has dedicated itself to the Divine Dibella. The Luna is transformed in devotion, so that it has no mouth or digestive organs. Thus, it exist only to copulate, then perish of starvation. In this, it honors the Divine Dibella greatly. The silk of the Luna is to be used in sacred vestments and the bedsheets of newlyweds. The Luna is to be cultivated by priests and honorables of the Orders, and as such, is often mistreated as these are ignorant. Yet try to record lineage, for thread may be warped.<BR>
<BR>
The Ancestor-Moth<BR>
Greatest and most powerful of the spirits of Moth, the Ancestor-moth is the willing carrier of the fjyron of mankind. It is required to record proper lineage in all cases. The Ancestor-Moth may only feed on the bodies of mortals, and, in consuming their flesh, will absorb the fjyron, the will to peace, of the deceased and the continuum of ancestors. The silk of the Ancestor-Moth holds dyes of all kinds most excellently, and it is well-suited to even the most ambitious applications of the arts - there is no enchantment it cannot hold. This silk may only be used in the creation of Ancestor-Cloth, which, by transcribing the proper lineage, may then become a focal point of the fjyron of one's ancestors, who will aid and abet the wearer. To use the issue of the Ancestor-Moth for any other purpose is an abomination. Furthermore, the worm may not be boiled or harmed in any way, and the silk must be harvested by hand, with great care, by unspooling the cocoons. This can be accomplished by the proper mantras, and the usage of soothing alchemicals, and proper encouragement for the nascent moth. <BR>
<BR>

斯芬克斯蛾<BR>

<BR>
雕文蛾<BR>
难以管束且傲慢的灵性。雕文蛾回避尸体，以文字为食：书籍、卷轴和文本。通过精心挑选文化优越且有益的文学作品，如帝国法典，可以创造出高级布料。无需记录谱系，因为这个家族自身记忆良好。雕文蛾是一种危险而叛逆的灵性，必须保持纪律。其丝粗糙而脆，难以使用，但在艺术方面潜力巨大，用于造纸时，可能制造出强大的魔法卷轴。<BR>
<BR>
月蛾<BR>

先祖蛾<BR>

On the Definition of Heresy<BR>
By Indoril Beroth<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The teachings of Saint Olms are among the earliest to delve into the dangers of heretical thinking. In writing them, he planted seeds for his successors to tend - seeds that would aid in cultivating the very garden of thought that we tend today. But when I contemplate the teachings of Saint Olms as of late, I find that I cannot help but be troubled by the assertions of those Temple scholars named Golsu Farelas and Ulmelyn Llaryn. Their writings have created an unspoken rift among their peers, and in doing so they have attracted the attention of the Ordination. It is clear that they mean well, and that they write in the spirit of understanding, but the arguments they make are in dire need of contextualization within the strictures of Determined Law. This is a book for both the layman and the scholar; it will give an explanation of the Laws Determined as well as the Laws Ordained, and seek to reconcile the worldviews of these two authors into one harmonious union.<BR>
<BR>
Heresy is not itself a violation of the Laws Determined. That would be impossible, for what is determined by the Tribunal may not be undetermined. It is, however, a violation of the Laws Ordained, which have been established by word and deed in the mundial world, rather than celestial triune decree beyond it. These laws are enforced and protected by the blessed House Indoril, the sacred Ordination and the glorious Temple of our Tribunal. They are breakable, and it is the moral duty of every Velothi to preserve them. To do otherwise, then, would be the simplest definition of heresy.<BR>
<BR>
Ultimately, nothing is truly beyond the will of the Tribunal. Everything which occurs, whether it is in the mundial world or beyond, follows the principles of the Laws Determined. The Laws Ordained, and the heresies that test them, both fall within the scope of this all-encompassing metajurisdiction. There is no extant form of heresy that may threaten the Laws Determined because, as has been established, what has been determined by the Tribunal may not be undetermined.<BR>
<BR>
And why should they? ALMSIVI sees farther than mortals and spirits both - they gaze across the span of eternity, reading and applying it in their way. There is no room for mistakes, no need for changes, when one sees in such a state as they. Would it then be fair to say that heresy is important? Certainly, for if it were not then the Tribunal would not have created the circumstances by which it exists. Would it then be fair to say that heresy is evil? Certainly, for if it were not then it would not be in violation of the Laws Ordained.<BR>
<BR>
One may contemplate or argue as to why this is the case, attempting to understand the will of the Three to the best of their ability, but to do so is of secondary importance. Of primary importance is reconciling these two realities within the greater scheme of what has been determined for us, and moving forward with the understanding that they are both true. There will come a time when heresy no longer exists, when what is ordained reigns true across all the garden of Resdayn, and when that time comes the Velothi will be all the more grateful for the work that is done in the garden today.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
论异端之定义<BR>
因多瑞尔·贝罗斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
圣奥姆斯的教诲是最早深入探讨异端思维危险的著作之一。在写下这些教诲时，他为后继者播下了需要照料的种子 -- 这些种子有助于培育我们今天仍在耕耘的思想花园。但当我最近思考圣奥姆斯的教诲时，我发现我不禁对神殿学者戈尔苏·法雷拉斯和乌尔梅林·拉林的论断感到困扰。他们的著作在同僚中制造了无形的裂痕，并因此引起了圣职团的注意。很明显，他们用意良好，并且是本着理解的精神写作，但他们提出的论点迫切需要在天定法的严格框架内进行语境化。这是一本既面向外行也面向学者的书；它将解释天定法和圣定法，并寻求将这两位作者的世界观调和成一个和谐的整体。<BR>
<BR>
异端本身并不违反天定法。那是不可能的，因为审判席所决定之事不可被否决。然而，它违反了圣定法，圣定法是通过言语和行为在尘世世界中确立的，而非通过超越其上的神圣三位一体法令。这些法律由受祝福的因多瑞尔家族、神圣的圣职团以及我们审判席的光荣神殿来执行和保护。它们是可以被打破的，而维护它们是每一位维洛提人的道德责任。反之，便是异端最简单的定义。<BR>
<BR>
最终，没有什么能真正超越审判席的意志。发生的一切，无论是在尘世世界还是超越其外，都遵循天定法的原则。圣定法，以及考验它们的异端，都落在这个包罗万象的元法域的范围之内。不存在任何现存的异端形式能够威胁天定法，因为正如已经确立的，审判席所决定之事不可被否决。<BR>
<BR>
它们又为何要威胁？奥姆希维比凡人和精灵都看得更远 -- 他们凝视永恒的范围，以自己的方式解读和运用它。当一个人处于他们那样的境界时，没有犯错的余地，也没有改变的必要。那么，说异端是重要的，公平吗？当然，因为若非如此，审判席就不会创造它得以存在的情况。那么，说异端是邪恶的，公平吗？当然，因为若非如此，它就不会违反圣定法。<BR>
<BR>

The Autobiography of an Orc Volume III<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>

我写下这些，以便他人学习。他们以为我们是金色精灵，所以我们的信仰也像金色精灵。我们看起来像金色精灵吗？我握着这支笔的是巨大、强壮、绿色的手，但这手更适合握成拳头！我想这足以说明相反的情况，对吧？但我的族人却对帝国人卑躬屈膝，锉短自己的獠牙，以免在弯腰亲吻将军妻子手时刺伤她们，而且不再保留被弃之民的古老神话，而这都要怪戈特沃格。他甚至抛弃了马拉卡，转而崇拜他曾经的自己 -- 崔尼马克。但暗夜社幸存下来，用迷失在自己城市中的弱者和蠢人的鲜血，写下对马拉卡的誓言。所以，我将写下我们从神王马拉卡那里学到的东西。
<BR>
<BR>
起初，有一头巨大的野兽在宁静中吃草。那是什么野兽、在吃什么并不重要，但确有野兽，且它确实在吃草。但后来它没有足够的东西可吃，于是它吃掉了自己，这很傻，因为它死了。现在野兽腐烂了，众所周知，腐烂的肉会生出东西，比如跳蚤、苍蝇和其他类似的害虫。由于肉很肥美，这些害虫变成了金色的牛虻和镀金的跳蚤，它们在这片丰饶之地上吃啊吃，有时甚至互相吞噬，它们的粪便与腐肉混合，变得非常混乱，直到一只食腐蜥蜴诞生。蜥蜴说：“停止你们的吃相！你们太没规矩了！你们所有人将有早餐、午餐和晚餐，这样混乱的吃法就会被制止。”问题就解决了。
<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
<BR>正如你所见，我们不喜欢圣甲虫。他是个粪**。圣甲虫不同意事情被解决的方式，于是他把一些粪便滚成一团，就像圣甲虫常做的那样，他滚啊滚，滚啊滚，直到它变成一个巨大的球，然后他直接把这个球滚回了死肉世界。

<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

<BR>与此同时，崔尼马克穿过诡计之王肠道的黏滑迷宫，肉质的墙壁在黑暗中挤压着他前进。在博索格的肠道里没有时间流泪，很快崔尼马克就在一个盲目的拐弯处迷失了自己，所有的呜咽和甜美都被消化，并从博索格两个臭洞中较小的那个呕吐出来，但正是作为马拉卡，他看到了通道尽头的亮光，如同根基中的一颗璀璨明星，为适应他的第二次诞生而重新命名。
<BR>
<BR>当博索格排泄出他的食物后，崔尼马克的追随者们撕裂了自己的长袍，哀嚎着，并将粪便涂抹在自己裸露的胸膛上。但随后他们听到从那堆污秽中传来一个尖叫声，它说：“停止像猪一样在粪便中打滚，别挡着我的阳光，你们这些愚蠢的**。”
<BR>
<BR>
崔尼马克的追随者们对此深感困惑，在粪泪中询问是谁这样对他们说话。
<BR>
<BR>
“如同埋藏在粪球深处的铁，你们找到了你们的神。擦干眼泪，因为正确的回应是诅咒。你们长有獠牙和吻部的形态揭示了这一点，从今往后，除了向上，别无他途。”
<BR>
<BR>我们看到，我们被改变了，就像我们的神一样，而这是真的。
<BR>

<BR>“现在你明白了，在泔水中也能找到珍珠。你以为你来自金色的牛虻，但那不过是愚人之金，像铜一样柔软。但现在你们已被提升为铁；坚韧、强壮且有弹性。你们是我偏爱的孩子，是第一个听到你们神祇啼哭的，他是粪与肉的新二元体，是净化的双重受胎，而在我身上代表了如来藏，这实际上是一个令人厌恶的混蛋，就像我一样。”
<BR>
<BR>
最后一部分我们不明白，因为它歪曲且是神语，但那时我们浑身是粪，所有新事物让我们感觉有点晕乎乎的，仿佛我们不是找到了马拉卡，而是刚刚发现并吃了那里生长的一种蘑菇，是我们萨满喜欢的那种，能带来神圣的幻象，也因此是我们与他立约的标志。马拉卡接着教了我们很多东西，让我们变得强大，给了我们诅咒和誓言，让我们对着敌人尖叫，以及更能描述他们的残酷词语，这些词语会在敌人的内脏中扭曲，驱使他们陷入疯狂的仇恨与愤怒。
<BR>
<BR>这就是真相，如果你不相信这一切，愿你的屁眼脱落并与你憎恨的邻居私通。并且诅咒戈特沃格，他不再是铁之民，而是生铁之民，愿他的宫殿倒塌在他身上，挤出他的内脏，在他身边形成他的孪生兄弟，因为我相信应该表现出一些怜悯，他应该在最后的日子里有人陪伴。

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR> Being a complete listing of the Fauna of Tamriel, with truthful description, assembled from the reports of sundry Savants, Naturalists, Mystics &c from across the breadth of the Empire.
<BR>
<BR><FONT COLOR="821E00" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">The Dreugh
<BR><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
Common parlance necessitates the inclusion of the Dreugh in this bestiary, but its place here among the baser creatures of lakes and oceans is otherwise wholly unwarranted. Pearl divers, shipwreck survivors and many others who make their living by the water will speak to their sapience. Indeed, tales of their deep water palaces come to us from all the known oceans, suggesting their civilization is in few ways inferior to those of the terrestrial denizens of Tamriel. This fact is the basis of a long-standing theory that the Dreugh are survivors from some unknown earlier age of the world, though much reduced in power. Whatever the truth of it, the Dreugh are reclusive and their aquatic habitat means few can follow where they go. Perhaps the catastrophe that separates their epoch of glory from our own taught them the simple virtue of remaining as unfathomable as the waters that are their home.<BR>
<BR><FONT COLOR="821E00" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">The Wormmouth
<BR><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
Vicious bipedal lizard-monsters that roam the rugged wilderness of the High Rock-Skyrim borderlands, Wormmouths are characterized by their insatiable drive to rend flesh with their massive filth-spewing jaws. Known for breeding surprisingly fast given their large size, Nord tradition attributes their origin to the maggots that feasted on the corpse of their Chief-God, Shor. The Witchmen warriors of High Rock commonly don armor stitched together from their thick hides.<BR>
<BR><FONT COLOR="821E00" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">The Hare or Ground Racer
<BR><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
Portents of shifting luck that trace and inhabit the warrens of Nirn. Hares can change sex at will, though only when they reach adult age. They breed so confusingly fast that females among a litter are said to sometimes give birth while still in the mother's womb. Depending on its gender when caught, hare flesh is accordingly used to treat barren women or seedless men. Hares are associated with deception and cunning, and Wood Elf sorcerers are said to favor their form as a disguise when traveling incognito through the lands of Men.<BR>
<BR><FONT COLOR="821E00" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">The Snow Whale
<BR><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
Much is written in Nordic lore of the snow whales, majestic beings that live among the highest mountain peaks and freely move through air, snow and ice as if swimming through water. Childrens' stories portray snow whales as the singers of clouds, and claim that their emanations are the cause of all the joy in the world. This is why Nords and children alike grow cheerful in the snow, and celebrate the cold weather even as it obstructs their paths and endangers their crops.<BR>
<BR><FONT COLOR="821E00" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">The Moth
<BR><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
There are many kinds of moths to be found in Tamriel, but all are derived from the Luna Moth, which migrates annually between Nirn and its moons in swarms of a million or more and in so doing marks out the safe aurbic currents used by travelers and mystics. In more recent times the moth has become a symbol of the Empire, the Legion and of the Elder Council. They have a relationship with the dead (hence the Cult of the Ancestor Moth), but the nature of this connection remains a secret to the uninitiated. They are not indigenous to our world, but can be found in Skyrim, Cyrodiil and High Rock. Their migrating swarms sometimes attempt to reach Morrowind, but they are killed by the ash cloud of Red Mountain and fall to the ground like countless autumn leaves.<BR>

Trinimac, satisfied with his revenge, withdrew from the place, going to prepare for another battle.<BR><BR>

I do not know of this secret, but perhaps another does.<BR>"""

来到我们哈芬加城的旅行者常常会遇到一些奇怪的野兽，它们在帝国的任何其他行省都没有类似的物种。拉基，我们这样称呼它，比普通的哈芬海姆灰狼稍小，是一种善于欺骗的生物。白天，它通常被发现睡在西境广阔松林的树冠下。它有着柔软的白色皮毛、大眼睛和轻柔的咕咕声，人们会认为它是妻子的完美宠物。然而，一旦黑暗降临我们的土地，拉基就会释放出一种仿佛被山屁毛洛克附身般的狂怒。它非常敏捷，可以轻松跳过最高的傲特莫，并通过从背后攻击猎物来迅速解决战斗。如果你发现自己面对这些生物，持续的警觉和快速的反应绝对是至关重要的，这一点怎么强调都不为过。<BR>
<BR>
早在第三纪元110年，独孤城的狼心女王波特玛接待了派安多尼亚的奥格努姆国王的来访，密谋对付她的兄弟安条克。随行人员中有一批我们现在称之为拉基的生物，作为外交礼物，还有两名锚莫驯养员。在一次狩猎中，一群拉基将年轻的尤利尔三世从一头受伤但狂暴的野猪的愤怒中救下，展示了这些野兽的用处，波特玛从此迷上了它们，从那以后，这些野兽跟着她走遍了独孤城城堡。<BR>
<BR>
任何塞普汀帝国的公民都会告诉你，波特玛在独孤城的统治臭名昭著，充满了对臣民的恐吓和压迫，随着红钻战争的爆发，她的残忍更是变本加厉。有传言说，她将囚犯切成片，用来喂她的宠物拉基。这类故事传遍了利尔莫斯国王马格努斯的营地，让黑沼泽明珠著名的阿尔贡长矛兵心中充满了恐惧。<BR>
<BR>
然而，狼心女王的早期战术胜利是短暂的，到了137年，红钻战争结束，利尔莫斯和西罗德的胜利军队肩负着恢复哈芬海姆昔日荣耀的任务。但女王那些臭名昭著的宠物后来怎么样了？根据哈芬海姆的史卡尔德人流传的传说，在独孤城城堡陷落后的混乱中，拉基背叛了它们的锚莫驯养员，通过波特玛房间的一扇窄窗逃出城堡，跳进护城河，游到了岸边。在接下来的几十年里，拉基交配繁殖，直到今天，它们对那些跋涉到我们美丽城市的人来说，仍然是一个始终存在的危险。<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>by Vantis Orvilius<BR>

<FONT COLOR="003300" >Tarei, ex-Legionary, The Reach<BR>

When my brother inherited the family farm, there was nowhere for me to go. So I joined the Legion, like many a likely lad. When our ancestors first came to Resdayn, it was at the end of a long and painful journey. The land they found themselves in was harsh, yes, but it was paradise for those wearied by wandering. <BR>

<BR>

<FONT COLOR="003300" >Sola Shaxhaal, Cultist, Bravil<BR>

All across my arms and legs you see the golden coils of the serpent, its head against my belly to speak wisdom to any child I might bear. It is my face that people notice, though. The writing is Akaviri, and no, I will not tell you what it means. All cults must have their secrets, no?
<BR>
Foreigners who are used to the stern, plain Colovians of the Legion are surprised when they see me with my tattoos and my cloak of bells, but In the green lands of the Niben we delight in announcing ourselves, and making a scene. Every faith and cult and personal superstition is a work of art, and we wear our faiths on our sleeve for all to see, in a riot of color and form. Nibenay is the most beautiful land in the Empire, the beating heart of Tamriel, and its people are like no other.<BR>

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_PearlBetwixtEmpires_01TR
A Pearl Betwixt Empires, vol. 1
帝国之间的珍珠，第1卷

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_PearlBetwixtEmpires_01TR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
A Pearl Betwixt Empires: An Overview of Cathnoquey<BR>
Volume I
<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
It has been well over a century since the Imperial Geographical Society last conducted a survey of the island of Cathnoquey. Initial surveys took place during and shortly after Emperor Uriel Septim V added the archipelago to the Empire during preparations for his ill-fated invasion of Akavir. The chaos of this time obviously prioritized military matters, which meant scholars could ill afford to better understand the cultural customs of this fascinating land. What work they produced has provided us with tantalizing enigmas but not, alas, clear answers.<BR>
<BR>
Though the Empire may one day bring all of Nirn (and beyond) under its beneficent rule, our current sovereign, Uriel Septim VII, has wisely chosen the modern era to be a period of consolidation rather than expansion. It is therefore the perfect time in which to better understand the myriad cultures which comprise the Empire, particularly those that are often overlooked by Western scholarship.<BR>
<BR>
These volumes are adapted from the journals of Clavus Temperian, an IAS member who undertook a voyage to Cathnoquey in 3E 414 in order to learn more about this distant Territory.<BR>
<BR>
The Flotilla Cities of the Chimeri-Quey<BR>
<BR>
Most educated Heartlanders have heard Cathnoquey noted with interest as an example of Man and Mer living together in peace. (Patriotic readers will no doubt recognize that the Empire itself has achieved this feat, on a grander scale.) Cathnoquey indeed hosts co-existing cultures: the Chimeri-Quey and the Keptu-Quey, the latter of whom were oft referred to in older Imperial documents as "Men-of-Keptu". It may surprise readers to know, however, that the Chimeri-Quey, the elves of this distant archipelago, rarely set foot on land at all.<BR>
<BR>
To foreign eyes, the renowned flotilla cities of the Chimeri-Quey may appear ramshackle, a chaotic assemblage of wood, tarp, barnacle, and iron. Most Chimeri-Quey live aboard "Greatships", colossal vessels which ply the open waters of the Padomaic with dozens of smaller boats lashed to their hulls. Aboard a Greatship, one might be forgiven for forgetting they are at sea. Chimeri-Quey settlements (and they are settlements) are just as replete with residences, services, and institutions as any Tamrielic town.<BR>
<BR>
The flotilla-city which hosted Clavus Temperian, Nefsilal-Mi-Anasotparsek-Mafa (a name which translates roughly as "Shining Net Spread Across the Waves") is a marvel and model of Chimeri-Quey self-sufficiency. A typical flotilla city consists of several dozen vessels, including multiple Greatships -- core vessels of enormous size, larger by an order of magnitude than Imperial Navy galleons. These Greatships are of ancient construction. Indeed, much of their wood has rotted away, the hulls held together by a framework of shells and jagged barnacles that give these ships the appearance of mountains moving upon water. The crustaceans living within the chitinized hulls are said to have a mutualistic relationship with the crew, even aiding in the defense of the Greatships when under attack.<BR>
<BR>
Greatships are connected by networks of planks and bridges. From a distance, they almost appear to be one gargantuan vessel. More remarkable still are the long nets of kelp and other vegetable materials that sprawl across the flotilla city. These slimy and glistening webs connect the core vessels to the smaller ships and act as mobile farms. Many Chimeri-Quey work on the kelp nets, plucking nutritious leaves with which form the staple of the Chimeri-Quey vegetable diet. Thicker strands act as walkways, allowing crew from one ship to cross over to any other. Reflecting the egalitarian tendencies seen in Cathnoquey as a whole, the Greatships are open to all. Provisions are stored in the immense holds and traded to other Chimeri-Quey in exchange for goods or labor. Imperial septims are uncommon, but accepted (aboard Nefsilal-Mafa, at least).<BR>
<BR>
Water remains a difficult issue for the flotilla-cities. Smaller sea plants symbiotic to the kelp nets have been bred to absorb and desalinate water (much like the sadrith mushrooms favored by the Telvanni of Morrowind). The ships themselves, meanwhile, are designed to collect as much rainwater as possible, with even the sails cleverly designed to funnel liquid to waiting barrels. Chimeri-Quey engineering ensures that there is enough water to get by, but the ever-present threat of shortage means that strict population control measures are enforced aboard the flotilla cities.<BR>
<BR>
As many as two dozen smaller ships make up the outer ring of Nefsilal-Mafa. These outer vessels are notable for their heterogeneity. Some are fishing ships with strong sails and immense hulls, whose captains will detach from the city in order to harvest the teeming waters of the Padomaic. Others are carefully insulated forge ships that specialize in light manufacturing. Swift tradeships, meanwhile, fly across the sea towards distant shores for unusual goods which cannot be produced on board. There are also small warships of good quality.<BR>
<BR>
While the core vessels have allegedly stayed afloat for centuries or millennia, these outer vessels are essentially normal seagoing ships. The Chimeri-Quey have incorporated ships from a wide variety of cultures into their flotilla-cities, so one may see Nord longships, Akaviri junks, and others of yet more exotic origin. The Chimeri-Quey are quick to insist that these vessels are purchased by legal means; piracy is a great sin in Quey culture.<BR>
<BR>
At the time of writing, Nefsilal-Mafa has fifteen outer vessels, though a sixteenth had recently been lost in a storm. (Its sinking with all hands was still being mourned by the city at the time of Temperian's visit.) But this number is ever-changing. Outer vessels often detach from a flotilla city for months at a time, and it is not unheard of for ships from one flotilla city to dock at the kelp nets of another and eventually become part of the new host. The precise calculations that isolated outer vessels use to find flotilla cities are a closely guarded secret of the Chimeri-Quey, though no doubt attributable to the population's preternatural navigational skill.<BR>
<BR>
Distinct from the main bulk of each flotilla city is the Shore-Khan's ship. These intrepid craft always sail a few days ahead of their flotilla city, using messenger pigeons to relay news to the main body. This is considered a dangerous assignment and a burden of leadership.<BR>
<BR>
St. Veloth at Sea: The Chimeri-Quey<BR>
<BR>
The descendants of the ancient Chimer look much like the modern Altmer, though smaller of frame and rougher of demeanor. While the Altmer praise luxury, the Chimer embrace hardship and danger. A settled life is anathema to these doughty mariners, who can often be heard to pity those who spend their lives on land.<BR>
<BR>
It is unfortunately difficult to get clear answers about the history of the Chimeri-quey. Responses are often evasive. A common refrain is "Who is to say, these days, so long after the departure?", accompanied with a slightly embarrassed smile. Regardless, St. Veloth is still venerated, his visage reproduced on hull and sail. The Chimeri-Quey seem to believe that the best way to honor St. Veloth's virtues is to maintain a perpetually nomadic existence. Many zealously faithful Chimeri-Quey consider the Altmer and Dunmer to have both fallen prey to sedentary lives of decadence and stagnation, a fate the elves of the high seas claim to avoid.<BR>
<BR>
Shrines to the so-called Good Daedra can be found throughout Nefsilal-Mafa. Each Greatship has at least one, typically an icon of brass and semiprecious stones that honors Mephala, Boethiah, or Azura (the latter of which is most popular).<BR>
<BR>
The fundamental unit of Chimeri-quey society is the crew, which consists of several interrelated families. Upon reaching adulthood, a Chimeri-Quey will receive a tattoo on the sole of the right foot, the design unique to their ship. This way, they will always walk the deck of their home, no matter where they go. Marriage always occurs between Chimeri-Quey of different ships. The husband moves to the wife's ship and becomes a part of her family. Though the father is the head of the family in domestic issues, the role of ship captain typically goes to a mother. She will determine who among the crew is sent to the Wave Council, and delegate responsibilities for the maintenance and running of the vessel.<BR>
<BR>
Due to the scarcity of resources and the narrow margins of healthy population aboard the flotilla cities, Chimeri-Quey will often depart for other flotilla-cities or take work as crewmen on non-Chimeri-Quey ships. The latter choice is considered a hardship, and many sad ballads are sung about Chimeri-Quey who had no choice but to make their way among strange crews. Not all Chimeri-Quey find foreign service disagreeable, however; many serve proudly in the Imperial Navy, which prizes the rare skill of Chimeri-Quey sailors.<BR>
<BR>
Decisions for a flotilla-city are made by the Wave Council, a collection of elected representatives who meet on one of the Greatships. Each outer vessel gets one representative, while a core vessel receives two. Meetings occur once a month. The most important responsibility of the Wave Council is to determine what materials the flotilla-city needs. For instance, should more food be required, the Council will determine that one of the outer vessels devoted to fishing will go out on an expedition. Officially, a two-thirds majority is required for any decision, but it is rare for the Wave Council to not maintain a running consensus. The Shore-Khan is a nominal leader elected by this Wave Council, who serve as the face of the flotilla city to the outside world. In all cases, the shore-khan is chosen from the crew of a Greatship, as outer vessels usually cannot spare the crew. Though great honors are given to the Shore-Khan, their job is a bleak and dangerous one. By custom, no Shore-Khan may hold the position for longer than ten years; former shore-khans enjoy great esteem among the Chimeri-Quey, and often speak loudest at the Wave Council.<BR>
<BR>
The insular nature of the Chimeri-Quey challenges the Empire's ability to meaningfully integrate them into the institutions of Imperial society. This may be beginning to change, however. Traders from Tamriel are no longer rare in the Padomaic Ocean, and Chimeri-Quey merchantmen now dock at ports throughout the Empire. Indeed, Chimeri-Quey have often set out to explore the Empire themselves (though many have no doubt been mistaken for tattooed Altmer). Their steadfastness and nautical skill speak to the benefits of counting the Chimeri-Quet among the Empire's citizens, benefits which will surely continue to grow as the Empire's eastern reach expands yet further.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
帝国之间的珍珠：卡特诺奎概述<BR>
第一卷
<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
帝国地理学会上一次对卡特诺奎岛进行勘测，已经过去了一个多世纪。最初的勘测发生在尤利尔·塞普汀五世皇帝在为他对阿卡维尔的不幸入侵做准备期间，将该群岛并入帝国之时以及之后不久。当时的混乱显然将军事事务置于优先地位，这意味着学者们无暇更好地了解这片迷人土地的文化习俗。他们所完成的工作为我们提供了一些诱人的谜团，但可惜，没有明确的答案。<BR>
<BR>
尽管帝国有一天可能会将整个奈恩（及其之外）纳入其仁慈的统治之下，但我们目前的君主尤利尔·塞普汀七世明智地选择了现代作为巩固而非扩张的时期。因此，现在是更好地理解构成帝国的无数文化的绝佳时机，尤其是那些经常被西方学术界忽视的文化。<BR>
<BR>
这些卷册改编自帝国考古学会成员克拉乌斯·坦佩里安的日记，他于第三纪元414年前往卡特诺奎，以了解更多关于这个遥远领土的信息。<BR>
<BR>
歧莫里-奎的船队城市<BR>
<BR>
大多数受过教育的心脏地居民都听说过卡特诺奎，它被有趣地视为人类与精灵和平共处的典范。（爱国读者无疑会认识到，帝国本身已在更大规模上实现了这一壮举。）卡特诺奎确实拥有共存的文化：歧莫里-奎和克普图-奎，后者在较旧的帝国文件中常被称为“克普图之民”。然而，读者可能会惊讶地发现，歧莫里-奎，这个遥远群岛的精灵，几乎从不踏上陆地。<BR>
<BR>
在外人眼中，歧莫里-奎著名的船队城市可能看起来摇摇欲坠，是木头、防水布、藤壶和铁的混乱组合。大多数歧莫里-奎居住在“巨舰”上，这些巨大的船只航行在帕多梅海洋的开阔水域，船体上绑着几十艘小船。在一艘巨舰上，人们忘记自己是在海上，也是情有可原的。歧莫里-奎的定居点（它们确实是定居点）像任何泰姆瑞尔城镇一样，充满了住宅、服务和机构。<BR>
<BR>
接待了克拉乌斯·坦佩里安的船队城市尼夫西拉尔-米-阿纳索塔帕塞克-玛法（这个名字大致翻译为“波光粼粼的网铺展在浪涛间”）是歧莫里-奎自给自足的一个奇迹和典范。一个典型的船队城市由几十艘船只组成，包括多艘巨舰 -- 体型巨大的核心船只，比帝国海军的大帆船还要大一个数量级。这些巨舰结构古老。事实上，它们的大部分木材已经腐烂，船体依靠外壳和参差不齐的藤壶构成的框架固定在一起，使得这些船看起来像在水上移动的山脉。生活在几丁质船体内的甲壳类动物据说与船员有共生关系，甚至在巨舰受到攻击时帮助防御。<BR>
<BR>
巨舰之间通过木板和桥梁网络连接。从远处看，它们几乎像是一艘巨大的船只。更引人注目的是，横跨船队城市的长长的海带网和其他植物材料。这些黏滑、闪闪发光的网络将核心船只与较小的船只连接起来，充当移动农场。许多歧莫里-奎在海带网上工作，采摘营养丰富的叶子，这些叶子构成了歧莫里-奎蔬菜饮食的主食。较粗的绳索充当走道，允许一艘船的船员穿行到任何其他船只。反映了卡特诺奎整体的平等主义倾向，巨舰对所有人开放。补给品储存在巨大的货舱中，并与其他歧莫里-奎交易以换取货物或劳动力。帝国塞普汀不常见，但也被接受（至少在尼夫西拉尔-玛法上是这样）。<BR>
<BR>
水对船队城市来说仍然是一个难题。与海带网共生的较小海生植物被培育来吸收和淡化海水（很像晨风泰瓦尼人喜爱的萨德里斯蘑菇）。同时，船只本身被设计成尽可能多地收集雨水，甚至船帆也巧妙地设计成将液体引导到等待的桶中。歧莫里-奎的工程学确保有足够的水维持生计，但始终存在的短缺威胁意味着在船队城市中实行严格的人口控制措施。<BR>
<BR>
多达两打的小型船只组成了尼夫西拉尔-玛法的外环。这些外围船只以其异质性而著称。有些是配有强力船帆和巨大船体的渔船，其船长会脱离城市，去捕捞帕多梅海洋富饶的海域。其他的是经过精心隔热的锻造船，专门从事轻型制造。与此同时，快速的贸易船跨越海洋，驶向遥远的海岸，寻找船上无法生产的不寻常货物。还有一些质量不错的小型战舰。<BR>
<BR>
虽然据称核心船只已漂浮了数世纪或数千年，但这些外围船只本质上是普通的远洋船只。歧莫里-奎已将来自各种文化的船只融入他们的船队城市，因此人们可能会看到诺德长船、阿卡维尔帆船，以及其他起源更为奇特的船只。歧莫里-奎很快会坚称这些船只都是通过合法手段购买的；海盗行为在奎文化中是一种大罪。<BR>
<BR>
在撰写本文时，尼夫西拉尔-玛法拥有十五艘外围船只，尽管第十六艘最近在一场风暴中失事了。（在坦佩里安访问时，该城仍在哀悼它的沉没，所有船员都遇难了。）但这个数字是不断变化的。外围船只常常一次脱离船队城市数月，而且一艘船队的船只停靠在另一船队的海带网上，最终成为新宿主的一部分，这并非闻所未闻。孤立的外围船只用来寻找船队城市的精确计算是歧莫里-奎严守的秘密，尽管无疑归功于他们超自然的航海技能。<BR>
<BR>
与每个船队城市主体不同是滨海汗的船。这些勇敢的船只总是在其船队城市前面航行几天，使用信鸽向主体传递消息。这被认为是一项危险的任务，也是领导的重担。<BR>
<BR>
海上的圣维洛斯：歧莫里-奎<BR>
<BR>
古代歧莫的后裔看起来很像现代的傲特莫，只是身材更矮小，举止更粗犷。傲特莫崇尚奢华，而歧莫则拥抱艰辛与危险。定居的生活是这些勇敢的航海者所深恶痛绝的，常常能听到他们同情那些终生在陆地上度过的人。<BR>
<BR>
不幸的是，很难获得关于歧莫里-奎历史的明确答案。回答往往是闪烁其词的。一个常见的说法是“现在谁又能说得清呢，毕竟离开那么久了”，并伴以略带尴尬的微笑。尽管如此，圣维洛斯仍受到尊崇，他的面容被复制在船体和船帆上。歧莫里-奎似乎相信，尊崇圣维洛斯美德的最佳方式是保持永恒的游牧生活。许多狂热忠诚的歧莫里-奎认为傲特莫和丹莫都成了久坐不动、腐朽停滞生活的牺牲品，而公海的精灵们则声称避免了这种命运。<BR>
<BR>
在整个尼夫西拉尔-玛法都可以找到所谓的良善迪德拉的圣祠。每艘巨舰至少有一个，通常是黄铜和半宝石制成的圣像，供奉梅法拉、波耶西亚或阿祖拉（后者最受欢迎）。<BR>
<BR>
歧莫里-奎社会的基本单位是船员组，由几个相互关联的家庭组成。成年后，歧莫里-奎会在右脚底纹上一个纹身，图案是他们的船所独有的。这样，无论走到哪里，他们都能走在自家船的甲板上。婚姻总是在不同船只的歧莫里-奎之间进行。丈夫搬到妻子的船上，成为她家庭的一部分。虽然父亲在家庭事务中是家长，但船长的角色通常由母亲担任。她将决定船员中的谁被派往波浪议会，并委派维护和运行船只的职责。<BR>
<BR>
由于资源稀缺以及船队城市健康人口的狭窄余地，歧莫里-奎常常会前往其他船队城市，或在非歧莫里-奎的船只上担任船员。后一种选择被视为一种苦难，有许多悲伤的歌谣传唱那些别无选择、不得不在陌生船员中谋生的歧莫里-奎。然而，并非所有歧莫里-奎都觉得外籍服务令人不快；许多人在帝国海军中自豪地服役，海军非常珍视歧莫里-奎水手罕见的技能。<BR>
<BR>
船队城市的决策由波浪议会做出，波浪议会由选出的代表组成，他们在其中一艘巨舰上开会。每艘外围船只获得一名代表，而核心船只获得两名代表。会议每月举行一次。波浪议会最重要的职责是确定船队城市需要哪些物资。例如，如果需要更多食物，议会将决定让专门用于捕鱼的外围船只之一出海远征。正式上，任何决定都需要三分之二的多数票，但波浪议会很少不能维持持续的共识。滨海汗是由这个波浪议会选出的名义领袖，担任船队城市对外界的形象。在所有情况下，滨海汗都是从巨舰的船员中选出的，因为外围船只通常抽不出船员。尽管滨海汗被授予巨大的荣誉，但他们的工作是暗淡而危险的。按照习俗，滨海汗的任期不得超过十年；前任滨海汗在歧莫里-奎中享有崇高的尊重，并常在波浪议会中发言最有分量。<BR>
<BR>
歧莫里-奎的孤僻性挑战了帝国将他们有意义地融入帝国社会制度的能力。然而，这种情况可能正在开始改变。来自泰姆瑞尔的商人在帕多梅海洋已不再罕见，歧莫里-奎的商船现在停靠在帝国各地的港口。事实上，歧莫里-奎自己也常常出发去探索帝国（尽管许多人无疑被误认为是纹身的傲特莫）。他们的坚定和航海技能说明了将歧莫里-奎算作帝国公民的好处，随着帝国东部疆域的进一步扩展，这些好处必将持续增长。<BR>

The Dragon's Black Scales, Spread Across the Sea<BR>
<BR>
As any diligent student of geography knows, the island of Cathnoquey is the greatest of the four large islands within the Queyan archipelago, itself surrounded by 56 smaller islands known to the Imperial Geographical Society. Cathnoquey proper is by far the biggest isle, easily larger than the rest of the isles combined. The Empire's Cathnoquey Territory encompasses the entirety of the archipelago, but most of the Territory's population lives on the four largest isles.<BR>
<BR>
Although it lies just north of the tropics, Cathnoquey is in truth a rather bleak place. Rocky beaches ring miles of stunted forests where the trunks of slender gray-trunked palms, seldom taller than a man, twist like wires as they struggle up from the stony landscape.<BR>
<BR>
Beyond these forests are hills of igneous desolation where stones of black glass reflect the sun's heat on travelers. The interior of Cathnoquey remains obscure, even to the Keptu-Quey. Dark rumors shroud the volcanic (though long-dormant) interior, and few go there willingly.<BR>
<BR>
Freshwater lakes and lagoons dot Cathnoquey's north, and it is here that most of the Keptu-Quey make their homes. The biggest native citadel, Yl$F6ccan, straddles a rocky strand that divides the great Nocc$F6ny Lagoon and the seas of the Padomaic Ocean.<BR>
<BR>
The industrious Keptu-Quey have cleared enough of the archipelago's ancient forests to set up extensive farmland. The staple crop is a filling variety of tuber called a nup root, which possesses a pleasantly sweet taste. Domestic animals tend to be similar to those found in the more settled areas of the Empire (especially after a century of trade with Tamriel), though there are more peculiar native beasts living in the wild. Other Keptu-Quey make their living by fishing in the lagoons, or via light manufacturing. Wasabi from the famed Wasabi Run is managed and cultivated by chartered Tamrielic growers, including many Nords from Skyrim.<BR>
<BR>
Sulfur and glass deposits can be found closer to the central volcano, but the Empire has had difficulty exploiting these resources. The Keptu-Quey are unwilling to work in mines, and the attempts of previous governors to correct this issue did not produce satisfactory results. The few mines in operation use convict laborers imported from Tamriel, but these wretched places are more valuable for their remoteness and impracticality of escape than any real material profits .<BR>
<BR>
The second largest island in the archipelago, Cinnanquey, hosts the largest Imperial presence, centered upon the thriving regional capital of Mare. Much of the Empire's colonial endeavors in the Padomaic are hosted at Port Mare, including the headquarters of the far eastern chapters of the Guilds. The easternmost large island, Cinvec, is primarily rural, aside from a handful of tiny settlements of the Keptu-Quey. The southernmost major island, Ll$E9nn$F6c$F6c$F6nn$E9ll, has been quarantined by Imperial edict since 3E 289 and is beyond the scope of this journal.<BR>
