From East, From West, From North: The Keptu-Quey<BR>
<BR>
Few human groups in Nirn are as puzzling as the Keptu-Quey. As the academic name for them suggests, researchers suspect that a distant relation to the Nedic-Keptic peoples who once inhabited Hammerfell, Cyrodiil, and Morrowind before the arrival of the Velothi. One justification for this theory is the bull heraldry so ubiquitous among the Keptu-quey, which resembles art known to have been produced by these ancient Tamrielic peoples. Other scholars contest these assumptions, and insist that the Keptu are in fact related to the lost Men of Akavir, driven out of the Uttermost East in ages past by the depredations of the Tsaesci.<BR>
<BR>
It should be noted now that Chimeri-Quey and Keptu-Quey are demonyms of Imperial design. The inhabitants, both Man and Mer, refer to themselves merely as Quey (though some have accepted Imperial prefixes in recent years).<BR>
<BR>
The nature of Chimeri-Quey society means that the elves often live beyond the reach of day-to-day Imperial authority (though they have gladly complied with Imperial tax collectors when summoned). As an island people, the Keptu-Quey have far more interaction with Imperial governance than their seaborne counterparts, exposure which has changed their culture considerably since the days before Empire came to the isles. Modern Keptu-Quey are far more enterprising than their ancestors of a century ago, and many can be found running profitable businesses in Port Mare or seeking work in ports as far afield as Firewatch, Tear, and Winterhold.<BR>
<BR>
Traditionally, many Keptu-Quey lived around (and sometimes within) immense conical citadels that have never been touched by hammer or chisel. Words cannot truly do justice to these remarkable fortresses, which are made of solid rock but appear as if molded from clay. Rounded turrets and parapets extrude from the living stone, and irregularly placed ovoid windows look out onto the sea in regular intervals, but the Quey insist that no masons ever built them.<BR>
<BR>
Though the citadels remain in use, most Keptu-Quey live in the towns which surround them. In older days, most Keptu-Quey dwelt in grass-roofed and cylindrical stone apartments called kenmennu. These communal structures would bind together several smaller stone huts reserved for the use of individual families. Kenmennu can still be found at the outskirts of towns and on the farms throughout the countryside, but buildings closer to towns' central citadels now more closely resemble those in Imperial settlements, with families and businesses existing under their own roofs.<BR>
<BR>
Keptu-Quey households are almost always inter-generational. A matriarchal figure, either the mother or grandmother, typically owns the family home, while an elder male figure acts as the head of the family unit. The parallels with the Chimeri-Quey family structure are probably not coincidental. Families collectively participate in the raising of children.<BR>
<BR>
Though the Keptu-Quey have adapted, somewhat, to the Imperial economy, they maintain a certain distrust of hoarding material goods. The intricate Keptu-Quey writing system, traditionally known only to priests and the most learned, proved too complex for the challenges of integration into the Empire. Modern Keptu-quey have adopted the common alphabet and script for most everyday purposes, including business and navigation. Families that have achieved great financial success are expected by their compatriots to expend much of their fortunes on the creation of fantastical (and utterly impractical) weapons. Cathnoquey is a peaceful realm, noteworthy for its lack of endemic violence, so this interest in such weapons hints at ancient traumas from generations past.<BR>
<BR>
Mingling of Man and Mer<BR>
<BR>
Early accounts state that contact between the Chimeri-Quey and Keptu-Quey was once rare and fleeting, consisting only of brief meetings when the Chimeri-Quey came ashore for trade. It is unclear when the relationship between the two peoples deepened into its modern form, but today, ships from the flotilla-cities frequently pay visits to Keptu-Quey towns, maintaining a constant system of contact. During visits, families exchange gifts, share food, and bless each other's children, relationships which often date back generations.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
帝国之间的珍珠：卡特诺奎概述<BR>
第二卷
<BR><BR>

龙之黑鳞，遍布大海<BR>

任何勤奋的地理学生都知道，卡特诺奎岛是奎安群岛四个大岛中最大的一个，该群岛本身被帝国地理学会所知的56个小岛包围。卡特诺奎本土是迄今为止最大的岛屿，其面积轻易超过其他岛屿的总和。帝国的卡特诺奎领地涵盖了整个群岛，但该领地的大部分人口居住在四个最大的岛屿上。<BR>
<BR>
尽管它位于热带以北不远处，卡特诺奎实际上是一个相当荒凉的地方。岩石海滩环绕着数英里的矮林，那里细长的灰色树干棕榈树，很少比人高，在石质景观中挣扎着向上生长，像电线一样扭曲。<BR>
<BR>
在这些森林之外是火成岩的荒凉山丘，黑色的玻璃石块将太阳的热量反射到旅行者身上。卡特诺奎的内陆地区仍然模糊不清，即使对克普图-奎也是如此。黑暗的谣言笼罩着火山（尽管长期休眠）的内陆，很少有人愿意去那里。<BR>
<BR>
淡水湖和泻湖点缀在卡特诺奎的北部，这里也是大多数克普图-奎安家的地方。最大的本土城堡伊洛坎横跨一道岩石海岸，分隔了大诺科尼泻湖和帕多梅海洋的海域。<BR>
<BR>
勤劳的克普图-奎已经清除了足够多的群岛古老森林，建立了广阔的农田。主要作物是一种名为纳普根的饱腹块茎，味道甜美。家养动物往往与帝国更定居地区发现的动物相似（特别是在与泰姆瑞尔进行了一个世纪的贸易之后），尽管野外还有更多奇特的本地野兽。其他克普图-奎通过在泻湖捕鱼或轻型制造业谋生。来自著名的山葵产地瓦萨比的山葵由特许的泰姆瑞尔种植者管理和栽培，其中包括许多来自天际的诺德人。<BR>
<BR>
在靠近中央火山的地方可以找到硫磺和玻璃矿床，但帝国在开发这些资源方面遇到了困难。克普图-奎不愿意在矿场工作，前任总督纠正这个问题的尝试也没有产生令人满意的结果。少数在运营的矿场使用从泰姆瑞尔进口的囚犯劳工，但这些悲惨的地方，其价值更多地在于它们的偏远和难以逃脱，而非任何实际的物质利润。<BR>
<BR>
群岛中第二大岛辛南奎拥有最大的帝国存在，以繁荣的地区首府马雷为中心。帝国在帕多梅的大部分殖民努力都在马雷港进行，包括公会远东分部的总部。最东边的大岛辛韦克，除了少数几个克普图-奎的小定居点外，主要是农村。最南端的主要岛屿莱诺科科内尔自第三纪元289年以来一直根据帝国法令被隔离，超出了本日记的范围。<BR>
<BR>
从东、从西、从北：克普图-奎<BR>
<BR>
奈恩上很少有人类群体像克普图-奎那样令人费解。正如他们的学术名称所示，研究人员怀疑他们与尼德-凯普提克人有远亲关系，后者曾在维洛提人到来之前居住于落锤、西罗帝尔和晨风。这一理论的一个理由是，克普图-奎中无处不在的公牛纹章，类似于已知由这些古代泰姆瑞尔民族创造的艺术。其他学者对这些假设提出异议，并坚持认为克普图实际上与失落的阿卡维尔之民有关，他们在过去时代被赛埃锡的掠夺赶出了极东之地。<BR>
<BR>
现在应该指出，歧莫里-奎和克普图-奎是帝国设计的民族名称。居民，无论是人类还是精灵，都只称自己为奎（尽管近年来有些人接受了帝国的前缀）。<BR>
<BR>
歧莫里-奎社会的性质意味着精灵们常常生活在帝国日常权威的范围之外（尽管他们在被召唤时欣然遵从了帝国收税员）。作为一个岛屿民族，克普图-奎与帝国治理的互动远比他们的海上同胞多得多，这种接触自帝国来到群岛之前的日子以来，已大大改变了他们的文化。现代克普图-奎比他们一个世纪前的祖先更具进取精神，许多人被发现经营着马雷港盈利丰厚的生意，或在远至火望、泪城和冬堡的港口寻找工作。<BR>
<BR>
传统上，许多克普图-奎居住在巨大的圆锥形城堡周围（有时在里面），这些城堡从未被锤子或凿子触碰过。文字无法真正描述这些非凡堡垒的壮丽，它们由实心岩石构成，但看起来像是用粘土模制的。圆形的塔楼和胸墙从原生石头中伸出，不规则放置的椭圆形窗户以规则的间隔眺望大海，但奎人坚称从未有过石匠建造它们。<BR>
<BR>
尽管城堡仍在使用，但大多数克普图-奎居住在环绕它们的城镇中。在过去，大多数克普图-奎居住在称为肯门努的茅草屋顶圆柱形石制公寓中。这些公共结构将几个供个别家庭使用的小石屋结合在一起。肯门努在城镇边缘和乡间的农场仍然可以找到，但靠近城镇中央城堡的建筑现在更类似于帝国定居点中的建筑，家庭和企业在各自的屋顶下存在。<BR>
<BR>
克普图-奎的家庭几乎总是几代同堂。一个母系人物，母亲或祖母，通常拥有家庭住宅，而一位年长的男性人物则作为家庭单位的首领。与歧莫里-奎家庭结构的相似之处可能并非巧合。家庭共同参与抚养孩子。<BR>
<BR>
尽管克普图-奎在某种程度上已经适应了帝国经济，但他们仍然对囤积物质财富保持一定的怀疑态度。克普图-奎复杂的书写系统，传统上只有祭司和最博学的人知道，被证明对于融入帝国的挑战来说过于复杂。现代克普图-奎在大多数日常用途中，包括商业和航海，已采用通用的字母和文字。取得巨大经济成功的家庭被他们的同胞期望将大部分财富用于制造奇特的（且完全不实用的）武器。卡特诺奎是一个和平的国度，以其缺乏地方性暴力而著称，因此对这类武器的兴趣暗示了来自过去世代的古老创伤。<BR>
<BR>
人与精灵的融合<BR>
<BR>
早期的记载表明，歧莫里-奎和克普图-奎之间的接触曾经是罕见而短暂的，仅限于歧莫里-奎上岸贸易时的简短会面。目前尚不清楚两个民族之间的关系何时深化为现代形式，但如今，来自船队城市的船只频繁访问克普图-奎的城镇，保持着持续的接触系统。在访问期间，家庭之间交换礼物，分享食物，并祝福彼此的孩子，这些关系往往可以追溯到几代人之前。<BR>

Peoples of the Reach<BR>
by Antony Cestus, Imperial Cartographer<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
I have visited the Reach of western Skyrim twice in my life. The first occasion was shortly after the War of Bend'r-'Mahk in 397 3E to record the shifting borders and general ruination of that devastating conflict. The second was seventeen years later to visit my nephew, a merchant who settled in Karthwasten. During these two visits I had the pleasure of meeting a great number of interesting people from a wide variety of backgrounds. I also met some people I would quite happily never see again. <BR>
<BR>
The Reach has been disputed territory throughout history, changing hands on numerous occasions. One constant has been the Reachmen. These people, described (rather unkindly) as a 'mongrel breed' in the Pocket Guide to the Empire, are a mixture of Breton and High Elf blood. The Reachmen have a distinct cultural identity entirely separate from the other races of the Reach. The majority live in isolated settlements in the wilderness entirely peacefully. I spent a week in a Reachmen camp and was impressed by the generosity of my hosts. Their religion, although archaic and shamanic, does bear some resemblance to the Nine Divines worshipped in the rest of Skyrim and I found no justification for the persecution the Reachmen have endured at the hands of Bretons, Redguards, Nords and others at various times in history. On the other hand, like all cultures there are those who have no respect for the property and lives of other people. As I continued on my way, heading north towards the town of Karthgad, my escort and I came under attack from a band of Reachmen witches. They slew four of my guard and took myself and three others captive. They treated us quite abysmally, and we feared for our lives. Luckily we were able to escape, although my good friend Ungolith was stuck by a poisoned arrow and died soon after. We were later informed that there are some Reachmen who rebel against Nordic rule and will stop at nothing in their efforts to drive all other races from the Reach. The witches that captured us were almost certainly members of this group.  <BR>
<BR>
The wilderness of the Reach is also home to a number of Orc tribes. The tribes made their living from raiding and pillaging neighbouring settlements and exacting tolls from those travellers who braved the forest paths in an attempt to shorten their journeys. Following the rebuilding of Orsinium and the lessening of prejudices against the Orcish race many of these tribes moved to Nova Orsinium. Those tribes that remained in the Reach are those that disagree with Gortwog gro-Nagorm's vision and religious beliefs and most of them, I am reliably informed, are peaceful and only wish to be left alone. Again, there are still some Orcs who attack strangers on sight, so travellers in the Reach would be advised to stick to the roads.  <BR>
<BR>
The Nords of the Reach are very similar to Nords elsewhere. They are a tough, uncompromising race, a people who never forget a grudge, or a trusted friend. However, the Nords of the Reach are, if anything, even more willing to take up arms to avenge a real or perceived slight than their kin elsewhere. This is probably due to the troubled history of the Reach. Indeed, many older Nords remember the War of Bend'r-Mahk well and need little excuse to recount their heroic and blatantly untrue war stories. One section of Nordic society in the Reach worthy of special mention is the Bear Clan of Karthgad. These Nords claim to be the defenders of the Reach, the first line of defense against the Bretons, Redguards and Reachmen. I could find no evidence to support this claim. In fact, several people told me (in confidence) that the Bear Clan are naught but petty criminals with visions of grandeur. Doubtless to say that I am unlikely to return to Amber Guard after making such claims in print!  <BR>
<BR>
The other major inhabitants of the Reach are the Redguards and Bretons. They co-exist peacefully, if at times a bit uneasily, with the Nords. The city of Karthwasten, which was captured from Hammerfell during the War of Bend'r-Mahk, has a large Redguard population. Most of them live in a separate area, walled off from the rest of the city. This has, at the time of writing (Last Seed, 420 3E), minimised sectarian violence in the city - although my nephew tells me there are always rumors of loyalist gangs attacking Nords and Redguard sympathisers foolish enough to wander the poor  quarter alone at night. Elsewhere though, the majority of races do live together without violence, meaning that the Reach has one of the richest mix of cultures in the whole of Skyrim, if not Tamriel.  <BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
河峪之民<BR>
帝国制图师 安东尼·塞斯图斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
我一生中曾两次访问天际西部的河峪。第一次是在第三纪元397年的本德'尔-马克之战后不久，记录那场毁灭性冲突的边界变动和普遍破坏。第二次是十七年后去探望我的侄子，一个在卡斯瓦斯滕定居的商人。在这两次访问中，我有幸遇到了许多来自不同背景的有趣人物。我也遇到了一些我相当乐意再也见不到的人。<BR>
<BR>
河峪在历史上一直是争议领土，多次易手。一个恒定的因素是河峪人。这些人，在《帝国袖珍指南》中被（相当不友善地）描述为“杂种”，是布莱顿人和傲特莫血统的混合体。河峪人拥有独特的文化认同，与河峪的其他种族完全不同。大多数人完全和平地生活在荒野中与世隔绝的定居点里。我在一个河峪人营地度过了一周，并对主人的慷慨印象深刻。他们的宗教，尽管古老且带有萨满教色彩，确实与天际其他地区崇拜的九圣灵有某些相似之处，我认为河峪人在历史上不同时期遭受布莱顿人、红卫人、诺德人等人的迫害是没有道理的。另一方面，像所有文化一样，也有不尊重他人财产和生命的人。在我继续上路，向北前往卡斯加德镇时，我和我的护卫遭到了一伙河峪女巫的攻击。她们杀了我四名护卫，并将我和另外三人俘虏。她们对待我们非常恶劣，我们为自己的生命担忧。幸运的是我们得以逃脱，尽管我的好朋友温戈利思中了毒箭，不久就死了。我们后来得知，有些河峪人反抗诺德人的统治，会不择手段地将所有其他种族赶出河峪。俘虏我们的女巫几乎可以肯定是这个群体的成员。<BR>
<BR>
河峪的荒野也是一些兽人部落的家园。这些部落以袭击和掠夺邻近定居点，并向那些冒险走森林小径以缩短行程的旅行者收取过路费为生。随着奥辛纽姆的重建和对兽人种族偏见的减少，这些部落中的许多已迁往新奥辛纽姆。留在河峪的那些部落是不同意戈特沃格·格罗-纳果姆的愿景和宗教信仰的部落，据可靠消息，他们中的大多数是和平的，只希望不受打扰。同样，仍然有一些兽人一见到陌生人就攻击，因此建议河峪的旅行者坚持走大路。<BR>
<BR>
河峪的诺德人与其他地方的诺德人非常相似。他们是一个坚韧、不妥协的种族，一个从不忘记怨恨或信任朋友的人。然而，如果说有什么区别的话，河峪的诺德人甚至比他们其他地方的亲属更愿意拿起武器来报复真实或感知到的轻蔑。这可能是由于河峪动荡的历史。事实上，许多年长的诺德人清楚地记得本德'尔-马克之战，并几乎不需要借口来讲述他们英勇但明显不真实的战争故事。河峪诺德社会中值得特别提及的一个部分是卡斯加德的熊族。这些诺德人声称自己是河峪的捍卫者，是抵御布莱顿人、红卫人和河峪人的第一道防线。我找不到支持这一说法的证据。事实上，有几个人（私下）告诉我，熊族不过是些有妄想症的 petty criminals。毫无疑问，在发表这样的言论之后，我是不太可能再回到琥珀卫了！<BR>
<BR>
河峪的其他主要居民是红卫人和布莱顿人。他们与诺德人和平共处，尽管有时有点不安。卡斯瓦斯滕城，在本德'尔-马克之战中从落锤夺取，拥有大量的红卫人口。他们中的大多数住在与城市其他部分隔离开的独立区域。在撰写本文时（第三纪元420年末种月），这已将城市中的宗派暴力降至最低 -- 尽管我的侄子告诉我，总有关于忠诚派团伙袭击那些愚蠢到独自在夜间漫步于贫困区的诺德人和红卫同情者的谣言。但在其他地方，大多数种族确实没有暴力地生活在一起，这意味着河峪拥有整个天际（如果不是泰姆瑞尔的话）最丰富的文化混合体之一。<BR>

Lady Cinnabar of Taneth<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
If you believed what that old goat Phrastus of Elinhir writes in what he's pleased to call his "Histories," you'd think that modern society's bias against reverence for the Daedric Princes was rooted in some kind of instinctive revulsion against the Lords of Oblivion, an abhorrence based on events of unspeakable cruelty that took place thousands of years ago.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Experimentation in the<BR>
Physicalities of the Werewolf<BR>
by Reman Crex<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Far too many books such as this one begin with some sort of justification. Some reason for study is concocted, in the hopes that the writer's obsession will be seen in a more noble light. I make no such pretensions. No werewolf killed my family, none ever threatened me personally, nor even an acquaintance of mine. My obsession is borne out of simple curiosity, with a strong dose of hatred for the unnatural. Is it possible to hate something without having been done harm by it? I am no philosopher, and thus here ends my introduction. On with my studies.<BR>
<BR>
I have endeavored, over the course of several decades, to perform a complete study of the physical nature of the creatures we call werewolves. I overlook entirely the origins of this plague, whether it is acquired voluntarily or inflicted, and how one might be cured. Such matters are filled with too much guesswork and rambling second-hand inanities from farmhands.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
Subject A<BR>
Captured: in Morrowind, while in beast form<BR>
Makeup: Male, Breton in his true form<BR>
Notes: Subject shows an unusually high degree of control over his transformations.<BR>
<BR>
Experiment 1 -- Subject's bodily proportions were thoroughly measured before, during, and after the transformation. As expected, the proportions were identical while in true form, but some minor swelling of the head was observed immediately after the return. Changes observed during transformation:<BR>
23% increase in shoulder width<BR>
17% narrowing of hips<BR>
47% lengthening of arms<BR>
7% increase in finger length (not accounting for claws)<BR>
As for the legs -- the lengthening of the foot to several times its normal length seems to account for the otherwise negligible changes in the thigh region.<BR>
<BR>
Experiment 2 -- Subject was coerced into changing as rapidly and as frequently as possible, at various times and at various levels of duress.<BR>
<BR>
Transformation times and effects were not viewed to change notably. Subject expired, concluding tests.<BR>

Subject B<BR>
Captured: in Cyrodiil, already imprisoned by local authorities, in true form<BR>
Makeup: Female, Nord in her true form<BR>
Notes: Subject's large size in both true and transformed forms makes an excellent fit for vivisection<BR>
<BR>
I believe I may have been the first to witness a werewolf transformation ply its effects on the internal workings of a creature. The heart is the first thing to swell, long before the lungs or bones shift to accommodate it. This may account for the intense chest pains that some of the afflicted report directly before their changes.<BR>
<BR>
More interesting were the changes observed in the muscles of the legs. I had expected a strengthening, as the beasts are known for great power and speed, but they also seemed to change color into a dusky brown. This could also be attributed to blood loss from the procedures.<BR>
<BR>
Before the subject expired, I worked applying some known "remedies" for the disease directly to internal organs. Wolfsbane petals applied to the bones seemed to render them brittle, and the ribcage nearly collapsed at the touch. The juice of ripened belladonna berries was pressed directly into the veins, and they could be seen to shrivel behind the flow as it moved through the system. Upon reaching the heart, the major vessels pulled away completely, and subject expired within minutes.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
狼人<BR>
生理特性实验<BR>
雷曼·克雷克斯 著<BR><BR>

太多像这样的书以某种辩护开头。人们编造出一些研究理由，希望作者的痴迷能被以更崇高的眼光看待。我不做这样的伪装。没有狼人杀害我的家人，也没有狼人威胁过我本人，甚至我认识的人都没有。我的痴迷源于单纯的好奇心，以及对非自然事物的强烈憎恨。有可能在没有受到伤害的情况下憎恨某物吗？我不是哲学家，因此我的引言到此结束。继续我的研究。<BR>

肩宽增加23%<BR>
臀围缩减17%<BR>
臂长增加47%<BR>
指长增加7%（不含爪子）<BR>
至于腿部 -- 脚部伸长到正常长度的数倍，似乎可以解释大腿区域微不足道的变化。<BR>
<BR>
实验2 -- 在不同时间、不同压力水平下，强迫受试者尽可能快速和频繁地变形。<BR>
<BR>
变形时间和效果未见显著变化。受试者死亡，实验结束。<BR>

受试者 B<BR>
捕获地点：西罗帝尔，已被当地当局监禁，处于真身状态<BR>
构成：女性，真身为诺德人<BR>
注：受试者在真身和变形状态下体型巨大，非常适合活体解剖<BR>

<BR>
在受试者死亡前，我尝试将一些已知的“疗法”直接应用于其内脏。附子草花瓣敷在骨头上似乎使它们变脆，肋骨笼在触碰下几乎塌陷。将成熟的颠茄浆果汁液直接压入血管，可以看到血管随着液流在系统中移动而枯萎。当液流到达心脏时，主要血管完全脱离，受试者在几分钟内死亡。<BR>

No one -- not the oldest Dark Elf of Mount Dagoth-Ur or the Ancient Sage of Solitude himself -- can recall a time when the Orc did not ravage our fair Tamriel. Obviously, the Orcs had been terrorizing the region of the Iliac Bay at least since the early years of the First Era.  <BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>A Pocket Guide to The Empire and its environs, First Edition<BR>

<BR>
Cyrodiil, or
<BR>
THE IMPERIAL PROVINCE
<BR>

Being a Description of the Lands<BR>

and the Divers Customs of the Inhabitants<BR>

and furthermore a useful history of those places<BR>

...<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>

Cyrodiil, Dragon Empire, Starry Heart of Nirn, and Seat of Sundered Kings... Indeed, if the history of the Nords is the history of humans on Tamriel, then Cyrodiil is the throne from which they will decide their destiny. It is the largest region of the continent, and most is endless jungle. Its center, the grassland of the Nibenay Valley, is enclosed by an equatorial rain forest and broken up by rivers. As one travels south along these rivers, the more subtropical it becomes, until finally the land gives way to the swamps of Argonia and the placid waters of the Topal Bay. The elevation rises gradually to the west and sharply to the north. Between its western coast and its central valley there are all manner of deciduous forest and mangroves, becoming sparser towards the ocean. The western coast is a wet-dry area, and from Rihad border to Anvil to the northernmost Valenwood villages forest fires are common in summer. There are a few major roads to the west, river paths to the north, and even a canopy tunnel to the Velothi Mountains, but most of Cyrodiil is a river-based society surrounded by jungle.<BR>

<BR>

Cyrodilic history truly begins by the middle of the Alessian Reformation, when civilization and cultivation had allowed the region to emerge as a discernible Tamrielic power. Its culture and military strength centered in the sacred Nibenay Valley, a grassland expanse with a vast lake at its heart. Several small islands rose from this lake, and the capital city sprawled across them, crisscrossed with bridges and gondola ferries. Rivers connected the city-state to both its profitable outlying territories and the friendly inland ports of Skyrim and Pellitine. Rice and textiles were its main exports, along with more esoteric treasure-goods, such as hide armor, moon-sugar, and ancestor-silk. The sheer size of Cyrodiil's physical theater, and frequent intervals of Elven tyranny, made its unification as a whole a slow and oft-interrupted process. At the height of Alessian influence, its western arm enjoyed a brief autonomy as the Colovian Estates, a demarcation that still colors an outsider's view of the Empire today; often, Cyrodiil has two faces, East and West, and any discussion of its later social history must first be tempered with a summary of this early divergence.<BR>

<BR>

Traditionally, the East is regarded as the region's soul: magnanimous, tolerant, and administrative. It was in the rain forests of the Nibenay Valley that the original Cyro-Nordic tribes, the Nibenese, learned a self-reliance that separated them culturally and economically from Skyrim. The Elven harassment of the First Empire gave rise to an elite form of support troop for the Valley armies, the battlemage. By the time the Alessian Doctrines filtered down from the north along the river trade ways, these mages had become the ruling aristocracy. They were quickly superseded by the Alessian priesthood, whose inexplicably charismatic religion found purchase in the lower classes. The traditional Nordic pantheon of Eight Divines was replaced by a baroque veneration of ancestor spirits and god-animals, practices encouraged by the mutable-yet-monotheistic doctrines of the Alessian faith. The doctrines eventually codified nearly every aspect of Eastern culture. Restrictions against certain kinds of meat-eating, coupled with the sentiments of the blossoming animal cults, soon made agriculture and husbandry nearly impossible. Thus, many of the Eastern Cyrodiils were forced to become merchants, which, over time, allowed the Nibenay Valley to become the wealthiest city-state in the region. Yet, under Alessian rule, no matter how rich or powerful the merchant class became it was still a tenanted citizenry, and the tithes they were forced to pay the priesthood were constant reminders of the state's true masters.<BR>

<BR>

The West is respected as Cyrodiil's iron hand: firm, unwavering, and ever-vigilant. The Cyro-Nords that settled it had relinquished the fertile Nibenay Valley long ago, determined to conquer the frontier. Their primitive ferocity was disinclined to magic or the need for industry, preferring bloody engagement and plunder instead. After they had captured the Nedic port-cities of the Strident coast, the Westerners embarked on a mastery of the sea. Their earliest voyages took them as far as the Iliac Bay and the Cape of the Blue Divide, whose ports they annually raided until the (then) superior Yokudan navies arrived, ca. 1E810. By the time of the Alessian Reformation, the Westerners were firmly in a position, both geographically and socially, to resist its doctrines. Hammerfell, its northern border state, was now protected by its own holy-avenging order, the Ra Gada, whose bloody intolerance for foreigners acted as West Cyrodiil's buffer against the Alessian priesthood. The pantheon of Eight Divines, therefore, survived unchecked in Western Cyrodiil, and relations with the increasingly Alessian East became strained. Ultimately, the West isolated itself from the theocratic hegemony of the Nibenay Valley, establishing an autonomous government, the Colovian Estates.<BR>

<BR>

Things persisted in this vein until the Thrassian Plague of 1E2200, which decimated more than half of Tamriel's population, particularly the western coastlands closest to Thras. After Bendu Olo, the Colovian king of Anvil, led the All Flags Navy to victory over the slugfolk of Thras, the glory of the Cyrodilic people became known throughout the world. The Colovian Estates began to overshadow the richer, more populous East then, which eventually lead to the War of Righteousness that ended Alessian rule. Control of the Nibenay Valley reverted to a mercantile-magocracy that was still far too arcane for Western tastes to entertain a reunification of Cyrodiil. Four hundred years would pass before that would happen, when Reman I, another proud son of the West, rallied the Valley's army to join his own and fight the Akaviri Invasion of 1E2703. The Cyrodilic forces engaged the Akaviri in every region of the north, eliciting their surrender at last in the Pale Pass of Skyrim. By war's end, the Cyrodiils found themselves not only united as a nation, but, too, responsible for the further protection of the northern human kingdoms at large. When the Elves of the Summerset Isles took umbrage at what they perceived as a renewed human imperialism, Reman was forced to prove them right. In order to prevent the Elves from attacking the already weakened northern kingdoms, he offered the captive Akaviri Horde amnesty in his future dominions if they would serve as the nucleus of the Army of the Second Empire of Men. Reman's own dynasty lasted for two hundred years, and in that span it conquered all the kingdoms of Tamriel except for Morrowind. Indeed, the Dark Elven Morag Tong were the doom of Reman's heirs, and the death of the last true Cyrodilic Emperor heralded the beginning of the Common Era.<BR>

<BR>

The Cyrodilic Empire endured for another four hundred years under the auspices of the Akaviri Potentate, fell, and suffered a similar span of years in the insurrections, misrules, and loss of power known as the Interregnum. Yet, the remnants of the Cyrodilic Empire refused to die, even though both East and West had become fragmented beyond measure. A petty king of the Colovian Estates, Cuhlecain, came to power and appointed an Atmoran as General of his legions. General Talos had studied in Skyrim, and used the thu'um. He could rout armies with his battle-cry and shout lesser men off their feet. A year later more than half of the Cyrodilic Empire was reclaimed or consolidated, and Cuhlecain saw fit to move into the Nibenay Valley, capture the capital city, and proclaim himself Emperor. By this point, High Rock and Skyrim, which bitterly opposed a return to Cyrodilic rule, gathered their armies for a joint invasion of the Colovian West. Talos met them on the field of Sancre Tor. The Nords that had come to cripple the Empire soon joined the General's forces, for when they heard his thu'um they realized he was Skyrim's Son and the Heir to the Empires of Men. The Bretons were sent back to High Rock with tales of Cuhlecain's new General, where they decided to combat the Emperor's sorcery with their own. In CE854, a nightblade from the Western Reach made his way to the Imperial Palace at Nibenay. There, the Witchman assassinated the Emperor, caught the Palace on fire, and slit the throat of General Talos. "But from the smoldering ruin he came, one hand to his neck and with Cuhlecain's Crown in the other. The legions wept at the sight. His Northern magic had saved him, but the voice that led them would be more silent from that night on. His word could no longer rout an army with a roar, but he could still command one with a whisper. He took for himself a Cyrodilic name, Tiber Septim, and the Nordic Name of Kings, Ysmir, the Dragon of the North. And with those names he took, too, the Red Diamond Crown of the Cyrodiils, and became their True Emperor." Thus was born the Third Empire of Men.<BR>

<BR>

Cyrodiil in the Third Empire is the young, vital embodiment of its ancient heritage. Internally, it has undergone an incredible restoration -- reconstruction of the ruined sections of the Imperial City is nearly complete, roads and cities destroyed in the Interregnum have been rebuilt, East and West are unified for the first time in four centuries. Cyrodiil's present stability and strength have not been seen since the Reman Dynasty; indeed, they were born under similar circumstances -- a Westerner winning the Eastern throne, forging them both into the greatest power in Tamriel. And now, in but twenty years time, Tiber Septim has secured Imperial authority in High Rock, Skyrim, and Hammerfell. Every human region stands with him against the Elven menace. The Emperor has gracefully attributed his success to his peoples, the Colovians and the Nibenese, whose cultures we shall now treat in their current incarnation.<BR>

<BR>

The Colovians today still possess much of the frontier spirit of their ancestors. They are uncomplicated, self-sufficient, hearty, and extremely loyal to one another. Whenever the East would tremble under the weakness of a leader, the Colovians would withdraw unto themselves, always believing they were keeping the national spirit safe until the storm passed. They realize that the Nibenay Valley is the heart of the Empire and the cultural center of its civilization, but it is a fragile center that only can be held together by the strength of character of its Emperor. When he falters, so do the Colovians. Yet when he is mighty, like Tiber Septim, they are his legions. Today, West Cyrodiils make up the majority of the soldiers in the Ruby Ranks. The Colovian nobility, all officers of the Imperial Legions or its West Navy, do not allow themselves the great expenditure of courtly life as is seen in the capital city. They prefer immaculate uniforms and stark standards hanging from the ceiling of their austere cliff-fortresses; to this day, they become a little perplexed when they must visit the grandly decorated assault of color that is the Emperor's Palace.<BR>

<BR>

By contrast, the Eastern people of Cyrodiil relish in garish costumes, bizarre tapestries, tattoos, brandings, and elaborate ceremony. Closer to the wellspring of civilization, they are more given to philosophy and the evolution of ancient traditions. The Nibenese find the numinous in everything around them, and their different cults are too numerous to mention (the most famous are the Cult of the Ancestor-Moth, the Cult of Heroes, the Cult of Tiber Septim, and the Cult of Emperor Zero). To the Colovians, the ancestor worship and esoteric customs of the East can often be bizarre. Akaviri dragon-motifs are found in all quarters, from the high minaret bridges of the Imperial City to the paper hako skiffs that villagers use to wing their dead down the rivers. Thousands of workers ply the rice fields after the floodings, or clear the foliage of the surrounding jungle in the alternate seasons. Above them are the merchant-nobility, the temple priests and cult leaders, and the age-old aristocracy of the battlemages. The Emperor watches over them all from the towers of the Imperial City, as dragons circle overhead.<BR>

<BR>

Places of Note: The Imperial City<BR>

<BR>

Refayj's famous declaration, "There is but one city in the Imperial Province,--" may strike the citizens of the Colovian west as mildly insulting, until perhaps they hear the rest of the remark, which continues, "--but one city in Tamriel, but one city in the World; that, my brothers, is the city of the Cyrodiils." From the shore it is hard to tell what is city and what is Palace, for it all rises from the islands of the lake towards the sky in a stretch of gold. Whole neighborhoods rest on the jeweled bridges that connect the islands together. Gondolas and river-ships sail along the watery avenues of its flooded lower dwellings. Moth-priests walk by in a cloud of ancestors; House Guards hold exceptionally long daikatanas crossed at intersections, adorned with ribbons and dragon-flags; and the newly arrived Western legionnaires sweat in the humid air. The river mouth is tainted red from the tinmi soil of the shore, and river dragons rust their hides in its waters. Across the lake the Imperial City continues, merging into the villages of the southern red river and ruins left from the Interregnum.<BR>

<BR>

The Emperor's Palace is a crown of sun rays, surrounded by his magical gardens. One garden path is known as Green Emperor Road-here, topiaries of the heads of past Emperors have been shaped by sorcery and can speak. When one must advise Tiber Septim, birds are drawn to the hedgery head, using their songs as its voice and moving its branches for the needed expressions.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>《帝国及其周边地区袖珍指南》，第一版<BR>

<BR>
西罗帝尔，或

奉帝国地理学会之权威颁布<BR>

帝国纪元864年<BR>

......<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>

西罗帝尔，龙之帝国，奈恩的繁星之心，分崩离析诸王之王座......诚然，若诺德人的历史即是泰姆瑞尔人类的历史，那么西罗帝尔便是他们将决定自身命运的王座。它是大陆上面积最大的区域，大部分是广袤无垠的丛林。其中心尼本奈河谷的草原被赤道雨林所环绕，并被河流分割。沿着这些河流向南行进，景色愈发具有亚热带风情，直至最终土地让位于阿尔贡尼亚的沼泽和托帕尔湾平静的水域。地势向西逐渐升高，向北则陡然抬升。在其西海岸与中央河谷之间，分布着各类落叶林和红树林，越靠近海洋则越稀疏。西海岸属于干湿交替地带，从里哈德边境到安维尔，直至瓦伦伍德最北端的村庄，夏季森林火灾频发。有数条主要道路通往西方，沿河路径通往北方，甚至还有一条通往维洛提山脉的林冠隧道，但西罗帝尔的大部分地区是一个以河流为基础的、被丛林环绕的社会。<BR>

<BR>

西罗帝尔的历史真正始于阿莱西亚改革运动的中期，彼时文明与开化使该地区崛起成为泰姆瑞尔一股举足轻重的力量。其文化与军事实力集中在神圣的尼本奈河谷，这片广阔的草原中心有一个巨大的湖泊。湖中矗立着数座小岛，首都便横跨其上，桥梁与贡多拉渡船纵横交错。河流将这个城邦与其富庶的外围领土以及天际和佩里廷友好的内陆港口连接起来。大米和纺织品是其主要出口商品，此外还有更为奇特的宝藏，如皮甲、月亮糖和先祖丝绸。西罗帝尔广袤的地理版图，加之精灵暴政的频繁时期，使其整体的统一过程缓慢且屡遭中断。在阿莱西亚势力鼎盛时期，其西部支脉曾作为科洛维亚各领地享有短暂的自治，这一划分至今仍影响着外界对帝国的看法；西罗帝尔常常展现出东西两副面孔，任何关于其后期社会史的讨论，都必须首先以对这一早期分歧的概述作为铺垫。<BR>

<BR>

传统上，东方被视为该地区的灵魂所在：宽宏、包容且善于治理。正是在尼本奈河谷的雨林中，最初的西罗-诺德部落 -- 尼本人，学会了自力更生，从而在文化和经济上与天际区分开来。精灵对第一帝国的骚扰催生了一种河谷军队的精锐支援部队 -- 战斗法师。到了阿莱西亚教义沿着河流贸易路线从北方传播下来时，这些法师已成为统治贵族。他们很快被阿莱西亚祭司阶层所取代，后者那种莫名富有魅力的宗教在下层阶级中找到了市场。传统的八圣灵诺德万神殿被一种对先祖灵魂和神兽的奇异崇拜所取代，这些做法受到了阿莱西亚信仰中既多变又趋向一神论的教义的鼓励。这些教义最终几乎规范了东方文化的方方面面。对某些肉类的饮食限制，加上蓬勃发展的动物崇拜情绪，很快使得农业和畜牧业几乎无法进行。因此，许多东方的西罗帝尔人被迫成为商人，随着时间的推移，这使尼本奈河谷成为该地区最富有的城邦。然而，在阿莱西亚统治下，无论商人阶级变得多么富有和强大，他们仍然是佃户公民，被迫向祭司阶层缴纳的什一税时刻提醒着他们国家真正的主人是谁。<BR>

<BR>

西方则被视为西罗帝尔的铁拳：坚定、不动摇、时刻警惕。定居于此的西罗-诺德人早已放弃了肥沃的尼本奈河谷，决心征服边疆。他们原始的凶悍对魔法或勤劳的需求不感兴趣，更喜欢血腥的搏杀和掠夺。在他们占领了斯特赖登特海岸的尼德港口城市后，西方人开始掌握航海技术。他们最早的航行远至髂骨湾和蓝界角，每年都袭击那里的港口，直到（当时）更为优越的尤库达海军到来，约第一纪元810年。到阿莱西亚改革运动时期，西方人无论在地理位置还是社会地位上都已牢牢占据了抵抗其教义的位置。其北方的边境国家落锤，现在由其自己的神圣复仇骑士团 -- 拉伽达保护着，后者对外来者血腥的不容忍态度成为西罗帝尔西部对抗阿莱西亚祭司阶层的缓冲。因此，八圣灵万神殿在西罗帝尔西部毫发无损地存续下来，与日益阿莱西亚化的东方的关系变得紧张。最终，西方将自己从尼本奈河谷的神权霸权中孤立出来，建立了自治政府 -- 科洛维亚各领地。<BR>

<BR>

情况一直如此，直到第一纪元2200年的瑟拉斯瘟疫，这场瘟疫消灭了泰姆瑞尔一半以上的人口，尤其是最靠近瑟拉斯的西部沿海地区。在安维尔的科洛维亚国王本都·奥洛率领全旗海军战胜瑟拉斯的蛞蝓民之后，西罗帝尔人民的荣耀闻名于世。科洛维亚各领地开始超越更富裕、人口更多的东方，最终导致了终结阿莱西亚统治的义战。尼本奈河谷的控制权又回到了商人-法师政体手中，其深奥程度仍远非西方口味所能接受，以至于无法考虑西罗帝尔的重新统一。四百年后，当另一位骄傲的西方之子雷曼一世召集河谷的军队加入他自己的队伍，以对抗第一纪元2703年的阿卡维尔入侵时，这一统一才得以实现。西罗帝尔军队在北方的每个地区都与阿卡维尔人交战，最终在天际的苍白关隘迫使他们投降。战争结束时，西罗帝尔人不仅发现自己团结成了一个国家，而且还承担起了进一步保护北方人类诸王国的责任。当夏暮群岛的精灵对他们认为新出现的人类帝国主义感到不满时，雷曼被迫证明了他们的看法是正确的。为了防止精灵攻击已经虚弱不堪的北方王国，他提出，如果被俘的阿卡维尔部落愿意作为第二人类帝国军队的核心，就可以在他未来的领地中获得赦免。雷曼自己的王朝持续了两百年，在此期间，它征服了泰姆瑞尔除晨风以外的所有王国。事实上，正是黑暗精灵的莫拉格·堂导致了雷曼继承人的覆灭，最后一位真正的西罗帝尔皇帝之死预示着共治纪元的开始。<BR>

<BR>

西罗帝尔帝国在阿卡维尔摄政的庇护下又延续了四百年，随后覆灭，并在被称为大空位的叛乱、暴政和权力丧失时期经历了同样漫长的岁月。然而，尽管东西方都已四分五裂到无以复加，西罗帝尔帝国的残余势力却拒绝消亡。科洛维亚各领地的一位小王库里凯因崛起掌权，并任命一位阿特莫拉人担任其军团的将军。塔洛斯将军曾在天际学习，并使用吐姆。他的战吼能击溃军队，将较弱者震倒在地。一年后，超过一半的西罗帝尔帝国领土被收复或巩固，库里凯因认为时机已到，便进军尼本奈河谷，攻占首都，自封为皇帝。此时，强烈反对回归西罗帝尔统治的高岩和天际集结军队，准备联合入侵科洛维亚西部。塔洛斯在桑克雷·托的战场上迎战他们。那些前来削弱帝国的诺德人很快加入了将军的部队，因为他们听到他的吐姆后，意识到他是天际之子、人类帝国的继承人。布莱顿人被关于库里凯因新将军的传说送回了高岩，并决定用自己的巫术来对抗皇帝的魔法。帝国纪元854年，一位来自西部河峪的夜刃潜入了尼本奈的皇宫。在那里，这位巫师刺杀了皇帝，放火烧了宫殿，并割开了塔洛斯将军的喉咙。“但他从闷烧的废墟中走了出来，一只手捂着脖子，另一只手握着库里凯因的王冠。军团见此情景潸然泪下。他北方的魔法救了他，但自那夜起，带领他们的声音将变得更加沉寂。他再也无法用一声怒吼击溃一支军队，但他仍能用低语指挥一支军队。他为自己取了一个西罗帝尔名字 -- 泰伯·塞普汀，以及诺德人的君王之名 -- 伊斯米尔，北方的巨龙。带着这些名字，他还戴上了西罗帝尔人的红钻王冠，成为了他们真正的皇帝。”第三人类帝国由此诞生。<BR>

<BR>

第三帝国时期的西罗帝尔是其古老遗产年轻而充满活力的体现。在内部，它经历了难以置信的重建 -- 帝都损毁部分的修复工作已接近完成，大空位期间被毁的道路和城市得以重建，东西方四个世纪以来首次统一。西罗帝尔当前的稳定与强盛是雷曼王朝以来所未见的；事实上，它们诞生于相似的情境之下 -- 一个西方人赢得了东方王座，将二者锻造成为泰姆瑞尔最强大的力量。如今，仅二十年间，泰伯·塞普汀已在高岩、天际和落锤确立了帝国权威。所有人类地区都与他站在一起，共同对抗精灵的威胁。皇帝谦逊地将他的成功归功于他的人民 -- 科洛维亚人和尼本人，我们现在就来谈谈他们当今的文化形态。<BR>

<BR>

今天的科洛维亚人仍保留着他们祖先的许多边疆精神。他们淳朴、自给自足、健壮，并且彼此极为忠诚。每当东方因领导者的软弱而颤抖时，科洛维亚人便会退回自身，始终相信他们是在守护民族精神，直到风暴过去。他们认识到尼本奈河谷是帝国的心脏，是其文明的文化中心，但这是一个脆弱的核心，只有靠皇帝的性格力量才能维系。当他动摇时，科洛维亚人也会动摇。然而，当他强大时，如泰伯·塞普汀，他们就是他的军团。如今，西罗帝尔西部人构成了红钻阶士兵的大多数。科洛维亚贵族都是帝国军团或其西部海军的军官，他们不允许自己像在首都那样在宫廷生活上挥霍无度。他们更喜欢一尘不染的制服和悬挂在简朴悬崖堡垒天花板上的朴素旗帜；直到今天，当他们必须造访装饰华丽、色彩斑斓的皇帝宫殿时，仍会感到些许困惑。<BR>

<BR>

相比之下，西罗帝尔的东方人民则喜爱花哨的服饰、奇异的挂毯、纹身、烙印和繁琐的仪式。更接近文明的源泉，他们更倾向于哲学和古老传统的演变。尼本人在周围的一切事物中都发现神圣性，他们的不同教派多到无法列举（最著名的有先祖蛾教派、英雄教派、泰伯·塞普汀教派和零皇教派）。对科洛维亚人来说，东方的祖先崇拜和深奥习俗常常显得奇异。阿卡维尔的龙纹主题随处可见，从帝都高耸的宣礼塔桥，到村民们用来送别逝者顺流而下的纸制箱舟。成千上万的工人在洪水过后在稻田里劳作，或在其他季节清理周围丛林的枝叶。在他们之上的是商人贵族、神殿祭司和教派领袖，以及古老世袭的战斗法师贵族。皇帝从帝都的塔楼上俯瞰着他们所有人，巨龙在头顶盘旋。<BR>

<BR>

值得注意的地方：帝都<BR>

<BR>

雷法伊著名的宣言：“帝国行省只有一座城市 -- ”可能会让科洛维亚西部的公民觉得有些冒犯，直到他们听到这句话的后半部分：“ -- 泰姆瑞尔只有一座城市，世界上只有一座城市；那，我的兄弟们，就是西罗帝尔人的城市。”从岸边望去，很难分清哪里是城市，哪里是宫殿，因为它们都从湖中的岛屿向天空延伸，一片金黄。整个街区坐落在连接岛屿的宝石桥上。贡多拉和河船在其被水淹没的低层住宅的水道中航行。蛾祭司在先祖的云雾中走过；家族卫士手持异常长大的大太刀在十字路口交叉，装饰着丝带和龙旗；新到的西方军团士兵在潮湿的空气中汗流浃背。河口因岸边的廷米土壤而染成红色，河龙在水中让它们的皮肤生锈。穿过湖泊，帝都继续延伸，与南部红河的村庄和大空位时期留下的废墟融为一体。<BR>

<BR>

皇帝的宫殿是阳光编织的王冠，周围环绕着他的魔法花园。其中一条花园小径被称为“绿色御道” -- 在这里，过往皇帝头颅造型的园艺雕塑经由巫术塑造，能够说话。当需要向泰伯·塞普汀进言时，鸟儿会被吸引到树篱头颅上，用它们的歌声作为其声音，并移动其枝条以做出必要的表情。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Political Hierarchy of Skyrim<BR>
by Lareus Beredi, Scholar of the Imperial Library<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Long Life to our Sovereign, Pelagius the Fourth, Emperor of Tamriel, Blessed One of the Nine Divines, Sustainer of Prosperity! Bringer of Justice to the Seditious!<BR>
<BR>
In the year of Akatosh, 3E 362, I have been given the honorable task of documenting the political landscape of the Fatherland of Man, Skyrim, for the education of Imperial envoys, diplomats and chartered merchants. In doing so I hope to foster greater understanding between our two great people united under the Dragon Banner.<BR>
<BR>
As per Nord tradition, the greatest possible authority in Skyrim is the title of High King. However, due to unstable and frequent transfers of power between the Holds, it is more often than not that the title of High King is an unclaimed entity. As a result, it would be better for the reader to imagine Skyrim as not one unified monarchy but of nine autonomous kingdoms, each swearing fealty to our Emperor. <BR>
<BR>
As of this writing, there are nine kings, each for the nine Holds of Skyrim: Haafinheim, the Reach, Falkreath, White Hold, the Pale, Winter's Hold, Eastmarch, Hrothgar, and the Rift. The selection of a king is dependent on what hold it is. The eastern Holds typically follow Absolute Primogeniture succession, where power is transferred to the previous king's eldest child, while in the western Holds it is decided in an event called a Kingsmoot. The Kingsmoot is an affair most Nordic, where every man or woman can travel to the capital and boast their prestige, battle prowess, virility, and wisdom and why they should become king surrounded by their peers, full of roasted meat, sweet mead, and threats of duels and fist fights.<BR>
<BR>
Below the kings are the jarls, who rule over wide tracks of land called jarldoms and are similar to Cyrodiil's own Counts. Jarls are chosen directly by the king and their holdings are split among their children at death, with the jarldom passing to the eldest child. A good amount of jarls can trace their heritage back to the 500 Companions. The jarl typically chooses the most prosperous or fortified town as his seat of power.<BR>
<BR>
Beneath the jarls are thanes, minor nobles who preside over the small towns and villages. In some cases, the position of thane is honorary and there is no bestowment of lands.<BR>
<BR>
Housecarls<BR>
At this time I would like to discuss another important part of nordic politics: the Housecarl. The Housecarl is no mere bodyguard, but is more like the House Guards of the Nibenay valley; a de-facto member of the family. Indeed, it is not unheard of for Housecarls to be adopted into the noble family or even marry into one, such as the famed King Hrodebert Ironheart and his housecarl Queen Mildres.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
天际的政治等级<BR>
拉雷乌斯·贝雷迪著，帝国图书馆学者<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
祝我们的君主，泰姆瑞尔皇帝，九圣灵祝福者，繁荣的维系者佩拉吉乌斯四世万寿无疆！为叛乱者带来正义者！<BR>
<BR>
阿卡托什历，第三纪元362年，我有幸承担了一项光荣的任务，记录人类祖国天际的政治格局，以供帝国特使、外交官和特许商人学习。借此，我希望促进在龙旗下团结的我们两个伟大民族之间更深的理解。<BR>
<BR>
根据诺德传统，天际最高的权威是至高王的头衔。然而，由于各领之间权力交接不稳定且频繁，至高王的头衔往往无人认领。因此，读者最好将天际想象成不是一个统一的君主国，而是九个自治王国，每个王国都向我们的皇帝宣誓效忠。<BR>
<BR>
在撰写本文时，天际的九个领各有九位国王：哈芬海姆、河峪、佛克瑞斯、白地领、苍原领、冬领、东陲、洛斯伽和裂谷。国王的选拔方式取决于具体的领。东部的领通常遵循绝对长子继承制，权力移交给前任国王的长子/女，而西部的领则通过称为“王选会”的活动来决定。王选会是最具诺德特色的事件，每个男人或女人都可以前往都城，在同伴面前夸耀自己的威望、战斗力、阳刚之气和智慧，以及为什么他们应该成为国王，周围满是烤肉、甜蜂蜜酒，以及决斗和拳斗的威胁。<BR>
<BR>
国王之下是领主，他们统治着称为“领”的广阔土地，类似于西罗帝尔的伯爵。领主由国王直接任命，其领地在死后分给子女，领主的头衔传给长子/女。相当多的领主可以将其血统追溯到五百战友团。领主通常会选择最繁荣或防御最坚固的城镇作为其权力所在地。<BR>
<BR>
领主之下是乡绅，是管理小城镇和村庄的低级贵族。在某些情况下，乡绅的职位是荣誉性的，并不授予土地。<BR>
<BR>
侍卫<BR>
在此，我想讨论诺德政治的另一个重要组成部分：侍卫。侍卫不仅仅是保镖，更像是尼本奈河谷的家族卫士；是家族的事实成员。事实上，侍卫被收养进贵族家庭，甚至与之通婚的情况并非闻所未闻，例如著名的赫罗德伯特·铁心国王和他的侍卫王后米尔德雷斯。<BR>
<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Port of Anvil<BR>
<BR>
A history of the Abecean's most significant trade city<BR>
<BR>
by Calixta Avidrian
<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
Anvil, largest and most prosperous city of West Colovia, can rightfully be called a jewel in the Red Dragon Crown. From here, the long Gold Road stretches out towards the distant markets of the Heartlands, allowing the passage of luxurious trade goods from the entire western Empire. None of the Colovian cities -- not even industrious Skingrad or the proud Hill of Kvatch -- can compare to Anvil's prosperity and population.
<BR>
Yet Anvil was not always great. For much of the early First Empire, the so-called Kingdom of the Strident Coast (or Stridenthia) was governed from the isle of Mischarstette by the powerful Shore-King dynasty, direct descendants of the Nordic conquerors. Anvil, at the time, was a negligible fishing village ruled by the minor House of Olo, vassals to the Shore-Kings.
<BR>
The fortunes of this small township would change dramatically. The Slug-Famine of 1E 2200 decimated the population of the West and toppled the august Shore-Kings. Allying himself first with the Marshal of the Isles, with whom he was fortuitously saved by a pilgrimage to Sancre Tor, Bendu Olo forged an alliance unlike any in history between dozens of peoples enraged by the plague and its origins in far-off Thras. This fine example of Cyrodiilic diplomacy in its infancy saw man, elf, and dreugh come together to wreak terrible vengeance on the Sload and topple the first Pillar of Thras. From humble origins, the Oloman dynasty thus rose to outshine its predecessors.
<BR>
As Mischarstette had been reduced to a mass grave of plague dead, Olo moved the capital of his hard-won kingdom to Anvil. Contacts with his allies of the All Flags Navy blossomed into fruitful trade arrangements, and soon the kingdom -- once the Kingdom of the Strident Coast -- became better known as simply the Kingdom of Anvil.
<BR>
Anvil's wealth was little diminished during the First Interregnum, and the rise of the Second Empire saw the town take on a new role as an important port in the conquest of the West. The death of Reman III in 1E 2920, however, initiated an era of decline. Attacks from the provincial powers and trade blockades from spiteful rival Colovian kingdoms tarnished Anvil's prosperity, while the death of the last blood relative of Olo signaled the end of a golden era. Weak-willed magistrates appointed by the Potentates could not stop this decline.
<BR>
The story of Anvil's submission to Tiber Septim is well attested in the histories. It is said that as the Ruby Ranks approached, the city's most influential families (in those days, only modest merchants) came unarmed to the Conqueror's camp under a flag of truce. They offered to throw open Anvil's gates and put all their ships into the service of a new West Navy, if only the Emperor would accept an innovative new model of government for the Kingdom: elective monarchy. The merchant captains argued that such a system would turn Anvil from a declining backwater into a thriving, competitive center of commerce -- one whose royal elections would swell the coffers of the Red Treasury in the bargain. Tiber Septim agreed to these terms, and Anvil became the West Navy's home port.
<BR>
In 3E 249, the Camoran Usurper marched his armies from Valenwood to the north, demanding the unconditional surrender of all in his path. The weak King Dorian, elected in a particularly paltry election year, was taken off guard and overwhelmed as the Imperial forces defending his kingdom crumbled on land and sea. During the Usurper's eighteen-year reign of terror, Anvil was ruled by necromancers and pirates, whose brief struggles to control the fiercely independent locals culminated in the total sack of Old Anvil near the end of the year 250. This atrocity nearly ended Anvil's existence, and would have, if not for the intervention of Commodore Fasil Conomorus. The Commodore was able to wrest control of the kingdom from the vile necromancers who had occupied it, burning thousands of dead in the process.
<BR>
Conomorus raised a new city on the ashes of Old Anvil, with high, thick walls, an even bigger port, and a new, impregnable castle: Goldstone. The new city swiftly regained her former population, then quickly raced past it, as merchants, priests, guildsfolk, and scholars arrived from around the Empire to capitalize on the opportunities offered by the gleaming new city. Though he ruled as King until his death, Conomorus wisely restored the royal elections for his successors, which further encouraged investment by the powerful merchant families. The city's rapid growth, made possible by immigrants from around the Western Empire, made Anvil the second most diverse city in the Imperial Province, only after Cyrodiil City itself. A century and a half later, Anvil stands as a shining monument to the indefatigable resilience of its people.
<BR><BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
安维尔港<BR>
<BR>
阿碧希安海最重要贸易城市的历史<BR>
<BR>
卡利克斯塔·阿维德里安 著
<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
安维尔，西科洛维亚最大、最繁荣的城市，完全可以被称为红龙王冠上的一颗明珠。从这里，漫长的金色大道向远方的心脏地市场延伸，使得来自整个西部帝国的奢侈品得以流通。没有任何一座科洛维亚城市 -- 哪怕是勤劳的斯金格拉德或骄傲的科瓦奇山城 -- 能与安维尔的繁荣和人口相媲美。
<BR>
然而，安维尔并非一直伟大。在第一帝国早期的大部分时间里，所谓的斯特赖登特海岸王国（或斯特赖登西亚）是由强大的滨海王王朝从米沙尔斯特特岛统治的，他们是诺德征服者的直系后裔。当时的安维尔只是一个微不足道的渔村，由滨海王的附庸 -- 奥洛家族统治。
<BR>
这个小乡镇的命运即将发生剧变。第一纪元2200年的蛞蝓饥荒摧毁了西方的人口，并推翻了尊贵的滨海王。本都·奥洛首先与群岛执法官结盟（他与后者曾因一次前往桑克雷·托的朝圣而意外获救），随后在数十个因瘟疫及其遥远的瑟拉斯起源而愤怒的民族之间，缔结了史无前例的联盟。这个西罗帝尔早期外交的绝佳范例见证了人类、精灵和蟹灵联合起来，对斯洛德进行了可怕的报复，并推倒了瑟拉斯的第一根巨柱。出身卑微的奥洛曼王朝由此崛起，超越了它的前任。
<BR>
由于米沙尔斯特特已沦为瘟疫死者的万人坑，奥洛将他来之不易的王国的首都迁至安维尔。他与全旗海军盟友的联系发展成富有成果的贸易安排，很快，这个王国 -- 曾经的斯特赖登特海岸王国 -- 变得更广为人知的名字就是安维尔王国。
<BR>
安维尔的财富在第一次大空位期间几乎没有减少，第二帝国的崛起使该镇承担了新的角色，成为征服西方的重要港口。然而，第一纪元2920年雷曼三世的去世开启了一个衰落的时代。来自地方势力的攻击和来自心怀怨恨的科洛维亚敌对王国的贸易封锁玷污了安维尔的繁荣，而奥洛最后一位血亲的去世则标志着一个黄金时代的终结。由摄政任命的意志薄弱的执政官无法阻止这种衰落。
<BR>
安维尔向泰伯·塞普汀臣服的故事在史书中有充分记载。据说，当红钻阶逼近时，城里最有影响力的家族（当时只是些普通的商人）手无寸铁地打着休战旗来到征服者的营地。他们提出敞开安维尔的大门，并将所有船只用于新的西部海军，只要皇帝接受王国一种创新的政府模式：选举君主制。商人船长们争辩说，这样的制度将使安维尔从一个衰落的穷乡僻壤转变为一个繁荣、有竞争力的商业中心 -- 其皇家选举还将借此充实红钻国库的财源。泰伯·塞普汀同意了这些条件，安维尔成为西部海军的母港。
<BR>
第三纪元249年，篡位者卡莫兰率领大军从瓦伦伍德北上，要求所有挡路者无条件投降。在选举年特别惨淡中被选出的软弱国王多里安措手不及，保卫其王国的帝国军队在陆地和海上崩溃。在篡位者十八年的恐怖统治期间，安维尔被死灵法师和海盗统治，他们为控制 fiercely independent locals 的短暂斗争最终在250年底以旧安维尔的彻底洗劫而告终。这一暴行几乎终结了安维尔的存在，如果不是法西尔·科诺莫鲁斯准将的干预，它本会如此。这位准将成功地从占领该王国的邪恶死灵法师手中夺回了控制权，在此过程中焚烧了成千上万的死者。
<BR>
科诺莫鲁斯在旧安维尔的废墟上建立了一座新城，拥有高大厚实的城墙、更大的港口和一座坚不可摧的新城堡：金石。新城迅速恢复了昔日的人口，然后很快超越，商人、祭司、公会成员和学者从帝国各地涌来，利用这座崭新城市提供的机会。尽管他以国王的身份统治直到去世，但科诺莫鲁斯明智地为其继任者恢复了皇家选举，这进一步鼓励了有权势的商人家庭的投资。这座城市在来自西部帝国各地的移民推动下迅速发展，使安维尔成为帝国行省中第二多元化的城市，仅次于帝都本身。一个半世纪后，安维尔作为其人民不屈不挠精神的闪亮丰碑屹立不倒。
<BR><BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Privileges of the Dead<BR>
<BR>
by Sato Voria<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Many, of late, have called for a ban on Necromancy. The ancient art, these voices claim, is an abominable practice which defiles the body and soul, disrespects the laws of Arkay, and preys on the well-deserved rest of the dead. Such superstitions are quite common in the provinces, especially in heathen Morrowind and in the northwestern regions which have had much to suffer from the foul Mannimarcean practices. Petitions have been made in the Elder Council to forbid the Necromantic practice, an action supported by many leading scholars in the Mages Guild. <BR>
<BR>
I freely admit that acts of Necromancy as practiced by primitives like the Reachmen or by the avaricious servants of Mannimarco should be persecuted whenever possible. But to consider such amateur displays as similar to the refined art of Nibenese necromancy, the ancient privilege of the battlemage aristocracy, is nothing short of an insult. Do we condemn a master of Destruction for the actions of every arsonist hedge-witch? Do we persecute a skilled alchemist for the misdeeds of every skooma-brewer? Of course not. Yet, to the opponents of Necromancy, every two-bit Worm cultist appears to be a peer of the esteemed Taxidermists of Mir Corrup.<BR>
<BR>
First, it must be understood that Necromancy is not merely a school of magic, but an aspect of the foundational death-rites at the heart of Ald Niben. To attack the institution of Necromancy is to strike at the very ties that bind the Niben people to their ancestors and birthrights. Worse, even, is that these arguments can just as easily apply to other ancient and noble practices -- such as the worship of the ancestor moth. After all, what is the weaving of ancestor silk but the capturing of a soul in enchantment? Are we to persecute the noble Order of the Ancestor Moth, too? Shall we burn our sacred silks to appease these boorish and anti-intellectual notions? This may seem farcical to some, but it is an easy step to make.<BR>
<BR>
Second is the great importance that Necromancy has played in the advancement of magic and arcane learning. The involvement of the Mages Guild in all this is quite puzzling -- after all, their members benefit greatly from the Corporeal Redemptions Act through which the Empire donates the bodies of executed criminals to trusted scholars. In this way, many great discoveries have been made in the fields of Restoration, Alteration and Alchemy,as well as lesser fields of study such as anatomy -- a fact that the esteemed Magisters are keen to forget. How, I wonder, will the ambitious masters of the Imperial University continue their studies without the Imperial Prison's constant supply of research material? Will they go out at night and rob the tombs, as some Breton wizards are wont to do?<BR>
<BR>
Third, we must recognize that not only the study, but also the fruit of Necromancy is of great importance. Not in the way of servile revenants, as some no doubt assume, but as the priceless artifice and masterworks found in the strongholds of both the battlemage and merchant aristocracies. Many noble Niben families have their entire capital bound up in the shape of a reanimated chrysophant fish, a rare albino mudcrab, or a delicate facsimile glyphmoth. Such wonders -- worth their weight in gold when alive, and many times more after the Taxidermist has wrought his craft -- stay in families for generations, and are often worth more than the palaces and manors they reside in. What will happen to this treasure trove if the provincial factions have their way? Will we burn the greater part of the Niben's wealth on a pyre? If so, we would not only lose countless works of art, but also most capital in the Niben basin -- an economical collapse would not be far off.<BR>
<BR>
Finally, we must not forget the sheer artistry of proper necromancy. The true necromancer does not murder or prey on the weak, he does not use his art to strain his life to unnatural lengths, and he does not call forth shambling horrors to serve as menial labor. A true necromancer delights in the delicate play of tendons and bones, the joy of making something that was once full of energy and vigor come to life again, the intellectual pleasure of tracing the workings of the mortal sphere -- so skillfully designed by the Divines, who no doubt would condone and encourage such curiosity in their children. Through Necromancy -- proper, thoughtful, noble Necromancy -- we meditate on the significance of death, and so we come to understand the designs of the Divines that much more clearly. No form of magic could be more virtuous.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
亡者的特权<BR>
<BR>
佐藤·沃里亚 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
最近，许多人呼吁禁止亡灵法术。这些声音声称，这种古老的艺术是可憎的做法，玷污了身体和灵魂，不尊重阿尔凯的法则，并侵扰死者应得的安息。这种迷信在行省相当普遍，尤其是在异教的晨风以及深受邪恶的曼尼马克做法之苦的西北地区。元老院已收到请愿书，要求禁止亡灵法术，这一行动得到了法师公会许多顶尖学者的支持。<BR>
<BR>
我欣然承认，像河峪人那样的原始人或曼尼马克贪婪的仆人所实践的亡灵法术行为，应尽可能受到追查。但是，将这种业余表演与尼本奈亡灵法术的精湛艺术 -- 战斗法师贵族的古老特权 -- 相提并论，简直是一种侮辱。我们会因为每个纵火的乡野女巫的行为而谴责毁灭系大师吗？我们会因为每个斯库玛酿造者的恶行而迫害技艺精湛的炼金术士吗？当然不会。然而，对于亡灵法术的反对者来说，每个微不足道的蠕虫教信徒似乎都与备受尊敬的米尔·科鲁普的标本剥制师平起平坐。<BR>
<BR>
首先，必须理解亡灵法术不仅仅是一个魔法学派，更是古尼本核心基础死亡仪式的一个方面。攻击亡灵法术的体制，就是打击将尼本人与其祖先和与生俱来的权利联系在一起的纽带。更糟糕的是，这些论点同样可以轻易地应用于其他古老而高贵的实践 -- 例如先祖蛾的崇拜。毕竟，编织先祖丝绸不就是在附魔中捕获灵魂吗？我们是否也要迫害高贵的先祖蛾教团？我们是否要焚烧我们神圣的丝绸来安抚这些粗鲁且反智的观念？这对某些人来说可能看似荒谬，但这一步很容易迈出。<BR>
<BR>
其次，亡灵法术在推动魔法和神秘学识进步方面发挥了巨大重要性。法师公会卷入这一切实在令人费解 -- 毕竟，他们的成员从《肉体救赎法案》中获益匪浅，该法案允许帝国将被处决罪犯的尸体捐赠给值得信赖的学者。通过这种方式，在恢复系、变化系和炼金术领域，以及解剖学等较小的研究领域，取得了许多重大发现 -- 这是尊贵的法师们急于忘记的事实。我想知道，如果没有帝国监狱源源不断提供的研究材料，帝都大学雄心勃勃的校长们将如何继续他们的研究？他们会像一些布莱顿巫师惯常做的那样，在夜间外出盗墓吗？<BR>
<BR>
第三，我们必须认识到，不仅亡灵法术的研究，其成果也至关重要。并非如某些人无疑设想的那样，作为卑躬屈膝的亡魂，而是作为战斗法师和商人贵族据点中发现的无价技艺和杰作。许多高贵的尼本家族将其全部资本以复活的金鳞鱼、稀有的白化泥沼蟹或精致的仿制纹蛾的形式存在。这些奇物 -- 活着时价值等重黄金，在标本剥制师施展技艺后价值更是高出数倍 -- 在家族中代代相传，其价值往往超过它们所在的宫殿和庄园。如果地方派系得逞，这笔宝藏将何去何从？我们是否要将尼本的大部分财富付之一炬？如果那样，我们不仅会损失无数艺术品，还会损失尼本盆地的大部分资本 -- 经济崩溃将为期不远。<BR>
<BR>
最后，我们绝不能忘记恰当亡灵法术纯粹的艺术性。真正的亡灵法师不会谋杀或猎杀弱者，他不会用他的艺术将自己的生命强行延长到非自然的长度，他也不会召唤蹒跚的恐怖之物来做卑微的劳动。真正的亡灵法师陶醉于肌腱和骨骼的精妙运作，陶醉于让曾经充满活力和生机的事物重获生命的喜悦，陶醉于追溯凡世运作机理的智力乐趣 -- 凡世是圣灵们如此巧妙地设计的，他们无疑会宽恕并鼓励其子民这种好奇心。通过亡灵法术 -- 恰当的、深思熟虑的、高贵的亡灵法术 -- 我们沉思死亡的意义，从而更清晰地理解圣灵的意图。没有哪种魔法形式能比这更有德性。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Proper Lock Design and Construction<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
I have encountered many thieves whose sole interest in locks is how to open them and thereby pilfer the protected contents of the room or chest. I have taken it upon myself to devise a system of locks that can defeat such villainous intent.<BR>
<BR>
The materials used to create a lock are of utmost importance. Shoddy brass or copper will give way to a well placed kick, thereby rendering the lock itself useless. I recommend steel over iron when choosing a material. More robust materials tend to be prohibitively expensive and necessitate the door being made of similar metals. I have been chagrined to stumble across the shattered shell of a wooden chest, its dwarven lock intact and still locked.<BR>
<BR>
Once these basics are settled, pay particular attention to the offset of the tumblers. A seven degree offset to the keyhole will allow a torque style key to work smoothly, while at the same time causing numerous headaches for the thief attempting to insert non-torque lockpicks.<BR>
<BR>
In similar fashion, the springs of the tumblers should be made by different smiths. Each smith will unknowingly create a spring with different tension than his fellow smiths. This variance will also create difficulties for anyone attempting to pick the lock.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
锁具设计与制造<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
我遇到过许多盗贼，他们对锁的唯一兴趣就是如何打开它们，从而窃取房间或箱子里受保护的内容。我已自行承担起设计一种能够挫败这种邪恶意图的锁具系统的责任。<BR>
<BR>
制造锁具所用的材料至关重要。劣质的黄铜或铜会因一记精准的踢击而屈服，从而使锁本身毫无用处。在选择材料时，我推荐钢而非铁。更坚固的材料往往价格高得令人望而却步，并且要求门也由类似金属制成。我曾懊恼地偶然发现一个碎裂的木箱外壳，其矮人锁完好无损，且仍然锁着。<BR>
<BR>
一旦这些基础问题解决，要特别注意锁簧的偏置。相对于钥匙孔七度的偏置可以让扭力式钥匙顺畅工作，同时给试图插入非扭力式开锁工具的盗贼带来无数麻烦。<BR>
<BR>
同样，锁簧的弹簧应由不同的铁匠制作。每个铁匠都会在不知不觉中制作出张力与其他铁匠不同的弹簧。这种差异也会给任何试图撬锁的人带来困难。<BR>

Purloined Shadows<BR>
by Waughin Jarth<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Chapter 1<BR>
The candle was lit, and the thief was standing there, blinking, caught. She was young, rather dirty, wearing ragged black clothes that were surely quite smart and expensive weeks ago when she had stolen them from one of the city's best tailors. The look of surprise slipped from her face, and she took on a blank expression as she put the gold back on the table.<BR>
<BR>
"What are you doing here?" the man with the candle asked, stepping from the shadows.<BR>
<BR>
"That's a stupid question," the girl replied, frowning. "I'm obviously robbing you."<BR>
<BR>
"Since nothing I have is missing," the man smiled, glancing at the gold on the table. "I would have to say that you're not robbing me. Attempting to rob me perhaps. The question I have is, why? You know who I am, I assume. You didn't just come in through an unlocked door."<BR>
<BR>
"I've stolen from everyone else. I've taken soul gems from the Mages Guild, I've robbed the treasury of the most secure fortress, I cheated the Archbishop of Julianos ... I even pickpocketed the Emperor Pelagius at his coronation. I thought it was your turn."<BR>
<BR>
"I'm flattered," the man nodded. "Now that your ambition has been thwarted, what will you do? Flee? Perhaps retire?"<BR>
<BR>
"Teach me," the girl replied, a little grin finding its way unconsciously on her face. "I picked all your locks, I slipped past all your wards ... You designed them, you know how difficult that was for someone without training. I didn't come here for six gold pieces. I came here to prove myself. Make me your student."<BR>
<BR>
The Master of Stealth looked at the little girl burglar. "Your skill is not in need of training. Your planning is adequate, but I can help you with that. What is without hope is your ambition. You are past stealing for your livelihood, now you steal for the pleasure of it, for the challenge. That's a personality trait which is incurable, and will lead you to an early grave."<BR>
<BR>
"Haven't you ever wanted to steal that which can't be stolen?" the girl asked. "Something that would make your name known forever?"<BR>
<BR>
The Master did not answer: he only frowned.<BR>
<BR>
"Clearly I was fooled by your reputation," she shrugged, and opened a window. "I thought you might want a willing accomplice on some great act of thievery which would go down in history. Like you said, my skill at planning is only adequate. I didn't have in mind an escape route, but this will have to do."<BR>
<BR>
The burglar slipped down the sheer wall, dashed across the shadowy courtyard, and within a few minutes was back at her room in the run-down tavern. The Master was waiting for her there, in the dark.<BR>
<BR>
"I didn't see you go past me," she gasped.<BR>
<BR>
"You turned on the street when you heard the owl call," he replied. "The most important tool in the thieves' repertoire is distraction, either planned or improvised. I suppose your lessons have begun."<BR>
<BR>
"And what is the final test?" the girl smiled.<BR>
<BR>
When he told her, she could only stare. She had, it seemed, not misunderstood his reputation for daring. Not at all.<BR>
<BR>
Chapter 2<BR>
For the week leading up to the Eighth of Hearthfire, the skies above Rindale were dark and alive as clouds of crows blotted out the sun. Their guttural squawks and groans deafened all. The peasants wisely bolted their doors and windows, praying to survival that most unholy of days.<BR>
<BR>
On the night of the summoning, the birds fell silent, their black unblinking eyes following the witches' march into the glen. There were no moons to light the way, only the leader's single torch in the gloom. Their white robes appeared as indistinct shapes, like the faintest of ghosts.<BR>
<BR>
A single tall tree stood in the middle of the clearing, every branch thick with crows, watching the procession without moving. The lead witch placed the torch at the base of the tree, and her seventeen followers formed a circle and began their slow, strange, wailing chant.<BR>
<BR>
As they sang, the glow of the torch began to change. It did not diminish at all, but its color became more and more grey, so it seemed a pulsating wave of ash had fallen on the witches. Then it grew darker still, so that for a moment, though the fire yet burned, it was darkest night in the forest. The penumbra continued until the torch was burning with a color without a name, emptiness beyond mere blackness. It cast a glow, but it was an unnatural scintillation falling on the witches. Their robes of white became black. The Dunmer among them had eyes of green, and ivory white flesh. The Nords appeared black as coal. The crows watching overhead were as pure white as the witches' cloaks.<BR>
<BR>
The Daedra Princess Nocturnal stepped out of the pit of uncolor.<BR>
<BR>
She stood in the center of the circle, the tree of pallid crows her throne, aloof, as the witches continued their chanting, dropping their robes to prostrate themselves naked before their great mistress. Wrapping her night cloak around her, she smiled at their song. It spoke of her mystery, of veiled beauty, of eternal shadows and a divine future when the sun burns no more.<BR>
<BR>
Nocturnal let her cloak slide from her shoulders and was naked. Her witches did not raise their head from the ground, but continued their hymn of darkness.<BR>
<BR>
"Now," said the girl to herself.<BR>
<BR>
She had been up in the tree all day, dressed in a ridiculous suit of mock crows. It was uncomfortable, but when the witches had arrived, she forgot all her aches, and concentrated on being perfectly still, like the other crows in the tree. It had taken considerable planning and study between her and the Master of Stealth to find the glen, and to learn what to expect in the summoning of Nocturnal.<BR>
<BR>
Gently, silently, the burglar eased herself down the branches of the tree, coming closer and closer to the Daedra Princess. She let herself break her concentration for just a moment, and wondered where the Master was. He had been confident in the plan. He said that when Nocturnal dropped her cloak, there would be a distraction, and it could be quickly taken in that instant provided the girl was in position at the precise right moment.<BR>
<BR>
The girl climbed along the lowest of the branches, carefully pushing aside the crows that were, as the Master said, transfixed by the Princess in her naked beauty. The girl was now close enough, if she only reached out her arm, to touch Nocturnal's back.<BR>
<BR>
The song was rising to a crescendo, and the girl knew that the ceremony would soon be over. Nocturnal would clothe herself before the witches ended the chant, and the chance to take the cloak would be over. The girl gripped the tree branch tightly as her mind raced. Could it be that the Master was not here at all? Was this, was this conceivably the entire test? Was it only to show that it could be done, not to do it?<BR>
<BR>
The girl was furious. She had done everything perfectly, but the so-called Master of Stealth had proven himself a coward. Perhaps he had taught her a little in the months that it took to plan this, but what was it worth? Only one thing made her smile. On that night when she had stolen into his stronghold, she had kept one single gold piece, and he had never suspected it. It was symbolic, as symbolic as stealing the cloak of Nocturnal in its way, proving that the Master Thief could be robbed.<BR>
<BR>
The girl was so lost on her mind that she thought she imagined it for a moment when a man's voice yelled out from the darkness, "Mistress!"<BR>
<BR>
The next words she knew she didn't imagine: "Mistress! A thief! Behind you!"<BR>
<BR>
The witches raised their heads, and screamed, ruining the sanctity of the ceremony, as they charged forward. The crows awoke and burst from the tree in an explosion of feathers and toad-like cries. Nocturnal herself whirled around, affixing the girl with her black eyes.<BR>
<BR>
"Who art thee who dares profane?" The Princess hissed, as the pitch shadows flew from her body enveloping the girl in their lethal chill.<BR>
<BR>
In the last instant before she was swallowed alive by darkness, the girl looked to the ground and saw that the cloak was gone, and she answered, as she understood, "Oh, who am I? I'm the distraction."<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
窃影<BR>
沃金·贾斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
第一章<BR>
蜡烛点燃了，盗贼站在那里，眨着眼睛，被抓了个正着。她很年轻，相当肮脏，穿着破烂的黑衣服，几周前她从城里最好的裁缝那里偷来时，这些衣服肯定相当漂亮昂贵。惊讶的表情从她脸上褪去，她将金子放回桌上，露出茫然的神情。<BR>
<BR>
“你在这里做什么？”拿着蜡烛的男人从阴影中走出，问道。<BR>
<BR>
“这是个愚蠢的问题，”女孩皱着眉头回答，“我显然是在抢劫你。”<BR>
<BR>
“既然我什么也没少，”男人微笑着瞥了一眼桌上的金子，“我得说你并没有在抢劫我。也许是在试图抢劫我。我的问题是，为什么？我想你知道我是谁。你不会只是从一扇没锁的门进来的。”<BR>
<BR>
“其他人都被我偷过了。我从法师公会拿走过灵魂石，我抢劫过最安全堡垒的金库，我骗过尤利安诺斯的大主教......我甚至在佩拉吉乌斯皇帝的加冕礼上扒窃过他。我想该轮到你了。”<BR>
<BR>
“受宠若惊，”男人点点头，“既然你的雄心受挫，你打算怎么办？逃跑？也许退休？”<BR>
<BR>
“教我，”女孩回答，脸上不自觉地露出一丝笑意，“我撬开了你所有的锁，我溜过了你所有的防护......是你设计的它们，你知道这对一个没受过训练的人来说有多难。我来这里不是为了六枚金币。我是来证明自己的。让我做你的学生。”<BR>
<BR>
潜行大师看着这个小女孩窃贼。“你的技能不需要训练。你的计划还算可以，但我可以在这方面帮你。没有希望的是你的野心。你早已不是为了生计而偷窃，现在你是为了乐趣、为了挑战而偷窃。这是一种无法治愈的性格特征，会让你早早就进坟墓。”<BR>
<BR>
“你就从未想过偷走那些无法被偷走的东西吗？”女孩问道，“一件能让你的名字永垂不朽的东西？”<BR>
<BR>
大师没有回答，只是皱起了眉头。<BR>
<BR>
“显然我被你的名声骗了，”她耸耸肩，打开一扇窗户，“我以为你可能需要一个心甘情愿的同伙，一起干一桩能载入史册的惊天盗窃案。就像你说的，我的计划能力只是一般。我没想过逃跑路线，但只好这样了。”<BR>
<BR>
窃贼沿着陡峭的墙壁滑下，冲过阴暗的庭院，几分钟后就回到了她在破旧客栈的房间。大师正在那里，在黑暗中等着她。<BR>
<BR>
“我没看见你从我身边经过，”她倒吸一口气。<BR>
<BR>
“你听到猫头鹰叫声时转到了街上，”他回答，“盗贼技能中最重要的工具是分散注意力，无论是计划的还是即兴的。我想你的课程已经开始了。”<BR>
<BR>
“那么最终的考验是什么？”女孩笑了。<BR>
<BR>
当他告诉她时，她只能瞪大眼睛。看来，她并没有误解他以胆大著称的名声。一点也没有。<BR>
<BR>
第二章<BR>
在炉火月八日之前的一周里，林代尔上空的天空一片漆黑，乌鸦的云层遮住了太阳。它们刺耳的呱呱叫声和呻吟声震耳欲聋。农民们明智地闩上门窗，祈求在最不神圣的日子里能幸存下来。<BR>
<BR>
在召唤之夜，鸟儿们安静下来，它们黑色、不眨动的眼睛注视着女巫们行进到峡谷中。没有月亮照亮道路，只有领队的一支火炬在黑暗中闪烁。她们的白袍看起来像模糊的形状，如同最微弱的鬼魂。<BR>
<BR>
一棵高大的孤树矗立在空地的中央，每根树枝上都站满了乌鸦，一动不动地注视着队伍。领头的女巫将火炬放在树根处，她的十七名追随者围成一个圆圈，开始缓慢、奇异、哀号的吟唱。<BR>
<BR>
当她们吟唱时，火炬的光芒开始变化。它丝毫没有减弱，但颜色变得越来越灰，仿佛一股脉动的灰烬浪潮落在了女巫们身上。然后它变得更暗，以至于有那么一刻，尽管火焰仍在燃烧，森林中却陷入了最黑暗的夜晚。半影持续着，直到火炬燃烧着一种无名之色，超越单纯黑色的虚空。它发出光芒，但那是一种落在女巫身上的、不自然的闪烁。她们的白袍变成了黑色。其中的丹莫有着绿色的眼睛和象牙般洁白的皮肤。诺德人变得像煤一样黑。头顶上注视的乌鸦变得像女巫的斗篷一样纯白。<BR>
<BR>
迪德拉公主诺克图娜尔从无色之坑中走出。<BR>
<BR>
她站在圆圈的中心，苍白乌鸦之树是她的王座，神情冷漠，而女巫们继续吟唱，脱去长袍，赤身裸体地匍匐在她们伟大的女主人面前。她用夜之斗篷裹住自己，对她们的歌声报以微笑。歌声诉说着她的神秘，诉说着蒙纱的美，诉说着永恒的阴影，诉说着太阳不再燃烧的神圣未来。<BR>
<BR>
诺克图娜尔让斗篷从肩头滑落，赤裸着身体。她的女巫们没有从地上抬起头，而是继续她们黑暗的赞美诗。<BR>
<BR>
“就是现在，”女孩对自己说。<BR>
<BR>
她一整天都待在树上，穿着一身可笑的模仿乌鸦的套装。很不舒服，但当女巫们到达时，她忘记了所有的疼痛，专注于像树上的其他乌鸦一样保持完全静止。她和潜行大师花了相当多的计划和研究才找到这个峡谷，并了解在召唤诺克图娜尔时会发生什么。<BR>
<BR>
窃贼轻柔、无声地沿着树枝向下移动，越来越接近迪德拉公主。她让自己稍微分了分神，想知道大师在哪里。他对这个计划很有信心。他说当诺克图娜尔脱下斗篷时，会造成一个分心的瞬间，只要女孩在精确的时刻就位，就能在那个瞬间迅速取走斗篷。<BR>
<BR>
女孩沿着最低的树枝爬行，小心翼翼地拨开那些 -- 正如大师所说 -- 被公主赤裸的美丽惊呆了的乌鸦。女孩现在离得足够近，只要伸出手臂，就能触碰到诺克图娜尔的背。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
by Anonymous<BR>

In the early days of Atmoran supremacy over the scheming Falmer, when the snow elves were fleeing into their mysterious winter hovels, there was once a great king of a certain valley filled with life. This king was known as Radr, the great Stag-King of those divided days of old, though he was not always known as such. For much of his life, he was Radr the Wanderer, for he lived a nomadic lifestyle akin to that of a snow elf (if such creatures could ever be noble and reasonable).<BR>
<BR>
One fateful morning, he had been hunting a beautiful doe from across the river. Its fur looked as soft as that of a rabbit, but its frame was as large as an ox. Were he to approach this magnificent beast head on, he would surely perish. However, if he succeeded in slaying the beast, then he would have a small fortune in hide to sell, and enough food to eat to become the size of a bear. So in his wisdom he crept slowly but steadily behind the beast as it was taking its morning drink. Using his trusty sword-staff, its long pole topped with a blade of unknown metals, he closed the distance. Striking the doe in the neck, its head rolled down into the river and with a sizable splash, floated gently on the current. He had done it. This had been a good day.<BR>
<BR>
As he began dragging his prize out from the river and into the forest, he noticed a small, shivering calf struggling to stand. It did not take Radr, wisest man in the valley, long to realize that this calf was the recent offspring of his morning's kill. Some believe that Radr carried the calf to camp with the intention of feasting on it as well, before changing his mind. However, the Radr of the songs I know would never think of harming such a defenseless creature. And so the calf was named Brumadhr, and he would grow to be the greatest elk to ever live.<BR>
<BR>
Years later, Brumadhr had grown to be a steed for our wandering hero. They had fought countless battles together against goblins, trolls, and elves of malicious speech patterns. Soon, though, Radr and Brumadhr would encounter their greatest enemy yet. They had been passing through a typical mountain village in Skyrim, nothing -- you might think -- of any particular value to our story. There was, however, talk of a mysterious figure who would appear during the coldest of winter nights. This figure they described as a demon in a cloak of the tundra's gale. This did not bother Radr, as he had been through far worse situations than some brawl with a Frost Atronach. He did, however, heed their warning for the night.<BR>
<BR>
Later that night, Radr awoke to a creaking in the walls of the hall where he slept. Like cackling, as if the beams themselves wished to swallow Radr into the chasm of the afterlife. Radr wisely chose to take his sword-staff with him as he left the eeriness of the hall to face the harsh blizzard outside. Though as he made it to the center of the village, the blizzard ceased. Soon there was no snowfall to be seen, not even as much as a soft breeze. He stood there, confused, before deciding to go back to sleep.<BR>
<BR>
As he returned to the hall, however, a voracious and foul creature flew at him from within the building. Tackling our brave hero to the ground, the white and snarling creature declared itself "Ushiltherin". Getting a more thorough look at the vile beast, Radr knew at once that it was a Falmer that had been terrorizing the village. Unfortunately for Radr, his sword-staff had landed as he fell in a snowdrift across the street. If he was going to survive this encounter, he would need to retrieve it, and fast. As luck would have it, though, Brumadhr has witnessed the snow elf grapple and claw at Radr, and charged straight for him. Ushiltherin was knocked back with gashes across its torso, but the beast was not yet finished with its rampage. Radr dove for his trusty weapon and turned as Ushiltherin lunged, soon to meet its end. Ushiltherin's skeletal, inhuman arms may have been longer than Radr's, but it was no match for a polearm's superior reach.<BR>
<BR>
As the animalistic life of the Falmer drained from the creature's eyes, dawn slowly crept upon them. Soon after, the village awakened and bore witness to the fruit of Radr the Wanderer's slaying. 令人生畏的波蒙德尔海之龙，如今被称为德雷德蒙德船长，是一位伟大的阿特莫拉战士和伊斯米尔。他在伊斯格拉谟的五百战友团之后不久来到泰姆瑞尔，带领着自己的舰队，他的“比五百更多一点”的战友团。但与伊斯格拉谟不同，他选择不去占领土地和建造城市。相反，他出发去探索整个泰姆瑞尔，寻找异域并对外敌作战。德雷德蒙德在他的探索和战斗中，既是人类的先驱，如同伊斯格拉谟一样，也是未来时代的先行者。<BR><BR>
列举德雷德蒙德舰队中的几艘阿特莫拉长船及其各自的船长：斧头“冰暴血脉剑锤”指挥“冰山号”，雷霆盾女阿尔德努埃克洛克指挥“莫拉凯恩号”，双环辛德维尔指挥“掠夺者号”，还有许多其他船长指挥许多其他船只；整个舰队规模太大，无法快速一一列举。到这个故事发生时，舰队甚至在访问尤库达期间，吸收了两艘奇怪的尤库船，船长和船员是奇怪的、皮肤黝黑的无名之人，他们无法用语言与阿特莫拉人交流，但他们用对屠杀精灵的渴望来歌唱。<BR><BR>
我们的故事开始于一个异常狂暴的海上黄昏；南方的精灵海，通常平静而友善，此时却翻涌撕裂，对德雷德蒙德和他的“比五百更多一点”战友团的闯入感到愤怒。海浪撞击着船只，试图将船体劈开，但就阿特莫拉人的经历而言，狂暴的大海还算温和；幽魂之海在风平浪静的日子里都有这么狂暴。德雷德蒙德在他的长船“雪鲸号”上不耐烦地等待着，船只在海浪中来回摇晃。他的斗篷在风中向后飘扬，仿佛一双翅膀，张开着准备将他带入空中。他在等待他的智者法尔内归来，他派法尔内去高精灵城市阿里诺尔抓人质以便审讯。在开始接下来的旅程之前，他们需要更多信息。<BR><BR>
在分叉尾的“雪鲸号”上，除了怒容满面、斗篷飞扬、碾压精灵的德雷德蒙德之外，还有他的船乡绅“快耳”克赫莱特，他能听到数里格外的低语；他的嘟囔者赫根拉尔，是嘟囔魔法专家；他的桨手：锤子弗里德伦格、持桨奥拉德、扬森·其名留摇篮（他是伊斯格拉谟五百战友团中扬斯多特的兄弟）、哈洛克、伍尔菲尔，以及那个唯一名字就是桨手的人，因为他除了说六句与他桨手职业相关的特定句子外从不说话；他的三位吐姆乡绅西里乌尔、瑟亚克和萨杜加；以及他的野兽看守人姆内南，他照看着德雷德蒙德的宠物：家猫菲克、狂暴野兽韦尔瓦，以及猴类东西唐莫。<BR>
<BR>
还有德雷德蒙德的精灵奴隶翻译，他们的名字不便提及；阴郁的雪精灵，说阿特莫拉语和雪精灵语，从伊斯格拉谟宣称的土地上被抓来；聪明的鸟精灵，说雪精灵语、高精灵语和鸟精灵语，身披羽毛，显然是在担任驻雪精灵大使时从同一片土地被抓来；以及年轻的海精灵，说鸟精灵语和海精灵语，从大陆西海岸的一个海精灵前哨被抓来，他向阿特莫拉人讲述了派安多尼亚和海精灵船只等情况，但对迷雾帷幕或海精灵海蛇 -- 这些只在奥格努姆附近出现 -- 一无所知，也并不知道任何真正对派安多尼亚有用的信息，因为他出生在前哨，而不是派安多尼亚本土。最后，还有他的战妻维亚莉，在他等待法尔内时站在他身边。<BR><BR>
“他到底在这该死的海上什么地方！”德雷德蒙德咆哮道，与其说是提问不如说是陈述。他漫不经心地抓挠着“雪鲸号”的船舷，将焦油撕扯入海浪。“他迟到了。”<BR><BR>
战妻维亚莉回答：“法尔内会回来的，丈夫。你不用担心。”<BR><BR>

“看到了吗？黎明要来了。如果他们还在那里，黑暗就再也无法保护他们了。我去接他们。”<BR><BR>

“他们回来了！”克赫莱特在船上的某个地方喊道，他比任何人都先看到了法尔林上的战士们，他的眼睛几乎和他敏锐的耳朵一样好。“他们也很着急！”<BR><BR>

Most of their guests didn't have much to say. One was a drunk who had been wandering around the docks looking for whatever High Elves drink, one was in charge of numbers, or something, and had been speaking to the third captive, a sailor from one of the crystalline ships docked in the harbor. The fourth refused to speak at all, so he died first, thrown overboard to flail in the water, handless and hapless. The one in charge of numbers died second, for he knew nothing about Pyandonea, and the drunk died third, thrown overboard after telling the Atmorans some incoherent story about the Sea Elf King Orgnum marrying a princess from a city called Sunhold. The sailor was actually helpful, though, so he got to live the longest.<BR>
<BR>
He spoke of the Sea Elf raids that came to the his Isles so often. He spoke of their ships with bug-sails and bug-hulls and serpent skin for rope. He spoke of their tactics, and of the many ways they were known to board ships, destroy ships from afar, and trick unwary Admirals. He spoke of the sea serpents themselves, who only came with the strongest of the Sea Elf fleets, the fleets led by Orgnum. In battle, the serpents would dive underwater and rise beneath High Elf ships, wrapping around them and crushing them. He told the Atmorans, too, of the mists that the Sea Elves commanded.<BR>
<BR>
They conjured mists wherever they liked, cloaking ships and distracting enemies. They even had a Mist-Veil, which cut their land from the rest of the world; it separated Pyandonea from the Isles, from the big continent, and even from the vague land called Aldmeris.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
The Mist-Veil loomed ahead. It blocked any view of the true horizon, and stretched to the right and left farther than even Kehlet's eyes could see. It was impenetrable, impossible, colossal. With all their magic, the High Elves had never pierced it, and as of today, they never have.<BR>
<BR>
The Atmoran fleet stayed its course, unshaken.<BR>
<BR>
"Mist-Veil's ahead! Thu'um-Thanes, clear the skies and clear our path! Mumblers, mutter us some full sails, to compensate for the wind we're ripping out of them!"<BR>

The muttering of his Mumblers became a babbling stream and the Thu'um-Thanes ran to the bow of each longboat and the ports and starboards of the fleet's sidemost and Thu'umed a chorus-like-thunder. As one, the great fleet cut into the Mist, and was soon engulfed by it. The Clear Sky Thu'ums warded off the Mist, lending the fleet a bubble of clear air and allowing the Atmorans some breathing room. The Atmorans pushed onward, with nothing but endless Mist in sight.<BR>

He cast his eyes downward and saw it his objective just ahead. Pyandonea; hostile cliff faces jutting from the sea, each crowned by abundant green, jagged, unwelcoming rocks that warned sailors away and strange, obscuring mists that hid much of the land from sight. And speaking of sight, not a single safe harbor or kind beach was in sight. It looked like they'd have to do a little searching.<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
"Go ahead."<BR>
<BR>
Kehlet rushed off, barking orders at the Snow Whale's crew. Dreadmund grinned. This land seemed hostile, but Dreadmund was certain that he could tame it, or at least some of it for a time, as he had so many other lands.<BR>
<BR>
And then a fleet of strange ships shot from behind the closest islands. Their hulls, which were of myriad colors from blacks to greens to garish rainbows to yellows to whites, seemed to be the unbroken shells of massive beetles, and the sails seemed to be the wings of the same, a single pair of rising from the deck, straight up with a slight tilt. The decks were built of green-tinted wood, probably with rooms built of the same below deck. The rigging and other ropes were the white, tightly coiled skin of whatever sloughed off of the Pyandonean serpents, as the Sea Elf had told them. The elves even wore bright, colorful dress, distracting the eye from the dismal pallor of their skin, as white as pure snow.<BR>

It reared its head and bit at Dreadmund, who caught hold of its fangs, both twice the length of a horker tusk. Dreadmund tore out the right fang and used the other as a lever to push the serpent's head to the deck. He stomped his foot onto the creature's lower jaw to keep it steady and drove the serpent's loose fang into its right eye. It shrieked, shaking planks and weapons and teeth. Kehlet, with his Quick-Ears, passed out.<BR>
<BR>
"Jahson, Hjaloc, Lunghaem, Savage! Chop this thing up while I've a hold on it, and clear the deck!"<BR>
<BR>

They cut through where its coils came to the gunwale and the serpent's shrieks grew louder again, earsplitting and dizzying. As coil after coil was severed and pushed over the gunwale, the serpent's cries subsided. The last thing it saw was Dreadmund's horned shadow playing across the deck. Dreadmund shoved its now bodiless head off the deck.<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
But Dreadmund did not have time to help them. The Sea Elf fleet was fast approaching, and the groaning, injured Snow Whale turned to meet it.<BR>

突袭派安多尼亚，卷二<BR>
一个在天际海盗中颇为流行的故事，阿提库斯·普林尼乌斯记述。<BR>

他们的大多数客人没什么可说的。一个是醉汉，一直在码头附近闲逛，寻找高精灵喝的酒；一个是管数字或类似事务的，一直在和第三个俘虏（一名来自停泊在港口的某艘水晶船的船员）说话。第四个拒绝说话，所以他第一个死了，被扔下船，在无助地水中挣扎，没有手，运气也不好。管数字的那个第二个死，因为他不知道关于派安多尼亚的任何事。醉汉第三个死，在给阿特莫拉人讲了一个关于海精灵国王奥格努姆与一个叫阳堡的城市公主结婚的语无伦次的故事后，被扔下船。不过，那个水手确实提供了帮助，所以他活得最长。<BR>

阿特莫拉舰队保持航向，毫不动摇。<BR>
