The violent waves of his emergence shoved the faering aside and nearly submerged it, but those aboard it, as well as those aboard the longboats in the distance, ignored the waves and watched in awe as Dreadmund, in flight, sank his fangs into Orgnum's carcass, ripped out his heart, and flung it north-east into the horizon with a mighty flick of his long neck. Then he dropped Orgnum into the sea. And then Dreadmund fell and landed in the Snow Whale's faering. Those aboard the faering sat agape, staring in awe, awe that he had survived.<BR>
<BR>
He looked up, grinning. "I think we're here to stay."<BR>
<BR>
A month later, Dreadmund and his followers had adapted to the land of Pyandonea and claimed a bloody chunk of it as their own. At first, their outpost had been a mere camp on a beach, but it had grown and it was alternately called Smallwall and Narrowwall (for the wall was too small to be called broad, and the beach was too narrow to ever hold a broad wall). At first, they knew nothing of the land, but they stole the oracle bones of Hermium who was a friend of the Sea Elves and who the Atmorans hated as though he was an old enemy. From the oracle bones, they learned to navigate the reaching kelp without being caught (which, luckily, they had not encountered during the initial battle) and they learned to effectively fight the Sea Elves and their sea serpents, to successfully raid and pillage their towns and villages. They learned that the huge beetles the Sea Elves used to build ships lived in the jungled interiors of the islands, though the Atmorans rarely saw them and never fought them, for they hated the jungle. They even learned some Sea-Elvish: words for insults, words for battle cries, and words for ordering the Sea Elves they captured about.<BR>
<BR>
They had learned, too, that there were as many kinds of serpent as there were kinds of dragon. Though the sea serpents -- who were lesser -- could not do so, many of the serpents could, more or less, Thu'um with their eyes. The most common examples were those serpents that shot jets of fire, streams of frozen wind, or both from their eyes (but never both at once, of course). There were serpents that could drain men's vitality with a glance, serpents that could Stare men unto stone, serpents that could Stare men's weapons out of their hands, serpents that could look somewhere and move there in an instant, and on and on.<BR>
<BR>
As the Atmorans explored further and further into Pyandonea, the islands packed tighter and tighter together, until some branches of the sea looked more like canyon rivers than ocean waters. They found waxy octopus elves, a giant who howled "Ilyadi" and who was like the karstaag-men except that he had more eyes, beaked reptiles with domed shells, and a wide variety of bizarre fish. They also found a great many rewards for their exploration: a shield that struck those who beheld it with fear, a flask that made the imbiber briefly immune to magicka, a sword which spread the injuries of a single enemy to all nearby enemies with each cut, and a chest filled with gold which, if emptied, refilled by the same time the next day. Those rewards have different names today: the first was called Fearstruck before it was destroyed, the second was called the Flask of Something-or-Other, the third disappeared even before it could be named, and the fourth was dubbed Orgnum's Coffer.<BR>
<BR>
And we can't forget their raids on the cities of the Sea Elves, where they claimed those treasures and captured Sea Elves as Stuhn had taught them. The cities ranged from a city built of beetle shells to a city of mixed High Elf crystals and Wood Elf plants, from a city of of ships, bridges, and scaffoldings afloat at sea to an underground city swarming with serpents. The Atmorans raided them all, one by one, and stole from them amid chaos and violence.<BR>
<BR>
There were rumors among the Sea Elves, extracted from those that the Atmorans captured, that the King Orgnum was gathering a fleet to push the Atmorans out. The Atmorans told them that Orgnum was dead, and they agreed, but insisted that he was also gathering the fleet and that they should flee. In response, the Atmorans simply shrugged, assuming that the Sea Elves were just nuts or that maybe Orgnum had turned himself into some sort of Draugr-Mage, or that he had escaped through trickery. <BR>

<BR>
Barenziah smiled involuntarily at the thought.  "I'd like that.  I think.  But it would be inconvenient, wouldn't it?  Babies are a lot of trouble, and I don't even have my own house yet."  <BR>
<BR>
"How old are you, Berry?  Seventeen?  Well, you've a year or two yet before you're fertile, unless you're very unlucky.  Elves don't have children readily with other Elves after that, even, so you'll be all right if you stick with them."  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah remembered something else.  "Straw wants to buy a farm and marry me."  <BR>
<BR>
"Is that what you want?"  <BR>
<BR>
"No.  Not yet.  Maybe someday.  Yes, someday.  But not if I can't be queen.  And not just any queen.  The Queen of Mournhold."  She said this determinedly, almost stubbornly, as if to drown out any doubt.  <BR>
<BR>
Katisha chose to ignore this last comment.  She was amused at the girl's hyperactive imagination, took it as a sign of a well-functioning mind.  "I think Straw will be a very old man before 'someday' comes, Berry.  Elves live for a very long time."  Katisha's face briefly wore the envious, wistful look humans got when contemplating the thousand-year lifespan Elves had been granted by the gods.  True, few ever actually lived that long as disease and violence took their respective tolls.  But they could.  And one or two of them actually did.  <BR>
<BR>
"I like old men too," Berry said.  <BR>
<BR>
Katisha laughed.  <BR>
Barenziah fidgeted impatiently while Therris sorted through the papers on the desk.  He was being meticulous and methodical, carefully replacing everything just as he'd found it.  <BR>
<BR>
They'd broken into a nobleman's household, leaving Straw to hover outside as lookout.  Therris had said it was a simple job but very hush-hush.  He hadn't even wanted to bring any other Guild members along.  He said he knew he could trust Berry and Straw, but no one else.  <BR>
<BR>
"Tell me what you're looking for and I'll find it," Berry whispered urgently.  Therris' night sight wasn't as good as hers and he didn't want her to magick up even a small orb of light.  <BR>
<BR>
She had never been in such a luxurious place.  Not even the Darkmoor castle of Count Sven and Lady Inga where she had spent her childhood compared to it.  She'd gazed around in wonder as they made their way through the ornately decorated and hugely echoing downstairs rooms.  But Therris didn't seem interested in anything but the desk in the small book-lined study on the upper floor.  <BR>
<BR>
"Sssst," he hissed angrily.  <BR>
<BR>
"Someone's coming!" Berry said, a moment before the door opened and two dark figures stepped into the room.  Therris gave her a violent shove toward them and sprang to the window.  Barenziah's muscles went rigid; she couldn't move or even speak.  She watched helplessly as one of the figures, the smaller one, leaped after Therris.  There were two quick, silent stabs of blue light, then Therris folded over into a still heap.  <BR>
<BR>
Outside the study the house had come alive with hastening footsteps and voices calling out in alarm and the clank of armor hurriedly put on.  <BR>
<BR>
The bigger man, a Dark Elf by the looks of him, half-lifted, half-dragged Therris to the door and thrust him into the waiting arms of another Elf.  A jerk of the first Elf's head sent his smaller blue-robed companion after them.  Then he sauntered over to inspect Barenziah, who was once again able to move although her head throbbed maddeningly when she tried to.  <BR>
<BR>
"Open your shirt, Barenziah," the Elf said.  Barenziah gawked at him and clutched it closed.  "You're a girl, aren't you, Berry?" he said softly.  "You should have stopped dressing as a boy months ago, you know.  You were only drawing attention to yourself.  And calling yourself Berry!  Is your friend Straw too stupid to remember anything else?"  <BR>
<BR>
"It's a common Elven name," Barenziah defended.  <BR>
<BR>
The man shook his head sadly.  "Not among Dark Elves it isn't, my dear.  But you wouldn't know much about Dark Elves, would you?  I regret that, but it couldn't be helped.  No matter.  I shall try to remedy it."  <BR>
<BR>
"Who are you?" Barenziah demanded.  <BR>
<BR>
"Ai.  So much for fame," the man shrugged, smiling wryly.  "I am Symmachus, Milady Barenziah.  General Symmachus of His Awesome and Terrible Majesty Tiber Septim I's Imperial Army.  And I must say it's a merry chase you've led me throughout Tamriel.  Or this part of it, anyway.  Although I guessed, and guessed correctly, that you'd head for Morrowind eventually.  You had a bit of luck.  A body was found in Whiterun that was thought to be Straw's.  So we stopped looking for the pair of you.  That was careless of me.  Yet I'd not have thought you'd have stayed together this long."  <BR>
<BR>
"Where is he?  Is he all right?" she asked in genuine trepidation.  <BR>
<BR>
"Oh, he's fine.  For now.  In custody, of course."  He turned away.  "You ... care for him, then?" he said, and then suddenly stared at her with fierce curiosity.  Out of red eyes that seemed strange to her, except in her own seldom-seen reflection.  <BR>
<BR>
"He's my friend," Barenziah said.  The words came out in a tone that sounded dull and hopeless to her own ears.  Symmachus!  A general in the Imperial Army, no less--said to have the friendship and ears of Tiber Septim himself.  <BR>
<BR>
"Ai.  You seem to have several unsuitable friends--if you'll forgive my saying so, Milady."  <BR>
<BR>
"Stop calling me that."  She was irritated at the general's seeming sarcasm.  But he only smiled.  <BR>
<BR>
As they talked the bustle and flurry in the house died away.  Although she could still hear people, presumably the residents, whispering together not far off.  The tall Elf perched himself on a corner of the desk.  He seemed quite relaxed and prepared to stay awhile.  <BR>
<BR>
Then it occurred to her.  Several unsuitable friends, had he said?  This man knew all about her!  Or seemed to know enough, anyway.  Which amounted to the same thing.  "W-what's going to happen to them?  To m-me?"  <BR>
<BR>
"Ah.  As you know, this house belongs to the commander of the Imperial troops in this area.  Which means to say that it belongs to me."  Barenziah gasped and Symmachus looked up sharply.  "What, you didn't know?  Tsk, tsk.  Why, you are rash, Milady, even for seventeen.  You must always know what it is you do, or get yourself into."  <BR>
<BR>
"B-but the G-guild w-wouldn't ... wouldn't h-have--"  Barenziah was trembling.  The Thieves Guild would never have attempted a mission that crossed Imperial policy.  No one dared oppose Tiber Septim, at least no one she knew of.  Someone at the Guild had bungled.  Badly.  And now she was going to pay for it.  <BR>
<BR>
"I daresay.  It's unlikely that Therris had Guild approval for this.  In fact, I wonder--"  Symmachus examined the desk carefully, pulling out drawers.  He selected one, placed it on top of the desk, and removed a false bottom.  There was a folded sheet of parchment inside.  It seemed to be a map of some sort.  Barenziah edged closer.  Symmachus held it away from her, laughing.  "Rash indeed!"  He glanced it over, then folded and replaced it.  <BR>
<BR>
"You advised me a moment ago to seek after knowledge."  <BR>
<BR>
"So I did, so I did."  Suddenly he seemed to be in high good humor.  "We must be going, my dear Lady."  <BR>
<BR>
He shepherded her to the door, down the stairs, and out into the night air.  No one was about.  Barenziah's eyes darted toward the shadows.  She wondered if she could outrun him, or elude him somehow.  <BR>
<BR>
"You're not thinking of attempting to escape, are you?  Ai.  Don't you want to hear first what my plans for you are?"  She thought that he sounded a bit hurt.  <BR>
<BR>
"Now that you mention it--yes."  <BR>
<BR>
"Perhaps you'd rather hear about your friends first."  <BR>
<BR>
"No."  <BR>
<BR>
He looked gratified at this.  It was evidently the answer he wanted, thought Barenziah, but it was also the truth.  While she was concerned for her friends, especially Straw, she was far more concerned for herself.  <BR>
<BR>
"You will take your place as the rightful Queen of Mournhold."  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Symmachus explained that this had been his, and Tiber Septim's, plan for her all along.  That Mournhold, which had been under military rule for the dozen or so years since she had been away, was gradually to be returned to civilian government--under the Empire's guidance, of course, and as part of the Imperial Province of Morrowind.  <BR>
<BR>
"But why was I sent to Darkmoor?" Barenziah asked, hardly believing anything she had just been told.  <BR>
<BR>
"For safekeeping, naturally.  Why did you run away?"  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah shrugged.  "I saw no reason to stay.  I should have been told."  <BR>
<BR>
"You would have been by now.  I had in fact sent for you to be removed to the Imperial City to spend some time as part of the Emperor's household.  But of course you had, shall we say, absconded by then.  As for your destiny, it should be, and should have been, quite obvious to you.  Tiber Septim does not keep those he has no use for -- and what else could you be that would be of use to him?"  <BR>
<BR>
"I know nothing of him.  Nor, for that matter, of you."  <BR>
<BR>
"Then know this:  Tiber Septim rewards friends and foes alike according to their deserts."  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah chewed on that for a few moments.  "Straw has deserved well of me and has never done anyone any harm.  He is not a member of the Thieves Guild.  He came along to protect me.  He earns our keep by running errands, and he ... he ..."  <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus waved her impatiently to silence.  "Ai.  I know all about Straw," he said, "and about Therris."  He stared at her intently.  "So?  What would you?"  <BR>
<BR>
She took a deep breath.  "Straw wants a little farm.  If I'm to be rich, then I would like for one to be given to him."  <BR>
<BR>
"Very well."  He seemed astonished at this, and then pleased.  "Done.  He shall have it.  And Therris?"  <BR>
<BR>
"He betrayed me," Barenziah said coldly.  Therris should have told her what risks the job entailed.  Besides, he'd pushed her right into their enemies' arms in an attempt to save himself.  Not a man to be rewarded.  Not, in fact, a man to be trusted.  <BR>
<BR>
"Yes.  And?"  <BR>
<BR>
"Well, he should be made to suffer for it ... shouldn't he?"  <BR>
<BR>
"That seems reasonable.  What form should said suffering take?"  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah balled her hands into fists.  She would've liked to beat and claw at the Khajiit herself.  But considering the turn events had taken, that didn't seem very queenly.  "A whipping.  Er ... would twenty stripes be too many, do you think?  I don't want to do him any permanent injury, you understand.  Just teach him a lesson."  <BR>
<BR>
"Ai.  Of course."  Symmachus grinned at this.  Then his features suddenly set, and became serious.  "It shall be done, Your Highness, Milady Queen Barenziah of Mournhold."  Then he bowed to her, a sweeping, courtly, ridiculously wonderful bow.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah's heart leapt.  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
She spent two days at Symmachus' apartment, during which she was kept very busy.  There was a Dark Elven woman named Drelliane who saw to her needs, although she did not exactly seem a servant since she took her meals with them.  Nor did she seem to be Symmachus' wife, or lover.  Drelliane looked amused when Barenziah asked her about it.  She simply said she was in the general's employ and did whatever was asked of her.  <BR>
<BR>
With Drelliane's assistance, several fine gowns and pairs of shoes were ordered for her, plus a riding habit and boots, along with other small necessities.  Barenziah was given a room to herself.  <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus was out a great deal.  She saw him at most mealtimes, but he said little about himself or what he had been doing.  He was cordial and polite, quite willing to converse on most subjects, and seemed interested in anything she had to say.  Drelliane was much the same.  Barenziah found them pleasant enough, but "hard to get to know," as Katisha would have put it.  She felt an odd twinge of disappointment.  These were the first Dark Elves with whom she'd associated closely.  She had expected to feel comfortable with them, to feel at last that she belonged somewhere, with somebody, as part of something.  Instead she found herself yearning for her Nordic friends, Katisha and Straw.  <BR>
<BR>
When Symmachus told her they were to set out for the Imperial City on the morrow, she asked if she could say good-bye to them.  <BR>
<BR>
"Katisha?" he asked.  "Ai.  But then ... I suppose I owe her something.  She it was who led me to you by telling me of a lonely Dark Elven girl named Berry who needed Elven friends -- and who sometimes dressed as a boy.  She has no association with the Thieves Guild, apparently.  And no one associated with the Thieves Guild seems to know your true identity, save Therris.  That is well.  I prefer that your former Guild membership not be made public knowledge.  Please speak of it to no one, Your Highness.  Such a past does not ... become an Imperial Queen."  <BR>
<BR>
"No one knows but Straw and Therris.  And they won't tell anyone."  <BR>
<BR>
"No."  He smiled a curious little smile.  "No, they won't."  <BR>
<BR>
He didn't know that Katisha knew, then.  But still, there was something about the way he said it ...  <BR>
<BR>
Straw came to their apartment on the morning of their departure.  They were left alone in the salon, although Barenziah knew that other Elves were within earshot.  He looked drawn and pale.  They hugged one another silently for a few minutes.  Straw's shoulders were shaking and tears were rolling down his cheeks, but he said nothing.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah tried a smile.  "So we both get what we want, eh?  I'm to be Queen of Mournhold and you'll be lord of your own farmstead."  She took his hand, smiled at him warmly, genuinely.  "I'll write you, Straw.  I promise.  You must find a scribe so you can write me too."  <BR>
<BR>
Straw shook his head sadly.  When Barenziah persisted, he opened his mouth and pointed at it, making inarticulate noises.  Then she realized what it was.  His tongue was gone, had been cut off.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah collapsed onto a chair and wept noisily.  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
"But why?" she demanded of Symmachus when Straw had been ushered away.  "Why?"  <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus shrugged.  "He knows too much.  He could be dangerous.  At least he's alive, and he won't need his tongue to ... raise pigs or whatever."  <BR>
<BR>
"I hate you!" Barenziah screamed at him, then abruptly doubled over and vomited on the floor.  She continued to revile him between intermittent bouts of nausea.  He listened stolidly for some time while Drelliane cleaned up after her.  Finally, he told her to cease or he would gag her for her journey to the Emperor.  <BR>
<BR>
They stopped at Katisha's house on their way out of the city.  Symmachus and Drelliane didn't dismount.  All seemed normal but Barenziah was frightened as she knocked on the door.  Katisha answered the knock.  Barenziah thanked the gods silently that at least she was all right.  But she'd also obviously been weeping.  In any case, she embraced Barenziah warmly.  <BR>
<BR>
"Why are you crying?" Barenziah asked.  <BR>
<BR>
"For Therris, of course.  You haven't heard?  Oh dear.  Poor Therris.  He's dead."  Barenziah felt icy fingers creeping round her heart.  "He was caught stealing from the Commandant's house.  Poor fellow, but that was so foolish of him.  Oh, Berry, he was drawn and quartered this very dawn by the Commandant's order!"  She started to sob.  "I went.  He asked for me.  It was terrible.  He suffered so before he died.  I'll never forget it.  I looked for you and Straw, but no one knew where you'd both gone to."  She glanced behind Barenziah.  "That's the Commandant, isn't it?  Symmachus."  Then Katisha did a strange thing.  She stopped crying and grinned.  "You know, the moment I saw him, I thought, This is the one for Barenziah!"  Katisha took a fold of her apron and wiped it across her eyes.  "I told him about you, you know."  <BR>
<BR>
"Yes," Barenziah said, "I know."  She took Katisha's hands in each of hers and looked at her earnestly.  "Katisha, I love you.  I'm going to miss you.  But please don't ever tell anyone else anything about me.  Ever.  Swear you won't.  Especially not to Symmachus.  And look after Straw for me.  Promise me that."  <BR>
<BR>
Katisha promised, puzzled though willing.  "Berry, it wasn't somehow because of me that Therris was caught, was it?  I never said anything about Therris to ... to ... him."  She glanced over at the general.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah assured her that it wasn't, that an informant had told the Imperial Guard of Therris' plans.  Which was probably a lie, but she could see that Katisha plainly needed some kind of comfort.  <BR>
<BR>
"Oh, I'm glad of that, if I can be glad of anything just now.  I'd hate to think--  But how could I have known?"  She leaned over and whispered in Barenziah's ear, "Symmachus is very handsome, don't you think?  And so charming."  <BR>
<BR>
"I wouldn't know about that," Barenziah said dryly.  "I haven't really thought about it.  There've been other things to think about."  She explained hurriedly about being Queen of Mournhold and going to live in the Imperial City for a while.  "He was looking for me, that's all.  On orders from the Emperor.  I was the object of a quest, nothing more than some sort of... of a... goal.  I don't think he thinks of me as a woman at all.  He said I didn't look like a boy, though," she added in the face of Katisha's incredulity.  Katisha knew that Barenziah evaluated every male she met in terms of sexual desirability, and availability.  "I suppose it's the shock of finding out that I really am a queen," she added, and Katisha agreed that yes, that's true, that must've been something of a shock, although one there was no likelihood of her experiencing firsthand.  She smiled.  Barenziah smiled with her.  Then they hugged again, tearfully, for the last time.  She never saw Katisha again.  Or Straw.  <BR>
The royal party left Rifton by the great southern gate.  Once through, Symmachus tapped her shoulder and pointed back at the portals.  "I thought you might want to say good-bye to Therris too, Your Highness," he said.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah stared briefly but steadily at the head impaled on a spike above the gate.  The birds had been at it, but the face was still recognizable.  "I don't think he'll hear me, although I'm quite sure he'll be pleased to know I'm fine," she said, seeming to sound light.  "Let's be on our way, General, shall we?"  <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus was clearly disappointed by her lack of reaction.  "Ai.  You heard of this from your friend Katisha, I suppose?"  <BR>
<BR>
"You suppose correctly.  She attended the execution," Barenziah said casually.  If he didn't know already, he'd find out soon enough, she was sure of that.  <BR>
<BR>
"Did she know Therris belonged to the Guild?"  <BR>
<BR>
She shrugged.  "Everyone knew that.  It's only lower-ranking members like me who are supposed to keep their membership secret.  The ones higher up are well known."  She turned to smile archly at him.  "But you must know all that, shouldn't you, General?" she said sweetly.  <BR>
<BR>
He seemed unaffected by this.  "So you told her who you were and whence you came, but not about the Guild."  <BR>
<BR>
"The Guild membership was not my secret to tell.  The other was.  There's a difference.  Besides, Katisha is a very honest woman.  Had I told her, it would have lessened me in her eyes.  She was always after Therris to take up a more honest line of work.  I value her good opinion."  She afforded him a glacial stare.  "Not that it's any concern of yours, but do you know what else she thought?  She also thought I'd be happier if I settled down with just one man.  One of my own race.  One of my own race with all the right qualities.  One of my own race with all the right qualities, who knows to say all the right things.  You, in fact."  She grabbed the reins preparatory to assuming a brisker pace--but not without sinking one final irresistible barb.  "Isn't it odd how wishes come true sometimes--but not in the way you want them to?  Or maybe I should say, not in the way you would ever want them to?"  <BR>
<BR>
His answer so took her by surprise that she quite forgot about cantering off.  "Yes.  Very odd," he replied, and his tone matched his words exactly.  Then he excused himself and fell behind.  <BR>
<BR>
She held her head high and urged her mount onward, trying to look unimpressed.  Now what was it about his response that bothered her?  Not what he said.  No, that wasn't it.  But something about the way he said it.  Something about it made her think that she, Barenziah, was one of his wishes that had come true.  Unlikely as this seemed, she gave it due deliberation.  He had found her at last, after months of searching, it seemed, under pressure from the Emperor, no doubt.  So his wish had come true.  Yes, that must be it.  <BR>
<BR>
But in a way, apparently, not altogether to his liking.  <BR>
<BR>
"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
真实的巴兰兹雅，第二部分<BR>
无名氏<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
巴兰兹雅和斯特劳在裂谷城安顿下来过冬，在镇上较贫穷的地段租了个便宜房间。巴兰兹雅想加入盗贼公会，她知道如果私自行动被抓会有麻烦。一天在酒吧里，她引起了公会一位知名成员 -- 一个名叫塞里斯的胆大年轻卡吉特 -- 的注意。她提出，如果他愿意担保她入会，她就陪他上床。他打量着她，咧嘴一笑，答应了，但说她仍然需要通过入会考验。<BR>
<BR>
“什么样的考验？”<BR>
<BR>
“啊，”塞里斯说。“先付钱，甜心。”他用一只手臂搂住她，俯身亲吻她，将舌头深深探入她的口中，空着的手伸进她的衬衫。<BR>
<BR>
“不错，”他过了一会儿说道，收回了舌头，但手没有收回。他的另一只手滑进她的腰带内，抚摸她的臀部。<BR>
<BR>
“我们上楼去吧。可以用我的房间，”巴兰兹雅对他的大胆既感到尴尬又兴奋。<BR>
<BR>
塞里斯放肆地咧嘴一笑。“何必麻烦？你想要我，不是吗？我敢打赌你会付钱给我，对吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“不，”巴兰兹雅说。她确实想要他，但没那么强烈。<BR>
<BR>
“不？好吧，一言为定，塞里斯信守诺言。但就在这里。现在。”他撩起她的裙子，把她拉到自己腿上，让她跨坐在他身上，面对着他。他解开她的衬衫，把它拉到她的肩膀上，露出她的胸部。<BR>
<BR>
“好一对，孩子。”她面朝着墙，但能感觉到其他顾客的目光。整个地方安静了下来。连吟游诗人都停止了演奏。她感到既恶心又有一股灼热的欲望。她的手松开了他勃起的阴茎，然后它进入了她的身体，她在痛苦和狂喜中尖叫起来。然后一切都变黑了。<BR>
<BR>
当她再次清醒时，她正坐在塞里斯旁边，他正在扣她的衬衫扣子。<BR>
<BR>
“那很痛！”她愤慨地说。<BR>
<BR>
“总是这样，孩子。没人告诉过你关于卡吉特男人的事吗？不过痛得舒服，不是吗？”<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹雅对他怒目而视。她还疼着呢。他的阴茎上有微小的倒刺。<BR>
<BR>
“好吧，如果你愿意，交易可以取消，”他耸耸肩。<BR>
<BR>
“不，我没那么说。只是我更喜欢私密一些，而且我想等一等，比如下次之前等一天左右。”<BR>
<BR>
塞里斯笑了。“你还不错，孩子。”<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
斯特劳会杀了她，也许还会杀了塞里斯。泰姆瑞尔里到底是什么鬼迷了心窍让她做出这种事？她忐忑不安地环顾房间，但其他顾客已经失去了兴趣，各自忙自己的事去了。她认不出任何一个人；这不是她和斯特劳住的客栈。运气好的话，斯特劳要过一段时间，或者永远不会发现。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
塞里斯无疑是她迄今为止遇到过的最令人兴奋、最有魅力的男人。他不仅告诉她成为盗贼公会成员所需的技能，还亲自训练她，或者把她介绍给能训练她的人。<BR>
<BR>
其中有一位懂些魔法的女人。卡蒂莎是一个丰满、主妇模样的诺德人。她嫁给了一个铁匠，有两个十几岁的孩子，非常普通和受人尊敬 -- 只是她非常喜欢猫（并且合乎逻辑地推断，也喜欢它们的类人对应物卡吉特），对某些魔法有天赋，并且结交了一些相当古怪的朋友。她教巴兰兹雅隐形术，并训练她其他形式的潜行和伪装。卡蒂莎自由地融合了魔法和非魔法才能，用一套来增强另一套。她不是盗贼公会的成员，但以一种母亲般的方式喜欢塞里斯。巴兰兹雅对她产生了好感，这是她从未对任何女性有过的，在接下来的几周里，她把自己的所有事情都告诉了卡蒂莎。<BR>
<BR>
她有时也把斯特劳带到那里。斯特劳赞同卡蒂莎。但不赞同塞里斯。塞里斯觉得斯特劳“很有趣”，并向巴兰兹雅建议安排一场他所谓的“三人行”。<BR>
<BR>
“绝对不行，”巴兰兹雅坚定地说，庆幸塞里斯这次是私下提出这个话题。“他不会喜欢的。我也不会喜欢！”<BR>
<BR>
塞里斯露出他那迷人的、三角形的猫科动物微笑，懒洋洋地瘫在椅子上，伸展四肢，卷起尾巴。“你可能会惊讶。你们两个都会。成双成对太无聊了。”<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹雅用瞪视回答他。<BR>
<BR>
“或者也许你不太喜欢和你那个乡下土包子一起，甜心。你介意我带另一个朋友来吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“是的，我介意。如果你对我厌倦了，你和你的朋友可以去找别人。”她现在已经是盗贼公会的成员了。她通过了他们的入会考验。她发现塞里斯有用但不是必不可少。也许她也有点厌倦他了。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
她和卡蒂莎谈了她和男人的问题。或者说她自认为的和男人的问题。卡蒂莎摇摇头，告诉她她在寻找的是爱，而不是性，当她找到合适的男人时她就会知道，斯特劳和塞里斯都不是她的合适人选。<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹雅疑惑地歪着头。“他们说黑暗精灵女人是妓 -- 妓 -- 什么来着。妓女？”她说，尽管她心存疑虑。<BR>
<BR>
“你的意思是滥交。虽然我猜有些确实成了妓女，”卡蒂莎事后补充道。“精灵年轻时是滥交。但你会随着年龄增长而改变。也许你已经开始了，”她满怀希望地补充道。她喜欢巴兰兹雅，已经变得相当喜欢她。“不过，你应该去认识一些好的精灵男孩。如果你继续和卡吉特、人类之类的人混在一起，你很快就会发现自己在怀孕。”<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹雅想到这里不由自主地笑了。“我会喜欢的。我想。但这会很麻烦，不是吗？孩子很麻烦，而我连自己的房子都没有。”<BR>
<BR>
“你多大了，贝瑞？十七岁？嗯，你还有一两年才会生育，除非你非常不幸。即使是和其他精灵，在那之后精灵也不容易生孩子，所以如果你坚持和他们在一起，你会没事的。”<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹雅想起了另一件事。“斯特劳想买一个农场，然后娶我。”<BR>
<BR>
“那是你想要的吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“不。现在不。也许有一天。是的，有一天。但如果我不能成为女王就不行。而且不是随便什么女王。是哀伤之城的女王。”她坚定地，几乎是固执地说道，仿佛要淹没任何怀疑。<BR>
<BR>
卡蒂莎选择忽略这最后一句话。她觉得女孩过于活跃的想象力很有趣，认为这是心智健全的标志。“我想在‘有一天’到来之前，斯特劳会变成一个非常老的人，贝瑞。精灵能活很长时间。”卡蒂莎的脸上短暂地露出了人类在思考众神赐予精灵的千年寿命时那种羡慕、渴望的表情。确实，由于疾病和暴力造成的损失，很少有人能真正活那么久。但他们可以。而且他们中有一两个确实活到了。<BR>
<BR>
“我也喜欢老男人，”贝瑞说。<BR>
<BR>
卡蒂莎笑了。<BR>
当塞里斯整理桌上的文件时，巴兰兹雅不耐烦地坐立不安。他一丝不苟、有条不紊，小心翼翼地把所有东西都放回原样。<BR>
<BR>
他们闯进了一位贵族的家，让斯特劳在外面做望风。塞里斯说这是个简单的活儿，但要非常保密。他甚至不想带任何其他公会成员一起去。他说他知道自己可以信任贝瑞和斯特劳，但其他人不行。<BR>
<BR>
“告诉我你在找什么，我来找，”贝瑞急切地低声说。塞里斯的夜视能力不如她，而且他不希望她用魔法变出哪怕一个小小的光球。<BR>
<BR>
她从未到过如此奢华的地方。甚至连她度过童年的斯文伯爵和英加夫人的暗沼城堡都无法与之相比。当他们穿过装饰华丽、回音巨大的楼下房间时，她惊奇地四处张望。但塞里斯似乎对楼上的小书房里那排满书的书桌以外的任何东西都不感兴趣。<BR>
<BR>
“嘘 -- ”他愤怒地嘶嘶道。<BR>
<BR>
“有人来了！”贝瑞说，片刻之后门打开了，两个黑影走进了房间。塞里斯用力把她推向他们，自己跳向窗户。巴兰兹雅的肌肉变得僵硬；她无法动弹，甚至无法说话。她无助地看着其中一个黑影，那个较小的，朝塞里斯扑去。两道快速、无声的蓝色光芒闪过，然后塞里斯蜷缩成一堆，一动不动。<BR>
<BR>
书房外，房子里充满了急促的脚步声、惊慌的呼喊声和匆忙穿盔甲的叮当声。<BR>
<BR>
那个身材高大的男人，看起来是个黑暗精灵，半提半拖地把塞里斯带到门口，把他塞进另一个精灵等候的怀里。第一个精灵头一摆，让他的蓝袍矮个同伴跟了上去。然后他悠闲地走过来审视巴兰兹雅，她已经能再次活动了，尽管她一试图动头就疯狂地抽痛。<BR>
<BR>
“解开你的衬衫，巴兰兹雅，”精灵说。巴兰兹雅目瞪口呆地看着他，紧紧抓住衬衫。“你是个女孩，不是吗，贝瑞？”他轻声说。“你几个月前就该停止打扮成男孩了，你知道。你只会引起别人对你的注意。还叫自己贝瑞！你的朋友斯特劳是不是太蠢了，记不住别的？”<BR>
<BR>
“这是一个常见的精灵名字，”巴兰兹雅辩解道。<BR>
<BR>
男人悲伤地摇了摇头。“在黑暗精灵中可不是，我亲爱的。但你对黑暗精灵了解不多，对吗？我很遗憾，但这也没办法。没关系。我会设法弥补的。”<BR>
<BR>
“你是谁？”巴兰兹雅质问道。<BR>
<BR>
“哎。名气也不过如此，”男人耸耸肩，苦笑了一下。“我是西马库斯，巴兰兹雅女士。泰伯·塞普汀一世皇帝陛下威严而可畏的帝国军队的西马库斯将军。我必须说，你让我在泰姆瑞尔追得好苦。至少在这一带是这样。尽管我猜，而且猜对了，你最终会前往晨风。你运气不错。在白漫城发现了一具被认为是斯特劳的尸体。所以我们停止了对你们两个人的搜索。是我疏忽了。但我没想到你们能在一起这么久。”<BR>
<BR>
“他在哪里？他没事吧？”她真切地惊恐地问道。<BR>
<BR>
“哦，他很好。暂时。当然，被拘留了。”他转过身去。“那么......你在乎他？”他说，然后突然带着强烈的好奇心盯着她。用那双红色的眼睛，除了她自己很少见到的倒影外，这双眼睛对她来说很陌生。<BR>
<BR>
“他是我的朋友，”巴兰兹雅说。这话在她自己听来语气沉闷而绝望。西马库斯！帝国军队的将军，而且 -- 据说和泰伯·塞普汀本人有友谊，能说得上话。<BR>
<BR>
“哎。你似乎有几个不太合适的朋友 -- 请恕我直言，女士。”<BR>
<BR>
“别再这么叫我了。”她对将军似乎带讽刺的口吻感到恼火。但他只是笑了笑。<BR>
<BR>
在他们交谈时，房子里的喧嚣和骚动渐渐平息了。虽然她仍能听到不远处有人，大概是住户，在一起窃窃私语。那个高个子精灵坐在桌角。他似乎很放松，准备待一会儿。<BR>
<BR>
然后她想到了。他说“几个不太合适的朋友”？这个男人知道她的一切！或者说，似乎知道得够多。这和知道一切是一回事。“他、他们会怎么样？我、我会怎么样？”<BR>
<BR>
“啊。如你所知，这所房子属于这个地区帝国军队的指挥官。也就是说，它属于我。”巴兰兹雅倒吸一口气，西马库斯猛地抬起头。“怎么，你不知道？啧啧啧。哎呀，你太鲁莽了，女士，即使对十七岁来说也是如此。你必须始终知道自己在做什么，或者自己陷入了什么。”<BR>
<BR>
“但、但是公、公会不、不会......不会 -- ”巴兰兹雅在颤抖。盗贼公会绝不会尝试违背帝国政策的任务。没人敢反对泰伯·塞普汀，至少她认识的人中没有。公会的某个人搞砸了。搞得很糟。现在她要为此付出代价。<BR>
<BR>
“我敢说。塞里斯不太可能得到公会的批准来干这个。事实上，我想知道 -- ”西马库斯仔细检查书桌，拉出抽屉。他选中一个，放在桌面上，取下一个假底。里面有一张折叠的羊皮纸。似乎是一张某种地图。巴兰兹雅凑近些。西马库斯把它拿开，不让她看，笑了起来。“确实鲁莽！”他浏览了一下，然后折叠起来放回原处。<BR>
<BR>
“你刚才还建议我追求知识。”<BR>
<BR>
“我说过，我说过。”突然他似乎心情极佳。“我们得走了，我亲爱的女士。”<BR>
<BR>
他护送她到门口，下楼，来到夜晚的空气中。周围没有人。巴兰兹雅的眼睛瞥向阴影处。她想知道自己是否能跑得过他，或者以某种方式避开他。<BR>
<BR>
“你不会是想逃跑吧？哎。你不想先听听我对你的计划吗？”她觉得他听起来有点受伤。<BR>
<BR>
“既然你提起了 -- 想听。”<BR>
<BR>
“也许你更想先听听你朋友的事。”<BR>
<BR>
“不。”<BR>
<BR>
他对此显得很满意。巴兰兹雅想，这显然是他想要的答案，但这也是事实。虽然她关心她的朋友，尤其是斯特劳，但她更关心自己。<BR>
<BR>
“你将就任，成为哀伤之城合法的女王。”<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
西马库斯解释说，这始终是他和泰伯·塞普汀对她的计划。自她离开后的这十几年里，哀伤之城一直处于军事统治之下，现在将逐步回归文官政府 -- 当然，是在帝国的指导下，并作为晨风帝国行省的一部分。<BR>
<BR>
“但为什么我被送到暗沼？”巴兰兹雅问道，几乎不相信自己刚刚听到的一切。<BR>
<BR>
“自然是为了安全。你为什么要逃跑？”<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹雅耸耸肩。“我看不出有什么理由留下。我本该被告知的。”<BR>
<BR>
“到现在你本该知道了。事实上，我已经派人来接你，准备把你送到帝都，在皇帝的家庭中待一段时间。但当然，我们可以说，那时你已经逃走了。至于你的命运，它应该，并且一直应该，对你来说是相当明显的。泰伯·塞普汀不会留下对他没用的人 -- 除了那样，你还能是什么对他有用呢？”<BR>
<BR>
“我对他一无所知。对你也一样，在这件事上。”<BR>
<BR>
“那么记住这一点：泰伯·塞普汀无论对朋友还是敌人，都按其功过给予赏罚。”<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹雅琢磨了一会儿。“斯特劳对得起我，也从未伤害过任何人。他不是盗贼公会的成员。他是来保护我的。他靠跑腿赚取我们的生活费，而且他......他......”<BR>
<BR>
西马库斯不耐烦地挥手让她安静。“哎。我知道斯特劳的一切，”他说，“也知道塞里斯的一切。”他专注地盯着她。“那么？你想怎么样？”<BR>
<BR>
她深吸一口气。“斯特劳想要一个小农场。如果我要变得富有，那么我想送一个给他。”<BR>
<BR>
“很好。”他对此似乎感到惊讶，然后高兴起来。“成交。他会得到它的。那么塞里斯呢？”<BR>
<BR>
“他背叛了我，”巴兰兹雅冷冷地说。塞里斯本应告诉她这项任务涉及的风险。此外，他为了自救，把她直接推入了敌人的怀抱。不是个值得奖励的人。事实上，不是个值得信任的人。<BR>
<BR>
“是的。然后呢？”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，他应该为此受苦......不是吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“这似乎很合理。这种痛苦应该以什么形式呈现？”<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹雅把手握成拳头。她本想亲手痛打、抓挠那个卡吉特。但考虑到事态的发展，这似乎不太像女王所为。“鞭刑。呃......你觉得二十鞭子会不会太多？我不想给他造成永久性伤害，你明白。只是教训他一下。”<BR>
<BR>
“哎。当然。”西马库斯对此咧嘴一笑。然后他的表情突然凝固，变得严肃。“遵命，殿下，哀伤之城的巴兰兹雅女王陛下。”然后他向她鞠了一躬，一个夸张的、宫廷式的、好得荒唐的躬。<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹雅的心猛地一跳。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
她在西马库斯的公寓里待了两天，期间她非常忙碌。有一个名叫德雷利安的女性黑暗精灵照料她的需求，但她似乎不完全是个仆人，因为她和他们一起吃饭。她似乎也不是西马库斯的妻子或情人。当巴兰兹雅问她时，德雷利安看起来很愉快。她只是说她在将军手下工作，做任何要求她做的事。<BR>
<BR>
在德雷利安的协助下，为她订购了几件精美的礼服和几双鞋子，外加一套骑装和靴子，以及其他一些小必需品。巴兰兹雅得到了一个属于自己的房间。<BR>
<BR>
西马库斯经常外出。她最多在吃饭时见到他，但他很少谈及自己或他在做什么。他热情而有礼貌，非常愿意就大多数话题交谈，并且似乎对她说的任何事情都感兴趣。德雷利安也差不多。巴兰兹雅觉得他们足够令人愉快，但就像卡蒂莎会说的那样，“难以深入了解”。她感到一阵奇怪的失望。这是她第一次与黑暗精灵密切交往。她本以为和他们在一起会感到舒适，最终感到自己属于某个地方、某个人、是某件事的一部分。相反，她发现自己渴望她的诺德朋友，卡蒂莎和斯特劳。<BR>
<BR>
当西马库斯告诉她他们明天就要出发去帝都时，她问她是否能和他们道别。<BR>
<BR>
“卡蒂莎？”他问道。“哎。但是......我想我欠她点什么。是她告诉我一个名叫贝瑞的孤独黑暗精灵女孩需要精灵朋友 -- 而且有时打扮成男孩，从而引导我找到了你。她显然与盗贼公会没有关联。而且除了塞里斯，似乎没有与盗贼公会有关联的人知道你的真实身份。那很好。我宁愿你以前是公会成员的事不要公开。请不要对任何人提起，陛下。这样的过去......不适合一位帝国女王。”<BR>
<BR>
“除了斯特劳和塞里斯没人知道。他们不会告诉任何人。”<BR>
<BR>
“不。”他露出一种奇怪的小小的微笑。“不，他们不会。”<BR>
<BR>
那么，他不知道卡蒂莎知道。但尽管如此，他说话的方式还是有些......<BR>
<BR>
在他们出发的早晨，斯特劳来到了他们的公寓。虽然巴兰兹雅知道其他精灵就在听得见的范围内，但他们单独留在了客厅里。他看起来憔悴而苍白。他们默默地拥抱了几分钟。斯特劳的肩膀在颤抖，眼泪顺着脸颊滚落，但他什么也没说。<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹雅试着微笑。“所以我们俩都得到了我们想要的，嗯？我将成为哀伤之城的女王，而你将拥有自己的农庄。”她握住他的手，对他温暖地、真诚地微笑。“我会给你写信，斯特劳。我保证。你必须找个抄写员，这样你也能给我写信。”<BR>
<BR>
斯特劳悲伤地摇了摇头。当巴兰兹雅坚持时，他张开嘴，指着它，发出含糊不清的声音。然后她意识到是怎么回事了。他的舌头不见了，被割掉了。<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹雅瘫倒在椅子上，大声哭泣。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
“但为什么？”当斯特劳被带走后，她向西马库斯质问道。“为什么？”<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
他们在出城的路上在卡蒂莎家停了下来。西马库斯和德雷利安没有下马。一切似乎正常，但巴兰兹雅敲门时很害怕。卡蒂莎应了门。巴兰兹雅默默地感谢众神，至少她没事。但她也显然一直在哭。不管怎样，她热情地拥抱了巴兰兹雅。<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
但显然，在某种程度上，并不完全合他的意。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Reality and Other Falsehoods<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
It is easy to confuse Illusion and Alteration. Both schools of magic attempt to create what is not there. The difference is in the rules of nature. Illusion is not bound by them, while Alteration is. This may seem to indicate that Alteration is the weaker of the two, but this is not true. Alteration creates a reality that is recognized by everyone. Illusion's reality is only in the mind of the caster and the target.<BR>
<BR>
To master Alteration, first accept that reality is a falsehood. There is no such thing. Our reality is a perception of greater forces impressed upon us for their amusement. Some say that these forces are the gods, other that they are something beyond the gods. For the wizard, it doesn't really matter. What matters is the appeal couched in a manner that cannot be denied. It must be insistent without being insulting.<BR>
<BR>
To cast Alteration spells is to convince a greater power that it will be easier to change reality as requested than to leave it alone. Do not assume that these forces are sentient. Our best guess is that they are like wind and water. Persistent but not thoughtful. Just like directing the wind or water, diversions are easier than outright resistance. Express the spell as a subtle change and it is more likely to be successful.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
现实与其他谬误<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
人们很容易混淆幻术系和变化系。这两个魔法学派都试图创造不存在的东西。区别在于自然规则。幻术系不受其约束，而变化系则受其约束。这似乎表明变化系是两者中较弱的，但事实并非如此。变化系创造的是每个人都认可的现实。幻术系的现实只存在于施法者和目标的意识中。<BR>
<BR>
要掌握变化系，首先要接受现实是虚假的。没有这种东西。我们的现实是更强大的力量为了取乐而施加于我们的感知。有人说这些力量是众神，有人说它们是超越众神的存在。对巫师来说，这其实并不重要。重要的是以一种不容否认的方式表达诉求。它必须坚持而不冒犯。<BR>
<BR>
施展变化系法术就是说服一股更强大的力量，按照要求改变现实比保持原状更容易。不要假设这些力量有知觉。我们最好的猜测是它们就像风和水的力量。持续但不思考。就像引导风或水一样，引导比直接抵抗更容易。将法术表达为一种微妙的变化，它更有可能成功。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Rear-Guard<BR>
by Tenace Mourl<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The castle would hold.  No matter the forces, the walls of Cascabel Hall would never fail, but that was small consolation for Menegur.  He was hungry.  In fact, he had never been so hungry.  The well in the atrium of the fortress supplied him with enough water to hold there until the Fourth Era, but his stomach reminded Menegur minute to minute that he needed food.<BR>
<BR>
The wagonload of supplies mocked him.  When his army, the forces of the King of Solitude, had left Cascabel Hall, and he had manned the battlements as the rear-guard to protect their retreat, they had left a wagon behind to supply him with enough food for months.  It was not until the night after they left that he inspected the larder and found that nothing edible was in the wagon.  Trunk after trunk was filled with netch armor from the army's incursion into Morrowind.  Apparently his Nord confederates had assumed that the lightly opaque material was hard tack in aspic.  If the Dunmer whose caravan had been raided knew about this, they would never be able to stop laughing.<BR>
<BR>
Menegur thought that his fellow mercenary and kinswoman Aerin would have found this amusing as well.  She had spoken with great authority about netch leather, being an expert of sorts on light armor, but she had made a point to mention that it could not be eaten like other leather in occasions of hardship.  It was a pity she couldn't be there to enjoy the irony, Menegur thought savagely.  She had returned to Morrowind even before the king's army had left, preferring a life as a wanted fugitive to a free existence in the cold of Skyrim.<BR>
<BR>
All the weeds in the courtyard had been devoured by the rear-guard's sixteenth day manning Cascabel Hall. The entire castle had been scoured: rotten tubers in the mulch pile found and consumed, a dusty bouquet in the countess's bedchamber eaten, almost every rat and insect but the most cunning infesting the castle walls had been tracked down and gobbled up. The castellan's chambers, filled with acrid, inedible law books, had yielded up a couple crumbs of bread. Menegur had even scraped moss from the stones.  There was no denying it: he would be dead from starvation before his army returned to break the ranks of the enemies who surrounded the fortress.<BR>
<BR>
"The worst part," said Menegur, who had taken to talking to himself on only the second day alone in the castle. "Is how close sustenance is."<BR>
<BR>
A vast arbor of golden apples stretched acre after acre near the castle walls.  The sunlight cast a seductive gleam on the fruit, and the cruel wind carried sweet smells into Cascabel to torture him.<BR>
<BR>
Like most Bosmer, Menegur was an archer.  He was a master of long and medium distance fighting, but in close quarters, as he would be if he dared to leave the castle and enter the enemy camp in the arbor, he knew he would not last long.  At some point, he knew he would have to try, but he had been dreading the day.  It was upon him now.<BR>
<BR>
Menegur put on the netch armor for the first time, feeling the powdery, almost velvet texture of the rendered leather against his skin.  There was also a barely perceptible throb, which he recognized as the remnant nematocysts of the netch's venomous flesh, still tingling months after its death with domesticated poison. The combination made him feel energized. Aerin had described the sensation perfectly, just as she had explained how to defend himself while wearing netch leather armor.<BR>
<BR>
Under cover of night, Menegur crept out of the back gate of the castle, locking it behind him with a rather cumbersome key.  He made for the arbor as quietly as he could, but a passing sentry, coming behind a tree, saw him.  Remaining calm, Menegur did as he remembered Aerin had instructed, only moving after the attack had been launched.  The sentry's blade glided against the armor and knocked to the left, throwing the young man off balance.  That was the trick, as he understood it: you had to be prepared to be hit, and merely move with the blow, allowing the membranous armor to divert the injury away. <BR>
<BR>
Use your enemy's momentum against him, as Aerin used to say.<BR>
<BR>
There were several more close encounters in the arbor, but each swing of an ax and each thrust of a sword found purchase elsewhere.  With handfuls of apples, Menegur ran the gauntlet back to the castle.  He locked the back gate door behind him and fell into an orgy of eating.<BR>
<BR>
For week after week, the Bosmer stole out to gather his food.  The guards began anticipating his raids, but he kept his schedule irregular and always remembered when attacked to wait for the blow, accept it, and then turn.  In such a way, he lived and survived his lonely vigil in Cascabel Hall.<BR>
<BR>
Four months later, as he was preparing for another seizure of apples, Menegur heard a loud clamor at the front gate.  Surveying the group from a safe distance on the battlements, he saw the shields of the King of Solitude, his ally the Count of Cascabel, and their enemy the King of Farrun.  Evidently, a truce had been called.<BR>
<BR>
Menegur opened the gates and the combined armies flooded the courtyard.  Many of the knights of Farrun sought to shake the hand of the man they had named the Shadow of the Arbor, expressing their admiration at his defensive skills and apologizing good-naturedly for their attempts to slay him.  Only doing their job, you know.<BR>
<BR>
"There's hardly a apple left on the vines," said the King of Solitude.<BR>
<BR>
"Well, I started on the edges and worked my way in," explained Menegur. "I brought back extra fruit to tempt the rats of out of walls so I could have a little meat as well."<BR>
<BR>
"We've spent the last several months working out the details of the truce," said the King. "Really quite exhausting.  In any rate, the Count will be taking back possession of his castle now, but there is a small detail we need to work out.  You're a mercenary, and as such responsible for your own expenses.  If you had been a subject of mine, things might be different, but there are certain old rules of law that must be respected."<BR>
<BR>
Menegur anticipated the strike.<BR>
<BR>
"The problem is," the King continued. "You've taken a good deal of the Count's crops while here.  By any reasonable computation, you've eaten an amount equal to and likely exceeding your mercenary's wages.  Obviously, I would not want to penalize you for the excellent job you've done defending the castle in uncomfortable circumstances, but you agree that it's important that we observe the old rules of law, don't you?"<BR>
<BR>
"Of course," replied Menegur, accepting the blow.<BR>
<BR>
"I'm delighted to hear that," said the King. "Our estimation is that you owe the Count of Cascabel thirty-seven Imperial gold."<BR>
<BR>
"Which I will gladly pay to myself, with interest, after the autumntide harvest," said Menegur. "There is more left on the vine than you suggest."<BR>
<BR>
The Kings of Solitude and Farrun, and the Count of Cascabel stared at the Bosmer.<BR>
<BR>
"We agreed to abide to the strictest old rules of law, and I've had time to read a great many books over the time you were making your truce.  In 3E 246, during the reign of Uriel IV, the Imperial Council, in an attempt to clear up some questions of property rights in Skyrim during those chaotic days, decreed that any man without a liege who occupied a castle for more than three months would be granted the rights and titles of that estate.  It's a good law, of course, meant to discourage absent and foreign landlords."  Menegur smiled, feeling the now familiar sensation of a glancing strike diverting. "By the rule of law, I am the Count of Cascabel."<BR>
<BR>
The rear-guard's son still hold the title of Count of Cascabel.  And he grows the finest, most delectable apples in the Empire.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
后卫<BR>
特纳切·莫尔 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
城堡会坚守住。无论敌军如何，卡斯卡贝尔厅的城墙永远不会倒塌，但这对梅内古尔来说只是小小的安慰。他饿了。事实上，他从未如此饥饿过。堡垒中庭的水井为他提供了足够维持到第四纪元的饮水，但他的胃时刻提醒着梅内古尔，他需要食物。<BR>
<BR>
那辆满载补给品的马车仿佛在嘲笑他。当他的军队，独孤城国王的部队，离开卡斯卡贝尔厅时，他作为后卫登上城墙保护他们撤退，他们留下了一辆马车，为他提供了足够数月的食物。直到他们离开后的那个晚上，他才检查了储藏室，发现马车里没有任何可吃的东西。一口又一口的箱子里装满了来自军队入侵晨风的网皮甲。显然，他的诺德同胞们以为那种半透明的材料是肉冻里的压缩饼干。如果那些商队被劫的丹莫知道了这件事，他们会笑到停不下来。<BR>
<BR>
梅内古尔认为，他的雇佣兵同伴兼女亲戚艾琳也会觉得这很有趣。她对网皮甲颇有研究，算得上是轻甲专家，但她特别指出，在困难时期不能像吃其他皮革那样吃它。真可惜她不能在场享受这种讽刺，梅内古尔恶狠狠地想。她在国王的军队离开之前就回到了晨风，宁愿过着被通缉的逃亡生活，也不愿在天际的寒冷中自由生活。<BR>
<BR>
在梅内古尔驻守卡斯卡贝尔厅的第十六天，庭院里所有的杂草都已被后卫吃光了。整座城堡都被搜刮过了：在覆盖物堆里找到了腐烂的块茎并被吃掉，伯爵夫人卧室里一束布满灰尘的花束被吃掉，几乎每一只老鼠和昆虫，除了最狡猾的那些，都被追踪并吞食了。城主那装满刺鼻、不可食用的法律书籍的房间里，也找到了几片面包屑。梅内古尔甚至从石头上刮下了苔藓。无可否认：在军队回来击溃包围堡垒的敌人之前，他就会饿死。<BR>
<BR>
“最糟糕的部分，”梅内古尔说，他在城堡里独自待的第二天就开始自言自语了，“是食物离得那么近。”<BR>
<BR>
城堡城墙附近，一大片金苹果园绵延数英亩。阳光在果实上投下诱人的光泽，凛冽的寒风将香甜的气味吹进卡斯卡贝尔厅，折磨着他。<BR>
<BR>
和大多数波斯莫一样，梅内古尔是一名弓箭手。他擅长中远距离战斗，但近距离作战，就像他如果敢离开城堡进入果园里的敌营那样，他知道自己撑不了多久。他知道总得试试，但他一直害怕那一天的到来。现在它降临了。<BR>
<BR>
梅内古尔第一次穿上了网皮甲，感受着处理过的皮革那种粉状、几乎像天鹅绒般的质感贴着他的皮肤。还有一种几乎察觉不到的搏动，他认出那是网皮虫有毒肉体的残留刺细胞，在它死后数月，仍带着驯化的毒液刺痛着。这种组合让他感到充满活力。艾琳完美地描述了这种感觉，就像她解释过穿着网皮甲时如何自卫一样。<BR>
<BR>
在夜幕的掩护下，梅内古尔从城堡的后门爬了出去，用一把相当笨重的钥匙锁上了门。他尽可能安静地朝果园走去，但一个路过的哨兵从一棵树后面走出来，看见了他。梅内古尔保持冷静，按照他记忆中艾琳的指示去做，只在攻击发起后才移动。哨兵的剑刃从盔甲上滑过，向左偏移，使那个年轻人失去了平衡。据他理解，这就是诀窍：你必须准备好被打中，然后只是顺着打击的方向移动，让那层膜状盔甲将伤害转移开。<BR>
<BR>
利用敌人的冲力对付他自己，就像艾琳常说的那样。<BR>
<BR>
果园里又有几次近距离遭遇，但每次斧头的挥舞和剑的刺击都落在了别处。梅内古尔抓了几把苹果，冒着重重危险跑回了城堡。他锁上后门，然后开始狂吃。<BR>
<BR>
一周又一周，这个波斯莫偷偷出去收集食物。守卫们开始预料到他的偷袭，但他保持不规律的作息，并总是记得在受到攻击时等待打击、接受它，然后转身。就这样，他在卡斯卡贝尔厅孤独的守望中活了下来。<BR>
<BR>
四个月后，当他正准备再次去摘苹果时，梅内古尔听到前门传来一阵喧闹声。他从城墙上安全的距离观察那群人，看到了独孤城国王、他的盟友卡斯卡贝尔伯爵以及他们的敌人法伦国王的盾牌。显然，他们已宣布休战。<BR>
<BR>
梅内古尔打开城门，联军涌入了庭院。法伦的许多骑士争相与他握手，他们称他为果园之影，表达对他防御技巧的钦佩，并善意地为自己试图杀死他而道歉。你知道，只是尽职而已。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
梅内古尔预料到了打击。<BR>
<BR>
“问题是，”国王继续说，“你在这里期间拿走了伯爵相当多的作物。按照任何合理的计算，你吃掉的量等于甚至可能超过了你作为雇佣兵的薪水。显然，我不想因为你在艰难环境下保卫城堡的出色表现而惩罚你，但你同意我们遵守古老的法律规则很重要，对吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“当然，”梅内古尔回答，接受了这一打击。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
独孤城和法伦的国王，以及卡斯卡贝尔伯爵瞪着这个波斯莫。<BR>
<BR>
“我们同意遵守最严格的古老法律规则，而在你们休战期间，我有时间读了很多书。在第三纪元246年，尤利尔四世统治期间，帝国议会为了澄清天际在那些混乱时期的一些产权问题，颁布法令，任何没有领主且占领城堡超过三个月的人，将被授予该庄园的权利和头衔。这当然是一项好法律，旨在阻止缺席和外来的地主。”梅内古尔笑了，感受到那种熟悉的、偏斜打击转移的感觉。“根据法律，我是卡斯卡贝尔伯爵。”<BR>
<BR>
这位后卫的儿子至今仍持有卡斯卡贝尔伯爵的头衔。他种植着帝国内最优质、最美味的苹果。<BR>

第二卷<BR>
<BR>
[作者注：下一首歌是以修饰过的散文形式传授给我的，因为氏族的某位祖先在轮到他记忆时忘记了曲调，导致原词也被遗忘了。我认为这突显了学术兴趣的必要性，要在这些传统永远消失之前记录下来。]<BR>
<BR>
“朱纳尔，你聪明得过了头，以至于没什么用，但你确实聪明。我们到达的这个乱糟糟的地方是哪里？”朔尔问道。<BR>
<BR>
“离这儿很远很远，”朱纳尔回答，投出狡猾的冷笑符文。这时苏恩举起手，揍了那家伙一下、两下，直到第三次斯图恩抓住了他的手。冷笑符文刺痛了他们俩，用充满毒液的聪慧倒刺激怒了兄弟俩，而睁大眼睛的朱纳尔则面无表情地对他们微笑。<BR>
<BR>
“是的，那非常聪明，”朔尔继续说，“但我的后裔将是有史以来从众神中诞生的最凶猛、最强大、最受赞誉的种族。我必须确保他们被授予所有高度和深度中最凶猛、最强大、[最丰腴？]的部分。所以我再问你一次。”<BR>
<BR>
“事实上，现实是侧向的侧向。存在不会向上坠落，虚空也不会向下坠落，而是它们一起向侧面坠落。这就是我们如何在两者之间航行的原因，”朱纳尔说，将他的手指扭成真正的符号。他话音刚落，一直尖叫着的吉讷就将大海鞭打成咸涩的鞭子，剥去了他的皮肤。<BR>
<BR>
“看来太聪明也不行，”朔尔观察着这一切，沉思道，“因为你会被殴打、羞辱，而且最糟糕的是，没什么用。那么，就靠战士们来建立我们在这片天空中对我们可能遇到的任何事物的统治了。前进，我亲爱的氏族！让我们跟随我刚刚在沙子里看到的这些脚印！”<BR>
<BR>
朔尔氏族的每个人都看到了面前的一串脚印，他们小心翼翼地每一步都踩在脚印里（因为他们知道这样会带来好运），第一次侧向旅行，远离松加德的船体，朝着未知的巨大黑暗体前进。<BR>
<BR>
“哦嚯！”朔尔喊道，“这根本不是未知的巨大黑暗体......它确实是一个巨大的物体，既黑暗又未知，但看看它多么有形！看看它咬噬的是我们的身体，而不是我们的勇气，烧焦的是我们的头发，而不是我们的心。不，在我们面前的是一条火焰之蛇。”<BR>
<BR>
“是一条龙，”朱纳尔说，并投掷了智慧骨，对此玛拉拔掉了他的舌头。<BR>
<BR>
“哦嚯嚯！”那条名叫奥杜因的蛇喊道，“你们这么快就回来了！嗯，我还饱着，从上个世界就饱着，饱到要爆了（我的食道燃烧的不仅仅是火），所以你们会有很多时间来享受这个世界。我现在要回去睡觉了，但记住，当我醒来时，我会吞噬你们创造的一切，凡人和众神的挣扎都将化为乌有。”说完他放了个屁，朔尔的氏族在其中听到了上个世界最后希望的永远消失。<BR>
<BR>
朔尔转身离开沉睡的奥杜因，面对他的氏族说：“我现在想起来了。明知这是好的，我们在这里建造世界大厅，并用在松加德与我们同行的天空之子填满它，但永远过去之后，那可憎的蛇会醒来，吞噬一切，只有我们这些乘坐松加德逃脱的人会回来再次重建。我明白我们所能做的一切都是徒劳，但我们必须辛勤劳作并克服困难，直到那最后一天到来。”<BR>
<BR>
听到这话，朔尔的氏族发出一阵欢呼，他们齐心协力竖起了世界大厅的第一根柱子，并称之为天空之喉。<BR>
<BR>"""

[After a victorious battle against the Nords of Skyrim at Mandul's Vale in 1E 820, the Redoran warriors participated in the age-old tradition of presenting the heads of their fallen enemies to the House's warchief. This is a recording of that event.]<BR><BR>

FIRST BLOOD. Master of Horns, Ulmethys Dun-Ammu, claims to have drawn first blood on the field and presents fourty-seven heads. The most important of these are identified as Varmir, reeve of Askareth; Holvilde Elf-Hammer, housecarl of the jarl of Dunkreath; and Brynvard Black-Teeth, captain of Hjolfrstad. He is given a flock of dozen trained Hoom beasts and his name is recorded in this book. In total the retinue led by Serjo Dun-Ammu took one hundred enemy heads. Each warrior is given a gold ring from the Hortator's finger.<BR><BR>

SECOND BLOOD. A young spearman from Serjo Venim's retinue claims second blood and presents four heads. One of the heads is identified as Vraggolaf of Dunkreath, a young prince of the Nord king's line. The young spearman is gifted with a silver neck chain from the Hortator's neck. The tip of her spear is dipped in precious resin and a red ribbon is tied to its shaft. Serjo Venim declares that she is now adopted as her sword-daughter. Her name, Meteresu Venim, is recorded here. In total the retinue of Serjo Venim took seventy-eight heads. Each warrior is given a tract of land south of Roryn.<BR><BR>

OTHER RECORDED HEADS.<BR><BR>

Serjo Selmuth Morvayn presents twenty-two heads. In total her retinue took sixty-three enemy heads. Each warrior is given a resin amulet.<BR><BR>

Serjo Hlevaaru Llethri and Serjo Ores Arobar present their heads jointly, sixteen heads each. They have a dispute over the head of Ulvmurd Half-Boar, thane of Ystralond, which they both claim to have cut off his shoulders. Since the war is now over the Hortator graciously allows them to settle their dispute in a duel, which is to take place during the victory feast. In total the retinues of House Llethri and House Arobar took one hundred and sixteen heads. [Scribe's Note: Later that night Serjo Llethri won the duel for the Nord's head, which she then gave to widow Arobar as a token of respect for the late Serjo Arobar.]<BR><BR>

Sera Rother Madras presents eleven heads. He is made Captain of Verarchen and a ceremonial blade is entrusted with his House and his name is recorded here.<BR><BR>

Sera Talna Ramoran presents three heads. A vengeful ghost takes the hold of one of these heads. Its white eyes open and the ghost moves its mouth: "Hear the words of Nojtur Long-Hair, vile skinchangers of the East! The hand that cut me down shall perish before the dawn! A thousand winters upon you!" Archers guarding the Hortator shoot the head, but the dead Nord's curse remains. Talna Ramoran is escorted out of the war tent with no gifts, but her name is recorded here. [Scribe's Note: The next morning she was found frozen to death outside the camp.]<BR><BR>

Riders of Houses Salothren and Sarethi return late to present eighty heads of routed enemies, made up of Nordic servants and camp followers. Though great in number these heads are of a lesser importance. The riders are given extra measures of mazte and flin for the feast to come.<BR><BR>

In total four-hundred and seventy-one enemy heads were presented and recorded. Heads of the most high-ranking enemies are buried with proper rituals under a heavy slab of stone. Their names are carved on the underside of the stone so should any of their spirit become restless they can read their own name to convince them they are indeed dead. The rest of the heads are treated with resin and placed on pikes around the war camp's perimeter. One hundred and fourty-six candles are lit for each fallen Redoran warrior.<BR><BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
[在第一纪元820年于曼杜尔谷战胜天际的诺德人后，勒多兰战士参加了将战败敌人的首级献给家族战酋的古老传统。以下是该事件的记录。]<BR><BR>

首血。号角大师，乌尔梅西斯·邓-阿姆，声称在战场上取得了首血，并献上四十七颗首级。其中最重要的被确认为：阿斯卡雷斯的管事瓦尔米尔；邓克雷思领主的侍卫霍尔维尔德·精灵之锤；以及约尔夫斯塔德的船长布林瓦德·黑牙。他获得了一群十二只训练有素的霍姆兽，他的名字被记录在此书中。大人邓-阿姆率领的随从总共取得了一百颗敌人首级。每位战士都从统谏使的手指上得到了一枚金戒指。<BR><BR>

次血。来自大人维尼姆随从的一名年轻枪兵声称取得了次血，并献上四颗首级。其中一颗被确认为邓克雷思的弗拉戈拉夫，诺德国王血统中的一位年轻王子。这位年轻枪兵获得了从统谏使脖子上取下的一条银项链。她的枪尖浸入了珍贵的树脂，枪杆上系了一条红丝带。大人维尼姆宣布她已被收为剑女。她的名字，梅特雷苏·维尼姆，被记录在此。大人维尼姆的随从总共取得了七十八颗首级。每位战士都获得了一块罗林以南的土地。<BR><BR>

其他记录的首级。<BR><BR>

大人塞尔穆斯·莫文献上二十二颗首级。她的随从总共取得了六十三颗敌人首级。每位战士都获得了一个树脂护符。<BR><BR>

大人赫列瓦鲁·莱斯里和大人奥雷斯·阿罗巴共同献上首级，每人十六颗。他们就伊斯特拉隆德的乡绅乌尔武尔德·半猪的首级发生了争执，两人都声称是自己将其斩下。由于战争已经结束，统谏使慷慨地允许他们通过决斗解决争端，决斗将在胜利宴会上进行。莱斯里家族和阿罗巴家族的随从总共取得了一百一十六颗首级。[抄写员注：当天夜里，莱斯里大人赢得了争夺诺德人首级的决斗，随后她将首级送给了阿罗巴遗孀，以示对已故阿罗巴大人的敬意。]<BR><BR>

瑟拉·罗瑟·马德拉斯献上十一颗首级。他被任命为维拉钦的队长，一把仪式用剑被托付给他的家族，他的名字被记录在此。<BR><BR>

瑟拉·塔尔娜·拉莫兰献上三颗首级。一颗复仇的鬼魂占据了其中一颗首级。它睁开白色的眼睛，鬼魂动了动嘴：“听好了，邪恶的东方换皮者！这是长发诺伊图尔的话！砍倒我的手将在黎明前灭亡！愿千个严冬降临于你们！”守卫统谏使的弓箭手射穿了那颗头颅，但死去的诺德人的诅咒依然存在。塔尔娜·拉莫兰被护送出战争帐篷，没有得到任何礼物，但她的名字被记录在此。[抄写员注：第二天早上，人们发现她冻死在营地外。]<BR><BR>

萨洛瑟伦和萨雷蒂家族的骑手们晚归，献上八十颗溃逃敌人的首级，这些敌人由诺德仆人和营地随从组成。尽管数量众多，但这些首级的重要性较低。骑手们获得了额外的玛兹忒和弗林用于即将到来的宴会。<BR><BR>

总共献上并记录了四百七十一颗敌人首级。最高级别的敌人首级被用适当的仪式埋葬在厚重的石板下。他们的名字被刻在石板底面，这样万一他们的灵魂变得不安，他们可以读到自己的名字，从而确信自己确实已经死了。其余的首级经过树脂处理，放置在战营周围的尖桩上。为每一位倒下的勒多兰战士点燃了一百四十六支蜡烛。<BR><BR>"""

次血。来自大人维尼姆随从的一名年轻枪兵声称取得了次血，并献上四颗首级。其中一颗被确认为邓克雷思的弗拉戈拉夫，诺德国王血统中的一位年轻王子。这位年轻枪兵获得了从统谏使脖子上取下的一条银项链。她的枪尖浸入了珍贵的树脂，枪杆上系了一条红丝带。大人维尼姆宣布她已被收为剑女。她的名字，梅特雷苏·维尼姆，被记录在此。大人维尼姆的随从总共取得了七十八颗首级。每位战士都获得了一块罗林以南的土地。<BR><BR>

其他记录的首级。<BR><BR>

大人塞尔穆斯·莫文献上二十二颗首级。她的随从总共取得了六十三颗敌人首级。每位战士都获得了一个树脂护符。<BR><BR>

大人赫列瓦鲁·莱斯里和大人奥雷斯·阿罗巴共同献上首级，每人十六颗。他们就伊斯特拉隆德的乡绅乌尔武尔德·半猪的首级发生了争执，两人都声称是自己将其斩下。由于战争已经结束，统谏使慷慨地允许他们通过决斗解决争端，决斗将在胜利宴会上进行。莱斯里家族和阿罗巴家族的随从总共取得了一百一十六颗首级。[抄写员注：当天夜里，莱斯里大人赢得了争夺诺德人首级的决斗，随后她将首级送给了阿罗巴遗孀，以示对已故阿罗巴大人的敬意。]<BR><BR>

瑟拉·罗瑟·马德拉斯献上十一颗首级。他被任命为维拉钦的队长，一把仪式用剑被托付给他的家族，他的名字被记录在此。<BR><BR>

瑟拉·塔尔娜·拉莫兰献上三颗首级。一颗复仇的鬼魂占据了其中一颗首级。它睁开白色的眼睛，鬼魂动了动嘴：“听好了，邪恶的东方换皮者！这是长发诺伊图尔的话！砍倒我的手将在黎明前灭亡！愿千个严冬降临于你们！”守卫统谏使的弓箭手射穿了那颗头颅，但死去的诺德人的诅咒依然存在。塔尔娜·拉莫兰被护送出战争帐篷，没有得到任何礼物，但她的名字被记录在此。[抄写员注：第二天早上，人们发现她冻死在营地外。]<BR><BR>

萨洛瑟伦和萨雷蒂家族的骑手们晚归，献上八十颗溃逃敌人的首级，这些敌人由诺德仆人和营地随从组成。尽管数量众多，但这些首级的重要性较低。骑手们获得了额外的玛兹忒和弗林用于即将到来的宴会。<BR><BR>

总共献上并记录了四百七十一颗敌人首级。最高级别的敌人首级被用适当的仪式埋葬在厚重的石板下。他们的名字被刻在石板底面，这样万一他们的灵魂变得不安，他们可以读到自己的名字，从而确信自己确实已经死了。其余的首级经过树脂处理，放置在战营周围的尖桩上。为每一位倒下的勒多兰战士点燃了一百四十六支蜡烛。<BR><BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Red Kitchen Reader<BR>
by Simocles Quo<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Though naturally modest, I must admit to some pleasure in being dubbed by our Emperor's father, the late Pelagius IV, as "the finest connoisseur in Tamriel." He was also good enough to appoint me the first, and to this day, the only Master of Cuisine in the Imperial Court. Other Emperors, of course, had master chefs and cooks in their staff, but only during the reign of Pelagius was there someone of rarefied tastes to plan the menus and select the finest produce to be served at court. His son Uriel requested that I continue in that position, but I was forced to graciously decline the invitation, because of age and poor health.<BR>
<BR>
This book, however, is not intended to be autobiography. I have had a great many adventures in my life as a knight of fine dining, but my intention for this book is much more specific. Many times I have been asked, "What is the best thing you ever ate?"<BR>
<BR>
The answer to that is not a simple one. Much of the pleasure of a great meal is not only in the food: it is in the setting, the company, the mood. Eat an indifferently cooked roast or a simple stew with your one true love, and it is a meal to be remembered. Have an excellent twelve-course feast with dull company, while feeling slightly ill, and it will be forgotten, or remembered only with distaste.<BR>
<BR>
Sometimes meals are memorable for the experiences that come before them.<BR>
<BR>
Fairly recently, in northern Skyrim, I had a bit of bad luck. I was with a group of fishermen, observing their technique of capturing a very rare, very delicious fish called Merringar. The fish is found only far from shore, so it was a week's voyage out beyond civilization. Well, we found our school of Merringar, but as the fishermen began spearing them, the blood in the water attracted a family of Dreugh, who capsized the boat and everyone on it. I managed to save myself, but the fishermen and all our supplies were lost. Sailing is not, alas, a skill I have picked up over the years, and it took me three weeks, with no provisions, to find my way back to the kingdom of Solitude. I had managed to catch enough small fish to eat raw, but I was still delirious from hunger and thirst. The first meal I had on shore, of Nordic roast boar, Jazbay wine, and, yes, filet of Merringar would have been excellent under any circumstances, but because of the threat of starvation I had faced, it was divine beyond words.<BR>
<BR>
Sometimes meals are even memorable for the experiences that follow them.<BR>
<BR>
In a tavern in Falinesti, I was introduced to a simple peasant dish called Kollopi, delicious little balls of flesh, thick with spices and juice, so savory I asked the proprietress whence they came. Mother Pascost explained that the Kollopi were an arboreal rodent that fed exclusively on the most tender branches of the graht-oak, and I was fortunate enough to be in Valenwood at the time of the annual harvest. I was invited to join with a small colony of Imga monkeys, who alone could gather these succulent little mice. Because they lived only on the slenderest branches of the trees, and only on the ends of those same branches, the Imga had to climb beneath them and jump up to "pick" the Kollopi from their perches. Imga are, of course, naturally dexterous, but I was then relatively young and spry, and they let me help them. While I could never jump as high they could, with practice, I found that if I kept my head and upper body rigid, and launched off the ground with a scissors-like kick, I could reach the Kollopi on the lowest branches of the tree. I believe I gathered three Kollopi myself, though with considerable effort.<BR>
<BR>
To this day, I salivate at the thought of Kollopi, but my mind is on the image of myself and several dozen Imgas leaping around beneath the shade of the graht-oaks.<BR>
<BR>
Then, of course, there are the rare meals memorable for what came before, after, and during the meal, which brings me to the finest thing I ever ate, the meal that began my lifelong obsession with excellent cuisine.<BR>
<BR>
As a child growing up in Cheydinhal, I did not care for food at all. I recognized the value of nutrition, for I was not a complete dullard, but I cannot say that mealtime brought me any pleasure at all. Partly, of course, this was the fault of my family's cook, who believed that spices were an invention of the Daedra, and that good Imperials should like their food boiled, textureless and flavorless. Though I think she was alone in assigning a religious significance to this, my sampling of traditional Cyrodilic cuisine suggests that the philosophy is regrettably common in my homeland.<BR>
<BR>
Though I did not enjoy food per se, I was not a morose, unadventurous child in other respects. I enjoyed the fights in the Arena, of course, and nothing made me happier than wandering the streets of my town, with my imagination as my only companion. It was on one such jaunt on a sunny Fredas in Mid Year that I made a discovery that changed my heart and my life.<BR>
<BR>
There were several old abandoned houses down the street from my own home, and I often played around them, imagining them to be filled with desperate outlaws or haunted by hundreds of evil spirits. I never had the nerve to go inside. In fact, had I not that day seen some other children who had delighted in teasing me in the past, I would never have gone in. But I needed a sanctuary, so I ran into the closest one.<BR>
<BR>
The house seemed to be as desolate on the inside as on the outside, further proof that no one lived there, and had not for some time. When I heard footsteps, I could only assume that the loathsome little urchins I hoped to avoid had followed me in. I escaped to the basement, and from there, past a broken-down wall that led to a well. I could still hear the footsteps above, and I decided that I was still loath to confront my tormentors. Knocking aside the rusty locks on the well, I slipped down below.<BR>
<BR>
The well was dry, but I discovered it was far from empty. There was a sort of a sub-basement to the house, three large rooms that were clean, furnished, and evidently not abandoned at all. My senses told me someone was living in the house, after all: not only my sense of sight, but my sense of smell. For one of the rooms was a large red-painted kitchen, and spread out on the coals of the oven was a roast, carved into small morsels. Passing a beautiful and appropriate bas-relief of a mother carving a roast for her grateful children, I beheld the kitchen and the wonders within.<BR>
<BR>
Like I said, food had never interested me before, but I was transfixed, and even now as I write this, words fail me in describing the rich aroma that hung in the air. It was like nothing I had ever smelled in my family's kitchen, and I was unable to stop myself from popping one of the steaming chunks of meat into my mouth. The taste was magical, the flesh tender and sweet. Before I knew it, I had eaten everything on the stove, and I learned at that very second the truth that that food can and should be sublime.<BR>
<BR>
After gorging myself and having my culinary epiphany, I was conflicted on what to do. Part of me wanted to wait down in that red kitchen until the chef returned, so I could ask him what his secret recipe was for the delicious meat. Part of me recognized that I had stolen into someone's house and eaten their dinner, and it would be wise to leave while I could. That was what I did.<BR>
<BR>
Time and again, I've tried to return to that strange, wonderful place, but Cheydinhal has changed over time. Old houses have been reclaimed, and new houses abandoned. I know what to look for on the inside of the house - the well, the beautiful etching of a woman preparing to carve out a roast for her children, the red kitchen itself - but I have never been able to find the house again. After a while, as I grew older, I stopped trying. It is better as it remains in my memory, the most perfect meal I ever ate.<BR>
<BR>
The inspiration for my life that followed all was cooked up, together with that fabulous meat, right there in the Red Kitchen.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
红厨房读本<BR>
西莫克勒斯·阔 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
尽管天性谦逊，但我必须承认，被我们的皇帝的父亲，已故的佩拉吉乌斯四世称为“泰姆瑞尔最杰出的美食鉴赏家”，我确实感到几分欣喜。他还慷慨地任命我为宫廷中第一位，也是迄今为止唯一一位膳食大师。当然，其他皇帝也有御厨和厨师，但只有在佩拉吉乌斯统治时期，才有一位品味卓绝的人来规划菜单，挑选最上等的食材用于宫廷。他的儿子尤利尔曾请求我继续担任此职，但我因年事已高和健康欠佳，不得不婉言谢绝了。<BR>
<BR>
然而，这本书并非自传。作为美食骑士，我一生中有过许多冒险，但这本书的意图要具体得多。我无数次被问到：“你吃过的最好的东西是什么？”<BR>
<BR>
答案并不简单。一顿美餐的乐趣很大程度上不仅在于食物本身：还在于环境、陪伴和心境。和你真正的挚爱一起吃一份平平无奇的烤肉或一锅简单的炖菜，那也会是一顿难忘的餐食。与乏味的同伴一起享用一顿十二道菜的盛宴，同时身体略感不适，那顿饭就会被遗忘，或者只留下厌恶的记忆。<BR>
<BR>
有时，一顿饭因其之前的经历而令人难忘。<BR>
<BR>
就在不久之前，在天际北部，我遇到了一点厄运。我和一群渔民在一起，观察他们捕捉一种非常稀有、非常美味的叫做梅林加鱼的技巧。这种鱼只在远离海岸的地方才有，所以我们在文明之外航行了一周。嗯，我们找到了梅林加鱼群，但当渔民开始用矛刺它们时，水中的血引来了一群蟹灵，它们掀翻了船和船上的所有人。我设法救了自己，但渔民和我们所有的补给都丢失了。唉，航海并非我多年掌握的技能，在没有补给的情况下，我花了三周才找到回独孤城王国的路。我设法抓到了足够的小鱼生吃，但我仍然因饥渴而神志不清。我在岸上的第一顿饭，有诺德烤野猪、雅兹贝酒，还有，是的，梅林加鱼片，在任何情况下都堪称美味，但因为我曾面临饿死的威胁，那顿饭的美味简直无法言喻。<BR>
<BR>
有时，一顿饭甚至因其之后的经历而令人难忘。<BR>
<BR>
在法琳奈斯提的一家酒馆里，我尝到了一种名为科洛皮的简单农家菜，那是一种美味的小肉球，香料和汁水浓郁，味道极其鲜美，我向女主人询问其来源。帕斯科斯特妈妈解释说，科洛皮是一种树栖啮齿动物，只以格拉特橡树最嫩的树枝为食，我很幸运，正好在瓦伦伍德赶上一年一度的收获季节。我被邀请加入一小群因加猴子，只有它们才能采集这些多汁的小家伙。因为它们只生活在树木最纤细的树枝上，而且只在那些树枝的末端，因加人必须爬到树枝下方，然后跳起来从栖身处“摘取”科洛皮。当然，因加人天生灵巧，但那时我还算年轻敏捷，它们让我帮忙。虽然我永远无法像它们跳得那么高，但通过练习，我发现如果我保持头和上半身僵硬，用剪刀腿式的动作从地面起跳，我能够到树最低处的科洛皮。我相信我自己采集了三只科洛皮，尽管费了相当大的力气。<BR>
<BR>
直到今天，一想到科洛皮我还会流口水，但我的脑海里浮现的是我和几十只因加人在格拉特橡树的树荫下四处跳跃的景象。<BR>
<BR>
当然，还有那些罕见的、因其前后及用餐过程中的经历而令人难忘的餐食，这让我想起了我吃过的最好的东西，那顿饭开启了我一生对美食的痴迷。<BR>
<BR>
作为一个在夏丁赫尔长大的孩子，我根本不喜欢食物。我认识到营养的价值，因为我并非完全的傻瓜，但我不能说用餐时间给我带来了任何快乐。当然，部分原因是我家厨师的错，她认为香料是迪德拉的发明，而好的帝国人应该喜欢水煮、毫无质地和味道的食物。虽然我认为只有她给这种做法赋予了宗教意义，但我品尝传统西罗帝尔菜肴的经历表明，这种烹饪理念在我家乡可悲地普遍存在。<BR>
<BR>
虽然我本身不喜欢食物，但在其他方面，我并不是一个忧郁、不爱冒险的孩子。当然，我喜欢看竞技场的比赛，没有什么比在镇上街道上漫步更让我快乐的了，想象力是我唯一的伙伴。就在年中月一个阳光明媚的弗雷达斯日，我进行这样一次短途旅行时，我发现了一件改变我心灵和生命的东西。<BR>
<BR>
在我家沿街的地方有几栋废弃的老房子，我经常在它们周围玩耍，想象里面挤满了绝望的逃犯，或者被数百个恶灵纠缠。我从不敢进去。事实上，如果不是那天我看到了一些过去喜欢捉弄我的其他孩子，我永远不会进去。但我需要一个避难所，所以我跑进了最近的一栋。<BR>
<BR>
房子里面和外面一样荒凉，进一步证明没有人住在那里，而且已经有一段时间了。当我听到脚步声时，我只能假设我希望能避开的那些讨厌的小顽童跟着我进来了。我逃到地下室，从那里穿过一堵破墙，来到一口井边。我还能听到上面的脚步声，我决定仍然不愿面对我的折磨者。我拨开井上生锈的锁，滑了下去。<BR>
<BR>
井是干的，但我发现它远非空无一物。房子下面有一个类似地下室的所在，有三个大房间，干净、有家具，显然根本没有被废弃。我的感官告诉我，毕竟有人住在这房子里：不仅是视觉，还有嗅觉。因为其中一个房间是一个漆成红色的大厨房，烤箱的炭火上铺着烤肉，被切成了小块。经过一幅美丽而贴切的浮雕，描绘了一位母亲为感激的孩子们切烤肉的情景，我看到了那个厨房和里面的奇迹。<BR>
<BR>
就像我说的，我以前从未对食物感兴趣，但我被吸引住了，即使现在我在写这段话，也无法用语言描述空气中弥漫的浓郁香气。那是我在家里的厨房从未闻到过的，我无法阻止自己把一块热气腾腾的肉塞进嘴里。味道神奇，肉质鲜嫩甜美。不知不觉间，我吃光了炉子上所有的东西，就在那一刻，我明白了食物可以，而且应该，是极致的这一真理。<BR>
<BR>
在狼吞虎咽并经历了烹饪顿悟之后，我对该做什么感到矛盾。我的一部分想在那个红色厨房里等到厨师回来，这样我就可以问他那美味肉食的秘方是什么。我的一部分意识到我偷偷溜进了别人的房子，吃掉了他们的晚餐，趁还能离开时离开是明智的。我照做了。<BR>
<BR>
我一次又一次地试图回到那个奇妙的地方，但夏丁赫尔随着时间的推移而改变。老房子被收回，新房子被废弃。我知道在房子内部要寻找什么 -- 那口井，那幅美丽的蚀刻画，描绘一个女人准备为孩子们切烤肉，还有那间红色厨房本身 -- 但我再也找不到那栋房子了。过了一段时间，随着我年龄增长，我不再尝试了。它留在我的记忆中，作为我吃过的最完美的一餐，这样更好。<BR>
<BR>
我此后一生的灵感，连同那美妙的肉，都是在那间红厨房里烹制出来的。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Redemption <BR>
Unknown <BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Vertius Felannus gazed down upon the rich valley of his homeland. The rich loamy earth clung to the hem of his simple woolen robe. He was dressed in the garb of his order, wearing the simple weave of Maran devotees. The thick folds of cloth hid his thin frame from the eyes of men and the teeth of the harsh wind. A faint smile played about the edges of his care-worn lips. It was the same gentle smile that was etched into his face by a combination of years of missionary work and a trust in the divinity of the Nine. His feet were unshod, epitomizing the virtue of humility by which he tried to live his life.<BR>
<BR>
He strode joyfully towards the village of Sten. The thatched roofs of the modest houses were partially obscured by a copse of flowering fruit trees, branches laden with their bounty. He carried with him nothing but his faith and a joy that stemmed from the knowledge that he would soon be home.<BR>
<BR>
The orange glow of sunset hung in the air, filling the empty pastures with a subtle glow; a light for the eyes and a light for the soul.<BR>
<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Redguards, Their History and Their Heroes<BR>
by Destri Melarg<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Frandar Hunding was born in 2356 in the old way of reckoning, in our beloved deserts of the old land. The traditional rule of emperors had been overthrown in 2012, and although each successive emperor remained the figurehead of the empire, his powers were very much reduced. Since that time, our people saw 300 years of almost continuous civil war between the provincial lords, warrior monks and brigands, all fighting each other for land and power. Our people once were artisans, poets, and scholars, but the ever evolving strife made the way the sword inevitable - the song of the blade through the air, through flesh and bone, its ring against armor: an answer to our prayers.<BR>
<BR> 
In the time of Lord Frandar the first Warrior Prince, lords called Yokeda built huge stone castles to protect themselves and their lands, and castle towns outside the walls begin to grow up. In 2245, however, Mansel Sesnit came to the fore. He became the Elden Yokeda, or military dictator, and for eight years succeeded in gaining control of almost the whole empire. When Sesnit was assassinated in 2253, a commoner took over the government. Randic Torn continued the work of unifying the Empire which Sesnit had begun, ruthlessly putting down any traces of insurrection. He revived the old gulf between the warriors - the sword singers - and the commoners by introducing restrictions on the wearing of swords. "Torn's Sword-hunt", as it was known, meant that only the singers were allowed to wear swords, which distinguished them from the rest of the population.<BR>
<BR> 
Although Torn did much to settle the empire into its pre-strife ways, by the time of his death in 2373 internal disturbances still had not been completely eliminated. Upon his death, civil war broke out in earnest; war that made the prior 300 year turmoil pale in comparison. It was in this period that Frandar Hunding grew up.<BR>
<BR> 
Hunding belonged to the sword-singers. This element of empire society grew from the desert artisans and was initially recruited from the young sons and daughters of the high families. They built the first temple to the unknown gods of War and build a training hall "The Hall of the Virtues of War". Within a few generations the way of the sword - the song of the blade - had become their life. The people of the blade kept their poetry and artisanship in building beautiful swords woven with magic and powers from the unknown gods. The greatest among them became known as Ansei or "Saints of the Sword". Each of these began their own training schools teaching their individual way of the sword. Those Ansei of the highest virtue wandered the country side engaging in battle, righting wrongs, and seeking to end the strife.<BR>
<BR> 
To sum it up. Hunding, was a sword-singer, a master, no, a Master Ansei at a time when the peak of the strife was reborn out of the chaos of Torn's death. Many singers put up their swords and became artists, for the pull of the artisan heritage was strong; but others, like Hunding pursued the ideal of the warrior searching for enlightenment through the perilous paths of the Sword. Duels of revenge and tests of skill were common place, and fencing schools multiplied.<BR>
<BR> 
Frandar do Hunding Hel Ansei No Shira, or as he is commonly known Frandar Hunding, was born in the far desert marches in the province of High Desert. Hunding is the name of the High Desert region near where he was born. No Shira means noble person or person of noble birth and Hel Ansei is his title of Sword Sainthood. 
Hunding's ancestors reach back to the beginning of recorded time in the high desert and were artisans and mystics, his grandfather was a retainer of the Elden Yokeda, Mansel Sesnit, and led many of the battles of unification prior to Sesnit's assassination.<BR>
<BR> 
When he was 14, Hunding's father died in the one of the many insurrections, and he was left to support his mother and four brothers. His prowess with the sword however, made his life both difficult and easy. Easy in that his services came in great demand as a guardian and escort. Hard in that his reputation preceded him, and many awaited their turn to face him in battle and gain instant fame through his defeat.<BR>
<BR> 
By the time Hunding was 30 he had fought and won more than 90 duels killing all his opponents. He became virtually invincible with the sword, gaining such skill and mastery that he finally stopped using the real swords created through the artisanship of his people and began using the Shehai or "way of the spirit sword".<BR>
<BR> 
All sword singers learn through their intense training and devotion to the gods of war and way of the sword, the forms of discipline that allow the creation of the spirit sword. This is a simple form of magic or mind mastery where by a image of a sword is formed from pure thought. The sword singer forms the sword by concentrating, and it takes shape in his hand - usually a pale thing of light, misty and insubstantial, a thing of beauty perhaps, a symbol of devotion to the Way and the gods, but no weapon. However, those Ansei of the highest level and sensitivity and those with talent in magic, can at times of stress, form a spirit sword, the Shehai which is far more than light and air - it is an unstoppable weapon of great might, a weapon which can never be taken from the owner without also taking his mind.<BR>
<BR> 
The Shehai became Hunding's weapon, and with this he slew bands of brigands and wandering monsters than infested the land. Finally upon finishing his 90th duel, defeating the evil Lord Janic and his seven lich followers, he was satisfied that he was indeed invincible. Hunding then turned to formulating his philosophy of"the Way of the Sword". He wrote his Learnings down in the BOOK OF CIRCLES while living as a hermit in a cave in the mountains of high desert in his sixtieth year.<BR>
<BR> 
In that year Hunding having enlisted in the many battles of the empire, defeating all opponents, had thought himself ready for death and retired to his cave to capture his strategy and mystical visions to share with other Sword Singers. It was after his completion of the scroll of the Circle that the Singers found him composing his death poem and preparing to join the gods of war in final rest.<BR>
<BR> 
At sixty he was a vigorous man, who thought himself through with life, but his people,the sword-singers needed him. They needed him as never before.<BR>
<BR> 
Torn's Sword Hunt, had separated the Singers from the common people, and the rise of the Last Emperor began the last great strife of the desert empire. The Emperor and his consort Elisa's final effort to wrest control of the empire from the people by destroying the sword-singers. Hira vowed to search out every Singer with his Brigand army composed of Orcs and castoffs of the wars of the empire, and to scourge them from the face of the planet.<BR>
<BR> 
The Sword Singers were never a numerous people. The harsh desert kept the births few, and growing up in the unforgiving wastes eliminated all but those of iron spirit and will. Thus the final strife which became knows as the "War of the Singers" found the people of the sword unprepared and unready to join together their individually great skills into an army that could defend their homes and lives.<BR>
<BR> 
Frandar Hunding was sought out, his death poem interrupted, and unceremoniously command of the singers was thrust upon him. To the unknown gods of war great thanks is owed that Hunding had the time in his cave to write down his years of accumulated wisdom, of strategy, of the way of the Shehai. The singers fled from their camps up into the desert hills and mountains. Fled to the foot of Hattu "the father of Mountains" where Hunding had gone to write in peace and to die, and there these remnants formed into the Army of the Circle - they learned Hunding's Way, his strategies his tactics, and the final great vision for a master stroke.<BR>
<BR> 
Hunding devised a plan of seven battles leading the Armies of Hira further and further into the wilderness to the foot of Hattu, where the final battle could be fought. Hunding called his plan the "Hammer and the Anvil". With each battle Hunding's Singers would further learn his strategies and tactics, grow strong in the use of the Shehai, and be ready to defeat their opponents in the seventh battle. And thus it was, the six first battles were waged, each neither victory or defeat, each leading to the next. The larger armies of Hira following the small army of Hunding. Outnumbered thirty to one, the singers never faltered from the Way. The stage was set, Hira and his Army maneuvered to the base of Hattu Mountain, where the hammer blow was delivered. The battle was pitched, and many singers fell that day. Hunding knew, that the singers who lived would be few, but Hira and his empire of evil would not live and so it went.<BR>
<BR> 
At the end Hunding and less that twenty thousand Singers survived the day, but no army of evil was left to pillage and murder, more than three hundred thousand fell that day on Hattu. Of those who were left to run and live, all were scattered to the four winds, and organized force no more.<BR>
<BR> 
The singers packed their lives, folded their tents, mourned their dead, and followed Hunding to the great port city of Arch, in the province of Seawind. There Hunding had a flotilla of ships waiting. The Singers left their desert for a new land. No longer welcome in the desert empire, they left to be sung about and spoken of in legend. The final great warrior, the singers of Shehai, the Book of Circles, all leaving that land where their virtue was unappreciated. Red, red with blood they were in the eyes of the gentle citizenry, never mind that they had saved them from a great evil.<BR>
<BR> 
The singers vowed to learn new ways as they traveled across the great ocean to their new land. To adopt a new name, but to honor the past. In honor of their final battle, they named their new land Hammerfell and adopted the name Redguards.<BR>
<BR> 
In honor to Hunding the great warrior prince, each household in Hammerfell has a place by the hearth an alcove really, just a niche, big enough to hold the scroll - The Book of Circles.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
红卫人，他们的历史与英雄<BR>
德斯特里·梅拉格 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
弗兰达·亨丁出生于2356年，按旧历计算，在我们古老土地心爱的沙漠中。皇帝的传统统治在2012年被推翻，尽管随后的每位皇帝仍是帝国的名义元首，但其权力已大为削弱。自那时起，我们的人民经历了近300年几乎不间断的内战，行省领主、武僧和匪徒互相争斗，争夺土地和权力。我们的人民曾经是工匠、诗人和学者，但不断演变的纷争使剑道成为必然 -- 剑刃划过空气、划过血肉和骨头、撞击盔甲的声音：这是对我们祈祷的回答。<BR>
<BR>
在第一位战士亲王弗兰达勋爵的时代，被称为“约克达”的领主们建造了巨大的石头城堡来保护自己和他们的土地，城墙外的城堡城镇开始发展起来。然而，在2245年，曼塞尔·塞斯尼特崭露头角。他成为了埃尔登·约克达，即军事独裁者，并在八年内成功控制了几乎整个帝国。当塞斯尼特在2253年被暗杀时，一个平民接管了政府。兰迪克·托恩继续了塞斯尼特开始的统一帝国的工作，无情地镇压任何叛乱的迹象。他通过引入佩戴剑的限制，重新唤起了战士（剑歌者）和平民之间的旧日鸿沟。众所周知的“托恩猎剑令”意味着只有剑歌者才被允许佩剑，这使他们与其余人口区分开来。<BR>
<BR>
尽管托恩为帝国恢复战前状态做了很多努力，但到他在2373年去世时，内部骚乱仍未完全消除。他死后，内战真正爆发；这场战争使得之前三百年的动荡相形见绌。弗兰达·亨丁就是在这个时期长大的。<BR>
<BR>
亨丁属于剑歌者。帝国社会的这一元素源于沙漠工匠，最初是从显赫家族的年轻子女中招募的。他们建造了第一座供奉未知战争之神的神殿，并建造了一个训练厅“战争美德之厅”。几代之内，剑道 -- 剑刃之歌 -- 成为了他们的生命。剑之民将他们诗歌和工艺保留在建造美丽剑刃上，这些剑刃编织着来自未知之神的魔法和力量。他们中最伟大的被称为安塞或“剑之圣徒”。他们中的每一位都开始建立自己的训练学校，传授他们各自的剑道。那些品德最高尚的安塞在乡间游历，参与战斗，匡扶正义，并寻求结束纷争。<BR>
<BR>
总而言之。亨丁是一位剑歌者，一位大师，不，是一位安塞大师，正值纷争的顶峰从托恩死亡的混乱中重生的时代。许多剑歌者放下剑，成为了艺术家，因为工匠传统的吸引力很强大；但其他人，像亨丁，则追求战士的理想，通过剑的危险道路寻求启迪。复仇决斗和技能测试司空见惯，剑术学校成倍增加。<BR>
<BR>
弗兰达·多·亨丁·赫尔·安塞·诺·希拉，或者他通常被称为弗兰达·亨丁，出生在远在沙漠边疆的高沙漠行省。亨丁是他出生地附近的高沙漠地区的名字。诺·希拉意为高贵之人或出身高贵之人，赫尔·安塞是他的剑之圣徒头衔。
亨丁的祖先可追溯到高沙漠有记载历史之初，他们是工匠和神秘主义者，他的祖父是埃尔登·约克达曼塞尔·塞斯尼特的侍从，并在塞斯尼特被暗杀前领导了许多统一战役。<BR>
<BR>
在他14岁时，亨丁的父亲在一次众多叛乱中去世，他留下供养母亲和四个兄弟。然而，他剑术的高超使他的生活既艰难又容易。容易在于他作为护卫和保镖的服务需求很大。艰难在于他的名声先于他，许多人等待轮到自己在战斗中面对他，并通过击败他来获得即时的名声。<BR>
<BR>
到亨丁30岁时，他已经战斗并赢得了90多场决斗，杀死了所有对手。他在剑术上变得几乎无敌，获得了如此高的技能和掌握程度，以至于他最终停止使用通过他人民的工艺制造的真剑，并开始使用舍海或“灵剑之道”。<BR>
<BR>
所有剑歌者通过他们高强度的训练和对战神及剑道的奉献，学习能够创造灵剑的纪律形式。这是一种简单的魔法或精神掌控形式，通过纯粹的意念形成剑的形象。剑歌者通过集中精神形成剑，它在手中成形 -- 通常是一种苍白的光物，朦胧而虚无，也许是一件美丽的东西，是对道和众神奉献的象征，但不是武器。然而，那些最高级别、最敏感以及有魔法天赋的安塞，在压力下能够形成一把灵剑，舍海，它远不止光和空气 -- 它是一把势不可挡的强大武器，一把永远无法从主人手中夺走而不夺走其心智的武器。<BR>
<BR>
舍海成为了亨丁的武器，他用它杀死了成群结队的匪徒和横行于这片土地的游荡怪物。最终，在完成他的第90场决斗，击败了邪恶的贾尼克勋爵和他的七个巫妖追随者后，他确信自己确实是不可战胜的。亨丁随后转向阐述他的“剑道”哲学。在他六十岁那年，他作为一名隐士住在高沙漠山脉的一个洞穴中时，将他的学识写进了《圆之书》。<BR>
<BR>
那一年，亨丁参加了帝国的多次战役，击败了所有对手，认为自己已经准备好了死亡，便退隐到他的洞穴中，记录下他的战略和神秘愿景，与其他剑歌者分享。正是在他完成《圆之书》的卷轴之后，剑歌者们发现他正在创作他的死亡之诗，并准备与战神们一起进入最终的安息。<BR>
<BR>
六十岁时，他是一个精力充沛的人，认为自己已看透人生，但他的人民，剑歌者们需要他。他们前所未有地需要他。<BR>
<BR>
托恩的猎剑令已将剑歌者与平民分隔开来，而末代皇帝的崛起开启了沙漠帝国最后一次大纷争。皇帝和他的配偶艾丽莎试图通过摧毁剑歌者来从人民手中夺取帝国控制权的最后努力。希拉发誓要用他的匪徒大军（由兽人和帝国战争的残渣组成）搜出每一个剑歌者，并将他们从地球上清除。<BR>
<BR>
剑歌者从来都不是一个人口众多的民族。严酷的沙漠使得出生率很低，在无情的荒原中长大，只有那些拥有钢铁精神和意志的人才能生存下来。因此，这场最终被称为“歌者之战”的纷争，使得剑之民毫无准备，也未能将他们各自强大的技能联合起来，组成一支能够保卫家园和生命的军队。<BR>
<BR>
人们找到了弗兰达·亨丁，打断了他的死亡之诗，并将剑歌者的指挥权草草地强加于他。感谢未知的战争之神，亨丁有时间在他的洞穴中写下他多年积累的智慧、战略和舍海之道。剑歌者们从营地逃到沙漠的山丘和山脉中。逃到哈图“群山之父”的山脚下，亨丁曾在那里平静地写作并准备赴死，在那里，这些残余力量组成了圆环军团 -- 他们学习了亨丁之道、他的战略、他的战术，以及最终一击的伟大愿景。<BR>
<BR>
亨丁制定了一个七场战役的计划，将希拉的军队一步步引向荒野，引向哈图山脚下，在那里可以进行最后的决战。亨丁将他的计划称为“锤与砧”。每经过一场战役，亨丁的剑歌者就会进一步学习他的战略和战术，在使用舍海上变得更强大，并准备好在第七场战役中击败对手。就这样，前六场战役打响了，每场既非胜利也非失败，每场都引向下一场。希拉的大军跟随亨丁的小部队。在三十比一的劣势下，剑歌者们从未背离道。舞台已经搭好，希拉和他的军队被调遣到哈图山脚下，在那里，重锤落下。战斗激烈进行，那一天许多剑歌者倒下了。亨丁知道，活下来的剑歌者会很少，但希拉和他的邪恶帝国将不复存在，事情就这样发生了。<BR>
<BR>
最后，亨丁和不到两万名剑歌者在当天幸存下来，但没有留下任何可以掠夺和谋杀的邪恶军队，超过三十万人在哈图山那一天倒下。那些留下来逃跑和生存的人，都被风吹散了，不再有任何有组织的力量。<BR>
<BR>
剑歌者们收拾起他们的生活，折叠起帐篷，哀悼死者，跟随亨丁来到了海风行省的伟大港口城市阿克。在那里，亨丁有一支小船队在等待。剑歌者们离开了他们的沙漠，前往一片新的土地。他们在沙漠帝国不再受欢迎，他们离开，成为传说中被歌颂和谈论的对象。最后的伟大战士，舍海的歌者，《圆之书》，全都离开了那片他们的美德不被赏识的土地。在温和的公民眼中，他们因鲜血而赤红，尽管他们曾将他们从巨大的邪恶中拯救出来。<BR>
<BR>
剑歌者们发誓要在穿越广阔海洋前往新土地的过程中学习新的方式。采用一个新名字，但要纪念过去。为了纪念他们的最后一场战役，他们将新土地命名为落锤，并采用了红卫人这个名字。<BR>
<BR>
为了纪念伟大的战士亲王亨丁，落锤的每个家庭在壁炉旁都有一个地方，一个凹室，一个壁龛，足够大，可以容纳那卷轴 -- 《圆之书》。<BR>
