"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Redguards, Their History and Their Heroes<BR>
By Destri Melarg<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Notes on the Redguards, their history and their heroes.<BR><BR>
This is a publishers proof of the initial draft of my book, "REDGUARDS, THEIR HISTORY AND THEIR HEROES".<BR><BR>
The following is a collection of the tales, myths and history of the Redguards. Much of their history is shrouded in mystery and in the mists of time. It is hard to distinguish between myths, and real history.<BR><BR>
Below are the first chapters of the draft by Destri Melarg<BR><BR>
Author's note as translated into the Modern Tongue of Hammerfell:<BR><BR><BR>
Frandar Hunding was born in 2356 in the old way of reckoning, in our beloved deserts of the old land. The traditional rule of emperors had been overthrown in 2012, and although each successive emperor remained the figurehead of the empire, his powers were very much reduced. Since that time, our people saw 300 years of almost continuous civil war between the provincial lords, warrior monks and brigands, all fighting each other for land and power. Our people once were artisans, poets, and scholars, but the ever evolving strife made the way the sword inevitable - the song of the blade through the air, through flesh and bone, its ring against armor: an answer to our prayers.<BR><BR>
In the time of Lord Frandar the first Warrior Prince, lords called Yokeda built huge stone castles to protect themselves and their lands, and castle towns outside the walls begin to grow up. In 2245, however, Mansel Sesnit came to the fore. He became the Elden Yokeda, or military dictator, and for eight years succeeded in gaining control of almost the whole empire. When Sesnit was assassinated in 2253, a commoner took over the government. Randic Torn continued the work of unifying the Empire which Sesnit had begun, ruthlessly putting down any traces of insurrection. He revived the old gulf between the warriors - the sword singers - and the commoners by introducing restrictions on the wearing of swords. "Torn's Sword-hunt", as it was known, meant that only the singers were allowed to wear swords, which distinguished them from the rest of the population.<BR><BR>
Although Torn did much to settle the empire into its pre-strife ways, by the time of his death in 2373 internal disturbances still had not been completely eliminated. Upon his death, civil war broke out in earnest; war that made the prior 300 year turmoil pale in comparison. It was in this period that Frandar Hunding grew up.<BR><BR>
Hunding belonged to the sword-singers. This element of empire society grew from the desert artisans and was initially recruited from the young sons and daughters of the high families. They built the first temple to the unknown gods of War and build a training hall "The Hall of the Virtues of War". Within a few generations the way of the sword - the song of the blade - had become their life. The people of the blade kept their poetry and artisanship in building beautiful swords woven with magic and powers from the unknown gods. The greatest among them became known as Ansei or "Saints of the Sword". Each of these began their own training schools teaching their individual way of the sword. Those Ansei of the highest virtue wandered the country side engaging in battle, righting wrongs, and seeking to end the strife.<BR><BR>
To sum it up. Hunding, was a sword-singer, a master, no, a Master Ansei at a time when the peak of the strife was reborn out of the chaos of Torn's death. Many singers put up their swords and became artists, for the pull of the artisan heritage was strong; but others, like Hunding pursued the ideal of the warrior searching for enlightenment through the perilous paths of the Sword. Duels of revenge and tests of skill were common place, and fencing schools multiplied.<BR><BR>
Frandar do Hunding Hel Ansei No Shira, or as he is commonly known Frandar Hunding, was born in the far desert marches in the province of High Desert. Hunding is the name of the High Desert region near where he was born. No Shira means noble person or person of noble birth and Hel Ansei is his title of Sword Sainthood.<BR><BR>
Hunding's ancestors reach back to the beginning of recorded time in the high desert and were artisans and mystics, his grandfather was a retainer of the Elden Yokeda, Mansel Sesnit, and led many of the battles of unification prior to Sesnit's assassination.<BR><BR>
When he was 14, Hunding's father died in the one of the many insurrections, and he was left to support his mother and four brothers. His prowess with the sword however, made his life both difficult and easy. Easy in that his services came in great demand as a guardian and escort. Hard in that his reputation preceded him, and many awaited their turn to face him in battle and gain instant fame through his defeat.<BR><BR>
By the time Hunding was 30 he had fought and won more than 90 duels killing all his opponents. He became virtually invincible with the sword, gaining such skill and mastery that he finally stopped using the real swords created through the artisanship of his people and began using the Shehai or "way of the spirit sword".<BR><BR>
All sword singers learn through their intense training and devotion to the gods of war and way of the sword, the forms of discipline that allow the creation of the spirit sword. This is a simple form of magic or mind mastery where by a image of a sword is formed from pure thought. The sword singer forms the sword by concentrating, and it takes shape in his hand - usually a pale thing of light, misty and insubstantial, a thing of beauty perhaps, a symbol of devotion to the Way and the gods, but no weapon. However, those Ansei of the highest level and sensitivity and those with talent in magic, can at times of stress, form a spirit sword, the Shehai which is far more than light and air - it is an unstoppable weapon of great might, a weapon which can never be taken from the owner without also taking his mind.<BR><BR>
The Shehai became Hunding's weapon, and with this he slew bands of brigands and wandering monsters than infested the land. Hunding then turned to formulating his philosophy of"the Way of the Sword". It was after his completion of the scroll of the Circle that the Singers found him composing his death poem and preparing to join the gods of war in final rest.<BR><BR>

The Emperor and his consort Elisa's final effort to wrest control of the empire from the people by destroying the sword-singers. Hira vowed to search out every Singer with his Brigand army composed of Orcs and castoffs of the wars of the empire, and to scourge them from the face of the planet.<BR><BR>
The Sword Singers were never a numerous people. The harsh desert kept the births few, and growing up in the unforgiving wastes eliminated all but those of iron spirit and will. Thus the final strife which became knows as the "War of the Singers" found the people of the sword unprepared and unready to join together their individually great skills into an army that could defend their homes and lives.<BR><BR>
Frandar Hunding was sought out, his death poem interrupted, and unceremoniously command of the singers was thrust upon him. To the unknown gods of war great thanks is owed that Hunding had the time in his cave to write down his years of accumulated wisdom, of strategy, of the way of the Shehai. The singers fled from their camps up into the desert hills and mountains. Fled to the foot of Hattu "the father of Mountains" where Hunding had gone to write in peace and to die, and there these remnants formed into the Army of the Circle - they learned Hunding's Way, his strategies his tactics, and the final great vision for a master stroke.<BR><BR>
Hunding devised a plan of seven battles leading the Armies of Hira further and further into the wilderness to the foot of Hattu, where the final battle could be fought. Hunding called his plan the "Hammer and the Anvil". With each battle Hunding's Singers would further learn his strategies and tactics, grow strong in the use of the Shehai, and be ready to defeat their opponents in the seventh battle. And thus it was, the six first battles were waged, each neither victory or defeat, each leading to the next. The larger armies of Hira following the small army of Hunding. Outnumbered thirty to one, the singers never faltered from the Way. The stage was set, Hira and his Army maneuvered to the base of Hattu Mountain, where the hammer blow was delivered. The battle was pitched, and many singers fell that day. Hunding knew, that the singers who lived would be few, but Hira and his empire of evil would not live and so it went.<BR><BR>
At the end Hunding and less that twenty thousand Singers survived the day, but no army of evil was left to pillage and murder, more than three hundred thousand fell that day on Hattu. Of those who were left to run and live, all were scattered to the four winds, and organized force no more.<BR><BR>
The singers packed their lives, folded their tents, mourned their dead, and followed Hunding to the great port city of Arch, in the province of Seawind. There Hunding had a flotilla of ships waiting. The Singers left their desert for a new land. No longer welcome in the desert empire, they left to be sung about and spoken of in legend. The final great warrior, the singers of Shehai, the Book of Circles, all leaving that land where their virtue was unappreciated. Red, red with blood they were in the eyes of the gentle citizenry, never mind that they had saved them from a great evil.<BR><BR>
The singers vowed to learn new ways as they traveled across the great ocean to their new land. To adopt a new name, but to honor the past. In honor of their final battle, they named their new land Hammerfell and adopted the name Redguards.<BR><BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
红卫人，他们的历史与英雄<BR>
德斯特里·梅拉格 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
关于红卫人、他们的历史和英雄的笔记。<BR><BR>
这是我著作《红卫人，他们的历史与英雄》初稿的出版校对稿。<BR><BR>
以下是红卫人的故事、神话和历史的合集。他们的大部分历史都笼罩在神秘和时间的迷雾中。很难区分神话和真实历史。<BR><BR>
以下是德斯特里·梅拉格手稿的前几章<BR><BR>
作者注，翻译成现代落锤语：<BR><BR><BR>
弗兰达·亨丁出生于2356年，按旧历计算，在我们古老土地心爱的沙漠中。皇帝的传统统治在2012年被推翻，尽管随后的每位皇帝仍是帝国的名义元首，但其权力已大为削弱。自那时起，我们的人民经历了近300年几乎不间断的内战，行省领主、武僧和匪徒互相争斗，争夺土地和权力。我们的人民曾经是工匠、诗人和学者，但不断演变的纷争使剑道成为必然 -- 剑刃划过空气、划过血肉和骨头、撞击盔甲的声音：这是对我们祈祷的回答。<BR><BR>
在第一位战士亲王弗兰达勋爵的时代，被称为“约克达”的领主们建造了巨大的石头城堡来保护自己和他们的土地，城墙外的城堡城镇开始发展起来。然而，在2245年，曼塞尔·塞斯尼特崭露头角。他成为了埃尔登·约克达，即军事独裁者，并在八年内成功控制了几乎整个帝国。当塞斯尼特在2253年被暗杀时，一个平民接管了政府。兰迪克·托恩继续了塞斯尼特开始的统一帝国的工作，无情地镇压任何叛乱的迹象。他通过引入佩戴剑的限制，重新唤起了战士（剑歌者）和平民之间的旧日鸿沟。众所周知的“托恩猎剑令”意味着只有剑歌者才被允许佩剑，这使他们与其余人口区分开来。<BR><BR>
尽管托恩为帝国恢复战前状态做了很多努力，但到他在2373年去世时，内部骚乱仍未完全消除。他死后，内战真正爆发；这场战争使得之前三百年的动荡相形见绌。弗兰达·亨丁就是在这个时期长大的。<BR><BR>
亨丁属于剑歌者。帝国社会的这一元素源于沙漠工匠，最初是从显赫家族的年轻子女中招募的。他们建造了第一座供奉未知战争之神的神殿，并建造了一个训练厅“战争美德之厅”。几代之内，剑道 -- 剑刃之歌 -- 成为了他们的生命。剑之民将他们诗歌和工艺保留在建造美丽剑刃上，这些剑刃编织着来自未知之神的魔法和力量。他们中最伟大的被称为安塞或“剑之圣徒”。他们中的每一位都开始建立自己的训练学校，传授他们各自的剑道。那些品德最高尚的安塞在乡间游历，参与战斗，匡扶正义，并寻求结束纷争。<BR><BR>
总而言之。亨丁是一位剑歌者，一位大师，不，是一位安塞大师，正值纷争的顶峰从托恩死亡的混乱中重生的时代。许多剑歌者放下剑，成为了艺术家，因为工匠传统的吸引力很强大；但其他人，像亨丁，则追求战士的理想，通过剑的危险道路寻求启迪。复仇决斗和技能测试司空见惯，剑术学校成倍增加。<BR><BR>
弗兰达·多·亨丁·赫尔·安塞·诺·希拉，或者他通常被称为弗兰达·亨丁，出生在远在沙漠边疆的高沙漠行省。亨丁是他出生地附近的高沙漠地区的名字。诺·希拉意为高贵之人或出身高贵之人，赫尔·安塞是他的剑之圣徒头衔。<BR><BR>
亨丁的祖先可追溯到高沙漠有记载历史之初，他们是工匠和神秘主义者，他的祖父是埃尔登·约克达曼塞尔·塞斯尼特的侍从，并在塞斯尼特被暗杀前领导了许多统一战役。<BR><BR>
在他14岁时，亨丁的父亲在一次众多叛乱中去世，他留下供养母亲和四个兄弟。然而，他剑术的高超使他的生活既艰难又容易。容易在于他作为护卫和保镖的服务需求很大。艰难在于他的名声先于他，许多人等待轮到自己在战斗中面对他，并通过击败他来获得即时的名声。<BR><BR>
到亨丁30岁时，他已经战斗并赢得了90多场决斗，杀死了所有对手。他在剑术上变得几乎无敌，获得了如此高的技能和掌握程度，以至于他最终停止使用通过他人民的工艺制造的真剑，并开始使用舍海或“灵剑之道”。<BR><BR>
所有剑歌者通过他们高强度的训练和对战神及剑道的奉献，学习能够创造灵剑的纪律形式。这是一种简单的魔法或精神掌控形式，通过纯粹的意念形成剑的形象。剑歌者通过集中精神形成剑，它在手中成形 -- 通常是一种苍白的光物，朦胧而虚无，也许是一件美丽的东西，是对道和众神奉献的象征，但不是武器。然而，那些最高级别、最敏感以及有魔法天赋的安塞，在压力下能够形成一把灵剑，舍海，它远不止光和空气 -- 它是一把势不可挡的强大武器，一把永远无法从主人手中夺走而不夺走其心智的武器。<BR><BR>
舍海成为了亨丁的武器，他用它杀死了成群结队的匪徒和横行于这片土地的游荡怪物。最终，在完成他的第90场决斗，击败了邪恶的贾尼克勋爵和他的七个巫妖追随者后，他确信自己确实是不可战胜的。亨丁随后转向阐述他的“剑道”哲学。在他六十岁那年，他作为一名隐士住在高沙漠山脉中的一个洞穴中时，将他的学识写进了《圆之书》。<BR><BR>

六十岁时，他是一个精力充沛的人，认为自己已看透人生，但他的人民，剑歌者们需要他。他们前所未有地需要他。<BR><BR>
托恩的猎剑令已将剑歌者与平民分隔开来，而末代皇帝的崛起开启了沙漠帝国最后一次大纷争。皇帝和他的配偶艾丽莎试图通过摧毁剑歌者来从人民手中夺取帝国控制权的最后努力。希拉发誓要用他的匪徒大军（由兽人和帝国战争的残渣组成）搜出每一个剑歌者，并将他们从地球上清除。<BR><BR>
剑歌者从来都不是一个人口众多的民族。严酷的沙漠使得出生率很低，在无情的荒原中长大，只有那些拥有钢铁精神和意志的人才能生存下来。因此，这场最终被称为“歌者之战”的纷争，使得剑之民毫无准备，也未能将他们各自强大的技能联合起来，组成一支能够保卫家园和生命的军队。<BR><BR>
人们找到了弗兰达·亨丁，打断了他的死亡之诗，并将剑歌者的指挥权草草地强加于他。感谢未知的战争之神，亨丁有时间在他的洞穴中写下他多年积累的智慧、战略和舍海之道。剑歌者们从营地逃到沙漠的山丘和山脉中。逃到哈图“群山之父”的山脚下，亨丁曾在那里平静地写作并准备赴死，在那里，这些残余力量组成了圆环军团 -- 他们学习了亨丁之道、他的战略、他的战术，以及最终一击的伟大愿景。<BR><BR>
亨丁制定了一个七场战役的计划，将希拉的军队一步步引向荒野，引向哈图山脚下，在那里可以进行最后的决战。亨丁将他的计划称为“锤与砧”。每经过一场战役，亨丁的剑歌者就会进一步学习他的战略和战术，在使用舍海上变得更强大，并准备好在第七场战役中击败对手。就这样，前六场战役打响了，每场既非胜利也非失败，每场都引向下一场。希拉的大军跟随亨丁的小部队。在三十比一的劣势下，剑歌者们从未背离道。舞台已经搭好，希拉和他的军队被调遣到哈图山脚下，在那里，重锤落下。战斗激烈进行，那一天许多剑歌者倒下了。亨丁知道，活下来的剑歌者会很少，但希拉和他的邪恶帝国将不复存在，事情就这样发生了。<BR><BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Refugees<BR>
by Geros Albreigh<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The smell of the bay oozed through the stones of the cellar, salt and brined decay. The cellar itself had its own scents of old wine turned to vinegar, mildew, and the more exotic spices of herbs the healers had brought with them to tend to the wounded. There were more than fifty people squeezed into the big earthen room which had once been forgotten storage for the brothel above. The groaning and whimpering had ceased for now, and all was still, as if the hospital had turned into a mass grave.<BR>
<BR>
"Mother," a Redguard boy whispered. "What was that?"<BR>
<BR>
The boy's mother was about to answer him when there was another rolling roar from outside, which grew louder and louder, as if some great but incorporeal beast had come into the cellar. The walls trembled and dust burst from the ceiling in a rain of powder.<BR>
<BR>
Unlike the last time, no one screamed. They waited until the weird, haunting sound had past, and then was replaced by the soft rumble of the distant battle.<BR>
<BR>
A wounded soldier began whispering Mara's Prayer from the Doomed.<BR>
<BR>
"Mankar," a Bosmer woman curled up in a cot hissed, her eyes feverish, flesh white and wet with sweat. "He is coming!"<BR>
<BR>
"Who is coming?" asked the boy, grasping his mother's skirt tight.<BR>
<BR>
"Who do you think, lad? The sweets monger?" a grizzled one-armed Redguard growled. "The Camoran Usurper."<BR>
<BR>
The boy's mother shot an angry look at the old warrior. "She doesn't know what she's saying. She's sick."<BR>
<BR>
The boy nodded. His mother was usually right. He had not yet even been born when people began whispering that the Camoran Usurper was coming towards her little village, and she had packed up their belongings to flee. Their neighbors had laughed at her, she said, saying that Rihad and Taneth would handily defeat him. Her husband, Lukar's father who he was never to meet, had also laughed at her. It was the harvest time, and she would miss out on the celebrations. But his mother, Miak-I, was right. Two weeks after she fled the village, she heard the tale that it had been obliterated during the night with no survivors. Rihad and Taneth had both fallen. The Usurper was unstoppable.<BR>
<BR>
Lukar had been born and grown up in refugee camps throughout Hammerfell. He had never known a friend for more than a few days. He knew that when the sky burned red to the west, they would pack up and move east. When it burned to the south, they moved north. At last, after twelve years of moving from camp to camp, they had taken passage across the Iliac Bay to the province of High Rock and the barony of Dwynnen. There Miak-I had promised, and hoped, that they would have a peaceful, permanent home.<BR>
<BR>
It was so green there, it blinded him. Unlike Hammerfell, which was only green in certain seasons and in certain places, Dwynnen was verdant year round. Until wintertide, when it began to snow, and Lukar had been frightened of it at first. He was ashamed to think of it now, when there was real danger, but the red clouds of war, the stink and pain of the refugee camp, that was familiar.<BR>
<BR>
Now, the red sky was on the horizon of the bay and coming closer, and he longed for the days when a scattering of white made him cry.<BR>
<BR>
"Mankar!" the Bosmer woman cried out again. "He is coming, and he will bring death!"<BR>
<BR>
"No one is coming," said a pretty young Breton healer, coming to the woman's side. "Hush now."<BR>
<BR>
"Hello?" came a voice from above.<BR>
<BR>
The whole room, almost together as one gasped. A Bosmer limped down the shoddy wooden stairs, his friendly face very obviously not that of the Camoran Usurper.<BR>
<BR>
"Sorry if I frightened you," he said. "I was told there were healers here, and I could use a little help."<BR>
<BR>
Rosayna hurried to take a look at the Bosmer's wounds on his leg and chest. Dishelved but still beautiful, she was one of the favorites at the brothel, who had learned her healing skill along with her more vocational skills at the House of Dibella. She carefully but quickly pulled the rent leather cuirass, chausses, tassets, grieves, and boots off him, and placed them to the side while she examined the injuries.<BR>
<BR>
The old Redguard warrior picked them up and studied them. "You were in the war?"<BR>
<BR>
"Next to it is probably a better way to put it," the Bosmer smiled, wincing slightly at Rosayna's touch. "Behind it, beside it, in front of it. My name's Orben Elmlock. I'm a scout. I try to avoid the real battle, so I can get back and report what I see. A good job for people who don't like the color of their own blood very much."<BR>
<BR>
"Hzim," said the warrior, shaking Orben's hand. "I can't fight anymore, but I can fix up this armor if you're going to return."<BR>
<BR>
"You're a leathersmith?"<BR>
<BR>
"Naw, just a jack of all trades," replied Hzim, opening up a small canister of wax to prep the hard but flexible leather. "I could tell you were a scout from the armor, though. Can you tell us what you've been spying on? We've been down in here for half a day now, with no word from the outside."<BR>

The cellar itself had its own scents of old wine turned to vinegar, mildew, and the more exotic spices of herbs the healers had brought with them to tend to the wounded. There were more than fifty people squeezed into the big earthen room which had once been forgotten storage for the brothel above. Unlike the last time, no one screamed. They waited until the weird, haunting sound had past, and then was replaced by the soft rumble of the distant battle.<BR>
<BR>
A wounded soldier began whispering Mara's Prayer from the Doomed.<BR>
<BR>
"Mankar," a Bosmer woman curled up in a cot hissed, her eyes feverish, flesh white and wet with sweat. "He is coming!"<BR>
<BR>
"Who is coming?" asked the boy, grasping his mother's skirt tight.<BR>
<BR>
"Who do you think, lad? The sweets monger?" a grizzled one-armed Redguard growled. "The Camoran Usurper."<BR>
<BR>
The boy's mother shot an angry look at the old warrior. "She doesn't know what she's saying. She's sick."<BR>
<BR>
The boy nodded. His mother was usually right. He had not yet even been born when people began whispering that the Camoran Usurper was coming towards her little village, and she had packed up their belongings to flee. Their neighbors had laughed at her, she said, saying that Rihad and Taneth would handily defeat him. Her husband, Lukar's father who he was never to meet, had also laughed at her. It was the harvest time, and she would miss out on the celebrations. But his mother, Miak-I, was right. Two weeks after she fled the village, she heard the tale that it had been obliterated during the night with no survivors. Rihad and Taneth had both fallen. The Usurper was unstoppable.<BR>
<BR>
Lukar had been born and grown up in refugee camps throughout Hammerfell. He had never known a friend for more than a few days. He knew that when the sky burned red to the west, they would pack up and move east. When it burned to the south, they moved north. At last, after twelve years of moving from camp to camp, they had taken passage across the Iliac Bay to the province of High Rock and the barony of Dwynnen. There Miak-I had promised, and hoped, that they would have a peaceful, permanent home.<BR>
<BR>
It was so green there, it blinded him. Unlike Hammerfell, which was only green in certain seasons and in certain places, Dwynnen was verdant year round. Until wintertide, when it began to snow, and Lukar had been frightened of it at first. He was ashamed to think of it now, when there was real danger, but the red clouds of war, the stink and pain of the refugee camp, that was familiar.<BR>
<BR>
Now, the red sky was on the horizon of the bay and coming closer, and he longed for the days when a scattering of white made him cry.<BR>
<BR>
"Mankar!" the Bosmer woman cried out again. "He is coming, and he will bring death!"<BR>
<BR>
"No one is coming," said a pretty young Breton healer, coming to the woman's side. "Hush now."<BR>
<BR>
"Hello?" came a voice from above.<BR>
<BR>
The whole room, almost together as one gasped. A Bosmer limped down the shoddy wooden stairs, his friendly face very obviously not that of the Camoran Usurper.<BR>
<BR>
"Sorry if I frightened you," he said. "I was told there were healers here, and I could use a little help."<BR>
<BR>
Rosayna hurried to take a look at the Bosmer's wounds on his leg and chest. Dishelved but still beautiful, she was one of the favorites at the brothel, who had learned her healing skill along with her more vocational skills at the House of Dibella. She carefully but quickly pulled the rent leather cuirass, chausses, tassets, grieves, and boots off him, and placed them to the side while she examined the injuries.<BR>
<BR>
The old Redguard warrior picked them up and studied them. "You were in the war?"<BR>
<BR>
"Next to it is probably a better way to put it," the Bosmer smiled, wincing slightly at Rosayna's touch. "Behind it, beside it, in front of it. My name's Orben Elmlock. I'm a scout. I try to avoid the real battle, so I can get back and report what I see. A good job for people who don't like the color of their own blood very much."<BR>
<BR>
"Hzim," said the warrior, shaking Orben's hand. "I can't fight anymore, but I can fix up this armor if you're going to return."<BR>
<BR>
"You're a leathersmith?"<BR>
<BR>
"Naw, just a jack of all trades," replied Hzim, opening up a small canister of wax to prep the hard but flexible leather. "I could tell you were a scout from the armor, though. Can you tell us what you've been spying on? We've been down in here for half a day now, with no word from the outside."<BR>
<BR>
"The entire Iliac Bay is one great battlefield on the waves," said Orben and sighed as Rosayna's spell began to close his jagged but shallow wounds. "We've shut off the invasion from the mouth of the bay, but I was coming from the coast, and the enemy's army is marching over the Wrothgarian Mountains. That's where I had my little scuffle. It's not too surprising, moving the flank in from the side while the front battle is occupied. It's a play right out of Camoran Kaltos's book of tricks the Hart-King borrowed."<BR>
<BR>
"The Hart-King?" Lukar asked. He had been listening quietly, understanding everything except that.<BR>
<BR>
"Haymon Camoran, the Camoran Usurper, Haymon Hart-King, they're all the same, lad. He's a complicated fellow, and needs more than one name."<BR>
<BR>
"You know him?" Miak-I asked, stepping forward.<BR>
<BR>
"Near on twenty years, before this whole black, bloody business. I was Camoran Kaltos's chief scout, and Haymon was his sorcerer and advisor. I helped them both, when they were vying for the Camoran throne, and began the conquest of - Ouch!"<BR>
<BR>
Rosayna has ceased her healing. With eyes of fury, she had reversed her spell, and the closed, mended wounds were opening again, dark infections returning. She held him with surprising strength when Orben tried to pull back.<BR>
<BR>
"You bastard," the healer courtesan hissed. "I have a cousin in Falinesti, a priestess."<BR>
<BR>
"She's fine!" Orben yelped. "Lord Kaltos was very adamant about not harming anyone who did not pose a threat ..."<BR>
<BR>
"I think the people of Kvatch would disagree with that assessment," said Hzim, coldly.<BR>
<BR>
"That was horrible, the worst thing I have ever seen," Orben nodded. "Kaltos wept when he saw what Haymon had done. My master did everything he could to stop it, begging the Hart-King to return to Valenwood. But he turned on Kaltos, and we fled. We are not your enemy, and we have never been. Kaltos could do nothing to prevent the horror that the Usurper has brought to the Colovian West and Hammerfell, and he has fought for fifteen years to prevent more."<BR>
<BR>
The frightening bestial roar passed through the cellar again, even louder than before. The wounded could not help groaning in helpless terror.<BR>
<BR>
"And what is that?" Miak-I sneered. "Another of Camoran Kaltos's tricks that the Usurper picked up?"<BR>
<BR>
"It is indeed a trick, as a matter of fact," Orben yelled, above the screech. "It's a phastasm he employs to scare people. He had to use fear tactics in the beginning when his power was ascending, and he has to fall back on them now for his power is waning. That is why it took him two years to conquer Valenwood, and another thirteen to half-conquer Hammerfell. No offense to you Redguards, but it isn't only your battle prowess that has been holding him back. He does not have the support he used to have from his Master -"<BR>
<BR>
The echoing roar increased in intensity before once again falling silent.<BR>
<BR>
"Mankar!" the Bosmer woman groaned. "He comes, and he will destroy all!"<BR>
<BR>
"His Master?" asked Lukar, but Orben's eyes had gone to the Bosmer woman, curled up in her blood-soaked cot.<BR>
<BR>
"Who is she?" Orben asked Rosayna.<BR>
<BR>
"One of the refugees, of course, from your friendly little war in Valenwood before you and your Kaltos changed sides," the healer replied. "I think her name is Kaalys."<BR>
<BR>
"By Jephre," Orben whispered under his breath, limping over to the woman's cot and wiping the sweat and blood streaked hair from her pallid face. "Kaalys, it's Orben. Do you remember me? How did you get here? Did he hurt you?"<BR>
<BR>
"Mankar!" Kaalys moaned.<BR>
<BR>
"That's all she says," said Rosayna.<BR>
<BR>
"I don't know what that it is," Orben frowned. "Not the Usurper, though she knew him too. Very well. She was a favorite of his."<BR>
<BR>
"His favorites, you, Kaltos, her, all seem to turn against him," said Miak-I.<BR>
<BR>
"That is why he will fall," replied Hzim.<BR>
<BR>
Armored footfall rang along the ceiling, and the cellar door burst open. It was the captain of Baron Othrok's castle guards. "The docks are on fire! If you want to live, you'll need to take refuge at Castle Wightmoor!"<BR>
<BR>
"We need help!" Rosayna called back, but she knew that the guards were needed for defense, not to help carry the sick to safety.<BR>
<BR>
With ten guards who could be spared and the most able-bodied of the wounded assisting, the cellar was emptied as the streets of Dwynnen filled with smoke, and fire began to spread through the chaos. It had been a single fireball miscast out at sea striking the docks, but the damage would be tremendous. Some hours later, in the courtyard of the mighty castle, the healers were able to set up the cots and begin to tend once again to the suffering of the innocent. The first person Rosayna found was Orben Elmlock. Even with his wounds reopened, he had helped carry two of the patients into the castle.<BR>
<BR>
"I'm sorry," she said as she pressed her healing hands onto his wounds. "I lost my temper. I forgot that I am a healer."<BR>
<BR>
"Where is Kaalys?" Orben asked.<BR>
<BR>
"She's not here?" Rosayna said, looking around. "She must have run away."<BR>
<BR>
"Run away? But wasn't she injured?"<BR>
<BR>
"It was not a healthy situation, but new mothers can surprise you with what they can do when it's all over."<BR>
<BR>
"She was pregnant?" Orben gasped<BR>
<BR>
"Yes. It wasn't such a difficult birth in the end. She was holding the boy in her arms when I saw her last. She said she had done it herself."<BR>
<BR>
"She was pregnant," Orben murmured again. "The mistress of the Camoran Usurper was pregnant."<BR>
<BR>
Word quickly spread throughout the castle that the battle was over, and more than that, the war was over. Haymon Camoran's forces had been defeated at sea, and in the mountains. The Hart-King was dead.<BR>
<BR>
Lukar watched down from the battlements into the dark woods that surrounded Dwynnen. He had heard about Kaalys, and he imagined a desperate woman fleeing with her newborn baby in her arms into the wilderness. Kaalys would have nowhere to go, no one to protect them. She and her baby would be a refugee, like Miak-I and him had been. Reflecting back, he remembered her words.<BR>
<BR>
He is coming. He is coming, and he will bring death. He will destroy all.<BR>
<BR>
Lukar remembered her eyes. She was sick, but not afraid. Who was this "He" who was coming if the Camoran Usurper was dead?<BR>
<BR>
"Did she say nothing else?" asked Orben.<BR>
<BR>
"She told me the baby's name," Rosayna replied. "Mankar."<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
In Regards to the Dunmeri Chitin Armor<BR>
by Roiwra, Military Historian and Enthusiast<BR>
1st Edition; Imperial City, Cyrodiil<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
All civilizations and societies are products of their environment. Although this is a very useful principle for those that aspire to study the history or culture(s) of Tamriel, it becomes even more prominent when one takes it upon him to analyze the Dunmer of the East.
<BR>
At first glance, it might seem peculiar that the Dunmer use animal parts to manufacture their armor instead of iron and steel like the Imperials and the Nords. However, one has to take into account the exodus to Morrowind. This fated migration to the East stripped the Chimer (ancestors of the Dunmer) from Aldmeri resources and methodology of the time, forcing the new nation to start from the ground up.
<BR>
As one might imagine, the first step was the development of agriculture and husbandry. Netch leather was used for clothing and insect resin for a plethora of tool making, and it was not long before warfare forced the denizens of Morrowind to come up with ways to defend themselves.
<BR>
The protective chitin of native insects had various applications before its use as means of defense. As argued by notable Dunmer historians, the implementation in shield-making probably predates use in armor, but not by much.
<BR>
The chitin style was a recipient of much experimentation early on, but its design eventually reached its apex. The modern style consists of a multitude of insect carapace layers, held together by powerful resinous glues that act as insulation, strengthening agent and padding.
<BR>
The material from which the armor is made permits air flow, allowing the warrior within to endure hot summer days and last longer in combat. As such, chitin armor has been (and continues to be) used by light infantry, whose main role is to outflank more heavily equipped adversaries.
<BR>
There is no doubt that chitin is a unique and cost-effective armor material that will be used for generations to come in land of the Dunmer. Perhaps other cultures, including that of the people of the Empire of Tamriel, could learn much from the adaptability of the Dunmer.

For Hrol had seen in his visions the snakes to come and sought to heal all the borders of his forebears. And to this host appeared at last a spirit who resembled none other than El-Estia, queen of ancienttimes, who bore in her left hand the dragonfire of the aka-tosh and in her right hand the jewels of the covenant and on her breast a wound that spilt void onto her mangled feet. And seeing El-Estia and Chim-el Adabal, Hrol and his knights wailed and set to their knees and prayed for all things to become as right. Unto them the spirit said, I am the healer of all men and the mother of dragons, but as you have run so many times from me so shall I run until you learn my pain, which renders you and all this land dead.<BR>
<BR>
And the spirit fled from them, and they split among hills and forests to find her, all grieving that they had become a villainous people. Hrol and his shieldthane were the only ones to find her, and the king spoke to her, saying, I love you sweet Aless, sweet wife of Shor and of Auri-el and the Sacred Bull, and would render this land alive again, not through pain but through a return to the dragon-fires of covenant, to join east and west and throw off all ruin. And the shieldthane bore witness to the spirit opening naked to his king, carving on a nearby rock the words AND HROL DID LOVE UNTO A HILLOCK before dying in the sight of their union.<BR>
<BR>
When the fifteen other knights found King Hrol, they saw him dead after his labors against a mound of mud. And they parted each in their way, and some went mad, and the two that returned to their homeland beyond Twil would say nothing of Hrol, and acted ashamed for him.<BR>
<BR>
But after nine months that mound of mud became as a small mountain, and there were whispers among the shepherds and bulls. A small community of believers gathered around that growing hill during the days of its first churning, and they were the first to name it the Golden Hill, Sancre Tor. And it was the shepherdess Sed-Yenna who dared climb the hill when she heard his first cry, and at its peak she saw what it had yielded, an infant she named Reman, which is "Light of Man."<BR>
<BR>
And in the child's forehead was the Chim-el Adabal, alive with the dragon-fires of yore and divine promise, and none dared obstruct Sed-Yenna when she climbed the steps of White-Gold Tower to place the babe Reman on his Throne, where he spoke as an adult, saying I AM CYRODIIL COME.<BR>
<BR>
Chapter 2: The Chevalier Renald, Blade of the Pig<BR>
And in the days of interregnum, the Chim-el Adabal was lost again amid the petty wars of gone-heathen kings. West and east knew no union then and all the lands outside of them saw Cyrodiil as a nest of snakemen and snakes. And for four more hundreds of years did the seat of Reman stay sundered, with only the machinations of a group of loyal knights keeping all its borders from throwing wide.<BR>
<BR>
These loyal knights did go by no name then, but were known by their eastern swords and painted eyes, and it was whispered that they were descended from the bodyguard of old Reman. One of their number, called the Chevalier Renald, discovered the prowess of Cuhlecain and then supported him towards the throne. Only later would it be revealed that Renald did this thing to come closer to Talos, anon Stormcrown, the glorious yet-emperor Tiber Septim; only later still, that he was under instruction by a pig.<BR>
<BR>
Long glory was wife to the all the knights of the dragon-banner, who knew no other and were brothers before beyond many seas and now were brothers under the law named the blade-surrender of Pale Pass. And having vampire blood these brother-knights lived for ages through and past Reman and then kept guard over his ward, the coiled king, Versidue-Shaie. The snake-captain Vershu became Renald became the protector of the northern west when the black dart was hooked into Savirien-Chorak.<BR>
<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
雷曼纳达<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
第一章：桑克雷·托与雷曼的诞生<BR>
在那些日子里，西罗帝尔人的帝国已经死去，只存在于记忆之中，因为战争、蛞蝓饥荒和邪恶的统治者，西方与东方分裂，科洛维亚的疏离持续了大约四百年。大地因这种分裂而病痛。曾经值得尊敬的西方国王，安维尔和萨查尔的，佛克瑞斯和德洛迪尔的，因骄傲和习惯变成了盗贼领主，忘记了盟约。在心脏地，情况也好不到哪里去，神秘主义者和虚假的蛾王子们沉浸在药物麻醉或邪恶的研究中，几代以来无人坐在王座上。蛇和蛇的警告被忽视，大地流淌着幽灵，深陷的洞穴直通寒冷的海港。据说，甚至连光荣之王的护符 -- 钦-艾尔·阿达巴尔也已丢失，其人民认为没有理由去寻找它。<BR>
<BR>
正是在这种黑暗中，赫罗尔国王从失落的特维尔以外的土地出发，带着一支由十八减一位的探险骑士组成的队伍，他们都是西方的儿女。因为赫罗尔在幻象中看到了即将到来的蛇，并试图治愈他祖先的所有边界。最后，一个灵魂出现在这支队伍面前，她酷似古时候的女王埃尔-埃斯蒂亚，她左手握着阿卡托什的龙火，右手握着盟约的宝石，胸前有一道伤口，虚空从伤口洒落到她残破的脚上。看到埃尔-埃斯蒂亚和钦-艾尔·阿达巴尔，赫罗尔和他的骑士们哀嚎着跪下，祈祷一切恢复正常。灵魂对他们说：我是所有人类的治疗师，是龙之母，但正如你们多次从我身边逃跑一样，我也会逃跑，直到你们学会我的痛苦，这种痛苦使你们和这片土地都死去。<BR>
<BR>
灵魂从他们面前逃走了，他们分散在山丘和森林中寻找她，都为自己成为一个邪恶的民族而悲伤。只有赫罗尔和他的盾乡绅找到了她，国王对她说：我爱你，亲爱的阿莱西亚，朔尔、奥瑞-埃尔和圣牛亲爱的妻子，我将使这片土地重获生机，不是通过痛苦，而是通过回归盟约的龙火，连接东西方，摆脱一切毁灭。盾乡绅目睹了灵魂在国王面前赤裸地张开，在附近的岩石上刻下“赫罗尔曾爱上一座小丘”的字样，然后在他们结合的景象中死去。<BR>
<BR>
当其他十五位骑士找到赫罗尔国王时，他们看到他已死在对抗一个泥堆的劳作之后。他们各奔东西，有些人疯了，那两个回到特维尔以外家乡的人对赫罗尔只字不提，并为他感到羞愧。<BR>
<BR>
但九个月后，那个泥堆变成了一座小山，牧羊人和公牛之间流传着窃窃私语。一个由信徒组成的小社区在这座不断增长的山丘最初翻腾的日子里聚集在它周围，他们最先称它为金丘，桑克雷·托。正是牧羊女塞德-耶娜，当她听到他的第一声啼哭时，敢于爬上那座山，在山顶她看到了它所诞生的东西，一个婴儿，她给他取名雷曼，意为“人类之光”。<BR>
<BR>
孩子的额头上镶着钦-艾尔·阿达巴尔，闪耀着昔日的龙火和神圣的承诺，当塞德-耶娜爬上白金塔的台阶，将婴儿雷曼放在他的王座上时，无人敢阻拦，他在那里像个成年人一样说话：我是西罗帝尔降临。<BR>
<BR>
第二章：骑士雷纳德，猪之刃<BR>
在大空位的日子里，钦-艾尔·阿达巴尔在逝去的异教国王的 petty 战争中再次丢失。那时，西方和东方没有联合，它们之外的所有土地都将西罗帝尔视为蛇人和蛇的巢穴。又过了四百年，雷曼的王座依然分裂，只有一群忠诚骑士的谋划才使其所有边界不至于豁开。<BR>
<BR>
这些忠诚的骑士当时没有名字，但以其东方的剑和画过的眼睛而闻名，有人低声说他们是古老雷曼的卫队后裔。其中一人，被称为骑士雷纳德，发现了库里凯因的 prowess，然后支持他走向王座。直到后来才揭示，雷纳德这样做是为了接近塔洛斯，别名风暴王冠，光荣的未来皇帝泰伯·塞普汀；更晚些时候才揭示，他是在一头猪的指示下行动的。<BR>
<BR>
漫长的荣耀曾是所有龙旗骑士的妻子，他们不认他人，是远渡重洋前的兄弟，现在则是苍白关隘剑降之下的兄弟。这些兄弟骑士拥有吸血鬼之血，他们活了很久，经历了雷曼时代并延续下去，然后守护着他的被监护人，盘绕之王，维西杜-沙伊。当黑色飞镖刺入萨维里恩-乔拉克时，蛇之船长维尔舒变成了雷纳德，成为了西北方的保护者。<BR>
<BR>

The Restless North, Book I
动荡的北方，卷一

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_RestlessNorthSHOTN_V1
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Restless North, Book I<BR>
by Alarne Gold-Quill<BR><BR>
"The snake-man brought his southern gods with him, and was clearly loved of them for he did as he pleased in those days and saw no misfortune."
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Hoari staggered back to the camp, a bucket of ice-cold stream water in each hand and his breath frosting in the twilight air. He made his way through the cookfires and groups of singing soldiers until he found his own tent in the deepening gloom. Demka had got a fire going and greeted him with a smile as he set the buckets down and began to mix the dough for their camp-bread. Hoari regarded her with a grin of his own as he stretched and kneaded their dinner, reflecting on the pleasant strangeness of his situation. Demka was a Redguard warrior in the service of Laintar and its thane Rog the Biter, having risen from itinerant sellsword to trusted retainer in her lord's household. It was unusual to see a Redguard serving in a Nordic army -- conventional wisdom, particularly of western Nords, was that her people were too free-spirited to fight effectively in formation -- but she had decisively proven her valor and discipline in Rog's shield wall. That was where she had found Hoari, and it did not take the two of them long to start sharing a tent on cold nights as the Laintar leidang marched north.<BR>
<BR>
They were travelling to join the gathering of chieftains and jarls outside Danstrar, where the palace of the Potentate still smouldered. The Tjaski-men had seized the southern throne through despicable guile and ordered the dissolution of all forces and clans independent of the Legions, a provocation to which the kingdoms and lesser holds of Skyrim had responded with outright rebellion. Hoari was only a woodsmith who had answered the summons of his thane, no great warrior like his war-wife or the other members of Rog's hird, but he was determined that in some small way the head of his axe would help to liberate the land from its shameful foreign occupation. Demka had laughed when he announced this, but not unkindly, and reassured him that her oath ensured they fought for the same goal. That same laugh brought him back to the present, and he blinked away the reverie.<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

The clever-man conferred with his companion and then rose to address the crowd, which pressed closer so as not to miss the words of so esteemed a lawspeaker and rememberer.<BR>

“我告诉过你什么，亲爱的？”德姆卡的声音在他上方歌唱，“剑刃才是对付不守规矩的死者的唯一方法。现在快点，起床帮我打倒它们！”<BR>
<BR>
当尖叫声和呼喊声终于传入他的耳朵时，霍阿里从他们帐篷的废墟望出去，看到一大群尸体蜂拥而至，穿过乡绅罗格的勒当营地。这尸群似乎无穷无尽，几乎包围了他们这支小小的队伍，尽管莱恩塔的诺德人仍在坚守，砍杀着那些冲过来的尸鬼。在黎明的空气中赤裸着、冻得发抖，霍阿里毫不犹豫地抓起他的斧头，跟在德姆卡身后冲入了混战。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Rislav the Righteous<BR>
By Sinjin<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Like all true heroes, Rislav Larich had inauspicious beginnings. We are told by chroniclers that the springtide night in the 448th year of the first era on which he was born was unseasonably cold, and that his mother Queen Lynada died very shortly after setting eyes upon her son. If he were much beloved of his father, King Mhorus of Skingrad, who already had plenty of heirs, three sons and four daughters before him, the chroniclers make no mention of it.<BR>
<BR>
His existence was so very undistinguished that we hear virtually nothing of him for the first twenty years of his life. His schooling, we can suppose, was similar to that of any "spare prince" in the Colovian West, with Ayleid tutors to teach him the ways of hunting and battle. Etiquette, religious instruction, and even basic statecraft were seldom a part of the training of a prince of the Highlands, as it was in the more civilized valley of Nibenay.<BR>
<BR>
There is a brief reference to him, together with his family, as part of the rolls of honor during the coronation of the Emperor Gorieus on the 23rd of Sun's Dawn 1E 461. The ceremony, of course, held during the time of the Alessian Doctrines of Marukh, and so was without entertainment, but the thirteen-year-old Rislav was still witness to some of the greatest figures of legend. The Beast of Anequina, Darloc Brae, represented his kingdom, giving honor to the Empire. The Chieftain of Skyrim Kjoric the White and his son Hoag were in attendance. And despite the Empire's intolerance of all elves, chimer Indoril Nerevar and dwemer Dumac Dwarfking were evidently there as well, diplomatically representing Resdayn, all in relative peace.<BR>
<BR>
Also mentioned on the rolls was a young mer in service to the Imperial court of High Rock, who was to have a great history with Rislav. Ryain Direnni.<BR>
<BR>
Whether the two young men of about the same age met and conversed is entirely the stuff of historian's fancy. Ryain is spoken of in praising words as a powerful land-owner, eventually buying the island of Balfiera in the Iliac Bay and gradually conquering all of High Rock and large parts of Hammerfell and Skyrim, but Rislav is not heard of again in history's books for another seventeen years. We can only offer supposition based on the facts that follow.<BR>
<BR>
Children of kings are, of course, married to the children of other kings to bind alliances. The kingdoms of Skingrad and Kvatch skirmished over common territory throughout the fifth century, until they reached a peace in the year 472. The details of this accord are not recorded, but since we know that Prince Rislav was in the court of Kvatch six years later, as husband to Belene, the daughter of King Justinius, it is fair to make an educated guess that they were married then to make peace.<BR>
<BR>
This brings us to the year 478, when a great plague swept through all of Cyrodiil and seemed particularly concentrated in the independent Colovian West. Among the victims were King Mhorus and the rest of the entire royal family in Skingrad. Rislav's only surviving elder brother, Dorald, survived, being in the Imperial City as a priest of Marukh. He returned to his homeland to assume the throne.<BR>
<BR>
Of Dorald, we have some history. The King's second son, he was slightly simple-minded and evidently very pious. All the chroniclers spoke of his sweetness and decency, how he saw a vision in his early years that brought him - with his father's blessing - from Skingrad to the Imperial City and the priesthood. The priesthood of Marukh, of course, saw no difference between spiritual and political matters. It was the religion of the Alessian Empire, and it taught that to resist the Emperor was to resist the Gods. Given that, it is scarcely a surprise what Dorald did when he became King of the independent kingdom of Skingrad.<BR>
<BR>
His first edict, on his very first day, was to cede the kingdom to the Empire.<BR>
<BR>
The reaction throughout the Colovian Estates was shock and outrage, nowhere more so than in the court of Kvatch. Rislav Larich, we are told, rode forth to his brother's kingdom, together with his wife and two dozen of his father-in-law's cavalry. It was surely not an impressive army, no matter how the chroniclers embellish it, but they had little trouble defeating all the guards Dorald sent to stop them. In truth, there was no actual battling, for the soldiers of Skingrad resented their new king's decision to give up their autonomy.<BR>
<BR>
The brothers faced one another in the castle courtyard where they had grown up.<BR>
<BR>
In typical Colovian fashion, there was no trial, no accusations of treason, no jury, no judge. Only an executioner.<BR>
<BR>
"Thou art no brother of mine," Rislav Larich said, and struck Dorald's head from his shoulders in one blow. He was crowned King of Skingrad still holding the same bloody axe in his arms.<BR>
<BR>
If King Rislav had no battle experience beforehand, that was shortly to change. Word spread quickly to the Imperial City that Skingrad, once offered, was now being taken back. Gorieus was an accomplished warrior even before taking the throne, and the seventeen years he had as Emperor were scarcely peaceful. Only eight months before Dorald's assassination and Rislav's ascendancy, Gorieus and the Alessian army had faced another of his coronation guests, Kjoric the White, on the fields of the frozen north. The High Chieftain of Skyrim lost his life in the Battle of Sungard. While the pact of chieftains was selecting a new leader, Cyrodiil was busily grabbing back the land of southern Skyrim that it had lost.<BR>
<BR>
In short, Emperor Gorieus knew how to deal with rebellious vassals.<BR>
<BR>
The Alessian army poured westward "like a flood of death," to borrow the chronicler's phrase, in numbers far exceeding what would be required to conquer Skingrad. Gorieus could not have thought actual battle was likely. Rislav, as we said, had little to no experience at warfare, and only a few days' practice at kingcraft. His kingdom and all of the Colovian West had just been ravaged by plague. The Alessians anticipated that a mere show of arms, and a surrender.<BR>
<BR>
Rislav instead prepared for battle. He quickly inspected his troops and drew up plans.<BR>
<BR>
The chroniclers who had heretofore ignored the life of Rislav now devote verse after verse describing the king's aspect with fetishistic delight. While it may lack literary merit and taste, we are at least given some details at last. Not surprisingly, the king wore the finest armor of his era, as the Colovian Estates then had the finest leathersmiths - the only type of armor available - in all of Tamriel. The king's klibanion mail, boiled and waxed for hardness, and studded with inch-long spikes, was a rich chestnut red, and he wore it over his black tunic but under his black cloak. The statue of Rislav the Righteous which now stands in Skingrad is a romanticized version of king, but not inaccurate except in the armor represented. No bard of the Colovian West would have gone to the market so lightly protected. But it does, as we will see, include the most important accouterments of Rislav: his trained hawk and his fast horse.<BR>
<BR>
The winter rains had washed through the roads to the south, sending much of the West Weald spilling into Valenwood. The Emperor took the northern route, and King Rislav with a small patrol of guards met him at a low pass on what is now the Gold Road. The Emperor's army, it is said, was so large that the Beast of Anequina could hear its march from hundreds of miles away, and despite himself, the chroniclers say, he quaked in fear.<BR>
<BR>
Rislav, it was said, did not quake. With perfect politeness, he told the Emperor that his party was too large to be accommodated in the tiny kingdom of Skingrad.<BR>
<BR>
"Next time," Rislav said. "Write before you come."<BR>
<BR>
The Emperor was, like most Alessian Emperors, not a man of great humor, and he thought Rislav touched by Sheogorath. He ordered his personal guards to arrest the poor madman, but at that moment, the King of Skingrad raised his arm and sent his hawk flying into the sky. It was a signal his army had been waiting for. The Alessian were all within the pass and the range of their arrows.<BR>
<BR>
King Rislav and his guard began riding westward as fast as if they had been "kissed by wild Kynareth," as the chroniclers said. He did not dare to look behind him, but his plan went faultlessly. The far eastern end of the pass was sealed by rolling boulders, giving the Alessian no direction to go but westward. The Skingrad archers rained arrows down upon the Imperial army from far above on the plateaus, remaining safe from reprisal. The furious Emperor Gorieus chased Rislav from the Weald to the Highlands, leaving Skingrad far behind, all the while his army growing steadily smaller and smaller.<BR>
<BR>
In the ancient Highland forest, the Imperial army met the army of Rislav's father-in-law, the King of Kvatch. The Alessian army likely still outnumbered their opponents, but they were exhausted and their morale had been obliterated by the chase amid a sea of arrows. After an hour's battle, they retreated north into what is now the Imperial Reserve, and from there, further north and east, to slip back to nurse their wounds and pride in Nibenay.<BR>
<BR>
It was the beginning of the end of the Alessian hegemony. The Kings of the Colovian West joined with Kvatch and Skingrad to resist Imperial incursions. The Clan Direnni under Ryain was inspired to outlaw the religion of the Alessian Reform throughout his lands in High Rock, and began pushing into Imperial territories. The new High Chief of Skyrim, Hoag, now called Hoag Merkiller, though sharing the Emperor's official xenophobia, also joined the resistance. His heir, King Ysmir Wulfharth of Atmora, helped continue the struggle upon Hoag's death in battle, and also insured his place in history.<BR>
<BR>
The heroic King of Skingrad, who faced the Emperor's army virtually alone, and triggered its end, justly deserves his sobriquet of Rislav the Righteous.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
正义的里斯拉夫<BR>
辛金 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
和所有真正的英雄一样，里斯拉夫·拉里奇的出身并不吉利。编年史家告诉我们，第一纪元448年他出生的那个春夜异常寒冷，他的母亲林娜达女王在见到儿子后不久就去世了。至于他是否深受父亲 -- 早已拥有众多继承人（在他之前已有三子四女）的斯金格拉德国王莫鲁斯 -- 的喜爱，编年史家并未提及。<BR>
<BR>
他的存在如此不起眼，以至于在他生命的前二十年里，我们几乎听不到任何关于他的消息。我们可以假设，他的教育类似于科洛维亚西部任何一位“备胎王子”的教育，由亚历德导师教他狩猎和战斗之道。礼仪、宗教指导，甚至基本的治国之道，都很少成为高地王子训练的一部分，不像在更文明的尼本奈河谷。<BR>
<BR>
在第一纪元461日日晓月23日，戈里乌斯皇帝的加冕典礼上，他的名字与家人一起作为荣誉名册的一部分被简要提及。当然，仪式是在马鲁克的阿莱西亚教义时期举行的，因此没有娱乐活动，但十三岁的里斯拉夫仍然目睹了一些最伟大的传奇人物。安奎那之兽达洛克·布雷代表他的王国，向帝国致敬。天际的酋长“白者”科约里克和他的儿子霍阿格出席了典礼。尽管帝国对所有精灵都不宽容，但歧莫因多瑞尔·尼瑞瓦和锻莫杜马克矮人王显然也在那里，以外交方式代表勒斯丹，一切相对和平。<BR>
<BR>
名册上还提到了一位为高岩帝国宫廷服务的年轻精灵，他将与里斯拉夫有一段伟大的历史。里安·迪伦尼。<BR>
<BR>
这两个年龄相仿的年轻人是否见过面并交谈过，完全是历史学家的想象。里安被赞誉为强大的地主，最终买下了髂骨湾的巴尔菲拉岛，并逐渐征服了整个高岩以及落锤和天际的大部分地区，但在接下来的十七年里，历史书中再也没有关于里斯拉夫的消息。我们只能根据随后的事实提出推测。<BR>
<BR>
当然，国王的子女会与其它国王的子女结婚以缔结联盟。斯金格拉德和科瓦奇王国在整个第五世纪因共同领土而发生过小规模冲突，直到472年才达成和平。这项协议的细节没有记录，但既然我们知道六年后里斯拉夫王子作为贾斯提尼乌斯国王的女儿贝莱娜的丈夫出现在科瓦奇的宫廷中，那么合理地猜测他们是为了和平而结婚的。<BR>
<BR>
这让我们来到了478年，那一年一场大瘟疫席卷了整个西罗帝尔，并似乎特别集中在独立的科洛维亚西部。受害者包括莫鲁斯国王和斯金格拉德整个王室的其他成员。里斯拉夫唯一幸存的哥哥多拉尔德，因为当时在帝都担任马鲁克的祭司而幸免于难。他回到家乡继承了王位。<BR>
<BR>
关于多拉尔德，我们有一些历史记载。作为国王的次子，他头脑有点简单，显然非常虔诚。所有的编年史家都谈论他的善良和正派，他早年如何看到异象，在父亲的祝福下，从斯金格拉德来到帝都，成为祭司。当然，马鲁克的祭司们不区分精神事务和政治事务。那是阿莱西亚帝国的宗教，它教导说抵抗皇帝就是抵抗众神。考虑到这一点，多拉尔德成为独立的斯金格拉德王国的国王后所做的一切，也就不足为奇了。<BR>
<BR>
他登基第一天颁布的第一道法令，就是将王国割让给帝国。<BR>
<BR>
整个科洛维亚领地的反应是震惊和愤怒，科瓦奇宫廷尤甚。据说，里斯拉夫·拉里奇带着他的妻子和二十四名岳父的骑兵，骑马前往他兄弟的王国。无论编年史家如何美化，这肯定不是一支令人印象深刻的军队，但他们毫不费力地击败了多拉尔德派来阻止他们的所有卫兵。事实上，并没有真正的战斗，因为斯金格拉德的士兵们憎恨他们的新国王放弃自治的决定。<BR>
<BR>
兄弟俩在他们长大的城堡庭院里面对面。<BR>
<BR>
以典型的科洛维亚方式，没有审判，没有叛国罪的指控，没有陪审团，没有法官。只有一个刽子手。<BR>
<BR>
“你已不是我的兄弟，”里斯拉夫·拉里奇说，一刀将多拉尔德的头从肩膀上砍下。他加冕为斯金格拉德国王时，怀里还抱着那把血淋淋的斧头。<BR>
<BR>
如果说里斯拉夫国王之前没有战斗经验，那很快就改变了。斯金格拉德曾主动献上，现在又被收回的消息迅速传到了帝都。戈里乌斯甚至在登基之前就是一位出色的战士，他担任皇帝的十七年几乎没有和平。就在多拉尔德被刺杀、里斯拉夫崛起前八个月，戈里乌斯和阿莱西亚军队在冰冻的北方战场上，面对了另一位参加他加冕礼的客人 -- “白者”科约里克。天际的大酋长在桑加德战役中丧生。在酋长盟约选择新领导人时，西罗帝尔正忙于夺回它失去的南部天际领土。<BR>
<BR>
简而言之，戈里乌斯皇帝知道如何对付叛逆的附庸。<BR>
<BR>
阿莱西亚军队向西涌去，“如死亡洪流”，借用编年史家的话，其数量远远超过征服斯金格拉德所需。戈里乌斯不可能认为真的会打仗。正如我们所说，里斯拉夫几乎没有战争经验，也只在治国之术上练习了几天。他的王国和整个科洛维亚西部刚刚遭受了瘟疫的蹂躏。阿莱西亚人预期只需要展示一下武力，对方就会投降。<BR>
<BR>
里斯拉夫反而为战斗做好了准备。他迅速检阅了他的部队，并制定了计划。<BR>
<BR>
此前一直忽略里斯拉夫生活的编年史家们，现在带着恋物癖般的喜悦，用一节又一节的诗句描述国王的仪表。虽然这可能缺乏文学价值和品味，但我们至少终于得到了一些细节。毫不奇怪，国王穿着他那个时代最好的盔甲，因为当时科洛维亚领地拥有全泰姆瑞尔最好的皮匠（那是唯一可用的盔甲类型）。国王的锁子甲经过煮沸和上蜡处理以增加硬度，并镶嵌着英寸长的尖刺，呈现出浓郁的栗红色，他把它穿在黑色束腰外衣外面，但在黑色斗篷里面。如今矗立在斯金格拉德的“正义的里斯拉夫”雕像是国王的浪漫化版本，除了所描绘的盔甲外，并不失真。科洛维亚西部的任何吟游诗人都不敢如此轻装上阵。但正如我们将看到的，它确实包含了里斯拉夫最重要的装备：他训练有素的鹰和他快速的马。<BR>
<BR>
冬雨冲刷了南方的道路，使西部森林的大部分地区溢入瓦伦伍德。皇帝选择了北路，里斯拉夫国王带着一小队卫兵在现在金色大道上的一个低隘口与他会面。据说，皇帝的军队规模之大，连安奎那之兽在数百英里外都能听到其行军的动静，编年史家说，尽管他极力克制，还是因恐惧而颤抖。<BR>
<BR>
据说，里斯拉夫没有颤抖。他极其礼貌地告诉皇帝，他的随行队伍过于庞大，无法安置在小小的斯金格拉德王国。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>RUMINATIONS ON THE ELDER SCROLLS<BR>
by Septimus Signus, College of Winterhold<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
Imagine living beneath the waves with a strong-sighted blessing of most excellent fabric. Holding the fabric over your gills, you would begin to breathe-drink its warp and weft. Though the plantmatter fibers imbue your soul, the wretched plankton would pollute the cloth until it stank to heavens of prophecy. This is one manner in which the Scrolls first came to pass, but are we the sea, or the breather, or the fabric? Or are we the breath itself?<BR>
<BR>
Can we flow through the Scrolls as knowledge flows through, being the water, or are we the stuck morass of sea-filth that gathers on the edge?<BR>
<BR>
Imagine, again, this time but different. A bird cresting the wind is lifted by a gust and downed by a stone. But the stone can come from above, if the bird is upside down. Where, then, did the gust come from? And which direction? Did the gods send either, or has the bird decreed their presence by her own mindmaking?<BR>
<BR>
The all-sight of the Scrolls makes a turning of the mind such that relative positions are absolute in their primacy.<BR>
<BR>
I ask you again to imagine for me. This time you are beneath the ground, a tiny acorn planted by some well-meaning elf-maiden of the woodlands for her pleasure. You wish to grow but fear what you may become, so you push off the water, the dirt, the sun, to stay in your hole. But it is in the very pushing that you become a tree, in spite of yourself. How did that happen?<BR>
<BR>
The acorn is a kind of tree-egg in this instance, and the knowledge is water and sun. We are the chicken inside the egg, but also the dirt. The knowledge from the Scrolls is what we push against to become full-sighted ourselves.<BR>
<BR>
One final imagining before your mind closes from the shock of ever-knowing. You are now a flame burning bright blue within a vast emptiness. In time you see your brothers and sisters, burnings of their own in the distance and along your side. A sea of pinpoints, a constellation of memories. Each burns bright, then flickers. Then two more take its place but not forever lest the void fills with rancid light that sucks the thought.<BR>
<BR>
Each of our minds is actually the emptiness, and the learnings of the Scrolls are the pinpoints. Without their stabbing light, my consciousness would be as a vast nothingness, unknowing its emptiness as a void is unknowing of itself. But the burnings are dangerous, and must be carefully tended and minded and brought to themselves and spread to their siblings.<BR>
<BR><BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>关于上古卷轴的沉思<BR>
塞普提默斯·西格努斯著，冬堡学院<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
想象一下，带着一种极佳织物制成的强视祝福生活在海浪之下。将织物盖在鳃上，你便会开始呼吸 -- 饮入它的经纬。尽管植物纤维浸透了你的灵魂，但那些可恶的浮游生物会污染织物，直至它散发出刺鼻的预言之气。这是卷轴最初出现的一种方式，但我们是海，是呼吸者，还是织物？或者说，我们就是呼吸本身？<BR>
<BR>
我们能否像知识流过一样流过卷轴，成为水，还是我们只是聚集在边缘的、被困住的海中污物沼泽？<BR>
<BR>
再次想象，这次有所不同。一只乘风破浪的鸟被一阵风托起，却被一块石头击落。但如果鸟是倒着的，石头可能来自上方。那么，那阵风又是从何而来？来自哪个方向？是众神送来的，还是鸟凭借自己的心念创造了它们？<BR>
<BR>
卷轴的全知视野使心智发生转变，使得相对位置在其首要性上成为绝对。<BR>
<BR>
我再次请你为我想象。这一次，你在地下，是一颗小小的橡果，被某个善意的林地精灵少女为了取乐而种下。你希望成长，却又害怕自己可能变成的样子，所以你推开水分、泥土、阳光，只想待在洞里。但恰恰是在这种推开中，你变成了一棵树，违背了自己的意愿。这是怎么发生的？<BR>
<BR>
在这个例子中，橡果是一种树蛋，而知识是水和阳光。我们是蛋中的小鸡，也是泥土。来自卷轴的知识正是我们所对抗的东西，以使自己变得全知。<BR>
<BR>
在你因全知带来的冲击而心智封闭之前，最后一次想象。你现在是广阔虚空中的一团明亮蓝色火焰。随着时间的推移，你看到你的兄弟姐妹，在远处和在你身边燃烧着的火焰。一片光点的海洋，一个记忆的星座。每个都燃烧得明亮，然后闪烁。然后又有两个取而代之，但并非永远，以免虚空被腐臭的光芒填满，吸走思想。<BR>
<BR>
我们的每个心智实际上都是那虚空，而卷轴的学问是那些光点。没有它们刺目的光芒，我的意识将是一片广袤的虚无，如同虚空不知自身为空。但那些燃烧是危险的，必须小心照料和关注，使其回归自身，并传播给它们的兄弟姐妹。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Sacred Witness: A True History of the Night Mother<BR>
by Enric Milnes<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
I have met countesses and courtesans, empresses and witches, ladies of war and slatterns of peace, but I have never met a woman like The Night Mother. And I never will again.<BR>
<BR>
I am a writer, a poet of some small renown. If I told you my name, you may have heard of me, but very likely, not. For decades until very recently, I had adopted the city of Sentinel on the coast of Hammerfell as my home, and kept the company of other artists, painters, tapestrists, and writers. No one I knew would have known an assassin by sight, least of all the queen of them, the Blood Flower, the Lady Death, the Night Mother.<BR>
<BR>
Not that I had not heard of her.<BR>
<BR>
Some years ago, I had the good fortune of meeting Pelarne Assi, a respected scholar, who had come to Hammerfell to do research for a book about the Order of Diagna. His essay, 'The Brothers of Darkness' together with Ynir Gorming's 'Fire and Darkness: The Brotherhoods of Death' are considered to be the canon tomes on the subject of Tamriel's orders of assassins. By luck, Gorming himself was also in Sentinel, and I was privileged to sit with the two in a dark skooma den in the musty slums of the city, as we smoked and talked about the Dark Brotherhood, the Morag Tong, and the Night Mother.<BR>
<BR>
While not disputing the possibility that the Night Mother may be immortal or at least very long-lived, Assi thought it most likely that several women - and perhaps some men - throughout the ages had assumed the honorary title. It was no more logical to say there was only one Night Mother, he asserted, than to say there was only one King of Sentinel.<BR>
<BR>
Gorming argued that there never was a Night Mother, at least no human one. The Night Mother was Mephala herself, whom the Brotherhood revered second only to Sithis.<BR>
<BR>
'I don't suppose there's any way of knowing for certain,' I said, in a note of diplomacy.<BR>
<BR>
'Certainly there is,' whispered Gorming with a grin. 'You could talk to that cloaked fellow in the corner.'<BR>
<BR>
I had not noticed the man before, who sat by himself, eyes hidden by his cloak, seemingly as much a part of the dingy place as the rough stone and unswept floor. Turning back to Ynir, I asked him why that man would know about the Night Mother.<BR>
<BR>
'He's a Dark Brother,' hissed Pellarne Assi. 'That's as plain as the moons. Don't even joke about speaking with him about Her.'<BR>
<BR>
We moved on to other arguments about the Morag Tong and the Brotherhood, but I never forgot the image of the lone man, looking at nothing and everything, in the corner of the dirty room, with fumes of skooma smoke floating around him like ghosts. When I saw him weeks later on the streets of Sentinel, I followed him.<BR>
<BR>
Yes, I followed him. The reader may reasonably ask 'why' and 'how.' I don't blame you for that.<BR>
<BR>
'How' was simply a question of knowing my city as well as I do. I'm not a thief, not particularly sure-footed and quiet, but I know the alleys and streets of Sentinel intimately from decades worth of ambling. I know which bridges creak, which buildings cast long irregular shadows, the intervals at which the native birds begin the ululations of their evening songs. With relative ease, I kept pace with the Dark Brother and out of his sight and hearing.<BR>
<BR>
The answer to 'Why' is even simpler. I have the natural curiosity of the born writer. When I see a strange new animal, I must observe. It is the writer's curse.<BR>
<BR>
I trailed the cloaked man deeper into the city, down an alleyway so narrow it was scarcely a crack between two tenements, past a crooked fence, and suddenly, miraculously, I was in a place I had never seen before. A little courtyard cemetery, with a dozen old half-rotted wooden tombstones. None of the surrounding buildings had windows that faced it, so no one knew this miniature necropolis existed.<BR>
<BR>
No one, except the six men and one woman standing in it. And me.<BR>
<BR>
The woman saw me immediately, and gestured for me to come closer. I could have run, but - no, I couldn't have. I had pierced a mystery right in my adopted Sentinel, and I could not leave it.<BR>
<BR>
She knew my name, and she said it with a sweet smile. The Night Mother was a little old lady with fluffy white hair, cheeks like wrinkled apples that still carried the flush of youth, friendly eyes, blue as the Iliac Bay. She softly took my arm as we sat down amidst the graves and discussed murder.<BR>
<BR>
She was not always in Hammerfell, not always available for direct assignment, but it seemed she enjoyed actually talking to her clientele.<BR>
<BR>
'I did not come here to hire the Brotherhood,' I said respectfully.<BR>
<BR>
'Then why are you here?' the Night Mother asked, her eyes never leaving mine.<BR>
<BR>
I told her I wanted to know about her. I did not expect an answer to that, but she told me.<BR>
<BR>
'I do not mind the stories you writers dream up about me,' she chuckled. 'Some of them are very amusing, and some of them are good for business. I like the sexy dark woman lounging on the divan in Carlovac Townway's fiction particularly. The truth is that my history would not make a very dramatic tale. I was a thief, long, long ago, back when the Thieves Guild was only beginning. It's such a bother to sneak around a house when performing a burglary, and many of us found it most efficacious to strangle the occupant of the house. Just for convenience. I suggested to the Guild that a segment of our order be dedicated to the arts and sciences of murder.<BR>
<BR>
'It did not seem like such a controversial idea to me,' the Night Mother shrugged. 'We had specialists in catburglary, pick-pocketing, lock-picking, fencing, all the other essential parts of the job. But the Guild thought that encouraging murder would be bad for business. Too much, too much, they argued.<BR>
<BR>
'They might have been right,' the old woman continued. 'But I discovered there is a profit to be made, just the same, from sudden death. Not only can one rob the deceased, but, if your victim has enemies, which rich people often do, you can be paid for it even more. I began to murder people differently when I discovered that. After I strangled them, I would put two stones in their eyes, one black and one white.'<BR>
<BR>
'Why?' I asked.<BR>
<BR>
'It was a sort of calling card of mine. You're a writer - don't you want your name on your books? I couldn't use my name, but I wanted potential clients to know me and my work. I don't do it anymore, no need to, but at the time, it was my signature. Word spread, and I soon had quite a successful business.'<BR>
<BR>
'And that became the Morag Tong?' I asked.<BR>
<BR>
'Oh, dear me, no,' the Night Mother smiled. 'The Morag Tong was around long before my time. I know I'm old, but I'm not that old. I merely hired on some of their assassins when they began to fall apart after the murder of the last Potentate. They did not want to be members of the Tong anymore, and since I was the only other murder syndicate of any note, they just joined on.'<BR>
<BR>
I phrased my next question carefully. 'Will you kill me now that you've told me all this?'<BR>
<BR>
She nodded sadly, letting out a little grandmotherly sigh. 'You are such a nice, polite young man, I hate to end our acquaintanceship. I don't suppose you would agree to a concession or two in exchange for your life, would you?'<BR>
<BR>
To my everlasting shame, I did agree. I said I would say nothing about our meeting, which, as the reader can see, was a promise I eventually, years later, chose not to keep. Why have I endangered my life thus?<BR>
<BR>
Because of the promises I did keep.<BR>
<BR>
I helped the Night Mother and the Dark Brotherhood in acts too despicable, too bloody for me to set to paper. My hand quivers as I think about the people I betrayed, beginning with that night. I tried to write my poetry, but ink seemed to turn to blood. Finally, I fled, changing my name, going to a land where no one would know me.<BR>
<BR>
And I wrote this. The true history of the Night Mother, from the interview she gave me on the night we met. It will be the last thing I ever write, this I know. And every word is true.<BR>
<BR>
Pray for me.<BR>
<BR>
Editor's Note: Though originally published anonymously, the identity of the author has never been in serious doubt. Any layman familiar with the work of the poet Enric Milnes will recognize Sacred Witness's familiar cadence and style in such books of his as 'The Alik'r.' Shortly after publication, Milnes was murdered, and his killer was never found. He had been strangled, and two stones, a black one and a white one, crushed into his eyesockets. Very brutally.<BR>

神圣见证：夜母真实史<BR>
恩里克·米尔恩斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
我见过伯爵夫人和交际花、女皇和女巫、战争贵妇和和平荡妇，但我从未见过像夜母这样的女人。我也再也不会遇到了。<BR>
<BR>
我是一名作家，一位小有名气的诗人。如果我告诉你我的名字，你也许听说过我，但很可能没有。直到最近，几十年来，我一直把落锤海岸的哨卫城当作我的家，并与其他的艺术家、画家、挂毯师和作家为伴。我认识的人中，没有人能一眼认出刺客，更不用说他们的女王 -- 血之花、死亡女士、夜母了。<BR>
<BR>
倒不是我未曾听说过她。<BR>
<BR>
几年前，我有幸遇到了佩拉恩·阿西，一位受人尊敬的学者，他来落锤为写一本关于迪亚戈纳教团的书做研究。他的文章《黑暗兄弟》以及伊尼尔·戈明的《火与暗：死亡兄弟会》被认为是关于泰姆瑞尔刺客组织的权威著作。很幸运，戈明本人当时也在哨卫，我有幸与两人坐在城里发霉的贫民区一个昏暗的斯库玛窝里，一边抽烟，一边谈论黑暗兄弟会、莫拉格·堂和夜母。<BR>
<BR>
阿西并不否认夜母可能是不朽的，或者至少非常长寿，但他认为最有可能的是，古往今来有几个女人 -- 也许还有一些男人 -- 曾担任过这个荣誉头衔。他断言，说只有一个夜母，就像说只有一个哨卫国王一样不合逻辑。<BR>
<BR>
戈明则认为根本不存在夜母，至少不是人类。夜母就是梅法拉本人，兄弟会对其的尊崇仅次于西帝斯。<BR>
<BR>
“我想肯定无法确知，”我用外交的口吻说。<BR>
<BR>
“当然有，”戈明咧嘴一笑，低声说。“你可以和角落里那个穿斗篷的家伙谈谈。”<BR>
<BR>
我之前没注意到那个人，他独自坐着，眼睛藏在斗篷下，似乎和粗糙的石头和未扫的地板一样，是这肮脏地方的一部分。我转回身问伊尼尔，那个人为什么会知道夜母。<BR>
<BR>
“他是个黑暗兄弟，”佩拉恩·阿西嘶嘶地说。“这再明显不过了。别开这种玩笑，说要和他谈论她。”<BR>
<BR>
我们转而讨论起关于莫拉格·堂和兄弟会的其他论点，但我从未忘记那个孤独男人的形象，他在肮脏房间的角落里，似看非看地看着一切，斯库玛烟雾像鬼魂一样在他周围飘浮。几周后，当我在哨卫的街上看到他时，我跟踪了他。<BR>
<BR>
是的，我跟踪了他。读者可能会合情合理地问我“为什么”和“怎么跟”。我不怪你们这么想。<BR>
<BR>
“怎么跟”只是因为我对我居住的城市了如指掌。我不是小偷，脚步不算特别稳健或安静，但几十年的闲逛让我对哨卫的小巷和街道了如指掌。我知道哪座桥会吱嘎作响，哪些建筑物会投下长长的不规则阴影，本地鸟儿开始唱晚歌的间隔时间。我相对轻松地跟上了那位黑暗兄弟的步伐，并避开他的视线和听觉。<BR>
<BR>
“为什么”的答案更简单。我有与生俱来的作家式好奇心。当我看到一种奇怪的新动物时，我必须观察。这是作家的诅咒。<BR>
<BR>
我跟踪那个穿斗篷的男人深入城市，走下一条狭窄得几乎只是两栋公寓楼之间裂缝的小巷，经过一道歪歪扭扭的栅栏，然后突然间，神奇地，我来到了一个我从未见过的地方。一个小庭院墓地，有十几块半腐烂的旧木墓碑。周围的建筑物没有一扇窗户朝向它，所以没人知道这个微型墓地存在。<BR>
<BR>
除了站在里面的六个男人和一个女人。还有我。<BR>
<BR>
那个女人立刻看到了我，示意我走近些。我本可以跑掉，但是 -- 不，我跑不掉。我刚刚在我定居的哨卫揭开了一个谜团，我不能离开。<BR>
<BR>
她知道我的名字，带着甜甜的微笑说出来。夜母是一个小老太太，头发蓬松雪白，脸颊像仍然带着青春红晕的皱苹果，眼睛友善，蓝得像髂骨湾。当我们坐在墓地中间谈论谋杀时，她轻轻地挽住我的手臂。<BR>
<BR>
她并不总是在落锤，也不总是可以直接指派任务，但看起来她很喜欢和她的客户面对面交谈。<BR>
<BR>
“我来这里不是为了雇佣兄弟会，”我恭敬地说。<BR>
<BR>
“那你为什么来这里？”夜母问道，她的眼睛从未离开过我。<BR>
<BR>
我告诉她我想了解她。我并不指望得到答案，但她告诉了我。<BR>
<BR>
“我不介意你们这些作家编造关于我的故事，”她轻笑道。“有些很有趣，有些对生意有好处。我特别喜欢卡洛瓦克·汤威小说里那个慵懒地躺在躺椅上的性感黑女人。事实是，我的历史不会是一个非常戏剧性的故事。很久很久以前，在盗贼公会刚刚起步的时候，我是个贼。入室盗窃时在房子里偷偷摸摸太麻烦了，我们很多人发现勒死房子的主人最有效。只是为了方便。我向公会建议，我们组织的一部分应该专门研究谋杀的艺术和科学。<BR>
<BR>
“在我看来，这似乎并不是一个很有争议的想法，”夜母耸耸肩。“我们有飞贼、扒手、开锁匠、销赃者，以及所有其他基本工作的专家。但公会认为鼓励谋杀对生意不利。太多了，太多了，他们争辩道。<BR>
<BR>
“他们也许是对的，”老妇人继续说。“但我发现，突然死亡同样可以获利。不仅可以抢劫死者，而且，如果你的受害者有敌人 -- 富人通常都有 -- 你甚至可以为此得到更多的报酬。当我发现这一点时，我开始用不同的方式杀人。勒死他们之后，我会在他们的眼睛里放两块石头，一黑一白。”<BR>
<BR>
“为什么？”我问道。<BR>
<BR>
“这算是我的一种名片。你是个作家 -- 你不希望自己的名字出现在书上吗？我不能用我的名字，但我想让潜在客户认识我和我的工作。我现在不这么做了，没必要，但在那时，那是我的标志。消息传开，我很快就有了一门相当成功的生意。”<BR>
<BR>
“后来这就变成了莫拉格·堂？”我问道。<BR>
<BR>
“哦，天哪，不是，”夜母笑了。“莫拉格·堂在我出生之前很久就存在了。我知道我老了，但我没那么老。我只是在最后一位摄政被谋杀后，他们开始分崩离析时，雇佣了他们的一些刺客。他们不想再成为堂的成员了，而既然我是唯一另一个值得一提的谋杀集团，他们就加入了。”<BR>
<BR>
我小心地措辞我的下一个问题。“你告诉我这些之后，会杀了我吗？”<BR>
<BR>
她悲伤地点点头，发出一声祖母般的小小叹息。“你是个如此友善、有礼貌的年轻人，我真不想结束我们的相识。你大概不会同意一两个让步来换取你的性命吧？”<BR>
<BR>
令我永远羞愧的是，我同意了。我说我不会透露我们见面的事，正如读者所见，这是一个我最终在多年后选择不遵守的承诺。我为何要如此危及自己的生命？<BR>
<BR>
因为我遵守了其他的承诺。<BR>
<BR>
我帮助夜母和黑暗兄弟会做了那些太卑鄙、太血腥，我无法诉诸笔端的行为。每当想起我背叛的人们，从那天晚上开始，我的手就颤抖。我试图写我的诗，但墨水似乎变成了血。最后，我逃走了，改了名字，去了一个没人认识我的地方。<BR>
<BR>
于是我写了这个。夜母的真实历史，来自我们相遇那晚她给我的访谈。我知道这将是我写的最后的东西。每个字都是真实的。<BR>
<BR>
请为我祈祷。<BR>
<BR>
编者注：尽管最初是匿名发表，但作者的身份从未受到严重质疑。任何熟悉诗人恩里克·米尔恩斯作品的外行，都会在《阿里克尔》等书中认出《神圣见证》熟悉的节奏和风格。出版后不久，米尔恩斯就被谋杀了，凶手至今未找到。他是被勒死的，两颗石头，一黑一白，被塞进他的眼窝。非常残忍。<BR>
<BR>"""

The distinction between these two conflicting views of the nature of the Mundus turns on this question: are the forces which govern the world conscious and personal, or unconscious and impersonal? Religion, as a conciliation of the superhuman power, assumes the former, for all conciliation requires that the being conciliated is a conscious or personal agent, whose conduct is uncertain and can to a certain level be influenced. In this, it stands in fundamental antagonism to magic, which takes for granted that the course of nature is determined by the operation of immutable laws acting mechanically. <BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
A Scholar's Guide to Nymphs<BR>
By Vondham Barres<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
I grew up a scholar, an ascetic devoted to knowledge, with eyes that saw beauty in a fascinating passage in a dusty tome, love in the candle that allowed me to study on starless nights, passion in a well-reasoned argument of a long dead issue. I was a student who never graduated and was never expelled.<BR><BR>
Though I am not defending myself, I should further define myself. I am not what you would call a prude. In fact, I can speak of subjects in a detached way that would make the most debauched strumpet in Skyhawk blush with discovered modesty. I wrote an essay the House of Dibella as a scholar should, analysing the cult of beauty and physical relations as one might study crop rotation or the digestive system of an orc. The acquaintances of mine who were inclined to wink and giggle I tolerated, but barely.<BR><BR>
With all that said, the reader will understand that when I decided to study the language of the nymphs in order to study their character and culture, it was not a decision I made on account of prurience or lust. Scholars have historically neglected the nymph as a subject worthy of research, and this neglect I attribute to prejudice. The sages with whom I have spoken on the subject have eloquently and intelligently formed sentences which, boiled down, can be translated as: "Nymphs look like beautiful, naked women who skip along tra-la-la and like to have indiscriminate sex. What could they have to say that would be of any interest?"<BR><BR>
So here I was faced with the most daunting of projects -- to study and research a species unstudied is a potentially rewarding challenge. If the subject was unstudied because the scientific community had deemed it beneath interest, a potentially rewarding but decidedly frustrating challenge. If I spent months in serious study of their language and culture and additional time in their company, and discovered nothing more than that the common prejudice is correct, the term "laughing stock" would not do me justice.<BR><BR>
So, excited and nervous for reasons unrelated to the notoriously promiscuous behavior of my subjects, I began my studies. I mastered the language, a melodious tongue that sounds like wild elf and faerie but share no vocabulary with them. I studied the lore, and found it to be on the whole, little more than pornography and crude conjecture. <BR>
I next had to find a nymph.<BR><BR>
From my centralized location in the Imperial City, I found it easy to send word around to several wellknown temples and guilds devoted to study in all the provinces. Not all replies back were serious in nature, but one, from the School of Julianos in Sentinel helped me considerably. To Magister Oitos and his disciples, I here offer my sincere gratitude.<BR><BR>
Nymphs are extremely shy creatures, no matter what the more obscene stories will tell you. No one who I've spoken with has had one seek him or her out. Thus to speak with a nymph requires energy and patience.<BR><BR>
Out of courtesy for her privacy, I will not here give the location of the little grotto off the coast of Hammerfell where I found the nymph. It took three months of patient waiting, leaving presents where I knew the nymph would be, before the nymph stood still at my approach.<BR><BR>
I remember I was carrying a bouquet of purple and white tetias, and she looked at them and then at me, and smiled. The effect of her smile was truly magical, I'm convinced. Her body was, of course, perfect; her face lovely and serene; her hair like silk flame. But until she smiled, she was beautiful in the abstract, a perfect statue by a master. The smile made her approachable and, thus, terrifying.<BR><BR>
"For you," I said, attempting my first utterance of Nymph to a real nymph.<BR><BR>
Her smile grew into a grin which became a giggle and then a laugh. The reader has doubtless heard of the silver laughter of the elves. The nymph's laugh is earthy and spontaneous, and very ... suggestive.<BR><BR>
"And what do you want from me in return, mortal?" she asked.<BR><BR>
"I am," There is no, I should say, known word in the Nymph language for scholar, "I am a man who likes to learn things. I want to learn things about you."<BR><BR>
And I did.<BR><BR>
Nymphs are the wisest, most wonderful creatures in Tamriel. My nymph, her name is Ayalea (a poor phonetic transcription of a word that sounds more like a light wind blowing through a small crack in a hollow chamber) and she knows more about the behavior and varieties of the deep woodland creatures than the greatest wood elf scholar I ever met. She taught me of flowers and ghosts and creatures too fast and timid to have ever been seen by man.<BR><BR>
Ayalea taught me how to learn for the very first time. How to open my mind to all of the possibilities of life and how to use that knowledge, not just to hold in my cramped brain like a dragon's horde.<BR><BR>
If you ever meet a nymph, speak to her.<BR><BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Editor's note: the writer Vondham Barres is no longer a scholar at the Imperial University. He deposited this manuscript and disappeared from the civilized world. His current whereabouts are unknown.<BR><BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
宁芙学者指南<BR>
冯德汉·巴雷斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
我从小就是个学者，一个致力于知识的苦行者，我的眼睛能在布满灰尘的巨著中看到引人入胜段落的美丽，能在让我在无星之夜学习的蜡烛中看到爱，能在对早已逝去的问题进行条理清晰的论证中看到激情。我是一个从未毕业也从未被开除的学生。<BR><BR>
虽然我不是在为自己辩护，但我应该进一步定义自己。我不是你们所说的那种拘谨的人。事实上，我能以一种超然的方式谈论一些话题，足以让天际鹰里最放荡的妓女因发现自己竟还有一丝羞耻而脸红。我像学者应该做的那样写了一篇关于蒂贝拉之家的文章，分析美的崇拜和肉体关系，就像人们研究轮作或兽人的消化系统一样。对那些倾向于眨眼和傻笑的认识我的人，我勉强容忍了他们。<BR><BR>
说了这么多，读者会明白，当我决定为了研究宁芙的性格和文化而学习它们的语言时，这个决定并非出于好色或淫欲。历史上，学者们一直忽视宁芙作为值得研究的对象，我将这种忽视归因于偏见。我就此主题交谈过的贤者们，他们用雄辩而睿智的语言组成句子，归纳起来可以翻译为：“宁芙看起来像美丽的、赤裸的女人，她们蹦蹦跳跳，唱着‘啦-啦-啦’，喜欢滥交。它们能说出什么有趣的东西呢？”<BR><BR>
于是，我面临着最艰巨的任务 -- 研究和调查一个未被研究过的物种，这是一个可能带来丰厚回报的挑战。如果这个课题之所以未被研究是因为科学界认为它不值得关注，那这就是一个可能带来丰厚回报但无疑令人沮丧的挑战。如果我花数月时间认真研究它们的语言和文化，并额外花时间与它们相处，结果发现除了普遍的偏见是正确的之外一无所获，那么“笑柄”这个词都不足以形容我。<BR><BR>
于是，我怀着与研究对象臭名昭著的滥交行为无关的兴奋和紧张，开始了我的研究。我掌握了这种语言，这是一种悦耳的语言，听起来像野精灵和仙灵，但与它们没有共同的词汇。我研究了相关传说，发现整体上，不过是色情内容和粗俗的猜测。<BR>
接下来，我必须找到一位宁芙。<BR><BR>
从我所在的帝都中心位置，我发现很容易向各省的几个致力于研究的著名神殿和公会传达信息。并非所有回复都是认真的，但其中一封来自哨卫的尤利安诺斯学派的回复对我帮助很大。在此，我向奥伊托斯大师及其门徒致以诚挚的谢意。<BR><BR>
无论那些更淫秽的故事会告诉你什么，宁芙都是极其害羞的生物。与我交谈过的人中，没有谁遇到过宁芙主动来找他们的。因此，与宁芙交谈需要精力和耐心。<BR><BR>
出于对她隐私的尊重，我不会在这里透露我在落锤海岸附近找到宁芙的那个小石窟的位置。我耐心等待了三个月，在我知道宁芙会出现的地方留下礼物，然后宁芙才在我走近时站着不动。<BR><BR>
我记得我拿着一束紫色和白色的泰提亚花，她看了看花，然后看了看我，然后笑了。我相信，她微笑的效果真的很神奇。当然，她的身体是完美的；她的脸可爱而宁静；她的头发像丝绸般的火焰。但在她微笑之前，她的美是抽象的，一尊大师的完美雕像。那微笑使她变得平易近人，因而也令人生畏。<BR><BR>
“送给你，”我说，这是我第一次尝试对着一位真正的宁芙说宁芙语。<BR><BR>
她的微笑变成了咧开嘴的笑，又变成了咯咯的笑，然后是放声大笑。读者无疑听说过精灵的银铃般的笑声。宁芙的笑声是自然的、发自内心的，而且非常......富有暗示性。<BR><BR>
“那么，你想从我这里得到什么回报呢，凡人？”她问道。<BR><BR>
“我是，”我应该说，宁芙语中没有已知的“学者”这个词，“我是一个喜欢学习的人。我想了解关于你的事情。”<BR><BR>
我确实了解了。<BR><BR>
宁芙是泰姆瑞尔最智慧、最美妙的生物。我的宁芙，她的名字叫阿雅莱亚（这只是一个词的糟糕的音译，听起来更像是一阵轻风吹过中空房间的一个小裂缝），她对深林生物的行为和种类的了解，比我见过的任何伟大的木精灵学者都要多。她教会了我关于花朵、幽灵以及那些速度太快、太胆小而从未被人类见过的生物的知识。<BR><BR>
阿雅莱亚教会了我如何真正地学习。如何敞开心扉，接纳生活中所有的可能性，以及如何运用这些知识，而不仅仅是像巨龙囤积财宝一样，把它们塞在我那局促的大脑里。<BR><BR>
如果你遇到宁芙，请和她谈谈。<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER">
* * *<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
编者注：作家冯德汉·巴雷斯已不再是帝都大学的学者。他寄存了这份手稿，然后从文明世界消失了。他目前的下落不明。<BR><BR>
