"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Songs of the Return<BR>
Volume 2<BR>
The First Tale of the Darumzu<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Our great lord Ysgramor, the harbinger of us all, did then sent forth his two beloved sons (with him the only other survivors of the brutalities of Saarthal) to seek out the bravest warriors of the land and mount the great return.<BR>
<BR>
Yngol and Ylgar, they were called, and they were known among Atmora as fine warriors with bright eyes and dawning futures. Yngol, the elder, was the brave strategist, bringing his learnings to bear on the battlefield that his enemies would be defeated before they even knew the battle had begun. Ylgar, the younger, was possessed of an unwavering spirit that drove his singular prowess to overwhelming feats in war. Together, the mind and the arm, they were capable of sowing a destruction most thorough and glorious to any foe who stood before them. <BR>
<BR>
Before they parted ways to gather their crews, the two clasped arms and necks in the old fashion and laughed at the heavens for their stories to come. <BR>
<BR>
Young Ylgar then took to the massive shipyards of Jyljyrfyk at the southern point and commissioned two ships for himself and his brother. He would command the Darmuzu, and his brother the Harakk, thus carrying the names of the two favored stars of their heavens. The shipmakers spirits had been suitably filled by Ysgramor's tales of the savage elves, and they set about to birth ships that befit their noble homeland. <BR>
<BR>
Arrangements having been made, Ylgar set forth to the academies of honored soldiers, seeking out his most trusted friends and advisors to join him on the venture of the Return. By now the stories of the new land to the south were spreading before him, and the emergence of his presence was enough to cause the finest warriors to lay down their present undertakings and follow him. <BR>
<BR>
So was he able to call to his side the great Shield-Sisters, Froa and Grosta (who thought and spoke as one), and they brought with their the wise war-teacher Adrimk, who first taught them to dance among the blades. She, in turn, mustered all the students at her command, whose names were not yet made, but some of whom would one day be know: Hermseskr (Who Threw his Shields), Urlach (Who Breathed Fire), Ramth the Greater, Merkyllian Ramth, and the Far-Sighted Uche, who would see the first of many dawns. <BR>
<BR>
On the Day of Final Passage, when the many-oarded fleets would last see the distant green summers of Atmora, the brothers were near in their father's wake as the freshly joined Five Hundred would eagerly press onwards towards Tamriel. Ylgar could see his well-minded brother smiling from afar across the waves, and they shouted war-cries to each other, longing for the soon-day when their assembled crews would draw the treacherous elf blood itno the ground which they would now claim for their own rights. <BR>
<BR>
But Kyne's ministrations are not to be taken lightly, and though her blessings gave wind to drive those brave sailors to their destiny, so too did her mmighty tears fall, to drive them apart. When the Storm of Separation first arose, young Ylgar had no fear, for his crew was strong and able, and their ship drove true through the forest of swells as though pulled by the rope of fate. <BR>
<BR>
When the skies cleared, and Ylgar glimpsed again, with new eyes, the land of his past and future home, he knew his brothers vessel was not within his horizon. The Darumzu, arriving late, drew forth onto the sands and Ylgar rushed to his father to seek word of his brother. The Grear Ysgramor, harbinger of us all, wept for his lost son, and sought comfort in the arms of his only remaining joy. The crew of the Harakk became the first deaths among the Five Hundred, and Ylgar was so enraged with love for his brother that his crew would soon be counted as the first among the many noble and honored names in the Companions. <BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
归乡之歌<BR>
卷二<BR>
达鲁姆祖初篇<BR><BR>

<BR>

<BR>
年轻的伊尔加随后前往南部的吉尔吉夫克的大型造船厂，为自己和他的兄弟定制了两艘船。他将指挥达鲁姆祖号，而他的兄弟则指挥哈拉克号，以此承载他们天空中两颗最受眷顾的星辰之名。造船工匠们的灵魂被伊斯格拉谟关于野蛮精灵的故事充分点燃，他们着手打造配得上他们高贵故乡的船只。<BR>

Spawn of Ash: A Comprehensive Guide to Vardenfell's Savages<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Special thanks to Sjorn the Scholarly for assisting me in my research. Without his brilliance, I would not be where I am right now.<BR>
<BR>
Many have feared the barren, lawless, ashy wastes of Vardenfell Island, a colossal, blight-spewing volcano. Civilization is scarce and limited to Imperial outposts and minor forts. It is rumored that the females among these barbarians also use slaves for erotic pursuits, and that sometimes a young fool, excited by the thought, will seek to be captured. As far as I've collected, these rumors are false, and propagated only to lure the unwise.<BR>
<BR>
The 'Urchalikus' haunt the frozen wasteland at the Northern edge of Vardenfell. They are known to raid undefended settlements to capture infants and toddlers, whom they are believed to ritually sacrifice to 'Dragoth Oor', before roasting and eating their corpses.<BR>
<BR>
The 'Erabinemsins' lurk in the archipelago of small islands that can be found east of the so-called "Azure Coast". <BR>
The 'Saynabs' plague the region of ash desert known to these savages as the "Morag Amar", which owe its name to the presence of the headquarters of the sinister Dark Brotherhood hidden somewhere there. This coterie of assassins is called 'Morag Tang,' "Dark Hands" in their crude language, while 'Morag Amar' means "Dark Heart." As a result, knights prefer to avoid the region unless in great numbers, and this is why the Empire has not succeeded yet in destroying the Dark Brotherhood.<BR>
<BR>
The 'Neveralines' are the most mysterious clan, the one which I have had the most trouble gathering information from. They hide in the numerous volcanic grottos adorning the cliffs of Vardenfell, and are believed to serve directly as the priests and bodyguards of 'Dragoth Oor.' They are practically never seen, as they do not attack foreigners outside of their claimed territory. The huge and ugly creature seem easy enough to tame for these savages, despite them being able to suck all of an elephant's blood in less than a minute.<BR>
<BR>

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_SpectrumStudyTR
The Spectrum Study
光谱研究

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_SpectrumStudyTR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
The Spectrum study<BR>
<BR>
by Avorina Claudie, researcher<BR>
in 2E231, Cyrodiil<BR>
<BR>
Preface<BR>
<BR>
This paper covers the subject of bodily attributes affected by magicka, and its derived forms. Only "health" is covered in extensively in this paper, or to be more accurate, the life force of a being flowing amidst nine mana channels. From now on, these channels will be addressed as daedron ports for the sake of clarity.<BR>
<BR>
Initial setting<BR>
<BR>

The major points of the magicka's own attributes are covered in several pieces, such as "An introduction to elementary magicka". These attributes are not in the scope of this paper.<BR>
<BR>
The research was set up first in a traditional way of Mages Guild and Imperial Academy - prewritten scrolls of a specified spell under watch were tested on the subjects; kwama, rats and a guar. Then, several casters attempted to cast the very same spells on the same subjects, and finally, the magicians commenced to fluctuate all their mana reservoirs to a specified daedron port for complete control of the effect.<BR>
<BR>
Between each of the three phases, extensive condition checks were made on the environment and subjects' states. These were done without magicka, but instead through Dwemer inventions: a device that displays the warmth on a scale, perhaps better known as Arkngthand Device, with respect to the Dwemer citadel such a tool was first encountered in.<BR>
<BR>
Another tool, Mundus Spectrum crafted by Linithrel, was used to measure the amount of magicka flowing through a specific point in the Mortal Plane. Its results were not the most accurate for reasons explained later. Still, we managed to achieve believable results through vigorous repeating of the tests.<BR>
<BR>
The Experiments<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
I Scrolls<BR>
<BR>
Writing spell scrolls is a theoretical subject that is thoroughly analyzed in the higher courses of the Academy. The only detail we need to consider here is that their effects are always as accurate as its author is in focusing his mind to write the scroll. The scrolls used by this experiment were written by Hasederian, one of the Academy stewards, whose area of expertise is exactly the static magicka, so very adequate precision was expected.<BR>
<BR>
Helbrog gra-Shorob, our visitor from Orsinium, began using the scrolls on a common specimen of a kwama forager, which was trapped inside a deep anti-magicka ebony box. As expected, the spell hit only the kwama in a non-lethal way. The amount of magicka measured with Mundus Spectrum was four standard units. Helbrog and two assistants repeated the experiment with identical scrolls on both an ebony box and a simple wooden box, ending up with the same results.<BR>
<BR>
II Traditional spellcasting<BR>
<BR>
Avorina Claudie then initiated the dynamic magicka part of the study. The material for casting a Minor Pinprick were supplied by the Cyrodiil Academy Library. There was a discussion on making more suitable spells for the purpose, but to have comparable results, traditional methods were used.<BR>
<BR>
When Avorina Claudie cast the spell, Spectrum gave the result of four units. With three other casters, the value ranged between four and five units - Helbrog managed to achieve three, Nieca Jahavie and Ianos Capare had to spend more mana on the spell.<BR>
<BR>
III. Mana flow control<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
III.I Background<BR>
<BR>
In great study of magicka by Vanus Galerion himself, an important discovery about certain properties on mana flow were made. At the time, however, necessary information was not available in order to experiment with the knowledge. Recently, however, a total of eight primary daedron ports have been found in Aetherius, the discovery of whom has made it possible to enhance the magickal properties in the exact way the revered master prophesied. There is a multitude of other ports, too, but that is not of concern in this study - they all behave in the very same way these basic ports do.<BR>
<BR>
As mentioned in Preface, the life force is flowing through nine ports. This ninth port is called the Salhia and is so far seems to be redundant, having the same results as Deima and Lewenta combined. It was nevertheless useful in estimating the amount of inaccuracies in the spells.<BR>
<BR>
Magicka, in principle, is a unique form of energy as is the life force of a being, Nirn elements and the Oblivion matter that is yet to be determined on a more deep level. These basic forces all interact through each other as they seemingly contain all the known matter and forces on Nirn. For purists, it should be noted that while magicka contains Aetherius, other sets of the Wheel are understood to interact through Oblivion matter, which, admittedly, has found little use in magician's studies yet.<BR>
<BR>
The phenomenon of Elvyr fields was first noticed by Amion, but he never lived to see Elvyr, his student, to actually witness one without equipment. The field was a first sign of magicka beyond conventional approach of mantras and gestures.<BR>
<BR>
III.II Theory<BR>
<BR>
The concept of threads are essential for understanding the higher principiums of spellcasting. Threads are links between points in Oblivion, Mundus and Autherius, through which life force and mana flow. A being's birth determines which threads are the most effective ones for that man or mer - one's firmament has been found to be rather effective as a thread, but has been debated to be much harder for people to fully spellbind than easily conceived threads such as Secunda or Massar. Do not confuse these threads with the objects of the night sky, though - most of the known threads don't have a visual pair in Nirn or Aetherius, for that matter. Instead, they join up with each other in Aurbis in circular paths to interconnect each of the stars, moons and Magnus through many more threads than there is for an eye to see. Alas, there are no threads for the eye to see, but since every object forms a thread from itself to Mundus, the expression is valid as a descriptive one.<BR>
<BR>
Daedron ports are perhaps another less-known term used in our research. So far, they have been all found in conjunction with threads and especially their ending points. The perceptions so far have proven that in fact, there are always two ports at the end of each thread, with each port having at least one thread connected to it. The ports seem to be capable of adjusting the amount of mana flow to the port conveyed by the caster and direct it to the appropriate thread.<BR>
<BR>
Perhaps a remark for less adequate in the terminology should be made here - magicka units and daedrons are considered the same, but they exist in different planes and thus should be used with respect to the plane under discussion.<BR>
<BR>
Some discussion is going on about whether the ports change the magicka to other form of energy too, called daedrons. This debate has initiated from the thought that the boundaries of magic are inside Aetherius, thus threads going through Aurbis. The term daedron port was first introduced by a Nord mage Veljeked to make a clear distinction between portals, threads and flow mechanisms.<BR>
<BR>
The final piece of theory covered here are flow mechanisms. Being the most crucial part in the way of controllability it gives to the caster. Mana flow begins from the surrounding field of the caster, determined by the location, alignment to Magnus and other visible magickal sources. The location, however, is not of great importance, since the daedron ports equalize the effect for the output port and not too exciting variations have been found in casting at specific points in common spellcasting. Magicka does not seem to be altered by any physical structures, only matter with equally powerful anti-magickal properties. This is why deep caverns are not mana-blocking by their nature. Of course, when a spell is complete and ready to be released, a part of it will turn into matter and be stopped by all and any physical elements. This transformation is called a Galeric Planar Conversion and is often referenced as one of the most important theoretical concepts of magicka along with Elvyr fields, which are derived from Gaplac, as some choose to call it.<BR>
<BR>
Hand gestures are the most important part in directing mana flow. They are covered in depth on several Academy courses, so here we will simply address the properties of rings. They are considered as ethereal ports to Oblivion, and thus hold great magical properties in spite of their size, even more so because hands are a common mage's most important tools due to their ability to redirect mana. The reason of hands suiting to all common spellbinding is the relation between fingers and ports - only few effects use more ports than eight, and even those don't require a single gesture for cast order to be complete, although effects could be arguably better if one had sixteen fingers for spells such as Astral Ideology, but after all, there are no known successful executions of that spell, so that direction is not really worth exploring.<BR>
<BR>
III.III Execution<BR>
<BR>
As with previous two experiments, the mana flow control part was started with the very same kwama and the Mundus Spectrum. As with all experiments so far, the Arkngthand Device was used to keep track of the room's status. Avorina Claudie begun by redirecting mana to Deima and Magnus. There was no difference in results - there were still four units of magicka, no less. Then, the experiment was continued with Lewenta and Magnus. Still, no variation. Even different casters did not have any success in bettering their own results from (II), and neither both Deima and Lewenta redirection, to which only Avorina was capable of, yielded any results.<BR>
<BR>
The spell was changed to a common Pinprick spell, courtesy of the Academy Library. The previous steps were taken, but this time the kwama were wounded so severely that they couldn't be used in any further experiments. The latter weren't needed anyway, because no results were achieved with any of the three redirection methods.<BR>
<BR>
With rats on full health and a Major Pinprick, Nieca Jahavie was finally able to lower her use of magicka to four units, with Ianos Capare still staying behind. The first thought was that she had actually learned something during the experiment, but further studies revealed that the reason was Deima's changed alignment to Magnus during the day. This part of the experiment was repeated next day at an earlier hour, and no success was made in the attempt by her part. This must not be confused with the relation of common casting and location - it is not affected by Aetherius' objects' alignment, but elaborate flow control seems to be.<BR>
<BR>
One of the most important aspects in Galerion's theory was the remark of mana being fully independent from Mundus. Thus, he envisioned that the properties of magickal units could allow multiple casters to prepare the same spell and direct all the mana to a single mage, opening enormous possibilities in the field of enchanting, in which massive amounts of mana and skill fortification is required. However, ordinary spells can be cast in the very same way, so Helbrog and Avorina proceeded to attempt casting Minor Pinprick in unison. The attempts were a failure at first few tries, for two different spells were cast at first. The same was tried with all the other variations of Pinprick, but no to end. As a standard procedure, other pairs of magicians were formed as well, but two similar and simultaneous spells were the only gained result.<BR>
<BR>
Later on, a possibly groundbreaking discovery was made. If there are enough daedrons in threads to form two similar spells, it will happen and the excess daedrons remain ungaplaced. This is also why the Spectrum never displayed any more than the exact double of a Pinprick spell's mana cost. In other words, if a spell being cast is too demanding in mana for a single person, a multitude of people can join in the binding process by casting the same spell, using all the mana their reservoirs have, and redirect it to the same destination simultaneously. The amount of people must be determined beforehand unless accidental multiple spells are in fact a desired effect and it has to be remembered that not anyone can join in the process - they must be able to grasp the spell's aspects fully, with only lack being the mana reservoir.<BR>
<BR>
The test with massively mana-draining spells was made with the Minor Windwalker, a classic example of any mage's dreams. After several days of timing practice, Avorina and Helbrog succeeded in completing the ritual to Helbrog, who then, according to her own words, just flied around the room. It was hard to determine where she was though, being invisible. All the effects were included and thus the experiment was declared a success.<BR>
<BR>
Last in schedule was testing the target object's size to the end result. The guar was trapped in a small lair and rendered effectively immobile by lack of space. All three spells were tested on it, both Nieca Jahavie and Ianos Capare succeeded at the first try to use only four points. The situation stayed the same through all spells except Major Pinprick, which Ianos was still unable to grasp with flow control.<BR>
<BR>
At no point of the tests was room temperature changed in any direction during the tests. This only shows that magicka is indeed fully independent of environment as long as non-elemental effects are exercised.<BR>
<BR>
Errors in the study<BR>
<BR>
Assuming that daedrons exist and the theory is solid, our results required only little adjusting. The Mundus Spectrum, as previously mentioned, sees only changes of mana fields on specific locations. This could have caused errors on the results, had the device been placed incorrectly. Yet, it never occurred that the spell would've been cast without Spectrum reflecting the change in magical balance nor was the shown result completely off scale. While most mages can't detect the lost mana to one-unit accuracy, both Avorina and Helbrog are capable of this, otherwise they would not have succeeded in redirecting mana with relative ease. Both of the less-adept researchers failed in their flow control attempts, so much analysis of their results cannot be extracted. Typographical errors might be present too, but since the essential data was checked by the Academy stewards, this has not usually been considered possible. If in doubt, feel free to repeat the experiment with the numerical data provided in the appendices.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
Conclusion<BR>
<BR>
All in all, the experiment was a success. Having in mind that magic research is empirical by its nature, failures were expected at first steps of the subject under evaluation. The most important discovery of this study, in fact, was found through trial and error. This property of simultaneous additive daedron effect can be summed up as a breakthrough on enchanting and devastating spell effects. However, with fellow mages realizing this, and having only a handful of powerful enough mages in Tamriel to attempt doing anything more than simple trinkets with the help of this knowledge, one can rest assured that it won't be misused.<BR>
<BR>
The size of the target object is an interesting property to be researched further. One could claim that casting powerful destruction spells on large monsters like the Storm Atronach, but the health of such powerful beings is far greater than the effect of a spell a common mage is able to thread properly. When targets get larger and possibly even static, the required mana to make any variation to the object's, such as a rock's, state are futile with thread approach. In these cases, it is simply easier to let the mana thread itself.<BR>
<BR>
To note that Ianos is only a Warlock by rank, the result of failing in all stages of mana redirection was not unexpected. Still, because this proves that adequate control of mana flows is dependent on the caster's intelligence, and that even very simple spells like the Pinprick, doing only the minimal amount of damage by minimal amount of magicka, are very demanding to cast, only very few men or mer will ever be capable of such an accuracy-requiring art. <BR>
"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
光谱研究<BR>
<BR>
阿沃里娜·克劳迪 著，研究员<BR>
第二纪元231年，西罗帝尔<BR>
<BR>
前言<BR>
<BR>
本文探讨了受魔能影响的身体属性及其派生形式。本文仅广泛探讨“健康”，或者更准确地说，是流淌在九个法力通道中的生命之力。为清晰起见，从现在起，这些通道将被称为迪德拉端口。<BR>
<BR>
初始设定<BR>
<BR>

魔能自身属性的要点已在其他几篇文章中涵盖，例如“基础魔能导论”。这些属性不在本文讨论范围之内。<BR>
<BR>
研究首先按照法师公会和帝国学院的传统方式设置 -- 在监视下，将预先写好的特定法术卷轴在受试者（夸蚂、老鼠和一只瓜尔）上进行测试。然后，几位施法者尝试对相同的受试者施展完全相同的法术，最后，法师们开始将他们所有的法力储备波动到一个指定的迪德拉端口，以完全控制效果。<BR>
<BR>
在三个阶段之间，对环境和受试者状态进行了广泛的状态检查。这些检查不使用魔能，而是通过锻莫发明：一种能显示热量等级的装置，也许更广为人知的名字是阿肯坦德装置，以首次发现这种工具的锻莫堡垒命名。<BR>
<BR>
另一种工具，由利尼瑟尔制作的梦达斯光谱仪，用于测量流经凡俗位面特定点的魔能量。由于其结果并非最准确，原因后述。尽管如此，我们通过反复多次测试，设法取得了可信的结果。<BR>
<BR>
实验<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
一、卷轴<BR>
<BR>
撰写法术卷轴是一个理论性课题，在学院的高级课程中已得到透彻分析。我们在此只需考虑的一个细节是，卷轴的效果总是与其作者在撰写卷轴时的专注程度一样准确。本实验使用的卷轴由学院总管之一哈塞德里安撰写，他的专长正是静态魔能，因此预计精度非常充足。<BR>
<BR>
我们来自奥辛纽姆的访客赫尔布罗格·格拉-肖罗布，开始对一只被困在深层的反魔能黑檀木箱中的普通夸蚂采集者使用卷轴。如预期，法术仅以非致命方式击中了夸蚂。用梦达斯光谱仪测得的魔能量为四个标准单位。赫尔布罗格和两名助手使用相同的卷轴，在黑檀木箱和普通木箱上重复了实验，结果相同。<BR>
<BR>
二、传统施法<BR>
<BR>
随后，阿沃里娜·克劳迪启动了研究的动态魔能部分。施放“微刺”术的材料由西罗帝尔学院图书馆提供。曾讨论过为此目的制作更合适的法术，但为了获得可比较的结果，采用了传统方法。<BR>
<BR>
当阿沃里娜·克劳迪施法时，光谱仪给出的结果是四个单位。对于其他三位施法者，数值在四到五个单位之间 -- 赫尔布罗格设法达到了三个，涅卡·贾哈维和伊阿诺斯·卡帕雷则必须在法术上花费更多法力。<BR>
<BR>
三、法力流控制<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
三.I 背景<BR>
<BR>
在瓦努斯·伽勒良本人对魔能的重大研究中，对法力流的某些特性有了重要发现。然而，当时还没有必要的信息来利用这些知识进行实验。但最近，在光界共发现了八个主要的迪德拉端口，这一发现使得能够按照这位受人尊敬的大师所预言的确切方式增强魔法属性成为可能。还有其他许多端口，但本研究不关心它们 -- 它们的行为方式与这些基本端口完全相同。<BR>
<BR>
如前所述，生命之力流经九个端口。这第九个端口被称为萨尔希亚，迄今为止似乎多余，其效果与戴玛和勒文塔相加相同。然而，它在估计法术中的误差量方面是有用的。<BR>
<BR>
原则上，魔能是一种独特的能量形式，就像生物的生命力、奈恩元素和尚未在更深层次上确定的湮灭物质一样。这些基本力量都通过彼此相互作用，因为它们似乎包含了奈恩上所有已知的物质和力量。对于纯粹主义者，应注意的是，虽然魔能包含光界，但理解轮盘的其他部分是通过湮灭物质相互作用的，诚然，这在法师的研究中尚未发现多少用途。<BR>
<BR>
埃尔维尔场现象最初由阿米翁注意到，但他未能活着看到他的学生埃尔维尔在无设备情况下实际观察到一次。该场是超越咒语和手势传统方法的魔能的第一个迹象。<BR>
<BR>
三.II 理论<BR>
<BR>
“线”的概念对于理解施法的高级原理至关重要。线是湮灭、梦达斯和光界中各点之间的联系，生命力和法力通过它们流动。一个生物的出生决定了哪些线对该人类或精灵最有效 -- 已发现一个人的天穹作为一条线相当有效，但争论点在于，与瑟昆达或马瑟尔等容易构想的线相比，人们完全束缚它要困难得多。不过，不要将这些线与夜空中的物体混淆 -- 大多数已知的线在奈恩或光界中都没有视觉对应物。相反，它们在奥比斯中以圆形路径相互连接，通过比眼睛能看到的多得多的线将每一颗星辰、月亮和马格努斯相互连接起来。唉，没有肉眼可见的线，但既然每个物体都形成了一条从自身到梦达斯的线，这种表述作为描述性语言是有效的。<BR>
<BR>
迪德拉端口也许是我们研究中使用的另一个不太为人所知的术语。到目前为止，它们都是与线，特别是线的终点一起被发现的。到目前为止的观察已经证明，实际上，每条线的末端总是有两个端口，每个端口至少有一条线与之相连。这些端口似乎能够调整施法者输送到端口的法力流量，并将其引导到适当的线上。<BR>
<BR>
也许这里应该对术语中的不足作一点说明 -- 魔能单位和迪德拉被认为是相同的，但它们存在于不同的位面，因此应根据所讨论的位面来使用。<BR>
<BR>
目前正在讨论端口是否也将魔能转变为另一种形式的能量，称为迪德拉。这场辩论源于这样一种想法：魔法的边界在光界内部，因此线穿过奥比斯。迪德拉端口一词最初由诺德法师维尔耶克德引入，以明确区分传送门、线和流动机制。<BR>
<BR>
本文涵盖的最后一部分理论是流动机制。这是它赋予施法者可控制性方式中最关键的部分。法力流从施法者的周围场开始，由位置、与马格努斯的对位以及其他可见的魔法源决定。然而，位置并不太重要，因为迪德拉端口使输出端口的效果均等，并且在普通施法中在特定点施放时未发现太令人兴奋的变化。魔能似乎不会被任何物理结构改变，只能被具有同等强大反魔能特性的物质改变。这就是为什么深洞穴本身并非法力阻隔的原因。当然，当法术完成并准备释放时，它的一部分将转化为物质，并被任何和所有的物理元素阻挡。这种转变被称为加勒里克位面转换，通常与埃尔维尔场一起被引用为魔能最重要的理论概念之一，而埃尔维尔场源自加普拉克，有些人选择这样称呼它。<BR>
<BR>
手势是引导法力流最重要的部分。它们在学院的几门课程中都有深入介绍，因此在这里我们只简要说明戒指的属性。它们被认为是通往湮灭的以太端口，因此尽管尺寸很小，却具有巨大的魔法属性，更是因为手是普通法师最重要的工具，因为它们能够重新定向法力。手适合所有普通束缚法术的原因在于手指与端口之间的关系 -- 很少有法术使用超过八个端口，即使是那些法术，也不需要单个手势就能完成施法顺序，尽管对于像星界意识形态这样的法术，如果有人有十六根手指，效果可以说会更好，但毕竟，该法术没有已知的成功执行案例，因此这个方向不值得探索。<BR>
<BR>
三.III 执行<BR>
<BR>
与前两次实验一样，法力流控制部分从使用相同的夸蚂和梦达斯光谱仪开始。与迄今为止的所有实验一样，使用阿肯坦德装置来跟踪房间的状态。阿沃里娜·克劳迪首先将法力重新导向戴玛和马格努斯。结果没有差异 -- 仍然是四个魔能单位，没有减少。然后，实验继续用勒文塔和马格努斯进行。仍然没有变化。即使不同的施法者也未能成功改善他们在（二）中的结果，而且即使是阿沃里娜唯一能够做到的将法力同时导向戴玛和勒文塔，也未产生任何结果。<BR>
<BR>
法术改为普通的“刺击”术，由学院图书馆提供。重复了之前的步骤，但这次夸蚂受伤严重，无法用于任何进一步的实验。反正后续实验也不需要了，因为三种重定向方法均未取得任何结果。<BR>
<BR>
当老鼠处于满血状态并使用“大刺击”时，涅卡·贾哈维终于能够将她使用的魔能降低到四个单位，而伊阿诺斯·卡帕雷仍然落后。最初的想法是她在实验过程中确实学到了一些东西，但进一步的研究揭示，原因是戴玛在白天的对位发生了变化。第二天更早的时候重复了这部分实验，她未能成功。这不能与普通施法和位置的关系相混淆 -- 它不受光界物体对位的影响，但精细的流动控制似乎受影响。<BR>
<BR>
伽勒良理论中最重要的方面之一是法力完全独立于梦达斯的论断。因此，他设想魔法单位的属性可以允许多个施法者准备相同的法术，并将所有法力导向一个法师，为附魔领域开辟了巨大的可能性，因为该领域需要大量的法力和技能强化。然而，普通法术也可以同样的方式施放，因此赫尔布罗格和阿沃里娜开始尝试一致施放“微刺”术。最初的几次尝试都失败了，因为起初施放的是两个不同的法术。所有其他变种的“刺击”术也尝试了相同的方法，但都无果而终。作为标准程序，也组成了其他法师对，但唯一获得的结果是两个相似且同时施放的法术。<BR>
<BR>
后来，可能取得了一项突破性的发现。如果线中有足够的迪德拉来形成两个相似的法术，就会发生这种情况，多余的迪德拉保持未转换状态。这也是为什么光谱仪显示的数值从未超过“刺击”术法力消耗的确切两倍的原因。换句话说，如果正在施放的法术对单个人来说法力需求过高，许多人可以通过施放相同的法术，使用他们法力池中的所有法力，并同时将其重定向到同一目标，来加入束缚过程。必须预先确定人数，除非偶然的多重法术实际上是期望的效果，并且必须记住，并非任何人都能加入这个过程 -- 他们必须完全掌握法术的各个方面，唯一欠缺的是法力池。<BR>
<BR>
对大量消耗法力的法术的测试使用了“微行风者”术，这是任何法师梦寐以求的经典例子。经过几天的时机练习，阿沃里娜和赫尔布罗格成功完成了对赫尔布罗格的仪式，据她自己说，她随后只是在房间里飞来飞去。不过，由于她处于隐形状态，很难确定她在哪里。所有效果都包括在内，因此实验宣布成功。<BR>
<BR>
计划中的最后一项是测试目标物体的大小对最终结果的影响。瓜尔被困在一个小巢穴中，由于空间不足而无法移动。所有三种法术都对其进行了测试，涅卡·贾哈维和伊阿诺斯·卡帕雷都首次成功地将魔能使用量降低到四点。除“大刺击”外，所有法术的情况都保持不变，伊阿诺斯仍然无法通过流控制掌握“大刺击”。<BR>
<BR>
在测试的任何时候，室温都没有向任何方向改变。这仅表明，只要施展的是非元素效果，魔能确实完全独立于环境。<BR>
<BR>
研究中的错误<BR>
<BR>
假设迪德拉存在且理论可靠，我们的结果只需要稍作调整。如前所述，梦达斯光谱仪只能看到特定位置法力场的变化。如果设备放置不正确，这可能导致结果错误。然而，从未发生过法术施放而光谱仪未反映魔法平衡变化的情况，也从未出现过显示结果完全偏离刻度的情况。虽然大多数法师无法检测到损失的法力精确到一个单位，但阿沃里娜和赫尔布罗格都能做到，否则他们不可能相对轻松地成功重定向法力。两位不太熟练的研究人员的流控制尝试都失败了，因此无法对他们的结果进行太多分析。可能还存在排印错误，但由于基本数据已由学院总管核对过，通常认为这不可能。如有疑问，请随时使用附录中提供的数值数据重复实验。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
结论<BR>
<BR>
总而言之，实验是成功的。考虑到魔法研究本质上是经验性的，在所评估主题的初始步骤中出现失败是意料之中的。事实上，这项研究最重要的发现是通过反复试验获得的。这种同时叠加的迪德拉效应特性可以概括为附魔和毁灭性法术效果上的一个突破。然而，由于其他法师意识到了这一点，而泰姆瑞尔只有少数足够强大的法师能够利用这一知识尝试制作比简单小饰品更高级的东西，我们可以放心，它不会被滥用。<BR>
<BR>
目标物体的大小是一个值得进一步研究的有趣特性。有人可能会声称对像风暴侍灵这样的大型怪物施放强大的毁灭性法术，但这种强大生物的生命力远高于普通法师能够正确引导的法术效果。当目标变大，甚至可能是静态时，使用线的方法来改变物体（如岩石）的状态所需法力是徒劳的。在这些情况下，让法力自行引导反而更简单。<BR>
<BR>
需要注意的是，伊阿诺斯只是巫者等级，他在法力重定向的所有阶段都失败，这一结果并不意外。尽管如此，这证明了充分控制法力流取决于施法者的智力，并且即使是像“刺击”这样仅用最少魔能造成最少伤害的非常简单法术，施放起来也非常苛刻，只有极少数人类或精灵才能掌握这种需要精度的技艺。<BR>
"""

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_StirkHistoriesPC
On Stirk
论斯特克

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_StirkHistoriesPC
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
On Stirk<BR>
by Calixta Avidrian<BR>
<BR>
<IMG SRC="PC\PC_maps_stirk.dds" WIDTH="240" HEIGHT="120"><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Set into the Abecean Sea like a gleaming pearl, Stirk Isle has long served as safe harbor for the many trade-ships that frequent the treacherous Abecean Sea. Though sometimes relegated to a rural backwater in less fortunate times, the island's excellent fishing waters and tropical climate have distracted many a pilgrim after a long journey to the temples of Anvil.
<BR>
As far as history has recorded, the Ayleid High Elves were the first people to set foot on Stirk. The isle seems to have been of little interest to the Ayleid sorceror-kings, whose culture was centered on their mighty Heartlands cities. It was only in the late decadent era that the Elven lords -- mistrustful of their cousins in Alinor, Valenwood, and the Direnni lands -- founded the sea-fortresses of Wormusoel, Nagaiarelle, and Vabriasel, designed to repel foreign invasions from the sea. Of course, the fall of the Ayleid Empire did not come from without, but from within, and these sea-fortresses were left to the mercy of wind and wave and time.
<BR>
Following Saint Alessia's Rebellion, the western Ayleid cities were easily toppled by the insurgent Colovian kings and their defecting elven allies. The Abecean strongholds were an exception, and their rump fleets long plagued the Strident Shore thereafter with skirmishes and incursions. But the efforts of these remnants were no match for Colo-Nordic courage and knowledge of the sea, and in 1E 343 the island of Stirk was finally conquered by Skalgar Half-Scorned, a vassal of the Shore-King. For his services, Skalgar was made the first Marshal of the Isles.
<BR>
Early records make little mention of settlements on Stirk. The great epics of the Colovian tradition occasionally note a hero or war-party from Stirk, though they rarely play roles of any significance. One saga tells how the Ra Gada invasion of 1E 808 was repelled at Stirk, one of only a few such cases in that one-sided conflict (though Redguard scholars naturally dispute this).
<BR>
The defenders of Stirk were much less successful against the Thrassian Plague. The island was ravaged by the disease, which all but eradicated the local population. Marshal Alvor Hurilus, spared from the plague by a timely pilgrimage to Sancre Tor, swore vengeance on the Sloadic menace and supported Bendu Olo's bid for the Strident Throne after the demise of the last Shore-King. The Marshals of the Isles continued to play a prominent role in the short-lived Oloman Confederacy and the War of Righteousness, in which Marshal-Captain Aravest the Night-Eyed is said to have led many daring raids up the Niben River.
<BR>
After the First Interregnum, the Marshals of the Isles were listed among the oath-bound of Reman. The isle, and the town of Charach (which is mentioned here in the histories for the first time), played a small part in the great western conquests as a military harbor and supply station, and later served as the most vital forward outpost of the Remans in their centuries-long cold war with the Summerset Isles.
<BR>
Stirk would reprise these roles during the Tiber Wars, as a key military asset in the great feats of Admirals Vasi Hadrach and Amiel Richton. Charach was assaulted twice, first by Redguard outlaws of the Restless League, and later by the Summerset Navy, whose occupation caused grievous destruction before the island could be reclaimed. After the war, the defeated elves were tasked with financing Charach's rebuilding and the construction of Duskwatch Keep, so that Imperial order in the surrounding seas might be preserved in perpetuity.
<BR>
Stirk was lucky to escape the ravages of the Camoran Usurper as his monstruous forces swept north through the mainland of West Colovia, though it was much plagued by the infamous pirates that sailed in those lawless days. For over a decade the Marshals of the Isles ruled their isolated lands much as their ancient ancestors had, alone, until the campaigns of Commodore Fasil Conomorus, later King of Anvil, finally put an end to the Usurper's scourge in Cyrodiil. Though the terrors of the Simulacrum and recent unrest in the Iliac Bay have caused a resurgence of such acts of piracy, it will surely only be a short while before the West Navy scours these seas again, and every inhabitant of Stirk can sleep safe with the knowledge that they, too, live under the Law and Peace of the Empire.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
论斯特克<BR>
卡利克斯塔·阿维德里安 著<BR>
<BR>
<IMG SRC="PC\PC_maps_stirk.dds" WIDTH="240" HEIGHT="120"><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
斯特克岛如一颗闪亮的珍珠镶嵌在阿碧希安海中，长期以来一直是频繁往来于危险重重的阿碧希安海的众多商船的安全港。虽然在不那么幸运的时期，它有时会沦为偏僻的乡下地方，但岛上绝佳的渔场和热带气候，让许多长途跋涉前往安维尔神殿的朝圣者流连忘返。
<BR>
根据历史记载，亚历德高精灵是第一批踏上斯特克岛的人。亚历德的巫师国王们似乎对这个岛兴趣不大，他们的文化以其强大的心脏地城市为中心。直到腐朽的时代晚期，精灵领主们 -- 不信任他们在阿里诺尔、瓦伦伍德和迪伦尼领地的表亲 -- 才建立了沃姆索尔、纳盖亚雷尔和瓦布里亚塞尔的海上堡垒，旨在抵御来自海上的外国入侵。当然，亚历德帝国的覆灭并非来自外部，而是来自内部，这些海上堡垒只能任凭风浪和时间摆布。
<BR>
继圣阿莱西亚起义之后，西部的亚历德城市很快被起义的科洛维亚国王和他们叛变的精灵盟友推翻。阿碧希安的据点是个例外，其残余舰队此后长期以冲突和入侵骚扰着斯特赖登特海岸。但这些残余势力的努力无法与科洛-诺德的勇气和海洋知识相匹敌，第一纪元343年，斯特克岛最终被滨海王的封臣斯卡加尔·半轻蔑征服。为了表彰他的功绩，斯卡加尔被任命为第一位群岛执法官。
<BR>
早期的记录几乎没有提到斯特克岛上的定居点。科洛维亚传统的伟大史诗偶尔会提到来自斯特克的英雄或战团，尽管他们很少扮演任何重要的角色。一个传奇故事讲述了第一纪元808年拉伽达的入侵是如何在斯特克被击退的，这是那场一边倒的冲突中为数不多的此类案例之一（尽管红卫学者自然会对此提出异议）。
<BR>
斯特克岛的防御者在对抗瑟拉斯瘟疫时则远没有那么成功。该岛被瘟疫蹂躏，几乎消灭了当地人口。执法官阿尔沃·胡里鲁斯因及时前往桑克雷·托朝圣而幸免于难，他对斯洛德的威胁发誓复仇，并在最后一位滨海王去世后支持本都·奥洛争夺斯特赖登特王位。群岛执法官在短暂的奥洛曼联盟和正义之战中继续发挥着重要作用，据说在其中，夜眼执法官队长阿拉维斯特领导了多次沿尼本河向上的大胆突袭。
<BR>
第一次大空位期之后，群岛执法官被列为雷曼的宣誓效忠者。该岛和查拉赫镇（历史上首次在此提及）作为军事港口和补给站，在伟大的西部征服中发挥了小小作用，后来成为雷曼王朝在与夏暮群岛长达数百年的冷战中最重要的前沿哨所。
<BR>
在泰伯战争期间，斯特克岛再次扮演了这些角色，成为上将瓦西·哈德拉赫和阿米尔·里克顿伟大功绩中的关键军事资产。查拉赫曾两次遭到袭击，第一次是被不安联盟的红卫逃犯，后来是被夏暮海军，其占领在岛屿被收复之前造成了严重的破坏。战后，战败的精灵负责资助查拉赫的重建和暮卫要塞的建设，以便帝国在周边海域的秩序能够永久维持。
<BR>
斯特克岛幸运地逃脱了篡位者卡莫兰的蹂躏，他那可怕的军队席卷了西科洛维亚的大陆，尽管该岛深受那些在无法无天的日子里航行的臭名昭著的海盗的困扰。十多年来，群岛执法官像他们古老的祖先一样，独自统治着他们与世隔绝的土地，直到后来成为安维尔国王的法西尔·科诺莫鲁斯准将的征战最终终结了篡位者在西罗帝尔的祸害。尽管幻象的恐怖和最近髂骨湾的动乱导致此类海盗行为再次抬头，但西部海军肯定不久就会再次清扫这些海域，斯特克岛的每个居民都可以安心入睡，因为他们知道，他们也生活在帝国的法律与和平之下。<BR>"""

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_StudyLockedNovelTR

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_StudyLockedNovelTR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>A Study of the Locked Novel<BR>
by Maros Quinnus<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
It is to the Empire's loss that Altmer authorities continue to deny access to the historical records of Summerset Isle. The ancient texts contained therein are almost certainly invaluable to Tamrielic history, and could elucidate the cultural origins of both man and mer. Regardless, the lords of Summerset Isle show no sign of budging on this matter.<BR><BR>
While Altmer academic literature is beyond the reach of our scholars, the same cannot be said for their popular literature, which can be found in diaspora communities all across Tamriel. Though such texts do not pretend to discuss historical or social fact, they nonetheless provide a window through which the Empire can better understand its Altmer subjects.<BR><BR>
However, such understanding must be tempered by the knowledge that Altmer literature is nearly impenetrable to the outsider. Literary styles are marked by obfuscation and obscurantism, reflecting the fact that their audiences consisted of the aristocracy and clerisy.<BR><BR>
The so-called "locked novels", thus named due to their secretive nature, provides an interesting example of this tendency. These novels were often written in the waning centuries of the Second Era. The precise content varies, though most take the form of a chivalric romance, a comedy of manners, or a picaresque.<BR><BR>
What unites and defines the locked novel is an assumption that the reader is intimately familiar not only with Altmer culture, but with the specific social circle for which the novel was written. Not the slightest trace of exposition can be found in such works. Characters are introduced without introductions. Important events are referred to, but never described.<BR><BR>
The most famous locked novel is Stinging, the Obtuse Barb in Dragonflesh Ripped (hereafter referred to as Stinging), which appears to have been written at the behest of House Vilyas, a now-defunct clan that once owned the fisheries east of Dusk.<BR><BR>
In 3E 176, nearly a century after House Vilyas' fall at the hands of the Maormer, Imperial authorities stumbled upon a cache of Vilyas tax records, letters, and orders that had somehow come into the possession of a Breton smuggler. The Vilyas documents were examined for the sake of thoroughness, but authorities found little that made sense. The documents seemed half-complete, and made symbolic references not found in any other Altmer writings.<BR><BR>
The truth was only revealed when an Altmer sympathetic to the Empire produced a copy of Stinging, and showed how House Vilyas had used the book as a code for its members. By referring to the contents of Stinging, an individual Vilyas family member or retainer could communicate in a way only understandable by those closest to him.<BR><BR>
Reading a locked novel became an act of group initiation and affirmation. Those who had read a particular novel could discuss confidential information while disguising it as a conversation about a literary work. Reliance on locked novels may have even hampered communication between the various houses and cliques, weakening Altmer resistance to Maormer and Sload depradations.<BR><BR>
Despite the practical intent behind locked novels, the authors also intended them to reach heights of artistic quality worthy of their owners. Surviving examples compare favorably with other, more widely circulated, Altmer texts. Phrases or lines of text deemed safe for wider readership were sometimes released to improve the patron's reputation. Access to a particularly intriguing locked novel acted as incentive for joining a clique or marrying into a family.<BR><BR>
Opacity became the downfall of the locked novel. Subsequent generations found them difficult to understand, especially as Altmer society evolved under imperial rule. Altmer paranoia prevented the creation of guidebooks or explanations to these works, so the underlying meaning was inevitably forgotten over time.<BR><BR>
As the value of locked novels decreased, their circulation increased, though few are still read today. Those that remain, such as Stinging, are known mostly for the beauty of their descriptive prose. The average Altmer (who was never intended to read such works) will not truly understand the novel, though he may pretend to.<BR><BR>
However, some diaspora Altmer have attempted to impose their own idiosyncratic interpretations to such narratives, coming up with explanations and backstories to replace those forgotten by the long-dead creators. These jury-rigged narratives help bring together those Altmer living in far-flung provinces like Skyrim or Elsweyr.<BR><BR>
In this way, the history of the locked novel repeats itself.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>封闭小说研究<BR>
马罗斯·奎努斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
傲特莫当局继续拒绝外界查阅夏暮岛的历史记录，这是帝国的损失。其中包含的古代文本对泰姆瑞尔历史几乎肯定具有无可估量的价值，并可能阐明人类和精灵的文化起源。尽管如此，夏暮岛的领主们在此事上丝毫没有让步的迹象。<BR><BR>
虽然傲特莫的学术文献超出了我们学者的触及范围，但他们的通俗文学则不然，这些作品可以在泰姆瑞尔各地的流散社区中找到。尽管此类文本并非旨在讨论历史或社会事实，但它们确实提供了一个窗口，帝国可以通过它更好地理解其傲特莫臣民。<BR><BR>
然而，这种理解必须考虑到，傲特莫文学对外人来说几乎是难以理解的。其文学风格以晦涩和蒙昧主义为特征，反映出其受众由贵族和知识分子组成。<BR><BR>
所谓的“封闭小说”，因其隐秘性而得名，为这种趋势提供了一个有趣的例子。这些小说通常写于第二纪元的最后几个世纪。具体内容各不相同，但大多数采取骑士浪漫小说、风尚喜剧或流浪汉小说的形式。<BR><BR>
定义并统一封闭小说的特征是，它假设读者不仅非常熟悉傲特莫文化，而且熟悉小说所针对的特定社交圈。此类作品中找不到丝毫的解释性文字。人物在没有任何介绍的情况下登场。重要事件被提及，但从未被描述。<BR><BR>
最著名的封闭小说是《刺，龙皮撕裂中的钝倒钩》（以下简称《刺》），它似乎是在维利亚斯家族的要求下写成的，该家族现已灭亡，曾拥有达斯克以东的渔场。<BR><BR>
第三纪元176年，在维利亚斯家族被锚莫击败近一个世纪后，帝国当局偶然发现了一批维利亚斯家族的税务记录、信件和命令，这些文件不知为何落入了一个布莱顿走私者手中。为了彻底调查，当局检查了维利亚斯文件，但发现几乎毫无意义。这些文件似乎只有一半完整，并包含在其他任何傲特莫著作中都找不到的象征性引用。<BR><BR>
直到一位同情帝国的傲特莫拿出了一本《刺》的副本，并展示了维利亚斯家族如何将这本书用作其成员的密码，真相才得以揭晓。通过引用《刺》的内容，维利亚斯家族的某个成员或家臣可以用只有他最亲近的人才能理解的方式进行交流。<BR><BR>
阅读封闭小说成为一种群体入会和确认的行为。那些读过特定小说的人可以讨论机密信息，同时将其伪装成关于文学作品的对话。对封闭小说的依赖甚至可能阻碍了不同家族和派系之间的沟通，削弱了傲特莫对锚莫和斯洛德掠夺的抵抗。<BR><BR>
尽管封闭小说背后有实用的意图，但作者也希望它们达到配得上其拥有者的艺术质量高度。现存的例子与其它流传更广的傲特莫文本相比毫不逊色。被认为对更广泛读者群安全的短语或文本行有时会被发布，以提高赞助人的声誉。接触到一本特别有趣的封闭小说，成为加入某个派系或与某个家族联姻的激励。<BR><BR>
晦涩难懂成为封闭小说衰落的原因。后代发现它们难以理解，尤其是在傲特莫社会在帝国统治下演变之后。傲特莫的偏执阻止了为这些作品编写指南或解释，因此其内在含义随着时间推移不可避免地被人遗忘。<BR><BR>
随着封闭小说价值的降低，它们的流通量增加了，尽管今天很少有人阅读它们。那些留存下来的，如《刺》，主要以其描述性散文的优美而闻名。普通的傲特莫（从来不是此类作品的预期读者）不会真正理解小说，尽管他可能会假装理解。<BR><BR>
然而，一些流散的傲特莫试图将自己特有的解释强加于这些叙事，提出解释和背景故事来取代早已死去的创作者所遗忘的那些内容。这些临时拼凑的叙事有助于将生活在遥远行省（如天际或艾斯维尔）的傲特莫聚集在一起。<BR><BR>
就这样，封闭小说的历史在重复自身。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><BR>
A Study On Guars<BR> 
by Gidiron Yoiua<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
Near the beginning of the Third Era, Emperor Tiber Septim is said to have made a tour of the newly incorporated Province of Morrowind. During the Emperor's visit to the Deshaan plains in the south east, he famously dubbed the species of striped guar found there 'tigers' -- a creature heretofore unknown to the Dark Elves. The ferocious tiger guar has since become a highly prized game animal for noble huntsmen and trophies can be found throughout the Empire.
<BR><BR>
Less well-known in the West is the tiger guar's smaller cousin, the common guar. Domesticated guar have been a valuable source of meat and hides for centuries prior to the founding of the Third Empire. Today the hardy bipeds can be seen throughout Morrowind, carrying merchants' packs, pulling carts, and serving as mounts in the infamously horseless province. With the recent reorganization of Vvardenfell Territory to a Provincial District, the island has finally become available for proper study. As such, I set out to study the guar in this largely unspoiled land.
<BR><BR>
Upon my arrival in Seyda Neen, a small settlement on the swampy southern coast of Vvardenfell, the only guar in sight belonged to a trader headed for Balmora. Upon interviewing the locals, I learned wild guar avoid the region for fear of sinking into the mire. Supposedly the man-sized mud crabs hiding along the shore are also known to prey on stray guar and, as a smirking old elf put it, 'careless outlanders who mistake them for rocks.' Having seen these sluggish crabs for myself, I do not think there is much cause to worry there. Nonetheless, an injured guar might very well fall prey to one.
<BR><BR>
After spending several hours in Seyda Neen I joined a group of pilgrims headed north. We had arrived on the same ship and it is always best to travel in numbers when treading unfamiliar ground. Our party made good speed and we entered the lush and fertile Ascadian Isles region before sunset. While I failed to spot any wild guar that first day, we encountered many in the days that followed. I observed many a wild guar drinking from the shallow pools surrounding Lake Amaya and rooting for the very nutritious corkbulbs that grow in the area. The farmers we met along the way were less than enthused about the wild guar's proclivity for digging up food, especially those farmers growing ash yams. Their domesticated guar at least had the decency to let a farmer dig up their meals without ruining the entire plot, or so they said. I certainly saw the odd farm guar digging for food when its owner wasn't looking.
<BR><BR>
While the pilgrims' tales of Vivec replacing a farmer's dead guar and Saint Seryn being tough as a guar sounded promising, they were not truly guar related and we parted ways at the Shrine of Humility. From there I traveled to Ald'ruhn with a young warrior sworn to House Redoran. The ashlands spreading out from Red Mountain in which the city can be found made for a shocking contrast with the green Ascadian Isles. Here I got to see the guar's true value as a beast of burden in hostile Morrowind. Where my companion and I had to cover our faces to keep the ash out of eyes and lungs, the guar in the area hardly seemed affected at all. Their thick skin provides ample protection from the elements while their eyes are protected behind a clear gelatinous layer. My companion informed me that House Redoran has guar mounted warriors patrolling the roads, protecting pilgrims and merchants from bandits and blighted horrors alike. Clad in native Dark Elven armor, these patrols can travel through any weather with ease. The primitive Ashlander nomads likewise travel through Vvardenfell's ash storms with their herds of guar and beetles. Their craftsmen are said to be adept at working guar hide. Unfortunately the danger posed by these barbarians meant I was not able to investigate these things for myself.
<BR><BR>
On the road to Ald'ruhn I had the opportunity to see the wild guar's territorial habits up close. Previously our large group deterred them, but now that it was just the two of us they were quite fierce. While my companion had no problem fending them off, a wild guar is quite fearsome at close range. Although their teeth are not all that dangerous, the natural strength and tenacity so prized in pack guar lends itself well to trampling hapless travelers. Keeping the high ground against a creature this size is recommended not only to prevent being knocked over, but also to scare off the guar. Unlike the tiger guar and despite its territorial behavior, the common guar is quite meek and easily demoralized. This holds true even when encountered in herds, once one guar in the herd is spooked the rest of the herd is liable to run off with it.
<BR><BR>
I ended up staying in Ald'ruhn for several months making forays into the ashlands surrounding the city aided by local hunters and scouts. These excursions and the occasional invisibility potion provided me with the opportunity to study the guar's mating habits in exquisite depth.
<BR><BR>
[For the next 10 pages the book graphically describes and depicts the entire guar mating process.]

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><BR>
瓜尔研究<BR>
吉迪隆·约尤亚 著<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
据说在第三纪元初期，泰伯·塞普汀皇帝巡视了新并入的晨风行省。在皇帝访问东南部的迪莎安平原期间，他将那里发现的条纹瓜尔物种命名为“老虎” -- 一种丹莫此前未知的生物。此后，凶猛的虎瓜尔成为贵族猎手们极为珍视的猎物，其战利品遍布整个帝国。
<BR><BR>
在西方鲜为人知的是虎瓜尔较小的表亲 -- 普通瓜尔。在第三帝国建立之前的几个世纪里，驯化的瓜尔一直是肉和皮的宝贵来源。如今，在晨风各地都能看到这种耐寒的两足动物，它们驮着商人的包裹，拉着大车，并在这个以无马闻名的省份充当坐骑。随着最近瓦登费尔领地被重新组织为行省区，该岛终于可以进行适当的研究了。因此，我开始在这片基本上未受破坏的土地上研究瓜尔。
<BR><BR>
当我到达瓦登费尔沼泽般南海岸的小定居点赛达·尼恩时，唯一能看到的瓜尔属于一个前往巴尔莫拉的商人。通过采访当地人，我了解到野生瓜尔会避开该地区，因为害怕陷入泥潭。据说，潜伏在岸边的人大小的泥沼蟹也会捕食迷路的瓜尔，正如一个咧嘴笑的老精灵所说，“还有那些把它们误认为石头的粗心外地人。”亲眼见过这些行动迟缓的螃蟹后，我认为无需过分担心。尽管如此，一只受伤的瓜尔很可能成为它们的猎物。
<BR><BR>
在赛达·尼恩待了几个小时后，我加入了一群向北前进的朝圣者。我们是乘同一艘船到达的，在踏足不熟悉的土地时，结伴旅行总是最好的。我们的队伍行进速度很快，我们在日落前进入了郁郁葱葱、肥沃的阿斯卡迪亚群岛地区。虽然第一天我没能发现任何野生瓜尔，但在随后的日子里我们遇到了很多。我观察到许多野生瓜尔在阿玛亚湖周围的浅水池中饮水，并挖掘该地区生长的营养丰富的软木鳞茎。我们沿途遇到的农民对野生瓜尔挖掘食物的习性不太感兴趣，尤其是那些种植灰烬山药的农民。他们驯养的瓜尔至少还知道让农民挖出食物而不毁掉整个田地，至少他们是这么说的。我当然见过奇怪的农场瓜尔在主人不注意时挖掘食物。
<BR><BR>
虽然朝圣者们讲述的维威克替换农民死去的瓜尔以及圣瑟琳像瓜尔一样坚韧的故事听起来很有希望，但它们与瓜尔并不真正相关，我们在谦卑圣祠分道扬镳。从那里，我与一位宣誓效忠勒多兰家族的年轻战士一起前往奥德-汝因。从红山蔓延开来的灰烬之地，与绿色的阿斯卡迪亚群岛形成了惊人的对比。在这里，我看到了瓜尔作为敌对晨风中驮兽的真正价值。当我和我的同伴不得不遮住脸以防止灰烬进入眼睛和肺部时，该地区的瓜尔似乎几乎不受影响。它们厚实的皮肤提供了充足的保护，免受恶劣天气的影响，而它们的眼睛则被一层透明的凝胶状物质保护着。我的同伴告诉我，勒多兰家族有骑着瓜尔的战士在路上巡逻，保护朝圣者和商人免受匪徒和枯萎恐怖的侵害。这些巡逻队身着丹莫本土盔甲，可以轻松地在任何天气下行进。原始的灰烬之民游牧民族也同样带着他们的瓜尔和甲虫群穿越瓦登费尔的灰烬风暴。据说他们的工匠擅长处理瓜尔皮。不幸的是，这些野蛮人构成的危险意味着我无法亲自调查这些事情。
<BR><BR>
在前往奥德-汝因的路上，我有机会近距离观察野生瓜尔的领地习性。以前我们的大队伍会吓跑它们，但现在只有我们两个人，它们就相当凶猛了。虽然我的同伴击退它们毫无问题，但野生瓜尔在近距离相当可怕。尽管它们的牙齿并非那么危险，但在驮兽瓜尔中备受推崇的天生力量和韧性，很容易用来践踏不幸的旅行者。面对这种体型的生物，占据高地不仅是为了防止被撞倒，也是为了吓跑瓜尔。与虎瓜尔不同，尽管有领地行为，普通瓜尔相当温顺，容易丧失斗志。即使在群体中遇到也是如此，一旦群体中的一只瓜尔受到惊吓，其余的瓜尔很可能会跟着它一起跑掉。
<BR><BR>
我最终在奥德-汝因待了几个月，在当地猎人和侦察兵的帮助下，深入城市周围的灰烬之地。这些短途旅行和偶尔的隐形药水让我有机会深入研究瓜尔的交配习性。
<BR><BR>

The Supposition of Freedom
自由之假说

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_SuppositionOfFreedomTR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Supposition of Freedom: A Response to The Purity of Freedom <BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
In his work, The Purity of Freedom, Iman Kanten argued for the independence of freedom from the influence of action and the physical world. In this work, I respond by citing contradictory points of evidence.<BR>
<BR>
Introduction: The Gift of Freedom<BR>
<BR>
What does freedom entail for us? This question is of penultimate importance, but I can only address it shortly for fear of revealing my own ignorance on the subject. Freedom, I believe, exists in its expression as rationality. It allows us to evaluate our own actions and stands as its own final judge, and it separates us from the lesser beasts and slaves (by which I mean the absolute, bound servants of the Daedra) who seem to have no control over their lives.<BR>
<BR>
The Presupposition of Freedom and Its Effects on Our Actions<BR>
<BR>
Are sentient creatures truly free? Consider this: when I will (and by "will" I do not mean to imply some great power on my own part - the words "will" and "want" are almost interchangeable here, but I emphasize the notion of free will in my selection) some event to occur and it seems that I possess the necessary capabilities to spur that event's transpiration, the actual fruition of that event is not guaranteed. That is, sentient creatures are not absolutely capable of free action. Why does this case exist? From my investigations, it would seem that it is the result of two complementary factors: the existence of prophecy and the nature of the Aedra as the world's creators. Based on my conclusions here, I will examine the issue of free will as well.<BR>
<BR>
As has been witnessed for countless generations, the power of prophecy and destiny cannot be denied. Their effects have reshaped the political (through the existence and current state of the Empire) and physical (i.e. the Western Warp) landscapes of our continent, and they have indelibly altered our perceptions of the world. In analyzing the concept of freedom, prophecy must be examined because we must question the degree to which it affects a sentient creature; that is, does prophecy alter not only our actions but even our mental states as well? We shall examine this question through the construction of artificial worlds in which the alternatives are the case. In the first world, we shall assume that prophecy binds only our actions and not our thoughts. In this world, those under the influence of prophecy would be forced to act in spite of their will; this idea strikes me as exceedingly odd. Historically, those under the power of prophecy have acted with an unparalleled surety, which seems counterintuitive considering the awkwardness with which we - and by this I mean ordinary individuals - approach actions that disagree with our thoughts. Consider the example of unwilling executioner raising his blade, or the example of an obstinate child grudgingly obeying his mother; in both cases, the person's actions disagree with their thoughts. Certainly this is not to say that those under prophecy's hold do not have doubts, but a difference exists between doubt and the contradiction of thoughts and actions. This evidence seems to quiet the thought that prophecy guides only our actions.<BR>
<BR>
If this is the case, however, we have thus lost a degree of freedom; prophecy must guide both our thoughts and our actions. Therefore, because prophecy binds us both physically and rationally, we retain essentially no freedom when acting under its influence. This idea threatens the very foundations of our freedom; it has been argued that every event, no matter how great or how small, can be prophesized or that a prophecy already exists for it - the prophets simply don't waste their time finding every inane aspect of the future. If every action or event has an associated prophecy to guide it, then no action is of our own will.<BR>
<BR>
In addressing this issue, it is important to note that a potential solution has been offered to counter this apparently deterministic view. Certainly, it is difficult to argue against the notion that a prophecy exists for each of our actions; however, if we examine the extent to which destiny actually determines our individual actions, the answer becomes significantly more clouded. While the eventual consequence or result may be determined, the means by which we reach that result could remain unwritten. This idea can be presented with the analogy of being in a closed room (representing fate). We are trapped within this room, but we are allowed a degree of freedom in that room. The analogy works only on such a simple scale, however, because each individual "free" action may be governed by a smaller determination - this idea extends from the decision to kill another person to the decision we make in regulating the rate of our breathing. It would seem that essentially every aspect of our lives could be determined.<BR>
<BR>
The second problem with the notion of freedom resides in the constitution of the Aedra, our creators. Collectively, the Aedra represent stasis, the inability to change. I will not address the peculiarities and apparent paradoxes of the Aedra in this volume (i.e. the fact that the Aedra can be killed, which would represent a shift in existence, while they embody stasis), but I will address one aspect of the nature of the Aedra because of its relevance to the topic at hand.<BR>
<BR>
The Aedra created our world (once more, a paradox given their nature), but the Aedra represent immutability. Freedom represents the ability to change, the ability to shift in thought and action from a destined course. How could the unchanging Aedra create a world in which its denizens possess something that they themselves do not? Perhaps the Aedra created a world in which something of a lesser version of their nature might exist and amuse them, some shady image of themselves. Given this information, the question becomes more complex and interesting: are even the Aedra free, and if so, does that necessarily mean that we ourselves are free as well?<BR>
<BR>
The first question we can never properly answer, for lack of proper evidence. They created the worlds and the laws which may suggest or refute the possibility of mortal freedom (depending upon whether they are free or not). However, did they create these laws spontaneously or did they base them off of higher laws by which they are themselves governed? Could they have created any other world than the one they did? These questions only dance around the originally proposed question but still touch on its edges. We can never determine whether the Aedra are controlled by unseen forces or if they act with true autonomy. The second part of the question, once more, cannot be properly addressed as of yet. Even presuming that the Aedra are free, what will they might have had in our creation (i.e. whether to make us free or not) cannot be determined - did they want something true to their image, or are we simply some sort of experiment of existence?<BR>
<BR>
Unfortunately, it seems that I can merely raise questions and not properly answer them. However, this work has hopefully inspired questions worth consideration within the reader's mind. These are the sorts of questions which drive us as sentient creatures, and answering them must be an imperative for our kind.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
自由之假说：对《自由之纯粹》的回应<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
在其著作《自由之纯粹》中，伊曼·坎滕论证了自由独立于行动和物理世界的影响。在这篇著作中，我引用矛盾的证据点来回应。<BR>
<BR>
引言：自由的礼物<BR>
<BR>
自由对我们意味着什么？这个问题至关重要，但我只能简短地讨论，以免暴露我自己在这个主题上的无知。我相信，自由存在于其作为理性的表达中。它让我们能够评估自己的行为，并作为自身的最终评判者，它也将我们与那些似乎无法控制自己生活的低级野兽和奴隶（我指的是迪德拉的绝对束缚的仆人）区分开来。<BR>
<BR>
自由之预设及其对我们行动的影响<BR>
<BR>
有感知的生物真的自由吗？考虑一下：当我意欲（“意欲”这个词并不意味着暗示我自己有什么伟大的力量 -- 在这里“意欲”和“想要”几乎可以互换，但我在选择中强调了自由意志的概念）某个事件发生，并且似乎我拥有推动该事件发生的必要能力时，该事件的实际结果并不保证。也就是说，有感知的生物并非绝对有能力采取自由行动。这种情况为何存在？根据我的调查，似乎是两个互补因素的结果：预言的存在和艾德拉作为世界创造者的本质。基于我在此的结论，我也将审视自由意志的问题。<BR>
<BR>
正如无数代人见证的那样，预言和命运的力量不可否认。它们的影响重塑了我们大陆的政治格局（通过帝国的存在和当前状态）和物理面貌（即西部扭曲），并不可磨灭地改变了我们对世界的看法。在分析自由的概念时，必须审视预言，因为我们必须质疑它在多大程度上影响有感知的生物；也就是说，预言是否不仅改变了我们的行为，甚至还改变了我们的心理状态？我们将通过构建假设其他情况为真的虚拟世界来审视这个问题。在第一个世界中，我们假设预言仅束缚我们的行动，而不束缚我们的思想。在这个世界中，受预言影响的人将被迫违背自己的意志行动；这个想法在我看来极其奇怪。历史上，受预言力量影响的人以无与伦比的确定性行动，考虑到我们 -- 我指的是普通个体 -- 在采取与我们思想相悖的行动时的别扭感，这似乎有违直觉。以不情愿的刽子手举起屠刀，或固执的孩子不情愿地服从母亲为例；在这两种情况下，当事人的行为都与他们的思想相悖。当然，这并不是说受预言控制的人没有疑虑，但疑虑与思想和行为的矛盾之间是有区别的。这个证据似乎平息了预言仅引导我们行动的想法。<BR>
<BR>
然而，如果是这样，我们就失去了一定程度的自由；预言必须引导我们的思想和行动。因此，由于预言在身体和理性上都束缚了我们，我们在其影响下行动时基本上没有自由。这个想法威胁到我们自由的基础；有人认为，每一个事件，无论大小，都可以被预言，或者已经存在关于它的预言 -- 预言家只是不会浪费时间去找出未来的每一个微不足道的方面。如果每一个行动或事件都有相关的预言来引导它，那么就没有行动是出于我们自己的意志。<BR>
<BR>
在讨论这个问题时，重要的是要注意，已经提出了一种潜在的解决方案来反驳这种明显的决定论观点。当然，很难反驳每个行动都存在预言的论点；然而，如果我们审视命运实际上在多大程度上决定了我们的个体行动，答案就会变得模糊得多。虽然最终的结果可能已被决定，但我们达到该结果的手段可能仍是未知的。这个想法可以用身处一个封闭房间（代表命运）的类比来呈现。我们被困在这个房间里，但在这个房间里我们被允许有一定程度的自由。然而，这个类比只适用于如此简单的规模，因为每一个“自由”的个体行动可能都受制于一个更小的决定 -- 这个想法从杀死另一个人的决定延伸到我们在调节呼吸速率时所做的决定。似乎我们生活的每一个方面都可能是被决定的。<BR>
<BR>
自由概念的第二个问题在于我们的创造者艾德拉的构成。集体而言，艾德拉代表着静止，即无法改变。我不会在本卷中讨论艾德拉的特殊性和明显的悖论（例如，艾德拉可以被杀死，这将代表存在的转变，而它们却体现着静止），但我会讨论艾德拉本质的一个方面，因为它与当前的主题相关。<BR>
<BR>
艾德拉创造了我们的世界（再次，考虑到它们的本质，这是一个悖论），但艾德拉代表着不变。自由代表着改变的能力，即从既定的过程中转变思想和行动的能力。不变的艾德拉如何能创造一个其居民拥有它们自身所没有的东西的世界呢？也许艾德拉创造了一个世界，其中可能存在其本质的某种较低级版本来取悦它们，一些它们自身的阴暗形象。基于这些信息，问题变得更加复杂和有趣：甚至艾德拉是自由的吗？如果是，那是否必然意味着我们自己也是自由的？<BR>
<BR>
第一个问题我们永远无法恰当回答，因为缺乏适当的证据。它们创造了世界和法律，这些法律可能暗示或驳斥凡俗自由的可能性（取决于它们本身是否自由）。然而，它们是自发创造了这些法律，还是基于它们自身所受的更高法律来制定的？它们能创造出不同于现在这个世界的其他世界吗？这些问题只是围绕着最初提出的问题打转，但仍然触及了其边缘。我们永远无法确定艾德拉是被看不见的力量所控制，还是以真正的自主行事。同样，问题的第二部分目前也无法恰当解决。即使假定艾德拉是自由的，它们在创造我们时的意愿（即是否让我们自由）也无法确定 -- 它们是想要一个符合它们自身形象的东西，还是我们只是某种存在的实验？<BR>
<BR>
不幸的是，看来我只能提出问题，而不能恰当地回答它们。然而，希望这部作品能在读者心中激发值得思考的问题。这些正是推动我们作为有感知生物的问题，回答它们必须是我们这类人的当务之急。<BR>"""

The Tale of Dro'Zira<BR>
Transcription and Commentary<BR>
by Sonia Vette<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
~The following is a tale overheard, as told by a Khajiit father to his cub, while making camp with one of their caravans. I have attempted to transcribe it as he told it, for the Khajiit do not often speak of their history to outsiders. In truth I do not believe he would have spoken at all, but for the vast helping of Moonsugar he had consumed that night.~<BR>
<BR>
Come and warm your fur by the fire, Ma'rashirr, and I will tell you of how our Dro'Zira came to be the greatest of all Khajiit! (ed: Dro'Zira I took in this case to be an honored ancestor)<BR>
<BR>
The ancient Khajiit heard the great roar of Alkosh the Great Cat King of Time (ed: known as Akatosh in the empire, and Alduin in Skyrim) and raced to his Voice. In three days' time they crossed the whole of Tamriel, resting not even for the moonsugar, for such was the speed of Khajiiti then.<BR>

They joined with the pride of Alkosh and were his strongest warriors. Lorkhaj, (ed: Shor in the Nordic) however, chose to give his roar to the Ra'Wulfharth to spite the Khajiiti warriors, for he was jealous of their devotion to Alkosh.<BR>

Seeing the ferocity of the Khajiiti warriors, Ra'Wulfharth could not bring himself to put them to death. <BR>

<BR>
As for the rest of the "Rhojiit" They grew small and lost their cunning altogether, which is why you should not hesitate to strike them down when they approach the wagons. So it was told by my father, and so I tell it now to you.<BR>
<BR>
Now, be a good cub and go fetch me some more moonsugar for these sweet cakes.<BR>
 <BR>
<BR>
~Much of the tale seemed to me, little more than a boast, but certain facts do seem to line up with what we believe is the truth behind the legends. It does raise questions as to why we do not know more about history of the Khajiit and what parts they have played that might not have been recorded by our written histories.~<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
德罗'兹拉的故事<BR>
转录与评论<BR>
索尼娅·维特 著<BR><BR>

~以下是偶然听到的一个故事，是一个卡吉特父亲在和他的一个商队扎营时讲给他的幼崽听的。我试图按照他讲述的方式转录下来，因为卡吉特人不常对外人讲述他们的历史。说实话，要不是他那天晚上吃了大量的月亮糖，我根本不相信他会开口说话。~<BR>

The Tale of King Vrage's Sons
弗拉格国王之子传奇

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Tale of King Vrage's Sons
<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
[This ancient epic poem tells the story of King Vrage's sons.]<BR>
<BR>
That was a good king,<BR>
that Vrage, called the Gifted,<BR>
with great strength and much warwyrd,<BR>
he conquered much of Merethland...<BR>
<BR>
