"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Basic Guide to Telvanni Construction<BR>
by Clagius Galenus<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
When one is given opportunity to visit Morrowind Province, one will undoubtedly notice the strangeness of construction, the glaring differences in architecture from more familiar Imperial-style buildings. Foremost in unusual design are the almost wholly alien structures favored by members of the Great House Telvanni. While that House is considered among the more xenophobic, and members are generally unwilling to part with hard-learned knowledge, we have been able to piece together a great deal of information from various sources about the fantastic dwellings of the Telvanni.<BR>
<BR>
Even the casual observer will note that Telvanni buildings are not, in fact, traditional buildings at all. Rather, they are totally organic structures grown into useful shapes to accommodate city life. Thick large vines curling about above merchant stalls and winding in curious paths overhead are common sights in any Telvanni town. Many hold the belief that Telvanni towers are plants, although that is technically incorrect; in reality, the structures are fungal in nature. The more curious will note the distinct mushroom shapes of the upper reaches of towers central in any Telvanni city.<BR>
<BR>
Although one will encounter any number of dwellings in a Telvanni town, it might come as a surprise that all pod-houses in a town are part of the same organism (although some structures in some towns are separate, so technically it is not one fungus, but a small colony). Instead of being several smaller fungi scattered about the countryside, all are merely outgrowths of the incredible towers that rise from the heart of the village. Therefore, when one inquires as to how such a city is built, how the towers are grown is the question one is truly asking.<BR>
<BR>
All Telvanni towers need magic and care to be properly grown, and require a great deal of expertise across multiple fields. It is necessary for one to be familiar with construction, primarily to select and prepare a site. Architecture, to understand what kind of shapes are appropriate for men and mer to live in, what growth patterns offer the greatest structural stability, and other such concerns. Magic, to be able to grow the fungus in the first place, and to guide its expansion later on. Mycology, again primarily for site selection--it is vital to know under what conditions the fungus can survive, and to what extent it can be manipulated through magical means. Morrowind's generally inhospitable environs seem to offer the Telvanni fungus ideal conditions in which to thrive. Indeed, Many Telvanni towns are found along coastlines, where harsh rocky shores meet the salt water of the seas.<BR>
<BR>
Telvanni cities can be grown from a single spore, and when one considers the grand scale of the resultant towers in which Telvanni counselors and elders reside, one begins to understand the sheer mastery of Telvanni sorcery. However, a single spore on its own is not enough for one to grow such a spectacular city. Spores require a magical catalyst in order to spur their remarkable growth. While it may be entirely possible for an especially powerful wizard to act as such a catalyst, it is virtually unheard of. Instead, one must procure at least two grand soul gems, and fill them with appropriately strong souls for this endeavor. Needless to say, this aspect of construction is much more dangerous than a more familiar gathering of wood and stone. The monsters whose souls are used--usually some sort of daedra--are among the most powerful one will encounter in all of Tamriel. Less adventurous individuals could purchase the necessary gems pre-filled from enchanters or adventurers, although the price for these are, quite reasonably, astronomical. Of course, the person seeking to grow a Telvanni tower is almost always an accomplished magician, and so much more capable of obtaining such items than a commoner.<BR>
<BR>
Within their own ranks, the Telvanni only offer to aid construction for members of a certain rank in the House, and require those seeking advancement into the upper echelons to have their own tower. While the Telvanni typically scorn outside interference--even that of the other Great Houses--it is considered good practice to begin growing a tower only after obtaining a construction contract from the proper Imperial authority. In addition to supplying a pair of soul gems, the prospective owner must also make a sizable financial contribution; the work on a tower is highly specialized, and requires a moderate number of laborers. On top of those standard necessities, at times key figures involved in tower construction will make their own demands. These unforeseen obstacles can range from simple male boredom (easily solved with the addition of women) to suggestions of enhancing security. In any event, the one thing that an ambitious wizard does not have to provide himself is the actual spore--presumably, with all the requirements that go along with the whole affair, there is quite an oversupply of unused spores.<BR>
<BR>
The spore is carefully seeded (an unusual expression, to be sure) along with the soul gems, and supervised over a period of time. Within a matter of days, a small number of mushrooms will have risen up from the site. At this point, one well versed in Telvanni construction will visit the burgeoning fungus, and, through some unknown means, allow the mushroom access to the power held within the gems it has grown around. It is believed that the Telvanni must wait until the fungus has enveloped the gems because only then that they can ensure the gems' power is being siphoned off by the fungus and is not consumed by some other avenue, or wasted. Further, it is also speculated that the Telvanni control the growth rate of the fungus by determining the degree of energy flow from the gems, explaining why new cities can sprout rapidly, while older ones remain more static. At any rate, it is at this point that the simplistic, familiar mushroom shape begins to change into the more exotic design seen in Telvanni cities. Even with the passive flow of power from the gem, it takes many craftsmen and architects to coax the fungus into creating the tiny buds that they will eventually later mold into large pods, which can then be hollowed out for Telvanni to use as housing.<BR>
<BR>
As the tower grows and one can finally step inside it, one will undoubtedly find their attention drawn to the man-sized, purplish crystals which are often found in the lower, older areas of the tower. These may seem mysterious for a moment, but after considering the building materials, are altogether expected. The crystals are the remnants of the soul gems, their forms twisted and changed through Telvanni magic and their symbiosis with the fungus.<BR>
<BR>
Those familiar with the lesser fungi of Tamriel might wonder how sturdy such a structure can be. A glance at a Telvanni town is show enough that the great mushrooms do not rely on accumbency to support themselves. Similar in effects to the less destructive mating of Telvanni and other, 'foreign' architectures is the town of Ranyon Ruhn on the mainland. Here a Telvanni tower has been grown, and all around the Velothi-styled town there are clear signs of this, but no damage has been done to the original buildings. A true marvel of Telvanni construction and fungal growth is their capital city of Port Telvannis. The tower at Port Telvannis, Tel Thenim, is one of the largest ever grown, and, appropriately, towers above the vertical city below. While the city's roots are firmly anchored in the soil most of the structures that the Telvanni dwell in are high above the ground, carved out of the massive shoots of the great tower. This gives the city an otherworldly appearance, given that its streets are many feet up into the air.<BR>
<BR>
There are a number of advantages to the Telvanni's choice of living arrangement. A growing organism can be quite resistant to harm, and the magical nature of the arrangement means that it requires very little in the way of maintenance. The Telvanni do not have to concern themselves with damaged roofs or rotting timbers, or many of the other myriad problems associated with western houses. Many foreigners do not know this, but the fungus also has a limited capacity to remove salt from water, rendering it potable for mer and men. Many Telvanni towns are found along coastlines to take advantage of this ability. Though it isn't a tested theory, the abundance of moisture in Telvanni-controlled areas, in addition to the fungus's propensity for absorbing water, suggest that these structures would not face much danger from fire.<BR>
<BR>
Some may find believe that living inside of a fungus that was grown with the soul of a creature unusual, but it actually quite effective. Inside, the air is often moist and faintly warm, but there is little indication that the structure around you is actually a living organism. The interior architecture is substantially different that of the other Great Houses, as there are often shafts that require levitation to reach to higher levels. This serves a dual purpose: taking less interior room in the tower, and preventing a good portion of the people of Tamriel from getting in, as the Telvanni--particularly those on the mainland--are not fond of outsiders. The tops of the towers are often flat, and this provides the resident a good view of all of those around, as well as a fairly secure summoning area.<BR>
<BR>
Morrowind is well suited for the magicka based Telvanni buildings. The Telvanni Isles, Azura's Coast and Boethiah's Spine regions are excellent for maintaining Telvanni structures. House Telvanni also has holdings on Vvardenfell. Although towers have yet to be constructed within the harsh, ashen Molag Amur region, it is believed that they will need more maintenance. Telvanni buildings are strong, well-built structures, and serve the Great House Telvanni and the people of Morrowind well.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
泰瓦尼建筑基本指南<BR>
克拉吉乌斯·加勒努斯 著<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
当一个人有机会访问晨风行省时，他无疑会注意到建筑的奇特之处，与更熟悉的帝国风格建筑相比，其建筑风格存在显著差异。最不寻常的设计是泰瓦尼大贵族成员偏爱的、几乎完全异形的结构。虽然该家族被认为是比较排外的，其成员通常不愿分享来之不易的知识，但我们还是能够从各种来源拼凑出关于泰瓦尼奇妙住所的大量信息。<BR>
<BR>
即使是随意的观察者也会注意到，泰瓦尼建筑实际上根本不是传统建筑。相反，它们是完全有机的结构，生长成有用的形状以适应城市生活。粗大的藤蔓缠绕在商摊上方，在头顶蜿蜒出奇特的路径，是任何泰瓦尼城镇的常见景象。许多人认为泰瓦尼塔楼是植物，尽管这在技术上是不正确的；实际上，这些结构本质上是真菌。更好奇的人会注意到任何泰瓦尼城市中心塔楼上部独特的蘑菇形状。<BR>
<BR>
尽管在泰瓦尼城镇中会遇到许多住所，但令人惊讶的是，城镇中的所有荚屋都是同一有机体的一部分（尽管某些城镇中的某些结构是独立的，所以严格来说，它不是一种真菌，而是一个小型菌落）。它们不是散布在乡间的几个较小真菌，而仅仅是从村庄中心升起的那些不可思议的塔楼的旁支。因此，当人们询问这样的城市是如何建造的时，他们真正问的是塔楼是如何生长的。<BR>
<BR>
所有泰瓦尼塔楼都需要魔法和照料才能正常生长，并且需要在多个领域拥有大量专业知识。一个人需要熟悉建筑，主要是为了选择和准备场地。建筑学，以了解什么样的形状适合人类和精灵居住，什么样的生长模式能提供最大的结构稳定性，以及其他类似问题。魔法，首先能够使真菌生长，并随后引导其扩张。真菌学，再次主要用于场地选择 -- 了解真菌在什么条件下可以生存，以及通过魔法手段可以操纵到什么程度，是至关重要的。晨风总体上是严酷的环境，似乎为泰瓦尼真菌提供了理想的生长条件。事实上，许多泰瓦尼城镇都位于海岸线上，那里是崎岖的岩石海岸与海水交汇的地方。<BR>
<BR>
泰瓦尼城市可以从单个孢子生长而成，当考虑到由此产生的塔楼的宏伟规模（泰瓦尼顾问和长老居住在其中）时，人们开始理解泰瓦尼巫术的精湛技艺。然而，单靠一个孢子是不足以生长出如此壮观的城市。孢子需要魔法催化剂来刺激其显著生长。虽然一个特别强大的巫师有可能充当这种催化剂，但这几乎是闻所未闻的。相反，人们必须至少获得两个巨型灵魂石，并为这一努力用足够强大的灵魂填充它们。不用说，建筑的这一方面比更熟悉的收集木材和石头要危险得多。其灵魂被使用的怪物 -- 通常是某种迪德拉 -- 是整个泰姆瑞尔中最强大的生物之一。不那么爱冒险的人可以从附魔师或冒险者那里购买预先填充好的必要灵魂石，尽管这些的价格相当合理，但高得惊人。当然，寻求生长泰瓦尼塔楼的人几乎总是一位有成就的魔法师，因此比平民更有能力获得此类物品。<BR>
<BR>
在他们自己的队伍中，泰瓦尼人只为家族中特定等级的成员提供建筑援助，并要求那些寻求晋升到高层的人拥有自己的塔楼。虽然泰瓦尼人通常蔑视外部干涉 -- 即使是其他大家族的干涉 -- 但人们认为，只有在从适当的帝国当局获得建筑合同后才开始生长塔楼是好的做法。除了提供一对灵魂石外，潜在的所有者还必须提供一笔可观的资金；塔楼的工作是高度专业化的，需要适量的劳动力。在这些标准必需品之上，有时参与塔楼建设的关键人物会提出他们自己的要求。这些不可预见的障碍可以从简单的男性无聊（通过增加女性来轻松解决）到加强安全的建议。无论如何，一个有抱负的巫师不必自己提供的一样东西是实际的孢子 -- 大概，考虑到整件事的所有要求，未使用的孢子供应相当过剩。<BR>
<BR>
孢子与灵魂石一起被仔细播种（这无疑是一种不寻常的表达方式），并在一定时间内受到监督。在几天之内，少量蘑菇就会从该地点长出来。此时，一位精通泰瓦尼建筑的人会去探访这正在生长的真菌，并通过某种未知的方式，让蘑菇接触它所环绕的灵魂石中蕴含的力量。据信，泰瓦尼人必须等到真菌将灵魂石包裹起来，因为只有这样才能确保宝石的力量被真菌吸取，而不是被其他途径消耗或浪费。此外，还有人推测泰瓦尼人通过决定来自宝石的能量流程度来控制真菌的生长速度，这解释了为什么新城市可以迅速发芽，而旧城市则保持相对静止。无论如何，正是在这一点上，简单、熟悉的蘑菇形状开始转变为泰瓦尼城市中看到的更具异国情调的设计。即使有来自宝石的被动能量流，也需要许多工匠和建筑师来诱导真菌创造微小的芽，然后他们最终会将其塑造成大的荚，然后可以挖空供泰瓦尼人用作住宅。<BR>
<BR>
随着塔楼长成，人们最终可以走进去时，无疑会发现自己被塔楼下部、更古老的区域中常见的人形大小的紫色水晶所吸引。这些水晶起初可能看起来很神秘，但考虑到建筑材料，它们完全是意料之中的。这些水晶是灵魂石的残余，它们的形态通过泰瓦尼魔法及其与真菌的共生关系而扭曲和改变。<BR>
<BR>
熟悉泰姆瑞尔较小真菌的人可能会想知道这样的结构有多坚固。看一眼泰瓦尼城镇就足以证明，巨大的蘑菇并不依靠依附来支撑自己。与泰瓦尼和其他“外来”建筑破坏性较小的结合效果相似的是大陆上的兰永·鲁恩镇。在这里，一座泰瓦尼塔楼已经长成，而在维洛提风格的城镇周围，到处都有明显的迹象，但原始建筑并未受到损坏。泰瓦尼建筑和真菌生长的真正奇迹是他们的首都泰瓦尼港。泰瓦尼港的塔楼泰尔·塞尼姆是有史以来生长的最大的塔楼之一，并且恰如其分地高耸于下方的垂直城市之上。虽然城市的根牢牢地扎在土壤中，但泰瓦尼人居住的大部分结构都高高地在地面之上，是从大塔楼的巨大嫩枝中雕刻出来的。这赋予了这座城市超凡脱俗的外观，因为它的街道悬空数英尺高。<BR>
<BR>
泰瓦尼人选择这种居住安排有许多优点。生长的有机体对伤害有相当的抵抗力，并且这种安排的魔法性质意味着它几乎不需要维护。泰瓦尼人不必担心损坏的屋顶或腐烂的木料，或与西方房屋相关的许多其他问题。许多外国人不知道的是，这种真菌还具有有限的从水中去除盐分的能力，使其可供精灵和人类饮用。许多泰瓦尼城镇位于海岸线以利用这种能力。尽管未经检验，但泰瓦尼控制区域的水分充足，加上真菌吸水特性，表明这些结构不会面临太大的火灾危险。<BR>
<BR>
有些人可能觉得住在用生物灵魂培育的真菌里很奇怪，但实际上它非常有效。内部空气通常潮湿且微暖，但几乎没有迹象表明你周围的结构实际上是一个活的有机体。内部建筑与其他大家族的建筑大不相同，因为经常需要漂浮才能到达更高层的竖井。这有两个目的：占用塔楼更少的内部空间，并阻止泰姆瑞尔的很大一部分人进入，因为泰瓦尼人 -- 尤其是大陆上的泰瓦尼人 -- 不喜欢外人。塔楼的顶部通常是平的，这为居住者提供了良好的视野，可以俯瞰周围的一切，也是一个相当安全的召唤区域。<BR>
<BR>
晨风非常适合基于魔能的泰瓦尼建筑。泰瓦尼群岛、阿祖拉海岸和波耶西亚之脊地区非常适合维护泰瓦尼建筑。泰瓦尼家族在瓦登费尔也有领地。尽管在严酷的、灰烬覆盖的莫拉格·阿穆尔地区尚未建造塔楼，但据信它们将需要更多的维护。泰瓦尼建筑是坚固、结构良好的建筑，很好地服务于泰瓦尼大贵族和晨风的人民。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Alik'r<BR>
By Enric Milres<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
I might never have gone to the Alik'r Desert had I not met Weltan in a little tavern in Sentinel. Weltan is a Redguard poet whose verse I had read, but only in translation. He chooses to write in the old language of the Redguards, not in Tamrielic. I once asked him why.<BR><BR>
"The Tamrielic word for the divinely rich child of rot, silky, pressed sour milk is ... cheese," said Weltan, a huge smile spreading like a tide over his lampblack face. "The Old Redguard word for it is mluo. Tell me, if you were a poet fluent in both languages, which word would you use?"<BR><BR>
I am a child of the cities, and I would tell him tales of the noise and corruption, wild nights and energy, culture and decadence. He listened with awed appreciation of the city of my birth: white-marbled Imperial City where all the citizenry are convinced of their importance because of the proximity of the Emperor and the lustration of the streets. They say that a beggar on the boulevards of the Imperial City is a man living in a palace. Over spiced ale, I regaled Weltan with descriptions of the swarming marketplace of Riverhold; of dark, brooding Mournhold; of the mold-encrusted villas of Lilmoth; the wonderful, dangerous alleys of Helstrom; the stately avenues of grand old Solitude. For all this, he marvelled, inquired, and commented.<BR><BR>
"I feel as if I know your home, the Alik'r Desert, from your poems even though I've never been there." I told him.<BR><BR>
"Oh, but you don't. No poem can express the Alik'r. It may prepare you for a visit far better than the best guide book can. But if you want to know Tamriel and be a true citizen of the planet, you must go and feel the desert yourself."<BR><BR>
It took me a little over a year to break off engagements, save money (my greatest challenge), and leave the urban life for the Alik'r Desert. I brought several books of Weltan's poems as my travel guide.<BR><BR>
"A sacred flame rises above the fire, The ghosts of great men and women without names, Cities long dead rise and fall in the flame, The Dioscori Song of Revelation, Bursting walls and deathless rock, Fiery sand that heals and destroys."<BR><BR>
These first six lines from my friend's "On the Immortality of Dust" prepared me for my first image of the Alik'r Desert, though they hardly do it justice. My poor pen cannot duplicate the severity, grandeur, ephemera and permanence of the Alik'r.<BR><BR>
All the principalities and boundaries the nations have placed on the land dissolve under the moving sand in the desert. I could never tell if I was in Antiphyllos or Bergama, and few of the inhabitants could tell me. For them, and so it came to me, we were simply in the Alik'r. No. We are part of the Alik'r. That is closer to the philosophy of the desert people.<BR><BR>
I saw the sacred flame of which Weltan wrote on my first morning in the desert: a vast, red mist that seemed to come from the deep mystery of Tamriel. Long before the noon sun, the mist had disappeared. Then I saw the cities of Weltan. The ruins of the Alik'r rise from the sand by one blast of the unbounded wind and are covered by the next. Nothing in the desert lasts, but nothing dies forever.<BR><BR>
At daylight, I hid myself in tents, and thought about the central character of the Redguards that would cause them to adopt this savage, eternal land. They are warriors by nature. As a group, there are none better. Nothing for them has worth unless they have struggled for it. No one fought them for the desert, but the Alik'r is a great foe. The battle goes on. It is a war without rancor, a holy war in the sense the phrase should always imply.<BR><BR>
By night, I could contemplate the land itself in its relative serenity. But the serenity was superficial. The stones themselves burned with a heat and a light that comes not from the sun, nor the moons Jone and Jode. The power of the stones comes from the beat of the heart of Tamriel itself.<BR><BR>
Two years I spent in the Alik'r.<BR><BR>
As write this, I am back in Sentinel. We are at war with the kingdom of Daggerfall for the possession of a grass-covered rock that belongs to the water of the Iliac Bay. All my fellow poets, writers, and artists are despondent for the greed and pride that brought these people into battle. It is a low point, a tragedy. In the words of Old Redguard, an ajcea, a spiral down.<BR><BR>
Yet, I cannot be sorrowful. In the years I spent in the glories of the Alik'r, I have seen the eternal stones that live on while men go dead. I have found my inner eye in the tractless, formless, changeless and changeable land. Inspiration and hope, like the stones of the desert, are eternal though men be not.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
阿利克'尔<BR>
恩里克·米尔雷斯 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
如果不是在哨卫城的一家小酒馆里遇到韦尔坦，我可能永远不会去阿利克'尔沙漠。韦尔坦是一位红卫诗人，我读过他的诗，但只是译本。他选择用红卫人的古语写作，而不是用泰姆瑞尔语。我曾经问他为什么。<BR><BR>
“泰姆瑞尔语中，用来形容腐烂、丝滑、压榨的酸牛奶的神圣丰富的孩子是......奶酪，”韦尔坦说，他乌黑的脸上露出如潮水般蔓延开的巨大笑容。“古红卫语中对应的词是姆卢奥。告诉我，如果你是一位精通两种语言的诗人，你会用哪个词？”<BR><BR>
我是城市的孩子，我会给他讲关于喧嚣与腐败、狂野之夜与活力、文化与颓废的故事。他带着敬畏和欣赏聆听关于我出生城市的故事：白色大理石建造的帝都，所有市民都因靠近皇帝和街道的净化仪式而深信自己的重要性。他们说，帝都林荫大道上的乞丐是住在宫殿里的人。在喝着加香料的麦酒时，我向韦尔坦生动地描述了河堡熙熙攘攘的市场；阴暗、沉思的哀伤之城；利尔莫斯布满霉菌的别墅；海尔斯特罗姆奇妙而危险的小巷；古老庄严的独孤城宏伟的大道。对于这一切，他惊叹、询问并评论。<BR><BR>
“尽管我从未去过那里，但我觉得从你的诗中，我了解了你的家乡，阿利克'尔沙漠。”我告诉他。<BR><BR>
“哦，但你并不了解。没有任何诗歌能表达阿利克'尔。它可能会让你比最好的旅行指南更好地为访问做好准备。但如果你想了解泰姆瑞尔，成为这个星球真正的公民，你必须亲自去感受那片沙漠。”<BR><BR>
我花了一年多的时间来结束各种应酬，存钱（这是我最大的挑战），然后离开城市生活，前往阿利克'尔沙漠。我带了几本韦尔坦的诗集作为我的旅行指南。<BR><BR>
“神圣的火焰在火堆上方升起，伟大而无名的男男女女的鬼魂，早已死去的城市在火焰中起落，启示的迪奥斯库里之歌，爆裂的墙壁和不朽的岩石，治愈又毁灭的火热沙粒。”<BR><BR>
我朋友《论尘埃的不朽》开头的这六行诗，让我对阿利克'尔沙漠的第一印象有所准备，尽管它们远未能描绘其真容。我拙劣的笔无法复制阿利克'尔的严酷、壮丽、短暂与永恒。<BR><BR>
各国在这片土地上划定的所有公国和边界，都在沙漠移动的沙粒下消融了。我永远无法分辨自己是在安提菲洛斯还是贝尔加马，很少有居民能告诉我。对他们来说，我也因此明白，我们只是身处阿利克'尔。不。我们是阿利克'尔的一部分。这更接近沙漠人民的哲学。<BR><BR>
在沙漠的第一个早晨，我看到了韦尔坦所写的神圣火焰：一片广阔的红色薄雾，似乎来自泰姆瑞尔深处的神秘。远在正午的太阳之前，薄雾就消失了。然后我看到了韦尔坦的城市。阿利克'尔的废墟被一阵无边的风从沙中吹起，又被下一阵风掩埋。沙漠中没有什么是永恒的，但也没有什么是永远死亡的。<BR><BR>
白天，我躲在帐篷里，思考着红卫人的核心性格，这种性格使他们接受了这片野蛮、永恒的土地。他们天生就是战士。作为一个群体，没有比他们更好的了。对他们来说，任何东西只有经过奋斗才有价值。没有人为了沙漠与他们战斗，但阿利克'尔是一个伟大的敌人。战斗仍在继续。这是一场没有怨恨的战争，一场在其应有意义上始终暗示的圣战。<BR><BR>
到了晚上，我可以思考这片土地相对的宁静。但这种宁静是表面的。石头本身燃烧着一种热量和光芒，并非来自太阳，也并非来自双月乔恩和乔德。石头的力量来自泰姆瑞尔自身心脏的跳动。<BR><BR>
我在阿利克'尔度过了两年。<BR><BR>
在写这篇文章时，我已回到哨卫城。我们正与匕落王国交战，争夺一块属于髂骨湾水域的、被草覆盖的岩石。我所有的诗人、作家和艺术家同仁都因驱使这些人投入战斗的贪婪和骄傲而感到沮丧。这是一个低谷，一场悲剧。用古红卫语来说，阿杰亚，一个向下的螺旋。<BR><BR>
然而，我不能悲伤。在阿利克'尔辉煌中度过的岁月里，我看到了那些在人类死去后依然存在的永恒石头。我在这片无路、无形、不变又善变的土地上找到了我的内在之眼。灵感和希望，就像沙漠中的石头，即使人类并非永恒，它们却是永恒的。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Alik'r<BR>
By Enric Milres<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
I might never have gone to the Alik'r Desert had I not met Weltan in a little tavern in Sentinel. Weltan is a Redguard poet whose verse I had read, but only in translation. He chooses to write in the old language of the Redguards, not in Tamrielic. I once asked him why.<BR><BR>
"The Tamrielic word for the divinely rich child of rot, silky, pressed sour milk is ... cheese," said Weltan, a huge smile spreading like a tide over his lampblack face. "The Old Redguard word for it is mluo. Tell me, if you were a poet fluent in both languages, which word would you use?"<BR><BR>
I am a child of the cities, and I would tell him tales of the noise and corruption, wild nights and energy, culture and decadence. He listened with awed appreciation of the city of my birth: white-marbled Imperial City where all the citizenry are convinced of their importance because of the proximity of the Emperor and the lustration of the streets. They say that a beggar on the boulevards of the Imperial City is a man living in a palace. Over spiced ale, I regaled Weltan with descriptions of the swarming marketplace of Riverhold; of dark, brooding Mournhold; of the mold-encrusted villas of Lilmoth; the wonderful, dangerous alleys of Helstrom; the stately avenues of grand old Solitude. For all this, he marvelled, inquired, and commented.<BR><BR>
"I feel as if I know your home, the Alik'r Desert, from your poems even though I've never been there." I told him.<BR><BR>
"Oh, but you don't. No poem can express the Alik'r. It may prepare you for a visit far better than the best guide book can. But if you want to know Tamriel and be a true citizen of the planet, you must go and feel the desert yourself."<BR><BR>
It took me a little over a year to break off engagements, save money (my greatest challenge), and leave the urban life for the Alik'r Desert. I brought several books of Weltan's poems as my travel guide.<BR><BR>
"A sacred flame rises above the fire, The ghosts of great men and women without names, Cities long dead rise and fall in the flame, The Dioscori Song of Revelation, Bursting walls and deathless rock, Fiery sand that heals and destroys."<BR><BR>

The Buying Game
买卖游戏

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Buying Game<BR>
by Ababael Timsar-Dadisun<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
So many people simply buy the items they need at the price they are given.  It's a very sad state of affairs, when the game is really open to all, you don't need an invitation.  And it is a game, the game of bargaining, to be played seriously and, I hasten to add, politely.  In Elsweyr, it is common for the shop-owner to offer the prospective buyer tea or sweetmeats and engage in polite conversation before commencing the business.  This eminently civilized tradition has a practical purpose, allowing the buyer to observe the wares for sale.  It is considered impolite not to accept, though it does not imply obligation on the part of the buyer.<BR>
<BR>
Whether this particular custom is part of the culture or not, it's wise for the buyer and seller to greet one another with smiles and warm salutations, like gladiators honoring one another before the battle.<BR>
<BR>
Bargaining is expected all over Tamriel, but the game can be broken if one's offer is so preposterously low that it insults the shop-keeper.  If you are offered something for ten gold pieces, try offering six and see where that takes you.  <BR>
<BR>
Do not look like you're very interested, but do not mock the quality of the goods, even if they deserve it.  Much better to admire the quality of workmanship, but comment that, regretfully, you simply cannot afford such a price.  When the shop-keeper compliments your taste, smile, but try to resist the flattery.<BR>
<BR>
A lot of the game depends on recognizing the types of shop-keepers and not automatically assuming that the rural merchant is ignorant and easily fooled, or the rapacious city merchant is selling shoddy merchandise. Caravans, it should be mentioned, are always good places to go to buy or trade.<BR>
<BR>
Knowing what you're buying and from whom is a talent bought only after years of practice.  Know the specialties of certain regions and merchants before you even step foot in a shop.  Recognize too the prejudices of the region.  In Morrowind where I hail from, for example, Argonians are viewed with a certain amount of suspicion.  Don't be surprised or insulted if the shopkeepers follow you around the shop, assuming you're going to steal something.  Similarly, Nords, Bretons, and Cyrodiils are sometimes treated coolly by merchants in the Summurset Isles.  Of course, I don't know any shopkeepers anywhere, no matter their open-mindedness, who aren't alerted when a Khajiit or a Bosmer enters their shop.  Even Khajiiti and Bosmeri shopkeepers.  <BR>
<BR>
If you see something you really like or need, buy it then and there at the best price you can get.  I cannot tell you how many times I passed up a rare and interesting relic, assuming that I could find it elsewhere in the region, perhaps at a larger town at a better price.  Too late, I discovered I was wrong, and when I returned to the shop weeks later, the item I wanted was gone.  Better to get a great purchase at a decent price and discover it again at a worse price than to miss out on your opportunities for ownership.  Occasionally impulsiveness is the best buying strategy.<BR>
<BR>
Sense the moves of the game, and everyone can win. <BR>
<BR>
"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
买卖游戏<BR>
阿巴巴埃尔·蒂姆萨尔-达迪森 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
许多人只是以给定的价格购买他们需要的物品。这真是可悲，当游戏真正向所有人开放时，你并不需要邀请。这是一场游戏，讨价还价的游戏，需要认真对待，而且我要补充说，要有礼貌。在艾斯维尔，店主在开始交易前向潜在买家提供茶或甜点并进行礼貌交谈是很常见的。这个极其文明的传统有一个实际目的，让买家有机会观察待售的商品。不接受被视为不礼貌，尽管这并不意味着买方有义务。<BR>
<BR>
无论这一特定习俗是否是文化的一部分，买家和卖家都应以微笑和热情的问候相互致意，就像角斗士在战斗前互相致敬一样，这是明智之举。<BR>
<BR>
在整个泰姆瑞尔，讨价还价都是预料之中的，但如果你的报价低得离谱，侮辱了店主，那么游戏就可能破裂。如果有人以十金币的价格向你提供某物，试着出价六金币，看看会怎样。<BR>
<BR>
不要显得你非常感兴趣，但也不要嘲笑商品的质量，即使它们确实如此。更好的做法是欣赏工艺质量，但遗憾地评论说，你实在负担不起这个价格。当店主称赞你的品味时，微笑，但尽量抵抗住奉承。<BR>
<BR>
游戏很大程度上取决于识别店主的类型，不要自动认为乡下商人无知且容易上当，或者贪婪的城市商人在销售劣质商品。值得一提的是，商队总是购买或交换的好地方。<BR>
<BR>
知道你在买什么，从谁那里买，是只有经过多年实践才能获得的才能。在踏入商店之前，就要了解某些地区和商人的专长。也要认识到该地区的偏见。例如，在我的家乡晨风，阿尔贡人受到一定程度的怀疑。如果店主跟着你在店里转，以为你要偷东西，不要感到惊讶或受侮辱。同样，诺德人、布莱顿人和西罗帝尔人有时会在夏暮群岛受到商人的冷遇。当然，我不知道有哪个地方的店主，无论他们多么开明，当卡吉特或波斯莫进入他们的商店时不会警觉。甚至卡吉特和波斯莫店主也是如此。<BR>
<BR>
如果你看到自己真正喜欢或需要的东西，就立刻以你能得到的最好价格买下它。我无法告诉你，我有多少次放弃了一个稀有而有趣的遗物，以为我可以在该地区的其他地方找到它，也许在更大的城镇以更低的价格。等我发现自己错了，为时已晚，几周后我回到商店时，我想要的东西已经不见了。与其错过拥有的机会，不如以一个不错的价格买下，即使以后发现能以更差的价格再次买到。偶尔，冲动是最好的购买策略。<BR>
<BR>
感知游戏的步骤，每个人都能赢。<BR>
<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Ebon Arm<BR>
By Witten Rol<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The ground shakes. The great armies continue to wage their unrelenting battle. The battlefield is red, the rivers flow crimson, the sky reflects a deep pink. In the distance lightning flashes, and thunder sounds. Two huge ravens begin circling the field; their blackness is vibrant against the various shades of red in this vista of death and suffering. The bright flashes of light and rumbling begin to increase. The redness surrounding the battlefield begins giving way to a golden glow from the east, almost like a summer's setting sun. From the false sunset a massive golden stallion and single rider approach. All become suddenly still on the field of battle as both sides recognize Reymon Ebonarm, God of War, and the companion and protector of all warriors, also known as the Black Knight and his mighty steed War Master.<BR><BR>
He rides into the middle of the blood soaked field and dismounts. He is a very imposing figure. His very tall and heavily muscled body is encased in ebony armor. His ebony helmet does not hide the flowing reddish blonde hair and beard which appear almost as shimmering gold, nor does it shield the steel blue eyes that seem to pierce all they fall upon. In his left hand he carries a massive ebony tower shield on which is emblazoned a fiery red rose. As he raises his right arm, all see an arm and a magnificent ebony blade which are extensions of each other. The fused arm and sword are a result and symbol of the wounds suffered by this god during titanic battles in the youth of this world.<BR><BR>
The ravens come to rest on his shoulders. And, as the point of the ebony blade seemingly touches the sky, lightning flashes, thunder roars. Then total quiet descends and a shudder rolls through both armies.<BR><BR>
The leaders of both armies approach Reymon Ebonarm and kneel. In turn they tell their reasons for this war. Each asks for the favor of the Black Knight for their cause. Reymon Ebonarm listens, but there is no acknowledgment that he has chosen to favor one side or the other in this fight. However, each of the leaders has heard the other state his position. And, each now knows that this war is baseless. They embrace and turn to their armies. They instruct their forces to bury their dead, tend their wounded and return to their homes.<BR><BR>
Reymon Ebonarm mounts his great golden stallion, War Master, and again raises the ebony blade skyward and extends the huge rose emblazoned ebony shield to both armies. A massive chorus of cheers rises from the armies. The ravens again take to the air. Lightning and thunder follow him as he rides into the sunset followed by the two birds.<BR><BR>
The armies do as they have been bidden. They care for their wounded and bury their dead. As they retreat towards their homes each warrior is sure that the great God Reymon Ebonarm, the Black Knight, has responded to their individual prayers for intervention. Each side has won, neither has lost.<BR><BR>
As the armies depart the field, the rivers begin to run clear, and a single red rose begins to bloom near the grave of a fallen hero.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
黑檀臂<BR>
威滕·罗尔 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
大地在颤抖。庞大的军队继续着他们无情的战斗。战场是红色的，河流流淌着深红，天空映出深粉色。远处闪电闪烁，雷声隆隆。两只巨大的乌鸦开始在空中盘旋；它们的黑色在这死亡与苦难景象的各种红色调中显得格外鲜明。明亮的闪光和隆隆声开始加剧。战场周围的红色逐渐被东方金色的光芒取代，几乎像夏日的落日。从这虚假的日落中，一匹巨大的金色种马和一位骑手出现了。战场上的一切突然静止，因为双方都认出了雷蒙·黑檀臂，战争之神，所有战士的伙伴和保护者，也被称为黑骑士，以及他强大的坐骑战争之主。<BR><BR>
他骑马进入血染的战场中央，然后下马。他是一个非常威严的人物。他那高大而肌肉发达的身体包裹在黑檀盔甲中。他的黑檀头盔没有遮住他飘逸的红金色头发和胡须，它们几乎像闪烁的黄金，也没有遮住那双似乎能刺穿一切所视之物的钢蓝色眼睛。他的左手拿着一面巨大的黑檀塔盾，盾上装饰着一朵火红的玫瑰。当他举起右臂时，所有人都看到一条手臂和一柄宏伟的黑檀剑，它们彼此延伸，融为一体。这融合的手臂和剑，是这位神祇在世界年轻时进行泰坦之战所受创伤的结果和象征。<BR><BR>
乌鸦落在他的肩上。当黑檀剑的剑尖似乎触及天空时，闪电闪烁，雷声轰鸣。然后，完全的寂静降临，一阵战栗席卷两支军队。<BR><BR>
双方军队的领袖走向雷蒙·黑檀臂，跪了下来。他们依次讲述发动这场战争的理由。每个人都请求黑骑士眷顾他们的事业。雷蒙·黑檀臂倾听着，但没有表示他在这场战斗中选择了偏袒哪一方。然而，每位领袖都听到了对方陈述的立场。并且，他们现在都知道这场战争是毫无根据的。他们拥抱，然后转向各自的军队。他们命令部队埋葬死者，照料伤员，然后返回家园。<BR><BR>
雷蒙·黑檀臂骑上他的金色种马战争之主，再次将黑檀剑指向天空，并将那面巨大的饰有玫瑰的黑檀盾伸向两支军队。军队中爆发出巨大的欢呼声。乌鸦再次飞向天空。闪电和雷鸣伴随着他，他骑马驶入夕阳，身后跟着那两只鸟。<BR><BR>
军队按命令行事。他们照料伤员，埋葬死者。当他们撤回各自家园时，每个战士都确信，伟大的神祇雷蒙·黑檀臂，黑骑士，已经回应了他们各自祈求干预的祈祷。每一方都赢了，没有输家。<BR><BR>
当军队离开战场时，河流开始变得清澈，一朵红玫瑰开始在一名阵亡英雄的坟墓旁绽放。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Faerie<BR>
By Szun Triop<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Faerie have been on Tamriel, in all probability, long before recorded history, perhaps since or before the days of the Elder Ones. The tales of their mischief are found in every culture, in most every village, town, and city-states in the Empire. Alternately they are called Faerie, Fey, Illyadi, Sprites, Pixies, and Sylphim, and their natures seem to flit from one story to the next with the same variation. It could almost be said that Faeries are anything unpredictable in nature.<BR><BR>
The noted scholar Ahrtabazus studying at the time in the Crystal Tower of Summerset Isle developed an interesting if controversial theory about Faerie. He organized the Fey variants on a chain, beginning with the glimmering sparks called Pixies or Whilloki by the Redguards at one end and the godlike beings such as Gheateus, Chonus, and Sygria at the other. In the middle are human and semi-human beings generating up to intelligent trees, brooks, rocks, even mountains. All of this was a new and completely original theory and would have prompted enthusiastic, if somewhat skeptical response had Ahrtabazus not added this footnote: "It may be that elves as a whole are part of this chain, above whilloki and below nephrine. They certainly have similar features and propensities for magicka as the other Faerie." (Ahrtabazus, "The Faerie Chain" Firsthold, 2E 456)<BR><BR>
No elf liked to be put in a hierarchy slightly above whimsical pranksters like the whilloki, and Ahrtabazus was challenged on his assumptions based on very slight coincidences. Nevertheless, with modification, his Fairie Chain theory has gained wider and wider acceptance since its publication.<BR><BR>
The hierarchical chain is not, in the strictest sense, an order of command. While Gheateus and Sygria are said to be surrounded by a host of minor Sylphim, faerie on the whole are not followers nor leaders. Their plans and schemes are not governed by a higher purpose, simply by their own whim.<BR><BR>
To this most faerie scholars agree. Because it is based on coincidental evidence and supported by auxiliary theories, it may very well be wrong.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
仙灵<BR>
苏恩·特里奥普 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
仙灵很可能在有记载的历史之前很久就已经存在于泰姆瑞尔了，也许自远古者时代或更早。关于它们恶作剧的传说，在帝国的每一种文化、几乎每一个村庄、城镇和城邦中都能找到。它们交替被称为仙灵、费伊、伊利亚迪、精灵、皮克希和西尔菲姆，它们的本性似乎随着故事的不同而同样多变。几乎可以说，仙灵的本质就是不可预测的。<BR><BR>
当时在夏暮岛水晶塔学习的著名学者阿赫塔巴祖斯，发展出了一个关于仙灵的有趣且有争议的理论。他将费伊的变体组织成一个链条，一端是被称为皮克希或红卫人称为威洛基的闪烁火花，另一端是像吉阿提斯、乔努斯和西格里亚这样的神性存在。中间是产生出智慧树、溪流、岩石甚至山脉的人类和半人类存在。这一切都是一个全新的、完全原创的理论，如果不是阿赫塔巴祖斯加了这条脚注，它本会引起热情（尽管有些怀疑）的反应：“可能精灵作为一个整体是这个链条的一部分，位于威洛基之上，尼弗林之下。他们当然与其他仙灵有相似的特征和魔法倾向。”（阿赫塔巴祖斯，《仙灵链》，首堡，第二纪元456年）<BR><BR>
没有一个精灵喜欢被置于仅仅略高于像威洛基这样的异想天开的恶作剧者的等级中，阿赫塔巴祖斯基于非常细微的巧合的假设受到了质疑。尽管如此，经过修改，他的仙灵链理论自发表以来已获得越来越广泛的接受。<BR><BR>
从最严格的意义上讲，等级链不是命令的序列。虽然据说吉阿提斯和西格里亚被众多低级西尔菲姆所包围，但总体而言，仙灵既不是追随者也不是领导者。他们的计划和阴谋不受更高目标的支配，仅仅受他们自己的奇思妙想支配。<BR><BR>
大多数仙灵学者都同意这一点。因为它基于巧合的证据，并由辅助理论支持，所以它很可能是错误的。<BR>"""

苏恩·特里奥普 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
仙灵很可能在有记载的历史之前很久就已经存在于泰姆瑞尔了，也许自远古者时代或更早。关于它们恶作剧的传说，在帝国的每一种文化、几乎每一个村庄、城镇和城邦中都能找到。它们交替被称为仙灵、费伊、伊利亚迪、精灵、皮克希和西尔菲姆，它们的本性似乎随着故事的不同而同样多变。几乎可以说，仙灵的本质就是不可预测的。<BR><BR>
当时在夏暮岛水晶塔学习的著名学者阿赫塔巴祖斯，发展出了一个关于仙灵的有趣且有争议的理论。他将费伊的变体组织成一个链条，一端是被称为皮克希或红卫人称为威洛基的闪烁火花，另一端是像吉阿提斯、乔努斯和西格里亚这样的神性存在。中间是产生出智慧树、溪流、岩石甚至山脉的人类和半人类存在。这一切都是一个全新的、完全原创的理论，如果不是阿赫塔巴祖斯加了这条脚注，它本会引起热情（尽管有些怀疑）的反应：“可能精灵作为一个整体是这个链条的一部分，位于威洛基之上，尼弗林之下。他们当然与其他仙灵有相似的特征和魔法倾向。”（阿赫塔巴祖斯，《仙灵链》，首堡，第二纪元456年）<BR><BR>
没有一个精灵喜欢被置于仅仅略高于像威洛基这样的异想天开的恶作剧者的等级中，阿赫塔巴祖斯基于非常细微的巧合的假设受到了质疑。尽管如此，经过修改，他的仙灵链理论自发表以来已获得越来越广泛的接受。<BR><BR>
从最严格的意义上讲，等级链不是命令的序列。虽然据说吉阿提斯和西格里亚被众多低级西尔菲姆所包围，但总体而言，仙灵既不是追随者也不是领导者。他们的计划和阴谋不受更高目标的支配，仅仅受他们自己的奇思妙想支配。<BR><BR>
大多数仙灵学者都同意这一点。因为它基于巧合的证据，并由辅助理论支持，所以它很可能是错误的。<BR>"""

The Faithful

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_TheFaithfulTR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
The Faithful<BR>
By Salves Arothran<BR>
<BR>
Fovila Llathram drank longingly from her cup, and set it on the windowsill. Gazing at the beautiful meadow outside, she felt only the merest shadow of the happiness it used to bring. Without her husband Tenivyn by her side, everything seemed a sad, pale reflection of itself. She sighed, drumming her dark fingers against the sill. Soon, she knew. Soon. Soon he would have his leave. Soon he would come back down from the horrific Red Mountain, and they would be together again. It had been such a very, very long time. Ghostgate had always been dangerous, but of late it seemed that Buoyant Armigers were having ever greater difficulty getting leave. It seemed, to her mind, that the Mountain was growing ever more reluctant to give them up.<BR>
<BR>
Fovila had had such nightmares. She dreamed that the Mountain itself was an immense evil beast, and Ghostgate was its maw. It called to the Temple feverishly, demanding Armigers and Ordinators to defend against its dark menacing shadows, to charge against it, to station themselves in its great mouth. Ghostgate existed because it could only eat so many unfortunate souls at once. Perhaps it was more like a plate than a mouth, for some would occasionally escape the blight storms long enough to visit home to spread tales of its ever increasingly warped monstrosity. She shook her head. Such dire dreams meant little, and it would be so achingly soon that her husband would return.<BR>
<BR>
A tear slipped past her cheek, and splashed into her drink. Fovila hadn't even realized she'd been staring forlornly into the cup. Time seemed so unimportant when she remembered the days when her husband held her close. Perhaps if they had had children, she wouldn't have felt so alone. But soon, she wouldn't be alone. When she saw him again, she knew those many, many lonely months would fade from her mind. If only for the few stolen moments Tenivyn's leave lasted.<BR>
<BR>
A wan smile had crept upon her face when she was jarred out of remembrance by a knock at her door. She thought her heart would leap out of her chest when she put a shaking hand around the knob and turned it. She thought she would surely faint when she saw the object of her affection filling the outline of the doorway. She thought the tightness of her hugging would shatter his light Chitin armor. None of those happened, and her heart was awash with joy. She knew Dunmer were supposed to be above such displays of emotion, but being face-to-face with Tenivyn, that was a distant concern, something for someone else far away to worry about.<BR>
<BR>
That someone else, it turned out, was not so far away. Tenivyn placed a hand on her shoulder and said heavily "Love, it is not that I do not appreciate your affection. But I have traveled far, and before that, I saw much conflict, and before that, I had to scale the faces of mountains. Though I long to hold you as you hold me, it is all I can do to hold my stance, such is my exhaustion."<BR>
<BR>
Saddened, but understanding, Fovila put one of his arms around her neck, and half carried, half dragged Tenivyn to bed. He collapsed with a word of thanks, and promptly passed out inside his armor. Heart soaring, Fovila laughed lightly and began to remove his armor. Her intentions were more practical than amorous; most armors were not kind to sheets, and besides that were not comfortable to spend the night in.<BR>
<BR>
Once done, she climbed into bed next to him. Placing a smooth hand on his rough cheek and gazing gratefully into his worn but handsome face, Fovila sighed happily. He was tired, and grimy, and sweaty, but he was home at last. She was too excited to sleep, but just feeling the warmth of his body again would be enough for tonight. There would be time enough to talk tomorrow.<BR>
<BR>
As the sun proclaimed a new day had dawned, Fovila's eyes fluttered open. How she had fallen into a slumber, she wasn't sure. Looking across at Tenivyn, she smiled again; he was still sleeping very soundly indeed. She reached over and ran a hand through his dark hair. Still in the grip of slumber, he raised his hand to meet hers. Again, Fovila thought her heart would burst with the love she felt. Then, as their hands met, Tenivyn mumbled "Aren", and a broad, lazy smile filled his face.<BR>
<BR>
Fovila was paralyzed for a moment in sheer horror. Her first reaction would have been to jerk her hand away, but in the second it took to register that the name was not her own, his hand had fallen back to the bed. She curled herself up in a ball, and stared at him in wounded incomprehension. Tears grew fat in her eyes, and rolled down her ashen cheeks. To wait so very long. . . and hear him call another's name. . . Did he not say he loved her before he dropped into unconsciousness the night before? Did those words hold any meaning for him?<BR>
<BR>
Frowning deeply, Fovila shook her head violently. No. She loved her husband. She trusted him. There must be some other explanation, surely. Nodding, she felt ashamed that she had so doubted his faithfulness. It couldn't be what it seemed like. There had to be another reason. But the name "Aren" echoed with a sort of hollow hatefulness in her head as Fovila prepared breakfast.<BR>
<BR>
As the day wore on, she thought less and less of Aren. Tenivyn's stories of the horror that lurked behind the ghostfence did much to replace her nagging suspicion with anxiety. Anxiety not just for her brave husband, but for all of Morrowind, and even for the rest of Tamriel, though such places seemed infinitely distant. For he warned that the blight was spreading where it hadn't reached before, and things were becoming even worse and more terrible in the places it had already left its tainted touch. But even though he bore dire warnings of a bleak future, Fovila was glad to hear his voice once more. She pushed the dark thoughts he'd shared with her to the back of her mind, and tried to bask in the radiance of Tenivyn's presence.<BR>
<BR>
When they had a moment alone, Fovila asked him a question that had been on her lips since the night before: "Tenivyn, my handsome, brave husband, do you still love me?"<BR>
<BR>
He seemed appropriately taken aback by it, and his response eased her troubled thoughts: "Of course I do, love. Though my duty takes me far from you, my heart always stays with yours."<BR>
<BR>
The remainder of his leave was as happy a time as she'd hoped, but ever in the back of her mind, "Aren" begged for further attention. It was a constant dull spiteful presence. Try as she might, she could not shake it; indeed, the more she ignored it, the more it seemed she COULD NOT ignore it.<BR>
<BR>
And so when the merry days of Tenivyn's all too short leave drew to a close, Fovila resolved to put the thought to rest. When Tenivyn left in the morning next, she would follow him all the way to Ghostgate if necessary. She had to know for sure. Surely, he was a faithful and noble husband, and she was just being a silly, jealous wife.<BR>
<BR>
As the sun rose, and Tenivyn departed with sorrowful words, Fovila waited for the brave Armiger to become a distant speck on the horizon before beginning her pursuit. Gripping a worn shortsword tightly, she battled back her fear of Kagouti and Alit, and other wild beasts. If there were any to be encountered, she hoped, they would be dispatched by her able husband first. It would be a long walk from her hometown to Ghostgate, but her determination would see her through.<BR>
<BR>
Days wore on, and Fovila became worried that she could not match her husband's pace. Such trouble had eluded her thus far, because though Tenivyn was of greater strength, he was also weighed down by his armor and weapons. Her fear was that she did not have the endurance for such a trip, that she could match his pace only for a short while. As her exhaustion and fear rose, she stared at the ground as she marched. What had she gotten herself into? Would her pettiness cause her death? But when her gaze dropped, she was relieved to see mounds of ash. Never had she thought to be grateful for the stuff, but in the ash she could see marks from her husband's boots. As long as there were no storms, she could relax her pace.<BR>
<BR>
As the ash on the ground grew thicker, Fovila knew Ghostgate was drawing ever closer. Tenivyn had stopped at a number of towns, but she had seen nothing suspicious; he had only purchased a bed for the night, to continue refreshed in the morning. Other Armigers thought him daft for making much of the journey on foot, she knew. One day, he had explained to her that seeing more of the land he fought so hard to protect made him that much more determined to contain the evil that spread from the Mountain.<BR>
<BR>
Walking, she thought of who Aren could be. With no towns left between Fovila and Ghostgate, it was doubtful the woman was a simple commoner. She might be a pilgrim, who had happened through the fence to make the journey to the Shrine of Pride. Or maybe she was an Armiger herself, though Fovila had never heard of a female Armiger. Perhaps she worked for the Temple in a less militaristic role, as a priestess. . . As the possibilities tumbled through her head, Fovila came to a troubling conclusion: Whoever Aren was, she was likely stronger than herself, so a confrontation would be unwise.<BR>
<BR>
Drawing her cloak tightly against herself to keep from being recognized, she finally entered Ghostgate a few minutes behind her husband. She cast about looking for him, pretending to be a pilgrim. When she caught sight of him again, he was renting another room. Odd, thought Fovila; from what she remembered of the place, Armigers and Ordinators had their own beds. But then a woman followed Tenivyn into the room, and the door closed behind them. Fovila was too shocked to be furious, but only for a second. "He does have a bed in the barracks" she whispered bitterly, "He just wanted something more private for sera Aren."<BR>
<BR>
Angered beyond words, Fovila knew she could do nothing to punish either yet. Time would be needed to think of something appropriate, something that would fill them with shame, fill them with a hurt equal to the hurt Fovila now felt.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
Upon returning home again, she sat and stewed in miserable spitefulness. She loved Tenivyn still, but his betrayal could not be ignored. Instead of tending the house, she plotted of ways to inflict deep, dire agonies on her cheating husband. Imagining and discarding scenario after scenario was a comfort all its own, if only a small one.<BR>
<BR>
As the days passed, Fovila needed to leave the house in order to purchase foodstuffs. While listening to the idle chatter of her fellow townsfolk (which now seemed ridiculously petty and meaningless), she heard a rumor that a necromancer had established himself in a cave to the west of town. One last plot drew itself in Fovila's mind, and a nasty smile came across her lips.<BR>
<BR>
Later that week, Fovila ventured west with the old worn shortsword once again in hand. She felt some small surprise that she didn't need the blade; it almost seemed the wild beasts were purposefully avoiding her. Perhaps they sensed her dark ire and thought better of attacking. Nonetheless, a necromancer and his servants would surely be a different matter.<BR>
<BR>
After searching a large area, Fovila satisfied herself that she had found the entrance of the proper cave. Placing a hand on its rough wooden door, she laughed cruelly. In there, she thought, lies my teacher, though he doesn't know it yet. Fovila clambered up the small hill the door was built into, and waited; she did not want to deal with the necromancer's servants, and surely even a master of profane magicks needed to eat sometime.<BR>
<BR>
Hours went by. Hours became a day. Nibbling at the rat meat she'd bought earlier, she waited. A day became two. Two, three. Her eyelids were heavy when she heard the slow creaking of the cavern door opening. Immediately, she was fully awake, no hint of drowsiness.<BR>
<BR>
"You there," the necromancer froze, as if expecting to be attacked, "Necromancer. You are going to teach me something." Reaching into her pocket, she threw a handful of gold down on the fellow. He flinched at the jingling, not knowing what to make of it. When the surprise wore off, he responded with rather more confidence.<BR>
<BR>
"Why would I help you? You are alone. It would be a simple matter for me to kill you, and take your gold, if that is all you offer."<BR>
<BR>
Fovila had expected as much, and so had thought of another approach. "The Temple persecutes you for your craft. I would use your knowledge to punish one who serves them, a Buoyant Armiger." The dark robed necromancer took a moment to mull it over.<BR>
<BR>
"This is a strange thing you want" he rubbed his chin, "But it is interesting. Come here again in a fortnight. You will find an amulet under this rock --" he pointed "Wear it before you enter, and my servants will leave you be. Bring 500 drakes with you, and I will consider your request." After a word of farewell, he stalked away.<BR>
<BR>
As the days passed, and the sun rose and fell and rose again, Fovila waited with barely restrained anticipation. Either the necromancer would teach her what she needed to complete her plan, or he would slay her. Should things go poorly and result in her demise, she reckoned that in itself a punishment fit for Tenivyn assuming he loved her as he said he did.<BR>
<BR>
When the appointed day came, Fovila again found the cave, and donned the amulet as she'd been instructed. The door to the cave creaked lightly as she entered, and as she closed it behind herself. Looking about, she saw that the cave was lit by candles sitting atop skulls in various stages of decay. Were her anger or determination not as deep, it might have intimidated her. As she rounded a corner and almost tripped over an animated skeleton, she only felt the barest echo of the fright that would have leapt through her just weeks before. The skeleton gave her a cursory glance with its eyeless head, then proceeded to ignore her completely. It seemed the necromancer had been honest about the amulet.<BR>
<BR>
After exploring at length, she entered a large room in which the necromancer waited. He was sitting at a desk, reading a book by candlelight. Gesturing toward a chair that sat opposite his desk, he read on for a few moments, then closed the book. Placing a hand on the book, he turned it so its spine faced away from her, as if she had an interest in his reading material.<BR>
<BR>
"So," he drew himself up from the chair and began pacing around the room, "You have more courage than I would have guessed. I trust my guards were not too rude?"<BR>
<BR>
"Not at all." Fovila answered.<BR>
<BR>
"Indeed. They are much more well mannered than the guards the House people employ. Those disagreeable fellows are always trying to kill me. It's impolite. Our Imperial benefactors have a much more enlightened attitude about my work. But you didn't come for a discourse on civilized behaviour. At any rate, I would like to apologize for my rude comments on the day we met. In my line of work, you understand, one can unfortunately become quite hostile to strange people, as most of them come bearing weapons." Fovila suspected the promise of 500 drakes had more to do with the necromancer's change in attitude, but she wasn't going to press the matter. "So, before I bore you further with my rambling, let me touch on the subject that you were actually interested in. Now: What was the subject you were interested in?" The odd repetitious turn of phrase caught Fovila off-guard.<BR>
<BR>
"I -- I want you to teach me a spell. It's not the. . . the sort of thing I could ask just anyone. People would ask questions, if I could even find someone to teach it at all."<BR>
<BR>
The necromancer smiled indulgently, "I know a lot of spells my superstitious kinfolk find objectionable. If you could be more specific. . . ?"<BR>
<BR>
"I need to know how to make one more susceptible to Corprus."<BR>
<BR>
Laughing, the necromancer exclaimed, "My, you aren't a person to upset! Though I see how that would certainly be of use against an Armiger, assuming you could cast it without drawing notice. I might have tried something like that myself, but alas, I'm afraid the guards would recognize me. . ." Fovila said nothing. "Erm. Those 500 drakes will be sufficient payment. Now, let us discuss the nature of the spell. . ."<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
The following morning, Fovila set out once more for Ghostgate. Since she was not watching her husband's every move, this time the trip would be much shorter; now she would be able to use silt striders, and guild guides, and boats where necessary. And she could also pack lighter, because her journey would be one-way this time. Nothing in her backpack would weigh as heavily upon her as did her heart. But she knew what she had to do, what she had planned to do, what she had trained to do.<BR>
<BR>
Travel was a blur to Fovila, so deep was she within her thoughts of vengeance. Neither the odd tree (still something uncommon in Morrowind) nor the repellent swamps could draw her attention. Beautiful meadows - not unlike the one she used to gaze out at lovingly at home - passed by without a glance. None of it mattered anymore, with Tenivyn's betrayal. Only one thing mattered now.<BR>
<BR>
She arrived in Ald'ruhn without a drake left in her pockets, but had no concern. For her, money had no more use. Stepping down off the silt strider, she looked to the east where the Tribunal Temple was built. A cruel crooked smile lived and died quickly on her face. Sure enough, a group of pilgrims were gathered there, preparing to make the hazardous journey to the Shrine of Pride just beyond the walls of the ghostfence. Pilgrims would travel in groups like this so that, even if an Ash Ghoul or some other twisted minion of Dagoth Ur waited, surely some would survive to make the pilgrimage and escape with their lives. Fovila removed a white cloak from her backpack and donned it, shaking her head. They might want to flee Red Mountain with their lives, but Fovila had no such intentions.<BR>
<BR>
When finally the group made its way out of Ald'ruhn, Fovila struggled to keep their slow, shuffling pace. She wanted to break into a sprint, the sooner to see Tenivyn's pain. But she held her dark desires in check. Still, she cursed every Kagouti and Alit and Cliff Racer that held up the pilgrims until the beasts were slaughtered.<BR>
<BR>
Ghostgate loomed somberly before them shortly, and there was a hush among the group. For most of them, this was a first. Then the portcullis was raised, and Fovila knew nothing stood in the way of her plan anymore. As the last of the pilgrims cautiously ventured into the wrong side of the ghostfence, Fovila let out a triumphant laugh so harsh that most of them flinched.<BR>
<BR>
"Tell the Armigers, none shall make the pilgrimage until I am dead!" Fovila called out behind her as she ran up the slopes of the foreboding Red Mountain. She did not look behind her to see what the pilgrims would do. She knew already. They would fetch Armigers and Ordinators, and follow them to the Shrine; the pathetic, soft Dunmer would use the excuse to get an armed escort to the Shrine. But the soldiers would find nothing. Not for weeks.<BR>
<BR>
"Weak." she spat at her race, running ever deeper into hostile territory. Her eyes surveyed the area quickly. She would need to find what she sought shortly, or be killed by any number of beasts.<BR>
<BR>
There. Just behind a rock, she could easily make it out. Casting the Weakness to Corprus Disease spell taught to her on herself, she dashed to it, and leapt upon the Lame Corprus. She clawed wildly at it, bit into its corrupted flesh, and let its tainted blood trickle down her throat. The man-shaped thing threw her off amid howls of pain, but she kept attacking. It opened up cuts on her soft ashen skin, but still she would not relent. Its blood mingled with hers as she lopped its head off with her shortsword.<BR>
<BR>
She would not let herself feel the agony that wracked her injured body. There was no time for that. Maybe she was infected already, but she did not know. Taking the shortsword, she split the dead monster open, her nose wrinkling at its foulness. That done, she threw the sword to the ground, and crawled inside the thing, casting the spell once again for good measure.<BR>
<BR>
Tenivyn looked perplexedly at the pilgrims. "But she did not run off in the direction of the Shrine?" As they shook their heads almost as one, he frowned. "Either she must be mad herself, or driven mad by the callings from the mountain, or she must be a necromancer, and went wandering off to secure followers. I can think of no other reason." He scratched absently at his stubble. "Nevertheless, we could let none of those situations go without some sort of investigation."<BR>
<BR>
And so Tenivyn gathered four other Armigers, and they walked haltingly to the Shrine of Pride with the pilgrims. Nothing was found of the madwoman, and not even so much as a blighted rat lurked on the path to the Shrine. Had she gone this way, she would have been unimpeded, but Tenivyn supposed that such things made little difference to the mad. After a cursory search, all retreated back to Ghostgate.<BR>
<BR>
As the weeks went by, Tenivyn wondered what had happened to the woman. Had she been transformed into one of those terrible ash creatures? Was she practicing obscene magicks in some obscure cave? Or was she beset by mindless beasts, and now lay dying on the nightmarish mountain? Though he had ventured out on a few raids since, he had seen nothing resembling the Dunmer woman described to him. True, they had slain a handful of women of the group that called themselves "sleepers", but none bore the telltale white cloak.<BR>
<BR>
Then it started happening, just as the mysterious woman had warned. At first, one or two pilgrims passed through the portcullis and simply never came back out. After that, a group of pilgrims went in, and three returned. Staring out of haunted eyes, they told of a horrific corprus-infected thing rending their fellows limb from limb. Its disgusting sores were covered by a frightfully stained cloth, which some asserted still had patches of white here and there.<BR>
<BR>
Tenivyn knew what he had to do, though the why of the woman's actions eluded him. Once more, he gathered a party of his fellow Armigers, and set out for the Shrine. The scene that welcomed them nearly caused his stomach to turn: The surviving pilgrims had not been exaggerating when they said their fellows had been rent limb from limb. Amid the carnage stood a lone figure resembling a female Corprus Stalker. She was still holding an arm she had torn off one of the unfortunates. The cloak she wore was awash in blood and ash and things less pleasant besides, but it did indeed have flecks of white hidden among the gore.<BR>
<BR>
The Armigers circled the beast, and drew their weapons. Behind the hood of the cloak, Tenivyn could see something stir in her sick, malevolent eyes.<BR>
<BR>
"Tenivyyyyn." she called from her raw throat. "Tenivyyyyn."<BR>
<BR>
His fellow Armigers paused, taken aback. Tenivyn recognized the voice, even as broken and ruined as it was. Tears streaking his face, he motioned the others to sheathe their weapons. He did not sheathe his own as he strode up to what he knew had been his wife Fovila.<BR>
<BR>
"Oh my love, what has happened to you!" he cried.<BR>
<BR>
"Uh. . . ren. Steal. . . you." she shuffled toward him. He looked at her in incomprehension, but she didn't seem to notice. "Love. . . me?" she asked, her corrupted flesh oozing and drooping as she spoke.<BR>
<BR>
"Of course I love you!" Tenivyn thought for a moment that he could subdue Fovila, and take her to the wizard at Tel Fyr, that he would cure her, and everything would be all right. But he knew that to be fantasy. Fovila might as well be dead already, and if she were dead. . .<BR>
<BR>
"Make you. . . kill me. Feel hurt. . . like me." she said, shuffling ever closer.<BR>
<BR>
"Oh, Fovila!" Tenivyn threw his arms around his wife, "Whatever my crime, I am sorry! I will love you forever!" He kissed her corprus-marred face. And still holding her, he plunged his blade through her back, through her heart, and into his own. Together, they collapsed and died.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
[Editor's note: While researching this legend, I have come across something interesting. It seems that Tenivyn did not actually ever sleep with someone other than his wife. While raiding strongholds on Red Mountain, the healer in the raiding party was slain, and Tenivyn became infected with some mind-altering blight disease. It took the group some weeks to retreat back to Ghostgate, and by that time his infection had become difficult to cure. Aren was the temple priestess who treated him through his fever dreams and violent episodes. Supposedly, when Tenivyn called her name in his sleep, it was merely an echo of her calming influence on his nightmarish slumber.<BR>
<BR>
As for his renting a room upon his arrival in Ghostgate, the woman with him at the time was indeed Aren. It seems that Tenivyn had twisted his ankle at some point during his journey back to Ghostgate, and requested that she heal it; the payment was for the healing, not the room. This explanation makes it easier to believe Fovila had so little trouble following him most of the way on foot (they both still used ship to get to Vvardenfell, of course).] <BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
信徒<BR>
萨尔维斯·阿罗斯兰 著<BR>
<BR>
福维拉·拉斯拉姆渴望地从杯中啜饮，然后把杯子放在窗台上。凝视着外面美丽的草地，她只感到它曾经带来的幸福最微弱的影子。没有丈夫泰尼文在身边，一切都显得悲伤、苍白的自反。她叹了口气，用深色的手指敲击着窗台。很快了，她知道。很快。很快他就能休假了。很快他就会从那可怕的红山下来，他们就会再次团聚。这已经过去了非常非常长的时间。幽魂之门一直很危险，但最近，似乎灵动扈从休假越来越困难。在她看来，似乎那座山越来越不愿意把他们交出来了。<BR>
<BR>
福维拉做过这样的噩梦。她梦见那座山本身是一个巨大的邪恶野兽，而幽魂之门就是它的嘴。它狂热地向神殿呼唤，要求卫兵和神殿卫兵抵御它黑暗威胁的阴影，向它冲锋，驻扎在它巨大的口中。幽魂之门存在，是因为它一次只能吞噬那么多不幸的灵魂。也许它更像一个盘子而不是一张嘴，因为有些人偶尔会逃脱枯萎病风暴，足以回家传播关于它日益扭曲的怪物的故事。她摇了摇头。这样可怕的梦意义不大，而且她的丈夫很快就会回来了，真是令人心痛。<BR>
<BR>
一滴泪滑过她的脸颊，溅入她的饮料中。福维拉甚至没有意识到自己一直在悲伤地盯着杯子。当她回忆起丈夫紧紧拥抱她的日子时，时间似乎变得如此不重要。也许如果他们有了孩子，她就不会感到如此孤独了。但很快，她就不会孤独了。当她再次见到他时，她知道那许多许多孤独的月份将从她的脑海中消失。哪怕只是为了泰尼文休假持续的几个偷来的片刻。<BR>
<BR>
一丝苍白的微笑爬上了她的脸庞，这时她被敲门声从回忆中惊醒。她用颤抖的手握住门把手转动时，以为自己的心会跳出胸膛。当她看到心爱的人填满门框的轮廓时，她以为自己一定会晕倒。她以为拥抱的紧度会震碎他那轻便的甲壳盔甲。但这些都没有发生，她的心中充满了喜悦。她知道丹莫本应超脱于这种情感的表露，但与泰尼文面对面时，那是一个遥远的顾虑，是远方的别人该操心的事。<BR>
<BR>
结果，那个“别人”并不那么遥远。泰尼文将一只手放在她的肩上，沉重地说：“亲爱的，不是我不感激你的爱意。但我走了很远的路，在那之前，我目睹了许多冲突，在那之前，我还不得不攀登山峰。虽然我渴望像你拥抱我一样拥抱你，但我能做的只是保持站立，我太疲惫了。”<BR>
<BR>
福维拉虽然悲伤，但表示理解，她将泰尼文的一只手臂搭在自己脖子上，半拖半拉地把他弄到床上。他说了声谢谢就瘫倒了，随即穿着盔甲昏睡过去。福维拉心潮澎湃，轻轻笑了起来，开始脱他的盔甲。她的意图更实用而非浪漫；大多数盔甲对床单不友好，而且穿着过夜也不舒服。<BR>
<BR>
完成后，她爬上床，躺在他身边。她将光滑的手放在他粗糙的脸颊上，感激地凝视着他疲惫但英俊的脸庞，福维拉幸福地叹了口气。他很累，很脏，还流着汗，但他终于回家了。她兴奋得睡不着，但只要再次感受他身体的温暖，今晚就足够了。明天有足够的时间交谈。<BR>
<BR>
当太阳宣告新的一天已经破晓时，福维拉的眼睛眨了眨睁开了。她不确定自己是怎么睡着的。她看着对面的泰尼文，又笑了；他确实还在熟睡。她伸手穿过他的黑发。仍在睡梦中的他抬起手来迎向她。福维拉再次感到自己的心会因感受到的爱而爆裂。然后，当他们的手碰在一起时，泰尼文喃喃地说：“阿伦”，脸上露出了一个宽大、慵懒的笑容。<BR>
<BR>
福维拉瞬间因纯粹的恐惧而僵住了。她的第一反应是抽回手，但就在她意识到那个名字不是自己的那一秒，他的手已经落回了床上。她蜷缩成一团，用受伤的不解凝视着他。泪水在她眼中汇聚变大，顺着她灰白的脸颊滚落。等了这么久......却听到他叫别人的名字......他昨晚陷入昏迷前不是说过爱她吗？那些话对他有任何意义吗？<BR>
<BR>
福维拉深深地皱起眉头，猛烈地摇了摇头。不。她爱她的丈夫。她信任他。肯定有其他解释。她点点头，为自己如此怀疑他的忠诚而感到羞愧。不可能像表面看起来那样。一定有其他原因。但当福维拉准备早餐时，“阿伦”这个名字在她脑海中回荡着一种空洞的恶意。<BR>
<BR>
一天过去了，她越来越不想阿伦的事。泰尼文讲述的关于幽魂之墙背后潜伏的恐怖故事，很大程度上将她挥之不去的怀疑转变为焦虑。不仅为她勇敢的丈夫焦虑，也为整个晨风，甚至为泰姆瑞尔的其他地方焦虑，尽管那些地方似乎无限遥远。因为他警告说，枯萎病正在蔓延到以前未曾到达的地方，而在它已经留下污染痕迹的地方，情况正变得比以往更糟、更可怕。但尽管他带来了对未来暗淡的可怕警告，福维拉还是很高兴再次听到他的声音。她把他告诉她的黑暗想法推到脑海深处，并试图沉浸在泰尼文存在的光辉中。<BR>
<BR>
当他们有片刻独处时，福维拉问了他一个自前一晚就一直挂在嘴边的问题：“泰尼文，我英俊、勇敢的丈夫，你还爱我吗？”<BR>
<BR>
他似乎对此感到适当的惊讶，他的回答缓解了她困扰的想法：“我当然爱你，亲爱的。虽然我的职责使我远离你，但我的心永远与你同在。”<BR>
<BR>
他剩下的假期如她所愿是一段快乐的时光，但在她的脑海深处，“阿伦”总是需要进一步的关注。那是一个持续、迟钝、恶意的存在。尽管她努力尝试，却无法摆脱它；事实上，她越是忽视它，似乎就越无法忽视它。<BR>
<BR>
因此，当泰尼文太短暂的快乐假期接近尾声时，福维拉决定让这个想法平息。明天早上泰尼文离开时，如果有必要，她会一路跟踪他到幽魂之门。她必须确定。他肯定是一个忠诚而高贵的丈夫，而她只是一个愚蠢、嫉妒的妻子。<BR>
<BR>
太阳升起，泰尼文带着悲伤的话语离开，福维拉等着那勇敢的卫兵变成地平线上的一个遥远小点，然后才开始她的追踪。她紧紧握着一把破旧的短剑，努力克制着对盾角蜥、鳄蜥以及其他野兽的恐惧。她希望，如果要遇到任何野兽，它们会先被她那能干的丈夫解决掉。从她的家乡到幽魂之门将是漫长的步行，但她的决心将支撑她走完。<BR>
<BR>
日子一天天过去，福维拉开始担心自己跟不上丈夫的步伐。到目前为止，这种麻烦还没有出现，因为虽然泰尼文力气更大，但他也因盔甲和武器而负重。她担心自己没有耐力进行这样的旅行，她只能短时间内跟上他的步伐。随着疲惫和恐惧的增加，她边走边盯着地面。她把自己卷入了什么？她的小气会导致她的死亡吗？但当她的目光下移时，她欣慰地看到成堆的灰烬。她从未想过会感激这玩意儿，但在灰烬中，她能看到丈夫靴子的印记。只要没有风暴，她就可以放慢脚步。<BR>
<BR>
随着地面上的灰烬越来越厚，福维拉知道幽魂之门越来越近了。泰尼文在许多城镇停过，但她没有看到任何可疑之处；他只是买张床过夜，以便第二天早上精神焕发地继续前进。她知道，其他卫兵认为他大部分路程都步行是愚蠢的。有一天，他曾向她解释说，更多地了解他奋力保护的土地，会让他更加坚定地遏制从山上蔓延的邪恶。<BR>
<BR>
走着走着，她想着阿伦可能是谁。福维拉和幽魂之门之间没有城镇了，那个女人不太可能只是个普通平民。她可能是个朝圣者，碰巧穿过屏障前往骄傲圣祠。或者她本人就是个卫兵，尽管福维拉从未听说过女性卫兵。也许她以不那么军事化的角色为神殿工作，比如女祭司......随着各种可能性在她脑海中翻腾，福维拉得出了一个令人不安的结论：无论阿伦是谁，她都可能比自己强壮，所以对抗是不明智的。<BR>
<BR>
她将斗篷紧紧地裹在身上以防被认出来，最终在丈夫身后几分钟进入了幽魂之门。她假装是朝圣者，四处张望寻找他。当她再次看到他时，他正在租另一个房间。奇怪，福维拉想；根据她对这地方的记忆，卫兵和神殿卫兵有自己的床。但随后一个女人跟着泰尼文进了房间，门在他们身后关上了。福维拉震惊得来不及愤怒，但仅仅持续了一秒钟。“他在营房里确实有床，”她痛苦地低声说，“他只是想为阿伦女士找个更私密的地方。”<BR>
<BR>
福维拉愤怒得说不出话来，她知道现在还不能惩罚他们中的任何一个。需要时间来想出一些恰当的东西，一些能让他们充满羞耻、充满与福维拉现在感受到的同等伤害的东西。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
再次回到家后，她坐着，在痛苦的恶意中煎熬。她仍然爱泰尼文，但他的背叛不能忽视。她没有打理家务，而是策划着如何给她出轨的丈夫施加深沉、可怕的痛苦。想象然后抛弃一个又一个场景本身就是一种安慰，尽管只是小小的安慰。<BR>
<BR>
日子一天天过去，福维拉需要离开家去买食物。在听着同镇居民（现在显得荒谬地琐碎和毫无意义）闲聊时，她听到一个谣言，说一个死灵法师在镇西的一个洞穴里建立了据点。最后一个计划在福维拉脑海中形成，她嘴角露出一丝恶毒的微笑。<BR>
<BR>
那周晚些时候，福维拉再次手持那把破旧的短剑冒险向西。她感到有些惊讶，竟然不需要用剑；野兽们似乎有意在避开她。也许它们感觉到了她黑暗的愤怒，认为最好不要攻击。尽管如此，一个死灵法师和他的仆从肯定是另一回事。<BR>
<BR>
在搜索了一大片区域后，福维拉确信自己找到了正确洞穴的入口。她把手放在粗糙的木门上，残忍地笑了。她想，里面躺着我的老师，虽然他还没有意识到。福维拉爬上建着那扇门的小山，等待着；她不想对付死灵法师的仆从，而且即使是亵渎魔法的大师，肯定也需要吃饭。<BR>
<BR>
几个小时过去了。几个小时变成了一天。她啃着之前买的老鼠肉，等待着。一天变成了两天。两天，三天。她的眼皮很重，这时她听到了洞穴门缓慢吱呀打开的声音。她立刻完全清醒了，没有一丝困意。<BR>
<BR>
“你，”死灵法师僵住了，好像预料到会遭到攻击，“死灵法师。你得教我点东西。”她把手伸进口袋，把一把金币扔到那家伙身上。他听到叮当声畏缩了一下，不知道是怎么回事。当惊讶消退后，他带着几分自信回应道。<BR>
<BR>
“我为什么要帮你？你一个人。如果这就是你提供的全部，对我来说杀死你，拿走你的金币是件简单的事。”<BR>
<BR>
福维拉预料到了这一点，所以想到了另一种方法。“神殿因你的技艺而迫害你。我想用你的知识来惩罚一个为他们服务的人，一个灵动扈从。”身穿黑袍的死灵法师花了一点时间仔细考虑。<BR>
<BR>
“你想要的东西很奇怪，”他揉了揉下巴，“但很有趣。两周后再来这里。你会在这块石头下找到一个护符 -- ”他指着说，“进去前戴上它，我的仆从就不会打扰你。带上500龙币，我会考虑你的请求。”道别后，他大步走开了。<BR>
<BR>
日子一天天过去，太阳升起又落下，又再次升起，福维拉几乎无法抑制期待地等待着。要么死灵法师会教她完成计划所需的东西，要么他会杀了她。如果事情进展不顺，导致她死亡，她认为这本身就是对泰尼文的惩罚，前提是他像他说的那样爱她。<BR>
<BR>
当约定的日子到来时，福维拉再次找到了那个洞穴，并按照指示戴上了护符。她进入洞穴时，门轻轻吱呀作响，她在身后关上了门。环顾四周，她看到洞穴由放置在处于不同腐烂阶段的头骨上的蜡烛照明。如果她的愤怒或决心不那么深，这可能会吓到她。当她转过一个弯，差点被一个活动的骷髅绊倒时，她只感受到了几周前会让她惊吓的恐惧最微弱的回声。那骷髅用没有眼睛的头粗略地瞥了她一眼，然后完全无视了她。看来死灵法师关于护符的话是诚实的。<BR>
<BR>
经过长时间的探索，她进入了一个大房间，死灵法师正在里面等着。他坐在一张书桌前，借着烛光读一本书。他朝书桌对面的椅子示意了一下，又读了一会儿，然后合上了书。他将一只手放在书上，把书转过来，让书脊背对着她，好像她对他的阅读材料感兴趣似的。<BR>
<BR>
“那么，”他从椅子上站起来，开始在房间里踱步，“你的勇气比我想象的要大。我相信我的守卫没有太无礼吧？”<BR>
<BR>
“完全没有。”福维拉回答。<BR>
<BR>
“确实。他们比家族雇用的那些守卫有礼貌得多。那些讨厌的家伙总是想杀我。这不礼貌。我们帝国的恩人对我的工作持更开明的态度。但你来不是为了讨论文明行为。无论如何，我想为我们见面那天我粗鲁的评论道歉。在我的工作中，你知道，不幸的是，一个人很容易对陌生人产生敌意，因为他们中的大多数人带着武器来。”福维拉怀疑那500龙币的承诺与死灵法师态度改变的关系更大，但她不打算追究这件事。“那么，在我继续用我的唠叨让你厌烦之前，让我谈谈你真正感兴趣的话题。现在：你感兴趣的话题是什么？”这句奇怪的重复措辞让福维拉措手不及。<BR>
<BR>
“我 -- 我想让你教我一种法术。这不是......那种我可以随便问别人的事。如果我能找到人教的话，人们会问东问西。”<BR>
<BR>
死灵法师宽容地笑了，“我知道很多我那迷信的同胞们认为可憎的法术。你能说得更具体些吗......？”<BR>
<BR>
“我需要知道如何让一个人更容易感染尸化病。”<BR>
<BR>
死灵法师大笑起来，惊呼道：“天哪，你不是个好惹的人！虽然我明白这肯定对对付卫兵有用，假设你能在不引人注意的情况下施法。我自己可能也尝试过类似的事情，但唉，恐怕守卫会认出我来......”福维拉什么也没说。“呃。那500龙币就足够支付了。现在，让我们讨论一下这个法术的性质......”<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
第二天早上，福维拉再次出发前往幽魂之门。由于她不用监视丈夫的一举一动，这次行程会短得多；现在她可以使用阔步沙蚤、公会向导，以及必要时使用船只。她也可以轻装打包，因为这次她的旅程将是一趟单程旅行。背包里的东西没有一样会像她的心那样沉重。但她知道自己必须做什么，她计划做什么，她训练自己去做什么。<BR>
<BR>
旅行对福维拉来说是一片模糊，她沉浸在复仇的思绪中如此之深。无论是奇特的树（在晨风仍然不常见）还是令人厌恶的沼泽，都无法引起她的注意。美丽的草地 -- 与她过去在家时深情凝视的那片草地并无不同 -- 在她眼前掠过，她一眼也没看。在泰尼文的背叛下，这一切都不再重要了。现在只有一件事重要。<BR>
<BR>
她到达奥德-汝因时口袋里没剩下一枚龙币，但她并不担心。对她来说，钱已经没有用了。她走下阔步沙蚤，向东望去，那里是审判席神殿的所在。一个残酷、扭曲的笑容在她脸上迅速闪过。果然，一群朝圣者聚集在那里，准备踏上危险的旅程，前往幽魂之墙外的骄傲圣祠。朝圣者们会这样结伴旅行，这样，即使有灰烬食尸鬼或达格斯·乌尔的其他扭曲仆从在等待，肯定也会有人幸存下来完成朝圣并逃脱。福维拉从背包里拿出一件白色斗篷披上，摇了摇头。他们也许想带着性命逃离红山，但福维拉没有这样的打算。<BR>
<BR>
当队伍终于走出奥德-汝因时，福维拉努力跟上他们缓慢、拖着走的步伐。她想冲刺，以便尽早看到泰尼文的痛苦。但她克制住了自己黑暗的欲望。尽管如此，她还是咒骂着每一个阻碍朝圣者的盾角蜥、鳄蜥和峭壁鸟，直到那些野兽被宰杀。<BR>
<BR>
不久，幽魂之门阴沉地出现在他们面前，人群中一片寂静。对他们大多数人来说，这是第一次。然后吊闸升起，福维拉知道再也没有什么能阻挡她的计划了。当最后一批朝圣者小心翼翼地进入幽魂之墙的错误一侧时，福维拉发出了一声刺耳的胜利大笑，大多数人都不禁退缩了。<BR>
<BR>
“告诉那些卫兵，除非我死了，否则谁也别想朝圣！”福维拉一边喊着，一边跑上不祥的红山的山坡。她没有回头看那些朝圣者会怎么做。她已经知道了。他们会叫来卫兵和神殿卫兵，跟着他们去圣祠；那些可怜、软弱的丹莫会用这个借口获得武装护卫前往圣祠。但士兵们什么也不会找到。几周内都不会。<BR>
<BR>
“软弱。”她对自己的种族吐了口唾沫，跑进敌对领土的更深处。她迅速扫视了一下周围。她需要很快找到她所寻求的东西，否则会被众多野兽杀死。<BR>
<BR>
那里。就在一块岩石后面，她可以轻易地辨认出来。她对自己施展了教给她的“尸化病弱点”法术，然后冲向它，扑向那只瘸腿尸化兽。她疯狂地抓挠它，咬进它腐败的肉里，让它的污血顺着她的喉咙流下。那人类形状的东西在痛苦的嚎叫中把她甩了出去，但她继续攻击。它在她柔软灰白的皮肤上划开了一道道口子，但她仍不罢休。当她用短剑砍下它的头时，它的血和她的血混在了一起。<BR>
<BR>
她不允许自己感受折磨着她受伤身体的痛苦。没有时间了。也许她已经被感染了，但她不知道。她拿起短剑，将死去的怪物劈开，鼻子因它的恶臭而皱起。完成后，她把剑扔到地上，爬进那东西里面，为了保险起见，再次施展了那个法术。<BR>
<BR>
泰尼文困惑地看着朝圣者们。“但她没有朝圣祠的方向跑？”当他们几乎一致地摇头时，他皱起了眉头。“要么她自己疯了，要么被来自山上的呼唤逼疯了，要么她一定是个死灵法师，跑去招募追随者了。我想不出其他原因。”他心不在焉地挠了挠胡子茬。“尽管如此，我们不能不对这些情况中的任何一种进行调查。”<BR>
<BR>
于是，泰尼文召集了另外四名卫兵，他们和朝圣者们一起缓慢地走向骄傲圣祠。没有找到那个疯女人的踪迹，通往圣祠的路上甚至连一只枯萎的老鼠都没有。如果她走了这条路，她本应畅通无阻，但泰尼文认为，这对疯子来说没什么区别。简单搜索之后，所有人都退回了幽魂之门。<BR>
<BR>
几周过去了，泰尼文想知道那个女人发生了什么。她是不是变成了那些可怕的灰烬生物之一？她是不是在某个隐蔽的洞穴里练习淫秽的魔法？还是她被无脑的野兽围攻，现在正躺在那噩梦般的山上奄奄一息？尽管此后他冒险出去进行了几次突袭，但他没有看到任何类似于描述给他的那个丹莫女人的东西。确实，他们杀了一些自称“沉睡者”的群体中的女人，但没有一个穿着那标志性的白色斗篷。<BR>
<BR>
然后，正如那个神秘女人警告的那样，事情开始发生了。起初，有一两个朝圣者穿过吊闸，就再也没有出来。之后，一批朝圣者进去了，只有三个人回来了。他们用惊恐的眼神盯着，讲述了一个可怕的感染尸化病的东西把他们的同伴撕成碎片。它那令人作呕的疮口被一块可怕的、沾满污渍的布盖着，一些人断言那块布上仍有一块块白色。<BR>
<BR>
泰尼文知道他必须做什么，尽管女人行为的原因让他困惑。他再次召集了一队他的卫兵同伴，出发前往圣祠。迎接他们的景象几乎让他翻胃：幸存的朝圣者没有夸大其词，他们的同伴确实被肢解了。在残杀中站着一个孤独的身影，像一个雌性尸化病追猎者。她仍然拿着她从某个不幸者身上撕下来的一只手臂。她穿的斗篷浸透了鲜血、灰烬以及其他更令人不快的东西，但它的确在血肉中隐藏着白色的斑点。<BR>
<BR>
卫兵们围住了那野兽，拔出了武器。在斗篷的兜帽后面，泰尼文能看到她那病态、恶毒的眼睛里有什么东西在翻动。<BR>
<BR>
“泰尼文 -- ”她用嘶哑的喉咙喊道。“泰尼文 -- ”<BR>
<BR>
他的卫兵同伴们停了下来，吃了一惊。泰尼文认出了那个声音，尽管它已经破碎不堪。泪水顺着他的脸颊流下，他示意其他人收起武器。他走向他深知曾是妻子福维拉的东西时，并没有收起自己的武器。<BR>
<BR>
“哦，我的爱人，你怎么了！”他哭喊道。<BR>
<BR>
“呃......伦。偷......你。”她拖着脚走向他。他不解地看着她，但她似乎没有注意到。“爱......我吗？”她问道，她腐坏的肉随着说话而渗出和下垂。<BR>
<BR>
“我当然爱你！”泰尼文曾以为他能制服福维拉，把她带到泰尔·菲尔的法师那里，他会治愈她，一切都会好起来。但他知道那是幻想。福维拉不如已经死了，如果她死了......<BR>
<BR>
“让你......杀了我。感受痛苦......像我一样。”她说，拖着脚走得更近了。<BR>
<BR>
“哦，福维拉！”泰尼文伸出双臂抱住他的妻子，“无论我犯了什么罪，我都对不起！我会永远爱你！”他亲吻了她被尸化病毁坏的脸。然后，他仍然抱着她，将刀刃刺穿她的后背，穿过她的心脏，刺入他自己的胸膛。他们一起倒下，死了。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
[编者注：在研究这个传说时，我偶然发现了一些有趣的事情。泰尼文实际上从未与他妻子以外的任何人发生过关系。当他在红山突袭据点时，突袭队中的治疗师被杀，泰尼文感染了一种改变心智的枯萎病。队伍花了几周时间才撤退回幽魂之门，到那时他的感染已经难以治愈。阿伦是神殿的女祭司，她在他发烧的梦境和暴力发作期间治疗他。据说，当泰尼文在睡梦中呼唤她的名字时，那只是她对他说噩梦般睡眠的安抚影响的回声。<BR>
<BR>
至于他到达幽魂之门时租了一个房间，当时和他在一起的女人确实是阿伦。似乎泰尼文在返回幽魂之门的途中扭伤了脚踝，请求她治疗；那笔钱是治疗费，不是房费。这个解释让人更容易相信福维拉大部分路程徒步跟踪他没有遇到什么麻烦（当然，他们俩仍然乘船前往瓦登费尔）。]<BR>
