梅法拉是艺术家，是舞蹈与死亡的编织者。她的性是创造的行为，也是意志的毁灭；她的谋杀是恐惧的带来者，也是夜晚的可能性。每一次死亡中都有新生，每一次新生中都有死亡，两者都有惊心动魄的美。在我们的家园，你只想看到灰烬和死亡吗？还是看到清晨亲吻蘑菇帽的光辉，看到活跃熔渠的扭曲色彩？熔岩蹂躏大地；熔岩也将大地冲刷干净。新的生长是更亮的绿色，但会吸引更多的蝗虫和豪族丹莫来掠夺土地。你希望看到哪一个？梅法拉提醒我们，万物皆有二元性，要尽可能从中获取快乐。在大地上轻快地跳舞，否则它会移动，但要深而快地呼吸，否则你永远不会知道我们这渺小存在带来的快乐。<BR>
<BR>
波耶西亚是战士：凶猛、骄傲、狡猾。他提醒我们永不停止战斗，即使看似失败。如果你不能穿越熔渠，就绕过它，沿着它走，等一天，建造自己的桥，但绝不让它成为你的障碍。完全投降是懦夫的出路，但只有虚假的战士才会把放下武器误认为是投降。面对邪恶的敌人，除了一个精灵能做什么和不能做什么之外，没有荣誉准则。但总要尊敬敌人，因为他们赋予你力量，就像烤熟的牛蛙心脏。当被暴力推向边缘时，我们比我们所知的更强大。多人的死亡造就了领导者。波耶西亚知道这一点，并用他的余烬追逐我们的脚底。<BR>
<BR>
阿祖拉是神秘，是清醒与沉睡之间的空间。她掌管着过渡：从白天到黑夜，从雨季到旱季，从婴儿到成年人。所有的变化都需要指引，而她的微笑是盾角蜥骄傲的獠牙，她推搡并引导她的敌人走向自我毁灭，或引导她的伴侣走向痛苦的觉醒。笛子从不停留在单音上，而是像跳舞的女人一样来回摇摆。当你失明时，你最能听到这一点，这就是为什么她会夺走你的眼睛。阿祖拉的领域是优雅及其随之而来的平衡。<BR>
<BR>
马拉卡斯是警告，是堕落者。一个没有部落、没有祖先的灰烬之民是什么？流放不在于行为，而在于内心。紧紧依偎你的祖先，但不要忘记我们的传承，那是任性者和怀疑者的道路。理想只是等待被推倒的柱子。那些僵化而不审视自己思想深处的人，会被潜伏在下面的黑暗吞噬，而他（马拉卡斯）就是这一教训的证明。要看到这个心怀不满的猎人，你必须睁大眼睛，但心要坚定。<BR>
<BR>
梅鲁涅斯·大衮是大地的雕塑家。当风吹浪打，当红山爆发时，他就在这些现象背后。我们来自大地，是脆弱的，在他面前逃跑。但记住这一点：就像骨头被重新打断以便重新接合，就像水蛭用它们的贪婪清理伤口的血液和感染物，我们也能够将其化为一种艺术，吞下我们过去的错误。熔岩烧掉谷壳，为新的放牧让路。在这方面，他是梅法拉的姐妹，是她的天才的笔触。<BR>
<BR>
莫拉格·巴尔是放纵的生育力，是权威、爱情和生育的扭曲者。就像蛆虫吞噬我们猎物的内脏，在他的适当位置，他会吃掉我们的丢弃物，但就像肉中松散的蛆虫，他会污染我们辛勤的劳动。他是现世神法令背后的真正力量，尽管明智的灰烬之民会为他欺骗的受害者感到悲伤，但他们也会认识到这种痛苦所催生的谎言。莫拉格·巴尔的教训反而体现在灰烬可汗的妻子在他即将冲锋陷阵之前的低语中；尽管她的臂力可能不如她战士丈夫强壮，但她的谨慎和同情心与伴侣的控制力和活力一样引导着她的部落，而那些腐化其中任何一个的人，都将被交给莫拉格的仁慈。<BR>
<BR>
谢尔格拉斯是缓慢的枯萎，是秩序的吞噬者。他是我们对抗豪族丹莫的盟友，在他们骄傲的外表上打出混乱的窟窿，但就像一只狂犬病的尼克斯犬，会在路上误打误撞咬到灰烬之民。吃了他的肉，你就会分享这种疯狂，所以要把他放逐到远离部落的地方。如果他来到帐篷周围嗅探，冷静地向他展示你作为尊贵客人应有的礼貌，但不要让他进来。
<BR>

> BOOK.FNAM T_Bk_TowerOrTombPC
Tower or Tomb
高塔或陵墓

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_TowerOrTombPC
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
<BR>Tower or Tomb<BR>
by Olsia Corantha<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
"To seek the truth, one must look below."<BR><BR>
The words of her mentor Arimus buzzed in Antera's head as she stumbled and ducked into the ruins of an under-tower. Dipping into a slick crevice of fallen pillars and muddy rubble, she shimmied and slithered through the hole further, and further down into a creeking void of rock, root, and mud. Within an instant, she flung herself back towards the wall as her eyes drifted downwards into the abyss. She had slid out of the crevice into the chasm of a spiral staircase, broken by millenia of decaying stone and tangled tree roots. Nearly falling, her chest grew heavy as she struggled to breath the damp, cold air. Her guide, Krevehtha, had warned her that exploring an Under-Tower, or "Gai'Devag" as the Imga call them, was a death sentence. They were dilapidated relics of the Ime Period of Imga, whose secrets have been lost to myth and legend, and were in equal parts sacred and treacherous. Not even the Imga, as reverent towards their history as they were known to be, venture into most Under-Towers, save for the especially brave or foolish.<BR>
<BR>
Arimus taught Antera much about history and magic. Late nights spent memorizing dates and names of Galerion's early life, writing papers on Shalidor's famed Glamoril, and so on. In the waning years of her youth, she felt herself drawn to the Imgan mystics of legend. Before she knew it, she became fascinated with the Imga. Their culture, history, traditions -- all of it. They were "HER Labyrinthian", "HER Galerion", and when Arimus was offered to position of head of the Mages Guild of Virimoor, she knew that she had to join him.<BR>
<BR>
During her days living in the Bosmer city, she absorbed everything she could from the Imga traders and mystics visiting. They seemed amused by Antera's fascination, and were more than eager to fuel her obsession. It wasn't long before she was invited to a nearby Imgan village to witness the Nab'Angoorfet, a native practice that would be considered under the School of Mysticism if the Imgan sages would ever allow the Mages Guild to study it. A refusal that no doubt had contributed to the Guild declaring many of their practices "hedge-magicks".<BR>
<BR>
The Nab'Angoorfet, from what she understood, was a mystical practice of stretching one's own soul across a great distance. It was an awe-inspiring display as she felt their spirits wrapping around her own, twisting and enrapturing her very life and history into themselves, if but for a moment. As the night grew long, Antera spoke to the sage-elders of the village who informed her of a Gai'Devag nearby. The residents of this village, or this "Imgan State" as they were quick to correct her, were supposedly descendants of those that lived in the Under-Tower over 3000 years ago. With no hesitation, she was quick to negotiate with them to secure a guide in the form of a young Imgan woman, Krevehtha.<BR>
<BR>
As the dawn broke, they left for the Under-Tower named Uurgelgra. Krevehtha assured her it was not too far from the Imgan State, but after hours of battling hallucinogenic brambles and vine-like Xaril Trees, Antera's feet grew weary and bloody from the endless flora determined to ensnare her. Nevertheless, her hunger for knowledge had been overpowering, despite her body's frailty. As they pressed on, the clouds grew dark without warning. Krevehtha assured her that these sudden rainstorms were common in this part of Valenwood and offered to take her back to the village, but Antera wouldn't be dissuaded by a seasonal shower. Not from this. So they continued onward through the monsoon. The cold autumn rain only strengthened her resolve.<BR>
<BR>
After what seemed like an eternity, they arrived at Uurgelgra, and it was magnificent. An ancient city swallowed by the jungle. Krevehtha attempted to dissuade Antera from entering the structure, but she ignored her. Her words meant nothing compared to the history beneath her feet, begging her to know it.  "You'll die down there!" Krevehtha scolded her as Antera approached the entrance, barely as Antera approached the entrance, barely able to hear Krevehtha over her own excitement. She waved her guide's warnings away. If Krevehtha had reservations about entering the ruins, then she need not remain by her side. She had done her job and was free to leave for shelter from the pouring rain, as Antera assured her.<BR>
<BR>
Antera climbed through the depths of the chasm for what must have been hours. She paid no mind to the shivers running through her body. What lied at the bottom was her prize, whatever that may be, and there was no one else there to take it.<BR>
<BR>
She eventually arrived at an end of the chasm, with a single hallway. Ducking the sinking walls, Antera arrived at a strange chamber. Advanced in functionality even by the most modern of magecraft standards, yet primitive in design. This mysterious artifact could provide her a clue as to the Imga's role in the Merethic, a portion of their distant history which scholars knew little to nothing of. Antera spent the night in the chamber, eating the rations the sage-elders had provided her with for the journey. And she spent what time she could examining the chamber, compelling her mind to theorize and study it. There were signs of the Fey, throughout, as well as traces of ancient enchantments long-since abandoned and depleted. She knew that any amount of time examining the structure would be inadequate, whether she had the supplies for it or not. Not wanting to burn through her remaining rations, she chipped a piece of the altar off and left to begin heading back up the chasm, so that she could crawl back to the surface and return to the guild.<BR>
<BR>
With great effort, and a few near-death slips off the roots bulging from the cracked walls, she made it to that same small crevice. Squeezing through with confidence, she shimmied further in. But as she pulled herself fully into the cramped space, she noticed that walls seemed tighter, the ceiling lower. There were more rocky corners than she remembered, and before long, she came to the horrid realization. The hole was caving in. Panicked, Antera pulled and shifted faster, as she felt gravelly mud rush down her face. She struggled, wormed, and slithered faster, unable to breathe, motivated by the glimmer of light off in the distance. Faster, faster, faster. Antera heard it before she felt it -- a crack. A stone dislodged itself from the ceiling, piercing her spine. She couldn't move as the pain surged up her back and into her neck. As a studious mage, she knew the basics of Recall -- the ability to return to her own spiritual anchor back at the Mages Guild, but the pain made her concentration void, and the panic set in by the collapsing crevice left little but twitching desperation.<BR>
<BR>
With little clarity of mind and body, Antera attempted the impossible: Through sheer determination, she would muster the strength to cast the spell. Her twitching hands, being berated by mud and small stones, spun the spell with as little grace and room. Her magicka swelled with a stuttering pace as her eyes began to drift downward. She felt a great release of pressure on her body, as the warmth drained out of her torso. Her eyes opened as painful slits, before growing wide in shock. She was back in that chamber, leaning up on the side of that ancient altar. Antera was confused, but her fading consciousness wouldn't allow her to speculate any further. She let out a defeated chuckle as she accepted her fate. "This place, this place will be my tomb."<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards">
<BR>高塔或陵墓<BR>
奥尔西娅·科兰萨 著<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
“追寻真相，必先俯察。”<BR><BR>
导师阿里穆斯的“追寻真相，必先俯察”这句话在安泰拉的脑海中嗡嗡作响，她跌跌撞撞地钻进了一座地下高塔的废墟。她滑入由倒塌石柱和泥泞瓦砾构成的湿滑裂隙，扭动身体，从洞口挤了进去，一路向下，坠入一个由岩石、树根和泥土构成的吱嘎作响的虚空。一瞬间，她的目光向下落入深渊，身体猛地弹回贴住墙壁。她从裂隙中滑出，落入一个螺旋楼梯的裂口处，楼梯因数千年的石料腐朽和树根缠绕早已破碎不堪。她险些坠落，胸口愈发沉重，呼吸着潮湿寒冷的空气。她的向导克雷维萨曾警告她，探索地下高塔 -- 因加人称其为“盖伊-德瓦格” -- 无异于自寻死路。这些是因加“伊梅时期”破败的遗迹，其秘密早已湮没在神话与传说之中，它们既神圣又凶险。就连以崇敬历史而闻名的因加人，也很少冒险进入大多数地下高塔，除非是特别勇敢或愚蠢的人。<BR>
<BR>
阿里穆斯教会了安泰拉许多历史和魔法知识。无数个夜晚，她都在背诵伽勒良早年生活的日期和名字，撰写关于沙利多著名的“生命之秘”的论文，诸如此类。在她青春将逝的岁月里，她感到自己被传说中的因加神秘主义者所吸引。不知不觉间，她开始对因加人着迷。他们的文化、历史、传统 -- 所有一切。他们是“她的拉布林西安”，“她的伽勒良”。当阿里穆斯被任命为维里穆尔法师公会会长时，她知道她必须和他一起去。<BR>
<BR>
在她居住在波斯莫城市的日子里，她从到访的因加商人和神秘主义者那里吸收了一切能学到的东西。他们似乎对安泰拉的着迷感到有趣，并且非常乐意为她的痴迷添柴加火。不久之后，她受邀前往附近的一个因加村庄，亲眼目睹了“纳布-安古尔菲特”。如果因加圣贤允许法师公会研究的话，这项本土实践本应被归入神秘学派。因加人的拒绝无疑促使了公会宣布他们的许多实践为“自然魔法”。<BR>
<BR>
“纳布-安古尔菲特”，据她理解，是一种将自己的灵魂伸展到远方的神秘实践。那景象令人敬畏，她感觉到他们的灵魂缠绕着她，将她的生命和历史扭曲并吞噬进去，哪怕只有一瞬间。夜色渐深，安泰拉与村中的圣贤长老交谈，他们告诉她附近有一个“盖伊-德瓦格”。这个村庄的居民 -- 或者说“因加国”，他们很快纠正了她 -- 据称是三千多年前居住在那座地下高塔中的人的后裔。她毫不犹豫，迅速与他们谈判，请来了一位年轻的因加女性克雷维萨作为向导。<BR>
<BR>
破晓时分，她们出发前往名为“乌尔盖尔格拉”的地下高塔。克雷维萨向她保证，那里离因加国不远。但经过数小时与致幻荆棘和藤蔓般的西里尔树的搏斗后，安泰拉的脚因那无穷无尽、执意要缠住她的植物而疲惫不堪、鲜血淋漓。尽管如此，她对知识的渴望压倒了一切，尽管身体虚弱。她们继续前行，天空毫无预兆地暗了下来。克雷维萨安慰她说，这种突如其来的暴雨在瓦伦伍德这一带很常见，并提出带她回村，但安泰拉不会被一场季节性的阵雨劝阻。尤其不会被这件事劝阻。于是她们继续在季风雨中前行。寒冷的秋雨只会更加坚定她的决心。<BR>
<BR>
仿佛过了很久很久，她们终于到达了乌尔盖尔格拉，那景象壮丽非凡。一座被丛林吞噬的古老城市。克雷维萨试图劝阻安泰拉进入那座建筑，但她没有理会。与她脚下那乞求她去了解的历史相比，她的话毫无意义。“你会死在那下面的！”当安泰拉走近入口时，克雷维萨责备道，安泰拉几乎听不见克雷维萨的声音，因为她的兴奋盖过了一切。她挥手打发了向导的警告。如果克雷维萨对进入废墟有所顾虑，那她不必留在她身边。安泰拉向她保证，她已经完成了自己的工作，可以自由离开去躲避倾盆大雨。<BR>
<BR>
安泰拉在裂谷的深处攀爬了大概几个小时。她没在意身体传来的阵阵颤抖。底部等待她的是她的奖赏，无论那是什么，而且那里没有其他人会去夺取它。<BR>
<BR>
她最终到达了裂谷的尽头，只有一条走廊。安泰拉躲避着下沉的墙壁，来到一个奇特的房间。其功能即使以最现代的魔法标准来衡量也堪称先进，但设计却十分原始。这件神秘的器物或许能让她了解因加人在精灵纪元所扮演的角色 -- 那是他们遥远历史的一部分，学者们对此知之甚少，甚至一无所知。安泰拉在房间里过了一夜，吃着圣贤长老们为她准备的旅途干粮。她花了所有能用的时间检查房间，迫使自己去思考和揣摩。到处都有精魂的痕迹，以及早已废弃、耗尽力量的古老附魔痕迹。她知道，无论花多少时间研究这个结构都是不够的，不管她是否有足够的补给。她不想消耗掉剩余的干粮，于是从祭坛上敲下一块碎片，离开并开始往回攀爬裂谷，以便爬回地表，回到公会。<BR>
<BR>
费了很大的力气，几次险些从开裂墙壁上鼓出的树根滑落丧命后，她终于到达了那个小裂隙。她满怀信心地挤了进去，扭动身体继续深入。但当她把整个身体都拉进那狭窄的空间时，她注意到墙壁似乎更紧了，天花板也更低了。比她记忆中多了更多岩石的棱角。不久，她意识到一个可怕的事实：那个洞正在坍塌。惊慌失措的安泰拉加快了拉扯和移动的速度，感到沙砾般的泥土顺着脸往下淌。她挣扎、蠕动、爬得更快，无法呼吸，远处微弱的亮光激励着她。快一点，再快一点，再快一点。安泰拉在感觉到之前先听到了声响 -- “咔嚓”一声。一块石头从天花板上脱落，刺穿了她的脊柱。剧痛从后背蔓延到脖子，她无法动弹。作为一个勤勉的法师，她懂得“召回”的基础知识 -- 一种能让她回到法师公会自己灵魂锚点的能力，但疼痛使她的注意力化为乌有，而裂隙坍塌带来的恐慌让她只剩下抽搐般的绝望。<BR>
<BR>
身心俱疲、意识模糊的安泰拉尝试了不可能之事：凭借纯粹的意志，她鼓足力量施展法术。她抽搐的双手被泥土和小石子砸打着，笨拙地在狭窄的空间里编织着法术。她的魔能以断断续续的节奏膨胀，同时她的目光开始向下垂落。她感到身体上的巨大压力得到了释放，温暖从躯干中流失。她痛苦地眯着眼睛睁开，随即震惊地瞪大。她回到了那个房间，靠在古老祭坛的旁边。安泰拉困惑不已，但逐渐消散的意识不允许她再作推测。她发出一声认命的轻笑，接受了命运。“这个地方，这个地方将成为我的坟墓。”<BR>

但行动已经逾期了。唯一的办法就是前进。将那些
亡灵留在身后，缓慢地，以如同鬼魂脚步般微小的步伐，
克塔拉进入水中，除了智慧之外一丝不挂。一个简单的法术防止那位浮上水面，避免引起鲨鱼的注意，因为到目前为止，还没有任何涟漪或水流暴露那位的行踪。克塔拉以最审慎的动作，缓慢地向前移动。过了一个小时，那位才移动了一步。过了一天，那位才走完通往藏宝洞穴所需距离的一半。整个过程中，一只眼睛盯着鲨鱼，另一只眼睛盯着洞穴的阴影。然而，即使在分裂的注意力下，其他细节也从浑浊的水中浮现出来，比如这个地方惊人的荒凉。尽管对实验室的寂静和坟墓的死寂并不陌生，克塔拉注意到，连湖中的珊瑚都坚硬而死亡，刮擦着那位的下腹，而鲨鱼身上也显示出可悲的腐烂迹象，保存魔法失效的地方，无人照看地溃烂着，而鱼类的寄生虫却乐于以侍从的腐烂和霉菌为食。它们充满脓液的黄色眼睛茫然地直视前方，无意识地绕圈游动。<BR>

<BR>最终，那位进入了洞穴，出现在一个石窟中，饥肠辘辘，但渴望的远不止食物，尽管虚弱得几乎无法扑腾到岩石地面上。一股恶臭浓重地弥漫在洞穴的阴影中。一个光球驱散了阴影，那位移开视线，原以为会被足以赎回国王的巨额灵魂石和黄金弄得眼花缭乱，但当那位抬起头观察洞穴的细节时，只发现了腐烂的遗骸和死去的斯洛德的软骨骨架。克塔拉将手伸进一具较新的尸体，在头部摸索着柔软易碎的记忆密码。那位闭上眼睛，低语一个咒语，与记忆对话，在其中游弋，被它们包裹和滋养，如同胎盘。缓慢，痛苦。垂死。领悟。灵魂陷阱。毒药。现在克塔拉明白了水池中没有活着的寄生虫，以及灵魂商人近乎无限的财富。一阵恶心感席卷全身，那位瘫倒在地。那位的身体痛苦地咕噜作响，灵魂开始滑脱，却欣然被魔法的网络缠住，沿着由一串闪亮灵魂石铺就的道路前行，并被财富的极乐景象所俘获。<BR>

<BR>吾的故事到此结束。对于这种鲁莽冲动来说，这确实是应得的惩罚。记住这个故事，小家伙们，要尊重你们的先辈，这样有一天，你们也可能长得足够老，拥有一窝小幼虫，以你们腹下的附着物为食。<BR>
<BR>"""

Argonian alchemists of the Black Marsh have long held that the phases of the moon dictate the precise positioning of the Calcinator. During the full moon, the Calcinator should face due South, aligned with the Southron pole star. It is well known that the Southron pole star is slightly offset from true south. The diligent Alchemist will refer to star charts for the specific day and time to more precisely align the Calcinator.<BR>

For each night of the phases of the moon after full, the Calcinator should be rotated clockwise one twenty-eighth of a circle. If the Alchemist is closer to the Southron pole star than the Northern Sisters, he should rotate it counter-clockwise instead. Set the device where the moonlight is shining on half of it. Of course, if it is a new moon, the Calcinator should be fully exposed instead.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The True Folk<BR>
By Haller<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The orcs, or Orsimer, are one of the more misunderstood and maligned races on Tamriel. Rather than being a thing to engender shame, this should instead be taken as a sign of the worthiness of the green-skinned people. For they are held in highest contempt by those who are themselves the ugliest of brutes.<BR><BR>
To understand this point of view, one must first understand the origins of the race. Long ago, the Orsimer were of the same blood as the proud and haughty Altmer. Those who would become Orsimer were especially faithful followers of the mighty Altmer god Trinimac. When the three sinister Daedra began misleading Veloth, it was Boethiah who consumed Trinimac. Such a corrupting force was the Prince of Plots that Trinimac was tainted forever, becoming transformed into Malacath.<BR><BR>
Rather than revile Boethiah whose foulness was such that it tarnished one of the highest gods of the Altmer, the Chimer celebrated his twisted majesty. It was a just reward that they later found their skins darkened to match the depravity of their hearts. And neither is it surprising that those who would go on to style themselves 'Dunmer' would find themselves changed by once again displaying their corruption, shocking even the Daedra who had so twisted them. Surely there is honor in being loathed by such a people.<BR><BR>
Only those Altmer who remained faithful to their befouled god became Orsimer; the rest retained their golden skins. Trinimac had been wounded in a profound way, and his followers bore that wound upon themselves as the transformation into their new, brutish appearance. They suffered this humiliation, and yet they remained loyal and steadfast to Malacath. The other Altmer, unchanged, treated their fellows as monsters and beasts, responding to the unwavering faithfulness of their brethren with malice and contempt.<BR><BR>
It is true, those who broke with Trinimac retained their pristine, golden form. Kept the purity of their blood. Kept their outward beauty. But for all their seeming perfection, their ethereal superiority, they are not the equal of the Orsimer. For while the Orsimer were changed physically, that crudeness reflects what lies under the skin of the "true", untainted Altmer. They look the part of elves, but inside they are hollow, warped creatures.<BR><BR>
For when Trinimac was crippled, when Malacath was born and needed the support of his people, the Orsimer did not abandon him. They ignored the taint of Boethiah's corruption, where others cherished it or shrank from it. For him, they made themselves pariah. That is true faith. That is the depth of honor that exists among orcs.<BR><BR>
So while other mer may look bright and brilliant, may carry themselves with a proud bearing, may call their worship just and pure, they are but shells filled with falsehoods. They are weak and selfish and greedy. They reveal themselves with their deeds.<BR><BR>
No, it is the Orsimer who are the True Folk.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
真正的民族<BR>
哈勒 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
兽人，或称奥斯莫，是泰姆瑞尔最常被误解和诽谤的种族之一。这非但不应引以为耻，反而应被视为绿皮肤民族价值的标志。因为他们被那些自身就是最丑陋粗野的人所极端鄙视。<BR><BR>
要理解这个观点，首先必须了解这个种族的起源。很久以前，奥斯莫与骄傲而傲慢的傲特莫同宗同源。那些后来成为奥斯莫的人，是强大的傲特莫神崔尼马克尤为忠实的追随者。当三个邪恶的迪德拉开始误导维洛斯时，是波耶西亚吞噬了崔尼马克。阴谋之大君的腐蚀力量如此之强，以至于崔尼马克永远被玷污，转变为马拉卡斯。<BR><BR>
歧莫没有唾弃波耶西亚 -- 其污秽玷污了傲特莫最崇高的神祇之一 -- 反而颂扬他那扭曲的威严。后来他们发现自己的皮肤变黑，以匹配他们内心的堕落，这正是应得的报应。而那些后来自称为“丹莫”的人，再次展现出他们的腐败而发现自身改变，甚至震惊了那些曾扭曲他们的迪德拉，这也就不足为奇了。被这样的民族所憎恶，其中必有荣耀。<BR><BR>
只有那些仍然忠于他们被玷污的神祇的傲特莫变成了奥斯莫；其余的人保留了金色的皮肤。崔尼马克受到了深刻的创伤，他的追随者们将这种创伤体现在自己身上，转化为他们新的、粗野的外貌。他们忍受了这种羞辱，却依然对马拉卡斯保持忠诚和坚定。其他未曾改变的傲特莫，则视他们的同胞为怪物和野兽，以恶意和轻蔑回应他们弟兄坚定不移的忠诚。<BR><BR>
诚然，那些与崔尼马克决裂的人保留了原始的金色形态。保持了血统的纯净。保持了外表的美丽。但尽管他们看似完美，拥有空灵的超凡，他们却无法与奥斯莫相提并论。因为当奥斯莫在身体上被改变时，那种粗野恰恰反映了“真正的”、未受玷污的傲特莫皮肤下隐藏的东西。他们外表看起来像精灵，但内心却是空洞、扭曲的生物。<BR><BR>
因为当崔尼马克被重创，当马拉卡斯诞生并需要他子民的支持时，奥斯莫没有抛弃他。他们无视波耶西亚腐败的污点，而其他人或珍视它，或畏惧它。为了他，他们让自己成为贱民。那是真正的信仰。那便是兽人内心深处所蕴含的荣誉之深。<BR><BR>
因此，当其他精灵可能看起来光彩照人，举止高傲，称他们的崇拜公正而纯洁时，他们不过是充满谎言的空壳。他们是软弱、自私和贪婪的。他们的行为会暴露他们自己。<BR><BR>
不，奥斯莫才是真正的民族。<BR>"""

The fellow crumpled into a heap, and Rethril quickly bound his hands and tied him to a nearby post. According to our intelligence report, there were but three more bandits occupying this area. Being of equal number, and, we assumed, much better training, Samson decided to do away with stealth. No longer trying to muffle the clanking of our armor, we alerted the remaining bandits of our presence. They quickly rushed down upon us from deeper in the cavern, and the battle was on. Our assumption was borne out, though the bandits were of greater skill than we had credited them with. Rethril and I were able to subdue our men without inflicting too grievous an injury upon either ourselves or our quarry. Samson had, however, become caught up in the moment. His opposite number among these bandits was Teleris Movon, the one we were truly after. The Dunmer had managed to inflict a number of small cuts where Samson's armor afforded little protection, and Samson did not react well to having his blood shed. Teleris Movon was on the ground and looked to be begging for his life, while Samson was about to strike a deathblow. I knew I could not hope to draw my weapon in time to deflect the blow, and my sprinting had tired me such that I probably wouldn't have wielded the blade with enough accuracy to do so anyway. As it was, I had been in such a rush that I felt near collapse. And so I placed a hand on Samson's shoulder, and cast Absorb Fatigue. It would take him out of the fight long enough for him to clear his head, and would leave me in a condition to arrest Teleris. I am proud that we were able to complete our mission without staining anyone's hands with blood, but I do regret having treated a superior officer as I did.<BR>

有一个词可以概括。考虑到这种情况，德雷斯可以被视为这种诅咒的良药。当然，是德雷斯及其盟友。我也必须祝贺所有看清德雷斯家族真相并决定加入我们行列的人，共同对抗那些难以忍受的外乡人不断酝酿的欺骗之潭。对于那些选择错误道路的人，我满怀同情地说：我只能为你献上我最简短的祈祷。<BR>
<BR>
德雷斯家族有几个强大的盟友，他们对我国所处的状况以及必须采取什么措施来阻止这种诅咒有着同样真实的见解。伟大的哈拉鲁家族有许多善意的人，他们与德雷斯家族的兄弟们有着一些相同的直觉。甚至还有一个相当不错，或者更确切地说，真正高贵的家族，始终忠于丹莫种族；那就是德伦家族。奥尔瓦斯·德伦目前是我们最坚定的支持者。甚至有这样的传言：德伦这个姓氏源自我们伟大家族的名字“德雷斯”。然而，这个家族中有一个叛徒。他的名字是维尼姆·德伦公爵，他为了加入帝国人的行列而公开背叛了他的姓氏。<BR>
<BR>
许多人问我，为什么帝国人和其他外乡人在我们眼中如此可怕，我很乐意回答。帝国人闯入我们的街道，偷走我们的土地，最重要的是，他们试图压制我们的传统。正是这一点让我如此鄙视他们。为此，我不会，也永远不会尊重他们。帝国人是一个根基腐朽的低等种族。<BR>
<BR>
然而，蹂躏我们传统的不仅仅是帝国人，而是所有的外乡人。我可以举出许多他们亵渎的例子，但我只提一个，而且是一个重大的亵渎。从我记事起，德雷斯家族，真正的丹莫家族，就一直喜欢奴隶。我们的领土位于黑沼泽的边缘。那是一个充满阴郁野蛮的阿尔贡种族的国家。这为我们提供了大量的新鲜奴隶。这些生物足够聪明，会在我们的边境附近保持警惕，害怕被我们的奴隶猎手捕获并在市场上出售。虽然我个人更喜欢智力更高、更卫生的奴隶，比如傲特莫、布莱顿人和一些帝国人，但他们在田间劳作也干得很好。我想，说实话，我相当喜欢任何奴隶，无论他们的性别或种族。<BR>
<BR>
然而，近年来，许多奴隶的爆发使得更多的起义迫在眉睫。另一群外乡人，双灯会，一直在稳步从地下崛起。这个组织由前奴隶和愚蠢的外乡人组成。我甚至看到许多丹莫为其服务。这些人成了我们身边挥之不去的刺。他们秘密地、也是非法地活动。这就是为什么雇佣了许多赏金猎人来追捕他们，并重新夺回任何丢失的奴隶。但这个组织依然存在。尽管我们做出了努力，他们似乎总能设法逃脱我们的掌控。我亲眼目睹了他们的罪行。我曾经拥有二十个奴隶，七个在我的庄园里，另外十三个在我的盐田里。在一个阴沉的夜晚，一群双灯会的罪犯潜入了奴隶围栏，从我这里带走了十五个奴隶。我勃然大怒！我只能称他们的行为为盗窃。<BR>
<BR>
我希望这份文件能有助于说服那些不信的人，让他们看清外乡人的真面目。德雷斯家族将继续致力于将腐朽的帝国人和其他恶心的外乡人从伟大的晨风国家中清除出去。他们屠杀我们的家人，羞辱我们的文化。这种行为将永远不可原谅。任何真正的丹莫都会立刻意识到这一点。希望我甚至能唤醒那些被帝国人描绘的欺骗性谎言所蒙蔽的沉睡丹莫。我可以向你们保证，我绝不会放弃斗争。德雷斯家族也绝不会放下武器，放弃斗争。我们将继续与我们的盟友一起拯救晨风，让它恢复应有的荣耀！<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
True Introspection of Telvanni Nobility <BR>
An Educational Tract and a Warning <BR>
by Indalen Hlormayn<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
A malicious pack of wolves is stalking Telvannis as of late. Envious and frightened of the eons-old wizard lords of House Telvanni, they seek to neuter us with their regulations and moralities, and ultimately to cast down our great works. I speak, of course, of the Cyrodiil hordes, those inexhaustible malcontents that torment all of Tamriel, seeking to bend its lands to their wicked yoke. Recently, Cyrodiil arrogance has grown beyond the pale -- their agents are now brazenly accusing us of necromancy, while ever-growing numbers of slippery abolitionists are inciting riot in our countryside. Many would justly argue that these slanderers and criminals deserve to be driven from our shores with prejudiced force. Yet, one must despair at the prospect -- the Empire does not lack bodies to throw into such a fight, so even though ultimate victory is not in doubt, the struggle will be prolonged and costly.<BR>
<BR>
I, therefore, nurture a desperate hope that words can still disarm the situation. Despite the absurdity of having to explain myself -- why would the dragon explain itself to the flea -- I must attempt the thankless task of educating the Cyrodiili to respect, or better yet, fear Telvanni superiority. Hence, this tract will make abundantly clear to all such trespassers -- if any can string more than two thoughts together, that is -- that the Telvanni will accede to absolutely no restraint on their freedom and any attempt to do so will come at a woeful price to would-be-offenders.<BR>
<br>
The tomfools of the Imperial government would have you believe that the current conflict is in some way "precipitated" by the Telvanni; nothing could be further from the truth. In fact, the Great House Telvanni is famed throughout all of Tamriel for its splendid isolation, as we have since millennia disavowed any pretense of seeking dominance over other lands. Our very founding dates back to the decision of the wisest Chimer wizards to abstain from the foolish War of the First Council that wreaked such havoc on Morrowind. In fact, we would be delighted to utterly ignore all of the myriad barbarians of Tamriel, were they not themselves so intent on banging on our gates! Protestations that we are enslaving "Imperial citizens" are, likewise, malicious and utterly stupid. Telvanni slaves are purchased on legal slave markets; where these creatures come from is not our business. Even if some former "citizens" find their ways to the pits, the very fact they succumbed to this fate is the surest condemnation of their worth -- what an absurd Empire it is that would defend the "rights" of such wretches. No, it is abundantly clear that any cause for strife stems singly from the twisted degeneracy of the Cyrodiils. These mongrels are confused and intimidated by the grand designs of the Telvanni, and as is natural to all imbeciles, they seek to cast down works of beauty and awe that go beyond their abilities.<BR>
<br>
In fact, the institution of slavery itself, which all Telvanni nobles rightly acknowledge as highly practical, but which the abolitionist scum believes a topic worthy of self-immolation, perfectly illuminates the contrast between Telvanni brilliance and Imperial lunacy. I could just leave it at "what we do with our own property is our own business" and anyone with an ounce of common sense would be satisfied. Yet, it is our misfortune that the abolitionist does not possess common sense; they instead feel that their "moral imperative" somehow supersedes basic decency. At this point, every Telvanni will guffaw -- "morality" is rightfully derided in our society as simply the moaning of the weak and frail. It is nothing but a desperate attempt to stave off the natural and rightful order: the domination of the lessers by their betters. <BR>
<BR>
But against my better judgement, let us wade into the moral muck, where the abolitionist so loves to roll, to see if their arguments can even stand on their own terms. They weep bitter tears over the "sufferings" supposedly inflicted in Telvanni pits and laboratories; they say that our experiments are "cruel" and "inhumane". Yet, what is the comparison to? Indeed, they seek to put forward that these mundane hardships can somehow outweigh the unimaginable eons of toil and self-sacrifice on part of the Telvanni masters. Over the centuries, many, myself included, have poured every shred of our health and every drake of our fortune into our great works. Not unheard of are cases where the profound quest of a Telvanni master has cost the blood of their own sons and daughters. It is absurd, insulting, and downright malevolent of the Cyrodiil abolitionists to suggest that we are now not allowed to spend the lives of our slaves, that their supposed "suffering" is cause enough to arrest our aspirations. How can the pathetic whines of Argonian beasts outweigh a millennium of toil from the greatest wizard-lords? Or how can the miserable, brutish life of a Khajiit be compared to a revelation on the nature of the planes or of the origin of disease? In the harsh light of logic, the outlanders' "moral argument" dissipates like mist and their envy and anti-intellectualism are laid bare for all to see.<BR>
<BR>
But perhaps it is not surprising that the abolitionist would sympathize so deeply with the Argonian -- the former is, after all, hardly higher than the latter in the hierarchy of intelligence. This criminal crowd of would-be moralists, in their quest to "enlighten" Morrowind, commit the most revolting acts of dishonesty and deceit -- they come disguised as traders or labourers, yet clutch a dagger poised to strike at the heart of Telvanni nobility. Until recently, the abolitionists' insanity was held in check by the armistice, but ever since the opening of Vvardenfell, the Empire has made a mockery of this document, letting ever increasing numbers of these criminals wash up on our shores. Now they roam Telvannis unchecked, free to infect misguided dunmer with their intellectual rot, inciting slave riots as they go.<br>
<br>
These outrages will not be allowed to continue. Any sort of compromise on slavery is abhorrent to Telvanni nobility and completely out of the question. In fact, so are any rules or regulations which hold a hint of arresting our scholarship. We have no patience for tender souls or the ignorant, outraged mob. Neither will we submit ourselves to the judgement of the Imperial governors, those babbling idiots. Why would we let those inferior to us decide what is "right" and what is "wrong"? We will decide only for ourselves where our limits lie. If the abolitionist scum continues in their provocations, we will have no recourse but to blast them off our shores. Such a contest would not even be close -- House Telvanni in its incessant exploration of cosmic mysteries has gained a profound understanding of the arcane schools that no feeble "battle mage" will ever dream of. This empire of men, furthermore, strikes us as teetering on the edge of a well-deserved demise -- an emperor emasculated by that hedge wizard, Tharn, with daedric doppelgangers for heirs. This is a scene better fit for a minstrel show than an "imperial" court. No, if there is any sense in them, the Cyrodiil must see that driving the Telvanni to violent means is not remotely in their interest. Let the abolitionists heed my warning then and crawl back to the hovels they came from, while we still allow them to.<br>
<br>
[Editor's note on the 2nd edition -- whereas Master Hlormayn's tract did not find the wide readership among outlanders it intended to, its popularity in Telvanni households has made it worthwhile to print a second edition for the benefit of this discerning market.]<br>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
泰瓦尼贵族之真我内省<BR>
教育性短文与警告<BR>
因达伦·霍梅恩 著<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
近来，一群恶毒的狼群正在泰瓦尼斯游荡。他们嫉妒并畏惧泰瓦尼家族那些存在了千万年的巫师领主，试图用他们的法规和道德来阉割我们，最终推翻我们的伟大成就。我指的当然是西罗帝尔的乌合之众，那些折磨着整个泰姆瑞尔、试图将这片土地置于他们邪恶枷锁之下的、不知疲倦的不满之徒。最近，西罗帝尔的傲慢已经越界 -- 他们的代理人现在竟敢厚颜无耻地指控我们使用死灵法术，而越来越多的狡猾废奴主义者正在我们的乡村煽动骚乱。许多人会公正地争辩说，这些诽谤者和罪犯应该被以偏见的武力驱逐出我们的海岸。然而，面对这种前景，人们不得不感到绝望 -- 帝国并不缺乏投入这场战斗的炮灰，因此，尽管最终胜利毋庸置疑，但斗争将是漫长而代价高昂的。<BR>
<BR>
因此，我怀着一丝绝望的希望，希望言语仍能化解局势。尽管不得不为自己辩解是荒谬的 -- 巨龙何必向跳蚤解释 -- 但我必须尝试这项吃力不讨好的任务，教育西罗帝尔人尊重，或者更好的是，畏惧泰瓦尼的优越性。因此，这本小册子将向所有此类侵犯者 -- 如果他们能把两个以上的想法串起来的话 -- 充分阐明，泰瓦尼绝不会接受对其自由的任何限制，任何这样做的尝试都将让潜在的冒犯者付出惨痛的代价。<BR>
<br>
帝国政府的蠢材会让你们相信，当前的冲突在某种程度上是由泰瓦尼“挑起”的；这与事实相去甚远。事实上，伟大的泰瓦尼家族以其出色的孤立主义而闻名于整个泰姆瑞尔，因为我们几千年来一直摒弃任何寻求统治其他土地的伪装。我们的建立本身就源于最睿智的歧莫巫师们决定不参与那场给晨风带来巨大浩劫的“第一议会愚蠢战争”。事实上，如果不是那些形形色色的泰姆瑞尔蛮族自己执意要敲打我们的大门，我们倒很乐意完全无视他们！关于我们奴役“帝国公民”的抗议同样是恶意且愚蠢至极的。泰瓦尼的奴隶是在合法的奴隶市场上购买的；这些生物来自哪里与我们无关。即使一些曾经的“公民”沦落到了奴隶坑里，他们屈服于这种命运的事实本身就是对他们价值最确凿的谴责 -- 一个会为这种可怜虫的“权利”辩护的帝国是何等荒谬！不，很明显，任何纷争的起因都完全源于西罗帝尔人扭曲的堕落。这些杂种被泰瓦尼的宏伟计划搞得困惑和恐吓，就像所有白痴的天性一样，他们试图摧毁那些超出他们能力范围的美丽和令人敬畏的成就。<BR>
<br>
事实上，奴隶制本身 -- 所有泰瓦尼贵族都正确地承认其高度实用性，而废奴主义渣滓却认为这是一个值得自焚的话题 -- 完美地阐明了泰瓦尼的才智与帝国的疯狂之间的对比。我本可以只说“我们怎么处理自己的财产是我们自己的事”，任何有一点点常识的人都会满意。然而，不幸的是，废奴主义者没有常识；他们反而觉得他们的“道德义务”不知何故超越了基本的体面。此时，每个泰瓦尼人都会放声大笑 -- “道德”在我们社会里理所当然地被嘲笑为只是弱者和脆弱者的呻吟。它不过是试图阻止自然且正义秩序的绝望尝试：即强者对弱者的统治。<BR>
<BR>
但与我更好的判断相悖，让我们涉足废奴主义者如此热爱的道德泥潭，看看他们的论点是否能自圆其说。他们为据称在泰瓦尼的坑和实验室里遭受的“苦难”流下痛苦的眼泪；他们说我们的实验“残忍”和“不人道”。然而，这是跟什么比较呢？的确，他们试图提出，这些平凡的苦难不知何故能胜过泰瓦尼大师们难以想象的、无数个世纪的辛劳和自我牺牲。几个世纪以来，包括我在内的许多人，将我们的每一丝健康和每一块金币都投入到了我们伟大的事业中。泰瓦尼大师深奥的探索以自己儿女的鲜血为代价，这样的例子并非闻所未闻。西罗帝尔的废奴主义者暗示我们现在不允许消耗我们奴隶的生命，他们所谓的“苦难”足以阻止我们的抱负，这是荒谬的、侮辱性的，也是彻头彻尾的恶意。阿尔贡野兽可怜的哀鸣怎能胜过最伟大的巫师领主们千年的辛劳？或者，卡吉特悲惨、粗野的生命怎能与关于位面本质或疾病起源的启示相提并论？在逻辑的严酷光芒下，外乡人的“道德论点”如雾消散，他们的嫉妒和反智主义暴露无遗。<BR>
<BR>
但也许废奴主义者如此同情阿尔贡人并不奇怪 -- 毕竟前者在智力等级上并不比后者高多少。这群自封的道德家的罪犯，在寻求“启蒙”晨风的过程中，犯下了最令人作呕的不诚实和欺骗行为 -- 他们伪装成商贩或劳工，却手握匕首，随时准备刺向泰瓦尼贵族的心脏。直到最近，停战协议还在抑制着废奴主义者的疯狂，但自从瓦登费尔开放以来，帝国就把这份文件当成了笑话，让越来越多的这些罪犯涌上我们的海岸。现在他们不受约束地在泰瓦尼斯游荡，自由地用他们的智力腐败感染被误导的丹莫，并沿途煽动奴隶暴乱。<br>
<br>
这些暴行不会继续下去。在奴隶制问题上的任何妥协都为泰瓦尼贵族所深恶痛绝，完全不可能。事实上，任何带有阻碍我们学术研究意味的规则或法规也是如此。我们没有耐心对待那些脆弱的灵魂或无知、愤怒的暴民。我们也不会屈服于帝国总督们 -- 那些喋喋不休的白痴 -- 的评判。我们为什么要让那些劣于我们的东西来决定什么是“对”、什么是“错”？我们将只为我们自己决定我们的界限在哪里。如果废奴主义者渣滓继续挑衅，我们将别无他法，只能将他们从我们的海岸上轰走。这样的较量甚至不会势均力敌 -- 泰瓦尼家族在对宇宙奥秘的不懈探索中，对神秘学派获得了深刻的理解，这是任何软弱的“战斗法师”做梦也想不到的。此外，这个人类帝国在我们看来正摇摇欲坠，走向它应得的灭亡 -- 一个被那个自然巫师萨恩阉割的皇帝，后代竟是迪德拉的拟身怪。这一幕更适合吟游诗人的表演，而非“帝国”宫廷。不，如果西罗帝尔人还有一点理智，他们必须看到，逼迫泰瓦尼诉诸暴力手段对他们绝无益处。那么，让废奴主义者留心我的警告吧，趁我们还允许，爬回他们来的那个窝棚去。<br>
<br>
[编者关于第二版的说明 -- 虽然霍尔梅恩大师的小册子未能在外乡人中达到预期的广泛读者群，但它在泰瓦尼家族中的受欢迎程度使得为这个有鉴赏力的市场印刷第二版是值得的。]<br>

The Truth of the Bear Clan
熊族之真相

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_TruthOfTheBearclanSHOTN
"""<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
We are the bears who have been guarding the border for centuries. Today we are nothing but footmen and Prisoners in our own country. We are the dreaded Bear Clan, the defamed of the Reach.  <BR>
<BR>
Once, when our clan came here, this stretch of water, known as Karth-River, had been a border between Nords and the Redguards and Bretons beyond. 'Karth' in our nordic tongue means as much as 'valuable stone'. At that time, not long after the dissensions about succession had ended, rumors of rich hunting-grounds, Silver, Iron, Aquamarines and other precious gems were heard throughout the decimated Rim of Sky. Many clans made their way west in hope of wealth, among them our honored Clan-Father Rigmad Bearhand and his kin. Instead of going where many other Nords went, the rich southern river-bend today known as Karthwasten, he made himself and his family free space in the middle of nowhere.  <BR>
<BR>
For several generations our clan lived as fishers and hunters in this remote place surrounded by dense forest. We drove out foul Reachmen whose bathing families disturbed the fish at the nearby riverbank so we could pursue our business unmolested. Through those generations we were able to carry on and fortify the fishing-abilities of our Clanfather Rigmad. But the long time of isolation also had a drawback for us: We became anything but a pretty sight to our Nord-brothers. Back in those days the first of many aspersions against us arose: That our clan would be one of half-breeds with the locals. Exactly those locals that we have been fighting for generations! It took many gatherings with other clans and intense use of speechcraft until we could finally establish that it was incest that had been accusable for our changed appearance. But even today we are object of mockery to those who still spread the falsity of intermingling around.  <BR>
<BR>
Time went on and centuries later, when Karthwasten was lost to Hammerfell and desert warriors pushed forward into our lands, our village turned out to be a firm holding against further conquest. This place became known as 'Karthgad', the Guard of Karth. I have heard imperials using the name Amber Guard. Those stay-at-homes believe that Karth refers to the Amber found in the bed of our Karth-River. No, the name of our town speaks of the heroic deeds of our fathers, not of worthless stones buried in gravel. There was nothing the warriors from the desert learned to fear as much as the ambushes of the Bear Clan. No clan knew how to sneak upon his enemies as the Bear Clan; no other clan could even hope to be able to steal the weapons from their enemies before falling upon them. Ungratefulness caused a further aspersion: That our clan unlike other Nord Clans would only lead ambushes for being too coward to face enemies in an open battle. Those who brought that up probably never visited our home, the dense Vorndgad Forest. You will be able to convince yourself that there is no way an open battle could be led between trees standing next to each other tightly as this.  <BR>
<BR>
Again a long time went by in which we were at least recognized for being the defender of the frontier. This ended with the conquest of the land beyond the river. We are no longer those who will protect our Nord Brothers against conquest from west. Since that time we have only been assigned dishonorable tasks from our king Barda. Further aspersions against us arose over time. That we would be nothing but a pack of greedy criminals, who would only steal and smuggle and enrich themselves. Knife-fighting is one of the High Arts, alongside poetry and philosophy. A combat with daggers is not an exercise of personal bravado, or a way of settling tawdry disputes. It is a demonstration of principles and a form of moral instruction for the masses. <BR>
 <BR>
All other physical contests are by their nature unequal. In wrestling, one fighter is bigger and stronger. In a sorcerous duel, one participant has a greater innate grasp of magicka than the other. When both knives are equally long and sharp they confer no inherent advantage, becoming merely a physical extension of the will of the fighter.  <BR>
The Hlaalu reject our stances, and mock the ordered traditions of combat. It is their folly, as they are forced to improvise what we have committed to memory. They favor the reverse grip, the posture of the backstabber, which for us is only deployed by amateurs or the purest masters. It adds strength to the blow, and conceals the attacker's motions, but it must be wielded with exceptional skill or the wielder risks cutting themselves and defeating their own efforts. People aren't like those Dwemer cogmen you see children throwing stones at during the harvest fair. They have their own ideas and approaches. Some are braggarts looking to show off. Some get into the knife fights because they just want an excuse to hurt someone. Some have a death wish. These things come out in the way they fight, and two thirds of the duel is about figuring out what kind of fetcher you're fighting against, while giving nothing away about yourself. That last bit is important- whoever masks their intent best, wins nine times out of ten. <BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Unseen People<BR> 
Unknown <BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
Erur Dan cursed his own folly and staggered his way through the barren tundra of Skyrim, attempting to stay warm under his crumbling bonemold armor. He shuddered at the thought of those regulars at the End of the World in Dagon Fel, heartily enjoying their fine food and drink as well as making him the laughingstock of the entire island of Sheogorad. Or perhaps it was just the bitter cold. How foolish was he to believe that he could brave the very winters of Skyrim, known to have caused the demise of many a swarthy adventurer, just for the mere glimpse of the fabled Falmer? And even if he found them, how could he prove it to his tavern-mates back in Dagon Fel? These thoughts swam icily through Erur's head causing him to fall to the ground in almost utter hopelessness. But he was determined to return to Morrowind, hopefully in one piece, to tell his tale to the entire town. Perhaps he could be an author and write a best-seller about his experiences and of his near death at the hands of the Skyrim winter only to press forwards and find the mythical mer. Sadly he was never a writer of sorts but there was plenty of room to "improvise" in his story if need be. Regardless, he would surely be contacted by Cyrodiil and asked to teach at the University, and the folks at Dagon Fel finally would give him the respect he had deserved all along.<BR>
<BR>
Wallowing in his soon-to-be success, Erur soon forgot he was lying in the snow until the bitter coldness piqued his sense. He gracefully tried to lift himself from his prostrate position but he found he could not. Again and again tried the unfortunate Bosmer, but to no avail. He was stuck and his only option to escape the very clutches of death was to shed his only instrument of survival, his thick winter robe. He was out of his robe quickly but a sharp icy gale soon brought him humbly to his feet. The very encounter would question one's own capacity to press forward although simply giving up would certainly be a more appealing route. Erur simply had too much to lose by giving up in such an early stage of his journey. Sure his tavern mates would beg on their knees to Queen Almalexia for mercy if he was found dead during his journey, but what good would that serve, lying in a lonely crypt underground? Rather, he would like them to bow and service his every need when he came to the tavern for his daily flin. Needless to say, his success in life was firmly in check. So the unfortunate outlander trudged onwards through the wilderness at a fast walk hoping that civilization was in the distance. Day passed to evening and still Dan found himself drowning in desperation. He had already had two close encounters with treacherous pitfalls and snow-covered ponds but he had not expected the howls that soon began to emanate from the wilderness all around him. They were isolated at first, often scaring Erur from his possessed march through the wild, but they soon they were louder, more clear, and were growing ever-closer. Dan began to run, unconscious to his position on the island, afraid of death from the winter but fearing death at the jaws of unknown creatures much more.<BR>
<BR>
Alas, Erur Dan was in no shape to run; even from the slowest of enemies he was easy bait and before long he had to right himself up against a tree to catch his breath. He thought to himself that he had cheated danger for the moment and began to collect some wood in hopes of starting a fire. Wood certainly was not in short supply in these parts and before long he had all the provisions ready for a grand fire fit to warm the cold-hearted King himself. However the wood was simply too damp and he could only muster a few wisps of flame before the fire was snuffed out. At this juncture, Erur decided to wait, although his chances for survival were growing slimmer by the moment, until the wood had dried sufficiently for a long-lasting fire. His rag-tag shell of a cuirass did not offer much protection against the cold, and Erur was resigned to pass the night shivering from the eternal cold of the wintry weather. Several times during the night he imagined seeing people pass by his location and he called out to them, but no adventurer would dare be in these parts during the dead of night. Several poachers had ventured into these very woods just days ago and their mutilated bodies were last spotted floating downstream through Winterhold itself.<BR>
<BR>
Erur sat in the very heart of the forest, oblivious to the dangers around him and assuming the red lights in the distance were towns that would offer him the security and comfort he had not felt since leaving Morrowind. But the lights were creeping ever closer and the intensity of their glow amplified with each passing moment. They approached silently like barbaric assassins and before long their bodies began to take form; the lupine predators from which he had vehemently ran earlier that day had finally cornered him. Much as Erur would have loved to flee the scene, his body would not comply; he must stand and fight. The pack of three wolves approached malevolently, teeth gleaming for bloodlust. As Erur drew his dagger they drew their fangs and jumped in unison, thirty needles poised to end the life of yet another mer. He stood his ground and nearly toppled over when the impact hit his fragile frame. He had expected all to be lost at this point but his fears were unfounded. The sound of claws breaking met his ears simultaneously followed by howls of agony. Erur was quick to react, thrusting the dagger deep inside the closest two wolves while stumbling towards the third, but it was too quick for him. Soon he found himself in the same predicament as he had been for the past few hours; he was still the prey. A rustling in a bush behind him caused him to swivel before being plowed into by the last of the pack. The wolf attacked the delicate region between the cuirass and helm, wanting to bite the neck region, but was denied consistently by the stubborn armor of Erur. In his throes, Erur lashed out at the wolf, gashing his throat and soon all was over.<BR>
<BR>
He wept at his victory knowing that though he could pass the night safely, hunger and thirst would surely overcome his body in the coming days. He fell into a fitful sleep, waking at sunrise only to see its splendor for perhaps the last time. He made a quick check of his provisions, which seemed to be untouched despite the attacks just hours ago. It was then that his eyes fell upon his armor, investigating the damage that had been dealt to it and deeming it destined for uselessness. However the armor was patched solidly where the cracks once were and the gaping holes were filed sturdily with ice. Such was this twist of fate that the cold that Erur had once regarded as an evil now came as a blessing. The thought was rejuvenating in itself as Erur quickly thought otherwise of building a fire and instead began to clean out the carcass of the biggest wolf and tailor himself a wooly drape. When the final product was achieved hours later, Erur was a fearsome sight, clad in an outfit suited for the most dangerous of war chieftains. With the robe providing the warmth he needed to sustain him through the forest without melting the ice that kept his armor together, Erur continued his crazed march through the wilderness fearing neither sounds, creatures nor death itself. Days and hours passed and there was no sign of any residence from the cold winter, and Erur seemed only to be marching towards death.<BR>
<BR>
Then it came, the godsend of every lost adventurer. First it was small wisps of smoke, then the occasional remains of human ventures. He heard the occasional laugher in the distance and soon the sounds of industry. He began to run, illusions filling his mind as his feet rapidly pounded the snow-covered floor. When he came upon it, he hardly knew what he was looking for. He had arrived in Windhelm, one of the great winter cities of Skyrim. The euphoria he expressed was silent, erased by the numbing cold as his body stabilized from his frenzied run. His senses would not render themselves active and he knew his best shot at recovery lay with much-needed rest and several bottles of Flin. He waltzed along like a drunkard, frostbitten in several places and finally made his way to Windhelm's Inn. He entered, and much to his displeasure found all eyes staring at him. But the looks were not of disgust; instead they were of wonder, of the fabulous excitement that must be tagged alongside each successful adventurer. Two pretty girls escorted him inside and paid for his Flin. Odd as it was, he did not object nor did he turn down their offer to show him their rooms upstairs. As he walked calmly alongside the two eager women, he could not help to suppress a smile and a laugh regarding his future. He knew he had an unseen benefactor alongside him throughout his journey, and that benefactor was already treating him to good luck even though his quest had ended. In the distance he was sure he heard a laugh, a tinkle to be exact, something strangely unfamiliar and inhuman. So, indeed they do exist.<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>The Uprising in Almalexia<BR>

<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>Witness reports from the archives of the Imperial Commission for Post-Simulacrum Restoration <BR>
<BR>edited by Ottrebus Auriil<BR>
<BR>
<FONT COLOR="003300" >A word from the editor<BR>
<BR>
<FONT COLOR="000000" >The decade of Jagar Tharn's false reign known as the Imperial Simulacrum (3E 389-399) was a turbulent time for all the Empire, but it can be argued that the chaos culminated in the easternmost province of Morrowind. During the Simulacrum, Morrowind engaged in a border war with Black Marsh, and the holds of Old Ebonheart and Firewatch became locked in a stalemate civil war. The event which preceded and attributed to the ignition of these senseless conflicts was the 3E 391 uprising in Almalexia. During the riots the streets of the capital citadel of Mournhold were overrun by masses of revolting peasantry and the regent of Morrowind, Lord Symmachus, was slain. <BR>
<BR>
After the fall of Jagar Tharn, the Commission for Post-Simulacrum Restoration ordered a collecting of witness reports to shed light on events of the revolt. The Commission permitted me to go through their archives and select a number of accounts for publication. In most cases, the interviewees suffered from a severe --and may I say convenient-- amnesia concerning the uprising. The three witness reports that I have chosen to publish here, however, give interesting insight into the uprising from three very different points of view.<BR>
<BR>
<FONT COLOR="003300" >Devyn Sobaris, a rickshaw<BR>
<BR>
<FONT COLOR="000000" >Did I take part in the uprising? B'vek no. But I saw and knew many who did. I remember this one gang of youngsters particularly well. "We're going to take Godsreach", they were shouting. They had crude clubs and staves in their hands. One boy donned a kettle for a helmet. "Go right ahead, but count me out," I told them. I pictured what their heads would look like on pikes above the city gates. <BR>
<BR>
I've lived in lower Almalexia all my life. The Imperial taxes don't mean a netchiman's wife's fart to me. I'm practically a beggar; how are they going to tax me? And I don't think the taxes meant that much to those youths, either. Sure,  times are tough, but a shrewd guy always gets by, and there's no un-shrewd common folk in this city. <BR>
<BR>
But you see, there were these... what's the fancy word for it... "aggravators"? Anyway, these folks -- outlanders most of them -- on the streets whispering to the commoners' ears. I worked a rickshaw in the city and heard a lot of their talk. One time, this Cyrod gal sits  down on my cart and begins to talk: "You know, the bread is so expensive because the Emperor has issued higher a tax on Deshaan flour." "The Queen probably went  west, because she doesn't care for Morrowind no more." "Where's the common folk going to go?" That sort of stuff. That sort of drivel. Anyhow, I dropped her off, took my money and paid no further attention. Still think she was getting paid for it. [Editor's note: The "outlanders" and the Imperial woman the witness refers to were most likely spies and agitators planted by Jagar Tharn, the Arch-Traitor.] <BR>
<BR>
<FONT COLOR="003300" >Thalrys Mendrano, a former household guard<BR>
<BR>
<FONT COLOR="000000" >I remember the day Lord General Symmachus talked to the people. They were gathered before the main gates of Mournhold, hundreds of them. Mostly peasants and commoners but I recognized among them some petty noblemer, too. They were disgruntled by the new taxes and displeased with the departure of the Queen. The Lord General walked towards them to soothe their anger, and we encircled him with shields to keep the rabble from reaching him. An Imperial taxman had been torn from his carriage and stoned to death in lower Almalexia the previous day, so we had to be careful. <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus talked reason but they would not listen. They kept clamoring for the Queen, justice, bread... One young lad called Symmachus Septim's cuckold.  I had my longspear at the ready and my arms were keen. My blood was up and I would have done it, but Symmachus stayed my hand. I remember how the Lord General looked at me and said: "Ai. The boy does not threaten me. Do not spill his blood." I am thankful he stopped me. Things would have gotten very ugly very fast.<BR>
<BR>
Then the rocks started flying. More and more people came, and more and more rocks flew. Symmachus fell into my arms, unconscious; a big gash by his temple. I ordered the retreat and we carried the Lord General back inside Mournhold. [Editor's note: Though this account suggests that Symmachus was grievously wounded by the stones flung at him, the more popular account of his death claims that he died of an assassin's poison dart at a much later stage of the uprising. Naturally, it would be disenchanting had the celebrated hero of the Empire fallen before the rebellion had properly begun.] <BR>
<BR>
<FONT COLOR="003300" >Lleevu Varis, a temple caretaker<BR>
<BR>
<FONT COLOR="000000" >The last day of the uprising... Yes, I do recall. I was working in the High Chapel that morning. The fighting had finally reached the streets of Mournhold the night before. I remember there was smoke all over the Temple courtyard, from the fires that burned in the bazaar and Godsreach.<BR>
<BR>
We were told that Lord Symmachus was coming to seek an audience with the goddess. I expected a war-council. I thought he would plead with the Mother of Morrowind to end the rebellion. But when they came, not long after morning's first light, I saw Symmachus was more fit to receive his last rites from the goddess rather than to counsel with Her. He arrived on a stretcher carried by only a handful of his household guards, all of them Dunmer. No Imperial soldiers  with him. I did not know it at the time, but they had already abandoned him. [Editor's note: There is no evidence in support of this claim. Quite possibly the Imperial Legionnaires were busy with the rebels.] They waited 'til noon, but Lady Almalexia wouldn't summon them. Symmachus' strength was withering away along with the spirit of his guards. He made this feeble, defeated gesture with his hand and the stretcher was lifted and they began to depart. <BR>
<BR>
Before they left, I overheard the guard captain's instructions to one of the royal couriers. Symmachus sent word to all the Houses; a call to arms, but not against the people. Now that's just a phrase to you foreigners, but for the Dunmer, there's fire in those words. When the right mouth says them, like Nerevar once did, they cannot be refused. Maybe Symmachus could have been the one; I don't know.<BR>

Nothing came of it, of course. Our Lady sees further than we do. Symmachus was dead by dusk and then they placed some puppet on his wife's throne and the whole thing was done and dealt with.<BR>"""

<FONT COLOR="003300" >编者的话<BR>

<FONT COLOR="000000" >杰迦尔·萨恩虚假统治的十年，被称为帝国幻象（第三纪元389-399年），对整个帝国来说是一个动荡时期，但可以说混乱在最东部的晨风行省达到了顶峰。在帝国幻象期间，晨风与黑沼泽卷入了一场边境战争，而旧黑檀心和火望的领地陷入了僵持的内战。引发这些毫无意义冲突的前奏事件是第三纪元391年的阿玛莱西娅起义。在暴乱中，首都哀伤之城都堡的街道被大批起义的农民占领，晨风的摄政王西马库斯大人被杀。<BR>
<BR>
杰迦尔·萨恩倒台后，帝国幻象后重建委员会下令收集目击者报告，以揭示起义事件。委员会允许我查阅他们的档案，并挑选一些叙述出版。在大多数情况下，受访者对于起义都患有严重的 -- 我可以说方便的 -- 失忆症。然而，我选择在这里出版的三份目击者报告，从三个截然不同的角度对起义提供了有趣的见解。<BR>
<BR>
<FONT COLOR="003300" >德文·索巴里斯，人力车夫<BR>
<BR>
<FONT COLOR="000000" >我参加起义了吗？维威克在上，没有。但我看到并认识很多参加的人。我尤其记得一帮年轻人。“我们要占领神临区”，他们喊道。他们手里拿着粗糙的棍棒和木杖。一个男孩把一个水壶戴在头上当头盔。“尽管去吧，但别算上我”，我告诉他们。我能想象他们的脑袋插在城门上方的长矛上会是什么样子。<BR>
<BR>
我一生都住在下阿玛莱西娅。帝国的税收对我来说连个养气母人的屁都不如。我几乎是个乞丐；他们怎么向我征税？而且我认为税收对那帮年轻人也没那么重要。诚然，时局艰难，但精明的人总能过得去，这座城市里没有不精明的平民。<BR>
<BR>

<FONT COLOR="003300" >萨利斯·门德拉诺，前家庭卫兵<BR>
<BR>
<FONT COLOR="000000" >我记得西马库斯将军大人对民众讲话的那一天。他们聚集在哀伤之城的主门前，成百上千的人。大部分是农民和平民，但我也认出了其中有几个小贵族。他们对新税收不满，对女王的离去感到不快。将军大人走向他们，试图平息他们的怒火，我们则用盾牌围住他，以防暴民接近他。前一天，一个帝国税务官在下阿玛莱西娅被从马车上拖下来用石头砸死了，所以我们不得不小心。<BR>

<BR>

<FONT COLOR="003300" >利武·瓦里斯，神殿管理员<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Val-Staag of the Vesturhola<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
In the hilly lands between the river Kart and the marsh-places of Hjaal there lived a tribe of Nords. These hill-folk deemed themselves Atmorans, yet none of Saarthal could remember them, nor their kin, and the sagas recalled no deeds done by their warriors. But they too quarrelled with the Falmer, hated as the elves were even in those days before the Tears.
<BR><BR>
So Ysgramor decided to send messengers to the western hills, to make palaver with these strange men who also fought against the elves, and to sing the skald-music as befits the making of peace between friends. For his envoys Ysgramor chose three: Bjaldr, a young warrior of renowned skill, Hranda, fairest of the skalds of Saarthal, and Qarl, called the Whale-Skin. Thus assembled, Ysgramor presented to his messengers a mighty wood-and-ivory spear, carved with fine likenesses of creatures from far Atmora. Then the king said: "I trust none but the true Northern Blood; if these hill-folk are indeed of that land, they will surely recognize these carvings." Then he dispatched his messengers amidst a winter storm.
<BR><BR>
But when Bjaldr, Hranda, and Qarl reached the western hills, they found themselves lost. None of the landmarks they sought appeared to the trio through the swirling snows, and all the world save the mighty thrust of the mountain now called Eldersblood looked as white as the purest Atmoran valley-blossoms. After a time, they came upon a deep valley, filled with bones of man and mer and beast alike. It was here that the three were set upon by elves.
<BR><BR>
Bjaldr gloried in the fighting, and with his axe slew the first elves to emerge from the hills. But Hralda and Qarl had seen more winters, and knew more of the elves' treachery, so they called out: "Come, Bjaldr, let us retreat from this place of death, and reconcile to ourselves the shape of this new land from the safety of the mountain."
<BR><BR>
But Bjaldr fought on, and replied, "Go then back to Elder-Blood, and take with you this fine wooden spear, placed in our keeping by our king Ysgramor. Take its length and break it in twain upon the mountain's shoulder, for to do so would bring upon us less dishonor than to retreat." Thus shamed by their companion, Hralda and Qarl Whale-Skin made ready to fight to their deaths against the unseen elves in the snow.
<BR><BR>
The three fought for hours against the elves, though their foe seemed limitless in number, and could move through the snow lighter of foot than the Nords. Many blows they parried, and for a time all three felt invincible. But Hralga was struck blind by an arrow to her eye, and Bjaldr took a cut to his axe-arm, so the three warriors prepared to make their end in glory as the elves closed in about them.
<BR><BR>
But as the warriors made their stand, a thunderous crack seemed to peel the snows from the cliffside, crashing down upon the elven host. Along the cliff-edge, the three saw a company of stout Nords, all wielding queer weapons made of stone and bronze, all towering in stature. Their leader was the largest of all, more than thrice the height of Bjaldr (who had in his youth been called the Tall) with rings of many metals sewn into his beard. When he spoke, his voice was like boulders crashing down a mountainside. "I am Val-Staag. Why have you come to my people's lands, and incited these elves to make further war upon us?"
<BR><BR>
The messengers responded, "Great Val-Staag, we sought you and your folk of the western hills. We carry a message from Ysgramor, of far Atmora, the mighty king of Saarthal." Hralga then began a battle-song, and Qarl knelt before Valstaag, presenting to him the great wooden spear. But when Val-Staag took the spear, he let out a great booming laughter, and it is said that his mirth was so loud it could be heard in Saarthal itself. "Why do you laugh?", asked Bjaldr, still bleeding from a dozen wounds. "We have fought bravely in defense of our honor, and that of our beloved king, to bring this to you. Do you not recognize the carven images upon its length?"
<BR><BR>
But Val-Staag replied, "Fear not, new friends, for it is not at your expense that I find merriment. I am old, and I have not seen such fine carvings from my home in many a year. In Atmora, such designs were made to adorn the mightiest of giant-axes, and crowned the holiest of our temples. I laugh at the unlikely honor of finding such mighty icons affixed to a tooth-pick such as this!"
<BR><BR>
Thus did Ysgramor' messengers win for Saarthal the friendship of Val-Staag and the men who dwelt in the western hills. For many years the two peoples traded in peace, but after the Five Hundred returned from Atmora to revenge the destruction of Saarthal, no signs of Val-Staag or his people were ever seen again.

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>

<BR><BR>

<BR><BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Vampires of the Iliac Bay<BR>
Part I<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
There are over one hundred distinct kinds of vampire in Tamriel. The Iliac Bay region alone has nine variations with unique powers and abilities. I have this information not only because I have been researching this blight of the world for the last ten years of my life, but because for the seven years before that, I was one of the creatures.<BR><BR>
Vampirism is a disease, like brain rot or cholera, but far, far more insidious. One can become a vampire through certain magical items or by the curse of a powerful wizard, but the most common cause is the bite or scratch of a vampire. There are no symptoms of vampirism except this -- if the victim sleeps after the attack but before he becomes a vampire, his sleep will be plagued with nightmares.<BR><BR>
During this two to four day period, when the disease has been spread but the victim is still mortal, most any temple healer can remove the curse of vampirism. There will be no further warning.<BR><BR>
I do not remember dying. I had been a scout for an order of knights which shall go nameless for this. A daughter of a local nobleman had been kidnapped by a mysterious character, and my captain had located his hideout. Deep in the dank underground chambers, I searched until I found the girl. Or what remained of her, a corpse the color of snow, drained of every drop of blood. I knew what the mystery man was right then, but he found me before I found the exit out. He took a good sized hunk out of my fighting arm before I managed to outrun him. I figured I was lucky to be alive. Some luck.<BR><BR>
My trip back to the knightly order was a five day journey. I decided to get some rest early to get my arm in better shape in case I found any more trouble. I can't remember the dreams I had that night -- only that I was doing something horrible and I couldn't stop myself. I woke up screaming. The next night, at an inn a little closer to my destination, my sleep was deep and dreamless. On the third night, I died.<BR><BR>
Of course, I didn't know that I died. I had gone to sleep in a nice warm feathered bed and I woke on a cold wet stone mortuary slab. Dazed, I opened the door to the mausoleum I was in, which I think must have been locked. I was in a cemetery not far from a town I knew, so I wandered in. It was late at night, so there were precious few souls in the streets. I paused to read a public notice and noticed the date. The date was two weeks later than I thought it must have been.<BR><BR>
As I puzzled over that, I saw a girl, a wench at my favorite tavern in that town, wandering toward me. I hailed her. She ignored me. I called her by her name, and she turned to me, smiling, but with an expression that told me she did not know who I was. I had visited her tavern on my way over to the mystery man's hideout, but she didn't know me!<BR><BR>
I told her my name. She angrily told me that it was a very poor joke, that I looked nothing like the brave knight who used to visit the town, and that if I didn't know he was dead.<BR><BR>
My emotions were a tangled skein. I could tell she was not joking, that I looked nothing like myself. I was touched by her sorrow at my death, and horrified by the idea dawning on me of what I had become. Suddenly, an overriding instinct overcame all my thoughts -- hunger. Without even thinking about what I was doing, I reached out and tore her throat open. I drained her until she looked like the corpse in the mystery man's dungeon.<BR><BR>
The rest of my story is told in Vampires of the Iliac Bay, Chapter II.<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
髂骨湾的吸血鬼<BR>
第一部分<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
泰姆瑞尔有一百多种不同的吸血鬼。仅髂骨湾地区就有九种具有独特力量和能力的变种。我之所以知道这些信息，不仅因为我过去十年一直在研究这种世界之灾，还因为在那之前的七年里，我曾是这些生物之一。<BR><BR>
吸血鬼化是一种疾病，类似于脑腐病或霍乱，但远比它们更隐蔽。一个人可以通过某些魔法物品或强大巫师的诅咒成为吸血鬼，但最常见的原因是吸血鬼的咬伤或抓伤。除了这一点外，吸血鬼化没有任何症状 -- 如果受害者在被攻击后、变成吸血鬼之前睡觉，他的睡眠将充满噩梦。<BR><BR>
在这两到四天的时间里，当疾病已经传播但受害者仍然是凡人时，几乎任何神殿的治疗师都可以移除吸血鬼化的诅咒。之后不会有进一步的警告。<BR><BR>
我不记得自己是怎么死的。我曾是一个骑士团的侦察兵，这里姑且不提其名号。当地一位贵族老爷的女儿被一个神秘人物绑架了，我的队长找到了他的藏身处。在潮湿的地下密室里，我搜寻着，直到找到了那个女孩。或者说，找到了她的遗骸，一具雪白的尸体，被吸干了每一滴血。我立刻知道那个神秘人是什么东西了，但他在我找到出口之前找到了我。在我设法逃脱之前，他从我用于战斗的手臂上咬下了一大块肉。我还以为自己能活下来很幸运。真是好运气。<BR><BR>
回到骑士团的旅程需要五天。我决定早点休息，让我的手臂恢复得更好些，以防再遇到麻烦。我不记得那晚做的梦了 -- 只记得我在做一些可怕的事情，而我无法阻止自己。我尖叫着醒来。第二天晚上，在离目的地更近一点的旅馆里，我睡得很沉，没有做梦。第三天晚上，我死了。<BR><BR>
当然，我并不知道自己已经死了。我在一张温暖舒适的羽绒床上入睡，却在一块又冷又湿的石头停尸板上醒来。我迷迷糊糊地打开了所在陵墓的门，我想那门应该是锁着的。我在一个离我认识的城镇不远的墓地里，于是我便走了进去。夜深了，街道上几乎空无一人。我停下来读一张公告，注意到了日期。那日期比我以为的晚了两个星期。<BR><BR>
正当我为此困惑时，我看到一个女孩，那是我最喜欢的酒馆里的侍女，正朝我走来。我跟她打招呼。她没理我。我叫她的名字，她转向我，微笑着，但那表情告诉我她不知道我是谁。我在去那个神秘人藏身处的路上曾去过她的酒馆，可她却不认识我！<BR><BR>
我告诉她我的名字。她生气地说这是个非常拙劣的笑话，我看起来一点也不像以前常来镇上的那位勇敢骑士，还说我难道不知道他已经死了吗。<BR><BR>
我的情绪一团乱麻。我看得出她不是在开玩笑，我看起来一点也不像我自己。我为她对我死亡的悲伤而感动，又为自己渐渐意识到自己变成了什么而感到恐惧。突然，一种压倒一切的本能占据了我所有的思绪 -- 饥饿。我甚至没想自己在做什么，伸出手，撕开了她的喉咙。我吸干了她，直到她看起来像那个神秘人地牢里的尸体。<BR><BR>
我故事的其余部分在《髂骨湾的吸血鬼》第二章中讲述。<BR>"""

I told in the first chapter of my story how I became a vampire and of my first kill. While it might (and, indeed, should) horrify the reader that my first victim was a friend of the mortal I used to be, it is my understanding that they are not uncommon first kills.<BR><BR>
I left the snow white corpse in the alley and ran to the only place I felt perversely safe, the mausoleum. For the first couple days of my undeath, I starved myself while I considered my fate. I relearned what I was capable of doing, and found that I was stronger, faster, tougher, and more agile than before. I had powers that as a knight I had only seen powerful mages wield. Later, I discovered additional abilities, such as a total immunity to disease. Helpful when descending on a plague-stricken city like a jackal.<BR><BR>
I also found my weaknesses. I could no longer stand the light of the sun -- exposure to it for longer than a few seconds burned me terribly. It also pained me to enter temples and other places of worship. The worst effect, of course, had to be my blood lust. If I did not kill a warm blooded creature once a night and drink its blood, my hunger would gnaw at me, and any wounds I suffered would not heal no matter how much I rested.<BR><BR>
Is this the moment for me to admit that there was a time I loved being a bloodsucking creature of the night? It is not impossible to live only at night, merely occasionally inconvenient. And I wouldn't have to kill humans every night, merely warm-blooded creatures. Orcs have a delicious, rich brothy blood; rats are a little sweet for the only meal of the night; werewolves are a real treat, almost decadent the tincture between human and beast. A real gourmet's delight.<BR><BR>
About a month after I died, I was having the best time of my life. One night, I received a letter from someone who said he was "family." Curious, I went to visit him at his tavern, and was told about the tribe of vampires to which I belonged -- the Montalion. In return for me performing certain duties for the "family," the man at the inn would train me in my vampiric abilities and skills.<BR><BR>
Though I never got very much detail, I surmised that the two main differences between the different vampire clans is geography and powers. Montalion alone have the gift for teleportation, but the other eight have powers of their own.<BR><BR>
My mentor (that is the title he used) would congratulate me after each mission I performed, and came to trust me more and more. If asked, he would tell me about the Montalion's newest alliances, who they were manipulating, who they were stalking. It was then I started to become frightened at last. They, and all of their rival clans, were draining the blood of Tamriel itself.<BR><BR>
I panicked. I had to find a cure. But nowhere could I find any book or rumor suggesting that vampirism is anything but permanent. So I resolved to kill myself, but I wanted to bring the Montalion down with me. I joined guilds they opposed, and failed any mission given to me spectacularly. I thought my mentor would turn against me, but he only became quieter, less forthcoming with information, never violent. He was not concerned. He had probably seen vampires like me before.<BR><BR>
Here's why he never attacked me: immortals can afford to be eternally patient.<BR><BR>
At last, he refused to give me any further missions. He wouldn't even talk with me, but he never left his tavern. I could come and go, and he'd watch but never talk. That's when I got another letter.<BR><BR>
There are several of us, you see, former vampires who know what to look for. We're patient too: we learned it in our unlife. We watch and listen, and anonymously contact the vampires we know wish to end the curse.<BR><BR>
Ending the curse is possible, but only just. It is very dangerous, but when you are cursed, the only real danger is no escape.<BR>"""

髂骨湾的吸血鬼<BR>

我在故事的第一章讲述了我如何变成吸血鬼以及我的第一次杀戮。我曾经的第一个受害者是我作为凡人时的朋友，这可能会（而且确实应该）令读者感到震惊，但据我所知，这种第一次杀戮并不罕见。<BR><BR>

现在是不是该承认我曾一度热爱成为夜间吸血的生物？只生活在夜晚并非不可能，只是偶尔不方便而已。而且我不必每晚都杀人，只需杀温血生物即可。兽人的血美味、浓郁，像肉汤；老鼠的血作为唯一的晚餐有点甜；狼人则是一种真正的享受，介于人与兽之间的味道几乎令人颓废。真正的美食家之乐。<BR><BR>
在我死后大约一个月，我正度过一生中最美好的时光。一天晚上，我收到了一封来自自称“家人”的人的信。出于好奇，我去他的酒馆拜访了他，并得知了我所属的吸血鬼部族 -- 蒙塔利昂。作为我为“家族”履行某些职责的回报，酒馆里的那个人会训练我的吸血鬼能力和技能。<BR><BR>
虽然我从没有得到太多细节，但我推测不同吸血鬼氏族之间的两个主要区别是地理和力量。只有蒙塔利昂拥有传送的天赋，而其他八个氏族各有各的力量。<BR><BR>
我的导师（他使用的头衔）会在我完成每次任务后祝贺我，并越来越信任我。如果我问起，他会告诉我蒙塔利昂最新的联盟，他们在操纵谁，在跟踪谁。那时，我终于开始感到害怕。他们，以及他们所有的敌对氏族，正在吸干泰姆瑞尔本身的鲜血。<BR><BR>
我惊慌失措。我必须找到解药。但我找不到任何书或谣言暗示吸血鬼化不是永久性的。所以我决定自杀，但我想拉蒙塔利昂一起陪葬。我加入了他们反对的公会，并以惊人的方式搞砸了交给我的每一项任务。我以为我的导师会与我反目，但他只是变得更沉默了，更不愿意透露信息，从未暴力相向。他并不担心。他可能以前见过像我这样的吸血鬼。<BR><BR>
这就是他从未攻击我的原因：不朽者能够承受永恒的耐心。<BR><BR>
最后，他拒绝再给我任何任务。他甚至不再和我说话，但他从未离开过他的酒馆。我可以自由进出，他会看着，但从不说话。就在这时，我收到了另一封信。<BR><BR>
你看，我们有好几个前吸血鬼，知道该寻找什么。我们也很有耐心：我们在亡灵生涯中学到了这一点。我们观察和倾听，并匿名联系我们所知道的希望结束诅咒的吸血鬼。<BR><BR>
结束诅咒是可能的，但也只是可能。这非常危险，但当你被诅咒时，唯一真正的危险是无路可逃。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Vampires of the Iliac Bay<BR>
Part I<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
There are over one hundred distinct kinds of vampire in Tamriel. The Iliac Bay region alone has nine variations with unique powers and abilities. I have this information not only because I have been researching this blight of the world for the last ten years of my life, but because for the seven years before that, I was one of the creatures.<BR><BR>
Vampirism is a disease, like brain rot or cholera, but far, far more insidious. One can become a vampire through certain magical items or by the curse of a powerful wizard, but the most common cause is the bite or scratch of a vampire. There are no symptoms of vampirism except this -- if the victim sleeps after the attack but before he becomes a vampire, his sleep will be plagued with nightmares.<BR><BR>
During this two to four day period, when the disease has been spread but the victim is still mortal, most any temple healer can remove the curse of vampirism. There will be no further warning.<BR><BR>
I do not remember dying. I had been a scout for an order of knights which shall go nameless for this. A daughter of a local nobleman had been kidnapped by a mysterious character, and my captain had located his hideout. Deep in the dank underground chambers, I searched until I found the girl. Or what remained of her, a corpse the color of snow, drained of every drop of blood. I knew what the mystery man was right then, but he found me before I found the exit out. He took a good sized hunk out of my fighting arm before I managed to outrun him. I figured I was lucky to be alive. Some luck.<BR><BR>
My trip back to the knightly order was a five day journey. I decided to get some rest early to get my arm in better shape in case I found any more trouble. I can't remember the dreams I had that night -- only that I was doing something horrible and I couldn't stop myself. I woke up screaming. The next night, at an inn a little closer to my destination, my sleep was deep and dreamless. On the third night, I died.<BR><BR>
Of course, I didn't know that I died. I had gone to sleep in a nice warm feathered bed and I woke on a cold wet stone mortuary slab. Dazed, I opened the door to the mausoleum I was in, which I think must have been locked. I was in a cemetery not far from a town I knew, so I wandered in. It was late at night, so there were precious few souls in the streets. I paused to read a public notice and noticed the date. The date was two weeks later than I thought it must have been.<BR><BR>
As I puzzled over that, I saw a girl, a wench at my favorite tavern in that town, wandering toward me. I hailed her. She ignored me. I called her by her name, and she turned to me, smiling, but with an expression that told me she did not know who I was. I had visited her tavern on my way over to the mystery man's hideout, but she didn't know me!<BR><BR>
I told her my name. She angrily told me that it was a very poor joke, that I looked nothing like the brave knight who used to visit the town, and that if I didn't know he was dead.<BR><BR>
My emotions were a tangled skein. I could tell she was not joking, that I looked nothing like myself. I was touched by her sorrow at my death, and horrified by the idea dawning on me of what I had become. Suddenly, an overriding instinct overcame all my thoughts -- hunger. Without even thinking about what I was doing, I reached out and tore her throat open. I drained her until she looked like the corpse in the mystery man's dungeon.<BR><BR>
The rest of my story is told in Vampires of the Iliac Bay, Chapter II.<BR>"""

Part II<BR><BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
