"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Way of the Exposed Palm<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Untrained pugilists are known to make a club of the hand and beat on their opponents like a drum. It is a truly uncouth way to victory. The way of the exposed palm is far more sophisticated and far more deadly.<BR>
<BR>
Consider this question. A man is struck in the chest by the flat of a plate. There is a small bruise but he is otherwise unharmed. Now break the plate and strike him in the chest with a shard using the same force. Now the man is dead or grievously wounded. How can this be? How can a small object harm more than a larger?<BR>
<BR>
This essential point is the first finger of the way of the exposed palm. The five part way is concentration, reaction, equilibrium, speed, breath control. To master unarmed combat all five digits must be mastered.<BR>
<BR>
The parable of the man and the plate is concentration. All of the blow is concentrated into a small point. Therefore it is more potent. To strike with just the thumb can be more deadly that to strike with the whole fist. However, only the highly trained fighter can do this.<BR>
<BR>
The second aspect of concentration is the mental discipline to think hard about what is being done. Distractions are ignored as the will maintains the ultimate goal. The truly deadly fighter can even block out his own pain in this manner.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
露掌之道<BR><BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
未经训练的拳斗士常将手攥成棒槌，像敲鼓般捶打对手。这等取胜之道，实在粗鄙不堪。露掌之道则精妙得多，也致命得多。<BR>
<BR>
试想此问：一人被盘子平面击中胸口，仅留下小块瘀伤，别无大碍。若将盘子击碎，用同样力道以碎片刺其胸口，此人便非死即重伤。此为何故？何以小物伤人甚于大物？<BR>
<BR>
此即为露掌之道的首要指法。其道有五，曰凝、应、衡、速、息。欲成徒手搏击之术，此五指缺一不可。<BR>
<BR>
人与盘之喻，关乎“凝”。将一击之力尽凝于一点，故而威力更甚。仅以拇指击人，或比拳击更为致命。然此事唯经严格训练之斗士方能为之。<BR>
<BR>
“凝”之第二要义，乃心志之训，需全神贯注于当下所行。摒除杂念，意志直指终局。真正致命的斗士，甚至能以此法隔绝自身之痛。<BR>

Wayrest, Jewel of the Bay
途歇城，海湾之珠

> BOOK.TEXT T_Bk_WayrestJewelOfTheBayHR
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Wayrest, Jewel of the Bay<BR>
by Sathyr Longleat<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Wayrest is one of the most glorious cities of western Tamriel: sparkling in her contemporary beauty, lustrous by her past. She is prized above all cities in High Rock -- no other city has contributed, and continues to contribute so much to the culture of the Bretons. The spirits of her genius children continue to haunt the streets; you can see them in the gabled roofs, grand boulevards, aromatic marketplaces. The people of Wayrest have an instinctive appreciation of their past, but are not obsessed by it, as the people of Daggerfall seem to be. One feels that one is in a modern city when one visits Wayrest, but there is a magic in the air that could only come from thirty-two centuries of civilization.<BR>
<BR> 
It is difficult for historians to declare a certain date for the foundation of Wayrest. A settlement of some variety had been existence where the Bjoulsae River feeds the Iliac Bay possibly since the 800th year of the First Era. The traders and fishermen of Wayrest were surrounded by hostile parties: the orc capitol Orsinium had grown like a poison weed to the north, and the Akaviri pirates and raiders crowded the islands to the west. There is no mystery to Wayrest's name. After the fighting most travellers had to endure passing through the eastern end of the Iliac Bay, the little fishing village on the Bjoulsae was a welcome rest.<BR>
<BR> 
Nowhere in the much vaunted censuses of the Skyrim Occupation is Wayrest mentioned. In the Annals of Daggerfall, King Joile's letter to Gaiden Shinji of the Order of Diagna contains the following reference: "The orcs have been much plaguing the Wayresters and impeding traffic to the heart of the land." The date given for the letter was 1E 948.<BR>
<BR> 
Wayrest only truly bloomed after the razing of Orsinium in 1E 980. The hard-working traders and merchants were instrumental in forming the Masconian Trade Way and thus reducing the pirate activity on the Bay. At this time, Wayrest occupied both banks of the Bjoulsae. A successful mercantile family, the Gardners, built a walled palace on the High Rock side of the river and, over time, allowed banks and other businesses within its walls. It was a Gardner, Farangel, who was proclaimed king when Wayrest accepted ambassadors from the Camorian Empire, and was granted the right to call itself a kingdom in the 1100th year of the 1st Era.<BR>
<BR> 
Although Wayrest became a kingdom under the command of one family, the merchants continued to wield incredible power. Many economists have alleged that Wayrest's eternal wealth, despite all her hardships, comes from this rare relationship between the merchants and the crown. The Gardner Dynasty fell, followed by the Cumberland Dynasty, which was followed by the Horley Dynasty, and finally, in the Third Era, the Septim Dynasty. No citizen of another kingdom of comparable age can, with one hand, name all the families who have ever ruled. Never has a king of Wayrest been deposed by revolution or assassination. Except for those of the Septim family, every king of Wayrest can trace his line back to a merchant prince of Wayrest. The merchants and king respect one another, and this relationship strengthens both.<BR>
<BR> 
One need only walk down the great boulevard of Wayrest to see physical proof of this unique alliance. Going north to south, Wayrest Boulevard suddenly divides, one half going west and the other going east. Both halfs end in identical squares: one at Castle Wayrest, the original palace of Aphren Gardner, and the other at Cumberland Square, where the oldest and wealthiest marketplace in Wayrest. The message here is clear: the king and the merchants are joined and equal.<BR>
<BR> 
Wayrest has survived blights, droughts, plagues, piracy, invasions, and war with good humor and practicality. In 1E 2702, the entire population of the city was forced to move into the walled estate of the Gardners as protection against the pirates, Akaviri raiders, and Thrassian plague. A less resourceful community would have withered, but the Wayresters have survived to enrich Tamriel generation after generation.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
途歇，海湾之珠<BR>
萨希尔·隆利特 著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
途歇是泰姆瑞尔西方最辉煌的城市之一：当代之美璀璨夺目，往昔之光辉映其间。它在高岩众城中地位尊崇，无出其右 -- 再没有哪座城市，曾为布莱顿文化贡献如此之多，并将持续贡献下去。她天才子嗣的英灵，依旧萦绕街巷；你可在人字屋顶、宽阔大道、香气氤氲的集市中窥见他们的身影。途歇人对其历史有本能的珍视，却不像匕落人那般沉溺其中。造访途歇，你感觉置身于一座现代都市，但空气中弥漫着一种，唯有三十二个世纪文明积淀才能孕育的魔力。<BR>
<BR>
史家难以断言途歇建城的确切时日。自第一纪元八百年许，彼欧塞河汇入髂骨湾之处，便已有某种聚落存在。彼时，途歇的商人与渔夫四面受敌：北边，兽人首都奥辛纽姆如毒草蔓延；西边岛屿，阿卡维尔海盗与掠袭者横行。途歇之名，并无玄妙。历经险阻，穿越髂骨湾东端的旅人们，在彼欧塞河畔这小渔村，终得一处舒心的休憩之所。<BR>
<BR>
天际统治时期那些被大肆吹嘘的人口调查中，并无途歇的踪影。在《匕落编年史》中，约伊尔国王致迪亚戈纳教团外传·真嗣的信中有如下记载：“兽人屡屡侵扰途歇居民，阻碍通往内陆腹地的交通。”信件的日期标为第一纪元948年。<BR>
<BR>
途歇真正的繁荣，始于第一纪元980年奥辛纽姆被夷平之后。勤劳的商贾们协力开辟了马斯康贸易航线，从而减少了海湾的海盗活动。彼时，途歇占据了彼欧塞河两岸。一个成功的商贾家族 -- 加德纳家族 -- 在河畔的高岩一侧建起了一座带围墙的宫殿，并随时间推移，允许银行等商业机构入驻其中。第一纪元1100年，当途歇接纳了卡莫里帝国的使节，并获准称王国时，被拥立为国王的，正是加德纳家族的成员 -- 法兰杰尔。<BR>
<BR>
尽管途歇成为由单一家族统治的王国，商人们的势力依旧强大。许多经济学家认为，途歇历经磨难而财富不竭，正源于商贾与王室之间这种罕见的关系。加德纳王朝之后是坎伯兰王朝，继而是霍利王朝，最终在第三纪元迎来了塞普汀王朝。其他年代相近的王国，其公民恐怕难用一个巴掌数清所有统治过的家族。途歇的国王，从未被革命或刺杀推翻过。除了塞普汀家族，途歇的每一位国王都能将血脉追溯至一位途歇的商界亲王。商人与国王彼此尊重，这种关系让双方都更加强大。<BR>
<BR>
只需漫步于途歇的大道，便能亲眼见证这独特联盟的明证。途歇大道自北向南，忽而分岔，一路向西，一路向东。两路的尽头，各是一方相似的广场：其一通往途歇城堡 -- 阿弗伦·加德纳最初的宫殿；其二则是坎伯兰广场 -- 途歇最古老、最富庶的集市所在。这寓意再明白不过：国王与商人，同心同德，并驾齐驱。<BR>
<BR>
途歇以乐观豁达与务实精神，度过了一次又一次的枯萎、干旱、瘟疫、海盗、入侵与战争。第一纪元2702年，全城居民被迫迁入加德纳家族的围墙庄园，以抵御海盗、阿卡维尔掠袭者与瑟拉斯瘟疫。换作其他不那么足智多谋的社群，或许早已凋零，但途歇人挺了过来，一代又一代地丰富着泰姆瑞尔。<BR>
<BR>"""

途歇是泰姆瑞尔西方最辉煌的城市之一：当代之美璀璨夺目，往昔之光辉映其间。它在高岩众城中地位尊崇，无出其右 -- 再没有哪座城市，曾为布莱顿文化贡献如此之多，并将持续贡献下去。她天才子嗣的英灵，依旧萦绕街巷；你可在人字屋顶、宽阔大道、香气氤氲的集市中窥见他们的身影。途歇人对其历史有本能的珍视，却不像匕落人那般沉溺其中。造访途歇，你感觉置身于一座现代都市，但空气中弥漫着一种，唯有三十二个世纪文明积淀才能孕育的魔力。<BR><BR>
史家难以断言途歇建城的确切时日。自第一纪元八百年许，彼欧塞河汇入髂骨湾之处，便已有某种聚落存在。彼时，途歇的商人与渔夫四面受敌：北边，兽人首都奥辛纽姆如毒草蔓延；西边岛屿，阿卡维尔海盗与掠袭者横行。途歇之名，并无玄妙。历经险阻，穿越髂骨湾东端的旅人们，在彼欧塞河畔这小渔村，终得一处舒心的休憩之所。<BR><BR>
天际统治时期那些被大肆吹嘘的人口调查中，并无途歇的踪影。在《匕落编年史》中，约伊尔国王致迪亚戈纳教团外传·真嗣的信中有如下记载：“兽人屡屡侵扰途歇居民，阻碍通往内陆腹地的交通。”信件的日期标为第一纪元948年。<BR><BR>
途歇真正的繁荣，始于第一纪元980年奥辛纽姆被夷平之后。勤劳的商贾们协力开辟了马斯康贸易航线，从而减少了海湾的海盗活动。彼时，途歇占据了彼欧塞河两岸。一个成功的商贾家族 -- 加德纳家族 -- 在河畔的高岩一侧建起了一座带围墙的宫殿，并随时间推移，允许银行等商业机构入驻其中。第一纪元1100年，当途歇接纳了卡莫里帝国的使节，并获准称王国时，被拥立为国王的，正是加德纳家族的成员 -- 法兰杰尔。<BR><BR>
尽管途歇成为由单一家族统治的王国，商人们的势力依旧强大。许多经济学家认为，途歇历经磨难而财富不竭，正源于商贾与王室之间这种罕见的关系。加德纳王朝之后是坎伯兰王朝，继而是霍利王朝，最终在第三纪元迎来了塞普汀王朝。其他年代相近的王国，其公民恐怕难用一个巴掌数清所有统治过的家族。途歇的国王，从未被革命或刺杀推翻过。除了塞普汀家族，途歇的每一位国王都能将血脉追溯至一位途歇的商界亲王。商人与国王彼此尊重，这种关系让双方都更加强大。<BR><BR>
只需漫步于途歇的大道，便能亲眼见证这独特联盟的明证。途歇大道自北向南，忽而分岔，一路向西，一路向东。两路的尽头，各是一方相似的广场：其一通往途歇城堡 -- 阿弗伦·加德纳最初的宫殿；其二则是坎伯兰广场 -- 途歇最古老、最富庶的集市所在。这寓意再明白不过：国王与商人，同心同德，并驾齐驱。<BR><BR>

便会过早衰亡。<BR>

万神殿已将其留给我们。<BR>
盲目的贪婪，再不能<BR>

重归此世。<BR><BR>

The Weight of Guilt
罪责之重

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
<BR>
Weight of Guilt<BR>
By Fuchon Cire<BR>
<BR>
It was deep in the month of Second Seed when a messenger brought a letter to my residence in Greenheart, which lies at the southern end of Valenwood. I presume similar letters were sent out to my various other residences, though considering the sharpness of the Emperor's eyes and ears, I would be not at all surprised to find that my location would be common knowledge within certain circles. At any rate the package was from near the heart of the Empire, a town just to the south of beautiful Cyrodiil itself. Breathless, the young messenger boy explained that the matter was of the utmost urgency, and I should, in all due haste, set sail for the capital.<BR>
<BR>
Upon unsealing and digesting the contents of the letter, I was much of the opinion of the youth. Given that the request for aid was issued by a member of the Blades, it was clearly not a small trifle. While it is true that I do have associations within that group, and had worked alongside them, as well as for them in the past, it is my experience that they typically like to keep things "in house," so to speak. That they had contacted me suggested that they had arrived at a dead end, in terms of their investigations.<BR>
<BR>
Ship rocking gently in Topal Bay on the way to my destination, I reread the package again, familiarizing myself with the case. It seems that in this town, certain citizens were being murdered at the rate of about two per week for three weeks. Then the killer struck the nephew of a Blades member, and that organization became heavily involved. Between the combined forces of the Blades and local law enforcement, little headway had been made.<BR>
<BR>
The author of the correspondence wrote that Intervention spells were not used, for after the first incident the nearest shrines were monitored, and there were no teleporting travelers at the times of the next few murders. The possibility that Recall was being used could not be discounted, but, the letter argued, some thought the killer might enjoy watching the chaos he'd left in his wake. I shook my head sadly, folded the letter back up, and placed it in my pocket.<BR>
<BR>
After we made landfall, I was greeted by Kevius Altenian, a fresh-faced youth who would see to my accommodations for the duration of the case; someone to worry about the trifles of room and board so I could remain wholly committed to the investigation. At times, I employ such people simply to hear them describe local rumors -- things that authorities might omit. The excitable fellow was somehow under the impression that I would have solved the case on the boat ride over, but that I had failed to draw any solid conclusions from the rather vague note did not seem to shake his confidence. He happily reached into his own pocket to pay a carriage to take us the remaining distance to the village.<BR>
<BR>
In town, Kevius led me to a nondescript two story house, which was, he said, the site of the first murder, and was currently serving as their headquarters of the investigation. As the victim had lived alone, there was no one left to protest it being used as such. The downstairs area contained four heavily armed and armored soldiers--Imperial Legion, by the designs--and two more common-looking individuals -- Blades. The Legionnaires visibly bristled when we entered, but a scarcely noticeable gesture from one of the Blades assured them all was in order. Normally, the Legion would be absent in such a case, but as with the Blades the killer had also struck the relative of a high-ranking Legionnaire.<BR>
<BR>
"Breton," one of the Blades--a burly redguard whose eyebrows met each other above his nose--greeted me casually. "My name is Sanrit. Let us survey the upstairs, hear your opinion, and we shall see if you've wasted a trip." Sanrit led the way to a staircase, down a short hall, and to a door. Knocking on the door, he said "Protectorate, you have a visitor." The door opened on a scene of carnage the likes of which I have rarely had the misfortune of seeing.<BR>
<BR>
Once upon a time, the room had clearly been something to behold. A sturdy bookcase lined one wall, opposite a large bed. Intricate designs had been carved into the wood of both, as well as the nightstand. A third wall, the one opposite the window, bore several pegs that would have held up a marvelous tapestry. Either during or after the killing, much of that had been laid waste. The bookcase was fractured, part of it leaning against a wall, another part wholly collapsed to the floor. The books it had held were strewn about the room, and were also partially shredded. Many loose pages had become stuck to the floor, as the blood soaking them had dried. The incredible craftsmanship displayed in the carvings similarly found itself obscured with blood, where it had not simply been scratched into unrecognizability. The window had but a few shards of glass left in it. As for the tapestries that once decorated the wall, they lay in hard, blood-dried piles on the floor. Even so, one could see where they had been torn. Remembering the package I'd been sent, I realized that this scene was three weeks old.<BR>
<BR>
"Anything you'd like to add?" asked the Protectorate bleakly. When I nodded, the fellow seemed shocked.<BR>
<BR>
"First of all, the victim likely knew the killer. Secondly, the window was used as a means of egress. Thirdly, the killer is in excellent physical condition, perhaps unnaturally so. And as a corollary, I do not believe any fortification spell was used -- you're looking for someone genuinely powerful." I paused, considering, "I may be able to deduce more, if I am allowed access to other scenes preserved similarly, and if I am allowed access to the bodies, assuming that they have not yet been disposed of."<BR>
<BR>
The Protectorate and Sanrit shot each other surprised looks. "I wouldn't mind getting a further opinion from you." the Sanrit said, "As to the first of your requests, the sites of the two most recent attacks have not yet been too much disturbed."<BR>
<BR>
"The first murder, and the last two? What of the other three sites?" I inquired.<BR>
<BR>
"One was at the inn, and the owner thoroughly cleaned the room in question. Can't rent out a slaughterhouse, he told me. The remaining two took place in homes occupied by families. Vile enough that children must be raised fatherless, but to make them live mere feet away from the undisturbed scene asks too much."<BR>
<BR>
"And the bodies?"<BR>
<BR>
"That may prove a touch more difficult. Three have been cremated, two buried. The last two -- which are indeed the last two -- are currently in the possession of a necromancer. Legally, they're her property, so you'll have to talk it over with her. I doubt she'll be receptive."<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
Once I had procured the name of the necromancer, who oddly enough was a Dunmer, I exited the building to inquire of her whereabouts to Kevius. He assured me that Artisa Arethi would not be too difficult to deal with; it seems that when she had first moved to Cyrodiil from Morrowind years ago, she was very defensive, and very, very private. As she realized that necromancy wasn't the absolute taboo in Cyrodiil that it was in Morrowind, she gradually softened her manner.<BR>
<BR>
Kevius was kind enough to give me directions to her home, but seemed taken aback when I made another request of him:<BR>
<BR>
"At the moment, I cannot tell you why, but I need for you to do something, not question it, and remain silent about it until further notice. Is this possible?" Cautiously, he agreed. "Very well, then. I want you to go to each of the houses these murders took place in, but I do not want you to enter any of them. You are to search around them, and try to find glass from a shattered window. Check the sites in the order they occurred. If you're able to find glass at one, sit and make sure no one disturbs it, and do not disturb it yourself. Are you willing to do this?" Kevius nodded with his regular animation.<BR>
<BR>
That done, we parted ways and I proceeded on to Artisa Arethi's home. Having seen necromancer's caves in Morrowind, as well as Velothi towers they seemed to enjoy invading, I must say a simple house was a nice change of pace. Artisa greeted me with surprising warmth, considering the situation.<BR>
<BR>
"Sera Fuchon," she explained "You must understand that -- despite my charm -- it is not everyone who offers their body to me to look after when they've passed to Oblivion. While I do pay surviving family members handsomely, there is a level of trust and familiarity involved. I mean, would you want your corpse handled by just anyone? No, I think not. So I must say, while having a number of bodies on hand is good for my practice, I'd rather have acquired them later in life. They were good sorts, and certainly undeserving of murder."<BR>
<BR>
"Then you would not mind showing me the bodies?" I asked hopefully.<BR>
<BR>
Artisa nodded. "Certainly. There are others who have promised me bodies, who I would similarly wish no ill upon. If doing so will help you identify or catch the killer, then I am at your service." she paused a moment, then went on cautiously "Sera Fuchon, I considered these people friends. While I'm not hunted as I would be back home, I do not have so many friends as to suffer much more loss." she resumed her normal speaking voice "I keep the bodies in the basement, on stone slabs. It's the coolest room in the house, and they keep better there. I do try not to offend the neighbors too much with the rot."<BR>
<BR>
As she began to lead me toward the stairs, she paused again, flustered. "Sera Fuchon, I almost forgot to warn you. And I -- I... let me explain... As you can see, I am not especially strong, or used to carrying around the weight of a dead body. There is someone in the basement for that, and it's... well, I'm not entirely sure it's legal to have him in the city. It's -- he's not -- that is... he's an Ogrim."<BR>
<BR>
"An Ogrim?" I considered thoughtfully, "Did you summon him?"<BR>
<BR>
"Well, yes. I doubt I could have snuck him into the city. I also doubt I could reproduce the spell; I'd been trying to summon a Daedroth -- takes up less space -- but I must have gotten something wrong. At any rate, he's cheaper to keep on than man or mer, he doesn't complain, and he follows direction. He does tend to... eat bodies when I've finished with them, though."<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
The basement was as Artisa described: stone and cold, the bodies resting peacefully on elevated slabs. And, of course, a titanic Ogrim filling one corner of the room. As I glanced at it, it stared back, perhaps not understanding why his mistress permitted me to be there. I looked away from it for a moment, turning my attention back to the corpse Artisa had led me to, when something nagged at me.<BR>
<BR>
Giving the Ogrim a more serious -- if distant -- inspection, I noticed that its massive hands had blood on them. As if finally shrugging off my presence, the Ogrim turned its back to me, and began doing something I could not see. I looked a question at Artisa, but she didn't seem to know what it was about. When I explained my concern to her, she smiled.<BR>
<BR>
"Oh sera, he's just eating. I used to get rats in here a few years ago, and he cleared that problem right up. Got a taste for them, I'm afraid. He likes them fresh -- live, that is -- but... but he prefers them tender too. So he..." Artisa balled her hand into a fist. "I can see your reason, though." As if to underscore her point, the cracking of bone could be heard from it's direction.<BR>
<BR>
That done, I began to look over the two bodies. Artisa had washed them, so it was much easier to see where and how they had sustained injury. Both were fairly well mangled, with long straight parallel cuts covering much of their bodies, and a number of deep gashes in their torsos. There were no large, obvious bruises that I could see, which was inconsistent with the scenes; if the victims had been as battered as their rooms and other injuries indicated, they weren't showing it as they should have.<BR>
<BR>
"Mistress Arethi, is there anything you can add? Did the spirits of these departed tell you anything?"<BR>
<BR>
She shook her head slowly, "I'm afraid they were already on their way to Oblivion when I received them. Nevus -- on your right -- wanted to know 'where the hairy thing went'. But he didn't seem too upset about it, just curious. Oblivion took him soon after." Artisa paused again, considering something. "I've heard a rumor... some people are saying a werewolf is to blame. With my big Ogrim here, I'm not too worried -- more just nervous -- but sera, can it really be true?"<BR>
<BR>
I scratched my chin, pondering "Right now, I'd be loath to say. I would like to know more before I begin throwing accusations around. In that cause... Not to assume too much mistress, but given your closeness to these victims, what could you tell me about their lives?"<BR>
<BR>
If Artisa was put off by my resumed questioning, she seemed at least understanding. "Nevus, whom you've already 'met', was an alchemist. He carried all manner of rare plants, and other such exotic items. He... he used to laugh that people complained about the smell of some of his concoctions while no one said a word about my corpses. The second victim, the one the Blades got all in a huff about, was a good friend of his. The other of my guests was Gratinius Dolan, an enchanter. He used to tell me about extraordinary items he made free of charge for Blades -- very concerned about the safety of the Empire, that one. Once, he offered to enchant the stone in the basement to keep my guests even colder, but I didn't want to impose. They were good, honest men."<BR>
<BR>
I nodded, "Thank you very much, mistress. I hope I have not taken up too much of your time."<BR>
<BR>
"Not at all" she assured me.<BR>
<BR>
With that, I bid her farewell, and began a circuit of the crime scenes trying to track down Kevius. I found him at the fifth scene, playing with a bit of straw in an alley. Every few moments, he would look down one side of the alley, then the other, obviously bored. When he spotted me, his relief was visible.<BR>
<BR>
"The others had been cleaned up already" he greeted me, "And sweepers came while I waited here. I shooed them off, but I'm afraid them may have gone to the last house already. But one is better than none, I hope."<BR>
<BR>
"I hope, too."<BR>
<BR>
I bent to inspect the small scattering of glass on the floor of the alley. Glass on stone, clear enough, but something was lacking. Something vital. I asked Kevius if he had noticed anything odd about it, but he just shook his head in confusion.<BR>
<BR>
"Did you see any of the murder scenes?" I asked patiently. When he nodded, I continued "The carnage, the blood everywhere. The walls, the floors, even the ceiling. Remember the ceiling? There are prints of the entire body, as if someone threw them up there, bleeding. Now I ask you: How does one soak so thoroughly in blood, leave bloody smears on the window sill, and leave no trace of it on the glass at our feet?" The boy stammered in surprise for a moment before I gave him the conclusion. "Someone escaped through the window of each scene, but that person did so while the victim was still alive. Whoever broke those windows is not the killer."<BR>
<BR>
As I stepped him through it, his face became progressively brighter, and before I could say that the person was a possible witness as to the real killer's identity, young Kevius shouted "May the gods be praised!"<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
Suddenly, Kevius' enthusiasm and interest in the case became clear, as he stammered to explain. "My father lives in Solstheim, working for the East Empire Company. Last month, I visited him there with news that my sister had finally decided to settle down with a good, charming fellow. While I was there enjoying the crisp air outside of Fort Frostmoth, there was some trouble with werewolves. One of them pounced on me, all fangs and drool, so I screamed for help. Well-armed guards were quick to respond, and chased off the beasts. I was checked for signs of injury, and finding none, I was released. Unfortunately for me, it seems it never occurred to the guard that the disease they carry is transmitted by saliva, not truly by bite; there was not a mark upon my body, they said, so I must be fine. I failed to tell them that I had swallowed and gagged upon the fetid spittle that thing rained on me. At that point though, my business in Fort Frostmoth had concluded, and not being one for pointless boring travel, I recalled back to my house in Cyrodiil."<BR>
<BR>
Stopping for breath for a moment, he continued shortly. "All was normal for a time, but after a few days, as night began to fall, I knew something was not quite right. I did not know at the time what was bothering me, though I suspected the worst. With that fear in mind, I went to see Crantilius Vasius. He had a brother in the Legion, so I thought he might know what to do to take care of the infection. I remember opening up his door, sweat pouring down my face, him greeting me, asking what was wrong, and then a blur. In the morning, I discovered Crantilius had been murdered. I was numbed by crushing guilt, because surely I was the one to do it. Throughout the day, I was too afraid to do anything. Then as darkness came, I panicked. I ran to see Gralilan Tulius; he had connections to the Blades -- I didn't know what connections -- and surely the Blades know everything about everything, or could find it out. Gralilan would be able to find me a cure, before I did too much more damage."<BR>
<BR>
"But morning came, and no cure had I. Gralilan lay dead in his house, and I was still alive, and still thought myself guilty. I left town, and sought out a cave that had been home to bandits before the Legion cleared them out. Bringing a few meager possessions, I magically locked the door and waited. When morning came again, I unlocked the door, hurried to town, and was overjoyed that no one had been killed in the night. That cave became my home. But after a week, there was another murder -- Falinia Rescius, an apothecary -- again someone I might have gone to for help. The door to my cave was intact, still locked, but the dirt and rock around it's bottom had been cleared away by desperate clawed hands. It was enough to slide under without disturbing the door."<BR>
<BR>
"Besides the overwhelming guilt, I began to feel a deep, gnawing hunger. As if despite my killing, I would never be satisfied. Horrified, I sat in my cave and tried to think of who else might be able to help me. Sadly, to date those people have all been victims. Crantilius and Gralilan, then Falinia Rescius, Ysronmir the sorcerer I thought might be able to at least paralyze me overnight, Vonvild the summoner I thought could contact something knowledgeable from Oblivion to cure me, Nevus the alchemist might have a potion to cure me, Gratinius the enchanter might craft something to suppress the disease. I... I thought when you arrived, you might solve the crimes, and find me. E -- Even though I knew I was guilty, I thought you might know some treatment for me. I was afraid you'd be my next victim."<BR>
<BR>
I blinked in astonishment. I knew a werewolf had been involved, and that the poor afflicted person was not the killer -- or rather, not this particular killer -- I had no idea it was someone right under my nose. I started slowly "So you remember breaking the windows, or the sound of it, maybe, in your hazy nighttime antics?"<BR>
<BR>
"I... well, sort of. I think it more convincing that I would wake up with shards still on me. But... but my arm was always so bloody..."<BR>
<BR>
"Do you mind if I had a look at it?" I asked, still feeling somewhat surreal. When he rolled up his sleeve, I immediately knew what had happened, and explained it to him. "You sought out those who could help you, as you feverishly stumbled about town on the verge of transformation. Seeing you in such terrible shape, your saviours would let you in and begin looking you over. Either when the transformation struck, or perhaps before, you would escape through a window, as to avoid harming them. I'm not sure where you went after that, but surely somewhere out of town. Though bloodlust consumed you, even as a werewolf you could not harm another. Just look at your arm! You must have sat somewhere in the darkness, gnawing on it to keep the worst of your hunger at bay."<BR>
<BR>
Suddenly, my mood darkened again. I knew who the killer was, and it troubled me. Yet besides Kevius' visiting the victims, it was the only other connection I could find between them, though it did not connect all of them. The conclusion was that the killer only intended to strike down a few of Kevius' saviours, but killed them all so as to more thoroughly frame Kevius.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
"I'm afraid I'll need your help again" I told Kevius. "That Protectorate fellow watching over the scene of the first murder, I need you to speak with him. Tell him I will have some interesting news for him, and to meet me at Artisa Arethi's house. Be sure to inform that Blade Sanrit as well; it is his investigation, after all."<BR>
<BR>
Bright and eager as before, Kevius did not hesitate. "Of course!" and immediately ran off.<BR>
<BR>
For my part, I hurried over to mistress Arethi's house myself, to explain and justify all the company she was about to have. She seemed a bit worried that I intended to show them to the basement, with the Ogrim hanging about, but I assured her that -- as unlikely as it sounded -- they would not only not mind, but be happy the beast was there. Besides that small concern, the young Dunmer was surprisingly accommodating.<BR>
<BR>
Minutes later, Kevius arrived, Sanrit and the Protectorate in tow. They both looked confused, though Sanrit also put his curiosity into words.<BR>
<BR>
"What purpose here? We've been following this case for weeks. Breton, we are well familiar with the injuries to the bodies, if that is what you intend to shed light upon."<BR>
<BR>
I smiled confidently. "Oh, the injuries are just a part of it. If you're bored with them, I'm sure there will be other items more of interest. I do not pretend to have all the pieces, but I've fit together what I've been handed very well."<BR>
<BR>
Sanrit and the Protectorate looked uneasily about as we descended the stairway to the basement. The sudden chill, the corpses, and the Ogrim would surely have a similar effect on most anyone. I walked around the raised stone slabs silently for a moment while the others collected their bearings. Perhaps nervous in the presence of a law enforcement official, Artisa gravitated toward me. Kevius studied the walls, resolutely refusing to look at the corpses he had never been responsible for. The Blade and Protectorate stood near the door, as far away from the Ogrim as possible. The Ogrim paid us no mind.<BR>
<BR>
"Well, I must admit some hesitancy. I truly do not know where to begin." I began slowly, "I'm sure you all remember Gralilan Tulius, the second victim, nephew of a Blade. With his passing, I think I do him no wrong by saying this: while it's true that he was such a nephew, I found it curious that it was not mentioned that he himself was a member of that organization." I raised a hand for silence, as the assembly grew noisy. "No, it was not any particular skill on my part that uncovered that truth. Just mere chance. I knew the victim years ago, and worked with him on another case."<BR>
<BR>
"Now, I know you investigators have been looking for a werewolf, but though you may find one, it won't be your killer. One of you knows what I'm talking about..." I trailed off, hoping the guilty party would expose themself. "... But it appears that person is waiting to be thoroughly convinced of what they already know. Oh well."<BR>
<BR>
I walked over to the body of Nevus, and gestured the rest to watch closely. Pointing to the long, even cuts on his torso, I continued. "See these wounds? They were parallel, so it was easy enough to pass them off as marks from a werewolf's claws. But if you are familiar with claw marks, you would see that these gouges are too straight. They are, in fact, not gouges at all. This type of injury comes from a blade; it's a cut, not a scratch, and it's intentionally made to look like it was inflicted by an animal. As you may or may not be aware, werewolves do not use weapons, at least not in lupine form. So the killer must be someone more conventional."<BR>
<BR>
"So then, the killer was aware of the werewolf, and indeed sought his victims out based on the werewolf's movements. The killer knows who the werewolf is. Public suspicion being what it is, the killer would have been able to hand his scapegoat over to the authorities at any time, and no one would have ever known he was the true killer. Why is the wolf still free, then? Because the killer knew I was coming. Because the killer knew the wolf would seek me out, and that would give him the opportunity to kill me and erase any doubt about the werewolf's guilt."<BR>
<BR>
"Now, since the guilty party has insisted on holding their tongue, I shall give the largest clue: The murderer knew I was coming to investigate well in advance of my arrival. Who would know that? The person in charge of the investigation, of course." I rounded on him, pointing an accusatory finger "Sanrit."<BR>
<BR>
I didn't know such a thing was possible, but the already dark redguard's face darkened further. He looked at the Protectorate in contempt, then said "Of course I did it, fool. You have uncovered so much in a day, you think I'm so inept that I would be stymied even after three weeks? I kept the Protectorate following false leads and outright fabricated leads because I didn't want this case solved. And I was in position to make sure it never was. When I finally did turn in Kevius, I would have blamed the pace of the investigation on these idiotic Protectorate."<BR>
<BR>
I nodded toward Sanrit, and went on. "Now that you have been so kind as to admit your crimes, would you resolve one last matter for me? I have my suspicions, but not certainty. Why kill anyone?"<BR>
<BR>
Sanrit shook his head in negation. "Little point wasting my breath, when I intend to kill you all, and let Kevius take the fall." He drew his sword and stalked toward me. I felt Artisa's arms close around me, seeking safety, and then I heard it. Moving with surprising speed and grace for it's bulk, the Ogrim swept us all behind it and roared ferociously at Sanrit. Jumping to see over the creature's massive shoulder, I saw the blood drain out of Sanrit's face. On my next jump, the redguard turned and ran.<BR>
<BR>
I half-leapt, half-climbed over the Ogrim and drew my own sword. Never had I had call to use the katana before, though as a gentleman's weapon I practiced with it often enough. Now was not the time for second-guessing, or hesitation. A killer would soon be loose in the streets.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
I chased Sanrit up one flight of stairs, and saw him pause in the living room. His hesitation told me he was weighing his chances of making it out the front door in time to elude me. Apparently, he thought it not worth the risk, and instead ran up another flight of stairs. Hot on his heels, I heard a crash ahead of me as he fled out of a window in what appeared to be Artisa's bedroom. I did not have time to ponder the irony that Kevius, scapegoat for the murders, had fled similarly so many times before. All I could do was follow Sanrit, as he leapt from one rooftop to the next. I feared he might start feeling the adrenaline rush redguards are so known for; if he did and kept running, I would never be able to catch up to him... and if he did and turned to fight, I did not know if I could hope to match him in combat.<BR>
<BR>
Three rooftops later, the burly fellow made up his mind. Just as I made the jump, he spun around and buried his free hand into my midsection. I tried to roll with the blow, though it wasn't the sort of blow one can truly roll from. I came to a stop laying on my back, and raised my katana to cover my face just as Sanrit lowered his blade in an attempt to decapitate me. The power behind his swing was such that he nearly succeeded anyhow. Kicking his legs out from beneath him, I sprang back to my feet and took on a traditional sparring stance.<BR>
<BR>
The murderous redguard quickly got up, and struck at me quickly and angrily. I parried each thrust, giving ground as I did so. I made a feint at his thigh to buy me enough time to jump to the next rooftop; having given so much ground on Sanrit's assault, I did not have a lot of roof left to work with for a second attack. There was the possibility that he might start running again, but I rightly banked on his wanting to see this impromptu duel through to the end.<BR>
<BR>
In his leap over, Sanrit twisted his body around to give himself a wide arcing swing, to make sure I would not take advantage of him as he did of me. It kept me from continuing immediately, but such twists inevitably leave an area open. I quickly lashed out as his exposed back, careful to hit him with the flat of my blade; while he may have no qualms about killing, I would much rather capture a criminal than slay one.<BR>
<BR>
My strike disrupted his balance on the tilted roof long enough for me to get in a second hit, this time on the wrist of his sword arm. The result went as I'd hoped: The sword flew from his hand. However, I had not imagined how fast the redguard could be, for he snatched the longsword out of the air with his other hand, and instantly turned to attack again. I had not counted on ambidexterity. A savage smile on his face, he trust at me again and again, slashing alternately at my arms and head.<BR>
<BR>
Running out of rooftop once more, I made my final jump, choosing the building carefully. I backed away from the edge as Sanrit followed. While he closed the distance, I switched the katana to my other hand; the heavy blows of an adrenaline fed redguard are enough to exhaust most any swordsman. As we crossed swords, I finally realized that I would not be able to weather the hail of shots he could lay down. He was simply too quick, too strong, and too unrelenting, and I was too unwilling to cause injury.<BR>
<BR>
We continued on until the last in a series of three strikes was so overwhelmingly powerful that I lost my footing. Finally triumphant, the redguard readied for one final death-dealing chop. He had had the luxury of having his mind on the battle the entire time, while I had not. Though he stood over me, victory within his grasp, now was the time my extracurricular thinking would pay off. Rolling away from him to create some distance, I cast an incredible burden spell at him. Sanrit had no time to react.<BR>
<BR>
The roof collapsed under his now-colossal weight, and he dropped into the building unceremoniously. Placement had concerned me quite a bit, but looking down into the gap, I saw my fears hadn't come true. Sanrit had fallen through the roof of the Protectorate compound, convenient right into an unoccupied jail cell. With Protectorate all around him, the clouds visible through the hole would likely be the last sky he would be seeing for some time.<BR>
<BR>
As an investigator though, one question still nagged at me: Why? I would not be satisfied with the conclusion until I knew what had driven the redguard to kill.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
Because Sanrit had admitted to the murders in the presence of one of the Protectorate, he knew his fate was pretty well sealed. As such, he did not object to answering my questions. From his responses, a clear picture began to emerge.<BR>
<BR>
When there are two Blades in a city, and one does not know of the other (As Sanrit did not know of Gralilan Tulius), there are typically two reasons: They're investigating separate, unconnected matters, or one outranks the other. Given the sensitive nature of their work, it's not uncommon for a Blade to have no direct correspondence with his superiors. Such was the case with Gralilan and Sanrit, and Sanrit was unhappy with the orders his unknown boss had been issuing. "A waste of his talents", as Sanrit himself said. If something were to happen to Gralilan, Sanrit believed he would be the one to take his place, and perhaps more importantly, his rank.<BR>
<BR>
It was through a casual conversation with Crantilius Vasius that Sanrit discovered who had been wasting his talents. Crantilius had made the mistake of assuming Sanrit already knew of his fellow Blade. The wheels in his head turning, Sanrit began to plot the demise of his superior. But once Crantilius heard that Gralilan's position was not common knowledge, he might grow suspicious of Sanrit. That was why Crantilius was the first victim; it was sheer luck that Kevius visited him on the same night.<BR>
<BR>
Taken aback by the sudden appearance of the werewolf, Sanrit decided to mock up the scene as if the werewolf had killed the man. After that, the redguard made every effort to find out the identity of the wolf; capturing it would certainly be a bright spot in his career. He could not imagine his good fortune when, the very next night, he followed Kevius to Gralilan's house. It seemed almost too good to be true, but Sanrit was not one to look a gift horse in the mouth.<BR>
<BR>
Once Gralilan had been murdered, and it became apparent there was a killer in town, Sanrit was immediately given the rank he so desired, and was placed in charge of the case as his first duty. Another Blade would have been sent, but it was thought Sanrit would be better suited, given that he was already familiar with the town and it's inhabitants. The Protectorate didn't make much fuss about having the investigation taken away because the graphic nature of the crimes disturbed so many of them.<BR>
<BR>
Now Sanrit had what he wanted, and could have turned in Kevius right then and there. But he worried that someone else might have known Gralilan's position, that his benefiting from the murder would seen suspicious. He knew Nevus was a close friend of Gralilan's (even though he hadn't known Gralilan was a Blade, he had known of him), but he couldn't think of a way to kill him without drawing suspicion; two killers in town would seem a terrible coincidence. With that in mind, he killed Falinia Rescius, Ysronmir, and Vonvild, to keep pace with his werewolf scapegoat.<BR>
<BR>
Around that time, it dawned on him that Kevius was seeking out those who might be able to treat his condition. Again, Sanrit laughed at his luck -- surely Kevius would visit the problematic alchemist, and give ample opportunity for his slaying. The redguard had intended to turn in Kevius immediately after that, but fate, it seems, suddenly stopped in it's favor toward him.<BR>
<BR>
Dissatisfied with the course of the investigation and it's rising body count, the Protectorate officer assigned to the case asked a Blade friend of his to request my aid. The officer informed Sanrit of his actions, and so Kevius remained free. Sanrit thought that Kevius would seek me out in the hopes I would have him jailed (and so be unable to hurt others). On one hand, Sanrit hoped Kevius would assume all the blame for the murders and I wouldn't question it. On the other, if I looked too hard into the case, he could always murder me and lay the guilt on Kevius once again. Gratinius Dolan was killed as Sanrit waited for my arrival. It is true that Gratinius also knew of Gralilan's rank through his charity, but Sanrit banked on his ability to manipulate Gratinius' fierce loyalty to the Empire to keep him from making any accusations.<BR>
<BR>
Sanrit was a powerful man, and his power was augmented by the adrenaline rush redguards are feared for. It was how he caused such destruction in the rooms where his victims were found. It was how he subdued his victims so quickly, though surprise certainly played it's role too (how many people witness a werewolf's transformation, then have a potential defender draw a sword on them?). It was how he tossed the bodies up with such ease, to leave bloody full-body prints on ceilings. Once he calmed himself, then he would make sure to inflict the "telltale clawmarks" on the bodies with his sword. Afterwards, he exited through the window that had already been broken by Kevius -- which was why the sill had blood on it, but not the glass. He could not very well go walking through town looking like a butcher without drawing curiosity.<BR>
<BR>
Sanrit undoubtedly bore me ill will, for if not for my intervention he may have gotten away with his crimes. I have not spent too much time worrying about vengeance, though. Because he murdered a fellow Blade, treason was among his charges; piled on top of seven murder charges (Crantilius, Gralilan, Falinia, Ysronmir, Vonvild, Nevus, and Gratinius), he did not keep the executioner long waiting.<BR>
<BR>
As for Kevius, he finally found someone to help him with his lycanthropy. As an unconventional disease, it's cure is known in the usual unconventional circles, and as a necromancer, Artisa Arethi was familiar with some rather unconventional circles. Because he never actually harmed anyone other than himself during his time as a werewolf, no charges were brought against him. He did, however, pay for the replacement of the windows he shattered. Maybe the weight of guilt had been removed from his shoulders, but his sense of responsibility remained intact. <BR>"""

<BR>
罪责之重<BR>
弗孔·西尔 著<BR>
<BR>
正值次种月深，一名信使将一封信送至我在绿心的寓所，绿心位于瓦伦伍德最南端。我想，类似的信想必也送去了我其他的住处，不过，考虑到皇帝的眼目之敏锐，我发现自己身处何地，在某些圈子里乃是常识，倒也不会感到丝毫意外。无论如何，这包裹来自帝国心脏附近，就在美丽的西罗帝尔以南的一个小镇。年轻的信使气喘吁吁地解释，此事十万火急，我必须尽快起航前往帝都。<BR>
<BR>
拆开信封，阅毕信函内容，我与那少年看法一致。既然求助是由刀锋成员发出，显然绝非小事一桩。诚然，我与该组织确有渊源，曾与他们并肩作战，也曾为他们效力，但据我所知，他们通常喜欢“内部解决”。他们联系我，说明他们的调查已然走进了死胡同。<BR>
<BR>
船只在托帕尔湾轻柔地摇晃，载着我驶向目的地。我再次拆读包裹，熟悉案情。似乎在那镇上，连续三周，每周约有两人遇害。随后，凶手袭击了刀锋成员的侄子，该组织便全力介入。然而，刀锋与地方执法部门合力，却进展甚微。<BR>
<BR>
信的作者写道，并未使用神佑干涉法术，因为第一次案发后，最近的圣祠便被监视起来，而随后几起谋杀发生时，也无传送的旅行者出现。使用“召回”法术的可能性不能排除，但信中认为，也有人觉得凶手或许乐于欣赏自己留下的混乱景象。我悲哀地摇了摇头，将信折好，放回口袋。<BR>
<BR>
登陆后，迎接我的是凯维乌斯·阿尔特尼安，一个面容青涩的年轻人。他将负责我在案件期间的食宿事宜；有个能操心这些琐碎的人，我便可全心投入调查。有时，我雇用这样的人，只为听他们讲述当地的流言 -- 那些当局可能忽略的事。这兴奋的小伙子不知为何，以为我在船上就能破案，不过，我没能从那语焉不详的信中得出什么确凿结论，似乎也并未动摇他的信心。他高兴地自掏腰包，雇了辆马车，载我们走完去村子的最后一段路。<BR>
<BR>
到了镇上，凯维乌斯带我来到一栋不起眼的两层小楼前。他说，这便是第一起命案现场，目前正被用作调查指挥部。因死者独居，倒也无人反对。楼下有四名全副武装、身着甲胄的士兵 -- 看纹章应是帝国军团 -- 还有两名装束寻常的人 -- 刀锋。我们进去时，军团士兵们明显警惕起来，但一名刀锋成员做了个几不可察的手势，他们便安心下来。通常情况下，此类案件不会有军团介入，但凶手和对付刀锋一样，也杀害了一名高阶军团士兵的亲属。<BR>
<BR>
“布莱顿人，”一名刀锋成员 -- 一个壮实的红卫人，眉毛在鼻梁上连成一线 -- 随意地招呼我，“我叫桑里特。我们先上楼看看，听听你的高见，也好看看你这趟是否白来了。”桑里特引路上了楼梯，穿过一段短廊，来到一扇门前。他敲了敲门，道：“护法官，有客来访。”门开了，映入眼帘的，是我毕生罕见的那般惨状。<BR>
<BR>
曾几何时，这房间定是赏心悦目。一面墙立着结实的书架，对面是一张大床。书架的木头、大床以及床头柜上，都雕着繁复精美的图案。第三面墙，也就是窗对面的那面，有几个挂钉，曾挂着精美的挂毯。惨案发生之际或之后，这些大多被毁坏了。书架碎裂，一部分歪斜地靠着墙，另一部分则完全坍塌在地。其上书籍散落四处，也有不少被撕得支离破碎。许多散落的纸张，因浸透鲜血又已干涸，粘在地板上。那些精美雕刻，即使没被刮得面目全非，也被血渍遮蔽。窗上的玻璃所剩无几。至于曾装饰墙壁的挂毯，则成了地上几堆干涸凝血的硬块。尽管如此，仍能看出被撕裂的痕迹。回想起我收到的那封包裹，我意识到，这已是三周前的现场了。<BR>
<BR>
“有何高见？”护法官语气阴郁地问道。我点点头，那人似乎有些惊讶。<BR>
<BR>
“首先，受害者很可能认识凶手。其次，凶手是从窗户逃走的。第三，凶手身体条件极佳，甚至可能异于常人。由此可推断，凶手并未使用强化法术 -- 你们要找的人，本身就拥有强大的力量。”我顿了顿，思索道，“若能让我查看其他保存完好的现场，再让我看看尸体（假设还未处理的话），或许能推断出更多。”<BR>
<BR>
护法官和桑里特对视一眼，颇感意外。“我倒不介意听听你的进一步见解。”桑里特说道，“至于你的第一个请求，最近两次袭击的现场，还未被过多破坏。”<BR>
<BR>
“第一起和最后两起？另外三处现场呢？”我问道。<BR>
<BR>
“一处是在客栈，老板把那间房彻底打扫了。他跟我说，总不能把屠宰场租出去吧。剩下两处，是在有家眷的房子里。孩子们没了父亲已是够惨，再让他们住在几英尺外、原封不动的凶案现场，也太过分了。”<BR>
<BR>
“那尸体呢？”<BR>
<BR>
“这恐怕有点麻烦。三具已火化，两具下葬。最后两具 -- 确实是最后两具 -- 现在归一位死灵法师所有。从法律上讲，那是她的财产，你得跟她谈谈。我怀疑她不会乐意。”<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
我问到那死灵法师的名字，说来也怪，是个丹莫。我出门找凯维乌斯打听她的下落。他向我保证，阿尔蒂萨·阿雷提不难相处；似乎多年前她刚自晨风迁至西罗帝尔时，很是戒备，且极其注重隐私。后来她意识到，死灵法术在西罗帝尔并非如在晨风那般绝对的禁忌，态度才逐渐缓和。<BR>
<BR>
凯维乌斯好心为我指了去她家的路，但当我向他提出另一个请求时，他似乎吃了一惊：<BR>
<BR>
“眼下，我还不能告诉你原因，但我需要你做件事。不要问为什么，且暂守口如瓶。能做到吗？”他谨慎地答应了。“很好。我要你去每处案发房屋，但不要进去。在房屋周围搜寻，寻找破碎窗户的玻璃碎片。按案发顺序逐一检查。如果某处找到了玻璃，就守在那里，确保无人破坏，你自己也不要动它。愿意做吗？”凯维乌斯一如既往地热忱地点了点头。<BR>
<BR>
交代完毕，我们便分头行动，我径直前往阿尔蒂萨·阿雷提的住所。我见识过晨风的死灵法师洞穴，也见过他们似乎热衷占据的维洛提塔楼，不得不说，这简朴的房屋倒是个不错的转变。阿尔蒂萨以出人意料的热情迎接了我，考虑到这情形。<BR>

<BR>
“那您不介意让我看看尸体吧？”我满怀希望地问道。<BR>
<BR>
阿尔蒂萨点点头。“当然可以。还有几位答应将遗体给我的，我也同样希望他们平安无事。若这能助您查明凶手，找出真凶，我自当效劳。”她顿了顿，又谨慎地说，“弗孔阁下，我把这些人当朋友。虽然在此地我不会像在家乡那样被追捕，但朋友也不多，经不起再失去更多了。”她恢复正常的语调，“我将遗体保存在地下室，放在石板上。那里是屋里最凉爽之处，更宜保存。我也尽量不让腐臭味太过打扰邻居。”<BR>
<BR>
她正要领我下楼，又停了下来，显得有些慌乱。“弗孔阁下，我差点忘了提醒您。我 -- 我......让我解释一下......您也看到了，我力气不大，也不习惯搬运死者的重量。地下室里有个帮手，它......嗯，我不太确定把它留在城里是否合法。它 -- 它不是 -- 就是说......它是个欧格林。”<BR>
<BR>
“欧格林？”我若有所思，“是您召唤来的？”<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，是的。我怀疑我能否把他偷偷带进城。我大概也无法重现那法术；我本想召唤个代德洛斯 -- 占地方小 -- 但肯定是哪里出了岔子。不管怎样，养他可比养人或者精灵便宜多了，他也不抱怨，又听话。只是，我用完尸体后，他往往会把它们......吃掉。”<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
地下室一如阿尔蒂萨所言：石头砌成，寒气逼人，尸体安详地躺在高架石板上。当然，还有个巨大的欧格林塞在角落里。我瞥它一眼，它也回瞪着我，或许不明白它的女主人为何让我待在这儿。我暂时移开视线，将注意力转回阿尔蒂萨带我来看的那具尸体上，就在这时，一丝异样在我心头萦绕。<BR>
<BR>
我更为仔细 -- 虽仍是保持距离 -- 地观察那欧格林，注意到它巨大的手上沾着血。那欧格林仿佛终于不在意我的存在了，转过身去，开始做什么我看不到的事。我向阿尔蒂萨投去询问的目光，她却似乎不明所以。我将疑虑向她说明，她笑了。<BR>
<BR>
“哦，阁下，他只是在吃东西。几年前我这儿闹老鼠，他把它们清理得一干二净。恐怕是吃上瘾了。他喜欢新鲜的 -- 活的 -- 但是......但他也偏爱嫩一点的。所以他就......”阿尔蒂萨将手握成拳状，“不过，我明白您的意思了。”仿佛为了强调她的话，它那个方向传来骨头碎裂的声音。<BR>
<BR>
这事放下，我开始检视那两具尸体。阿尔蒂萨已将尸体洗净，因此可以更清楚地看到他们受伤的位置与情形。两人都伤痕累累，全身遍布长而直的平行切痕，躯干上还有几道深深的裂口。我未见到任何大面积、明显的瘀伤，这与现场情况不符；若受害者真如他们房间及其他伤口所示遭受重击，那么尸体上应有相应的痕迹才对。<BR>
<BR>
“阿雷提女士，您还有什么补充吗？这两位逝者的灵魂，可曾对您说过什么？”<BR>
<BR>
她缓缓摇头，“恐怕我接收他们时，他们已在去往湮灭的路上了。内乌斯 -- 您右手边这位 -- 想知道‘那毛茸茸的东西去哪儿了’。不过他倒没显得多难过，只是好奇。没多久，湮灭就把他带走了。”阿尔蒂萨又顿了顿，思忖着什么，“我听到个传闻......有人说这是狼人干的。有我这大欧格林在，我倒不太担心 -- 只是有点紧张 -- 但阁下，这难道是真的吗？”<BR>
<BR>
我摸了摸下巴，沉吟道：“眼下，我还不便妄下定论。我想了解更多情况，再下判断。为此......恕我冒昧，女士，既然您与这些受害者关系亲近，您能跟我讲讲他们生前的事吗？”<BR>
<BR>
我重拾问话，阿尔蒂萨若有不悦，至少表现得很理解。“内乌斯，您已经‘认识’了，是个炼金术士。他随身带着各种稀罕植物，还有其他异域珍奇。他......他以前常笑说，人们抱怨他某些炼金品的味道，却对我这些尸体毫无怨言。第二位受害者，就是让刀锋们怒不可遏的那位，是他的好友。我另一位客人是格拉提尼乌斯·多兰，是个附魔师。他常跟我讲，他无偿为刀锋制作了多少非凡的物件 -- 那人非常关心帝国的安危。有次，他还想把地下室的石头附上魔，让我的‘客人’们保存得更好，但我不想太麻烦他。他们都是善良、诚实的人。”<BR>
<BR>
我点点头，“非常感谢，女士。希望没占用您太多时间。”<BR>
<BR>
“一点也不，”她向我保证。<BR>
<BR>
言毕，我向她告辞，开始绕犯罪现场寻找凯维乌斯。我在第五处现场找到他，他正在一条小巷里摆弄一根稻草，不时地看看巷子这头，又看看那头，显然百无聊赖。看见我时，他如释重负。<BR>
<BR>
“另外几处已经被清理过了，”他迎上来说，“我在这儿等的时候，清洁工来过。我把他们赶走了，但恐怕他们可能已经去了最后那家。不过，总比一处都没有强，希望如此。”<BR>
<BR>
“希望如此。”<BR>
<BR>
我弯下腰，检查巷子地上那零散的几块玻璃。石头上的玻璃，清晰可见，却少了点什么。至关重要的东西。我问凯维乌斯可曾觉得有何异样，他茫然地摇了摇头。<BR>
<BR>
“你亲眼看过那些凶案现场吧？”我耐心地问道。他点头后，我继续道：“那惨状，遍地血迹。墙上，地上，甚至天花板上。还记得天花板吗？有整个人的印记，像是有个浑身是血的人被扔了上去。现在我问你：一个人满身是血，在窗台上留下血迹，又怎么会在我们脚下的玻璃上不留一丝痕迹呢？”那少年惊愕得一时语塞，我才道出结论。“有人是从每处现场的窗户逃走的，但那人是在受害者还活着的时候逃走的。打碎窗户的人，并非凶手。”<BR>
<BR>
我一步步引导，他的脸色越来越明亮，还没等我说那可能是真凶身份的目击者，年轻的凯维乌斯便喊道：“愿众神受赞美！”<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
突然间，凯维乌斯对这案子的热情与兴趣有了答案，他结结巴巴地解释起来。“我父亲住在索瑟泰姆，为东帝国公司工作。上个月，我去那儿看他，告诉他我妹妹终于决定和一位英俊善良的小伙子安定下来了。我在霜蛾堡外呼吸清冽空气时，那里闹了狼人。一只狼人扑向我，满嘴獠牙，口水直流，我吓得大声求救。全副武装的守卫很快赶到，赶走了那畜生。他们检查我有没有受伤，没找到伤口，就把我放了。不幸的是，他们似乎从未想到，他们携带的疾病是通过唾液传播的，而非真正的咬伤；他们说我身上没有伤痕，所以一定没事。我没告诉他们，我当时吞下并呛出了那东西喷在我身上的腥臭唾液。不过那时，我在霜蛾堡的事已办完，我又不喜欢无聊乏味的旅行，就用召回法术回到了我在西罗帝尔的房子。”<BR>
<BR>
他停下来喘了口气，很快继续道。“起初一切正常，但过了几天，夜幕降临时，我意识到事情不太对劲。当时我不清楚困扰我的是什么，但猜到了最坏的情况。怀着这恐惧，我去找克兰提利乌斯·瓦修斯。他有个兄弟在军团，我想他或许知道该如何处理这感染。我记得，我打开他的门，汗水顺着脸淌，他跟我打招呼，问我怎么了，然后便一片模糊。早上，我发现克兰提利乌斯被杀了。我被沉重的负罪感压得麻木，因为那一定是我干的。一整天，我都害怕得不敢动弹。然后，夜幕降临，我慌了。我跑去找格拉利兰·图利乌斯；他与刀锋有关系 -- 我不清楚是什么关系 -- 但刀锋肯定无所不知，或者能查出来。格拉利兰一定能在我造成更大破坏之前，找到治愈我的方法。”<BR>
<BR>
“但早晨来临，我并未找到治愈之法。格拉利兰死在他家中，而我，还活着，仍认为自己是凶手。我离开镇子，找到一个曾为匪徒占据、后被军团清剿的洞穴。我带上几件简陋家当，用法术锁上门，等在那里。次日清晨，我打开门，匆匆赶回镇上，欣喜地发现夜里无人被杀。那洞穴便成了我的家。但一周后，又发生了一起谋杀 -- 法莉尼娅·雷修斯，一个药剂师 -- 又是一个我可能去求助的人。我洞穴的门完好无损，仍锁着，但门底边的泥土和碎石，被绝望的利爪刨开了。缝隙足以让我滑出去，而不惊动门。”<BR>
<BR>
“除了巨大的负罪感，我还开始感到一种深深的、啃噬般的饥饿。仿佛尽管我杀了人，却永远无法满足。我恐惧地坐在洞穴里，拼命想还有谁能帮我。可悲的是，这些人如今都成了受害者。克兰提利乌斯和格拉利兰，然后是法莉尼娅·雷修斯，我曾以为至少能让我昏睡一夜的巫师伊斯罗米尔，我以为能召唤湮灭智者来治愈我的召唤师冯维尔德，或许有药能救我的炼金术士内乌斯，或许能做出压制疾病的附魔师格拉提尼乌斯......我......我想，你来了，或许能破案，找到我。我 -- 即使我知道自己有罪，我以为你或许知道治愈我的方法。我害怕我会成为你的下一个目标。”<BR>
<BR>
我惊讶地眨了眨眼。我知道有狼人牵扯其中，那可怜的感染者并非凶手 -- 或者，至少不是这一系列案子的真凶 -- 却没想到，他竟一直就在我眼皮底下。我缓缓开口：“所以，你记得打碎窗户，或者，在你那朦胧的夜间疯狂中，记得那声响？”<BR>
<BR>
“我......嗯，有点印象。我觉得更合理的解释是，我醒来时身上还带着碎片。但......但我的手臂总是血迹斑斑......”<BR>
<BR>
“介意让我看看吗？”我问道，仍觉有些不真实。他卷起袖子，我立刻明白了怎么回事，向他解释道。“你徘徊在变身边缘，昏昏沉沉地跌撞在镇上，寻找能帮助你的人。看到你这般惨状，救助你的人会让你进去，开始查看你的状况。要么在变身发生的那一刻，要么就在之前，你会从窗户逃走，以免伤害他们。我不确定之后你去了哪里，但肯定是在镇外。虽然嗜血欲望吞噬了你，但即便变成狼人，你也不会伤害别人。看看你的手臂！你一定是在某个黑暗角落，啃噬着自己的手臂，来抵御最强烈的饥饿。”<BR>
<BR>
倏忽间，我的心情再次阴郁下来。我知道凶手是谁，这让我困扰。然而，除了凯维乌斯拜访过受害者之外，这竟是我能找到的他们之间唯一的联系，尽管这联系并未涵盖所有受害者。结论是，凶手本只想除掉凯维乌斯的几个救助者，却将所有见过凯维乌斯的人都杀了，好更彻底地嫁祸于他。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
“恐怕我还需要你帮忙，”我对凯维乌斯说，“需要你去和看守第一案发现场的那位护法官说一声。告诉他我有些有趣的发现，请他在阿尔蒂萨·阿雷提家与我碰面。务必也通知刀锋桑里特；毕竟，这是他在调查。”<BR>
<BR>
凯维乌斯一如之前那般热忱急切，毫不犹豫。“当然！”他立刻跑开了。<BR>
<BR>
至于我，则匆匆赶往阿雷提女士家，向她解释并说明，她家为何要迎来这么多客人。她似乎有点担心，我要把他们领进有欧格林的地下室，但我向她保证 -- 虽然听起来难以置信 -- 他们不仅不会介意，还会很高兴那野兽在那儿。除了这点小小的顾虑，这位年轻的丹莫出乎意料地通情达理。<BR>
<BR>
几分钟后，凯维乌斯来了，身后跟着桑里特和护法官。两人都一脸困惑，桑里特更是将好奇问出了口。<BR>
<BR>
“来这里作甚？此案我们跟了数周了。布莱顿人，你要是想让我们看尸体上的伤痕，我们早已了然于胸。”<BR>
<BR>
我自信地笑了笑。“哦，伤痕只是其中一部分。你们若看腻了，想必还有更引人入胜的东西。我虽不奢望拼凑出全貌，但已将我手中的线索拼接得相当完整。”<BR>
<BR>
走下通往地下室的楼梯时，桑里特和护法官不安地环顾四周。突然的寒意、尸体，还有欧格林，定会让大多数人感到不适。我默默绕过高架石板走了几圈，其他人则定了定神。或许是因执法官员在场而紧张，阿尔蒂萨向我靠拢。凯维乌斯研究着墙壁，坚决不看那些并非他造成的尸体。刀锋和护法官站在门边，离欧格林尽可能远。那欧格林对我们毫不理会。<BR>
<BR>
“嗯，我得承认，我有些犹豫。真不知从何说起。”我缓缓开口，“想必诸位都记得第二位受害者格拉利兰·图利乌斯，刀锋的侄子。他的死，我想我这样说不算不敬：他确实是刀锋的侄子没错，可我觉得奇怪的是，他本人也是该组织成员这一点，竟无人提及。”我举手示意，压下逐渐嘈杂的声音。“不，发现这一事实，并非靠我什么特殊本领。纯粹是偶然。我多年前便认识这位受害者，曾与他共事，处理过另一起案件。”<BR>
<BR>
“现在，我知道诸位调查员一直在搜寻狼人，但即便你们找到了狼人，那也并非你们的真凶。你们之中，有人明白我在说什么......”我话音渐弱，希望真凶能自我暴露。“......但看来那人还在等着，等着我们对他们已知的事实予以彻底证实。也罢。”<BR>
<BR>
我走到内乌斯的遗体旁，示意其他人仔细看。我指着躯干上那些长而整齐的切口，继续道：“看到这些伤口了吗？它们相互平行，所以很容易被误认为是狼人的爪痕。但若你熟悉爪痕，便会发现这些沟痕太笔直了。事实上，它们根本不是沟痕。这种伤痕由利器造成；是切割伤，而非抓伤，而且故意做成像是野兽所为。诸位或许知晓，狼人不用武器，至少狼形时不用。所以凶手，必定是更为寻常之人。”<BR>
<BR>
“所以，凶手知道狼人的存在，并且确实是根据狼人的行踪来选择受害者。凶手知道狼人是谁。依目前公众的猜疑，凶手随时可以将替罪羊交给当局，而无人知晓他才是真凶。那狼人为何至今仍逍遥法外？因为凶手知道我要来。因为凶手知道狼人会来找我，而这正好给他一个杀我的机会，从而彻底洗清狼人的嫌疑。”<BR>
<BR>
“既然真凶执意保持沉默，我便给出最大的线索：凶手在我抵达之前，就早已知道我要来调查此事。谁会知道？自然是负责调查此案的人。”我转向他，伸出手指，厉声指控：“桑里特。”<BR>
<BR>
我不曾想，那张原本就黝黑的脸，竟还能更黑几分。他轻蔑地看了护法官一眼，说道：“当然是我干的，蠢货。你一天之内就查出这么多，以为我会无能到三周还毫无头绪？我让护法官追查假线索，甚至编造线索，就是不想此案告破。而我处心积虑，确保它永远不会告破。等我最终将凯维乌斯交出去时，我便会把这调查的缓慢，都怪到这些愚蠢的护法官头上。”<BR>
<BR>
我朝桑里特点点头，继续道：“既然您如此好心，承认了罪行，那能否再为我解最后一个谜团？我虽有怀疑，却不敢肯定。为何要杀人？”<BR>
<BR>
桑里特摇头否认。“何必多费口舌，反正我要杀光你们，再让凯维乌斯当替罪羊。”他拔出剑，向我逼近。我感到阿尔蒂萨的手臂环住了我，寻求庇护，随即，我听到了那声响。那欧格林以与其庞大身躯不相称的敏捷与优雅，将我们扫到身后，朝桑里特发出骇人的怒吼。我跳起来，越过它巨大的肩膀看去，只见桑里特脸色刷白。我再跳起时，那红卫人已转身逃跑。<BR>
<BR>
我半跳半爬地翻过欧格林，拔出自己的剑。我从未有过使用这柄武士刀的机会，尽管作为绅士的佩剑，我时常练习。此刻容不得迟疑，更容不得犹豫。很快，凶手便要逃到街上去。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
我追着桑里特上了一层楼，见他在客厅稍作停顿。他的犹豫告诉我，他在权衡能否及时冲出前门摆脱我。显然，他以为风险太大，转而跑向另一段楼梯。我紧随其后，只听前方传来一声破碎的巨响，他从一扇窗户逃了出去，那似乎是阿尔蒂萨的卧室。我无暇去想，作为谋杀案的替罪羊，凯维乌斯此前也曾多次这般逃跑，这是多么讽刺。我只能跟着桑里特，看着他从一个屋顶跳到另一个屋顶。我担心他那红卫人闻名的肾上腺素会开始飙升；若是如此，他若继续逃跑，我将永远追不上他......而若他转身应战，我又能否与他匹敌，实未可知。<BR>
<BR>
跳过三座屋顶后，这壮汉拿定了主意。就在我跳起的瞬间，他猛地转身，空着的那只手狠狠击中我的腹部。我试图顺势翻滚卸力，但这等重击，又岂是翻滚能化解的。我倒地停下，仰面朝天，刚举起武士刀护住脸面，桑里特的剑已挥下，直取我的头颅。他挥剑力道之大，即便如此，我险些还是被斩。我一脚踢向他腿部，趁其失去平衡，迅速弹起，摆好迎战的架势。<BR>
<BR>
那杀人的红卫人迅速起身，愤怒地挥剑向我猛攻。我格挡着他每一次刺击，且战且退。我虚晃一剑，佯攻他大腿，以此争取时间跳向另一座屋顶；在桑里特的猛攻下，我且战且退，脚下的屋顶已所剩无几，无法支撑第二轮交锋。他或许会再次逃跑，但我想，他定是希望这场临时决斗能有个了断，我赌对了。<BR>
<BR>
跃过来时，桑里特扭身挥出一记大弧度的斩击，以免我像他对我那样，趁他跃起时偷袭。我无法立即追击，但这种扭转，必然会露出破绽。我迅速攻向他暴露的后背，特意用了刀背；他或许杀人如麻，但于我而言，活捉罪犯总比杀死好。<BR>
<BR>
一击之下，他在倾斜的屋顶上失去平衡，给了我第二次出击的机会，这次砍中了他持剑的手腕。结果如我所愿：长剑脱手飞出。然而，我低估了红卫人的速度，他竟用另一只手凌空接住了长剑，立即转身再次进攻。我未曾料到，他竟能左右开弓。他脸上挂着狰狞的笑，对我频频突刺，交替挥砍我的手臂和头部。<BR>
<BR>
屋顶再次逼近尽头，我最后一次跳起，谨慎地选择了落脚点。桑里特紧随其后，我背向边缘退开。他逼近时，我将武士刀换到另一只手上；肾上腺素激增的红卫人，那沉重的打击足以耗竭任何剑士的体力。剑刃相交，我终于明白，我无法承受他那如雨点般的猛攻。他实在太快，太强，太不知疲倦，而我又太不愿伤他。<BR>
<BR>
我们继续缠斗，直到第三轮交锋最后一击，力道如此之强，我竟失了平衡。这红卫人终于胜券在握，准备挥出最后一斩，取我性命。他全程心无旁骛，专注于战斗，而我却并非如此。他居高临下，胜利在握，此刻，我那些分心的思考，终于要派上用场了。我向旁翻滚，与他拉开距离，朝他施放了强力的沉重术。桑里特已来不及反应。<BR>
<BR>
他体重骤增，屋顶轰然塌陷，他狼狈地摔进楼里。我本颇为担心落点，但朝塌陷处望去，便知担心是多余的。桑里特摔穿了护法官驻地的屋顶，恰巧掉进一间空牢房。四周全是护法官，透过那洞看到的云朵，怕是他一时半会儿能见的最后天空了。<BR>
<BR>
然而，作为调查者，一个问题仍在我心中萦绕不去：为何？若不查明是什么驱使这红卫人杀人，我便不会对这结论释怀。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
因桑里特是在护法官面前承认的罪行，他知道自己结局已定。因此，他并未拒绝回答我的问题。从他口中，一幅清晰的图景逐渐浮现。<BR>
<BR>
当一个城市中有两名刀锋，而其中一人不知道另一人存在（正如桑里特不知道格拉利兰·图利乌斯），通常有两种可能：他们各自在调查不相干的事，或是其中一人级别高于另一人。鉴于他们工作的敏感性，刀锋不与上级直接联络，亦非罕见。格拉利兰与桑里特即是如此，而桑里特对他那不知名上司下达的命令很是不满。正如桑里特所言，“浪费了他的才华”。桑里特相信，格拉利兰若出了什么事，他便可取而代之，或许更重要的是，接替其级别。<BR>
<BR>
与克兰提利乌斯·瓦修斯的一次闲聊中，桑里特才发现是谁在浪费他的才华。克兰提利乌斯误以为桑里特已知道其同僚刀锋的身份。这一疏忽，让桑里特开始谋划如何除掉他的上司。可一旦克兰提利乌斯得知格拉利兰的身份并非人尽皆知，他便可能对桑里特起疑。这就是为何克兰提利乌斯成了第一个受害者；凯维乌斯恰巧在当晚造访了他，纯属运气。<BR>
<BR>
狼人突然出现，桑里特措手不及，便决定伪造现场，将一切嫁祸给狼人。此后，这红卫人便竭力查明狼人身份；若能抓住它，定是他职业生涯中的亮点。翌日晚间，他跟踪凯维乌斯至格拉利兰家时，简直不敢相信自己的好运。这似乎好得不像真的，但桑里特怎会吹毛求疵。<BR>
<BR>
格拉利兰被杀，镇上显然有了杀人犯，桑里特立刻被授予了他梦寐以求的级别，并被指派负责此案，作为他的第一项职责。本可另派刀锋前来，但考虑到桑里特对镇上居民与情况早已熟悉，他们认为桑里特更合适。护法官们对调查权被移交并无太多抱怨，毕竟，那惨烈的犯罪现场令他们中不少人深感不安。<BR>
<BR>
如今，桑里特得偿所愿，本可当即交出凯维乌斯。但他担心，万一有别的人知道格拉利兰的身份，他从谋杀中获利便会惹人怀疑。他知道内乌斯是格拉利兰的密友（尽管内乌斯不知道格拉利兰是刀锋，但他认识格拉利兰），却想不出不惹人疑窦地除掉他；镇上出现两个杀手，未免太巧合了。抱着这念头，他杀了法莉尼娅·雷修斯、伊斯罗米尔和冯维尔德，好与他的狼人替罪羊保持同步。<BR>
<BR>
大约此时，他突然意识到，凯维乌斯在寻找可能医治他病患的人。桑里特再次为自己的好运窃喜 -- 凯维乌斯定会拜访那个碍事的炼金术士，给他提供绝佳的杀人机会。这红卫人本打算在那之后就交出凯维乌斯，但命运似乎突然不再眷顾他。<BR>
<BR>
负责此案的护法官对调查进展与不断攀升的死者人数愈发不满，遂请一位刀锋朋友请求我的协助。该法官将他的行动告知了桑里特，凯维乌斯这才得以继续逍遥。桑里特以为，凯维乌斯会来找我，期望我将他送进监狱（这样他就不能再害人了）。一方面，桑里特希望凯维乌斯担下所有罪责，而我不会追根究底；另一方面，若我深查此案，他也可将我杀死，再将罪名扣在凯维乌斯头上。格拉提尼乌斯·多兰在桑里特等待我到来时被杀。格拉提尼乌斯确实因慈善事业知晓格拉利兰的级别，但桑里特相信，他能利用格拉提尼乌斯对帝国的赤诚，让他不敢声张。<BR>
<BR>
桑里特本身已是强者，而红卫人那令人闻风丧胆的肾上腺素更是如虎添翼。这便是他能将现场破坏得如此彻底的缘由。这便是他能如此迅速制服受害者的原因，当然，出其不意也是因素之一（多少人目睹狼人变身，紧接着，一个潜在的护卫者会拔剑相向？）。这让他能轻松将尸体抛起，在天花板上留下血迹斑斑的全身印记。待他冷静下来，便用剑在尸体上留下“标志性的爪痕”。之后，他从已被凯维乌斯打破的窗户逃走 -- 这便是为何窗台有血迹，而玻璃上却没有。他总不能浑身血淋淋地走在镇上，徒惹人注目。<BR>
<BR>
桑里特定是对我怀恨在心，若非我介入，他本可逍遥法外。不过，我倒未花太多时间担心报复。因他杀害同僚，便已犯了叛国罪；加之七项谋杀指控（克兰提利乌斯、格拉利兰、法莉尼娅、伊斯罗米尔、冯维尔德、内乌斯和格拉提尼乌斯），刽子手倒也没让他等太久。<BR>
<BR>
至于凯维乌斯，他终于找到了能帮他治愈狼化症的人。这是一种非常规疾病，其疗法自然存在于非常规的圈子里，而作为死灵法师的阿尔蒂萨·阿雷提，恰恰熟悉某些相当非常规的圈子。因为他变身狼人期间，除了自己，并未伤害任何人，故未对他提出任何指控。不过，他倒是赔偿了所有被他打碎的窗户。也许，罪责的重担已从他肩上卸下，但他的责任感，依然完好。<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="821E00" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"> <IMG SRC="TR\tr_arena_bookart.dds" WIDTH="240" HEIGHT="120"> <BR>
Welcome to the Arena<BR> 
<BR>
Interview with Arminius Aurix, Editor of the Kragenmoor Arena <BR> <BR>
*** <BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Most folks who come to the arena don't know who I am. I prefer it that way. I always say, it's the fighters that should be at the center of attention. Me, I stay on the sidelines, overseeing everything. I plan and schedule the games, I pick the fighters and their equipment, and decide who's fighting who. That's the job of an editor. If the attention is ever on me, it's because I'm doing the job wrong. <BR>
<BR>
There are people, I know this, who think that what happens in the arena is unseemly. They think we peddle death. Perfumed noblemen and silly little priests have refused my hand and called me a bloodmonger to my face! I call them hypocrites. Death is a natural part of all life, isn't it? In the arena we do not hide this truth. We drag it out into the open for everyone to see. It is not only enterntainment, I think, but a great public service that we provide. Everyone who witnesses the games will come to a profound realization: we are not creatures of spirit. We are blood and bone, all of us. <BR>
<BR>
Slaves? No, there's hardly any fighting slaves here in Kragenmoor. I'd forgive you for thinking that it's because the crowds would find it upsetting, but in truth people do not care whether it's a shackled man or a free one bleeding for their amusement. What they care about -- and what, in turn, I care about -- is that we put on a good show. And the fact is most slaves have no notion whatsoever of showmanship. They are timid. Passive. When they do fight, they fight like spastic rabbits. It is a sorry display. They're only interested in their own survival, not in the grand drama of combat. Can't really fault them for that, though -- they've been dealt a rotten hand. <BR>
<BR>
Our fighters are trained professionals, all of them. I oversee their training myself. A good arena fighter is a master of all martial disciplines. They are familiar with all types of weapons. Short blade, spear, axe... no matter. The more exotic, the better. As for their other equipment, light armor or no armor at all is preferable. The crowds will perceive wearing heavy armor as cowardice, but a bare chest -- that's bravado. That's real, mortal danger. A veteran fighter's scars are badges of honor that should be on display for all to see! <BR> 
 <BR>
You ask why would anyone wish to become a fighter of their own free will? First, you must know that not every fight is to the death. It would be a terrible waste of talent otherwise. Sometimes there's a draw, sometimes the other fighter yields. Second, the pay is not bad. The most successful fighters retire this business quite rich, in fact. But the third reason is the most important one: it's that there's glory to be won in the arena. It is easy to overlook, but it's true. The adoration of the crowd can be more intoxicating than any wine. The arena offers anyone, now matter how lowborn or downtrodden, a chance to make a name for themselves. To become hero of the public and have their memory live on in songs and epitaphs etched into the arena walls long after their bones have turned to dust. To be loved and remembered for an eternity. <BR>
<BR>
Isn't there an old Dark Elven adage that says you can "reach heaven by violence"? That's what the arena can give you. If you've got what it takes.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="821E00" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><IMG SRC="TR\tr_arena_bookart.dds" WIDTH="240" HEIGHT="120"><BR>
欢迎来到竞技场<BR>
<BR>
克拉根穆尔竞技场主编阿米尼乌斯·奥里克斯访谈录<BR><BR>
***<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
来竞技场的人大多不知道我是谁。我倒喜欢这样。我总说，焦点该是那些斗士。我呢，就待在边上，统管全局。我策划安排赛事，挑选斗士和装备，决定谁与谁对阵。这便是主编的工作。若聚光灯照到了我身上，那准是我失职了。<BR>
<BR>
我知道，有些人认为竞技场里的事有伤风化。他们觉得我们兜售死亡。那些浑身香气的贵族和愚昧的小祭司们，拒绝与我握手，当面骂我是嗜血的屠夫！我倒要叫他们伪君子。死亡是万物生命自然的一部分，难道不是吗？在竞技场，我们从不遮掩这真相。我们把它拖到光天化日之下，让所有人都看见。我想，这不仅是一种娱乐，更是我们提供的一项伟大公共服务。每个亲眼见证比赛的人，都将领悟一个深刻的道理：我们并非灵魂的造物。我们皆是血肉之躯，仅此而已。<BR>
<BR>
奴隶？不，克拉根穆尔这儿几乎没有奴隶斗士。要是你猜想那是因为观众会觉着不舒服，那我得说你错了，其实人们并不在意为他们取乐而流血的是枷锁缠身还是自由之身。他们在意的 -- 也因此是我在意的 -- 是我们能否奉献一场好戏。事实是，大多数奴隶压根不懂什么是表演。他们畏缩、被动。即使上场，打起架来也像抽筋的兔子，那副模样实在可怜。他们只关心自己能否活命，对战斗的宏大戏剧性毫无兴趣。不过，这也不能怪他们 -- 毕竟命运待他们不公。<BR>
<BR>
我们的斗士，个个都是受过训练的专业人士。我亲自监督他们的训练。优秀的竞技场斗士，须精通所有格斗技艺。他们熟悉各种武器。短刃、矛、斧......不论何种，越稀奇古怪越好。至于其他装备，轻甲或者干脆不穿甲才最受欢迎。观众会觉得穿重甲是怯懦的表现，而赤裸上身 -- 那才是勇气的象征。那才是真正的、致命的危险。老练斗士身上的伤疤，是荣耀的徽章，就该让所有人都看见！<BR>
<BR>
你问，为何有人心甘情愿去做斗士？首先，你得明白，并非每场比赛都至死方休。否则，人才岂不白白浪费？有时战平，有时一方认输。其次，报酬不菲。实际上，最成功的斗士退役时往往相当富有。但最重要的，是第三点：竞技场里能赢取荣耀。这道理容易被忽略，却千真万确。观众的欢呼与崇拜，比任何美酒都更令人沉醉。竞技场为任何人 -- 无论出身多么低微，境遇多么困顿 -- 提供了一个出人头地的机会。成为公众的英雄，让名字在歌声中流传，让事迹刻入竞技场的石壁，在骸骨化为尘土后，仍被铭记、被热爱，直至永恒。<BR>
<BR>
古老的丹莫谚语不是说了吗？“凭暴力可登天堂”。这便是竞技场能给予你的。前提是，你得有那本事。<BR>
<BR>"""

The Windhelm Letters<BR>
<BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR>
The following transcribed letters were recovered from a strongbox found after a fire consumed a house in Solitude in the early part of the 3rd Era. Nobody by the addressed name lived at the home, and it is unknown how long the family had owned the strongbox. The letters are believed to have been written during the reign of Jarl Elgryr the Unminded, who ruled Windhelm in the Second Era and about whom few other records are extant. <BR>
<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
My dearest Thessalonius,<BR>
<BR>
I hope this letter reaches you, and finds you well. It is getting more difficult to find paper within the city, but I still save the scraps sent by the city's tax agents. I hope you don't mind a household reckoning on the reverse of this.<BR>
<BR>
Windhelm remains as cold as ever, but nothing compared to the heart of her king. Smoke and revelry rise from the palace daily, while we have little wood or coal to keep the chill off. I fear for the little ones, but they're so brave, having never known any other kind of life. We all speak of you daily, and hope that we may come to see you soon.<BR>
<BR>
Yours, Reylia<BR>
____<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
Dear Thessalonius,<BR>
<BR>
Your last message arrived safely, but the promised gold mentioned within did not. When I mentioned this to the courier, she shrugged and turned to the door with no other word. While hearing from you brings joy to us all, I would caution you to not trust that particular woman again.<BR>
<BR>
The minds of the city grow numb with cold and silence. We starve, and the unminded one makes no appearance, no speech, nothing to succor his people. His wizard has been seen walking the streets of the city at odd hours, visiting homes. I saw him paint some horrid symbol on one door -- it dripped like blood before vanishing like sand in the wind. The next dawn, nobody who lived there still drew breath. I am a friend to one of the scullery maids who was sent to clean out the house. She described the most horrible things to me and the children, but I will spare you the details.<BR>
<BR>
The worst of it is, that was a house that supported the king. If that's what happens to his friends, what will be the fate of the rest of us?<BR>
<BR>
But don't let this shift your mind from its important tasks. We all know you work to free us, and pray for your success and swift return.<BR>
<BR>
Love, Reylia<BR>
____<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
This next letter was scribbled onto a piece of cloth with what appears to be charcoal.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
Thess.,<BR>
<BR>
I hope you didn't actually ... [illegible] ... efforts are important, but our sufferings must remain ... [illegible] ... retaliation can be swift and terrible. If you no longer care for me, at least think of your ... [illegible] .... Love always, R<BR>
____<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
Dear Thessalonius,<BR>
<BR>
Weeks go by and we have no word from Solitude. I tell the children that you're simply very busy, but it's getting harder to make excuses for you. If you can no longer send money (and I understand, smuggling anything of value into the city has become a fool's errand), at least send word that you still live and work for the freedom of Windhelm.<BR>
<BR>
As regards your issue that I mentioned previously, worry not. With food shortages being what they are, I have removed it from my concerns.<BR>
<BR>
Always yours, Reylia<BR>
____<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
My dearest Thessalonius,<BR>
<BR>
It was good to hear from you at last. Please forgive the rantings of a starving mind. We have at last depleted the basement stores of food, even with the strictest rationing. I see the little ones' faces growing thin and my heart weeps for them. They are, in some ways, brave. I think they're looking after me moreso than I them.<BR>
<BR>
Please come home. I strongly desire to look upon your face.<BR>
<BR>
R<BR>
____<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
Papa,<BR>
<BR>
Ma said to write you, so we love and miss you. Ma is tired a lot, but has lots of visitors, so we are being good and helping.<BR>
<BR>
Love, Stessl and Shapl<BR>
____<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
Thessalonius,<BR>
<BR>
I don't have much time. The city has finally broken. The gates of the palace will not keep us out. The storming begins soon. I have gathered those who still have a spirit to live, and we are taking our own fortunes to hand. I hope to see you on the other side of this. Pray for us as we once prayed for you.<BR>
<BR>
Your Reylia<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Woodcutter's Wife<BR>
Volume I<BR>
<BR>
As Told By <BR>
Mogen Son of Molag<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Legend tells of a woodcutter who built a shack deep within the pine forest. There, he hoped to live in peace with his family.<BR>
<BR>
The woodcutter's family lived well for a time, but without warning, the weather turned bitterly cold and spoiled the harvest. Before long, with their meager supply of food all but gone, the family was starving.<BR>
<BR>
Late one snowy night, a traveler knocked on the cabin door seeking shelter from the biting cold. Always generous of heart, the woodcutter welcomed the stranger into his home, apologizing that he had no food to offer.<BR>
<BR>
With a smile, the traveler cast off his cloak to reveal the garments of a mage. As the woodcutter and his family looked on, the mysterious visitor reached into his satchel and withdrew a scroll tied with a silver ribbon. No sooner had the wizard unfurled the scroll and read the words aloud, when a great feast appeared from out of thin air. That night, nobody in the woodcutter's cabin went hungry.<BR>
<BR>
Day by day, the snow piled up. Every night, the mage produced another scroll from his bag and read the words, each time summoning a new feast. On the fifth night, the woodcutter's wife awoke her husband to confess her mistrust of their magical guest. Surely, she argued, there was some price to pay for the magical feasts that everyone enjoyed night after night.<BR>
<BR>
The woodcutter would have none of it. After nearly dying from the lack of food, his family was eating well. The divines had sent them a gift, he explained, and it was foolish to question their wisdom.<BR>
<BR>
But the woodcutter's wife would not be persuaded. Every night, she grew more fearful and more desperate. She was certain that the family had entered into a devil's bargain, and the time would soon come when the mage would ask for something unspeakable in return for his gifts.<BR>
<BR>
While everyone in the cabin slept, the woodcutter's wife snuck out of bed and took her husband's axe in hand. She crept into the traveler's room and with one swing, lopped off his head.<BR>
<BR>
Suddenly, the wizard's disembodied head awoke. His eyes opened wide and when he beheld his maimed body, he let forth a terrible cry.<BR>
<BR>
Awakened by the horrified scream, the woodcutter and his children rushed into the room and gasped at the terrible sight of the decapitated mage.<BR>
<BR>
With his last gasp of breath, the traveler laid a fearful curse on the woodcutter's wife. After her mortal death, she was damned to rise once again and walk the woods alone only to burn at the rising of the sun.<BR>
<BR>
To this day, those who walk the pine forest late at night tell tales of a weeping woman glimpsed between the trees. She carries a bloody axe, the stories say, and is terrifying to behold.<BR>
<BR>"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
樵夫之妻<BR>
卷一<BR>
<BR>
讲述者<BR>
莫拉格之子莫根<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
传说有位樵夫，在松林深处搭建了一间木屋。他希望能与家人在那里安居乐业。<BR>
<BR>
樵夫一家起初过得不错，但天气骤然酷寒，收成尽毁。没过多久，他们仅存的一点食物也消耗殆尽，一家人陷入了饥饿。<BR>
<BR>
一个风雪交加的深夜，一位旅人叩响了木屋的门，希望能躲避刺骨的严寒。樵夫一向心地善良，便邀请这位陌生人进屋，并抱歉地说自己拿不出食物款待。<BR>
<BR>
旅人微笑着脱下斗篷，露出了法师的装束。樵夫一家惊奇地看着这位神秘访客从行囊中取出一卷系着银丝带的卷轴。法师展开卷轴，大声诵读，霎时间，一桌丰盛的宴席凭空出现。那一夜，樵夫木屋里再无人挨饿。<BR>
<BR>
日复一日，积雪越来越深。法师每晚都会从袋中取出一卷新的卷轴，诵读咒文，变出一场新的盛宴。第五个夜晚，樵夫的妻子摇醒丈夫，坦言她对这位神秘来客的不信任。她争辩说，大家每晚享用的魔法盛宴，肯定是要付出代价的。<BR>
<BR>
樵夫根本听不进去。一家人此前差点饿死，现在终于能吃饱饭了。他解释说，这是圣灵赐予他们的礼物，质疑圣灵的智慧是愚蠢的。<BR>
<BR>
然而，樵夫的妻子不为所动。每个夜晚，她的恐惧与绝望都在加剧。她确信，一家人是与魔鬼做了交易，法师很快就会要求他们付出难以言喻的代价，以换取这些礼物。<BR>
<BR>
当木屋里所有人都沉沉睡去，樵夫的妻子悄悄下床，拿起了丈夫的斧头。她蹑手蹑脚地走进旅人的房间，手起斧落，砍下了他的头颅。<BR>
<BR>
突然，法师的头颅睁开了眼睛。他双眼圆睁，当看到自己残缺的身体时，发出了一声可怖的嚎叫。<BR>
<BR>
樵夫和孩子们被这骇人的尖叫惊醒，冲进房间，看到身首异处的法师，惊得倒吸一口凉气。<BR>
<BR>
旅人用尽最后一口气，对樵夫的妻子施加了可怕的诅咒。她死后，将注定再次复活，在林中独行，并在日出时被烈焰焚尽。<BR>
<BR>
直至今日，那些在深夜穿行于松林的人，仍会讲述在树影间瞥见哭泣女人的传说。故事里说，她手提一把血斧，其貌可怖。<BR>
<BR>"""

Part 2: Sheor the Tusked-Trickster<BR>
<BR>
Now let me tell you of Sheor, also called the Tusked-Trickster. Sheor was trusted with the important duties of a scout and spent his days mapping the Steppes ahead of the tribe alongside his companion and lover, Kyne. In their seclusion did thoughts of menace manifest betwixt their rutting (who influenced the other I cannot say). It was on one night in a time without nights that The Accursed Two returned to the Celestial Camp.<BR>
<BR>
"Holy hosts, I bring to you a mind of revelatory power. I mean to bring Mortality to Substance and I require the assistance of my brothers and sisters! Kyne herself has laid the foundation of our proposition. Heed her!"<BR>
<BR>
So it was that many of the gods participated in the creation of Nirn, like Magnus Sun-Shaped, who worked with Kyne in the shaping the basis of the new reality. These beings would become the aedra. Those who sat and watched their brothers and sisters and did nothing (save the Funny-Man, who yelled and yelled for Zeyht to invent cheese) became the daedra.<BR>
<BR>
It was just before their creation was finished that Sheor spoke once more:<BR>
<BR>
"Brethren! We are but on the cusp of reaping the benefits of our toiling. I ask you to sing with me in celebration!"<BR>
ON THIS AUSPICIOUS DAY OF DAYS<BR>
SHEOR ASKS HIS EQUALS FOR THREE GIFTS<BR>
HE SHALL NAME THEM WITH HEART AFLUTTER:<BR>
LET THE DAWN BECOME NEW LIKE NO OTHER DAWN BEFORE<BR>
LET THE CORPSE OF THE OLD AND CYNICAL FORM THE FOUNDATION OF THE NEW AND HOPEFUL<BR>
AND LET NIRN BE TORN FROM THE MIND OF THE ARTISAN<BR>
AND BE MADE WHOLE INCARNATE<BR>
NE NU-MANTIA; ALTADOON LORKHJ<BR>
<BR>
Then something horrible happened.<BR>
<BR>
In the creation of this world, the aedra found themselves unable to move their tents and their herds of spectra refused to leave, mucking up the place with bleating. Worse yet, our ancestors were cursed with this mortality (this is why we tell our children to hold back tears when they scuffle their knees, to not grant the Trickster his due). The daedra watched on in a combination of envy, horror, and amusement at the expense of their kin.<BR>
<BR>
"Why have you done this, brother?" cried Zeyht, his mouth spilling forth with locusts.<BR>
<BR>
"You desire my motivations? Know this, for our children shall not! For-"<BR>
<BR>
Yet Sheor was unable to complete his rambling diatribe, as Orc-Friend Trini himself set himself upon the traitor, pummeling him into theological particulates.<BR>

<BR>
“神圣的众位，我为你们带来一个蕴含启示之力的想法。我打算将‘死亡’引入‘物质’，这需要兄弟姐妹们的协助！吉讷已为我们提议奠定了基础。请听从她！”<BR>
<BR>
于是，众多神灵参与了奈恩的创造，例如形如太阳的玛格努斯，他与吉讷一同塑造了新现实的基础。这些存在后来成为了艾德拉。而那些只是坐视兄弟姐妹们劳作而无所作为者（除了那位“滑稽者”，他不停地叫嚷着让泽伊特发明奶酪）则成为了迪德拉。<BR>

<BR>
“同胞们！我们辛勤劳作，丰收在即。我恳请你们与我一同高歌庆祝！”<BR>
在此吉日中的吉日<BR>
舍奥尔向其同等者求取三件礼物<BR>
他心潮澎湃，即将道出它们之名：<BR>
愿这黎明焕然一新，前所未有<BR>
愿陈旧与讥讽之躯，成为崭新与希望之基<BR>
愿奈恩脱离造物主之思绪<BR>
化为完整之化身<BR>
新 奴-曼提亚；阿尔塔顿 洛克杰<BR>

<BR>
在这世界的创造过程中，艾德拉们发现自己无法移动帐篷，他们的灵性兽群也拒绝离开，咩咩叫着将地方弄得一团糟。更糟的是，我们的祖先被这“死亡”所诅咒（这就是我们教导孩子，在擦破膝盖时要忍住眼泪，不给欺诈者留下任何把柄的原因）。迪德拉们则以一种混杂着嫉妒、恐惧和幸灾乐祸的心态，看着他们的同胞。<BR>

<BR>

Yngol and the Sea-Ghosts<BR><BR>

Masser and Secunda passed over Ysgramor's people as their fellowship landed in long-boats upon the rocky shores of Hsaarik Head on their journey from Atmora to Mereth. Boats littered the coast, but Ysgramor did not count his kin, Yngol's among them.<BR>
<BR>
Ysgramor commanded the sea-ghosts to surrender his kin, and a great gale darkened the sky. The seas thrashed and churned, and a wrathful storm appeared. Ysgramor took up the oars and rowed into the storm alone.<BR>
<BR>
Upon the Sea, Ysgramor wrestled the sea-ghosts, and the storm carried him along the jagged coast. Two fortnights passed without relief, until finally the storm broke. Come the next dawn, Yngol's long-boat was found in the icy surf, but the vengeful sea-ghosts had already taken Yngol and his clansmen.<BR>
<BR>
In his terrible grief, Ysgramor slew a dozen dozen beasts and burned them in honor of his fallen kinsman. A barrow-hill was dug in the Atmoran tradition, and Yngol was laid to rest with rites and honors among his clansmen far below the rocky face of Hsaarik Head, the first Children of the Sky to perish in Tamriel.<BR>
